_meta.builtFrom: recipe_sets.jsonl + recipenlg.csv (joined on the CSV index column)
_meta.selectionRule: WEAK-2: quality-filtered (steps mention >=1/3 of ingredients, title foods present, no foreign meats); per normalised title the most complete variant + <=1 more with Jaccard <= 0.25; titles sampled in seeded-hash order

d: Wash potatoes; prick several times with a fork.
Microwave them with a wet paper towel covering the potatoes on high for 6-8 minutes.
The potatoes should be soft, ready to eat.
Let them cool enough to handle.
Cut in half lengthwise; scoop out pulp and reserve.
Discard shells.
Brown ground beef until done.
Drain any grease from the meat.
Set aside when done.
Meat will be added later.
Melt butter in a large kettle over low heat; add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually add milk; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in potato, ground beef, salt, pepper, 1 cup of cheese, 2 tablespoons of green onion and 1/2 cup of bacon.
Cook until heated (do not boil).
Stir in sour cream if desired; cook until heated (do not boil).
Sprinkle with remaining cheese, bacon and green onions.
Mix taco sauce, sour cream and cream cheese.
Spread on pizza pan.
Brown meat.
Drain off fat and add taco seasoning.
Spread over cream mixture.
Layer with raw vegetables.
Top with cheese. Serve with chips.
Add enough liquid to chicken soup and consomme to make 4 cups of water.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook at 350° for 1 hour.

In a small bowl, combine oil and garlic powder. Brush over the bread. Mix together thyme, marjoram, paprika and grated cheese. Place bread halves on a baking sheet; sprinkle with cheese and herb mixture. Bake in 425° oven for 7 to 9 minutes, until lightly browned. Cut each half into 5 slices.
Sift flour, baking soda and salt onto wax paper.
Preheat oven to moderate (350°).
Beat butter, margarine, brown sugar, granulated sugar, egg, milk and vanilla in a bowl until well blended.
Slice peeled potatoes in round, pretty thin slices.
Layer in a deep casserole dish with butter and salt.
Pour can of milk over the potatoes.
Make sure they are completely covered with milk. Bake, uncovered, for about 1 hour at 475°.
Wash and peel potatoes, slicing very thin.
Use 1 tablespoon of the butter and place in a shallow baking dish.
Evenly layer one half of the potatoes in the dish, sprinkling lightly with salt and add 1/2 of the cheese.
Layer remaining potatoes, lightly salt and place remaining cheese on top.
Sprinkle with chopped chives and bake at 450°
for 45 minutes until potatoes are tender and browned on top.
Cream butter; gradually add sugar, beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer.
Add eggs and beat until blended.
Stir in orange juice, lemon extract, salt and coconut, mixing well.
Pour into pie crust.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Prepare and partially bake a crust to fit a 9-inch pie pan using a basic pie dough recipe.
Saute onions in oil and butter over low heat until golden yellow.

Beat together eggs, half and half, flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg, then add onions and half of the grated cheese. Pour into crust; sprinkle remaining cheese on top and bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown. Garnish with parsley.
Serves 4.
Slice potatoes and onion.
Put on bottom of pan.
Drain green beans and put on top.
Layer hamburger over beans.
Pour celery over hamburger.
Place biscuits on top.
Spread cheese soup over biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Spread crushed pineapple in the bottom of baking dish. Spread cherry pie filling over the pineapple.
Spread yellow cake mix over pineapple and cherry filling.
Melt margarine and drizzle over the other ingredients.
Bake at 350° until golden brown on top.
Spread pie filling in bottom of 8-inch square pan.
Combine cake mix, water and egg; beat well.
Pour over pie filling. Sprinkle coconut and pecans on top.
Drizzle melted butter over top.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Serve warm.

Building from bottom of covered (tall) casserole dish (2 1/2-quarts), spread in layers, 2 cubed raw potatoes (1/4-inch cubes), 2 diced raw carrots, diced celery (enough to cover layer), small can peas, drained, 1 1/2 tablespoons Minute rice (cover peas), 1/2 pound raw ground chuck.
Pat down; add 1 cup tomato soup.
Final layer, another 1/2 pound ground chuck.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours covered.
Mix Kool-Aid according to directions on package.
Add lemonade and orange juice, plus water called for one can.
Add pineapple juice and sugar; stir.
Makes 2 gallons or 64 (1/2 cup) servings.
Wash tomatoes and remove stem ends.
Cut tomatoes in half crosswise.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Brush over cut surface of tomatoes with butter.
Combine bread crumbs, rosemary, basil, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle crumbs over tops of tomatoes.
Pour remaining butter over top of crumbs.
Broil under low heat with tops of tomatoes about 3-inches from heat for 10 to 12 minutes until tomatoes are heated through and crumbs are well browned.
In top of double boiler, combine chocolate, sugar and salt. Stir in boiling water.
Over simmering water, heat until chocolate is melted.
Add milk and coffee; stirring.
Mix in nutmeg.
Top with whipped cream.
Sprinkle with instant coffee, if desired.
Heat oven to 375°.
In small bowl combine cheese, pepperoni, oregano, pizza sauce and pepper; mix well.
Separate dough onto 4 rectangles.
Firmly press perforations to seal.
Spread each rectangle with about 3 tablespoons mixture.
Starting at shortest side, roll up each rectangle; pinch edges to seal.
Cut each roll into 6 slices.
Place cut side down, 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden brown.
Serve warm.

Mix all ingredients in pot and bring to a rolling boil for 2 minutes. Add 3 cups quick oats, 1/2 tsp. vanilla, and pinch of salt. Beat and stir until all oats are mixed in and coated. Drop by spoonful onto waxed paper and cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In greased 9 x 13-inch pan, place layer of cheeses and layer of peppers.
Pour eggs over top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until eggs are set.
Cut into appetizer size squares.
Cream butter, sugar and egg yolks.
Cream and mash potatoes and mix.
Add milk.
Sift dry ingredients.
Add nuts and raisins. Beat egg whites.
Fold in last and bake in 350° oven until done. May cover with chocolate icing or any other favorite icing.
(May use 1/4 cup cocoa in cake for chocolate flavor, if desired.)
Make a large patty for each person.
Place each patty separately in foil.
Sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce over meat; dash with salt and pepper.
Place slice of onion on top of meat.
Place sliced potato on top of onion.
Place sliced carrot around meat.
Sprinkle with all-purpose flour, seasoning and a little more sauce over vegetables.
Wrap tight in foil. Bake 1 1/4 hours at 325°.
Serve hot.
Sift confectioners sugar and cocoa into a very large bowl; stir in pecans.
Stirring frequently, melt cheese in the top of a large double boiler over simmering water.
Add butter to melted cheese, stirring until butter melts; stir in vanilla.
Add melted cheese mixture to sugar mixture.
Stir until well blended.
Press into a 10 1/2x15 1/2 jellyroll pan.
Cover and chill until firm.
Cut into 1 inch squares.
Store in an airtight container in a cool place. Yield:
about 12 1/2 dozen pieces.
Combine cucumbers, onion and salt and refrigerate 2 hours. Dissolve sugar and vinegar and set aside.
Drain cucumbers and rinse salt off.
Add sugar and vinegar mixture.
Stir, pack and freeze.
A bit of summer heaven in winter!
Break the cauliflower and broccoli into small flowerets and steam until tender, 7 to 10 minutes.
Melt margarine; remove from heat.
Gradually add flour.
Stir to make a roux and add milk gradually, blending well until smooth.
Return pan to heat and stir until sauce thickens and comes to a boil.
Cool a little and add egg yolk and cheese.
Stir well and add nutmeg.
Whip the egg white until stiff and fold carefully into sauce.
Place vegetables into 6 small greased ramekin dishes and season.
Divide the sauce evenly between dishes and bake immediately in preheated 375° oven for 35 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve at once.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine flour, sugar and baking powder in a bowl.
Set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix well the oil, milk, egg and vanilla.
Add the liquid ingredients to the dry and stir just until combined.
Don't overmix or the muffins will be tough. Gently fold in the chocolate chips.
Spoon batter into 24-cup mini muffin pan or 12-cup regular muffin pan that is sprayed lightly with cooking spray.
Bake 15 - 20 minutes or until golden brown. You can use regular chips if you use regular muffin pans only. Enjoy!
In covered Dutch oven or saucepan (4-quart) over medium heat, cook butter, carrots, onions, cabbage, parsley and salt for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add chicken broth, green beans and caraway seed.
Reduce to low heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes or until vegetables are fork-tender.
Brown ground beef, bell pepper, onions and celery.
Preboil noodles.
Mix noodles with meat sauce.
Add tomato soup, water and mushrooms.
Cover with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes; bake uncovered the last 15 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar; add
eggs
one
at a time.
Add flavorings
plus the anise
seed.
Sift
together
the
flour, baking powder and salt into a
large bread bowl.
Make well in center; add the first mixture and mix as for old fashioned tea cakes, incorporating all of the flour.
In large bowl, mix 1/2 cup flour, sugar, salt, lemon peel and yeast.
Combine milk, water and margarine in saucepan.
Heat liquid (120° to 130°).
Gradually add to dry mix.
Beat 2 minutes on medium speed.
Add egg and 1/2 cup flour.
Beat high 2 minutes. Stir in more flour to make soft dough.
Cover and rise in oven until double (30 minutes).
Place meat, seasoning, onion and water in skillet over low fire.
Slice potatoes thin and place on top.
Put lid on skillet and cook until potatoes are done.
Stir into meat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat the butter in a heavy pot and stir in the onions and mushrooms.
Cook them slowly, stirring occasionally for 20 to 25 minutes or until soft.
Add the scallops and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add milk and meat slowly without boiling. Stir in the mustard, sherry and parsley.
Sprinkle with freshly ground pepper just before serving.
Serve with crusty French bread and chilled frascati wine.
Use an 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Arrange slices of ham in bottom.
Place chicken breast on each slice of ham.
Mix the soup, sour cream, whiskey and mushrooms together; spoon over chicken and ham, covering completely.
Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Serve with wild rice.
Serves 6 to 8.
Delicious!
Mix margarine and cheese.
Add flour, Rice Krispies and pepper.
Roll into balls and place on greased cookie sheet. Flatten with a fork.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Combine first five ingredients and fill medium size muffin pans; round tops, meat loaf fashion.
Combine brown sugar and prepared mustard and spread over tops of cups.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix the oil, vinegar and sugar with the seasoning packet for the dressing.
Mix cabbage, red peppers, nuts and onions with dressing.
Add broken Ramen noodles just before serving.
Cut the tomato and eggs into wedges.
Toss salad greens and celery in a large bowl.
Arrange remaining ingredients over greens.
Line the bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan with graham crackers.
Mix pudding and 3 cups milk until thick; add Cool Whip.
Put half of mixture on graham crackers, then top with another layer of graham crackers.
Repeat layers.

recipes.t: Hershey'S Great American Chocolate Chip Cookies
d: Heat oven to 375°.
Stir together flour, baking soda and salt. In large bowl, beat margarine, sugar, brown sugar and vanilla until creamy.
Add eggs; beat well.
Gradually add flour mixture, beating well.
Stir in milk chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 9 to 11 minutes or until slightly browned.
Cool slightly; remove to wire rack.
Cool completely.
Makes 6 dozen cookies.
In skillet, brown chicken in oil.
Pour off fat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover; simmer for 45 minutes, or until done.
Stir occasionally.
Makes 4 servings.
Melt butter in a frying pan.
Put salt and pepper on the meat. Brown chops and onions together.
Grease casserole.
Lay potato slices on bottom of casserole.
Remove the browned chops from the pan; place on top of the potatoes.
Add the soup and milk to the onions; stir until mixture is smooth.
Pour over chops.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Uncover; bake another 30 minutes.

Mix together the crumbled Ricotta, spinach and Parmesan. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Fill crepes with the mixture; roll up and place in a buttered ovenproof pan. Cook at 375° for 10 minutes. Heat tomato sauce with basil (option 1 tablespoon of sugar). After baking crepes, spoon tomato, basil sauce over crepes. Elegant, inexpensive and delicious meal.
Combine milk, lemon juice and vanilla.
Mix until well blended.
Fold in remaining ingredients, one at a time.
Mound mixture into crust.
Freeze until firm, 2 to 3 hours.
Let stand at room temperature 15 minutes before serving.
Thaw bread slightly.
Cut in half and then in half again (lengthwise). Cut into cubes and roll in sugar and cinnamon.
Put in well-greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Wash broccoli and cauliflower.
Break into small pieces.
Chop onion.
Add cheese.
Mix mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar in small bowl until creamy.
Pour over salad ingredients.
Stir until coated.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare puddings according to package directions. Fold in cool whip until well blended. Fold in cookies and walnuts. Sprinkle crushed oreos over top. Make approximately 12 servings.

recipes.t: Baked Pork Chops And Sour Cream
d: Brown chops in flour, salt and pepper.
Then place chops in a shallow baking dish.
Mix water, soup, ginger, rosemary and onion rings.
Pour over chops; cover with foil and bake for 1 hour or more at 350° until done.
Remove chops and mix gravy with sour cream.
To make glaze:
Melt jelly; whisk until smooth.
Mix cornstarch and water.
Stir into jelly.
Bring to boil; cook and stir 4 to 5 minutes until mixture is the consistency of thin jam. Cool to room temperature.
Brush inside of each pie shell with 1/4 cup jelly mixture.
Gently toss strawberries with remaining jelly mixture to coat.
Mound strawberry mixture into
pie shells, dividing equally.
Turn several strawberries in each pie so that point ends face up.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours or up to 8 hours before serving.
Cut each pie into 8 wedges; top each serving with 2 tablespoons whipped cream.
Yield:
24 servings (three 9-inch pies).
In large food processor with chopping blade process parsley, thyme, basil, tarragon and garlic until finely chopped.
Add cream cheese, butter, Worcestershire and vinegar; process until well mixed and creamy.
Line a 1 1/4-quart plastic container or shallow bowl with plastic wrap. Spread herb cheese into container; refrigerate.
To serve, uncover container and invert cheese on to serving board or plate, remove container and plastic wrap. With small spatula or knife smooth surface. Garnish with fresh herbs.
Mix cottage cheese, pineapple and oranges.
Sprinkle diet Jell-O over this; stir well.
Stir in pecans, then stir in the whipped yogurt mixture.
Chill.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix pineapple, sugar, egg and flour.
Cook over medium heat until thick, stirring constantly.
When cool, add cream cheese and Cool Whip.
Mix with a whisk.
Refrigerate.
Serve with sliced fruit such as apples, pears and strawberries.
Tie spices in cheesecloth or tea strainer and place in slow cooker.
Add apple cider (or juice) and sugar, stirring well. Cover.
Simmer on low 1 hour.
Remove spices and stir in orange juice and lemon juice.
Continue heating 1 more hour.
Serve cider from cooker set on low.
Yield: 10 to 11 (1 cup) servings.

Tear off a piece of non-stick foil about 10-12 inches long. Peel and cut the potatoes, add the sliced onions and peppers, along with the tablespoon of butter and salt and pepper into the center of the foil.
Fold the foil and close it tightly at the top and on the sides.
Cook it on the grill on low for approximately 30 minutes.
Once the potatoes are done, open the packet (be careful of the steam), put slices of the cheese on the potatoes and close the packet up so it can melt.

In a bowl, microwave peas for 4 minutes, covered. Heat oil in a 10-inch skillet. Add ginger and garlic. Add peas and cabbage. Stir-fry on medium-low heat until crisp-tender. Add salt and black pepper. (Do not overcook when cabbage is soft.)
Mix flour, sugar and salt; next mix egg and milk all together. Add squash and flavoring.
Pour into pie shell and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Flatten chicken slightly and dust with flour.
Mix eggs with Parmesan cheese, 2 tablespoons parsley, salt and pepper. Dip chicken in egg mixture.
Heat oil in pan and brown chicken on both sides over medium-high heat. Discard oil and wipe pan out.
Melt butter in pan. Add chicken broth and 2 tablespoons parsley. Squeeze juice from lemon in sauce and put lemon in sauce.
Return chicken to pan.
Simmer 10 minutes or until tender.
Add wine and pepper.
Simmer 5 minutes. Remove to serving dish.
Pour sauce over chicken and garnish with lemon and parsley.
Prepare grits in boiling salt water.
Stir in cheese, butter or margarine, milk, eggs and garlic.
Cook over low heat until cheese is melted.
Pour into a 2-quart greased casserole.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 350°. Place salmon in a shallow baking dish. Pour in the olive oil and lemon juice. Smear the pressed garlic onto the salmon. Spoon the oil and lemon over the fish. Sprinkle the salt, pepper and garlic powder onto the salmon. Place tinfoil over the baking dish and bake the salmon for 10 minutes at 350°.
Crumble ingredients with pie blender. Beat 1 egg in cup and finish filling cup with ice water.
Mix all together.
Roll into crust.
Makes 2 (2-crust) pies or 4 single or 8 apple dumplings. Crust freezes well.

recipes.t: Aunt Eva'S Old Fashion Peach Shortcake
d: Sift first 3 ingredients.
In a measuring cup, put melted margarine and egg, then finish filling to 1 cup with milk.
Add to flour mixture and beat well.
Put into greased and floured 9-inch cake pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool.
Split in half and put peaches between and on top of shortcake.
Serve with ice cream or Cool Whip.
Makes a beautiful dish and it is delicious.
Mix butter, sugar and flour together. Add nuts and vanilla. Mix well.
Roll into small balls. Bake in slow oven at 300° for 30 to 40 minutes.
As soon as they come out of the oven, roll in powdered sugar.
This forms a sort of icing.
Heat milk in heavy saucepan to boiling point (212°).
Combine candy, molasses and ginger in container of electric blender; add milk.
Blend on high speed until smooth.
Serve in mugs; top with whipped cream.
Serve immediately.
Yield: about 2 1/2 cups.
Mix cornstarch and 2 tablespoons sugar with water and cook together until clear.
Set aside.
Add a dash of salt to the egg whites.
Beat until foamy and standing in peaks.
Add cornstarch mixture and continue to beat until creamy.
Add 6 tablespoons sugar gradually.
Beat until stiff.
Pile on pie and bake at 325° for approximately 30 minutes or until a delicate brown.
In a 2-quart casserole, combine eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla and salt.
Add rice and raisins.
Mix well.
Microcook at High, uncovered, for 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir every 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Let stand 30 minutes without stirring.
Grill salmon
to
inches
from
hot
coals, after brushing with 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Turn one time and cook 6 to 8 minutes on each side, or until fish flakes.
Serve with salsa sauce.
(If
steaks
are large, cut in half.) For sauce: Mix the vegetables
and
seasonings with 1/4 cup of olive oil. Place 1/3 of
the
mixture
in
blender
or food processor and blend 1 minute.
Stir
the blended mixture into the remaining chopped vegetables.
Serves 4.
Slice cucumber in half lengthwise.
Scoop out seed and pulp. Cut into thin slice.
In a salad bowl, combine lettuce and cucumber and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix other ingredients.
Pour over vegetable.
Toss lightly.
Mix flour, sugar, soda, cinnamon and salt.
Add carrots, oil, eggs and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add pineapple, coconut and walnuts. Makes 9 inch square pan (for 9 x 13, double recipe).
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool.
In skillet with oil, cook chicken breasts with onion.
When chicken is cooked through, add tomato sauce, mushrooms and parsley flakes.
Simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve over rice.

Combine sugar, water and syrup in pan, bring to a boil and cook to a hardball stage. While syrup is cooking, beat the egg whites with cream of tartar and salt. Don't beat until dry. When syrup is ready, pour slowly into egg whites and beat with mixer until smooth, at medium speed. Continue to beat until it stands in soft peaks. 10-15 minutes. Add vanilla. Drop by teaspoon onto wax paper.
Stem and wash grapes.
To each 5 pounds grapes, add 2 cups water.
Cover and let come slowly to a boil; simmer until well cooked.
Remove from heat and place in cloth sack to drain.
Mix butter and mustard.
Place potatoes in greased casserole dish.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Pour butter mixture over potatoes.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Prepare macaroni and cheese dinner
as directed.
Stir in soup.
Fold
in
tuna.
Pour
into a 9-inch casserole dish. Sprinkle with cracker crumbs and dot with margarine.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.

Combine sugar, cornstarch and salt in a saucepan. Gradually add milk and blend well. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened. Cook over low heat and stir 2 minutes longer. Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter and vanilla. Pour into individual dessert dishes. Cover and chill for 2 hours. Makes 4 servings.
In a saucepan, stir soup.
Gradually stir in broth and water. Heat to boiling and add potatoes. Boil 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until vegetables are done.
Makes about 8 1/2 cups or 6 servings. Recipe may be doubled.
In a Dutch oven, cook beef and onion until meat is browned and onion is tender.
Drain.
Combine ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Stir into beef mixture. Heat thoroughly.
Serve on buns.
Pour brine off dill pickles and use for another purpose. Leave pickles in the jar.
Combine remaining ingredients in a saucepan.
Heat until sugar dissolves.
Pour mixture over pickles and seal jar.
Refrigerate 2 days before serving.
Crunch one roll of Ritz crackers and cover bottom of casserole dish.
Mix all other ingredients and spread on top of crackers. Crunch second roll of Ritz crackers and use for topping.
Place small amounts of butter on top if desired.
Vary quantities of ingredients to suit personal tastes.
Bake at 325° until cheese melts, approximately 25 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and mix well.
Add baking powder to flour.
Stir, then slowly mix into other ingredients. Fold in pecans.
Make into a roll and wrap in waxed paper.
Chill in refrigerator overnight.
Slice thin and bake at 375° for 8 to 12 minutes.
Flour the fillet of chicken with the cornstarch.
Add salt and pepper.
Heat oil with butter in a frying pan on medium-high heat. Brown each side of the fillets for 5 minutes.
Place them on a plate.
Empty the cream in the pan, scraping the bottom with a spatula to recover the juices.
Let it heat without boiling.
Add the parsley.
Taste for flavor.
Then pour over the fillets.
Serve hot.
Wash broccoli well; pick off leaves and peel outer skin.
Cut florets and chop well.
Cut and chop stem of broccoli and mix with florets.
Wash cauliflower well; pick off leaves.
Use only florets of cauliflower; chop florets and add to broccoli.
Mix in onion and bacon.
Add mayonnaise to broccoli and cauliflower.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 8-inch square baking pan.
Melt butter in large saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in brown sugar and honey until combined.
Stir in oats and almonds.
When well mixed, press into prepared pan using back of wooden spoon.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove from oven and place on wire rack.
Press mixture down again and cut into bars.
When cool, remove bars and store in airtight container at room temperature or wrap and freeze.

Soak beans several hours and drain. Put in large pot leaving room for plenty of water. Chop onion and garlic; add to beans. Slice sausage thin and add to beans the last 45 minutes of cooking. Cook rice by package directions.
Serve beans over rice. This recipe will fill a 48-quart cooler.
Take a stick of oleo and melt in 9 x 13-inch pan or casserole dish.
Use 1/2 of dressing and spread evenly over oleo.
Sprinkle chicken over dressing.
Combine both soups and chicken broth.
Mix well.
Add chopped onion and sage to mixture and pour over chicken.
Take other half of dressing and sprinkle over top. Bake 35 or 40 minutes at 350°.
Prepare zucchini by scooping out pulp, leaving 1/4-inch shells; mince pulp.
Melt butter in skillet and saute pulp and onion until tender.
Squeeze water out of spinach.
Add to zucchini mixture.
Keep warm while making sauce.
Season pork loin.
Place fat side up in roasting pan. Bake at 325° to 350° until 1/2 hour before the roast is done.
Combine all remaining ingredients except cornstarch and liqueur.
Cook over low heat 5 minutes. Blend cornstarch with some of the sauce and stir until smooth.
Add to the rest of the sauce and stir until slightly thickened. Add the liqueur and continue stirring for 5 to 10 minutes.
Crush crackers fine. Mix well with peanut butter.
Cook milk and sugar to a slow boil.
Boil 3 minutes.
Add vanilla to crackers and pour milk and sugar after it has boiled over crackers and peanut butter.
Mix until thick and pour in a greased pan that has been greased with margarine.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Combine all the vegetables.
Mix oil, sugar, vinegar and salt. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Pour over vegetables and toss gently.
Chill 8 to 10 hours.
Drain before serving.
Cook shells and set aside.
In saucepan, saute garlic and mushrooms in margarine.
Mix with cottage cheese, spinach and Mozzarella cheese.
Spoon cottage cheese mixture into cooked shells and place in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan sprayed with Pam. Pour spaghetti sauce over shells and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cook at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Cut potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes.
Add sour cream, onion, chopped olives, salt and pepper into large pan.
Add potatoes; heat, stirring frequently, until the cream bubbles and potatoes are heated through.
Garnish with paprika and parsley.

recipes.t: Southern Chicken Salad In Baked Pie Shell
d: Poach and skin chicken; cut into 1-inch chunks.
Blend the mayonnaise and whipped cream.
Toss to coat chicken, celery, pineapple and nuts.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mound in baked pie shell.
Chill; serve in wedges.
Cook flour with milk over low heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Let cool.
Cream butter and shortening.
Add sugar, salt and vanilla.
Beat at high speed with mixer.
Gradually, add thickened milk mixture and beat well.
May be used on any type of cake or cream rolls.
Freezes well.
Place layer of carrots, pepper and onion in dish.
Be sure to slice vegetables thin.
Mix remaining ingredients; beat well.
Pour over vegetables and refrigerate.
Dissolve raspberry Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Stir in pie filling.
Pour into 9-inch square pan and chill until partially set.
Dissolve lemon Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Combine cheese and mayonnaise and mix well.
Stir in lemon Jell-O, pineapple and marshmallows.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spread lemon mix over cherry layer.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Chill until firm. Cut into squares and serve.
Blend sugar and cinnamon.
Place bread under broiler rack for about 3 minutes; remove.
Spread butter (margarine) on untoasted side, sprinkle with sugar mixture, return to oven and broil until sugar is melted.
Cut into fancy shapes, if desired.
Split and bone chicken breasts.
Remove and discard the skin. Season the flour with salt and pepper to taste; add nutmeg. Dredge the breasts lightly in the flour mixture.
Dip the breasts into the eggs and then in a mixture of bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese, coating thoroughly.
Brown on all sides in the melted butter.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Serves 4.
Cream shortening and sugars in mixing bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg.
Add salt, soda, flour and water; mix well. Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop by heaping tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 11 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cool on cookie sheet.
Beat shortening, sugar, eggs and vanilla until light and fluffy at medium speed.
At low speed, beat in flour, soda, salt, cinnamon and cloves.
Stir in raisins and nuts.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Drop by spoon on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Fry bacon.
Spread frozen pie crust with 1 tablespoon melted butter.
Crumble bacon into bottom of pie and add Swiss strips. Mix 2 cups heavy cream with 4 eggs and 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper.
Pour over bacon and Swiss.
Bake at 425° for first 15 minutes.
Drop temperature to 350° and bake another 30 minutes.
Cream together brown sugar, 1/2 cup sugar, shortening, vanilla and egg; mix well.
Add cream of tartar, flour, baking soda and salt; mix well.
Roll into 1-inch balls and roll into sugar. Place on ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes, or until done.
Makes 3 to 4 dozen.
Cream applesauce and sugar and then add eggs.
Continue to beat.
In a separate bowl, crush bananas.
Add nuts and bananas to mixture.
Mix flour, soda and salt in a separate bowl.
Add to mixture and beat well.
Turn into loaf pan and bake just until knife comes out clean, about 1 hour at 350°.
Cut corn from cob, about 4 to 5 cups of corn.
Melt butter or drippings in skillet; add corn and saute quickly for about 5 minutes.
Add bacon and salt; arrange in buttered casserole in alternate layers with the sliced tomato.
Place in oven at 350° for about 30 minutes or until corn is tender.
Serve hot.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Mash together the garlic and salt.
Beat in the mustard and vinegar, then beat in the oil and yogurt.
Stir in the herbs. Season with pepper.
Makes about 1 1/4 cups.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Blend Crisco and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Add 1 cup flour and salt.
Stir in milk.
Pat evenly in greased pan.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes or until light brown.
Beat eggs, 1 cup brown sugar and vanilla until thick.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour mixture in pan.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes or until brown.
Cool.
Frost and garnish with cherries, if desired. Cut into squares.

Mix cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended. Add eggs; mix until blended. Stir in 1/2 cup white chocolate. Pour into crust; sprinkle with almonds and remaining white chocolate. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until center is almost set. Cool. Refrigerate 3 hours or overnight.
Brown the hamburg.
Layer in roaster or 5-quart casserole dish the hamburg, onion, green pepper, mushrooms, salami, pepperoni, potatoes, salt and pepper and 1/2 of diluted soup.
Sprinkle each layer with cheese, ending top layer with soup mixture. Cook, covered, in oven at 350° for 2 hours, or until potatoes are well cooked.
For first layer, place a thin layer of Minute rice.
Then a thin layer of sliced raw potatoes, then a thin layer of lean ground beef, salt and pepper.
Then put layer of onions.
Then spread tomato soup with water over layers.
Repeat layers approximately 3 times.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Add sour cream and green chiles.
Pour half into casserole.
Top with cheese.
Pour rest of rice mixture over and top again with cheese. Dot with margarine and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Cook and stir pepper and garlic in margarine until tender. Add tomatoes and salad dressing.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in rice and top with cheese.
Sprinkle with olives.
Serves 4.
Per serving, contains 344 calories, 17.7 fat grams, 32.6 carbohydrates and 31.9 cholesterol.
Heat butter and garlic over low heat in small saucepan, about 15 minutes.
Add lemon juice, pepper and olives; heat thoroughly, but do not boil.
Cook broccoli according to package directions. Drain and arrange in heated serving dish.
Sprinkle lightly with seasoned salt, then pour sauce over all.
Yields 12 to 14 servings.
Butter and flour 9 inch tube pan.
Sift together flour and baking soda.
Combine eggs, mince meat, condensed milk, fruits and nuts.
Fold in dry ingredients.
Pour into pan.
Bake slow at 300° oven for 2 hours.
Until center springs back when lightly touched with fingers and top is golden.
Cool slightly and turn out of pan.
Put in 9 x 12-inch dish a layer of stuffing.
Pick chicken off bones and lay on top of stuffing.
Add layer of cooked broccoli. Add layer of noodles (if desired).
Add 1 can of cream of chicken soup.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Can make up your choice of vegetables.
Heat oil; add meat. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add onion, mushrooms and carrots. Stir-fry until onion turns clear.
Add cornstarch mixture.
Bring to boil and stir until thickened.
Add bok choy and broccoli. Cook until desired doneness.
Serve over rice.
Foil line cookie sheets.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Mix together the granola, condensed milk, ginger and almond extract in a large bowl.
Stir the mixture until it's well blended.
Next, drop the dough by teaspoonfuls onto foil-lined cookie sheet.
Place a candied cherry piece on each cookie.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Yields 6 dozen.
Cook deer meat.
Add chili seasoning with tomato sauce and tomato juice.
Takes about 20 to 25 minutes.
Add kidney beans, if desired.
Great with hot dogs!
In large electric skillet or frying pan with tight fitting lid, fry ground beef and onion until brown and onion is tender.
Drain grease.
Add all other ingredients.
Cover tightly and simmer for 30 minutes until rice is tender and all liquid is absorbed.
Yields 8 servings.
Cook first 4 ingredients in a 10-inch, oven safe skillet over medium-high heat, stirring until meat crumbles; drain. Stir in beans, steak sauce and pepper.
Bring to a boil over medium heat. Cut biscuits in half and arrange on meat mixture. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Brush biscuits with butter and broil 4 inches from heat (with oven door partially open) 2 minutes or until browned. Serve immediately.
Drain salmon and remove bones.
Combine salmon with cream cheese, mashing together with fork until blended.
Stir in lemon juice, onion, salt, pepper and liquid smoke.
Mix well.
Add pecans and 1 tablespoon parsley until well combined.
Transfer to serving dish.
Chill.
Sprinkle with parsley, green onions and green peppers.
Serve with crackers of your choice.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups spread.
Cook chicken until tender.
Bone and cut into bite size.
Mix broth, cream of chicken soup and cream cheese together.
Melt margarine and pour over crackers.
Mix.
Layer crackers in bottom of baking dish, then chicken, then soup mixture.
Repeat until all ingredients are used, topping with crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Set oven to 350°.
Prepare macaroni and cheese according to directions on package.
Brown beef, onion and bell pepper.
Add corn, tomato paste, water and seasonings.
Add the macaroni and cheese to the beef mixture, stirring well.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook pepper and onion in margarine, about 5 minutes.
Mix with other ingredients and bake in casserole dish for about 30 minutes at 350°.
Heat over simmering water.
Stir until chocolate and marshmallows are melted.
Remove double boiler top from heat and blend in 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Serve hot.

recipes.t: Aunt Jeanette'S Fast Cherry Crumb Cake
d: Add the following to a greased rectangular pan:
the whole can of pineapple (juice, too!) and the whole can of cherries. Sprinkle the dry cake mix over the fruit.
Cut the margarine in slices and place on top. Bake at 350° for 48 to 50 minutes.
Drain pineapple, reserving 3 tablespoons syrup.
Combine pineapple, chicken, onion, parsley, curry, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Combine yogurt with pineapple syrup.
Mix 1/3 cup yogurt mixture into chicken mixture.
Toss lightly.
Cut avocados into halves and remove seed.
(They may be peeled or not, as desired.) Spoon chicken into avocado halves.
Mix cake mix, 1 egg, and 1 stick butter well and spread in a greased 9 x 13 cake pan.
Then, mix 1 stick butter, 8 oz. cream cheese, 1 box powdered sugar, 2 eggs, and 1 tsp. vanilla well and pour over bottom layer.
Top with 1-2 c. chopped pecan pieces. Bake at 300 degrees for 45-50 minutes.

recipes.t: Super Lo-Cal, Lo-Fat Creamy Broccoli Soup
d: In saucepan, add broccoli, onion and water; cover and simmer until florets are tender, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Pour vegetables and liquid into work bowl of food processor and process until smooth; set aside.
(Blender can be used, but divide mixture in thirds to process.)
In same saucepan, heat margarine until bubbly and hot.
Add flour and cook, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Stir in broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is smooth and thickened.
Add pureed vegetables and seasonings to saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until thoroughly combined and heated.
Pour into soup bowls and sprinkle with parsley, if desired.
Enjoy!
Makes 4 servings.
Mix
pudding and buttermilk.
Fold in
whipping
cream. Break up cookies and fold into salad.
Add oranges and pineapple. Chill.
In a large casserole greased with margarine, break up bread. Grate Cheddar cheese and mix with bread.
In a blender, mix quickly eggs and milk.
Pour over bread and cheese mixture.
Cover with foil and let sit in fridge overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour; 35 to 40 minutes covered, 20 to 25 minutes uncovered.
Dissolve 1 pint of lime in 2 gallons of water.
Peel, seed and cut cucumbers into strips.
(Use large cucumbers, even the white ones; use the meat only.
You can fix small ones the same way.) Pour lime mixture over cucumbers and let stand for 24 hours.
Drain and rinse cucumbers.
Fill with ice cold water and let stand for 3 hours.
Drain.
Mix vinegar, sugar, salt and spices together.
Pour over cucumbers.
Let stand overnight.
Put on stove next morning and boil for 35 minutes.
Put in jars and seal.
Makes 10 pints.
Melt butter.
Stir in flour and nuts.
Press into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cool.
Beat egg white until foamy.
Brush over the bottom and sides of pastry.
In a small bowl combine flour and sugars.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Sprinkle 2/3 into bottom of pastry.
Top with peaches.
Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until filling is bubbly and peaches are tender.
Boil the potatoes and process them through a colander, then mash them thoroughly.
Add 6 cups of water.
Brown the flour in the butter and add the potatoes and water with the chopped celery, parsley, thyme, salt and white pepper.
Beat in two egg yolks just before serving.
You will never miss the cow.
Combine beans, picante sauce and 1 cup cheese; stir over low heat until cheese is melted.
On serving platter, layer chips, bean mixture, lettuce, sour cream and tomatoes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Makes 8 servings.
Mix oil, vinegar and sugar. Mix with vegetables. Marinate overnight. Add lemon pepper and celery; salt to taste.
Can use less oil. Add enough water to make 1/2 cup.
Heat the pineapple juice and water to boiling.
Stir in the lemon Jell-O until dissolved.
Cool to room temperature. Meanwhile, mix the cream cheese until light and fluffy.
Heat milk and add to cheese.
Mix until well blended.
Then add carrots, pineapple and vinegar; put the Jell-O mixture into the cheese and mix well.
Pour into container and chill.
Combine cream cheese, whipping cream and garlic in work bowl of food processor or blender.
Process until smooth.
Stir in chives, thyme and pepper.
Refrigerate to blend flavors.
Allow to stand at room temperature about 30 minutes prior to serving.
Arrange chicken parts (or 4 breasts) in 12 x 8-inch baking dish, bone side down, thicker portions toward edges of dish.
Top with 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms.
Stir 1/2 teaspoon dried basil into 2 cups of pasta sauce (onion and garlic is great) and pour over chicken.
Cover with waxed paper.
Microwave High for 17 minutes or until fork can be inserted in chicken with ease and juices run clear, rearranging pieces once.
Serve over cooked pasta.
Serves 4.
Cream sugar, margarine and shortening in mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add flour and eggs; beat well.
Add flavorings; mix well.
Stir in Sun-Drop.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 1/4 hours.
Cool in pan for several minutes. Invert onto serving plate.
Spread frosting over cake.
Yield:
16 servings.

In small mixing bowl, blend together soup and milk; set aside. Cook rotini according to package instructions. In large mixing bowl, combine green peppers, onion, chicken, pimiento, cheese and cooked rotini. Pour on soup mixture and mix thoroughly. Pour into 9 x 13 greased casserole. Sprinkle with bread crumbs. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes. Serves 7 to 9.

Grind together peppers, garlic and onion. Put in crock pan (not aluminum). Add salt and add just enough water to cover. Let set 2 hours and drain. Add oil, vinegar and water. Cook 30 minutes. Seal in hot jars. Makes 12 pints.
Cream shortening and margarine in bowl.
Add mashed potatoes, potato water, sweetener and egg; beat well.
Sprinkle with yeast. Stir in gently.
Let stand
for 1 1/2 hours in warm place.
Stir in flour gradually.
Knead on floured surface until smooth.
Let rise, covered, in warm place 5 to 6 hours or doubled in bulk. Roll out on floured surface 1/2-inch thick.
Cut to desired size. Place on floured towel.
Let rise in warm place 1 1/2 to 2 inches or until doubled in bulk.
Deep fry in 375°
oil until light brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Yields 50 doughnuts.
In microwave on High, melt chocolate morsels and shortening together.
Stir until mixture is smooth.
Pour 1/2 of the melted chocolate into an 8-inch foil lined square pan.
Spread evenly. Refrigerate until firm (about 15 minutes).
Chop or shred cabbage.
Add sliced onions and chopped green peppers.
Pour white sugar over cabbage mixture and let stand while mixing dressing.
Heat oil, vinegar, celery seed and salt to a rolling boil.
Pour immediately over cabbage.
Store in refrigerator.
Keeps 10 days.
Rinse broccoli well and cut flowerets into bite-size pieces. Toss with raisins, onion and crisp bacon pieces.
Combine cream cheese and remaining ingredients in blender.
Pour over broccoli. Mix well.
Serve well chilled.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray Pam on a 10-inch tube pan.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Cream together the butter, shortening and sugar.
Add extracts.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Sift flour with baking powder and salt; add to egg mixture alternately with milk.
Blend well after each addition.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Cool 15 minutes before turning gently onto plate.
Mix first 3 ingredients and place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle nuts over mixture.
Mix cream cheese and box confectioners sugar and spread over nuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
When cool, cut in squares.
Whip the Dream Whip. Add sugar and cream cheese.
Mix well. In deep dish, put 1 layer of ladyfingers.
Spread with mixture. Cover with pie filling.
Repeat in layers.
Chill at least 3 hours. Serves 10 to 12.
Lightly spray 8 x 8 pan; place apple in pan and sprinkle with lemon juice and water.
Combine remaining ingredients and cover apples.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until apples are done and brown.
Beat egg whites at high speed with an electric mixer until stiff peak forms.
Set aside.
Beat butter and shortening until creamy; gradually add sugar beating well.
Add egg yolks, 1 at a time, beating until blended after each addition.
Combine flour, cocoa and baking soda; add to butter mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Beat at low speed until blended after each addition.
Stir in coconut, chopped pecans and vanilla.
Fold in egg whites.
Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 8 inch cake pans.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes our clean. Cool in pans 10 minutes.
Remove cake layers to wire rack and cool completely.
Soak raisins in mandarin juice.
Melt butter, brown chicken breasts on both sides.
Cook over low heat 15 to 20 minutes until chicken is done.
Remove chicken from skillet, place on serving platter and keep warm.
Pour off all but 3 tablespoons of pan drippings and stir in flour, paprika, salt and pepper, mix.
Add half and half and cook over low heat until smooth and thick.
Stir in raisin and mandarin juice mixture and heat through.
Pour sauce over chicken.
Serve over wild rice.
Serves 6.
In 3-quart casserole, combine the water, uncooked rice, soup mix and onion.
Cover, cook on 100% power (High) for 4 to 5 minutes or until boiling.
Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Stir before serving.
Garnish with parsley, if desired.
Place chicken, water, onions, leek, celery, salt and pepper in 8 to 10-quart Dutch oven.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat and simmer covered for 1 hour to 1 1/2 hours.
Add carrots and parsnips; simmer covered for 30 more minutes.
Remove chicken and refrigerate if you are not planning to use as main meal.
Lift vegetables from broth with slotted spoon, then strain broth. Return vegetables to broth.
Add parsley and dill if desired. Heat through and serve in bowls with Matzo Balls.
Serves 15.

recipes.t: Potatoes And Tomatoes With Fresh Coconut
d: Peel potatoes, then dice into 3/4-inch pieces and put into bowl of cold water.
Heat oil in heavy 3-quart pot over medium-high flame.
When hot, add finely chopped garlic.
Stir about 5 seconds before adding red pepper and cumin seed.
Stir for another 3 seconds.
Garlic should brown lightly, red pepper should darken and cumin seed should sizzle.
Lower heat to medium.
Add grated coconut and stir for 10 to 15 seconds.
Cream butter and sugar until smooth.
Add vanilla and eggs, one at a time.
Add yogurt, mix at medium speed.
Mix in flour, salt, soda and poppy seed.
Put in muffin tins.
Bake at 400° approximately 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 14 muffins.
Wash peas and put in 6-quart pot.
Add 6 cups water and 2 onions.
Cook on low heat for 45 minutes.
Add carrots and celery. Cook for an additional 30 minutes on low heat, continuing to be sure it remains boiling.
Serves 4 to 6.
Dust veal strips with flour, salt and pepper.
Saute veal in 2 tablespoons butter, sauteeing quickly.
Remove veal from pan.
In skillet, heat remaining butter and add onion.
Cook until lightly glazed.
Add parsley and sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the flour; stir. Add cream and stock, cooking over low heat until sauce is smooth. Add meat and cook until tender.
Stir in last two ingredients when skillet is removed from heat.
Serves 8.
Put apples in baking dish.
Sprinkle jello on top.
Mix sugar, flour and margarine well.
Put on top of apples.
Bake 30 minutes until apples are done.
Brown meat, onions, salt and pepper; drain.
Add beans and soup; mix well.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Peel potatoes and cook until tender; mash, using butter and milk.
Pour meat mixture into casserole pan; drop spoonfuls of potatoes on top. Make sure to leave openings in the middle for steam to escape. Bake at 350° until potatoes start to brown.
Slice potatoes into a large piece of foil.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Crumble bacon over potatoes.
Add onion and cheese. Dot with butter.
Wrap loosely and seal well with double fold. Cook in 350° oven for about 1 hour or until done, turning occasionally.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cook sugars, syrup, cream and salt over high heat until mixture forms a soft ball (235°) when dropped in water.
Remove from heat. Add flavoring and pecans.
Beat until creamy.
Drop from spoon onto waxed paper.
Bake pie shells and set aside.
Place milk into a saucepan and place saucepan of milk into a larger pan of water and turn heat to medium.
Add sugar, salt, Cook & Serve pudding mix, and egg yolks.
Mix with just enough milk to pour and beat into hot milk.
Stir until thick.
Set into a pan of cold water and add butter and vanilla and beat well.
When slightly cool, pour into pie shells.
Take whites of eggs and add baking powder and beat until thick.
Add sugar and vanilla and pour into pie shells spreading well and brown under broil.
Mix salt, pepper and cinnamon.
Rub spice mixture on both sides of roast.
Brown roast in some oil in a roaster.
Now mix the vinegar and brown sugar together and pour over the roast.
Add onions and bay leaves and pot in oven. Bake for 3 - 4 hours at 350 degrees.
Bring to a boil for 1 minute, 9 cups of water and 2 cups of sugar.
Take off stove and add 1 (12 ounce) can frozen orange juice and lemonade.
Let cool.
Add brandy.
Stir and put in a gallon bucket; put in freezer.
Let sit for 24 hours.
Put 2/3 cup Smash in glass and add 7-Up to fill glass.
Serve with a straw.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Trim cauliflower into small florets. Brush a deep ovenproof dish with melted butter or oil.
Place florets in dish.
Heat oil in frying pan.
Add the fresh bread crumbs and toss over medium heat until crisp and golden.
Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from pan and drain on paper towels. Combine tomato pasta sauce.
Pour over cauliflower in prepared dish.
Sprinkle with combined bread crumbs and cheeses.
Sprinkle with extra pepper.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until cauliflower is tender, cheese has melted and top is brown.
Serves 4. Prep time: 20 minutes.
Total cooking time:
20 to 25 minutes.
Beat eggs until lemon colored.
Add flour, baking powder, salt, cottage cheese, shredded Jack cheese and melted butter.
Blend smoothly and stir in chilies.
Pour mix into well-greased 9-inch square dish.
Bake in 350° preheated oven 35 minutes or until top is lightly brown and center appears firm.
Cut in squares and serve hot.
Serve with coarsely chopped and sauteed red pepper and green onions.
Accompany with bran muffins.
Mix jello with 1 cup boiling water.
Add frozen strawberries and stir until separated.
Add drained crushed pineapple and nuts. Put 1/2 mixture in bowl and set in refrigerator 10 to 15 minutes (until slightly gelled).
Remove from refrigerator and spread with sour cream.
Pour remaining jello on top and return to refrigerator.
(Should remaining jello gel, place bowl in warm water and stir until slightly thin.)
Layer #1:
Mix flour, nuts and butter and make crust.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Scrape carrots.
Cut into 1/4-inch diagonal slices.
Simmer carrots, green pepper and onion in small amount of water over low heat until carrots are tender; drain.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over vegetables.
Refrigerate several days before serving.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease (with extra amount of softened butter) and lightly flour a 10-inch tube pan.
Set aside.
Combine the butter and cream cheese in a large mixing bowl.
Beat mixture with an electric mixer until well blended and creamy for 2 minutes.
Gradually add sugar while continuing to beat on medium speed.
Beat until the mixture is light and fluffy for 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating after the addition of each egg until it is thoroughly absorbed.
Sift together the flour, salt and baking powder.
Slowly add this combination to the egg mixture, blending well.
Stir in the coconut flavoring and vanilla flavoring, then the flaked coconut.
Beat well for 1 minute.
Dissolve yeast and 1-1/2 teaspoons sugar in warm water; set aside until bubbly.
Beat 2 eggs, 2 tablespoons sugar and salt. Add cream and butter.
Beat.
Add yeast mixture and slowly blend in flour.
Mix well and let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 5 or 6 parts.
Form into balls.
Press into greased pans, forming a 1/2 inch ridge around outside of the pan.
Let rise 15 minutes.
Pour rice, prune, poppy seed, apple, cherry or any cake and pastry filling over the center.
Top with Cheese topping.
Bake at 350 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes.
Use a skillet or wok.
Saute onion, green pepper, salt and pepper in chicken fat.
Place potatoes on top of ingredients in skillet or wok, then chicken breasts on top of potatoes.
Pour in broth.
Cover and simmer gently, about 30 minutes.
Do not stir.
In medium bowl, combine the first 3 ingredients.
Spread cheese mixture on cut side of each bread half.
Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Broil 4 inches from heat for 3 minutes, or until bubbly and lightly browned.
Soak bread in hot milk.
Set aside.
Beat together eggs and sugar.
Add to soaked bread/milk mixture.
Add vanilla, raisins and grated apple.
Add brandy last.
Bake in well-greased pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Trim all fat from roast, brown and drain.
Combine 1/4 cup flour, salt and pepper.
Coat meat with flour mixture.
Place all vegetables except mushrooms in crock-pot and top with roast. Cover and cook on low setting for 10 to 12 hours.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix cocoa, sugar and salt; add water and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in milk; heat to boiling, but do not boil.
Beat with rotary beater just before serving.
Serves 6.
In large mixing bowl cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat until creamy. Mix flour and soda.
Add to creamed mixture and mix well.
Add buttermilk, jam and allspice.
Mix well.
Stir in walnuts, raisins and coconut.
Pour into lightly greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake 1 hour in preheated 325° oven. Cool 15 minutes in pan.
Loosen cake and invert onto cooling rack. Serves 12 to 16.
Combine chicken, eggs, olives and mayonnaise.
Fill sandwiches (3 slices to a sandwich).
Set aside 1 cup of flour.
Mix remaining flour, sugar, salt, garlic and yeast.
Stir in water and margarine.
Mix in enough reserved flour to make soft dough.
Knead 4 minutes.
Roll dough 18 x 8 inches.
Spread mayonnaise down center third of length.
Top with cheese and onions.
Seal long edges over filling at 1 inch intervals; seal ends.
Set on greased baking sheet.
Cover.
Place over large shallow pan of boiling water; let rise 15 minutes.
Bake for 20 minutes or until done.
In medium bowl, beat cream cheese until smooth.
Stir in mayonnaise, cucumbers, green onions, lemon juice, dill and hot pepper sauce.
Cover and chill.
Serve with fresh vegetables, crackers or chips.
Cream margarine, sugar and egg.
Add remaining ingredients. Drop and bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix pudding and buttermilk.
Add oranges (I drain 1 can), Cool Whip (I use 16 ounces) and shortbread cookies.
Refrigerate.
In ungreased 8-inch cake pan, mix together flour, sugar, soda and cocoa.
Make 3 wells in flour mixture.
Put vinegar in one, vanilla in one and corn oil in 3rd.
Pour water over all and mix with fork until entirely moist.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes until just done.
Ice as desired.
Bake cake as directed for about 25 to 30 minutes in a rectangular pan.
Then remove from oven and punch holes all through the cake with a fork.
Then pour the condensed milk on the cake, covering it completely.
Let cool about 10 minutes.
Then mix the rest of the ingredients together and spread over the cake and store in refrigerator.
Combine crab, cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Add lemon juice, curry powder, Worcestershire sauce and onion to taste.
Put in 7 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish; top with cheese and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Brown ground beef, onion and green pepper; drain.
Prepare rotini noodles according to package directions; drain.
Mix all ingredients together except cheese.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan and cover with cheese.
Bake in 350° oven until cheese is melted.
Cook pasta in boiling water until just done and rinse in cold water.
Add enough salad dressing to thoroughly coat the pasta. Add Parmesan cheese and vegetables.
You may use any other vegetable you choose.
Enjoy!
This makes enough for 10.
For pasta, drop penne into kettle of boiling water; return to boil and boil gently for 8 to 10 minutes or until tender.
Drain; toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Return to pan and keep warm. For sauce, saute garlic slowly in 3 tablespoons olive oil in skillet until softened, but not browned.
Add olives, basil, red pepper and tomato sauce.
Heat.
Stir in cheeses and heat, stirring until chunks begin to melt.
Pour over pasta.
Pass additional grated Parmesan cheese to sprinkle over if desired. Makes 4 servings.
Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in hot water.
Use the pineapple juice and enough cold water to make the 2 cups cold liquid.
Add to Jell-O and let set until it starts to congeal.
Add pineapple and marshmallows.
Fold in whipped cream.
Refrigerate a few hours before serving.
Heat sugar and milk in saucepan to boiling.
Boil for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add saltine crumbs, peanut butter and vanilla.
Mix well so that peanut butter is melted.
Add coconut and peanuts and stir until mixture is stiff.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on wax paper to form mounds.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add flour.
Batter will be stiff. Pack in 9 x9-inch ungreased pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Sift together flour, soda and salt.
Cream together margarine and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg.
Stir in Baby Ruth pieces and dry ingredients.
Add vanilla and blend well. Chill dough for 30 minutes.
Drop by 1/2 teaspoon onto greased baking sheet.
Bake in oven at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until done.
Remove from baking sheet onto wire racks to cool.
To enhance flavoring, add caramel flavoring.
Soak beans overnight.
Place salt pork in the bottom of a bean pot, drain the beans and to pot with all other ingredients.
Cover with hot water and bake at 325° for 5 or 6 hours.
Add more water as needed and reduce temperature to 300° for last hour.
Add more molasses, if desired.
Fork test, done when beans are tender, but not mushy.
Serves 10 hungry people.
Pour salmon juice into measuring cup and set aside.
Put salmon in mixing bowl and 1 egg.
Break up salmon and mix the egg real good.
Fork in 1/2 cup flour.
Mixture is thick.
Add a little pepper, 1/4 salmon juice and add 1 teaspoon baking powder. Beat with a fork.
It must foam.
Pour into salmon mixture.
Mix with fork.
Scoop with small spoons into hot oil.
Makes brown tidbits.
Stick with toothpick and serve with dip or put a hot sauce over them.
Combine flour, salt, baking powder and soda; set aside.
In mixer bowl thoroughly combine sugar, brown sugar and margarine. Add eggs and vanilla; beat well.
Add Rice Krispies and raisins, mixing until it combines.
Drop cookies on greased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for about 16 minutes or until light golden brown.
Mix cornstarch and sugar in small saucepan.
Pour in orange juice and mix well.
Heat, stirring until thickened.
Stir in butter and ginger.
Pour over cooked carrots.
Cook onion and celery in part of broth until tender, then puree.
Crumble cornbread and toasted bread.
Mix with rice, pureed onion mixture and enough broth to make a fairly soupy mixture.
Heat bacon grease in shallow baking pan and add dressing mixture and bake at 400° until brown on top and crusty on edges.

recipes.t: Oven Baked Halibut A La Orange
d: Line a 12 x 8 x 2-inch shallow baking dish with foil.
Lightly brush both sides of halibut steaks with oil.

Arrange in dish. Sprinkle with orange peel and dill. Cover dish with foil and bake at 450°, allowing 10 to 12 minutes cooking time per inch of thickness measured at its thickest part or until halibut flakes when tested with a fork.

recipes.t: Julienne Of Beets And Carrots Or Carrots And Parsnips
d: Cook beets.
Slip off skins and julienne.
Julienne carrots or parsnips. Cook to desired tenderness.
Melt butter and add to it a little orange juice.
In a 2-cup casserole, slightly beat eggs.
Add sugar and blend.
Pour in milk and blend with salt and cinnamon.
Add raisins and bread cubes.
Dot with butter.
Heat pear juice to boiling.
Pour over jello and dissolve. While hot, pour jello over cream cheese.
Mix well with mixer until blended.
Place mixture in refrigerator or freezer until it starts to set.
Add whipped cream with mixer until well blended. Add nuts and pears; pour into serving bowl.
Chill until firm.
Beat sugar, Pet milk and egg yolks until sugar is dissolved. Beat egg whites until stiff; fold in with vanilla.
Pour in freezer.
If not enough to fill to line, fill with milk.
Any fruit you desire can be added to this.
Low-fat sour cream and mayonnaise may be used.
In large bowl, mix pineapple and sugar.
In saucepan, bring water and gelatin to a boil.
Pour over sugar and pineapple and stir.
Refrigerate until slightly set.
Add carrots, celery, cottage cheese, nuts, whipped topping and mayonnaise to pineapple mixture.
Refrigerate until set.
Mix all ingredients together in a large pot; cover and bake at 200° for four hours or simmer for four hours.
Stir every hour.
If mixture becomes too thick, add the extra clam juice.
This freezes well.
Mix mayonnaise, cream cheese, lemon juice, chili sauce and crabmeat
all together and fill mushroom caps with mixture. Cook 1 to 2 minutes on High in your microwave.
Watch carefully!
Cook garlic in oil 1 minute.
Stir in next 6 ingredients. Heat to boiling constantly stirring.
Reduce heat & simmer until thickened about 3 minutes.
Cook & drain sausage, stir in 1 c. salsa mixture.
In ungreased casserole dish layer 1/2 of cheese (sliced 1/4 inches) then sausage mixture.
Top with 1/2 cheese. Bake uncovered at 400 degrees 8-10 minutes.
Heat remaining salsa mixture & pour over cheese.
Serve with chips.
Cook pasta to al dente and drain.
In large skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat and saute shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes or until shrimp are firm and opaque.
Remove shrimp; set aside. Add tomatoes and mushrooms to skillet and saute for 5 minutes. Stir in brandy, basil, salt and pepper.
Add cream and cook until sauce is reduced by 1/3, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in Parmesan. Reduce heat to low and add shrimp to sauce.
Stir for 1 to 2 minutes to heat shrimp.
In heated serving dish, pour sauce over warm pasta, toss gently and serve.
Arrange vegetables on largest round glass platter that will fit microwave.
Place broccoli around edge; arrange cauliflower next to broccoli.
Alternate squash, mushrooms and peppers toward center of dish.
Combine melted butter, garlic salt and pepper and drizzle over vegetables.
Cover with waxed paper and microwave 10 to 15 minutes.
Vegetables should remain crisp, not mushy.
Cream shortening. Add sugar slowly while creaming mix.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Combine milk and almond extract. Add flour and milk alternately to creamed mixture.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry. Fold in. Pour into 10-inch square shallow cake pan. Bake in moderate oven at 375° for 30 minutes. Cool.
Frost as desired. Cut into squares.
Turn on oven and set at 350° (moderate).
Mix first 7 ingredients in a 2-quart bowl.
Stir in potatoes until well mixed. Put mixture into a shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup cheese and paprika over top.
Bake near center of oven about 1 hour or until potatoes are tender.
Brown beef in 12-inch skillet or Dutch oven.
Drain.
Add chicken, broth, mushrooms, rice, onion, green pepper, barbecue sauce and seasoning; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes or until rice is tender.
Add tomatoes; mix lightly.
Melt butter in pan.
Add celery and onions.
Saute until tender.
Blend in flour and seasonings.
Gradually add chicken broth, stirring constantly.
Heat to boiling.
Add cream and crabmeat.
Season with nutmeg to taste.
Do not boil!
Brown and drain ground beef, onion, salt and pepper.
Add Prego, tomato juice, oregano and sweet basil; simmer 20 minutes. Cook macaroni until tender and drain.
Grate cheese.
Layer in 2-quart casserole dish the meat sauce, macaroni, cheese, macaroni and meat sauce.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Add remaining cheese on top and bake until melted.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix sour cream, deviled ham, chopped chives, horseradish and Worcestershire sauce in bowl.
Blend well.
Chill for 1 hour. Serve with potato or corn chips.
In saucepan, melt margarine over medium heat; stir in green onion and carrot.
Cook, stirring, 1 minute; stir in corn, vinegar, sugar and zucchini.
Cover and cook 5 minutes, stirring often, until hot.

recipes.t: No Cook, No Can Cucumber Pickles
d: Fill 1 gallon glass or plastic jug with sliced cucumbers. Dissolve salt in enough water to cover cucumbers.
Let set for 3 days.
Pour off water, rinse 3 times in cold water.
Soak 24 hours with alum in water to cover.
Pour off and rinse 3 times in cold water.
Cover with white vinegar, let set for 7 days.
Drain vinegar off and throw away.
Rinse 1 time.
Heat 1 cup vinegar and 3 cups sugar until sugar is dissolved.
Cool and pour over cucumbers (will not cover pickles), add pickling spice and turmeric (put spice and turmeric in soft cloth tied up).
Let set for 24 hours.

Combine first 5 ingredients in a large bowl. Make a well in center of mixture. Combine water, oil, vinegar and vanilla. Add to dry ingredients, stirring well. Spoon batter into paper-lined miniature muffin pans, filling 2/3 full. Combine cream cheese and next 3 ingredients, stirring well. Stir in chocolate morsels. Spoon about 1 teaspoon cream cheese mixture over chocolate batter. Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes. Yield: 5 dozen.
Preheat oven to 375°.
To Bisquick add sugar and the drained cherries.
Stir in milk to make a stiff dough.
Spread in greased 10 x 6 x 2-inch pan or 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Heat the juice from the cherries with water added to make 1 1/4 cups and the remaining cup of sugar.
Also add 1/2 teaspoon almond extract and a few drops of red food coloring.
Add butter and bring to a boil.
Pour over the dough and bake for 30 minutes.
Serve hot with vanilla ice cream.
Flour chicken breasts and brown in oil. Drain fat from pan and add consomme to chicken; simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
Add 1/2 to 1 cup sour cream to make a creamy sauce. Add several shakes of black pepper.
Put chicken and sauce in baking dish. Sprinkle with cheese and brown under broiler.
In a well-buttered, 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, beginning and ending with cheese, layer cheese and chiles.
Mix eggs with salt, pepper and garlic powder to taste.
Pour egg mixture over layered cheese and chiles.
Beat eggs well and dip chicken in them, then dip chicken in bread crumbs.
Fry in oil and brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towel.
Put the chicken in a casserole dish.
Dissolve bouillon in a cup of hot water and add reserved mushroom liquid; stir well. Pour over the layered chicken and add the mushrooms.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
At end of baking time, remove from oven and add enough slices of cheese to cover chicken.
Return to oven and bake until cheese melts.
Combine butter, evaporated milk, sugar and salt in medium, heavy saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Boil for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Shake meat with seasoned flour in plastic bag.
Brown meat in shortening in Dutch oven or stew pot.
Add soup and water; cover. Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover.
Cook 1 hour or until vegetables are tender.
Stir occasionally to thicken.
Uncover and cook to desired consistency.
Serves 5.
Combine eggs and sugar.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to egg mixture.
Stir in dates, cherries, chocolate pieces and nuts.
Bake in 325° oven for 1 1/4 hours.
Let stand overnight before slicing.
Toast sesame seed under broiler until brown.
Cream butter and brown sugar.
Add egg and vanilla; mix well.
Sift flour with spices; add to creamed mixture and blend.
Stir in nuts.
Spread 1/4 inch thick in 13 x 15-inch greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Spread melted chocolate over while still hot.
Sprinkle with sesame seed and cut while warm.
Add rice to boiling water; set aside.
Melt butter and fry onion until soft.
Add Cheez Whiz to onion and butter to soften. Add soup, milk, salt, pepper, rice and broccoli.
Mix well.
Add chicken; mix again.
Place in 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Sprinkle with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 350°, covered, for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer.
This freezes well. Mix ingredients and freeze.
To use, thaw and add bread crumbs. Bake according to directions.
Beat butter at medium speed of electric mixer; gradually add sugar, beat well.
Add eggs, one at a time; beat well after each one.
Add the Kahlua and chocolate; beat until blended.
Combine flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt; add to the mixture in mixing bowl; alternate with the milk until all is used (begin and end with flour).
Mix well after each addition.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 23 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool on wire racks for 10 minutes; remove from pan and cool.
Stir 1/2 cup nuts into 1 cup of the frosting; spread between layers.
Frost rest of cake. Sprinkle with reserved nuts.
Combine flour, baking soda and salt.
Beat butter and brown sugar in a large bowl at medium speed until creamy.
Beat in egg until light and fluffy.
Beat in melted chocolate and vanilla.
At low speed, beat in flour mixture.
Fold in nuts, chocolate and candies.
Grease baking sheets.
Drop dough by tablespoons, 2 inches apart on prepared pans.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool cookies on rack.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
Melt cream cheese and milk, stirring constantly.
Add remaining ingredients. Pour into buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Combine squash, sugar, oil and egg.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
Add to squash mixture.
Add soda, dissolved in milk.
Add vanilla.
Drop on greased baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes in 375° oven.
Soften cream cheese; beat until fluffy.
Add milk, lemon juice, vanilla and red food coloring.
Mix well.
Pour into a vanilla wafer crust in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Slice bananas over the top.
Spread whipped cream over the top.
Chill and serve.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease large baking dish with butter flavor Crisco.
Melt butter flavor Crisco in large skillet.
Add mushrooms.
Saute until mushrooms give up their liquid, about 5 minutes.
Place grits in large bowl.
Mash if they are leftovers. Add mushrooms, eggs, evaporated milk, cheese, paprika and cayenne. Stir gently to mix.
Pour into casserole.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Drain juice from pears and boil 1 cup of juice to dissolve gelatin.
Put remaining ingredients in blender, including gelatin. Blend; add nuts.
Pour into serving dish and garnish with shredded cheese, chopped peanuts, sliced canned pears, etc. Chill.
Brown ground beef, drain off fat.
Mix in a bowl canned milk and canned mushroom soup.
Add to ground beef and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve on roll like Sloppy Joes.

Sift flour; measure and resift 3 times with baking powder and salt. Cream butter and shortening; blend in sugar gradually. Add beaten egg and beat until smooth and fluffy. Add flour mixture alternately with milk, beating well after each addition. Spoon into buttered muffin pans, filling about 2/3 full. Bake at 400° for 25 minutes. Makes 24 muffins.
Boil potatoes in jacket until done.
Peel and mash.
Add butter, sugar, vanilla, sprinkle of nutmeg & cinnamon.
Combine the beaten eggs and milk.
Mix with potatoes until well blended. Pour into pie shells.
Bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Bring first three ingredients to a boil. Take off heat and add peanut butter, vanilla and oats.
Drop by spoonful onto wax paper.
Cut onion, celery and carrots finely.
Fry in oil until lightly brown.
Add small amount of grated cheese, garlic and parsley.
Add clean shrimp, tomatoes, tomato paste and 1/2 cup water.
Cook until done.
Use more water, if needed.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over spaghetti.
Cut about 1 1/2 inches from tops of melons.
Scoop out seeds. Wipe cavity with paper towels.
Drain pineapple, reserving syrup. Add water to syrup to measure 1 1/4 cups.
Heat syrup-water mixture to boiling.
Pour over gelatin.
Stir to dissolve.
Cool to lukewarm.
Stir in milk and pineapple.
Chill to consistency of unbeaten egg whites.
Spoon into cantaloupe cavities.
(Depending on cavity size, there may be enough gelatin mixture to fill a third cantaloupe.)
Chill in upright position at least 3 hours, or until firm.
Slice into 1-inch rings to serve.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cook sausage in half lengthwise.
Cut crosswise into 1/4-inch slices.
In a 10-inch skillet, combine rice, sausage and remaining ingredients except optional toppings.
Mix well, breaking up tomatoes with large spoon.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Remove from heat; let stand covered 5 minutes.
Top as desired and serve with additional salsa or picante sauce.
Makes 4 servings.
Boil together sugar, honey and water until syrup spins a thread.
Slowly pour syrup over stiffly beaten egg whites, beating continuously.
Beat until mixture holds in shape.
Blend in extract and coconut.
Drop from teaspoon onto waxed paper or spread in a buttered 9-inch square pan; cool and cut into squares.
Beat eggs and egg white until creamy.
Add milk and cream. Sprinkle in salt and pepper.
Stir in meats and cheese.
Pour into an unbaked pie shell.
Add mushrooms; layer tomatoes.
Sprinkle with additional cheese, if desired.
Bake for 10 minutes at 425°, then for 10 additional minutes at 350°.
(You can also add 1/4 cup sauteed onions for more flavor.)
Serves 8.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, cream together milk, shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well.
Combine spinach, stuffing mix, cheese, butter, scallions, 3 eggs and nutmeg.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Refrigerate or freeze until ready to use.
Bake on greased baking sheet at 350° until golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes, if thawed, and 20 minutes, if frozen.
Makes 70 balls.
Add sugar to beaten eggs; beat until stiff.
Add remaining ingredients.
Use a Number 2 can crushed pineapple (drained). This was a recipe of Carolyn T. High.
Freeze in ice cream churn.
Crumble angel food cake into bite size pieces.
Prepare pudding according to directions, then mix whipped topping with pudding.
Put cake pieces in a 9 x 13-inch pan and top with the pudding mixture.
Chill.
Top with cherry pie filling and chill again.
Combine pretzels, cereals and nuts in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Cook and stir brown sugar, oleo and corn syrup in a medium saucepan over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil.
Let the mixture boil without stirring for 4 minutes.
Remove heat.
Put roast in a large piece of heavy aluminum foil.
Cut slits in meat and insert slivers of garlic.
Cover roast with soup. Sprinkle Worcestershire sauce over meat.
Sprinkle onion soup mix over meat.
Add desired seasoning.
Cover tightly with foil, leaving room around meat.
Place in pan.
Cook at 250° from 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (meat is tender and juicy and gravy is made). Delicious!
Microwave (High) butter in uncovered 1-quart dish 15 to 20 seconds or until softened.
Blend in sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Blend in vanilla.
Add flour, ice cream syrup and salt; mix well.
Grease bottom only of 8-inch square dish.
Spread batter in dish.
Cover loosely with plastic wrap.
Sprinkle chicken breasts with salt and set aside.
Combine egg, flour and milk, stirring until smooth.
Dip chicken in egg mixture. Roll in cracker crumbs.
Fry chicken in 1-inch hot oil until brown. Drain on paper towel.
Yields about 3 dozen.
In medium saucepan, add water.
Place over high heat.
Add carrots.
Cover pan and cook for 10 minutes.
Add zucchini.
Cook 5 minutes.
Remove pan from heat and drain.
Puree vegetables until smooth in food processor.
Transfer pureed vegetables in large saucepan.
Add skim milk and place over medium heat uncovered.
Stir constantly with wire whisk.
Sprinkle in flour, cinnamon and pepper.
Add chicken bouillon.
Continue stirring until dissolved.
Makes 4 servings.
Calories 117, cholesterol 2 mg, fat 1 gram.
Saute carrots, onion and green pepper in butter in skillet over medium heat until tender.
Stir in corn.
Cook until heated through.
Yields 4 servings.
Melt butter in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; set aside. Combine flour and next 5 ingredients.
Combine egg and buttermilk. Dip chicken in egg mixture, coating well.
Place chicken in baking dish, turning once to coat with butter.
Sprinkle with chopped pecans.
Bake chicken at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 8.
Melt butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Remove from heat and stir in the parsley, tarragon and walnuts.
Good on asparagus, green beans or broccoli.
Yield:
1/3 cup.
Drain mandarin orange and pineapple chunks. Mix all ingredients and refrigerate. Best if made night before. Can add any other fruit to taste and more sour cream.

recipes.t: Eva St. Clair'S Orange Cake Squares
d: Cream shortening; gradually add sugar, mixing well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine milk, extract and orange rind; set aside.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; add to creamed mixture alternately with milk mixture, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Beat 3 minutes on medium speed of an electric mixer.
Pour into a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Pour Orange Glaze over warm cake, spreading evenly.
Cut cake into squares to serve. Yield:
15 to 18 servings.
Pour half and half in mayonnaise and stir well.
Add Blue cheese, lemon juice, sugar and garlic.
Spray a tube pan with Pam.
Put rolls in pan.
Mix together the pudding, sugar and pecans.
Melt the margarine and pour over rolls.
Sprinkle the mixture over the rolls.
Let rise overnight. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Thin cream cheese with mayonnaise and curry, enough so it will spread thin on a plate.
Layer the chopped food on top of cream cheese. Serve with crackers.
In large bowl with wire whisk or fork, mix olive oil, vinegar, cumin and salt.
Add celery, scallions, pink beans, black beans and black-eyed peas.
Gently toss to coat well.
To serve, stir in celery leaves.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Measure 1 1/2 cups gelatin; add applesauce and cinnamon to gelatin in a bowl.
Chill until set, but not firm.
Chill remaining gelatin until slightly thickened.
Blend in yogurt and spoon over gelatin in bowl.
Chill until set, about 3 hours.
Garnish with additional yogurt, if desired.
Makes 4 cups or 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake first 6 ingredients until done. Boil sugar, milk and butter for a few seconds.
Add chocolate chips.
Remove from heat.
Immediately spread on brownies.
Layer lettuce, onion, bacon bits, cauliflower and cheese in bowl.
Mix other ingredients together well and spread on top.
Put drippings into skillet.
Melt.
Add cabbage, sugar, water, salt, pepper and vinegar.
Stir to blend.
Cover pan and simmer 30 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.

recipes.t: Penne With Tomatoes And Balsamic Vinegar
d: Put olive oil and garlic into skillet over medium heat.
When garlic sizzles, add tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Add rosemary and cook 10 to 12 minutes, then turn off heat.
Cook pasta al dente; drain and transfer to pot with the sauce.
Turn on the heat to very low and toss the pasta and sauce for about 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and make a well in the middle of pasta.
