Pour the vinegar into the well and toss thoroughly for a few seconds. Serve at once.
Crush crackers and mix with melted oleo.
Press into 9 x 13-inch dish (save some crumbs for top).
Soften ice cream and mix with dry pudding, then stir in milk.
Pour over crumbs.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle crumbs on top.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Saut meat and broccoli until tender. Toss in prepared pasta, then add tomatoes. Stir until hot. Season to taste and add cheese. Serve immediately.
Heat tomatoes, soften gelatin in vinegar.
Add to warm tomatoes stir until dissolved.
Then add chili peppers. Refrigerate until firm.
Present servings on lettuce leaf with daub of mayo.
Crumble bacon. Cook fettucine as package directs.
Drain and return to cooking pan over medium heat. Add bacon, peas, tomato, butter, cream, salt and white pepper.
Heat to warm through, stirring constantly. Serve immediately.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Rub chicken with garlic salt.
Place chicken in buttered baking dish and sprinkle with lime juice, tarragon, salt, pepper and onions.
Then pour white wine over chicken and bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until done.
Turn chicken after 20 minutes.
Fry bacon and crumble.
Cook ground meat and drain.
Mix all ingredients together and bake for 1 hour at 350° or slow cook 6 to 8 hours.
Brush
cooked
pastry shell with mustard.
Saute onions in butter,
add
spinach and stir over moderate heat to evaporate moisture.
Stir
in
salt,
pepper,
nutmeg and Ricotta. Taste for seasoning.
Blend
in
eggs
and
cream.
Pour into pastry shell. Sprinkle with cheese and dot with butter.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until set.
Combine the water and sugar in a small bowl.
Stir in the yeast. Set aside until the mixture becomes bubbly. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and baking soda.
Stir to mix. Cut in the shortening using a pastry blender, a fork or your fingertips until the mixture resembles cornmeal.
Add the yeast mixture and buttermilk. Stir with a large wooden spoon until well mixed.
This will not be a smooth dough.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the dough until needed; it will keep about 1 week. Makes about 8 cups of dough.

Mix sugar, margarine and syrup in a saucepan and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from stove burner and add the soda and butter flavoring. Pour over popped corn, peanuts and pecans; mix until coated. Put on cookie sheets and bake 1 hour in 200° oven. Stir every 15 minutes. When cool, store in covered containers. Keeps a long time.
Cook cauliflower in boiling salted water.
Drain; cool and break into flowerets.
Arrange alternate layers of cauliflower, bacon and cheese in well greased casserole.
Beat eggs with milk and seasonings.
Pour over all.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Place butter in pan in hot oven (400°) until melted.
Sift corn meal, salt and sugar together in bowl.
Put creamed corn, eggs, sour cream and onion into bowl and mix well (always mix wet ingredients into dry).
Pour the melted butter very slowly into the mixture and stir.
Pour into hot pan.
Bake at 375° to 400° for about 45 minutes or until golden brown across the top.
In a large nonstick skillet with ovenproof handle, brown meat and onion.
Drain off any accumulated fat.
Add potatoes, tomato sauce, salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Spread evenly in bottom of skillet.
In medium bowl, with fork, lightly beat eggs.
Blend in yogurt; spread over meat mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, or until topping is set.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Slowly boil chicken until it is ready to fall off the bone. Remove chicken and set aside to cool.
Add water and 3 to 4 bouillon cubes to make approximately 6 cups of broth.
Stir into broth, 3 tablespoons of soup greens, tomato sauce and 1/2 pound spaghetti noodles (broken into thirds).
Cook until noodles are tender.
Break apart chicken and add to soup to warm.
Put sugar, water and butter in a heavy saucepan.
Place over low heat.
Stir carefully until sugar is dissolved.
Then cook, without stirring, until mixture forms a hard ball in cold water. Remove from heat and add vanilla; stir.
Pour into a shallow, buttered pan.
When cool enough to handle, pull with fingertips into rope-like lengths.
Then cut into chewable size pieces with buttered kitchen scissors.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add egg yolks, beating after each. Stir in cooled melted chocolate.
Blend in vanilla and add water until it is at spreading consistency.
Melt butter, add flour and stir until lightly cooked.
Add onion, garlic, parsley and green onion until clear.
Add crawfish and cook over a low fire for about 10 minutes.
Add wine and simmer until blended.
Slowly add cream
and simmer over low fire. Do not boil.
Add seasoning with extra paprika.
Remove wrappers from tamales, place in ovenproof dish.
Mix water and chili together, then pour over tamales.
Melt Velveeta cheese and pour over tamales and chili mixture.
Bake in oven for 30 minutes on 350°.
If you're in a hurry, bake on High in microwave for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs and sugar in bowl.
Melt shortening and chocolate in pan.
In another large bowl, add flour, baking powder, salt and vanilla.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour small square pan.
Mix all ingredients above and beat 2 minutes. Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool.
Put on icing.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Sift dry ingredients together and add alternately with egg yolks and buttermilk.
Add vanilla, mashed bananas and nuts.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake in large greased and floured tube pan at 325° for about 1 1/2 hours.
Saute green pepper and onion in a small amount of Crisco in a small baking dish.
Add uncooked Minute rice and 1 can cream of mushroom soup plus 1/2 can of water.
Salt and pepper to taste. Put shredded Cheddar cheese to cover on top.
Cover with foil. Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Slice cookie dough as directed on package. Arrange slices in bottom of ungreased 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan.
Using floured fingers, press dough evenly into pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool completely. In small bowl, beat cream cheese, sugar and vanilla until fluffy. Spread mixture over cooled cookie crust.
Arrange fruit over cream cheese.
In small bowl, combine orange marmalade and water; blend well.
Spoon marmalade mixture over fruit.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
Cut into squares.
Store in refrigerator.
Serves 12.
Cut potatoes into strips.
Coat skillet with oil over medium heat.
Saute lightly the onions and bell pepper.
Add potatoes and stir to coat with oil.
Cook, stirring for 2 minutes.
Add squash and seasonings; gently mix.
Cover and heat on low.
Cook until potatoes are tender, checking and turning often.
Combine sour cream or yogurt, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, celery salt, paprika, garlic salt, salt and pepper and mix well.
Dip chicken in mixture, then into stuffing.
Roll up chicken and place in 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Refrigerate 24 hours.
Pour melted oleo over chicken and bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Scrub potatoes; cook in boiling water just until tender. Drain, peel and dice as soon as cool enough to handle.
Mix 2 tablespoons vinegar with oil and 1 teaspoon salt.
Pour over potatoes; mix lightly.
Chill.
Blend mayonnaise with remaining tablespoon vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, mustard, tarragon and dill weed.
Stir in onion and capers.
Shortly before serving, pare, core and dice pears to measure 3 cups.
Add to potatoes along with celery.
Pour mayonnaise mixture over and toss lightly.
Yield:
6 servings.
Saute onion in butter until transparent, not brown. Add all flour and enough milk to blend. Add salmon and mix.
Add the rest of the milk.
Allow to thicken.
Do not allow to boil. Add oyster crackers.
Serve immediately.
Brown onion, celery and beef in margarine. Stir. Add salt, pepper, cooked noodles and soup.
Put in large casserole and bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
This is good with cheese sprinkled on top.
Yields 8 servings.
Cook ground beef and sausage with oregano until done; drain. Add Cheddar cheese soup and tomato soup; simmer 15 minutes.
Cook package of egg noodles.
Pour all into large casserole dish and mix thoroughly.
Sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese over top.
Bake 25 minutes at 325°.
Preheat oven at 350°.
Cut precooked potatoes in 1/4-inch slices.
Arrange half of the potatoes in a greased shallow 2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper.
Cover with tuna, then with remaining potato slices.
Beat eggs, milk and cheese together, then pour over potatoes, sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake for 45 minutes or until custard is set and potatoes are golden brown.
Makes 6 servings.
Cream the butter and sugar. Add molasses and eggs.
Dissolve soda in water and add to mixture.
Add spices and the flour. Drop by spoonfuls on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 6 to 12 minutes; for large cookies, 12 to 15 minutes.
Cool on towel or foil. Will be like cake. Do not overbake!

recipes.t: Cheese Cake With Sunshine Vanilla Wafers
d: Place vanilla wafers in small baking cups.
Scald milk.
Mix cornstarch and sugar.
Add egg yolks.
Add this mix to scalded milk.
Cook until thick, then add vanilla. Layer cookies and bananas in a bowl, repeating until all gone. Top with a meringue, if desired.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Add salt.
Drain grease.
Add hamburger to spaghetti sauce.
Pour hamburger mixture in ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add pepperoni, mushrooms or whatever you like on pizza.
Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese on top. Combine in bowl eggs, flour and milk.
Beat until smooth.
Pour batter evenly over top of cheese. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until crust is golden brown. Cut into squares and serve.

recipes.t: Breakfast Made Beautiful(Make This The Night Before)
d: Grease with oleo a large oblong casserole dish. Trim crust from slices of bread.
Butter bread on one side only.
Arrange slices, buttered side up, to completely cover bottom of dish. Cover the bread slices with half of the sausage.
Lay slices of cheese over sausage.
Repeat bread, sausage and cheese.
Combine eggs and milk. Pour over casserole.
Cover and refrigerator overnight.
Next morning, let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle bacon bits over the top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes, depending on your oven.
Preheat oven to 325°.

Grease and flour a 12-cup tube pan. Cream together butter and sugar using a heavy-duty electric mixer. Add eggs one at a time and with the mixer running continuously at medium speed, add lemon juice and vanilla.
Finally, add the flour a little bit at a time.
Pour thoroughly mixed batter into prepared pan and bake for 1 1/2 hours or until a straw test shows that it is done.
Remove to a rack to cool about 15 minutes, then turn out onto the rack.
Grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Thaw spinach and drain thoroughly.
Cook potatoes and mash.
Add margarine, sour cream and seasonings.
Stir in spinach.
Turn into baking dish, sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13 pan.
Spread graham cracker crumbs over butter.
Pour milk over crumbs.
Add chocolate and butterscotch morsels.
Put coconut and nuts on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes till golden brown.
Place fettucini sauce in a heavy stockpot; add milk, onions, red peppers, carrots, broccoli and black pepper; stir well to combine.
Heat to 160° or until the vegetables are tender; stir frequently.
Stir in the tortellini.
Hold at 160° for service. Garnish with Parmesan cheese.
Yield:
20 to 22 (8 ounce) servings.
In large bowl combine yeast from foil packet with the flour mixture.
Stir in 1 cup hot tap water, egg and margarine, until dough pulls cleanly away from sides of bowl.
Turn dough onto lightly floured surface.
With greased or floured hands, shape dough into a ball.
Knead dough for 10 minutes, until smooth. Cover with inverted bowl, let rest for 5 minutes.
Score flank on one side; coat both sides with the 2 tablespoons flour.
In skillet, brown meat in hot oil.
Season with a little salt and pepper.
Add bouillon cube, 1 cup water, parsley, sugar and thyme.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until beef is tender.
Remove beef to serving platter.
Measure pan juices; add enough water to make 1 1/4 cups.
Combine the 3 tablespoons flour and the 1/2 cup cold water.
Stir into the pan juices; add Kitchen Bouquet and cook, stirring, until mixture thickens and bubbles. Pour a little gravy over meat; pass remainder.
Saute onion in butter. Combine with undrained spinach, noodles, cheeses, salt and pepper; mix well. Turn into buttered casserole dish. Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350° for 30 minutes.
Beat egg whites stiff with cream of tartar.
Slowly add sugar and vanilla.
When stiff, fold in chocolate chips.
Drop by 1/2 teaspoon onto foil-lined cookie sheet.
Put all cookies in oven at the same time.
Close the door and turn off the oven.
Leave cookies in oven 8 hours or overnight.
Beat eggs with a beater until foamy.
Add vanilla, salt and sugar.
Add milk and mix in a blender.
Serve cold with cinnamon or nutmeg.
Makes enough for four people.
Rinse chicken.
Cook in water to cover in saucepan until tender.
Bone and chop chicken; reserve broth.
Place chicken in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bring soup, 1 soup can reserved broth and tarragon to a boil in saucepan, stirring to mix well.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle peas and carrots over soup mixture.
Spread Biscuit Topping evenly over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until brown.
Yield:
6 servings.

Place beans in large casserole or bean pot. Fry bacon until crisp. Add onion rings and garlic. Cook in bacon fat for a few minutes. Add dry mustard, vinegar, and sugar. Cook over low heat 20 minutes. Pour sauce over beans. Bake at 350° for 60-75 minutes. Serves 12-16.
Place chicken in a single layer in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Combine soup, soup mix, sour cream, lemon juice, dill and mushrooms; pour over chicken.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
In a nonstick skillet, melt margarine.
Add onion and pepper. Cook until tender.
Add ground beef.
Continue to cook until done, not brown.
Drain.
Add beans, sauces, corn and ketchup and cook about 15 minutes.
If it becomes too dry, add a little water.
Peel the apples.
Take out the core and the seeds.
Cut into small pieces.
Put apples into a blender or food processor.
Add the orange juice.
Add the cinnamon to the apples and the orange juice.
Blend until the mixture is creamy.
Spoon into cups or bowls.
Makes four servings.
Dip chicken in melted butter, then in remaining ingredients. Bake uncovered in greased pan at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes.
Mix cake mix, margarine, 1 egg and nuts until crumbly.
Pat into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Whip 1 egg.
Add 10x sugar and cream cheese.
Spread on top of crumbly mix.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool; cut into squares.
Peel and dice onions.
Fry in butter until golden brown.
Pour off and mash boiled potatoes.
Add ground giblets and dried bread which has been soaked in potato water and if needed, broth from giblets.
Mix all together and add enough salt, pepper and sage to taste.
Melt 1/4 pound of butter and while it is hot, mix this in well.
After it has cooled, stuff fowl with it.
It has a different flavor than any dressing one can get.
Put dressing left over in dish and bake the last hour that bird is cooking and mix the two together.
Makes a moist dressing.
Melt butter and mix with sugar.
Beat egg and add with butter and sugar mixture.
Mash bananas and add to mixture.
Mix well. Add flour and soda.
Pour in pan.
Bake for 35 minutes.
In skillet brown chicken on each side.
Transfer to casserole dish add curry powder, soup, milk, lemon and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 35-40 minutes until done; serve on rice or noodles.
(Can substitute broccoli for asparagus.)
Cook cauliflower in salted water with lemon juice until tender; drain.
Saute mushrooms and green pepper in butter. Combine white sauce, peas, red pepper, Worcestershire sauce and half of cheese.
Add cauliflower, mushrooms and green pepper. Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with remaining cheese. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until lightly brown.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt and soda.
Beat butter. Gradually beat in sugar until lite and fluffy.
Blend in egg and vanilla.
Blend into flour mixture.
Add oats, apple and 1 1/2 cups coconut.
Drop by tablespoon onto ungreased cookie sheet. Sprinkle with remaining coconut.
Bake at 375° for about 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Soften margarine and cut into dry cake mix until thoroughly blended.
Pat into 13 x 9-inch glass baking dish.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Spread pie filling over cake mix.
Sift together first two ingredients.
Bring to a boil next 4 ingredients.
Add to flour and sugar mixture.
Add buttermilk, soda, vanilla and eggs.
Bake at 350°.
Makes 3 layers.
Cream the butter until soft.
Add sugar alternately with lemon juice.
Add a dash of salt.
Beat until smooth and light.
Add grated rind of lemon.
Spread and sprinkle coconut on top and sides of cake.

recipes.t: Platanos Maduros En Leche(Plantains In Milk)
d: Peel the plantains.
Wash, then cut lengthwise deep, but not enough to cut in half.
The idea is to fill the plantain.
Melt butter (low heat) in frying pan large enough to hold the plantains.
Fry the plantains in butter with medium heat.
Brown on both sides.
When browned, remove from the pan.
Fill each plantain with a slice of American or Mozzarella cheese.
Roll them in the sugar and return to the heat.
Pour the milk over them and break the stick of cinnamon into the milk.
Cover and simmer them for 1 hour over low heat.
Let potatoes cool, peel and shred.
Layer potatoes and butter; season with salt.
Repeat for 3 layers.
Pour whipping cream over top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream will bubble up.
Recipe may be halved.
In large bowl, mix together all ingredients except red cabbage.
Let set in refrigerator for a few hours or overnight. Add extra dill, parsley or onions if desired.
Hollow out the red cabbage and fill with dip.
Serve with raw vegetables.
In a medium saucepan, stir together the sugar and cocoa.
Stir in the milk and butter.
Cook over medium heat until boiling. Stir constantly.
Boil for one minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir in peanut butter.
Add oats and peanuts.
Stir to mix well.
Quickly drop mixture by rounded teaspoonfuls onto wax paper or foil.
Cool completely.
Store in a cool, dry place.
Combine apples, 2/3 cup sugar, 1/4 cup cider and lemon juice in a 10 to 12-inch Dutch oven.
Cook, stirring until boiling. Reduce heat.
Simmer uncovered, 3 minutes or until apples are almost tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir together remaining cider and cornstarch.
Add to apple mixture.
Cook, stirring until thickened and bubbly.
Keep warm.
Combine flour, 1/4 cup sugar, baking powder and cinnamon.
Cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Combine egg and milk and add to flour mixture, stirring just to moisten.
Drop into 12 mounds on top of hot apple mixture.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve warm with ice cream.
Makes 6 servings.
Melt together butter and chocolate.
Cool.
Add sugar and applesauce.
Mix flour, spices, salt and soda together.
Blend with applesauce mixture.
Add nuts and raisins.
Bake in 8-inch square, greased and floured pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes. Yield: 16.
Cook rice in beef broth according to package directions. Combine bread crumbs, milk, egg and seasoning.
Add 1/4 cup onion and 1/4 cup cheese.
Mix well.
Spread mixture evenly on waxed paper to approximately 12 x 10-inch.
Combine cooked rice, 1/4 cup cheese and remaining onion.
Spread on top of beef.
Roll up jelly roll style and seal ends.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease either a 9-inch round or a 8-inch square cake pan.
Sift flour, sugar and soda together.
Mix applesauce, oil and vanilla in a bowl; add the dry ingredients and stir just until flour is moistened.
Spread batter into prepared pan.
Bake 30 minutes.
For a 2-layer cake, double the recipe.
In large kettle, brown sausage, onion and garlic; drain off fat.
Add water, carrots, tomato, bouillon, Italian seasoning and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 30 minutes. Add zucchini, beans and rotini.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes or until rotini is tender, stirring occasionally.
Makes 2 1/2 quarts.
A meal in a bowl.
Add grits to boiling salted water and cook until thick, stirring occasionally (30 to 40 minutes).
Mix thoroughly the other ingredients, reserving enough cheese to sprinkle on top.
Mix with slightly cooled grits and place in buttered baking dish.
Bake about 1 hour at 350°.
Combine cheeses; divide equally between two tortillas.
Place ham and green chiles over cheese.
Top with another tortilla.
In a long butter dish, spread blueberry filling evenly across bottom.
Spread pineapple even for next layer.
Slice the margarine thinly and place evenly on top.
Bake at 325° or 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.
In large skillet, cook and stir onion and green pepper in oil over medium heat until onion is tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat to boiling.
Cool.
Cover; refrigerate several days.
Makes about 3 cups.
Stir-fry cabbage in oil and salt.
Add carrot and onions.
Add broth.
Cook, tossing a minute or so.
Stir in soy sauce.
Serves 4 to 6.
Brown meat and onion in fat.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Add soup and milk; bring to a boil.
Cook noodles in boiling water as directed.
Combine meat mixture with noodles.
Put in casserole.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Serves 6.
Brown hamburger.
Cook noodles.
Layer noodles, peas and hamburger in small casserole bowl. Mix soup and 3/4 can water. Pour over top of casserole.
Brown in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Combine cake mix, milk, eggs, oil and pudding mix in bowl; mix well.
Pour into 3 greased 9-inch round cake pans.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Cool in pan for several minutes.
Remove to wire rack to cool completely.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix Crisco, peanut butter, sugar, milk and vanilla in large bowl.
Beat at medium speed of electric mixer until well blended.
Add egg, beat until just blended.
Combine flour, salt and baking soda.
Add to creamed mixture and mix at low speed until just blended.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet.
Flatten slightly with crisscross pattern with fork. Bake at 375° for 8 minutes.
Combine Jell-O and boiling water.
Add while Jell-O is still hot the pineapple and bananas.
Cover top with small marshmallows while hot and let set in refrigerator.
Before serving, cover with salad dressing and grated Longhorn cheese.
Fix in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Get vinegar and water to boil.
Cut tomatoes to desired size. Put 1 teaspoon salt and sugar to quart jar.
Pack tomatoes and about 12 peppers to a quart.
Fill jars with boiling vinegar and water.
In about 30 days hot peppers and tomatoes will be ready to eat.
In saucepan, combine water and cornstarch. Stir in milk. Cook, stirring constantly, over medium heat until thick and bubbly. Cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Makes 2 cups.
Melt shortening in large skillet.
Brown meat on all sides. Dissolve bouillon cube in 1 cup water and add to meat.
Add soup, garlic, soy sauce, onion salt, salt and pepper to taste.
Heat until boiling.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour or until meat is tender.
Serve over noodles.
Mix yeast well with warm water.
Pour juices into a gallon jug.
Add yeast and sugar.
Place a large balloon over jug. Secure with a rubber band.
Balloon will get large.
Wine will be ready in 21 days.
Mix together the pie filling, 2 teaspoons of cinnamon and nutmeg.
Place a spoonful in a flour tortilla and roll, closing both ends.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Put flax seed in a bag.
Pour over it 1 1/2 pints water.
Let simmer down to 1/2 that amount.
Remove from heat and add other ingredients while still hot.
Give any amount as often as needed. Half of recipe makes 1 pint.

recipes.t: Baked Chicken, Rice And Cream Of Mushroom
d: Cut fryers up in small pieces; sprinkle seasoned salt, black pepper and garlic powder.
Sprinkle or shake all ingredients in a bag with chicken.
Put in a 9-inch oblong pan with soups, rice and onion.
Cover and cook at 300° for 1 hour or until good and done. Serves 6 to 8.
In a shallow glass baking dish, mix the vinegar, mustard, soy sauce, honey, basil, thyme and pepper.
Add the chicken and turn to coat all sides.
Allow to marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a grill or broiling rack, reserve the marinade and place in a 1-quart saucepan.
Heat sugar and water until sugar dissolves; cool.
Combine fruit juices, ginger ale, sparkling water and fruit.
Add syrup; pour into punch bowl.
Add ice cubes.
Drop in sherbet by spoonful or in balls, using an ice cream dipper.
Makes 20 to 25 servings.
Mix together carrots, green pepper and onion in a bowl. Combine
other ingredients in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil
over medium heat.
Stir occasionally.
Pour over carrot mixture
and
refrigerate
several hours. Store
covered in refrigerator.
Yields ten 1/2 cup servings.

Cut 1/2 of the chocolate into chunks. Mix flour with baking powder, salt and baking soda, set aside. Melt margarine in saucepan add sugar. Blend in egg and vanilla. Gradually stir in flour mixture. Stir in chocolate chunks and 2/3 c. coconut. Spread in greased 9 inch square pan. Bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes. Cool in pan. Meanwhile, melt remaining chocolate in sauce pan over low heat. Stirring constantly. Cool slightly; stir in sour cream. Spread over top of brownies. Sprinkle with remaining coconut, chill until firm, about 10 minutes. Cut into squares.
Boil sugar and water for 3 minutes and cool.
Add the juices and chill.
Just before serving add chilled ginger ale.
Makes 50 servings.
Layer the beans, onion, tomatoes, celery, green pepper, dressing, lettuce, cheese and eggs in large salad bowl.
Cover tightly.
Refrigerate several
hours
or
overnight.
Top with corn chips.
Toss gently before serving.
Makes 8 servings.
Cream together melted butter and sugars.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Mix together flour, oatmeal, salt, baking powder and soda.
Combine these two mixtures, then add chocolate chips, chocolate almond bar and walnuts.
Mix well.
Make golf size balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet spaced 2 inches apart. Bake at 375° for 6 to 8 minutes.
Makes about 120 cookies.
Combine cream cheese and soup (undiluted) in double boiler. Heat and stir until smooth.
Dissolve gelatin in water according to package directions, then add soup mixture.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Blend well.
Pour into 5-cup mold.
Refrigerate until firm.
Serve with fresh vegetables and crackers.
Saute sausage and drain.
Beat eggs with milk, salt and mustard.
Layer the bread cubes, sausage and cheese in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Pour egg mixture on top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream margarine and sugar; add eggs one at a time and mix well.
Stir in bananas.
Combine dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture.
Mix until smooth.
Fold in pineapple and coconut.
Spoon into 2 greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake for 1 hour or until tests done.

Cook spaghetti; drain. Make cream sauce out of the next 4 ingredients. Blend in cheese, sherry and white pepper; heat until cheese melts. Add mushrooms. Remove from heat. Add shrimp. Add spaghetti to sauce. Turn into large shallow casserole. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and slivered almonds. Heat under broiler until lightly brown. Serves 12.

In a small saucepan, combine butter, brown sugar and syrup. Simmer until bubbly. Pour over bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch glass dish. Remove crust from bread and place slices over syrup mixture. Beat eggs, milk, flavoring, sugar and salt. Pour over bread; cover and refrigerate overnight.
Lightly mix beef, eggs, deviled ham, bread crumbs, salt, dry mustard and hot pepper sauce.
Shape into 3/4-inch meat balls. Arrange in jelly roll pans.
Bake at 375° for about 15 minutes. Heat mincemeat, apple juice and vinegar until bubbly.
Add to meat balls; bring to boil again.
Simmer, covered, for about 10 minutes. Serve warm.
Grease a 9-inch spring-form pan.
Dust generously with graham cracker crumbs.
Combine cheeses and beat on high speed until smooth.
Gradually add sugar, beating after each addition.
Add eggs and beat well.
Add next 5 ingredients, beating on low speed until mixture is smooth.
Pour batter into pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Turn off oven.
Let cheesecake stand in oven for 2 hours.
Cool completely.
Cover and chill at least 4 hours.
Arrange whole berries on top of cheesecake and drizzle with your favorite strawberry glaze.
Chill thoroughly.

Place the 4 chicken breast halves between pieces of plastic wrap and flatten with mallet from center out to form thin cutlets. On each cutlet, place a slice of Mozzarella and Swiss cheese. Mix Ricotta and Parmesan cheeses with egg yolk.
Divide among cutlets, placing a spoonful at wide end of each cutlet.
Roll up cutlets from wide end.
Roll each in flour; dip in egg and coat with crumbs.
Secure with toothpicks.
Brown chicken in oil and butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley.
In a 2-quart microwave-safe casserole, place potatoes.
In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine picante sauce, lime juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Cook, uncovered, on High for 45 to 60 seconds or until heated through.
Add sauce to potatoes.
Stir in tomatoes, olives, onion and parsley.
Warm all when ready to serve.
Cream the butter.
Gradually add brown sugar and white sugar. Cream well.
Add egg yolk and vanilla.
Beat well.
Blend in flour to form a stiff dough.
Shape into small balls.
Put on greased cookie sheets.
Flatten to size of a 50 cent piece with the bottom of a glass dipped in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 7 to 9 minutes, until golden brown.
Cool and frost with Browned Butter Frosting.
Put broccoli and water into small microwave dish; sprinkle on salt and add margarine.
Microwave on High for 4 1/2 minutes; turn dish 1/4 turn and microwave for additional 3 1/2 minutes.
This serves two, depending on size of broccoli used.
Increase time and water for more servings.
You can establish this based on experimenting if you undercook slightly, then add more time to achieve your desired degree of doneness.
This procedure cooks the vegetables to a good consistency and color without its becoming soggy.
Mix flour and garlic salt.
Coat eggplant.
Cook in oil over medium heat, turning once, until golden brown.
Pour 1/2 of tomato sauce into ungreased oblong 13 1/2 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Add eggplant.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Add remaining tomato sauce.
Sprinkle with oregano and Mozzarella cheese.
Cook, uncovered, in 325° oven until hot and bubbly, about 25 minutes.
Brown ground chuck and onion; drain and cool.
Place in mixing bowl with bread, crumbled, milk, egg, drained mushrooms, 1/2 cup Mozzarella cheese, garlic salt, salt, pepper and Italian seasoning to taste.

recipes.t: Pull Apart Cake Or Bubble Bread
d: Cut each biscuit into quarters.
Mix together 3/4 cup sugar and 3 teaspoons cinnamon.
Roll biscuit pieces to coat.
Layer in ungreased tube pan with nuts.
Combine 3/4 cup oleo, 1 cup brown sugar and rum or milk.
Bring to a boil.
Pour over biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 40 minutes.
Cake will not slice, just pull apart.
May also use frozen bread dough instead of biscuits.

Mix together sour cream, cream of chicken soup, cream of mushroom soup and chicken broth. Place chicken in 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Pour mixture over chicken. Mix cracker crumbs with butter and spread over casserole. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes, until crackers are brown.
Combine dry ingredients.
Mix together melted butter, beaten eggs, milk and mashed bananas.
Add to dry ingredients and mix just enough to combine.
Pour into greased loaf pan and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
In large saucepan combine sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and butter.
Bring to boil over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened.
Stir in beets and oranges.
Cook until hot.
Serve. Also good cold.
Saute onions, including tops, and bell pepper in butter.
Add remaining ingredients and bake in a deep baking dish (10 x 7 1/2 x 3-inch) for 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350° or until center has cooked and knife comes out clean when inserted.
Combine tuna or chicken, soups, vegetables and 2 cans of water.
Mix and add noodles and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Prepare favorite chicken salad recipe for about 6 people. Place 1 1/2 teaspoons chicken salad (depending on size of cucumber slices) on the cucumber slice and top with a toasted pecan half. Makes 48.

Cream together margarine, sugar and vanilla. Blend flour and cocoa together and add to this mixture. Refrigerate 1 to 3 hours. Mold a scant tablespoon of dough around each chocolate drop. Shape into balls. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until set. Cool. Roll in 10x sugar. Makes 4 1/2 dozen.
Blend refried beans with taco mix.
Spread in 9-inch pie plate.
Mash avocados and combine with sour cream and lemon juice. Spread mixture over beans.
Sprinkle with cheese, tomatoes, chilies, olives and green onions.
Have cooked rice ready.
Have onion, parsley, bell pepper, celery, green onions and garlic chopped and ready.
In medium skillet, saute butter and chicken livers for 2 minutes.
Add onion and apple and stir for 5 minutes until apple softens.
Stir in brandy and cream.
Transfer mixture to blender and blend 2 to 3 minutes or until smooth.
Refrigerate this mixture for 1 hour.
Pepper, but do not salt, chicken breasts.
Wrap slice of bacon around each.
Place a layer of dried beef in bottom of baking dish.
Place bacon wrapped breasts in dish.
Cover with mixture of chicken soup, sour cream and cream cheese.
Cover with foil. Place in 325° oven for 2 hours.
When tender, remove foil and let brown slightly.
Serve on bed of rice.
Slice chicken breasts.
Combine honey, lime juice and mustard. (I use a combination of Kosciusko and a stone-ground mustard.) Place chicken in a baking dish.
Pour marinade over chicken, turning to coat.
Let stand for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once.
Make a bed of lettuce in the bowl.
Place a layer of English peas on the lettuce, then a layer of chopped onion.
Add sugar to mayonnaise and spread over onions.
Top with package of shredded Cheddar cheese.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan generously.
Spread the bread cubes over bottom of pan.
Sprinkle cheese cubes over bread.
In bowl beat eggs.
Add milk and seasonings.
Mix well.
Pour over cheese-bread in pan carefully.
Cover with plastic or foil and place in fridge overnight.
Next morning sprinkle bacon bits over mixture and bake 1 hour at 325°.

recipes.t: Pasta With Sausage And Cream Sauce
d: Melt butter in skillet; stir in sausage and fry until brown. Drain grease.
Stir in cream, wine, 1 tablespoon parsley, nutmeg and 1/2 cup Parmesan.
Simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
Put sugar, milk and corn syrup into saucepan.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture begins to boil.
Clip a candy thermometer to side of pan.
Cook for about 12 minutes or until mixture reaches 234°, soft ball stage.
Remove from heat.
Add butter and almond extract.
Beat until fudge begins to thicken. Quickly stir in walnuts and cherries.
Beat until fudge is no longer glossy.
Score into squares while warm.
Brown the beef, onion and garlic.
Drain the grease.
Add cream cheese and melt into the meat mixture.
Add the other ingredients.
Serve warm in a crock-pot or fondue pot with corn chips.
Pierce chuck roast; cover with meat tenderizer and pepper well. Mix marinade of vegetable oil, ketchup, vinegar with garlic and a few shakes of Worcestershire sauce.
Cover roast and marinate at least 12 hours.
Grill and baste with marinade.
Roast has better texture when room temperature before grilling.
Peel and clean shrimp.
Smash and dice garlic.
Brown garlic in unsalted butter.
Chop parsley.
Slice mushrooms and stir in the warm unsalted butter.
Add coarsely chopped shrimp.
After shrimp turns pink, stir in parsley.
Pour over hot linguine.
Add Romano cheese, salt and pepper to taste.
Cook carrots in boiling water until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Drain and cool.
Combine carrots, onion and green pepper in large serving bowl.
Combine soup, sugar, oil, vinegar, Worcestershire and salt.
Pour over vegetables.
Stir gently to combine.
Cover.
Refrigerate at least 24 hours to blend flavors.
In large skillet over medium-high heat, brown chops in oil on one side, about 2 minutes; turn chops and add salsa and chiles to skillet.
Lower heat; cover and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes. Uncover; top each chop with one tablespoon of cheese.
Cover and simmer just until cheese melts.
Serves four.
Bake biscuits as directed on can.
In a 3-quart pot, add peaches, sugar, butter, nutmeg, cloves, cinnamon, vanilla and lemon flavor.
Cook until it starts to get thick.
Break open your cooked biscuits and place the bottom part on a greased square pan. Pour your peach mixture over the biscuit bottom, then place the top part of the biscuit over the mixture.
Let bake in hot oven for 15 minutes.
Serve with ice cream or cheese, if desired. Serves 6 to 8.
In a large bowl, combine water, yeast, sugar and salt.
Stir until dissolved.
Add flour (dough will be wet).
Place dough onto floured platter.
Spread brown sugar in pie crust; sprinkle with flour.
Pour milk over it.
Dot with margarine.
Do not stir.
Sprinkle pie with cinnamon or allspice.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes until set.
In a 2-quart casserole or larger, layer the ingredients twice in this order:
cornbread, beans, vegetables and bacon.
Top with cheese.
Mix sour cream and salsa together and spread over entire top of dish so no air holes are showing.
Cover and chill 2 to 3 hours.
Place 1 cup crumbs in ungreased 8 inch square pan. Thoroughly cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well. Spread carefully over crumbs.
Combine cream, nuts and pineapple. Spread over creamed mixture, then sprinkle with remaining crumbs. Let stand 18 to 24 hours in refrigerator.
Cut into squares and serve.
May top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Serves 12 - 16.
Heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken.
Cook and stir 3 minutes. Drain; reduce heat to medium.
Stir in combined dressing, juice and sugar. Add rice and green pepper. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Add oranges and pineapple.
Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
I also add pea pods.
Preparation time:
10 minutes.
Cooking time:
10 minutes plus standing. Makes 4 servings.
Place fish in shallow baking dish and cover with milk. Refrigerate 1 hour.
Drain and pat dry.
Combine egg white and lemon juice in a separate shallow dish and set aside.
Combine oat bran, paprika and black pepper.
Dip fillets in egg mixture then oat mixture.
Saut in oil in nonstick skillet 3 minutes on each side or until evenly browned.
Serves 4.

recipes.t: George Washington'S Cherry Tree Cake(Make This In Honor Of His Birthday Or Someone Else'S!)
d: Cream sugar and oil; add eggs and vanilla.
Sift flour, baking soda and cinnamon and add to first mixture.
Stir in pie filling and chocolate chips.
Pour in two greased and floured cake pans or a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
You can frost if you like.
A rich and moist cake.
Place crackers on foil covered cookie sheet.
Melt butter, margarine and sugar.
Bring to boil.
Boil 3 minutes.
Pour mixture over crackers and sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cool.
Break apart.
Cut zucchini in half lengthwise and cut into slices about 1/2-inch thick.
In a large frying pan, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-high heat.
Add half the zucchini and brown on both sides.
Add the remaining oil and butter; saute the rest of the zucchini.
Remove with slotted spoon.
Bake a devil's food cake.
Completely cool and cut into strips.
Mix up chocolate pudding.
Using a large bowl, put layer of cake strips in bottom of bowl.
Cover cake strips with chocolate syrup.
Next, put a layer of chocolate pudding, then a layer of nuts and a layer of Cool Whip.
Start completely over, ending with Cool Whip.
Swirl top with chocolate syrup, chopped nuts and top with cherries.
Cook water, sugar and syrup until it reaches soft boil stage. Add 1/2 of the syrup mixture to stiffly beaten egg whites.
Cook other half of syrup to crack stage when dropped into cold water. Add this to egg whites, beating all the time.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Stir with a large spoon until it loses its gloss.
Pour into buttered pan.
Beat the egg with a fork.
Bring the broth to a simmering point.
Remove from heat and slowly drizzle in the beaten egg, stirring slowly.
The egg should become stringy-looking rather than making the soup appear milky.
Garnish with parsley.
Serve hot.
Cream the cream cheese with sugar and mayonnaise.
Add pineapple (drained) and cranberry sauce.
Use mixer to mix well. Add Cool Whip.
Put into cupcake liners and freeze.
Or can be frozen in any dish desired.
Thaw slightly before serving.
A good way to store in freezer is to let mixture freeze and put into Ziploc bags.
Cook broccoli according to package directions.
Meanwhile, cook bacon and garlic until bacon is crisp.
Add vinegar; heat. Brown bread crumbs in butter.
Pour sauce over hot broccoli and sprinkle with crumbs.
Makes 3 servings.
Brown meat and onions together with garlic.
When all browned, add beans and catsup.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add eggs, milk and oil.
Blend just until moistened.
Spoon into a greased baking pan (8 or 9-inch square). Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook sausage, onion, celery, green pepper and garlic until meat is no
longer pink and vegetables are tender; drain. Add cream cheese, green onion and parsley. Cook and stir over low heat until cheese is melted. Set aside.
Pour pie mix in ungreased 13 x 9-inch cake pan.
Sift dry cake mix over top of pie mix.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup melted butter on top. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serve with whipped cream or ice cream.
Brown and drain sausage and hamburger.
Combine all ingredients in crock-pot and cook on high until cheese melts. Stir frequently.
Reduce heat and serve from crock-pot with corn chips or tortilla chips.
Combine 2 teaspoons sugar and 1 tablespoon cornstarch in saucepan.
Add 1/2 cup water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thick and clear.
Cool.
Beat egg whites with salt and vanilla until soft peaks form.
Add 4 tablespoons sugar after adding cornstarch mixture.
Beat until it stands in stiff peaks.
Spread on pie.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Peel potatoes, slice or cut into 1/2-inch pieces and boil in salted water just until tender.
(Be careful not to overcook or the potatoes will become mush.)
Meanwhile cut bacon into small pieces. Cut onion into small pieces or green onions into thin slices.
Mix together vinegar, water, sugar, pepper and salt.
Fry bacon in skillet until crisp, then scoop bacon out of skillet into vinegar mixture, leaving drippings in skillet.
Saute onion in drippings. Add flour to onion in skillet and stir until smooth and thickened. Drain potatoes (when tender) and pour into skillet.
Add bacon/vinegar mixture and stir gently to mix evenly.
Cook pasta according to package directions, adding broccoli to water last 2 minutes of cooking time; drain well.
Add process cheese spread and milk to pasta mixture in saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until process cheese melts.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Place bacon slices in skillet and cook until crisp; remove from skillet to cool.
For fresh corn, cut off cob (it is better cut off cream style).
Mix corn, salt and sugar; pour
into bacon drippings in skillet.
Crumble bacon strips into corn.
Add 1/2 cup water.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes over low heat.
Stir often.
Combine brown sugar and flour.
Add egg yolks and water and beat with
electric
mixer
until creamy and smooth.
Heat the can of
milk
until
hot and add the creamy mixture.
Cook until thickened; stir constantly.
When thickened, remove from heat. Add butter and vanilla.
Pour into an 8-inch pie shell. Top with meringue.
Dust chicken with flour.
Melt oleo in heavy skillet and add chicken.
Cook over moderate heat about 15 minutes on each side. Pour mushrooms with broth into saucepan. Add bouillon cube and heat.
Blend wine and cornstarch (to mushrooms) until thickened. Allow sour cream to come to room temperature.
Place in bowl, stir until smooth.
Add to sauce.
Remove chicken to warm place.
Pour sauce into skillet.
Heat and serve over chicken and rice on platter.
Mix together butter, dates and sugar.
Cook over low flame, stirring constantly until mixture boils.
Mix together egg (beaten), milk and salt.
Add to date mixture.
Cook 2 minutes and cool.
Add nuts and Rice Krispies.
Form into 1-inch balls and roll in chopped nuts or coconut.
Store in refrigerator.
Saute mushrooms and onion in butter with juice of 1 lemon. Saute cauliflowerets in butter with garlic, basil, salt and pepper to taste.
Mix all ingredients and put in greased casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Add ground beef and brown.
Stir in pinto beans, rice and tomatoes.
Mix well.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Serves 6 to 8.
Brown ground chuck and drain.
Add taco mix, water and olives. Simmer 5 minutes. Separate rolls and put in ungreased 9 x 10-inch pie plate to make crust.
Sprinkle 1 cup crushed chips over bottom crust. Spoon on meat mixture, the sour cream, cheese and top with remaining corn chips.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes. Slice and serve. Top individual servings with as much lettuce, tomato and taco sauce as desired.
Freezes well.
Cover vegetables with water and simmer until tender.
Bring the bouillon cubes and 2 quarts of water to boil, being sure that the bouillon cubes are dissolved.
Melt butter in another pan; add flour to butter slowly.
Stir constantly.
In just a few seconds, it will be thick.
Then add to this mixture, stirring quickly, 1 cup of the boiling water with bouillon cubes, then add a little more, then add all of this mixture to the water mixture.
Stir thoroughly.
Add this mixture to the vegetable mixture.
Do not drain vegetables.
Add Cheez Whiz to soup and stir until dissolved. Add peas to soup.
Add chicken cubes.
Add bacon crumbles.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
You're done.
Place 4 slices bread in greased 8-inch pan.
Combine all ingredients, except soup and eggs.
Spread evenly over bread in pan.
Blend together soup and eggs, pour over sandwiches.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until set and lightly browned.
Coat chicken lightly with melted margarine and dredge in seasoned dry bread crumbs.
Place in an ungreased shallow baking pan.
Oven fry at 425° for 5 to 9 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through.
For crisper chicken, coat pan with 1 tablespoon melted margarine or vegetable oil and preheat oven for 5 minutes before adding chicken.
Toast Chex crumbs in a 300° oven for 10 minutes; set aside. Combine egg, seasoned salt and taco sauce.
Stir in ground beef and Chex.
Shape into 4 oval patties to fit bread loaf.
Broil or grill for 10 to 12 minutes, or until done.
Turn midway.
Place, end to end, on split French bread.
Spoon on additional taco sauce.
Top with tomato, lettuce and cheese.
To serve, place top on loaf and slice crosswise.
Cut tomatoes to bite size.
Cut olives in half.
Rub bowl with garlic; add tomatoes, olives and cheese.
Sprinkle with vinegar and olive oil.
Add seasonings and toss.
Marinate for at least 4 hours on counter.
If longer, store in refrigerate until 1 to 2 hours before serving.
Taste improves the longer it stands at room temperature.
Peel and grate potatoes in large pot.
Dice onion and green pepper.
Add water (enough to cover potatoes).
Bring to a boil; reduce to simmer and cover for 20 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Add cheese and milk; cook 10 minutes longer to melt cheese.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Wrap each breast with 1 slice ham and 1 slice Swiss cheese. Combine sour cream, mushroom soup and Durkee's spread.
Place chicken in 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Spread sour cream mixture over chicken.
Cover and bake for 2 1/2 hours at 250°.
Grease and flour bottoms of 2 (9-inch) layer cake pans.
Mix first 4 ingredients; set aside.
In large bowl with mixer at high speed, beat next 3 ingredients for 3 minutes or until light and fluffy.
At low speed, beat in real mayonnaise.
Add flour mixture in 4 additions alternately with water, beginning and ending with flour.
Pour into pans.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until cake tester comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes. Remove; cool on racks.
Frost.
Makes 2 (9-inch) layers.
Whip cream cheese.
Mix in confectioners sugar.
Blend in Cool Whip.
Spread in pie shells.
Top with pie filling.
Place egg yolks, Sucaryl and next 4 ingredients in blender and blend 2 seconds.
Add apples.
Blend until fine.
Pour into buttered pie plate.
Bake at 450° for 25 minutes.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Add remaining ingredients and process along with 1 teaspoon Sucaryl.
Put meringue on pie, spreading to edges.
Brown at 350° until golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Serves 6, 155 calories per serving.
Place trout in a 12 x 8-inch baking dish.
In small bowl, combine crumbs, onion, pepper, mushrooms, salt and pepper.
Spread over fish; top with lemon slices.
Cover with wax paper. Microwave at High 5 to 7 minutes, or until fish flakes easily. Let stand 3 to 5 minutes.
Contains 133 calories per serving.

Mix bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, oregano, salt and pepper and set aside. In a hot skillet, add some butter and saute garlic. Next melt remaining butter. Now roll each piece chicken in butter, then roll in mixture. Put in 13 x 9 baking dish. Bake at 350° for 55 minutes. Just at done, place 2 slices Mozzarella cheese on each chicken breast; put back in oven until it melts.
Melt oleo in 9 X 13 pan.
Stir in both cans of corn and cornbread mix.
Add eggs and stir with fork.
Drop sour cream and cheese by spoonfuls on top, then fold in gently.
(Optional:
may add 1 can of chopped green chilies)
Fry out a good bit of white bacon.
Cut into small pieces. Cook slow as to get all the grease out.
Chop or grind clams, white potatoes and onions.
Add clams and juice and a small amount of water; mix.
When done, add a 1/2 stick of butter, salt and pepper to taste.
Combine flour, soda and salt.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each.
Add dry ingredients to cream mixture, alternating with sour cream and ending with dry ingredients.
Add flavor.
Generously grease and flour 10-inch tube pan.
Cover bottom of pan with nuts.
Spoon batter over nuts. Sprinkle with nutmeg or mace.
Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours. Remove from oven and remove from pan immediately.

recipes.t: D.P. Whitmer'S Blueberry Muffins(This Recipe Won Third Place In "Connecticut Post" Contest.)
d: Lightly spray the inside of muffin tins with nonstick spray. With a paper towel or tissue, gently wipe the spray inside each muffin cup.
Spread soft butter around inside of each muffin cup liberally.
Set aside tins in cool place.
Into a bowl, put 1/3 cup flour, 1/3 cup confectioners sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; mix well, then add the fresh or hard frozen berries and mix well. Reserve at room temperature.
In small saucepan, over low heat, melt chocolate in water; stir.
In large bowl, beat sugar and shortening until fluffy. Beat in egg yolks and vanilla.
Stir in chocolate mixture.
In medium bowl, combine flour, baking soda and salt; add to batter alternately with buttermilk until blended.
Cream softened oleo and cheese.
Blend in flour and chili powder.
Work it with hands and shape into small balls; press on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Makes 4 dozen.
Beat margarine and sugar together.
By degrees, add dried milk.
Flavour with vanilla and beat until very smooth.
(GE)
Line 13 x 9-inch pan with foil.
Grease bottom and sides of foil-lined pan.
Place graham crackers on bottom of pan, cutting crackers to fit.
Microwave chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter in microwavable bowl on High 2 minutes.
Stir until melted.
Spread 1/2 of the melted chocolate over graham crackers.
Microwave remaining 4 tablespoons butter in 4 quart microwavable bowl on High 45 seconds or until melted.
Add marshmallows.
Mix to coat. Microwave 1 1/2 minutes or until melted, stirring after 45 seconds. Add cereal.
Mix to coat well.
Press firmly over chocolate-coated graham crackers in pan.
Drizzle with remaining melted chocolate. Cool.
Cut into squares.
Makes 24.
Drain juice from pineapple and add enough water to make 2 cups of liquid.
Heat this and add jello.
Dissolve.
While still hot, add marshmallows; cool.
Add cottage cheese, pineapple, nuts and cherries.
Whip cream and fold other ingredients into this.
Chill until firm.
Beat eggs in separate bowl.
Take first 4 ingredients and place onto counter top lined with wax paper.
Take a rolling pin and roll ingredients into a crumblike mixture.
Cover all pieces of fish in egg mixture and then cover fish with crumb mixture to create batter taste.
Cook fish in skillet of oil for 6 minutes. Serves 3 to 4 people.
Very tasty!
Mix ingredients in large pot.
Heat on medium heat until mixture is hot (do not boil).
Serve hot.
Leftover juice can be refrigerated and reheated.
In large bowl combine undrained pineapple chunks, undrained mandarin orange sections and undrained fruit cocktail with the flaked coconut and lemon juice.
Sprinkle the instant lemon pudding mix over the fruits and toss lightly to combine.
Chill. Just before serving, peel and slice bananas; fold into fruit mixture.
Serve in dessert dishes; top with approximately 2 1/2 tablespoons Cool Whip.
If desired garnish with tiny bit of grated lemon or grated orange peel.
Serves 9.
Boil potato in slightly
salted
water
until cooked. Mash hot potato, adding as much powdered sugar as it will hold to make dough that can be rolled out.
Add vanilla during this process. Roll out
on
powdered
sugar to 1/4-inch thickness. Spread with peanut
butter
generously.
Roll
up
and slice. This candy keeps very well.
Shell and devein shrimp
and
bone
chicken; set aside. In large skillet, cook
onion
in butter until tender.
Remove onion to bowl with
slotted spoon.
In drippings, cook chicken until browned on both
sides.
Into
chicken skillet measure 3 tablespoons parsley.
Add
onion,
tomato
sauce, water, wine, salt, pepper and basil.
Bring quickly to a boil.
Add shrimp; reduce heat to low; cover
and
simmer
for 5 minutes or until chicken and shrimp are tender.
Serve with rice.
Serves 6.
Cream sugar, shortening and molasses.
Add egg, allspice, cloves, ginger and coffee.
Mix.
Add enough flour to make stiff dough.
Chill.
Roll out 1/4-inch thick.
Cut with cookie cutters. May decorate with sugar toppings.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cream together butter, salt and garlic.
Mix in bread crumbs, parsley, sherry, pepper and paprika.
Peel and devein shrimp. Toss into simmering water and cook just a few minutes, only until they turn pink.
Rinse with cool water and drain.
Place cubed bread into greased 9X13 pan.
Top with Cheddar. Beat eggs, milk, mustard and onion powder; slowly pour over bread and cheese.
Bake at 325 degrees for 30-35 minutes.
Cover with bacon and bake another 10 minutes or until knife in center comes out clean.
Combine first 5 ingredients in heavy saucepan.
Cook over medium heat.
Stir constantly until thick and smooth; set aside to cool.
Scald milk and add sugar.
Set aside to cool.
Mix yeast and warm water; let it sit for a few minutes.
Cut butter into flour and add eggs.
Combine flour, yeast and milk mixtures. Dough will be moist.
Divide in half.
Roll each half out on a floured surface to fit the bottom of a jelly roll pan.
Spread cooled pineapple filling and cover with second half.
Seal edges; snip surface of dough to let steam escape.
Cover with clean towel and let rise in a warm place for about one hour.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Frost with confectioners sugar frosting.
May want to use 2 cans of canned pie filling or substitute other canned fruit or fresh fruit or pineapple.
Heat cider, cloves, allspice, cinnamon and sugar to boiling; cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Strain punch and pour into punch bowl.
Float oranges in bowl.
Makes 32 servings (about 1/2 cup each).
Make a simple syrup by dissolving sugar in hot water.
Add lemon juice; let cool.
Dilute syrup with water to taste.
Just before serving add apples.
Serve over ice.
Marinate quail breast overnight in Italian dressing.
Split breast on both sides of bone; stuff with the jalapeno pepper slices.
Drizzle mixture of melted butter and picante sauce over each breast.
Wrap 1 slice bacon around each quail; secure with toothpick.
Wrap in heavy foil.
Bake for approximately 2 hours at 300°.
Best results when put on smoker or pit for 2 hours.
In a small bowl combine cream cheese, dill and garlic powder. Blend well.
Spread about 1 tablespoon mixture on each tortilla. Top each with carrot, broccoli and onions.
Roll up each tortilla and cut in half.
In skillet, cook meat, onion and garlic until meat is brown and onion is tender; drain.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
In saucepan, combine meat mixture, tomato sauce, rice and chili powder.
Cook over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, or until hot and bubbly, stirring occasionally. Stir in half of the cheese until melted.
Spoon onto a plate.
Top with remaining shredded cheese.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Saute onion, garlic and oil until tender; stir in flour, pepper and Tabasco sauce.
Blend and add milk slowly and cook on medium heat until boiling.
Add cheese and stir until smooth and add to macaroni and pour into a greased 2-quart casserole dish and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cut Crisco into flour and salt.
Sprinkle in cold orange juice and "stir" only until dough leaves sides of bowl.
The secret is, do not handle the dough very much.
Divide dough into two equal parts and roll out, one at a time on well floured area.
Place in pie plate and flute, poke holes in it and bake for your one crust pies.
Bake at 425° until lightly brown.
In a 4-quart saucepan, place tomatoes, chopped, and liquid from the can.
Add 1 cup of water and 1 cup chicken broth.
Deskin as much chicken as you want meat in the stew.
Add onion, salt and pepper to taste and 1 teaspoon of sugar.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer about 1 hour.
During the last 30 minutes, add the diced potatoes.
Remove the chicken; cook and take meat off the bones.
Chop the meat and return it to the pan.
Add the corn and butter beans and continue cooking until the beans are done.
Saute celery and onion in butter.
Add soup, milk and 1/3 jar Cheez Whiz.
Make layers of rice, asparagus, chestnuts and soup mixture in a buttered casserole dish. Add remaining Cheez Whiz on top of last layer in teaspoonfuls.
Bake, covered with foil, 25 to 30 minutes in a 350° oven.
Place potatoes in a buttered 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Add bell pepper and pimentos.
Mix lightly.
Combine milk and salt and pour over potato mixture.
Cover with foil.
Bake in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove foil.
Cover with mixture of bread crumbs and cheese.
Drizzle 1/3 cup butter over top.
Continue baking for 15 minutes or until cheese melts.
First, peel and slice potatoes thick and put in kettle. Bring to boil.
Remove immediately and drain.
Grease crock-pot and layer them in there; cook until done.
Sprinkle paprika on top and always end up with soup on top.
You can also bake this in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 15 minutes, uncovered and cook for 45 minutes at 375°.
Mix sugar, eggs and shortening.
Put flour, salt, nutmeg, ginger, soda and baking powder in sieve.
Add to sugar mixture alternately with sour milk.
Combine dressing, beans, potatoes, ham, celery, green onion, parsley and chives in a large salad bowl.
Cover; refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Before serving, stir in snow peas or sugar snap peas.
To serve, if desired, place halved tomato slices on a platter.
Top the salad mixture, or mound portions of salad on individual lettuce lined plates.
Makes 6 servings.
Dissolve yeast in water.
Put Crisco, milk, sugar and salt on stove.
Get lukewarm.
Add flour.
Mix and knead.
Let set 15 minutes.
Knead and roll.
Let stand 15 minutes, then bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine hot popped corn, nuts, pretzels and bran squares.
In a small saucepan, melt margarine with mustard. Pour over popcorn mixture, tossing gently to coat.
Sprinkle herb and spice mix over coated corn and toss again. Spread coated corn on baking sheet and bake at 350° for 3 to 5 minutes. Serve immediately or store in airtight container.
Makes 2 1/2 quarts.
Cook chicken breast.
Add Japanese cucumbers and bean sprouts. Mix these ingredients.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spray a 9-inch square baking pan with Pam or Baker's Joy.
In a small mixing bowl, soak raisins in Port and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, sift together oat bran, flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Place in another bowl the brown sugar, oil, milk, corn syrup, vanilla and egg substitute; mix with an electric beater for a minute or two.
Add carrots to the liquid mixture, then stir in the flour mixture, then the raisins and Port.
Pour mixture into prepared baking pan; bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until a toothpick, when inserted in center of cake, comes out dry.
Let cool to room temperature, then cut into squares.
Beat first 3 ingredients until creamy.
Beating water, egg, and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Cover and chill for about 2 hours.
Heat oven to 350.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 - 9 minutes.
Place Hershey kiss in center of cookie while still warm.
In a small saucepan, stir together pineapple juice, honey, cornstarch, and ground ginger.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly, cook and stir for 2 minutes more.
Stir in fruit.
Serve over pancakes, waffles or French toast.

recipes.t: Chicken Livers Wrapped In Bacon(For Parties)
d: Cut chicken livers in about 3 or 4 pieces each. Stir in other ingredients, except bacon. Cover and put in refrigerator for about 1 hour. Cut bacon slices in half.

Wrap each piece of chicken liver with a piece of bacon; fasten with a toothpick. Place in a broiler pan or any bread pan that is deep enough to catch the grease while cooking. Bake in oven at about 350°. Bake until bacon is done.
Sprinkle bottom of pastry with 1 tablespoon each of sugar and flour.
Combine the remaining sugar and flour; stir in honey and cream.
Pour mixture over apples.
Mix gently until slices are well coated.
Spoon apples into pie shell.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg and dot with butter.
Bake at 425° for 45 minutes.
Soften
cream
cheese
to
room temperature and combine with drained
pineapple
and 1/2 cup pecans and green onions. Roll into
ball
and
roll in 1/2 cup pecans. Refrigerate and serve with crackers.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease and flour 8-inch square pan. Combine flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, mustard and pepper.
Set aside.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan well.
Line pan with whole graham crackers.
Cook together 1 cup sugar, 1 stick butter and 4 sticks oleo.
Cook 3 minutes.
Pour over crackers and sprinkle slivered almonds on top.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.

Cream shortening, eggs and sugar. Add eggs 1 at a time, beating well after each one. Sift flour, salt, baking powder and cocoa. Add to cake mixture alternately with milk and vanilla. Pour in tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Dice orange sections, reserving several for garnish.
Prepare topping mix with 1 cup of the milk as directed on package, using large mixing bowl.
Add remaining 1 3/4 cups milk and pudding mix. Blend, then beat at high speed for 2 minutes, scraping bowl often.
Fold in oranges.
Spoon into pie shell.
Chill at least 4 hours.
Garnish with rest of oranges.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Prepare rice as directed on package, omitting margarine and salt.
Mix rice, turkey, celery, peppers and parsley in a large bowl.
Add dressing; mix lightly.
Serve warm or refrigerate until ready to serve.
Makes 6 cups or 6 servings.
Cut chicken into 1/2-inch cubes.
Cut peppers into strips. Cook pasta according to package; drain.
Meanwhile, add cooking oil and preheat wok over high heat.
Stir-fry chicken 3 minutes or until lightly browned.
Add green peppers, onion, cumin and red pepper.
Stir-fry 3 minutes (adding more oil if needed).
Stir in drained pasta, corn, chili peppers and salt.
Cover and cook 2 minutes or until hot.
Stir in tomatoes.
Sprinkle with cheese. Cover and cook 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.
In
double
boiler, stir until smooth butter, sugar and cocoa. Add
egg
and vanilla.
Then, remove from heat and add coconut, graham
cracker crumbs, chopped nuts; spread mixture in 9
x 9-inch
square pan.
Mix butter, confectioners sugar, pudding powder
and
cream.
Spread
on
first mixture.
Melt chocolate and butter, spread on cake.
Refrigerate until firm. Cut into small pieces.
Mix and sift flour and baking powder.
Beat egg yolks, then add sugar and beat until thick.
Add water, lemon rind and lemon juice.
Stir in flour and then blueberries.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Turn into greased pudding mold and steam 1 hour over rapidly boiling salted water.
Serve with nutmeg or lemon sauce.
Makes approximately 6 servings.
Mix together soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic.
Simmer in saucepan.
Cut chicken into 1-inch chunks.
Dip chicken in beaten egg, then dip chicken into flour.
Fry the coated chicken nuggets in oil until browned.
Dip chicken nuggets into soy sauce mixture, then bake them in 325° oven for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle chicken with sesame seed, if desired.
Serve with rice and whatever sauce remains.
Beat concentrate for 30 seconds.
Blend in ice cream and whipped topping.
Whip until smooth.
Pour into crust.
Freeze at least 4 hours.
top with additional whipped cream.
Put the oats in bowl; set aside.
Put oleo, sugar, chocolate and milk in pan; boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add peanut butter; stir until dissolved.
Add vanilla.
Pour all over oatmeal; stir until oatmeal is all covered.
Put waxed paper on cookie sheets; drop by spoonful.
Set in cool place to harden.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix softened butter and cream cheese until smooth.
Gradually add the flour to form a pastry dough. Line tart tins with tart size paper tartlet cups.
Mix the remaining ingredients for filling.
Measure cold water into small bowl.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold water.
Let stand 1 minute.
Add sugar to the mixture.
Stir until gelatin dissolves.
Pour boiling water into medium bowl. Stir in gelatin mixture.
Combine milk, vanilla and almond extract.
Stir milk mixture into gelatin mixture.
Divide mixture between four serving dishes.
Refrigerate until set, about 3 hours.
Pare and slice kiwis.
Arrange slices and strawberries over each dessert.
Makes 4 servings.
Break the cauliflower into its flowerets, cutting the bigger ones in halves or quarters so that all the pieces are about 1/2-inch in size.
Put the oil in a soup pot along with the garlic, salt, pepper and the cut-up cauliflower.
Stirring gently, cook over medium heat until the vegetable bits are well oiled and flavored.
Add the tomato paste, hot water, the potato slices and 2 teaspoons salt and bring to a boil.
Break the pasta into 1 or 2-inch lengths as you put it in the pot.
Continue boiling until the pasta is well cooked, has absorbed some of the water and the cauliflower, garlic and tomato have lent their flavors to the pasta.
Before serving discard the garlic clove.
Serve with a sprinkling of Parmesan cheese.

recipes.t: Cream Cheese-Olive Dip Or Spread(Heloise'S Recipe)
d: Mix cream cheese with mayonnaise.
Stir in pecans, olives, olive liquid and pepper.
It will be a little mushy but will thicken in the refrigerator. The spread will keep for weeks.
It makes a great spread for crackers or finger sandwiches.
(Also, low calorie cream cheese and mayonnaise can be used with good results.)
Chill Veg-All thoroughly.
Prepare macaroni according to package directions.
Drain; combine macaroni, Veg-All, bacon and 1/2 can of onion rings.
Add mayonnaise, 1/2 of the parsley and seasoned salt.
Toss gently.
Serve immediately or chill 1 to 2 hours.
Mix cake mix, 1 egg and 1 stick margarine.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Blend cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla and 2 eggs.
Spread on first mixture.
Sprinkle with pecans that have been rolled in small amount of powdered sugar.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Bring sugar, syrup and butter to a boil.
Remove; add peanut butter.
Combine Cheerios, corn flakes and peanuts in a bowl. Pour boiled mixture over cereals and mix well.
Pour into buttered pan and cool.
Cut into squares.
Sprinkle brisket with pepper and paprika.
Slice onions on top to cover.
Mix remaining ingredients well and pour over meat. Marinate overnight.
Bake at 300° to 325° for about 3 to 4 hours, depending on oven and thickness of meat.
When ready to serve, slice very thinly against the grain and serve with sauce.
Bring sugar, water and cream of tartar to boil, covered.
Boil 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add margarine and baking soda. Pour over popcorn and stir thoroughly.
Must be cane sugar or it will just crumble up and not stick to the popcorn.
Set aside 4 perfect strawberries with stems.
Wash and cap remaining strawberries.
Puree strawberries in blender, food processor (with a steel blade) or food mill.
Combine puree with confectioners sugar and lemon juice.
Pour mixture into a 1-quart metal pan or ice cube tray.
Freeze until mushy and frozen 1/2 inch around sides.
Place oil in skillet, about 1-inch.
Let it get hot.
Cut small hole in center of biscuits with salt shaker lid.
Drop into oil.
Turn when brown.
Brown other side.
Drain on paper towel. Roll in sugar, powdered sugar or cinnamon.
Makes 20 donuts and 20 holes.
Combine cheese, flour, paprika and pepper.
Add beaten egg whites and shape into small balls.
Roll in cracker crumbs.
Fry in hot oil at 375°.
Drain.
Serve hot.
Yield:
8 servings.
Place chocolate in empty coffeepot.
Place coffee and orange peel in brew basket.
Prepare coffee using 3 cups water.
Serve hot with whipped topping.
Makes 4 cups.
Brown sausage; drain.
Add potatoes and tomatoes; cook over medium heat 5 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Beat eggs and 2 tablespoons water.
Pour over ingredients in skillet; cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes or until egg mixture is set in center and cheese is melted.
Uncover; let stand 5 minutes before cutting into wedges.
Remove one end from each of four 1-pound cans (the kind used for canned fruits and vegetables); rinse cans, dry and grease well.
In a large bowl, combine the graham and all-purpose flours, soda and salt.
Stir in yogurt, molasses, raisins and walnuts; mix well.
Divide batter evenly between cans.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 1 hour or until a wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in cans 10 minutes; then turn out and stand loaves upright on a wire rack to cool completely.
Cut loaves crosswise to make thick or thin slices as you prefer.
Makes 4 small loaves.
Place the oats and butter in a bowl and pour on the coffee. Let stand 20 minutes.
Stir in the sugars and eggs. Mix well.
Add flour, salt and soda.
Stir in spices.
Bake in a 13 x 9 greased baking pan at 350° for 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease 2 large baking sheets.
In large bowl, sprinkle yeast over water.
Stir until well blended and yeast is dissolved.
With spoon, gradually stir in sugar, salt and 3 1/2 cups flour until dough is soft and slightly sticky.
Turn dough onto floured table or board.
Knead.
Turn 1/4; repeat. Knead 5 to 7 minutes adding another 1/2 cup flour if needed until dough is smooth and elastic.
Dough should not stick.
Cut dough in half and cut each half into 6 equal size pieces.
With floured hands, roll one piece of dough back and forth between palms of hands to form a dough rope.
Cook spaghetti, drain and set aside.
Slice onions and mushrooms.
Cut the pound of bacon in half then in half again; set aside.
Saute the onions and mushrooms in margarine, remove and set aside.
In same frying pan cook bacon until almost done (not crisp).
Drain bacon grease.
Add onions and mushrooms to bacon. Add oregano, spaghetti, half and half and stir over medium heat. Add Parmesan cheese.
Mix well.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes and remove. Serve with a salad and garlic bread.
Soften active dry yeast in warm water.
Scald milk in sugar, salt and butter; cool to lukewarm.
Mix in 2 cups flour, yeast, eggs, cardamom and fruit.
Add enough remaining flour to make a stiff dough.
Knead on floured surface; place in a greased bowl and grease top of dough.
Cover.
Combine cracker crumbs and margarine; press into 1 1/2-quart oblong Pyrex dish.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Cream the cheese and milk.
Gradually add sugar.
Spread mix over graham cracker crust.
Sprinkle pecans over cream cheese mixture.
Whip cream with vanilla.
Spread over pecans.
Chill.
When cold, spread cherry pie filling on top.
Chill overnight.
Cut chicken into 1/2-inch strips.
Remove florets from broccoli.
Set aside.
Peel stalks and cut into thin slices.
Coat chicken with 1 tablespoon stir-fry sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in hot wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add chicken and stir-fry three minutes.
Remove.
Mix sugar and flour together, then add cream slowly until smooth.
Add vanilla.
Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 375° until bottom of crust begins to brown, then lower heat to 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Mix
cream cheese and Eagle Brand milk; add lemon juice and whip
for 4 minutes or until thick.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Set in
refrigerator
for
2 hours.
Fold in fillings on top.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Cook over medium to low heat until marshmallow cream melts.
Gradually stir 1/4 of hot mixture into egg substitute.
Add remaining hot mixture, stirring constantly until mixture thickens (1 or 2 minutes).
Remove from heat.
Stir in bourbon and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg.
Let cool.
Chill for 3 hours.
Remove vanilla bean and discard.
Stir in ice milk just before serving.
Sprinkle with nutmeg, if desired.
Makes 16 (1/2 cup) servings.
Contains 113 calories, fat 0.9 g, saturated fat 0.5 g and cholesterol 4 mg.
In casserole, combine sugar, margarine and water.
Cook uncovered 1 minute.
Stir after margarine melts.
Separate biscuits.
Cut each into quarters and add to the sugar mixture. Push them away from the center.
Cook uncovered for 2 1/2 minutes. Let stand 2 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Add sherbet and blend until dissolved. Chill until almost set. Fold in fruit and marshmallows. Chill until firm. Makes 6 servings.
Patty hamburger meat.
Place in foil.
Layer veggies on top. Top with butter and Worcestershire sauce.
Seal tightly.
Bake over open fire or in a 350° oven for 30 minutes or until done. Over fire, turn after 15 minutes and cook 15 minutes more.

recipes.t: Sun-Maid Raisin Nut Cake(Our Family Christmas Cake Since 1936)
d: Cream butter with brown sugar.
Add molasses, beaten eggs and buttermilk, in which the soda has been dissolved.
Mix and sift the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and cloves.
Add to this dry mixture the Sun-Maid raisins (cut in pieces) and walnuts (coarsely chopped).
Combine dry ingredients with the first mixture.
Bake in 3 layers in moderate oven at 350° for about 25 minutes.
When cool, cover with your favorite icing.
I use Caramel Icing.
Rinse wheat in water until water is no longer cloudy.
Soak for 5 minutes.
Squeeze dry by cupping hands and pressing between palms of hands.
Use food processor to pulsate parsley to save time or chop fine on cutting board.
Chop onions, mint leaves and tomatoes very fine.
Place vegetables in a large bowl; add wheat, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and mix well.
Serve with fresh small grape leaves or place salad on romaine lettuce leaves used as scoops.
Serves 6.
Coat chicken legs with dressing and bread crumbs.
Arrange chicken on round microwave-safe plate, spoke fashion with meaty portion towards outer edge of plate.
Blend a little hot sauce with the mustard.
Add the mustard mixture and cheese to the remaining hot sauce; stir over low heat until cheese melts.
Add and stir in the tarragon.
Good on cauliflower, asparagus and green beans.
Yield:
1 1/2 cups.
Mix Dream Whip as per instructions on box.
Add instant vanilla pudding and peanut butter.
Place in pie shell and sprinkle with chopped nuts or chocolate chips.
Refrigerate.
Brown beef and garlic in oil.
Add, then cover and simmer 20 minutes the tomato paste, tomatoes, salt, pepper and oregano. Cook noodles according to directions on package.
In an 11 x 7-inch dish, alternate layers of noodles, meat sauce, 12 ounces cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese.
End with Mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
In a large saucepan, combine coconut milk and curry base and cook until blended over medium heat.
Add chicken, seasoning sauce and lemon juice and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add remaining ingredients, except mushrooms and garlic chili pepper sauce.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and garlic chili pepper sauce to taste.
Cover and simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Add cold water, vinegar, mayonnaise, salt and pepper.
Blend with rotary beater.
Pour into refrigerator tray.
Quick chill in freezing unit until firm, about 1-inch from edge, but soft in the center, about 15 to 20 minutes.
In large bowl, dissolve yeast and sugar in water.
Stir in one cup flour, salt, two eggs and oil.
Add remaining flour gradually, stirring until combined.
Turn out onto a lightly floured board. Knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic (adding small amounts of flour as needed).
(Pretend you are making pottery.) Put dough in a large oil-coated bowl, turning over once to coat whole ball.
Cover bowl with large dish cloth and let rise in warm place for one hour.
Punch down dough, turn over in bowl, re-cover with cloth and let rise another 45 minutes.
Punch down again, place dough on lightly floured board and cut in two.
Mix all ingredients in a large pan with a lid; use a whisk to mix.
Insert meat, making sure all meat is covered.
Replace lid to pan and place pan in refrigerator at least 24 hours.
Prepare meat before sauce.
Cut off all fat and sinue.
Brown meat.
Add onions, pepper, sauce, beans and Tabasco. Add water if it seems dry.
Simmer, for taste.
In small bowl beat cream cheese and pineapple until combined. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. roll in 1 inch balls.
Roll in coconut.
Refrigerate overnight or 6 hours.
Serve.
In skillet, over medium heat, heat chicken in margarine.
Cook chicken 10 minutes or until brown on both sides.
Stir in soup, water and pepper.
Heat until boiling.
Add in broccoli and reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes or until chicken and broccoli is fork-tender.
Mix the first 5 ingredients altogether; pat down in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat the eggs, powdered sugar and cream cheese together for 5 minutes.
Pour the mixture over the first mixture in the pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
May add chocolate chips, if you wish.
Melt butter in heavy skillet.
Stir in sugar, egg yolk and dates.
Cook and stir over low heat 5 minutes or until mixture is thick.
Remove from heat.
Stir in lemon juice, peel and nuts. Cool.
Drop or roll into balls and roll in powdered sugar. Delicious!!
I double this recipe.
Boil cured ham hocks until tender.
Remove ham hocks from boiler.
Add collard greens to liquid in boiler.
Put ham hocks on top of greens.
