Then put bacon drippings in and bring to a boil. Simmer on low heat until tender.
Add a pinch of salt and chopped onion.

recipes.t: New Year'S Black-Eyed Peas And Sausage
d: Fry bacon.
Drain grease, leaving 2 tablespoons in pan.
Add celery, green pepper, onion and garlic to the bacon drippings and saute until onion is clear.
Transfer to Dutch oven and add peas, water, salt, pepper and tomato.
While bringing peas to a boil, fry sausage and drain well.
Add sausage to peas and simmer for 40 minutes or until desired thickness of broth.
Mix together with fingers the flour, soda, oatmeal and brown sugar.
Add margarine.
Mix well and line a greased 9 x 13-inch pan (cover bottom well).
Brown meat in oil and season with salt.
Add onions and saute until tender.
Add water, soup base, salt and paprika.
Cook until meat is tender (falling apart).
Add tomatoes.
Heat to boiling. Mix cornstarch and water.
Add to broth to thicken.
Serve over noodles.
Cream butter.
Add sugar and egg.
Stir in milk and vanilla. Sift remaining dry ingredients together.
Add to butter mixture and blend well.
Stir in raisins or pecans, if desired.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on a lightly greased baking sheet.
Allow room to spread.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes.
Cream shortening, sugar and vanilla.
Beat in eggs.
Add chocolate which has been melted.
Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Stir in nuts.
Form in 1-inch balls.
Roll in 4x sugar. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.

Sift flour and spices together. Beat eggs well; add sugar. Add flour and liquids, alternately, to egg mixture, mixing thoroughly after each addition. Add walnuts; mix thoroughly. Stir baking soda into the cognac; mix it into batter. Pour into greased 9 x 12-inch pan. Bake approximately 45 minutes in 400° oven. As soon as cake is baked, remove from oven and cut into squares. Pour warm honey into all lines and around edges of warm cake. Grate walnuts over cake.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Put the oatmeal in a medium bowl.
Pour boiling water on the oatmeal and let stand while preparing the rest of the ingredients.
Cream butter and sugars (brown and granulated) until fluffy.
Sift the dry ingredients (flour and cinnamon), then add them to the butter and sugar mixture.
Pour in the vanilla and the oatmeal.
Stir until well blended.
Pour into 2 (9-inch) layer pans or one 12 x 9 x 2-inch utility pan.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes or until done.
Brown ground meat, draining away as much grease as possible; add chopped onion and brown with meat.
Add seasonings and undrained tomatoes.
Peel potatoes and cut into small cubes.
Chop carrots and celery finely.
Simmer 45 minutes or more, according to size of vegetable pieces.
Serves 4 meals.
It freezes perfectly.
Cut in together flour, oleo and nuts.
Press into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Let crust cool.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and Cool Whip together and spread onto cooled crust.
Mix milk and both packages of pudding together and spread onto cheese mixture.
Cool 6 to 8 hours.
Top with Cool Whip (optional).
Serves 10.

recipes.t: Quick Sock It To Me Cake Iii
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix together cake mix, sugar, oil, eggs, pecans, and vanilla.
Fold in the sour cream.
Put half the batter in a bundt pan.
Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the batter in the pan.
Pour remainder of the batter on top.
Bake for 70 minutes until cake tests done.
Beat egg. Combine with Ricotta and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cover bottom of casserole dish with sauce. Add a layer of rice. Add a layer of Ricotta.
Add sauce and a layer of Mozzarella and some Parmesan. Repeat until all ingredients are used.
Put sauce on top and sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbly.
Chop bacon and cook until crisp. Drain.
In a large pot, combine onions, brown sugar, vinegar and mustard.
Heat well. Add bacon and all cans of beans (undrained).
Mix well and heat slowly to blend flavors.
In small bowl combine teriyaki sauce, water, sherry, garlic and ginger.
Arrange fillets in 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Pour mixture over fillets.
Turn fish over to coat both sides.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Microwave uncovered on High for 4 to 5 minutes (flakes easily with fork).
Melt butter and brown seeds, almonds and crushed noodles. Drain on a paper towel.
Fry bacon until crisp; set aside.
In same frypan brown beef after rolling in flour.
Brown mushrooms, onion and green pepper. Parboil carrots 10 minutes.
Add 1 tablespoon flour, 2 cups bouillon (undiluted) and chili sauce.
Put all ingredients in casserole.
Dice bacon; spread on top.
Bake at 350° about 2 hours or until tender.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Make cake according to package directions.
Let cool.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan crumble cake.
Pour pudding over cake.
Spread evenly with pie filling and chill.
Mix whipped topping and spread evenly over pie filling.
Cover and chill until serving.

Choose uniform potatoes, scrub and pare. Roll in flour which has been seasoned with salt, pepper and herbs, fresh or dried. Place in buttered casserole dish and dot with butter. Add bay leaf and garlic. Cover and bake in 450° oven for 45 - 60 minutes or until potatoes are done.
Fry onion in 1/2 tablespoon oleo, then add to meat with salt, pepper and egg yolks.
Mix in cream and bread crumbs.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Roll in small balls and saute until brown.
May be frozen at this time.
Make roux with 1 tablespoon oleo and flour.
Add beef bouillon.
Add meatballs to gravy, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Mix deviled ham and onion.
Mound mixture on plate.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Frost ham mound with cream cheese mixture. Refrigerate overnight.
Combine flours; in a large bowl, thoroughly mix 1 1/2 cups flour mixture, sugar, salt, caraway seed and undissolved yeast. Combine water, milk and margarine in a saucepan.
Heat slowly until liquids are warm (margarine need not be melted).
Gradually add to dry ingredients and beat for 2 minutes at medium speed of electric mixer, scraping bowl occasionally.
Add 1/2 cup flour mixture or enough to make a thick batter.
Beat at high speed for 2 minutes, scraping bowl occasionally.
Add remaining flour. Batter should be stiff.
Stir until well blended or use dough hooks.
Cover; let rise in warm place free from draft until more than doubled in bulk, about 45 minutes.
Stir batter down.
Beat vigorously 1/2 minute.
Turn into well-greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven, about 40 to 50 minutes or until done.
Remove from casserole and cool on wire rack. Makes 1 loaf.
Clean husks.
Mix masa and butter well.
Add other ingredients.
Add sugar to taste.
Put 2 tablespoons masa (prepared) in corn husk, flatten and add fruit.
Roll and fold. Steam for 45 minutes.
Spoon 1/4 of dip over each tortilla, spreading to edges. Sprinkle each with 1/4 of chicken.
Roll up.
Place seam side down on a plate or flat dish.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Cut each roll into six 1-inch pieces.
Serve with salsa.
Makes 24 appetizers.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch loaf pan.
Combine Bisquick, cheese and sugar in a large bowl. Combine other ingredients in a second bowl.
Mix well.
Stir in dry mixture and blend thoroughly.
Beat slightly to remove lumps.
Turn into pan and bake until golden, 45 to 50 minutes.
Makes 14 to 17 servings.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine Crisco, brown sugar, and granulated sugar in large bowl.
Beat at medium speed with electric mixer until well blended.
Beat in eggs.
Add peanut butter.
Beat until blended.
Spread broken tortilla chips in bottom of casserole dish. Pour chili over chips.
Top with cheese, onion, olives and/or peppers.
Bake until warmed through.
Serve with sour cream and lettuce.
In skillet, brown the meat and onion; drain fat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Place in a greased 2-quart casserole.
Top with potatoes.
Combine soup and milk; pour over potatoes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Yields 2 to 3 servings.

Melt butter, then add onion and bell pepper. Cook on medium heat for 20 minutes. Add Ro-Tel tomatoes and cream of mushroom soup. Bring to a boil. Lower fire to medium heat and let cook for 20 minutes. Add crawfish and cook for 15 minutes or until crawfish is tender. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Yields 6 or 7 loaves.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Combine first 4 ingredients in large bowl; dissolve and carefully add beaten eggs.
Check temperature of mixture; if warm (around 100°), then add yeast, 1/4 cup warm water and sugar which have been combined.
Beat in half the flour (whole wheat or white). Work in remainder of flour.
Turn out on board floured with white flour.
Knead at least 10 minutes (board side will be "blistered" when kneaded enough).
Let rise to almost double; bake.
Combine beef, onion, bread, 1/2 cup of the water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper and nutmeg in large bowl; mix well.
Shape into 4 patties.
Cook patties in hot oil in large skillet until browned. Stir in gravy and 1/4 cup of water.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until cooked through.
Saute onion and mushrooms; add soup, cheese and broccoli in a casserole dish.
Top mixture with crumbled toast and sprinkle with butter.
Cook at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a skillet, cook ground beef and onions until beef is browned and onion is tender; drain.
In a greased 9 x 13-inch dish, spread refried beans; sprinkle beef mixture over beans.
Add layers of olives (reserving some for garnish), green chilies and cheese.
Spread taco sauce over all.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Separate yolks from whites.
Beat whites until light; add salt and beat until stiff and dry.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored; add milk and pepper.
Fold egg whites and baking powder into the yolks.
Melt butter in frying pan; pour in egg mixture and heat slowly until omelet has set.
Put in a 325° oven for 30 minutes, or until omelet browns on top.
Serve immediately with Spanish sauce.
Yield:
5 servings.
Pull each biscuit out to about 6-inches long.
Dip in melted butter and roll in mixture of nuts, cinnamon and sugar.
Bake in 425° oven for 8 to 10 minutes.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix dry ingredients and add margarine.
Blend well.
Add eggs and mix well.
Spread all but one cup in the pan.
Use a wet spoon and push in place.
Place apples in rows on the dough, not too many (makes the dough soggy). Sprinkle with 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon.
Form the last dough and rub between hands over the apples.
Bake at 350° until the apples are soft, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Cream butter, sugar, egg and vanilla until light and fluffy. Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt; add alternately with milk to creamed mixture.
Stir in 1/2 cup peanut butter pieces. Drop by teaspoon, 2 inches apart, onto lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 7 to 9 minutes, or until set, but not dry.
Cool slightly.
Remove from cookie sheet onto wire rack.

Cook rice. Combine cooked rice with milk, salt, sugar, eggs, vanilla and pineapple. Pour into 1 1/2 quart baking dish. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Cover with foil. Place on bottom of oven, watch so it doesn't burn. Cook about 30 minutes at 350 degrees or until done.
In a food processor, smoothly puree fish, adding eggs one at a time.
Pour in cream with motor running.
(If using a blender, smoothly puree fish and eggs; scrape container sides.
Add cream with motor running.)
If making ahead, cover and chill up to 3 hours.
Cut chicken up your way.
Salt and pepper all pieces.
Mix together eggs, mustard and milk.
Dust chicken in salt, pepper and flour mixture, then put into egg mixture, then roll in flour mixture.
In a heavy iron skillet, pour about 1 to 1 1/2 inches of oil.
Heat to 325° to 350°.
Fry a few pieces at a time until golden brown, about 7 to 10 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl with mixer at medium speed, cream butter and both sugars. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until light and fluffy.
Add shortening, vanilla and lemon peel.
Beat until well mixed.
Blend sugar and oil well with electric mixer.
*Beat in eggs, one at a time and continue beating until light.
Add pumpkin; blend.
Sift flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and salt into creamed mixture.
Beat at low speed until blended.
Pour batter into 4 greased 6 x 3 1/2 x 2-inch loaf pans or 2 greased 9 x 5 x 2 3/4-inch loaf pans.
Bake in a moderate oven (350°) for 1 hour or until lightly browned.
When done, leave in pans for 10 minutes on wire rack.
Remove from pans and cool completely on wire rack.
Sprinkle confectioners sugar.
Wash and dry lettuce and tear into bite-size pieces.
Cut papaya and avocado into small chunks and add to lettuce.
Cut vegetables into small pieces.
Mix dressing mix, mayonnaise and milk; pour over vegetables, coating all pieces. Store in refrigerator.
Mix
oil
and
sugar; add eggs.
Sift flour, cloves and cinnamon;
add
alternately
with
plums.
Add nuts; mix well. Bake
at 300° in lightly greased Bundt pan.
Cake is done when toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Very moist and tasty!
In a small bowl, mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup milk.

In medium size saucepan, over moderate heat, heat remaining 1 1/2 cup milk. When milk is just under boiling, add peanut butter, honey and salt. Mix thoroughly, then stir in cornstarch mixture and continue cooking about 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Pour about 1/2 cup of the hot mixture into beaten egg then return this mixture to the saucepan and cook 1 minute longer.
Remove pan from heat, add vanilla and heat about 1 minute.
Cool.
Pour into individual dessert dishes, cover and refrigerate several hours before serving. Yield:
4 servings.
Toss potatoes and green beans together.
Combine vinegar, onion, salt, sugar and dill.
Pour over potatoes and toss to coat evenly.
Cover and chill to blend flavors.
Add chopped eggs, sour cream and pimento and toss lightly.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix thoroughly 1/4 cup soup, beef, bread crumbs, egg, onion, salt and 1/8 teaspoon each:
pepper, sage and thyme.
Shape firmly into 6 mini meat loaves in a skillet.
Brown loaves in shortening.
Pour off fat.
Stir in remaining soup and seasoning and water.
Cover; cook over low heat 20 minutes or until done. Stir occasionally.
Serves 6.

Soak whole cucumbers in salt brine in crock (1 1/4 cups salt and cold water to cover). Let stand 3 days. On days 4 to 6, rinse daily with clear water. On the seventh day, cut in very thin slices and boil in a solution of 5 cups water, 3 tablespoons alum and 2 1/2 cups vinegar. Drain and cover with hot spiced vinegar made as follows: 3 pints vinegar and 7 pounds sugar and tie cinnamon and cloves in cheesecloth bag. Drop in solution. On days 8 to 10, reheat vinegar and pour over pickles. On eleventh day, seal in jars, covering with hot spiced vinegar. Makes 10 to 12 pints.
Grease a large Bundt pan (cake pan).
Layer frozen rolls in pan. Mix cinnamon with sugar and pour over rolls.
Layer one at a time chopped nuts, brown sugar and pudding mix.
Slice margarine and place around the rolls.
Cover pan with cloth and set in warm draft free place overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Invert pan over serving dish and let stand a minute so syrup will cover cake.
Decorate with cherries on top if desired.
Best served while warm.
Preheat oven at 400°.
Beat egg; stir in milk and oil.
Add rest of ingredients.
(Batter will be lumpy.)
Fill 12 muffin cups about 3/4 full.
Bake until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Combine sugar and water.
Boil to soft ball stage (236°); pour slowly, beating constantly, onto egg whites.
Add flavoring. Continue beating until icing holds its shape when dropped from spoon.

recipes.t: Quick-Haluski With Cabbage And Low-Fat Cottage Cheese
d: Chop cabbage; boil until tender.
Boil shells as per directions on box and drain.
Melt oleo; drain cabbage and add to oleo.
Combine shells
with cabbage, then add 1 carton of low-fat cottage cheese.
May be topped with dry or chopped fresh dill.
Mix all ingredients together.
Stir in mayonnaise; salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.t: Jumbo Shrimp In Spicy Wine Sauce
d: In a frying
pan,
saute
the shrimp in olive oil for 1 minute,
sprinkle
with
jalapeno
and red pepper flakes.
Add lemon juice
and
wine
to pan
and cook shrimp, covered over medium heat
for
more
minutes or until shrimp turns pink. Remove shrimp
to a serving bowl.
Strain the sauce and reduce it over
high heat
to make 1/2 cup. Pour sauce over shrimp. May be served hot or cold.
Makes 6 servings.

Preheat oven to 350 F. Mix dressing and chiles in a blender until smooth. Transfer to a small bowl, chill. Combine flour and taco mix in a shallow dish, mix well. Stir in oil until mixed well. If using wings remove tips first. Coat chicken with mixture on all sides. Place on slightly greased cookie pan. Bake for 15 minutes, turn over and bake an additional 15 minutes, or until chicken is tender. Mix parsley in with ranch dressing. Use dressing as a dipping sauce.
Cook pineapple, sugar and salt.
Boil 10 minutes.
Add to Jell-O and refrigerate until at least soupy.
Fold in cheese and whipped cream.
Refrigerate.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut in margarine. Beat eggs and milk together, then add date crystals to soften. Stir egg mixture into flour mixture; blend well.
Turn dough onto lightly floured board and pat to 3/4-inch thick.
Cut into 12 scones; place on greased baking sheet.
Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.

Prepare rice as directed on package. In a large skillet, saute mushrooms, green peppers, onions and shrimp. Shrimp will turn pink. Add soup to the rice and stir. Add shrimp mixture to rice and soup. Stir and transfer to a well-greased 2-quart baking dish. Sprinkle with stuffing mix. Bake at 350° uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes or until heated through. Serves 6.
Pour oil into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Spread on bottom of pan. Put cake mix, eggs and water into pan.
Stir until blended, about 2 minutes.
Spoon pie filling into batter to create a marble effect.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
When cool, sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Brown hamburger and onions in oil.
Add potatoes, carrots, seasonings, and water; simmer gently 20 minutes or until vegetables are soft.
Pour into a deep casserole and cover with short biscuit crust (according to package) and bake until crust is brown (about 25 minutes) in hot oven at 400°.
My mom usually makes this as a two crust pie instead of using biscuit dough.

Cut cake in half. Tear into small pieces and spread on bottom of glass or metal dish. Mix Dream Whip as directed. Add powdered sugar and cream cheese to Dream Whip. Mix well. Spread over broken pieces of cake. Tear other half of cake and place on top of that. Mix strawberries in glaze and spread over cake. Cool in refrigerator.
Heat oven to 350°; grease and flour 3 round pans, 9 x 1 1/2-inch.
Mix flour, sugar, baking soda, salt and cinnamon in a large bowl; add oil and eggs.
Stir until all dry ingredients are moistened (do not beat).
Stir in bananas, pecans, vanilla and pineapple.
Divide batter evenly among pans.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes; remove from pans.
Cool completely on wire rack. Fill layers and frost side and top of cakes with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup pecans on top of cake.
Refrigerate any remaining cake.
Cream the sugar and butter.
Add eggs, flour, cornstarch and vanilla.
Mix until well blended and smooth. Add cream.
Make small balls about 1 inch in diameter, then roll about 9 inches long and twist into a figure eight.
Grease cookie sheet lightly and sprinkle with flour before putting roskette dough on the sheet.
Bake at 350° in preheated oven for about 20 minutes. While still warm, carefully remove from cookie sheet to cool. Makes about 5 dozen.
Mix thoroughly graham cracker crumbs, sugar and oleo.
Mix cream cheese with sugar and eggs.
Put graham cracker mix in loaf pan and spread with mixture.
Bake 15 minutes at about 350°. Cool.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten eggs and beat well. Add dry ingredients, beating well.
Add oatmeal, vanilla and nuts. Shape in rolls and wrap in waxed paper.
Place in freezer and bake as needed.
Slice 1/4 inch thick.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for 10 minutes.
Yields 5 dozen.
Wash and remove outer skin from broccoli and cut into small pieces.
Mix sugar, cornstarch, oyster juice, chicken broth and ginger (a jar works great!).
Place broccoli pieces in pan with approximately 1/4 cup of water.
Cover and steam approximately 3 to 4 minutes until broccoli is tender, not too done!
Drain any excess water; toss in ginger and stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add sauce; stir again until broccoli is coated and remove to warm plate.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cream together shortening, sugar, vanilla and flavoring.
Add egg.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Add to first mixture and blend well.
Spread half in a buttered 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Cover with layer of jam or jelly.
Pat rest of dough on top.
Bake 25 minutes.
Cool.
Cut in bars.
Makes about 20.
In a large skillet, cook together beef, peppers and onions, stirring with a fork to break up meat, until meat is browned and vegetables are tender.
Drain off excess drippings.
In a small bowl, mix together remaining ingredients, except buns.
Add to beef mixture in pan.
Mix well; cook over low heat for 50 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spoon on buns.
Serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 475°.
Mix flour and salt.
Pour Wesson oil and milk into a measuring cup (don't stir).
Add all at once to flour.
Stir until mixed.
Press into balls.
Smooth and flatten slightly.
Roll between 2 sheets of waxed paper.
Press into pie pans.

recipes.t: Rice With Lamb Sauce(Riz Bi Yahkna)
d: In saucepan, brown meat and onion in oil.
Add tomato sauce and seasoning.
Let cook over med. heat till meat is cooked through and sauce thickens a bit. Meanwhile in another saucepan, melt butter and add rosemarino.
Stir constantly till golden brown.
Add rice and water to cover all.
Cover and slowly boil till water is absorbed and rice is cooked.
In a frying pan, brown onion in oleo.
When rice is cooked, add onion mixture to rice. Serve sauce over rice.
Pour 3/4 cup of the chocolate sauce into chocolate crumb crust, spreading lightly to cover bottom and sides of crust. Refrigerate until set.
Fill crust with ice cream.
Freeze until firm, about 2 hours.
Let stand at room temperature about 10 minutes before ready to serve.
Top with remaining 1/4 cup chocolate sauce.
Put concentrate, rum (use O.J. can for measure) and vanilla in a large container, an old water jug works well.
Shake well until ingredients are mixed.
Place in the freezer until it becomes slushy.
Once slushy, add ice and shake again until mixed. Slowly add the cream soda.
Agitate the container a few times to mix. Do not shake hard.
Dissolve jello in boiling water; add juice, salt and rind. Chill until slightly thickened.
Whip Milnot until very stiff; gradually beat in sugar, then jello mixture.
Line bottom of 8 x 12-inch dish with vanilla crumbs.
Pour mixture over crumbs. Sprinkle with remaining crumbs.
Chill.

Slice eggplant, onion and tomatoes into very thin slices. Arrange in layers in greased casserole: eggplant, onion and tomatoes (in that order), seasoning lightly between layers. Combine lemon juice and oil; drizzle on top.
The dressing will penetrate, even though it appears scant.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for about 50 minutes, basting occasionally with juices that form in the dish.
Leftovers freeze well.
Soften in a 1-qt. saucepan the gelatin in cold water.
Stir in sugar, cocoa and salt.
Stir over medium heat until gelatin and sugar dissolve completely, about 5 minutes.
Don't boil.
Remove from heat.
Stir in 1 c. Pet milk.
Chill in small bowl until firm.
Beat in with mixture at low speed until mixture is broken up.
Add 2/3 cup Pet milk and the vanilla.
Beat at high speed until mixture fills bowl.
Let stand a few minutes or until mixture mounds when dropped from spoon.
Heap into a graham cracker crust.
Shave a Hershey bar over the top.
Chill.
Cut very fine as for relish the cukes, peeled and with seeds removed.
Add 1/4 cup of salt and let stand overnight.
Drain in morning and add onions, chopped fine, vinegar, sugar, flour, turmeric, dry mustard, mustard and celery seed.
Cook 1 hour and put in hot jars.
Mix peanut butter and maple syrup.
Add Rice Krispies.
Put half mixture in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread softened ice cream on top of mixture.
Put rest of Krispies mixture on top.
Freeze.
Enjoy!
Preheat oven to 425°.
Fry sausage in heavy medium skillet over medium heat until cooked through, turning occasionally. Drain.
Dice sausage.
Dust one side of pie crust with 1 teaspoon of flour.
Gently transfer crust into pan.
Arrange half of Mozzarella over bottom of crust.
Spread 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce over Mozzarella.
Sprinkle half of Jack cheese atop sauce. Drizzle 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce over cheese.
Repeat layering with remaining Mozzarella, 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce, remaining Jack cheese, pepperoni and sausage.
Sprinkle with olives and drizzle with remaining 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce.
Top with remaining pie crust.
Pinch edges of crust together to seal.
Crimp edges to make decorative border.
Bake until golden brown, about 40 minutes.
Let pie stand 30 minutes before serving.
Sift flour and measure out 3 cups.
Scald milk in small saucepan.
Remove from heat.
Stir in sugar, salt and shortening. Cool until lukewarm.
Pour water into bowl; sprinkle yeast in and stir until dissolved.

Add lukewarm mixture and eggs; mix well. Add flour 1/2 cup at a time, until mixture is a soft pliable ball. Sprinkle remaining flour on board and knead mixture until firm. Place in greased bowl and cover with dish towel.
Keep in a warm place and let rise until double in bulk.
Put back on floured board and knead.
Make 3 balls of dough the same size.
Add fruits and nuts at this point.
Make balls into long cones.
Place side by side and braid as hair.
Place in a greased bread pan.
Let rise again for approximately 1 hour.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes. Make a glaze of milk and powdered sugar; drizzle over coffee cake while still warm.
Mix cream cheese, grated onion, Worcestershire sauce, mayonnaise, lemon juice and garlic salt well.
Spread on bottom of serving dish.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
In small bowl, mix chili sauce, ketchup, horseradish sauce and lemon juice.
Mix well.
Add to chilled dish.
Cover with backfin crabmeat and chill at least 1/2 hour.
Wash the kumquats in warm water; drain and dry.
Gently prick each kumquat with a skewer in 2 or 3 places.
Combine the water and sugar in a saucepan (not aluminum).
Bring to a boil and add the kumquats.
Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, or until syrup is thick and clear.
Stir in the ginger and lime juice.
Pack in sterile jars and seal.
Makes about 3 pints.

recipes.t: Mom'S Best Pecan Pie(Ethel Greenwood Chadwick)
d: Cream butter, sugar and flour.
Add eggs.
Add syrup, salt, vanilla and nuts. Bake in 9-inch pie shell for 50 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Season flour with salt, pepper, garlic powder and parsley. Coat chicken with flour mixture and brown evenly in oil.
Mix soup and milk and pour over chicken. Top with onion slices and thyme. Simmer 30 minutes, basting often.

Combine cheese and butter. Mix well. Add flour and peppers. Roll 1/4-inch thick on lightly floured board, then cut into rounds. Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Brush with egg white and top with pecan half. Bake at 425° until light brown (10 to 15 minutes).
Do not lift lid.
Do not stir until done!
Cook in a crock-pot for approximately 2 hours on high, until cheese and margarine melts.
Switch to low for 1 1/2 hours.
Place cornflakes in a large mixing bowl and set aside.
In a large saucepan combine corn syrup, brown sugar and sugar.
Bring to a boil, stirring often.
Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter and peanuts; mix well.
Pour over cornflakes.
Blend. Spread evenly in a well oiled 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle chocolate chips evenly over surface.
Bake 10 minutes at 250°.
Remove and smooth over top.
Cool and cut in 1-inch squares.
Cook beans in boiling salt water until tender; drain.
Heat olive oil in large skillet.
Add onions, parsley, garlic, ham and bacon; cook until ham and bacon are done.
Add wine, nutmeg and salt.
Add beans and small amount of water, if necessary.
Cover; simmer until heated through.
Coarse black pepper sprinkled on top can be added.
Makes 6 servings.
Cut off 2 large sheets of foil.
Lay them like a cross.
Onto foil slice potatoes, carrots and onion.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and margarine.
Fold foil to seal pouch securely.
Grill until done, 55 to 60 minutes.
Open pouch and sprinkle cheese over vegetables.
Close pouch; return to grill until cheese melts, about 1 minute.
Serves 6.
Melt fat in deep heavy pan; add chopped onions and diced jalapenos and cook over low heat until done, but not browned.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, about 10 minutes.
Drain liquid from beans into small bowl and save.
Add beans, soup, chili powder and salt to beef in pan.
Stir well.
Cover pan and let chili cook slowly over low heat for about 30 minutes.
If chili gets too dry, add desired amount of bean liquid.
Can be made ahead of time and reheated.
It even tastes better the next day.
Use a 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Line pan with crushed pineapple. Add berries.
Pour dry cake mix on that.
Pour butter next and last, nuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Slice eggplant 1/2-inch thick after removing skin.
Dice to make 5 cups.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in skillet and saute the eggplant slowly for 5 minutes.
Place in casserole with alternate layers of sliced onions, diced tomatoes and cheese (saving 1/4 cup for to).
Season each layer.
Top with crumb which have been mixed with remaining cheese and dot with remaining butter.
Bake in oven at 375° until vegetables are tender and surface nicely browned, about 35 to 40 minutes.
Makes 5 generous servings.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add milk and mix.
Add pecans and mix until very stiff.
Roll out into balls about 1 inch or less in diameter.
Place in waxed paper and cover.
Let sit for 2 hours or overnight in refrigerator.
Put first 2 ingredients in microwave on High for 2 minutes. Stir in vanilla (and nuts if desired) and pour into greased pan.
Quarter oranges and seed.
Leave peeling on oranges.
Chop or grind cranberries, oranges and pecans.
Add sugar and blend. Refrigerate in covered bowl for at least 4 hours before serving. Can be frozen.
Serves 6 to 8.
Great for the holidays.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In saucepan, brown ground beef.
Drain fat.
Add canned items.
Let simmer 10 minutes.
Pour into baking dish.
Top with cheese.
Bake until cheese melts.
Put well drained, hot squash in large mixing bowl.
Add egg, margarine, mayonnaise, sugar, half of cheese and half of cracker crumbs.
Season with cayenne pepper, salt, pepper and herbs (oregano is especially good in this dish).
Mix all ingredients well.
Put into buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole and top with remaining cheese and crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Crookneck squash or a mixture of crookneck and zucchini may be used.
Cook noodles to desired doneness as directed on package; drain.
Heat oven to 325°.
Lightly grease 2-quart casserole.
In large bowl, combine cream cheese and margarine; blend well.
Add sour cream, cottage cheese, salt, sugar and eggs.
Stir in noodles.
Pour into prepared casserole.
Bake at 325° for 60 to 75 minutes or until set.
Serve warm.
Makes 12 (1/2 cup) servings.
Combine first 5 ingredients in large bowl.
Prepare 4 servings mashed potatoes (omit butter).
Fold in mayonnaise.
Add egg yolks, one at a time.
Beat until fluffy.
Stir into vegetable mixture.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold in.
Pour into greased 2 quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until knife comes out clean.
Serve at once.
Cook noodles and drain.
Cook beef, onion, celery, green peppers, salt and pepper.
Spoon off fat or drain on paper towels. Place noodles in casserole dish; toss with butter.
Stir in meat mixture with cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix salsa and eggs together.
Combine cheeses.
Put half of cheese mixture in bottom of 9 x 9-inch pan.
Pour egg mixture over cheese.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350°. Cut in squares and serve with Town House crackers.
Combine everything but the maraschino cherry in a shaker and shake until well combined.
Pour in a tall glass and add the cherry.
Lightly sprinkle pork chops with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown pork chops on both sides. Reduce heat.
Drain tomatoes and add liquid to pork chops. Coarsely chop tomatoes and add to pork chops; stir in rice.
Place a green pepper ring on each chop.
Cover and simmer 40 to 45 minutes or until chops are tender.
Yield: 4 servings.

Place gelatin and 1/2 cup cold water in bowl; let stand while you put sugar, salt and 1/2 cup cold water in deep stew kettle. Boil to soft ball (235°). Pour gelatin mixture into the hot syrup. Beat it and beat it and beat it. Grease flat pan well on bottom and sides. Powder with powdered sugar and cornstarch. Pour mixture into pan and dust top; cool. Cut into squares and dust bowl on all sides.

Season pork roast with seasoned salt and black pepper. Heat oil in Dutch oven. Dredge the roast in flour and brown on all sides in oil. Heat soups and water together in saucepan. Add onion and garlic. Drain fat from pork. Pour soup mixture over pork roast in the Dutch oven. Cover. Place in a 325° to 350° oven. Bake until well done.
In a large saucepan, melt butter or margarine.
Add flour, salt and pepper.
Stir until smooth and bubbly.
Add milk. Continue stirring until mixture thickens and boils.
Add eggs and beef.
Stir and simmer until hot.
Serve over potato or rice.
Bring pineapple and juice to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Stir in Jell-O until dissolved.
Let cool.
Take out of refrigerator and add the buttermilk and Cool Whip.
Fold in until lumps disappear.
Then add the nuts.
Pour in an 8-inch square dish. Cool at least 4 hours.
Cook pasta. Drain. Mix dressing as instructed on the back of the package. Drain mushrooms and olives. Mix all ingredients together. Chill.

Heat sugar and Karo syrup until sugar melts. Add peanut butter to sugar and Karo. In large bowl, add mixture to the 6 cups of Rice Krispies and mix well. Butter bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan. Pour Rice Krispie mixture into pan and press evenly.
In quart punch bowl or large glass salad bowl, combine fruit juices and sugar.
Pour over ice and stir in gingerale.
Serve with an ice cube or crushed ice in each glass.

In a mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Spread onto bottom of crust. Sprinkle with chopped pecans. In another bowl, combine pudding mixes. Add milk and vanilla. Beat on low speed for 2 minutes. Spoon over the pecans. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Top with whipped cream and pecan halves.
Mix cereal with margarine.
Beat sugar into eggs; add cereal mixture and remaining ingredients, blending well.
Pour into 1-quart baking dish; place in pan of hot water.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Stir thoroughly.
Bake 20 minutes longer, or until knife inserted 1-inch from center comes out clean.
Serve warm or cool with whipped cream.
In a large pan, break up lettuce in bite size pieces.
Spread evenly.
Sprinkle celery all over.
Sprinkle eggs all over, then sprinkle peas all over.
Sprinkle onions all over and pepper. Crumble bacon and sprinkle all over.
Mix mayonnaise and sugar and spread like frosting.
Sprinkle cheese all over.
Refrigerate 8 to 12 hours or overnight, covered.
Mix cheese, mayonnaise, onion and pecans and shape into ball. Roll in crumbled bacon.
Serve with crackers.
Wash fruit; score peel into quarters.
Remove sections of peel with fingers, leaving fruit whole.
Sliver peel as directed to yield 1 cup; reserve.
Rinse peeled fruit in cold water and gently scrape off excess white membrane with a small knife.
Carefully remove center white core and slightly separate sections at one end to resemble "petals"; set aside in deep medium bowl.
Pour boiling water over spices and bay leaf; steep 5 minutes and strain liquid into saucepan.
Add slivered peel, sugars and tangerine juice; bring to a boil, stirring, until sugar is dissolved.
Boil briskly for 10 minutes until syrupy; immediately pour syrup over tangerines and baste for several minutes.
Refrigerate several hours, preferably overnight, until thoroughly chilled, basting several times.
Serve on individual dessert plates with some of the syrup and peel; sprinkle tops with coconut.
Combine buttermilk and sweet milk; add sugar, eggs and margarine together.
Slowly pour in cake mix.
Blend and pour into Bundt pan that has been greased and floured.
Cook at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Stir together flour, baking powder, cinnamon and ginger. Combine egg, applesauce, honey, oil and juice.
Add to flour mixture.
Stir just until moistened.
Batter should be lumpy. Fold in pecans and raisins.
Fill 12 muffin cups 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cook macaroni; add peas during last minutes and drain thoroughly.
Mix tuna and mayonnaise into macaroni.
Serve on a bed of lettuce.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cut potatoes up like fries.
Add salt and pepper and cut up onion.
Cook potatoes and onion in Crisco until done.
Add cream-style corn.
Cook about 5 minutes.
Add Cheddar cheese, then cover.
When cheese melts, it's ready to serve.
Pound chicken breasts until flat; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle each with 1/2 teaspoon parsley, 1 1/2 teaspoons butter and 1 teaspoon cheese.
Roll up and secure with toothpicks. Dip rolls in milk and roll on coating mix.
Place in a greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes; drain. Combine soup and broth.
Pour over chicken; bake 30 minutes. Yield:
8 servings.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix beans, onion and pepper sauce; set aside.
Mix baking mix and sour cream until soft dough forms; beat 20 strokes.
Gently smooth dough into ball on floured board. Knead 20 times.
Roll dough 1/2 inch thick.
Cut with floured 2-inch cutter.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press an indentation about 1 1/4 inches in diameter in center of each round with floured hands.
Fill each with generous teaspoonful of bean mixture.
Spread within indentation.
Top with chilies and cheese. Bake until brown, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, cocoa, soda and salt in a large bowl. Add Wesson oil,
vinegar and water.
Mix real good.
Pour into greased 9 x 12-inch
baking
pan.
Bake in oven at 350° for 45 minutes.
Quarter and boil chicken with salt, pepper and onion and garlic powders until done.
Remove chicken.
Let cool; strain broth.
Add vegetables (celery, carrots and onion).
Let cook until real tender.
Debone chicken, cut into bite-size pieces. Add cream of chicken soup to vegetables and let dissolve.
Add chicken and cooked noodles.
Let simmer for 10 minutes, then serve.
Boil chicken until tender.
Remove bones and skin.
Place chicken in casserole.
Pour melted butter over chicken.
Mix flour and milk.
Pour over chicken.
Mix the soup and broth together. Pour over the other mixture.
Cook in 350° oven until thickened.
Chop pepperoni.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
In large bowl, measure flour, corn meal, sugar, baking powder and salt.
With wire whisk, beat eggs, milk, oil and sour cream until smooth.
Stir egg mixture into flour mixture.
Stir in pepperoni, cheese, onion and green chilies.
Spoon batter into pan. Bake for 45 minutes, or until golden brown and toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Makes 14 servings.
Saute garlic, crushed, in olive oil.
Add chopped tomatoes. Stir in Brie; pour bow ties into tomato mixture.
Add pine nuts, basil, salt and pepper.
Combine onion, Rot-tel tomatoes, soup (no water added), chicken, Velveeta (cubed) and Doritos (crushed).
Mix well and pour into casserole dish.
Top with grated Cheddar cheese. Microwave 5 to 6 minutes or until hot and cheese is melted.
Drain fruit cocktail.
Save syrup and add enough water to the syrup to make 1 cup liquid.
Bring liquid to boil.
Dissolve gelatin in hot liquid; stir until dissolved.
Add ginger ale. Refrigerate until slightly thick; fold in fruit and marshmallows. Pour into mold.
Chill until firm.
Combine soup and milk until well blended.
Add cheese, pimento, mushrooms and salt.
Blend well.
Add potatoes and mix well.
Pour into greased casserole dish.
Bake at 375° for 1 1/2 hours until potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork.
Soak salt cod in water overnight.
Combine the flour and egg in a bowl.
Stir in enough water to make a thick paste and reserve.
Remove any skin and small bones from the fish and chop very fine.
Add the scallions, garlic, parsley, thyme, allspice, salt and pepper.
Stir in reserved flour paste until thoroughly combined.
Heat enough oil in a heavy pan to deep fry the fritters.
Place 2 tablespoons of the mixture in the pan at a time. Allow the fritters to cook until well browned.
Remove fritters from the oil and allow to drain on paper towels.
Makes 25 fritters.

recipes.t: My Favorite Winter Salad(Makes 8 Or 10 Servings)
d: Combine gelatin and cranberry sauce over medium heat; stir until almost boiling and gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in nuts, mandarin oranges, undrained pineapple and ginger ale.
(I add 1/3 pint cottage cheese.)
When fizzing stops, pour mixture into a mold or glass dish.
Allow to chill and set.
Combine the shortening and frosting mixture thoroughly.
Blend in one egg at a time; beat for 1 minute.
Sift together the flour, soda and salt; add to the creamed mixture alternately with the milk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients.
Blend thoroughly after each addition.
Pour into 2 well-greased and lightly floured 9-inch round cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes (9 x 13-inch pan for 45 to 55 minutes).
Cool; frost with remaining Chocolate Frosting.
Serves 12.
Saute chicken in oil and butter until brown.
Add cream of chicken soup and chicken broth.
Stir and simmer for 15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked.
Add broccoli.
Cook ziti as directed. Drain; mix with chicken and broccoli.
Mix eggs, oil and apricot nectar in bowl.
Add cake mix and beat 4 to 5 minutes on medium speed.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan or Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes. While cake is baking, melt together over heat sugar, butter and rum.
As soon as cake is done, pour rum mixture all over top, slowly, while still in pan, allowing it to seep in.
Let cool several hours before removing from pan.
Serve plain or as shortcake.

recipes.t: Fried Peppers Salad-Romania(Salata De Ardei Prajiti)
d: Wash peppers, take out cores and cut into thin strips. Chop onions and fry in oil until soft. Mash up tomatoes until pasty. Add tomatoes, salt (to taste) and peppers into frying pan. Fry at slow heat until most of the liquid is absorbed. Serve cold.
Saute onion and garlic in olive oil.
Wash and cut mushrooms and add to onion and garlic.
Add the chicken; brown chicken before mushrooms.
Then add mushrooms.
When mushrooms are practically cooked, add tomatoes and peppers.
Salt and pepper. Cook for about 1 hour.
Add extra basil.
Brown beef well in oil.
Add vegetables and simmer until meat is tender.
Add sunflower seeds to thicken and salt to taste. Serves 4.
Thread mushrooms on skewers.
Combine butter, dill and garlic salt; brush over mushrooms.
Grill over hot coals for 10 to 15 minutes, basting and turning every 5 minutes.
Yield: 4 servings.
Cut vegetables into bite size pieces.
Steam until crisp-tender.
Spread vegetables over boboli shell.
Sprinkle with oregano.
Arrange sliced tomato over vegetables.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Slice mushrooms on top.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Cool slightly.
Serve.
Saute the onions until tender in the butter.
Add 2 cups soft bread crumbs, the sugar and salt and pepper.

In a buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole dish, arrange alternating layers of tomatoes, then the bread crumb mixture, starting and ending with tomatoes. Combine 1/4 cup crumbs with 1 1/2 teaspoons melted butter and sprinkle over top of casserole.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Heat olive oil; add onions until semi-translucent.
Add beef. When beef is browned, add a jar of brown gravy and marinara.
Mix thoroughly while still heating.
Turn down to a simmer; add cream and white wine.
Add all to pasta and pour into a baking pan.
Put Mozzarella cheese on top; add seasonings.
Put in oven at 350° and bake for half an hour or until bubbly.
Enjoy!
Cook chicken until tender; remove from broth and cut into small pieces.
Add celery, onions, salt, pepper and garlic to broth. Cook until tender.
Add chicken and corn and cook about 1/2 hour. Thicken a little with flour and water.
Very good.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Coat pan with olive oil.
Return drained broccoli to pan and add other ingredients.
Cook a few minutes until cheese melts.
Cool.
Stretch and roll dough 16 x 5 inches.
Spread mixture to 1/2 inch of edge.
Fold over and pinch edges.
Put seam on bottom.
Put on greased pan.
Put 1-inch slit on top.
Brush top with egg and water (beat egg with 1 teaspoon water).
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Garnishes:
Additional cheese and sour cream and chopped cilantro.
Combine beef, milk, 1/3 can soup, dry onion soup mix, parsley flakes, thyme and nutmeg.
Place in a 12 x 9 x 2 1/2-inch baking dish.
Shape into a loaf. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done. Heat remaining soup and sour cream, stirring constantly.
Serve over meat loaf.
Serves 8.
Cut
warabi into 1-inch lengths.
I pile the stem ends, middle part
and tips
separately.
Bring water to boil; add salt.
Add warabi, stem end first, then middle part.
Bring to boil;
cook for about 1 minute, then add the tips.
As soon as tips
turn color,
drain in sieve and dunk in a large bowl of water.
Drain and dunk in water several times until the warabi is cooled.
(The trick here is to cool it immediately, or else the
warabi
will turn
brown
or black, although it is still edible.)
Drain
well. Toss
together
warabi
and
remaining ingredients.
Can be eaten right away.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Melt oleo; add onion and celery and saute gently several minutes.
Add rice and stir until well coated with oleo and deep golden color (but not brown).
Add consomme, water, salt and pepper.
Turn into 2-quart casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Fold in sliced ripe olives and cheese and return to oven for 5 minutes.
Serves 8.
Delicious served with steak.

Slice apples into rings. Place half the amount in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Dot with 1/4 cup of the butter. Combine the sugars and spices. Sprinkle half the amount over the apples. Repeat the process for the second layer. Bake at 350° for 55 minutes. Serves 8.
In a large pot, place hen; cover with water.
Add salt, pepper and whole onion.
Cook until tender.
When done, reserve liquid for broth to be used in dressing.
Break toast into small pieces; crumble cornbread.
Put celery and onions in saucepan.
Cover with water and cook until tender.
In large roasting pan, add toast and cornbread; pour in celery and onion mixture.
Stir in eggs, sage, salt, pepper and reserved hen broth.
Add more broth if needed for desired consistency.
Mix thoroughly.
Leave in roasting pan. Place hen on top of dressing.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for about 1 hour or until brown.
Serve with gravy of your choice.
Peel and quarter 2 kiwi fruit.
Place kiwi fruit and cherries in container of electric blender; blend on high speed until smooth.
Pour into a punch bowl.
Add club soda, ginger ale and orange juice.
Mix well.
Peel and slice remaining 1 kiwi fruit; garnish punch with kiwi fruit slices.
Spoon ice cream into punch. Serve immediately.
Makes about 25 (1/2-cup) servings.
Place 1/2 cup sauce in bottom of 2-quart oblong casserole dish.
Alternate layers of noodles, Ricotta cheese, spaghetti sauce, sausage, Parmesan cheese and salt.
Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, pumpkin and soda.
Mix in remaining ingredients; stir well.
Drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Yields 9 dozen.
In small bowl, soften unflavored gelatin in 1/2 cup of the cold water; set aside.
In small saucepan, bring milk to a boil. Remove from heat.
Add sugar immediately and stir to dissolve. Add sour cream, vanilla and softened gelatin mixture to the hot milk and beat until smooth and creamy.
Set mixture aside but do not refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Peel bananas and cut them lengthwise. In a small bowl, combine orange juice and sugar.
Pour over bananas.
In second bowl, mix bread crumbs, nutmeg and cinnamon. Sprinkle over bananas.
Bake 20 minutes.
Combine beans, tomatoes, potatoes, and water.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and stir in cumin, butter, salt and black pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 15 to 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Add more water, if needed. Serve with a sprinkling of grated cheese over top, if desired.
Saute onion and celery in butter for 5 minutes.
Add diced potatoes, water and salt.
Heat to boiling; cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Blend flour with 1/4 cup milk, then add 1 3/4 cups milk.
Stir into potato mixture.
Cook until thick.
Add tuna; heat and serve.
Mix the cream cheese and green onions. (This can be done a day in advance and placed in an airtight container in refrigerator for better flavor.)
Combine juices and water.
Just before serving, add soda. Serves 40 (1/2-cup) servings.
Melt almond bark in microwave on Low or Medium for 5 to 7 minutes.
In
a
large
bowl
combine
marshmallows,
Rice Krispies,
Capt'n
Crunch and peanuts.
Add melted almond bark and drop
by
spoon.
May add different cereals but if Capt'n Crunch is not
used
add a couple large spoonfuls of peanut butter for flavor.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Remove bacon and discard all but 2 tablespoons drippings.
Saute onions in drippings until tender. Crumble bacon; add with mushrooms to skillet and set aside. Meanwhile, combine beef, pork, cheese, pepper, garlic powder and steak sauce in a large bowl.
Shape into 16 patties.
Divide bacon mixture and place over 8 of the patties.
Place remaining patties on top and press edge lightly to seal.
Grill over medium coals until well done.
(Pork sausage in burgers requires thoroughly cooking).
Serve on buns with lettuce if desired.
Makes 8 servings.
Prepare chocolate pudding with 1 3/4 cups milk.
Pour into pie shell.
Prepare vanilla pudding with 1 3/4 cups milk.
Pour carefully over the chocolate layer.
Fold chocolate syrup into whipped topping and spread over vanilla layer.
Chill for 3 hours.
Brown meat in hot
oil,
add
flour, tomato and seasonings. Brown hominy and onion
in oil,
add
to meat mixture. Place in casserole, sprinkle
with cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Place chicken breasts in long baking dish in a single layer. Mix remaining ingredients and pour over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add cabbage, celery, green pepper, onion, salt and pepper.
Cover and cook vegetables over low heat 10 to 12 minutes, stirring mixture often.
Serve at once.
Mix first 4 ingredients together and use as a spread for the bread slices.
Put any kind of sliced sandwich meat and sliced cheese over the filling, adding a little mayonnaise between the meat and cheese and other slice of bread.
(A variety of meats, breads and cheeses in the same batch makes for a real surprise package!)
Fresh and moist and yummy!!
Mix first 5 ingredients and let set until slightly congealed. Chill large bowl and beaters.
Pour in evaporated milk and beat until it stands in peaks.
Combine with chilled and whipped Jell-O mixture.
In another bowl, combine chocolate wafer crumbs with melted butter and spread 1/2 of the mixture on the bottom of a 13 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Pour in the Jell-O mixture and spread remaining crumbs on top.
Chill overnight if possible.
In a nonstick skillet coated with cooking spray, saut garlic, onions, ham and peas 2 minutes or until soft.
Add white wine and simmer 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Whisk together next 5 ingredients and add to pea mixture.
Cook mixture over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes or until thickened.
Add 1/4 cup water and cooked pasta to skillet; cook 2 minutes or more to heat through.
Season with freshly ground black pepper and Parmesan cheese to taste. Makes 6 servings.
Cut unpared into 1/4 -inch-thick slices.
Place overlapping slices in a buttered oven-to-table, 13 x 9 inch baking dish.
Mix Margarine and Oil.
Brush slices with mixture.
Pour remaining over Potatoes.
Sprinkle with Garlic, Salt and Thyme.
Bake at 400 for 25 to 30 minutes or until Potatoes are done and browned at the edges.
Serve immediately.
Serves 4.
Brown beef and onions, drain.
Add all remaining ingredients, except coleslaw.
Stir and blend together.
Place coleslaw in bottom of a 2 qt casserole dish.
Spoon mixture over slaw.
Cover and bake at 400 degrees for 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease an 8-inch square pan. Combine flour and sugar, cut in margarine until mixture resembles fine meal.
Press into greased pan and bake 20 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Meanwhile, mix eggs, brown sugar and vanilla beating well.
Stir in soda, walnuts, raisins and coconut. Spoon over hot crust, spread evenly.
Return to oven; bake an additional 20 to 25 minutes or until top is set.
Cool, cut into bars and serve.
In saucepan, beat egg yolks slightly; add 1 cup sugar slowly until mixed and creamy.
Sift dry ingredients and add to sugar mixture.
Mix until all blends; add milk and vanilla gradually and cook on low heat until thick.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 1/4 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon cream of tartar.
Top pie with meringue and brown at 400°.
Brown ground beef and drain well.
Add chopped celery, green pepper, onions, carrots, tomato sauce and water.
Simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in cooked spaghetti, mushroom soup, oregano, salt and pepper; mix well.
Pour into casserole and top with cheese.
Bake in 300° oven for 30 minutes.
Brown beef and sausage until brown; drain grease.
Add cubed cheese; stir until melted with ground beef.
Add sausage and seasonings.
Spread onto bread slices.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir together flour & brown sugar; cut in cold butter until mixture is crumbly.
Stir in 1/2 cup peanut butter chips.
Press mixture on bottom of greased 12 x 9 baking pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Meanwhile combine condensed milk, egg and vanilla; stir in remaining chips and nuts.
Spread evenly over baked crust. Bake 35 minutes at 350°. Cool completely in pan.
Cut in squares.

Preheat oven to 325°. Grease bottom of 9 x 13 pan. In large bowl, mix the thawed whipped topping, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in nuts. Spread mixture into pan. Sprinkle chocolate chips on top. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until tooth pick comes out clean. Do not overbake. Cool and slice.
Lay beef slices on bottom of baking dish.
Wrap each piece of chicken with a slice of bacon.
Lay on top of beef slices.
Mix and blend well cream cheese, cream of chicken soup and sour cream. Pour over chicken.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Excellent served with rice.
Save liquid from Fri Chik.
Mix with other liquids.
Pour over grated Fri Chiks and bread crumbs.
Saute onions and celery in margarine.
Mix all together.
Bake in bread loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Soften yeast in warm water with 1 teaspoon sugar.
Stir in salt and 1/3 cup sugar; mix well.
Stir in yeast mixture; add well beaten egg to mixture.
Mix; add 3 cups of flour, stirring mixture until it is smooth elastic.
Add corn oil; mix.
Add remaining 3 cups flour; mix well.
Cover with wax paper; let rise until dough has doubled.
Knead dough in remaining flour; roll dough to 1/4 to 1/2-inch thick.
Cut to desired shapes; place in greased pan. Cover; let rise until double in size.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes in preheated oven at 400°.
Rub butter on top when rolls are light brown.
Makes about 3 dozen.

recipes.t: Marinated Artichoke Hearts With Pasta In A Creamy Sauce
d: Pour liquid from hearts into skillet.
Add oil, butter, onion and garlic; saute until soft.
Add hearts and basil and cook for five minutes (you may wish to cut hearts in half).
Take off heat and stir in remaining ingredients.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour onto 1/2 to 3/4 pound cooked pasta and mix completely.
Enjoy!
Mix rice, chicken, 2 beaten eggs, 1/2 can crushed tomato bits and 1/2 can cream of mushroom soup.
Mix ingredients well.
Place in greased molds (ovenproof).
Cover top with aluminum foil.
Place molds into larger pan and put 1 can water into larger pan.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Combine barbecue sauce, sugar and seasonings in a 1 1/2-quart bowl.
Cover.
Microwave on High for 2 1/2 minutes, until hot. Stir in wieners; cover.
Microwave 4 to 6 minutes, stirring once. When hot, serve with cocktail picks.
Makes about 1 quart.
Brown and crumble meat.
Add chopped onion and cook until onion is soft.
Tomatoes need to be cut up.
Add salt, pepper and 1/3 cup grated cheese.
Pour into casserole dish and sprinkle cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Grind ingredients together and let stand overnight in salt, then rinse good with cold water and drain.
Turn into large pan and add sugar, vinegar, turmeric and water.
Bring to a boil. Simmer for 3 minutes, then put in canning jars and seal.
Makes approximately 6 quarts.
Bake cake on greased and floured 10 x 15-inch sheet pan. Prepare vanilla pudding with milk.
Cool.
Cook crushed pineapple with 3/4 cup sugar and flour.
Mix butter, margarine and 1 cup sugar with pudding and beat until smooth.
Spread pudding on cake, then spread with pineapple and sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Wash the okra and drain well.
Place in skillet with 2 tablespoons of margarine and let it cook slowly, stirring frequently, until the sticky substance has disappeared.
Cut corn from cob. Put okra and corn in alternate layers in a greased casserole, sprinkling with salt and pepper as you go along.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt; stir in corn meal. Add eggs, milk and shortening; beat until just smooth.
Pour into greased pan.
Bake at 425° for 20 to 25 minutes.
I used the cornbread recipe in 1936-1943.
At that time, there was a grist mill across Highway 30.
The man delivered the meal.

Combine the rice, flour and milk. Heat butter in a 10-inch skillet. Add onions and cook until tender. Spread the rice mixture evenly in the skillet. Press it down firmly with a spatula. Cook over medium heat until bottom is golden brown. Turn out onto serving dish, brown side up. Serves 4.
Saute onions in margarine.
Remove onions from skillet.
Add meat to skillet.
Heat thoroughly.
Heat process cheese spread in saucepan over low heat.
Fill roll with meat and onions.
Top with process cheese spread.
Brownie Crust:
Stir together the brownie mix, butter and chopped pecans to form a crumb mixture.
Set aside 1 1/2 cups crumb mixture.
Put remaining mixture in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking pan to form crust. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cook chicken until done.
Remove bones from chicken.
Grind chicken.
Bring 2 cups milk to a boil.
Add flour, cold milk, salt and pepper to boiling milk.
Cook until it forms a sauce.
Pour over ground chicken.
If filling is a little thin, add crushed cracker crumbs to thicken.
Tear bread into stuffing like pieces.
Place in deep dish bowl.
Place applesauce on top of bread.
Place brown sugar on top and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Heat in microwave for 1 minute.
Pour milk over and serve or place back into microwave to heat milk also.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a 1 1/2 gallon container, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add lemon juice and next 3 ingredients, stirring until blended.
Cover and chill.
Pour mixture into a large punch bowl, gently stirring in chilled ginger-ale.
Yield - 1 1/2 gallons.
Cut rabbit into serving size pieces.
Combine wine, vinegar, onion and spices; bring to a boil and remove from heat.
Salt the rabbit meat liberally and allow to stand for 15 minutes.
Rinse, salt lightly and pour the cooled liquid over the meat.
Store in the refrigerator for 3 days.
Mix the marinade with an equal volume of beef broth and pour into a roaster.
Bake, covered at 325° until tender.
When half done, pour some of the sour cream over the rabbit and continue doing this at intervals until it is gone.
Brown the meat; drain off fat.
Add tomato sauce, garlic salt, pepper, basil and 1/2 cup water.
Cover; simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a 2-quart casserole, layer half each macaroni, cottage cheese, shredded cheese and meat sauce.
Repeat. Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cut eggs in half lengthwise and remove yolks.
Mash yolks, then stir in mayonnaise, yogurt and Parmesan cheese.
Add Worcestershire sauce, if desired.
Fill the egg halves with the yolk mixture.
Mix and brown ground beef, salt, pepper, garlic powder, cayenne pepper and onion in a large saucepan.
Add tomato juice and potatoes.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Add rice, turn off heat, cover and let stand 15 minutes.
If soup becomes too thick, you can add water or more tomato liquid.
Makes 6 servings.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 3/4 cup of the sugar, a little
at a
time,
beating
after each addition.
Put egg yolks in top of double boiler.
Beat until thick.
Add remaining 3/4 cup
of sugar, lemon juice and peel to the egg yolks. Cook over boiling
water until thick, stirring occasionally. Soften gelatin in the 1/4 cup of water and then add to the egg yolk-lemon mixture.
Cool.
Fold in egg white mixture, using a rubber spatula.
Put
half
of
the
angel
cake crumbs in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour half
of
the
sauce
over
cake.
Repeat layers. Let
stand
in
refrigerator
overnight.
Cut
into squares.
Top each with a dollop of whipped topping.
Cream butter and brown sugar; stir in flour.
It is crumbly. Press into a 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Heat Crisco oil in large skillet on medium heat.
Add potatoes, onions, green pepper and garlic.
Cook on medium heat, turning occasionally, until potatoes are tender.
Add broth, meat, salt, hot pepper sauce and pepper to taste.
Cook until meat is hot. Makes 8 servings.
Contains 230 calories, fat 9 g (81 cal or 35% of total calories), sat fat 2 g (9% of total calories), carb 15 g, protein 22 g, chol 60 mg and sodium 100 mg.

recipes.t: Creamed Diced Carrots With Green Pepper
d: Melt butter in a 2-quart saucepan over moderate heat.
Add onion and carrots; stir.
Cover, lower heat, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add green pepper, cover and cook for 2 minutes. Sprinkle in flour, stir, then add half and half, broth and seasonings.
Stir well.
Bring the mixture to simmer, stirring constantly, then cover and cook over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the carrots are done.
They should be slightly crunchy.
Cook onion in cooking oil until tender; blend in flour.
Add milk and stir while it thickens.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well and cool.
Shape into patties.
Roll in bread crumbs and fry in deep hot fat until done.
Makes 25 croquettes.
Spread one side of each cracker with pizza sauce.
Top each with a piece of cheese and a slice of pepperoni.
Arrange crackers on a paper towel lined plate.
Microwave at 50% (Medium) for 30 seconds to 1 1/2 minutes or until cheese melts, rotating dish 2 or 3 times during cooking.
Spread bottom of pie plate with cream cheese.
Add beans, spreading evenly over cream cheese.
Sprinkle with olives.
Spread salsa over mixture and top with Cheddar cheese.
Heat at 375° until Cheddar cheese has melted.
Serve warm with taco chips.
Bone chicken breasts if not previously boned.
Pound each half breast to about 1/4 inch thickness.
Combine chopped shrimp, margarine and green onion.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon shrimp mixture onto center of each breast.
Roll breast and skewer or secure with toothpick.
Heat 1 inch oil in skillet.
Make batter from flour, baking powder, salt and water.
Roll or dip each breast in batter.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown (about 15 minutes), turning frequently.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve quickly to retain crispiness.
Beat eggs and powdered sugar well.
Add almonds, walnuts, lemon extract, warm milk and flour which baking powder has been added to.
Bake in moderate oven (325°) for 45 minutes.
Decorate cake with whipped cream and fruit.
Mix the pork sausage, venison hamburger and egg.
Season with the chopped celery, onion, crushed sage and salt and pepper.
Put in 9-inch bread pan.
Cover with catsup.
Bake 1 hour at 325° to 350°.

recipes.t: No Bake Strawberry Or Blackberry Icebox Pie
d: Clean berries.
Set aside.
In bowl, mix condensed milk and lemon juice.
After well blended, add berries (strawberries sliced and blackberries whole).
Put in baked pie shell.
Pour whipped whip cream on top of pie.
Refrigerate.
Mix with fork the cake mix, oil and eggs.
This will form a ball like pizza dough.
Pat half of the mixture into a 9 x 13-inch cake pan, ungreased.
Melt in saucepan the butter, condensed milk and chocolate chips.
Put over cake mixture and then put rest of cake mixture on top.
Swirl with knife. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Rich, chewy and utterly delicious!
Dressing:
Shred the peel from the orange; peel and section orange over bowl to catch and reserve 1 teaspoon juice.
(Set aside sections.)
Combine peel, juice, yogurt, honey and poppy seed.
Cover and chill.
Cook beef, rice and onion until lightly browned.
Add spices, olives, tomato juice and boiling water.
Place in greased casserole.
Cover and bake in 300° oven for 1 hour.
Uncover, sprinkle with cheese and continue baking about 10 minutes, or until cheese melts.
Brown sausage; add celery, onion and green pepper.
Cook until tender in skillet.
Put into 3 cups of boiling water after skimming off grease.
Add noodle soup and rice.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until rice is cooked.
In soup pot, cook onions in butter very slowly over low heat until soft, but not browned.
Add flour; stir to blend.
Add chicken broth and liquid from oysters or mushrooms; simmer 5 minutes until thickened.
Add light cream and oysters or mushrooms; heat to simmer; do not boil.
Season with salt, pepper and mace (a favorite colonial seasoning, the yellow outer coating of nutmeg). Makes about 10 servings.
Mix vegetables together.
Dissolve salt in 8 cups of water and pour over vegetables.
Let stand in cool place overnight, then drain.
If too salty, rinse and drain again.
Tie spices in cheesecloth.
Add to vinegar and 1 cup water.
Let simmer 5 minutes.
Add sugar; stir until dissolved.
Add vegetables and simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring to a boil and pack boiling ingredients in hot jars and seal.
In a skillet, cook the onion in butter over moderately low heat, stirring, until softened; add zucchini.
Saute the mixture 3 to 5 minutes or until tender.
Stir tomatoes and herbs; cover for 1 to 2 minutes.
Cream butter, add sugars, then add egg and vanilla.
Sift together flour, soda, cinnamon, salt and baking powder and add to creamed mixture.
Last, add cornflakes, oats, coconut and nuts. Shape dough with hands into small balls and place about 2 inches apart on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes. Yields approximately 3 dozen cookies.
Fit 1 pie crust into 1 9-inch pie plate (according to package directions).
Do not bake.
Combine chicken and remaining ingredients.
Spoon into pie shell.
Moisten edges of pastry with water.
Place remaining crust on top.
Fold edges under and flute. Cut slits in top.
Bake at 400° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Soak mushrooms in warm water until soft, about 30 minutes; drain.
Rinse in warm water; drain.
Remove and discard stems; chop caps finely.
Mix mushrooms, pork, bamboo shoots, green onions, egg white, cornstarch, salt, 2 teaspoons soy sauce, 1/2 teaspoon sesame oil and the white pepper.
Cream butter and brown sugar; add eggs and vanilla.
Sift in dry ingredients.
Fold in raisins, drop by teaspoonful on baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Yields approximately 5 dozen.

recipes.t: Low-Fat Chocolate Eclairs(Only Fat From Frosting And Graham Crackers)
d: Mix contents of both boxes pudding with skim milk until thick. Prepare Dream Whip according to directions (use skim milk).
Fold Dream Whip into pudding.
Layer bottom of baking dish (9 x 13 x 2-inch) with graham crackers.
Brown onion and meat, drain.
Add meat mixture to soups, beans and sauce.
Bring mixture to boil.
Tear tortillas into strips and layer in casserole dish; then add meat mixture and strips of tortillas.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes at 400 degrees.
Cut Mozzarella into 1/4 to 1/3-inch thick slices.
In a shallow bowl, combine bread crumbs and parsley.
In second bowl, beat the eggs with small amount water and add some salt and pepper.
Place flour in third shallow bowl.
Dip the cheese slices into flour until completely covered.
Dip floured cheese into egg mixture, then in bread crumbs, then repeat the egg and bread crumbs until sides and edges are covered.
Heat olive oil in 2 large skillets on medium.
Saute cheese slices until crispy and golden brown (a few minutes on each side; watch carefully). Remove from heat and drain on paper towel.
Serve immediately.
Mix cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together. Add milk, eggs and shortening.
Mix together.
Add onion and let stand 5 minutes.
Fold in cheese, corn, green chili peppers and red peppers.
Spoon about 1/3 cup batter into greased and floured 2 1/2-inch muffin cups.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Makes 15 muffins.
Put zucchini or cucumbers in a bowl with green pepper and onion.
Mix with salt and celery seed.
Let stand at room temperature 1 hour.
Cut bacon into 1-inch pieces and fry in large skillet.
Drain off all but approximately 2 tablespoons of grease.
In a large jar mix sugar, vinegar, water and flour.
Shake vigorously until creamy.
Add to pan; add spinach.
Slice eggs and add to pan. Cook approximately 5 minutes.
Serve over mashed potatoes.
Melt chocolate chips in a double boiler.
Add peanut butter and mix well.
Crush peanuts fine and add with Rice Krispies to chocolate.
Mix well and put in the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix margarine, mayo, cheese and garlic salt.
Mashing with a fork, add crabmeat.
Spread on 12 English muffin halves.
Cut into quarters or smaller.
Dissolve jello in boiling water and add pineapple juice.
Chill until slighlty thickened, then beat until frothy.
Fold in pineapple.
Add cottage cheese, horseradish, whipped cream and nuts.
Chill in mold for at least two hours or overnight.
Unmold onto lettuce bed.
Fill center with pineapple chunks.
Cream butter and Crisco until fluffy, add sugar, then add eggs one at a time, beating well.
Add flavors; add milk and flour alternately beating well.
Bake time:
One hour and 15 minutes at 325°.
Cream
margarine
and
sugar
together;
add eggs, beat well. Add
cracker
crumbs, nuts and coconut.
Stir in baking powder, then add milk;
mix well.
Butter and flour 4 (9-inch) cake
pans; divide batter among them.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 40 minutes.
Remove to wire rack to cool.
Ice.
Grease and flour 9 or 10-inch spring-form pan.
Heat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine flour and 3/4 cup sugar.
Cut in butter until mixture resembles crumbs.
Reserve 1 cup of this mixture for topping.
To remaining mixture, add baking powder, soda, salt, sour cream, 1 egg and extract.
Blend well.
Spread batter over bottom and up sides (2 inches) of pan.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Blend in frozen orange juice. Fold in Cool Whip.
Fold in crushed pineapple and Mandarin oranges.
Fold in miniature marshmallows and coconut.
Chill until firm.
Dip chicken breasts in egg whites, then roll chicken breasts in crushed corn flakes.
Arrange in microwave dish.
Cover with Saran Wrap except for one corner.
Cook in microwave for 20 minutes.
Microwaves vary so check to see if chicken is done.
You may have to add some time.
Turn dish every 5 minutes during cooking.
Combine 1/4 cup corn syrup, brown sugar and butter in medium saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture begins to boil.
Remove from heat.
Add cereal, stirring until well coated.
Press in 9-inch pie pan to form crust.
Stir together peanut butter, fudge sauce and the 3 tablespoons corn syrup.
Spread half the peanut butter mixture over crust.
Freeze until firm.
Allow ice cream to soften.
Spoon into frozen pie crust.
Freeze until firm.
Let pie stand at room temperature before cutting.
Sprinkle over few chopped peanuts, then warm remaining peanut butter mixture and drizzle over top.
In a small saucepan sprinkle gelatine over 1/4 cup cold water. Let stand 1 minute.
Stir over low heat until gelatine is completely dissolved.
In a large bowl with electric mixer, beat cream cheese, sugar and vanilla until blended.
Gradually beat in gelatine mixture and remaining 3/4 cup water until smooth.
Pour into crust.
Chill until firm.
Garnish, if desired, with fresh or canned fruit.
Melt oleo in casserole dish.
Saute onions and carrots.
Add rice and saute until opaque.
Add bouillon cubes, bay leaf, salt, thyme and water.
Bring to boil.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in parsley.
Serves 12.
Mix cake mix, pudding and eggs and pour into 9 x 13-inch pan. Combine brown sugar, pecans and butterscotch chips and sprinkle over cake mixture.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Shred cabbage and put half of it in a greased casserole.
Add half of the sliced potatoes and half of the hamburger.
Sprinkle salt and pepper over this and add the remaining half of the ingredients in the same manner.
Pour over milk and bake in a 350° oven for 2 hours.
Beat egg whites until stiff. Add salt and gradually add sugar, beating until dissolved. Fold in remaining ingredients. Drop by teaspoon on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake 1/2 hour (30 minutes) in a 325° oven.
Take one slice of pumpernickel bread.
Spread with approximately 1 teaspoon of cream cheese.
Place 1 slice of cucumber over cream cheese.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Mix oil, sugar and eggs.
Add flour; beat well, then add nuts, pineapple, coconut and flavoring.
Grease tube pan.
Bake 1 hour at about 350°.
Pound chicken and dip in bread crumbs (plain).
Sprinkle lemon pepper seasoning over it.
Melt butter or oil over medium heat and brown chicken, then drain and line in dish.
Pour sauce over chicken and cut tomato wedges for top of each piece.
Lay Swiss cheese over each piece.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Stir-fry meat in oil.
Add soy sauce.
Add Chinese stir-fry (follow directions on package).
Prepare Rice-A-Roni (follow directions on box).
Add rice mix to vegetable mix.
Add water chestnuts.
Add soy sauce as needed.
Prepare cake according to directions on box.
Making 2 round layers. Split layers in half making 4 layers after cooling.
Blend sugar, sour cream and coconut.
Spread all but 1 cup between layers.
Blend remaining cup of sour cream mixture with cool whip. Spread on top and sides of cake.
Seal in air tight container and place in freezer.
Leave in freezer for at least 2 days.
Set out 2 hours before cutting.
Refrigerate after cutting.
Mix in electric
mixer
or
food processor fitted with steel knife.
Beat
liverwurst until softened.
Add butter and cream cheese and blend
until light and fluffy. Add parsley, onion, brandy and curry
powder. Add salt and pepper.
Spoon into serving container. Cover and chill.
Serve with crudites and assorted crackers.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Form small bite-size meatballs. Brown balls, then remove from skillet.
Stir tomato paste into drippings.
Add beer to this mixture.
Return meatballs to sauce. Simmer 20 to 30 minutes.
A pinch of dill seed may be added to the sauce.
Serves 20 to 30.
Keep warm in chafing dish and serve with toothpicks.
(This freezes well.)
Combine cheeses until creamy.
Add eggs, taco seasoning and chilies.
Pour into spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes. Remove from oven and spread sour cream on top.
Return to oven for 5 more minutes.
Cool.
Then refrigerate overnight.
When serving, remove sides.
Pour a jar of salsa on top.
Serve with nacho chips.
Cook 1 cup tapioca, pinch of salt and 5 cups boiling water for 20 minutes, stirring often.
Take off heat and add one package of raspberry Jell-O, 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water.
Mix well.
Put in bowl and set in refrigerator.
Stir often until set.
Next day, add frozen raspberries and Cool Whip.
Heat the undiluted soup and add and melt the cream cheese. When the cream cheese is blended, add the gelatin and stir well. Cool.
Add the onion, pepper, celery, mayonnaise and shrimp.
Pour into a mold if desired or into a square or oblong dish. Refrigerate.
Beat eggs.
Combine sugar and oil and pour over eggs.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Add nuts and raisins.
Bake in greased muffin tins at 400° for 15 to 18 minutes.
Brown hamburger in large skillet with onion and green pepper. Add salt, pepper and garlic powder to taste.
Cook macaroni noodles according to package directions.
Drain.
Rinse with hot water and drain again.
Put noodles in large bowl and add margarine.
Mix.
Drain hamburger.
Squeeze out excess grease with paper towels.
Mix well in bowl with noodles.
Serve.
Mix cheese, sugar, vanilla and egg yolk until really creamy. Grease 9 x 13-inch pan and spread 1 package of crescent rolls on it.
Top with cream cheese mixture.
(You can add nuts or fruit on top of this.)
Top with other package crescent rolls.
Brush with beaten egg white.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Allow to cool, then cut into squares.
Boil water and pour over Jell-O.
Stir and add berries and cranberry sauce.
Add nuts.
Pour into a 2-quart oiled ring mold and refrigerate overnight.
In a large mixing bowl, combine beef, onion, salt, pepper, egg, bread crumbs and paprika; mix well.
Pack firmly into a greased baking dish.
Top with sliced onions.
Bake at 350°, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes and uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes. Let stand for about 5 minutes before slicing.
In a large skillet, saute the mushrooms in the butter until brown. Sprinkle with the
seasoning salt. Add Worcestershire sauce and simmer until almost all of the sauce is absorbed. Add the brandy and continue to simmer until the mushrooms are tender. Great with steak or roast.
Line bottom and sides of heavy saucepan with washed lettuce leaves.
Add peas.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, nutmeg and sugar. Add butter.
Cover with more lettuce leaves.
Whip the cream and fold in the grated Heath bars and fudge topping.
Split the angel food cake into three layers.
Fill and frost the cake with the whipped topping mixture.
Refrigerate until served.
Fry diced bacon. Add chopped onion, chopped pepper, sugar, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and chopped garlic. Simmer 10 minutes. Add drained beans. Bake in casserole for 1 hour in 350° oven.
Saute onions and pepper to juice of tomatoes in saucepan and bring to boil.
Let simmer until reduced about half in volume. Cut tomatoes in small pieces or mash and add with seasoning to juice.
Let simmer briefly.
(Should be quite thick.)
Serve over patties.
Put chicken between 2 pieces of wax paper and pound to 1/4-inch thick.
Put 2 tablespoons chiles and 1 strip cheese in center of each chicken piece.
Roll up and tuck ends under. Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, chili powder, salt, cumin and pepper.
Roll each stuffed chicken piece in shallow bowl containing melted butter.
Roll in crumb mixture.
Place chicken rolls seam side down in baking dish and drizzle with little melted butter.
Cover and chill 4 hours or overnight.
Bake, uncovered in preheated 400° oven for 20 to 30 minutes.
Toast one side of bread rounds under broiler on baking sheet. Spread onion, mayonnaise and cheese mixture on untoasted side. Broil 3 inches from heat for 2 to 3 minutes, or until golden brown.
Makes 20.
In skillet, quickly brown
meat in hot oil.
Add gravy, water and spaghetti sauce, stir. Cover and cook over low heat 20 minutes, stirring
occasionally.
Add
zucchini,
