cover and cook 10 to 12 minutes
or until zucchini is to desired tenderness. Serve over noodles or rice.
Makes 4 servings.
Bread and fry chicken.
Place in long baking dish.
In medium size bowl, mix together broth, butter, flour, lemon and seasonings. Pour over cutlets.
Bake at 350° for approximately 3/4 of an hour, covered with foil.
Remove foil and bake another 15 minutes.
Cook 4 ounces of macaroni.
Cut 4 frankfurters lengthwise and insert slice of cheese.
Wrap with a slice of bacon.
Fasten with a toothpick.
Mix soup with milk.
Bring to a boil and add macaroni.
Put in greased baking dish and top with frankfurters. Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Saute leeks in butter 5 minutes.
Blend in flour and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually blend in water.
Add salt, pepper and potatoes; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes, partially covered.
Add milk; bring to a simmer.
Blend in cream. Turn off heat and add butter.
Garnish with chives or parsley.
To cherry jello add 2 cups hot water, 3/4 cup cold water, crushed pineapple and juice.
To strawberry jello add 2 cups hot water, 3/4 cup cold water and strawberries.
Allow cherry jello to set.
Spread sour cream over cherry jello and pour on partially set strawberry jello layer.
Refrigerate overnight.
Heat oven to 350°.
Thaw and drain raspberries.
Butter a 9-inch spring-form pan.
Line bottom with waxed paper.
Butter paper.
Grind almonds and 1 cup sugar to a powder; combine with flour.
Melt butter.
Add Amaretto.
Beat white and salt until peaks.
Fold 1/4 of almond mixture at a time into whites, alternating with butter.
Pour into pan.
Gently push raspberries into top of cake.
Cook for 45 to 50 minutes.
Cool and mold. Dust with confectioners sugar.
Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and paprika; stir well. Dredge chicken in
breadcrumb mixture.
Arrange chicken in a shallow baking pan, coated with cooking spray.
Dot with margarine and bake, covered, at
for 30
minutes.
Pour wine over chicken. Cover and
bake
minutes;
uncover and bake 15 minutes.
Serves 6.
Low in calories and fat grams.
In medium bowl, soak croutons in bourbon until all liquid is gone, making sure croutons are completely saturated and soggy.
Add ketchup and beef and mix well.
Form into patties.
Place on medium-hot grill.
Combine the beef, salt, pepper, onion, green pepper and 1/2 can tomato sauce.
Press into greased 9 x 12 x 2-inch baking dish. Bake on the lowest shelf in hot oven (450°) for 10 minutes. Broil 5 minutes more.
While meat is cooking, combine remaining tomato sauce, sugar and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a boil. Boil for 3 minutes.
Add meat drippings if desired.

recipes.t: Believe It Or Not Pork Chops
d: Brown pork chops; place in baking dish.
Mix Coke and ketchup together; pour over pork chops.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Believe it or not:
This is delicious!
Drain juice off peaches; cut peaches into bite size chunks. Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Use peach juice to mix in last; refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours.
Serve chilled.
Can use pineapple with strawberry or lime jello instead of peach.
Place shrimp in bottom of large bowl and sprinkle with cayenne pepper and lemon juice.
Cube red potatoes.
Trim and dice scallions; add to bowl with green peas.
Mix lightly with mayonnaise and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
When ready to serve, arrange on a bed of red or green leafy lettuce.
Garnish with pepper strips and beets.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Sift together flour and sugar.
In pan, mix oleo, cocoa, shortening and water.
Bring to boil and pour over sugar mixture. Mix well.
Add soda, buttermilk, salt, eggs, cinnamon and vanilla.
Pour into greased and floured sheet cake pan and bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a 13 x 9-inch pan.
In a large mixer bowl, blend cake mix, eggs, water and oil at low speed until moistened.
Beat 2 minutes at high speed.
Pour into pan.
Sprinkle nuts and chocolate pieces over batter.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Pour mulberries into greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish. Pour honey or sugar over berries.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Combine egg, milk, oil and honey or brown sugar in mixing bowl; blend well.
Fold in flour, baking powder and salt, adding a small amount of milk, if necessary, to form very soft dough. Spread dough over berries.
Bake at 400° for about 20 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean.
Serves 6 to 8.
Boil all ingredients except corn starch and water for 5 minutes.

In a large mixing bowl, combine powdered sugar, cream cheese, whipped topping and walnuts; mix well. Fold in cake cubes. In a serving dish/bowl, pour half of the cake mixture. Pour half of the cherry filling on top of the cake mixture. Repeat layers until all ingredients have been used. Chill 3 hours before serving. Makes 6 servings.
Combine pretzels, sugar and oleo.
Mix well.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 400° for 7 minutes.
Then cool.
Blend together cream cheese, 1 cup sugar and Cool Whip.
Spread over cooled crust.
Dissolve jello in 2 cups boiling water.
Stir in strawberries and pineapple.
Chill until thick.
Pour over cream cheese layer.
Chill thoroughly.
Cook potatoes in salted water.
Peel and mash.
Then stir in sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Just before serving, fold in cream and pecans.
In a small mixer bowl, combine 3/4 cup of the all-purpose flour, the yeast, caraway seed or pepper and salt.
Add water and oil.
Beat with electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds, scraping bowl constantly.
Beat on high speed 3 minutes.
Stir in the whole-wheat flour and as much of the remaining all-purpose flour as you can.
In an iron pot, outside, cook hens and middling meat until half done.
Add hamburger and onions; continue cooking until hens are done.
Add potatoes and cook to pieces, then add tomatoes and butter beans.
Cook stew until well done.
Add corn and butter; cook until corn is done.
Season in the beginning and throughout the cooking.
Cook the stew to desired thickness (approximately 7 hours cooking time).
Serves around 100 people.
Heat butter, sugar and milk until warm, not hot.
Add marshmallows.
Heat until marshmallows melt.
Bring to boil and remove from heat.
Add Hershey bar, chocolate chips and nuts. Stir (do not beat) until all is dissolved.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Refrigerate to set.
Cut in squares.
Beat eggs 5 minutes with electric mixer.
(This is an important step.)
Add all other ingredients.
Mix well.
Pour into a 1 x 10 x 15-inch jelly roll pan that has been well-greased and floured. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup chopped nuts.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until done.
When done, turn out on a tea towel that has been sprinkled with powdered sugar.
Roll up like jelly roll.
Cool. When cool, unroll and fill.
Combine cornmeal, salt and oil.
Pour hot water and mix.
Add flour and baking powder.
Mix well.
Blend in egg.
Make 8 to 10 patties.
Cook in hot oil in skillet or in the oven on greased cooking sheet until browned on both sides.
Takes 10 to 15 minutes on top of stove and 20 to 25 minutes in the oven.
Brown sausage; add onion, pepper and mushrooms and saute until tender.
Add tomatoes and green chilies.
Simmer 10 minutes or until meat is completely cooked.
Serve over fettucine.
Serves 4 to 6.
Grease 1 (9 x 13-inch) pan.
Cook medium egg noodles.
When done, drain.
Put noodles back in pot.
While still hot, add margarine.
Stir, with a spoon, sugar, vanilla and Ricotta cheese plus sour cream.
Add eggs.
Blend together.
Stir Jell-O and pineapple together.
Add sour cream, Cool Whip and nuts.
Stir well.
Will be ready to eat.
Have margarine and cheese at room temperature.
Blend margarine and cheese together.
Add flour, salt and cayenne pepper.
Roll out to desired thickness and cut in shapes or put through a cookie press.
Bake at 325° until light brown.
Combine egg yolks, juice of lemons, sugar, cream and salt in double boiler and cook until custardy.
Stir constantly.
Chill, then add whipped cream, pineapple, cherries, almonds and green grapes.
Chill for 24 hours and garnish with whipped cream and grated coconut.

Combine peaches and sugar. Add water to cover. Cook down until tender. Mash peaches with potato masher and let cool. Cut pastry dough about 5 x 8-inches. Place 1/4 cup peaches in each crust. Fold over and stick edges of crust together. You may have to dampen edges to get them to stick good. Fry until brown in a well-greased skillet.
In a saucepan, melt margarine, then stir in flour and salt until blended.
Slowly add Sprite and milk, stirring until mixture is smooth.
Add cheese and stir until it is melted into the mixture.
Pour mixture into a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish.
Break eggs into the sauce.
Bake at 350 degrees until eggs become firm. Serves 6.
Sprinkle rice evenly into 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Mix remaining ingredients, except chicken and Parmesan cheese.
Pour 1/3 of the mixture over rice.
Arrange chicken breasts over soup mixture; cover with remaining soup mixture.
Cover with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 2 hours.
Put spinach in bowl.
Press down and season with salt and pepper.
Add bacon and chopped eggs.
Break lettuce and put on top.
Season again and layer next with peas and onions, then cheese.
Cover completely with mayonnaise.
Cover bowl tightly and put in refrigerator overnight.
Toss just before serving.
Mix pineapple juice and almond flavoring. Add ginger ale just before serving.
Soften yeast in 1/2 cup of the warm water.
Mix sugar, salt, shortening and yeast (which has been softened).
Add remaining 1/2 cup of water and the egg.
Add flours and mix well.
Knead on lightly floured board for 5 minutes.
Let rise until double in bulk (about 1 hour).
In a mixing bowl, combine flour, ground nuts,
1/4 cup sugar and brown sugar, then cut in butter until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Form the mixture into a ball and knead until smooth.
On a lightly floured surface, roll dough to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch circles.
Place 1 inch apart on an ungreased cookie sheet. Lightly sprinkle with the additional sugar, then lightly press a whole nut in the center of each cookie.
Bake in a 375° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove and cool on wire rack.
Brown steaks seasoned with desired amounts of salt, pepper and seasoned salt.
Add oregano, soup and milk.
Lower heat and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Boil first 5 ingredients for 20 minutes.
Add vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
Add cream of chicken soup and cheese.
Simmer until cheese melts, about 20 minutes.
Place popcorn in large bowl.
Add melted butter; toss to coat. Sprinkle with gelatin; toss until evenly coated.
Brown sausage; drain all but 2 tablespoons fat.
Pat sausage in casserole.
Brown meat.
Put in casserole.
Lightly brown peppers, onions, garlic and potatoes.
Add to casserole.
Put in spices; lightly toss.
Add beef broth; cover.
Cook at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cook until clear the sugar, water and cornstarch.
Remove from heat and add jello and some butter.
Let this filling cool.
Add berries to this.
Put in pie shell.
Put topping on top, such as Cool Whip.
Cut meat into small pieces.
Season and boil until tender. add beef stew, corn, peas, potatoes and carrots.
Let cook for about 10 to 15 minutes or until tender.
Add onion soup mix, mushroom pieces and macaroni.
Let simmer until it has made a gravy.
Season to your taste.
Turn off.
Let cool.
Mix sugar, cocoa, oleo and milk; boil one minute.
Add remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on wax paper.
In heavy saucepan, combine brown sugar, flour and salt.
Stir in water.
Stir in evaporated milk and corn syrup.
Cook, stirring constantly until thickened.
Stir in nuts, butter or margarine and rum flavoring.
Serve warm over scoops of vanilla ice cream or slices of angel cake.
Makes 2 cups sauce.
Brown hamburger and onion; salt to taste.
Add tomato paste, chili mix, chili powder and water.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Layer in glass casserole dish(s): meat mixture, tortillas (approximately 3), pinto beans, olives and cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves approximately 4 to 6.
Melt butter and combine with rest of ingredients except ice cream.
Spread half of mixture in a 6x12 inch pan.
Top with softened ice cream.
Spread remaining mixture over top of ice cream.
Freeze until firm.
Cut into squares and serve with Amber Sauce.
Thoroughly brown meat in hot fat.
Add water, garlic, sliced onions and seasonings.
Simmer covered about 2 hours.
Add carrots, potatoes and small onions.
Continue cooking 30 to 40 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add mushroom soup, mushrooms and frozen peas.
Cook 5 minutes more.
Push garlic through press.
Combine with ginger, stock, soy sauce, honey and seed in a small dish.
Microwave, uncovered, on High until bubbly, about 2 to 2 1/2 minutes.
Toss with cooked broccoli or other vegetables; sprinkle on carrot.
Serve warm as a side dish or slightly chilled on lettuce as a salad.
Serves 4.
Dissolve jello with boiling water.
Then add strawberries and juice, pineapple with juice and nuts.
Mix.
Pour half into 13 x 9-inch pan or mold.
Refrigerate 1/2 hour to firm.
Leave remaining jello mixture out on counter.
Spread sour cream over chilled jello.
Pour remaining mixture on top of sour cream. Chill.
Makes 8 cups.
Line 9-inch pie pan with pastry.
Mix sugar, flour, salt and cinnamon.
Add to apples and mix thoroughly.
Set aside.
Crush pears and spread in bottom of pastry lined pan.
Sprinkle with rum. Heap apple mixture over pears.
Dot with butter.
Put on top crust and seal.
Crimp edges.
Cut slits for steam to escape.
Bake in 400° oven for 45 minutes or until apples are tender.
With rolling pin, roll out bread slices until they are flat. Mix together cream cheese, Cheddar cheese and egg until smooth and creamy.
Spread this mixture on bread slices.
Place one asparagus spear on each bread slice.
Roll up.
Melt butter in pan and dip each pin-wheel lightly in the butter.
Place rolls in pan until they are almost frozen.
Slice with very sharp knife into bite size pieces.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 15 minutes.
(May be frozen and baked at a later date at same temperature but for approximately twice the time.)
In a skillet, brown the beef with onion, garlic and seasonings; stir to separate meat.
Combine in 1 1/2-quart casserole dish with soup, water and noodles.
Place the cheese around the edge of the casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Yields 4 servings.
Blend flour, sugar and shortening.
Add egg yolk and water mixture.
Stir until dough forms ball.
Roll out.
Recipe makes three two-crust pies, plus single crust.
Dough may be kept in freezer several weeks.
Thaw at room temperature.
Mix will not make dough tough.
Brown ground beef and sausage with onion and garlic.
Add package of taco mix.
Stir and brown.
Place in Dutch oven.
Add the peeled tomatoes (juice and all).
Add tomato paste, pepper and Worcestershire.
Bring to boil.
Add chili powder; simmer.
Add water, if needed, or flour to thicken.
Simmer for about 15 minutes.
Mix flour, cheese spread and margarine thoroughly.
Shape into 50 balls.
Cut Smok-Y-Links into 16 pieces each.
Shape cheese mixture around each piece.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease 12-inch pizza pan or cookie sheet.
In large frying pan, brown ground beef and onion.
Drain well.
Stir in salt, pepper, chili powder and tomato sauce.
Simmer while preparing crust.
Separate crescent dough into 16 triangles. Arrange 13 triangles around pan, spoke fashion, with narrow tips of triangle extending over pan about 5 inches.
Press remaining triangles in center of pan.
Seal perforations.
Spread meat over dough and sprinkle with cheese.
Bring dough tips over filling to the center.
Pinch edges to seal.
Brush with milk.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Peel potatoes and make cross wise slices on them about 1/4 inch apart; do not cut all the way through.
About every second slice, insert a slice of onion, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Place 1 tbsp. butter on top of each potato.
Wrap in foil and bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Beat egg yolks.
Cream together butter, sugar and egg yolks. Add raisins and pecans.
Add vinegar and vanilla, mixing well. Fold in beaten egg whites.
Put in an unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes.
Melt butter or margarine in a skillet.
Add onion and cook over medium heat until soft, stirring occasionally.
Blend in ketchup, molasses, Tabasco, brown sugar, salt and dry mustard. Bring to boiling.
Stir in baked beans.
Put mixture into casserole dish.
Put bacon across top of beans.
Bake at 375° for about 20 minutes or until bacon is cooked.

recipes.t: Crab Rangoon Spread And Won Ton Crackers
d: Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly brush cookie sheet with butter. Cut won tons in half; arrange on sheet.
Brush with butter and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 5 to 7 minutes, until golden brown.
Cool on paper towels.
Repeat until won tons are all done.
Mix
jello
and boiling water and place in refrigerator to thicken slightly.
Butter an 8 x 8-inch glass pan with 1 teaspoon butter or margarine.
Saute onion, garlic and parsley in a little butter until onion is translucent.
Meanwhile, drain and chop artichoke hearts.
While they are still "draining," beat eggs until they are light.
Add bread crumbs and seasonings.
Mix well.
Stir in cheese, sauteed onion, garlic and parsley and artichoke hearts. Put in greased pan.
Bake 35 minutes at 325°, until it feels firm to touch.
Let stand 15 minutes before cutting into squares.
Cream butter with cream cheese.
Add confectioners sugar and vanilla.
Form into balls.
Chill.
Coat with melted chocolate.
Halve and core pears (don't peel; personally I just use canned pears).
Spoon pecans into center of pears.
In small saucepan, combine corn syrup, brown sugar, butter, water and salt and dissolve.
Spoon over pears.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Baste frequently with syrup in bottom of dish.
Serve with whipped cream.
Serves 6.
Make hamburger patties, fry slightly on both sides, then fry onions lightly.
In a roasting pan, layer patties and onions. Pour bottle of ketchup mixed with water on top of patties and onions.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Marinate artichoke hearts for 2 to 3 hours in olive oil and lemon
juice.
Tear
lettuce
into bite-size
pieces and combine with
remaining
ingredients in large salad bowl; add artichoke hearts with their marinade and toss lightly.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Stir in frozen strawberries, pineapple, mashed bananas and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. Pour half of mixture into 13 x 9 x 2-inch oiled pan.
Spread with 8 ounces sour cream.
Cover with remaining jello mixture.
Chill until firm.
Sift flour and soda; set aside.
Over medium heat, bring water, dates, apples and raisins to boil.
Reduce heat.
Simmer 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in margarine.
Pour into bowl. Cool slightly.
Stir in dry ingredients, oats, beaten eggs, vanilla and walnuts.
Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 12 to 14 minutes.
Saute onion in heated olive oil until golden brown.
Add garlic.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add puree.
Season with thyme, basil, dash of paprika and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Cut
onion
into thin vertical slices.
Separate slices into strips;
set
aside.
Heat
1 tablespoon oil in wok over high heat
(or use heavy skillet).
Add mushrooms; stir-fry 1 minute. Use
a
slotted
spoon
to place mushrooms in a large bowl;
set aside.
Heat
second tablespoon oil, add onion and stir-fry
1 minute.
Spoon
cooked onion into bowl with mushrooms.
Heat remaining tablespoon of oil over high heat.
Add beans; gently stir-fry until bright green and glossy with oil. Reduce
heat
to low.
Add broth and sugar.
Cover and simmer until beans are tender, 10 to 20 minutes, depending on age and size
of beans. Stir occasionally.
In skillet, cook onion.
Add carrots, potatoes and 1 cup broth.
Cover, simmer until tender (about 25 minutes), add more broth if needed.
Cut chicken in quarters; add 5 minutes before end of cooking time.
Brown ground beef and onion together.
Drain excess fat.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Add 1 can of Tall Boy vegetable soup to the ground beef.
Do not dilute soup; add straight to ground beef. Mix and let simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally. Serve with creamed potatoes and rolls.
Dissolve apricot gelatin in boiling water.
Add nectar.
Let cool.
Break angel food cake into small pieces.
Add 1 1/2 cartons Cool Whip in gelatin mix.
Blend well.
Using 10-inch tube pan, put layer of cake, gelatin mixture and continue, ending with gelatin mix.
Cover and put in refrigerator for at least 6 hours.
Unmold on cake plate and ice with remaining Cool Whip and garnish with halves of apricots.
Serves 12.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and water. Cook until thick. Stir in jello; cool completely. Pour over berries. Put in pie shell and top with whipped cream or Dream Whip.
In medium saucepan melt 2 Tbsp. of margarine.
Add mushrooms and cook over medium heat about 3 minutes or until tender.
Remove mushrooms, leaving juices in pan.
Stir in cornstarch.
Gradually stir in milk.
Add remaining margarine, salt, pepper and onion salt.
Stirring constantly, bring to a boil over medium heat and boil for 1 minute.
Stir in turkey and mushrooms until well mixed. Serve in puff pastry shells.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix ingredients (except mushroom soup) together and form into patties.
Brown and drain grease.
Add cream of mushroom soup; simmer for 1/2 hour on each side.
Serve over rice or noodles. Yields 4 servings.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
Transfer to a large bowl.
Add chicken, apples, celery, tomatoes and onions.
In a small bowl, combine picante sauce, mayonnaise, chutney and curry powder, mixing well.
Combine with pasta mixture; cover and chill.
Serves 6.
In saucepan, combine chicken broth, onion, one of the vegetable and seasoning combos following.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and simmer for the time indicated or until vegetables are tender (remove bay leaf if using broccoli).
Place 1/2 of vegetables in blender, cover and blend 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth.
Pour into bowl.
Repeat with remaining mixture and set all aside.
Mix sugar and cocoa, then add canned cream and margarine. Cook until thick, approximately 10 to 12 minutes.
Combine first 4 ingredients and microwave on High for 2 minutes.
Stir and repeat.
Add vanilla and soda and stir. Combine cereal, pretzels and nuts in brown paper bag.
Pour syrup mixture over all and shake sack to coat.
Microwave on High for 1 1/2 minutes.
Shake again and repeat.
Spread out to cool.
Add bag of M&M's when cooled.
Cream sugar and margarine at medium speed until combined. Gradually add egg substitute, beating well.
Combine sour cream and baking soda; stir well and set aside.
Combine flour and salt; with mixer running at low speed, add to creamed mixture alternately with sour cream mixture, beginning and ending with the flour mixture.
Stir in vanilla.
Spoon batter into 10-inch tube pan coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 35 minutes or until wooden pick inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes; remove from pan. Cool on wire rack.

recipes.t: Summer Salad With Creamy Lime-Honey Dressing(Used As Dessert Or Salad)
d: In bowl, stir lime juice, water and sugar until sugar dissolves.
Add banana; set aside.
In large serving bowl, layer blueberries (reserve 1/2 cup for garnish), nectarines, strawberries, bananas, watermelon and grapes.
Garnish with 1/2 cup blueberries, kiwi and cherries.
Pour lime-sugar syrup over fruits.
Cover loosely and chill.
To serve, spoon an assortment of fruits and berries with some of the syrup into dessert bowls; top with Creamy Lime-Honey Dressing (recipe follows).
Beat eggs; dip chicken in.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Brown in butter in a pan.
After browning, place in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Pour in chicken broth.
Salt and pepper each breast.
Sprinkle grated up cheese over each and also mushrooms.
Cook at 350° about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Cook a big pot of rice.
Put breast on top of rice, then some juice.
Use 1/2 chicken breast per person.
Saute in skillet until beef and onio are brown and tender. Cook and drain.
Combine beef, spinach, soup and sour cream. Season to taste.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Top with grated cheese and bake at 350° for 30
minutes.
Brown beef in skillet.
Beef forms crust in pie tin or quiche pan. Beat eggs slightly; add milk, then mayonnaise, then salt, pepper and cheese.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 300°.
Bake 30 minutes.
Test with knife like custard.
Cool 10 minutes; cut in wedges.
Serve.
Cook noodles as directed on box.
Combine sliced, peeled cucumbers (thin), chopped onion, pepper and tomato.
Add vinegar and mayonnaise in large bowl.
Add cooked noodles.
Mix well. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Add cheese and mix before serving.
Saute ground beef, onion and celery,
Add chili sauce, ketchup, mustard, and butter.
Salt and pepper to taste and dab of open pit.
Grease sides of two 8-inch layer pans.
Line bottom of each pan with waxed paper dusted with flour.
Sift together flour, sugar, salt and baking powder into a large mixing bowl.
Add the shortening and 1/2 cup milk; beat 2 minutes on low speed of mixer. Add remaining milk, vanilla and egg whites.
Beat 2 minutes. Bake in a moderate 375° oven for 25 minutes.
Make pie layer:
Into medium bowl, combine corn syrup, pecans, eggs, vanilla, sugar, dash of salt and 2 tablespoons melted butter.
Mix well.
Pour pecan mixture into lightly greased 9-inch pie pan.
Bake in a preheated 400°
oven for 15 minutes.
Beat egg, sugar and shortening together.
Sift flour and meal together with salt and baking powder, then gradually add to other mixture, alternating with the clabber.
Pour into iron cornstick pans and bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Makes 1 dozen.
Rinse chicken (removing any loose fat) and lay flat.
Sprinkle (in this order) seasoned pepper, garlic powder and parsley on one side of chicken.
Put in skillet (seasoned side up).
Pour soy sauce over chicken, then pour water around chicken.
Place lid on skillet, steam chicken (approximately 5 to 7 minutes, each side), turn twice.
Remove lid and continue cooking until done (most of liquid should be gone when chicken is done).
Approximate cooking time:
20 to 30 minutes.
Serve with your favorite side dishes.
Saute shrimp, celery, garlic and onions in Dutch oven until shrimp are nearly done.
Add crabmeat and 1 cup water and simmer about 5 minutes.
Add 2 cups cooked rice.
Mix and simmer together until done, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Add plenty of red pepper and salt to taste.
Serves 6 to 10 people.
Mix all soups and mushrooms.
Pour rice and soup mixture into a flat greased 3-inch baking dish.
Press in raw chicken.
Cover with 1/8 to 1/4 cup melted butter and dust with paprika.
Bake 2 1/2 hours at 275°.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix braunschweiger, 1/2 of the cream cheese, pickles, juice, Tabasco sauce, garlic salt, Worcestershire sauce and mayonnaise thoroughly.
Form into a round mold.
Place chicken in a baking dish.
Pour salad dressing over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 minutes.
Place rice, vegetables and 1/2 can of onions around and under chicken. Combine bouillon and Italian seasoning; pour over chicken and vegetables.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes; top with remaining onions.
Bake 2 or 3 minutes longer.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
(I usually double the recipe.)
Stir olives into cream cheese.
Spread on flour tortillas. Sprinkle with seasoning of choice.
Roll up and slice into 1-inch slices.
Put into fridge until ready to serve.
Slice cookie dough thin and place on bottom, sides and corners of 13 x 9-inch pan (do not grease or flour).
Pack way up.
Cream the cream cheese, 1/2 cup sugar, 2 eggs and vanilla until smooth. Pour on top of cookie dough.
Mix together the 1 cup sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 4 eggs and spice, then add pumpkin and evaporated milk.
Mix well and pour over cream cheese mixture.
Bake at 370° for 45 to 55 minutes or until a toothpick can be inserted into center, dry.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Garnish with whipped cream.
Cut meat into thin strips.
Sprinkle meat with salt, pepper and garlic.
Roll in flour.
Brown meat slightly in oil.
Remove meat and drain.
Add onions and mushroom soup and water.
Mix well.
Place meat, mushrooms and onions in mixture.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add bell pepper strips.
Cook 5 more minutes.
Serve over noodles.
Garnish with parsley, tomatoes and mushrooms. Serves 5 to 6.
Cook pasta.
Cut chicken into 1/2-inch pieces.
Dip chicken into beaten egg, then bread crumbs which have been mixed with salt and pepper.
Spread coated pieces on platter.
(This can be done several hours ahead and refrigerated.)
Combine first 3 ingredients and bring to a hard boil.
Pour over jello, stir until dissolved.
Add pineapple and juice.
Allow to cool and add Coke.
Pour into a large mold and chill overnight. Serves 10 to 12.
Beat together eggs, brown sugar, corn syrup, sugar, margarine, vanilla and salt.
Spread sunflower kernels evenly in the bottom of the unbaked pie shell.
Pour in the sugar mixture.
Bake in 350° oven for 50 to 60 minutes or until center is almost set (it will jiggle slightly).
Cover potatoes, celery and onion with water.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and cook on medium-high heat until potatoes are tender.
Reduce heat to low and add soup, cheese, milk and margarine.
Simmer until cheese has melted, stirring occasionally.
Cream together sugar, molasses and margarine.
Sift the dry ingredients.
Start adding dry ingredients to sugar mixture.
Add along the hot water and soda.
When all is mixed well, have eggs beaten and add at the last.
Stir in good.
Cook ground beef with green pepper and onion.
Add chili block and mix together in large pan.
Add water.
Add chili with beans and canned tomatoes. Cook slowly for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Serves 5 to 6.
Combine pear juice, brown sugar and oil in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat; stir in lemon juice, maple syrup and cinnamon.
Arrange pear halves, cut side up, in a small, shallow baking dish.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Pour brown sugar mixture over pears and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 4.
Chop bacon strips and fry in skillet, add vinegar and water and bring to boiling.
Sprinkle salt and sugar on lettuce and pour boiling mixture over the lettuce.
Prepare rice as label directs, but do not add margarine and use only 1/2 tsp. salt.
While rice is cooking prepare dressing: In large bowl, with wire whisk, mix lemon juice, oil, pepper, and remaining 3/4 tsp. salt until blended.
Add hot rice to dressing and toss to coat.
Cool slightly, about 30 minutes, tossing occasionally.
Meanwhile in 5 quart dutch oven heat, 3 quarts water to boiling over high heat.
Add corn and cook 5 minutes. Drain. When corn is cool enough to handle, cut kernels from cob. Add corn to rice with radishes, peas, mint and chives.
Toss until evenly mixed.
If not serving right away, cover and refrigerate up to 8 hours.

recipes.t: No Fail Sour Cream Chocolate Cake
d: Mix water, margarine and chocolate in a large heavy saucepan. Heat until chocolate is melted.
Take from heat and add sugar, eggs and sour cream, mixing with a spoon.
Sift in flour, soda and salt.
Mix well with a spoon.
Do not overbeat.
Stir in vanilla. Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan in 350° oven for about 35 minutes.
Test to see if top springs back when touched with your finger.
Do not overbake.

recipes.t: Brown Bears In An Apple Orchard(Method:  Skillet Or Dutch Oven)
d: Pour applesauce into one large or two small skillets.
If applesauce is too thick, add up to 1/2 cup water.
Heat applesauce until boiling.
Prepare gingerbread batter according to package directions.
(*You may also need eggs and/or oil.)
Sift together flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
Add water, vanilla, shortening, sugar, eggs. Serves 8.
Add cold water to gelatin and let stand two minutes.
Dissolve over hot water.
Stir dissolved gelatin into cranberry sauce.
Add pineapple, celery, lemon juice and chopped nuts.
Chill until mixture begins to jell; fold in marshmallows.
In a pan, brown beef; drain.
Add onion, sauce, chili powder and garlic; simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Separate biscuits; pat 5 on bottom of an ungreased casserole dish.
Combine 1/2 cup cheese, sour cream and egg.
Mix well.
Mix together meat and sour cream mixtures.
Pour on biscuits.
Arrange rest of biscuits on top. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Brown beef and drain.
Add onion and rice, brown slightly. Add remaining ingredients and place in casserole.
Cover with lid or foil.
Bake for 45 minutes in 350° oven until rice is done and most of moisture is absorbed.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Cook noodles and drain.
In large skillet, cook meat, onion and celery until meat is brown and onion is tender.
Drain off fat.
Stir in tomato sauce and salt.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir in cottage cheese, sour cream and cream cheese, then add noodles.
Pour into ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Slice tomato and arrange on top. Cover and bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Layer tomato slices and green pepper rings in shallow glass dish.
Shake remaining ingredients, except lettuce, in tightly covered jar.
Pour onto vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
In a 9-inch square pan dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Stir in pineapple, cranberry sauce and wine.
Chill until mixture thickens slightly.
Fold in pecans.
Chill until firm.
In small bowl beat cream cheese with sour cream until smooth.
Spread over gelatin.
Keep chilled until serving time.
Cut into squares and serve.
Mix cake mix with butter, 1 egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Press into a 9 x 17-inch pan for crust.
Mix margarine and sugar; cream together.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add milk and graham cracker crumbs alternately.
Add vanilla, baking powder, coconut and pecans.
Put in 3 greased and floured cake pans and bake at 350° until done (approximately 25 to 30 minutes).
Prepare chili according to package directions; cool.
Reserve 2 1/2 cups chili.
Wrap remaining chili tightly; freeze for later use.
Fry tortillas in 2 inches hot oil, pressing down centers with large ladle to form shell.
Continue frying until crisp and golden; remove with tongs.
Drain.
Arrange greens in taco shells; top with chili, process cheese food, tomatoes, avocado and olives.
Serve with sour cream and additional process cheese food, if desired. Makes 4 servings.
Blend Duncan Hines butter mix, sour cream, sugar and oil and add eggs, one at a time.
Mix brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts.
Oil and flour cake pan.
Then pour 1/2 batter in pan, then add sugar mixture, then add rest of batter.
Bake at 320° for 55 minutes.

recipes.t: Wieprzowina With Smietanie (Baked Pork Chops In Sour Cream)
d: Salt and pepper the pork chops on both sides and fry in margarine until brown; then place in casserole.
Mix together remaining ingredients and pour mixture over the chops.
Bake, covered, for 1/2 hour in preheated 350° oven.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch pan. Pour pineapple with juice in pan, then sprinkle dry cake mix over pineapple.
Sprinkle pecans over cake mixture.
Melt butter or margarine and pour over pecans.
Bake for 50 minutes.
Cherry pie filling or apple pie filling may be substituted for crushed pineapple.
Mix onions, tomatoes and tomato sauce in a saucepan. Simmer, covered, for 3 hours. Add tamales with sauce and all other ingredients. Top with cheese before serving.
Place potatoes in a large Dutch oven and cover with water. Bring to a boil.
Boil until potatoes are tender; remove from water and cool.
Slice potatoes into 1/4-inch slices.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add onion, garlic, celery and dill.
Toss to coat well.
Add mayonnaise, a few tablespoons at a time, until salad is mixed well.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 3 (9-inch) layer cake pans.
In a large bowl, cream the butter.
Gradually add the sugar; beat until fluffy.
Add the beaten eggs and melted chocolate.
Sift the dry ingredients; blend in alternately with the milk.
Add the nuts and vanilla.
Pour into prepared pans.
Bake for 35 minutes, or until the center of the cake feels solid.
Cool and remove the layers from the pans.
Fill and frost.
In a medium saucepan combine pudding mix, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg and egg nog.
Mix well.
Over medium heat, cook and stir until thick and bubbly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in rum.
Cool.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon into pie shell.
Chill 4 hours or more.
Crush
candy
bars and set aside.
Pinch half the angel food cake into small pieces and spread into a long Pyrex pan. In another
bowl,
mix
butter, egg yolks and sugar.
Fold in whipped topping.
Mix
until
creamy.
Spread
whipped mixture over cake pieces.
Sprinkle 1/2 the crushed candy bars on
top
of cake.
Repeat process to make 2 layers.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Sylvia'S Collard Greens With Smoked Turkey
d: In a 4-quart saucepan, bring the water and smoked turkey to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat and simmer, covered, for 1 hour. While the turkey is cooking, wipe the collards with a damp towel, then wash two or three times or until all the dirt and grit has been removed. Chop the greens into 1/2-inch pieces. You will have 10 cups of chopped greens. Add the collards, oil, salt, black pepper, sugar and red pepper flakes to the saucepan. Return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes longer. Discard the turkey before serving or chop the turkey meat and add it to the collards. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Chop onion and bell pepper very fine.
Set aside.
Put salad oil, sugar, ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and salt into blender.
Mix well.
Pour into bowl with onion and bell pepper. Chill until cold.
Ready to serve.
Fry sausage and crumble in pieces.
Mix sausage, onions and beans, then add soup, paste, mustard and sugar.
Can be done in crock-pot or casserole in oven.
Bake at 300° to 350° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Scald milk.
Cool to lukewarm in bowl.
Add yeast, sugar and 1 1/2 cups flour; mix well.
Let stand until bubbly.
Stir in salt, eggs, oil and remaining 1 1/2 cups flour to form soft dough. Knead on floured surface until smooth and elastic.
Place in greased bowl, turning to coat surface.
Let rise, covered, in warm place until doubled in bulk.
Roll 1/4-inch thick on floured surface.
Spread with 3 tablespoons softened butter.
Sprinkle with mixture of cinnamon and 1/2 cup brown sugar.
Roll as for jelly roll.
Slice 1 1/2 inches thick; place in greased baking dish.
Combine 1 tablespoon butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar and water in bowl.
Drizzle over rolls.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until golden brown.
Yield:
12 servings.
In large skillet heat oil, then add chicken, stirring well for about 2 minutes.
Add celery and cook until bright green.
Add garlic powder, green pepper and green onion, stirring until done. In bowl mix teriyaki sauce, cornstarch, then add to skillet.
Then add orange slices and pineapple chunks.
Stir until thickened. Serve over white steamed rice.
Serves 4.
Make brine of a proportion of 2 cups salt to one gallon water. Boil
and pour over cucumbers, boiling hot.
Let stand one
week. In
hot
weather, skim
daily.
Drain
and cut in chunks.
For the
next
three
mornings,
make
a boiling hot solution
of one gallon water and one tablespoon powdered alum and
pour
over the pickles.
On the fourth morning, drain the alum
water
and
heat 6
cups vinegar, 5 cups sugar, 1/3 cup pickling
spice
and 1 tablespoon celery seed to boiling point and pour
over
the pickles.
On the fifth morning, drain off this liquid
and save; add 2 more cups sugar to the liquid and heat to
boiling
point; pour over the pickles.
On the sixth morning, drain
liquid
again and save; add one more cup sugar and
heat;
pack
the
pickles in sterilized canning jars and pour the
liquid
over
until the jars are filled;
seal while hot.
After cutting chicken into cubes, marinate with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Cut onion and squash into cubes.
Mix sauce:
soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil and tapioca powder with 1/2 cup of water and set aside.
Saute onion until browning in 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, then add marinated chicken, stirring until it is cooked.
Add cut squash and onion; stir until half cooked, then add mixed sauce.
Keep it at a boil.
Add toasted cashews and chili before you serve.
Serves 6 to 8 people.
Let all items set at room temperature.
In bowl, mix cheese and eggs; in different bowl, mix milk and fruit (drain fruit).
Combine mixtures, then put the juice from the two lemons.
Brown pie crust to your liking; let cool and pour filling in.
Let set in icebox 6 to 7 hours, then serve.
Make up the powdered drinks and the lemonade according to directions, except scant the water slightly (to compensate for melting ice).
Combine all of the ingredients.
Some of the punch may be frozen in ring molds to be used in the punch bowl.
Cream butter and cream cheese.
Sift flour and baking powder; add to creamed mixture.
Chill dough 2 to 3 hours.
Combine flour, sugar and cocoa.
Cut in margarine until crumbly.
Reserve 2 cups.
Press rest on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 3 minutes.
Stir over low heat until the first 3 ingredients are well dissolved.
Stir in lemon juice.
Cool to room temperature.
Stir yogurt into the cool jello mixture.
Pour into a 6 cup mold. Refrigerate overnight.
Melt margarine and butter.
Add light brown sugar, dark brown sugar and dates.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until dates melt (about 6 minutes).
Remove from heat; add Rice Krispies and pecans; mix well.
When cool, roll into balls and then roll balls in powdered sugar.
Makes about 214.
Split the eggplant lengthwise and hollow, leaving a 1-inch thickness with skin intact.
Saute garlic and onions in oil; then add pieces of eggplant and mushrooms and cook until tender.
Stir in bread crumbs and blend in marinara sauce.
Fill the eggplant with this mixture; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Serve with pasta and a healthy smile.
Mix together tuna, celery, cheese, parsley and pimiento.
Set aside.
Mix together lemon juice, mayonnaise, salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Spoon over tuna and toss lightly.
Divide mixture evenly among bottoms of buns. Put tops on, wrap in foil and place on cookie sheet.
Bake in 400° oven about 20 minutes. Serve hot.
Serves 4 and has about 490 calories per serving.

Cream margarine, sugar and shortening until light and fluffy. Add egg yolks (well beaten). Add flour, soda and buttermilk and mix well. Stir in nuts, coconut and vanilla. Beat egg whites until stiff. Gently fold into batter. Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13 pan. Bake at 350° until cake is done.
In a bowl, mash avocados with lemon juice.
Spread mixture evenly in the bottom of a 9-inch pie plate.
Spread sour cream evenly over avocado mixture.
Spoon taco sauce over sour cream layer.
Sprinkle green onions over taco sauce.
Top with cheese. Cover and chill for several hours.
Serve with chips.
Makes about 4 cups.
Boil haddock fillet for 15 to 20 minutes, being careful to keep it whole.
Saute scallops in butter with dash of paprika. Boil lobsters for 20 to 25 minutes.
Pick off meat.
Flake haddock.
Mix haddock, lobsters, scallops, shrimp and clams in a dish; mix lightly.
To make
herb butter, chop all herbs in food processor. Add softened
butter and mix together.
Pack into crocks.
The butter will keep
up
to
2 days in the refrigerator or can be frozen for future
use.
Cut bread lengthwise into halves and spread each half
with
softened
herb butter.
Put them on a baking sheet and
toast
in the oven until crispy.
Slice and serve immediately.
After
cooled,
this is good served with a cold pasta salad.
Cut potatoes into chunks.
Place on heavy-duty foil. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and soup mix.
Dot with butter. Seal foil well. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Cream butter with sugar and eggs.
Add bananas and vanilla. Sift together dry ingredients and add alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture.
Blend well.
Stir in dates and nuts.
Pour into tube, loaf or layer pan.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
In saucepan, combine soup, water and cheese.
Heat until cheese melts.
Stir occasionally.
Add remaining ingredients and heat.
Combine cookie crumbs and 2 Tbsp. melted butter.
Spread 3/4 of the crumbs on the bottom of a 7x11-inch pan.
Pour boiling water over jello in large bowl to dissolve well. Add softened sherbet and Cool Whip.
Mix well with beater or in a mixer.
Add crushed pineapple and oranges.
Place in a 9 x 12-inch dish.
Cool until set and serve.
(Makes a large amount.)
Line bottom of a
x 13-inch pan with half of graham crackers.
Cut to fit if necessary.
Beat powdered sugar and 3 tablespoons cream. Spread on crackers and top with remaining crackers.
Chill.
Heat to boiling water and juice.
Add jello and dissolve.
Cool until partially set.
Divide into 2 parts. Add 3/4 cup
of
evaporated
milk to one part and beat at high speed until fluffy.
Pour over crackers.
Chill.
Add 3/4 cup water and fruit
to
other part.
Pour over whipped layer and chill until set.
Cut into squares.
Cream butter and add sugar.
Blend thoroughly.
Add egg yolk and vanilla.
Sift flour and baking soda and mix well with first mixture.
Spread in ungreased pan and then prick deeply with a fork.
Bake in a 250° moderate oven for 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Scald 1 cup milk. Add 1 cup honey and sugar. Stir over medium heat until the sugar is dissolved.
Cool the mixture. Beat in the butter and eggs.
Sift together the flour, salt and baking soda and stir into the batter.
Beat well. Add the walnuts and orange rind.

Pour the batter into a floured and buttered loaf pan and bake the bread in a moderately slow oven at 325° for about 1 hour. Cool the bread for 15 minutes in the pan and then turn it out on a wire rack to cool. Serve thinly sliced with butter or cream cheese.
With no white on the rind, blot dry with paper towels.
Put rind into a quart jar.
Add 2 cups of vodka, screw on top and store for 2 days in a cool, dark place.
Remove peel, add sugar and shake until sugar dissolves.
Add 1 cup vodka and stir.
Close jar and store again for 1 week at least.

In a slow cooker, mix cream of mushroom soup, dry onion soup mix, brown gravy mix and water. Place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture. Cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours.

Blend first 3 ingredients well. Spray bundt pan with Pam, sprinkle nuts or raisins on bottom of pan. Layer frozen buns on top of nuts or raisins. Sprinkle butterscotch pudding over rolls evenly. Pour oleo mix over rolls. Cover with a paper towel. Let stand at room temperature over night. Cover loosely with aluminum foil and bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Invert immediately on plate. Enjoy!!
Heat oil and brown cubes of meat.
Remove meat and cook onions and garlic until golden brown.
Put meat back in with onions and garlic.
Add salt, pepper and tomatoes.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until meat is tender.
Add undrained peas and mushrooms.
Stir in the uncooked macaroni.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Brown pork chops with salt.
Lay in flat pan.
Pour sauce over top.
Place pineapple ring and cherry on each pork chop.
Cover with foil and bake 1 1/2 to 2 hours at 350°.
Watch to see if dry. Serve with warm applesauce.
Combine apples and cinnamon in bowl.
Spoon apples evenly over pizza shell.
Drizzle with margarine.
Sprinkle with raisins, nuts and cheese.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Serve warm or cold.
Cream butter and sugar.
Mix in egg and vanilla.
Stir in pancake mix and chocolate chips.
Bake 15 minutes at 375°.
Put olive oil in stew pot.
Place chicken in pot, brown the chicken lightly.
Add oregano, adobo seasoning and Sason seasoning.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add salad olives, bay leaves, onions, garlic, potatoes, and carrots.
Simmer for 10 minutes. Add tomato sauce.
Cover and cook until done.

Rinse and drain chicken. Mix together on a plate, bread crumbs and spices. Pour 1/2 bottle of dressing on a plate. Dip chicken in dressing and then into bread crumbs. Turn to coat both sides. Place on a shallow baking dish and cover with foil. Bake at 350- 400 degrees for approximately 1 1/2 hours. Uncover the last 15 minutes to brown.
Place onion, cucumber and raw potato in saucepan; add broth, parsley and seasonings.
Bring to boil; cover and let cook until potato is barely tender (about 10 minutes).
Put through blender and chill thoroughly.
When ready to serve, stir in cream and serve in chilled soup bowls.
Finely mince (tops and all) the green onions. Stir into the sour cream.
Add lemon juice, mayonnaise, cheese, salt and pepper. Allow to stand several hours before serving.
Makes 4 generous servings.
Cook rigatoni according to package.
Cook broccoli according to package.
Cool and mix together.
Melt Velveeta cheese in saucepan.
Add milk and oleo; mix together.
Mix with broccoli and rigatoni.

skillet

Mix gelatin completely in hot water.
Add cold water and fruit juices.
Stir in sugar; chill.
When ready to serve, puree bananas in blender.
Mix fruit juice with ginger ale and pureed bananas. Garnish with fruit slices or ice ring made of strawberries frozen in lemonade.
Preheat oven at 350° for 10 minutes.
In 8-inch round glass baking dish, spread soft cream cheese evenly along bottom.
Evenly layer chili on top.
Next, top with shredded cheese.
Bake for about 15 minutes or until chili is bubbling.
Once out of the oven, sprinkle tomatoes and spring onions on top.
Beat egg and sugar; combine with water.
Let come to almost boil.
Combine flour and vinegar and stir well; combine vinegar combination with sugar, egg and water.
Stir continuously until almost clear.
When sauce is clear (sticky), pour over the apples and cabbage already cut and in bowl.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Combine next 4 ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Stir to melt shortening.
Cool to lukewarm. Add softened yeast.
Gradually add flour to form a stiff dough.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Stir in the mashed potato and 1/2 cup sugar.
Cover; let stand in a warm place until doubled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the milk to the butter and stir until melted. Cool.
Mix in the eggs, 1/2 cup sugar and salt.
Stir into yeast mixture.
Add the flour gradually, stirring in enough to form a soft dough.
Knead dough on a floured surface until smooth.
Place in a greased bowl; grease top of dough.
Cover and let rise until double, about 1 1/2 hours.
Punch down dough and divide into two portions.
Roll out one portion of dough into a 12-inch square 1/4-inch thick; brush with 1 tablespoon melted butter.
Cut dough into 2-inch squares.
Turn up the corners together.
Cook broccoli according to package directions.
Drain well. Combine soup, eggs, mayonnaise, onion, salt and pepper.
Add to broccoli.
Pour into a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with cheese on top.
Pour melted margarine over cheese.
Spread stuffing on top.
Bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes at 350°.
Serves 8.

In saucepan, combine sugar, water and spices. Bring to boil, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes. Strain. Combine with grapefruit juice, lime juice and ginger ale. Pour over ice cubes and garnish with lime slices. Very refreshing!
Prepare macaroni and cheese as directed on package.
Set aside.
Brown ground hamburger and onion in skillet.
Drain off fat.
Stir in chili powder.
Add tomatoes and juice.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add corn and stir.
Pour all into macaroni and cheese. Mix well.
Yields 6 servings.
Cream margarine and sugar in mixer.
Add eggs (unbeaten), sour cream, flour, baking powder and baking soda.
Mix well.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Grease and flour large tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Paint chicken breasts on both sides with mustard.
Sprinkle lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce over and allow to marinate at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes.
Preheat broiler or outdoor grill.
Grill chicken for 3 to 4 minutes each side or until just tender.
Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve hot.
Tear cake into small hunks and put in 9 x 13 pan.
Whip Dream Whip according to package direction.
Cut cream cheese into small bits and add to Dream Whip.
Whip until smooth.
Pour over cake and stir gently until all the cake is covered.
Pour pie filling on top and smooth so it will look nice,
Refrigerate at least 3 hours before serving.
Cook onion in margarine.
Stir in
chicken
and
cook. Add 1/4 cup picante sauce
and cream
cheese
and
cook until heated. Stir in 1 cup cheese.
Spoon about 1/3 cup mixture in center of tortilla and roll up.
Place
seam side down in 7 x 12-inch dish. Top with
remaining
sauce and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Sprinkle cheese and pepperoni on bottom of 9-inch pie plate.
Set aside.
Beat eggs, milk and basil with wire whisk until well blended.
Pour egg mixture over cheese and pepperoni.
Bake 25 minutes or until knife inserted in center of pie comes out clean.
Makes 6 servings, 240 calories each.
Combine sugar, honey and water in saucepan; boil until syrup will harden when dropped in cold water, or hard ball stage on thermometer.
Pour syrup slowly over stiffly beaten egg whites. Add lemon flavoring and beat until stiff enough to hold peaks and drop on waxed paper.
Add chopped nuts if desired.
Brown slices of tenderloin in a little oil.
Remove meat and discard oil.
Return meat to pan, put 1/2 can sauerkraut on top of meat, layer of onions, half the carrots and half the potatoes. Then repeat with the other half of vegetables.
Pour water and reserved juice on top of all.
Bake in oven in a tightly covered pan at 325° for about 3 hours.
Drain the fruit and combine with the cottage cheese and Cool Whip in a medium mixing bowl.
Sprinkle the jello over the top and stir to mix well.
Add pecans, if desired.
Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Beef Tips With Mushrooms And Onions
d: Melt margarine in a large saute pan.
Saute mushrooms, onions and garlic. Remove from pan with broth remaining.
Add sirloin and brown over medium heat. Remove meat to dish with mushrooms and onions.

Add remaining ingredients to broth in pan, making sure to make a paste with cornstarch first to avoid having lumps in gravy. Stir this constantly until mixture thickens. Add back the beef, mushrooms and onions and mix together with gravy. Pour this into a large casserole dish.
At this point the dish can be refrigerated for cooking the next day. Bake, covered, in a 325° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
This is delicious served with rice and green beans. Also a good dish to fix on Saturday and cook on Sunday morning for a perfect Sunday lunch.
Enjoy!
Cream together the cream cheese, margarine and powdered sugar. Add pudding and slowly beat in milk.
Fold in 4 ounces Cool Whip; reserve rest for top.
Line a 9-inch pan with wafers.
Slice bananas on top of wafers.
Top with pudding mixture.
Refrigerate. Top with Cool Whip before serving.
Prepare marinade by combining sugar, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, white wine and calamansi or lemon juice.
Shell shrimp, leaving tails.
Wrap shrimp with 2 to 3 strips each of carrot and spring onion in lumpia wrapper.
Roll.
Seal with cornstarch paste. Deep-fat fry.
Serve hot.
Blend butter or margarine with garlic and honey.
Slice bread in half lengthwise.
Spread butter mixture thickly on both cut sides of bread.
Sprinkle lightly with basil, then paprika.
Put loaf back together and coat lightly with olive oil.
Wrap in foil and bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Slice in large hunks and serve hot.
In 3-quart casserole dish, combine chicken, celery, garlic and ginger.
Cover with lid; microwave on High 5 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink, stirring once during cooking.
Stir in broth and water.
Cover; microwave on High 5 minutes or until hot and bubbling.
Combine egg, orange, raisins, rind, shortening and vanilla. Sift flour, baking powder, soda, salt and sugar into orange mixture; mix well.
Stir in pecans.
Pour into a well-greased 5 x 9 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 325 to 350° for 1 hour, or longer (check with a toothpick at 1 hour).
Sprinkle gelatin over 1/4 cup milk in a medium saucepan.
Let stand 1 minute.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until gelatin dissolves; remove from heat.
Add salt, sugar and 1 cup milk. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Let mix cool.
Drain apricot halves and reserve 1/4 cup syrup.
Combine apricots, cherries, peaches, pears, guava shells and pineapple ring in 2-quart Wonderlier.
Combine reserved apricot syrup and curacao and pour over fruit.
Marinate overnight.
Saute chopped onions and garlic in olive oil.
Add Italian spices.
Add rest of ingredients.
Thicken with cornstarch.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift dry ingredients and mix.
Combine egg whites, yolks, orange zest and orange juice.
Add to dry mixture. Set aside for 20 to 30 minutes.
Lightly grease a baking sheet and mark 5-inch circles on the surface.
Drop a spoonful of batter in each circle.
Spread evenly to cover the area.
Prepare and bake only one sheet at a time. Bake until the edges are a light brown, but the center is soft (5 to 6 minutes). Quickly remove cookies from the pan with a spatula.
Mold cookies around orange to create cupped shapes.
Once shaped, cool on rack.
Fill with fresh fruit, ice cream or pudding.
Rinse green beans very well.
Put some butter in pan, then add chopped onion.
Let let 3 to 5 minutes, then pour beans in and let cook 5 minutes more.
Put vinegar in and let simmer slow for 3 more minutes.
Combine
cake
mix, milk, egg whites and orange concentrate. Beat
minutes
at
medium
speed of electric mixer. Fold in the 1/2 cup coconut.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9 x 1 1/2-inch
layer pans.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 minutes; cool. Frost and fill with Fluffy White Frosting.
Brown and drain sausage.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 15 minutes.
Combine sugar,
butter and milk.
Bring to rolling boil over medium
heat,
whisking
constantly
to avoid scorching. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add marshmallow cream. Stir until smooth.
Add nuts and vanilla, stir until blended. Pour into
a buttered
8-inch square pan.
Place on wire rack and cool.
Cut into squares.
Yield 3 pounds.

In medium mixing bowl, combine egg, stuffing mix, milk, onion soup mix and 2 tablespoons barbecue sauce; add ground beef and mix well. Shape into loaf and put in meat loaf pan. Drizzle 1/4 cup barbecue sauce over meat. Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Mix the dry ingredients in large bowl. Mix milk, bananas, egg whites and oil together.
Add the dry ingredients to liquid and mix.
Line muffin pans with paper baking cups or spray with Pam baking spray.
Fill each cup with batter. Bake for 17 minutes.
Makes 12 muffins.
In saucepan, brown both meats and drain.
Mix in spaghetti sauce and spices.
Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions.
In 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking pan, spread 1/4 of the meat sauce.
Layer noodles, meat sauce, cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese (alternating layers).
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown and bubbly.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Heat crushed pineapple.
Add jello and mix well.
Let cool to room temperature.
Add cream cheese, softened and blended with the milk.
Fold in Cool Whip or prepared Dream Whip.
Spread bread crumbs.
Sprinkle evenly with dry ingredients. Peel apple; cut into bite size pieces.
Add to bread.
Measure milk into 1-quart measuring cup.
Add butter.
Microwave on High 4 minutes.
Stir eggs into milk.
Add vanilla, cinnamon and sugar to taste.
Taste for flavor of eggnog.
Pour mixture over bread and apples.
Mix up and microwave for 9 to 12 minutes.
Spread approximately 1 teaspoon of peanut butter on each side of cracker.
Wrap 1/2 bacon slice around cracker; use a toothpick to secure.
Place in glass dish on 4 to 5 layers of paper towels. Microwave on Medium to crisp bacon.
Top with cheese.
Microwave to melt cheese.
Brown sausage; drain.
Mix sausage, cheese, Tabasco, Bisquick and milk.
Make into balls; place on greased (I use Pam) cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Rub lemon all over chicken; add salt and pepper.
Pour oil in brown bag; stuff chicken with stuffing and place chicken in bag. Bake at 325° for 4 hours.
Spread crescent rolls in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Brown hamburger.
Mix in seasoning mix, beans and tomato sauce.
Pour mixture over baked rolls and top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese melts.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes and sour cream.
Serves 6. Enjoy.
Combine the condensed milk and evaporated milk.
Add the plain milk.
Stir in the sugar and a pinch of salt.
Mix well to dissolve the sugar.
Add the cut-up or mashed fruit.
Stir well.
Soften yeast in water.
Scald milk, add shortening, honey and salt.
Cool to lukewarm.
Add softened yeast and flours.
Knead well, cover and let rise until doubled.
Punch down and shape into 2 loaves.
Place in greased loaf pans, cover and let rise until double again.
Bake in 375° oven for about 1 hour.

recipes.t: Greek Style Kabobs With Pita Bread
d: Cut pork into bite size pieces.
Season with lemon juice, salt, pepper, oregano and olive oil.
Skewer meat and cook on the grill.
Brush pita bread with a bit of oil and grill as well. When the meat is tender, put 1 skewer on each pita and slowly draw out the skewer leaving the pieces of meat in the pita.
Add the onion, tomato, parsley and sauce.
Roll the pita.
A piece of grease-proof or wax paper can be rolled along the bottom half of the pita for a less messy sandwich.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat.
Mix in bananas, flour and salt.
Add nuts, chips and maraschino cherries. Pour into a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Spray casserole (the size pan a little smaller than 9 x 12) with Pam.
Spread rice in bottom of pan.
Place chicken in a single layer on top of rice and season lightly with Cavender's. Put cheese on top of chicken; set aside.
Mix soups, wine and milk in a small bowl.
Pour over chicken mixture.
Sprinkle stuffing mix on top and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake uncovered 40 minutes at 350 degreees.
After removing from oven, let sit about 15 minutes before serving.
Brown chicken in skillet coated with nonstick spray.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Combine water, soy sauce, ketchup, pepper, garlic, sugar, scallion and apple juice.
Add to pan and cook over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes.
Reduce to low, add chicken and cook, covered, until tender (20 to 25 minutes).
Remove chicken. Dissolve cornstarch in 1 tablespoon water, add to pan mixture and cook over medium heat until thick (3 to 4 minutes).
Pour sauce over chicken on platter.
Sprinkle with seed.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Blend cream cheese and 5 tablespoons oleo.
Add all but the last three ingredients and mix well. Separate dinner rolls into 4 rectangles and seal perforations. Spoon 1/2 cup meat mixture onto center of rectangle.
Pull 4 corners together and seal.
Brush with 3 teaspoons oleo and dip into bread crumbs.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes on ungreased cookie sheets.
Each serving equals 3 protein, 1 fat, 2 bread and 13 optional calories.
Cook the first 4 ingredients in heavy pot until it reduces to 1/2 in amount.
Add 1 to 2 cups sugar at a time and taste after each addition.
Make it as sweet as you like.
Add salt and taste. Add more, if needed.
Pack in hot jars and seal.
It is very close in taste to a chili sauce.
Wash potatoes and pat dry.
Coat skins with margarine. Sprinkle with garlic salt.
Bake at 450° for 1 hour (potatoes should be placed on cookie sheet).
In a saucepan, combine dates, water and sugar.
Cook over medium heat.
Stir constantly until it thickens.
Remove from heat. Add nuts.
Slice cookie dough into 36 slices (thin).
Place 27 cookies on cookie sheet.
Place 1 tablespoon of date nut mixture on top of each slice.
Cut remaining 9 slices into thirds.
Place each third onto date top mixture.
Sprinkle with orange peel.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool and serve. Makes 27 cookies.
Cook the noodles.
Drain and set aside.
Saute the meat, onions and garlic in oil until the meat loses its pink color and the onions are tender.
Add pepper, tomato sauce, catsup and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring mixture to a boil, then simmer gently about 5 minutes.
Mix in the cooked macaroni and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Combine sugar, margarine, syrup, salt and flavoring.
Bring to a boil.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add soda.
Pour mixture over popcorn; mix well.
Scatter in large shallow pan. Bake at 250° for 1 hour, stirring frequently.
Mix the first 4 ingredients; cook until it forms a real soft ball in cold water.
Add the coconut; cook until 240°, or until it forms a soft ball.
Add the butter and vanilla.
Let cool until bottom of pan is warm.
Beat with electric mixer (add a few drops of red coloring if pink color is desired) until it begins to hold its shape when dropped from spoon.
Drop onto wax paper; top with pecan halves or pieces.
Store in tins.
Mix crab and shrimp (rinsed and shredded) together and set aside.
Cook shallots in oleo in small saucepan until soft, 5 minutes.
Beat eggs with whisk; add milk, vermouth and hot sauce. Mix together.
Add crab and shrimp and additional milk to make 3 cups.
Pour into baked pie shell and bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes or until knife in center comes out clean.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook green beans with seasonings for approximately 2 hours, until very tender.
Cook them down so there isn't a lot of water left in them.
Add onion and tomatoes and cook for another hour or so.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine coconut, sugar and flour, then add egg whites, almond extract, then last almonds.
Stir good.
Drop teaspoon size on lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes.

In a very large bowl, mix first 3 ingredients and set aside. In a saucepan, combine the sugar, corn syrup and butter and cook to little more than soft-ball stage. Add vanilla. Pour over popcorn mixture and mix well.
Spread on cookie sheet to cool.
Drain cherries and set aside juice.
In a saucepan, melt butter and add juice from the cherries; mix well.
Add cornstarch and sugar.
Stir until smooth.
Heat, stirring constantly, until clear and thickened; remove from heat.
Add cherries and almond extract. Put cake on individual plates.
Pour sparkling cherry sauce over slices.
Stir brandy and bitters with ice.
Strain into champagne glasses.
Fill with iced champagne.
Drain fruits separately; reserve juices. Chop apricots. Dissolve gelatin in 2 cups hot water; add 1/2 cup pineapple juice and 1/2 cup apricot juice. Chill until thickened.
Add marshmallows, pineapple and apricots.
Place in an 8 x 8-inch container. Chill until firm.
Mix together oats, All-Bran, shredded wheat (4 large biscuits) and oil.
Pour boiling water over all and let cool.
Then add buttermilk, eggs and sugar and mix.
Sift together salt, flour and baking soda.
Mix all together well and store in glass gallon jar in refrigerator.
Keeps fresh up to 3 months.

Preheat oven to 350°. Slice bacon strips in thirds. Wrap 1/3 bacon strip around a Little Smokie. Secure bacon with a toothpick. Place in a 9 x 13 baking dish. Sprinkle brown sugar to cover. Drizzle water on top. Bake until bacon is cooked (around 50 minutes).
In a small bowl, combine Cheddar cheese, chilies and 1 tablespoon of margarine.
Melt over low heat.
Set aside mixture.
Soak bananas in pineapple juice for 30 minutes.
Drain and reserve juice.
Heat oven to 400°.
Place bananas in pie shell. Sprinkle with combined sugar, flour and spices.
Add 3 tablespoons of pineapple juice.
Top with pastry crust and vent.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes or until crust is browned.
Cut fish into 3-inch pieces.
Sprinkle with lemon and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.
Combine other ingredients and add beer.
Brown meat with the onion and bell pepper, chopped fine.
Add the catsup, chili and relish. Simmer for 1 hour and serve on warm hamburger buns.
Beat one egg white with 1 teaspoon vanilla until peaks form. Add 1/2 cup sugar.
Gradually stir in coconut; stir in one tablespoon flour.
Set aside.
Dissolve cocoa in hot coffee.
Set aside.
Beat 3 egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add 1/2 cup sugar and continue beating.
Set aside.
Add soda to sour cream. Set aside.
Mix the first 5 ingredients together for 8 minutes.
Add the vanilla and butter extract.
Mix well.
In another bowl, mix the sugar and cinnamon.
Pour half the batter into an ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour half the sugar mixture over the batter.
Put the rest of the batter over this and sprinkle the remaining sugar mixture on top.
Mix well with a knife.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Brown together ground beef, onion and garlic in a heavy frying pan over medium heat.
Stir until meat loses its pinkness.
Add salt and chili pepper.
Place 1/2 cup ground beef filling, 1/2 cup cheese and 1/2 cup diced tomatoes onto 1/2 of each tortilla.
Fold other half over.
Remove any air pockets by pressing down.
Pour oil into skillet to 1/4-inch depth.
When oil is hot, place filled tortillas into pan a few at a time.
Saute over medium to high heat until golden on each side, 45 seconds on each side.
Remove from pan onto paper towels.
Cut into wedges and serve.
Note: Substitute canned sweet potatoes and pineapple, if desired
Dissolve lemon jello in hot water.
Add cold water and ice cubes.
Let set until semi-firm.
Add softened cream cheese.
Beat until well mixed and smooth.
Let set until firm.
Serve on lettuce leaves and sprig of parsley.
Can use a mold or cake pan. Cut in squares to serve.
Peel potatoes and place in frying pan over low heat.
Add 1 teaspoon sugar and 1 teaspoon flour.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Slice onion rings and Polish sausage on top.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Melt chocolate and margarine in heavy pan.
Add butter flavoring and nuts.
Stir to cool and remove from heat.
Combine sugar, flour, eggs and vanilla.
Mix until blended.
Do not beat! Add chocolate mixture and again mix carefully but do not beat. Put into 18 paper cups and bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes.

Warm cream cheese, sour cream, butter and eggs until room temperature. Preheat oven to 375 degrees. In a large bowl, whip cream cheese until fluffy. Beat in butter and sour cream, then add cornstarch, sugar, vanilla and lemon juice. At high speed, beat mixture until very well blended. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Pour cheesecake batter into a well-buttered 10 inch spring form pan. Place pan in a larger pan and add enough warm water to come halfway up side of pan.
Cook asparagus in boiling salted water 10 minutes. Mix mushroom soup, cream, lemon juice and egg yolk; season. Heat thoroughly. Pour over drained asparagus arranged on toast. Serves 6 to 8.
In a large skillet, brown ground beef with onions and green pepper.
Drain and discard fat.
Add green beans and tomato sauce; cook until warm.
In a greased 10-inch glass pie plate, pat enough biscuits together to form a bottom crust.
Bake in 350° oven until slightly brown.
Remove from oven and spoon ground beef mixture over crust.
Arrange shredded cheese over beef mixture.
Cut remaining biscuits in halves or quarters and roll in small balls. Arrange on top of cheese.
Return to 350° oven and bake until biscuits are golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Pour 1/2 of cornbread mix in casserole.
Add sausage and cheese; do not mix.
Pour rest of mix over top.
Bake at 325° for about 35 to 45 minutes.
Place milk and cottage cheese in blender container.
Process on high speed until smooth and creamy. Stir in soup mix. Refrigerate, covered, for 1 hour. Serve with fresh vegetables.
Brown hamburger and onion over medium heat.
Spoon off excess fat.
Add chili powder, garlic salt and salt; mix well.
Add tomato sauce and 1/2 can water and beans.
Spread over meat mixture.
Combine first four ingredients, mixing well.
Reserve 1/3 cup mixture; firmly press remaining mixture on bottom of a 9-inch spring-form pan.
Beat cream cheese until light and fluffy; gradually add 1 1/2 cups sugar and mix well.
Add eggs one at a time; beat well after each.
Add sour cream and flavorings; mix well.
Pour into prepared pan; sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture.
Bake at 475° for 10 minutes; reduce to 300° and bake 50 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Chill.

Cut beef into bite size pieces and brown in oil. Add onions and flour; stir to coat meat. Add wine, broth and seasonings. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes. Remove bay leaf and add mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve over noodles or rice.
Salt and pepper ribs.
Cover with onion slices.
Mix rest of ingredients and pour on ribs.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Remove cover the last 20 minutes.
In mixer bowl, beat cooking oil into butter until blended. Beat in the 1/3 cup sugar.
Add orange juice, baking powder and baking soda; mix well.
Add enough of the flour, a little at a time, to make a medium-soft dough.
Shape dough into 2-inch ovals and place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake in 350°
oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until cookies are golden.
Cool on a wire rack.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan. Melt peanut butter and margarine or butter in bowl over hot water. Add remaining ingredients.
Stir until blended.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes. Cool and cut into squares.
Yields about 2 dozen squares.
Heat oven to 400°.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in medium bowl.
Cut in chilled butter or margarine with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Add yogurt and stir until dry ingredients are moist.
(Dough will be sticky.)
Turn dough out onto floured surface.
With floured hands, form ball and knead 4 to 5 times.
Spray or grease a baking sheet. Pat dough on baking sheet to 8-inch circle.
Cut into 12 wedges, cutting almost, but not all the way through dough.
Make small slit in each wedge and fill with 1 teaspoon jam.
Sprinkle with pecans. Bake at 400° for 13 to 15 minutes until golden.
Serve warm.
Sprinkle the
pecans
in
bottom of greased and floured 10-inch fluted
tube
pan. In
large mixer bowl, combine cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, the 3/4 cup water, oil and the 1/4 cup rum.
Blend well.
Beat
at
medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into prepared pan. Bake
in 325° oven for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes.
Invert on serving plate.
Prick
cake with long-tined fork.
In a saucepan, combine pie filling, pineapple, sugar, cornstarch and food coloring (if desired); mix well.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Cook and stir for 2 minutes.
Cool.
Fold in bananas and nuts.
Pour into pie shells. Chill for 2 to 3 hours.
Garnish with whipped cream.
Store in the refrigerator.
Yields 12 to 16 servings.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Add salt and pepper.
Set aside.
Combine flour, salt, pepper, oregano, eggs and milk.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan and sprinkle lightly with cornmeal. Pour batter into pan.
Sprinkle meat over and bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Spread sauce over meat and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 15 minutes more.
Melt margarine.
Mix flour with margarine.
Slowly add milk. Cook until thickened to make white sauce.
Add all other ingredients.
Keep hot over double boiler.
Serve over crisp toast, biscuits, patty shells or rice.
Cream butter in large mixing bowl; gradually add sugar, beating
well.
Add
eggs, one at a time, beating mixture well after
each addition.
Combine 3 3/4 cups flour, baking powder and nutmeg;
add to creamed mixture alternately with bourbon, beginning and ending
with flour mixture.
Mix well after each addition.
Dredge raisins
and
pecans
in
remaining
1/4 cup flour;
stir into batter.
Spoon batter into a heavily greased 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at
for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool
cake
in
pan
for
minutes. Remove cake from pan and let cool completely.
Wrap a slice of ham around each breast and place in long casserole dish.
Mix the soup and sour cream together.
Pour over meat and bake at 350° until done (about 35 to 40 minutes).
This is excellent with rice.
Heat all but 3 squares of chocolate with 1/4 cup milk in large microwavable bowl at High 1 1/2 to 2 minutes.
Stir until completely melted.
Or heat in heavy saucepan over very low heat. Beat in cream cheese, sugar and remaining milk.
Gently stir in whipped topping until smooth.
Spoon into crust.
Freeze until firm.
Remove from freezer.
Let stand 30 minutes at room temperature until pie can be cut easily.
Melt remaining chocolate about 15 seconds; drizzle over pie.
Mix together pie filling and pineapple (do not drain) in bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle 1 box white cake mix over top.
Dot one stick of butter on top of cake mix.
Sprinkle nuts on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Top with Cool Whip to eat.
Combine salmon with its liquid, crackers and Grape-Nuts cereal.
Mix well. Add egg, milk and onion. Stir until well blended.
Make into small patties. Fry in melted butter (I use Pam) in a skillet. Brown on both sides. Serve.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Cook celery in water until tender.
Add salt, milk, cheese, minced onion and celery soup.
Brown almonds in margarine.
Add to celery mixture and pour into a buttered casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Beat sugar and margarine until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg, juice and orange peel.
Combine remaining ingredients; stir into juice mixture until moistened.
Spoon batter into six muffin cups coated with a cooking spray.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Cool on rack; serve warm.
Makes 6 large muffins.
Cook hamburger in skillet until lightly brown.
Add taco seasoning with small amount of water.
Simmer until water is gone; stir occasionally.
Take up into bowl.
Chop or shred onion, tomatoes and lettuce; place in separate small bowls.
May also serve with sour cream and taco sauce.
Roll tenderloin in flour; brown in oil with onion, celery and garlic.
Add soup and water with rice and pour all into casserole; cover tightly.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Brown hamburger with one onion.
Cut up celery.
Soak barley in water; drain.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Cut chicken into 1/2 pieces.
Dip in egg and bread crumbs seasoned with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Heat oil in skillet.
Add 1/3 of chicken and saute 30 seconds until golden. Remove with slotted spoon and repeat with remaining pieces. Discard oil.
Cook pasta.
In 2-quart saucepan, combine soup, cheese, mustard and pepper. Over low heat, heat until cheese is melted.
Stir often.
Add broccoli.
Heat through.
Stir often.
Serve over potatoes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles as directed and drain.
In a large bowl, combine hot noodles, eggs and 1/2 of cheese.
Mix well.
Press mixture into greased 12 x 9-inch baking dish.
Bake 20 minutes or until lightly browned.
Spoon sauce onto noodle "crust." Add topping and additional cheese.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes more. Serves 8.
Saute
onions
and cauliflower in butter.
Combine
all other ingredients, except beaten eggs; mix
with onions and cauliflower.
Place in bread loaf pan.
Pour
in
beaten eggs. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix juices and tequila.
Pour all but one cup into ice cube trays (preferably metal) fitted with dividers.
Freeze for several hours or up to 2 days.
Refrigerate remaining one cup mixture.
In large skillet, brown meat with onions.
Drain off fat.
Stir in kidney beans, tomato sauce, undrained tomatoes, uncooked macaroni, green pepper, water, chili powder and garlic salt.
Bring to boil; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often.
Remove skillet from heat.
Sprinkle meat mixture with Monterey Jack or Cheddar cheese (both can be used).
Cover and let stand for 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 6 servings.
Using a large bowl, mix 1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup sugar, salt, orange peel and undissolved yeast.
Combine milk, water, orange juice and 1/2 cup butter; heat until warm.
