Gradually add to dry mixture.
Beat for 2 minutes at medium speed.
Add egg and 1/2 cup flour to make thick batter; beat 2 minutes on high.
Stir in enough additional flour to make soft dough.
Turn out on pastry cloth; knead until smooth.
Put in greased bowl, turning to grease top.
Cover with towel; let rise until double.
Mix cranberries, marshmallows and sugar and chill overnight. Next day before serving, add the remaining ingredients except for whipping cream.
Whip the cream and fold into the mixture, creating the Fluff.
Serve in a crystal bowl.
Serves 8 to 10.
Soak the dried beans, dried peas, lentils, etc., in water overnight.
Put dried beans into kettle with water.
Bring to a boil; simmer for 2 1/2 hours with stew meat.
Add tomatoes, onion, celery, potatoes, carrots and seasonings; simmer 1/2 hour longer.
Cut up and brown chuck roast.
Cut up chicken.
Coarsely chop onion and green pepper.
Put all ingredients in stew pot and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
In saucepan, combine water, cranberries and sugar; bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes or until all berries pop. Add gelatin; stir until dissolved.
Stir in undrained pineapple and grapes.
Pour into 5-cup ring mold.
Chill until firm. Yields 8 to 10 servings.
In saucepan, melt chips with Eagle Brand and 2 tablespoons margarine.
In large bowl, combine pecans and marshmallows.
Pour chocolate mixture into nut mixture.
Add vanilla.
Spread into wax paper-lined 13 x 9-inch pan.
Chill 2 hours and cut into squares. Makes about 40 squares.
Mix flour, salt and baking powder.
Cut in shortening until mixture is cornmeal-textured.
In a 1-cup measure, beat together vinegar and egg, then fill to 1-cup mark with cold tap water.
Mix together flour and vinegar-egg-water mixtures.
It will be soft and sticky.
Working on a very well floured board, roll out a piece of the dough to approximately 1/8-inch thick and 2 to 3-inches wider than your pie pan.
Put in lightly floured pie pans.
Roll out equal size circles for top crusts.

Set oven control to broil and/or 550°. Broil lamb chops with tops about 3-inches from heat until brown, about 7 minutes. Cut cheese to fit chops. Turn lamb chops. Broil until done, 5 to 7 minutes longer.
Place onion and cheese slice on each lamb chop. Broil until cheese begins to melt, about 30 seconds.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Combine any type of pasta (3 or 4 kinds) and cook until tender; drain.
Add spaghetti sauce, chopped pepperoni, mushrooms and green peppers; simmer 30 minutes. After the ground beef has been drained, add to sauce mixture.
Save out 9 tablespoons of peach juice from canned peaches. Set aside.
Place all remaining peaches and juice in pot over medium heat; stir occasionally.
In large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking soda and cinnamon.
Set aside.
In another bowl, thoroughly beat banana until no large pieces remain.
Add in peach juice and skim milk.
Mix well.
Add liquid ingredients to dry ingredients (not the warming peach mixture).
Mix together well.
Set aside. When peach mixture begins to bubble, add in potato flakes and stir constantly for about a minute.
Pour peach mixture into an 11 x 15-inch pan.
Drop dough mixture by large spoonfuls onto the top of peaches.
Place in 350° oven for about 25 minutes, or until toothpick comes out clean from the biscuits.
Let stand after cooking for an hour or more.
Serve warm with fat-free frozen vanilla yogurt or ice cream.
Cook cabbage and cauliflower until tender, add onions and stir.
Drain the liquid from the cooked mixture.
Butter and salt to taste.
Pour into a well-greased casserole dish.
Layer with cream of celery soup, next layer of Cheddar cheese, then top with crushed potato chips or saltine crackers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine macaroni, tuna, tomato sauce, Parmesan cheese and Italian seasoning in a medium size bowl.
In a 1 cup measure, combine instant chicken broth and boiling water; stir into tuna mixture.
Spoon mixture into a 6 cup baking dish.
Top with slices of Mozzarella.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly hot and cheese is melted.
In saucepan, bring butter and sugar to a boil, stirring constantly.
In a bowl, combine Rice Krispies, nuts and coconut. Pour butter sauce over Rice Krispies mixture and mix well.
Press 1/2 of mixture into bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Spread softened ice cream over Rice Krispies.
Top with remaining 1/2 of Rice Krispies mixture.
Freeze before serving.

In 5-quart crock-pot, place soup, milk, spinach and bacon. Melt butter in skillet. Saute onion and oysters. Cook 5 minutes. Add wine. Cover and cook 20 minutes on low. Add to crock-pot. Simmer 1 hour or longer.
Skee-rum-ious.
Place rice in bottom of large greased roaster. Mix soups and milk and pour over chicken and rice. Sprinkle with dry ingredients. Cover tightly with aluminum foil. Bake 3 hours at 325°.

recipes.t: Carrot Cake And Cream Cheese Filling
d: (Be sure to grate carrots and refrigerate before starting.) Mix oil and sugar; beat well.
Add eggs.
Sift all dry ingredients 2 or 3 times.
Mix with sugar mixture.
Add nuts and carrots, a small amount at a time, until well mixed.
Pour into well-greased and floured pans (three 9-inch pans).
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes, or until done.
In medium saucepan, combine water, potatoes, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer until potatoes are tender.
Add salmon after pulling skin off and deboning.
Add dill weed.
In small bowl, combine milk and cornstarch; blend with wire whisk until smooth.
Slowly stir in soup.
Bring to a boil and reduce heat.
Cook an additional 2 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
If you like more salmon, you can use two cans. Pour salmon juice in pot with potatoes and cook along in soup.
Add barley to boiling salt water.
Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Cook vegetables in oil until tender.
Combine with barley. Top with cheese.
Bake in casserole at 350° for 20 minutes.
Place corn in a large skillet; turn on medium heat.
Add butter, whipping cream, sugar and salt.
Stirring constantly, heat until most of the whipping cream and butter is absorbed into the corn.
Mix eggs, sugars, oil
and vanilla.
Sift flour, salt, soda, cinnamon and nutmeg. Stir everything together. Add apples
and nuts.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Combine sugar, egg substitute, oil and vanilla; add apples. Combine flour, soda, salt as desired and cinnamon; add to mixture. Add nuts and pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch. Add cream, rhubarb and butter. Mix well. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture comes to a boil.
Mix together refried beans, Monterey Jack cheese, cumin and garlic powder.
Put in double boiler or microwave oven until spreading consistency.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Work in shortening.
Add milk.
Roll out on a floured board.
Cut in 4 squares.
Place apple on each square and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Fold and pinch edges together.
Place in baking dish and put Syrup (recipe follows) over all.
Bake 45 minutes or until done.
Baste 3 or 4 times during baking time with Syrup.
Slice chicken into bite size pieces.
In a large bowl, mix soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice, cheese, string beans (drained but leave moist) and mushrooms (drained but moist).
Put chicken in medium size roaster.
Pour mixture over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Remove from oven; add 3/4 package croutons, pushing into mixture.
Top with biscuits.
Return to oven and bake at 350°, uncovered, for 20 minutes, until biscuits are brown. Enjoy!

recipes.t: Spareribs And Potatoes In Hoisin Sauce
d: Have spareribs cut Chinese style 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Pare potatoes and cube as for stew.
Brown spareribs; add potatoes, salt, hoisin sauce, sugar and water.
Bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer 25 minutes.
(Add more water if necessary.)
Gravy will be made by itself without thickening.
Serve with rice.

recipes.t: Scrambled Eggs With Crabmeat And Vermouth
d: Break eggs into large mixing bowl and beat with whisk until well blended.
Heat half of butter in top of double boiler over simmering water.
Pour in eggs and stir with whisk until they just begin to set.
Stir in remaining butter and crabmeat and continue cooking for about 15 minutes or until eggs are creamy (do not overcook).
Remove pan from heat and stir in vermouth, salt and pepper.
Spoon eggs on serving plates and sprinkle with toasted almonds.

recipes.t: Debbie Nicholson'S Excellent Moist Zucchini Bread
d: Blend all dry ingredients. Beat eggs.
Add oil, sugar, zucchini and vanilla. Add dry ingredients and blend well.
Add chopped nuts. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Soak strawberries in vodka for 1 hour.
Add orange juice and cranberry juice.
When ready to serve, add ginger ale and sherbet. Make a block of ice to float in punch.
Blend first 7 ingredients in a saucepan and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove bay leaf and cloves.
In a large frying pan, melt margarine.
Mix in flour. Add tomato mixture slowly, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Cook until thickened and smooth. Add beans and heat.
Mix all ingredients except avocado together; not more than 1/2 an hour before serving.
Cut avocado; scrape skin well and mash. Mix into tomato mixture.
Squeeze lemon over top of mixture to prevent discoloration and wrap tightly.
To serve, pour off extra lemon and edge with tostados.
Cook prunes with a little water.
Mash fine and add the chopped nuts.
Add the sugar to the beaten egg whites; beat well again.
Add the prune and nut mixture.
Put the prune stuff into a baked pastry shell.
Bake very slowly for about 25 minutes.
Serve with a generous dollop of real whipped cream.
Bake baking powder biscuits, split and spread with margarine. Fry onion and celery in oil until onions are soft and clear.
Stir in soup mixed with milk.
Heat and stir so it doesn't stick.
Add chicken.
Add peas.
Heat until hot only.
Add salt and pepper, if needed.
When the chicken is bubbly hot, spoon it between and on top of the biscuits.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a large bowl.
Add apples and toss gently.
Stir in beaten egg and margarine.
Pour mixture into pastry shell.
(For firmer crust, brush first with egg white.)
If desired, may sprinkle with chopped pecans.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake for 50 minutes or until it quits shaking.
Check after 1 hour.
Cook the squash, covered, in the salt and water in a large saucepan over high heat until soft, about 15 minutes.
Drain well; let stand in a colander for at least 30 minutes or press down with your hand to force out most of the liquid.
Puree the pulp in a food processor or put through a food mill; it should yield about 4 cups.
Add the eggs, butter, sugar, salt and pepper.
Blend thoroughly.
Fold the cranberries into the mixture.
Pour into a buttered 2-quart baking dish or two smaller ones.
Top with grated nutmeg and bake in a preheated 350° oven until golden and does not shake in the middle when jiggled, about 45 minutes for one casserole, 30 minutes for two.
Yields 8 servings.
Cut monterey jack cheese into cubes.
Combine eggs and sour creme in a large bowl.
Add corn, bread crumbs, green chillies, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Stir in monterey jack cheese cubes. Spoon into a greased 10 inch quiche pan or a square baking pan Bake at 350 or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean Sprinkle with cheddar cheese.
Bake 5 or 10 minutes longer.
Cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Preheat a heavy skillet.
Add shortening.
When sizzling hot, add popcorn.
As soon as it starts to pop, add salt and sugar. Shake vigorously while corn pops so melted sugar will not burn. Empty into large bowl and add a few peanuts.
Mix pudding mix with buttermilk and Cool Whip.
Add fruit and graham crackers.
Use immediately or will keep in refrigerator overnight.

Preheat the oven to 425°. In a large bowl, combine the soup, milk, chicken and peas and carrots; mix well. Pour the filling mixture into a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate. Cover with the pie crust, pressing against the pie plate to seal and flute, if desired. Make several slits in the crust to create steam vents. Place pie on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until heated through and the crust is golden. Let sit for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve.
Combine cooked vegetables and butter until butter is melted. Add Parmesan cheese, garlic powder and pasta; toss gently to mix. May serve hot or cold.
In frying pan, saute vegetable oil, garlic and onion.
Add tomato paste or tomato puree and simmer.
Add meatballs and simmer about 1/2 hour more.
Blend cheese, mayonnaise and milk.
Add juice, sugar, oranges, cherries and pecans.
Fold in whipped cream and spoon into paper baking cups.
Freeze in muffin tins.
Makes 18.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Bring 2 quarts of water to boil.
Add plum tomatoes for 1 minute, remove to colander and refresh under cold water.
Peel tomatoes, chop and set aside.
Blanch asparagus in same water for 2 to 3 minutes.
Refresh under cold water; set aside.
Heat olive oil in saute pan until hot.
Add garlic and tomato; saute for 2 minutes.
Season well with salt and pepper. Remove from heat; set aside.
Place popcorn in roasting pan.
In heavy saucepan, stir together sugar and syrup.
Stir constantly.
Cook until mixture boils.
Stir in peanut butter.
Cook without stirring 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla and baking soda.
Pour peanut butter mixture over popcorn.
Stir to coat well.
Bake in 250° oven, stirring occasionally, 1 hour.
Cool stirring some to break apart.
Store in tightly covered container.
Drain and rinse hominy.
Butter a 3-quart casserole.
Divide hominy into 3 portions.

Layer 1 portion in bottom of casserole. Dot with sour cream and margarine and season with salt and pepper. Add a layer of 1/2 of the green chiles and green onions, which have been sauteed in 2 tablespoons margarine.
Repeat layers, ending with hominy on top.
Dot with sour cream and cover with grated cheeses.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes at 350° or until lightly brown.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add eggs and mix well.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk.
Pour into greased loaf pan and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook pudding as directed.
Add margarine.
Pour into cake mix. Mix well.
Pour into greased and floured cake pan (9 x 13-inch). Drop butterscotch chips over cake.
Sprinkle pecans over chips. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Saute onion in butter; add soup, 1/2 the cheese and garlic. Then add mushrooms, broccoli, rice and ham and stir in pimentos. Chill overnight.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes (covered).
Ten minutes before done, uncover and put on remaining cheese and fried onion rings.
Combine Veg-All, celery, onion and chestnuts.
Add cheese and mayonnaise, mixing well.
Place mixture in greased casserole; top with crushed crackers and dribble with margarine.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In blender or food processor, place tofu and yogurt.
Add chopped vegetables and salt and pepper to taste.
Place on serving platter with bagels, crackers or pita bread.
Mix together sugar, oil, eggs and milk in a large mixer bowl. Beat until well blended. Sift together flour, salt, cinnamon and soda. Gradually add to liquid mixture. Beat until smooth.
Stir in oats, butterscotch chips, raisins and nuts. Spread into buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Let cool. Spread icing over top. Cut into 24 squares.
Bake cake as instructed on box.
Make lime Jell-O as instructed.
Make red Jell-O as instructed.
Set aside.
Mix instant pudding and Dream Whip with vanilla extract and chill.
Combine egg, stuffing mix, onion soup mix and 2 tablespoons barbecue sauce.
Add raw ground beef.
Mix well.
Shape into 5 small loaves.
Cok covered for 8 to 10 minutes or until meat loaves are no longer pink.
Spoon over remaining barbecue sauce on loaves.

recipes.t: Aunt Viola'S Clam Pie(An Old Eastern L.I. Tradition)
d: Slice potatoes and onions and parboil 15 minutes in water barely to cover.
Drain.
To potatoes and onions, add butter; sprinkle with flour, salt and pepper.
Add clams, clam juice and cream or milk; stir and bring to a boil.
Put in pastry-lined pie pan.
Cover with top crust; seal edges and slit top.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes, then at 400°
for 35 to 40 minutes.
Serve hot.

Sift together, flour, soda, cream of tartar and salt, (several times). Cream butter and sugar until light. Add eggs, then Anise seed. Chill until firm enough to shape. Shape into small balls an inch in diameter. Sprinkle more anise seed on greased baking sheet and place dough balls far apart. Bake in hot oven, at 400 degrees for 8 minutes.
Crush graham crackers and add melted butter and sugar. Reserve 2 tablespoons.
Press rest firmly into 8 x 13-inch pan and chill.
Whip cream and add marshmallows carefully.
Put 1/2 of mixture on chilled crust.
Cover with fruit pie filling.
Add remaining marshmallow mixture.
Top with reserved crumbs. Refrigerate overnight.
Boil chicken completely.
Remove from broth, cool and debone. Cook your yellow rice in remaining chicken broth.
If necessary, you may have to add a little more water.
After rice has cooked completely, add chicken, cream of chicken soup, pimientos and jalapeno peppers.
Stir well.
Pour into baking dish and top with Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Saute onion in butter.
Add ground meat, salt and pepper. Saute cabbage.
In a 2-quart baking dish, place 1/2 cabbage on bottom.
Place ground meat mixture on top of cabbage and cover with remaining cabbage.
Pour a large can of tomato soup on top. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In blender, blend yogurt and Ricotta cheese until smooth. Combine eggs, sugar and flour until smooth and add to blended cheese mixture; blend.
Add vanilla and salt; blend.
Add juice and peel; blend.
Pour into greased 8-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Mix syrup and sugar in big saucepan. Bring to boil over medium heat, stirring frequently. Remove from heat. Stir in peanut butter and cereal. Press mixture in well-greased 13 x 9 x 2 pan. Melt chocolate and butterscotch pieces in double boiler or microwave and spread over cereal mixture. Cool. Cut into 1 x 2-inch bars.
Wash cucumbers.
Pack in gallon jars that will seal.
Add pickling spices, pickling salt and alum.
Fill the gallon jar with cold water and vinegar.
Seal with hot lid.
Cook cranberries and apples until soft in 1/2 cup water. Strain into a bowl.
Add pineapple and sugar; mix well.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1/2 cup boiling water and add to mixture.
Chill until set.
Combine margarine and chocolate in a small pan.
Cook on low until chocolate melts.
Combine sugar and next three ingredients in a small bowl.
Add corn syrup and milk.
Stir with wire whisk until blended.
Add to saucepan.
Cook potatoes in boiling salted water about 30 minutes or until tender; drain and cool slightly.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes; set aside.
Combine parsley and onion and set aside.
Combine mayonnaise, sour cream, celery seed, salt and pepper and horseradish; stir well.
Place 1/3 of potatoes in a 13 x 9-inch dish; top with 1/3 mayonnaise mixture, 1/3 sliced eggs and 1/3 of onion and parsley mixture.
Repeat layers twice.
Cover and chill for 8 hours.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Combine vanilla wafers and walnuts in processor or blender and chop finely.
Mix powdered sugar, butter and orange juice concentrate in medium bowl.
Add to cookie crumbs and process until blended.
Form mixture into 1-inch balls.
Roll in coconut.
Serve at room temperature.
Store cookies in fridge.
Makes 60 cookies.
Peel the brown skin off the back and grate (by hand or in blender) with some of the water.
Strain and squeeze to extract coconut milk.
Blend custard powder or cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water.
Bring 1/2 cup water to boil.
Add custard paste and bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Boil until color darkens.
Remove from fire.
Cool slightly.
Add coconut milk. Sieve custard.
Add condensed
and evaporated milk.
Add essence last.
Freeze.
(You may churn in ice crem freezer for a creamy texture.)
Put the vegetable oil in saucepan or melt the butter.
Add the squeezed garlic, lime juice, lemon juice, vermouth, salt and pepper; cook with medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add fresh, cleaned shrimp and cook for 6 minutes; don't overcook.
Make sure that the linguine is prepared so that it is finished to your liking at about the same time that the shrimp sauce is finished.
Serve with Chilean wine and
a nice smile.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix eggs, brown sugar and Bisquick. Pat Bisquick mixture in pan and sprinkle with chocolate chips and chopped nuts.
Bake at 350°
for exactly 25 minutes.
Let cool and cut into squares.
Cook sugar, water and salt until it forms a soft ball when dropped in cool water.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and marshmallow cream.
Beat until it begins to thicken.
Add pecans and mix with a spoon.
Spoon out and let set.
Puree berries in blender; add juices.
Add ice cubes one at a time; crush.
Pour into tall glasses.
Garnish with whole berries.
Beat eggs well; add sugar and flour mix.
Add milk, oleo and vanilla.
Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Sprinkle nutmeg over top of pie.
Set pie on baking or cookie sheet.
Bake in moderate oven until a toothpick comes out clean.
In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, onion, salt and pepper.
Stir in eggs and celery.
Cover and chill.
For each serving, spoon about 1/2 cup onto a lettuce leaf or spread on bread.
Yields 3 to 4 servings.
Prepare all ingredients ahead of time.
Marinate chicken breast strips in soy sauce and garlic mixture of water, soy sauce and cornstarch.
Heat wok and put in oil; swirl to coat.
Cook chicken until white.
Remove.
Cook carrots a few minutes, then add broccoli.
(Add oil, water or 1/2 cup bouillon or broth, if needed.) Stir-fry until broccoli begins to get tender (bright green).
Then add onion.
Stir-fry a few more minutes.
Then add mushrooms and soy sauce mixture.
Stir until thickened (2 to 3 minutes).
Serve over hot rice.
Slice bananas into large bowl.
Cover with cherries.
Peel and section grapefruit and oranges.
Mix all fruits.
Chill.
Combine sour cream, honey and salad dressing.
Add to fruit before serving.
Makes 7 to 8 servings.
Combine water and white bread.
When bread is soaked, crumble into meat with remaining water.
Mix in eggs, onion, seasonings and oatmeal.
Mix well.
With wet hands, shape into loaf and put into baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Spread ketchup over top and bake 30 minutes more.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl or on a pastry board.
Add the eggs, one by one, mixing well and kneading until the dough has a uniform consistency.
Let it stand for 30 minutes.
Take the dough, one small piece at a time and roll it between the palms of your hands into thin pencil-like strips.
With a sharp knife, cut the strips into 1/4-inch pieces, each piece should be about the size of a pea.
Cover bottom of hot ovenproof pan with butter, swish to cover bottom.
Mix rice with mandarin peel, put in pan and stir to coat rice with butter.
Cook over low heat for 2 minutes, stir constantly.
Pour chicken stock over rice, add saffron and bay leaf, salt and pepper to taste.
Mix all ingredients.
Place in 450° oven for 20 minutes.
When rice is cooked, all liquid absorbed, remove bay leaf.
Add almonds and mandarin segments. Serve warm.
Serves 4 to 6.

Brown pork chops on both sides and drain grease. Using oven dish, layer pork chops, mushrooms and onion. Top with Minute rice. Combine soup and water; pour over mixture. Cover and bake at 300° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
In a large saucepan, heat the chicken broth; do not let it boil.
Place slices of avocado in the bottom of each soup plate. Top with 2 slices of lemon.
Pour the chicken broth over the avocado and lemon.
Add 1 1/2 tablespoons of sherry to each bowl. Sprinkle chopped parsley on top.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Coat beef with flour, salt and pepper.
Brown in oil at medium heat.
Drain fat.
Drain and reserve liquid from potatoes, carrots and beans.
Add water to make 2 cups.
Add meat.
Stir in tomato sauce and thyme.
Cover and simmer 1 3/4 hours.
Add vegetables. Simmer 15 minutes longer.
Saute onion and green pepper in oil with salt and pepper.
Add sauce and about 1/2 can of water.
Simmer about 30 minutes on low heat.
Put sausage in a baking pan.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Cut into pieces and put into sauce.
Cook on low gas and simmer another 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix butter, sugar, flour and nuts together.
Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Cool.
Place a 14-inch sheet of heavy-duty foil on the counter for each serving.
Oil or spray the foil.
Place fillet(s) on foil. Add lemon juice and spread over fish.
Cover the fillet(s) with any amount you desire of celery, onion, sliced potatoes, salt and butter.
Add small bits of butter, as desired.
Place on grill over medium-low heat for 35 to 45 minutes.
Open and serve.
Mix all dry ingredients except 2 cups of the white flour. Heat milk, syrup and vegetable oil (follow directions on yeast package). Add to flour mixture, then add the egg.
Add the remaining flour until consistency is right.
Let rise until doubled.
Knead and form into loaves.
Let rise again in bread pans, approximately 20 minutes. Bake at 425° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Combine cake mix, oil and eggs in large bowl.
Stir in butterscotch chips and pecans.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto greased baking sheet.
Spread pie filling in bottom of 8-inch square pan.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over filling.
Pour melted butter over cake mix; sprinkle nuts over butter.
Bake at 375 degrees F for 45 minutes or until top is brown and filling bubbles.
Sift all dry ingredients and cut in cheese and butter.
Add ice water and roll to a thickness of 1/8-inch.
Cut in strips and twist.
Bake at 350° for about 15 minutes.
Cook sugar, cornstarch, milk, salt and egg yolks in double boiler until thick.
Remove from fire; add gelatin which has been soaked in water.
Divide mixture and grated chocolate to one half.
Cool other half before adding beaten egg whites.
Let mixtures set in separate bowls in refrigerator until they begin to thicken.
Beat each mixture until smooth.
Pour chocolate mixture into baked graham cracker shell.
Carefully pour white mixture on top.
Let stand in refrigerator several hours.
Serve with whipped cream and grated chocolate.

recipes.t: Quick Raisin Bread(A Very Old Family Recipe)
d: Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cinnamon. Add milk to eggs.
Stir liquid into dry ingredients and mix just until smooth.
Stir in melted fat and raisins (and nuts if desired).
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Let stand 20 minutes. Bake at 350° about 1 hour.
Break eggs in pan; beat them, then put sugar in.
Put milk and water in.
Add vanilla, pineapple with juice and French bread. (Soak bread pieces and put in before pineapple.)
Cut oleo on top. When butter melts; stir.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until done.
Cook butter, flour and milk until thick.
Add onion and cheese.
Cook until cheese melts.
Add paprika; cook until soft and red pink.

Wrap bacon around pork loin. Use toothpicks to hold bacon to loin. Salt and pepper loin. Put loin in bowl or marinade dish. Pour 1/2 cup orange juice over pork loin. Add Worcestershire sauce. Marinate for 8 to 24 hours. Wrap loin in tinfoil and grill at 350°.
In a bowl or Ziploc bag, mix marinade. Combine the olive oil, orange juice, orange zest, garlic, tarragon, salt and pepper.
Blend butter and flour, then press into a 13 x 9-inch pan. Press nuts into top of crust.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool thoroughly.
Mix together shortening, brown sugar, sugar and eggs; stir in sour cream, vanilla, flour and salt.
Place on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
In large mixing bowl, stir together flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
Set aside.
In small mixing bowl, stir together eggs, milk, butter and brown sugar.
Add to flour mixture.
Stir until blended.
Pour batter onto waffle iron.
Bake until steaming stops.
Makes 12 waffles, 4 squares each.
Cream butter and sugar until light.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Blend in vanilla.
Sift cocoa, flour, baking powder, soda and salt together.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with beer, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Stir in sauerkraut, raisins and/or nuts (optional). Turn into two 8 or 9-inch greased and floured cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cool and frost as desired.
Preheat oven to 250° and combine.
Pour melted butter into shallow baking pan.
Stir Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder. Add Chex's and Planters dry roasted peanuts.
Mix until all are coated with sauce.
Heat in 250° oven for 45 minutes.
Stir every 15 minutes.
Spread on paper towel.
Pour into bowl; it's ready to serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, sour cream, oil, vanilla and rum.
Beat 5 minutes; batter will be stiff.
Stir in chocolate pieces and nuts.
Spoon into a greased and floured 2-quart Bundt pan.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean.
Let cool in pan 10 minutes.
Then turn out; serve warm or cold, plain or with vanilla ice cream.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix the dry ingredients together; set aside.
Mix the honey and applesauce together.
Add the egg replacer mixture, banana, raisins and walnuts.
Add the wet mixture to the dry and mix well.
Turn into a nonstick 13 x 9-inch pan and flatten slightly with a spatula.
Bake for 1 hour, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Blend cream cheese, peanut butter, sugar and Cool Whip.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Chill for about two hours.
Cut meat into bite size chunks and place in a large bowl. Thaw and drain carrots, onions and beans.
Clean the mushrooms and cut in half.
Cut yellow pepper into strips.
Add these vegetables to the meat.
Drain syrup from pineapple and add enough water to make 1 1/2 cups liquid.
Heat to boiling; pour over gelatin.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Stir in pineapple and remaining ingredients.
Turn into a 10-inch ring mold and chill until firm. Unmold and garnish with pineapple slices and salad greens as desired.
Serves 10.
Can be frozen.
Melt 3 tablespoons margarine in small saucepan.
Blend in flour and sour cream.
Stir until thick.
Add wine.
Add 1/2 cup of this sauce with bread crumbs and crab meat.
Spread on fillets, roll up.
Place seam side down.
Sprinkle with cracker meal. Garnish with dill.
Dot pan with margarine.
Cook in oven at 350° for 20 or 30 minutes.
Pour remaining sauce over rolls.
Mix this recipe by hand.
Mix oil, sugar, eggs, soda, salt and vanilla flavoring.
Add flour and mix.
Add apples, pecans and coconut.
Bake in a tin pan at 300° for 1 hour, then 30 more minutes at 325° to brown it.
Mix the flour, baking soda and almonds.
Set aside.
Heat butter slowly in a small deep saucepan.
Cool.
Carefully spoon off into a large bowl the clarified butter from top of cloudy solids which have settled at the bottom of the pan.

Add sugar, brandy, lemon juice, extract, oil and egg yolk to butter. Beat well. Add the flour-nut mixture in fourths, mixing thoroughly after each addition. Shape dough into 3/4-inch balls and place on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at
350° for 15 minutes.
In medium saucepan, combine rhubarb, water, sugar and food coloring.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes or until rhubarb is tender.
Remove from heat.
Add gelatin, stirring to dissolve.
Add cream cheese cubes and stir until melted.
Refrigerate 30 minutes or until mixture begins to thicken. Pour into medium size bowl and fold in whipped cream, strawberries and pecans.
Pour into mold or serving container.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Serves 8 to 10.
Rinse the fillets and pat dry.
Place in a baking dish to accomodate the number of fillets you are serving.
Drizzle melted margarine over fillets. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with slivered almonds 10 minutes prior to the finished baking time.
Of course, this can be adapted to your microwave.
Melt butter; blend in paprika.
Dredge chicken breasts in flour, salt and pepper.
Brown in paprika butter, turning until brown on all sides.
Add onions and consomme.
Cover and cook over low heat 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Add sour cream and Bleu cheese.
Continue cooking over low heat 10 to 15 minutes longer.
Serves 4.
Line baking pan with foil.
Dot 1/2 stick of margarine on bottom.
Sprinkle 1/2 onion soup.
Lay steak pieces on margarine. Dot remaining margarine on top of steak; sprinkle with remaining soup.
Cover with green beans.
Do not drain.
Add potatoes.
Add foil to top and fold closed with the bottom of foil.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Sort and wash beans.
Combine beans, water, ham hock, onion, garlic and salt in a large pot.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover and simmer 1 hour.
Remove ham hock and shred ham from bone; return to bean mixture.
Simmer until done.
Soak prunes overnight, saving 2 cups water to use later.
Cut prunes into bits and cook prunes, liquid, sugar and oleo.
Cool. Sift flour, salt, spices and baking soda.
Add beaten eggs and sifted dry ingredients to cooled mix.
Pour into 2 greased 5 x 9-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 350° , one hour.
Yields 1 pound size loaf.
Mix first 4 ingredients well.
Add both milks.
Cool, slowly stirring often and well until thickens.
Add slightly beaten egg yolks.
Cook about 1 minute.
Add butter and vanilla.
Cook about 2 to 3 minutes more, until smooth and thick.
Cool well.
Add to baked pie shell.
Pour boiling water over the rest of the ingredients and stir until all the salt has dissolved and allow to cool.
Chop beef and onions up fine.
Add cream cheese and 1/2 Cheddar cheese.
Mix in Accent and garlic salt.
Roll in remaining cheese.
Serve with crackers.
Cook carrots in cold water until tender, 25 to 30 minutes. Melt butter in saucepan; add brown sugar, ginger and caraway seed. Drain carrots; return to pot and add butter mixture.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve immediately.
Cook beans in water with salt, bacon drippings and meat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours in heavy pot (or crock-pot on low heat for 8 to 10 hours).
Add onion, garlic and bay leaf (for crock-pot, add at the beginning).
If beans become dry, add small amount of hot water. Serve on mounds of rice; also good with tossed salad and French bread.
Serves 4.
Mix first 5 ingredients together.
Make into patties.
Brown patties on both sides and put in a casserole.
Cover with one can of onion soup and one can of water.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Blend first four ingredients.
Add spices.
Add molasses, soda, sour milk and flour to make dough stiff enough to roll.
Mixture will be soft and gooey; roll in plenty of flour.
It will stick and be gooey.
Roll 1/2-inch thick.
Cut into shapes and bake at 400° for about 12 minutes.
Frost with white frosting and top with coconut.

recipes.t: Eggplant With Hot Garlic Sauce(Based On Honolulu'S Maple Garden Restaurant Recipe)
d: Blend ginger, garlic, sugar, shoyu, vinegar and hot pepper sauce in a bowl.
Mix cornstarch with water in a separate bowl. Blend into first mixture.
Heat the oil to 360° in a wok or deep-fryer.
Cook the eggplant and pork until eggplant is golden brown and pork is tender.
The pork will take much less time to cook.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Remove all but 1 teaspoon of oil from pan.
Add sauce mixture and heat until slightly thickened.
Place eggplant in serving container and pour sauce on top.
Cover and heat in oven or microwave oven before serving.
Do not try to mix or eggplant will break apart.
Makes 4 servings.
Trim off excess fat from ribs.
In a large skillet, brown ribs in oil.
Place in a roasting pan.
Place apple wedges and onion rings over ribs in pan.
Combine all ingredients for sauce.
Baste ribs with sauce.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Uncover.
Pour remaining sauce over ribs.
Bake at 350° for another 40 to 50 minutes or until ribs are no longer pink near the bones.
Preheat oven to 325°.
In a large mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in pineapple and lemon juice.
Fold in the bread cubes.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2 baking dish. Bake uncovered for 35 to 40 minutes or until set. Sprinkle cinnamon over top.
Mix the mashed potatoes with the powdered sugar; roll into balls.
Dip into a mixture made by mixing the chocolate chips and milk chocolate in a double boiler.
Add a small amount of wax to keep thin.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Peel and core apples. Stuff the centers with mixture of brown sugar, raisins and cinnamon.
Roll out pastry and cut into 4 circles approximately 8 inches in diameter, depending on size of the apples.
Place an apple in the center of pastry circle and brush the edge with beaten egg.
Draw up pastry to enfold the apple, pressing edge to seal.
Brush tops of pastry with remaining egg.
Bake in shallow dish for 40 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream.
Grease a 10-inch quiche or pie plate.
Spread cranberries in bottom of dish.
Sprinkle with 1 cup sugar and the pecans.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add remaining sugar and beat until blended.
At low speed beat in flour, shortening and butter.
Pour batter evenly over cranberries and nuts.
Bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour or until golden brown.
In 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan, mix well sugar, ginger and garlic salt.
Set aside.
In large bowl with fork, beat egg whites with teriyaki sauce until blended.
With rubber spatula, stir in walnuts until well coated.
Transfer to jelly roll pan.
Stir with spatula until nuts are coated with sugar mixture.
Bake in preheated 250° oven.
Stir occasionally until coating is dry. Store airtight for up to 3 weeks.
Makes 2 cups.
Saute onion and pepper.
Brown ground meat.
Add all ingredients.
Put into casserole and season.
Add cheese on top and bake in 400° oven for 30 minutes.
Beat shortening until light.
Add brown sugar and beat until fluffy.
Beat in egg to blend.
Sift together flour, baking soda, salt and cocoa.
Beat flour mixture alternately with milk into creamed mixture; stir in nuts.
Drop rounded teaspoonful of dough 2 inches apart onto lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) for 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove from oven and top with marshmallow halves.
Set pan on rack until cookies are cool enough to handle.
Melt chocolate chips with butter; stir in cinnamon.
Holding cookies in hand, use a small spatula and swirl their tops with chocolate mixture to cover marshmallows; cool.
In a glass brandy snifter or fruit bowl, start with pound cake and place each layer on top of the last.
Make 2 or 3 layers of each.
End with Cool Whip and place several whole strawberries on the top.
Serves 12 to 15.
Trim excess fat from meat.
Sprinkle 1 teaspoon salt in large skillet or Dutch oven.
Brown meat slowly on both sides in skillet. Stick cloves into onions.
Add onions to meat along with the carrots, celery, 1/3 cup water, corn syrup and anchovies.
Cover and simmer about 2 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
Transfer meat to serving platter and keep meat warm while preparing gravy. Skim excess fat from pan juices; remove cloves.
Blend the 1/4 cup cold water with the flour; stir into juices (mash carrot if desired).
Cook and stir until mixture is thick and bubbly.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve gravy with roast.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Add milk gradually to peanut butter in a bowl, blending until smooth.
Add pudding mix.
Beat slowly with hand beater or at lowest speed of electric mixer until well blended, about 2 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Spread filling about 1/2-inch thick on 12 of the crackers.
Top with remaining crackers, pressing lightly and smoothing around edges with spatula.
Freeze until firm, about 3 hours.
Makes 12 sandwiches.
Add ingredients in layers.
Put lettuce, onions, peas and mayonnaise, with sugar mixed in, into a 13 x 9-inch glass cake dish.
Refrigerate overnight.
Next day, sprinkle cheese, eggs and bacon on top of salad.
Garnish with tomatoes and/or grated cheese, if desired.
Serve slightly chilled.
Pour pie filling into crust, reserving a couple spoonfuls for top.
Mix milk, instant vanilla pudding and Dream Whip.
Beat together until thick.
Spread over cherries.
Decorate with reserved cherry filling.
Use deep skillet with lid.
Place bacon grease in skillet.
Let melt and add frozen green beans and onion.
Let fry in skillet while you cut up the sausage in about 1/2-inch pieces.
Add sausage.
Scrub potatoes and quarter.
Add to skillet.
Cover.
Let cook on medium-high 1 hour.
Stir every 15 to 20 minutes to prevent burning.
Great served with corn bread.
Serves 5.
Place cucumbers, onions, bell pepper and salt in a large glass bowl.
Refrigerate for two hours.
(Do not drain.)
Whisk together vinegar, sugar and celery seed.
Pour over cucumber mixture and store in refrigerator.
Makes about 10 cups.
Place whole peppers on a broiler pan; broil 4 inches from the heat until the skins blister, about 2 to 3 minutes.
With tongs, rotate pepper slightly; broil until all sides are blistered and lightly blackened.
Place pepper in a brown paper bag; close bag and let stand for 15 to 20 minutes.
Peel off the charred skin and discard; remove stem and seeds.
Cut peppers into 1/4 inch wide strips.
In a shallow container, combine the oil, parsley, garlic, oregano and salt; add peppers and toss.
Cover and chill for 3 to 4 hours.
Serve on lettuce leaves if desired.
Yield: 6 servings.
Sift together the first 5 ingredients into bowl.
Add the shortening and orange rind.
Measure the orange juice and water or milk into a liquid measuring cup.
Add 2/3 of this liquid to dry ingredients.
Beat on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Add remaining liquid and the unbeaten eggs.
Beat 2 more minutes.
Bake in two 8 x 1 1/2-inch greased and floured pans at 350° for about 30 minutes, or until done.
Mix raspberry Jell-O according to directions on package.
Add in cranberry sauce.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch Pyrex.
Place in refrigerator and let set.
After completely set, evenly spread sour cream over Jell-O mixture and place into refrigerator and let chill.
Next, mix cherry Jell-O according to directions on package; set aside and let cool.
When cooled down, carefully pour onto sour cream.
Place into refrigerator and let completely set.
In a 8 to 10-inch heavy frying pan, stir sesame seed over low heat until golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Crush in a mortar and pestle or food processor.
In a bowl, mix onion, soy sauce, oil, vinegar, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, mustard, Worcestershire and sesame seed.
Place steak in a 9 x 13-inch dish and pour sesame mixture over top.
Cover and chill, turning occasionally, at least 4 hours or overnight.
Cook steak over hot coals, turning once to your liking, 5 to 6 minutes a side for medium-rare.
Cut across the grain in thin slices to serve.
Serves 4.
When
the
younger set wants a milk shake, beat the egg; add peaches,
orange
juice
and milk and mix well.
This will make enough for two small-fry appetites.
Cream together 2/3 cup of butter and 1 1/2 cup sugar. Separate 3 egg yolks, reserving the whites.
Slightly beat the yolks and mix with 1 cup of jam; whip into creamed mixture.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda, salt, ground cloves and cinnamon.
Add dry ingredients alternately with 1 cup sour milk. Beat the 3 egg whites and fold into the batter.
Add vanilla. Bake in 3 lined layer cake pans in 350° oven for 25 minutes or until done.
Test with a toothpick.
Cool and frost with cream cheese frosting or a vanilla frosting.
Combine chocolate, brown sugar and evaporated milk.
Bring to a boil.
Add butter and stir occasionally until candy reaches soft ball stage (238°).
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and nuts, mixing until candy begins to harden.
Turn into a buttered 9-inch square pan.
Cut into 2 dozen squares.
Melt corn oil in a large skillet.
Pour vegetables into pan. Sprinkle
salt
and
sugar on top of ingredients.
Cover and cook over
medium
heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Vegetables will be crisp,
just
as
good
the next day, if there are any left. Serves 6 to 8.
Cook 1 cup sugar, cornstarch and water until thick.
Then add Jell-O.
Let cool and add strawberries to mixture.
Mix Cool Whip, sour cream and 3/4 cup sugar.
Spread in between layers and on top. Pour strawberry mixture over this.
Put in refrigerator and chill.
Sift the first 3 ingredients together.
Cream the next 3 ingredients together.
Stir into creamed mixture half dry ingredients.
Add cherry juice and milk.
Add rest of flour. Blend in chocolate (use unsweetened chocolate squares only, not cocoa), pecans and cherries.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
While still warm, spoon on marshmallow cream and cool.
Frost with icing.
Bake cake as directed using high altitude directions.
Cool several hours or overnight.
Slice in 3 layers.
Mix pudding using 1 1/2 cups milk.
Let stand until thick.
Use a large dishpan to chop cabbage in.
Bring vinegar, sugar and salt to boil in large pan.
Add peppers, cabbage and onion. Bring back to boil for about 5 minutes.
Have about 8 to 10 quart jars and lids hot and ready to fill.
Sprinkle chicken breasts with oil and bake in a 13 x 9-inch pan for 45 minutes at 350°; drain.
Melt 1 stick oleomargarine and simmer peppers and mushrooms until slightly soft, about 10 minutes.
Put mushrooms and peppers on chicken breasts. Pour the margarine and juice over chicken breasts.
Pour the Sauterne over all and cover tightly with foil if not serving immediately.
Can be reheated at 250° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cut cheese into triangles.
On ungreased cookie sheet, separate rolls into triangles.
Place 3 slices of pepperoni and one slice of cheese on each roll.
Start at shortest side of triangle and roll to opposite point; curve into crescent shape.
Brush roll with egg white.
Bake 10 to 14 minutes.
Place potatoes and onion on a large piece of heavy-duty foil. Dot with margarine.
Combine cheese, parsley, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour over potatoes.
Fold foil over potatoes and add broth.
Seal the edges well.
Grill, covered, on medium heat for 35 to 40 minutes or until tender.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine 1 cup sugar, butter and 1/4 cup milk in saucepan and cook until small amount forms hard ball in cold water.
Stir constantly after mixture starts to boil.
Remove from fire and stir in 1 1/4 cups hot milk gradually; cool.
Blend shortening, salt and vanilla.
Add 3/4 cup sugar gradually and cream well. Add eggs singly and beat well after each addition.
Sift flour and baking powder 3 times.
Add flour to creamed mixture alternately with butterscotch mixture, mixing each addition until smooth.
Pour in 2 square 8-inch greased pans.
Sprinkle nuts over batter.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Use any type of fruit (I prefer apples) and prepare as for a pie.
In long baking dish, put apple filling in, then take 1 box yellow cake mix and sprinkle over apples.
Slice 1 stick margarine over top of cake mixture.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Real good with ice cream or Cool Whip.
Brown margarine over gentle heat.
Stir in sugar gradually, adding cream as necessary.
Beat in vanilla extract.
Beat until fluffy.
Spread on cake.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large bowl.
Cut in butter with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Stir in cheese and raisins.
Make a well in center of mixture.
Combine egg and milk.
Add to dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.
Spoon into greased and floured muffin pans.
Bake at 425° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove from pans.
Yield: 14 muffins.

recipes.t: Poulet Au Vin Blanc(Chicken With White Wine; Serves 4)
d: Coat chicken with flour, salt and pepper.
Shake off excess flour and reserve.
Cook gelatin, tapioca pudding mix, sugar and orange juice over low heat until thick, approximately 10 minutes.
Cool.
Add remaining ingredients and place in serving bowl.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving.
Best if chilled overnight.
Combine first 8 ingredients in a large bowl.
Pour about 1/3 of mixture into an electric blender; blend until smooth.
Pour into a pitcher or bowl; repeat procedure with remaining mixture. Cover and chill several hours.
Garnish with cucumber slices and fresh dill weed, if desired.
Yield: about 5 cups.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and milk.
Stir dry ingredients together.
Combine with shortening mixture.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.

Brown sausage; drain. In a greased casserole, combine sausage, sauce, pasta and Parmesan cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Top with Mozzarella cheese; heat until cheese melts. Serve with garlic bread and salad.
Fill the kitchen sink with cool water; add about 2 to 3 tablespoons salt and swish around.
Place catfish in water for approximately 30 minutes.
Remove fish from water, rinse and place in large bowl of milk.
Combine cornmeal, flour, salt, cayenne pepper and garlic powder.
Dredge catfish with mixture, shaking off excess.
Fill deep skillet half full with canola oil.
Heat to 350°.
Add catfish in a single layer and fry until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes, depending on size.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Makes 4 servings.
Put together flour, chopped pecans and melted butter in baking dish and bake 15 minutes; cool.
Mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and 1 cup Cool Whip.
Mix and put on top of the crust.
Put remaining ingredients on top of cream cheese mixture.
Add Cool Whip and decorate with chocolate shavings or nuts.
Heat soup, cream cheese and gelatin.
Cool, then add mayonnaise; mix well.
Add whatever else you want (celery, onion, etc.).
Mix well and pour into mold.
Chill about 4 hours or overnight.
Place strawberries in a large bowl, reserving several for garnish; set aside.
Rub sugar cubes over rind of oranges until soaked with oil.
Crush cubes with wooden spoon in a small bowl. Add juice of oranges; stir until sugar is dissolved.
Pour over strawberries.
Cover and chill 2 or 3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with whipped cream, reserved strawberries and mint leaves. Yield: 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Whisk egg yolks with honey for 5 minutes.
Add orange peel.
Sift whole-wheat flour with salt. Gradually stir in egg and honey.
Add wine and olive oil, stirring constantly, as small amounts are added.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and fold into batter.
Line the bottom of an 8-inch spring-form pan with oiled parchment or a brown paper shopping bag.
Oil the pan and paper well.
Pour in batter and bake for 20 minutes.
Turn oven off and let cake sit for 10 minutes.
Remove cake from oven.
Turn over and detach from spring pan carefully.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove from pan.
Drain.
Crumble. Saute onion in bacon grease until wilted but not brown.
Add sauerkraut, tomatoes, brown sugar and salt.
Cook over low heat for 45 minutes.
Add bacon.
Serve.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.

recipes.t: Sweet Onion Sandwich(Don'T Miss This One)
d: Preheat oven to 375°.
In large skillet sprayed with nonstick cooking spray, brown and saute onions over medium heat until brown, adding garlic salt and black pepper while cooking.
Spray one side of bread slices with nonstick cooking spray and toast.
Place thick pile of cooked onions on 2 slices of toast and top with 1 slice cheese.
Warm at 375° long enough to melt cheese.
Top with bread slice and serve warm.
Recipe makes 2 servings.
Ultra low-fat.
Wash and remove stems from mushrooms.
Chop stems.
Saute stems, oil, butter, bread cubes, garlic, salt, basil, oregano and salt.
Fill caps with mix.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350°.
Slice wieners, onions and peppers.
Lightly brown wieners in hot oil in skillet.
Remove to bowl.
In same skillet, cook remaining ingredients until tender, stirring often.
Add wieners and heat thoroughly.
Saute celery and onions with butter.
Cook rice (do not use Minute rice) and drain.
Add soup, Cheez Whiz, broccoli (thawed and uncooked) and water chestnuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until hot completely through.
Into a medium size saucepan measure 1/4 cup of the sugar.
Add cornstarch, salt and water.
Stir to dissolve, then cook over medium heat stirring constantly until mixture thickens.
Add the remaining 3/4 cup of sugar and return to heat; cook until sugar is dissolved.
Add almond flavoring and fresh peaches.
Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour into an 8-inch square pan or pie pan.
Top with cereal mixture, (or the fresh peach mixture can be poured directly into individual serving dishes and then topped with cereal mixture).
Serve with cream, whipped topping or ice cream.
Place cereal in a bowl.
Add sugar, butter and syrup to a saucepan.
Boil 3 minutes; remove from heat and add condensed milk.
Boil additional 3 minutes.
Pour over crisp rice; mix well. Spray Pam into mold (1 time only).
Fill mold with mixture. Press in.
Remove to wax paper; allow to set 1 hour.
Seal in plastic wrap.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove and drain on paper towels. Drain off fat.
Return 1/4 cup to skillet.
Add celery and onion and cook 1 minute.
Blend in flour.
Stir in water and vinegar; cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is thick and bubbly. Stir in sugar, salt and pepper.
Grease bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cover bottom with layer of Rice Krispies and sausage.
Sprinkle with dry onions, rice and Cheddar cheese.
At this point you can freeze for later use. Combine celery soup, eggs and milk.
Mix and pour over casserole. Sprinkle Rice Krispies over the top.
Put in 325° oven for 45 minutes.
Combine chicken, 1/4 cup picante sauce, cream cheese, onion and oregano in skillet.
Place over low heat until cheese is melted. Stir in 1/2 cream cheese.
Place chicken mixture in center of each tortilla.
roll and place seam side down in lightly greased 12 x 7-inch baking dish. Spoon remaining 3/4 cup picante sauce over enchiladas. Cover with remaining cheese. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt butter in 13 x 9 inch baking pan in oven.
Sprinkle graham cracker crumbs over melted butter, stir well and press onto bottom of pan.
Sprinkle with nuts, coconut and Shapes & Morsels.
Pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until light golden brown.
Cool completely in pan on wire rack.
Prepare chicken by loosening the breast skin from the meat. Place 3/4 teaspoon rosemary and 1 tablespoon of butter on each side of the breast under the skin.
Take the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of rosemary and place inside the cavity.
Truss the bird. Sprinkle with salt and pepper to your taste.
Rotisserie for 2 hours, or until meat pulls from the bones easily.
Mix beef with salt and pepper.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
In skillet with lid, heat oil.
Add meat balls and cook, turning or shaking, until browned on all sides.
Soften cream cheese.
Add remaining ingredients except bread, blending well.
Sandwich mixture between bread slices.
Trim crusts.
Cut sandwiches in thirds.
(18 bars).
Combine meat with cracker crumbs, milk and eggs.
Shape into loaf.
Blend mustard, sugar and pineapple juice and bring to a boil.
Pour over ham loaf and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
Melt shortening in a 3 or 4-quart saucepan over low heat. Remove from heat; let cool.
Add sugar, molasses and egg; beat well.
Sift together flour, soda, spice and salt; add to first mixture.
Mix well.
Chill.
Form into 1-inch balls; roll in granulated sugar and place on a greased cookie sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake in a moderately hot 375° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until done.

Place spinach in a 1-quart microwavable casserole dish and microwave on High for 7 to 9 minutes, until defrosted and cooked. Let cool slightly and then place clean dry towel in dish to remove excess water.
In a 2-quart bowl, combine spinach, cream cheese, tomato, onions, garlic and jalapenos.
Microwave on High for 3 to 4 minutes, until mixture is smooth.
Stir in cheese and milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve piping hot with tortilla chips.
Place half of bread in bottom of a shallow, buttered 2 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Mix together next 5 ingredients and spread over bread cubes.
Top with remaining bread cubes.
Beat eggs; add milk and soup.
Pour over casserole.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Top with cheese and bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cut the eel in pieces of 4 to 5 cm each. Spice with salt, pepper, thyme and laurel.
Melt butter in a large pan. Add the chopped spices and slightly stew. Add the eel and cover with the white wine.
When cooking point is reached, put a lid on the pan. Lower the fire and let it all stew for about 15 minutes. Thicken the sauce with the egg yolks and add some lemon juice.
You can eat this delicacy either warm or cold with brown bread or chips and a pint of beer! Cheers!
Line pie plate with 3 squares of crescent roll dough.
Save remaining square for strips for top of pie.
In a large bowl, mix beaten egg, salami, cheeses and seasonings.
Place meat mixture in pie shell.
Use remaining square; cut strips and lace top of pie.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour or until brown.
Enjoy.
Pack wieners, onions and peppers in a gallon jar.
Heat vinegar and spices and pour over wieners.
Keep out of refrigerator.
These will keep indefinitely.
Good to take on camping trips.
Combine powdered sugar, peanut butter and peanuts until consistency of
biscuit
mix.
Spread
of this mixture on baked
crust bottom.
Combine cornstarch, sugar, salt and milk and mix
well.
Add
gradually
to
beaten
egg yolks and cook until thickened.
Add
butter
and vanilla and carefully pour custard over
mixture in baked crust.
Top with meringue, made with 3
egg whites and 6 tablespoons sugar.
Sprinkle meringue with balance of
peanut butter mixture and bake at 325° until lightly browned.
Saute onion and green pepper in butter.
Stir in
chili. Prepare corn muffin mix according to package directions.
Spread corn muffin batter on the bottom of greased 2-quart casserole. Spoon chili mixture over batter.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes in a 400° oven or until cornbread is done (an inserted toothpick comes out clean).
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Using a food processor, shred the cabbage and carrot.
Add the pineapple and dressing.
Mix well and chill.
Toss peas, onions and bacon together.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add sufficient sour cream to hold together.
This salad is best made one day ahead and kept in refrigerator.
Stir occasionally to mix flavors.
Brown onion in bacon drippings.
Add ground beef and brown. Add tomato soup, water, uncooked noodles, salt and pepper.
Cook until noodles are tender.
Add corn.
Place in baking dish.
Cover with grated cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Yields 4 to 5 servings.
If using navel orange, peel and section it, then cut sections into bite-sized pieces.
Combine rice, fruit, peppers and almonds. In small bowl, whisk together salad oil, seasoned rice vinegar, cinnamon, lime juice and honey; pour over rice mixture and gently stir.
Chill.
Serve with honey-mustard dressing.
Mix Bisquick and cheese.
Stir in eggs and butter or oleo. Fold in zucchini.
Fry in butter or oleo.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes on each side.
Put acini de pepe, salt and oil in boiling water.
Cook until tender, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Rinse and drain pasta.
Cool to room temperature.
Add pineapple, sugar, marshmallows and cherries to the pasta.
Sprinkle pudding mix over this and mix lightly. Add coconut, pecans and Cool Whip; fold in lightly.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.
In a large mixing bowl, mash bananas with mixer (30 seconds). Add cake mix, milk, oil, eggs and vanilla.
Blend on low for 1 minute, scrape down sides of bowl and beat 2 minutes on medium. Add chocolate chips.
Pour into 6 (6-inch) loaf pans that have been sprayed and floured.
Press crescent rolls onto a large round pizza pan or jelly roll pan.
Bake at 375° about 10 minutes.
Cool.
Spread mixture of cream cheese, mayonnaise and Ranch dressing on cooled crescent rolls.
Top with peas, small pieces of broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, fresh mushrooms or any other vegetables you prefer. Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over vegetables.
Great finger food.
Preheat skillet to 325°.
Brown hamburger and drain fat. Sprinkle meat with salt and pepper.
Add cooked celery, carrots and potatoes.
Simmer 30 minutes, covered.
Prepare strawberry Jell-O according to package directions. Refrigerate until the consistency of syrup.
Slice cake in thin serving pieces and line bottom of 13 x 9-inch glass pan.
Layer partially thawed strawberries on cake; pour syrupy Jell-O over top.
Refrigerate until firm.
Prepare vanilla pudding according to package directions, using 2 3/4 cups milk instead of 3 cups. Cool pudding and spread on Jell-O - strawberry layer.
Refrigerate 2 to 4 hours.
Cover with whipped cream and nuts.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Sprinkle meat with seasoned flour.
Brown with onion.
Cover and cook slowly for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until meat is almost tender.
Add potatoes, carrots and celery.
Cook for 20 to 30 minutes.
Add peas during last 8 to 10 minutes of cooking. Makes 4 servings.
Remove skin.
Mix flour, paprika, salt and pepper on sheet of waxed paper.
Place bread crumbs on another sheet of waxed paper. Beat egg white and milk in pie tin.
Coat chicken in flour mixture, dip into egg mixture and coat with bread crumbs.
In large pan, arrange chicken pieces.
Bake 25 minutes in 475° oven.
Turn and bake 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Smoked Pork Chops
d: Brown chops on both sides in butter in a large skillet.
Pour broth over chops.
Cover and simmer 20 to 30 minutes, or until tender.
Remove chops from skillet; set aside.
Combine cornstarch, brown sugar, soy sauce and vinegar; stir well and add to pan drippings.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Return chops to skillet.
Add green pepper, onions and pineapple.
Cover and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.

recipes.t: Mama Watts' No Crust Coconut Pie
d: Melt margarine and add sugar and flour.
Beat in eggs and add milk and flavoring; mix well.
Pour into 2 well-greased 9-inch pie pans or 1 large pie pan.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup coconut on top of each pie.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes until golden brown.
One pie takes about 45 minutes, less for 2!
In heavy saucepan, over low heat, combine sweetened condensed milk, chips and salt.
Cook and stir until chips melt.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vinegar and cinnamon.
Serve warm with apple wedges for dipping.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Sprinkle chicken pieces on both sides with salt and paprika. Cook walnuts in oil, stirring, until lightly browned.
Remove nuts with slotted spoon.
Drain on paper towels, reserve.
Brown chicken pieces well in same pan.
To chicken add ginger, onion, garlic and tomato juice.
Bring to boiling.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer until chicken is tender, about 40 minutes.
Remove chicken to serving dish and keep warm.
Skim fat; cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced and slightly thickened.
Taste, add salt, if needed.
Pour over chicken, sprinkle with reserved walnuts and parsley.
Cook noodles according to directions on box.
Brown hamburger and season to taste with salt, pepper, chili powder and Italian seasoning.
Add spaghetti sauce and simmer.
Combine cream cheese, sour cream, cottage cheese and onion in a bowl.
Mix well.
Layer 1/2 of noodles in bottom of 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan (approximately 5 to 6 pieces).
Spread 1/2 of cheese mixture and 1/2 of sauce mixture.
Layer rest of noodles, cheese mixture and top with sauce.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, combine the soy sauce, chili powder and garlic.
Add skinned and cut up chicken and scallions (cut into 1-inch sections with green tops), and stir to coat the chicken well.
Flatten biscuits on ungreased baking sheet with bottom of floured custard cup.
This will leave a rim.
Fill biscuit centers with onion mixture. Bake in oven following directions on biscuit can.
In buttered 9 x 9-inch baking dish, place a layer of cubed chicken, bread crumbs, cheese and broccoli.
Combine soup, milk and pepper; pour over mixture.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350°; let stand for 5 minutes.
Serves 6.
Saute onion and green pepper until onion is transparent.
Stir in flour until smooth and then add milk gradually, stirring constantly.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Remove from heat; add cheese, salt, pepper and sugar.
Stir together, then add beaten eggs.
Pour into greased 7 x 10-inch Pyrex casserole.
Top with bread crumbs which have been tossed with 2 teaspoons of melted margarine.
Set in shallow pan of hot water.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
I prepare the sauce ahead of time and put it into my crock-pot to simmer about 3 hours ahead of time.
The sauce consists of the hamburger, pork burger, spaghetti sauce, green pepper and onion. This makes the sauce thicker.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Slice Italian bread in half and place on foil.
Mix scallion, mayonnaise, garlic, seasoning, mushrooms and cheeses.
(It is best if this mixture marinates about 2 hours.)
Spread mixture on bread.
Place bread in oven for approximately 5 minutes until cheese begins to melt. Set oven on broil until cheese is finished melting and bread browns.
Be careful not to burn.
Bread will brown in 1 to 2 minutes. Serve.
Heat applesauce.
Remove from heat.
Stir in gelatin until dissolved.
Add orange juice and pineapple.
Add celery and nuts. Chill until ready to serve.
Combine greens, zucchini, carrot and peanuts; toss.
Pour dressing over salad; toss.
Serve.
Place meat and onions in 10-inch skillet. Cook until beef loses pink color.
Drain.
Spread soup over beef.
Add noodles, zucchini and seasoning over beef.
Simmer, covered, until noodles are done.
Stir in sour cream and warm through.
Wash and drain sauerkraut.
Mix sugar, salad oil, vinegar and water well.
Pour over salad and marinate overnight.
Drain before serving.
In blender container, combine milk, Choco-bake and vanilla. Process at high speed until smooth, about 15 seconds.
Add ice cream, blend until smooth.
Serve immediately.
Dissolve cheese and butter in boiler;
Add milk, flour and salt.
Mix well.
Spread cherries in bottom of greased 9 x 12-inch baking dish. Sprinkle dry cake mix on top.
Top with almonds.
Pour butter evenly over all.
Bake 45 minutes in 375° oven, until nuts are brown.
Put crushed graham crackers in a big bowl and add marshmallows, coconut and chopped nuts.
Heat the sugar, eggs, butter and vanilla over low heat; cool.
Pour over first mixture, then into cake pan and pat down with a spoon.
Put in refrigerator.
Cut into bars. They are better if stored a day before using.
Drain fruit and mix with marshmallows, coconut and cottage cheese.
Serve immediately or pour into mold and chill from 8 to 10 hours in refrigerator.
Serves 8.
Oil a covered casserole large enough to hold mixture.
Combine rice and vegetables in casserole.
Pour consomme over mixture. Cover casserole.
Put in oven and bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Remove casserole from oven.
Stir gently and return to oven, uncovered, for about 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed.

recipes.t: Chipped Beef And Cream Cheese Party Dip
d: Blend together first 4 ingredients.
Add chopped green pepper, onion flakes and garlic salt.
Heat nuts in melted butter and sprinkle over top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Serve warm from plate with assorted crackers.

recipes.t: Fat-Free Chocolate Strawberry Brownies(This Recipe Is Adapted From A Recipe Printed In The Baltimore
d: Heat oven to 325°.
Thoroughly coat a 9 x 13-inch pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Set aside.
With an electric mixer, combine the sugar and cocoa.
Gradually pour in the egg substitutes and jam/preserves, beating on low speed until the sugar is no longer grainy.
Add the vanilla, salt and almond extract and beat briefly to mix.
Combine the flour and baking soda and stir in with a flexible rubber spatula.
Do not overmix.
Pour into prepared pan and bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Brownies should be slightly underbaked but not runny in the center.
Allow to cool and cut into 2 x 2-inch bars.
Hollow out onions.
Make stock.
In pan, brown onion flesh with garlic and margarine.
Add Maggi and water.
Add celery; simmer.
In medium saucepan over medium heat, saute peppers and onion slices in oil until tender.
Stir in steak sauce and horseradish; keep warm.
In lightly greased medium skillet over medium-high heat, cook sandwich steaks until done.
On roll bottoms, portion beef, pepper mixture and cheese.
Broil sandwich bottoms for 3 to 5 minutes until cheese melts; replace tops.
Serve immediately. Makes 4 sandwiches.
With serrated knife, cut hollow into bread 1/2-inch away from sides and bottom; remove from loaf.
Cut piece which has been removed from loaf into strips, 1 to 1 1/2-inch wide strips.
Mix oil and garlic.
Brush inside of shell and bread slices.
Place cut up cheese in bread shell.
Place filled shell and slices in a single layer on a 10 x 15-inch pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°. Remove bread slices.
Cook filled shell 10 minutes more and serve with grapes.
Serves 10 to 12 people.

Beat milk, eggs, margarine, Splenda and vanilla in a large bowl with electric mixer for 30 seconds. Add mashed bananas and beat 1 minute. Add flour mixture. Mix with spoon until just blended. Put into greased or sprayed muffin tins or nonstick muffin pans. Bake at 350° approximately 20 to 25 minutes.
Layer with beans, roast, onion and seasonings and then pour tomato sauce on top.
Cover with water to 2 1/2 inches from the top of the roaster pan.
Bake at 250° for 12 hours in oven.
This may be cooked in a slow cooker.
Cook on low for approximately 12 to 18 hours.
Add a salad and bread and you have Sunday dinner.
Puree 1/3 peppers and vinegar at a time in a blender.
Add salt, sugar and mustard to puree mixture and bring to boil.
Boil for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Mix flour and water to a paste mixture and add to mixture while it is at a boil.
To make hotter, add hot pepper seeds.
The more seeds the hotter it is. Put in sterilized canning jars and seal.
Makes 8 to 10 pints.
In the top of a double boiler over simmering water melt the butter and chocolate.
Add the water and vanilla and stir until blended.
Add the sugar and whisk until smooth.
Pour over the cooled cheesecake.
Garnish with the strawberries.
Saute bacon until crisp in a kettle.
Remove and set aside for next step.
Stir onion into drippings in kettle; saute until soft. Add potatoes, salt and clam juice.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in clams, tomatoes, thyme and cooked bacon.
Simmer 15 minutes longer.
You may use fresh clams instead of canned, but be sure to grind them and still juice the bottle of clam juice.
Cream sugar, shortening, cinnamon, ginger, ground cloves and salt.
Add 2 eggs and mix well.
Add syrup.
Add molasses and mix. Mix in flour.
Save about 1 cup flour for rolling dough. Refrigerate dough a couple of hours or more.
Roll and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Sugar tops of cookies after they are rolled.
In a bowl, combine the fruit (except bananas) and lemon juice. Sprinkle with pudding mix. Stir gently for 1 minute or until mixture thickens. Fold in bananas. Refrigerate before serving.

Combine apples, sugars, cornstarch, spices and salt and let stand while preparing crust. Fit bottom pastry in an 8-inch pie pan. Fill with apple mixture. Drizzle with melted butter. Top with other pie pastry. Seal and flute edges. Brush top crust with milk. Then sprinkle lightly with sugar. Bake at 400° for 50 to 55 minutes.
Saute celery and onion in a tablespoon of margarine or oil. Mix soups and milk in a large saucepan.
Add celery and onions; stir well.
Add water chestnuts and chicken.
Mix lightly.
In a 7 x 11-inch baking dish, put a layer of dry noodles in the bottom. Add chicken mixture and top with rest of noodles and slivered almonds.
Bake 30 minutes in 350° oven.
Serves 6 to 8.
A cranberry salad and green peas go well with this.
Sprinkle salt over pork chops and fry in cooking oil.
Set aside to cool.
In a large pan, cook noodles in water.
Add salt and cook until tender.
Drain.
Add mushroom soup and peas. Simmer while you chop pork chops into chunks.
Add pork chops and cook an additional ten minutes on low heat.
Serve.
Cook spinach according to directions.
Wash mushrooms, cut off stems, chop stems and reserve.
Slice mushrooms thinly.
Prepare cheese mix according to directions.
Reserve 2 cups for topping. When sauce thickens, add cheese, well drained spinach and sliced mushrooms.
Simmer five minutes.
Cream
shortening;
gradually
add sugar, beating until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each. Combine
flour,
baking powder and salt; add to creamed mixture alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Mix
well
after each addition.
Stir in flavorings. Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans. Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes or until a wooden toothpick comes out clean. Cool
in
pans for 10 minutes.
Remove from pans
and
let
cool completely.
Spread Lemon-Orange Filling between layers.
Spread top
and
sides
with
Luscious White Frosting and sprinkle with coconut.
Yield: one 3-layer cake.
Bake the chicken.
Cook broccoli according to package.
Drain. Put broccoli in a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Place chicken on top of broccoli.
Mix other ingredients and pour over chicken. Sprinkle mixture with butter and bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Wrap each trout in aluminum foil individually; place in baking pan.
Dot with butter.
Pour the wine over them.
Cover with green peppers, onions and tomato slices.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper or garlic salt and paprika. Seal the aluminum foil.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, or until flesh flakes easily away from the bones when touched with a fork. Serves 1 trout per person.
All liquids should be cold.
In punch bowl, combine pineapple, grapefruit and lemon juices and lemonade mix and water.
Carefully pour in carbonated beverage.
Add sherbet.
About 2 hours before serving, place butter, brown sugar and spices in skillet.
Drain pear halves; arrange on top of butter mixture.
Set aside.
With spoon, scoop out 6 to 8 servings of ice cream into individual bowls and return to freezer until 10 minutes before serving.
Simmer pear halves in butter mixture in skillet for 10 minutes, turning occasionally.
Place a hot pear half on top of ice cream.
Spoon glaze over top of each pear.
Place melon cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Cover and freeze 30 minutes or until firm.
Position knife blade in food processor bowl; add frozen melon, sherbet and lime juice.
Process until smooth.
Pour into glasses.
Garnish with strawberries if desired.

Combine egg whites, sugar, and salt. Beat in rest of ingredients one at a time. Blend well and chill for 20 minutes. Preheat oven to 350. Do just 2-3 cookies at a time. Drop slightly rounded teaspoon full of thick batter for each cookie on a greased cookie sheet. Spread the dough very thin using the back of the spoon, make rounds about 3 inches in diameter. Bake for 5 minutes or until edges turn light brown. Place on wire rack. Working quickly place a fortune in each cookie, fold opposite sides together, crease crosswise at the center of the straight edge to form a flattened side, then bend backward to form the traditional shape. Cool in muffin tins to hold shape. Yields 4 dozen.
Cook sugar, syrup, milk and peanuts over low heat.
Cook until soft ball stage.
Remove from heat; add oleo and vanilla.
Butter platters and drop by tablespoons on plate.
Combine
flour, salt, pepper and allspice.
Dredge meat, reserving excess flour.
Brown meat in shortening. Remove meat to Dutch oven or large pan. Heat apple juice and bouillon cube and stir to dissolve.
Pour liquid over meat; cover tightly and cook slowly 2 hours.
Add carrots, celery, potatoes and thyme; cover and
continue
cooking for 30 minutes, or until meat and vegetables are
tender.
Remove
meat
and
vegetables to warm platter.
Yield: 8 to 10 servings.
Mix together first 4 ingredients with your hands. Shape into 2-inch balls.
Melt chocolate chips and wax together on low to medium heat. Roll peanut butter balls in
melted chocolate.
Put in refrigerator on waxed paper and let cool and dry.
Combine cooked rice and Italian salad dressing; cover and chill several hours or overnight.
Add mayonnaise to undrained rice mixture and stir until combined.
Fold in radishes, cucumber, chopped tomato, green pepper, celery and green onion.
Press into 5 1/2 cup ring mold.
Cover, refrigerate at least 2 to 3 hours.
Stir
flour into strips of meat.
Add soy sauce and let set for 1/2 hour.
Saute onions and bell peppers in 1/4 stick margarine.
Brown
steak
in 1/4 stick margarine; stir to keep from
burning.
Add
peppers,
onions,
salt and pepper.
Cook rice
in
water.
When done, stir rice into meat mixture.
Add more soy sauce to desired taste.
In a mixing bowl, combine hamburg, onion, mushrooms, egg, soup and spices.
Mix well with hands.
Crush crackers with hands and add to mixture.
Mix.
Place in bread pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Mix first 6 ingredients until smooth.
Cut butter and flour together until size of beans.
Pour liquid mixture over dry ingredients.
Mix with spatula just until flour is moist. Refrigerate at least 4 hours up to 4 days.
Bring water and sugar to boil.
Add peanuts.
Cook slowly and keep stirring until dry.
Put on a cookie sheet and bake slowly at 250° until peanuts get done.
Make a circular cut around the stem end of the tomatoes; remove this part and squeeze tomatoes to remove the water and seeds without spoiling their shape.
Season with salt and place in an oiled baking dish.
Bake for 4 minutes in a 450° oven.
Stuff tomatoes with mushroom stuffing, prepared as follows:
Saute chopped onion in butter and add finely chopped mushrooms.
Brown until almost all liquid has evaporated.
Season with salt and parsley.
Bake stuffed tomatoes in a 450° oven for about 15 minutes.
Serve immediately.

recipes.t: Chicken Fruit Salad With Poppy Seed Dressing
d: Slice pineapple in half through fruit and leaves lengthwise (top to bottom).
Scoop out pineapple and cut fruit into 1-inch chunks.
Drain; combine fruit and chicken.
Toss lightly with dressing and chill.
Spoon into pineapple shells.
Sprinkle top with nuts and serve.
Mix chocolate bar, milk and marshmallows; heat until melted, stirring until smooth.
Cool to room temperature.
Whip the heavy or whipping cream until stiff; fold into chocolate mixture.
Pour into crust.
Chill several hours, until firm.
May garnish with whipped cream and shaved chocolate.
Sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper.
Arrange chicken, skin down, in greased shallow baking dish.
Combine oil, honey, lemon juice, paprika and mustard in small bowl; baste chicken with sauce.
Cover and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Turn chicken and brush with sauce.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until tender.
Remove crust from bread and cut into 1-inch squares.
In double boiler, melt cheese and margarine.

When creamy, fold in egg whites. Dip cubes into mixture and place on wax paper lined cookie sheet and freeze. When frozen, place in plastic bag and keep in freezer. To serve, bake at 450° for 8 minutes.
Cut eggplant into 1-inch thick slices lengthwise.
Cut the slices into strips 1-inch wide.
Cut the strips into 1-inch cubes. These should be about 6 cups.
Heat the oil in a heavy flameproof casserole and add the eggplant cubes.
Cook stirring about 2 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, red wine vinegar, water, bay leaf, coriander, thyme and salt and pepper to taste.
Blend well.
Bring to a simmer.
Cover the casserole and cook 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Scrape the mixture into a serving bowl and let stand until cool before serving.
Combine the juice concentrate, sugar, dry milk, vanilla and cold water in a blender and process at high speed.
Add ice cubes, a few at a time.
