Blend until slushy.
Serve immediately.
Yields 4 servings.
A very refreshing cool drink on a hot day and evening.
Melt butter; add sugar, eggs, coconut and raisins.
Mix well, then add vanilla and vinegar.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes.
On strip of foil, place hamburger patty, string beans and potato in that order.
Sprinkle on salt and pepper.
Close foil tightly.
Place in a 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Take 1 egg white and brush over pie shell.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Saute onion in butter until golden.
Sprinkle pie shell with cheese, then ham, then onion.
Beat egg slightly and add remaining ingredients.
Beat until well combined.
Pour over cheese mixture.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until golden.
Chop 1 onion into small pieces; drain your choice of meat. Mix with cream cheese.
Mix all ingredients together and serve on crackers.
Beat together water, eggs, vegetable oil, honey and sugar. Mix flour with baking soda, salt, cinnamon and allspice.
Add gradually to liquid mixture, stirring just to blend.
Fold in citron and coconut. Spoon into a greased and floured 9 x 5 x 4-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center of loaf comes out clean. Cool on rack in pan 10 minutes.
Carefully remove from pan and cool on rack. Wrap cooled loaf in aluminum foil and store overnight before cutting.
Press dough into a cookie sheet with sides.
Cold dough is easier to work with.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Let cool. Mix cream cheese, 1/2 cup sugar and vanilla.
Spread over cooked crust.
In a saucepan over medium heat, cook, stirring constantly, until thick and bubbly, 1/2 cup sugar, the orange and lemon juice and the cornstarch.
Let cool to lukewarm.
Place a variety of sliced fresh fruit such as kiwi, strawberries, peaches, grapes, etc. over the crust.
Cover with the fruit juice mixture.
Chill at least 4 hours.
Mix cottage cheese with dry Jell-O.
Use electric mixer.
Add pineapple.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Chill until firm.
I use an 8 x 11-inch Pyrex pan for this.
To serve, cut in squares and put on lettuce.
Fill tortilla with cheese; melt in microwave for 45 seconds. Top with sauce.
The night before, cook linguine and refrigerate.
Mix Salad Supreme and Italian dressing; refrigerate overnight.
Chop veggies; add to both linguine and salad dressing.
Salt and pepper chicken lightly.
Roll in flour.
Melt butter in large casserole.
Place chicken in butter and heat oven to 425°.
Bake 30 minutes, uncovered.
Turn and bake 15 to 20 minutes.
In a saucepan reduce wine by 1/2 and remove it from heat.
Add preserves and Worcestershire sauce and let cool.
Arrange chicken and peaches in a glass baking dish.
Top with preserve mixture and marinate overnight.
Sprinkle brown sugar over the top and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serve over steamed rice.
Peel and cut cucumbers and onions into thin slices.
Add cucumbers, onion and remaining ingredients in a bowl and toss.
Rinse turkey and pat dry.
Melt butter and add flour to make a paste.
(Paste should be heavy enough to stick to turkey without falling off.)
Prepare grill for indirect cooking with pan under turkey.
While coals are heating, cover turkey in paste.
This prevents the need for basting.
Cook turkey on grill for 13 minutes a pound, or until it reads 170° on meat thermometer.
(Don't touch bone with thermometer.)
Add 8 coals per side every hour until turkey cooks.
This turkey is moist and beautifully pink edged with good smoky flavor.
Saute onion in butter until slightly browned; spoon into pie shell.
Add milk and 1 1/4 cups of the sour cream.
Blend flour and salt with remaining 1/2 cup sour cream.
Skin chicken and dry with paper towel.
In bag, combine flour, salt and pepper.
Shake chicken in mixture.
Heat oil slowly.
Brown chicken on both sides.
Place in baking dish (13 x 9-inch).
In small bowl, combine vinegar and sugar, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Blend in remaining ingredients.
Brush chicken with sauce and pour remaining over chicken.
Bake, covered, for 30 to 45 minutes.
Place cinnamon, cloves, and allspice in a double thickness of cheesecloth; bring up the corners of cloth and tie with a string to form a bag.
Place cider and brown sugar in a slow cooker; stir until sugar dissolves.
Add spice bag.
Place orange slices on top.
Cover and cook for 2-5 hours.
Remove spice bag before serving. Yield: 2 quarts.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Beat eggs, then add pumpkin, oil and bran cereal.
Add dry ingredients, mixing only until combined.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts.
Cook beef until browned; drain fat.
Add pepper and onions. Cook until tender.
Stir in everything else except cheese.
Spoon half of the meat mixture into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Top with half of the cheese.
Spoon remaining meat mixture over cheese.
Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Top with remaining cheese.
Let stand loosely covered until cheese melts.
Serves 8 to 10.
Cook angel hair pasta according to directions. While pasta is cooking, cut up the vegetables.
Mix pasta, vegetables, dressing and spices while pasta is still warm. Top with grated cheese. Refrigerate overnight.
In skillet, brown hamburger meat.
Do not drain.
Add flour (sufficient amount to make a gravy).
Add milk until just barely covers meat in pan.
If gets too thick, add more.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Serve on white bread.
In small bowl, with electric mixer at medium speed, beat cheese, milk, ginger and 3 tablespoons limeade concentrate until smooth.
Set aside.
In large bowl, toss avocado and strawberries with remaining limeade.
Place vanilla ice cream and frozen orange juice concentrate in punch bowl.
Add pineapple juice and ginger ale.
Stir and serve.
Place thawed turkey in roasting bag and bake at 350° about 4 to 6 hours.
The last hour of cooking, stuff with the following: Mix seasoned and cornbread dressings together with chicken broth, 2 cups chopped (finely) celery and 2 cups of chopped onions.
If more broth is needed, take from turkey bag.
Place prepared dressing around turkey and finish baking.
Turkey can be served whole on platter with dressing placed around it or you can debone turkey before serving.
Mix cake mix, oil and oranges with juice.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating after each one.
Pour batter into 2 (9-inch) greased cake pans.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until it tests done. Cool.
Combine pineapple, juices, pudding mix and whipped topping. Spread over cake and between layers.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.t: Egg Bread For Muffins, Corn Sticks, Or Bread
d: Heat oven to 450 degrees. Grease and heat pan. Beat egg and add milk and shortening. Blend in meal and sugar. Pour into hot greased pan. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Makes about 14 muffins, 18 sticks or 1 medium size skillet of bread.
In large bowl, beat eggs at high speed until thick and fluffy. In separate bowl, combine sugar and oil.
Beat into eggs.
Sift together flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt.
Add to egg mixture, along with vanilla.
Stir in nuts.
Spread apples in a buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Pour batter over apples.
Spread to cover apples.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Split each almond into 2 halves.
Using mortar and pestle, crush the cumin, coriander and saffron together.
Soak the raisins in hot water for a few minutes and drain.
Saute all of these ingredients for a few minutes in the butter.
Add the cooked rice and toss to color the rice and coat each grain with butter.
Add salt and freshly ground pepper to taste.
Serving Size:
8. Preparation Time:
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine first 5 ingredients in 1 1/2-quart saucepan.
Cook until butter melts, stirring constantly. Add sour cream.
Drain green beans; then add.
Mix well.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Top with cheese and crackers.
Sprinkle butter over top.
Bake 30 minutes.
In small bowl, combine first 4 ingredients until smooth; spread into crust.
Chill while preparing filling.
In medium bowl, combine pudding mix and milk with electric mixer; beat at low speed for 2 minutes.
Fold in 1 cup whipped topping and coconut; spread over chocolate.
Spread remaining topping over pudding.
Cover and freeze until firm but not frozen.
To serve, hull strawberries and cut in half.
Arrange berries on top of pie. Makes 8 servings.

recipes.t: Chicken, Green Beans And Rice(Low Calorie And Fat)
d: Cook chicken ahead and cut up.
Saute chicken, mushrooms and garlic in oil for 2 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients, except rice.

(**For broth, use liquid from cooking chicken and use liquid drained from green beans and mushrooms; if more is needed, add water and a small amount of chicken base for 13 3/4 ounces.) Bring to a boil; stir in rice.
Remove from heat; cover and let stand 5 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Cut unpeeled potatoes and zucchini into 1/2-inch pieces.
Heat oil in skillet.
Add potatoes.
Stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth.
Cover and cook over low heat 5 minutes.
Add onion, zucchini, tomato and seasonings.
Stir.
Cover and cook until vegetables are tender.
Mix drained tuna, dressing, mustard, vegetables, pimento, seasonings and 1/2 cup of the bread crumbs.
Shape mixture into 15 (2-inch) balls.
Roll in remaining 3/4 cup bread crumbs, coating well.
Flatten balls into small patties.
Refrigerate 30 minutes. Heat 1/2 cup oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add tuna patties.
Cook 5 minutes on each side or until golden brown, adding additional oil, as needed.
Remove from skillet; drain on paper towels.
Makes 8 servings.

recipes.t: Lemon Garlic Brussels Sprouts And Carrots
d: In large skillet over medium heat, melt margarine.
Add Brussels sprouts, carrots, garlic, basil and pepper.
Saute about 7 minutes until tender, stirring frequently.
Stir in lemon juice; cook about 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Makes 6 servings, 2/3 cup each.

recipes.t: Currant Jelly(This Recipe Takes Some Time.)
d: Wash fruit and mash.
Place in saucepan.
Add water and simmer 10 minutes, stirring often.
Place in jelly bag (similar to a cheesecloth that allows liquid to drain through) and let drain several hours.
Do not squeeze.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Heat butter in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan until melted.
Remove and stir in seasoning.
Add Chex mix until all pieces are coated.
Mix in nuts.
Heat 20 minutes, stirring midway.
Remove and sprinkle evenly with cheese.
Toss to coat all pieces.
Spread on paper towels to cool.
Slice squash and cook in salted water until tender.
Drain in colander.
Beat eggs together with chopped onion.
Add squash and butter.
Cover bottom of casserole with squash mixture. Slice fresh tomatoes thinly
and place on top of squash. Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Repeat layers ending with cheese on top.
Sprinkle with paprika and bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 8.

recipes.t: Lillie'S Crispy Bread And Butter Pickles
d: Soak whole cucumbers in mixture of lime and water overnight. Mix until lime dissolves, rinse cucumbers and drain.
Slice cucumbers into 1/4 inch slices and return to large container.
Add onions.
Pour salt over all and mix well.
Cover with cubed or chipped ice and let stand for 3 hours.
Drain container.
In a large kettle, mix vinegar, sugar and spices, tied in a cheese cloth bag.
Bring mixture to a rolling boil.
Add onions and cucumbers and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pack into jars, remove spices and pour hot syrup into jars to within 1/2 inch of the top and seal.
Combine flour, butter, brown sugar and nuts.
Bake at 325° in long Pyrex dish for 20 minutes.
Stir every 5 minutes until light brown.
Cool, but remove enough crumbs to sprinkle on top of mixture.
Leave a good layer in dish.
In large bowl, beat frozen berries, sugar, egg whites, cream cheese, lemon juice and salt. Beat slowly and gradually increase to high speed.
Beat about 10 minutes, then fold in whipped topping.
Pour over crumbs and top with crumbs.
Freeze.
Can be served with berries on top.
(Can be made a day ahead.)
Halve beans lengthwise.
Saute onion in margarine in saucepan until soft.
Stir in beans.
Toss until well coated.
Stir in seasonings, 1/4 cup water and bouillon cube, crushing bouillon with spoon until dissolved.
Cover.
Cook for 10 minutes or until beans are crisp-tender.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Grate or blend apples to fine consistency.
Chop dates.
Grind sunflower seeds finely in nut mill.
Add other ingredients.
Form mixture into cake shape.
Garnish with additional coconut or strawberries.
Refrigerate to set.
Slice before serving.
Serves 4 to 8.
Grind pepper with onions. Drain and put in vinegar mix. Simmer 20 minutes. Drain and pack in hot jars. Spoon hot vinegar to wet relish.
Seal jars.
Cream sugar, butter, egg and vanilla until light and fluffy. Sift flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon together.
Stir into creamed mixture.
Fold in nuts and apples.
Spread into a well-greased and floured (8-inch) pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
In a medium bowl, stir cream cheese with a spoon until soft. Add dry pudding mix, dry milk and pineapple with juice.
Mix well. Blend in 1 tsp. coconut extract, rum extract and 1/4 cup Cool Whip. Spread mixture evenly into pie crust.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes. In a small bowl, combine remaining 3/4 cup Cool Whip and 1/2 tsp. coconut extract.
Spread mixture evenly over cheesecake filling. Sprinkle coconut evenly over top.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Serves 8. 233 calories per serving (7 grams fat).
Cook box of macaroni to package directions.
Drain.
Add butter and milk and cheese.
Drain tuna and combine with macaroni. Stir over low heat until warm.
Cook celery in small amount boiling water until just tender (about 5 minutes).
Drain.
Combine celery, almonds, chestnuts and mushrooms.
Mix well.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Melt butter; blend in flour.
Cook 1 minute.
Add broth and half and half.
Cook until thickened.
Pour over celery.
Combine cheese and bread crumbs.
Sprinkle over casserole.
Top with melted butter.
Bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Flour chicken strips and saute in hot oil until golden brown. Remove to baking dish. Discard oil from pan.
Melt butter. Add chicken broth, lemon juice, lemon rind, Proscuitto,
wine and garlic.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Pour over chicken and serve.
In large skillet, fry bacon over medium-high heat until crisp. Drain on paper towel, crumble bacon and set aside.
Reserve 1/2 cup of bacon grease.
Fry okra and onion over medium-high heat until brown but not dry.
Add rice and crumbled bacon, reserving some bacon for garnish.
Cook until thoroughly heated.
Serve from skillet or in casserole dish.
Garnish with crumbled bacon. Serves 4 to 6.

recipes.t: Fettuccine With Shrimp And Creamy Herb Sauce
d: In 2-quart saucepan, blend soup mix and milk thoroughly. Bring just to boiling point, stirring frequently.
Add shrimp. Simmer 3 minutes.
Toss shrimp, hot noodles and cheese.
Cream butter and sugar, add vanilla and eggs and blend well. Add flour and baking soda and mix well.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on foil lined cookie sheet or roll out and cut with a cookie cutter. Bake at 400° 10 minutes.
Cut up fruits, nuts and raisins.
Put all together in a bowl with 1/2 cup flour and mix well to keep fruits from sticking together.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Add spices.
Add whiskey, milk and rum.
Add this to fruit and nut mixture.
Mix well.
Add flour and mix well.
Grease cookie sheets and drop by teaspoonful, one at a time.
Bake at 275° for approximately 12 to 15 minutes.
When cooled completely, store in airtight cans.
Will keep for weeks.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix together the 3 cans of soup and mayo in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Place raw chicken breasts, cut in half, or long strips into soup mixture.
Press down to cover with sauce. Place cheese slices on top.
Then sprinkle with crumb dressing mix and bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until chicken is done and top is brown.
Preheat oven to 275°.
Melt bakers chocolate in the water. Combine sugar, Mazola and egg.
Sift together flour, baking powder, salt and baking soda.
Combine liquid, dry and chocolate mixtures.
Bake for 1 hour.
In a double boiler, melt chocolate bits and butter.
Spread over cake.
Combine all ingredients except bay leaves, ham and white wine.
Place bay leaves in bottom of pan.
Place ham on top of bay leaves.
Spread paste over ham.
Add white wine in bottom of pan. Bake at 300 to 325° for 20 minutes per pound of ham, basting frequently.
Simmer all but beans in skillet for 10 minutes.
Add beans; bake in large casserole for 2 hours at 325°, covered.
Serves 8.
Dip chicken wings in eggs (beaten);
coat
with
flour. Fry in oil
15 to 20 minutes. Lay chicken wings
in
a
pan neatly. Combine the first 6 ingredients in a bowl
to
make a sauce;
pour sauce over chicken wings.
Bake at 350°
for
30 minutes. Turn chicken wings over before
removing
from
the oven.

Heat oven to 375 degrees. Beat eggs in large bowl using electric mixer on medium speed for 15 seconds. Add syrup, vanilla, flour and brown sugar and beat for 15 more seconds. Stir in chocolate chips and pecan halves with a large spoon. Pour pecan mixture into frozen pie crust. Bake on center oven rack for 45 minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean. Serves 10.
Cut ham julienne 1/4 inch thick; wrap breast over ham.
Dip in whipped egg and roll in bread crumbs.
Sprinkle with butter.
Place in pan and cover with foil.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/4 hours.
Serve with chicken fricassee sauce.
Scald tomatoes and remove skins.
Quarter and cook until soft and well separated (20 minutes at least).
Add sugar, salt and bread, broken up in pieces.
Then cook for another 10 minutes, stirring often.
Have tomatoes simmering on medium heat.
Do not burn!
They are ready for jars at this point.
Mix all together.
Add a little vegetable oil to skillet.
Fry slowly.
Add water and simmer until done.
In shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish combine potatoes, oil and black pepper.
Firmly press mixture across bottom and up sides of dish to form a shell.
Bake uncovered at 400° for 15 minutes.
In the meantime brown ground beef in large skillet; drain.
Stir in gravy mix, water and garlic powder and bring to a boil.
Stir in frozen mixed vegetables.
Reduce heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese and 1/2 can French fried onion rings. Pour this mixture into potato shell.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and onions and bake 5 minutes longer.
Serve with extra gravy if desired.
Make sauce by placing lemon juice, salt, pepper (as desired), green onions and olive oil in a blender or food processor; process until completely smooth.
Set aside.
Melt 1 stick butter.
Cook onions in butter until transparent. Mix soup and cornbread dressing.
Mix sour cream, pepper and corn.
Put a little cornbread mix on top.
Cook at 300° for 1 hour.
Wash and cut potatoes lengthwise into wedges.
Brush with Miracle Whip salad dressing.
Sprinkle with onion salt and pepper. Place on greased jelly roll pan.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 50 minutes or until golden brown.
Place Sausages in Water bringing to a boil and simmer until the sausages are firm. Remove the sausage,
being careful not to pierce them when taking them out (this could add unwanted fat to the soup). Cut the sausage into bite-size pieces and return to the water.
Spoon desired amount of sauce onto pita bread.
Add your choice of toppings.
Top with cheese.
Place on cookie sheet for 15 to 20 minutes in 350° oven.
Kids love them!
In medium saucepan, bring water and salt to a boil.
Add carrots; cover and cook over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes or until tender.
Drain; cover to keep warm.
Melt butter in pan on low heat; stir in syrup.
Add carrots.
Cook until carrots are well glazed, stirring constantly.
Serve, topped with pecans. Makes 6 (1/2-cup) servings.
Mix in large bowl the chili, beans, onion, soup, green chilies and milk.
Spray casserole liberally with Pam.
Place layer of broken pieces of tortilla chips in bottom of pan and spoon meat mixture over.
Continue layering chips and meat mixture, ending with topping of grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
May be divided and frozen for future use.
Take approximately 1/2 loaf of white bread and break into pieces.
Take 3/4 of the package of sausage and tear into small pieces.
Take the eggs, crack and put in mixing bowl.
Add the bread and hunks of sausage and mix.
Add some milk every so often. Form into 4 to 5 cakes (looks like large hamburgers) and fry in large skillet with butter until golden brown.
Serve with fresh applesauce and cinnamon rolls.
Drain cherries and halve them.
Save juice.
Dissolve jello in the hot water.
Add grape juice, Cola and 1/4 cup cherry juice. Cool.
When it begins to set, stir in pecans and cherries.
Pour in 8 x 8-inch dish or salad mold.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce leaves if desired.
Soak 2 pkgs yeast in 1/2 c warm water.
Melt 1/2 c margarine in 1 c hot water.
Add 1 c cold water, salt and sugar.
When lukewarm add yeast and well beaten eggs.
Add 7 1/2 c flour to mixture, 2 c at a time and vigorously after each addition.
Cover and store in refrigerator.
Roll out and cut into rolls, placing in greased pan and let rise 2 hours before baking.
Bake at 400 for 10 - 15 minutes or until dough is light brown.
Dough will keep several days in refrigerator, but should be worked down each day until used.
Mix 1 cup brown sugar, flour, milk, baking powder, salt and raisins together.
Put into a deep dish.
Combine boiling water, butter, 1 1/2 cups brown sugar and nutmeg.
Pour over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
When put to bake, batter is on bottom and sauce on top.
When completed, these are reversed.
Boil rice as directed. Melt butter.
Add soup, lemon juice, onion and pepper.
Stir until smooth. Add shrimp and parsley. Pour into buttered casserole dish.
Press 6 green pepper rings into top with butter pats.
Cover with cheese and bake.
Mix flour, sugar, salt, mustard and cayenne.
Mix egg yolks and milk; stir in flour mixture.
Cook over low heat until thick, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Then add apple cider vinegar and butter.
Mix into dressing and cool.
Makes one cup.
Melt
the
chocolate with butter in the top of a double boiler over medium heat.
Remove from water and cool slightly. Combine the eggs, sugar, salt, corn syrup and rum in a mixing bowl
and beat
to
blend.
Beat
in the cooled chocolate and butter.
Place pecans
in the bottom of the pie shell and add the egg mixture. Bake in a preheated oven (350°) for 40 to 50 minutes.
The
top should be soft and the center not quite set when
the pie is shaken.
Serve with whipped cream that barely holds a soft peak. Serves 6 or 8.
Boil potatoes with skins on until done.
Drain and let cool. Thinly slice unpeeled potatoes.
In skillet, melt butter and saute pepper and onion until tender.
Add soup, milk and 4 ounces of cheese and stir over low heat until cheese is melted.
Stir in hot pepper sauce, green chilies and salt.
Add potatoes and toss gently.
Pour into buttered casserole and top with 1/4 cup grated cheese.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly. Serves 6 to 8.
In a large skillet, cook onion and garlic in oil until onion is soft.
Break up tomatoes and add with juice to skillet.
Stir in crushed red pepper.
Increase heat and boil sauce.
Stir until liquid has evaporated (about 18 minutes).
Season with salt and pepper.
Keep warm.
Add 1/2 cup sugar into eggs and beat until smooth. Combine remaining sugar, oil and melted chocolate.
Stir into egg mixture. Add vanilla. Sift flour and measure.
Add salt and blend into creamed mixture. Add nuts and beat thoroughly until smooth.
Line two greased 8-inch shallow pans.
Pour mixture into pans and bake for 25 minutes in a 350° oven.
Rub flour, salt and pepper into round steak.
Brown in a skillet.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours until meat is tender.
Serve over noodles or rice, if desired.
Serves 4 to 6.
Squeeze spinach until dry.
In medium bowl, stir together spinach, sour cream, mayonnaise, soup mix, water chestnuts, green onions, lemon juice and Parmesan cheese.
Cover; refrigerate 2 hours.
If desired, serve with pumpernickel bread, crackers or vegetables.
Makes 3 cups.
Combine cake mix, Cool Whip, egg and lemon mixture; mix well. Mixture can be chilled for easier handling.
Drop by teaspoon in bowl of powdered sugar.
Coat dough well; form into balls.
Place balls 1 1/2 inches apart on well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Let cookies cool; remove from cookie sheet. Makes 4 dozen.
In a large skillet or Dutch oven, brown ground beef.
Stir in carrots, 1 cup water and onion soup mix.
Cover and cook over low heat until carrots are almost tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in noodles, tomatoes, corn, 1 cup water, basil and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat until noodles and vegetables are tender, about 8 minutes, stirring several times. If needed, to prevent sticking, stir in 2 or 3 tablespoons water.

recipes.t: Roll-Ups With Cream Cheese Filling And Feta Cheese
d: Mix cheeses and egg yolks to creamy paste.
Cut edges evenly from bread.
Press bread square down with rolling pin.
Brush slice of bread with butter that has been melted.
Drop a teaspoon of mix and roll into wheels.
Cut wheels in half and coat with egg whites and then in sesame seed.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Freezes well.
Put rice in a 2-quart casserole dish.
Brown pork chops on each side in a skillet.
Set aside.
Pour soup and water into skillet and mix with the pan drippings.
Pour liquids over the rice and place pork chops on top.
Cover casserole and bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Serves 4.
Blend cream cheese, milk, confectioners sugar and Cool Whip. Spread over cooled crust.
Cook water, sugar and cornstarch until thick.
Add Jell-O to this mixture and stir until dissolved.
Add strawberries to Jell-O mixture.
Spread over cream cheese mixture.
Refrigerate until gelled.
You may use any fruit and any flavor of Jell-O.
Cream butter.
Mix sugar and flour through sifter.
Gradually add to butter.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Form balls; press down with thumb or fork.
Bake at 250° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Roll in powdered sugar.
Heat oven to 350°.
Generously grease and flour 12-c. Bundt cake pan or tube pan, 10x4 inches.
Mix brown sugar, flour, cocoa and margarine until crumbly; reserve.
Beat cake mix (dry), water, oil and eggs in large bowl on low speed, scraping bowl frequently, 2 minutes.
Pour about 1 2/3 c. batter into pan; sprinkle with about 1 1/3 c. of the crumbly mixture.
Pour about 1 2/3 c. batter into pan; sprinkle with remaining crumbly mixture.
Pour remaining batter into pan.
Bake until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean, 45 to 55 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes; invert on wire rack or heatproof serving plate.
Remove pan; cool cake completely. Spread top of cake with Chocolate Glaze, allowing some to drizzle down side.
Cook meat and onions until meat is brown.
Add salt.
Spray skillet with nonstick cooking spray and fry tortillas until limp. Spoon equal amounts of meat mixture on tortillas.
Top each with taco sauce and cheese.
Roll up; place seam side down in lightly greased 6 x 10-inch pan.

Cream the shortening. Add sugar gradually; blend well. Add egg and vanilla. Blend. Sift dry ingredients and add to shortening mixture alternately with apple butter. Blend well. Drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto greased baking sheet. Keep 2-inches apart. Bake at 350° for about 12 minutes or until edges brown. Remove with spatula and cool on wire rack.
In a large mixer bowl, sprinkle yeast over the water.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in salad oil, sugar, salt, milk and 2 cups flour.
Beat on medium speed for 5 minutes or until dough pulls from sides of bowl in stretchy strands.
Stir in more flour (about 1 cup) to form a stiff dough.
Turn onto a lightly floured board.
Knead for 10 minutes or until smooth.
Turn dough over in a lightly greased bowl.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Let rise in a dark place for 1 hour or until doubled.
Turn dough out onto a board. Knead to expel trapped air.
Cut into 12 equal pieces.
Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Roll each piece out into a log, about 12-inches long.
Set breadsticks, 1-inch apart, on a greased baking sheet.
Brush tops lightly with oil.
Sprinkle with caraway seed. Let rise in a warm place for 20 minutes or until puffy.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool on pan for 2 minutes.
Peel and slice cucumbers to about 1/4-inch thick.
Beat together the eggs, salt and pepper.
Dip the cucumber in the egg mixture then in the bread crumbs.
Fry a few slices at a time in the butter in a large skillet until light brown.
Drain well and serve while still hot.
Yields 6 servings.
Beat egg yolks, sugar and salt.
Stir in milk; mix well.
Mix 1/4 cup flour with water.
Add to egg mixture.
Cook over medium heat until mixture starts to thicken; add vanilla.
Remove from heat and cool.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Stir in custard. Add whipped cream and marshmallows.
Chill and serve with coconut cake.
Take the chicken and garlic salt and salt it a bit, then paprika it thoroughly.
Next, spread it out in one layer in a shallow baking pan.
Dilute the soup with the cream, pour it over the chicken and sprinkle with parsley on top.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
In container of blender combine chocolate bits, eggs, coffee, rum or orange flavored
liqueur, and milk.
Blend mixture at high speed for 2 minutes.
Pour mousse into 4 dessert cups and chill.
Mix boiling water, soda and margarine; let cool.
Add sugar, eggs and remaining ingredients; mix well.
Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Makes 6 dozen.
Make 6 patties, dip in egg, then in flour or bread crumbs. Brown patties in 1 tablespoon oil.
Season with salt and pepper. Drain grease.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook on medium heat for 10 minutes or until done.
Serves 6.
Beat eggs. Add corn syrup, sugar, oleo, pumpkin and vanilla. Beat well. Arrange pecans on bottom of pie shell.
Pour mixture over pecans. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until tests done.
Brown ground beef until crumbly.
Add onion, chili seasoning mix, tomato paste and water.
Combine thoroughly.
Simmer about 10 minutes.
Place 1/2 bag (about 2 cups) corn chips in bottom of 2-quart casserole.
Spoon 1/2 chili meat mixture over corn chips. Place 1/2 can pinto beans over meat mixture, then place 1 can olives over beans.
Sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese.
Repeat the meat, pinto beans and olive layers.
Arrange remaining corn chips over top and sprinkle with remaining cup grated cheese. Cover and bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.

Mix tomato juice and puree in a large kettle. Add all of the spices. Mix and heat to almost a boil. Brown hamburger in skillet. Drain off grease. Add to kettle. In the skillet, cook onion half done. Drain. Add to kettle. Bring to a simmer. Add kidney beans. Cook spaghetti. Add to kettle; turn off heat. Let set for 1/2 hour.
Place all ingredients (except tomato soup and water) into a large casserole.
Pour tomato soup and water over top.
Top with a layer of bacon strips.
Bake 2 hours in 350° oven.
Dissolve gelatine in 1/4 cup cold water.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Mix jello and gelatine and chill slightly until thickened.
Stir in peach pickles, pecans, pickle juice and pineapple.
Pour into one large bowl or individual molds and chill.
Cream butter until fluffy.
Add chives, lemon peel, lemon juice and pepper; mix.
Shape 3/4 cup of this mixture into six 2-inch sticks.
Freeze firm.
Place chicken between sheets of waxed paper; pound to flatten.
Salt lightly.
Place 1 butter stick on each.
Roll up; secure with wooden picks.
Combine egg and 1 tablespoon water.
Coat chicken with flour.
Dip in egg; coat with crumbs.
In skillet, heat remaining butter mixture.
Add chicken; cook over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, turning to brown all sides.
Bake in shallow baking pan at 400° for 20 minutes.
Serve over hot cooked noodles, if desired.
Makes 6 servings.
Pour milk and syrup into a tall glass.
Stir.
Add enough club soda to reach rim of glass.
Stir top with whipped cream.
Also add sprinkles and a cherry if desired.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In the pie shell, place the brown sugar, flour and salt.
Mix with your fingers.
Pour the evaporated milk over the flour and sugar, but do not stir or mix this in.
Dot with butter and cinnamon liberally over all.
Bake for 50 minutes or until the filling just bubbles up in the middle. The filling will never completely set, but that's the way it's supposed to be.
This pie is best eaten at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a mixing bowl, combine cake mix, 1 1/4 cups root beer, oil and eggs.
Beat on low speed for 2 minutes or by hand for 3 minutes.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool completely on wire rack. In a mixing bowl, combine whipped topping and remaining root beer.
Beat until soft peaks form.
Frost cake.
Store in refrigerator.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Heat the cottage cheese to lukewarm then put in a bowl and combine sugar, onion, soft butter, dill seed, salt, soda, egg and dissolved yeast.
Cook all meats until tender and then grind meats, tomatoes and onions.
Mix all this until onions are tender.
Can add more salt and pepper to taste. Makes about 2 1/2 to 3 gallons.
In a large glass salad bowl, spread the 2 cans of bean dip. Top this with the avocados which have been dipped in lemon juice. Sprinkle this with black pepper.
Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise and taco seasoning mix.
Spread on top of avocados.
Chop the large bunch of onions, including the tops.
Layer over sour cream mixture.
Chop the tomatoes and layer over the onions.
Top them with the ripe olives which have been chopped.
Cover with the Cheddar cheese.
Chill!
Serve with the Doritos.
Combine sugar, cream, butter and ginger.
Boil to soft ball stage, stirring constantly.
Cool to lukewarm; add vanilla and beat until creamy.
Add pineapple and nuts.
Spread on oiled surface to harden.
When hard, break into pieces.
Enjoy!
Heat oven to 375°. Cook and stir beef, onion and garlic in skillet until beef is brown; drain.
Stir tomatoes, sauce, chilies and
bouillon.
Cook until bouillon is dissolved. Mix flour
and water.
Stir
in
beef
mixture.
Heat to boiling. Cook
1 minute.
Pour
into 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix Bisquick, 2 tablespoons cornmeal and the milk until soft dough forms.
Beat. Drop
by tablespoon onto beef mixture; sprinkle with
remaining cornmeal.
Bake, uncovered, until biscuits are golden brown, 20 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix the cream cheese, mayonnaise and Ranch dressing until smooth.
Spread the cream cheese mixture thinly over tortillas. Layer meat, tomatoes and lettuce.
Roll tightly; cut in slices. Chill until ready to use.
Preheat oven to 500°.
With boning knife, carve ribs from roast and save.
Rub roast generously with soy sauce and seasonings.
Place roast on top of ribs in roasting pan.
Bake 30 minutes.
Reduce heat to 300° and cook for 20 minutes per pound. Transfer roast from pan to platter.
Let stand 10 minutes before carving.
Heat 2 inches of oil in deep fat fryer to 375°.
Beat 1 cup of baking mix, milk and egg with hand beater until smooth.
Coat cheese lightly with baking mix.
Insert a round wooden toothpick in each cube.
Dip into batter, covering cheese completely.
Fry several cubes at a time, turning carefully until golden brown,
1 to 2 minutes.
Drain on paper towel.
(Leave toothpicks in.
Keep oil moving with basket or slotted spoon.)
Spread softened cream cheese in bottom of 13 x 9-inch casserole dish.
Spread onion evenly over top.
Heat (prepare) chili according to directions and then pour over cream cheese. Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over Skyline.
Heat approximately 2 minutes in microwave.
Serve with chips for dipping.

In a bowl, combine cake flour, whole-wheat flour, 2 tablespoons sugar and salt. Cut in the butter until crumbly. Add oil and toss with a fork. Gradually add water and buttermilk. Toss until mixture sticks together; shape into a ball, cover and put in refrigerator for at least an hour to chill. Then roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 14-inch circle. Place on a parchment-lined or lightly greased baking sheet. (I use pizza pan.)
Heat oil over medium heat.
Saute chicken, turning frequently. Add onion, garlic and pepper.
Saute until softened.
Stir in tomatoes and boil for a few minutes.
Add potatoes, wine, salt and pepper to taste.
Let simmer until done.
Do not add water, but may add tomato sauce, if needed.
Serve over white rice.
Cook noodles until tender; drain and rinse.
Drain and save juices from pineapple and oranges.
Combine juices with eggs, sugar, flour, salt and lemon juice.
Boil and pour over noodles. Refrigerate overnight.
Next day, add cold fruit and Cool Whip. Serves at least 15 people (1 1/2 cups each).
In a large container, combine tea with pineapple juice, orange juice, lemon juice and grapefruit juice.
Add sliced cherries and reserved cherry juice.
Chill thoroughly and pour into a large jug before leaving for your picnic.
Cook corn meal in water on top of stove until combined well. Add milk, eggs and salt to corn meal mixture.
Pour in greased 9-inch square pan and bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Chop the tuna, then mix all the ingredients, except the bread crumbs and oil, together.
Form patties.
Dip each patty in the bread crumbs and fry in hot oil.
Serve with macaroni and cheese or soup.
Mix together crackers, butter and sugar.
Press into bottom of an 8 x 10-inch baking pan.
To the eggs, add 1/2 cup sugar and cream cheese.
Mix until smooth.
Spread over graham cracker crust and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Chill.
Top with pie filling and whipped cream.
Soften the ice cream in a large bowl.
Crush macaroons and stir into ice cream.
Add remaining items and mix well.
Place in refrigerator trays and freeze.
Cook meat until golden brown in cooking oil.
Add garlic and onion; stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
Then add 3 tablespoons of soy sauce and about 2 1/2 cups of water or more.
Simmer for 2 to 5 minutes.
Then add your noodles.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Dip cheese in combined eggs and milk; coat with crumbs. Repeat dipping and coating.
Chill.
Fry in deep hot oil (375°) for 1 to 2 minutes or until lightly browned.
Makes 28 appetizers.
Melt margarine in large saucepan on medium-high heat.
Add celery, onion and poultry seasoning.
Cook and stir until onion is tender.
Add broth and bring to boil.
Stir in apples, rice and cinnamon; cover.
Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in walnuts and parsley.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine Ricotta, Mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses in small bowl and mix.
Half each biscuit horizontally making 20 thin biscuits. If kitchen is hot, refrigerate half the dough.
Shape one piece of dough into an oval about 2 1/2 x 4-inches.
Place a slice of pepperoni slightly off center on the dough.
Top with one level tablespoon of cheese mixture.
Moisten edge and fold dough over to enclose filling.
Pinch edges to seal.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet.
Repeat.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Saute mushrooms in olive oil and garlic.
Season with coarse black pepper and dash of Tony Chachere seasoning.
Set aside. Cream the softened cream cheese together with green onions and sauteed mushrooms.
Add seasoned salt, as needed.
Roll crescent rolls out in jelly roll fashion; fill with cream cheese mixture. Brush with egg and sprinkle with poppy seed.
Bake at 375° until golden brown (10 to 20 minutes); slice into one-inch pieces and serve.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease an 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Pour pie filling into pan. Sprinkle dry cake mix on top; pour melted butter over cake mix. Sprinkle with nuts. Bake at 325° for 35 minutes.

recipes.t: A La Simple La Orange Chicken Breast
d: Place chicken breasts in baking dish.
Salt and pepper chicken. Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
The last 10 to 15 minutes of baking, mix together dry onion soup packet and jar of orange marmalade and spread on top of chicken breasts.
Continue baking another 15 minutes.
Serve with wild rice and mandarin orange salad.
Combine flour, sugar and salt in pot and mix until well blended.
Add boiling
water,
stirring
rapidly
to
prevent lumping.
Cook until thickened
about
10 minutes.
Add butter or margarine.
Cool, then add lemon juice and cream.
Store in refrigerator.

Place broccoli in package on microproof plate and put in microwave oven. Cook on High for 4 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside. Combine soup, carrots, sour cream, flour, onion, salt and pepper in 1 1/2-quart microproof casserole.
Cut broccoli into 1-inch pieces. Stir into soup mixture. Cover and cook on High for 6 minutes. Remove from oven. Stir and set aside.
Place butter in 2-cup glass measure.
Cook on High for 1 minute. Remove from oven. Add stuffing cubes to butter and blend well. Spoon over broccoli mixture.
Place in microwave and cook on High for 6 minutes. Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Line 9-inch pie plate with aluminum foil; set aside.
In large skillet, melt butter.
Add coconut, stir occasionally until lightly toasted.
Blend in 1 cup peanut butter chips, stir until morsels melt and mixture is combined.
Press evenly on bottom and sides (not over rim) of foil-lined pie plate.
Chill in refrigerator until firm, about 45 minutes.
Remove foil and place back into pie plate.
Butter a 2-quart Bundt pan heavily, using 2 tablespoons of butter.
Sprinkle
pan
with
the 1/2 cup of finely chopped nuts, then the 2 tablespoons of sugar; set aside.
Cream 1 cup of butter with
cream cheese and 1 1/2 cups of sugar.
Beat in egg yolks one
at a time until thoroughly blended. Sift flour with
baking powder
and
salt; gradually blend into creamed mixture.
Stir in remaining
pecans.
Beat egg whites stiff, then
fold into creamed mixture.
Carefully pour into prepared pan.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake pie crust for 6 to 8 minutes until set; allow to cool.
Layer pie crust with 3/4 cups of cheese, then spaghetti sauce, pepperoni, onion and remaining 3/4 cup cheese.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine eggs, cream, salt and pepper; mix thoroughly and pour over filling.
Place on cookie sheet and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, or until top is golden and knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool for 15 minutes; cut into wedges.
Yields 6 servings.
Preparation time:
1 hour and 30 minutes.
Spray a large skillet with nonstick spray.
Add the chicken and cook over medium heat until lightly browned.
Stir in the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Stir in the macaroni and reduce heat to a medium boil.
Cover with a lid and let simmer 10 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Add the broccoli and cheese.
Stir until cheese is melted.
Serves 6.
Place beets and half the beet liquid in blender.
Add remaining ingredients and blend until smooth.
Chill at least 3 hours.
Serve garnished with a dollop of sour cream and a pinch of chopped tarragon or parsley.
Serves 6.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Mix well. Add flour, baking powder and salt.
Mold into balls.
Roll in a mixture of chopped nuts and cinnamon.
Place on greased baking sheet, about 2 inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Remove right away from baking sheet.
In large bowl mash the egg until well crumbled.
Blend in oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, pimento and onion.
Add cabbage and olives. Toss to mix.
Serve in lettuce cups.
Beat margarine and sugar well. Add cinnamon and blend in flour.
Divide dough in half.
Press half into buttered 8-inch square pan.
Add egg to other half and mix well.
Brown meat, onion and garlic until done.
Mash up tomatoes until soupy.
Put in large pot.
Add water with this until pot is almost full.
Leave room for meat and okra.
Let this cook to a boil, then simmer.
Put okra in skillet with 3 tablespoons oil and brown until okra is no longer sticky.
Add with what you already have cooking.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add over cooked rice. Salt and pepper to your taste while cooking.
It's ready (eat).
Have meat 1/8-inch thick, cut in 1/4 x 1-inch pieces.
Put in hot oil and simmer slowly until nearly tender.
Drain liquid from sprouts and mix with cornstarch, molasses and sauce.
Add to meat to cook 15 minutes longer.
Saute onions in 1/2 of the butter until glassy; saute celery in remaining butter until nearly tender.
Add this to meat.
Cook 5 minutes.
Add sprouts and cook 3 minutes longer.
If Chinese chestnuts are available, slice thinly and add to the sauce.
Cook potatoes in boiling salted water until tender.
Drain and cool slightly.
Peel and slice.

Brown sausages in skillet. Arrange 2/3 of potato slices in bottom of buttered baking dish. Layer eggs over potatoes. Arrange sausage links in center of casserole and place remaining potato slices around edge.
Combine sour cream, milk, flour, salt and pepper.
Pour over casserole. Sprinkle with chives.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Cook and stir sugar and butter until creamy.
Add cashews. Cook and stir until brown and creamy.
Pour onto wax paper lined cookie sheet.
Cool and break into pieces.

recipes.t: Pork Chops With Raisin Pine Nut
d: Preheat broiler.
Spray rack in broiling pan with nonstick spray.
Arrange chops on rack and broil 6 inches from heat, until brown and done to taste, 4 or 5 minutes on each side.
In 9-inch nonstick skillet heat oil; add pine nuts and onions and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until brown.
Continue to stir; cook 1 minute longer.
Stir in broth and vermouth and bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; stir in raisins and rosemary and let simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
To serve, arrange chops on serving dish and top with sauce.

recipes.t: Chicken Breast Baked In Lemon And Garlic
d: Heat small skillet; add olive oil.
Heat and add garlic. Saute 30 seconds.
Stir in lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Bring to boil; set aside.
Arrange chicken in lightly buttered shallow baking dish, enough to hold chicken in single layer.
Pour garlic mix over chicken; sprinkle with grated lemon peel.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 10 to 15 minutes more or until chicken is done.
Transfer to plates; pour from dish into small skillet.
Add broth and bring to boil.
Cook until reduced by 1/2 and mixture is syrupy.
Pour over chicken and serve.
Combine cake mix, fruit cocktail, 1 cup coconut and the eggs. Beat at high speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into a large greased pan; sprinkle with brown sugar.
Combine chocolate, butter and syrup in double boiler and melt until smooth. Take off heat. Add vanilla, confectioners sugar and Rice Krispies.
Mix until everything is coated.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
May chill until firm and cut into squares.
In large bowl, pour can of peaches in and mix jello with syrup in peaches.
Break pound cake into the peaches and Jello mixture. Press down. Mix instant vanilla pudding (large) according to direction.
Pour over cake.
Cover with Cool Whip.
Refrigerate for several hours before serving.
Brown hamburger meat and add chilli seasoning mix.
Combine tomato soup, water, kidney beans and onions in a boiler.
Bring to a boil.
Then add hamburger meat mixture, after you drain it, to the soup mixture.
Melt together 1/2 cup butter and 1 square chocolate.
Add 1 cup sugar, 1 cup flour, baking powder, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 2 eggs and 1/2 to 1 cup nuts.
Spread in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Mix together the cream cheese, 1 egg, 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, 2 tablespoons flour and 1/4 cup chopped nuts.
Spread over chocolate mixture; sprinkle with 6 ounces chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with 2 cups miniature marshmallows. Bake 2 minutes longer.
Spread with icing and swirl with marshmallows.
Put onion and garlic in cooking pan with potatoes.
Add enough water to cover potatoes.
Bring to a boil.
Simmer 30 to 35 minutes or until tender.
Remove the onion and garlic.
Drain the potatoes in a colander until thoroughly drained.
Pat dry, if necessary, to remove excess moisture.
Cut potatoes into chunks and mash by hand or use electric mixer.
Mash potatoes until free of lumps.
Add the desired amount of evaporated skim milk and whip until creamy. Season with pepper to taste.
Preheat oven
to
Coat chicken breasts with sour cream and then
roll in stuffing mix to cover chicken.
Melt 1 stick of butter.
Place
chicken in baking dish.
Pour melted butter over top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Combine onion, garlic and oil in 2-quart glass measure.
Cover with plastic wrap; microwave on High 3 minutes or until onion is tender, stirring every minute.
Add chili powder and next 4 ingredients.
Stir well.
Microwave, uncovered, on High 6 to 9 minutes or until slightly thickened, stirring every 3 minutes. Add remaining ingredients; stir well.
Microwave, uncovered, on High 6 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Grind cheese, pepper, bacon and onion in meat grinder (medium). Add mayonnaise, mustard, garlic or oregano and mix well.
Spread on English muffin halves.
Brown under broiler 3 to 4 minutes.
Serve hot.
Makes 12 to 15 muffin halves.
Brown the first 3 ingredients lightly in pan.
Add salt, consomme, water and cumin seed.
Let come to a boil; cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Can be reheated.
Serves 12.
In a 9 x 13-inch baking dish, layer graham cracker and chocolate pudding (made as directed on box) in about 4 layers, ending with chocolate pudding.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with chocolate chips for decoration, if desired.
Refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
Brown ground beef
and drain. Add
to
ground beef in large skillet,
sliced
potatoes,
chopped
onion,
salt and pepper. Add water to
cover.
Bring to boil; cover and simmer until done. If your guys are late, it's still good...
One loaf equals 4 pies.
Take dough out of freezer 4 hours before use.
Cook frozen spinach as directed on package.
Saute 1 small onion (chopped) and 1 clove garlic (chopped).
Add cooked, drained spinach and fry 15 minutes.
Let cool.
Cream together sugars and margarine.
Mix in eggs and flavorings.
Gradually add milk and flour to make a soft dough. Roll out on floured board and cut.
Bake on a lightly greased cookie sheet at 370° for 7 to 9 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Blend in shortening until it resembles coarse meal. Add vinegar and 1/2 cup milk all at once, stirring only to combine. Turn out on slightly floured board.
Knead gently 5 or 6 times.
Divide dough into 16 equal parts. Roll each on board with palm of hand to 6-inch cylinder.
Brush with remaining milk. Combine cereal, salt and caraway or poppy seed.
Roll each in cereal.
Place on sheet and bake 15 minutes.
Layer fruit and nuts in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix brown sugar and flour well and sprinkle over fruit.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Serve hot or chilled.
Blend together butter, sugars and eggs.
Mix in flour, soda, salt (if used), vanilla and water. Stir in coconut and nuts. Drop by teaspoons onto baking sheet and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Place chicken in buttered 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Stir together soups and milk.
Pour over chicken.
Spread frozen peas over top of soup.
Lay slices of cheese to cover the peas.
Top with a layer of Tater Tots.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour until bubbly and Tots are golden brown.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream and milk.
Then add other ingredients and mix well.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Top with chopped nuts, if desired.
Use with crackers.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Add 1/2 cup sugar, shortening and salt to scalded milk.
Cool.
Add 2 cups flour and beat well.
Add eggs, yeast and lemon flavoring.
Beat well and add remaining flour.
Knead until smooth.
Place in greased bowl.
Cover and let rise until doubled (1 1/2 hours).
Preheat oven to 375°.
Butter a small baking dish.
Trim off any tough stalks and bottom from fennel.
Add trimmed fennel and lemon juice to boiling salted water.
Cook 10 minutes; drain. Place boiled fennel in buttered dish; add hot stock.
In a small bowl, combine bread crumbs, cheese, lemon peel, salt and pepper. Sprinkle over boiled fennel.
Bake in preheated oven 30 to 35 minutes or until fennel is tender and topping is golden brown. Makes 2 servings.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder, soda, salt and cinnamon. Stir in brown sugar.
With a spoon, blend in margarine, egg and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly after each addition.
Mix in oats, raisins and pecans.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Dip tops of balls in sugar.
Place on ungreased baking sheet 3 inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes or until tops are brown.
Makes 3 dozen.
Preheat oven to 200°.
Beat egg whites, vanilla, cream of tartar and salt at high speed until soft peaks form.
Beat in sugar, a few tablespoons at a time, until meringue is stiff and shiny.
Sift cocoa on top of meringue and carefully fold into mixture.
Fold in ground pecans.
Drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets.
Place a pecan half on top of each meringue.
Bake 1 1/2 hours or until firm and dry.
Remove from sheets and cool on wire racks.
Yield:
Approximately 3 dozen cookies.
Cream sugar and butter; add eggs, then sour cream.
Add corn and vanilla; mix in cornmeal, salt and baking powder.
Bake until golden brown at 325° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Saute onion, green pepper and meat into Crisco until lightly browned.
Add sauce and seasonings and let simmer while mixing cornbread mixture.
Pour batter mixture over the hot meat mixture. Bake in a 6 x 10-inch pan for 20 to 25 minutes.
Turn out on a platter upside down and serve.
Cut up wings.
Combine soy sauce, water and garlic powder. Place wings in baking pan.
Pour in liquid mixture.
Bake, uncovered, 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Put milk and butter in top of double boiler.
Add the marshmallows; heat until melted.
Pour over cracker crumbs, chopped fruits and nuts and coconut.
Mix quickly and pour into pan.
Let chill thoroughly before unmolding, then store in refrigerator.
Saute celery and onion in butter.
Combine the first 3 ingredients together and mix with the soup, rice and water.
Pour into casserole dish and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Place pork roast in 5-quart Dutch oven.
Add Polish sausage and sauerkraut.
Add 1 quart of water and cover with lid.
Cook until pork is tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours in a 375° oven. Remove from the oven.
Arrange canned biscuit dough over top of dish and bake an additional 30 minutes.
You have a complete meal ready to eat.
In skillet, heat beer.
Chop up onion, green pepper and mushrooms.
Set aside.
Add steak to skillet.
Cook on high until juice runs out, about 5 to 10 minutes, then add onion, green pepper and mushrooms to skillet.
Reduce heat.
Cover; let cook until the beer evaporates.
Serve.
Overnight:
Soak the fruit and sugar in 1 cup cold strong tea. The next morning add the flour and the well beaten egg.
Mix well.
Pour into a well-greased, foil lined loaf pan.
(It will look awful, but don't give up!)
Bake for 2 hours on middle shelf at 300°.
Take out of oven and leave in the pan until next day. Slice and serve with butter.
Keeps well wrapped in foil.
Can be frozen.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add red pepper, scallions and broccoli.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, cream, noodles and chicken. Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer over low heat 25 to 30 minutes or until noodles are tender.

Mix cake as directed on box. Add 2 cups flour. Beat 3 minutes with mixer, then stir in as much of the remaining flour with wooden spoon. Knead on floured board about 3 minutes. Place in large greased bowl. Let rise for 1 hour. Punch down and divide in half. Cover and let stand 10 minutes. Roll each half and spread with butter, sugar and cinnamon. Roll up like a jelly roll. Cut in 1-inch pieces. Place in two 13 x 9-inch pans.
Saute vegetables in oil until onions are soft.
Stir in bulgur, coat well with oil.
When sizzling add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Stir well, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add chicken and water if needed.
Simmer 5 minutes or until chicken is hot.

Grease 9X13 inch pan and a 8X8 inch pan. Tear bread into 1 inch pieces, divide between the 2 baking dishes. Sprinkle ham and onion over bread pieces. Mix eggs and milk together; pour over bread and ham mixture. Melt butter and cheese together; pour over above mixture. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes (8X8 inch pan) - 60 minutes (9X13 inch pan).
In medium saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon butter and just enough water to cover bottom of pan (about 1/4 cup).
Cut apricots into fourths or half. Add apricots to saucepan; pour sugar on top and mix.
Place saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, to keep apricots from sticking and until apricots are softened. This takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
Place
sausage in a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish.
Microwave on High
for
to
minutes or until no longer pink. Drain excess fat.
Stir in eggs, sour cream, chives, mushrooms and basil. Microwave on High for 4 to 5 minutes or until eggs are set
but moist.
Stir every minute.
Total cooking time is 6 to 8 minutes. Yield:
4 servings.
Combine beef coarsely into 3 to 5-quart casserole.
Mix in carrots and celery.
Cover and microwave on High for 3 1/2 to 6 1/2 minutes or until beef is set, stirring once or twice.
Add remaining ingredients.
Microwave, covered, 12 to 18 minutes, or until vegetables are tender, stirring once or twice.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Serves 4 to 6.
In large frypan, brown ground beef and onions, add green peppers, cooking slightly.
Then add tomato sauce and the next six ingredients.
Simmer at least five minutes.
Serve over tortilla chips and top with shredded lettuce, diced fresh tomatoes, chopped onions, green peppers, shredded sharp cheese, sour cream and salsa, if desired.
In a small saucepan, melt butter.
Add cream and stir in Parmesan cheese.
Just heat.
Do not allow mixture to come to a boil.
Pour over hot drained pasta seasoned with freshly ground pepper and toss.
Serve with additional Parmesan cheese on the side.
Serves 6.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Add green onions, olives and water chestnuts.
Mix well.
Add curry powder, salt, dill weed and pepper.
Drain artichokes, reserving marinade.
Cut artichokes into quarters; stir into rice mixture.
Mix reserved artichoke marinade with mayonnaise; toss with rice mixture. Refrigerate overnight to let flavors blend.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Yield:
10 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place the pecans on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for about 10 minutes.
Do not allow the pecans to brown.
Remove the nuts from the oven but leave the oven turned on.
Melt the butter and oil in a large skillet.
Add the brown sugar, salt, curry and ginger.
Blend well.
Add the pecans and stir with a wooden spoon until well coated.
Add the chutney and mix well.
Place the pecan mixture on paper towels on the baking sheet and place in the oven.
Turn the heat off.
Let the pecans dry in the oven about 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven, salt lightly and let cool completely.
Store in an airtight container.
Combine seasonings in small sealable bag. Combine beans and measure 2 heaping cups into sealable plastic bag.
For gift giving, include packet of beans, seasoning, and recipe. (See Soups, Salads, and Sauces for recipe.)
Put water, oil, lemon juice, salt, onion, pepper and fajita seasoning in frying pan.
Cook on medium high heat until onions and peppers are slightly tender.
Add chicken and cook until all pink coloring is gone.
Remove from heat and spoon fajitas into tortillas.
Add the toppings of your choice.
Enjoy!
Remove skins from tomatoes by placing them in boiling water for one minute, then put in cold water.
Remove tomato cores and then measure out 2 gallons of tomatoes which should be put in the blender for a brief time.
(You might also prefer blending peppers and onions.)
Add all other ingredients and cook in an open pot for thirty minutes.
Bring water to a boil with onion, salt, sugar and pepper. Remove from heat.
Combine cornmeals and add 1/3 to water in thin stream, stirring constantly, until very thick.
Vigorously stir in rest of cornmeal.
Cool to room temperature.
Form cornmeal mixture into 3-inch rounds 1/2-inch thick.
Combine water and chocolate in a small heavy saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until chocolate melts.
Remove from heat; cool.
Cream shortening.
Gradually add sugar, beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Add cooled chocolate and vanilla.
Mix just until blended.
Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 17 to 19 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes.
Remove from pans and cool completely on wire racks.
Spread Fluffy White Filling between layers.
Spread Chocolate Frosting on top and sides of cake.
Yield:
one 3-layer cake.
Remove skin from chicken.
In 2-quart oblong baking dish, arrange chicken.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, in small bowl, combine soup, brown sugar, water, vinegar and Worcestershire sauce; set aside.
Spoon soup mixture over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes more or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear.
Mix the cornstarch in a little cold water. Add to boiling water and jello. Boil for 2 minutes. Let cool. Add Equal and pour in strawberries. Pour this mixture in crust and chill. Top with Cool Whip.
Line a 9-inch pie pan with rich pastry.
Slice tomatoes thin and mound slightly in center.
Sugar mixture should be added gradually between layer of tomatoes.
Add lemon juice, allspice and butter on top.
Add top crust and bake at 425° for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 325° when pie starts to bubble and continue baking until filling has thickened and tomatoes are tender.
Remove from oven and cool.
Enjoy with ice cream.
Combine sugar, cornstarch and water and cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add butter and food coloring.
Stir until blended well.
Place peaches in baked pie crust and pour mixture over them.
Top with whipped cream before serving, if desired.
Boil noodles 5 minutes and drain.
Saute meat and onions, drain.
Add tomato sauce and soup.
Stir in noodles.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole and cover with grated cheese.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Batter; Blend the eggs, beer and spices.
Add the flour, mixing well.
The batter should be thick and creamy (if not, just adjust by adding more beer or flour).
Lightly salt potatoes.
Blend in the next 8 ingredients, beating constantly.
The mixture should be fairly moist.
If not, add a bit of cream and more butter.
Pile into an ovenproof serving dish and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix bits and crumbs.
Add milk and mix well.
Stir in nuts. Grease a large cake pan (9 x 13-inch) and add mixture.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 minutes.
Let cool 45 minutes before cutting.
Slice onion and mushrooms; saute in margarine (about 1/4 cup) until tender.
Brown/saute each side of chicken.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Cover with onion and mushrooms.
Bake in oven at 350° for about 30 minutes or until tender.
Before serving, sprinkle with Monterey Jack cheese and melt.
In large mixing bowl, sift together cake mix and cornstarch. Add water, eggs, oil and vanilla.
Mix until smooth.
Grease and flour pans.
Pour half the batter (3 cups) into 1 pan.
Add cocoa to remaining batter, stirring until blended.
Pour this batter into other pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cool in pan 10 minutes. Remove and cool on rack.
Freeze layers for 2 hours.
Split each layer in half.
Brush each layer with Amaretto.
Put a chocolate layer on plate and spread with 1/3 custard filling.
Repeat with remaining layers ending with yellow.
Frost with whipped cream.
Mix Crisco with flour.
Blend dry ingredients together, then add eggs and vanilla; blend well.
Fold in pineapple and nuts last. Make into bar.
Bake in 350° oven 15 or 20 minutes.
Dilute juices according to directions on can and mix in a large punch bowl.
About 10 minutes before serving, combine strawberry ice cream and 1/2 gallon of the vanilla ice cream. When ready to serve, add ginger ale and float the other 1/2 gallon of vanilla ice cream on top.
Makes 50 (4 ounce) servings.
Mix all dry ingredients.
Add eggs, buttermilk and oil. Batter will keep in the refrigerator for 6 weeks and can be baked as needed.
Or I prefer making up the muffins and putting them in the freezer.
Bake 25 to 35 minutes at 350° in muffin tins or use Pam or paper liners.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Set out but do not grease a 10-inch tube pan. Sift flour and 1/4 cup sugar 3 times; set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, beat egg whites, cream of tartar and salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining cup of sugar. Continue beating until very stiff peaks form.
Sift about 1/4 of the flour mixture over egg whites and gently fold.
Repeat with remaining flour mixture, 1/4 at a time; fold in flavoring.
Spoon batter in tube pan. Run knife through batter to eliminate air pockets.
Bake in lower third of preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Invert pan.
To remove, run knife up and down between cake and pan to loosen it.
Makes 16 servings.
Calories:
126 per slice.
Serve with fresh strawberries and whipped cream or whipped topping.
Grease and flour Bundt pan.
Lightly brown almonds in 1 tablespoon margarine.
Sprinkle over bottom of prepared pan.
Set aside.
Mix cake mix, eggs, Amaretto, water and vegetable oil. Beat well for 2 minutes.
Pour batter over nuts.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Mix sugar, 1/2 cup margarine, Amaretto and water in saucepan.
Boil 3 minutes.
Pour over hot cake while still in pan.
Remove from pan after 1 hour.
Pat fish dry.
Mix soda and vinegar.
Stir vinegar mixture and water into flour and salt mixture.
Beat until smooth.
Dip fish into batter.
Fry about 3 minutes.
Cook potatoes in skins until almost tender and then remove skins.
Mix ground beef, egg, salt and pepper.
Cover each potato with hamburger, pressing well.
Place balls in greased 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Pour tomato juice over balls and top with onions and peppers.
Bake at 350° until meat is done and potatoes tender. Serves 6 to 8.
In a frying pan, let oil set on stove eye until you mix the flour and water, then fry until golden brown.
Put in plate and cut in half.
On one half, put mayonnaise and on the other half put your tomatoes.
Salt it and put it together.
Eat and enjoy!
For filling, in a small mixing bowl, combine apple, raisins, sugar, flour, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Set aside.
Lightly brush 1 sheet of the phyllo dough with some of the melted margarine. Place another sheet of phyllo dough on top of the first sheet, then brush with margarine.
Top with the third sheet of phyllo. Do not brush with margarine.
Cut the stack of phyllo sheets lengthwise into four strips.
Cream the butter and sugar. Add egg.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt. Add alternating with sour cream to butter mixture. Fold in dates or raisins.
Spoon into small muffin tins. Bake at 375° for 20 minutes. While hot, roll puffs in 3/4 cup melted butter, then mixture of 1 cup sugar and 2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Makes 36.
Cook hamburger and sausage together.
Drain fat.
Take muffin tin and spray with Pam.
Flatten biscuits with your hands and place in muffin cup.
Biscuits should come up approximately halfway in muffin cup.
Place 1 tablespoon of pizza sauce inside biscuits.
Fill biscuits with your favorite pizza topping, such as pepperoni, mushrooms, hamburger and sausage.
Fill them full because biscuits will rise around the meat.
Top with shredded Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Make Jell-O according to package directions.
Cut in cubes. Split one banana in half and place in banana split dish.
Put cubed Jell-O between both slices.
Pour whipped cream on top.
Sprinkle with chopped pecans.

Combine sugar, flour, margarine and egg yolks, beating until smooth. Beat in lemon juice. Add milk slowly while stirring so it doesn't curdle. Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into lemon mixture. Bake pie shell briefly (5 minutes), then pour in filling. Bake 30 to 45 minutes at 350° until filling is firm.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease and dust a 12-inch tube cake pan.
In a large mixing bowl using a mixer, cream butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy.
Add sugar and mix at least 10 minutes.
Add extract and mix in.
Add flour alternately with eggs, beginning and ending with flour.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake for 65 to 70 minutes.
In top of double boiler, over boiling water, heat butter and chocolate, stirring until melted and well blended.
Allow to cool slightly.
Blend syrup, sugar, salt and vanilla into beaten eggs. Add chocolate; blend well.
Mix the first seven ingredients together and make small balls. Roll in cracker crumbs.
Combine milk and brown sugar; pour over meatballs.
Add sherry until almost covered.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Can make and refrigerate the day before.
Cook hamburger and sausage.
Add the rest of it.
Combine soup, sour cream and garlic.
Add green beans; stir well.
Put in a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Combine cracker crumbs, cheese and butter; sprinkle on casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 20 minutes.
Top with French fried onion rings or toasted sliced almonds.
Bake 10 additional minutes. Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Note:
Reserve 1 cup flour for nuts and raisins.
Place cubed cake in bottom of a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Combine pudding, milk and frozen yogurt.
Pour over cake.
Dissolve Jell-O in water; add frozen strawberries.
Pour over yogurt mixture. Chill until set; top with Cool Whip.
Beat butter 30 seconds until soft.
Add sugar.
Beat until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Beat well after each.
Stir together flour, baking soda and salt.
Add to mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Beat well after each.
Stir in pecans and lemon peel.
Put the soda in the warm coffee, then melt margarine in coffee also. Cook raisins just a little in hot water in microwave or on top of stove.
Place brown sugar in
mixing bowl. Add coffee mixture and egg.
Beat.
Mix together and add the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg.
Add raisins.
Spread in a greased jelly roll pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Frost with powdered sugar frosting.
Combine margarine, soy sauce and garlic salt and pour over the top of the first four ingredients.
Bake in 200° oven for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Press crescent rolls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes by directions on roll package.
Mix the cream cheese, Ranch dressing mix and milk; spread over crust.
Add toppings, then refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, stir together noodles, cream, egg yolks, sugar, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir in raisins, pineapple and vanilla.
In a medium bowl, beat egg whites until stiff.
Fold egg whites into noodle mixture.
Pour into a greased 7 x 11-inch glass baking dish.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes or until top is light brown.
Cover and store in refrigerator until ready to present.
Give with reheating instructions.
Yield:
12 to 15 servings.
Prepare Jell-O according to package directions.
While Jell-O is still soupy, add carrots and pineapple; stir.
Refrigerate Jell-O for desired consistency.
Gently pound pork and cut into 1 ounce pieces.
Saute in butter until brown.
Add enough stock to cover pork.
Add apple filling. Cover and simmer until most of the liquid is gone.
Turn heat up high and add brandy.
Cover until demi-glazed.
In small saucepan, sprinkle gelatin over water; let stand for 1 minute.
Stir over low heat until dissolved.
In blender, combine rest of ingredients for 2 minutes.
While processing, gradually add gelatin.
Pour into dessert dishes and chill.
Garnish with strawberries and sliced almonds.
Combine the soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of the vinegar, ginger, garlic and pepper in a medium bowl.
Add the chicken breast halves; toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat the broiler.
Combine the hoisin sauce and the remaining 2 tablespoons vinegar in a cup.
Broil chicken 3 inches from heat source for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it is opaque in the center.
On a cutting board, slice each breast half lengthwise into 1/2-inch thick strips.
Boil water.
Stir in jello and sugar and dissolve.
Add pineapple juice, almond extract, limeade and 4 cups water. Freeze.
When ready to use, add 2 bottles ginger ale.
Cover frozen shrimp with warm water for about 5 minutes.
Pull apart and rinse with cold water.
Place all ingredients except shrimp in a large pan.
Let boil for about 5 minutes and reduce heat.
Add shrimp and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Pour through colander to drain.
Can be put back on stove to keep warm.
Boil together slowly white sugar, brown sugar, butter and Carnation milk until forms a soft ball when dropped in water. Remove from heat; add vanilla.
Mix together chocolate chips and marshmallow cream.
Keep stirring until smooth.
Pour in a 9 x 13 baking pan and let cool.
Cut into squares.
Hand cutting vegetables is important.
Boil together for 10 minutes the tomatoes, celery, onions and peppers.
Add salt and let stand overnight.
Drain in colander, do not press.
Return to pan.
Add sugar, brown sugar, vinegar and pepper.
Put pickling spices, cinnamon and ginger in spice bag.
Add to mixture.
Bring to a boil.
Simmer 10 minutes and can.
Very good.
Do not double recipe.
Cook and mash carrots.
Beat eggs and mix together with milk, salt, butter and sugar.
Grate cheese and add to the other ingredients, including the bread crumbs.
Place mixture in a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole and bake for about 30 minutes in a 350° oven. Serves 8 to 10.
Cream shortening; gradually add sugar, beating at medium speed of an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolk, lemon rind and lemon juice; beat well.
Gradually add flour; mix just until blended.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
In large bowl, combine first six ingredients; set aside.
In small bowl, combine vinegar, garlic powder and oregano.
Slowly add oil, whisking until smooth and thickened.
Add to vegetable and cheese mixture.
Toss gently.
Cover; chill thoroughly, stirring several times.
Lightly salt and pepper chicken.
Brown in margarine until golden.
Mix sauce ingredients, mayonnaise and Grey Poupon; add zucchini, squash, onion, and garlic to sauce.
Place chicken and pan drippings in the bottom of a casserole.
Pour sauce/vegetable mixture on top of chicken and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheese on top and return to oven for approximately 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Enjoy.
Place asparagus spears in a large skillet; add boiling water and salt.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes or until tender.
Remove asparagus and keep warm.
Drain cooking liquid, reserving 1/2 cup in a small saucepan.
Combine cornstarch and cold water; stir into liquid.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly; cook and stir 1 minute more.
Stir in butter until melted.
Spoon over asparagus; sprinkle with sesame seed and serve immediately.
Serves 6 to 8.
Beat egg whites until foamy; beat in sugar a little at a time to make meringue like.
Beat in vanilla and cream of tartar.
Fold in the 3 cups crushed saltine crackers.
Lightly grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan and spread in meringue/cracker mixture.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes.
After cake is cooled, top with Cool Whip and cover that with the cherry pie filling. Refrigerate.
Melt butter in frying pan.
Add milk with flour beaten in. Pour in green beans, salt and pepper.
Toss and shake over a hot fire for five minutes.
Serve hot.
Cream the peanut butter and brown sugar.
Add egg and bananas. Dissolve baking soda in hot water, then add to mixture.
Add flour, salt and oatmeal.
Microwave raisins for a few seconds to soften.
Add raisins and mix well.
Bake in greased muffin tin or baking cups for 20 to 25 minutes.
Melt butter and marshmallows in double boiler.
Mix remaining ingredients and add to butter and marshmallow mixture.
Press into pan lined with wax paper; refrigerate.
Combine sour cream, sugar, salt, crushed pineapple, banana and enough red food coloring to give a pink tint.
Lightly fold in nuts and cherries.
Spoon into fluted muffin cups which have been placed in muffin pans.
Freeze.
Cover with plastic wrap and store in freezer.
Remove from freezer about 15 minutes before serving to loosen paper cups from pan.
Peel off paper cup and place on salad greens.
Fills 12 large muffin cups.
Mix Cheddar cheese and softened cream cheese together.
Fold in scallions and mushrooms.
Spread mixture on chicken breasts. Fold in half and secure with toothpicks.
Bake cake as directed on box.
Cook the sugar, water and cornstarch until thickens; remove from heat.
Add the jello.
Add the frozen strawberries to jello mixture.
Crumble cake.
Layer cake, then jello mixture.
Layer again; add Cool Whip on top.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 3 (9-inch) cake pans. Cream butter, shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Combine flour, soda, salt and cocoa and gradually add to butter mixture, alternately with buttermilk.
Add vanilla and food coloring.
Blend well.
Pour into pans and bake 25 to 30 minutes. Cool and frost.
Boil and drain potatoes.
Cook noodles and drain.
Saute onion in oleo until tender.
Add potatoes and noodles and stir until coated with onion mixture.
Top with cheese.
When cheese is melted, serve.
Cream the oleo and sugar.
Add eggs and mix.
Add vanilla and honey.
Add flour and baking powder.
Can be mixed ahead and kept in refrigerator.
Drop by teaspoons on hot waffle iron and bake. Keeps well and will freeze.
Makes about 7 dozen.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add beaten egg yolks and sour cream.
Sift dry ingredients, using enough flour so dough can be easily handled.
Roll thin; cut into desired shapes.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix together potatoes, sugar, melted butter, beaten eggs and vanilla.
Place in a buttered casserole dish.
Combine brown sugar, flour, butter, and chopped nuts and put on top of sweet potato mixture.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a 10-inch nonstick skillet, heat oil; in batches, brown chicken pieces on all sides.
Over bottom of shallow 3-quart casserole, spread onion slices; top onions with chicken pieces.
In a 2-cup measure of bowl combine juice, honey and seasonings; pour mixture evenly over chicken and top chicken with olives.
Cover casserole and bake until chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Combine beaten eggs with milk; add to dry ingredients.
Mix.
Stir in melted butter.
Pour batter onto preheated waffle iron.
Bake until crisp.
In a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat, cook beef, green pepper, onion, chili powder and garlic until beef is browned and vegetables are tender, stirring to separate meat.
Spoon off fat. Add soup, undrained kidney beans, vinegar and cinnamon.
Heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low.
Cook 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve over spaghetti. Sprinkle with cheese, if desired.
Melt butter in top of double boiler.
Meanwhile, beat egg yolks well.
Add sugar, salt and flour.
Add hot water and lemon juice, then stir into melted butter.
Cook in double boiler until thick, stirring all the time.
Use as filling and/or icing for white cake.
Prepare plums.
Cream butter or oleo with sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat after each addition.
Sift together flour, salt, cream of tartar and baking soda.
Blend yogurt and lemon peel and add to creamed mixture alternately with dry ingredients.
Stir until well blended.
Add chopped nuts and chopped plums; mix well.
Divide between 2 greased and floured 9 x 5-inch loaf pans . Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 50 to 55 minutes or until bread tests done.
Parboil the potatoes until nearly done.
