Cut them up and place in a casserole with the sour cream and soup.
Blend in the seasonings.
Top with the bread crumb and cheese mixture.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
In microwave or double boiler, melt unsweetened chocolate, 1 cup of chocolate chips and butter; cool 10 minutes.
In other bowl, beat sugar and eggs for 2 minutes.
Beat in vanilla and chocolate mixture.
Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt and beat into mixture.
Stir in remaining chocolate chips.
Cover and chill 3 hours.
Remove 1 cup dough and with lightly floured hands roll into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until slightly puffed.
Cool 3 to 4 minutes and transfer to wire rack. Dust with powdered sugar.
Put oleo, cocoa, oil
and water in a pan and bring to a boil. Sift plain flour. Add sugar into a large mixing bowl. Pour cocoa mixture
into
this.
Mix
eggs,
soda, vanilla and buttermilk in a separate bowl.
Add to first mixture.
Bake in a long pan in a 400° oven for 20 minutes.
After cake has been baking 15 minutes, start the icing.
Place 1/2 cup water and salt in small saucepan; bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and reduce heat.
Cook 15 minutes or until tender.
Drain, reserving liquid.
Set potatoes aside.
Add enough water to potato liquid to make 1 cup.
Set aside.
Melt butter in a 3-quart Dutch oven.
Add onion; saute until tender.
Blend in flour and pepper.
Stir in milk and potato liquid.
Cook over medium heat until mixture is bubbly and slightly thickened.
Add cooked potatoes and ham; heat gently.
Remove from heat and stir in cheese.
Top with croutons, if desired.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Separate dough and loosely tie each piece of dough into a knot, tucking in ends.
Arrange rolls 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Brush with butter and sprinkle with poppy seed. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.t: Green Beans In Onion And Garlic Sauce
d: Dissolve bouillon cube in water using a large saucepan over moderate heat.
Add the beans and simmer until nearly all the liquid has evaporated, turning them constantly.
Heat the oil and butter in a pan.
Add the garlic and the spring onions (shallots or scallions).
Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the beans and toss in the fat until well coated.
Sprinkle with the soy sauce, sugar and sherry.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Serve hot.
Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Beat together sugar, oil and vanilla until blended. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until blended.
Stir in flour mixture, a little at a time, until smooth.
Stir in beets and walnuts.
Turn into an oiled 8 1/2 x 4 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven until done, circa 1 hour.
Loosen edges and turn out on a rack.
Place cake in a plastic bag and let stand overnight at room temperature.
Combine apples, bananas, grapes and pineapple in a bowl.
Mix applesauce, pineapple juice concentrate and pecans in a bowl.
Pour over fruit, mixing well.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine eggs, banana, butter, fruit spread and vanilla in a medium bowl.
Add flour, coconut, baking powder and salt; mix well.
Stir in nuts.
Drop a tablespoon of dough 2 inches apart onto lightly greased cookie sheets.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool on wire racks. Store in tightly covered container.
Heat oil in large skillet.
Coat steak in flour, salt and pepper.
Brown meat, stirring several times.
Add sliced onions to steak.
Cook until onions are clear, but not brown.
Reduce heat to low; drain off fat.
Combine flour and melted margarine.
Press into 9 x 13-inch dish or pan and bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Cool completely. Blend cream cheese, powdered sugar and 1 cup whipped topping. Spread over pastry in pan.
Add a layer of 2 or 3 bananas, sliced. Top with prepared instant pudding.
Sprinkle on the 1/2 box of crushed vanilla wafers.
Top with whipped topping.
Chill.
Cook broccoli for 2 minutes; drain.
Put in a small casserole dish.
Mix soup and sour cream together; pour over broccoli.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Blend bananas and strawberries together.
Mix with next 5 ingredients; chill.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Blend well.
Spread cheese mixture on each slice of flattened bread.
Roll 1 spear (jelly roll fashion) in each bread slice. Fasten with toothpicks.
Dip rolls in melted butter.
Freeze.
When frozen firm, slice in thirds.
Bake 15 minutes at 400°, until brown.

recipes.t: Mom'S Pork Chops With Fried Apples
d: Make a batter of the egg, milk, salt, sage and pepper.
Dip chops into batter and brown in fat, turning once.
Cook slowly and until well cooked.
Place on platter and keep warm.
Draw off some drippings and make a milk gravy, using another pan.
Melt margarine, cream cheese and milk together in a saucepan. Add corn and chilies to cheese mixture; salt and pepper to taste. Pour into a greased casserole dish and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Add flour and soda.
Mix.
Pour in oats.
Mix well.
Take half of the mixture and press into a well-greased 9 x 11-inch pan.
Press hard to make crust.
Spread jam softly not to break oat mixture.
Sprinkle remaining mixture. Gently press together for top crust.
Bake 20 minutes at 400°. Cut into bars.
Mix fruit and marshmallows;
stir in sour cream.
Chill and serve.
Good with cookies.
Cut cake horizontally into 3 layers.
Drizzle with mixture of pineapple juice and almond flavoring.
Combine crushed pineapple and pudding mix in bowl.
Mix well.
Fold in whipped topping. Spread between layers and over top and sides of cake.
Sprinkle with almonds.
Makes 16 servings.
Pour water over gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Add drink and lemon rind and juice.
Chill until slightly thick; beat until foamy.
Fold in whipped cream and chill until firm.
Top with fresh strawberries or raspberries if desired.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Brown sausage and turkey in a large pot and drain well.
Cut cheese into chunks and add to the meat.
Heat over low heat and melt cheese.
Place bread slices on cookie sheets.
Spoon mixture onto each slice.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes, until cheese is melted and bread is crisp.
Mixture can be made ahead of time and microwaved to spoon on bread.
In large skillet, brown meat; drain off fat.
Stir in beans, soup and pepper.
Pour into casserole dish.
Arrange apple slices on top.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake, uncovered, at 450° for 25 minutes.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
In saucepan, combine soup mixes, salad dressing and vinegar. Gradually stir in water. Add remaining ingredients except steaks. Bring mixture to boil and let simmer 10 minutes.
Cool.
Marinate steaks overnight for better taste.
Broil over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes; turn and baste with sauce and broil additional 10 to 12 minutes longer.
Baste both sides before removing.
Enjoy!

In shallow dish beat eggs with milk. Dip steaks in mixture; coat with flour seasoned with salt and pepper. In large skillet, over medium high heat, saute steaks in oil and butter, turning once; cook 5 minutes for medium rare. Remove to serving platter; spoon milk gravy over steaks.
In large mixing bowl, cream together cheese, onion, horseradish and Miracle Whip.
Cut beef into small slivers and put 1/4 of it into mixture.
Set rest of beef aside.
Mix cheese mixture into a ball.
Place remaining beef on ball sides.
Serve with your favorite crackers.
Melt margarine in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Dip both sides of chicken in margarine; place skin side up in pan. Sprinkle with salt, tarragon and pepper.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Bring raisins to boil, drain and cool.
Mix together butter, sugar and eggs, one at a time.
Add dry ingredients, then add cherries, nuts and raisins.
Pour batter into ungreased tube pan. Bake 15 minutes at 350° and then lower to 300°.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Cool before removing from pan.
Beat egg, add sugar gradually, then melted shortening and vanilla.
Combine with remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet and flatten with fork.
Bake in oven at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Makes 60 cookies.
Mix
butter,
sugar
and water in saucepan.
Place over low heat; stir constantly until mixture comes to a boil.
Boil hard for
1 minute; remove from heat.
Stir in milk and vanilla. Gradually
add 10x sugar, beating until smooth after each addition.
Cool
to spreading consistency. Makes enough for 2 layers or 1 (9 x 13-inch) pan.
Bake cake mix according to package.
Take handle of wooden spoon and make holes in cake.
Pour Eagle Brand milk and creme of coconut over cake.
Top with drained pineapple and Cool Whip. Cover Cool Whip with coconut.
Refrigerate.
In large pan, heat oil on medium; add onion, green peppers and garlic.
Stir 5 minutes until tender.
Add tomatoes and juice (break up tomatoes with fingers).
Stir in peanut butter until peanut butter dissolves.
Add pepper and chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Add rice.
Reduce to simmer; cover and cook 40 minutes, until rice is done, then add chicken and cook 10 minutes longer. Serve each bowl garnished with parsley.
Cook potatoes; drain but save water.
Saute bacon and onion until brown.
Mash potatoes; add bacon and onion, parsley, salt, nutmeg and Worcestershire sauce.
Stir in milk.
Heat over low flame. Sprinkle with cheese.
Add reserved water if soup is too thick.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place bread cubes in buttered 3-quart casserole dish.
Pour butter over cubes; toss.
Combine eggs, molasses, cinnamon and nutmeg in a large bowl.
Gradually stir in milk and vanilla.
Stir in raisins.
Pour entire mixture over the bread cubes.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes or until set.
Serve warm, drizzled with heavy cream.
Serves 8.
Melt American cheese and milk in a double boiler for 12 minutes.
Cook pimento, egg, vinegar and sugar for 30 minutes and while still warm add 1 cup mayonnaise.
Brown hamburger.
Take skin off sausage; mince up and cook. Saute 4 garlic cloves in olive oil until almost done.
Add tomato sauce along with crushed tomatoes and a sprinkle of oregano.
Add in hamburger and sausage.
Drain off fat.
(Simmer for flavor.) Grate Mozzarella cheese in bowl.
Add large curd cottage cheese, 4 eggs, oregano, salt and pepper; mix together.

Combine onion soup mix and water and set aside. Flour, salt and pepper steaks and brown quickly on both sides in small amount of oil. Place into greased 9 x 13-inch casserole and pour soup mix over steaks. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until tender. Good served with rice or mashed potatoes.
Heat sour cream, Cheez Whiz and green chilies.
Pour over hominy and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown ground beef.
Drain.
Add vegetables and gravy.
Mix. Put mixture in one pie crust.
Use second crust as lid.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
In a bowl, toss chicken, celery, green pepper, onion and mayonnaise; cover and chill.
Just before serving, mix in potato chips.
Serve on salad or lettuce leaves.
Garnish with melon wedges and strawberries.
Sift flour and salt.
Rub in butter until mixture resembles fine bread crumbs.
Stir in dates and sugar.
Beat egg and add to dry ingredients with sufficient milk to give soft dough.
Place on floured surface and knead lightly.
Pat out to approximately 1 cm. (1/2-inch) using a 5 cm. (2-inch) floured cutter, cut into rounds. Place onto lightly greased over tray.
Glaze tops with milk. Bake in a very hot oven 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes approximately 12 scones.
Cut chicken cutlets into cubes, about 1/2 to 1-inch.
Roll chicken pieces in flour.
In large pot, saute floured chicken in butter until lightly browned, over low heat.
Add mushrooms and peppers into pan.
Add wine and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes or until peppers are softened.
This meal can be served over rice or noodles.
Pour water into a large container with a rack.
Bring water to a boil using high heat.
Remove seeds and membrane center from pumpkin and discard.
Cut pumpkin into wedges (do not peel).
Place pumpkin on rack over boiling water.
Cover container and steam pumpkin at medium heat for 30 minutes or until pulp is tender.
Dot pumpkin with margarine and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.

recipes.t: Easy Chicken Stew With Scallion Dumplings
d: Combine chicken breasts and stock in a large pot; bring to boil over high heat.
Reduce heat and simmer for at least 10 minutes, but a half hour won't hurt.
Add the carrots, onion, celery and bay leaf; simmer, partially covered, for 20 minutes. Make Scallion Dumplings as shown.
Saute onion in oil until golden.
Stir in rice.
Heat through and add remaining ingredients.
For a creamy effect, break an egg over the rice and mix it well into the rice.
The Japanese add any vegetable or cooked meat to Cha-Han, as they are available. Serves 4 to 5.
Mix all ingredients (except ham) with mixer until smooth. Spread a thin layer of cream cheese on a tortilla.
Add a layer of ham.
Top with another tortilla, cream cheese, ham, etc.
Repeat layers until all ingredients are used.
The top tortilla should be plain.
Should be enough tortillas to make 2 stacks, 5 layers each.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cut into small, pie-shape wedges.
Heat oven to 300°.
Mix nuts and margarine in medium bowl.
Add cheese, garlic powder, oregano and celery salt; toss.
Spread in ungreased jelly roll pan.
Bake, stirring occasionally.
Stir in cereal.
Cool.
Store in airtight jar.
Mix all ingredients, except liver sausage, into paste.
Mash sausage; blend into paste.
Shape and chill.
Blend cream cheese. Add milk.
Add garlic powder to taste.
Frost ball.
Garnish with olives.
Serve with crackers.
Mix livers, water, bouillon cube, onion and thyme in 1-quart saucepan.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat and simmer uncovered until liver is done, about 15 minutes.
Cool mixture; drain and reserve 1/4 cup broth.
Mix liver, reserved broth and remaining ingredients in blender or food processor.
Blend smooth. Refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Makes 2 cups.
Combine the first 3 ingredients and simmer 20 minutes. Combine the beef, egg, bread crumbs, salt, oregano, basil and 1/2 cup prepared sauce.
Form meat mixture into free standing loaf and place in shallow baking dish. Bake at 375° for 50 minutes.
Pour remaining sauce over. Arrange sliced Mozzarella cheese on top. Bake 15 minutes longer.
Cook carrots in small amount of boiling salted water for 5 minutes or until tender-crisp.

Drain. Place in shallow 1 1/2-quart, oiled baking dish. Add zucchini, tomatoes and croutons, tossing until combined. Pour milk into saucepan. Whisk in cornstarch, seasoned salt, black pepper and dill weed. Add butter. Bring to a boil. Cook, stirring until smooth and thickened.
Pour over vegetables. Bake at 375° for 25 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley. Serves 4.
Serve with poultry and baked potatoes.

Add Jell-O to boiling water and stir until Jell-O is completely dissolved. Add vodka, liqueur and cranberry juice. Stir well. Pour into little plastic cups and leave in refrigerator overnight. When ready to serve, squirt a little whipped cream on top. How to eat a Jell-O shot: Put plastic cup in mouth; close mouth enough to let tongue go around the inside rim to loosen the Jell-O from the cup. Down it in one swallow.
Mix butter, thyme and cayenne.
Spread on pork.
Place pork on rack in roasting pan.
Pour orange juice over it.
Roast at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes per pound or until temperature on meat thermometer reaches 185°.
Remove meat to platter and keep warm.
Mix molasses, sugar, and butter in a pan.
Melt it.
Add cream and spices, mix.
Mix the baking powder with a little of the flour.
Mix everything in a large bowl.
Put the dough in aluminum pan in the refrigerator.
Leave to harden a few days.
Take a little of the dough out, hit it a little, mix a little more flour in it if needed.
Sprinkle flour on a table, roll the dough as thin as possible.
Press shapes in it.
Put the cookies on a greased baking sheet.
Cook 5 - 10 minutes until brown.
Generously grease a 12 cup Bundt pan.
In a large bowl, combine flour mixture, yeast and cheese.
Mix well.
Stir in hot water, oil, egg and chives.
Knead dough for 5 minutes.
Cover and let rest 5 minutes.
Rub the birds lightly with salt, then brown in oil.
Remove to heated casserole.
In same oil, saute carrot, onion, green pepper and mushrooms.
Blend in flour; stir in heated broth.
Season to taste with salt.
Pour this sauce and wine over quail.
Cover and bake at 350° about 1 hour.
Serve over rice.
Combine sugar, water, syrup and salt in saucepan.
Stir until sugar is completely dissolved.
Cook rapidly until small amount in cup of cold water forms a hard ball (260°).
Add molasses and butter.
Cook slowly until a small amount forms a hard ball and cracks when you bite and doesn't stick to your teeth (275°; lower altitude 280°).

Pour this over a dishpan sprayed with Pam and half full of buttered popcorn with Planters nuts sprinkled on top. Mix cooked syrup with popcorn and nuts with large wooden spoon. Divide and place on 3 buttered cookie sheets.
Pound down flat and cool.
Store in airtight containers.
Heat oven to 375°.
Cream butter and cheese until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg, vanilla and half of the cake mix (dry) until smooth.
Stir in remaining cake mix and the coconut.
Mix seasoning from onions to black pepper.
Wash roast and cut several 2-inch slits at an angle as deep as possible without going all the way through the meat.
Stuff as much seasoning as possible into each slit.
Pour remaining seasoning over roast.
Place in roasting pan.
Add 1 cup water.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 375°. Add 1/2 can soup and gravy mix.
Stir every 5 minutes until well blended.
Bake another 30 minutes to 1 hour until done.
To your favorite biscuit recipe, add 1 cup grated Swiss cheese and 2 tablespoons caraway seed.
Cut out biscuits.
Sprinkle with kosher salt and butter and bake.
Different!

After dough or manual cycle is completed in bread machine, and before the baking cycle begins, remove the dough from the machine. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and carefully form into a ball without punching down.
Place onto a greased cookie sheet and let rise about 1 hour until double in size.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 375° for 25 to 35 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool.
Hollow out cooled bread like a pumpkin, reserving "lid" to put back on.
Fill with your favorite meat, soup or whatever.
Replace the top.
Serve and enjoy.
In a blender, add milk, sugar, peanut butter and vanilla. Blend on high speed.
Add ice until the smoothie gets thick.
Make sure all ice is chopped up.
Melt butter and add flour, blending well.
Add milk gradually and cook until thickened.
Add half of cheese and seasoning; cook until cheese is melted, stirring constantly.
Clean the shrimp and cut in half.
Mix with rice and sauce.
Cut wing end piece off and discard.
Rinse chicken and pat dry.
In shallow pan, melt butter.
Add seasoned salt, garlic powder and tarragon.
Mix well.
In shallow pan, combine bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Dip wings, one at a time, in butter mixture, completely coating, then coat in bread crumb mixture, pressing down to coat completely.
Place on greased baking sheet. Bake in a 400° oven for 45 minutes to an hour until golden brown. Serve hot.
Heat broiler or grill.
In bowl, combine peppers, basil, oil and cheese.
Place bread, cut side up, on rack 4-inches from heat source (or cut side down on grill over medium coals); toast 3 minutes or until golden.
Rub with garlic; top with pepper mixture and return to broiler 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Cut crosswise into 8 pieces.
Mix onion, black olives, mayonnaise, salt, mustard and shredded cheese thoroughly.
Spread cheese on split muffin halves. Bake in preheated 350° oven for 10 minutes.
Makes 8 muffin halves.

recipes.t: Chicken With Leek And Mushroom Sauce
d: Heat 1 1/2 teaspoons oil in a skillet and saut the chicken until lightly browned on both sides, about 5 minutes. Remove from the skillet and keep hot. Heat the other 1 1/2 teaspoons oil in the same skillet used for the chicken (do not wash out in between; you want that great chicken flavor in the bottom of the pan). Add the leeks and cook, stirring for 2 minutes. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes more. Add brandy and cook for 2 minutes. Transfer this to a mixing bowl. Whisk chicken broth with flour and add to the same skillet. Cook, whisking until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Return mushroom mixture, chicken and juices to skillet. Reduce heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through, about 4 minutes. Serves 4.

recipes.t: Fresh Apple Cake With Cream Cheese Icing
d: Combine sugar, oil, eggs and vanilla; add the apples. Sift together flour, soda, cinnamon and salt; add to apple mixture. Mix thoroughly (batter will be thick). Add nuts and mix again.
Pour into greased and floured 8 x 8-inch square pan, loaf pan or Bundt pan. Bake 90 minutes at 325°. Test cake with toothpick.
(Can add 3/4 cup raisins, if desired.)
Shuck, silk and wash corn.
Split each row of kernels with sharp knife.
Carefully slice just the tips of corn into a large bowl.
Using dull side of knife, run it down the cob to extract all the milky pulp from corn.
Put cut off corn into deep microwave dish with butter, salt and pepper.
Cook, covered, on High for 10 minutes.
Add milk and arrowroot or cornstarch.
If you like it thicker, add more.
Cook on 70% power for 6 to 10 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes until desired consistency.
Prepare pudding as directed on package using low-fat milk. Mix pudding, sour cream, pineapple and sweetener.
Pour into pie shell.
Top with Cool Whip and garnish with kiwi fruit. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Bring water and bouillon cubes to boil for 10 minutes.
Lower temperature.
Add chicken, onion, celery, tomatoes and spices; cook over low-medium heat for 2 to 3 hours.
Remove chicken from soup; remove all meat from bones.
Return chicken to soup.
Boil macaroni until done.
Spoon orzo and soup into bowls.
Saute chopped onion in butter; pour into a casserole dish. Slice potatoes and place over onion.
Overlap potatoes with sliced artichokes.
Pour whipping cream over all; top with Parmesan cheese and cook at 375° for 1 hour.
Soak peas overnight in water.
Drain.
Combine all ingredients, except rice, in 6 quart pressure cooker.
Secure lid. Cook at 15 pounds of pressure for 35 minutes.
Remove pressure, then remove lid.
Place ham on carving board, trim fat; slice.
Cream the butter.
Add sugar, egg, vanilla and salt.
Add flour and mix well.
Add oatmeal and blend.
Add pecans and blend. If too dry, add a tablespoon of water.
Form into balls the size of a small walnut.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Roll in powdered sugar while still warm.
Makes about 4 1/2 dozen.
Combine mustard and brown sugar; spread on pork chops.
Place a chop vertically at one end of oblong baking pan, fat edge up. Next to it, place a pineapple ring, a green pepper ring and an onion slice.
Repeat until all are used.
Fasten together with skewers.
Pour pineapple juice over all.
Cover pan with foil. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Yield: 6 servings.
Prepare cornbread as package directs.
Cut into 6 pieces.
In skillet, brown meat with onion, green pepper and garlic; drain. Stir in tomatoes and tomato sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Serve over cornbread.
Prep and cook time:
30 minutes.
In top of
a
double boiler, melt butter and chocolate. Blend with a whisk, then add oats and combine well.
Form into golf size balls.
This mixture is both crumbly and wet and you might
not think it
is
going
to
hold
together,
but
surprise...it does. Place in
a waxed paper lined pan and chill. When the cookies are firm,
roll them in confectioners sugar. Store them in the refrigerator, but allow them to come to room temperature 30 minutes before serving.
Cook the hamburger and sausage; drain.
Put this in a bowl with the mushroom soup, tomato soup or sauce, chili powder and onion and green pepper, which have been sauteed in 1/2 stick margarine.
Cook the egg noodles.
Remove the skin from the salmon.
In the bottom of a pan, place enough orange slices to have under the salmon.
Lay the salmon on top and sprinkle it with the nutmeg.
Place the remaining slices of orange over the salmon.
Pour on the wine and orange juice and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes or until the salmon is cooked.
Remove the salmon from the pan and place on serving dish.
Cook rotini.
Set aside to cool.
Mix together mayo, water, vinegar and sugar until smooth.
Add rest of spices, onion and celery to dressing.
Pour over rotini and mix thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Stir salad two or three times during refrigeration.
Saute onion until tender in butter in saucepan.
(Onion should look transparent.)
Add remaining ingredients; simmer, covered, 10 minutes.
Add 2 pounds chopped, chipped ham and heat through. Serve over hamburger rolls.
Combine.
Mix eggs and pudding mix well.
Beat 2 minutes. Spread in a greased and floured pan.
Sprinkle with chips and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Use a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cream the shortening and sugar together.
Beat in eggs.
Add prunes, dry ingredients, pecans and milk.
Bake in a 350° oven.
In a large skillet over moderate heat, saute onion in butter. Remove onion and set aside.
Cut 8 small zucchini squash into 1/2-inch rounds.
Saute in skillet with remaining butter.
Add water, salt and pepper.
Cook covered with tight-fitting lid for 6 to 8 minutes;
add onion.
Blend in with a fork.
Do not overcook as squash becomes soggy and loses it shape.
Skin and bone chicken; cut into small cubes.
Saute in oil until firm and white.
Stir in celery and cook, about 1 1/2 minutes or until crisp and tender.
Add bean sprouts, water chestnuts, soup, soy sauce and pepper.
Cook 1 minute longer; stir in pimento and onions.
Heat but do not overcook.
Spoon over rice and top with noodles and soy sauce.
Makes 6 servings.
Place the water in a large pan and bring it to a boil.

Brown the sausage and drain off excess fat. Add the celery, onions and green pepper and simmer for 10-15 minutes. When the water is boiling, pour in the rice and soup and allow it to boil gently for 15 minutes. Combine with the sausage and vegetable mixture in a large casserole dish, add the almonds and bake, covered, for 1 hour at 375°f. 190°c. gas mark 5. Uncover and bake for a further 15 minutes.
In a 10 x 6-inch baking dish, combine lemon juice, salt and paprika.
Add halibut steaks and marinate 15 minutes.
Turn steaks after 10 minutes. Cook onion in margarine until tender, but not brown.
Place onion on top of halibut and top with 6 green pepper strips.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork.
Heat
butter in skillet until hot. Add corn, ham, onion and green
pepper.
Saute,
stirring
often,
until onion and pepper are
crisp and tender (about 5 minutes). Stir in salt, pepper
and milk. Cut down heat. Let warm just long enough to heat thoroughly.
Combine apricot nectar, pineapple juice and concentrate for limeade in a punch bowl; stir in ginger ale.
Make a ring with punch and add lime slices or whole strawberries (or if you prefer, add ice cubes).
Float a few lime slices and whole strawberries on top.
Makes about 50 punch cup servings.
In a mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and butter.
Add cheese, onions, garlic salt; mix well.
Spread on both sides of each slice of bread.
Wrap loaf in a large piece of heavy duty foil.
Seal tightly.
Grill, covered over medium coals for 8 - 10 minutes turning once.
Unwrap foil; grill 5 minutes longer.
Yield 10 -12 servings.
Combine the butter and the sugar and beat well.
Add the eggs, one at a time if using an electric mixer.
Sift the dry ingredients together and add alternately with the coffee or milk. Fold in the fruit and nut mixture.
Spread thin in a greased baking pan.
Bake in a moderate oven, 350°, for about thirty minutes.
Cool and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Cut into squares.
Makes about thirty-two cookies.
Melt butter with garlic.
Add wine, then shrimp.
Cook for 5 minutes (don't overcook).
Add parsley.
Sprinkle with celery salt.
Combine first three ingredients.
Let stand for 15 minutes. Combine sugar and next 4 ingredients.
Add to apple mixture. Spoon into 9-inch pastry crust.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Then sprinkle with walnut topping.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake for 30 to 45 minutes.
Can serve with ice cream.
Rinse wings and pat dry.
Cut apart; discard tip.
Arrange in one layer on large cookie sheet lined with foil.
Mix soy sauce and oil; brush over wings.
Mix brown sugar, salt and chili powder.
Sprinkle evenly over top of wings.
Place under broiler until golden brown.
Remove from oven.
Mix soup and vinegar. Pour over wings.
Bake, uncovered, in 350° oven for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Cool.
Combine ground beef and Manwich according to instructions on can.
Prepare crust according to directions.
Spread Manwich over crust.
Top with cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes. Serve with lettuce, tomatoes and sour cream.
Boil water and margarine.
Add flour; mix vigorously.
Remove from heat for 5 minutes.
Add eggs, one at a time, and mix.
Drop from a tablespoon onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool on rack.
Cream the butter and peanut butter together.
Add sugar gradually. Add egg and beat well. Add remaining ingredients that have been sifted together.
Mix thoroughly.
Mold into balls using rounded teaspoonful of dough.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet. Flatten with fork (crisscross).
Bake 12 to 15 minutes in a 375° oven.
Cook noodles as directed and drain.
Brown meat in pan and add sauce, salt and pepper; set aside.
Blend well the cream cheese, cottage cheese, sour cream, onion and parsley.
Butter pan and spread 1/2 noodles, then the creamed cheeses, then the rest of the noodles.
Sprinkle with melted butter.
Top with meat.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Grease and flour 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Combine cake mix, eggs and water in a large bowl.
Beat at medium speed with mixer for 2 minutes.
Stir in pecans.
Pour into pan.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees or grill to medium-high.
Spray foil with nonstick cooking spray.
Center one fish fillet on each sheet of foil.
Top with green onions; place frozen vegetables around fish.
Sprinkle fish with thyme, marjoram, salt and pepper. Top with margarine.
Bring up foil sides.
Double fold top and ends to seal packet, leaving room for heat circulation inside. Repeat to make two jackets. Bake 18-20 minutes on a cookie sheet in oven or grill 10-12 minutes in covered grill.
Drizzle with lemon juice.
Makes 2 servings.
Slice apples or pears. Pour water over and sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Mix flour, sugar and egg. Sprinkle over apples.
Melt butter and pour over.
Bake at 350° about 45 minutes or until done.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Wash chicken thoroughly (inside and out).
Mix oil, vinegar, salt, paprika and black pepper in a small bowl.
Pour mixture inside and over chicken and massage into meat. Let excess remain in bottom of baking dish.
Stuff chicken with apple, orange, onion and celery (as full as possible).
Sprinkle paprika and parsley flakes on top of garnishment.
Cook in preheated oven at 400° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Reduce heat to 325° (lay sheet of tinfoil on top to prevent from burning) and continue cooking for 45 minutes (longer if chicken is very large).

Brown meat in butter and oil in skillet. Add mushrooms. Stir in 3/4 cup bouillon, wine, soy sauce and onion salt; continue cooking. Remove meat from skillet into 2-quart casserole dish. Leave drippings.
Overlap the bottom of a greased 13 x 9-inch pan with tortillas. Beat eggs with milk, then add cheese and salsa.
Mix together.
Add meat, if desired.
Bake at 350° for good hour.
It's done when an inserted knife comes out clean.
Slice the cucumbers and onion into a container with a cover. Mix sour cream with sugar to taste.
Pour over cucumbers and onion, folding into the vegetables.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cut sausage diagonally into 1/2-inch slices.
Wash potatoes; cut into 1/3-inch crosswise sections.
Layer sausage, potatoes and next 5 ingredients in order given in a large Dutch oven, sprinkling each vegetable layer with salt and pepper.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer 35 to 45 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Fire roast the chile by placing it directly in the flame of gas burner or laying it on a electric burner.
Rotate slowly until skin is darkened and blistered.
Place on cutting board and scrape skin off.
Skin should slide off easily.
If not, place back in fire.
Remove seeds and chop coarsely.
Place tomatoes, chilies, onions and seasonings in blender for 30 seconds.
Add cilantro and pulse for 5 seconds.
Place in the fridge for 30 minutes to chill. Enjoy!
Beat margarine and 1/2 cup confectioners sugar and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Add flour and walnuts.
Take enough dough and cover each candy kiss.
Bake at 375° for 8 minutes (not brown, just set).
Do not remove from cookie sheet until cool.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Store in airtight container.
Do not refrigerate or freeze.
Heat milk, marshmallows and candy in 3-quart saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly, until marshmallows and candy are melted and blended.
Refrigerate about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally until mixture mounds slightly when dropped by spoon.
Beat whipping cream in chilled large bowl with electric mixer on high speed until soft peaks form.
Fold chocolate mixture into whipped cream.
Pour into pie crust.
Refrigerate, uncovered, for at least 8 hours or until set. Garnish with sliced strawberries.
Saute onions, sprinkled with garlic, in butter.
Remove from pan.
Saute scallops in same butter, sprinkled with Worcestershire sauce and sugar.
Mix onion, scallops and two milks and heat slowly.
Add pepper and a pat of butter.
Mix Jell-O in hot water. Cool. Stir in cherry pie filling. Refrigerate for one hour. Mix together cream cheese and Cool Whip. Fold into Jell-O mixture and place in a decorative mold.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Place chicken in a single layer in a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
In a bowl, combine soup, sour cream, soup mix and pepper.
Blend thoroughly.
Spread over chicken.
Sprinkle with noodles.
Bake for 1 hour or until chicken is tender.
Serves 4.
In a large pot bring water to boil.
Add yellow squash, zucchini, and onions.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 6 minutes. Drain and reserve in a large bowl.
In a small bowl whisk together soup, sour cream, cheese, salt, and pepper.
Add soup mixture to reserved squash.
Mix together.
Transfer to a large baking dish. Cover with foil and bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Top with crumbled cornbread and with butter.
Bake 10 additional minutes.
Cut smoked sausage in to 1/2-inch pieces.
Saute sliced onion with sausage.
Add tomato sauce.
Add 1 can of water or more.
Add basil and garlic powder.
Cut up the peeled potatoes in bite-size pieces and add to sausage.
Simmer until potatoes are about half done.
Add drained green beans.
Stir and simmer, covered.
If it looks dry, add more water.
Pour peas in bowl; mash well with potato masher.
Add egg, salt, pepper, flour and onions.
Mix well.
Pour oil in skillet and cook on medium heat.
Drop mixture by heaping tablespoon into hot oil.
Brown.
Lightly coat large nonstick skillet with olive oil.
Heat over medium.
Add onion and garlic.
Saute 1 minute.
Add tomatoes with juice.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 30 minutes.
Stir in salt and pepper.
Use sauce immediately or cool and refrigerate, covered, for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

Spray large dish with Pam spray. Place large can pineapple on bottom. Layer blueberries on top of pineapple. Add crumbled cake mix on top. Pat with butter and sprinkle nuts on top. Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes or until brown.
Heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add broccoli, tomatoes, black olives and garlic.
Saute for 4 to 5 minutes.
Cook bow tie pasta.
Combine with sauce and add Romano cheese.
In
1 quart bowl combine cauliflower, carrot and water. Cover with
plastic
wrap.
Cook at High 6 to 7 minutes. Stir once. Sprinkle
vegetables
into pie shell.
Sprinkle cheese over vegetables.
Pour
cream
into
cup measure.
Cook at Medium 2 to 2 1/4 minutes.
Give each child a cookie.
Have prepared mixture of cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip.
Smooth on cookie.
Arrange sliced fruit on tray.
Let each child top pizza as desired.
They may want to make faces or try to make their cookie look like a real pizza.
Get creative!
Top with shredded coconut, if desired.

recipes.t: How To Bake A Frozen Turkey Breast
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Wrap turkey breast in foil, using drugstore method of wrapping.
Place wrapped breast in aluminum baking pan.
Bake for 3 hours.
Remove from oven and carefully open top of foil, folding back.
Place margarine on top of turkey and season with salt and pepper.
Return to oven and bake an additional 30 minutes to brown.
Cool and slice.

recipes.t: Miss Frances Stephens' Pineapple Cake For A Crowd
d: Mix 3/4 cup undrained pineapple with coconut and set aside. Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
Work shortening until soft, then add sugar until mixture is creamy. Add eggs, one at a time and beat after each one.
Mix flour mixture and remaining undrained pineapple into batter alternately. Pour into baking pan.
Sprinkle batter with pineapple and coconut mixture and chocolate morsels.
Bake 25 minutes at 325° in greased pan.
In a saucepan, combine 1 cup water and milk.
Bring to a boil. Remove from heat and stir in cereal, butter, molasses, sugar and salt.
Cool to lukewarm.
Heat remaining water to 110° to 115° and pour into large mixing bowl.
Sprinkle with yeast and stir until dissolved.
Add cereal mixture and whole wheat flour.
Beat well. Add enough all-purpose flour to make a stiff dough.
Turn out onto a floured surface.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Place in a greased bowl, turning once to grease top. Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour. Punch the dough down.
Shape into two loaves and place in greased 8 x 4 x 2-inch loaf pans.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Yield: 2 loaves.
If cooking for two, wrap one loaf in heavy-duty aluminum foil and freeze to enjoy later.

Bake lemon cake mix according to directions on package for 9 x 13-inch pan. Cool 15 minutes. Stir together lemonade concentrate and powdered sugar. Blend thoroughly. Poke top of warm cake every 1/2-inch with long-tined fork, wiping fork occasionally to reduce sticking. Drizzle lemonade mixture evenly over top of cake. Cover and refrigerate about 2 hours or until chilled. Spread frosting of your choice over top of cake and sprinkle with sugar for garnish. Cover loosely and refrigerate until serving time. Any remaining cake should be refrigerated.
Boil raisins in water until almost dry.
Mix applesauce, oil, eggs, vanilla, pecans and 7 packages of Sweet 'N Low together and set aside.
Mix soda, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and 9 packages of Sweet 'N Low.
Put all together and mix well.
Place in oiled and floured 9 x 13-inch pan or tube pan.
Bake until done. Twenty-four servings = 1 fruit and 1 bread.
Drain roasted peppers; place in a bowl.
Mix with Provolone. Dress with spices and olive oil.
Refrigerate overnight or serve immediately.

In a large 10-inch pan, melt butter; stir in sugar and dates. Remove from heat and add egg; beat and return to heat and continue cooking over a medium heat and stirring constantly, until mixture starts to boil.
Remove from heat and add remaining ingredients except the 2 1/2 cups of coconut.
Stir well and let stand about 20 minutes.
You may cool in refrigerator.
Roll into balls and roll in coconut.
Great for the holidays.
May be frozen and used at a later date.
Makes 4 to 5 dozen.
Season chicken as preferred; roll in flour.
Place in rectangular baking pan or casserole dish.
Mix soup with 1 can of water and pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
Chicken will form its own crust and soup will make gravy.
Grease and flour a loaf tin, 9 1/2 x 5 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch.
Sift together first three ingredients.
Add nuts.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly after each addition.
Add the flour mixture alternately with the milk, beating well after each addition.
Bake in the prepared loaf pan in a moderate oven (350°) for about 1 to 1 1/4 hours.
Cut scallops in half; soak them in milk for 10 minutes.
Drain and dry on towel.
Dust scallops lightly with flour.
Heat butter in skillet.
Add garlic and stir.
Add scallops and saute until lightly brown and just heated through.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in parsley and serve at once with lemon wedge.

recipes.t: Faren'S Yummy Milkshake(This Recipe Is For 1 Serving)
d: Pour milk into blender container.
Add ice cream, jam and pudding mix.
Cover tightly; blend until mixed well.
Pour your milkshake into a tall glass and enjoy.
Grind bologna and cheese into large bowl.
Add all other ingredients and stir.
Sift all dry ingredients together.
Add oil, vinegar, vanilla and 2 cups cold water.
Blend until mixed well.
Put in 9 x 12-inch glass baking dish.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Lola Hexom'S Asparagus Corned Beef Casserole
d: Cook Creamettes in unsalted water; drain.
Add mushroom soup and heat until blended.
Make white sauce of butter, flour and milk.
Add cheese and let melt.
Add the rest of ingredients.
Use a greased casserole.
Pour sauce over all and stir lightly.
Put potato chips on top.
Bake for 60 minutes at 350°.
Serves 15.
Mix first five ingredients together and cook until smooth. Add almonds.
Drop by level tablespoon onto lightly greased and floured cookie sheet approximately 4 inches apart.
Because cookies will spread, place only 4 to 6 cookies on cookie sheet at one time.
Bake at 350° for 6 to 8 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool slightly.
Carefully lift each cookie, using a wide spatula, and place on dowel or rolling pin to cool into curved shape.
If cookie hardens before removing from pan, return pan to oven for a few seconds to soften cookies.
Remember to grease and flour cookie sheet with each batch.
Makes 18 cookies.
In medium bowl beat the butter, sugar and vanilla extract until smooth and creamy.
Mix in flour and salt until well combined.
Add the nuts, mixing well.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour or until dough is stiff enough to shape into marble size balls.
Place cookies on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes or until set, but not brown.
While still warm, roll into powdered sugar.
Let cool.
Roll in sugar again.
Mix together sugar, Karo syrup, water, vanilla and raw peanuts.
Cook over low heat until peanuts begin to pop.
Remove from stove.
Stir in soda.
Stir well.
Spread very thin on greased pan. Set until cool.
Break into desired pieces.
Dissolve lemon juice and honey.
Add gin. Put in crock and let stand overnight.
(Leave lemon rinds in mixture.) Next morning squeeze rinds and strain.
Makes about 1/5 and a half.
Serve in old fashion glasses over shaved ice.
Mix milk, egg, butter, sugar and salt.
Add orange juice, flour, baking powder and vanilla. Gently fold in the chopped apples.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls into hot oil (350°), until golden brown, turning to brown evenly.
Drain on paper towel. Roll in powdered sugar.
Enjoy!
Season pork chops and spread one side with mustard.
Heat butter in a skillet and brown the chops mustard side up.
Turn and brown the mustard side and spread browned side with mustard.
Add grapes to the pan and shake it.
Cover and simmer over low heat until chops are tender and cooked through.
Remove the chops to a warm platter.
Skim most of the fat from the dripping.
Add sour cream to pan and heat but do not boil.
Pour sauce over meat. Serves 4.
Shred cabbage and
add sugar. In
saucepan
add
oil, vinegar, honey, salt, prepared mustard and celery seed.
Bring all to boil.
Pour over cabbage.
Let refrigerate overnight.
Combine flour, salt and pepper.
Coat meat with mixture. Brown on both sides in shortening in large skillet.
When meat is well browned, add water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until tender.
Remove chops to heated platter.
Prepare milk gravy. Serve gravy with chops.
Cook sweet potatoes, drain and mash. Combine first five ingredients and

spoon into a buttered casserole dish. Bake at 325 degrees for 25 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle with coconut. Arrange marshmallows on top and bake 10 to 15 minutes longer until marshmallows are golden brown.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar, butter and yeast dissolved in water. Add lemon rind and salt.
Mix well, beating until light.
Add flour.
Knead for 15 minutes or until dough is smooth.
Don't leave dough too soft.
Cover with cloth.
Let dough rise to double in bulk.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Have plenty of oil, keeping heat about medium to low.
Make donuts, about 1/3 cup each.
Stick finger through the center of dough to stretch the hole or just spoon dough in hot oil.
Fry until golden, turning once. Remove from oil.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Put pats of butter, meat tenderizer, 1/4 cup oil and dry red wine over roast.
Sprinkle rosemary, garlic cloves, salt and pepper.
Add cut potatoes into pan, cut lengthwise.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Take out potatoes and continue cooking meat until done as desired.
Mix together cake mix, pudding, eggs, rum, water and oil for 2 minutes.
Pour into tube pan, greased and lined with the pecan halves.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Cool cake for 5 minutes, then pour glaze over it.
In saucepan, combine sugar, unsweetened chocolate, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Stir in water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over low heat until chocolate melts.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat and simmer 4 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add milk; heat over low heat until mixture is hot.
Beat with rotary beater until foamy. Serve in mugs or cups.
Garnish with whipped dessert topping. Makes 6 servings.
Beat cream until stiff.
Fold in sugar, sour cream and peel. Serve over strawberries.
Sprinkle with grated chocolate.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Drain canned shrimp and rinse with cold water.
Cut large shrimp in half.
Remove crusts from bread and cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place half the bread cubes in a well-greased baking dish (12 x 8 x 2-inch).
Cover with a layer of shrimp, green pepper and half the cheese.
Top with remaining bread cubes and cheese. Combine eggs, mustard, salt and pepper; beat.
Add milk and mix well.
Pour over bread; sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in a moderate oven (350°) for 45 to 50 minutes, or until firm in the center. Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Cut the top off of each tomato.
Scoop out pulp and seeds. Salt inside of each tomato.
Invert tomatoes and drain 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Slice peppers and mushrooms.
Place chicken breasts in oblong baking dish and season as desired. Place sliced vegetables and onions around chicken.
Mix dressing and pour over chicken and vegetables.
Bake until done, approximately 30 to 40 minutes.
Best served with wild rice or dressing.
Brown hamburger and onion; add to boiled and drained Creamettes.
Add tomato soup and peas (drained).
Simmer until warm and serve.
Add peanut brittle, vanilla and sugar to whipped cream; toss gently.
Place into mold and freeze.
Combine olive oil, Parmesan cheese, sugar and red wine vinegar.
Add sliced onion, chopped palm, chopped artichokes and pimento.
Stir.
Cover and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Rinse and drain lettuce.
Tear into bite sized pieces.
Combine all and toss just before serving.
Heat cooked, shredded beets in melted butter in saucepan. Stir in flour, sugar and salt.
Add sour cream and vinegar.
Heat thoroughly, stirring frequently, but do not boil.
Ground together the ham and pork.
Mix tapioca through ground meat.
Combine with other ingredients and mix well.
Bake in 7 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan (or form a loaf and bake in 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan) at 450° for 20 minutes.
Decrease temperature to 375° and bake 45 minutes longer.
Serve hot or cold.
Serves 8 to 10.

recipes.t: Chicken Nachos - Meets The Four F'S (Fine Finger Football Food)
d: Rinse and cube the chicken breasts.
Add water, taco seasoning, Cajun seasoning, honey, red pepper and cubed chicken to skillet.
Bring contents to a boil; reduce to simmer.
Cook for 30 minutes, until sauce is slightly thickened.
Lightly coat an 11 x 7 inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Arrange chilies in dish and top half of each with Jack cheese and turkey (cut as necessary to fit chilies).
Fold edges of chilies together and place seam side down in dish.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, whisk together the milk and eggs.
Add this to the flour mixture, beating until smooth.
Pour over the chilies.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Remove from oven and turn off the heat.
Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the top and return to the oven 1 minute to melt the cheese.
Serve immediately.
In a large mixer bowl, cream butter, sugar, eggs, vanilla and salt until well blended.
Stir in melted chocolate.
Add flour and nuts.
Drop by heaping teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart on well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cool 1 minute before removing.
While warm, sprinkle with powdered sugar.

In a 9-inch pie plate, flour bottom of pan and put pie crust in. Poke vent holes in crust bottom with fork. In a large bowl, mix chicken soup, potato soup, 1/2 cup milk, shredded chicken and vegetables. Pour mixture into pie crust. Top with second pie crust and trim edges to fit. Poke vent holes in pie top. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until crust is brown.
Cook pineapple,
sugar,
salt
and egg until thickened; add the gelatin.
Let cool.
Beat the chilled evaporated milk, then fold into the chilled mixture and then the cottage cheese and strawberries.
Put it in a baked crust.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix chicken, 1/2 of green chilies, 1 can soup, 1 cup sour cream and spices.
Spoon onto tortillas and fold like a burrito.
Place in baking pan with sides touching each other.
Mix other can of soup, 1 cup sour cream, remaining chilies and milk.
Spread over tortillas.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Thinly slice green onions (including tops).
Combine with white rice, finely chopped tomatoes, olive oil and vinegar. Cover and chill.
Add warm water to croutons; mix and press into buttered 10-inch pie plate.
Scramble hamburg and onion; drain off fat. Add cheese, eggs, catsup or barbecue sauce and cup of croutons. Press onto crouton crust.
Top with sliced tomatoes.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Top with cheese; bake 2 minutes longer.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
In large bowl, dissolve yeast in water.
Stir in egg.
Add flour mixture.
Press dough into prepared pan.
Blend garlic, salt and butter.
Dip sharp knife into butter, then cut lengthwise and crosswise at 1-inch intervals.
Brush with remaining mixture; let rise.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In pan, mix first 5 ingredients; stir until sugar and butter are melted.
Pour into ungreased 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Separate biscuits; flatten to 3-inches oblong. Spread with peanut butter.
Twist biscuit 3 or 4 times.
Bake 15 or 20 minutes or until brown.
Let cool 3 minutes, then remove from pan.
Mix beef, milk, basil, oatmeal, mustard, green pepper, onion, egg and catsup thoroughly.
Place mixture in large baking dish. Shape into donut shape.
Place mixed vegetables in center of ring. Add potatoes and any remaining mixed veggies to outside. Bake, covered, at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Remove cover and bake 30 minutes more to brown.
Sprinkle salt, pepper and paprika over chicken.
Brown chicken in 2 tablespoons butter.
Set aside in casserole.
Add 4 tablespoons butter to drippings.
Saute mushrooms.
Arrange chokes between chicken.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms.
Add chicken broth, sherry and rosemary.
Cook and stir a few minutes.
Add to casserole.
Cover and bake at 375° for 40 minutes or more.
Serve over rice.
Brown roast beef and onion in oil in frying pan.
Mix remaining ingredients together in a crock-pot.
After roast beef is browned, put in crock-pot with sauce.
Add onion to sauce.
Cook on high for 5 to 7 hours.
Mix beef with liquid and pat into patty.
Broil until desired doneness.
Spread catsup on side (half) of bun.
Mayonnaise on other.
Place hamburger, lettuce, tomato and onion between buns.
Line bottom of greased glass dish (8 x 10 x 2-inch) with green chiles.
Pile Longhorn cheese on top.
Beat eggs with 3 tablespoons water and pour over top.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Cool 10 minutes.
Cut into squares and serve on square crackers, such as Triscuits.
In a large pot, cover beef and bones with water.
Let stand 1 hour.
Add onion and celery.
Simmer, covered, for 2 hours. Remove beef and bones.
Discard bones.
Set aside beef.
Strain broth into bowl and chill to congeal fat.
Lift off fat and discard.
Return broth to pot.
Cut beef into bite size pieces and add to pot.
Add barley and simmer for 1 hour.
Add remainder of ingredients except salt and pepper.
Simmer for 20 minutes or until veggies are tender.
Add salt and pepper.
Serve.
Combine butter, brown sugar and Tabasco in a pot and heat until melted.
Place wings in large baking pan and cook in oven at 350° to 375° until fat is rendered.
Remove from oven and drain off all fat, about 1 hour.
Pour sauce over wings; return to oven and bake until crisp.
Sprinkle Ranch mix over all and bake another 10 minutes.
Mix together tomato soup, sugar, mustard and garlic salt.
Add vinegar and oil.
Mix well.
Let stand 24 hours before using. (Always refrigerate.)
Shake well before using.
Soften gelatin in water; add hot milk and mix well.
Beat eggs until thick and add sugar.
Mix well.
Stir milk into egg mixture; add sherry and salt.
Chill until thick.
Fold in whipping cream and almonds.
Pour into cups and top with vanilla wafers, crushed. Chill or freeze.
Cook noodles.
Drain.
Cut in half crosswise.
Melt butter in pan.
Stir in flour and cook over low heat for 2 minutes.
Stir in milk and cook.
Stir constantly over medium heat until thickened. Add garlic, thyme and pepper.
Place 2 to 3 tablespoons sauce in bottom of square 2-quart casserole dish.
Place layer of noodles over sauce, then layer 1/2 of the ham, 1/2 can asparagus, 1/2 cup of the sauce and 1/3 cup of mixed cheeses.
Repeat layers.
Top with remaining noodles and last of sauce and cheese.
Cook on High power for 9 to 10 minutes, turning it twice.
Thaw frozen spinach 2 hours at room temperature.
Saute green onions in 1/4 cup butter until tender.
Add spinach and simmer until almost all the liquid evaporates.
Crumble Feta cheese into large bowl.
Add cottage cheese, eggs, parsley and dill weed.
Mix well.
Add spinach mixture and mix until thoroughly blended.
Layer 1/2 of phyllo pastry in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish, brushing each sheet of pastry with melted butter.
Spread cheese mixture evenly over top of phyllo.
Repeat layering with remaining phyllo, brushing each sheet with butter.
Bake in a preheated 425° oven for 25 minutes.
Allow to stand 10 minutes before serving.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Wash cabbage and cut up; set aside.
Fry sausage in heavy pot or large skillet.
Add cabbage and 1 glass water.
Stir and cook until cabbage is almost done; add potatoes.
Cook until potatoes tender (salt and pepper to taste when you add the cabbage to sausage).
Stir often, scraping drippings from bottom of pot. This makes cabbage and potatoes brown.
Add a little water at a time as needed to loosen crust from bottom of pot.

Parboil potatoes. Cool and grate into large casserole. Add oleo (save 2 to 3 tablespoons for top), soup and onions to sour cream. Mix all together. Sprinkle cheese on top. Add reserved oleo to cereal. Sprinkle on top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
In a heavy saucepan, combine margarine, sugar and milk.
Bring to a boil.
Stir constantly.
Continue for 5 minutes over medium heat and stir in chocolate until melted.
Add remaining ingredients.
Place into greased shallow pan.
Put in fridge until firm (about 20 minutes) and cut into squares.
Mix sugar, cocoa, salt and 1/4 cup milk in saucepan.
Heat to boiling and boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Mix in 1/4 stick butter and set aside to cool.
Cook bacon in deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Remove bacon from drippings.
Cut
steak
in
pieces.
Brown
in
bacon drippings.
(Do
not
dredge in flour.) Add salt and pepper to taste and
paprika.
Add
water.
Cover and cook about 2 hours in a 350°
oven.
Add water if needed.
Add the peeled vegetables about 1 hour after placing in the oven.
Melt butter in a skillet.
Add flour and milk, stirring until smooth and thickened.
Stir in wine, salt, chicken, capers and almonds.
Spread on toast; top with cheese and broil until cheese melts.
Makes 16 canapes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spread pie filling in 9-inch square pan.
Beat cake mix, egg, extract and 1/3 cup water for 4 minutes. Pour over filling.
Sprinkle with coconut and pecans.
Drizzle with butter.
Bake for 40 minutes.
Serve warm.
Top with whipped cream.
Place baking chocolate in a 4-cup glass measuring cup. Microwave at 100% power for 1 minute.
Add water, butter, corn syrup and sugar.
Cover and microwave at 100% for 2 minutes. Uncover and whisk ingredients together.
Cover and microwave another 2 minutes at 100% power.
Add semi-sweet chocolate pieces and whisk well.
Add cream and whisk again.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Place butter in a 9 x 5-inch pan and place in oven to melt.
Mix together dry ingredients in large bowl.
Add milk, honey and egg and beat well.
Pour into hot pan of butter.
Bake 25 to 35 minutes.
Cook onions in bacon grease until tender.
Combine egg and milk; add to buttermilk baking mix.
Stir until just moistened. Add onion and 1/2 of cheese.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder.
Cut in margarine and add sugar.
Mix to a light dough with beaten egg and milk.
Turn onto a floured board.
Roll out 1/4-inch thick.
Cut into small rounds. Put 1/2 tablespoon of jam on half the circles, brush other half with milk and pinch together.
Fry in oil for 6 to 8 minutes (deep-fry).
Toss in sugar and cinnamon mixture.
In a small mixing bowl, mix crackers, sugar and 1/2 cup butter.
Press lightly into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Rinse and drain onions.
Mix water, vinegar, brown sugar, tomato paste and cumin in large skillet.
Stir in onions and raisins.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and boil gently, uncovered, stirring 3 or 4 times, for 15 to 20 minutes or until liquid is syrupy.
Pack in jars.
Cool, cover and refrigerate.
Serve with roast meats, deli meats or poultry.
Brown beef in skillet.
Drain off excess fat.
Add onion and green pepper and cook until onion is transparent.
Add raisins, olives, garlic and bay leaf.
Cook 15 minutes over low heat. Serve over rice.
Serves 4 people.
Meat and rice may be mixed together before serving.
Wash beans thoroughly. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Boil for 2 minutes. Cover. Remove from heat.
Let stand 1 hour. Add ham, salt and pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer 2 1/2 hours.
Remove ham bone and cut off meat.
Add onion, meat and tomatoes.
Mix
well.
Cover and simmer 1 hour longer. Stir in milk.
Heat a few minutes more and serve.

Mix Raisin Bran, flour, baking soda, sugar, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl with airtight cover. Blend eggs, oil and buttermilk and mix well. Add this to large bowl and mix well. Fold in fruit cocktail. Do not use batter until it has been refrigerated for 24 hours.
Mix with a spoon or electric whipper the cream cheese, Cool Whip, powdered sugar and water.
Mix until creamy.
Pour the filling into the graham crust.
Put either cherry or blueberry filling spread on top.
Refrigerate.
In punch bowl, combine concentrates, juices and water. Stir well. Stir in strawberries, ginger ale and club soda. Serve immediately. Yields 25 (1 cup) servings.
Soften cream cheese, then add mayonnaise.
Mix until well blended.
Add parsley, chopped egg, onion, pepper and shrimp; chill.
Serve with crackers.
Arrange fruit in crust.
In food processor or blender, process cottage cheese and yogurt on high speed until smooth.
Mix gelatin and cold water.
Add to mixture, blending well.
Pour over fruit in crust.
Cover and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Garnish with dollops of yogurt and fruit just before serving.
Mix dip and let sit 4 to 5 hours.
"Light" versions of mayonnaise and sour cream may be used.
To cut down on saltiness, boil dried beef for a minute and drain well before adding it to mixture.
Cut off top(s) of rye bread, scoop out center and cut into cubes for dipping later (fresh vegetables may be used also). Fill the center of bread with dip.
You can eat the whole thing.
Mix cracker crumbs and butter.
Press into bottom of a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 8 minutes.
Beat egg whites and vanilla slightly in large bowl.
Gradually beat in sugar and berries.
Beat at high speed 12 to 15 minutes.
Mixture is fluffy and has large volume.
Fold in whipped cream; spread over crumb crust.
Freeze overnight.
In a large bowl, mix well honey, lemon juice, mustard and salt.
Beat in oil until well mixed.
Add cabbage and nuts; toss to mix well.
Just before serving, stir in oranges and grapefruit. Serve immediately.
Makes 6 servings.
Boil squash until tender; drain and mash.
Layer squash and onion.
Mix eggs and butter.
Pour over squash.
Top with cream of mushroom soup.
Sprinkle cheese over soup.

recipes.t: Hotel Juana'S Roasted Monkfish With Thyme Flowers, Spinach And Red(Ingredients For 4 Persons)
d: Remove the filets from the monkfish and brush with olive oil and fresh thyme flowers.
Peel the 3 half pepper and cut in large julienne.
Cook in boiling salted water; refresh in ice water and drain.
Reheat just before serving in a saucepan with olive oil. Make the red pepper coulis.
Season the monkfish filets with salt and pepper.
In a Teflon frying pan, add olive oil, 2 cloves garlic and lightly brown the filets, finishing the cooking in the oven. When done, set aside covered with aluminum foil.
Wash fresh blueberries.
Mix sugar and water and therm-flo until dissolved and then bring to boil.
Stir until thick and clear.
Add to berries and mix until berries are coated.
Put into pint or quart jars and can in hot, boiling water, 10 to 12 minutes.
Slash fat every 2 inches on edges of steak.
Place on broiler pan or grill about 2 inches from heat.
Cook 5 minutes each side for rare, 6 minutes each for medium or 7 minutes each for well done.
Season with salt and pepper after cooking.
Drop lobster into pot of boiling water.
Bring water back to boiling.
Reduce heat to simmer.
Cook tails completely.

recipes.t: Potluck Favorite Grits And Cheese(1977 Cookbook)
d: Stir
boiling
water,
grits and salt together and cook until smooth and thick.
Stir cut up cheese and margarine into cooked grits
until
melted.
Add beaten eggs; mix well.
Pour into buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix 4 cups wheat flour with salt.
Mix yeast with 1/2 cup warm water until dissolved.
Add all wet ingredients into flour and mix.
Add remaining ingredients; but add flour slowly; until dough is workable for kneading.
Knead for 8 - 10 minutes.
Combine meat, mixed vegetables (thawed), salt, pepper and parsley in a deep mixing bowl; mix well.
Add salt, pepper, corn flakes and 1/2 of tomato soup (undiluted).
Mix well to blend. Place 1/2 of the meat mixture in a buttered 6 x 16 x 2 1/2-inch baking dish; pack.
Dot top with 1/2 of the butter.
Place rest of meat mixture in baking dish.
Dot with rest of butter and pour rest of soup over the top.
In a preheated 375° oven, bake 1 hour. Remove.
Let stand 15 minutes before slicing.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in apricot nectar, lemon peel and juice.
Mix well.
Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes or until thickened, stirring constantly.
Pour into a bowl and place in refrigerator or freezer for 15 to 30 minutes to chill quickly.
Mix together sugar,
Karo
and hot water.
Boil to soft ball stage.
Pour into mixing bowl.
Add cream of tartar, food coloring and
flavoring.
Beat
until creamy.
Drop onto waxed paper; swirl tops.
Set
in
hot
water
if mixture gets stiff until able to work again.
Wrap a slice of bacon around each piece of chicken; secure with toothpicks.
Place on greased 10 x 7-inch baking dish. Combine remaining ingredients and pour over chicken.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 2 hours.
Put chicken meat, broccoli and peas in a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Combine sauce ingredients and pour over chicken and vegetables.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
Good served over rice.
In shallow dish, mix together first 5 ingredients.
Dip chicken pieces in evaporated milk and coat with crumb mixture. Place in single layer in shallow roasting pan.
Bake in 400° oven for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve hot or cold.
Makes 8 servings.
Per Serving:
235 calories, 39 g protein, 6 g carbohydrate, 5 g fat, 121 mg cholesterol and 317 mg sodium.
Cut up onions and celery.
Add about 1 tablespoon of water and cook in microwave until done.
In greased casserole, put all ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease cookie sheets.
In large bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, margarine, 1 cup coconut, almond extract and egg at low speed until well mixed and dough forms.
In small bowl, beat egg white and water until foamy. Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Dip in egg white mixture; roll in coconut.
Place 2 inches apart on greased cookie sheets.
Place cherry in center of each cookie, pressing down lightly.
Bake at 375° for 11 to 14 minutes, or until edges are light golden brown. Yields 3 dozen cookies.
Cook macaroni; set aside.
Brown sausage, onion and green pepper until sausage is done; drain well.
Combine sausage mixture with remaining ingredients, except cheese.
Spoon mixture into a greased 2 quart casserole; sprinkle with cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Prepare loaf pan by lightly greasing and coating with plain bread crumbs.
Mix chopped dates with water and baking soda; let cool.
Beat eggs; add sugar.
Add date mixture; stir thoroughly. Gradually add flour, baking powder, salt and pecans.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Mix softened margarine and cheese until
well blended.
Add mayonnaise and blend well.
Add well drained crab, lemon juice and garlic powder; mix well.
Spread on 12 English muffin halves.
Cut each half into fourths.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Cook
the
first
3 ingredients in lightly salted water until tender.
Drain.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Slowly add milk; stir until thickened.
Add
cheese;
blend
until
melted. Preheat oven
Layer the drained cabbage mixture and cheese
sauce in
a greased casserole. Make several layers, ending with
sauce.
Bake until
bubbly.
Top with crumbs (we use cornbread crumbs that are sprinkled with poultry seasoning or you
could
use
cornbread stuffing
mix).
Return to oven until lightly browned.
Makes 4 servings.
Place water, salt, nutmeg and butter in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring mixture to a full rolling boil over high heat.
Add flour, all at once.
Remove pan from heat.
Stir until mixture forms a ball and leaves sides of pan.
Beat in eggs, one at a time until mixture is smooth and shiny.
Add cheese and stir until blended. Drop mixture by teaspoons into almonds in a shallow pan.
Roll to coat evenly and shape each into a 3/4-inch ball.
Place on waxed paper and let stand 10 to 15 minutes.
Measure into bowl the flour and butter
Cut butter into flour with fingertips.
Then add egg yolk, and sour cream.
Mix well and shape into ball.
Sprinkle with flour and knead until smooth. Chill dough for 20 minutes.
Prepare filling.
Rub
chicken
with ginger.
Dip pieces in soy sauce; coat with basic barbecue sauce.
Let stand 1 hour or more.
Bake for 30 minutes at 400°.
Baste with more sauce; turn and baste again.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes more or until fork-tender, basting often with sauce and pan juices.
Mix ground beef, salt, pepper, onions and green pepper.
Mix, then add corn meal.
Mix.
Bake 1 hour and 45 minutes at 350°.
Combine sugar, cornstarch, butter and water.
Stir and cook to the boiling point.
Cool slightly; add vanilla.
The sauce may be thinned with cream.
Cut a slice off the tops of the peppers.
Remove the white pith and the seeds.
Parboil the peppers for 3 minutes in boiling water; remove and drain.
Heat the oil in a frying pan.
Add the onion, garlic and grated courgettes (zucchini) and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, then stir in the parsley, breadcrumbs, cheese, egg and salt and pepper to taste.
Combine the ingredients thoroughly.
Fry meat.
When almost done, put in the onions and scallions until the meat is done.
Add the red pepper, potatoes, Everglade seasoning, salt, pepper and rutabaga.
Bring to a boil, then add the butter.
Cook until done and spice to suit yourself.
In
a saucepan, combine 1 1/4 cups of the orange juice, cranberry
sauce
and gelatin.
Cook and stir over medium heat until
gelatin
dissolves. Stir
in
remaining
orange juice. Transfer
to
medium
mixing
bowl.
Apply a seal; chill until partially
set
(consistency
of an unbeaten egg white).
In a small
mixing
bowl,
beat whipping cream to soft peaks; fold into
gelatin mixture.
Apply seal;
refrigerate until mixture mounds.
Pour
into the gel-ring mold.
Apply seal; chill 4 to 6 hours or until set.
To unmold salad, immerse mold into warm water for 20 to 30 seconds; do not melt gelatin. Remove large seal; center
an inverted serving plate over mold.
Carefully lift
off inner
salad
with orange wedges and garnish with orange leaves,
if desired.
Garnish outer edge of salad with additional whipped cream and cranberries, if desired. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
In a small bowl, gently blend sour cream, vinegar and seasonings.
Cover and chill.
When ready to serve, toss cabbage and green pepper lightly with dressing.
Combine crumbs, 3 tablespoons sugar and oleo for 9-inch crust. Bake
at
for 10 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, 3/4 cup sugar, lemon juice and rind.
Mix well.
Add eggs, one at a
time. Pour
mixture
in crust and bake at 300° for 55 minutes.
Combine sour
cream,
2 tablespoons sugar and vanilla; spread over cheese cake.
Bake 10 minutes more.
Heat grill.
In small bowl, combine all sauce ingredients. Blend well and set aside.
When ready to barbecue, place pork chops on gas grill over medium heat or on charcoal grill 4 to 6 inches from medium-high coals.
Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, or until pork is tender and no longer pink, turning once and brushing chops generously with sauce during last 5 minutes of grilling.
Melt butter in a Pyrex baking dish in a preheated 400° oven. Meanwhile, shake chicken pieces in flour, salt, pepper and paprika mixture in a plastic bag.
Place chicken, skin side down, in melted butter.
Bake 30 minutes, then turn chicken and bake 15 more minutes.
Heat chicken soup (do not dilute) and mushrooms (add liquid, too) together on top of stove.
After chicken browns the additional 15 minutes, pour soup mixture over chicken.
Reduce oven heat to 350° and continue cooking 15 to 30 minutes more.
Saute onions, celery and carrots for 3 to 8 minutes in oil. Cover.
Add rolled oats after 5 minutes, adding water (small amount).
Add cauliflower, then squash, Herbamore, bay leaf and water to cover.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Add water to 1 cup level.
When done, remove bay leaves and process in a food processor.
Makes a thick, tasty soup perfect for cold weather cooking.
Mix Jell-O with boiling water; chill until half set.
Whip whipping cream and cream cheese.
Add with cherries and pineapple to lemon Jell-O.
Top with nuts.
Check leaves carefully. Remove stems if large. Wash 5 or 6 times in changes of warm water.
Put into heavy saucepan with tight lid (rather have pressure cooker, 10 pounds pressure, for 20 minutes).
Add washed greens, few at a time.
Cover with ham, drippings, salt and sugar.
Cook until tender. Serve with hot pepper sauce.
Brown beef.
Add taco seasoning and refried beans. Layer into a greased casserole. Next, layer sour cream and top with cheese. Bake at 350° until cheese has melted. Serve with tortilla chips.
In a large skillet, saute onion and garlic in olive oil (5 to 10 minutes or until wilted, but not brown).
Add chopped carrots and more oil; saute for another 5 minutes.
Add can of tomatoes and chop them with a spoon.
If not enough liquid, add can of tomato sauce.
Add salt, pepper and hot red pepper to taste.
Add some fresh basil.
Simmer for 1 hour or until sauce cooks down. Serve sauce over rigatoni.
Coat vegetables in corn meal, salt and pepper to taste. Cook in oil for about 30 minutes.
Chop the onion, pepper and garlic.
Fry in olive oil about 5 minutes. Add meat. Stir and cook good for 10 minutes. Add sauce, raisins, olives and tomatoes.
Cook on low heat 40 minutes, covered.
Serve over rice!
Heat butter in electric skillet until melted.
Stir in instant bouillon.
Add Brussels sprouts, carrots and cauliflower.
Cover and cook over medium heat 4 or 5 minutes.
Stir-fry vegetables 4 minutes.
Add peas.
Stir-fry until peas are crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in almonds, salt and lemon pepper.
In a large pan, brown chicken with garlic in butter.
Add broth, soup, water, oregano, salt and pepper.
Cover; simmer 20 minutes.
Add rice and peas; cook 25 minutes or until tender, stirring now and then.
Scrub and soak ham about 24 hours.
Put in roasting pan and add water to cover and begin to cook the ham.
Skim after the first hour.
Then add peas and pork chops; cover and cook 2 1/2 to 3 hours more.
Cool to room temperature and lift out ham.
Skim, score and add cloves.
Glaze ham with sugar, mustard and vinegar (mixed); put in a separate pan and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Strain broth from peas; remove meat from chops and cook onion in broth. Place meat, peas and onions in casserole dish; cover with broth thickened with a little flour and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Dice vegetables into small pieces.
Place in large bowl and cover with 1 cup sugar.
Let stand for 15 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup vinegar and toss lightly.
Salt, pepper and celery seed should be added last.
Heat oven to 350°.
Butter a 1 1/2-quart shallow baking dish. Cook spinach and set aside to drain.
Melt 1/4 cup butter.
Saute onion until tender.
Combine spinach, onion, cream, 1/3 cup bread crumbs, pecans, salt, nutmeg and pepper in large bowl and mix. Put in baking dish.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter and stir in spinach.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Dissolve gelatin in 2 cups hot water.
Dissolve cream cheese in a little hot water.
Mix jello and cream cheese together.
Add pineapple (juice included) and nuts.
Mix well.
Chill until firm.
Simmer frankfurters in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and cool.
Combine potatoes, salt, pepper, oil and vinegar.
Arrange drained string beans in bottom of greased or oiled 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Over the beans arrange potatoes in alternate layers with onions and sliced frankfurters.
Cover and bake in 400° oven 35 to 40 minutes.
Serves 4.
Good when garden is just coming in and you don't have enough of anything for a dish.
Mix all vegetables together in large bowl.
Salt and pepper.
Mix flour and meal and shake over veggies, turning to coat all veggies.
Dump into large skillet and cover.
Fry until tender and it is brown as you want it.
Yummy good.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Put bacon drippings in a baking dish or skillet and let melt while oven is heating.
Beat eggs until frothy.
Add corn meal, salt and baking soda; stir until combined. Add buttermilk and stir well.
Remove hot pan from oven, swirl drippings to coat pan (or skillet).
Pour drippings into batter. Stir well, pour batter into pan and bake 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Cabbage And Meat Balls
d: Shred cabbage; saute in pan in olive oil with sliced or diced onion.
Add ketchup according to amount being made.
Add ginger ale (1 small bottle or can).
Make meat balls as you normally would. Place on top of cabbage mixture and cook until meat balls are done. Serve with rice.
Place brisket in 9 x 13-inch pan (fat side down).
Pour Pepsi so that it comes 2/3 up on beef.
Sprinkle beef with dry soup and garlic powder.
Cover pan during baking.
Bake at 250° for 5 hours.
After baking, cool completely.
Cut against the grain. Reheat meat when ready to serve, either on rolls or alone.
Combine raisins, water and soda.
Let stand overnight.
Add remaining ingredients.
Put in 3 greased and floured 1-pound coffee cans.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
Turn upside-down and shake out.
Saute onion in butter.
Add soup, plus 1/2 can of water from each can.
Let simmer for about 15 minutes.
Add crawfish tails and pepper to taste.
Serve over rice.
Finely chop the onions and dried beef.
Mix cream cheese, and add 1-2 Tbsp. worchester sauce to taste.
Sprinkle in some dried beef.
In a soup bowl, firmly pack the bottom and 1/2 side of the bowl with the dried beef.
Add the mixture.
Refrigerate.
When ready to serve, get a plate to serve the cheeseball on.
Turn the bowl upside down and gently have the cheeseball come on to the plate.
Serve with crackers of your choice.
Cook potatoes, green pepper and onion in oleo until lightly browned.
Season to taste.
Break eggs over potato mixture.
Cover and cook on low heat until eggs are done.
Sprinkle cheese over eggs, cover and cook until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.

recipes.t: Mix In The Pan Carrot Cake
d: In an 8-inch pan with fork mix well flour, sugar, cinnamon, salt, baking soda, baking powder and nutmeg.
Add remaining ingredients to mixture and mix briskly with fork until blended. Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes or until pick comes out clean and cake pulls away from sides of pan.
Cool, frost or sprinkle with 10x sugar.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Mix salt and flour.
Pound 1/4 cup of this mix into the cube steaks.
Melt 4 tablespoons of butter.
Add cube steaks and brown well.
Place steaks in a large baking dish. Melt 2 tablespoons butter.
Add onions and cook until tender. Melt 2 tablespoons butter; saute mushrooms.
Spoon onions and mushrooms over browned steak.
Add remaining flour to butter and drippings remaining in the skillet.
Stir in bouillon and mustard and cook, stirring constantly until thick (make sure to get out all the lumps).
Add cream and mix well.
Pour sauce over the vegetables and meat.
Cover and bake 1 1/2 hours (test after 1 hour to see if it is done).
Mix cinnamon with 6 tablespoons sugar.
Sprinkle over apples and nuts; set aside.
Beat butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla together.
Add dry ingredients and juice alternately.
Grease and flour 10-inch tube pan.
Pour 1/2 batter in pan.
Sprinkle on 1/2 of apple/nut mixture.
Add remaining batter and sprinkle on remaining apple/nut mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Cool completely.
Frost with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Slice squash and onions into thin slices.
Place in microwave-safe dish in layers beginning with squash, onion cheese and garlic powder.
Butter a 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking pan.
Place first 4 ingredients in a large bowl and mix well.
Add butter and work in until the oat mixture is crumbly using fingers.
Set 2 cups of it aside.
Press remaining mixture onto bottom of buttered pan. Spread preserves over top and crumble the rest of the oat mixture on top.
Pat gently but firmly.
Bake squares at 400° for 20 minutes.
Cool completely and then cut into small squares.
Boil potatoes in water until tender.
Add ham and onions. Cook 10 minutes more.
Add soups, corn and milk.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Stir, heat thoroughly, but do not boil.
Serve with corn muffins.
Mix cheese, flour and pepper.
Coat chicken and brown in butter.
Set chicken aside.
In same pan, saute mushrooms.
Add butter if needed.
Blend in remaining flour mixture.
Mix broth and wine; mix in pan with mushrooms until thickened, adding broth if too thick.
Cook slowly until sauce is desired consistency. Put chicken in 9 x 12-inch glass baking dish.
