Spread artichoke hearts on top, then pour mushrooms with gravy on top.
Add some juice from artichoke jars.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour at 375°.
If using stuffing mix, prepare as directed.
Press stuffing into greased 9-inch pie plate or quiche pan, forming crust.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven.
In small bowl, combine turkey and Swiss cheese, set aside.
In separate bowl, beat eggs, milk and pepper.
Sprinkle turkey and cheese mixture over hot crust.
Pour egg mixture over turkey.
Lower oven temperature to 350° and bake 30 to 35 minutes or until knife comes out clean.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Add seafood to chopped vegetables.
Stir in mayonnaise, salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix as for salad.
Put in 3-quart casserole and top with chips.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Saute onion and garlic in salad oil in large frying pan until soft (not browned).
Remove with slotted spoon to set aside. Shape ground beef into large patty and brown (in same pan) on both sides, then break into chunks.
Stir in onion mixture, tomatoes, beans, chili, salt and pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Place 3 tortillas (cut in quarters) in 3-quart baking dish.
Top with about one cup of sauce and repeat until all is used, ending with sauce.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Stick several wedges of tortillas on top.
Bake in hot oven at 400° for 30 minutes.
Put each chicken breast, bone side down, on wax paper.
Pound with mallet to flatten to 1/4-inch thickness.
Put a ham slice and cheese stick on each piece of chicken.
Fold edges over cheese to cover completely.
Roll up tightly and secure with wooden pick or string.
Coat chicken with flour seasoned with salt (and pepper to taste).
Brown in 2 tablespoons of butter in 10-inch skillet. Sprinkle chicken with remaining flour.
Add wine and chicken bouillon cube to skillet.
Heat, stirring, until bouillon is dissolved.
Cover skillet and simmer until chicken is tender (20 minutes).
Remove chicken from skillet; sprinkle with paprika and keep warm.
Add half and half to pan drippings.
Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Blend in peas.
Spoon sauce over chicken. Serve with rice.

Mix cool whip and cream cheese together. Mix pudding mix as directed. Then mix pudding with cool whip and cream cheese mixture. Add can of condensed milk to mixture. Slice bananas up in a bowl then squeeze lemon juice over bananas to keep them from turning black. Place a layer of cookies in a flat dish. Then place bananas. Then put your filling mix on top of the bananas. Then put more cookies on top of filling. Then refrigerate.
Boil onion and squash in 1/2 cup water until tender.
Season with mayonnaise, salt, pepper and margarine.
Add eggs, cracker crumbs and cheese.
Brown beef with onion in 10-inch skillet; drain off fat.
Stir in water, rice, crushed bouillon cubes and dry mustard.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer until liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Stir in green pepper and tomato.
Sprinkle cheese over top.
Cover and remove from heat.
Let stand 2 to 3 minutes to melt cheese.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix flour, salt, 5 Tbsp. sugar, & shortening together.
Add fruit, dates, nuts, and orange peel.
Divide the fruit ingredients into 3 equal portions in separate bowls.
Divide yeast equally into 3 cups.
Add 1 Tbsp. sugar into each yeast cup. Add 2 Tbsp. lukewarm water to each yeast cup to soften the yeast.
Add a few drops of 1 food coloring to each of the yeast cups.
In each yeast cup, add 1 Tbsp. flour to make a batter.
Divide lukewarm milk into 3 equal parts.
To each 1/3 fruit mixture, add 1 cup of yeast mixture and 1 portion of lukewarm milk.
Knead until well mixed and a soft dough is formed.
Grease bowls and dough.
Let rise in warm place until doubled in size.
Punch down & let rise again. divide each bowl of dough into 3 equal portions.
Roll each portion into ropes;
about 9 inches long.
Then braid (1 piece of each color) forming a loaf.
Place in greased loaf pans, allowing bread to double in size.
Bake in 350°F. oven for about 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix celery, mushroom soup and chicken soup with the spices. Add carrots, onions and potatoes.
Put chicken whole in a baking bag.
Pour the ingredients over the chicken and seal loosely.
Bake at 300° for 2 hours.
Melt margarine in skillet.
Brown beef and onion until done. Add beans, salt and chili sauce and blend and heat.
Spoon onto toasted buns.
Spread chopped broccoli/cheese mixture over fish fillets. Roll up and place seam side down in greased 11 x 7 inch baking dish. Squeeze lemon juice over all.
Drizzle top with a little oil and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake uncovered at 350° for approximately 30 - 35 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, combine biscuit mix, sugar and dry gelatin.
Combine in a small mixing bowl the eggs, milk and oil; stir into dry ingredients until moistened.
Beat vigorously by hand 1 minute until smooth.
Pour batter into greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for about 25 to 30 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool 5 minutes.
Mix chicken, onion, celery and green peppers with salad dressing like chicken salad.
Spread half on bottom of a 2 1/2-quart casserole.
Toast bread, cut and layer alternately with salad.
Beat eggs and combine with milk.
Pour over chicken.
Let sit at least 1 hour or overnight.
Before you put it in the oven, pour 1 can of cream of mushroom soup over.
Bake 1 hour at 325°. Last 10 minutes of baking, sprinkle grated cheese on top.

recipes.t: Midnight Mommy Russian Chocolate Beet Cake
d: Parboil (do not cook) beets.
Peel and grate fine.
Cream sugar and eggs.
Add oil and grated beets.
Melt chocolate in double boiler and add.
Sift flour and baking soda.
Add slowly to mixture.
Add vanilla.
In a medium bowl, mix gelatin with sugar substitute.
Add hot pineapple juice and stir until gelatin is completely dissolved. Stir in vanilla ice milk, flaked coconut and rum extract and blend thoroughly.
Place ribs in a greased roasting pan.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a saucepan, combine the remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil; cook for 1 minute.
Drain ribs. Spoon sauce over ribs.
Cover and bake for 1-1/2 hours.
Uncover; bake 30 minutes longer, basting once.
Yield:
4 to 6 servings.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, place 1 cup whipping cream. Stir in gelatin.
Allow to soften at least 5 minutes. Stir in vanilla milk chips.
Microwave on High for 1 to 1 1/4 minutes or until chips are melted and mixture is smooth when stirred.
(Stir with wire whisk if needed to melt chips completely.)
Chill 15 minutes or just until mixture is lukewarm.
In small mixer bowl, beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually beat in sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold into vanilla mixture.
Pour into crust. Cover and chill until firm.
Just before serving, cover top of pie with chilled cherry pie filling.
Makes 8 servings.
In medium bowl, combine gelatin and water; stir until completely dissolved.
Cool.
Add rest of ingredients, except sour cream.
Divide in half.
Pour half the mixture into a 13 x 9-inch dish.
Refrigerate until set.
Keep remaining gelatin at room temperature.
When first half is set, spread sour cream over it. Pour on remaining gelatine.
Cover and refrigerate until cold.

recipes.t: Penne With Vodka And Tomato Sauce
d: Heat oil in medium skillet.
Add onion; saute until tender, but not browned (about 5 minutes).
Stir in garlic; saute 1 minute.
At this point, add Prosciutto or panchetta and saute 1 to 2 minutes.
Add vodka and red pepper; simmer 2 minutes.
Add red pepper and add tomatoes, stirring to break up tomatoes with side of spoon.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until sauce is reduced and thickened.
Slowly stir in room temperature heavy cream.
Reduce heat and cook about 3 to 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Cook Brussels sprouts according to directions on package.
Be sure they are tender.
Drain.
Place Brussels sprouts in greased baking dish and stir in cream of celery soup, salt and pepper. Cover with dry bread crumbs and dot with butter.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Serves 5 to 6.
Chop onion, celery and garlic.
Melt butter in frying pan.
Add onion, celery and garlic.
Cook until onion is clear in color and celery is tender.
Be careful not to burn garlic.
Pour over stuffing mix.
Add water and baby food.
Mix until moist.
Add more water, if necessary.
Stuff bird and cook as directed.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Mix together sugar, brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Add the oil and stir until crumbly. Reserve and set aside 3/4 cup of the mixture for topping. Add vinegar to the milk and stir into the sugar mixture. Add the egg and soda and mix well. Pour into 13x9 pan. Sprinkle with the reserved topping. Bake 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Spoon apple pie filling evenly into ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Grate rind from lemon; sprinkle over filling.
Cut lemon in half.
Juice lemon halves. Drizzle juice over filling.
Sprinkle with half the cinnamon; pour dry cake mix evenly over apples so it reaches all sides of pan. Sprinkle remaining 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon over cake mix.
Sprinkle walnuts over top; drizzle melted butter over entire pan.
Bake in 350° oven until top is golden and bubbly and walnuts have browned about 55 minutes.
Remove to wire rack and let cool for 10 minutes. To serve, spoon crisp into bowls; top with scoop of vanilla ice cream, if desired.
Serves 12.
Trim all fat off bear meat.
Be sure to clean out kernel (musk gland) to avoid gamy taste.
Cut meat into 3-inch cubes. Season flour with Parmesan and black pepper.
Mix well.
Roll meat cubes into seasoned flour.
Cover well.
Wash chicken wings, breaking in two at the joints.
Remove tips and keep for soup.
Combine the crumbs and all the dry ingredients.
Dip wing pieces in melted butter and then into the crumb mixture.
Place wings in a single layer on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake uncovered for 18 minutes at 350°.
Serve hot.
Makes 32 appetizers.
Follow directions for layer cake. Cool. Can use 8 or 9-inch pans.
Slice each layer in half to make four layers.
Mix powdered sugar, sour cream, coconut, vanilla and Cool Whip for filling. Spread between layers, on top and on sides of cake.
Put in airtight container.
Place in refrigerator for 4 days.
Do not peek.
Mix all ingredients, pour into baking dish, sprinkle extra shredded Cheddar on top. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Brown beef in skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently. Drain fat.
Add next 6 ingredients; bring to boil.
Remove from heat.
Stir in mayonnaise.
Place mixture in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Flatten biscuits slightly and arrange overlapping around edge of casserole.
Brush biscuits with mayonnaise.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes
or until biscuits are browned.
(We like a little more mayonnaise, sometimes I precook vegetables.)

In a food processor, combine the packed basil, garlic, raw pine nuts and oil and puree until a uniform sauce results. Scrape the mixture into a bowl and stir in the grated cheese. Set aside. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the orzo until tender. Drain well, rinse, drain again and place in a large bowl. Toss with a couple of tablespoons of the reserved pesto dressing, or more to taste. Reserve any leftover pesto for another use. To serve, add the tomatoes and toasted pine nuts to the salad, toss with more pesto dressing and black pepper to taste, and scatter with fresh basil.
Peel and devein shrimp; set aside.
Combine water and soy sauce in a large Dutch oven.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Add rice; cover, reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Saute onion and green pepper in 2 tablespoons melted butter until crisp-tender.
Add shrimp and saute over medium heat 3 minutes or until shrimp is done.
Stir into rice.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet.
Add eggs.
Cook without stirring until eggs begin to set on bottom.
Draw a spatula across bottom of pan to form large curds.
Continue until eggs are thickened, but still moist.
Do not stir constantly.
Stir eggs and pepper into rice mixture; toss gently.
Garnish, if desired.
Cook chicken with lots of water.
Salt and pepper to taste. Cool, skin and debone chicken.
Chop celery and onion and add to stock; boil about 10 minutes.
Add noodles and cook another 10 minutes.
Add other ingredients including chicken.
Cook another 10 minutes.
If needed, add chicken broth.
Do not add water.
Prepare meat sauce.
Cut eggplant lengthwise into slices about 1/4-inch thick.
Coat each slice with flour and shake off excess. Heat about 1/4 inch oil in a wide frying an over medium-high heat. Dip eggplant slices in egg mixture.
Drain briefly and cook without crowding.
Adding oil as needed, until browned and tender when pierced.
Drain, when browned, on paper towels.
Mix jello (allow for juice in pineapple).
Refrigerate until it starts to jell, then whip.
Whip the cream; add 3 tablespoons sugar and add to whipped jello.
Add the remaining ingredients and pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan or dish and jell.
Brown ground beef.
Add tomatoes.
Mix cornmeal and water and add to tomato mix by spoonfuls, stirring constantly.
Simmer, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add chili powder, corn, olives, salt and pepper.
Heat through.
Add boiling water to jello.
Stir until dissolved.
Add cold water to juices.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Serves 35 to 40.
Heat oven to 375°.
Peel potatoes and slice thin.
Toss with flour.
Alternate layers of potatoes and mushrooms in well buttered baking dish, sprinkling each layer with seasonings.
Pour in broth mixed with wine.
Cover and bake 45 minutes.
Uncover. Sprinkle with cheese and continue baking another 30 minutes. Serves 6.
Cook turkey and garlic in margarine over low heat 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in vegetables.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes or until vegetables are heated, stirring occasionally.
Add cheese; stir until cheese is melted.
Serve over rice.
Melt butter in a 3-quart saucepan over low heat.
Add marshmallows, stirring until melted.
Add remaining ingredients, stirring until well coated.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cool. Cut into bars.
In large mixing bowl, beat eggs, oil and sugar together.
Sift flour, salt, soda and cinnamon together and add to egg mixture. In another bowl, stir vanilla, apples, nuts and coconut together, then add batter.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes or until done.
Let cool enough to handle pan and turn out on rack to cool completely.
Spread half of the bread slices lightly with mustard, then with the corned beef spread.
Add 2 thin slices of Swiss cheese and a dollop of sauerkraut.
Top with remaining bread slices and grill slowly in a buttered skillet.
Remove when cheese is soft and bread is golden.
Makes 18.
Stir boiling water into gelatin in large bowl for 2 minutes or until completely dissolved.
Stir in tomato and lemon juices. Stir in salsa.
Pour into a 5-cup mold.
Refrigerate 4 hours or until firm.
Unmold.
Serve with tortilla chips, if desired.
Cream butter and sugar until light; add eggs.
Beat well after each egg is added.
Add jam and beat well.
Add sifted flour, soda, salt, cloves and allspice, alternately with buttermilk, beating until smooth.
Stir in raisins and nuts.
Pour into 9-inch layer pans.
Bake at 325° for about 35 minutes.
Frost with caramel frosting.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In bowl of electric mixer, cream sugar and butter, until soft and fluffy.
Add eggs, all at once. Continue beating, until light.
Mix in remaining ingredients, except pie shell.
Combine well.
Pour into prepared pie crust. Reduce heat to 300°.
Bake about 1 hour, or until pie is firm.

Combine milk, garlic powder and Worcestershire sauce. Add dove breast and marinate 12 hours in refrigerator. Milk mixture should cover the breast. Drain and salt and pepper; roll in flour to coat. Fry until golden brown.

recipes.t: Pollo Con Cipolla (Onion) And Red Roasted Peppers
d: In a large frypan heat the oil, add onion, garlic and red pepper and gently fry for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces, salt and pepper and fry until browned on both sides.
Mix the tomato paste with a little water and stir into the pan; add wine and cook on low for about 10 minutes, covered.
Chop one sprig of rosemary and sprinkle over chicken.
Cook another few minutes until chicken is tender, adding a little of the stock to moisten. Transfer to serving dish and garnish with rosemary.
Serves 4.
Mix brownie mix, adding 1 extra egg.
Bake and cool completely. Mix together the cream cheese and sugar; whip and fold in pineapple.
Spread on top of brownie.
Refrigerate.
Top with fruit of choice:
bananas, strawberries, chopped nuts and/or shredded coconut.
Drizzle with Hershey's syrup.
Eat within 24 hours.
Mix dry ingredients together in large bowl.
Reserve 1 tablespoon to toss with berries.
Make a well in center of dry ingredients.
Combine milk, eggs and butter.
Add to dry ingredients.
Stir until moistened.
Toss berries with reserved flour mix.
Stir into batter.
Spoon into greased muffin pans 2/3 full.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake 15 minutes at 400°.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add chilies and dried mint and cook a minute or so to heat through.
Add cream and salt to taste and let it almost come to a boil.
Remove from heat, place in a blender or food processor, whirl smooth and put back in the pan.
Bring to a boil over high heat and cook down, stirring until reduced and slightly thickened.
Put peas in boiling salted water and cook only until the water comes to a boil again. Drain them and put in the cream sauce.
Cover and simmer 1 to 2 minutes. Serves 4.
Place pea pods and carrot in a strainer.
Set the strainer in a sink.
Pour boiling water over vegetables for about 1 minute, then pat dry.
Place vegetables in a medium-size bowl and stir in orange rind, oil and seed.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Makes 4 servings.
Heat oven to 350°.
Use loaf pan.
Slice Jack cheese and layer bottom of pan with 1/2 of Jack cheese.
Add 1/2 of spinach to cheese, add cottage cheese then rest of spinach.
Add remaining Jack cheese slices on top.
Brown ground meat with chopped onion, pepper and celery. Season with salt, pepper (a dash of garlic salt, too).
Add mushrooms, if desired.
Layer in casserole:
noodles, ground meat mixture, cream-style corn, tomatoes and sprinkle top with Parmesan cheese.
Just keep layering until all ingredients are used.
This makes 2 medium casseroles with 2 layers in each.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes until heated through.
Saute
vegetables, shrimp and scallops in olive oil and seasonings.
Set
aside.
Broil
flounder
until
flaky.
Lay vegetables
and seafood mixture on top of flounder and broil a few more minutes.

recipes.t: Microwave Tomato Shells Stuffed With Curried Chicken
d: Cut a slice from stem end of each tomato.
Scoop out pulp and invert tomatoes to drain.
Melt butter in a 1 1/2-quart glass casserole in microwave oven (30 seconds at High).
Blend in flour, onion and curry powder.
Stir in milk.
Cook uncovered for 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 minutes at High or until thickened and smooth.
Stir occasionally.
Stir in mixture of salt, pepper and garlic powder and then chicken.
Fill tomato shells with chicken mixture and place in a 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Heat uncovered in microwave oven for 4 to 6 minutes at High or until thoroughly heated.
Rotate dish one-quarter turn once.
Beat egg whites until foamy.
Add sugar.

Gradually beat until stiff. Fold in almonds, cherries, syrup, vanilla and almond flavoring. Fold confectioners sugar into whipped cream. Fold into beaten egg mixture. Pour into chilled graham cracker crust. Garnish with cherry pieces and slivered almonds.
Freeze until firm.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large saucepan, bring apples, raisins and apple juice concentrate to a boil over medium heat. Cook until apples are soft (about 3 to 5 minutes).
Let cool to room temperature.
In another saucepan, boil milk and add vanilla and spices.
Combine milk with cooked apples and fold in egg whites.
Add bread pieces to mixture and fold until mixed evenly.
Combine ground beef, onion, salt and 1/4 teaspoon oregano. Shape into 4 patties, rising the edge 1/4 inch to form a center well.
In baking dish, arrange patties.
Heat 5 1/2 minutes; drain.
Fill center well with spaghetti sauce.
Sprinkle with oregano; heat 1 to 2 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Let stand, covered, 4 minutes before serving.
Yields 4 servings.
Cream sugar and Crisco.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add flour and buttermilk alternately to other mixture.
Bake in tube or Bundt pan in 350°
oven for 1 hour.
Cook until top is good and brown.
Melt chocolate over hot water.
Combine with syrup and juice. Add rest in any order.
Let stand 30 minutes.
(I never had that much time.)
Form into 1-inch balls (or whatever size you wish). Roll in granulated sugar.
Sprinkle gelatin over 1/2 cup orange juice in a blender. Heat remaining cup of juice to boiling and add to blender.
Cover and blend at high speed until gelatin dissolves.
Add orange rind, 1/2 cup sugar, salt, egg yolks, cottage cheese and vanilla.
Cover and blend until smooth.
Pour into large bowl; chill until mixture mounds slightly when dropped from a spoon.

recipes.t: Pasta With Escarole And Sun-Dried Tomatoes
d: Wash escarole thoroughly in cold water several times; drain in colander.
In a large skillet, add oil and garlic.
While cooking pasta, heat oil and garlic in skillet, then saute cut up escarole, sun-dried tomatoes, salt, pepper and dash of hot pepper flakes. Do not overcook.
Before draining pasta, add some of that water to skillet.
Drain pasta; pour escarole mixture over pasta.
Mix first six ingredients together and pour in 9 x 13-inch pan (greased).
Sprinkle cake mix on top of pumpkin mixture.
Melt and drizzle melted butter over top of cake mix.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool.
Top with Dream Whip.
Serves approximately 15 large servings.
Put caramels, milk and oleo in a 1-quart glass measure cup. Heat on Medium to High in microwave for 4 to 5 minutes, until caramels melt.
Arrange pecans in groups of 3 on buttered baking sheet.
Spoon 1 tablespoon of warm caramel mixture over each group of pecans.
Refrigerate, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Put chocolate chips in 2-cup glass measure.
Heat on Medium for 5 to 6 minutes, until melted.
Spoon enough chocolate over carameled pecans to cover.
Allow to cool.
Remove from sheet.
Store in single layer in covered container in the refrigerator.
Cook onion and butter until tender, but not brown.
Stir in chicken, 1/2 cup of picante sauce and cumin.
Heat through. Remove from heat; stir in 1 cup of the cheese.

Combine cornstarch and the 1/4 cup water in a 3-quart saucepan. Add boiling water. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil. Boil 1 minute until thickened. Stir in sugar, lemon rind and butter; cool. Stir in eggs and lemon juice. Pour mixture into a 9-inch pastry lined plate.

Roll out remaining pastry, cut slits for steam to escape. Adjust over filling; flute to make stand up edge. Brush top with 1 tablespoon milk. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon sugar. Bake in a 375° oven for 30 minutes, then at 425° for 10 minutes or until golden.
Add a little of the salad dressing to cooked noodles, then remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Just before serving, toss with the remaining salad dressing.
In 2-quart saucepan, cook onions in margarine until tender. Add milk and cream cheese; stir over medium heat until cream cheese is melted.
Add remaining ingredients; heat thoroughly. Stir occasionally.
Slice zucchini thin.
Arrange slices on a greased baking sheet.
Spoon margarine on top of each slice.
Sprinkle with cheese, salt and pepper.
Place under broiler for about 5 minutes.
Boil white sugar, milk and oleo for 4 minutes.
Have ready the crackers and butterscotch bits.
Add nuts.
Beat well and pour into buttered pan.
Pop popcorn and put in a large kettle in a moderate oven, 300°.
Bring to boil white sugar, brown sugar, glucose and water; wash sides down and add salt.
Cook to 300° and add butter.
When butter is well mixed in, take off the fire and add soda.
Mix with vanilla.
Stir in well.
Take the corn out of oven.
Set on warm part of stove.
Scrape all the syrup into the corn and mix the whole thing together.
Pour on a cold dry slab or wax paper. Spread out while hot.
This can be rolled into balls.
When cool, break into a size you wish.
A great caramel corn.
Store in airtight container to prevent corn from getting sticky.
If using mostaccioli, cook and cool. Drain and slice artichoke hearts.
Lightly mix all ingredients except dressing.
Sprinkle with freshly ground pepper.
Mix half (or to taste) of the artichoke marinade with Italian dressing and pour over salad. Chill 2 to 4 hours if possible.
Serve on a bed of torn lettuce. Serves 4 to 6.
Place layers of cabbage and onion in large bowl; top with 1 cup sugar.
Set aside.

recipes.t: Trail Jam - Make Fresh Berry Jam While Camping!!!!!!
d: In pan, combine berries, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Over brisk fire, boil fruit, stirring until it reaches desired thickness.
Serve warm or cooled.
Makes 1 1/4 cups to put on pancakes or spread on campfire biscuits.
Combine the first 5 ingredients in bowl.
Cook the margarine, honey and brown sugar until melted.
Pour butter mixture over cereal mixture; mix until well blended.
Spread into a 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown, in a 325° oven, stirring occasionally.
Spread on wax paper to cool; stir in 1/2 cup raisins.
Mix together soup, sour cream and chilies.
Set aside.
Brown hamburger with onion.
Warm tortillas in a frying pan with butter to soften.
On each tortilla, add some of the soup mixture, some of the hamburger and some of each of the cheeses down the center. Roll to seal.
Cut tomatoes in 4 squares.
Crush up garlic cloves.
Add garlic salt to taste.
Add oregano and 1 cup of olive oil (depending on texture, 1 1/2 cup of olive oil).
Chill and serve with Italian bread.
Melt 2 Tbsp. butter in large pan.
Add hotdogs and fry till slightly browned.
Add onion and saut until soft.
Add catsup (I add about 1/2 cup water to make it more moist).
Add spices and simmer about 20 - 30 minutes.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Spoon flour into measuring cup; level off.
Combine flour and baking soda and set aside.
In a large bowl, cream the shortening, brown sugar, vanilla and eggs.
Add flour mixture.
Blend well with mixer.
Add by hand the remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.
Remove from cookie sheets and cool.
Mix together egg yolks, butter and sugar.
Add 1 tablespoon gelatin, softened in 1/4 cup cold water.
Heat on low to dissolve. Beat whipping cream and vanilla.
Add to egg mixture (fold in). Pour mixture into pie shell.
Top with strawberries and partially set jello.
Refrigerate to set.
Pour cherry pie filling into bowl.
Drain pineapple tidbits. Add to cherries.
Slice the banana into other fruit.
Add the walnuts and Cool Whip.
Mix well and chill.
Preparation time 5 minutes.
Combine soy sauce, lime juice, chili oil, garlic and ginger. Reserve 1/3 cup mixture for dipping sauce.
Set aside.
Cut tenderloin lengthwise into halves and crosswise in 4-inch slices. Cut slices in 1/2-inch strips.
Add to soy sauce; toss and coat. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes longer.
To prevent sticking, spray grid with nonstick cooking spray.
Prepare grill.
Remove pork from marinade.
Place pork strips, bell peppers and onion on 8 to 10-inch skewers.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes, turning one at a time. (One vegetable, 1 1/2 starch, 2 meat, 248 calories from fat 16%, 4 fat grams, 229 protein and 30 g carbohydrates.)
Combine juices, cornstarch, vegetable oil and honey in a saucepan, stirring well.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in poppy seed.
Cover and chill thoroughly.
Peel cantaloupes and cut each melon into four 3/4-inch slices.
Place slices on individual salad plates. Combine strawberries and honeydew melon balls.
Spoon 1/2 cup strawberry mixture over each cantaloupe slice.
Spoon poppy seed mixture evenly over fruit.
Chop or dice bologna.
Add finely chopped celery, minced onion, pepper, sweet pickles, croutons and boiled eggs.
Add potato chips, mustard and salad dressing; mix well.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce.
In a bowl, combine oats and coconut; set aside.
In a saucepan, combine milk and butter.
Stir in sugar and cocoa; mix well.
Bring to a boil.
Add oat mixture, stirring constantly; cook for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat; stir in vanilla.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls 1 in. apart onto waxed paper.
Cool.
Mix well and make patties.
Put in skillet and fry until done; drain grease.
Take 1 cup tomato juice and sugar; mix together. Pour over hamburger patties.
Cover; simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine pineapple and oranges with shredded cabbage.
Mix all ingredients.
Refrigerate overnight.
This is a great dip for vegetables and if made with low-fat cottage cheese and mayonnaise, it is very healthy.

recipes.t: Garlic Chicken Fillets In Balsamic Vinegar
d: Split chicken breasts in half lengthwise and dredge in flour; remove excess.
In a large, heavy skillet, heat oil over medium heat.
Cook chicken on one side, about 2 to 3 minutes, or until golden.
Add garlic.
Turn chicken and continue cooking, about 2 to 3 minutes, or until golden.
Add stock, balsamic vinegar and pepper.
Reduce heat.
Cover skillet and cook 5 to 10 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Remove chicken from skillet.
Keep warm.
In a large greased casserole, place a layer of potatoes, then of onions, then some of each of the cheeses.
Season well with salt and pepper.
Repeat layers until ingredients are used up. Pour bouillon over the top.
Sprinkle on some reserved Parmesan. Cover and bake at 375° for 1 hour or until the potatoes are very tender.
Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Using fingers press perforations on dough to seal and form a solid rectangle.
Remove casing from cheese and place in center of sough.
Cover cheese with preserves. Fold dough around cheese.
Brush top with beaten egg white.
Bake in a 350 degree preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until brown. Garnish with sesame seeds.
Allow to set and cut into wedges and serve.
Mix sugar, flour, allspice, salt, lemon rind and honey in a saucepan and heat to blend mixture.
Add cranberries and apples and let cool.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Line strips of crust for lattice top.
Brush top with milk and bake in hot oven (425°) for 30 to 40 minutes or until brown and apples are tender.
Place beans and 1 cup of water in small saucepan; bring to a boil, cover and turn off heat.
Allow to sit 1 hour, then drain. Brown the oxtail well in lard or oil.
Place the oxtails in a 6-quart stove-top casserole.
Add the garlic, onion, tomato and enough water to just cover contents of pot.
Add allspice, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer 3 1/2 hours, adding the beans after 1 1/2 hours.
Stir occasionally.
Remove lid last hour for a thicker sauce.
Season with salt, pepper and Tabasco.
Serve with white cooked rice.
Cut cantaloupe into 1/2 to 3/4-inch size pieces.
Mix with sugar and let set overnight or all day.
Add lemon juice and cook until clear and thick.
Mix eggs, milk, flour, salt and pepper.
(Batter will be thick.)
Heat water to boiling.
Press batter through the holes in a colander (preferred one with large holes), a few tablespoons at a time, into the boiling water.
Stir once to prevent sticking. Cook about 5 minutes or until Spaetzle rise to surface and are tender.
Drain.
Toss Spaetzle with butter or margarine.
Serve with gravy or just plain.
Place graham crackers on cookie sheet or jelly roll pan.
In saucepan, melt oleo.
Stir in brown sugar and bring to a boil for a full 2 minutes.
Pour over graham crackers and smooth over. Sprinkle walnut pieces on top.
Bake at 350° for 7 minutes. Remove from oven and add chocolate pieces.
Smooth over to give tree bark appearance.
Return to oven for 2 to 3 minutes to melt chocolate, if necessary.
Cool completely.
Break into pieces.
In heavy 4-quart pot, heat oil.
Season roast on all sides and put in pot and brown thoroughly.
Remove roast and slice to desired thickness.
Mix flour, onion, green pepper, garlic powder and parsley into oil drippings in pot.
Cook over medium-high heat until brown.
Add about 3 cups water and simmer.
Return roast to gravy and simmer until tender.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with rice.
Bring a
full pan of water to a boil.
Add one piece of pork at a time.
Once pork is completely done, remove from the water. Mix
the soy sauce and mustard together.
Dip the pork in sauce. Place
pork
on
a
large
piece of lettuce and add slices
of celery.
Carefully
roll the pork and celery up in the lettuce. This dish is nonfattening, so serve and enjoy!
Mix margarine and garlic, spread on 1 half of bread.
Sprinkle grated cheese, parsley and basil on top.
Layer tomato and add Mozzarella on top.
Shake pepper to taste.
Cover with other half of loaf.
Wrap in aluminum foil.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Serve with salad and crock of soup.
Yum!
Melt cheese in a double boiler.
Crumble sausage into cheese, stirring constantly.
Add Bisquick mix and cayenne pepper.
Roll into small balls.
Freeze on cookie sheet for best results and cook as needed (if cooked right away, they will flatten some). Bake at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes, depending on whether or not frozen.
In a large frying pan, saute onions and peppers in a tablespoon of oil until tender.
Add crushed tomatoes, spices and salt and pepper to taste.
Put sausage in a large baking pan. Stick several times with a fork.
Add about 1/2 inch of water to the bottom of pan.
Bake at 350° until sausage is done; drain water.
After draining water off of sausage, pour sauce over, then cover with tinfoil and put back in oven.
Cook slowly at about 300°.
The longer it cooks, the better it is, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Salt and pepper chicken, coat large skillet with spray.
Put on medium-high until hot.
Add chicken and cook 3 minutes on each side unti lightly browned.
Remove chicken.
Set aside.
Wipe skillet with paper towel.
Coat skillet with spray; when hot.
Add onion and garlic.
Saute 1 minute.
Add green beans, chickpeas, tomatoes and oregano; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer 30 to 35 minutes.
Yields two servings.
Combine crumbs, cheese, salt, pepper and parsley flakes.
Mix well to combine.
Dip chicken pieces in melted butter, then roll in crumb mixture.
Arrange chicken in shallow baking dish, skin side up.
Pour remaining butter over chicken and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Do not turn chicken.
Line a cookie sheet with foil.
Take 1 inner package from a box of graham crackers; break along the perforations.
Place in cookie sheet, all sides touching.
In a saucepan, melt butter, margarine and sugar.
Bring to a boil and stir; boil for 3 minutes.
Pour over crackers; sprinkle with 1 cup finely chopped walnuts.
Bake at 350° for 8 minutes.
Wash bird and pat off moisture.
Combine garlic powder and pepper.
Cover the turkey inside and out with garlic and pepper mixture.
Wrap the bird in heavy duty foil lengthwise, then sideways, rotating directions with 10 to 12 layers.
Mix sugar and whipping cream.
Divide between 2 baking pans. Sprinkle pecans over sugar mixture.
Roll each bread dough into a 12 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface.
Brush with melted butter.
Mix together brown sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over dough.
Roll dough jelly roll style and pinch to seal.
Cut into slices.
Place rolls into pan with mixture.
Let rise in warm place until doubled in size.
(Can refrigerate overnight, covered; leave at room temperature for 20 minutes.)
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve warm.
Scoop out tomatoes with spoon.
Simmer tomato pulp with chopped parsley until thick paste.
Scramble eggs and cheese together in skillet.
Mix with tomato mixture.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Restuff tomatoes and serve for breakfast.
Have ingredients at room temperature.
Cream sugar, shortening and butter.
Add 1 egg at a time.
Add vanilla flavoring then milk and flour.
Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Layer beef, rice and cheese sprinkled with garlic powder in greased casserole until all is used.
Pour tomatoes over all and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Wash and slice potatoes (do not peel).
Place in a saucepan and cover with water.
Boil until tender.
Drain completely.
Line a greased casserole dish with a single layer of cooked potatoes. Sprinkle with part of the cheese and then with part of the bacon. Continue to layer in that order.
Pour melted butter over all. Bake for 15 minutes in 350° oven.
Add potatoes and onion to oil and water in a 2 to 3-quart boiler or saucepan.
Cook on medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add shrimp; salt and pepper.
Cook another 15 minutes, making sure potatoes are soft.
Mixture should be thick, not soupy.
Mix flour, shortening and milk like making biscuits.
Roll out flat like pie crust.
Sprinkle cheese over dough.
Roll up jelly roll style.
Cut into pieces.
Brown ground beef; add tomato sauce, oregano, salt, pepper, onion and sour cream.
Layer noodles, cheese and meat.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine oil, vinegar and Ramen chicken flavoring.
Shake well and pour over sliced cabbage.
Add sesame seed and sliced almonds plus Ramen noodles.
Pepper and salt to taste.
Heat oven to 375°.
Spread melted margarine in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Separate dough into 13 biscuits.
Snip each biscuit into eighths, using kitchen cutters.
Place biscuit pieces in bowl. Toss with 1 3/4 cups of salsa.
Spoon evenly into baking pan. Sprinkle with cheese, bell pepper, onions and olives.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 45 minutes or until edges are deep golden brown and center is set.
Let stand 15 minutes.
Cut into squares with serrated bread knife.
Serve with cup of salsa.
Makes 12 to 15 servings.
Combine first 7 ingredients in a large bowl and refrigerate overnight.
Roll in crumbs, place on cookie sheet and pour one-half of the butter-shortening mixture over the chicken.
Bake 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Pour over the remaining mix and bake 15 minutes more.
Cream shortening and sugar in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy; beat in vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly after each addition.
Add self-rising flour, alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour. Beat until smooth; add hot coffee and stir until blended.
Pour batter into greased and floured cake pans, or one oblong 12 x 9 1/2-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Frost with Coconut-Pecan Frosting.
Drain pineapple.
Cut ham into chunks.
Put ham, pineapple, cream cheese and all other ingredients into food processor.
Blend until smooth or you can't identify any chunks of cream cheese. Adjust seasonings to your taste.
Great on sliced baguette bread.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix the cake mix and eggs together.
Fold in the pie filling.
Place in the greased pan.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Let cake cool thoroughly.
Heat oven to 350°.
Microwave chocolate and margarine in large microwavable bowl on High 2 minutes or until margarine is melted. Stir until chocolate is completely melted.
Stir granulated sugar into melted chocolate mixture.
Mix in eggs and vanilla until well blended.
Stir in flour.
Fill greased 1 3/4 x 1-inch miniature muffin cups 2/3 full with batter.
Bake for 20 minutes or until toothpick comes out with fudgy crumbs.
Do not overbake.
Cool slightly in muffin pans.
Loosen edges with tip of knife.
Make 1/2-inch indentation in top of each brownie.
Line pie pan with bottom crust.
Place half of the apples in the crust; set aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine sugars, gingersnaps, cinnamon, nuts and butter.
Sprinkle half over apples in crust.
Top with remaining apples and sugar mixture.
Cover with top crust which has a few slits cut in it.
Cover loosely with foil.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Combine bulgur wheat with cold water and allow to stand for at least an hour to absorb moisture.
Then combine bulgur wheat with parsley, chopped green pepper, minced onions, mint and tomatoes. Stir together oil and lemon juice; pour over wheat and mix well. Add salt, if desired (1 teaspoon).
Chill if made ahead.
Blend cheese and mayonnaise until smooth; stir in 57 Sauce, bacon and onion.
Cover; chill.
Serve as a dip with raw vegetables, crackers or potato chips.
Makes about 2 cups.
In a large bowl, place steak, onion, peppers and garlic.
Set aside.
In a small bowl mix 1/2 bottle of steak sauce with 1/2 bottle of Worcestershire.
Add black pepper and stir well.
Pour this mixture over steak and vegetables, tossing to coat evenly; let marinate at least 1 hour, the longer the better.
Drain marinade back into smaller bowl, adding the remainder of the steak sauce and mix well.
Place steak on grill, turning and basting frequently until done (medium to medium-rare is best).
In a skillet, place drained marinated vegetables and a small amount of the marinade; saute until tender.
Cut steak in thin strips (against grain).
Any marinade remaining can be poured over steak strips.
In large bowl, beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in Eagle Brand until smooth.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour in crust and chill 3 hours or until set.
Top with pie filling before serving.

recipes.t: Zucchini Crumb Pie(Tastes Like Apple Pie)
d: Cook zucchini in lemon juice with sugar and raisins.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Add crust mix, cinnamon and nutmeg to thicken. cool.
Mix flour, salt, pepper, oil and steak.
Rub flour mixture into meat well.
Brown in Dutch oven or kettle.
Add beer, broth, onions, garlic, bay leaf and thyme.
Bring to boiling; cover and simmer over low heat 2 1/2 to 3 hours until tender.
Use lemon juice to cook turkey, then put macaroni in with turkey.
Next, add spaghetti sauce.
Add all other ingredients. Stir and let simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
Fill trimmed and chilled celery stalks with cream cheese and top with peanut butter.
Add a swarm of raisins (Texas Bugs).
Cream shortening and 2 cups sugar in a bowl until smooth. Beat in eggs and honey.
Add dry ingredients and vanilla, mixing well.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Roll in sugar.
Place 2 inches apart on baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Yields 5 dozen.
Mix all ingredients in saucepan.
Place on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes (or until sugar starts sticking to pecans).
Pour out on wax paper (or greased platter).
Break apart when cool.
Oil the bottom of a steel pan or Dutch oven.
First, add the onion, then the zucchini (sliced with the skin on), then the string beans and herbs.
Add 1/4 cup water.
Cover tightly.
Cook on very low heat for about 20 minutes.
In 2 to 3-quart saucepan, combine prunes, figs, Port, water and honey.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until fruits are tender but not soft, about 10 minutes.
Remove fruits to bowl with slotted spoon.
Bring liquid in saucepan to boil over medium heat. Cook about 5 minutes until reduced by one-third.
Remove from heat; stir in lemon juice, then pour over fruit.
Cool, cover and chill. To serve, place in serving dishes with orange segments and pour liquid over.
Makes 6 servings.
Contains 232 calories, dietary fiber 8.3 g and fat 6 g.
Cream
cup
margarine in mixer bowl; add cake mix, eggs and
water and beat for 4 minutes. Pour into greased and floured 10 x 15-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes; cool. Whisk
flour
into milk in saucepan; add 1/2 cup margarine.
Cook until
thickened,
whisking
constantly; cool. Combine
with remaining
ingredients in bowl; beat for 4 minutes.
Cut
cake into
1 1/3 x 2 1/4-inch pieces.
Split each piece into 2 layers. Spread with filling.
Cook cranberries and water until cranberries crack, then mash. Add jello and sugar.
Mix together and add pineapple and let set to jell.
Prepare biscuit mix as directed on package.
Roll dough on lightly floured board, about 10 x 12-inches.
Spread honey to within 1 inch of edge of dough.
Combine spices and sugar; toss with apples.
Spread apples and spices evenly over dough.
Roll like a jelly roll.
Bake in a greased pan with sides at 350° for 40 minutes.
Slice and serve warm with whipped cream or hot vanilla sauce.
Place ingredients as listed in a 9 x 15-inch dish.
Spread mayonnaise over top.
Sprinkle with sugar, cheese and bacon.
Do not toss.
A great salad for family or church gathering.
I usually double everything except lettuce.
Chill 6 to 8 hours.
Scald milk; slowly add 3/4 cup flour to hot milk and beat thoroughly; cool.
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup milk and 1 tablespoon sugar; add to cooled mixture and beat well.
Let rise until double in bulk.
Add salt to eggs and beat until thick and lemon colored.
Add sugar and continue to beat.
Add flavorings and remaining flour.
Knead for 10 minutes.
Add butter; continue kneading for 10 minutes, or until dough leaves the fingers.
Add almonds, fruit peels, or both, if desired.
Mix well.
Let rise until double in bulk.
Punch down and let rise again.
Punch down and divide into 2 parts.
Place in greased pans, or into fluted tube pan (10-inch).
Let rise 1 hour.
Bake at 325°
for 40 minutes.
Decorate with white lucre.
Sprinkle with colored sugar or baker's confetti.
Saute chicken and onions in olive oil until white.
Add veggies and saute 2 more minutes.
Add spaghetti sauce and shrimp. Simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes or until shrimp is cooked and chicken is cooked through.
Stir in spinach; cook to 3 to 5 minutes.
Serve over noodles, topped with cheese.
Clean and cut celery stems into bite-size pieces.
Cook until soft; drain.
Mix the sugar, vinegar and water.
Bring to a good boil.
Add cooked celery pieces.
Set aside to cool and the refrigerate.
Keeps well.
Use as a sour side dish for any meal.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
In a large bowl, combine cake mix, margarine and milk; mix well.
Press half of dough evenly in bottom of greased pan.
Sprinkle chocolate chips and nuts evenly over dough; drizzle evenly with ice cream topping.
Crumble remaining dough mixture over ice cream topping. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until caramel begins to bubble.
Cool completely and cut into bars.
Makes 36 bars.
Combine mustard and molasses in small saucepan.
Add other ingredients.
Cook over low heat for about 10 minutes.
Place chicken in flat casserole and pour mixture over it.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 15 minutes longer.
Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch baking dish with Pam; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine zucchini, onion, cheeses, pepperoni and spices.
Mix thoroughly and set aside.
In another bowl, combine oil, eggs and Bisquick.
Mix well.
Add to zucchini mixture and blend thoroughly.
In a large bowl or plastic bag combine lime peel, lime juice, vegetable oil, sesame oil and salt.
Add chicken to marinade. Cover and refrigerate 4 hours or longer if desired, turning occasionally.
Remove chicken from marinade.
Reserve 1/4 cup marinade.
In a small bowl, combine 1/4 cup marinade, honey and sesame seed.
Grill or broil chicken with marinade-honey mixture several times while cooking.
Cook hamburger meat until done; drain off excess grease and add taco seasoning and tomato sauce to the meat.
Cook until it has cooked down a little.
Cut up lettuce and tomatoes in a large bowl.
Add cheese, olives, onion and Fritos.
Pour hamburger mixture over salad and toss.
Lightly toss shrimp in flour and saute in butter 2 to 3 minutes.
Add onions; saute one minute longer.
Remove from pan. Add wine and boil until sauce thickens.
Return shrimp to pan. Add salt, pepper and lemon juice and cook 1 to 2 minutes longer. Serve over rice.
Broiled tomatoes and steamed broccoli make colorful accompaniments.
Dissolve jello; cool.
Add soda.
Chill until partially set. Drain pineapple (reserve juice).
Fold in pineapple and sliced bananas.
Pour into a 9 x 12-inch glass pan and set until firm.
Beat together until well blended the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Add the combined flour, soda and salt; mix well.
Stir in oats, cheese, wheat germ and bacon.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 14 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Cool 1 minute on cookie sheet; remove to wire cooling rack.
Store in loosely covered container. Yield:
about 3 dozen cookies.
Crush strawberries; add sugar and 1 cup of milk.
Beat until creamy.
Gradually add remaining ingredients except ice cream, beating well.
Put 1 or 2 scoops ice cream into each chilled glass.
Fill with strawberry mixture.
If desired, garnish with strawberries.
Makes 5 cups.
Cut bread into 1-inch thick slices, leaving slices attached at the bottom.
In a bowl, combine butter, onions and mustard; spread on both sides of each slice of bread.
Cut each cheese slice diagonally into four triangles; place between the slices of bread.
Cut bacon in half width-wise and then lengthwise; drape a piece over each slice.
Place the loaf on a double thickness of heavy-duty foil.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes or until bacon is crisp.
Yields 10 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a casserole.
Cook spinach and artichokes according to directions on the packages.
Drain well.
Melt yeast in 1/2 cup warm water and 1 teaspoon sugar.
Add milk to pudding mix and cook until thick; add oleo.
Let cool until lukewarm.
Add eggs, salt and yeast.
Mix in the flour. Place dough in well-greased bowl and let rise until double.
Knead down and let rise again.
Make into rolls as desired.
Let rise again.
Bake in 350° oven until brown.
In
shallow
baking
dish, mix egg white and water.
In another
shallow
dish,
mix
together
bread crumbs, paprika, salt,
garlic
powder, pepper and bay leaf.
Dip chicken first in egg
water mixture
and then in bread crumbs, dredging to coat. Place
chicken on round glass dish with large pieces to the outside.
Place butter in one cup glass measuring cup and microwave
on
High
seconds
or
until melted.
Pour over chicken.
Microwave
chicken
uncovered on High for 5 minutes. Rotate
a quarter turn and microwave on High 5 minutes.
Cover chicken with waxed paper;
rotate a quarter turn and microwave 5 minutes more.
Remove from oven; let stand covered about 10 minutes.
Return to oven for additional cooking if fork cannot be inserted
in
chicken with ease when testing for doneness. Makes 4 servings.
Mix milk, biscuit mix, eggs, butter and pepper in blender for 15 seconds.
Pour into greased 9-inch pie pan.
In small skillet, cook pepperoni, green pepper, onion and mushrooms in butter until tender.
Stir in oregano.
Add pepperoni mixture into pan (with biscuit mixture) and then add 1 cup of Mozzarella to mixture. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 375°.
Sprinkle remaining 1/4 cup of Mozzarella onto top of quiche and bake for 2 minutes longer.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
In saucepan over medium-high heat, blend butter and brown sugar.
Heat to boiling and boil 4 minutes.
Cover a cookie sheet (or jelly-roll pan) with foil and butter lightly.
Place single layer of crackers on foil close together.
Pour butter mixture over crackers, spreading evenly.
Bake at 375° for 5 minutes. Immediately sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Allow to soften, then spread evenly.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Refrigerate until cool. Cut into squares with a knife or pizza cutter.
Store in covered container in refrigerator.
Can be kept 1 to 2 weeks.
Also can be frozen.
Combine
potatoes,
sugar,
milk, 1/3 cup melted margarine, vanilla and eggs;
mix well.
Put in greased baking dish 11 x 13-inch or equivalent.
Cut chicken breast halves into 8 pieces each. In cup, mix curry powder, bouillon, sugar and salt.
In nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, in hot salad oil, cook onion until golden brown.
Add chicken and curry powder mixture and cook until chicken just loses its pink color throughout, about 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in raisins and 3/4 cup water; heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low.

Grill, poach or fry the sausage links until fully cooked. Simmer in tomato sauce for 30-45 minutes. Meanwhile, prepare rice and mix the vegetables into it. Serve the sausage over the rice and veggies.
Please read this before you start!
I find that a can of cranberries (1 pound can, whole) will do the same thing as raw. Crush them and be sure that you do not put any more juice than 3 cups.
I use the cranberry juice to make the 3 cups, adding it to the water and the pineapple juice.
Cut down or leave out the sugar.
Heat oil in extra deep, 12 inch nonstick skillet on med-low. Peel and finely chop onion adding to skillet as you chop.
Seed and finely chop pepper, adding as you chop.
Raise heat to med-hi and cook 5 minutes or until onion is tender.
Mix softened butter with coffee. Add confectioners sugar while mixing. Continue until icing is thick enough to spread.
Wash and prepare fruit.
Place fruit in kettle (large one). Add lemon juice and pectin.
Bring to a boil.
Add sugar.
Cook for 1 minute.
Pour into jelly jars.
Skim off foam first.
Seal. Place in hot water to cover jars and process for 5 minutes.
Keeps real well for 1 year.
Cut steak into strips; roll in flour and brown in skillet. Place steak, water, tomatoes, chopped onions, bell pepper and remaining ingredients in crock-pot. Cook all day. Serve over rice or noodles.
Butter large sheet pan.
Place pineapple on bottom of pan. Next, place blueberries.
Sprinkle sugar on top of blueberries. Sprinkle dry cake mix on top of blueberries and sugar.
Pour melted margarine on cake mix.
Sprinkle coconut and nuts on top. Bake according to directions on cake mix box.
In a baking pan, dump pineapple with juice and cherry pie filling.
Top with cake mix.
Pat with margarine.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serve hot or cold with ice cream.
Beat yolks real good.
Gradually add sugar and cream and beat until stiff.
Stir in part of the flour.
Place enough dough on breadboard, spreading on softened butter.
Fold batter, then spread on more butter.
Continue process until butter and flour are all used up.
After each addition, pound with rolling pin until thoroughly mixed.
Set in a cool place until chilled.
Put vegeburger in bowl.
In a separate bowl, put bread crumbs with ketchup and slightly beaten egg.
Mix well.
Add to vegeburger.
Then add cheese, pepper, onion, lemon juice and salt. Mix well.
Shape into 12 balls.
Sprinkle with baco chips.
Place in shallow baking pan.
Bake at 350° for about 40 minutes.
Turn once during baking.
In skillet, brown onion and ground beef.
Drain.
Add soups and pizza sauce to beef mixture.
Stir and cook until heated. Cook noodles according to package directions, reducing cooking time by 5 minutes.
Drain.
Tear lettuce into pieces and place in bottom of large dish. Layer tomato, onion, beans, Doritos and cheese.
Pour whole bottle of creamy Italian dressing over all.
Beat egg whites until very stiff.
Add 1/2 of powdered sugar slowly.
Add vanilla, salt and cream of tartar.
Add remaining powdered sugar.
Spread on cookies.
Halve or quarter scrubbed potatoes.
Put into an oven-proof casserole dish.
Coat potatoes with fat free salad dressing. Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake at 350° covered for 45 minutes.
Scald milk and water together; add Crisco and anise seeds and let cool to room temperature.
Mix flour and sugar in large bowl - make a well, when cool pour above liquid into well.
Add yeast and sugar to warm water and let stand till frothy - almost double in volume - pour into well.
Add all the eggs and mix well.
Knead until not sticky adding more flour as needed.
Divide into 8 parts and put into greased 8 inch x 4 inch baking pans and let rise until double.
Bake at 350° until nicely browned (about 30 minutes).
Brush left over egg whites on top of loaves to make them shinny.

Wash chops; pat dry and season with salt and pepper. In large skillet, heat oil. Flour chops and sear in the oil. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side to brown. Remove and pat dry on paper towels. Put the chops back in the skillet and add the chopped onions and chopped garlic to pot with 1/4 cup water. Put lid on the pot and steam chops approximately 20 minutes.
Cream margarine and cheese together.
Combine flour and onion mix.
Mix all ingredients together.
Make small rolls as for refrigerator cookies.
Slice and bake for about 15 minutes at 350°.
Makes about 4 dozen.
Will slice better if chilled for 3 or 4 hours.
In glass mixing bowl, put sugar, water and butter; microwave on High for 30 seconds, just until it starts to bubble.
Stir. Make paste of flour, cornstarch and a little milk.
Combine with sugar mixture using wire whisk; add rest of milk and egg yolks and mix well.
Microwave on High 4 minutes; whisk well and return to microwave for another 3 minutes.
If not thick enough, cook another minute.
Cover with plastic wrap and cool for 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir again, then pour into pie shell.
Serve with whipped topping.
Warm soup and 1/2 can milk on stove.
Arrange stuffing mix in large plate.
Dip chicken in warm soup, then roll both sides in stuffing mix.
Place chicken, skin side up, on broiler pan or other drip type pan.
Put dab (1/2 tablespoon) butter on each piece.
Place in oven at 375° to 400° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Just before serving, pour remaining soup over chicken.
Serve with white rice and a salad.
Brown sausage; drain and cool.
Crumble sausage into bowl. Beat eggs in another bowl.
Add milk, salt, mustard and bread cubes; mix well.
Add cheese and sausage; mix again.
Spoon into a 12 x 8 x 2-inch glass baking dish.
Cover; refrigerate overnight. Remove dish from refrigerator.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes, or until egg mixture is set.
Cut into squares to serve. Makes 8 servings.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Let cream cheese soften at room temperature and then spread in bottom of casserole dish.
Put chili and cooked ground beef on top of cheese.
Then put a layer of peppers.
Top with Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts.
Melt margarine and mix with crushed graham crackers and sugar. Press into bottom of spring-form pan base.
In a large bowl, combine 2 cups lukewarm water, yeast and flour and stir 1 to 2 minutes.
Cover and let rise 1 hour.
In another large bowl, combine cornmeal, salt and 2 cups hot water; stir until water is completely absorbed.
Cover and let soften at room temperature 1 hour.
Stir down yeast mixture, then stir in cornmeal mixture and blend thoroughly.
(Dough will be liquid and batter-like.)
Cover and let rise 2 hours.
(Dough will be bubbly and will rise only slightly.)
Stir down dough and spoon into 2 well-buttered 8-inch round cake pans, filling them about 3/4 full. Cover and let rise 2 hours.
(Dough will rise only slightly.)
Bake in preheated 425° oven for 50 to 60 minutes or until top is a pale golden brown.
Cool on racks.
Heat 5 minutes just before serving. Makes 2 loaves.
May be frozen up to 3 months.
Drain the beans well; toss in a bowl with the sliced onion and celery.
Mix vinegar, salad oil, sugar and salt well.
Pour over the bean mixture; mix well.
Place in airtight container; refrigerate overnight.
This salad keeps well for at least a week.

Cut salmon into steaks. Marinate for 30 minutes. Dry on paper towels. Sprinkle with crushed peppercorn. Put small amount of cooking oil in skillet. Fry, skin side up. Flip 1 time (approximately 2 minutes per side). Puncture with knife. When knife slides through easily, it's done.
Spread pineapple in 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Crumble cake mix evenly over pineapple; sprinkle with almonds.
Dot evenly with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and add carrots, squash, onion, eggplant and yellow pepper.
Saute, stirring and tossing, about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, garlic, thyme, salt and pepper.
Cook, again tossing and stirring, about 3 minutes.
Add basil.
Stir to combine.
Serve immediately.
Makes approximately 6 servings.
Put cake mix, pudding mix, fruit cocktail (juice and all), 1 cup of the coconut, eggs, and oil into mixing bowl and beat on medium speed 4 minutes.
Combine the brown sugar and chopped nuts in a separate bowl.
Pour cake batter into a greased & floured 9 X 13 cake pan and sprinkle with nut/sugar mixture.
Bake 1 hour at 325° or until cake springs back when touched and pulls away from the pan.
Do not under bake.
Bring margarine, white sugar and evaporated milk to a boil in a medium pan, simmer for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the remaining 1 1/2 cups coconut and spoon over the cake that has cooled for 15 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.
Brown meat and drain.
Combine meat, tomato juice, kidney beans, stewed tomatoes and chili seasoning.
Bring to boil and stir; reduce heat and simmer until ready to eat.
Put corn chips in bottom of bowl; pour chili over chips.
Top with cheese; eat when cheese melts.
"Mmmm good."
Fry bacon in skillet; remove, drain, crumble and set aside. In a small amount of the bacon grease, saute celery, onion and bell pepper until tender.
Add all tomatoes and cook together 15 to 20 minutes on low flame.
Add drained peas, salt and pepper. Cook 10 more minutes on low flame.
Add crumbled bacon just before serving.
Set oven broiling rack in lower guides.
Preheat oven to 325°. Sift together flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg into large bowl.
Add shortening, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Stir in oats and raisins.
Drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 325° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes.
Remove from sheet.
Chop broccoli and cauliflower into bite size pieces.
Add carrots, bacon, onion and cheese.
In small bowl, mix Miracle Whip, sugar, vinegar and bacon drippings.
Pour over vegetables and stir to coat.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours before serving.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Add yogurt, pineapple and nuts.
(Only add bananas if salad will be eaten in 1 day, as they will turn dark.)
Heat butter; add onion and saute.
Add broth and bring to boil.
Add noodles and salt and boil 3 minutes.
Add broccoli and garlic; cook for 4 minutes.
Add milk, cheese and pepper; cook until cheese is melted.
Steam broccoli until it is still crunchy.
Cool broccoli, then refrigerate.
Before serving cold, add a very small amount of Italian salad dressing.
Makes a great hors d'oeuvres.
Brown and drain hamburger.
Stir in soups.
Heat to boiling. Pour into cake pan.
Lay Tater Tots on top.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Brush fish with oil and sprinkle lightly with ginger and garlic.
Broil 3 to 4 inches from heat source for about 5 minutes or until fish flakes when tested with fork.
Stir together yogurt, orange peel and mint leaves.
Season to taste with white pepper. To serve, spoon yogurt sauce over fish or serve separately. Serves 6.

recipes.t: Wild Rice And Chicken Breast Casserole
d: Mix rice, soup, soup mix and water.
Place in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place chicken breasts on top of rice mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
(Cover with foil to prevent drying out.)
Coat 8-inch square baking dish with cooking spray.
Sprinkle with half gingersnap crumbs.
Stir pumpkin, sugar, 1/2 cup nuts and pumpkin spice in bowl until well blended.
Stir ice cream in large bowl until smooth.
Stir in pumpkin until well blended.
Pour into baking dish.
Sprinkle with remaining crumbs.
Place plastic wrap on surface.
Cover with foil and freeze at least 4 hours.
Heat milk, water, salt and pepper to boiling in 2-quart saucepan.
Gradually add grits.
Reduce heat.
Simmer about 5 minutes.
Stir in cheese and onions. Stir 1 cup of hot mixture in eggs.
Stir into remaining hot mixture in saucepan.
Pour into greased 1 1/2-quart casserole. Dot with margarine.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake uncovered in a 350° oven.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Serves about 8.
Rub garlic over both sides of chops.
Heat olive oil in 10-inch nonstick skillet.
Add veal chops.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes over medium heat, turning once.
Transfer to plate.
Sprinkle with salt. Keep warm.
Drain excess fat from skillet.
Cook and stir over high heat 1 minute or until desired.
Stir in sesame oil.
Pour sauce over chops.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Serves 2.
Spray frying pan or wok with butter flavor Pam.
Quickly saute over medium-high heat the cubed chicken meat; add some water (1/4 cup) to bring up flavor.
After chicken is just about done, remove and set aside in covered dish.
Re-spray pan.
Over medium heat, add onion and green pepper; when onion is partially cooked, add broccoli.
Cover, heat and add 1/4 to 1/2 cup of chicken broth and season to taste.
When those vegetables are tender-crisp, add pea pods and sliced mushrooms, continue sauteing.
Stir 1 teaspoon cornstarch and remaining broth (water can be used or added for more juices); set aside.
Add chicken; saute some more to heat and mix thoroughly.
Add cornstarch mix.
Turn off heat and serve over 2/3 cup rice.
Each serving:
325 calories (including rice), 2 gm. fat.
Score flank steak on both sides.
Place meat in plastic bag; set in a bowl.
For marinade, in a bowl combine vinegar, water, Worcestershire sauce, cooking oil, garlic and red pepper.
Pour over meat in bag.
Place in refrigerator 4 to 24 hours.
Preheat broiler.
Meanwhile, place meat on rack in broiler pan.
Boil 3 to 4-inches from heat for 5 minutes.
Brush with marinade.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes more.
Place on platter.
Thinly slice meat diagonally across grain.
Makes 4 servings.
Contains 185 calories.
Cook manicotti.
Drain and place in bowl of cold water; set aside.
Set oven at 350°.
In medium bowl, combine cottage cheese, 1 1/2 cups Mozzarella cheese, egg and egg white, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, parsley, oregano, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Drain manicotti.
Pat dry with a paper towel.
Fill shells with the cheese spread.
Put 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce over bottom of 3-quart baking dish.
Arrange filled manicotti on sauce. Cover with remaining sauce.
Sprinkle remaining cheeses.
Cover dish loosely with foil.
Bake 40 minutes until hot and bubbly.
Melt milk chocolate flavored disks, the white chocolate flavored disks and the peanut butter in the microwave.
Melt on Defrost for 1 minute, then check every 10 seconds until melted. Stir in 2 cups of crushed pretzels (I used pretzel sticks, which I put in a sealed plastic bag and crushed with a rolling pin.
I left some chunks for crunch.)
Spread on cookie sheet really thin; refrigerate.
When set, break up in small pieces to serve.
Heat chilies, tomato, onion and hot sauce on medium heat until soft; add cubed cheese and cook at medium heat until melted. Serve with tortilla chips or similar dip product.
Brown sausage, pepper, garlic and onion.
Add cream, cheese, parsley and marjoram.
Blend together and mix into cooked kluski noodles.
Cream the shortening and sugar together.
Add egg; mix well and set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together the flour, soda and salt.
Chop the orange half in a blender with the buttermilk or yogurt.
Add alternately the flour mixture to the sugar mixture, stirring only until the ingredients are moistened.
Pour into greased muffin cups.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes. Makes 9 to 12 small muffins.
Cut 1 cup butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Stir in buttermilk until dry ingredients are moistened. Knead dough 3 or 4 times on lightly floured surface.
Roll dough to 1/2-inch thickness.
Cut with a 1 1/2-inch biscuit cutter. Place on lightly greased baking sheets.
Bake at 425° for 12 to 14 minutes.
Brush with melted butter.
Serve with ham and mustard.
Combine dry ingredients.
Blend eggs, milk, butter and honey. Add to dry ingredients, stirring until moistened.
Pour into greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake in a 400° oven for 30 minutes, or until done and brown.

recipes.t: Fast And Easy Chili Con Queso
d: Heat all ingredients over low heat, mixing well.
Use as a dip with flour tortillas.
Chop mushrooms fine and saute in butter for 5 minutes. Sprinkle flour over butter mixture and add cream and seasonings. Spread filling on slices of bread with crust removed.
Cut in half, roll and fasten with toothpicks.
Place on cookie sheet and toast in oven.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Coat steak with flour.
Brown on both sides in a small amount of oil in skillet.
Arrange onion over steak.
Cover with tomatoes.
Combine remaining ingredients with 1 soup can of water in bowl.
Pour over all.

In medium skillet, melt butter and cook potatoes until tender. In a large bowl, beat onion soup mix, eggs and milk. Add egg mixture into skillet. Cook, covered, over low heat for 25 minutes or until almost set. Top with cheese.
Let stand, covered, 5 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Cook whole beets until tender, in boiling water for about 30 minutes.
Let cool; peel and dice.
Combine diced beets, sugar and ginger in medium saucepan and cook over medium-low heat for 30 minutes.
Add chopped lemon and continue cooking until slightly thickened, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, about 30 minutes.
Stir in almonds.
Transfer to jars with tight-fitting lids and seal.
Combine pineapple chunks, pears and oranges in a bowl; toss gently and set aside.
Combine 2 tablespoons of the pineapple juice and the remaining ingredients in a jar.
Cover tightly and shake vigorously.
Pour over fruit and toss gently.
Cover and chill up to 24 hours.
Serves about 10.
Take mushroom and remove stems to have center to fill.
Mix together sour cream, cream of mushroom soup, and Pepperidge Farm stuffing mix.
Put in center of mushrooms.
Place mushrooms in melted margarine.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Add parsley on top before cooking.
Place first 4 ingredients in blender and blend at high speed until onion is pureed.
Add next 4 ingredients and blend again. Add cream, 1/3 at a time and blend until very smooth.
Pour into a 1-quart mold and chill overnight.
To unmold, dip bottom and sides of mold into warm water and invert onto a serving plate.
Decorate mousse with parsley.
Cream together powdered sugar and butter.
Mix in orange peel, juice and extract.
Place in pastry tube; pipe into dates. Makes about 32.
Melt butter.
Add sugar, eggs, vinegar and nuts.
Put in uncooked pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: When The Wife'S Away Taco Salad
d: Brown beef; drain fat.
Add seasoning and 1 cup water.
Simmer to thicken.
On a large plate layer beef, lettuce, tomato, sour cream, kidney beans, sauce and cheese.
Enjoy.
Butter a baking dish.
Put in the apples and water.
With a fork, mix flour, sugars, cinnamon, butter and salt.
Spread mixture over apples and bake at 350° until apples are tender and topping is crisp, about 40 minutes.
Serve with ice cream or whipped topping.

Combine stuffing mix, margarine and broth in bowl; mix well. Press half of mixture over bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Combine chicken, onion, celery, salad dressing, eggs, milk and salt in medium bowl; mix well.
Spoon into prepared dish.
Top with remaining stuffing mixture.
Bake at 325° for 35 minutes. Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Yields 8 servings.
Mix jello, marshmallows and water and let cool until syrupy. Add pineapple, cream and cottage cheese and mix.
Pour into flat glass dish.
Cut into squares and serve on lettuce leaf.
(I substitute small box of Cool Whip for cream.)
Brown hamburg with garlic and onion.
Put in crock-pot and add all vegetables.
Season with salt and pepper or any of your favorite spices.
(Optional:
A can of Hunt's tomato sauce can be added for color.)
Cook for 5 hours or until all vegetables are tender.
Drain juice from clams and place in separate bowl.
Melt margarine and oil in medium size saucepan.
Add onion and saute five minutes.
Add the clam juice, garlic powder, parsley, oregano and chopped garlic.
Cook 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes cooking, add cheese and clams and cook five minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Best served over linguine.
Cook shells as directed. Saute broken up chopped meat in butter and chopped parsley.
Season with salt and pepper.
Fill parboiled shells immediately.
Cover bottom of baking dish with sauce.
Arrange filled shells in single layer over the sauce.
Top with remaining sauce; sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Pour 1 cup boiling water
over
lime
jello
and mix.
Add lemon juice.
Line bottom of
pan
with pineapple.
Place maraschino cherries in centers of pineapple.
Pour
in
lime jello mixture.
Let set until firm.
Pour 1 cup boiling water over
lemon
jello and mix.
Mix salad dressing with cream cheese and
add
to
slightly congealed lemon jello mixture and beat. Pour mixture
on
lime
jello.
When
it
begins
to congeal, pour 1 cup boiling water over strawberry jello.
Mix and add 1 cup cold water.
Add sliced bananas and when slightly set, pour next to center lemon mixture.
Chill until firm.
In a large bowl, blend all ingredients except eggs.
Beat at medium speed for 1 minute.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat 1 minute after each addition.
Spread batter in a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes until cake tests done with a toothpick.
Cool right side up for about 15 minutes, then remove from pan.
Mix the powdered sugar, 6 maraschino cherries (chopped) and 2 tablespoons juice from cherries.
Pour over cake while still warm to make a glaze.

recipes.t: Awesome Chicken Enchiladas(These Are Out Of This World Vaya Can Dios.)
d: Cook chicken; dice chilies and slice olives.
Mix olives, diced chilies, sour cream, soup and 1/2 cheese.
Divide that in half.
To one half, add chicken (remove chicken from bones, tear into small bite size pieces).
Place some mixture on each tortilla; roll. Cover rolls with remaining sauce and cheese.
Bake at 350° covered for 15 minutes and 15 minutes uncovered.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease muffin cups.
Melt butter in skillet with onion and peppers; cook until tender about 7 minutes, stirring often.
Cool to lukewarm.
Whisk sour cream and eggs in medium bowl.
Stir in cooled onion mixture.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, soda in large bowl.
Make well in center.
Add sour cream mixture, stirring just until blended.
Fill muffin cups 3/4 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes 10 muffins. This is a great smelling complement to hearty soups.
In a Dutch oven, brown meat in oil; drain.
Add celery, onion and green pepper; saute 5 minutes or until tender.
Stir in broth, tomatoes, potato, carrot, garlic salt, clove and bay leaf.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat; simmer uncovered for 1 hour or until meat is tender.
Discard clove and bay leaf.
Stir in parsley.
Brown beef in skillet.
Push to one side and saute onion. Drain fat.
Stir in 2 cans of tomato sauce, salt and oregano. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Shred cheeses together (except Ricotta). Spread 1/2 can of remaining tomato sauce in bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Add layer of uncooked noodles, slightly overlapping. Add half of the meat and sauce mixture.
Sprinkle with 1/3 of cheese mixture.
Repeat with one more layer.
Add remaining noodles.
Cover with remaining tomato sauce, Ricotta and cheese. Cover with foil.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.

recipes.t: Raccoon With Red Wine And Garlic
d: Clean raccoon well.
Cut into 8 sections.
Parboil in water to cover.
Add whole onion, 6 cloves garlic, bay leaves, 1 cup chopped celery and 1 teaspoon peppercorns.
Cover.
Cook over low heat for 2 hours.
Remove meat from kettle and drain.
Set aside.
Soak beans overnight.
Drain water.
Add more for cooking. Slice sausage in large pieces and cook together with beans until tender.
Cook rice and set aside.
Serve sausage and beans on rice and garnish with pepper and sour cream.
Drain beans and discard liquid.
Cut up bacon in small pieces and chop onion.
Brown bacon in pan with onion.
Do not drain grease.
When bacon is brown, add brown sugar, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and mustard.
Cook over medium-low heat until sugar is melted.
Put sauce mixture and drained beans in a large casserole dish and bake for 50 minutes at 400°.
Excellent for fellowship or a picnic.
Feeds a crowd.
Add a little milk to hamburger meat.
Prepare Stove Top dressing.
Place about 1/4 cup of the dressing in hamburger patty, flattened, for each bundle.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown sausage in a skillet.
Remove sausage and set aside.
Add beef and onion to skillet and cook until browned; drain fat.
Combine beef mixture, sausage, beans, molasses, sugar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, ketchup and bacon in a large casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered for 30 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a bowl.
Add to apples.
Put apples and mixture in pie crust.
Dot on top with butter.
Put pie crust on top and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Cook macaroni; add tomato juice.
Gradually stir in black pepper, green pepper and onion.
After you have added these ingredients, let simmer.
Add salt to taste.
Slice mushrooms and place on a large sheet of aluminum foil. Top with butter, spices, garlic and sherry or brandy.
Wrap, folding edges tightly under. Place on grill 10 to 15 minutes. Serves 4.
Have butcher cut 1 to 2 inches off drumsticks so they can fit in the crock-pot.
Remove skin and place in crock-pot; add seasonings.
Mix soup with 1/2 can of white wine.
Pour over drumsticks, cover and let cook all day on low.
Serves 2.
Butter a large casserole or deep dish pie pan.
Cook broccoli and green onion in a little water with a dash of salt for 5 to 6 minutes.
Drain well.
In a bowl, combine tomato soup and half and half.
Add sugar
to pineapple and bring to a boil.
Add jello and let
cool. Whip
chilled Pet milk and fold into pineapple mixture.
Store in refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, mix together cake mix, 1 egg and margarine.
Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
In a medium bowl, mix together cream cheese, confectioners sugar, 2 eggs and vanilla.
Pour over mixture.
Sprinkle pecans on top.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cool completely before cutting.
Best if stored in refrigerator.
Stir together flour, baking powder and salt.
Set aside.
Cream margarine with mixer.
Add sugar gradually, beating well after each addition, until light and fluffy.
Stir in egg; beat 1 minute. Combine milk and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients.
Alternate with milk/vanilla mixture, beating well after each addition.
Spread cake batter in greased, floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread the berries evenly over top of the batter.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until center of cake springs back when lightly touched. Cool 5 minutes.
Combine vanilla, powdered sugar and cream or milk with melted butter.
Spread over cake; leave berries exposed. Serve with vanilla ice cream.
In large bowl, cube cooked potatoes in 1-inch cubes.
Add diced
celery stalks, chopped onion, and chopped hard boiled eggs. Mix in spices, sugar, and vinegar.
Gradually mix in mayo to desired consistency.
Chill for at least three hours. Add salt & pepper to taste before serving.
Garnish with paprika for a perfect summer salad.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, grated cheese and pepper in a large bowl.
Lightly flour cutlets on both sides.
Saute cutlets in oil 2 or 3 minutes on both sides each and remove.
In frying pan saute onion lightly in a little olive oil, then add crushed tomatoes and wine and seasoning.
Simmer 10 minutes.
In roasting pan, put half the tomato mixture on bottom, spreading sauce around, then add the chicken cutlets.
Spread out; top with rest of sauce and then add the Mozzarella cheese to each cutlet.
Cover pan with aluminum foil; bake for 40 minutes.
Put cooked macaroni in buttered baking dish.
Mix soup, milk, onion, 1/2 grated cheese and 1/2 diced ham.
Pour over macaroni and top with remaining cheese and ham.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Peel turnips and cut into 1/2-inch cubes or 2 x 1/2-inch sticks.
Cook, covered, in a small amount of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Drain.
Stir in margarine or butter, sliced green onion or snipped parsley and lemon juice. Season to taste.
Makes 4 servings.

Brown the rice in a little butter, then put 2 cans tomato juice until rice is cooked. Simmer over low heat while you cook the hamburg and onions. After cooked, add the tomatoes and pepper. Put the rice on a plate, then add the hamburg mix. Eat with tortillas.
