In small chafing dish or fondue pot over low heat, heat undiluted soup, wine, chives and Worcestershire until hot and bubbly, stirring occasionally.
Cut bread into 1 1/2-inch chunks. To serve, let guests spear bread with fondue forks and dip into hot mixture.
Makes 3 cups.
Melt butter in large frying pan.
Add potatoes and fry until brown.
Place in 9-inch square baking dish.
Sprinkle with cooked and crumbled bacon.
Stir together egg yolks, mushrooms and cheese.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry.
Fold cheese mixture into whites.
Pour over bacon.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until set.
Serves 6.
In large saucepan, brown sausage; drain.
Remove half of sausage; set aside.
Stir tomato sauce, paste, water and brown sugar into sausage; simmer 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, in medium bowl, combine remaining sausage, Ricotta cheese, 2 cups Mozzarella, egg and parsley.
In 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish, pour 1/3 spaghetti sauce mixture.
Stuff manicotti noodles with Ricotta mixture and place on top of sauce.
Pour remaining sauce over filled noodles, top with remaining Mozzarella and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 20 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Put the shells in a small amount of water and boil for 1 minute. Discard the shells and put shrimp into the water.

Cook until done, set aside reserving the liquid. In a small pan, boil sliced onion (to tame the taste a little) for 1 minute and drain. Mix together the onion, tomato and green pepper, add lime juice, parsley, pepper and salt. Then add shrimp and reserved liquid. Add olive oil and stir.
In a saucepan, combine tomatoes, corn and beans. Heat through. Garnish servings with cheese and sour cream, if desired. Serves 4.
Layer peas, ham, cheese and onion.
Beat remaining ingredients; pour over.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Wash leeks thoroughly and cut into chunks.
Cook in water. Add butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer, until tender, adding a little water if necessary. The broth can be thickened by adding a little cornstarch, if desired.
Melt baking chocolate on low in microwave, stirring constantly.
Dip each apple in melted chocolate and cool completely on wax paper.
Melt caramels on low in microwave, stirring constantly.
You may have to add a little corn syrup to be able to stir the melted caramels.
Dip each cool chocolate apple in the caramel, then sprinkle with chopped almonds.
Serve when cool.
Bring crushed pineapple with juice to a boil and add jello, buttermilk, coconut and pecans.
When cool, fold in Cool Whip.
Mix green beans, peas, vegetables, water chestnuts, celery, onions, green peppers and pimento and chill.
Add sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper.
This makes dressing.
Mix well and pour over chilled vegetables.
Slice sausage in 1/4-inch slices.
Brown in wok or large skillet.
Add onions when sausage is nearly done.
Drain.
Add tomatoes, zucchini, lemon juice, salt, Tabasco sauce and oregano. Cook uncovered for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Combine crushed corn flakes, Zesty Italian Dressing Mix, Parmesan and parsley flakes.
Dip chicken breasts in milk then the crumb mixture.
Place in lightly greased 12 x 8 x 2 dish.
Bake 375° for 18 minutes.
Cut cucumbers lengthwise in slices.
Pack in jars with onion, 2 or 3 stalks of celery and dill.
Heat sugar, salt, vinegar and water.
Pour over pickles.
Put lids and rings and place in a hot water bath until water cools.
Ready in 3 weeks.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water; add frozen strawberries. Stir until thawed; add bananas, pineapple and raisins.
Pour 1/2 in large bowl; chill until firm.
Add 1/2 cup Cool Whip.
Add remainder of mixture.
Chill, then add remainder of Cool Whip, then refrigerate until ready to eat.
Cut zucchini in chunks, boil for about 15 minutes. Drain well. Put zucchini, ham, scallions, salt and pepper in casserole dish and cover with sliced cheese.
Bake in 350° oven until cheese melts, approximately 20 minutes.
Whip eggs until light.
Add sugar gradually until thick.
Add remaining ingredients (use the 6 cup milk fill line on freezer canister).
Brown meat and butter.
Add tomato sauce and set aside to cool.
Cook noodles.
Mix meat, cream cheese, sour cream, onions and green peppers.
Put half of noodles in bottom of greased casserole.
Add cheese.
Mix and add balance of noodles.
Do not stir.
Add meat and melted butter on top.
Bake at 375° for about 1 hour.

recipes.t: Lowbush Cranberry Nut Bread With Simple Cranberry Sauce
d: Grate the rind and squeeze the juice from both oranges and put in a measuring cup.
Add additional liquid (juice or milk) to make a total of 2 cups.
Mix liquid, butter, sugar and eggs in a bowl. Add flour, salt and baking powder.
Stir briefly.
Fold in cranberries and walnuts.
Spoon into greased and floured loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Best when it is cooled and wrapped overnight before slicing.
Prepare rice according to package directions.
Saute onion, pepper and celery in butter for 4 to 5 minutes or until tender-crisp.
Combine rice, sauteed vegetables and remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Spoon mixture into greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Blend oats in blender until it becomes a fine powder.
Set aside.

Combine butter, sugars, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in flour, salt and oatmeal. Toss in chocolate chips, grated Hershey bar and pecans. Drop onto lightly buttered cookie sheet and bake 6 to 8 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine beef, salt, onion, oregano, rosemary and rice.
Shape the mixture into 1 1/2-inch balls.
Heat the oil in a heavy 12-inch skillet over moderately low heat for about 1 minute.
Cut the meatballs, uncovered, turning frequently until browned on all sides (about 5 minutes).
Add the tomato sauce and water; cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve with a green salad and crusty Italian bread.
Makes 4 servings.
Place the stew meat into stew pan and season.
Add carrots, onions and celery (the amount you desire).
Pour chicken soup and water over all the ingredients.
Brown ground beef well and drain off excess grease.
Put ground beef and remaining ingredients in crock-pot.
Stir well. Cover and cook on high for 1 hour, stirring until cheese is fully melted.
Serve immediately or turn to low for serving up to 6 hours later.
Serve with tortilla or corn chips.
This recipe may be doubled for 3 1/2, 4 or 5 quart models.
Sprinkle Jell-O over pineapple and juice. Heat until dissolved. Cool. Combine Cool Whip and milk. Mix thoroughly and add to Jell-O-pineapple mixture. Add nuts, if desired.
Melt over low heat sugar, honey, butter and peanut butter. Add in oats; stir.
Bake in greased pan in preheated oven at 325° for 1/2 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook frozen, chopped broccoli according to directions but do not overcook.
Drain in strainer.
Stir in cooked rice, shredded cheese, slightly beaten eggs, milk, margarine, onion, salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Combine egg, pie filling and salt.
Add corn syrup, pecans and vanilla.
Pour into a pie shell.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 325°.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes longer or until set.
Preheat the oven to 375°.
Lightly grease a 10-inch quiche dish or pie pan.
Set aside.
In a 10-inch skillet, melt butter over moderate heat.
Add leeks, potatoes, salt and pepper.
Cook for 1 minute.
Add the water; simmer, covered, for 12 minutes.
Mix sugar, oleo, eggs and raisins with mixer.
Add flour, oatmeal, soda, salt and vanilla.
Drop by spoonfuls on greased sheet. Bake at 300°.
Makes 5 or 6 dozen.
Unroll dough; place on greased or parchment-lined cookie sheet. Press dough into 12 x 8-inch rectangle.
Spread sauce on dough to within 2-inches of long sides and 1/2-inch of short sides.
Top with ham, cheese, peppers and Italian seasonings.
Fold long sides of dough over filling; pinch to seal.
Pinch short sides to seal. Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden.
Serves 6.
Mix unflavored gelatin with 1 cup cold water.
Stir lime gelatin into 1 cup of boiling water.
Add to unflavored gelatin mixture.
Stir in cold water.
Pour in oiled pan.
Chill several hours.
Let children use cookie cutters to cut favorite shapes. Remove shapes with spatula and eat!
Beat egg yolks.
Add sugar, flour and milk.
Cook in double boiler until creamy.
Stir constantly.
Remove from heat; add vanilla.
Place alternate layers of crackers, fruit and nuts.
Add the pudding.
Sprinkle coconut on top.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 4 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Spread over the pudding.
Bake in oven at 350° until brown.

recipes.t: Whole Wheat Not So Sweet Dough
d: In a mixing bowl, combine yeast, powdered milk, salt and cereal.
Add 2 cups warm water and stir until yeast and milk dissolve.
Add shortening, molasses, eggs, remaining 1 1/2 cups warm water and wheat flour.
Beat well.
Stir in 4 cups all-purpose flour.
Use remaining 1 1/2 cups flour to add dough while kneading until dough is smooth.
Shape dough into ball.
Cover with damp towel.
Allow to rest on lightly floured board for 15 minutes. Divide dough into equal 4 parts.
To bake just do what each recipe tells you to do.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Reconstitute the "butter" granules according to the directions on the package.
Cut each potato in half.
Scoop out the center, leaving about 1/4-inch of potato on the inside of each skin.
(Use leftover potato to make Shepherd's Pie.)
Cut skins into quarters.
Dab liquid butter substitute onto the white side of each potato skin.
Sprinkle with garlic powder and pepper, if desired.
Place prepared skins, skin side down, on a baking sheet.
Bake 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Turn skins over and bake another 5 minutes or until crisp.
Serve immediately.
Serves 12; 4 per serving.
Combine 1/4 cup butter, water and contents of stuffing mix seasoning packet in pan.
Stir and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add crumbs.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Stir mixture and spoon along both sides of a 2-quart baking dish.
Arrange broccoli down center.
Sprinkle with salt.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter and stir in flour.
Remove from heat, adding cream cheese.
Stir until smooth. Add milk and bouillon.
Return to heat and cook, stirring constantly.
Add green onions.
Spoon sauce over broccoli; sprinkle with cheese.
Cover and bake at 350° for 40 minutes, until broccoli is tender.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Yield:
6 servings.
Mix egg, milk, and salt.
Allow bread to soak.
Combine meat and vegetables.
Mix in bread.
Shape into loaf.
Put in pan and top with ketchup.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Chicken Cooked With Vermouth And Tomatoes(Poulet Chasseur)
d: Peel and chop the shallots; peel the onions but leave them whole.
Melt the Crisco; add the oil and beat together for a moment.
Place the chicken in one layer in the pan; brown the pieces on both sides.
After adding the onions to flavor them a little and the shallots after 2 to 3 minutes so that the shallots melt but do not color.
Remove the pan from heat; add vermouth and when warm, ignite with a match.
Tip the pan until the flames die down.
Simmer for 5 minutes to reduce the liquid in half.
Drain tomatoes; roughly chop.
Add the juice to the pan and mix well. Cover and leave for 1 hour without lifting the lid.
Cut shrimp into 3 to 4 pieces.
Mix with onion, bell pepper and celery.
Stir in remaining ingredients except oil and mix well. Cover bowl and refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours.
Prepare a 5-inch souffle dish with a 2-inch paper collar. Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a bowl over a pan of hot water until thick and creamy.
Remove from heat; whisk while cooling.
Put the water into a small bowl; sprinkle the gelatin over it and leave to "sponge."
Melt the chocolate.
In a bowl over hot water, melt the gelatin.
Add the gelatin to the egg mixture; mix well.
Add the melted chocolate and brandy; mix again.
Whip cream lightly and fold into the mixture.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold in carefully.
Pour the mixture into the souffle dish and refrigerate.
Decorate with whipped cream and chocolate.
In small saucepan, over low heat, combine margarine and spices.
Stir until margarine is melted.
Pour spice mixture over popcorn in a large bowl; mix thoroughly to coat.
Makes 4 (2-cup) servings.
Cook potatoes and onion with oil in hot saucepan.
Add chicken, chicken broth, parsley and salt.
Heat to boiling. Lower heat; cover and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in Pet milk and simmer.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine squash, green onion, green pepper and celery in large bowl.
Toss lightly.
Combine wine vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper, canola oil, cider vinegar and garlic.
Mix well and spoon over vegetables.
Chill about 12 hours, stirring occasionally.
Drain and serve.
Serves 10 to 12.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Beat white sugar into egg whites.
Crumble Ritz crackers and add to egg whites.
Add walnuts to mixture.
Pat into pie tin.
Bake 25 minutes at 325° to 350°. Cool.
Add Cool Whip and spread over cooked pie.
(Can add 1/2 teaspoon coffee to Cool Whip for mocha flavor.)
Mix together tomatoes, onion, garlic, basil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Mix well and refrigerate (covered) at least overnight.
Brown ground beef. Drain.

In a large Dutch oven, put stewed tomatoes, tomato paste, beans, ground beef and macaroni. Add 1 to 2 cans of water to these ingredients to obtain your desired consistency. Add pepper and chili powder to your taste.
Simmer on low heat, stirring occasionally, for 2 hours.
Grease an oblong baking dish.
Mix together in baking dish the apples, sugar and cinnamon.
In a large bowl, mix the remaining ingredients.
Pour over apples in greased baking dish and bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until nicely browned.
Mix ground beef, cracker crumbs, salt, pepper, milk and onion. Form in loaf pan and refrigerate overnight.
Slice and fry until brown
on both sides.
Remove from pan.
Put slices in a 9 x 13-inch
pan
and
pour 2 cans of mushroom soup and water. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix all juices and water together.
Just before serving, add chilled sodas.
Garnish with fruit.
May add 1/2 bottle vodka. Makes about 2 gallons.
Heat honey to boiling and add peanut butter.
Pour over cereal and press into buttered 8 x 8-inch square pan.
Melt jelly on stove and pour over top.
Cover and chill until firm.
Cut in 2-inch squares.
Kids love em!
Slice 1/2-inch slivers across the raw bacon and fry until crisp.
Set aside.
Add chopped onion to 2 tablespoons bacon fat until golden.
Blend in flour and tomato juice.
Cook until thickened.
Add Lea & Perrins sauce, sauerkraut, bacon bits and pepper.
Put into a 2-quart casserole.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Add sugar gradually to beaten eggs, beating well after each addition.
When mixture becomes very stiff, add remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Pour into 1 gallon freezer and freeze.
Combine mayonnaise and salsa.
Spread on bread.
Layer ingredients in order listed.
In a large skillet, brown ground beef; drain.
Stir in the taco seasoning, kidney beans and salsa; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Keep eggs and cream separate.
To the egg mixture, gradually add a pound of powdered sugar.
Beat until smooth.
Whip in the cream.
Slice 3 large bananas and 1 pineapple; cut into cubes. Beat these into cream and chill.
When cold, serve them in pretty glasses.
Put cornstarch, salt, garlic and sherry in bowl; stir well. Add chicken that has been cut in 3/4-inch pieces (bite size) and mix well.
Let sit for 1/2 to 1 hour.
Stir again to make sure all pieces are separated.
Add 1/4 cup of oil to skillet and when hot, add chicken stirring quickly about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add vegetables and sprinkle liberally with soy sauce.
Continue stirring about 3 to 5 minutes.
Vegetables should be medium crisp, not mushy. Serve with a bowl of fluffy white rice.
Sift together flour, baking powder, salt and brown sugar.
Cut in shortening and butter or margarine.
Reserve 1 cup of this mixture for topping.
Combine coffee, milk and soda.
Add to remaining flour mixture, mixing thoroughly.
Add beaten eggs. Spoon into prepared muffin pans, filling half full.
Add cinnamon to topping mixture; sprinkle on top of batter.
Bake at 375° for about 25 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen muffins.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Peel potatoes; cook with garlic in boiling salted water.
Meanwhile, saute mushrooms in 2 tablespoons butter until tender.
Drain potatoes; discard garlic.
Whip potatoes with 1/4 cup butter, cream, egg yolks, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and dash of pepper.
Stir in mushrooms and parsley.
Spoon into casserole.
Melt rest of butter; toss with bread crumbs.
Sprinkle over potatoes.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serves 8.
Cook carrots until tender; drain.
Saute onion in 3 tablespoons margarine until soft.
Stir in soup, salt, pepper, cheese and carrots.
Spoon into a 2-quart greased casserole dish. Toss bread stuffing mix with 1/2 cup melted butter.
Spoon on top of carrot mixture.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix yeast with warm milk, then add salt, sugar, oil and eggs. Mix real good.
Lastly, add flour.
If dough is too soft, add more flour.
If too stiff, add a little water.
Let rise to top of bowl; take spoon and work it down.
Put on floured waxed paper.
Get a small amount and shape into rolls.
Put in greased pan.
Let rise again.
Bake in a 375° oven until brown.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine rice, milk, eggs, brown sugar and butter in casserole.
Place casserole in baking pan.
Fill pan with enough water to go 1/2 way up side of casserole.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Stir in raisins and vanilla.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Return to oven.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream.

Blend butter and cream cheese. Add sugar; cream thoroughly. Add egg, lemon juice and rind; blend well. Measure flour and baking powder together, mixing well. Add to cream cheese mixture. Mix thoroughly. Chill dough 30 minutes. Heat oven to 350°. Force dough through cookie press onto an ungreased baking sheet. Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until slightly browned. Makes about 5 dozen 2-inch cookies.
Boil together brown sugar, butter and water until sugar dissolves (medium heat).
Mix in Corn Chex, Rice Chex, Wheat Chex and pecans.
Spray cookie sheet with Pam and bake for 15 minutes at 300°.
Take out of oven; stir and bake for 10 more minutes.
Total baking time:
25 minutes.
Combine raspberries, wine, sour cream, sherbet and milk in blender container.
Process until well blended.
Strain, if desired.
Pour into small bowls.
Float lime slices on top.
Add several drops of fresh lime juice.
Serves 8.
Combine first 4 ingredients in large bowl, mix well.
Add eggs, jalapenos, onion, oil and corn; mix well.
Gently fold in cheese.
Line cupcake pan with paper liners.
Fill 1/2 full with batter.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Yields approximately 2 dozen.
Cream together potatoes, sugar, salt, eggs, butter, milk and vanilla.
Turn into lightly greased casserole dish.
Mix together brown sugar, melted butter, flour and pecans.
Spread over potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Then dissolve red hot candies in 1/2 cup boiling water and add to jello mixture.
Add remaining ingredients; stir well.
Refrigerate until set.
Add beaten egg to vegetables.
Mix in flour to coat vegetables.
Place vegetables and flour in strainer and shake out extra flour.
Flour should only coat vegetables.
Fry on medium heat until the vegetables are tender.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Sift flour once and measure.
Sift sugar 5 or 6 times.
Put 1/2 of the sugar in the flour and sift 15 times.
Add salt to egg whites and beat until foamy, then add cream of tartar and beat until stiff.
Fold in sugar and then fold in sugar and flour mixture.
Add flavoring.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
(I use pieces of wax paper for the sifting process.)
Soak apples overnight in the pineapple juice.
Combine cream cheese, brown sugar, vanilla and Heath Bits to make a stiff dip.
Combine flour, oats, soda, cinnamon and salt; set aside. Cream margarine and gradually add sugars.
Beat until light.
Add egg and vanilla.
Mix well.
Alternate additions of dry ingredients and pumpkin.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Use ice cream scoop or 1/4 cup measure to drop dough onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes (until firm).
One cup of raisins can be substituted.
Saute onion and add garlic. Remove to serving platter.
Saute chicken until golden on both sides.
Replace with onion mix.
Add broth, seasonings and peanut butter.
Whisk until hot and smooth. Add chicken, cover tightly and simmer 30 minutes, turning chicken once.
Serve with Spatzle (chunky little German noodles).
Serves 4.
Mix sausage, bread, eggs, milk, soup and cheese.
Refrigerate overnight and bake for 40 to 50 minutes at 350° the next morning (until bubbly).
Line bottom of an 8-inch square pan with graham cracker squares, cutting to fit as necessary.
In a 2-quart microwave-safe bowl, stir together sugar and corn syrup.
Microwave at High (100%), stirring every 2 minutes, until mixture boils; boil 3 minutes.
Stir in chocolate chips, peanut butter and peanuts. Pour over crackers; spread carefully.
Cover and refrigerate until firm.
Cut into 2-inch squares.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Makes 16 servings.
Roll pork chops in flour; sprinkle with salt and pepper. Brown pork chops and place in a glass baking dish.
Sprinkle with onions and rice.
Combine cream of chicken soup and water.
Pour over pork chops and rice.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until rice is done.
(Ovens may vary.)
Cook, rinse in cold water and drain macaroni.
When macaroni has cooled, toss with all other ingredients.
Add salt and pepper. Stir in 3/4 bottle of 16 oz. size Wishbone Italian dressing. Chill well.
Add remaining bottle of dressing and stir before serving.
Fry chicken using desired coating, do not overcook.
Season with salt, pepper, parsley and garlic powder, drain remaining oil from pan.
Add wine, broth, mushrooms and artichoke hearts. Sprinkle chicken with grated cheese and simmer, covered, for 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve with noodles.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook noodles in water with 1 teaspoon corn oil until soft. In a bowl, mix tomato soup, Parmesan, garlic and oregano.
When noodles are cooked, drain and add to soup mixture.
Layer noodles, cooked sausage, pepperoni and noodles again on top.
Bake in a large bowl in a 350° oven for approximately 20 to 25 minutes.
Blend softened cream cheese, mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce.
Add olives, parsley and onion.
Shape into a log on waxed paper.
Chill.
Roll in dried beef.
Grease baking dish or casserole dish.
Place a single layer of bread slices on bottom of dish (crusts may be removed, if desired).
Add a layer of meat slices (any meat may be used, preferably not too much fat).
Add a layer of Cheddar cheese, grated or sliced.
Combine the remaining ingredients and pour over casserole.
Adjust the quantity of eggs and milk so they are sufficient to fill dish to approximately 3/4 level.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Cover chicken with water.
Add salt and celery stalks; cook until chicken is tender.
Season bread with sage, thyme and pepper.
Layer chicken, cut into small pieces, with the seasoned bread cubes in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch casserole.
Dot with butter; pour broth from chicken (strained and celery removed) over the casserole.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Peel and cut potatoes into bite size pieces.
Cook until tender and drain.
Cook sausage with onion, green pepper and mushrooms until meat is no longer pink.
Drain and return to pan. Add tomato sauce.
Add cooked potato chunks and beans.
Add water to desired consistency.
Add seasonings to taste.
Simmer until ready to serve.
Makes about 3 quarts.

recipes.t: Ooey Gooey Bars Or Cheese Bars
d: Mix in oblong cake pan the first 3 ingredients and let set for about 5 minutes.
Pat thin on bottom of pan.
Mix in mixing bowl the next 3 ingredients.
Alternate:
sprinkle chips on top of cake mix batter then pour cream cheese mixture over them.
Sprinkle this top with chopped pecans.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Cool and then cut into squares.
May use a can of coconut on top of chocolate chips.
Grease pan with butter.
Better with black walnuts.
Cook and stir beef and onion.
Drain. Stir in catsup, mustard and soup.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat. Simmer 5 minutes. Heat oven to 375°.
Grease Bundt pan.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Beat 30 seconds.
Spread 2 cups batter in bottom and 2-inches up side and center of pan.
Spoon beef onto center of batter.
Drop remaining batter by spoonfuls 1/2-inch apart.
Bake until light brown and firm, about 25 minutes.
Invert on heatproof plate.
Bake cake as directed per box.
While cake is warm, poke holes in cake with a wooden spoon handle.
Mix Jell-O with boiling water and pour over cooled cake.
Cool in refrigerator until completely cooled.
Mix pudding with cold milk; add lemon extract and food coloring.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Spread pudding mix over cooled cake.
Keep cake refrigerated.
Sprinkle
gelatin over water in a small saucepan.
Stir over low
heat
until
completely dissolved.
Blend in 2/3 cup whipping cream
and
bring
mixture to a boil.
Put in blender and add chocolate chips.
Process until chips are melted.
Add 1/3 cup whipping
cream, eggs and vanilla, mixing well.
Pour into a bowl and chill until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Combine egg yolks, milk and oil.
Mix into dry ingredients.
Fold in egg whites.
Bake in your favorite waffle iron.
Pound meat with meat mallet to tenderize.
Place in plastic bag.
Combine picante sauce, oil, lemon juice, pepper and garlic powder.
Pour into bag and fasten securely.
Refrigerate 3 to 24 hours, turning several times.
Drain meat, reserving marinade. Place meat on grill over hot coals or on rack of broiler pan. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes on each side or until well done, basting frequently with reserved marinade.
Remove from grill; slice across grain into thin strips.
Place meat on heated tortillas. Top with chunky guacamole and additional picante sauce or whatever you like.
Roll up.
Makes 6 servings.
Prepare pork chops, trimming excess fat.
Dredge chops in Tarragon Flour.
Brown in oil on both sides using medium-high heat.
Pare and slice potatoes thin.
Slice onions thin.
Add water to skillet with browned pork chops; stir well.
Cover and cook on medium-high for 10 minutes.
Add potato slices; cover. Add onion slices, ringed.
Cover and cook, adding water to keep gravy.
Add sliced apples and sugar when almost done.
Total cooking time is approximately 40 minutes.
Combine vinegar with milk and set aside.
Cream butter, Crisco and sugar, then add milk alternately with dry ingredients.
Add almonds.
Drop with teaspoon on cookie sheet and flatten with fork.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Layer items in casserole dish; top with grated cheese, then bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Peel, cube and boil the potatoes.
Peel and dice the onions. Cube and fry the uncooked sausage (if chosen).
Melt the margarine in a pan.
Lightly saute the onions, then brown potatoes.
Mix the eggs and milk, then add salt, sweet paprika, ground nutmeg and pepper (to taste), chives and the precooked sausage (if chosen).
Brown chicken on both sides in oil over medium heat.
Remove chicken and add garlic in the skillet.
Saute for a minute. Combine broth, soy sauce, brown sugar and crushed red pepper. Place chicken in skillet and pour sauce over it.
Cover tightly and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes.
Remove chicken to serving platter.
Stir in cornstarch dissolved in water.
Stir and cook until thickened.
Pour over chicken.
Steam broccoli; set aside (chop when cool).
Saute onions, bell pepper and seafood in margarine.
Add Cheez Whiz; stir while adding cream of mushroom soup.
Add chopped broccoli and rice. Stir well.
Spread into baking pan; sprinkle bread crumbs over top.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°.
Spray cookie sheet with cooking spray. In a large bowl and using electric beater, cream margarine.
Add sugars and beat until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg and vanilla.

recipes.t: Green Chili And Cheese Brunch Casserole
d: Place buttered muffin halves face down in 13 x 9 x 2-inch casserole dish.
Brown and crumble sausage.
Mix in chiles. Layer sausage mix, alternating with cheese, over muffins.
Top with onion.
Combine beaten eggs with sour cream and pour over casserole.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Next day, remove and let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Bake uncovered at 350°, approximately 35 to 40 minutes, and serve warm.
Melt chocolate chips and caramel sauce together.
Add milk. Keep warm.
Serve with strawberries, pineapple, sliced apples, etc.
Mix ginger, onion and Karo and pour over beans in a 2 quart ovenproof casserole.
Stir to mix well.
Arrange bacon slices over top of beans.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour or until bubbly.
During baking, baste bacon slices often with juices in casserole to glaze.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown and drain ground beef.
Stir in Sloppy Joe sauce.
Mix well.
Transfer to 13x9 inch pan.
Sprinkle with cheese.
In bowl combine biscuit mix, eggs and milk until well blended.
Pour over cheese.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake uncovered at 400° for 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Cook macaroni as directed on package.
Rinse and drain.
Melt butter.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper, mustard and paprika. When well blended, add milk slowly, stirring constantly over low heat until mixture thickens and boils.
Add cheese and Worcestershire sauce until cheese has melted.
Add drained macaroni and pour mixture into greased 2-quart baking dish. Bake in moderately hot oven at 400°.
Place noodles in flat casserole dish.
Place cut up chicken on top.
Salt and pepper chicken.
Combine soup and water; pour over chicken.
Sprinkle onion soup mix on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/3 hours.
Heat milk (with cinnamon stick if desired) until bubbles begin to appear around edge of pan.
Stir sugar and salt into eggs.
Add hot milk slowly to egg mixture, stirring constantly.
Return to double boiler and cook over low heat, while stirring, until mixture coats spoon.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla. Sprinkle with nutmeg, if desired. Chill and serve from pitcher.
Saute onions and celery in Pam sprayed frypan until onion turns clear.
Add tomatoes and flour.
Stir until thickened.
Then add this to ingredients and combine it all together.
Place in Pam sprayed baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Heat pineapple and juice with sugar and water.
Stir in gelatin to dissolve.
Chill until partially congealed.
Fold in cream cheese, then nuts, then Cool Whip.
Refrigerate until well set.
Serve.

In a Dutch oven, combine the water and bouillon. Add the cream cheese; cook and stir until cheese is melted. Stir in the remaining ingredients. Simmer, uncovered, for 18 to 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Brown hamburger; drain and add all ingredients.
Cook in crock-pot until all cheese has melted, then dip with your favorite chips.

Spray a large casserole dish with cooking oil spray. Arrange a layer of sliced onions on bottom. Add a layer of potatoes on top of onions. Sprinkle potatoes & onions with salt & pepper and flour. Cut up a pat of butter to place on top of potatoes. Arrange ham slices on top of potato layer. Repeat, ending with a layer of onions. Pour milk over dish until the ingredients are almost covered. Cover and bake at 350 degrees about 1 hour or until potatoes are tender.
Mix flour, baking powder and spices.
In a large bowl, beat oleo and sugar with electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in egg. Gradually add flour mixture, beating until blended. Divide dough in thirds.
Shape each into a ball. Flatten to 1-inch thick rounds. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate 1 hour or until firm enough to roll.
Fry hamburger, adding the next 6 ingredients after it is browned.
Mix well and set aside.
Combine and set aside the cottage cheese, sour cream and chopped chilies.
Grate cheese. Crush slightly the Doritos.
Mix cranberries with sugar.
Let set overnight.
Mix all ingredients together.
Thaw pastry according to package instructions (approximately 20 minutes).
While pastry thaws, soak the tomatoes in boiling water to soften.
Cook the sausage, then cut into 1/2-inch slices. Cut these slices crosswise.
Quarter the tomatoes.
Dissolve yeast in warm water and let stand 5 minutes.
Place flours and salt in food processor bowl.
Turn on machine and slowly add yeast-water mixture.
Keep machine on until dough ball forms.
Place ball in greased bowl.
Cover with towel and let rise 1 hour in warm place.
Punch dough down and turn out on lightly floured surface.
Roll dough into a log about 1 1/2-inches thick. Cut into 12 pieces vertically.
Roll each piece into 6-inch circle.
In heavy skillet over high heat, cook one Chapati at a time, 1 to 2 minutes, until bubbles form.
With tongs, turn to other side, 1 to 2 minutes until golden brown.
Saute chicken breasts in butter or oil until done.
Remove meat from bones, chop and set aside.
Chop together the cheese and onion in a food processor and mix with the chicken.
Fry the corn tortillas until soft and pliable.
Stuff tortillas with chicken mixture and roll them up.
Lay enchiladas in baking dish.
Make a roux with the butter and flour.
Add the chicken broth.
Boil until thickened.
Add the sour cream and chilies.
Heat until warm.
Pour sauce over enchiladas.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serve with picante, tomatillo or other sauce of your choice.
Put marshmallow cream in a bowl; set aside.
Mix sugar, water and salt; bring to a boil.
Boil hard for 2 1/2 minutes.
Pour 1/3 syrup into cream and beat well.
Pour 1/3 and beat well.
Add remaining 1/3 and beat.
Add vanilla and chopped nuts.
Beat about 3 minutes.
Put on wax paper by spoonfuls immediately, as it gets hard fast.
Saute mushrooms and onion in butter with juice of 1 lemon. Saute cauliflower flowerets in butter with garlic, basil, salt and pepper to taste.
Mix all ingredients, put in greased casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Lightly brown ground beef.
Add onion; cook until tender, but not brown.
Add corn, soups, sour cream, pimento, salt and pepper. Mix well.
Stir in noodles, cooked and drained.
Pour into 2-quart casserole.
Mix bread crumbs and 3 tablespoons melted butter; sprinkle over top.
Bake in moderate oven, 350°, for 30 minutes until hot.

In teapot, pour boiling water over tea bags. Cover and brew 5 minutes. Remove tea bags. Stir in sugar and lemon juice. Chill. For every four servings, in 5 cup blender, combine 3/4 cup tea mixture, 1 1/2 cups strawberries, 1/3 cantaloupe and 2 1/2 cups crushed ice. Process at high speed until well blended. Garnish with fresh fruit or mint leaves.
Heat oven to 375°.
Brown meat and onions; drain.
Stir in taco seasoning mix, beans and tomato sauce.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Unroll dough into 4 long rectangles.
Place in ungreased 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan; press over bottom and 1-inch up sides to form crust.
Brush dough with oil; sprinkle with cornmeal.
Spoon hot meat mixture over crust.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Return to oven until cheese is melted.
Cut into squares.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes and taco sauce.
Yields 8 servings.
Fry seasoned hamburger and onions.
Drain fat.
Add 1 package chili seasoning mix.
Stir in well.
Melt chips in a heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and quickly stir in noodles, nuts and vanilla so they are evenly coated.
Dip out by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper. Chill and refrigerate.
Melt margarine in a heavy saucepan.
Add brown sugar, white sugar and milk.
Let come to a full boil.
Boil 2 minutes 45 seconds.
Do not stir while cooking.
Add vanilla.
Cool.
Beat. Add coconut and a few pecans.

recipes.t: French Green Beans With Water Chestnuts
d: Cook beans according to directions on package.
Add drained water chestnuts and heat thoroughly.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Yields 6 servings.
Saute onion and garlic in 1/2 pound butter until softened. Add livers and saute until lightly browned but still rare.
Blend in batches (1/3 at a time).
Add remaining 1/2 pound melted butter, brandy, whipping cream, salt and pepper.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Add pureed truffle, if desired.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart terrine.
Chill. Serve with crackers or French bread.
In a 2-quart dish, saute butter, onion, parsley and celery on High for 4 minutes in microwave.
Stir in cream cheese.
Microwave on High 1 minute, if cheese is not softened.
Add garlic powder, Tabasco sauce, salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix well.
Fold crabmeat in gently.
Microwave on High 4 minutes.
Serve with Melba rounds.
In Dutch oven, cook mushrooms and onion in margarine 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, cook 2 minutes more.
Gradually add 5 cups water, cook, stirring, until mixture thickens and boils.
Add remaining ingredients except chives.
Cover, simmer 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Garnish with chopped chives.
Makes 8 servings, about 50 calories each.
Brown hamburger.
Drain.
Add chopped onions, carrots, celery, potatoes and a little water.
Cook until vegetables are done.
In pan, combine Cheddar cheese soup, potato soup and milk.
Add hamburger.
Cook until warm.
Cream together the shortening, sugars, eggs and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture. Mixture will be hard to mix with mixer. Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet and bake at 325° until done.
Cut
squash in half lengthwise and remove seeds.
Wash, core and dice apples.
Combine with syrup and margarine.
Fill squash with this mixture. Brush with margarine.
Place inside 14-inch Dutch
oven
and
pour
in a 1/4 cup of boiling water. Bake 1 hour at medium heat.
Make
sure
water level is maintained. Replenish water as necessary.
Pull greens apart into bite size pieces and pile in a large bowl.
Add onion to greens.
Add oil and mix thoroughly.
Add wine vinegar and mix again.
Add salt and pepper.
Serve with spaghetti and Italian bread.
Preheat oven to 350°. Combine caramels and 1/3 cup evaporated milk in top of double boiler.
Heat, stirring constantly until caramels are melted completely.
Remove from heat and set aside. Combine cake mix, 1/3 cup evaporated milk and butter.
Beat until mixture holds together.
Stir in nuts.
Press half of cake mixture into a well-greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 6 minutes.
Sprinkle chocolate chips over crust and cover evenly with caramel mixture. Drop by teaspoon the remaining cake mix evenly over top.
Bake 17 to 20 minutes.
Cool and then chill 30 minutes before cutting into small squares.
Stretch dough to fit pizza pan.
Make indentations with fingers in the dough.
Spread olive oil all over dough.
Sprinkle with chopped garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Bake in a 400° oven for about 30 minutes.
Five minutes before pizza is done, sprinkle the Mozzarella cheese on top.
Return to the oven and finish cooking.
Cook rice until tender. Brown the beef lightly in butter in a large skillet. Add salt, pepper, onion and green pepper.
Drain rice and stir in meat mixture. Add sugar, ketchup and tomato sauce.
Mix well. Simmer 5 minutes.
Ready for serving.
Brown steak in a pan.
Drain.
Remove any grease from pan. Put steak pieces back in pan.
Add bell pepper strips and onion slices.
Mix tomato-rice soup with 1 can water and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over steak, peppers and onions.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Stir and cook over low heat or simmer for 30 minutes.
Combine cheese and buttermilk to a paste; season with Tabasco sauce and stir in Blue cheese.
Refrigerate.
Pound into steak a mixture of self-rising flour, salt and garlic salt.
Fry steak quickly on all sides in 3 tablespoons hot oil.
Remove; cook all of the steak.
Add more oil if needed.
When all of the steak is cooked, remove from pan.
Add 3 tablespoons self-rising flour; brown well, adding oil if needed.
Mix water or milk and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour into browned flour; cook until a thin gravy.
Add more milk if needed.
Return browned steak to gravy; simmer for 30 minutes.
May add chopped onion to meat before the simmering starts.
Serve with rice, green beans and garden salad.
Cook potatoes.
Make mashed or whipped potatoes.
While potatoes are cooking, brown the meat.
Grease a large casserole dish.
Drain meat of any excess grease.
Put meat in a casserole dish.
Next add corn.
Last, top with mashed potatoes and a few pats of butter.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Drain cherries and pineapple, reserving juice.
Add enough water to juice to make 2 cups liquid.
Bring liquid to boil.
Add gelatin, stirring to dissolve.
Stir in cola.
Chill until lightly thickened.
Combine celery, pecans, cherries, pineapple and coconut, if desired.
Beat cream cheese until smooth and fluffy; add to fruit
mixture, stirring well.
Fold cream cheese mixture into gelatin; pour into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Chill until firm.
Cut into squares to serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine the oat bran, baking powder, baking soda and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Stir to mix well.
Add the brown sugar and stir to mix well.
Use the back of a wooden spoon to press out any lumps in the brown sugar.
Put the yogurt, apple juice, egg and oil in a small bowl and stir to mix well.
Add the yogurt mixture to the oat-bran mixture and stir to mix well. Fold in the apple and if desired, the nut or dried fruit.
Coat the bottoms only of muffin cups with nonstick cooking spray and fill 3/4 full with batter.
Bake for about 16 minutes or just until a wooden toothpick inserted into the center of the muffin comes out clean.
Remove the muffin tin from the oven and allow it to sit for 5 minutes before removing the muffins.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Refrigerate or freeze any leftovers not eaten within 24 hours.
Place water, spices and sugar in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high flame; reduce flame.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Add juices. Heat through.
Makes 4 servings.
Wipe chicken dry.
Make paste of Italian dressing, flour, salt, lemon juice and butter.
Brush on chicken.
Refrigerate several hours or overnight.
In a saucepan, melt peanut butter and butter.
In a large bowl, combine powdered sugar and cereal.
Pour peanut butter mixture over cereal mixture.
Blend together with hands.
Form into 1/2-inch balls.
Chill until firm.
In separate double boilers, melt butterscotch and chocolate pieces.
Dip candy balls in butterscotch and place on wax paper.
Dip candy balls in chocolate and place on wax paper.
Unroll crescent rolls; pinch seams of 4 rolls together to form a rectangle.
Place cream cheese block on dough; sprinkle with basil.
Wrap dough around cream cheese; pinch seams to seal. Place block wrapped with dough on baking sheet with seam down. Brush top of dough with egg; bake 20 minutes or until brown in 400° oven.
Serve with crackers.
Melt milk, candies and butter together.
Add to powdered sugar.
Allow to cool.
Spread on sugar cookies.
Enjoy!
Saute bacon in medium-size saucepan until lightly browned.
Add celery and onion.
Saute until onion is transparent.
Drain off all excess fat.
Place vegetables and bacon in large pot.
Add tomato, tomato sauce, water, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in cornstarch mixture.
Cook, while stirring, until bubbly and thickened.
Add lettuce.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes. Crackers can be added to increase crunchiness.
Cook okra in 2 tablespoons shortening until tender and no longer slimy.
Brown flour in 4 tablespoons shortening to make a roux.
Add all ingredients to the crock-pot and let simmer about 6 to 8 hours.
Serve over rice.
Serves 8. One cup yields about 150 calories.

Preheat oven to 350°. Combine first 6 ingredients in a bowl; spoon into a 1-quart casserole. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly. Serve with toasted bread. Yield: 2 cups.

recipes.t: Lemon Or Orange Chocolate Chip Cookies
d: Mix flour, soda and coriander with wire whisk and set aside. Preheat oven to 300°.
In another bowl, cream butter and sugar with electric mixer at medium speed to form a grainy paste.
Add eggs and extract and beat.
Scrape sides of bowl.
With mixer at low speed, combine with flour mixture.
When all ingredients are blended, add chocolate chips.
Do not overmix.
Drop dough by teaspoons onto greased baking sheet 1 1/2 inches apart; they'll spread.
Bake 15 minutes on center rack of oven.
Do not brown! Immediately transfer to cooling racks.
Yields 4 dozen.

Mix crumbs and butter together. Put 1/2 in bottom of pan. Mix Dream Whip as directed. Beat sugar and cream cheese together. Mix Dream Whip with cream cheese mixture. Put half on crumbs. Put strawberries on top of cream cheese mixture. Put strawberry glaze on strawberries. Then put other half of cream cheese on strawberry glaze. Add other half of crumbs.
Combine water, tomato sauce and spaghetti sauce mix in a small saucepan.
Simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes.
Mix 1 cup Mozzarella, Ricotta, Parmesan, eggs, salt and pepper.
Stuff cheese mixture into cooked shells, using about 1/4 cup for each shell.
Mix flour, milk, salt, pepper and Accent together.
Knead into meat thoroughly.
Sprinkle excess flour on dough board.
Knead. Roll out 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick.
Cut into various size pieces. Brown in hot grease.
Remove and make gravy.
Drop meat back into gravy.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450°.
In mixing bowl, sift together dry ingredients.
Cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse meal.
In another bowl, combine egg and milk.
Beat lightly with fork.
Add to flour mixture all at once, stirring enough to make soft dough.
Turn out onto floured board, knead 15 times.
Roll out to 1-inch thickness.
Cut into 2-inch rounds.
Place on ungreased baking sheet, about 1-inch apart.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes or until golden.
Makes 16 biscuits.
Melt fat in a large skillet.
Pare and slice the potatoes. Spread 1/2 of potatoes in the skillet.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Arrange 1/2 the Spam strips over the potatoes in spoke fashion.
Add another layer of potatoes, the onion, green pepper and Spam strips.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Beat the eggs with a small amount of milk.
Pour the eggs over all.
Cover and cook until the eggs are set, about 10 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Cover and cook until the cheese melts. Serves 4 to 6.
Put dates and raisins in 1/2 cup boiling water and let stand awhile, then drain.
Cream the butter and Sucaryl; add egg.
Sift flour, baking soda, spices and salt.
Add to the mixture.
Add vanilla, fruit and oatmeal.
Chill dough.
Drop by teaspoonful on greased baking sheet.
Bake 12 minutes in a 350° oven until slightly browned.
Cook lasagna as package directs and drain. Preheat oven to 350°.
In saucepan over medium heat, melt butter and saute mushrooms and onion 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add cream cheese and bouillon.
Cook until cheese is smooth and bouillon is dissolved, stirring often.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream, eggs, nutmeg and chicken, mixing well.
In a 13 x 9-inch baking dish, layer 1/2 of noodles, chicken mixture and shredded cheese.
Repeat layering.
Cover and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 5 to 10 more.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Place fish in sprayed 9 x 13 baking dish.
Combine juice and oil and drizzle over fish.
Top with slices of tomato and onion. Combine all spices and sprinkle on top of tomatoes and onion. Bake uncovered 10-15 minutes or until fish flakes with fork. Serves 2.
Grate zucchini; sprinkle salt over zucchini and let sit for 1/2 hour, then squeeze out all liquid very well.
Saute lightly onion in butter or margarine.
Add flour, pepper and milk; cook with sauteed onions until thickened.
Separate eggs.
Combine zucchini, milk and onion mixture with shredded cheese, corn, egg yolks and salt to taste.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks and add to mixture, folding in last.
Pour mixture into a 2-quart greased casserole. Bake for approximately 1 hour at 350° until puffy and brown.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add cold water, diced orange sections and grated carrots.
Mix well.
Pour mixture into mold and chill until set.
Garnish with chopped nuts.
Cut up rabbit; remove fat, wash and dry.
Mix flour, salt and pepper and roll rabbit in mixture.
Brown in Crisco.
Place in baking dish.
Cover with water and scrapings from browning pan. Add last 3 ingredients.
Bake at 400° for 1/2 hour; turn down to 375° for 1 1/2 hours or until done.
Line a cookie sheet with foil.
Top with crackers, side by side, in a single layer.
In microwave, melt oleo.
Stir in sugar and cook 1 minute in microwave on High.
Stir and drizzle over crackers.
Sprinkle with chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool on cookie sheet on rack.
Store in an airtight container 1 week or freezer for 1 month.
Makes 36.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in pineapple with juice and sugar.
Let cool.
(You may put into freezer for a short time until it starts to gel.)
Fold in remaining ingredients. Spoon into a 9-inch square pan.
Refrigerate until firm.
Pre-heat oven to 350°.
Get 13 X 9 cake pan and fill the bottom with pie filling.
Then put the yellow cake mix on top of the pie filling.
Melt the butter and pour it on top of the cake mix.
Spread evenly.
Put in oven and bake for 20 to 30 minutes.
Toss vegetables together with nuts and chicken.
Add croutons and dressing of choice and serve.
Steep tea in water for 10 minutes.
Remove tea bags and mix tea with remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Ginger ale may be chilled and added just before serving if more carbonated punch is desired.
Serves 15.
Cream margarine, powdered sugar, vanilla, Pet evaporated milk and flour.
Mix well.
Chill.
Roll out on floured surface to 12-inch rectangle.
Cut into 3 x 1 1/2-inch rectangles.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 325° for 12 to 16 minutes. When cookies are cool, mix caramels and Pet milk.
Heat until caramels melt.
Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat; stir in oleo, powdered sugar and pecans.
Put 1 teaspoon this filling on each cookie.
Very good!
In 9 x 13-inch pan, combine crushed vanilla wafers and melted butter.
Mix and press into bottom of pan.
Top with vanilla pudding and slices bananas evenly over pudding.
Cover with Cool Whip.
Drizzle hot fudge over top.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts. Refrigerate.
Mix together the first 6 ingredients.
Refrigerate until firm. Take a handful of the rice mixture and place a cheese chunk in the middle.
Roll into a ball and roll again in the bread crumbs. Fry the rice ball as you would a meat ball.
Can add tomato sauce to the top, if desired.
In a medium saucepan, melt butter.
Blend in flour, salt and a dash of pepper.
Gradually stir in milk and cheese.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and smooth.
Stir in sour cream and macaroni.
Heat through (do not boil).
Serve.
Combine
cornbread,
flour,
baking powder, salt, sugar and milk;
make
a
well
in center of mixture.
Combine eggs, water and
oil;
add
to dry ingredients, stirring until moistened. Fold in corn and remaining ingredients.
Spoon mixture into a greased
x
x
2-inch
pan.
Bake at 425° for 35 minutes or until
a knife inserted in center comes out clean. Yields 15 servings.
About 45 minutes before serving or early in day:
Preheat oven to 425°.
In large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and baking soda.
With pastry blender or two knives used scissor-fashion, cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix together garlic, salt, pepper and nutmeg; set aside.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes.
Add 3 tablespoons flour to shredded cheese.
Layer in greased pan: hot dogs, cheese, onion, milk, oleo and dry ingredients; then potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Pour heavy cream on top after baking.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Beat all together.
Pour into omelette pan that has been greased with butter.
Cook on low to medium until egg is cooked through and cheese is melted through.
Salt and pepper to taste. Serve with toast and choice of jam.
Heat soup, gelatin and salt to boiling, then take off heat. Add mayonnaise and cream cheese; mix all together with whisk. Stir in celery, onion and shrimp.
Mold and chill until firm. Unmold and serve with crackers.
Prepare fettucini by directions; drain.
While noodles are cooking, cook and stir garlic in oil on low heat in skillet until golden brown.
Stir in cheese spread, milk and Parmesan cheese. Stir until melted thoroughly and add fettucini noodles.
Stir lightly.
Serve immediately.
Place ground coffee (get coffee ground for type coffee maker used) in basket with filter.
Add cocoa and salt.
If coffee maker is not automatic, do not perk longer than 10 minutes.
This makes a strong coffee, so if you desire less strong coffee, cut down on amount of ground coffee.
Heat water until boiling.
Stir in gelatin and stir until thoroughly dissolved.
Add yogurt and stir until dissolved.
Pour in can of pineapple, including juice.
Stir until well blended. Pour into mold or molds.
Chill until set.
This salad may be made with a variety of flavors of yogurt, fruit and gelatin.
Prepare pastry crust.
Melt butter or margarine; cool.
Beat egg yolks slightly, stir in sugar, flour and salt.
Add butter or margarine, buttermilk and vanilla.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form; fold into buttermilk mixture.
Pour into crust.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350°, bake 15 to 20 minutes or until knife inserted in pie center comes out clean and pie is golden brown.
Cool and chill before serving.

In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium-high heat. Saute celery and onion until tender. Add potatoes and broth. Cover and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 12 minutes. Stir in milk and seasonings. Add the cheese and heat only until melted. Garnish with parsley and cheese. Yield: 8 servings.
Place olive oil in heavy skillet.
Add onion rings and saute until very lightly browned and transparent.
Do not overcook.
Add garlic, pepper, bay leaf and vinegar.
Set aside.
Melt peanut butter, margarine and chocolate chips.
Set aside. Mix cereal, raisins and nuts.
Combine both mixtures in large bowl.
Dump into trash bag with powdered sugar and shake until coated.
Combine ham and butter in an 8-inch round dish covered with wax paper.
Cook at High 2 to 3 minutes; stir once.
Combine cream cheese and milk; blend in eggs, salt and pepper.
Add to ham. Cook, covered, at Medium for 5 to 6 minutes or until eggs are almost set.
Stir twice.
Let stand, covered, 3 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
Boil water first. Cook noodles, drain noodles and pour cheese and salsa and mix together.
Saute onion and garlic in oil.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Remove bay leaves and puree.
Brown rabbit in small amount of oil.
Set browned rabbit aside.
Saute onion, celery, bell pepper and green onions until wilted.
Add water, rice, parsley and rabbit; mix well.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is done, about 30 minutes.
Combine half the chocolate chips and 1/2 the shortening in glass bowl.
Microwave on Medium until melted.
Mix well.
Spread in foil-lined 8-inch square dish.
Chill for 15 minutes.
Mix 1/2 cup milk, yeast, 2 teaspoons sugar and 2 tablespoons flour.
Let this mixture stand for 10 minutes.
Cream shortening, egg yolks, sugar, salt and milk.
Add this to first mixture.
Add the flour and knead well.
Cover and let rise in warm place until double in size.
Stir ginger preserves and marmalade together until soft.
Split cake into 2 layers.
Spread half of this mixture over bottom layer of split cake.
Beat cream with sugar and vanilla until stiff. Spread half of cream over ginger and marmalade mixture, sprinkle with nuts.
Put on top layer, repeat ginger, cream and nut layer.
Brown meat and onion.
Add chili seasoning, tomato soup and water.
Add corn and cook about 10 minutes.
Pour contents of can in top of double boiler.
Add salt; cook until thickened.
Add corn flakes, finely crushed (measure before crushing).
Add gumdrops, nuts and flavoring.
Take out by teaspoonful and roll in coconut.
Let stand on waxed paper until firm.

Brown hamburger. Add chopped onion and taco seasoning. Combine refried beans and cream cheese. Cut tortillas into strips. In a 13 x 9-inch pan layer 1/2 hamburger mixture, then tortilla strips, then 1/2 refried bean mixture, then top with 1 cup each of Pepper Jack and Cheddar cheese. Repeat layers then top with remaining cheese. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes. Serve with sour cream, salsa, shredded lettuce and diced tomatoes.
In a bowl, mix shrimp with lemon juice, pepper flakes and salt.
Cook fettuccini according to package directions.
Keep warm in pot.
Heat oil and stir-fry onion, pepper strips and salt until peppers are tender-crisp; remove to bowl.
In same pan, heat oil and add asparagus and shrimp mixture.
Stir-fry until asparagus are tender-crisp and shrimp turn opaque, about 3 minutes.
Stir in pepper mixture and water; heat through.
To serve, toss fettuccini with shrimp mixture and soy sauce.
Sprinkle with grated lemon rind.
Serves 4.
Prepare with care.
Spread mustard on the inside portion of one slice of bread, then spread mayonnaise on the inside portion of the other slice of bread.
Next place the onion slice on the mustard side of first slice of bread, then place bologna (1 slice) over the onion slice.
Now place the slice of cheese over this slice of bologna, then the other slice of bologna over the cheese.
Now you are ready to place the slice of tomato over this second slice of bologna, and the last slice of bread over this.
(Be sure mayonnaise side is next to the tomato.)
Ready to devour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In medium bowl, combine crumbs, sugar, butter and egg white.
Blend.
Press on bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan.
Place pan on baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until slightly brown.
Cool on rack.
Reduce oven temperature to 300°.
In a large frying pan, steam chilies, jalapenos and tomatoes. Push to remove air.
Place in a plastic bag to steam. Remove skins.
Beat first 3 ingredients.
Shape into desired look.
Top with chopped nuts and cheese.
Soften topping at room temperature. Using an electric mixer, whip together Cool Whip, sour cream, sugar, vanilla and coconut. Chill.
Serve as a dip for fresh fruit or spoon over fresh fruit as a dressing.
Brown ground beef with onions and garlic.
Chop fresh tomatoes in meat and cook until soft.
Add Ranch Style beans and enough water to keep it from sticking.
Add salt and pepper. Simmer about 1 hour.
Serve over rice.
Cut eggs lengthwise.
Remove yolks and set whites aside. Place yolks in a bowl and mash and cream.
Add crumbled, crisp bacon, mayonnaise, margarine, mustard and paprika until blended. Spoon mixture into whites.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour or up to 24 hours.
Place raw meat in a 7 x 11-inch pan.
Add vegetables.
Blend salt, sugar and tapioca.
Sprinkle over meat and vegies.
Add tomato juice.
Cover pan with foil, sealing tight around edges. Bake at 250° for 4 hours.
If it gets too thick, add water.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine eggs, bread, juice, seasonings and garlic to ground beef.
Prepare foil (13 x 10) and spread ground beef mixture within about an inch of the foil.
Arrange ham in the middle and sprinkle half the cheese over it.
Beginning with the short end, roll the meat, lifting the foil as you go and seal the edges of the meat on all sides.
Discard foil.
Bake in a 13 x 9 baking dish at 350° for one hour.
Add remaining cheese on top for an additional fifteen minutes.
Shell Garbanzo beans if you want a finer consisitancy. Squeeze lemons and add all ingredients in food processor.
Add liquid from beans to make dip the consistency you want.
Dissolve the 2 jellos in the boiling water.
Mix all ingredients together; chill.
Frost with 1 cup sour cream.
Heat large pot of water to boiling.
Add pasta and cook to desired consistency.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add asparagus; cover and cook 3 minutes.
Add squash and mushrooms; cook 4 to 5 minutes longer until vegetables are tender.
Remove from heat; stir in tomatoes and 1/2 cup boiling water from pasta pot.
Drain water from pasta and return pasta to pot.
Add sauce and toss to coat.
Season with pepper.
Serve with Parmesan cheese.
Peel and thinly slice the apples.
Peel and grate the sweet potatoes.
Pour apple juice concentrate into a stainless steel Dutch oven.
Add apples and sweet potatoes and cook over low flame until tender, but not mushy.
Stir in dates and raisins to heat through.
Add spices to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Place all in a casserole.
Lightly toast almonds on a baking sheet under broiler.
Cover entire top of casserole with the nuts.
Steam broccoli according to package.
Heat oil and saute onion, parsley and garlic until onion is tender.
Stir in broccoli.
Take off heat, put into bowl and add all other ingredients; stir and serve.
Serves 6.
In a medium bowl, combine Grey Poupon, cream, ginger and honey. Beat until stiff.
Fold in pecans.
Serve on sliced fruit.
Makes about 1 1/4 cups.
In a small saucepan, bring pineapple to a boil.
Remove from heat and stir in gelatin until dissolved.
Cool to room temperature.
Stir in cottage cheese and whipped topping, chill until set.
Yields 1 serving.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix dressing, egg yolks, flour, sugar and pepper in large bowl until smooth.
Stir in corn, cheese and onions.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form; fold into corn mixture.
Pour batter into greased 4-cup souffle dish or 9-inch square baking dish.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Makes 6 servings.
Place egg white, sugar, cream of tartar and vanilla in a deep small bowl.
Mix well, add boiling water; beat at high speed until stiff peaks form.
After 4 to 5 minutes, frost 2 layer cake. Sprinkle with coconut.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place the honey, sugar, raisins, water, shortening, cinnamon and salt in a saucepan and boil for 3 minutes.
Cool about 30 minutes.
Add the flour and the baking soda which have been mixed together.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into 10 x 16-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Roll each biscuit out individually, then spread each with pizza sauce.
On one side of each biscuit, layer all veggies and top with cheese.
Then take other side and fold over top of the veggies. Close by using fork to press together.
Place each on greased cookie sheet.
Brush with butter on top and bake about 25 to 30 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs 1 at a time, beating well. Sift dry ingredients together and add alternately with milk.
Add lemon extract.
Bake in 2 (9-inch) layer cake pans at 350° for 30 or 40 minutes.
With finest blade of food chopper, grind together cheese, cheese spread, onion and garlic.
Add lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix thoroughly and stir until cheese is soft and pliable.
Form into long rolls and roll in chili powder. Wrap in waxed paper until ready for use.
Spread on crackers or use for sandwiches.
Keep cool until ready for use.
Drain pineapple (save 1 cup of juice).
Heat oil in saucepan. Saute onions and green peppers for 3 minutes.
Mix cornstarch, vinegar, ginger and soy sauce.
Add pineapple juice.
Add onions and peppers.
Cook, stirring often, until mixture thickens.
Add the pineapple chunks.
Brown ground beef, then add spices, sauce and cornstarch. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Add cheese and melt.
Serve with French bread cubes.
Douse gobbler with seasonings and lay to rest in slow cooker (or deep, deep casserole).
Mix sour cream with flour, soup, mushrooms and soda pop.
Pour all over everything.
Cover pot and cook on low (or bake at low temperature) from breakfast until dinner.

recipes.t: Easy Chicken And Rice Slow Cooker
d: In a slow cooker combine mushrooms, celery, onion dill weed and pepper.
Top with chicken.
Pour soup and broth over chicken. Cover, cook on High 2 1/2 to 3 hours or Low 5 to 6 hours.
If using low turn slow cooker to high heat setting.
Stir uncooked rice into mushroom mixture.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes more.

In a skillet, brown beef, onion and green pepper; drain grease. Stir in beans, tomato sauce, tomatoes, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in noodles and heat through. Yield: 6 servings.
Saute hamburg, onions and peppers.
Beat eggs, milk, salt, nutmeg, pepper and dry mustard.
Add cooked hamburg mixture.
Pour in pie crust.
Add cheese.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes or until set and cheese is browned.
Place croutons and cheese in the bottom of a greased 6 x 10-inch baking dish.
Brown sausage and drain if needed.
Beat eggs and add all other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until firm in center.
Serve immediately.
Serves 6.
Chop onion, 1/2 bunch cilantro, garlic and bell pepper.
Add long grain rice.
Add hamburger meat and mix well.
Shape into meatballs, about 1-inch diameter.
Set aside.
Combine oil, sugar, catsup, vinegar and Worcestershire sauce. Wash spinach and add chopped onion.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Drain on paper towels and add to spinach.
Slice eggs; add to spinach. Pour dressing over salad and toss.
Layer potatoes, onion rings, salt, pepper and cottage cheese. Spread layer with mayonnaise.
Repeat layers, ending with mayonnaise.
Cover with plastic wrap and store in refrigerator for 3 days.
Do not disturb!
Place about 3 dozen tortilla chips on ungreased baking sheet. Spread 2 teaspoons refried beans on each chip; sprinkle with green onions and cheese.
Top each with a slice of pepper.
Save remaining chips and peppers for other uses.
Bake at 350° for 5 minutes.
Makes about 3 dozen.
Melt butter and stir in peanut butter.
Add remaining ingredients: nuts, powdered sugar, coconut, graham cracker crumbs and vanilla. Mix well and roll into balls.
Brown meat in skillet; don't let it get hard.
Add flour and stir.
Add a little oil, if needed.
Stir and cook 2 or 3 minutes. Add milk, salt and pepper.
Cook and stir until thick.
Add hot sauce and coffee.
Add more milk, if needed.
Saute onions, pepper and mushrooms in small amount of butter; brown sausage and drain.
Put bread in bottom of long bread pan; mix milk and eggs well.
Add sausage, vegetables and
cheese. Pour over bread.
Let set in fridge overnight.
Pour soup over top.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Combine 3 ingredients and bring to a boil in saucepan.
Line cookie sheet with foil.
Cover with Keebler Club crackers.
Pour liquid over crackers slowly until it soaks in.
Sprinkle almonds over all.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Put oil, ginger and garlic into a 2-quart microwave dish. Cook, uncovered, in microwave oven for 2 minutes at High.
Add onion, broccoli, cauliflower and pepper to casserole; stir.
Cover dish.
Cook in microwave 3 to 4 minutes at High or until vegetables are crisp.
Blend cream cheese and butter and beat in the sugar.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon together and gradually work into creamed mixture.
Beat until smooth.
Place chicken breasts in a single layer in shallow baking dish.
Blend butter and Durkee's.
Pour over chicken.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Uncover; bake 15 minutes more until brown.
Serve chicken atop bed of rice.
Pour drippings over all.
Place meat in roasting pan.
Surround with potatoes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Top with onion soup mixture.
Cover tightly.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 2 1/2 to 3 hours or until meat is tender.
Brown beef in frying pan over high heat.
Add taco seasoning mix and water; stir.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
While beef is cooking, place taco shells in 350° preheated oven for 5 to 10 minutes.
Fill heated taco shells with 1 to 2 tablespoons meat. Top with lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, taco sauce and sour cream.

recipes.t: Black Linguine With Calamari And Scallops In A Garlic Butter Sauce
d: Saute in olive oil, garlic, calamari, scallops and basil. Deglaze with white wine; add salt and pepper.
Reduce 1/2 of liquid.
Add tomatoes; add butter at the end.
Warm pasta.
Serve on top of black linguine and garnish with fresh basil.
In a large baking dish, place chicken, egg noodles and bell pepper.
Sprinkle dry ingredients over chicken.
Mix barbecue sauce and water; pour over the top.
Cover; bake for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Clean chicken off.
Put crackers in Ziploc bag and crush them up into dust.
Put the eggs in a bowl and stir them up, then put the chicken in the bowl of eggs.
Take chicken out when covered with eggs.
Then put the chicken in the bag of crackers.
Zip up bag and shake until chicken is covered in crackers.
Cut bread into 1/2-inch slices, cutting to but not through bottom crust. Combine butter, mustard, parsley, garlic and red pepper. Spread on cut sides of alternate bread slices.
Cut cheese and meat to fit bread slices. Add cheese, meat, tomatoes and sweet peppers to buttered slits.
Place on baking sheet. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes or until crisp and hot (or wrap in foil and grill over medium coals for 20 minutes, turning often).
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well each time.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together and add alternately with buttermilk.
Add extract and mix well.
Add coconut last.
Bake in a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan or Bundt pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Pour topping on while cake is hot and leave it in the pan for 1 hour.
In a large punch bowl, mix together pineapple juice, lemonade, orange juice, cranberry juice and apple juice.
Add the ice cubes. Float the lemon slices on top for garnish.
Very refreshing and pretty!
Soak cucumbers in water and lime overnight.
Rinse well.
Then soak in cold water for 2 hours, then rinse and put in ice for 1 hour.
Make your syrup with sugar, salt, vinegar, pickling spice and add ginger right before the cucumbers.
When syrup is boiling, add cucumbers and boil for 20 minutes, then simmer for 1 hour. Put in sterilized jars and seal.

Bring chicken stock, parsnips, onion, curry powder, pepper and bay leaf to boil. Reduce heat and simmer, covered and stirring often, for about 30 minutes or until vegetables are very tender. Discard bay leaf. Transfer in batches to blender or food processor; puree until smooth. Return to pan; add milk and heat thoroughly.
Wash greens, discarding stems.
Pat dry and tear into bite size pieces to make about 6 cups.
Place greens in large bowl. Add onions and freshly ground pepper.
Cover and chill thoroughly. At serving, cook bacon in deep skillet until crisp.
Slowly stir in vinegar, lemon juice, sugar and salt.
Add dandelion mixture. Toss until leaves are coated and slightly wilted (not cooked), 1 to 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with chopped egg.

recipes.t: Pull-A-Part Bread With Cinnamon And Pecans
d: Spray Bundt pan with nonstick spray.
Layer a few pecans on the bottom and sprinkle some cinnamon and sugar on top.
Cut each biscuit in fourths.
Roll each piece in cinnamon/sugar mixture thoroughly in pan.
After doing can, sprinkle butter and more pecans.
Layer more biscuits, butter and pecans.
Pan should be half full.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cool and dump onto plate.
Drain fruits, reserving syrup.
Add water to syrup to make 2 cups.
Heat in a saucepan.
Add jellos; stir to dissolve.
Blend in cream cheese in blender on low speed.
Add fruits and nuts. Add cake mix; stir all together.
Pour in pan and chill.
Freezes well.
Beat eggs and sugar until light colored.
Add oil until well blended.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to egg mixture. Beat 2 minutes.
Add nuts, vanilla and squash (squeezed in paper towel).
Mix thoroughly.
Pour batter into well-greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Blend 1 cup powdered sugar plus 1 tablespoon milk until smooth.
Drizzle over cooled cake.
In a medium saucepan, combine the pudding and pie filling and milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture comes to a full boil.
Saute onions until golden in large frypan. Add potatoes and squash (tomatoes, if desired).
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Occasionally turn vegetables carefully with spatula. Ready to serve with potatoes are soft.
Saute onions and pepper in butter until clear and soft.
Stir in flour and mix thoroughly.
Remove from stove and stir in cream until smooth.
Return to stove and cook over medium heat until thickened (add milk if too thick).
Add shrimp, cheese, pimento, mustard, salt, pepper and Tabasco sauce.
Stir until cheese is melted but do not boil.
Spoon over potatoes (6).
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then cooking oil, gumdrops and nuts; add to dry ingredients and mix until combined.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 5-inch baking pan or two small loaf pans; bake in 350° oven for 1 hour or until done and cool.
Brown chicken well in oil.
Add garlic, salt and thyme.
Drain pineapple juice from can into skillet. Add wine, cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove chicken to serving plates.
Stir sour cream into pan juices; add pineapple and green onions and heat through. Spoon over chicken and serve.
Drain peaches and reserve juice.
Chill.

Blend jello, sugar, cinnamon and cloves together very well, then add 1 cup boiling water, 2 tablespoons vinegar and reserved juice. Refrigerate, stirring occasionally, to keep spices off bottom. After mixture starts to thicken, add peaches.
Chill until firm.
Sift flour, baking powder, soda and salt together three times. Cream shortening and sugar thoroughly; add vanilla, pineapple and coconut.
Mix well.
Add dry ingredients and mix.
Drop by teaspoon on greased baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.
Mix hamburger, onion, crumbs, salt, pepper, 1 teaspoon dill and 2 tablespoons water.
Shape into 1-inch meatballs.
In 12-inch skillet in hot oil, brown meatballs, 1/2 at a time. Remove.
Into skillet drippings, stir flour and 1 teaspoon dill. Gradually add broth.
Heat to boiling.
Return meatballs; bring to boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Skim off fat; stir in sour cream.
Heat through.
Do not boil.
Serve over rice.
Combine pineapple juice and water to make 2 cups.
Heat to boiling.
Add Jell-O and stir to dissolve.
Stir in cranberry sauce, lemon juice, peel and nutmeg.
Chill until mixture thickens slightly.
Add sour cream; stir until thoroughly combined.
Fold in pineapple and pecans.
Pour into an 8-cup mold.
Chill until firm.
Unmold onto a serving plate.
Garnish with fresh strawberries and lemon twists, if desired.
Yields 12 servings.
Mix together sugar and syrup, boil and add peanut butter. Pour into large bowl with rice krispies. Press into buttered pan. Prepare topping: Melt both chips and spread on top of bars.
Cook macaroni.
Brown onion and fat.
Add meat and brown.
Pour soup and milk over meat mix.
Put 1/2 macaroni in casserole and 1/2 cup green beans or asparagus and 1/2 meat mix.
Top with 1/2 cup cheese and repeat process.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Heat oven to 325°.
Butter a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Chop chocolate. In a small saucepan, combine chocolate and butter and melt over low heat, stirring occasionally until smooth.
Let cool.
With mixer at medium-low speed, beat cream cheese and 2/3 cup of sugar until smooth.
Beat in 1 egg, 1 teaspoon of vanilla and the lemon juice; set aside.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt.
On medium-low speed, beat remaining eggs and 1 1/2 teaspoons of vanilla until frothy.
Gradually beat in remaining sugar.
Beat in chocolate mix.
Pour half of chocolate batter into pan.
Carefully spoon on cream cheese mix.
Smooth surface.
Spoon remaining chocolate mix on cheese mix and smooth.
Bake about 1 hour until knife stuck in center comes out clean.
Cool and chill before cutting.
Whisk together eggs and whiskey glass of peanut oil until nice and golden yellow.
Add flour, a small amount at a time.
All flour may not be used in mixing dough, but the rest will be used when rolling out dough.
Cut a piece of dough and roll out to be nice and thin.
Then make strips (about 1-inch wide) with a ravioli cutter.
Saute diced onions in oil.
Add chopped meat to brown.
Take browned meat from skillet and drain in strainer.
Return drained meat to skillet and add tomato sauce and chili powder.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Put meat into deep Pyrex pie plate.
Ask butcher to "crack" the pork loin roast as that the roast is cut through at the bone.
Coat with salt and pepper.
Put fresh or dried rosemary between each "crack." Coat outside with rosemary.
Bake at 350° after first broiling for a few minutes to brown the roast.
Cook about 1 1/2 hours until done.
Serve with cooked couscous which has been flavored with 1/4 cup olive oil and chopped, fresh mint.

recipes.t: Hash Brown And Egg Brunch Casserole
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
In deep 9-inch skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add onion and peppers; cook until onion is softened. Add potatoes and cook, covered, over medium heat 5 minutes.
Beat eggs and cream together; stir in chiles, salt and pepper.
Pour over potato mixture.
Sprinkle cheese evenly over top.
Cover and bake 10 minutes.
Uncover and continue baking 15 to 17 minutes until set in center.
Mix in saucepan the sugar and syrup and bring to a boil.
Boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter and mix. Pour over corn flakes-coconut mixture that is in a very large bowl, that has been sprayed with Pam.
Spray Pam on hands as needed while making mixture into balls.
Place on wax paper.
Cream margarine and sugar until well blended.
Add molasses, vanilla and eggs; mix well.
Add dry ingredients and mix well. Drop by teaspoons onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes at 350° (or until lightly browned).
Cook and stir brown sugar, Karo syrup and peanut butter until melted.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour in a pan and chill.
Cut in squares.
Put crumbs on bottom of Pyrex dish.
Mix fruit, sugar and lemon juice together.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour over crumbs. Sprinkle top with more crushed cookies.
Freeze 4 to 6 hours. So refreshing.
Sift flour, salt and 2 tablespoons sugar together.
Beat eggs until light.
Add milk and mix well.
Add butter.
Heat 8 or 10-inch frying pan hot enough for pancakes to brown quickly.
Pour batter into frying pan in desired size; brown on both sides. Remove pancakes to large plate and heap with strawberries.
Roll pancakes with strawberries inside.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar; garnish with crisp bacon and whole unstemmed strawberries.
Keep finished pancakes warm.
Makes about 5 large pancakes or 10 small ones.
Combine cake mix, 2/3 cup coconut, water and egg whites.
Beat for 2 minutes at high speed and 1 minute on low speed.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan; bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes, or until a wooden pick inserted in middle comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes.
Punch holes all over top with 2-pronged fork.
Pour cream of coconut over cake; let it cool.
Mix thawed Cool Whip and sour cream together; spread over cooled cake.
Chill at least 4 hours before serving.
Can also be made with white cake mix.
Put a 13 x 9-inch baking pan or a large cast-iron skillet into the oven and heat oven to 425°.
Meanwhile, process eggs, milk, juice, sugar, flour and salt in blender or food processor until well blended.
Add butter to hot pan and heat 1 to 2 minutes until butter sizzles (check often so it doesn't get brown).
Holding hot pan with pot holders, tip to coat bottom with butter. Immediately pour in batter.
Bake about 20 minutes until puffed and brown. Dust with confectioners sugar and serve with toppings. Yields 6 servings at 312 calories each.
Slice cabbage finely.
Melt margarine in large skillet.
Add cabbage; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper; simmer 10 minutes, or until sausages are done.
Combine all ingredients except popcorn and cook until reaches 290°, measuring with a candy thermometer.
When the mixture reaches 290°, pour over the popcorn while popcorn is spread out on a cookie sheet.
Add 2 more tablespoons of butter and mix the popcorn and ingredients together while on cookie sheet.
