Let stand to cool and store in airtight tin.
Makes 1 1/2 quarts of caramel popcorn.
Shelf life should be 2 to 3 weeks.

recipes.t: Beef With Snow Peas And Baby Corn
d: Brown beef in wok or large skillet.
Drain.
Add garlic; cook until tender.
Set aside.
Wipe wok with paper towel.
Heat vegetable oil in wok over medium-high.
Add snow peas and red bell pepper; stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Stir in ground beef mixture, baby corn, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over rice.
Melt margarine in Pyrex dish.
Mix eggs and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well (whisk works well).
Break bread slices into melted margarine.
Pour milk and egg mixture over bread.
Sprinkle with raisins, if desired.
Sprinkle top with cinnamon.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes at 375° until set in middle.
Cook potatoes.
When done, cool and add salt, chopped eggs, mayonnaise, onion and mustard.
Now pour the vinegar solution over potatoes and stir lightly.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease bottom of two 8-inch cake pans. Line bottom of pans with wax paper.
Grease and flour waxed paper and sides of pans. Mix cake by directions on box. Add jam, raisins and nuts.
Mix well.
Pour in pans.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pans for 10 minutes.
Turn out on wire racks.
Remove wax paper and cool completely.

recipes.t: Passion Salad(Strawberry Filling For Mini Pie Shells)
d: Cream together cream cheese, condensed milk and vanilla instant pudding. Add Cool Whip and beat until smooth. Fold in strawberry pie filling. Can be spooned into pastry shells and chilled.
Cook ground beef, onion and spices until browned.
Drain; set aside.
Spread 1 can crescent rolls on bottom of loaf pan.
Spread tomato soup on top of rolls.
Next, spread beef mixture over tomato soup.
Top with cheese.
Lastly top with second can of crescent rolls.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until browned on top.
Melt butter in a large baking pan. Add chicken. Add apples to the pan with the chicken.
Pour the apple brandy and cream over the chicken and apples.
Put in a 350° oven and bake for 1 1/2 hours or until chicken is done.
Flour chicken and fry in olive oil until brown.
Add garlic, vinegar, broth, thyme and bay leaf.
Cook over moderate heat for 15 minutes.
Remove chicken.
Add butter and saute mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Pour over chicken and serve.

recipes.t: Green Beans With Ketchup And Bacon Dressing
d: Mix together onions, ketchup, sugar and water; simmer 5 minutes.
Add beans and crumbled bacon.
Finish on top of stove or oven.
Blend powdered sugar and cocoa.
Add milk, butter and marshmallows, but do not stir.
Cook 3 minutes on High in microwave; then stir and add vanilla and nuts.
Stir to blend. Pour into a greased pan or line pan with foil.
Place in freezer 20 minutes or refrigerator 1 hour.
Spread a thin layer of cream cheese on 1 slice of bread. Cover the cream cheese with another slice of bread to make a cream cheese sandwich.
Cut the bread in the shape of a snowman.
Spread another thin layer of cream cheese over the top of your snowman. Decorate your snowman sandwich using the raisins and walnuts to make eyes, a nose, a mouth and buttons.
Makes one sandwich.
Cream butter and sugar well; add egg yolks and beat well until thoroughly blended.
Stir the baking powder into the cracker crumbs.
Add the milk and crackers crumbs alternately and blend thoroughly.
Stir in the chopped nut meats.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and fold these into the mixture last.
Bake in two 8-inch pans in moderate oven, 350°, about 45 minutes.
In large skillet, saute chicken and onion in hot oil until chicken is no longer pink.
Add vegetables and saute 2 minutes longer.
Add spaghetti sauce and shrimp.
Simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes or until shrimp turns pink and chicken is cooked through. Stir in spinach and let cook 3 to 5 minutes longer.
Serve over hot, cooked fettucine and top with Provolone.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
The shrimp may be cooked first and then put in at the end.
Chop cabbage into medium-size pieces and spread in bottom of greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish (prefer glass; tomato and metal gets bitter taste).
Brown meat and onion, breaking up meat as it cooks.
Stir in rice, salt and pepper.
Spoon mixture over cabbage.
Heat butter, half and half, salt and cheese.
Stir until melted.
Mix in potatoes and bake in a 2-quart baking dish at 350° for 45 minutes.
Add sour cream and continue cooking for 15 minutes.
Garnish with bacon.
Brown beef, onions and celery.
Brown uncooked rice.
Combine ingredients in casserole and mix well with soups and soy sauce. Cook 45 minutes at 350°.
After 30 minutes, top with Chinese noodles.
Return and finish cooking for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, combine vinegar, salt and pepper.
Add garlic and mustard.
Finally, add oil and whisk until well blended.
If desired, you may add 1 finely chopped cooked egg to dressing.
Cut steak into 2-inch strips; mix cornstarch and soy sauce; set aside.
Heat chicken stock; set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet or wok until very hot.
Add garlic; cook 2 to 3 minutes. Add beef; saute quickly, keeping it moving just until it loses color (30 seconds).
Add onion and salt and pepper to taste, stirring constantly for another half minute or so.
Add chicken broth; bring quickly to a boil.
Add cauliflower, a few at a time. Cook 3 minutes.
Add snow peas, stirring constantly for another few minutes.
After 7 minutes maximum, cauliflower should be tender and pea pods should be bright green.
Add soy sauce mixture.
Mix throughly; stir until thickened.
Turn into a serving dish.
Serves 6.
Cook sugar and water in saucepan to 220°.
Remove from heat; stir in cocoa, vanilla and marshmallows until melted.
Cool, without stirring, until bottom of pan just feels warm to hand. Beat to thicken and serve warm over ice cream.
Makes 2 cups of sauce.
In medium saucepan, stir together sugar, cocoa and gelatin. Gradually stir in milk.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil and gelatin is dissolved.
Cool slightly.
Add yogurt and vanilla; blend gently until well combined.
Pour into dessert dishes. Refrigerate 6 hours or until set.
Top with fruit.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Line 18 muffin pan with paper liners or grease them well.
Sift flour with baking powder and salt.
Mix together butter, granulated sugar, eggs and vanilla about 4 minutes.
Add flour mixture, alternating with milk; beat until smooth.
Fold in blueberries.
Scoop about 1/4 cup batter into muffin cups.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Makes 18 muffins.
Lightly mix sugar, zucchini and oil.
Add eggs; mix well. Combine flour, soda, nutmeg, cinnamon and baking powder. Gradually add to egg mixture, blending thoroughly.
Stir in pecans, raisins and pineapple.
Pour into two 9 x 5 x 3-inch greased and floured loaf pans.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake for 50 minutes, or until done.
Makes 2 loaves.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cake mix, pudding mix and butter.
Add first egg.
Mix well until crumbly, about 1 minute. Save 1/2 cup of crumbs for top.
Put remaining crumbs in a cake tin, 13 x 9 x 2-inch (greased).
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes; press in pan.
Combine macaroni, celery, cheese and ham.
Mix mayonnaise and remaining ingredients.
Pour over salad, toss and chill.
Makes 8 cups.
Drain pear halves, reserving 1/4 cup syrup and 1 pear half. Mash remaining pear halves; drain. Combine the first 1/3 cup sugar, gelatin and salt.
Stir in reserved pear syrup, egg yolks, lemon peel and lemon juice.
Cook and stir until slightly thickened.
Add mashed pears. Cool until mixture mounds.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks.
Gradually add remaining sugar, beating until stiff.
Fold in pear mixture.
Turn into pie shell. Chill. Garnish with whipped cream and reserved pear half, sliced.
Make a syrup of the sugar and water by boiling for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add tea and jello.
Add all fruit juice and let stand for 24 hours.
Add Hawaiian Punch and ginger ale when ready to serve.

Combine all ingredients except matchstick cucumber pieces, in a food processor or blender. Cover and process or blend until nearly smooth. Press mixture through a fine mesh strainer, 1/3 at a time, holding strainer over bowl to catch juices (you should have about 1 2/3 cups strained juices). Discard solids. Transfer strained juices to a 2-quart square baking dish. Cover and freeze for 3 to 4 hours or until firmly frozen. Break up frozen mixture. Transfer mixture to a chilled large bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until slushy, but not melted. Return to baking dish. Cover and freeze for 2 to 3 hours or until firm.
Line a loaf pan with heavy brown paper.
Grease paper well. (Use about a 4-inch deep pan and a brown paper sack.)
Chop pecans, dates, cherries and pineapple into medium-sized pieces. Place all ingredients in mixing bowl.
Mix until blended.
Turn into prepared loaf pan and press with spoon, or use your hand, to level the top.

recipes.t: New York Deli Style Cheese Cake
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Have all above ingredients at room temperature.
Cream the cheese.
Add sugar slowly.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix well.
Add sour cream, bit by bit, followed by juice and vanilla.
Grease and line spring-form pan with graham cracker mixture.
(For crunchier crust, add 2 tablespoons melted butter.)
Bake for 10 minutes.
Cool, then add cheese mixture for baking.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn oven off.
Leave cake in oven for 1 1/2 hours with oven door cracked open.
Open door all the way and leave cake in for 1/2 hour longer.
(Slow cooling is the secret.)
Melt chocolate chips in double boiler; add butter, egg and pecans.
When mixture is slightly cooled, add marshmallows.
Stir to coat.
Use wax paper 18-inches long and put down a heavy coat of coconut.
Pour mixture over coconut.
Roll into a log 1 1/2 to 2-inches.
Chill, slice and serve.

Brown pork in oiled skillet. Spray 9 x 13 glass baking dish with Pam cooking spray. Place a layer of sliced potatoes into greased baking dish. Place diced onion on top of potatoes and then layer diced green peppers over onions. Transfer browned pork over into baking dish over green pepper layer. In separate bowl, mix soup and water and mix well. Pour soup mixture over meat to cover. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until done.
Mix vanilla, sugar, cinnamon, eggs and milk with a fork.
Dip one slice of bread in mixture and brown on preheated skillet. After browning on both sides, sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Melt butter in a 9-inch square baking dish.
Sprinkle crushed cereal over butter, then layer alternately all ingredients over top, except milk.
Pour milk evenly over top.
Bake in a 350 degree oven for 25 minutes.
Refrigerate until set and cut into squares.
Crush large bag of Oreo cookies (put in Ziploc bag and roll with a rolling pin).
Melt margarine and mix together with Oreo cookies.
Pat into a 9 x 11 pan.
Take ice cream and let soften. Scoop it over and spread over crumb crust. Use a small can of Hershey's chocolate (about the size of tomato paste can) and drizzle it over the ice cream.
Throw on a handful of salted peanuts.
Put in the freezer.
Just before serving, cover the top with Cool Whip and sprinkle crushed Oreo cookies over the top. This should be made in time to put in freezer several hours before serving.
Place chicken cutlets in casserole, leaving some space between.
Cutlets may be placed on top of one another, if necessary.
Add 2 cans of condensed soup and the wine.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Cover casserole with lid or foil and bake at 300° for 1 1/4 hours.
Salt, pepper and flour chicken.
Brown chicken and onions in small amount of shortening in large skillet.
When chicken is brown, add enough water to make gravy.
When gravy is at your consistency, add 1/2 bell pepper (chopped or in strips) for flavor.
Let simmer 15 to 20 minutes, then add Worcestershire to taste.
Let simmer an additional 15 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Brown beef in melted butter.
As meat begins to turn color, add onion. Saute until meat is well browned.
Stir in tomato sauce and pepper. Simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes.
Combine sour cream, cottage cheese, carrots and cooked noodles.
Mix well. Alternate layers of meat mixture and cottage cheese mixture in a greased 3-quart casserole dish, beginning and ending with noodles. Top with Cheddar cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Pare and cut squash in small pieces; cook until tender. Drain.
Add milk slowly to mayonnaise.
When it begins to thicken, add cheese and seasonings.
Place squash in casserole.
Cover with sauce.
Bake at 400° until brown on top.
Cook bacon until lightly browned.
Add 3 cups milk, potatoes, onions, salt and pepper.
Bring to boil.
Cover.
Reduce heat and simmer about seven minutes until potatoes are tender.
Wash and pick over beans.
Cover with water and soak overnight.
Next morning, simmer beans in salted water until tender to bite.
Drain and save water.
Place in bottom of large bean pot or crock-pot.
Alternately layer cooked beans with a mixture of brown sugar, tomatoes, onions, mustard, salt and pepper.
Top with bacon.
Add enough of water in which beans were cooked to cover beans.
Cover with lid; cook until tender.
If using crock-pot, put on low for 8 to 10 hours, stirring occasionally.
Do not add extra water.
Combine cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, sour cream, vegetable oil and almond extract.
Combine the sugar, cinnamon and nuts.
Pour 1/3 of the batter into a 10-inch tube or Bundt pan.
Sprinkle with half of the sugar mixture.
Repeat layers and top with remaining batter.
Bake at 350°
for about 50 minutes.
Cool 15 minutes before inverting pan.
Saute butter, onion and bell pepper.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cover with grated cheese and paprika.
Bake for 15 minutes more.

Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Cube bread and cream cheese. Place both in greased pan. In a blender or with beaters, mix eggs, milk, syrup and butter. Pour over cubed bread and cream cheese. Cover with Saran Wrap overnight or for several hours. Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 40 minutes or until golden brown and puffy. Serve with hot maple syrup. Serves approximately 6 to 8 people.
Mix oil, vinegar, and sugar together.
Bring this mixture to a boil.
Set this off to cool about five minutes.
pour over corn and pea mixture.
Set in refrigerator until cool.
Eat and enjoy!
Blend flour into butter.
Add evaporated milk and liquid from mushrooms.
Add chicken broth to make 4 cups of liquid.
Add turmeric, salt and oregano to liquid.
Cook until sauce is thickened.
Add grated cheese.
In flat baking dish, put 2 to 3 cups of cooked rice.
Layer chicken and mushrooms over rice.
Pour cream sauce on top and top with cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Spray skillet with Pam.
Cook potatoes and onion on medium heat, covered, turning often with spatula.
Season to taste with Mrs. Dash, pepper and Parmesan.
Combine sugar and milk in saucepan; stir over low heat until sugar is dissolved.
Add dates; cook to soft ball stage.
Turn candy onto cold damp towel; roll towel around candy and refrigerate for several hours.
Shape candy into balls.
Dip into lime juice and roll in sugar.
Combine the first 5 ingredients together and press 3/4 of the mixture in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven and pour chocolate chips over mixture.
Combine the 6 tablespoons flour with the caramel and pour over chocolate chips. Sprinkle remaining 1/4 mixture on top.
Bake 15 minutes longer. Cool and cut into bars.

Cook Rice a Roni as directed on box except use chicken broth instead of water. Melt 1/2 stick of margarine in a skillet and add bell peppers, onions, celery, sage and mushrooms. Cook until tender. Remove from heat and add to Rice a Roni. Add chicken and salt and pepper to taste. Pour into baking dish. Melt remainder of margarine and drizzle over top. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Lightly grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
Place 6 tortillas on bottom. Then layer meat, beans (undrained) and remaining tortillas torn up on top.
Mix soup and chopped Ro-Tel tomatoes together and spread over tortillas. Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.

Cut potato vertically into 20 slices. Place in single layer on greased baking sheet. Brush each slice with taco sauce. Sprinkle with chilies and cheese. Bake 25 minutes until potatoes are tender and cheese is golden brown.
Combine beans, onions, horseradish and mustard in shallow baking dish.
Slice corned beef hash into 8 slices and arrange with pineapple slices on top of beans.
Sprinkle with brown sugar. Dot with butter.
Bake for about 25 minutes at 400°.
Serves 4.
Heat oven to 350°; melt margarine in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
In a saucepan, heat sugar and water until it is dissolved. Cut Crisco into flour until fine crumbles; add milk and stir with fork until dough leaves side of bowl.
Turn onto floured counter; make into a ball.
Flatten and roll out until 1/4-inch thick. Sprinkle with cinnamon; add pears or apples.
Roll up like a jelly roll.
Now slice up in circles about 15 of them.
Place in the buttered casserole.
Pour the sugar water over the dough.
(This looks like too much liquid, but the dough will absorb the liquid.) Bake about 50 minutes.
You can use dewberries, peaches or other fruit.
Serves 12 to 13.
Cook first 4 ingredients until bubbly.
Remove from heat. Stir in confectioners sugar.
Beat until consistency desired and spread on cake before it hardens.
Wash, drain and stem berries.
Crush 2 cups of berries and combine with water, sugar and cornstarch.
Bring to boiling point and simmer about 2 minutes or until clear.
Add butter and enough red food coloring to give good color.
Fill baked and cooled pie shell with cooled berry mixture.
Cover with remaining sliced berries.
Chill. Top with cream before serving.
Combine grape juice, lemon juice and cider; sweeten to taste. Just before serving, add ginger ale.
Fill glasses about 3/4 and drop a scoop of orange sherbet on top.
Serve immediately.
In a saucepan, soften gelatin in grape juice and lemon juice. Bring to a rolling boil, dissolving gelatin; boil for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Stir in liquid sweetener.
Pour into hot, sterilized jars.
Seal; store in refrigerator.
Makes 1 1/2 pints.

recipes.t: Pat Jenneskens' Artichoke And Mushroom Chicken
d: Put flour in a plastic bag.
Add chicken and shake to coat thoroughly.
Heat oil in a frypan over medium heat.
Add chicken and saute until golden.
Remove to a warm platter and keep warm. Pour off any oil left in pan.
Add butter and melt over medium heat.
Add garlic, artichoke hearts and mushrooms.
Saute for 5 minutes.
Prepare rice as directed on package.
Mix artichokes, including liquid, mayonnaise, olives and bell pepper.
Pour into rice mixture; stir well.
Chill for 1 hour.
Serve.
Makes approximately 6 (1/2 cup) servings.
Brown onion, garlic and beef together in 6-quart Dutch oven. Add sauce and spices.
Bring to boil.
Add beans.
Simmer for 2 hours.
Cut bacon into 1-inch segments and brown to a crisp.
Add onion and saute.
While this is cooking, boil potatoes until soft; drain water, leaving enough to cover an inch above potatoes.
When cooked, add bacon, onion, corn and milk to potatoes and simmer on low for 30 minutes.
Serve with cornbread or crackers.

recipes.t: Pork Tenderloin With Garlic Mustard Sauce
d: Mince garlic.
Slice scallion.
Cut pork into 8 diagonal slices.
Sprinkle meat with salt and pepper and coat lightly with flour.
Heat oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add pork and cook until brown on each side about 3 minutes. Remove and cover to keep warm.
Chop tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers and onions in a food processor until finely cut, but not pureed.
Combine with remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Serves 8.
Contains 90 calories per 1-cup serving.
Set aside 1 3/4 cups of chocolate candies.
Place remaining candies in a large plastic bag.
Crush with rolling pin.
In a saucepan, combine crushed candies, milk and butter.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until candies are melted and mixture is smooth.
Cool to room temperature.
Frost top of each cookie with 1 1/2 tablespoons of chocolate mixture.
Frost cones, leaving 1 inch at tip unfrosted.
Holding frosted cone by tip, fill each with 2 teaspoons candies; center filled one on top of frosted cookie to form "hat."
Place each hat on baking sheet.
Repeat until all cookies and cones are used.
Decorate witches hats with remaining candies.
Allow 15 minutes to set.
Chop onion into very small pieces. Then add finely chopped onion, bread crumbs, salt, oil and baking powder to the ground chicken.
Mix it well.
In large skillet, melt margarine; saute green onions and garlic, when tender, add basil and tomatoes.
Meanwhile, cook tortellini according to package directions.
When cooked, saute drained tortellini in sauce about 10 minutes.
Place in baking dish, sprinkle with Mozzarella cheese and bake until cheese is melted.
Divide scoops of sherbet among 8 tall glasses.
Add 1 tablespoon orange marmalade to each glass.
Fill glasses with ginger ale.
Stir with a long spoon to mix.
Serve at once.

recipes.t: Peanut Butter And Potato Chip Cookies
d: Cream shortening, sugar and eggs.
Add peanut butter.
Add flour, soda and vanilla (dough will be stiff).
Blend in chips and nuts.
Drop by heaping teaspoons on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Makes 3 dozen.
My grandchildren love them.
In a clean glass bowl, beat egg whites until foamy.
Add cream of tartar; continue beating, adding honey and vanilla.
Gradually add nonfat dry milk, beating constantly.
In a mixing bowl combine brown sugar, eggs, milk, oil and vanilla.
Mix well.
Combine flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir into batter.
Stir in oats, chocolate chips and raisins. Let stand for 5 to 10 minutes.
Drop by teaspoon onto greased baking sheets.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove immediately.
Yields 3 1/2 or 4 dozen.
Mix ground beef, onion and black pepper, then brown and drain off grease.
Add your red pepper, Texas Pete, tomato sauce, tomato paste, spaghetti mix and Texas red chili and simmer about 20 minutes.
Then cook noodles until done.
Then take out your baking dish and lay a row of noodles, then your sauce, then sprinkle both types of cheese and repeat.
Then bake for about 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Melt margarine.
Add mushrooms and garlic.
Combine cornstarch and milk.
When smooth, add to mushroom mixture.
Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Stir in rest of ingredients. Pour into pastry shells.
Cover pie with pastry.
Seal and flute edges. Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Peel and cube eggplant to make 6 cups.
Mix with the chopped green pepper and chopped onion.
Cut 3 pieces of heavy-duty foil about 12 x 18-inches.
Divide the eggplant mixture evenly on foil. Place 1 teaspoon margarine on mixture; sprinkle with basil or if preferred use chopped fresh basil.
Close foil tightly.
Place foil packs on grill 3 to 4 inches from heat.
Cook for about 35 minutes. Chop tomato and place on another piece of foil.
Close foil and place on grill the last 15 minutes of eggplant cooking time. Remove vegetables from foil; blend together in large bowl.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Yield:
4 servings. Carbohydrate 11 g, protein 2 g, fat 3.3 g, calories 75.
Wash
and
clean
lobster.
Remove
stomach
sack
and reserve tomally, if
desired.
In large saucepan, heat oil and saute garlic and onion until tender but not brown.
Add tomato sauce and
tomatoes;
stir
well, squashing tomatoes slightly. Add the rest of
the ingredients and cook for 20 minutes.
Add lobster to cooking
sauce
and
cook an additional 30 minutes. Serve over linguine,
cooked according to package directions. Makes 4 servings.
Soften cream cheese; mix all ingredients together.
Place in a shallow 9 x 9-inch baking pan or a 1-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in a 350° oven until bubbly and light brown, about 15 minutes.
Serve with crackers or toast.

recipes.t: Stuffed Spinach And Cheese Pasta Shells
d: Squeeze spinach dry.
Transfer spinach to large bowl.
Add Ricotta, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese, basil and garlic to bowl.
Season with salt and pepper.
Blend together.
Preheat oven to 350°. Spoon 1/2 cup marinara sauce evenly over bottom of 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Fill each pasta shell with spinach mixture.
Place shells, filling side up, in dish.
Spoon remaining sauce over shells.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese.
Cover loosely with foil and bake until heated through, about 30 minutes.
Cook and stir broccoli in dressing 2 minutes.
Cook tomatoes in small saucepan over low heat 5 minutes.
Serve over fettuccine. Top with Kraft 100% grated Parmesan cheese, if desired.
Makes 4 servings.

Heat the oil in 12-inch skillet over moderately high heat for 1 minute. Add the sausage and saut, stirring occasionally for 5 minutes. Drain on paper toweling. Reduce the heat to moderate; add the onion in the skillet. Saut, stirring occasionally, for 3 minutes or until softened. Add the garlic and saut, stirring occasionally, for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, lima beans, marjoram and pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook for 10 minutes. Stir in the corn and sausage, then return the mixture to a boil. Cover and cook for 5 minutes or until the lima beans are tender and sausage is cooked through. Serves 4.
In large saucepan, combine tomatoes, tomato sauce, meat, onion, pepper, chili powder, cumin and cayenne pepper.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in kidney beans and simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes.
Garnish with shredded Cheddar cheese, if desired. Serves 6.
In a medium large Teflon frypan, brown meat in very tiny amount of oil (or spray pan with Pam).
Add onion and saute until soft. Add bell pepper; stir a minute and then add entire can tomatoes. Break tomatoes into small pieces.
Add fajita seasoning.
Stir occasionally over medium heat until tomato juice has cooked down and mixture is a thick gravylike consistency.
Serves approximately 4.
Melt water, marshmallows and butter or margarine over low heat until marshmallows are melted.
Bring to a boil and remove from heat.
Add chocolate bits and beat until smooth.
Spread on cooled cake.
Combine flour, sugar and spices.
Pat a little of this in pie crust.
Add some apple slices.
Sprinkle with spice mixture. Continue until pan is full.
Pour molasses over all.
Dot with butter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes at 425°.

Saut carrots and zucchini in margarine in 10-inch skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes. Add tomatoes and juice, mushrooms, water, basil, thyme and kielbasa. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in rice. Cover; remove from heat and let stand 8 minutes, stirring after 4 minutes. Season with hot sauce to taste. Serves 5.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut Crisco into ingredients.
Add eggs, milk and vanilla, making into a soft dough.
Brown ground beef, add seasoning, soup, milk and onions. Layer into greased casserole with chilies and cheese reserving part of cheese for top.
Warm in oven until cheese melts.
Serve over Dorito chips.

recipes.t: Braised Salmon With Roasted Almonds(Makes 4 Servings)
d: In a mini processor, finely grind the almonds. In a large skillet, heat 3 tablespoons of the olive oil. Stir in the almonds, the onion, cilantro, garlic, anchovies and cayenne and season with salt and pepper. Add the salmon to the skillet and spoon some of the almond mixture on top. Season the salmon with salt and pepper and drizzle with a little olive oil. Cover the salmon and cook over moderate heat for 5 minutes. Reduce the heat to moderately low and cook until the salmon is just opaque throughout, 8 to 10 minutes longer.

recipes.t: No Bake Banana Peanut Butter Fudge Bars
d: Melt oleo in large skillet.
Stir in vanilla.
Add oatmeal and brown sugar.
Heat and stir 5 minutes on low heat.
Set aside 1 cup of this mixture.
Press remaining mixture in 9 x 13 pan (sprayed).
Sprinkle banana over top.
Melt chocolate chips and peanut butter together on low heat.
Pour and spread over banana. Sprinkle with reserved oatmeal mixture.
Press down lightly. Chill 2 hours before cutting.
Store in the refrigerator.

recipes.t: Baked Potato Soup(Great On A Cold Night!)
d: Wash potatoes and prick them several times with a fork; bake at 400°
for 1 hour or until done.
Let cool.
Cut potatoes in half
lengthwise
and
then scoop out pulp.
Set pulp aside. Discard
skins.
Melt
butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat; add
flour, stirring until smooth. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually
add
milk; cook over medium heat, stirring
constantly
until
mixture
is
thickened and bubbly. Add
potato
pulp, salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons green onions, 1/2 cup
bacon and 1 cup of cheese.
Cook soup until thoroughly heated, but do not boil.
Stir in sour cream.
Add extra
milk
if necessary for desired thickness. Serve with remaining onions, bacon and cheese.
Mix flour, soda and salt; set aside.
In large mixing bowl, cream margarine and brown sugar until fluffy.
Beat in egg.
Blend in flour mixture at low speed alternately with milk until well blended.
Stir in vanilla and rhubarb.
Turn into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle with remaining sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
May sprinkle with powdered or regular sugar.
Serve with whipped topping, ice cream or just plain.
Melt butter; add flour and seasonings.
Blend well.
Add milk, meat stock and pimentos that have been put through sieve.
Cook 20 to 30 minutes, stirring until mixture thickens.
This makes 10 servings.
In 6-quart pan on a medium stove, pour oil.
Add cardamon, cinnamon and the cloves.
When spicy smells come, add onion and hot pepper.
When onion gets light brown, add ginger and garlic pastes, turmeric powder and salt.
After a few minutes, add water.
Allow the water to boil.
Add the coriander leaves, minced leaves and the rice.
Mix and cover for 7 minutes.
Mix again and put in preheated 300° oven for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and remove all the cardamon, cinnamon, cloves and hot pepper.
Transfer to serving dish.
If you like, garnish with cashew nuts and fried onions and serve it hot.
Dissolve yeast in water.
Heat milk to lukewarm; add oil, honey and salt.
Stir together and add whole wheat flour.
Add yeast and eggs; beat well.
Let rise in warm place 15 minutes. Punch down; add remaining flour and knead for a few minutes.
Pat out to 12-inch square and cut into 2-inch squares.
Place on greased baking sheet.
Cover and let rise in warm place 10 minutes.
Bake 12 minutes at 425°.
Lightly butter 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread 1 cup peanut butter chips evenly over bottom of pan; set aside.
In 2 1/2-quart pan, melt butter; add sugar, corn syrup and water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly to hard crack stage (300° to 310°). Remove from heat; stir in peanuts.
Immediately spread mixture evenly into prepared pan, being careful not to disturb chips. Quickly sprinkle remaining peanut butter chips and chocolate chips over candy.
Cool completely.
(I put it in refrigerator).
Break into small pieces and store in tightly covered container.
In large bowl, combine Eagle Brand milk and water.
Add pudding
mix
and beat well.
Chill for
5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon 2 cups pudding into
3 quart glass bowl; top with half the vanilla wafers, half of the strawberries and half of chocolate chips.
Add remainder
of pudding and repeat layers. Garnish with chips, crushed
wafers and strawberries. Chill 2 to 3 hours before serving.
Combine the hot water and vanilla in a small bowl; stir well. Combine the sugar and cinnamon; stir well.
Brush both sides of tortillas with margarine; brush each side with water mixture and sprinkle each side with sugar mixture.
Place on a wire rack in a jelly roll pan.
Bake at 400° for 6 1/2 minutes or until lightly browned.
Serves 4.
Melt almond bark and peanut butter together in double boiler. Then add other ingredients.
Drop from spoon onto wax paper and let harden.
Slice tomatoes and arrange on a plate.
Peel and slice avocados and arrange on top of tomatoes.
Pour Italian dressing (oil and vinegar type) over tomatoes and avocados.
Season with pepper and salt.
Chill 30 minutes to 1 hour before serving.
Combine soups, cheese and wine in large, shallow baking dish. Add chicken, bone side down.
Cover pan with foil and bake in moderately slow oven at 325° for 2 1/2 hours.
Remove foil.
Add sliced almonds and bake 30 minutes longer.
Serve with rice or mashed potatoes.
Simmer sugar and water over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Chill. Add remaining ingredients.
Blend sugar and spices.
Stir pumpkin and beaten eggs into sugar mixture. Add milk, stirring well.
Pour into pie shell and bake at 425° for 20 minutes. Lower oven temperature to 350°.
Bake 20 minutes longer or until inserted knife comes out clean.
Cut up all fruit and mix with apple juice.
Cream butter and sugar.
Mix well.
Add eggs one at a time, alternating flour.
Add fruit, nuts, and spices.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake 10-15 minutes at 350°.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Grease and lightly flour three 9-inch cake pans. Spread the coconut on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring about every 30 seconds, until the coconut begins to brown slightly. Remove immediately from the pan to prevent further browning. Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Set aside. In another bowl, cream together the butter, sugar, and extracts. Add the egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Combine the flour, baking soda, and salt and stir to mix. Add to the creamed mixture alternately with the buttermilk. Fold in the beaten egg whites and 1 cup of the toasted coconut. Spoon the batter into the prepared pans. Bake for about 25 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted into center of one of the layers. Remove the layers from the pans immediately and cool completely on rack.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Wash shrimp; spread in a single layer in baking dish.
Mix all other ingredients except butter.
Pour over shrimp; dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Stir several times while cooking. Peel when cool enough to handle.
Use French bread for dipping in sauce.
Serves 2.
Great with corn-on-the-cob.

Combine all ingredients except cilantro and rice in large soup pot and heat to boiling. Reduce heat to medium high and cook for about 2 hours or until beans are tender (you may have to add additional water if needed). Add rice and cilantro to soup and cook 5 more minutes.
Saute crabmeat blend with onion and butter.
Add other ingredients and mix.
Allow to cool and serve cold or put into casserole dish and top with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° until heated through.
This can be served hot as a casserole or cold with crackers.
Mix lemon juice with Eagle Brand milk and sugar.
Fold in Cool whip.
Add angel food cake and mix well.
Garnish with grated lemon or lemon slices. Chill at least 4 hours before serving.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Slowly add sugar.
Stir in crushed saltines, dates, pecans and almond flavoring.
Bake in preheated oven at 270° for 1 hour.
The pan must be well-greased. It is best to draw the batter to the outside of the pan.
When cool, cut in wedges.
Serve with a scoop of ice cream.
Drain pineapple, reserving 1/4 cup syrup.
Combine pineapple, reserved syrup, marshmallows and cherries; mix lightly.
Let stand for 1 hour.
Fold in whipped cream.
Sprinkle with almonds and coconut.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix dry ingredients together in separate bowl; add to pumpkin. Add milk, vanilla and butter.
Pour in crust and sprinkle top with cinnamon.
Bake at 350°.
Makes approximately 3 pies.
In large bowl blend yogurt, Fruit Sweet, margarine, applesauce and mashed banana.
Stir in flour and soda.
In separate bowl, beat egg whites until stiff, then fold into batter.
Mix in rolled oats, cereal and raisins.
Spoon into 12 muffin cups which have been sprayed with nonstick coating.
Bake 20 minute at 350° or until firm.
Makes 12 muffins.
Brown meat; drain grease.
Add all ingredients and simmer until onion and pepper are tender.
Serve on toasted hamburger buns.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine cake mix, pudding mix, eggs and sour cream and beat five minutes.
Meanwhile in a small bowl combine nuts, sugar, cocoa and cinnamon.
Alternate, spooning layers of cake batter and topping into greased and floured two quart Bundt pan, beginning and ending with cake batter.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes or until cake tester inserted comes out clean. Let cool 10 minutes; turn out.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
In large casserole dish, combine water and uncooked rice. Stir until rice is evenly mixed in dish.
Place chicken in liquid. Cover chicken and rice with cheese.
Cover with aluminum foil. Cook at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Serves 4.
Mix sugar and cornstarch together.
Blend in remaining ingredients with whisk.
Cook until thickened.
Chill.
Dressing may be served plain or folded into whipped cream for fruit salad. Pineapple, apples, bananas and marshmallows make a good combination.
Preheat toaster oven at 350° for 2 minutes.
Layer one half zucchini into bottom of small casserole.
Cover with one half tomato slices, one half pepper slices and 3 slices cheese.
Repeat layers.
Dot surface with butter.
Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes, or until zucchini is tender.
Serves 6.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix marmalade and butter; spread in 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan.
Stir baking mix and water to a soft dough. Gently smooth dough into a ball on floured cloth-covered board. Knead 5 times.
Roll into 8-inch square; place on marmalade-butter mixture in pan.
Pat evenly in corners; cut into 36 squares.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Invert pan on serving plate.
Biscuits will break off into small bite size pieces.
Serve warm.
Can be baked ahead and reheated.
Place butter, evaporated milk, marshmallows, and morsels in the top of a double boiler.
Heat on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until all ingredients are melted. When mixture is smooth, stir in the vanilla extract.
Place the small pieces of broken graham crackers in a large bowl.
Stir in marshmallow mixture until each piece of cracker is well coated.
Put mixture in a 13x9 inch pan that has been sprayed with cooking spray. Sprinkle the top with remaining marshmallows.
Allow s'mores to set for about 30 minutes before cutting.
Use a warm knife for easier cutting.
Heat oven to 275°.
Spread pecans on ungreased 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake at 275° for 10 minutes.
In medium saucepan, combine sugar, orange juice, cinnamon, salt and cloves.
Bring to a boil; boil 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat; stir in nuts.
Using slotted spoon, remove nuts to foil or waxed paper.
Separate with fork; let dry.
Store in airtight container in cool, dry place.
Makes 4 1/2 cups.
Mix meat, salt and pepper, 1/2 cup rice and egg.
Make small meat balls (set aside).
In a large pot, combine chili sauce, grape jelly and water.
Mix well.
Add meat balls.
Mix cake mix, margarine and 1 egg and press in greased and floured pan (10 x 12-inch).
Then add crushed pineapple, coconut and nuts.
Mix cream cheese, 2 eggs and confectioners sugar.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes in 350° oven until light brown.
Chop the first three ingredients together and saute in 1 teaspoon cooking oil.
Add mushrooms and pimentos.
Cook together until onion and bell pepper become tender.
Add corn and green beans.
Stir until warm.
Decorate with almonds.
Mix milk and pudding together.
Heat on medium heat until just boiling.
Add cake mix and blend until smooth.
Add pecan chips. Pour in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle butterscotch morsels on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Miss Donna'S Quick Seafood Corn Chowder
d: Heat potato soup and butter in saucepan.
Add milk, corn and seafood.
Season to taste with parsley, pepper and lots of Worcestershire.
Combine pineapple and peaches in electric blender.
Process until smooth.
Pour mixture into 9-inch square pan.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Freeze until almost firm, stirring occasionally.
Spoon mixture into container of an electric blender; process until smooth.
Return mixture to pan and freeze until firm. Let stand at room temperature 5 minutes before serving.
Yields 1 quart.
Press softened cream cheese onto large round plate or tray. Sprinkle taco sauce seasoning on top.
Spread bean dip on next. Spoon on picante sauce.
Layer remaining ingredients ending with cheese.
Serve with dip chips.
Mix together 1/2 teaspoon dry mustard, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 cup heavy cream.
Cover bottom of 10 x 6 x 2-inch glass baking dish with the 1/4 pound sliced cheese.
Cover with one half the cream mixture.
Break 10 eggs over this.
Cover with remaining cream mixture.

Sprinkle grated cheese over the top. Bake in slow oven, 325°, for 20 minutes or until cheese melts and eggs set; or cover with Saran and hold in refrigerator uncooked. For morning guests, bring to room temperature, uncover and bake.

recipes.t: Cold Oven Pound Cake A La Gooch
d: Cream together the margarine, shortening, sugar and the flavorings.
Add to the cream 6 eggs, one at a time, thoroughly beating the mixture after adding each egg.
Finally, to mixture, add 1 cup of milk and 3 cups of flour.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour mixture into tube pan.
Place in cold oven and turn oven on to 350°.
Cook 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Let stand in pan 15 minutes; remove and serve hot.
Cream together butter, sugar and egg.
Add bananas.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and nutmeg.
Mix.
Stir in oats and nuts.
Pour in a sheet pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
While warm, glaze with powdered sugar.
Shell and wash peas in a heavy pot.
Cover with water and add salt pork and salt.
Bring to boil, cook on low until tender.
Wash okra and place on top of peas.
Cook for 5 minutes and turn off, leaving okra to steam until fork-tender.
Do not overcook okra as okra will become slimy.
Thaw shrimp if frozen.
Measure 1 1/2 cups flour; set aside. In a 1-quart mixing bowl, combine the remaining 1 1/2 cups flour, milk, baking powder, curry powder and salt.
Place reserved flour and coconut in 2 separate shallow pans.
Dredge shrimp in flour, dip in bowl, then roll in coconut.
Fry in hot oil at 350° until coconut is golden brown.
Drain on paper towel before transfering to warming tray.
Serve hot with Sweet and Sour sauce.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Tail section may be left on for easier handling.
Saute onions, celery and bell pepper until brown.
Add garlic, stewed tomatoes, Ro-Tel tomatoes, salt, pepper and Worcestershire sauce to taste, water, rice and chosen meat.
Let come to a boil. Cover and cook 25 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is reduced.
Place sugar, salt and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and add vanilla. Serve warm.

recipes.t: Orange Gold Cake With Orange Butter Frosting
d: Cream butter and sugar.
Add yolks, one at a time, beating constantly.
Beat in orange rind and juice.
Sift together dry ingredients; add alternately with milk, beating until smooth. Pour into greased and floured spring-form pan.
Bake at 375° for about 1 hour, until done.
Cool; remove from pan.
You make up each package of Kool-Aid using 2/3 cup of sugar in each pitcher of Kool-Aid.
You pour the Kool-Aid in ice trays and freeze it.
After frozen, you put each kind of ice in glass and pour in some Sprite, then drink.
Mix chicken, almonds and celery in bowl.
Combine mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
Blend into chicken and toss lightly.
Yields 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine cheese, flour, cereal, sugar, salt, cayenne, mustard, melted butter and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix with your hands until well blended. Form mixture into one-inch balls and arrange about one inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Use a fork to form a crisscross pattern while pressing balls into disks about 1/4-inch thick. Bake until edges are golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
These freeze well.
In a small bowl mix eggs, onion, bacon, mustard and mayonnaise.
Mix until creamy.
Form into 1-inch balls.
Roll in cheese or parsley-chives.
Arrange on plate.
Garnish with parsley sprigs, cherry tomato halves and or radish roses.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Combine potato, scalded milk (cool to lukewarm) and 1 tablespoon sugar.
Add crumbled yeast and 2 cups flour.
Mix thoroughly.
Add sugar, salt, shortening, eggs and 2 cups flour. Knead lightly.
Place in a greased bowl.
Let rise to double in size.
Shape into 3 (1/2-inch) balls.
Put into muffin tin.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Day 1:
Mix together Cool Whip, sour cream, sugar and about 1/2 cup milk. Refrigerate overnight to give sugar time to dissolve. Will be thin.
Cook macaroni as directed on package; drain.
Meanwhile, in large saucepan over medium heat, brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Stir in cooked macaroni, soup, beans and corn.
Cook until thoroughly heated.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine flour and pepper in a bag for shaking.
Shake each piece of chicken in flour until coated.
Melt butter in baking dish.
Add flour coated chicken to baking dish (skin side down). Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
While chicken is baking, combine soup, mushroom sauce and water in a pan and heat.
After 30 minutes, turn chicken over.
Pour off any remaining butter and cover with gravy.
Bake for an additional 30 minutes at 350°.
Cook broccoli according to package directions, but without salt.
Drain.
Place 3/4 of the broccoli (including all stalks) into your food processor or blender.
Add remaining ingredients and puree until smooth.
(Add reserved broccoli florets and process briefly for a slightly chunky texture.)
Makes 3 guilt-free servings.

Mix together: box of cake mix, crisco, peanut butter, and eggs. Mix well. Roll into small balls and place on cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10-12 minutes. Remove from cookie sheet and cool. Make a cookie sandwich by spreading cream cheese frosting on the flat side of one cookie and topping with the flat side of another.
Combine butter and seasoning. Spread over corn. Yields 8 servings.
Combine sour cream, sugar and orange juice.
Beat in coconut. Cover and refrigerate.
In another bowl, combine cake mix, gelatin, water, oil and eggs, mix well.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9 inch round cake pans.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes.
Remove from pans and cool completely. Split cakes in half, horizontally.
Set aside 1 cup of coconut filling.
Spread remaining filling between cake layers. Refrigerate.
Beat cream until stiff peaks form.
Fold into reserved filling.
Frost top and sides of cake.
Garnish with oranges.
Refrigerate.
In greased 2-quart glass measure, cook sugar, corn syrup and salt on High for 2 to 3 minutes, until boiling.
Cook 4 minutes. Stir in nuts, butter, vanilla and cinnamon.
Cook 2 minutes. Immediately, stir in baking soda until light and foamy.
Quickly, pour onto greased cookie sheet; spread.
Cool; break into pieces. Makes 1 pound.
Line 17 x 11-inch cookie sheet with foil.
Mix sauce ingredients and spread over chicken.
Marinate overnight.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 1 hour.
Trim excess fat from steak.
Crack peppercorns coarsely and mince garlic.
Press peppercorns and garlic into both sides of steak; let stand at room temperature 1 hour.
Make a thick paste of salt and water.
Cover top side of steak with half the mixture. If cooking over coals, cover salt side with a wet cloth or paper towel and place salt side down on grill.
(Cloth or paper towel holds salt in place; will char as steak cooks but will not affect taste.)
Cover the top with remaining salt mix and another piece of towel.
If broiling, put salt side up, 3 inches from heat.
Put salt on other side of steak when turned.
Cook 15 minutes on each side for rare, 25 minutes for medium rare.
Remove salt before eating.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Combine pumpkin, brown sugar, salt, spices and molasses; mix well.
Add eggs and milk; mix thoroughly.
Pour into pie shells. Bake at 425° for 40 to 45 minutes, or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Break Cinnamon Crisp into bite-size pieces.
Spread Cinnamon Crisp pieces, raisins, nuts and sunflower seeds on large greased jelly roll pan, about 15 x 10-inch.
In small saucepan, melt oleo with honey.
Drizzle over graham mixture.
Bake in preheated 250° oven for 45 minutes.
Allow to cool in pan.
Loosen mixture with metal spatula.
Store in airtight jar or container.
Beat margarine until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients (except almonds); mix well.
You can knead this like a dough. Refrigerate 1 hour.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Place 1 1/2-inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Flatten slightly with a lightly floured fork.
Slide slivered almonds into the top of each cookie. Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes to barely light gold.
Makes about 30 cookies.
Grind Spam, cheese and onion together.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Put mixture on hamburger rolls and broil until cheese bubbles or wrap in foil and bake 15 minutes at 400°.
Cook your fresh vegetables, done but firm. Combine soup, Cheez Whiz, milk and seasonings.
Pour over vegetables which were placed in a greased casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Add browned bread crumbs and bake, uncovered, another 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Bake tortillas until crisp, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Increase oven heat to 350°.
Brown meat in a frying pan; drain off any fat and add tomato paste, chilies and tomatoes, half the chopped onion and cayenne pepper.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Layer beef mixture, broken tortillas, remaining onion and cheese three times, in that order, in a 2-quart casserole. Cover and bake 30 minutes.
Serve with lettuce,
tomato and salsa, if desired.
Good with refried beans and fresh corn-on-the-cob.
Serves 4.
Pour cottage cheese on bottom of casserole dish.
Mix hamburg with sweet basil and oregano.
Pour over cottage cheese.
Mix milk, eggs and biscuit.
Pour over hamburg.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Preheat oven to
Cook until crust forms.
About 1 1/2 hours before serving, chop onion.
Peel and slice white and sweet potatoes, keeping in separate piles.

In a nonstick 10-inch skillet with ovensafe handle (or wrap with double thickness of heavy duty foil) in hot salad oil, cook onion until tender. With a slotted spoon, remove onion to bowl and set aside.
In remaining oil in skillet, arrange white potatoes in layer, overlapping slices.
Sprinkle sauteed onions over potatoes.
Dot with 2 tablespoons margarine or butter and sprinkle with 3/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Arrange sweet potato slices over white potato layer.
Dot with butter, salt and pepper, and add onion as with white potatoes.
Continue layers until potatoes run out.
Bring broth to boil over high heat; add carrots and celery. Reduce heat and simmer until vegetables are crisp and tender.
Add peas, corn, chicken and potatoes. Cover and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Stir in macaroni, pepper and parsley. Heat through.
Makes 2 quarts.
Serves 4.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in hot water.
Combine all ingredients and turn into a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until brown.
Make mashed potatoes according to package directions.
Brown ground meat; drain.
Saute onions.
Layer ground meat, green beans and corn.
Pour tomato soup over all.
Top these layers with mashed potatoes.
Sprinkle potatoes with Parmesan cheese. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown around edges and bubbly.
Place 1 slice of pineapple on each lettuce leaf.
Spread each slice of pineapple with cottage cheese.
Add a thick sliced of jellied cranberry sauce.
Top with a dollop of cottage cheese in the center.
Brown sausage and crumble; drain excess fat and cool sausage. Combine all ingredients.
Roll into 1-inch balls.
Place on baking sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes, until puffed and brown.
Cool on wire rack or paper towel.

recipes.t: Aunt Dorothy'S Chicken In Wine Sauce
d: Skin chicken breast, flour and fry in small amount of shortening.
Remove from skillet.
Make gravy with drippings by adding 3 to 4 tablespoons flour.
Mix with drippings, then add about 1 1/2 cups of water.
Stir gravy and cook until smooth.
Chop dried beef and add to gravy, then add remaining ingredients to make sauce.
Stir until well blended.
Place fried chicken in casserole dish.
Pour sauce over chicken.
Cook in oven for 30 minutes at 350°.
Serve over rice.
Cool eggs and push through fine sieve.
Press egg into straight sided glass or jar and refrigerate for several hours. When ready to serve, turn out carefully and slice the same thickness as pineapple.
On salad plate, arrange lettuce cups.
In center, place pineapple slice.
Atop this thick slice tomato dipped in French dressing.
Top with egg mixture.
Use French dressing.
In a large saute pan, heat the oil until hot.
Add the tomatoes and saute over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 30 seconds more.
In a large pot, bring water to boil.
Add pasta and 1 tablespoon of salt.
Cook pasta until tender, but still has some bite.
Remove 1 1/2 cups of the pasta cooking water and pour it over the tomatoes.
Drain pasta and transfer to a large bowl.
Bring tomato mixture to a boil.
Add the pasta, basil, salt and pepper; toss thoroughly and serve at once.
Pass the cheese separately.
Steam green beans 5 minutes.
Heat oil in skillet.
Saute garlic, onion and beans 3 to 4 minutes.
Add tomatoes, parsley, red wine vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper.
Cook for 5 minutes more.
Chill.
Serve at room temperature.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Bring 1 1/2 cups sugar, water and candies to a boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour into a 12 x 18 x 2-inch pan, reserving 1/2 cup for topping. Sift the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar. Cut in shortening thoroughly until particles are fine.
Break egg into measuring cup and add enough milk to measure 2/3 cup.
Beat with a fork to combine. Add to dry ingredients all at once.
Stir until dough clings together in a ball.
Knead lightly on floured board 12 to 15 strokes.
Roll out to a 12-inch square.
Spread with 1 tablespoon melted butter. Cover with the apples. Roll as for a jelly roll. Cut into 8 (1 1/2-inch) slices and place on syrup in pan.

Bake in moderately hot oven at 400° for 30 minutes. Spoon reserved syrup over biscuits, 1 tablespoon on each, and continue baking 10 or 15 minutes longer until golden brown. Serve warm with plain or whipped cream.
Warm crock-pot with water.
Dump water.
Put 1/4 cup barbecue sauce in pot.
Place a layer of chicken pieces in pot.
Salt chicken and cover with sauce.
Place another layer of chicken, salt and sauce as before.
Cook until tender.
Heat oil in a frying pan on high heat.
Mix flour, salt, seasoning salt and Accent in a Ziploc bag.
Then place some of the fish with mixture and shake.
Finally, take out floured fish and place them in hot oil.
Fry until golden brown, or light brown. Last, when done, take out and place in bowl.
(Repeat process until all of fish is done.)
Beat together egg whites, salt and cream of tartar until foamy.
Gradually add sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.
Fold in 1 cup of the coconut and the nuts. Spread in a well buttered 9-inch pie plate, building up the sides.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until
lightly browned.
Cool.
Boil noodles; drain.
Add sausage, seasoning, tomatoes and sliced or diced onion.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; simmer 30 minutes.
Serve hot.

recipes.t: Maduro En Gloria (Ripe Plantains In Heavens)
d: Cut plantains in slanted slices and fry in hot oil until they are golden.
Mix the sugar, cornstarch and ground cinnamon; add milk, shredded cheese and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly.
Grease a Pyrex dish with 1/2 tablespoon of butter.
Pour in half of milk mixture and other ingredients.
Place fried slices of plantain on top.
Cover with remaining milk mixture and dot with butter.
Bake in oven at 350° for 30 minutes or until cheese is just melted.
In 13 x 9-inch pan, buttered, place 1/2 of cubes.
Spoon Mascarpone cheese.
Sprinkle blueberries.
Then add rest of bread cubes, mixed eggs, milk and syrup.
Pour over.
Chill overnight. Bake 350° covered with foil for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake another 30 minutes.
Combine pumpkin, marshmallows, cinnamon and salt in top of double boiler.
Stir constantly until marshmallows are melted. Remove from heat and chill thoroughly.
Whip cream.
Beat pumpkin mixture until fluffy, then fold in whipped cream.
Pour into baked pie shell and refrigerate.
Saute onion in skillet, sprayed with cooking spray, until the onion is browned. Add rice, tomatoes, pesto sauce and beans. Cook until heated. Serves 4.
Heat oven to 400°.
In ungreased 3-quart baking dish, combine hot dogs, beans, ketchup and mustard; mix well.
In medium bowl, lightly beat egg.
Add milk and oil.
Stir in corn meal; mix well. Spoon batter over hot dog mixture.
Spread evenly.
Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes or until light golden brown.
Cook Posoli in water to cover until kernels pop.
Add red chile and pork.
Bring to boil in covered kettle.
Simmer until meat is cooked and corn is tender, at least 3 hours, on low.
Add more water if needed.
Add onion and seasonings.
Cook for 1 more hour.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Put in casserole.
Combine margarine and stuffing mix.
Place on top of casserole.
Bake at 350°
for 30 minutes.
Put a layer of sliced potatoes in baking dish.
Sprinkle chopped onion and place sliced cheese over them with a little salt and pepper.
Repeat layer.
Brown ground beef with onion and green pepper.
Drain excess fat.
Combine all ingredients in large pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer about 5 minutes.
Also, good over spaghetti.
Mix oleo and sugar together; add pretzels and put all in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Smooth with back of spoon to form crust.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Let cool.
Mix Dream Whip following instructions on package.
Mix the Dream Whip and cream cheese until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Pour 1/3 of mixture over the pretzel crust.
Add crushed pineapple.
Pour remaining cream cheese mixture over top. Top with reserved crushed pretzels and/or cherries.
Refrigerate.
Drain syrup from pineapple.
Measure and add enough water to make 2 1/2 cups.
Heat to boiling; remove from heat.
Add lemon and lime gelatins and salt.
Stir until dissolved.
Chill until consistency of unbeaten egg whites, then fold in drained pineapple, cheese and almonds.
Pour into 2-quart ring mold.
Chill until firm.
Turn out onto large plate and tuck lettuce frills under edges.
Serve on lettuce.
Serves 12.
Cook bacon in skillet until crisp; reserve 3 tablespoons drippings.
Crumble bacon and set aside.
Cook lima beans as directed on package; drain.
Heat wok or large skillet until hot. Add bacon drippings and vegetable oil; rotate to coat.
Add onions and corn; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add lima beans, tomatoes and okra; stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add chicken broth, sugar, salt, pepper and crumbled bacon.
Cover; continue cooking a few minutes.
Serve over rice, if desired.
Yields 6 servings.
In large bowl, mix together the cilantro, sausage, red pepper flakes and five spice powder.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and brown the gingerroot and garlic until fragrant and golden.
Add sausage and saute until cooked.
Drain the sausage mixture; arrange a few of the wonton skins on a clean surface.
Use only one skin at a time.
Keep the others covered with a damp towel. Spoon 1 or 2 tablespoons of the sausage mixture onto each skin. Crimp the edges and tie with a length of green onion.
Pierce the bottom of each wonton with a skewer.
In a deep pot, heat about 2 inches of oil.
When the oil is hot enough, drop the wonton into it.
Cook until light and crispy, about 7 to 10 minutes.
Transfer to a paper towel to drain.
Keep warm as you cook others.
Serve immediately with red hot chili only, spicey mustard, honey or soy sauce.
Combine beans, celery, pickle relish, onion and cheese.
Blend seasonings with mayonnaise.
Add to bean mixture and toss lightly. Spoon into 1-quart shallow baking dish.
Sprinkle with corn chips.
Bake at 450° for about 10 minutes.

recipes.t: Chocolate Darlings(Old Fashioned Cookie Recipe; 40 Years Old)
d: Beat first 3 ingredients well.
Add melted chocolate and vanilla.
Mix dry ingredients and add alternately to batter with 1/2 cup milk.
Add dates and nuts.
Mix well.
Drop batter by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Combine chilled grapefruit juice and sugar; chill.
Just before serving, add chilled lemon soda.
Pour in glasses and top with small scoop of lime sherbet.
Makes about 10 cups.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add vanilla.
Mix together dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture.
Drop by spoonfuls onto lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake on top oven rack at 325° for 10 minutes for chewy cookies.
(May want to add a tablespoon or so more flour and bake a bit longer.)
Remove chicken skin.
Pour salad dressing into 13
x 9 x 2-inch
baking pan.
Add chicken, turning to
coat all
sides. Refrigerate 4 hours.
Drain and reserve
dressing. Combine all ingredients.
Dip chicken into egg mixture,
then into
crumb mixture.
Return coated mixture to baking pan.
Spoon remaining dressing over chicken.
Bake in 350° oven for 40
to 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Crumble cookies in bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Spread half the cookies in pan.
Layer with 1/2 the ice cream, 1/2 nuts and 1/2 chocolate syrup or hot fudge.
Repeat layers.
Top with whipped cream and cherries.
Freeze until set and slightly firm. Serve.
Heat oil in a 10-inch skillet over moderately high heat (about 300°).
Add ground beef and cook until lightly browned, stirring occasionally with a fork to break up meat.
Drain off any excess fat.
Sprinkle uncooked noodles over meat.
Mix flour, sugar, eggs and milk.
Cook until thickened, stirring often to keep from sticking.
Add peanuts and vanilla. Pour into cooled baked shell.
Add meringue and brown.
Mix the ground beef with evaporated milk and salt and pepper. Form into 5 large, thin patties.
Make the Stove Top dressing according to package directions, adding 2 tablespoons water.
Put dressing on each patty. Fold meat up around the dressing, leaving a small opening at the top.
Mix mushroom soup, water, catsup and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over top of each bundle.
Bake about 1 hour in a 350° oven. Serves 5.
Peel sweet potatoes and slice 1/4 inch thick.
Cook, covered, in 2 inches of salted, boiling water 10 minutes; drain.
Peel and core apples.
Cut into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Combine brown sugar, butter, ginger and nutmeg.
Sprinkle salt in an iron frypan (do not grease).
Add the chopped meat and brown.
Add onion, green pepper and tomato sauce. Cook until tender.
Sprinkle top with cheese and cover with corn bread (make according to box directions).
Brown beef and onions together (drain).
Mix with macaroni. Add tomato sauce and seasonings.
Toss well.
Top with cheese and pepperoni (optional).
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 375°.
Combine
onion and
water;
let
stand 10
minutes
to soften.
Grease 8-inch round
cake pan.
Prepare hot roll mix according to package directions;
set
aside
5 minutes.
On a floured board, shape dough into 7 inch circle.
Place in pan. Let rise in warm place until
doubled in size, 30 to 60 minutes. Preheat oven to 375°.
Bake until bread is golden brown and sounds hollow when
tapped with fingers, about 25 minutes. Remove from pan; cool on a rack.
Makes 10 slices.
Melt margarine in large skillet and brush up on sides. Sprinkle
the
brown
sugar
over
margarine.
Place pineapple rings over bottom and put cherries in the middle of the rings. Sprinkle
pecans
over all.
Spread the crushed pineapple over the nut layer.

Spread the two pie crusts out on a cookie sheet, lined with aluminum foil. Cut each crust to the shape of a Christmas tree without cutting into the aluminum foil. Sprinkle the spices over the trees and press lightly into the dough with your fingers. Take small bits of the leftover dough and roll into small balls. Place the balls on the trees as you would hang Christmas ornaments. Press slightly into the dough to flatten the balls. Bake the trees at 425° until lightly browned. Cool. Decorate with cream cheese that has been tinted green and place the whole cloves to look like pine cones or branches. Sprinkle on some parsley. The dough that was placed as ornaments can be decorated with white or other colored cream cheese. Yellow cheese, rolled into balls, can be added as extra decorations. Serve with a knife nearby so guests can cut the trees into eating pieces.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt margarine.
Saute red pepper, onion and mushrooms until tender.
Remove from skillet.
In same skillet, brown sausage over medium heat until no longer pink; drain.
Add to mushroom mixture.
In a medium bowl, beat eggs lightly; stir in Monterey Jack cheese and mushroom-sausage mixture.
In another medium bowl, combine broccoli, Ricotta cheese and parsley flakes.
In a large bowl, thoroughly mix shortening and margarine. Then beat in sugar, vanilla and salt until fluffy and light and spreading consistency.
Store covered at room temperature.
In 9 x 13-inch pan, bake cake according to package.
In saucepan, combine sugar and pineapple juice.
Cook until thickened.
Pierce cake.
Pour mixture on top.
Combine pudding and milk.
Beat cream, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Spread as icing over cake.
Refrigerate overnight.
Sprinkle coconut over top before serving.
Mix together corn, Bisquick mix, egg, butter and milk.
Pour half of batter into greased pan (8 x 8-inch).
Cover with shredded cheese.
Pour remaining batter on top.
Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
If using fresh beans, wash and clip ends.
Cover with enough water to boil string beans.
Cut onions and put appropriate seasonings.
Put all other ingredients in except potatoes.
Put potatoes in the last 35 minutes and cook until it's to your liking.
Cover shallow baking pan with foil.
Soak chicken in the teriyaki sauce about 2 hours. Drain well. Drop chicken in mayonnaise and coat both sides of chicken with crumbs.
Place in pan. Bake 15 minutes, turn and continue baking for 15 to 20 minutes or until done and browned.
Combine and mix together the muffin mix, oil, corn, eggs, garlic salt and pimiento.
(Omit the pimiento if your children are like mine and complain of bits of "red" in their corn.)
Pour into an ungreased, 8-inch, round microwave-safe dish.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Cream butter with electric mixer; add sugar slowly.
Cream well; add eggs, slowly, one at a time, beating well.
Add flavoring and mix 2 minutes longer.
Mix rest by hand.
Add fennel seed.
Now add flour and baking powder.
Mix well.
Put by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Toss cabbage, onions and carrots together.
Heat to a boil the sugar, vinegar, mustard and celery salt.
After it is boiling, add salt, pepper and oil.
Do not stir mixture.
Watch it because it will boil over.
Let set 24 hours.
(You don't have to.)
Mix dry ingredients in bowl.
In another large bowl, cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add eggs and beat thoroughly.
Put grated apples, chopped cherries and cherry juice together in a bowl.
Add dry ingredients and apple-cherry mixture alternately, in small amounts, to butter mixture.
Add nuts, raisins and vanilla. Pour into large greased tube pan or 2 loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Check after an hour.
Cream butter and sugar.
Blend in molasses until smooth.
Stir in eggs and beat well.
Dissolve the soda in cup of hot water and stir into molasses mixture.
Sift together flour, salt and spices. Stir gradually into molasses mixture until well blended.
Add raisins.
Bake in greased 8 x 8-inch pan in 350° oven 25 to 30 minutes.
Place potatoes, margarine, onion, green pepper, water, salt and pepper in skillet.
Cover; cook for 20 to 25 minutes.
Stir in cheese and milk; simmer and stir occasionally until cheese melts.
Saute onion in butter until limp but not browned.
Add rest of the ingredients except fish.
Simmer for 5 minutes to combine flavors.
Place fish fillets in a baking dish and bake in a preheated 400° oven for 25 minutes.
Separate cauliflower into flowerets.
Cook 5 minutes in boiling, salted water until tender-crisp.
Drain.
Put in a shallow 2-quart well buttered baking dish.
Heat 1 tablespoon butter in frying pan.
Add red and green pepper and garlic.
Saute 1 1/2 minutes.
Sprinkle over cauliflower.
Mix cornstarch into milk.
Add 2 tablespoons butter to frying pan; stir in milk and custard mixture.
Cook, stirring, until thickened.
Add salt, pepper and cheese.
Stir until cheese is blended in.
Pour over vegetables.
Mix bread crumbs and butter.
Sprinkle on top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Brown cubed steak.
Add ground steak.
Saute onions and garlic.
Add tomato paste and water.
Add cayenne, cumin and jalapeno pepper, then simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hour.
Add dark kidney beans, if preferred.
Simmer, covered, for 5 minutes more.
Combine marshmallows and milk in saucepan.
Cook over low heat until marshmallows are melted, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Soften gelatin in cold water 5 minutes.
Add softened gelatin, salt and vanilla to marshmallow mixture.
Mix well.
Chill until partially set, 30 to 60 minutes.
Beat chilled marshmallow mixture with electric mixer (medium speed) until smooth.
Fold in whipped cream and fruit cocktail.
Put in crust.
Prepare sauce in medium bowl.
Sprinkle dry milk over water. Beat until just blended.
In medium saucepan, melt margarine over low heat.
Blend in flour, salt and bouillon.
Remove from heat. Gradually stir in milk.
Place over medium heat; stir constantly until thickened.
Add mushrooms.
Remove from heat.
On underneath side of each breast, place 1 or 2 slices cheese and 1 slice ham. Spoon 1 tablespoon of sauce over ham.
Fold and secure together. Place in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour 1/2 of sauce over chicken and bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Heat the remaining sauce and serve.
Grease and flour a 14 x 10 x 2-inch cake pan.
Sprinkle 1 cup of chopped nuts and 1 cup of coconut over bottom of pan.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook broccoli until just tender.
Drain and set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and blend in flour. Add milk, cooking and stirring, until thickened.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Beat eggs lightly.
Add some cream sauce to the eggs; blend and add back to the sauce.
Add spices.
Fold in broccoli and pour into a greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Top with saltines and bake 30 minutes.

Reserve liquid and chop meat of steamed clams in coarse bits. Add to these chopped canned clams, divide between 24 half shells. Add teaspoon of liquid to each shell, sprinkle bacon and bell pepper on top and top with grated cheese.
Bake in oven at 400° for 14 minutes.
Place under broiler and brown.
Serve immediately.
Cut beef in small pieces.
Put in 5-quart kettle with onion, celery and seasonings.
Cover with water; bring to a boil and stir to mix well.
Reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook until meat is tender, then add tomato paste and stir; bring to a boil.
Add about 6 cups water; let come to a boil.
Add rice and cook until rice is done, about 1/2 hour.
Combine crumbs and margarine; press into bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, sugar and milk with electric mixer until well blended. Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well.
Stir in nuts; pour over crust.
Return to oven and bake for 45 minutes.
Loosen cake; cool before removing.
Chill in refrigerator.
Drain pineapple and add kiwi; arrange decoratively on top of cake.
Mix vinegar, sugar, oil, pickle juice, salt and pepper.
Heat until sugar melts.
Mix with remaining ingredients.
Chill overnight.

recipes.t: Blue Ribbon Icebox Cookies(My Favorite Cookies And Easy!)
d: Melt shortening.
Add sugars.
Add beaten eggs.
Add spices and vanilla.
Add flour and soda, sifted together.
Add dates and nuts.
Shape into rolls in waxed paper or Saran Wrap.
Refrigerate the rolls until needed.
(Keep indefinitely.)
Slice more than 1/4-inch thick when you slice them.
Bake in 350° oven for about 15 minutes.
Yum!!
Brown onion and potatoes in oil or margarine over medium heat. Add remaining ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Bake pastry shell at 450° for 8 minutes.
Be sure to prick shell before baking.
Saute onion and green pepper.
Arrange a layer of 1/2 the cheese, 1/2 the tomatoes, 1/2 the onion and green pepper mixture and 1/2 the salami into the baked pie shell. Repeat layers.
Beat eggs; stir in milk and remaining ingredients. Pour over layers in pastry shell; bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Reduce temperature to 350°; bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until set.
Melt the chocolate together with the shortening; beat eggs, and sugar gradually, then add flour sifted with salt.
Next add chocolate-shortening mixture, vanilla and nuts.
Turn into two greased shallow pans, 9x13-inch.
Bake in a hot oven 450° about 10 to 12 minutes.
Cut into squares while warm.
May be dusted with powdered sugar while warm.
Brown the beef with diced onion, green pepper, minced garlic and tomatoes.
Add cooked spaghetti (not too done).
You should have approximately 2/3 meat mixture and 1/3 spaghetti.
Mix together all ingredients except chicken and vegetables, until well incorporated.
Add chicken breast and broccoli to mixture.
Place in covered dish and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.
Top with bread crumbs and serve.

Heat oven to 375 degrees. In bowl, mix graham cracker crumbs, flour and baking powder. In mixer bowl, beat sweetened condensed milk and margarine until smooth. Add crumb mixture; mix well. Stir in raisins, coconut and nuts. Drop by tablespoons on lightly greased cookie sheet. Bake for 9 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned. Cool 2 to 3 minutes; remove from cookie sheet. Store loosely covered at room temperature.

Beat butter until creamy; add sugar gradually, mixing well. Beat in egg yolks; stir in almond extract and flour and mix well. Shape into 1-inch logs, using about 1 teaspoon dough for each log. Dip in slightly beaten egg whites; roll in slivered almonds. Place on cookie sheet; bake in preheated 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until light golden brown.
Yield:
about 40 to 50 logs.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix broccoli, soups, 1 cup milk, the ham and onion powder in ungreased baking dish, 13 x 9 x 2-inches.
Mix baking mix and milk.
Pour evenly over soup mixture.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Bake 30 minutes until golden brown.
Let stand at least 5 minutes.
In small bowl combine water, yeast and sugar.
Stir until dissolved.
Set aside.
In large bowl make pudding mix according to package directions.
Add butter, eggs and salt; mix well.
Add the yeast mixture; blend.
Gradually add flour and knead until smooth and the dough is no longer sticky.
Add sprinkles of flour until the dough is soft and silky feeling, but no longer sticky. Place in very large greased bowl.
Cover and let rise until double in bulk (about 1 hour).
Mix shortening and sugars until creamy; add egg.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Mix in sugar and egg mixture; add coconut and vanilla.
Roll in small balls (the size of a walnut).
Dip tops of balls into water, then in colored sugar.
Press them out on ungreased cookie sheet using fork.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Do not overcook!
Remove with egg turner and let cool.
Beat egg whites, water, salt and sugar until ropey consistency.
Add vinegar and continue beating until thick. Cover Pyrex pie plate with waxed paper.
Pour mixture onto plate. Bake for 1 1/2 hours in 300° oven.
Remove from oven and turn upside-down on plate.
When cool, cover with whipped cream and strawberries.
Mix mustard with the garlic, lemon juice and pepper in a bowl. Adjust to taste.
Stir in mayonnaise.
Coarsely chop chocolate in food processor.
Combine chocolate and shortening in microwave-safe dish.
Cook at 50% (Medium) power for 6 minutes until melted smooth.
Stir at 2 minute intervals. Combine chocolate with remaining ingredients. Mix well.
Drop by teaspoon on waxed paper.
Let cool completely; store in airtight container.
Yields approximately 5 dozen.
Heat vinegar, sugar and butter in a saucepan.
Beat eggs and flour until smooth.
Pour in vinegar mixture until it starts to boil.
Stir until it thickens.
Chill.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add mayonnaise and mustard to cabbage when ready to serve.
Lightly spray 9-inch pie plate with nonstick cooking spray or grease lightly.
Combine oats, flour, melted margarine and brown sugar, mixing well.
Cream butter, gradually add sugar; add eggs.
Combine dry ingredients; add to cream mixture, alternating with milk.
Stir in lemon rind, fold in berries and pour in loaf pan.
Bake for 55 minutes at 350°.
Combine pie filling mix, milk, butter and chips in saucepan. Cook and stir the mixture over medium heat until mixture comes to a full bubbling boil.
Remove from heat.
Cool 5 minutes, stirring twice.
Pour into pie shell.
Place plastic wrap lightly over pie to avoid skin from forming.
Refrigerate 3 hours.
Garnish with whipped topping and grated chocolate.
Melt butter in 4-quart pot.
Stir in onions and cabbage.
Heat 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and simmer another 10 minutes.
Stir in veggies, tomatoes and seasonings. Simmer 10 minutes.
If using frozen or fresh veggies, simmer until tender.
Place drink mix in nonmetal bowl.
Add milk, stir to dissolve. Sprinkle gelatin over water in glass measuring cup.
Let stand 2 minutes to soften.
Microwave on High for 40 seconds.
Stir well. Let stand 2 minutes or until completely dissolved.
Gradually stir into milk mixture.
Let stand 15 minutes or until slightly thickened.
Stir in whipped topping.
Pour into dishes. Refrigerate 2 hours until firm.
Garnish with mandarin oranges. Makes 8 servings.
Mix thoroughly 1/2 cup soup, beef,
bread crumbs, egg, carrots, onions, salt, pepper and thyme.
Shape firmly into loaf. Place in shallow baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until done.
In saucepan, blend remaining soup, water and 2 tablespoons of drippings.
Heat.
Stir occasionally.
Serves 8 to 10.
Cook 6 potatoes in water with 1 onion and reserve at least 3/4 cup water when potatoes cooked.
Mash potatoes with 2 egg yolks and cooked onion.
Take 3/4 of mixture and line bottom of casserole dish.
Place cooked vegetables on top of potatoes.
Cook together 3/4 cup potato water, milk, butter and flour to boiling until thickened and pour over vegetables.
Place remaining potatoes over this mixture and sprinkle top with shredded cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine chicken, mushrooms, sauce, salad dressing and onion.
Mix lightly.
Top muffin halves with chicken mixture and broccoli.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake for 10 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Continue baking until cheese begins to melt.
Make 6 sandwiches.
Mix rice with 3 cups wate rand dry onion soup.
Line bottom of 9 x 11-inch glass pan with rice mixture.
Layer chicken over this. Cover with cream of mushroom soup.
(Optional:
Add fresh mushrooms.)
Bake 1 hour and 45 minutes at 350°.
Add water, so rice won't dry out, if needed.
Mix mayonnaise, onion, sugar and vinegar together and pour over broccoli flowerets.
Toss and add bacon bits.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cream the margarine; add
sugar.
Add
egg, vanilla and nuts.
Add other dry
ingredients
alternately
with
milk. Bake
in
a greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan at 350° for 50 minutes.
Frost with butter
and confectioners
sugar
frosting (make with canned, unsweetened milk).
Place 1/2 nut meat on each piece of cake.
In bowl mix cabbage and noodles.
Brown sliced almonds in oil.
Mix salad oil, sugar and seasonings.
Mix and toss all ingredients together.
Chill overnight.
Beat yolks with salt until thick.
Gradually add sugar; beat until thick and puffy.
Add hot milk; mix.
