Cut off roots and stem ends of onions.
Using a sharp knife one should make a deep "X" on top of each onion, cutting halfway down. Place each onion on a 6 x 6-inch piece of aluminum foil with "X" up.
Bring up corners of each square.
Top each with 1 teaspoon olive oil.
Twist foil together tightly to completely enclose onions.
Place twist up on a large baking sheet.
Bake 40 minutes at 350° until tender.
Have the butcher bone the ham.
Combine fruit and wine in large mixing bowl; soak at least 4 hours, stirring occasionally. Fill the cavity of the boned ham with stuffing.
Bake in 350° oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Set a mixing bowl in a basin of simmering water.
Add the chocolate and the coffee; heat, stirring often, until chocolate is blended and melted.
Combine the yolks, salt and sugar in another bowl.
Set the bowl in a basin of simmering water and beat the yolk mixture rapidly with a wire whisk.
Beat until it falls in a "ribbon" when the whisk is lifted.
Spoon the chocolate into the yolk mixture.
Return the bowl to the simmering water and continue beating.
Gradually add the butter; beat.
Remove the bowl from the heat.
Continue beating until the mixture thickens and becomes spreadable.
Add walnuts.
Cool.
Spread over the 2 cakes. Decorate with the 12 large walnuts.
Sift flour and salt.
Combine butter and sugar and mix thoroughly.
Add vanilla and eggs.
Beat well.
Stir in bran flakes and raisins.
Add flour mixture and stir thoroughly.
Spread in a well-greased 9 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Cool in pan on wire rack.
Frost with your favorite icing. Let stand until set.
Cut into bars.
Beat egg whites and add sugar gradually.
Add the salt and vanilla.
Fold in carefully the dates and nuts.
The mixture will be quite stiff.
Then drop from teaspoon upon a well-greased cookie sheet.
Place a candied cherry on top.
In a deep skillet heat oil; stir in rice, stirring occasionally until rice is golden (2 to 3 minutes).
Stir in chicken broth and ginger root.
Continue until mixture comes to full boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover; continue cooking until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in all remaining ingredients except onion.
Continue cooking until shrimp turns pink, stirring occasionally.
Stir in onion and cook 2 to 3 minutes, then serve. Yields 5 to 6 servings.
Combine veggies in saucepan with water; boil until veggies are 2/3 cooked.
Drain excess water.
Add meat, milk and cream to saucepan; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add cornstarch to thicken. Season to taste.
Brown
ground
beef, onion and pepper. Drain meat.
Put in bottom
of ovenware dish. Place Cheddar cheese soup, then onion soup,
then
mushroom
soup
on top of meat. Stick Tater Tots on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes or until Tots are brown and mixture bubbly.
Combine margarine, sugar and softened cream cheese, mixing until well blended.
Blend in eggs, lemon juice and rind.
Add combined dry ingredients; mix well.
Chill for several hours. Shape level tablespoons of dough into balls.
Place on greased cookies sheet; flatten slightly, indent centers and fill with preserve.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
When cool, sprinkle with confectioners sugar, if desired.
Yields 6 dozen.
Cut lobster into bite size pieces; toss in flour.
Saute in butter for 3 minutes.
Add wine; cook for 1 minute.
Add cream, salt and pepper.
Add egg yolks and stir.
Cook just under boiling point until thick.
If allowed to bubble, Newburg may break.
Serve on golden brown toast.
Blend sherbet, limeade and vanilla ice cream until smooth, about 1 1/2 minutes.
Add milk; blend 30 seconds.
Pour into chilled glasses.
Top each with scoop of sherbet or vanilla. Serve immediately.
Yield:
5 cups.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together flour, baking powder and baking soda; set aside.
In a large mixer bowl, beat margarine or butter with an electric mixer on medium to high speed until fluffy. Add sugars and beat until combined.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating 1 minute after each addition.
Add flour mixture and sour cream to egg mixture alternately, beating after each addition, just until combined.
Fold in sausage and berries.
Mix crumbs and butter.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix condensed milk and coconut.
Spread over crumb mixture.
Bake 15 minutes longer.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Spray large shallow metal roasting pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Cut potatoes into 1-1/2 inch chunks; place in pan.
Drizzle 1 tablespoon oil over potatoes; toss to coat.
Bake 10 minutes.
Cut bell peppers into 1-1/2 inch chunks. Cut onion through core into 1/2-inch wedges.
Add bell peppers and onion to pan.
Drizzle remaining 1-1/2 teaspoons oil over vegetables; sprinkle with garlic, salt and black pepper.
Toss well to coat.
Return to oven; bake 18 to 20 minutes or until vegetables are browned and tender, stirring once.
Transfer to large serving bowl.
Drizzle vinegar over vegetables; toss to coat.
Add basil; toss again.
Serve warm or at room temperature with additional black pepper if desired.
Serves 6.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar and oleo in bowl.
Mix well. Reserve 1/2 cup crumbs.
Spread remaining in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Pour milk over this.
Sprinkle with chocolate chips and nuts.
Top with reserved crumbs.
Cream the butter, gradually adding sugar and beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt. Repeat sifting and add to creamed mixture alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour.
Mix just until blended.
Gently stir in pecans and vanilla.
Spoon batter into greased loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until cake tests done.
Cool in pan 10 minutes.
Remove from pan and cool completely on a wire rack.
Cook broccoli according to directions.
Place broccoli and sausage in bottom of 2 pie crusts.
Mix evaporated milk, water, eggs and milk together; set aside.
Combine flour, cheeses, salt and pepper and put over sausage.
Pour in milk-egg mixture.
Bake 45 minutes or until browned at 350°.
Sift flour and salt into a bowl.
Add shortening and cut it in with 2 knives or a pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle in the water.
Mix lightly.
Turn out onto a pastry board and shape in a ball.
Roll dough 1/8-inch thick into an 18 x 12-inch rectangle.
Cut into 6-inch squares.
Peel apples and core.
Place in center of pastry square.
Mix sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Pour into center of each apple.
Pat with oleo.
Bring points over apples and press edges together.
Brush surface with milk.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until apple is tender.
Cut jicama into thick julienne strips.
Combine jicama and red onions in serving bowl.
Combine remaining ingredients in a covered jar; shake to mix.
Pour dressing over jicama and toss.
Serving size:
1/8 recipe.
Calories:
Protein:
1 g. Carbohydrates: 8 g. Total Fat:
1 g. Saturated:
Trace.
Cholesterol:
0 mg. Fiber:
less than 1 g. Sodium:
5 mg.
Diabetic Exchange:
2 vegetables.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes and soup.

Layer half of the mixture in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish. Dot with half of the butter and sprinkle with half of the cheese. Repeat layers. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
Yields 12 servings.

Cut marshmallows in quarters; put into double boiler; add orange juice and cook until marshmallows are thoroughly dissolved. Chill slightly; pour into sherbert glasses; chill in refrigerator and serve with whipped cream.
Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place roast in roasting pan with cover. Sprinkle onion soup mix all over the roast.
In bowl, mix mushroom soup, 1 can water, chopped onion and jar of mushrooms; stir until well combined.
Pour over roast.
Cover; place in oven for 1 hour. After 1 hour, remove from oven and turn roast over, then place potatoes all around.
Cover and return to oven 1 more hour.
Remove and serve with carrots, corn or my favorite green beans.
Serves 4 to 5.
Heat oven to 350°.
Arrange chicken in pan.
Dot with butter, cover with foil and bake for 30 to 40 minutes.
While chicken bakes, saute sliced mushrooms, sliced green onions, 2 tablespoons butter, 2 to 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic salt.
Spoon sauteed mixture over cooked chicken.
Top with Provolone cheese and bake again for 5 to 8 minutes or until cheese melts.
Serve it up and enjoy!
Slice bread and let it set out overnight.
Mix cream cheese and feta.
Spread over bread slices.
Chop tomatoes very fine. Spread on top of cheese covered bread.
Top each bread slice with 1/2 Calamata olive.
Makes a great presentation on a tray.
Place
onions
in
hot oil about 10 minutes, keep stirring. Add basil leaves, pepper and salt to taste.
Add 2 cups plum tomatoes after onions are limped.
Add water and bring to a
boil. Simmer 1/2 hour.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese and add 2 beaten eggs last.
Pour them slowly; when cooked, serve hot.
Chill mixture in refrigerator until thick but not firm.
Whip 2 packages of Dream Whip with 1 cup milk, then add pineapple mixture to Dream Whip and blend.
Tear angel food cake into 1-inch pieces or smaller.
Line large mixing bowl with Saran Wrap, then put layer of cake, layer of pineapple mixture.
Repeat, adding layers (3 or 4 layers of each) ending with layer of mixture.
Chill until firm, then turn cake upside down.
Remove Saran Wrap and frost with 1 package of Dream Whip.
Cover with coconut.
Keep refrigerated until served.
Cut dried beef.
Reserve 1/4 cup for topping.
Brown remaining beef and onion in drippings and drain.
Melt butter; add flour and blend together.
Gradually add the milk.
Cook slowly, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Combine dried beef, onion, macaroni and cheese sauce and pour into a greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Top with 1/4 cup dried beef.
Bake in 300° oven for 45 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine all ingredients except sunflower seeds.
Refrigerate until firm enough to handle.
Form into a ball and roll in sunflower seeds.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. Makes 1 cheese ball.
Roll 8 to 10 green beans in 1/2 slice of bacon and secure with a toothpick.
Combine other ingredients and pour over green beans. Marinate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut off crust of bread.
Roll bread with rolling pin until very flat.
Mix Ricotta cheese with egg.
Spread 2 teaspoons Ricotta cheese on each slice of bread.
Roll up jelly roll style. Dip in butter.
Roll in cinnamon sugar.

recipes.t: Hot Squash Casserole(A Country Thanksgiving At The Lamars)
d: To prepare:
Cook squash, green pepper and onion until tender. Drain and mash.
Add cheese and tomatoes.
Place in buttered 2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle broken tortilla chips on top. Bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until bubbly.
Brown stew beef in large pot (no fat or oil, no flour).
When meat is brown, add water to cover, bouillon, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper and onion; simmer until meat is nice and tender (several hours).
Add potatoes, carrots and any other veggies; cook until done.
Mix cornstarch and water; put into stew to thicken, if desired.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine shortening, 1/3 cup sugar, salt and boiling water. Let cool to lukewarm.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add flour and egg.
Mix well and add to shortening mixture.
Refrigerate for 3 hours.
Shape into walnut size balls.
Blend remaining sugar and cinnamon.
Dip balls into sugar mixture.
Layer in rows in tube pan.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Bake at 475° for 40 minutes.
Mix first 3 ingredients together and pour into cooked pie crust.
Top with whipped cream.
Let set, in refrigerator, at least 3 hours before eating.
Mix together the first 4 ingredients and let set.
Mix together at room temperature cream cheese, sour cream, Cool Whip and marshmallows.
Mix well and leave at room temperature, creaming occasionally, until marshmallows are melted.
Shortly before serving, spread cream mixture on Jell-O and sprinkle with nuts.
Mix sausage, flour and Worcestershire sauce until blended. Form balls and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown.
After browning, you can keep these in freezer bags and freeze for later use.
These are good at breakfast or anytime.
Delicious just to snack on.
Enjoy!
Blend until smooth the soup, cream cheese, garlic powder and Tabasco sauce. Fold in tuna and parsley. Refrigerate 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Dip the chicken in the eggs.
Place the bread crumbs in a shallow bowl; coat the chicken with the crumbs. In a large skillet, heat the oil until moderately hot.
Place the chicken in the frying pan and brown lightly on both sides.
Remove from the pan and place in a baking dish.
Top each breast with a slice of cheese.
In a saucepan mix together the heavy cream, Parmesan cheese, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cook until mixture is hot and has thickened.
Pour over chicken and bake for 25 minutes or until cheese is melted.
This is great served over pasta.
You can put the whole dish together and put it aside in the refrigerator for a day or two, then 30 minutes before ready to serve, bake it.

In small bowl, combine salt, turmeric, mustard seed, celery seed, allspice, vinegar and sugar. Mix cucumbers and onions in microwave-safe bowl. Pour vinegar mixture over and cook, uncovered, on HIGH for 5 minutes. Stir well. Cook for 5 minutes more. Cool. Pour into a sterilized quart jar. Refrigerate.
Combine sugar and butter and cream until smooth.
Add eggs and beat well.
Sift cinnamon, allspice, cloves, flour, soda and salt together.
Dust walnuts and dates with a small amount of flour mixture.
Add remaining flour mixture alternately with the beer to creamed mixture; blend well after each addition.
Stir in walnuts and dates.
Peel and cut squash or eggplant into large strips (like large french fries).
Soak in 3 tablespoons salt water.
The longer you soak them, the better, but at least 15 minutes before frying.
Mix 1 egg, salt, pepper and sugar to taste; then mix well 1 cup biscuit mix and 1/2 cup milk.
Dip squash or eggplant in egg mixture; then into biscuit mix and deep fry.
Del-ici-ous.
Combine first 5 ingredients and marinate in sugar, oil and vinegar mixture.
Refrigerate overnight.

recipes.t: Nutty Squares(This Recipe Is Very Good.)
d: In a large bowl, mix oleo, sugar, flour, vanilla and egg yolk. Spread mixture onto a large greased cookie sheet until about 1/4-inch thick.
Moisten top of dough with unbeaten egg white. Sprinkle with brown sugar and nuts.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes.
Cut into squares while still warm.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown sausage in frying pan; drain grease.
Line Dutch oven with foil and grease foil.
Line bottom of foil with 1/2 the bread pieces (remove crust if desired). Next, layer with 1/2 of the eggs (beaten).
Layer with 1/2 of sausage, onion and green pepper.
Layer with 1/2 of the cheese. Repeat all the layering, ending with the cheese.
Bake approximately 1 hour.
Put gelatine in 1/2 cup cold water.
Stir until it is the consistency of a soft pudding.
Brown beef and onion.
Drain.
Mix in bowl the soups, milk, chili sauce, peppers, olives and browned beef.
In wide casserole, layer tortillas, beef mixture and cheese.
Start with tortillas and end with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes uncovered and 10 minutes covered.
Combine marshmallows, evaporated milk and orange juice in a small bowl.
Combine graham cracker crumbs and spices; mix well. Stir in coconut, fruits and nuts.
Add liquid mixture.
Press together until moist and sticky.
Mix sugar, milk, margarine and cocoa and boil 3 minutes.
Add salt, vanilla and oats.
Cool slightly.
Add walnuts and/or coconut.
Drop by spoonfuls on waxed paper.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Brown beef and drain. Add potatoes, water, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 30 minutes. Add onions and Worcestershire sauce. Uncover and continue cooking for 15 minutes or until thick as desired.
Boil potatoes and onion with just enough water to cover.
When tender, add peas (do not drain) and corned beef chopped into chunks; heat through.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cook noodles according to directions. Set aside.
Pound chicken breasts flat.
Dip breasts in water, shake off, then place in bread crumbs to coat.
Brown both sides in frying pan with oil. Remove and set aside. In a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer noodles, chicken and spaghetti sauce.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Delicious!
Heat oven to 350°.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Crumble turkey into skillet, stir in green onions, garlic and seasoned salt.
Cook until turkey is no longer pink, stirring to finely break up turkey; drain.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix cream cheese and sour cream in medium bowl, stir in turkey mixture, olives and Tabasco sauce.
Spoon mixture evenly into pie plate, 9 x 1/4-inch.
Sprinkle with almonds; bake until hot and bubbly, about 15 minutes.
Spread on bread slices.
Makes 12 to 14 servings.
Boil 3 cups water and dissolve Jell-O.
Add remaining 3 cups of water. Stir lemonade until melted. Combine lemonade and cranberry juice. Freeze this mixture in a freezer bag.
A few hours before serving, remove from freezer (should be slushy). Just before serving, add 7-Up and sherbet.
Makes 12 to 15 servings.
Mix cottage cheese and dry jello.
Fold in Cool Whip and pineapple.
Serve chilled.
Cream oleo.
Beat egg with orange juice, rind, sweetener and vanilla.
Add to oleo.
Reserve 1 tablespoon flour.
Sift the remaining flour with salt, baking powder and soda.
Add to egg mixture.
Add sour cream.
Mix reserved flour with the nuts and raisins.
Stir into batter.
Drop by tablespoon on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Fry sausage.
Melt cheese into sausage.
Add onions and seasonings; stir thoroughly.
Spread on party rye.
Place on cookie sheets and freeze 24 hours.
Combine eggs, sugar, butter, milk, pumpkin, biscuit mix and cinnamon in blender.
Cover and blend at low speed for 3 minutes. Pour into a greased 9-inch pie plate or quiche pan.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Bake on a cookie sheet for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle top with granola and continue to bake for another 20 minutes or until center feels firm.
Cool on wire rack.
Serve with vanilla ice cream.
Saute first 4 ingredients until meat is brown.
Remove from heat.
Add rice.
Salt and pepper heavily.
Layer sliced cabbage and meat mixture in a 2-quart casserole.
Pour V-8 juice over top. Cover and cook in a 350° oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Cook pasta in boiling, salted water until just tender, following package directions; drain.
Mix yogurt, lemon juice, sugar and a pinch of salt together.
Whip cream until stiff and stir into yogurt mixture.
Combine cheese, walnuts, fruits, pasta and yogurt mixture in bowl.
Separate endive into leaves, then tear into pieces.
Arrange endive pieces on 4 salad plates.
Spoon pasta salad on top and serve.
Cut chicken breasts into bite size chunks and stir-fry in olive oil until done (only a few minutes).
Leftover chicken may also be used.
Chop celery, snow peas and any other vegetables.
Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Serve at once or chill.
Adjust amount of ingredients to suit number of guests.
Combine cake mix, oil and mandarin oranges with liquid.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Mix well for 2 minutes.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake in preheated oven at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool completely.
In large saucepan, heat oil.
Add onion and saute over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add water and bouillon cubes.
Heat to boiling, stirring occasionally, until cubes are dissolved. Gradually add noodles and salt so that bouillon mixture continues to boil.
Cook, uncovered, for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in broccoli and garlic powder.
Cook 4 minutes more.
Add milk, cheese and pepper and continue cooking until cheese melts, stirring constantly.
Yield:
Makes about 4 quarts or 12 servings.
Cream margarine, sugar, vanilla and almond flavoring.
Beat in egg.
Sift dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture.
Chill at least 1 hour.
Divide into thirds, roll and cut in shapes.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet on upper oven rack at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes or until very lightly browned on bottom of cookies.
Let set on cookie sheet a few minutes before removing.
Do not overbake.
Frost when cool.
Melt butter; saute onion, green onion, bell pepper, tomato and shrimp or crawfish until cooked.
Add cooked rice and mix; put in a casserole dish.
Bake at 450° until bubbly and turn off heat.
Mix first 8 ingredients in a large bowl.
In a 2 cup measure, mix milk, applesauce and egg.
Combine liquid and dry ingredients, mixing just to combine.
Batter will be lumpy.
Fill muffin cups that have been sprayed with cooking spray, 3/4 full.
Bake for 20 minutes at 425°.
Muffins should be golden brown.
For children under 4, omit raisins.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Coarsely chop walnuts and sprinkle nuts in bottom of pan.
Mix cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, water, oil and rum.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Remove cake and let cool before placing on serving plate.
Cube
meat and brown
along
with
onion.
Add
water, ketchup, salt and pepper.
Add carrots. Cook about 30 minutes. Add potatoes
and a bit of cornstarch; cook until all vegetables
are tender and a thick consistency has been established. Cut a thin crust for top and bake until crust is done.
Cream butter and brown sugar together.
Sift the flour, soda, salt, cinnamon and cocoa.
Mix in the applesauce.
(Raisins may be added.)
Bake in greased pan at 350° for 45 minutes.
Dissolve jello in boiling water; add 3/4 cup cold water and mix well.
Chill to egg white consistency. Stir in 3 cups peaches, 1 tablespoon sugar, sliced banana and chopped pecans. Pour into 8-cup mold and
chill
until set.
Soften Knox gelatine in 3 tablespoons cold water.
Scald the half and half and stir into gelatine.
Beat
remaining
ingredients together and join with
half and
half
mixture.
Pour
the well-blended mixture over the jello and chill at least 8 hours.
Heat oven to 325°.
Lightly grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
In a large bowl, beat eggs, oil and vanilla until well blended.
Beat in flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda and salt. When completely mixed, batter will be very thick.
Stir in nuts and apples.
In a medium bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks.
Combine chicken, celery, grapes, almonds, parsley, salt and mayonnaise with whipped cream, folding well.
Chill.
Just before serving, mound chicken salad in center of a pretty plate lined with fresh lettuce and garnish with more grapes.
In 6 quarts of water, cook bones, onion, celery and salt until tender.
Peel off meat from bones.
Discard bones (or give to your dog).
Add shredded cabbage, tomatoes, basil, pepper, parsley and garlic.
Cook until cabbage is tender, adding water as necessary (about 1 hour).
Add veggies; cook until tender.
Enjoy!

Have all cheese at room temperature. Grate the Cheddar cheese and the sharp cheese. Add the soft cream cheese, Blue cheese and the horseradish. Mix well with hands or a big mixer. Roll into large ball. Use wax paper or counter top. Spread pecans (chopped fine) and roll the cheese ball until well covered. Use your thumb and make dent in top of the cheese ball. Put a red cherry in it.
Saute broccoli in olive oil 2 to 3 minutes.
Add next four ingredients and simmer 5 minutes.
Reduce heat and add crumbled Feta.
Heat, do not boil.
Toss with 8 ounces cooked pasta. Serves four.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add bell pepper; saut 4 minutes.
Add tomatoes; reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add pasta and black pepper, stirring well.
Place about 1 1/2 cups pasta mixture into each of 4 bowls; top each.
Serving with 1 tablespoon basil and 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.
Serve with Caesar salad and bread.
Place shrimp in baking dish.
Melt butter; pour over shrimp. Sprinkle with garlic powder, onion powder, Parmesan cheese and Mozzarella cheese.
Cover with marinara sauce.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes in 400° oven.
Enjoy!
In greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish, stir uncooked macaroni, milk, Worcestershire sauce, salt and 1 1/2 cups of the cheese until well blended.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake in 350° oven for 50 minutes.
Uncover and top with remaining cheese and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake 10 minutes more or until cheese is melted.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Combine sugar, lemon juice, chopped onion, dijon mustard& salt in blender.
Blend for 5 seconds, while still blending open jar lid and pour in the oil slowly and then the poppy seeds.
You can make this the day before the salad.
For salad mix all ingredients in large bowl.
Pour dressing over salad just before serving.
Put dry Jell-O into cottage cheese.
Mix.
Add Cool Whip, drained fruit and nuts.
May be chilled or used right away.
Bake and cool pie shell as package directs; set aside.
In 3-quart saucepan combine pudding mix and milk.
Cook and cool for pie, as package directs.
Pour into cooled crust.
Chill several hours until set.
Spread 1 cup of whipped topping over filling. Arrange strawberries and blueberries on top.
Pipe or dollop with remaining whipped topping.
Just before serving, dust with powdered sugar.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients but margarine.
Pour into pie shell and dot with margarine, then put top on pie.
Cut slits and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Bake at 425° for 35 to 50 minutes.
Cut biscuits in 1/2.
Roll into soft balls.
Bake on a greased cookie sheet as directed on can.
Melt butter.
Mix all remaining ingredients; stir and pour over hot rolls.
Chop the cabbage in large pieces.
Preboil until tender, about 8 minutes.
Drain the cabbage.
Make 2 cups white sauce, then add the cheese.
Stir until the cheese is melted.
Pour over the drained cabbage, stirring slightly to blend.
Place the cabbage mixture in a sprayed or buttered 2-quart casserole dish.
Pour the melted margarine on top of cabbage mixture.
Sprinkle the crushed crackers on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix cake mix as directed.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch sheet cake pan.
Pour half the batter in pan.
Spread evenly.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Melt Kraft caramels with milk and margarine. Pour caramel mixture over cake.
Sprinkle chocolate chips and chopped pecans over caramel mixture.
Add small amount of coconut, if desired.
Pour remaining batter into pan.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Cool before serving.
Combine sugar, Karo syrup, water and butter in 2-quart glass container; microwave on full power for 17 to 18 minutes, until mixture reaches 270° (hard-ball stage).
Remove from oven and add the raw cashew bits.
Return to oven and cook 5 to 6 minutes longer, until mixture reaches 300° (brittle stage).
Stir in coconut, vanilla and soda.
This temperature is very important as the brittle will remain sticky if this temperature is not reached. Pour onto buttered platter, working quickly.
Cool partially by lifting edges with spatula so mixture won't stick.
When firm, but still warm, turn over.
Pull as thin as desired at this point. When cool, break into pieces and store in airtight container. Makes 2 pounds.
Roll out 1 loaf of bread dough to fit a lightly oiled jelly roll pan.
Brown beef, onions and mushrooms.
Drain.
Spread on dough.
Sprinkle with olives, cheese, salt and pepper; pour sauce over all.
Roll out other loaf of bread dough and top, pinching edges.
Put holes in top and bake at 375° until brown, about 30 minutes.
In a heavy 2-quart saucepan, bring sugar, sour cream or yogurt and oleo to a boil.
Cook to a soft ball stage, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and add vanilla and cinnamon. Stir until mixture begins to thicken.
Add nuts and stir until well coated.
Turn out onto buttered cookie sheet.
Separate into clusters, individual nuts or small pieces.
Makes 1 1/2 pounds.
Place sliced
quince
in water quickly after slicing to prevent darkening. Drain
and
place
in
kettle
with 2 cups water.
Cook,
covered,
until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes. Add sugar and boil on high heat to thicken syrup.
Add vanilla and lemon juice
quickly.
Stir 2 or 3 times and boil for 3 or 4 more minutes.
Stir in almonds until evenly distributed and quickly remove
from heat. Cool, then place in glass containers for refrigerator or canning jars for storing.
Cut bread in half lengthwise.
Hollow out both pieces of bread and set removed portions aside.
Melt butter over low heat.
Add pieces of bread that were set aside and cook until golden.
At the same time, also add garlic and sesame seed.
When it turns golden, remove from heat.
Now add sour cream, Monterey Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, parsley and 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese.
Combine apricots and water, let set 10 minutes; drain well. Sift together dry ingredients.
Beat butter, sugar, fruit rinds, eggs and lemon juice together until fluffy.
Combine flour and butter mixtures with sour cream.
Fold in apricots, candied fruits and nuts.
Drop onto greased cookie sheet 1 1/2 inches apart. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix pudding.
Fold in pineapple, then Cool Whip, coconut and nuts.
Chill until firm and serve.
Melt 1 stick margarine and mix with 2 cups crushed vanilla wafers.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Beat other stick of margarine and 1 cup sugar until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time and beat for 5 minutes.
Add 1 tablespoon vanilla and beat. Smooth over crumbs in pan.
Drain pineapple and spread over topping.
Slice bananas and add to top of pineapple.
Cover with Cool Whip, add 1/4 crushed wafers and then add chopped nuts. Refrigerate overnight.
Cream butter until very soft.
Gradually beat in some of the sugar.
Add the egg white and salt; mix well.
Then, slowly add remaining sugar while stirring.
Thin, if necessary, with cream. Divide into small portions; color each portion as desired.
This frosting is put through a pastry tube.
In large skillet melt 1/2 cup butter or margarine.
Add livers, onions, apple, thyme, salt and pepper.
Cook about 10 minutes until livers are grayish-brown and onions are soft.
Spoon mixture into food processor or blender container and process until smooth.
Cut remaining butter or margarine into 4 pieces.
Add with brandy to livers; process until smooth.
Spoon into 4 1/2 cup mold or tureen. Cover and chill.
(Can be made ahead to this point.)
Wrap well and freeze up to 1 month.
Thaw in refrigerator about 24 hours.
I separate the boiled eggs for the garnish.
Chopped yellows around outside, chopped whites around outside of yellow.
Cut bread slices into circles.
Place into greased pan and press dough.
Fill with cheese and ham.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Boil chicken in water with bouillon.
Cook spinach according to package.
Place chicken in baking pan. Cut to lay flat.
Scoop spinach on top of chicken.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Top with a slice of your favorite cheese.
Broil until cheese melts.
Brown ground beef in skillet.
Drain off excess fat.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Blend in tomatoes, tomato paste, salt and chili powder.
Spread half of meat mixture in 1-quart casserole dish.
Arrange half of cheese slices over meat mixture. Top with remaining meat mixture.
Mix flour, corn meal, sugar, baking powder and pepper flakes. Whisk together egg, milk, oil and corn.
Pour liquid mixture over dry ingredients.
Mix lightly.
Place broccoli in a 2-quart casserole.
Dot with 1/4 cup butter, salt and pepper.
Mash mushrooms in 3 tablespoons of butter and saute until golden.
Put mushrooms and butter in casserole. Refrigerate.
When ready to serve, bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until broccoli is tender at 375°.
In a small bowl, combine lime juice and pulp, vanilla and cinnamon (it's best to use a whisk or fork so cinnamon doesn't clump up).
In a large bowl, combine tangerines, bananas and coconut. Pour lime mixture over them and toss well until the fruit is coated.
Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled in small sundae dishes for dessert or breakfast.
Pour 1 to 2 tablespoons olive oil in 7-inch nonstick skillet frypan.
Heat to hot.
Put in scallions and peas.
Cook 5 to 10 minutes.
Add asparagus and cook until tender (10 to 15 minutes). Water may be added during cooking to prevent drying of vegetables. Serve hot as side dish.
Salt and pepper may be added to taste. Season with sprinkle of dried basil, if desired.
Mix together yeast, salt and sugar.
Place 4 cups of flour in a bowl.
Add oil to yeast mixture.
In medium bowl, stir together dates, boiling water, oil and vanilla.
In small bowl, mix flours, sugar, walnuts, cinnamon and baking soda.
Add date mixture and stir until moistened.
Makes 12 muffins.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Freezes well.
Wash the Cornish hens and pat dry.
Cover with butter and salt to taste.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Mix jam and lemon juice and coat the hens.
Bake 45 more minutes.
Combine cheese, sherry, curry and salt.
Blend well.
Stir in chutney; chill.
Turn into dish.
Top with chives.
Brown breakfast sausage.
Add a layer of sliced potatoes and a layer of creamed corn.
Continue until casserole is full.
Put sausage on top.
Cover with tomato soup.
Bake in oven until done.
Cook and bone chicken and cut into bite size pieces.
Cut corn tortillas into 1-inch strips or squares.
Combine soups, milk, onion and salsa.
Grease a 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Arrange 1/2 of the tortillas in pan.
Top with half of the chicken, olives and mushrooms.
Repeat.
Pour soup mixture over all.
Top with full pound of cheese.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine syrup and sugar in heavy skillet.
I like to use an iron skillet.
Bring to a boil and then reduce to medium high heat.
Cook, stirring often with wooden spoon, until mixture will spin a thread when dripped from the spoon or to a firm ball stage. Pour over the popped corn and stir until well coated.
Butter your hands and carefully form into balls.
Mixture will be hot. Handle it carefully.
Soak bread crumbs in milk for several minutes.
(If using dehydrated onions, soak in milk, also.)
Mix all ingredients together well.
Form in two individual loaves and place in greased pan.
Cover meat loaves with chili sauce.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) for 45 minutes or form in single loaf in 4 3/4 x 8 3/4-inch loaf pan.
Cover with chili sauce and bake 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Sprinkle yeast over water.
Let stand for several minutes.
Stir to dissolve yeast.
Add sugar, salt, butter, 1/2 cup cheese, oregano and 3 cups flour.
Beat with mixer at low speed until blended.
Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes. Beat in remaining flour gradually with wooden spoon. Cover bowl with waxed paper and towel.
Let rise for 45 minutes. Stir down. Beat for 30 seconds or 25 strokes. Turn into lightly greased 1 1/2 or 2-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake for 55 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 8 servings.
Mix 1
cup
sugar, milk, flour, baking powder, salt and butter; pour
in
buttered pan.
Pour
cherries over top.
Dot with pieces of
butter then pour over juice and enough boiling water to make 2 cups.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Brown pork sausage and onion.
Drain.
Add mushrooms, soup and milk.
Add eggs.
Serve over baked biscuits.
About 2 hours before serving:
In Dutch oven or large kettle over high heat, heat pork butt, split peas, carrots, onion, celery and 2 quarts of water to boiling.
Put ground beef with tenderizer in pan with oil; fry until cooked.
Drain fat and add onion, corn, tomatoes, salt and pepper. Cook until everything is tender.
Beat shortening, maple syrup and egg.
Sift all dry ingredients together.
Add to first mixture alternately with milk. Mix well.
Add raisins, nuts and oatmeal.
Drop by spoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° about 15 minutes.
Yields 3 dozen.
Make meat balls.
Line bottom of big pan with half of cabbage. Cut up celery and onions.
Put on top of cabbage, then add meat balls on top.
Then add rest of cabbage.
Then add chopped tomatoes.
Add brown sugar, vinegar and soy sauce, then add bouillon cubes in a circle around pan.
Never stir, always shake the pan.
Start cooking on high for 5 minutes.
Turn down to medium.
When meat balls come to the top it's done.

Beat whites with salt and vanilla until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in sugar. Beat yolks until thick and lemon-colored. Fold yolks into whites; carefully fold in flour and nuts. Line bottom and sides of 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch jelly roll pan with waxed paper. Spread batter evenly in pan. Bake in moderate oven (375°) for 12 minutes or until cake springs back when lightly touched. Cool 5 minutes. Loosen sides of cake; turn out onto towel sprinkled with sifted confectioners sugar. Peel off paper. Cool to lukewarm. Starting at narrow end, roll cake and towel together. Cool on rack. Unroll; spread with whipped cream. Reroll cake; chill.
Combine molasses, sugar, shortening and vinegar in saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Sift remaining ingredients together.
Add to molasses mixture.
Return to heat; cook until thick, stirring constantly. Drop 1/2 teaspoonfuls onto a greased baking sheet about 3 inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 3 to 5 minutes or until slightly browned. Cool slightly before removing from sheet with a greased spatula. Roll slightly for a curly edge.
Yields 6 dozen.
In punch bowl, combine apple juice, lemonade and orange juice. Stir in ginger ale.
Add ice.
Float sherbet on top.
Add fruit. Serves 58.
Discard discolored pinto beans; rinse remainder under cold running water.
Drain well.
Transfer to large bowl.
Add enough cold water to cover.
Let soak at least 8 hours or overnight.
Saute onion
in
the
butter
until the onion is clear, then add the pepper.
Stir in all other ingredients and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Best barbecue sauce you've ever had.
Beat egg whites until stiff but not dry.
Gradually add sugar, beating constantly, until stiff but not dry. Beat in flour and almonds.
Spoon heaping teaspoonfuls of batter onto well-greased cookie sheet.
Spread batter to make mounds 2-inches in diameter. Prepare only 6 at a time.
Bake in very hot oven at 450° for 3 to 4 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool a few seconds and carefully remove from cookie sheet with spatula.
If cookies stick, return to oven for a few minutes. Roll with fingers, overlapping cookie to form cones.
Press overlapped ends at wide end to seal and hold shape.
Cool and just before serving, fill with sweetened cream.
Makes 2 or 3 dozen.
Mix together pumpkin, milk, egg, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and hot water.
Pour into pastry lined pie pan.
Bake at 375° for 50 to 55 minutes.
Combine
beans,
cheese,
milk and onion salt in baking dish. Crumble
shredded wheat mix with melted butter.
Sprinkle over green beans.
Bake in 375° oven for 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Place butter on a 15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch jelly roll pan and place in oven to melt, about 7 minutes. Meanwhile, beat egg whites with salt until frothy; gradually add sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold in almonds and cinnamon.
Pour mixture onto jelly roll pan, toss with butter. Bake about 40 minutes, tossing every 10 minutes, until almonds are crisp.
Crush bananas; add sugar, cinnamon, raisins and vanilla.
Mix; add eggs and flour (if large bananas, use 2 small or 1 extra large egg).
Fry in oil and then top with warm rum.
In a large bowl, with mixer at medium speed, beat cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth.
Gradually beat in sugar.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Beat in rind, juice and vanilla.
Pour into pie crust.
Place on cookie sheet.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes.
Chill 4 hours.
Bring chicken broth and orange juice to a boil.
Stir in rice. Cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Saute green onions, mushrooms and red pepper in margarine for 5 minutes.
Add to cooked rice along with the garlic powder.
Brown meat; drain fat.
Add chili powder and red pepper.
Add beans, water and tomatoes.
Simmer until heated through.
Serve with warm tortillas.
Serves 5 to 6. Decrease chili powder and pepper for not so hot stuff!
Combine dry cake mix, pecans and 1/3 cup evaporated milk and melted butter.
Press 1/2 batter into greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° until brown (approximately 8 minutes).
Melt caramels with 1/2 cup evaporated milk.
Pour over baked lower layer.
Cover with chocolate morsels. Top with remaining batter.
Bake until brown.
Saute the onion in margarine until tender.
Add the chopped potatoes.
Pour enough water just to cover.
Cook on medium heat until potatoes are soft.
Line 1 (9 x 13-inch) sheet cake pan with 1 can crescent roll dough.
Mix on low speed cream cheese and powdered sugar to a spreading consistency.
Spread mixture over dough evenly.
Top with 2nd can crescent roll dough.
Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Combine cooked rice, pimentos and cooked chicken.
Fold warm gravy into mixture until mixture is coated.
Serve warm or chill.
Chop the onion and peppers. Put in everything else. Roll up in tortilla like burritos with both sides open. Refrigerate 2 hours. Cut each tortilla into 8 pieces.
Top each chicken breast with 1 slice of ham and cheese.
Roll up; secure with toothpicks.
Dip in beaten eggs.
Coat with cereal flake crumbs.
Place chicken rolls in a greased baking dish; drizzle with margarine.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until done.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook pasta according to package directions; add sliced zucchini and/or squash 1 minute before end of cooking time. Drain.
In bowl, toss hot pasta and zucchini with artichoke hearts, marinade, olives, sun-dried tomatoes, parsley, salt and pepper.
Makes 6 servings.
Beat yogurt and sugars at medium speed.
Add eggs and vanilla; mix well.
Combine flour, soda, salt and oats.
Gradually add to yogurt; mix well.
Stir in raisins.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on Pam-sprayed cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool on wire rack.
Allow cheese and margarine to become room temperature.
Mix together adding garlic and flour.
Add enough milk to help form into a ball.
Chill 1 hour.
Mix cake mix, oil, Jell-O and wine together.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Pour into well-greased, floured Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Cool completely.
Beat the egg in a deep bowl.
Add the sugar, nutmeg and anise seed.
Beat well.
Sift the flour, salt and baking powder.
Knead well, adding more flour if the dough is too sticky.
Roll out on a floured board with a floured rolling pin, to slightly less than 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into 1-inch strips, then cut on an angle, making diamond shapes.
Cut a slit in each and pull a corner through.
Or use the unslit diamond shape.
Fry in deep hot oil until golden brown.
Drain on absorbent paper.
Roll in sugar. (Makes 6 dozen cakes.)
Melt margarine in pan.
Blend in flour and salt.
Add half of the skim milk, stirring steadily, to the boiling point.
Mix in sugar, then cook on low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in remaining milk.
Grease pan.
Combine milk, eggs, molasses and butter.
Beat well, then add cinnamon and flour.
Bake in a big bread pan (9 x 13-inch) on a old wood stove (for a large family) in 350° oven. Check after 30 minutes.
Check with toothpick.
If it comes out clean, cake is done.
Makes 9 x 13-inch cake.
Mix ingredients together, except cookies.
Spread mixture on chocolate cookies.
Chill until firm.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together muffin mix, cereal and spice.
In a small mixing bowl combine eggs and milk; add all at once to muffin mixture, stirring until blended but still slightly lumpy.

Pour about 1/4 cup batter onto a hot well-greased griddle. Cook over medium heat, 1 to 2 minutes per side or until golden brown, turning to cook other side when pancakes have a bubbly surface and slightly dry edge.
Serve with margarine or butter and syrup.
Makes eight 4-inch pancakes.
Cook noodles in boiling salt water until tender.
Place in baking dish.
Add tuna, onion and eggs.
Blend Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour over tuna mixture.
Sprinkle with cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Blend first 4 ingredients with cheese.
Season with parsley and chives to taste.
Shape into 1/2-inch balls.
Roll in ground nutmeats mixed with chopped parsley.
Wash spinach; drain.
Combine oil and vinegar in mixer bowl; beat for 3 to 5 minutes or until well blended.
Add sugar, onion, catsup, salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Beat well.
Combine spinach, eggs, tomato and bacon in large bowl.
Add desired amount of dressing; toss to mix.
Dressing will keep well in refrigerator. Yield:
6 servings.
Season ground beef.
Make into 5 or 6 hamburger patties. Place slice of potato, slice of onion, slice of green pepper and a slice of tomato on each side of meat patty.
Wrap each patty with vegetables in foil and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Serve hot. Yields 5 or 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift dry ingredients; cream shortening and sugar.
To the creamed mixture; add eggs and lemon juice. Then blend in pineapple and syrup.
Add flour mixture slowly while beating.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheets.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, mix soup mix and flour. Stir in water. Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring occasionally, 5 minutes, or until gravy is thickened. Makes about 2 cups of gravy.
Drain, flake and clean salmon.
Combine all ingredients (except pecans and parsley).
Shape into 2 balls or loaves on wax paper.
Wrap and chill for several hours.
Roll chilled balls or loaves in parsley and pecan mixture.
For serving, turn out onto a dish and serve with assortment of crackers or fresh vegetables. This is a delicious spread! My daughter grave me the recipe.
She serves it often to her guests in California.
Combine turkey, cantaloupe, celery and green onion.
In small bowl, mix oil, vinegar, oil, mustard, soy sauce, red pepper flakes and garlic.
Combine mixture with turkey/cantaloupe mixture.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Mix and sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat egg.
Add sugar and mix thoroughly.
Add milk and flour alternately to the egg and sugar mixture.
Add chopped nuts, black walnuts or pecans.
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Let stand 20 minutes, then bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Fry chopped onion in vegetable oil.
Add cardamom while oil is still hot, then add peas.
Stir it on medium heat for about 3 minutes, then add rice and 2 cups of water.
Bring it to boil. Turn the heat down and let it cook until the rice is tender.
In medium saucepan, cook spinach according to package directions; drain well.
In same pan, combine spinach, cheeses, onion, mint and pepper.
Heat through over low heat, stirring occasionally.
Cook sausage and ground beef with onion until meat is brown and onion tender.
Drain.
Butter bottom and sides of 9 x 13 pan.
Line the bottom with 8 slices of bread.
Layer meat and cheese mixture, beginning with meat, ending with cheese, until all are used up.
In a large bowl, combine eggs, milk, dry mustard, salt and pepper. Pour over layers in baking dish.
Cover; refrigerate overnight.
Let dough rise.
Roll out into rectangle.
Spread sausage evenly over dough, also, cheese, parsley, garlic salt and pepper. Roll dough jellyroll fashion.
Place seam side down on cutting board.
Cut into 1-inch slices.
Bake at 300° for 25 to 35 minutes on greased cookie sheet until brown and sausage is done.
Peel and slice potatoes thin; place one layer in greased casserole.
Sprinkle with onion, green pepper, salt and pepper. Add more potatoes and another layer of onion, green pepper, salt and pepper.
Continue until all ingredients are used.
Add 4 cups of milk to cream of mushroom soup and spread over top.
Cover and bake until potatoes are tender at 350°.
Serves 4.

Preheat oven to 350°. Grease a 9 x 12 baking dish. Boil chicken nuggets in broth until done. Remove chicken and strain broth. Reserve 3 cups. In 4-quart saucepan, melt butter. Add flour, stirring until bubbling and foamy. Do not brown. Whisk in reserved broth. Add salt and pepper, stirring until smooth and thick. Remove from heat. Add mushrooms, peas and carrots and chopped eggs. Pour into casserole. Roll pastry to 14 x 11-inch rectangle. Place on top of casserole. Fold under excess pastry. Do not stretch pastry. Crimp edges with fork. Cut 6 (1-inch) slits in top of pastry. Brush top of pastry with egg mixture. Bake 35 minutes or until golden.
In a large bowl, mix Ricotta, 1 cup Mozzarella, egg, spinach and seasonings.
In greased 9 x 13-inch pan, layer:
1/2 cup sauce, 1/3 of uncooked lasagne noodles and 1/2 of spinach. Repeat, then finish with the last 1/3 of the noodles and the remaining sauce.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup Mozzarella over the top.
Pour the water around the edges.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Stand 15 minutes, then serve.
Mix together sugar, mustard and molasses.
Add vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, pineapple juice and lemon juice.
Mix well and heat.
Serve hot.

recipes.t: Santa Fe Super Chief'S French Toast
d: Beat eggs with cream and salt, blending well.
Place in a shallow dish and coat the bread slices thoroughly, turning to soak both sides through.
Fry until nicely browned in hot fat.
Cook noodles in boiling salted water.
Drain.
Mix soup, milk and salt and heat, stirring constantly.
Add
cheese, stir until melted.
Add
remaining
ingredients,
except
cup almonds and the crumbs.
Mix with noodles, put
in buttered
2 quart casserole, top with crumbs and
remaining almonds. Bake, uncovered, in hot 400° oven for about 20 minutes.
Serves 6.
Place cooked and chopped broccoli and chicken in an ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Beat soup and milk.
Pour over broccoli and chicken.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Toast almonds and sesame seed in oven at 350° for 15 minutes. Stir twice.
Mix together oil, vinegar, sugar, pepper and chicken flavor seasoning packet from soup.
Put on cabbage.
Add other ingredients just before serving.
Mix potatoes, ham and onion flakes and roll into balls.
Roll balls in butter and then in corn flakes.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Serve with cheese sauce.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add eggs.
Add applesauce mixed with soda.
Sift flour and measure 4 cups.
Add to mixture.
Stir well. Bake in appropriate size sheet cake pan at 275° for approximately 55 to 60 minutes.
Mix Zwieback crumbs with 3 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon grated lemon rind in small bowl.
Blend in melted butter.
Press evenly over bottom and sides of 8-inch spring-form pan.
Set pan in a 12-inch long piece of foil; fold foil up along side to catch any butter that may bubble out.
Chill while making filling.
Mix all remaining ingredients.
Pour into crust and bake at 500° for 12 minutes.
Lower to 250° and bake for 2 hours or until firm on top.
Cool.
Garnish with canned or fresh fruit.
Cherries are great!
Spread peanut butter on hamburger bun.
Place slice of pineapple on top and the top with slice of American cheese.
Top with a maraschino cherry.
Bake in a 400° oven until cheese begins to melt.
Combine sugar and flour; mix thoroughly.
Add juice from cherries and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture is thick and clear.
Add cherries, oleo and lemon juice. Let stand and make pastry.
Fill shell and top with remaining pastry.
Pierce the top and flute edges.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes, then reduce heat to 350° for 45 minutes or until done (top will be golden brown).
Saute pork. Cook rice until tender. Chop tomatoes and cucumber. When done, drain rice. Add eggs and scramble. Add tomatoes, cucumber and pork. Add soy sauce to flavor.
Wrap each chicken breast in a strip of bacon; lay in bottom of shallow, ovenproof dish.
Pour soup and sour cream over the chicken.
Sprinkle almonds over soup.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake at 325° for 2 hours.
Remove foil and let it brown slightly. Serve over rice.
Heat oven to 400°.
In medium saucepan, heat chili until hot. Spread chips in single layer onto ungreased baking sheet.
Spoon beans over chips; top with chili, cheese and chilies.
Bake 5 to 7 minutes or until heated through.
Garnish with guacamole, if desired.
Makes about 5 servings.
Wash and dry chicken parts; remove skin, if desired.
Melt butter in shallow baking pan.
Add remaining ingredients, except chicken.
Mix well.
Roll chicken in mixture and arrange in a single layer in same pan.
Bake at 375°, basting occasionally, for 40 minutes (30 minutes if boneless chicken is used).
Serves 4.
Cook noodles 8 minutes in boiling water.
Drain.
Melt oleo in large skillet; saute chopped onion and cabbage until cabbage is tender.
Add salt and pepper seasoning.
Mix together with noodles in casserole.
Spray 9-inch pie dish with Pam.
Combine crackers, crumbs, sugar and cinnamon in bowl.
Gradually add Butter Buds.
Press into bottom and sides of pie dish.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
Saute onions, carrots, green pepper and celery in oil. Do not season!
Add noodles and undiluted soup to veggies.
Mix it all together.
Wash and scrub potatoes (do not peel).
Slice 1/4-inch thick. Melt margarine and mix with onion soup mix, salt and water.
In a 1 1/2 or 2-quart casserole, put a layer of potatoes, then a layer of onion soup mixture.
Repeat until all has been used.
Bake 45 minutes at 350° (uncovered).
Dissolve jello in boiling water; stir in cold water and pear juice, lemon juice and cranberry sauce.
(Break up cranberry sauce a little before adding to mixture.)
Chill until consistency of unbeaten egg whites.
Fold in chopped pears and pecans.
Spoon into a 7-cup mold or a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Chill until firm.
Makes 10 servings.
Brown all sides of roast to "seal" roast; season to taste, e.g. salt, pepper, garlic, etc.
Fill Dutch oven or roasting pan 1/2 full with water.
Add soups and stir.
Put in roast and cover. Bake for 3 hours at 350°.
You can add common or favorite vegetables while roasting.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Spray 8-inch baking dish with PAM.
Layer macaroni in dish.
Spread cottage cheese over macaroni. Sprinkle on spices.
Then layer vegetables.
Add Mozzarella evenly over vegetables.
Pour chicken broth over entire mixture.
Spread on tomato paste.
Sprinkle top with bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake for 1 hour at 350 degrees.
Follow directions for pudding mix.
When pudding is chilled, put puffed rice in a large bowl.
Add peanut butter and honey; mix well.
Pour pudding over rice mixture.
Put Cool Whip on top. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Makes 8 servings.
Scald milk.
Add sugar, salt, nutmeg and cool to warm. Sprinkle yeast on the 2 tablespoons warm water to dissolve. After milk has cooled, add oil, eggs and dissolved yeast.
Blend with wooden spoon.
Gradually add flour, beating well.
Cover with wax paper, then towel.
Let rise until doubled.
Turn soft dough onto well floured board and knead well, but gently.
Roll out to 18 x 12-inches and cut into 2 x 2-inch squares.
Cover again with towel and let rise 30 or 40 minutes.
Fry in deep fat at 375° until golden brown (takes about 1 or 2 minutes to brown).
Drain on paper towels and while warm sprinkle on sugar or shake in paper bag.
Use plenty of confectioners sugar.
This doughnut does not taste like our regular doughnuts.
Cream butter; gradually add sugar, beating well.
Add eggs, one at a time, then add pumpkin.
Gradually stir in dry ingredients, chocolate morsels and nuts.
Bake in a greased loaf pan at 350° for about 1 hour.
Take out of oven and cool in the pan for 10 minutes; then remove and cool on a wire rack.
Makes 1 loaf.
Mix pie filling and milk well.
Dump other ingredients in and mix well.
Refrigerate.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9-inch pie plate. Place eggs, milk, margarine, vanilla, melted chocolate, sugar and baking mix in blender and blend on high 1 minute.
Pour into plate and bake about 30 minutes or until custard leaves no indentation when pressed lightly in center.
Cool before serving with whipped cream. Store in the refrigerator.
Makes 8 servings.
In a large bowl, blend shortening and both sugars until well blended. Add eggs and milk; stir until well blended.
Stir in flour and baking soda until well mixed.
Stir in chocolate chips or M&M's (or both, if desired).
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes until lightly browned.
(Longer if a crisp cookie is desired.)
Saute onions in butter until clear.
Add thyme, basil, tomatoes and tomato paste.
Stir this and let simmer for 10 minutes.
Make a paste with 6 tablespoons broth with flour.
Stir into soup.
Add rest of chicken broth, salt and pepper to taste.
Add sugar and baking soda.
If serving right away, add 1 cup half and half.
If saving, freeze in a 2-quart jar.
Do not add half and half if going to freeze, it tends to curdle.
Combine all vegetables.
Whisk the vinegar, vegetable oil, Equal, salt, celery seed, mustard seed and pepper.
Pour over vegetables; toss to blend.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. Makes 8 servings.
Mix together pecans, flour, sugar and butter.
Spread on a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, stirring often.
Cool and crumble.
Spread half the crumbs in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Slice ice cream and place slices on top of crumbs.
Pour ice cream sauce on top of ice cream and top with rest of the crumbs.
Freeze.
Cut in squares to serve.
(Use any flavor of ice cream and sauce.)
Cream together brown sugar, butter, shortening and eggs.
In another bowl, add molasses to boiling water, then mix in with creamed mixture.
Add all dry ingredients to creamed mixture and stir thoroughly until blended and smooth.
Bake at 350° in greased and floured 15 x 12 x 1-inch pan.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes (do not overbake).
While still warm, frost with thin white icing. Cool.
Cut into bars.
In saucepan over low heat, melt butter. Stir in flour, salt, pepper and paprika until smooth.
Gradually stir in milk; cook, stirring constantly until thickened and smooth.
Add cheese and cook until cheese is melted.
Pour over hot cooked vegetables.
Beat eggs until foamy or whiz in the blender.
Add the soup and bacon.
Melt the margarine in a skillet and cook eggs as you would for scrambled eggs.
Spoon into warmed pitas and top with the shredded Cheddar.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add onions, green pepper, ground beef and bacon.
Cook, stirring often until meat is browned.
Spoon off excess fat.
Drain tomatoes, measuring juice.
Add water to juice to make 1 1/2 cups.
Add the liquid, tomatoes, salt, sugar and thyme to mixture in skillet.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes longer.
Heat oven to 400°.
Prepare Savory Crunch.
Mix spinach, soup and Worcestershire sauce in greased pie plate (9 x 1 1/4-inch). Arrange mushrooms on top.
Sprinkle Savory Crunch evenly over mushrooms.
Bake, uncovered, until hot and bubbly, about 20 minutes.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Makes 5 or 6 servings.
Combine cranberries, marshmallows and sugar.
Cover and chill overnight.
Add apples, grapes, nuts and salt.
Fold in whipped cream.
Chill.
Garnish tray with lettuce or other greens.
Place pineapple spears on tray and heap cranberry mixture on pineapple.
Boil together brown sugar, margarine, salt, vanilla and corn syrup for 5 minutes.
Mix well occasionally.
Remove from heat and add baking powder.
Stir in quickly.
Pour over popped corn mixing well.
Put in 2 large flat pans and place in oven at 250° for 1 hour.
Stir 3 or 4 times.
Add 1 package nuts.
Drain and flake salmon; mix with mayonnaise.
Trim crusts from bread.
On each of 4 slices of bread, place a slice of cheese (trim to fit), 1/4 salmon mix and another slice of cheese.
Top with remaining bread slices.
Beat eggs with milk.
Coat each sandwich in egg mixture and saute on both sides until browned.
Makes 4 sandwiches.
Preheat oven to 350°. In a bowl, combine eggs, pumpkin puree and oil. Add dry ingredients and mix well. Add cranberries and mix. Divide dough into 2 (8 x 4-inch) loaf pans. Bake 50 minutes.
Crust: Preheat oven to 350°. Beat egg white and cream of tartar in medium bowl to soft peaks.

Gradually beat in sugar, beating to stiff peaks. Spoon mixture into ungreased 9-inch glass pie pan, spreading bottom and up sides to form a bowl shape. Bake 40 minutes or until firm to touch and lightly browned.
Cool on wire rack.
Combine milk and butter in a 2-cup glass dish.
Cook on High for 2 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, salt and yeast in large mixing bowl.
Add milk mixture and egg.
Mix 2 tablespoons of soup mix and 1/4 cup cheese in small bowl; set aside.
Add remaining soup mix and cheese to batter.
Divide batter evenly between 2 well-greased 8 x 4-inch microproof loaf pans.
Sprinkle with reserved onion-cheese mixture.
Rinse rice; drain.
Brown rice with a teaspoon of grease. Combine onion, celery, pepper, garlic, tomato, salt and pepper and 3 cups hot water.
Let cook for 20 minutes on low heat.
Add sausage and 1/2 cup hot water; simmer for 10 minutes.
In large frying pan, melt 1 teaspoon butter on low-medium heat. Whip eggs in mixing bowl.
Dip loaf bread in eggs.
Sprinkle with cinnamon to taste.
Cook in melted butter until golden brown. Smother with butter.
Sprinkle white powdered sugar over bread, then add syrup to taste.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add egg and almond extract.
Cream again.
Sift together the flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves and allspice.
Set aside.
Dry raisins on paper toweling.
Mix raisins with a tablespoon or two of the dry ingredients.
Add raisins to creamed mixture.
Add dry ingredients and blend well.
Add cranberry sauce, mixing well.
Pour into a greased 9-inch angel food pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven 1 hour or until it tests done.
Blend together oil and sugar in large mixing bowl.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Stir in bananas and almond extract.
Cut oranges into pieces and add to banana mixture.
Stir in remaining ingredients except graham cracker crumbs.
Mix well. Grease bottom and sides of an 8 x 4-inch or 9 x 5-inch (1 1/2-quart) loaf pan.
Sprinkle with graham cracker crumbs.
Shake out excess.
Pour batter into pan, spreading evenly.
Bake 55 minutes at 325°.
Yields 1 loaf.
Slightly brown the ground beef with the onion.

Add celery which has been partially cooked in very little water and drained. (May want to save some celery water if mixture looks too dry.) Add cooked rice, soy sauce, soups, salt and almonds (optional). Mix well.
Bake 30 minutes in a 350° oven in slightly greased baking dish.
The last 15 minutes, sprinkle with chow mein noodles.
Brown as desired.
Soften butter; cream in brown sugar, then powdered sugar.
Add in cinnamon and nutmeg and beat well.
Fold in ice cream.
Store in tightly sealed container in freezer.
Mix to taste with hot water; add rum, if desired.
Combine juice, sugar, water and cornstarch in saucepan.
Stir well.
Cook until thickened.
Stir in pineapple, raisins, margarine, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Cook over low heat, stirring until heated.
Stir in vanilla.
Place 1/2 cup or so of ice cream in dessert dish.
Spoon 3 tablespoons warm pineapple sauce over ice cream.
Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon toasted coconut, if deserved. Serve immediately.
Boil potatoes 10 minutes; drain.
Arrange in 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Pour margarine over potatoes, sprinkle all sides with salt, pepper and paprika.
Turn 2 or 3 times while baking.
Bake in 325° oven 1 to 1 1/4 hours.
Baste before serving.
Beat butter and sugars.
Add egg and beat.
Add juice and vanilla.
Add flour, salt and soda; then peel and pecans.
Shape into two 1 1/4 rolls.
Wrap in waxed paper. Chill until firm. Slice 3/16-inch thick.
Bake on ungreased baking sheet at 375° for 8 or 9 minutes.
Mix flour, salt and shortening.
Add 1/4 cup water and mix. Roll this as a pie crust.
Spread mixture of 3/4 cup sugar and 1 stick margarine (softened) on the crust.
Roll like a jelly roll and cut into 1-inch thick crossways.
Lay flat in a 9-inch pie pan and bake at 350° until brown.
Cook pasta to al dente.
Rinse anchovies in lukewarm water and place in milk.
Soak for 1/2 hour.
Saute onion and garlic in oil. Remove anchovies and discard milk.
Dice anchovies and add to pan.
Cook for several minutes until anchovies begin to come apart.
Add spaghetti sauce and cream and mix thoroughly.
Add pepper and cheese.
Serve over pasta.
Serves 4.
Cook noodles in salted water.
Cut sausage links into 1/2-inch pieces and brown in skillet.
Drain grease and add sliced onion and green pepper.
Cover and steam.
Prepare spaghetti sauce according to directions.
Add sausage, onion and green pepper. Set aside.
In a bowl, mix well 1/2 cup soup, beef, sausage, crumbs, cheese, onion, egg and Worcestershire sauce.
In baking pan, firmly shape into 8 x 4-inch loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours. Reserve 2 tablespoons drippings.
In saucepan, heat remaining soup, water and reserved drippings to boiling, stirring occasionally. Spoon over meat loaf.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles as directed on package. In medium skillet, brown turkey with pepper and onion.
Stir in salt, margarine and basil.
Cook 1 minute.
Blend in soup and milk.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream.
Combine noodles and turkey mixture.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with buttered bread crumbs, approximately 1/3 cup.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes.
Thaw fish fillets and cut into bite-size pieces.
In small skillet, saute pork and onion until golden; drain and put into crock-pot with fish.
Add all remaining ingredients except evaporated milk.
Cover and cook on low 6 to 9 hours until potatoes are tender (high 2 to 3 hours).
Add evaporated milk last half hour.
Serve in large bowl with French bread.
Cut up fajita meat in small strips. Marinate in fajita marinade mixture.
Brown meat in skillet, adding onion, pepper, garlic and comino.
Cook to desired consistency.
Serve on tortillas with garnishes of choice (salsa, lettuce, tomatoes, etc.).
Cream sugar, butter and shortening in large mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks; beat well.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk, beating well after each addition.
Add coconut extract; mix well.
Fold in egg whites and coconut.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Place in cold oven.
Set oven temperature to 325°.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Cool in pan for several minutes.
Invert onto serving plate.
Drizzle glaze over top and side of cake.
Yield:
24 servings.
Combine chicken, celery, cheese, mayonnaise, almonds, onions, lemon juice and salt.
Mix lightly.
Pour into baking dish.
Toss Corn Flakes crumbs and margarine together; sprinkle over mixture. Bake at 325° for 35 minutes.

recipes.t: Salad Of Boston Lettuce And Blueberries
d: In a small bowl or a jar, whisk or shake together blueberry or white-wine vinegar, walnut and vegetable oils, mustard, salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon water.
(The vinaigrette can be prepared up to 2 days ahead and stored, covered, in the refrigerator.)
With food processor or electric mixer, blend together Cheddar and cream cheese until well blended.
Add chopped green pepper and remaining ingredients.
Process until well blended.
Serve with crackers.
Spread is better if prepared the night before it is to be served.
Mix first 4 ingredients and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Stir in margarine and put into pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Melt chocolate; add margarine, sugar and egg and beat well.
Add the next 6 ingredients to the chocolate mixture and spread over the baked layer.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cool; frost with fudge frosting.
Drain beets.
Mix sugar, lemon juice, butter, orange juice, salt and pepper in a double boiler.
Heat.
Mix cornstarch and cold water.
Stir into orange juice mixture; cook until slightly thickened.
Add drained beets to orange juice and heat thoroughly.
Brown turkey & onion in large skillet, drain fat. Add chilies, salsa, chopped tomatoes and refried beans. Simmer for 20-30 minutes on low heat. Salt & Pepper to taste.
Place neck bones in deep/wide pan.
Cover with onion and bell pepper and sprinkle on salt, pepper and garlic.
Add 2 cups of water.
Place the top on the pan or cover with aluminum foil. Bake in oven at about 375° about 2 hours or until tender.
Beat Crisco, molasses, eggs and sugar until fluffy; sift flour and spices together and add to molasses mixture and milk.
Bake in Bundt pan for 45 to 50 minutes at 350°.
Glaze with a thin glaze of corn syrup (good with Cool Whip).
Place chicken breasts in baking dish.
Top with chipped beef. Mix soup and sour cream.
Pour onto chipped beef.
Sprinkle on frozen peas and chopped pimento.
Crumble bread cubes and add. Bake at 250° for 3 hours.

recipes.t: Mother Wineman'S World Famous Rhubarb Crisp
d: Mix first 4 ingredients and put in 9 x 13-inch buttered pan. Beat egg and combine remaining ingredients until crumbly.
Place crumbly mixture on top of rhubarb.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until bubbly.
Chopped walnuts are a tasty addition to the topping.
Drain peaches.
Lay on plate flat side down.
Put black olive circles for eyes, raisins for nose and kiwi circle for a surprised mouth.
Put shredded cheese on top for hair.
Any other fresh fruits and vegetables available can be used also.
Put shredded cabbage
in baking dish.
Pour potato soup and water over cabbage.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven until cabbage
is
tender.
Sprinkle
on bread crumbs and bake until crumbs are lightly brown.
Sprinkle pork butts with salt and pepper.
Add paprika and garlic. Let stand for about 10 minutes.
Fry in deep fat.
Serve on slices of rye bread with sauerkraut.
In a medium saucepan, melt the butter, then add sugar, blending well.
Set aside to cool.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Blend flour and baking powder together, then add to mix.
Add vanilla and nuts, making sure to blend thoroughly.
Spread batter into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan; bake at 350° for approximately 30 minutes.
Check with cake tester to be sure it is completely baked.
While still warm, cut into squares and dust with confectioners sugar.
This dish is a marvelous first course, although a little goes a long way.
To begin, lightly oil a 2-quart ring mold.
Next, place the cod, bay leaf, lemon and peppercorns in a deep frying pan.
Cover with water and poach for about 25 minutes, or until the fish flakes.
Remove fish from stock and allow to cool.
Flake the fish.
Liberally line the ring mold with the smoked salmon, making certain that every slice overlaps a little with the next and that plenty is left to hang over the outer and inner edges of the mold.
Put 4 tablespoons of water into a saucepan.
Sprinkle the gelatin into the water and let the water completely absorb the granules.
Drain syrup from fruit into 1-cup measure; add water to make one cup.
Heat to boiling in small saucepan.
Stir in gelatin and stir until gelatin dissolves.
Beat in cranberry sauce and add lemon juice.
Chill until thick as unbeaten egg white.
Stir in oranges, cottage cheese, celery and nuts.
Spoon into 6-cup mold. Chill several hours or overnight.
Cut round steak into serving pieces; season with salt and pepper and place in slow cooker.
Sprinkle onion soup mix over top and pour tomatoes over all.
Cover and cook on low, 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 hours.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cut pork in 1 to 1 1/2-inch cubes.
Rub with salt and pepper and oregano.
Broil on skewers over charcoal for 15 minutes or until brown.
Baste with mixture of lemons, oil, salt and pepper, mixed well.
Baste often until done.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
Bake cake according to package directions in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Also make pudding according to directions and spread over the top of cake.
Slice bananas and place on top of pudding in rows.
Spread whipped topping over the bananas.
Sprinkle with nuts and serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Boil chicken until done, then debone the chicken.
Place chicken in glass casseorle dish.
Pour both soups over top of chicken.
You'll need to smooth it over the tops evenly.
In bottom of a 9-inch square baking dish, place a layer of potatoes.
Sprinkle lightly with flour, salt and pepper.
Place a layer of sausage and sprinkle with cheese.
Continue layering until pan is full (usually 3 layers).
Pour milk into dish.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes until potatoes are done.
Remove from oven and let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Cook
and
drain
packages
frozen chopped broccoli. Add oleo, eggs, cheese, mayonnaise, onions, mushroom soup and water chestnuts.
Put
in
casserole.
Top
with crushed Ritz crackers. Bake on 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix 2 1/2 cups flour, sugar, salt and yeast; add margarine. Gradually add water and beat about 2 minutes.
Add 1 cup flour; beat.
Stir in enough flour to make stiff dough; knead a few times.
Divide into 4 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a 15-inch long loaf.
Place on greased baking sheet sprinkled with corn meal.
Brush with peanut oil.
Cover with plastic wrap and freeze until firm.
Remove from baking sheet and wrap each loaf with plastic wrap; may keep frozen up to 6 weeks.
Remove from freezer; place on ungreased baking sheets, corn meal side down. Let stand, covered with plastic wrap, at room temperature, about 1 1/2 hours.
Let rise until double, about 1 1/2 hours more.
Gently brush with combined egg white and cold water and sprinkle with sesame seed.
Bake at 450° for 20 minutes.
Grease two 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pans.
In a medium bowl stir together flour, baking powder, cinnamon and ginger.
In a large bowl with mixer at medium speed, beat together margarine and sugar until smooth.
Beat in corn syrup.
Add eggs; beat until well mixed.
With a wooden spoon, stir in apples.
Stir in flour mixture, raisins and nuts.
Set power select at Medium.
In oblong baking dish, arrange ribs, onion and celery.
Heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
Cover with plastic wrap; set power select at High for 5 minutes and at low for 60 minutes or until ribs are tender.
Rearrange ribs once and baste with sauce occasionally.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Add marshmallows; stir until partially dissolved.
Chill until syrupy.
Fold in applesauce, walnuts and the mayo.
Spoon into a 1-quart mold; chill until firm.
Unmold and garnish with watercress or lettuce.
Makes six servings.
Drain and rinse shrimp and clams.
Mix all ingredients together and serve in a fondue pot.
Serve with crackers or choice of dippers.
In a large heavy saucepan brown the rhinoceros in the butter. Add the garlic, onions, parsley and seasonings and saute until the onions are golden.

recipes.t: Chicken Stuffing Casserole And Pimento Mushroom Sauce
d: Prepare stuffing according to package and spread in 13 x 9 x 2-inch glass dish.
Layer thickly with chicken. In saucepan, melt butter, blend in flour.
Add salt and pepper.
Add cool broth and thicken.
Stir in eggs quickly.
Pour over chicken and dressing. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Let set for 10 minutes before cutting.
Prepare filling mix according to package directions for pie using 1/2 the liquid; cool.
Line 12 muffin cups with paper cupcake wrappers.
Sift flour with sugar and baking powder into bowl.
Add butter and milk; blend well at low speed for 1 1/2 minutes.
Add egg and vanilla and beat another 1 1/2 minutes at low.
Fill baking cups half full.
Top with teaspoon of filling (reserve remaining filling for topping).
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes until cake springs back when touched lightly in center. Cool and spread with remaining filling.
Cook carrots in salted water until tender.
Drain.
Put into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Mix mayonnaise, onion, horseradish, salt and pepper together.
Add to carrots.
Stir.
Wash and pat chicken dry.
Dip in melted butter; coat with cracker crumbs.
Place on baking dish or pan.
Pour any extra butter or crumbs over top.
Cover lightly with aluminum foil. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Clean chicken.
Cut chicken breasts into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Place chicken pieces in beaten eggs and refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
Coat chicken pieces in bread crumbs.
Brown chicken in melted margarine.
Layer pieces in baking dish.
Sprinkle grated cheese and mushrooms over chicken.
Repeat layer.
Pour chicken stock over.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours (325° glass dish).
Tender and delicious!
Crush cereal.
Place in large mixing bowl.
Add egg, tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Beat well.
Add ground beef.
Mix only until combined.
Shape into 6 loaves, about 4 inches long.
Place in single layer in shallow baking pan.
Bake in oven at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Top each loaf with 1/2 cheese slice.
Return to oven.
Bake 10 minutes longer or until cheese melts.
Cook instant rice as per directions on package.
Blend banana, sugar, sweetener, cool water and cooked rice until smooth and creamy.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add to blended mixture and chill.
When mixture has congealed slightly, whip with electric beater until light and fluffy.
Cook potatoes in
salted water in a very large saucepan until very soft. Place
sieve
over a large bowl.
Pour potatoes and liquid into sieve and force potatoes through.
Return to saucepan. Stir in cucumber, pepper, cream, milk and onion. Simmer gently for about 5 minutes or until cucumber is tender. Add dill, salt and
pepper.
Serve
hot
or
cold.
Yield:
4 servings.
Scald milk, then cool until warm.
Dissolve in yeast.
Add beaten eggs.
Add salt and 1 cup gluten flour.
Beat well.
Add melted butter and then add rest of gluten flour.
Beat well.
Add sugar, cardamon and raisins; knead 2 cups of white flour into dough.
Add more if necessary.
Should be soft.
Knead 20 minutes. Divide and make 2 braids.
Let rise on floured cookie sheets 1 1/2 hours until doubled in size.
Glaze with beaten eggs and raw sugar. Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Be sure to use a fresh camel, the frozen variety has a gamey taste.
Most experts say the one-hump camel is far tastier than the two-humper.
Skin and clean the camel and lamb; pluck the chickens.
Boil up the rice.
Shell the nuts and seeds; fry them brown and mix them with the rice.
Hard-boil your eggs, peel 'em, chop 'em and throw 'em in.
Next, stuff the chickens with this mixture, then stuff the lamb with the chickens.
(If company's coming, you might want to add a half-dozen or so more chickens.) Stuff the camel with the lamb that's been stuffed with the stuffed chickens.
Add salt and pepper.
Bake at 350° until brown.
(Oven too small, try the clothes dryer!)
When it's done, spread the remaining rice mixture on a rather large platter and place the camel in the middle.
Decorate with a sprig of fresh parsley and serve.
I must admit I haven't tried it yet, as our neighborhood market is fresh out of camels.
So I'll file the recipe and wait until Uncle Arthur opens a Dromy-Dairy.
Beat the eggs; then add the oil, cheese, milk, baking powder and flour.
Pour mixture in a deep ovenproof pan that has been greased and floured.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool and slice.
Can be served cold or hot.
Dissolve gelatin in cold water; stir in hot water.
Add sugar and salt; stir until dissolved.
Blend in orange and lemon juices. Chill until mixture begins to thicken.
Fold in grapes, fruit and nuts.
Put into a 5-cup bowl or mold.
Oil bowl or mold before putting in mixture.
Chill until firm.
Combine softened cream cheese, Cheddar cheese and milk.
Blend well.
Reserve 1/2 cup onions.
Stir in remaining onions and olives.
Shape into a ball; roll in reserved onions.
Garnish with stuffed green olive slices or as desired.
Serve with crackers or tiny party rye.
Slice and seed enough peppers to make 2 gallons (mix as desired).
To this, add boiling water to cover.
Let stand 5 or 10 minutes.
Layer steak on bottom of casserole dish.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Layer onions, carrots and then potatoes.
Heat soup, water and margarine and pour over other ingredients.
Cover and bake for 1 1/2 hours at 375°.
In a small bowl, combine cream cheese, 2 tablespoons butter, parsley, basil and lemon-pepper.
Stir in water; keep warm.
In a saucepan, saut garlic in remaining butter until lightly browned. Place noodles in a serving bowl; top with garlic mixture. Sprinkle with half of the Parmesan cheese; toss lightly.
Spoon cream sauce over noodles and sprinkle with remaining Parmesan. Garnish with parsley if desired.
Makes about 8 servings.
