Roll chicken in eggs and then bread crumbs.
Fry chicken in olive oil for 20 minutes.
Pour spaghetti sauce over chicken, top with cheese.
Cover and cook for additional 30 minutes.
Cut chicken into approximately 1 inch cubes.
Cut bacon strips in half.
Wrap chicken cubes with 1/2 strip of bacon. Secure with tooth pick.
Fry in oil until golden brown.
Drain well.
Cover with soy sauce.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Put grated coconut in each peach half; turn upside down in pie crust.
Beat egg yolks and mix with instant pudding.
Sprinkle coconut over peaches, then put pudding over all.
Beat egg whites with sugar.
Put over pie.
Bake pie under broiler until brown.
Fry bacon and break into small pieces.
Cook 1 onion in small amount of bacon fat until browned.
Add water, tomatoes and celery.
Simmer a while with Tabasco sauce and Worcestershire. Then add clams and potatoes and simmer until potatoes are done.
In a mixing bowl, combine nuts, dates and cherries.
In another bowl, stir together flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add to nut mixture, stirring until nuts and fruit are well coated. Beat eggs until foamy.
Stir in vanilla; fold into nut mixture. Mix well.
Pour into a greased and waxed paper-lined 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 45 minutes.
Mix thoroughly lime gelatin and boiling water.
Add pineapple and place in refrigerator to congeal.
Mix lemon gelatin with boiling water.
Put into refrigerator to congeal.
When both mixtures are firm, whip the cream until stiff.
Take package of cream cheese and mix with lemon gelatin with mixer.
Fold whipped cream into lemon Jell-O-cream cheese mixture.
Pour on top of lime Jell-O.
Cover and let stand overnight in the refrigerator.
Microwave Directions:
In large microwave-safe bowl, combine popcorn, cereal and nuts.
In 4-cup microwave-safe measuring cup, combine brown sugar, margarine, corn syrup and salt.
Microwave on High for 1 1/2 minutes; stir.
Microwave on High for 45 seconds to 2 minutes or until mixture comes to a rolling boil.
Stir in vanilla and baking soda.
(Mixture will become foamy.)
Pour over popcorn mixture and toss to coat.

Combine oats and milk; let stand 15 minutes. Beat egg and honey. Combine flour, baking powder and salt. Stir with egg mixture into oat mixture. Fold in carrots and orange rind, stirring only to moisten. Spoon into 12 muffin cups sprayed with nonfat cooking spray. Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes. Serves 12.
Drain asparagus and reserve liquid.
Spread asparagus in bottom of a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Dot with butter; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Combine mushroom soup with enough liquid to make 1 1/2 cups.
Pour over asparagus.
Sprinkle with cracker crumbs and grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, or until casserole is bubbly.
Clean onions; chop and put in a large skillet.
Add water and cook until tender and water is gone.
Add shortening and eggs, beaten.
Cook until eggs are done.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water and chill until it is the consistency of the unbeaten egg white.
Add egg white to gelatin and beat until fluffy and holds shape.
Pour into dishes and chill.
Top with Sauce.
Combine soup, stuffing, onion and paprika.
Spoon stuffing in 9-inch pie pan.
Arrange pork chops and press slightly into stuffing.
Combine sugar and mustard; spread lightly over pork chops.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Be sure pork chops are done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Remove 1/2 cup cookie dough for later use.
Mix flour with remaining cookie dough.
Put on pan, making 14-inch round.
Bake for 15 minutes, until lightly browned.
Let cool 10 minutes.
Loosen from pan; let cool completely.
Blend the cream cheese, brown sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Spread on cooled cookie dough.
Peel and slice apples thin.
Dip apples in lemon-lime soda and put on top of cream cheese mixture.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Heat caramel topping; spread on top.
Sprinkle nuts on top of topping.
Very delicious!
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Add sugar and lemon juice.
While hot, add raspberries, then fold in Cool Whip. Refrigerate and serve.
Heat 4 cups of milk.
Beat eggs; add sugar and 1/2 cup milk. Add flour and cornstarch.
Slowly add 1/2 cup milk to heated milk. Stir constantly.
Cool very good and add 2 cups Cool Whip.
Beat very good.
Delicious with cake and pies.
Beat 1 cup sugar into egg yolks, then stir in milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring.
Beat 3 tablespoons sugar into egg whites until they peak.
Mix whipping cream, cinnamon, pumpkin and vanilla.
Add to milk.
Cool 3 hours.
Top with egg whites.
Add dash of nutmeg.
Serves 8.
A holiday delight!
Enjoy!

recipes.t: Hot Italian Sausage And Spinach Pie
d: Brown sausage.
Drain and cool.
Cut into small pieces.
In small bowl, mix the reserved egg yolk with 1 teaspoon water.
In large bowl, combine all other ingredients.
Pour into pie crust. Top with additional crust and brush with the egg and water mixture.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cool for 15 minutes and top with hollandaise sauce.
For the apples, cut 1/4-inch thick and soak for 30 minutes in a brine made from the juice of the lemons, salt and water.
Spread on parchment paper on a cookie sheet.
Bake 2 to 3 hours in a 200° to 250° oven.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sift first 6 ingredients together and add the creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Add remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Drop by teaspoonful onto greased cookie sheet.
(I spooned batter into small paper bonbon size baking and party cups and placed cherry on top.)
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes.
While warm, sprinkle with sherry or brandy, if desired.
(I prefer them without the booze.)
Makes about 12 dozen miniature cakes.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Put back in pan and mix 1 can cream of chicken soup and 1 can milk and pour over macaroni; mix.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add corned beef (broken up) and mix with macaroni mixture.
Pour in casserole dish.
Top with thin slices of sharp cheese.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes in 350° oven.
Wash, drain and
shred cabbage.
Place juice in a large nonaluminum saucepan with
an
equal amount of water.
Add the cabbage and slowly bring
to
a boil.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the
bouillon, lemon juice, salt and pepper plus any other spices
and
vegetables
you wish.
Cover
and cook slowly for another 5 to 15 minutes, depending on the degree of doneness desired for
the
other
ingredients.
Serves 8.
For best results, reheat it very slowly.
Freezes well.

recipes.t: Pretending-To-Be-Red Cabbage Slaw From Northwoods Inn
d: Shred cabbage so it is irregular, with some fine and some coarse shreds.
Place in bowl with oil, vinegar, sugar, salt, seasoned salt, pepper, onion powder and paprika.
Mix well.
Prepare macaroni and cheese dinner using package directions. Add next 4 ingredients; mix well.
Use butter to coat casserole dish and sprinkle potato chips on bottom of bowl.
Add tuna mixture.
Top with potato chips and Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Put fat in saucepan.
Blend in flour, salt, pepper and mustard.
Add milk; boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Blend in mayonnaise.
Add potatoes and onion.
Break up bacon and blend in. Put in 2-quart casserole dish.
Top with crumbs.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves up to 10.
Place carrots in a buttered casserole.
Mix together all the ingredients except the bacon and add to carrots.
Crumble the bacon and sprinkle on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Arrange asparagus or broccoli in a greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish and set aside.
Salt, pepper and paprika chicken breasts after cutting into strips or nuggets.
Dredge chicken in flour.
Fry chicken in oil until almost done, not all the way. After frying, layer chicken on top of vegetables.
Mix soup, whipping cream, pimentos, milk and chili powder together.
Pour over vegetables and chicken.
Bake uncovered 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Serve over rice with salad and/or bread for a complete meal.
Wonderful!
My family's favorite.
Combine popped corn, roasted peanuts and pecans in large roasting pan.
Melt the butter in a large pan; stir in the sugars, corn syrup and salt.
Bring to a boil and boil 5 minutes, stirring often (244°).
Remove from heat; and stir in soda.
Bake at 250° for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Viennese Crescents(From "Jane Brody'S Good Food Gourmet")
d: In a medium-sized bowl, beat together butter and sugar until fluffy and well blended.
Add the vanilla and almond extracts and mix well.
Add the milk and blend for a few minutes (the milk won't go into the mixture completely).
Gradually add the flour, a little at a time, mixing well.
It's okay for the dough to be a little crumbly by the time you've added all the flour.
Add the ground almonds and mix as well as possible (break up the dough and distribute the almonds throughout).
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon and lemon juice; mix well.
Add apples and raisins; turn into 8-inch square baking dish.
In small bowl, combine remaining ingredients; sprinkle evenly over apples.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes or until apples are tender.
Serve warm.
Stir boiling water into gelatin in medium bowl 2 minutes or until completely dissolved.
Measure 1 1/2 cups; stir in applesauce and cinnamon.
Pour into bowl or 8 dessert glasses.
Refrigerate until set but not firm.
Refrigerate remaining gelatin until slightly thickened.
Mix in yogurt; spoon over gelatin in bowl. Refrigerate 2 hours or until set.
Garnish with additional yogurt, apple slices and mint leaves, if desired.
Slice cucumber and onion.
In bowl add sour cream vinegar, sugar, dill, salt and pepper.
Toss cucumbers in sour cream mixture.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Cut baking potatoes lengthwise into thin wedges, having washed them good.
Leave skins on.
Put Parmesan cheese and paprika into a plastic bag.
Shake to mix, then add the potato strips.
Shake to coat potatoes with mixture.
Remove from bag and place on cookie sheet and bake in 425° oven for 30 minutes or until crisp. Optional:
Spray cookie sheet with Pam before putting potatoes on it.
Serve with ketchup or salsa.
(Make your own vegetable oil spray using a flavorful oil and a spray bottle.)
Scrub yams.
Drop into boiling water.
Cover and cook until tender.
Drain, cool and peel.
(May also be peeled, sliced or diced and cooked in boiling water and drained.)
Combine brown sugar, cornstarch, salt and pepper.
Stir in apple juice and lemon juice.
Heat until mixture is bubbly and slightly thickened.
Add butter and lemon rind.
Mash or process yams with juice mixture. Place in a 1-quart casserole dish.
Dab with a little extra butter. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until heated.
Wash beans; remove ends.
Cut beans in 1-inch pieces.
In medium saucepan, combine beans, water and soup mix.
Bring to boil.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes or until beans are tender; drain beans.
Turn into serving dish; stir in butter until melted. Combine almonds, Parmesan cheese and paprika.
Sprinkle over beans.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add flour, salt, vanilla and oats. Roll into finger shapes about 1-inch long.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes (or until light brown).
Roll while warm in powdered sugar.
Cool and roll again.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Spray a large baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
On a large piece of wax paper, combine flour and seasonings.
On another piece of wax paper, place cereal.
Coat florets evenly in flour mixture.
Place egg white in shallow bowl.
Dip florets in egg white, then coat in cornflake crumbs.
Place florets on prepared sheet.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until golden and tender.
Serve with Ranch dressing for dipping.

Crumble corned beef into a medium bowl. Add cottage cheese, scallions, green pepper, parsley and seasonings. Mix thoroughly. Chill several hours to blend flavors and to firm mixture. Remove mixture from bowl and shape into a ball. Spread cream cheese evenly over ball. Sprinkle paprika and parsley in a sizable sheet of plastic wrap (optional). Wrap ball in this plastic and refrigerate. Serve on a cheese board or tray with assorted crackers and thick cucumber slices for spreading. Garnish with sprigs of parsley, if desired.

recipes.t: Skillet Pot Roast With Vegetables(Football Sunday Dinner)
d: In a large skillet, brown roast in hot fat.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Put in large Dutch oven.
Add water to partially cover meat.
Cover pot tightly.
Simmer for 1 hour, adding water when necessary.
Boil squash; drain and add butter.
Beat egg and add to squash.
Add onion, salt and pepper, then crackers.
Pour into a 2-quart Pyrex casserole and sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix beef with beaten egg.
Add chopped onion and salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately on buttered ry bread.
Heat electric frypan to 220°. Melt butter in pan; add dates and salt. Beat eggs and sugar and add to pan. Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Cool, then add fruit and nuts. Stir in Rice Krispies and flavoring. Form 1 1/2-inch balls and roll in coconut or extra chopped nuts. Store in refrigerator. Will keep up to 1 month.
Butter the bottom and sides of a 9 x 13 x 3-inch baking pan. Layer vanilla wafers on the bottom (whole wafers).
Cook the berries (no sugar added) slowly until they are just ready to burst (should still be whole and firm).
Cool.
Layer the cooled berries over the wafers.
Prepare pudding according to directions and layer the pudding over the berries.
Prepare Dream Whip according to directions and layer over the pudding. Make about 3/4 cup of crushed vanilla wafer crumbs and sprinkle over the Dream Whip. Chill for 2 hours.
A cake this size will make 10 to 12 nice size servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Rinse chicken inside and out; pat dry. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Rub garlic over the skin, then place inside cavity.
Stuff lemon and onion inside cavity.
Tie legs together.
Mix pudding mix and milk in bowl at lowest speed of rotary beater until blended, about 30 seconds.
Blend in pumpkin, spice, and 2 cups of Cool Whip.
Whip.
Pour into pie shells.
Chill 4 hours.
Garnish with remaining Cool Whip and pecans.
Drain cherries; save juice.
Add water to cherry juice to make 5 cups.
Over medium heat, heat cherries, liquid, sugar, lemon juice and anise seed to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Using a blender, blend mixture until smooth, 1/2 mixture at a time.
Then heat mixture to boil again.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine refried beans, jalapeno relish and enchilada sauce together in a bowl, mixing together.
Add 6 ounces of cheese and mix (add fresh jalapenos, optional).
Wipe inside of bowl with paper towel (this keeps from burning the inside of the bowl.)
Sprinkle with remaining 2 ounces of cheese.
Cover and place in oven for about 15 minutes.
Stir and cook for 15 minutes longer or until bubbling or cover and microwave for about 10 minutes.
Stir before serving.
Dip tortilla chips.
Trim fat from chops.
Mix flour, salt and pepper.
Dip chops in mixture.
Preheat electric skillet to 360°; add oleo.
Brown chops on both sides.
Add 1/2 cup of water, cover and open vent. Set dish at medium.
Simmer and time dish for 30 minutes.
After frypan shuts off, lay corn and broccoli in frypan and add remaining 3/4 cup water.
Close vent and continue simmering for 10 to 13 minutes.
Serves 4.
Cook
and
drain
broccoli.
Combine
mushroom soup and salad dressing.
Arrange
in layers in baking dish, broccoli, soup mixture,
eggs
and pimento, nuts and bread crumbs.
Bake in a 350° oven for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold water in a medium saucepan. Let stand 1 minute.
Add tomato juice to remaining ingredients except lettuce.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until gelatin dissolves. Cool to room temperature.
Pour mixture into a lightly oiled 4-cup mold.
Cover and chill at least 8 hours.
Unmold onto a lettuce lined plate.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Place tortilla on working surface and spread with beans and rest of ingredients through green chiles.
Roll up and wrap tightly in plastic wrap.
Place in refrigerator for at least 2 hours. Slice into 1-inch rounds and serve with guacamole and salsa.
Put the water on to boil; dash of salt in water.
Put the rice in boiling water; cover and turn fire low and cook 20 minutes or until the rice is done.
Simmer the cut dates in butter a few minutes.
Saute almonds in another pan in butter until they are a little brown.
Add the almonds and dates to the rice and serve.
Fork whip egg and oil together in a shallow bowl.
Place the flour in another shallow bowl.
Dip the cutlets first in the flour, then in the egg mixture and then again in the flour. Arrange the coated cutlets on a nonstick cookie sheet.
Place in a very hot 450° oven and bake 6 minutes on each side.
Cut each large tomato into 3 thick slices.
Squeeze each gently to remove some of the seeds.
Arrange the tomatoes, with cut sides up, on the rack of a broiler pan.
In a small bowl, combine the sour cream with the salt, pepper, sugar, flour, green onion and green chilies; stir until well blended.
Spoon mixture evenly over the tomatoes, then sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top.
Just before serving, place tomatoes in a preheated broiler about 4 inches from heat; broil just until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown, about 4 minutes.
The tomatoes will be just warm.
Makes 8 or 9 servings.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Press onto the bottom of an 8-inch spring-form pan.
Chill.
Dissolve the gelatin in the boiling water and cool to lukewarm.
In a blender, thoroughly mix the cream cheese and sugar.
Slowly add the gelatin and blend well.
Pour the mixture into the chilled crust and refrigerate until firm.
In a saucepan, bring the crushed pineapple with juice, the water and cornstarch to a boil, stirring constantly. Cool 15 minutes and spread over the top of the cheese cake.
Chill at least 1 hour.
Yields 16 servings at 125 calories per serving.
Place parsley and garlic in food processor or blender. Process using on/off turns until finely chopped. Add the olives and process until finely chopped but not pureed.
Transfer to medium bowl. Place artichoke in food processor and process until finely chopped, not pureed. Add to olive mixture. Stir in red peppers, capers and lemon juice. Season with black pepper.
Saute onion in oil until tender.
Add picante sauce, water and green chilies.
Bring to a boil; then add rice.
Bring to simmer. Add smoked sausage that has been sliced.
Cover and simmer until rice is done.
Stir occasionally.
Heat butter in large saucepan; add frozen peas.
Cover and cook slowly until peas are just defrosted.
Do not add water. When peas are thawed completely, add lettuce, onion and seasonings.
Mix lightly.
Cover tightly and steam for 4 minutes, no more!
Yields 6 servings.
Mix cheeses and dressing mix together. Refrigerate 1 hour. Mix ham into cheese mixture. Form a ball. Roll ball in nuts and parsley. That's it!
Put water, vinegar, sugar, salt and pickling spices into a pan and boil for 3 minutes.
Put remaining ingredients into jar and then add boiled water mixture.
Close jars and place jars into water bath.
Boil until green pepper changes color.
In a bowl, cream together the butter, Eagle Brand milk and powdered sugar.
Add the coconut, nuts and flavoring.
Chill in refrigerator at least an hour, then roll dough into balls.
Place on greased cookie sheet and chill again.
Soften yeast in water.
Add soup and dressing mix.
Slowly add flour to form stiff dough.
Knead about 5 minutes.
Place in greased bowl, cover, let rise until double, about 30 minutes. Shape dough into 4 (10-inch) loaves.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Cover; let rise until light and double, about 30 minutes. Bake at 400° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cool immediately on wire racks.
Cook sausage in a skillet until browned; drain and set aside. Combine next 5 ingredients, mixing well. Cut in shortening until it resembles coarse meal. Dissolve yeast in warm water (105° to 115°).
Let stand 5 minutes. Add yeast to buttermilk, stirring. Add to dry ingredients, stirring until dry ingredients are moistened.
Knead in sausage. Turn dough out onto a floured surface.
Knead lightly. Roll out dough and cut into rounds.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Combine the flour, cocoa and salt and set aside.
Line cookie sheets with foil.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat butter and sugar until creamy.
Add eggs and chocolate syrup; mix well.
Add flour mixture; mix well.
Stir in chocolate morsels and oats; mix.
Drop by heaping tablespoonful onto pans.
Bake for 10 minutes; rotate trays and switch shelves.
Bake an additional 10 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes and remove from trays.
Heat oil in Dutch oven. Brown 1-inch cubes of meat.
Stir in other ingredients. Simmer and cook 10 minutes.
Mix biscuit mix and water. Drop on stew.
Add oregano and paprika.
Cover tightly and simmer 20 minutes or until dumplings are done.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot water.
Let it cool before adding to cake mix.
Mix oil with cake mix.
Add eggs, one at a time. Add Jell-O and flavoring; mix well with mixer.
Grease and flour Bundt pan or tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in regular home oven.
Mix together separate the salad dressing, dill weed and garlic salt.
Stir all together.
Boil and debone chicken and save broth.
Cook vermicelli in chicken broth.
Chop and saute onion and pepper in margarine; combine vegetables, tomatoes, Worcestershire sauce, mushrooms and cheese with vermicelli.
Stir until cheese melts and add chicken which has been torn into small bits.
Stir well.
Add some broth to assure a moist casserole.
Bake at 350° until hot and bubbly.
Grind together first 4 ingredients and sprinkle with salt. Let set 3 hours; drain well.
Boil together vinegar, sugar, mustard and allspice.
Add the well drained vegetables and cook for 25 minutes.
Pack in sterile jars and seal.
Makes 6 to 7 pints, according to size of vegetables.
Brown meat and onions until meat is done and onions are tender.
Boil potatoes, then rice or mash them.
Add to meat and onions.
Add salt, pepper and poultry seasoning to taste. Refrigerate until you are ready to use it.

recipes.t: Gramma'S Creamed Green Beans And Mushrooms
d: Cook green beans to desired tenderness in salt water.
Drain. In large skillet, saute mushrooms in butter until soft.
Add half and half and cornstarch, then seasonings to taste.
Stir constantly.
Bring to boil, turn down heat until thickened.
Add cooked, drained green beans to mixture and simmer on low heat until all ingredients are coated.
Taste and adjust seasonings. Serves 8 to 10.
Into a mixing bowl, place shortening and sugar and beat until light and creamy.
Add the eggs and vanilla, beating to mix.
Mix together the flour and baking powder, then add to the shortening-egg mixture and beat slowly to mix.
Combine sugar, shortening and water and bring just to a boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add chocolate bits and vanilla.
Stir until chocolate melts.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Sift dry ingredients together; add nuts.
Spread in 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Mix together chili, cheese and onions.
Blend well.
Separate a portion of filling to spread over top of enchiladas.
Spoon filling in each flour tortilla and roll.
Place in pan and spread remaining filling over top of enchiladas.
Bring pot of salted water to boil.
Add onions; cook 3 minutes to loosen skins.
Drain and cool.
Cut root ends from onions. Squeeze onions at stem end (onions will slip out of skins). Combine pearl onions, sherry, raisins, honey, water, butter and thyme in skillet.
Boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to very low; cover and simmer until liquid evaporates and onions caramelize.
Mix Jell-O according to directions on package.
Refrigerate until it has thickened.
Put marshmallows and a little heavy cream in top of a double boiler and melt.
Beat remaining heavy cream and cream cheese.
Add melted marshmallows and mix.
Stir in drained pineapple and chopped nuts.
Add mixture to thicken Jell-O.
Pour into a mold.
Mix hamburger, onions, green pepper, some of the Tater Tots and half of the cheese together.
Place in a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine milk and soup together and pour over.
Top with remaining Tater Tots and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Make meatballs and brown and drain grease away.
Layer bottom with 1/2 of the flour tortillas.
Add 1/2 green peppers, onions, meatballs and 1 quart of salsa.
Repeat another layer and top with cheese.
Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Top with sour cream and black olives.
Melt oleo in long dish.
Pour over crackers and almonds.
Mix well.
Drain corn and spread over bottom of pan.
Cover with green beans.
Mix sour cream, soup, onions and cheese.
Pour over beans.
Sprinkle crackers and almonds; mix over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a 10-inch skillet, combine soup, milk and mustard.
On medium heat, heat to boiling.
Stir in broccoli.
Return to boiling, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook 5 minutes until broccoli is tender.
Stir in pasta and chicken and heat thoroughly.
Serve.
Filling:
Mix four cups cottage cheese with 2 eggs and 1 Tbsp. salt.
In the top of a double boiler, mix egg yolk with some of milk.
Add remaining milk, 2 tablespoons sugar, salt and tapioca. Cook 8 to 10 minutes over rapidly boiling water. Stir frequently.
Prepare rice as label directs.
In a 10-inch skillet over medium heat, heat sausage links and water to a boil. Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Remove cover; continue cooking.
Turn sausage links frequently until water evaporates.
Remove sausage links to paper towel and drain.
Dice sausage links.
In drippings remaining in skillet over medium heat, cook red and green peppers until tender.
Stir occasionally. Stir in rice, sausage links, chopped tomato and salt to taste.
Heat through.
Stir cake mix and pie filling together (very thick).
Combine eggs, vanilla, oil and nuts; add to cake mix and blend well. Place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool and serve plain or frost with vanilla icing with 1 teaspoon cherry extract mixed in.
Brown ground beef.
Add water, add onion and add green pepper. Add chili powder.
Add garlic powder.
Add tomato paste.
The longer it cooks the better chili is.
Slice sausage thinly.
Peel and cube potatoes.
Add peas and 1 cup of water.
Cook until potatoes are soft and then add milk. Season with pepper.
Layer chicken breast and broccoli in baking dish.
Mix chicken soup, sour cream, mayonnaise and Cheddar cheese.
Pour over broccoli and chicken.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
(You may also top with bread crumbs.)
Cut dried beef in small pieces. mix all ingredients together. Cut the middle out of the round loaf of Hawaiian bread. Put the mixture in the middle of the bread, wrap in foil and
bake at 325 degrees for 1 hr.
Serve with Ritz crackers. When the dip is almost gone, cut the bread into pieces and dot the remainder of the dip on it.
Place livers, onion and soda crackers through food grinder. Add beaten eggs, flour, parsley flakes, salt and pepper.
Mix well, drop by teaspoons into boiling chicken broth.
Cover and let simmer for about 30 minutes.
Line bottom and sides of a 9 x 13-inch dish with vanilla wafers.
Cover wafers completely with sliced bananas.
Overlap them a bit.
Prepare pudding according to package directions, using 3 cups milk.
Add sweetened condensed milk and fold in whipped topping.
Pour over bananas; chill and serve.
Serves 12 to 15, possibly more because it is very rich.
Keeps well overnight.
Mix thoroughly 1/4 cup soup, beef, bread crumbs, egg, onion, salt and 1/8 teaspoon each pepper, sage and thyme.
Shape firmly into 6 mini meat loaves.
In skillet, brown loaves in shortening. Stir in remaining soup and seasonings and water.
Cook over low heat for 20 to 30 minutes.
Place rolls in 9-inch round pie plate.
All points should go toward center.
Press into plate.
Sprinkle chips over crust (half).
Top with mixture.
Sprinkle with cheese and remaining chips.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add balance of ingredients, except raisins and English walnuts.
Bake in 2 large cake pans.
Before putting in oven, put drops of butter all over them.
Next cover thickly with brown sugar.
Drop a few seedless raisins and English walnuts on top.
Raisins can be omitted.
Bake at 350° until done.
In a 3-quart casserole, combine broccoli and water; cover and microwave for 1 minute on High.
Drain and rinse in cold water. In a bowl or plastic bag, combine broccoli, mushrooms and dressing.
Refrigerate at least 8 hours.
If using a bowl, stir several times.
With a bag, just turn bag over several times. Remove vegetables to serving platter with slotted spoon.
Cook onions and garlic in oil in a large, heavy pan, until tender.
Add remaining ingredients.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer until fish flakes easily with fork, about 5 minutes.
Makes 8 servings (about 1 1/4 cups each).
Contains 210 calories per serving.
Heat oil in a skillet.
Roll tube biscuits flat and fry in hot oil
until
puffy
and
golden
brown.
Place on paper towels. Serve with butter, honey, jam and a piece of bacon.

recipes.t: Date, Nut & Chocolate Chip Loaf Cake
d: Soak first four ingredients together in a small bowl (preferably over night). Then mix together margarine, sugar, & eggs in a large bowl. Blend into margarine mixture: 3 c. flour - alternate with date mixture, salt, nuts, vanilla, and chocolate chips. Place mixture into greased & floured loaf pans. Makes 2 large or 3 small loaves. Bake at 350° for about 60-70 minutes.
Mix butter and cocoa in saucepan and blend in sugar, vanilla, egg, crumbs, coconut and nuts.
Mix well and press into ungreased 11 1/2 x 7 1/2-inch or 9 x 9-inch pan.
Refrigerate.
Grease and flour a Bundt pan.
Separate eggs.
Beat egg whites and 6 tablespoons sugar; let stand.
Cream butter and sugar; add yolks, one at a time.
Cream together.
Add vanilla and lemon flavoring.
Mix well.
Add flour, salt and milk; beat.
Fold in egg whites.
Bake at 300° for 3 hours or until done.
Saute thin slices of parsnips in butter until tender, then add apricot jam and continue to cook until jam thickens.
Combine ham, seasonings and mayonnaise.
Slit franks almost to ends, three-quarters way through.
Stuff franks with mixture and wrap with bacon strips, securing with toothpicks.
In a 12-inch skillet
over
medium heat, in hot butter, cook next 4
ingredients
until vegetables are tender.
Remove from heat.
Meanwhile,
cut
Italian
bread in half crosswise. Hollow out each half, leaving a 1/4-inch shell.
Crumble bread in
large bowl.
Beat
cream
cheese
until
smooth;
stir
in pimentos, red pepper, cabbage mixture and bread crumbs.
Pack mixture
into hollowed
out crust.
Wrap tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate until mixture is firm, at least 4 hours.
In a large bowl, combine ground beef, eggs, bread crumbs, Spatini mix and catsup.

Cook and drain macaroni. Saute sausage, onion and green pepper in skillet until sausage is done. Drain. Combine sausage mixture and the rest of ingredients except cheese. Pour into casserole dish, sprinkle with cheese. Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Trim excess fat from beef.
Prick beef on all sides with a fork.
Rub in garlic powder and onion soup mix.
Pour Pepsi over and under meat; cover with foil.
Bake for 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours at 325°.
Cool and refrigerate overnight in the original pan.
Next day, skim off solidified fat that has formed on liquid.
Slice meat and reheat in juices.
Combine eggs, sugar, syrup, vanilla and salt.
Mix well. Combine butter and cocoa.
Stir in mixture.
Add pecans and coconut. Turn into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Boil yams, mash and let cool.
In large bowl, cream together butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each egg.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Sift flour, soda, baking powder, cinnamon, salt and nutmeg.
Beat into first mixture; add nuts and turn into a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 20 minutes or until a wooden pick comes out clean.
This recipe was given to me by Mrs. Aleece Lane in 1989.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add the linguine and cook at a rolling boil until just tender.
Drain; rinse under cold water.
Drain again and set aside in a large mixing bowl.
Place the garlic, vinegar, brown sugar, peanut butter and soy sauce in a food processor.
Process for 1 minute.
With the motor running, slowly add the sesame and hot chili oils through the feed tube and process until well blended.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grate and squeeze the rind and juice from the orange and lemon and keep separate (lemon is used for the icing).
Cream sugar and butter.
Add orange juice, orange rind, and egg yolk.
Mix. Stir in baking soda into the sour cream.
Add to mixture.
Combine flour, salt, and baking powder and add to mixture.
Beat the egg white and fold in last.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Coat cookie sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt onto waxed paper. Cream shortening, sugar and eggs until fluffy.
Mix in orange rind and juice.
Stir in flour mixture until blended.
Mix in pecans. Drop dough in rounded teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheets leaving 3 inches between cookies.
Bake in 375° oven for 12 to 15 minutes until brown.
Remove to wire rack.
Frost with Orange Icing while warm.
Mix together sugar, egg yolks, butter and flour.
Fold in egg whites.
In a nine-inch pie plate, place unbaked pie shell. Spread rhubarb on bottom.
Pour mixture over rhubarb.
Bake at 350° until almost done.
Then turn to 375° to brown.
For each train, glue end of 1 ribbon onto wide side of 1 gum package.
Glue 4 peppermint candies onto side of gum package to make wheels.
Glue roll of ring-shaped candies onto ribbon-topped gum package to make engine.
Glue 1 chocolate kiss and 1 caramel onto engine.
Glue peppermint candies onto sides of 2 rolls of ring-shaped candies and 2 gum packages to make train cars.
Glue remaining ribbon onto top of gum and candy train cars, spacing cars about 1/2-inch apart.
Glue assorted candies onto top of ribbon on gum and candy train cars.
Makes 4 candy trains.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten eggs.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to shortening mixture alternately with sour cream.
Add vanilla.
Fold in apples by hand.
Bake in a well-greased 13 x 9-inch pan at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Mix together as pie crust 4 cups of the flour, the salt, 1 cup sugar and butter or margarine.
Add the remaining flour and blend. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.
After yeast works well, add to the warm milk.
Add all to the flour mixture; knead.
Let rise as usual.
This can be made into rolls or coffee cake.
If making coffee cake, after putting into pans, spread a thin coat of sour cream and some sugar on top.
After rising, bake at 375° until brown.
Add more sour cream; sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon and return to oven until it bubbles up.
Mix milk, salad dressing, vinegar and sugar in bowl and place in microwave or a double boiler.
Add cheese and melt, stirring occasionally. Add pimentos.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch bake dish with margarine.
Pour cherries in bake dish.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over cherries.
Sprinkle nuts over top of cake mix.
Melt margarine; pour over nuts.
Sprinkle sugar on top for a glaze. Bake for 45 minutes.
Cook celery and onion in margarine until tender.
Stir in flour.
Add broth and 1 package frozen broccoli.
Simmer 1 hour. Put vegetables through a food mill or puree in blender.
Return to broth.
Add second package of broccoli and cheese.
Simmer 30 to 45 minutes until broccoli is tender and cheese is melted.
Add cream if desired.
Crush corn chips in package.
Grease a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Layer the corn chips, chili, onion and cheese; repeat layers.
Top with crushed chips.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Mix sugar and butter until creamy.
Melt chocolate and add to creamed mixture.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating 5 minutes after each egg is added.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Line pan with crushed graham crackers. Pour mixture into it and sprinkle top with crushed crackers.
Top with whipped cream and keep refrigerated.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Cut roast beef into strips.
Saute garlic, peppers and onions in olive oil until tender.
Combine roast beef strips with all ingredients and toss. Serve warm or cold.
Cut carrots, zucchini and avocado into slivers.
Cook rice. Warm sushi sheets to make more flexible.
Spread rice over sheets 1 inch from one and and 2 inches from other end.
Wet the ends. Lay slivers of carrots, zucchini and avocado and roll tight.
Roll back and forth to seal ends.
Cut rolls into 1-inch pieces.
Be careful in cutting.
Combine all ingredients except hot dogs in large pan; cook for 20 minutes.
Add hot dogs to sauce; cook until liquid has boiled down and is slightly thick.
Can be put in the crock-pot on low for about 6 hours.
Mix apple juice and Sure-Jell in large pan and bring to a boil. Add sugar.
Cook until mixture jells, stirring constantly.
Pour mixture into jars.
Mix together Cheddar cheese, mayonnaise, onion, nuts, black pepper and dash of cayenne. Form with well in middle.
Fill with strawberry or raspberry preserves.
Let spinach thaw out, then squeeze out all water and juices. Chop apple in fine pieces and mix with spinach.
Then empty dry vegetable soup mix into bowl.
Mix in sour cream and mayonnaise, and salt, or nature seasoning spices blended.
Mix them real good. Then take a loaf of Hawaiian bread.
Cut out center of the bread. Place spinach dip in center of the bowl made with loaf.
Cut the center of the bread, and place loaf in center of cake plate.
Then place cut bread around loaf.
Mix shortening, sugar and eggs; stir in butter, milk and vanilla.
Sift dry ingredients together and add nuts.
Combine with cream mixture and let stand 1 hour.
Bake at 400° in a greased cookie sheet.
Frost with chocolate frosting.
Slowly sift pectin into crushed berries.
Set aside 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add corn syrup, stirring well. Gradually stir in sugar.
When sugar is dissolved, add lemon juice.
Remove crusts from bread (save crusts for bread crumb toppings).
Flatten bread with finger tips or rolling pin.
Spread generously with dip.
Lay three whole beans on edge of slice of bread, roll up and roll in melted butter.
Arrange about 1 inch apart on cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake 12 minutes at 400°.
Yields 8 servings.
Saute onions in butter in a large skillet for 5 minutes.
Add hominy, green chilies, sour cream, chili powder, and pepper;
add 1/2 cup cheese.
Stir well.
Pour into a lightly greased 10 x 6 x 2 baking dish; bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining 1 cup cheese over top, bake an additional 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Yield:
6-8 servings.
Measure water, molasses, shortening, sugars and salt into a big bowl.
Heat until shortening is melted and mixture is warm. Stir in yeast and rye flour; beat.
Stir in as much white flour as possible and then with your hands work in rest.
Knead until smooth (I don't use quite as much flour).
Let rise until double in bulk.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Makes 5 loaves.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Cut the onion, bell pepper and zucchini into chunks; place in a large bowl.
Add the garlic, corn and mushrooms.
Coat vegetables with olive oil.
Stir in the herbs and salt.
Mix well.
Place vegetables in a large baking dish and bake until tender, about 20 minutes.
Serves 4.
In skillet, brown beef and cook onion until tender.
Stir to separate meat.
Add soup, chili powder and beans.
Cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In 9 x 13-inch pan, bake cake according to directions. Meanwhile in medium saucepan, combine pineapple with juice and sugar.
Cook over medium heat stirring occasionally until thick and syrupy.
When cake is done, remove from oven and pierce top with a fork at 1-inch intervals.
Pour pineapple mixture over cake and spread evenly.
Cool completely.
Combine pudding mix with milk.
Blend until thick.
Spread over cake.
Beat whipping cream until soft peaks form.
Add sugar.
Beat until stiff.
Spread over cake.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Refrigerate.
Beat yams, butter, honey and seasonings together in large mixing bowl until light and fluffy.
Stir in milk, pecans and raisins.
Turn mixture into a 1-quart baking dish.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 minutes.
Combine soup, milk, brown sugar and cinnamon in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 2 minutes.
Add butter, toast, almonds and raisins.
Spoon half of the soup mixture in the bottom of a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with apples and remaining toast mixture.
Cover and bake at 350°
for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 5 minutes more.
Serve with whipped cream.
Dissolve yeast in 2 tablespoons warm water.
Add butter, salt and soda; mix well.
Cook squash in small amount of water until tender; drain.
Add margarine and mash.
Combine remaining ingredients, except breadcrumbs and pecan halves.
Add to squash.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart buttered casserole. Top with breadcrumbs; dot with margarine.
Garnish with pecan halves.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook ground beef and onion until meat is browned and onion is tender in large skillet over medium flame; drain.
Add cubed cheese and chili.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until cheese is melted.
Serve hot with tortilla chips.
Makes 4 cups.
Mix sugar and oil together; beat.
Add 1 egg at a time and beat well.
Mix all dry ingredients, except soda, together.
Put soda in buttermilk.
Alternate adding dry ingredients and buttermilk; mix well.
Add prunes and nuts; mix well.
Pour into a greased and floured Bundt pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Beef Stew In Cream Sauce With Turnips(Low-Carb)
d: Brown beef in grape seed oil on high in large Dutch oven pan. Sprinkle seasonings on beef. Add turnip chunks. Add water. Cover pan. Reduce temperature to low simmer. Cook 2 hours. When there is about 20 minutes left, melt butter in saucepan and saute mushrooms and onions until tender.
Add to beef mixture. Add cream and Parmesan cheese.
Simmer whole pot until 2 hours total are up.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Measure water in separate bowl. Add yeast and 1/2 teaspoon of flour mixture to water.
Stir and set aside.
Cut shortening into the remaining flour mixture.
Add water mixture.
Mix. Dump onto floured board and knead.
Let rise.
Knead again.
Pinch off and shape into rolls.
Brush with melted butter. Let rise.
Bake in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Add salt, garlic and oregano to chili sauce.
Place strips of pork (2 x 6-inch) in the chili sauce and marinate 24 hours.
To prepare, cut into small pieces and fry in fat.
Add chili sauce to cover and cook until pork is done, approximately 1 hour at 400°.
Beat butter and sugars together.
Add eggs, vanilla and peanut butter.
Stir in oats.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Roll into balls and flatten on lightly greased cookie sheets.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes at 350°.
Makes 6 dozen cookies.
Combine milk, egg and stuffing crumbs in bowl.
Let stand 2 minutes. Add onion and beef.
Mix well.
Place in shallow baking dish and shape into 2 small loaves. Top with barbecue sauce. Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
For 4 to 6 servings, double all ingredients but use 1 egg.
In a small bowl, mix potatoes and garlic salt, then spread it in a 1 1/2 qt. greased baking pan.
Sprinkle ham over potatoes.
Dice bacon and onion; brown in butter in skillet. Grate potatoes.
Put in eggs, milk and salt; stir well.
Put into baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until brown.
Serve with sour cream.

recipes.t: Sausage And Hash Browns Pie(Makes One 10-Inch Pie)
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
In medium bowl, combine potatoes, margarine and bouillon.
Spoon into lightly greased 10-inch pie plate; press on bottom and up side rim to form crust.
Bake 25 minutes.
Reduce oven temperature to 350°.
In large skillet, cook sausage and onion; pour off fat.
Stir in eggs, cottage cheese and cheese food pieces.
Pour into prepared crust.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until set.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Garnish as desired. Refrigerate leftovers.
Chop garlic fine.
Add salt and basil and mash into paste. Rub pork chops with the paste and leave for 1 hour.
Cut the bread diagonally into 1-inch slices.
Blend the butter, 1 tablespoon parsley, oregano, dill and garlic.
Put the bread slices together again after putting the butter mixture on each slice.
Shape aluminum foil around the bread in a boat like fashion, twisting the ends and leaving the top open.
Spread a small amount of the butter mixture on top of bread, then sprinkle liberally with Parmesan cheese and the 1 tablespoon parsley.
Heat in 400° oven for 8 to 10 minutes.
Saute onions in butter.
Combine stuffing and beef broth in large bowl.
Add parsley, ground chuck, Parmesan cheese, egg, salt and pepper.
Mix lightly until well blended.
Shape into a loaf and place in a shallow baking pan. Bake in 375° oven for 30 minutes.
Pour tomato sauce over the top and sprinkle with oregano.
Continue baking for 30 minutes longer.
Serves 4 to 6.
Put butter in skillet and melt, cooking celery and onions that have been chopped up.
When slightly brown, add meat.
While cooking or before, put bread that has been slightly toasted, in milk that has been almost boiled.
Pour milk over broken bread pieces and let stand 30 minutes.
Then add all ingredients together.
Cut cheeses in small pieces.
Combine over low heat until cheeses melt.
Stir in wine and crab; heat through.
Serve in chafing dish with Shredded Wheat wafers.
Makes 3 cups.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce and onions.
Refrigerate. In small skillet, saute the almonds with 1 tablespoon sugar and butter; set aside.
In a separate bowl, combine oil, vinegar, 1/4 cup sugar and seasonings.
Mix well.
Just before serving, add noodles, almonds and dressing to lettuce.
Mix well.
Use a slow cooker. One hour before serving, add 1 cup sour cream and mix in. Pour over cooked noodles.
Melt chocolate and butter together in top of double boiler. Take off heat, stir in milk; blend in flour.
Stir in vanilla and nuts.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Drop by teaspoonful onto foil lined baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool thoroughly on wire racks.
Makes about 65 cookies.
Use large cucumbers.
Peel, slice and core out centers for 1 gallon rings.
Place in large pan or gallon glass jar.
Mix pickling lime with enough water to cover.
Let stand 24 hours. Drain.
Wash in clean water.
Soak in cold water for 3 hours.
Mix red food coloring, powdered alum and enough water to cover cucumbers in large kettle.
Simmer 2 hours.
Drain.
Bring to a boil the vinegar, sugar, 1 cup water, cinnamon sticks and red hots. Pour over cucumbers.
Reheat syrup for 3 days and pour over cucumbers.
After 3 days, pack cucumbers into hot jar and pour hot syrup over them.
Seal.

Combine sweet potatoes, flour, sugar, and milk. Beat at medium speed for one minute. Add salt & vanilla mixing well. Stir in coconut and pecans. Melt butter in 9 x 13 pan in oven at 400 degrees. Pour butter into sweet potato mixture, mixing thoroughly. Spread batter in baking dish. Bake at 400 degrees for 30-40 minutes or until edges are brown.
Combine raisins and apple juice in a large bowl and let stand for five minutes.
Add buttermilk, egg whites, oil and honey; whisk until smooth.
Sift the flour, cornmeal, baking powder and baking soda into another large bowl.
Whisk in brown sugar, ginger and cardamom.
Add bananas and toss lightly.
Add dry ingredients to buttermilk mixture and stir just to mix with a wooden spoon.
(Stir as little as possible, or the muffins will be tough.)
Line muffin tin cups with paper liners and spray lightly with vegetable oil spray.
Spoon batter into cups, filling each two-thirds full.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 30 minutes, until puffed and lightly browned.
Turn onto a wire rack to cool.
Makes 12 muffins.
Chop fine or grind pecans.
Crumble wafers.
Mix them well with sugar.
Beat egg whites until stiff (peaks).
Add to dry ingredients; mix well.
Add vanilla.
Pour mixture into well buttered glass pie pan.
Cook in a preheated 350° oven for 25 or 30 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cream together first 6 items, then add flour, soda and salt and mix well.
Add raisins and oats; mix well.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes or until golden brown at 350° on greased cookie sheet.
Combine dates and boiling water; cool.
Add soda into date mixture.
Cream the shortening and sugar.
Sift together the salt, cocoa and flour.
Add egg and date mixture.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Brown meat with bell pepper, onion, garlic salt and pepper in a large pot or wok; drain off excess fat.
Add soup and water; mix well.
Spray or grease a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Place a layer of tortilla chips in bottom of pan.
Pour on some of the meat mixture.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with additional chopped onion and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for about 1 hour or until bubbly in a 350° oven.

Place carrots in a skillet; add 1-inch water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes or until crisp-tender. Drain. Cut a thin lengthwise slice out of each carrot. Scoop out carrot, leaving a 1/4-inch shell; set aside. Process the removed carrot in a blender until finely chopped. Transfer to a bowl; add mayonnaise, onion, horseradish, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Spoon into carrot shells. Place in a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine the ground beef, eggs and crackers.
Mix soup mix and milk; then add.
Shape into two loaves in shallow baking dish; bake 1 hour.
Mix corned beef hash, 1 egg and bread crumbs together well. Press into bottom of pie plate, sides and bottom.
Mix 3 eggs and milk well.
Lay cheese on top of corned beef in pie plate. Sprinkle cheese with flour.
Pour milk and egg mixture in pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Melt 1/2 cup butter and 4 squares chocolate over low heat in a heavy saucepan.
Cool.
Stir in sugar.
Add 4 eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Add flour, salt and 1 teaspoon of vanilla; mix well.
Pour into a greased and floured 10 x 15-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or just until firm.
Do not overbake.
Melt remaining 1/2 cup butter and 1 square of chocolate over low heat in a heavy saucepan.
Stir in powdered sugar, blending well.
Remove from heat.
Add egg, vanilla and lemon juice.
Stir in pecans.
Spread frosting over warm brownies.
Mix dry ingredients.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add buttermilk and butter or margarine.
Stir just until mixed.
Let stand 5 minutes before pouring flapjacks on hot griddle.
Makes about 18 flapjacks.
Cook cauliflower and broccoli according to package directions; drain.
Cut up any large pieces; combine both cans of drained corn.
Stir in cheese and soup.
Fold in cooked veggies and mushrooms in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Toss onion rings with melted butter; sprinkle on top.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Mix meat, onion, salt, garlic, egg and crackers up in a large pan.
Make into patties and place in pan.
Drip mushroom soup over each pattie.
Cook in oven at 350° until done.
Combine flour and brown sugar.
Cut in margarine to form crumbs.
Measure 3/4 c. of crumbs with 1/4 c. nuts and set aside. To remaining crumb mixture add the next 7 ingredients.
Combine milk and eggs and stir into dry ingredients just to moisten.
Heat milk. Add melted butter and margarine.
Add sugar and oil.
Stir to dissolve.
Add beaten eggs and salt.
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water. Add to above.
Stir
and knead in flour. Depending on day, may need a little more flour.
Place in greased bowl and turn. Cover.
Let rise.
Punch down.
Let rise again. Form into loaves.
Let rise again.
Brush on the glaze (2 eggs, beaten) and bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until done.
Mix graham cracker crumbs, butter and cinnamon together. Spread about 1/4 c. of the crumb mixture on the bottom of a buttered deep 10 inch cake pan.
Separate eggs and beat yolks well.
Add milk, lemon juice, rind and applesauce to beaten egg yolks.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Fold into milk mixture. Pour into the cake pan.
Cover with remaining graham cracker crumbs. Bake at 350° degrees for 50 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar. Add eggs then other ingredients and flour enough to roll.

Cook cabbage, covered, in boiling salted water for about 10 minutes. Drain. Melt butter or margarine in saucepan; blend in flour, dry mustard, salt and pepper. Stir in milk and cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and boils. Add cheese and onion and cook until cheese melts. Place drained cabbage in 1 1/2-quart baking dish. Add diced ham and pour sauce over all. Mix well with a fork and top with bread crumbs. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbly and brown. Serves 6.
Combine water and chicken bouillon.
Cook vegetables in water mixture until soft.
Add milk slowly, stirring to combine. Combine flour and sour cream.
Add to soup mixture, stirring slowly.
Lower heat and simmer on low until slightly thickened and ready to serve.
Drain tuna but leave in medium size chunks. Rinse with cold water and drain well. Toss lightly with pineapple, green pepper, celery and mayonnaise.
Pile in 1/2 papaya or in lettuce cups. Sprinkle lightly with parsley. Serve on plate with tomatoes, ripe olives and heated French roll.
Makes 3 to 4 servings.
Crumble cornbread and biscuits; add herb stuffing, onions, celery, sage and poultry seasoning.
Let set overnight.
Add eggs, broth and salt.
I buy chicken broth in cans and mix with turkey broth.
Bake at 350° until done.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add marshmallows and cream cheese and stir with wire whisk until dissolved.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Chill until congealed.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Drain.
Mix remaining ingredients together except cheese.
Pour ground beef and onions in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Pour remaining ingredients on top.
Sprinkle cheese on top. Spread Ritz crackers on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Use 1/2 box cake mix and 1/2 of required ingredients on box (but use only 1 egg).
Pour over the already mixed crushed pineapple and brown sugar.
I use the juice also.
Microwave for 4 to 4 1/2 minutes.
Rotate and bake 4 1/2 minutes more.
Use 8-inch square dish, uncovered.
May look undone, but will finish cooking while resting.
In skillet, saute almonds in melted margarine until golden brown (5 minutes).
Remove almonds from margarine and set aside. Combine flour, salt and pepper.
Dust chicken with mixture and shake off excess.
Stir rosemary into margarine left in skillet. Over medium heat, brown chicken on both sides.
Stir in wine and cover.
Cover over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove chicken to platter and sprinkle with almonds.
Dredge meat in flour and garlic mixture.
Saute in 2 tablespoons margarine.
Set aside.
Saute mushrooms in 2 tablespoons margarine.
Mix gravy according to package directions; mix with meat, mushrooms and sour cream on low until hot.
Cut jicama into small cubes and blanch in boiling water for 1 1/2 minutes.
Drain.
In a saucepan, melt butter and add green peas, stirring until all are coated with butter.
Add jicama and seasonings; simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until jicama and peas are tender.
Jicama remains slightly crisp. Serves 4 to 6.
In skillet fry bacon until crisp.
Drain on paper towel.
To drippings add pepper, salt, celery and onions.
Cook until tender.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until okra is tender, stirring occasionally.
Combine chocolate and Schnapps in warm mug and top with whipped cream.
Cream the cream cheese, powdered sugar and small carton of Cool Whip.
Prepare vanilla and chocolate pudding with milk.
Add pudding mixture to cream cheese mixture.
Mix until smooth.
Pour into crusts and top with large carton Cool Whip, chopped nuts and grated chocolate.
In microwave, melt 16 ounces milk chocolate morsels.
Melt 1 stick margarine.
Mix together and add 1 cup peanut butter.
Pour 1 large box Crispix cereal in large container.
Add mixture and stir.
Pour 1/2 box powdered sugar over cereal.
Mix and toss. Pour mixture in large paper bag and add remaining sugar (10x) and shake.
Store in container.
Eat and enjoy!
Skin chicken.
Place in Ziploc bag.
For marinade, in a bowl, combine cooking wine, oil, vinegar, basil, oregano, onion powder and garlic.
Pour over chicken to coat well.
Marinate 5 to 24 hours in the refrigerator, turning bag occasionally.
Drain, reserving marinade.
Grill on an uncovered grill over medium coals for 20 minutes, brushing occasionally with marinade.
Turn chicken and grill for 15 to 25 minutes more or until tender and no longer pink, brushing often with marinade.
Cut
the onions in half across.
Melt butter in skillet. Put cut
side down and fry until brown.
Turn upward in baking dish. Sprinkle with herbs; pour in cider.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 375°.
Sift together or just stir together flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Mix together shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, milk and vanilla.
Stir dry ingredients into sugar mixture, then stir in oatmeal, chopped nuts or coconut and wheat or corn flakes. Drop by teaspoonful 2-inches apart on greased baking sheet (I use Pam).
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Makes about 8 dozen.

recipes.t: Tomato Pepper Steak In Crock Pot
d: Cut steak into 2
1/2 to 3 inch pieces.
Heat shortening in large skillet.
Coat steak with flour, salt and pepper.
Brown steak in shortening over medium heat (about 10-15 minutes).
Cut peppers and onions into large rings.
Layer meat, peppers, and onions in crock pot.
Cover with tomatoes and tomato juice.
Cook on low heat for 3 to 4 hours.
Serve over cooked rice.
Put raw rice in bottom of buttered casserole.
Top with tomatoes.
Saute onions and green peppers in butter.
Mix with olives and salt and pour over tomatoes.
Top with grated cheese and bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 60 to 75 minutes.
Place cooked rice on plate and add cubed ham of desired amount.
Microwave until warm, about 2 minutes on High (100%). Place desired amount of cheese on top of ham and microwave until cheese is melted, about 30 seconds.
Serve immediately, letting each individual salt and pepper to taste.
Place meat, onions, seasonings and water in Dutch oven or heavy kettle.
Cook meat without frying on top of stove.
Stir constantly for first few minutes.
When meat is fully cooked, remove from heat and strain.
Let the liquid cool and the fat come to the top. Remove most of the fat.
You can do this after it becomes solid and cold.
Return the balance of the liquid to the meat.
Trim ends from pea pods.
Bring 3 cups water to boil. Carefully lower pea pods into water.
Simmer over medium heat 1 minute.
Drain.
Immediately immerse in cold water.
Drain and refrigerate until chilled.
Chop beef fine.
Combine with rest of ingredients.
Slice slit on one side of pea pod; fill with mixture and arrange in dish with sides touching to keep from falling. Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Serve cold.
Makes 60.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease large cookie sheet. In large bowl, combine butter, parsley, onion, mustard, and lemon juice. Blend well. Add cheese, cooked broccoli and ham. Mix lightly. Set aside.
In a bowl blend apples and carrots.
Add butter, lemon extract and eggs.
Beat to mix.
Sift together flour, sugar, powder, soda and salt.
Add to apple and carrot mixture.
Stir in nuts if desired.
Mix well.
Bake in greased and floured bread pan.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour or until done when tested with toothpick. Cool in pan 10 minutes before removing.
Put bread on a rack to complete cooling.
Bring first 5 ingredients to a simmer, then add onion and green pepper.
Cook another minute.
Pour over rice.
Stir and serve.
For apple filling, in a small mixing bowl, stir together apple, nuts, brown sugar, margarine or butter and cinnamon; set aside.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored.
Gradually add 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons of sugar, vanilla and nutmeg; beat well. Slowly stir in rum and brandy.
Cover and refrigerate overnight. Place chilled mixture in punch bowl.
Gradually stir in cream and milk.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add 3 tablespoons of sugar; beat until stiff.
Fold whites into chilled mixture.
Sprinkle with nutmeg as desired.
Yields 2 1/2 quarts.

Wash beans and cook with ham hocks in 3 qts. of water. When beans are done, mix flour with small amount of water into a smooth paste. Add sour cream and milk; mix well. Add to the bean soup. Add vinegar and cook until soup comes to a full boil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cream butter; gradually add sugar, beating until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flour, mixing well.
Stir in lemon juice and lemon extract.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan. Bake at 350° for one hour and 15 minutes.
Remove from pan and cool completely.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar on top.
In saucepan, combine soup and cream cheese.
Heat slowly, stirring constantly, until blended.
Stir in sour cream, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Heat through.
Stir in 1 tablespoon water.
Transfer to fondue pot or small chafing dish.
Keep warm over fondue or chafing dish burner.
Serve with tortilla chips or corn chips.
Makes about 2 cups.
Mix cake mix and pudding together.
Add sour cream, eggs, oil and water.
Blend until creamy.
Add chocolate chips and nuts. Pour batter into greased tube pan.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Brown ground beef, onion and pepper.
Drain.
Add the following: chili beans, corn, mushrooms and tomatoes.
Add Ro-Tel according to your taste, and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes. Pour into large baking dish and top with a layer of sliced Velveeta cheese.
Top this with Mexican cornbread (mixed according to package directions).
Bake at 400° until cornbread is done.

Combine in mixing bowl eggs, flour and cocoa. Beat at medium speed until well blended. Add butter and nuts and continue to beat about 1 minute. Transfer to lightly greased 8-inch square pan and bake in preheated 350° oven 35 to 40 minutes or until firm on top. This cake forms a thick fudge sauce in the bottom of pan and cannot be tested with a toothpick insertion.
Combine cheese, margarine and milk at medium speed in mixer until well blended.
Add combined potato chips and flour.
Mix well.
Shape teaspoons and flour.
Mix well.
Shape teaspoonfuls into balls and place on ungreased cookie sheets.
Flatten slightly.
Bake at 375°
for 12 to 14 minutes, or until golden brown.
Makes approximately 3 dozen.
Soften gelatin in cold water; dissolve in hot coffee.
Stir in honey and salt.
Chill until jellied.
Add rum.
Whip the cream and fold it into the gelatin mixture.
Pour into refrigerator trays or a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Freeze.
When there is a frosty border of 1-inch around the pans, turn into a mixer bowl and beat smooth. Stir in almonds and re-freeze.
Serve with rum-flavored whipped cream and additional almonds as garnish.
Cut whale into 1-inch squares. Takes 4 weeks. Add potatoes and carrots and place in 400-gallon pot. Cook 4 weeks at 350°. Garnish with parsley. Serves 3,700. Salt and pepper to taste.
Plunge tomatoes into boiling water for ten seconds.
Peel and quarter them.
Heat olive oil in large saucepan.
Add onion and garlic and saute.
Add tomatoes.
Season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook until liquid has evaporated.
In large bowl, cream butter, sugar and vanilla until fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix flour, soda and nutmeg.
Add half the flour mixture to butter mixture and beat well.
Gradually mix in the remaining flour, beating well after the last addition.
Fold in nuts and apples.
Brown ground pork; drain and add celery, onion and cabbage. Add soy sauce, black pepper and garlic powder.
Cover, cook over medium heat 10 to 15 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and shrimp.
Take egg roll wrappers and lay flat with one corner toward you.
Put about 3 rounded teaspoonfuls of filling in center of egg roll wrapper.
Fold bottom corner up, slide corners toward center and roll upward.
Seal top flap with water and flour mixture.
Have about 1 to 1 1/2-inches of hot cooking oil.
Gently put egg roll in until brown on that side and turn.
Take only a few seconds on each side.
Don't overcook.
In a frying pan cook onion and green pepper in butter until tender.
In a greased casserole dish combine all ingredients except paprika.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes until done.
Serves 6.
Combine macaroni, tuna, pickle, relish, eggs and green onions. Cover with French dressing and let stand overnight.
Toss with mayonnaise before serving.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Add drained vegetables.
Pour mixture into baking dish and arrange on top the pork chops in single layer.
Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with soy sauce.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours. Turn pork chops after one hour.
Place oil, vinegar, orange rind, Dijon mustard, mustard seed, salt and pepper in food processor; process until well blended. Set aside.
Marinate chicken, cut into 1-inch cubes, in onion soup mix, oil and water (overnight).
Load wooden or metal skewers alternately with meat and veggies until full.
Season with pepper. Grill for 10 to 15 minutes (ensure chicken is fully cooked between veggies).
Place water in a 3-quart microwavable casserole.
Cover with lid.
Microwave on High for 7 minutes or until water boils.
Stir in pasta and re-cover.
Stirring midway through cooking, microwave on High for 6 to 8 minutes or until done.
Drain and cool slightly. Return pasta to same casserole and toss with dressing.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Serve.
Cream the butter and Crisco until very light.
Add brown sugar and cream well.
Add sugar and beat until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla.
Beat in eggs one at a time; beat well.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk.
Being and end with dry ingredients.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan and bake 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Prick bottom and sides of pie crust and bake for 5 minutes at 375°.
Line bottom of crust with thin layer of Swiss cheese, then sprinkle on Colby and Cheddar cheeses and top with remaining Swiss cheese.
Beat eggs with milk.
Add salt, pepper, nutmeg and spinach.
Pour mixture on top of cheeses.
Sprinkle scallions on top; dot with melted butter.
Place pie on nonstick cookie sheet and bake at 375° for an hour or until mixture is set.
Serves 4 to 6.
In a 9 x 12-inch cake pan, pour in the pie filling.
Top with the entire box of cake mix, spreading evenly over pie filling. Melt butter; pour over cake mix.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes in a 350° oven.
Top with chopped pecans the last 5 minutes.
Open all cans and drain off excess liquid.
Finely chop water chestnuts and olives. Then mix all the ingredients together.
This makes a lot of sandwiches.
The mix can be stored in the fridge for several days.
Great for potlucks.
Cream butter and confectioners sugar in large mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flavorings alternately with flour, beating well after each addition.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Invert onto serving plate.
May spread with cream cheese icing if desired. Yield:
16 servings.
Mix well together the oil, sugar and eggs.
Add apples.
Sift together soda, flour and salt and add.
Stir in nuts and 2 teaspoons vanilla.
Place in a 10 x 16-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for approximately 35 minutes or until brown.
Let cool in pan.
Mix brown sugar, evaporated milk and vanilla in saucepan. Let come to a boil; remove from heat and pour over cake.
Cut in squares.
Cream butter and sugar. Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix together 3 cups flour, baking powder and salt.
Add this gradually to creamed mixture. Add flavorings.
Dredge candied fruit and nuts with the other cup of flour.
Add the creamed mixture to this dredged fruit.
Mix well, then bake in a large tube pan about 3 hours at 275°.
Coat squirrel pieces with flour seasoned with salt and pepper. Brown in oil and remove from skillet.
Line baking dish with foil and place cooked squirrel in dish.
Add onion and garlic; sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Blend soup with a small amount of water.
Pour over squirrel.
Seal foil tightly.
Bake at 325° for 2 hours.
Open foil and add green onions and parsley.
Reseal and cook for additional 10 to 15 minutes.
Beat eggs until thickened.
Add sugar, cinnamon, ginger and cloves, then orange juice and lemon juice.
Place 1 cup in punch bowl.
Add ice cream and gradually add ginger ale.
Then add remaining egg mixture.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Combine frozen vegetables, soup mix, macaroni, water and juice in a large heavy pan; bring to a boil.
Cook ground beef in a nonstick skillet or in the microwave until meat is cooked, stirring to crumble; drain.
Stir meat into vegetable mixture. Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally to keep macaroni from sticking.
Yield: about 2 quarts.
Makes about 8 (1 cup) servings.
Mix together cukes, peppers, onions and salt and let sit overnight.

recipes.t: South Of The Border Stack Up
d: Brown meat; drain off fat.
Add onion, green pepper, seasoning mix and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish:
two tortillas, meat sauce and cheese. Repeat.
Cover dish with foil and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Steam clams and pry open.
Drain off and measure liquid; there should be 1 cup.
Put the carrot, potatoes and celery into the chicken broth.
Cover and boil gently until tender.
Then cut clams finely with sharp kitchen scissors.
Saute the clams and onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Blend flour evenly into this mixture. Add broth and vegetables gradually, stirring constantly to keep smooth.
Add the clam broth, cream and seasonings.
Heat just to boiling and serve immediately.
Makes about 8 cups.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Dump applesauce into it.
Dump pineapple on top of that.
Spread cake mix (dry) over that.
Melt margarine and pour on top of the cake mix.
Sprinkle nuts over the butter.
Do not stir.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Top with Cool Whip or cream.
Puree strawberries and sugar in blender until smooth; press mixture through sieve.
Lightly whisk in cream and cinnamon. Chill completely.
Cut sausage into 1-inch pieces and brown.
Remove sausage to paper towel.
In the same skillet, saute onion, pepper and garlic. Add tomatoes, salt, oregano and Tabasco; bring to boil.
Stir in rice and beans.
Remove from the heat and let stand 10 minutes. Fluff rice mixture.
Spoon onto a serving plate and arrange sausage on top.
Mix jello, water, marshmallows and cream cheese.
Add pineapple, pecans and mayonnaise.
Stir in whipped cream and let set.
Layer potatoes and onions in a 13 x 9 pan.
Combine Parmesan cheese and 3/4 cup each Cheddar and Mozzarella, sprinkle over potatoes and onions.
Top with bacon, butter, salt and pepper. Bake for 35-40 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with remaining cheeses.
Brown hamburger.
Mix soup and milk together.
Mix tomato sauce and spaghetti sauce mix together.
In casserole dish, put 1/2 package raw noodles in bottom, 1/2 of hamburger and 1/2 of shredded cheese.
Repeat again.
Then top with soup and milk mixture and finally, tomato sauce mixture.
Bake for 1/2 hour at 400°.
Serves 6.
Combine flour and sugar.
Let ginger ale lose its bubbles and add to mixture.
Pour into lightly greased bread pan and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
In a bowl, combine spinach, sour cream, mayo, soup mix, mushrooms and onions and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Serve with vegetables or crackers.
Skin chicken.
Mix sage, rosemary, oregano, garlic and pepper to make paste.
Rub chicken well with paste and place in bowl. Add oil and mix to coat.
Cover and place in refrigerator overnight.
Drain before cooking.
Saute chicken in nonstick pan about 10 minutes per side.
No additional oil will be needed.
Add wine and lemon juice to chicken and simmer a few minutes.
Serve chicken with the sauce spooned over the top.
Saute onion in butter until soften.
Add the bay leaf, thyme stock, tomatoes and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer 20 minutes. Add turkey and simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and serve garnished with additional minced thyme if desired and serve.
Combine sugar, salt and cornstarch.
Stir in water and cook 15 minutes.
Add butter.
Pour over sweet potatoes in a flat pan, so each piece is covered.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Combine raisins, shortening and 1 1/4 cups water.
Heat to boiling, stirring until shortening melts.
Cool to lukewarm. Soften yeast in remaining 1/2 cup water.
Add sugar, salt, spices and 1 cup flour.
Mix well.
Add raisin mixture.
Gradually add remainder of flour.
Knead 3 minutes.
Brush dough with oil. Cover; let rise in bowl until double, about 1 3/4 hours.
Punch down.
Shape into 2 medium loaves.
Brush top with oil.
Let rise until double (45 minutes).
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Make a syrup of brown sugar and water.
Cook 5 minutes and cool.
Mix cornstarch and egg yolks and cook until it coats a wooden spoon.
Mix with syrup and strain.
Add cream, beaten egg whites and vanilla.
Add milk to the fill line on a gallon freezer.
Freeze until firm.
Brown flour in oleo.
Add beef broth and hot sauce.
Add Veg-All, beef and salt; mix well.
Pour meat mixture into crust. Mix together cheese, milk and eggs.
Pour over meat mixture.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes, until cheese mixture is browned.
Serves 4.
Put pie filling and pineapple in ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan. Pour dry cake mix over and dot with butter.
Cover with coconut and sprinkle nuts over.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350° or when browned and pie filling bubbles up.
Chill juices.
Let frozen juices thaw in refrigerator.
Don't chill 7-Up.
Mix the juice first, then Southern Comfort, then the 7-Up.

Preheat oven to 450°. In large bag, add all ingredients, except milk. Close bag and shake until potatoes are evenly coated. In a 9 x 13-inch pan, arrange potatoes. Discard bag. Bake, uncovered, for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally. Turn potatoes into large bowl. Mash potatoes and stir in hot milk.
Combine banana, lime juice and sugar and mix thoroughly. Using an electric mixer, whip the cream with the salt until it is very stiff.
Fold bananas into the cream and spread into a large shallow baking dish.
Freeze solid.
In small skillet, saute bell pepper and onion,1 to 2 minutes. Add garlic, ketchup and Chili powder. Mix well. Heat thoroughly. Makes about 1 1/2 cups sauce.
Separate biscuits into 2 sections.
Enclose quartered fruit in biscuit half and seal edges.
Put into baking dish.
Mix butter, sugar, and water.
Pour mixture over the fruit filled biscuit halves.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain liquid from salmon into measuring cup and add milk to make 1/2 cup of liquid.
Melt butter and stir in flour to thicken, then add milk and onion.
Mix into salmon.
Shape into haystacks and roll in crumbs.
Make 3 inch height for dinner servings or 1 1/2-inch height for hors d'oeuvres.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cube zucchini and chop onion.
Add water and boil together for 15 minutes, drain.
Add remaining ingredients except margarine and stuffing.
Layer 1/2 stuffing mixture on bottom of dish. Then layer all of filling mixture.
Pur remaining stuffing mixture on top.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Mix dry seasoning, oil, wine and garlic, along with tomato sauce.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Fry eggplant slices.
Put line of eggplant in glass dish; cover with half of cheese.
Put remaining eggplant slices on next.
Pour tomato sauce mixture on top.
Cover with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Roast peppers.
Remove skin and dice.
In a nonstick skillet coated with cooking spray, saute sliced onions and peppers. Season with 1/8 teaspoon salt.
Place peaches in boiling water for a few minutes.
Peel.
Working over a bowl to collect peach juice, slice or dice peaches.
Mix white wine with peaches and juice. Combine with onions in skillet and cook until liquid is reduced by 1/2.
Serve warm over turkey cutlets which have been grilled, broiled or pan-fried.
Serves 4.
Mix lime Jell-O, lemon Jell-O and hot water well; cool.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well and set in refrigerator.
When thick, cut into squares.
Can be served on lettuce.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles by directions on package; drain.
In a large frying pan, fry sausage and beef until brown; stir often.
Add onion, pepper and mushrooms; cook about 3 minutes.
Drain off excess fat.
Add salt, pizza sauce and noodles; stir just enough to mix.
Pour into a large greased bake dish.
Place pepperoni on meat mixture.
Top with cheese.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, uncovered.
Cook spaghetti and drain off water.
Brown hamburger and drain off grease.
Onion and olives are optional.
Pour in tomatoes. Add salt, pepper and oregano.
Let simmer.
Mix in with sauce and shredded cheese.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Add shortening, 2/3 cup milk and flavoring.
Beat well.
Add rest of milk and stiffly beaten egg whites.
Beat well.
Bake at 350°.
Brown hamburger and drain off excess grease.
Peel, slice and cook onion and potatoes until tender.
Add just enough water to boil.
Add the cooked hamburger, peas and milk.
Simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Dissolve raspberry gelatin in 1 cup boiling water.
Add cranberry juice cocktail.
Chill until thickened, about 1 hour. Fold in apple, celery and walnuts.
Spoon into 6-cup ring mold and chill until set, about 15 minutes.
Dissolve lemon gelatin in 1 cup boiling water.
Chill until slightly thickened, about 45 minutes.
Combine Cool Whip and mayonnaise.
Fold into lemon gelatin.
Spoon into mold and chill until firm.
Bake or buy angel food cake the day before you want to serve it.
Slice cake across in three layers.
Cook lemon pudding as directed on box, then cool.
Whip cream and mix with cooled pudding.
Spread on each layer, spread and sides on top. Refrigerate cake until ready to serve.
Cook rice 40 minutes or until done.
Let set 15 minutes.
Add meat and cook together 20 minutes.
Add cabbage.
Cook 10 minutes.
Add salt to taste.
Add peppers; mix and done.
Peel 3 to 5 medium beets, cover with water and add 1/2 tablespoon salt.
Boil on medium heat until tender (easily poked with fork).
Remove beets from soup, cut into cubes.
Add cubes and sliced beet leaves to the soup and boil until leaves lose green color.
Remove from heat.
At room temperature, add 2 teaspoons lemon concentrate.
Chill.
Wash beans, then put in 5-quart kettle.
Add beans and water to top; add bacon that has been cut into 1-inch pieces.
Cook for 1 1/2 hours, then add the brown sugar and cook 1/2 hour longer, or until beans are soft.
Peel and core pears.
Seed both kinds of the peppers.
Coarsely grind pears, peppers and onions.
Place ground mixture in a large pot, adding the vinegar and sugar.
In a muslin bag, combine celery seed, pickling spices and mustard seed.
Tie bag shut and place in the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes. Remove spice bag.
Pour into sterilized canning jars and seal tightly.
Store pear relish in cellar or a cool, dry place.
Yields 8 pints.
Mix cream cheese and mayonnaise together until smooth. Add drained tuna, onion and celery. Warm tomato soup. Mix gelatine and cold water together quickly and mix with soup.
Immediately put mixture with tuna. Pour into mold that has been sprayed with Pam. Refrigerate overnight or until firm.
Serve on Ritz or Townhouse crackers.
Beat cream cheese with electric mixer until fluffy.
Add Eagle Brand milk; beat until smooth.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla. Pour into 9-inch pie shell.
Chill for 3 hours.
Top with strawberry or blueberry glaze, if desired.
