Heat oven to 375°.
In large skillet, brown pork chops.
Place pork chops in ungreased 13 x 9-inch baking pan; drain liquid. Arrange sweet potatoes around pork chops.
Pour syrup over pork chops and sweet potatoes and in bottom of pan.
Arrange biscuits next to chops and potatoes.
Return to oven.
Bake, uncovered, 17 to 25 minutes or until biscuits are brown and pork chops are tender.
Saute cabbage in bacon fat on low heat.
Add mixture of sugar, vinegar and water.
Cover and cook over low heat until cabbage is tender.
Add cooked noodles and crumbled bacon.
Serve hot.
Boil sugar, water and cinnamon sticks with cream of tartar for 5 minutes. Pour over peeled and sliced oranges.
Marinate for 3 days in refrigerator.
Delicious.
In a large bowl, mix lime juice, water, orange juice, garlic, pepper and salt.
Place chicken breasts in a bowl.
Cover and marinate overnight.

recipes.t: Nan'S Banana Nut Ice Cream(5-Quart Freezer)
d: Mix sugar, flour and salt.
Add eggs and beat well.
Add evaporated milk and half and half, stirring well.
Strain mixture into the ice cream cylinder.
Add mashed bananas and nuts.
Add enough milk to fill the cylinder.
Stir and freeze according to your freezer's instructions.
Cut loaf of bread lengthwise.
Spread one side of bread with mustard and the other side with garlic butter.
Add corned beef, ham, turkey and both cheeses.
Top with lettuce and onion.

Place brown sugar, cream and butter in a skillet or heavy pot and brown lightly. Mix together egg yolks, flour and milk; beat well. Add to sugar mixture; cook until thick, stirring constantly over medium heat. Add vanilla. Pour into baked crust. Top with meringue if desired.
Layer ingredients in order given in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 to 60 minutes.
(Jello and cake mix are dry.) This is best served cold when juices are thickened.
Add whipped topping if desired.
In pan, brown mushrooms in butter. Add remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil over low heat. Stir. Serve over patty shells. Makes 4 servings.
Place lima beans in large pan and cover completely with water.
Cook for 1 hour over medium heat, stirring occasionally. If water evaporates, add enough to keep beans covered.
Add salt, diced sausage and Rotel tomatoes to beans and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours or until beans are tender.
Serve beans over white rice.
In medium saucepan combine pudding mix, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg and egg nog. Mix well over medium heat.
Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in rum, if desired. Cool or chill thoroughly.
Beat until smooth.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon into prepared pastry shell. Garnish with additional nutmeg.
Chill 4 hours or until set.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Saute zucchini in butter for 1 minute.
Add mushrooms and peas and saute for about 1 minute.
Add cream, cheese, basil and pepper and simmer about 1 minute.
Add crab; stir until heated and serve over the pasta.
Boil carrots for about 5 to 8 minutes.
Put carrots and apples in baking dish; stir in just enough honey to cover the carrots and apples.
Add cinnamon to taste.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes, or until tender.
Cream shortening and sugar; add vanilla and eggs, one at a time and beat.
Add sifted dry ingredients and milk alternately, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Fold in blueberries. Place in large tube pan, greased and floured.
Sprinkle with mixture of sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Dissolve yeast in 1/2 cup warm water.
Cream together sugar and Crisco. Add beaten eggs, then remaining 2 cups warm water. Add salt and dissolved yeast.
Stir in flour, 2 cups at a time. Dough should not be too sticky. Add orange peel. Cover and let rise until double. Punch dough and knead a short time.
Shape into round balls to half fill a muffin pan.
Let rise. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
May be glazed with glaze made with powdered sugar and orange juice.
Cook peas and celery following directions.
Mix soup and water; stir and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes.
Whip with fork until smooth.
Spoon onto a platter.
Hollow center of potatoes to make a nest.
Spoon peas into hollow.
Put potatoes and onion in saucepan.
Cover with water; add salt.
Cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer about 10 minutes.
Mash potatoes in their liquid.
Add milk and butter. Stir; if soup is still too thick, add milk.
Keep on medium heat until serving time.
Serves 5.
Wash and dry vegetables but do not peel.
Cut all vegetables into chunks and place in a 2-quart casserole dish.
Dot butter throughout casserole.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over top of vegetables.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top of cheese.
Lightly sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake for 1 hour in 350° oven.
In a mixing bowl, combine sugar, flour, orange peel and cinnamon. Add pears and raspberries; toss to coat. Set aside.
Knead onion soup in ground beef.
Roll the beef into meatballs and brown in Dutch oven; drain fat off meatballs.
Add 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup and 1 can of milk to meatballs.
Let simmer about 1 hour.
Turn heat off.
Let set for another hour.
This is one recipe that the longer it sets the better it tastes.
Serve meatballs on bed of rice and don't forget the gravy.
Combine first 6 ingredients in saucepan.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Blend flour and milk in a bowl.
Add to soup.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly. Stir in parsley and cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Cook until cheese is melted.
Makes 6 servings.
Put asparagus on foil with butter and salt and pepper. Grill on medium for about 10 minutes.
Mix 1 cup sour cream, 2 Tbsp. of red wine vinegar, 1/4 cup dijon mustard, pinch of red pepper, 2 teaspoons of sugar and microwave for 1 1/2 minutes then pour over.
Chip up and fry meat.
Chop pepper and onion and add to fried meat and grease.
Cook until light brown. Slice up sausage and cook a few minutes longer.
Add tomato juice, hot sauce, salt, pepper and sugar. Bring to simmer. Add cold water.
Pour in rice and cook until about 3/4 cooked or tender, then add raw shrimp that have been prepared.
Keep stirring several times all the way through cooking.
Chop cranberries;
add sugar and let stand 10 minutes. Mix gelatine with
sugar
and
salt;
add
to

hot water until dissolved. Add lemon juice, rind and mayo to gelatine mixture and blend with beater. Quick chill this mixture in refrigerator tray, 15 minutes or until firm, 1 inch from edge, but soft in center. Then
beat until
fluffy. Fold in cranberry mixture, pineapple and
nuts. Pour
into
1 quart mold and chill until firm. Unmold on lettuce.
Top with mayo.
Serves 6.
In medium bowl, mix peanut butter and vanilla.
In medium saucepan, mix sugar and cream together.
Bring to a boil and boil 3 minutes.
Pour over peanut butter and vanilla mixture and beat for 2 minutes with electric mixer or until it thickens.
Add crushed crackers and mix with a spoon.
Press in a buttered pan.
It will be very thick and will set up fast.
May be cut right away.

Place cooked broccoli in greased baking dish. Place chicken on top of broccoli. Mix soup, milk, mayo, lemon juice and curry. Pour over broccoli and chicken. Sprinkle grated cheese over mixture and top with buttered bread crumbs. (Can substitute crushed croutons for bread crumbs and margarine.) Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Serves 6. Can freeze. Can do ahead.
Cream together butter or margarine and sugar till light and fluffy. Add 2 eggs; beat well. Blend in sour cream.
In a 5-quart Dutch oven or heavy saucepan, heat oil and brown lamb on all sides, removing shanks to make room for others as they are browned.
When all shanks have been browned and removed, add onions and garlic and saute, stirring until onions are golden. Stir in all remaining ingredients.
Return lamb shanks to Dutch oven, turning to coat with sauce.
Bring to boiling.
Cover; reduce heat and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until lamb
is tender. Remove cover and cook over medium heat until sauce is thickened and coats lamb shanks about 20 minutes longer.
If there is a lot of fat on top of the sauce, spoon it off before reducing the sauce.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine peaches with melted margarine.
Stir flour, baking powder, milk and Equal together.
Spread peach mixture in a 9 x 9-inch square pan.
Pour batter over peach mixture.
Sprinkle cinnamon on top and bake at 350° for 55 minutes.
Halve cucumbers lengthwise and slice.
Bite size slice celery, bell peppers, tomatoes and onions.
In very large bowl, mix vinegar and sugar.
Add veggies; fill remainder of bowl with water.
Mix very well.
Refrigerate 4 hours and serve.
Great for summertime get togethers.
Wash and slice tomatoes, boil until soft.
In another large pan, slice onions; cover with a small amount of water and cook until tender.
Run the tomatoes and onions through straining sieve.
Mix in pepper.
Boil this mixture rapidly until it has reduced to almost half the original volume.
Place vinegar in an enamel pan; add a spice bag containing the cinnamon sticks, cloves and garlic.
Allow this to simmer about 30 minutes, then bring to a boil.
Place cover on pan and remove from heat.
Allow this to stand in pan until next steps.
When tomato mixture has cooked down to half, add vinegar mixture of which there should be 1 1/4 cups.
Add paprika, sugar and salt.
Boil rapidly until thick for about 10 minutes.
Pour while boiling into sterilized jars.
Place caps on firmly tight.
Process in boiling water bath for 5 minutes.
Makes 6 pints.
Cook rice according to package directions, except add the chicken bouillon cube, a bay leaf, a dash of clove, a dash of cayenne, a splash of olive oil and anything else you might desire to the water.
Most recipes call for whole brown rice to be cooked for 45 minutes.
Cook it only 35 to 40 minutes.
It taste better and has a nuttier texture.
Once your rice is on, start the chicken wings.
Combine tuna, egg, bread crumbs, mayonnaise, onion, parsley, mustard and poultry seasoning.
Mix well.
Shape into 40 balls. Roll in corn flakes.
Dip in melted butter.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Serve on cocktail picks.
Butter bread.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan, buttered side up. Beat together the next 3 ingredients.
Pour over bread.
Grate Cheddar cheese and sprinkle on top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Combine oats, sugar replacement, salt, vanilla and liquid shortening in medium bowl.
Stir to mix well.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Add beaten egg and chopped walnuts and stir to blend thoroughly.
Pack onto greased cookie sheet by small amount of cookie mixture (level teaspoonful).
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Prepare cake according to package directions.
Bake in a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
When cake is baked, poke holes in cake surface with a fork.
Spread pineapple and juice over cake while hot.
Let cool.
Prepare pudding according to package instructions.
Spread pudding over cake.
Cool in refrigerator for 1/2 hour.
Spread Cool Whip over cake.
Serves 12.
Bring to boil the water, oil and salt. Remove from heat.
Stir in potatoes.
Cool slightly.
Stir in egg yolks and enough flour to make a dough stiff enough to handle.
Divide in fourths on lightly floured surface.
Roll each fourth into a rope 3/4-inch in diameter.
Cut in 1-inch pieces.
Press each lightly with tines of fork.
Drop 1/4 of gnocchi at a time into boiling salted water. Simmer about 5 minutes or until they float to the surface. With slotted spoon, remove to serving dish.
Keep warm. Pour hot tomato sauce over gnocchi.
Serve with Parmesan.
Flour chicken strips; season with salt and pepper and pan-fry in a small amount of oil until golden.
Combine broth, butter, garlic powder and parsley in saucepan.
Heat until butter melts and garlic dissolves.
Pour over chicken strips in frypan and cook slowly until broth thickens slightly (about 30 to 45 minutes). Serve over hot, cooked rice.
In hot oil, saute cabbage and onions.
Add rest of ingredients.
Cook 45 minutes.
Serves a crowd.
Mix sausage, bread crumbs and eggs with hands and roll into balls.
Fry in skillet until golden brown.
Drain and put in crock-pot.
In bowl, mix remaining ingredients and pour over meatballs.
Simmer in crock-pot for 1 hour.
Cook and stir chicken, onion, and pepper strips in oil until lightly browned. Add all other ingredients except rice. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes Serve over rice.
Heat olive oil in large skillet.
Add shallots and garlic; reduce heat to medium-low.
Saute until soft and transparent.
Add tomatoes; cook 5 minutes more.
Stir in tomato paste, Cajun spices and wine and bring to boil.
Lower heat and simmer.
Add shrimp and simmer 5 more minutes.
Toss cooked pasta with sauce.
In a small bowl, finely mash banana.
Add sour cream, sugar, poppy seed, lemon juice, mustard and salt.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Arrange salad greens and fruit on a platter.
Or serve greens in individual salad bowls.
Serve with dressing.
This is a nice dressing to use up that banana that we always find has gotten too ripe to eat.
Mix the oil, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, flour and baking powder all together and spread in a greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Drain the pineapple and put on dough.
Cream the cream cheese and 1 cup sugar.
Add the 5 eggs and 2 tablespoons dry pudding and pour over the pineapple.
Bake at 325° for about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat egg and milk in a large bowl.
Add meat, oats, onion and pepper.
Mix well.
Shape into 5 individual loaves and place in a baking dish.
Mix remaining ingredients and spoon over loaves.
Reserve glaze for basting.
Bake about 45 minutes, basting once or twice with glaze.
Serve remaining glaze warm in gravy boat.
Allow cream cheese to come to room temperature.
Cream together mayonnaise, Parmesan, Romano cheese, garlic, basil and garlic salt. Mix well.
Add the artichoke hearts and spinach (careful to drain this well), and mix until blended.
Store in a container until you are ready to use.
Spray pie pan with PAM, pour in dip and top with cheese.
Wash zucchini, but do not peel.
Cut into thin slices.
Put into a 10-inch skillet.
Add carrots, onions, salt, black pepper and basil.
Pour olive oil over top; stir gently until well mixed with vegetables.
Over medium heat, saute vegetables for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover vegetables; cook 5 minutes longer.
Remove cover; stir and cook about 10 more minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve hot.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine sugar with flour.
Add milk and butter.
Cook until thick; add coconut and nuts.
Preheat oven to 325°. Cream together the butter, the margarine and the oil. Gradually add sugar and eggs; beat well. Add the baking powder and flour.
Mix well. Add the milk and all flavoring. Mix well. Bake in a greased angel food pan 1 1/2 hours.
Cook celery, green pepper and onion in butter until tender. Prepare stuffing mix. Stir in vegetables, shrimp, mayo, parsley and cayenne.
Heat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs, oil, sugar and vanilla together.
Add flour; stir until just mixed.
Pour into greased baking pan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until brown.

recipes.t: Baked Vegetable And Seafood Won Tons
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
In medium bowl, combine soup mix, cheese, crab, garlic powder and pepper.
Place 1 tablespoon mixture on center of each won ton.
Brush edges with water.
Fold each corner into center and press to seal.
Boil together orange juice, sugar and cream of tartar to soft ball stage (234°).
Add nuts and beat immediately.
Spread on waxed paper or foil and break apart as desired.
These are a lovely Christmas treat.
Cream sugar and butter; add milk and salt.
Sift baking powder into flour and add to mixture.
Fold stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake in 3 layers.
Never fails.
Use any frosting.
Bake at 350° until done.
Prepare apples, dates and nuts.
Cream together butter and sugar and beat until light and fluffy.
Add the well beaten egg and blend until smooth.
Stir in the fruit and nuts.
Sift together the dry ingredients and add alternately with the sour milk. (Make sour milk by adding 1/2 teaspoon vinegar to 1/2 cup milk.)
Place in a greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan and let stand 10 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until bread tests done.
In large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon butter over medium high heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add parsley, shrimp and vermouth and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until shrimp turn pink.
Do not overcook.
Transfer shrimp mixture to small bowl.

In same skillet, heat 3 tablespoons butter until melted. Reduce heat to low and add cream, Parmesan and red pepper flakes. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.
Stir in salt and pepper.
To serve, place warm fettucine in serving dish.
Add shrimp mixture and toss gently to coat thoroughly.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs.
Add cream, oil and salt. Stir baking powder with meal.
Add egg mixture.
Add corn and both peppers.
Mix well.
Pour half into a greased ovenproof 2 1/2 to 3-quart casserole.
Sprinkle half of the shredded cheese over top. Add remaining mixture and sprinkle other half of cheese over all. Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.

recipes.t: Herb Jenneskens' Beef Tenderloin In Marchand Sauce
d: Roast beef in a 400° oven for 35 minutes or to desired doneness.
While tenderloin is roasting, prepare sauce.
Cook shallots and wine in saucepan until reduced to 1/4 original volume.
Cool slightly.
Cream butter with parsley, salt and pepper.
Blend into wine mixture.
Slice beef into 1/2-inch thick slices and serve with sauce.
Yields 8 servings.
Slice cabbage and wash.
Lay cabbage in frying pan.
Slice onion, green pepper and potatoes over cabbage.
Pour in water and stripple drippings.
Cook on high until boiled down.
Reduce heat and cover.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Remove cover and cook until tender.
In a medium bowl, mix gelatine with sugar.
Add boiling water; stir until gelatine is completely dissolved.
With wire whip or beater, blend mayonnaise, Italian dressing and lemon juice. Chill, stirring occasionally, until mixture is consistency of unbeaten egg white.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Turn into a 9-inch mold; chill until firm.
Serves 6.
Use recipe for Minute Rice (number of servings you prefer). Dice pork chops and fry in small amount of oil (number of pork chops depend on servings of rice).
Add green onions to pork chops and mushrooms; simmer for a few minutes.
Mix rice with pork chop mixture and simmer on low heat, about 3 to 5 minutes; stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
(This can also be prepared in a wok.)
Serve over chow-mein noodles; sprinkle with soy sauce.
Mix lima beans, soup, onion and green pepper.
Place in greased casserole dish.
Top with sausage links.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Drain beans well.
Rinse kidney beans and drain again on paper towels.
Combine beans, onion rings, salt, pepper and sugar in a deep bowl.
Warm vinegar but do not boil.
Stir in oil and pour over beans.
Toss lightly, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Drain and serve in a bowl, surround salad with crisp greens, cherry tomatoes or tomato wedges.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Fry meat in a large pan.
Add onion, garlic, potatoes and cabbage.
Simmer until mixture turns light brown, stirring frequently.
Pour in chicken broth.
Add salt and pepper.
Cover. Simmer until brown.
Wash and drain chicken.
Mix all dry ingredients together in bag and shake.
Pour oil in deep frying pan and heat to very hot. Put chicken in bag and coat well.
Place in hot oil.
Put in butter; cover and let fry until golden brown and tender.
Serve with rice and vegetable.
Makes about 4 servings.
Place rice in greased casserole with chicken on top.
Sprinkle with onion soup.
Mix celery soup and 2 cans water.
Pour over the mixture.
Bake, covered, at 325° for 2 hours.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine noodles, poppy seed, almonds, butter and rinds.
Toss together lightly.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Turn into buttered casserole and top with sour cream.
Bake in moderate (350°) oven for 20 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Cook and bone chicken.
Cook stew beef and pork until well done (meat will be stringy; add water as needed).
Combine beef, pork and chicken in large open pot.
Add sauces, onion and ground beef; stir constantly, simmering very slowly, for about 1 hour. Add extra sauce or water, if needed, to keep hash from sticking.
Place unopened raspberries in large bowl.
Add hot tap water to cover; set aside to thaw.
Drain thawed raspberries, reserving 1/4 cup of the syrup (reserve remaining syrup for another use).
Peel bananas; cut diagonally into 1/4-inch slices.
Arrange on four individual dessert plates in sunburst pattern.
Brush or drizzle with 2 teaspoons of the lemon juice.
Use 1/2 cup boiling water per pack of Jell-O.
Add sugar and lemon juice and some of the pineapple juice while hot.
Let the Jell-O mixture begin to congeal (do not let it set), then add the crushed drained pineapple, Cool Whip, avocado and nuts.
Keeps 3 or 4 days in refrigerator.
Blend cheese with melted oleo.
Stir in flour, salt and paprika-blend.
Wrap 1 teaspoon dough around each olive.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet for 10 to 15 minutes at 400°.
Combine pineapple, grapes, almonds and sunflower seeds.
Toss with yogurt.
Tear up spinach and line salad bowl.
Then add pineapple and grape mixture.
Oil a shallow baking pan and place shallots in single row. Bake at 350° under tender, approximately 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and place in blender or food processor until smooth.
Blend heavy cream into shallots in blender or processor.
Cream margarine and sugar; add egg, cream, pineapple, salt and nuts.
Beat well.
In a Pyrex dish, place a layer of wafers and then filling alternately.
Place in refrigerator.
Before serving put whipped cream on top.
Cut corn from cob.
Chop cabbage, onions, peppers and celery fine.
Mix all ingredients and bring to a full, rolling boil. Boil for 20 minutes.
Seal in hot jars.
Invert jars until cool.
Mix juice by package directions.
Place sugar, 2 cinnamon sticks and cloves in pan.
Add juice.
Simmer for 10 minutes. Pour into mugs.
Serve with cinnamon stick stirrers.
Makes 12 cups.
Remove crusts from bread and roll out flat with rolling pin. Mix together cheese, egg yolk, 1/8 cup sugar and vanilla.
Spread 1 teaspoon on each slice and roll up.
Melt butter and roll breads in it, then a mixture of sugar and cinnamon.
Place seam side down on cookie sheet.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cut in half.
Serve warm or cold.
Clean, wash and dry fish.
In a saute pan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil; saute garlic over a medium heat, being careful not to burn.
Add basil, oregano and mint; lower heat and saute 2 minutes. Add lemon juice and remove from heat.
In a separate pan, saute fish with remaining olive oil for approximately 3 minutes.
Add wine; heat 1 minute.
Add sauteed spices and cook 3 minutes over medium heat.
Serve with rice or pasta immediately.
If you use nonstick cookware, you can substitute water for the oil.
Blend cheese and sour cream.
Add soup mix and Worcestershire. Cut crust off bread and flatten with rolling pin.
Spread with mixture and roll up.
Cut into thirds.
Cut bacon and wrap around rolls; secure with toothpicks.
Bake at 350° until brown, about 15 minutes.
Yield:
Combine vinegar, sugar, water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Mix orange juice, sherbet and vanilla ice cream in a large punch bowl.
Stir in chilled ginger ale. Serve.

Mix cake mix, pecans, 1 egg and melted margarine together and pour into bottom of 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan. Mix 10x sugar, cream cheese, 2 eggs and coconut together and spread on top of other mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cover raisins with boiling water; let stand 5 minutes.
Drain. Combine flour, baking powder, cinnamon, baking soda and salt.
In large bowl, beat sugar, shortening and eggs until fluffy.
Add flour mixture and milk; beat on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Stir in carrots, raisins and nuts.
Spread into greased and floured 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Bake 35 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean.
Cool completely.
Cook noodles as directed on package.
Saute onions in margarine until tender.
Add grated cheese to hot mashed potatoes until cheese melts.
Mix thoroughly.
Combine milk, shortening, sugar and salt.
Cool to lukewarm by adding water.
Add yeast, egg and onions.
Add flour, mix to soft dough and shape.
For round buns, roll dough to 1/4-inch thick an cut with 3 1/2-inch cutter.
For square buns, roll dough to 9 x 12-inch rectangular shape.
Cut into 12 (3-inch) squares.
For wiener buns, divide dough into 12 parts, then shape into long, narrow buns.
Place on greased sheet.
Let rise in warm place until double in bulk.
Bake 15 minute at 400°.
Cream butter and sugar; add the egg yolks, well beaten, then the cream and flour with spices alternately, then the well beaten egg whites.
Last of all, the well floured fruit.
Bake about 2 hours.
Cover top first hour with buttered paper.
This was probably baked in a brick oven at Mount Vernon.
Have fun improvising.
In 3-quart saucepan, place beans and bacon.
Add enough water to cover.
Bring to a full boil.

Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until beans are crisply tender (20 to 25 minutes). Add remaining ingredients and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for another 10 to 15 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix milk and sour cream together.
Add lemon juice and mix well.
Pour into graham cracker crust and top with pie filling of choice.
Bake at 325 degrees until bubbly.
Cool completely and serve.
Add salmon juice to gelatin.
Flake salmon.
Mix with onion, cream cheese and gelatin.
Shape like a log and chill.
Drain liquid from corn into measuring cup; add milk or cream to measure 1 cup.
Melt butter; add flour, salt and pepper.
Stir to blend.
Slowly add liquid and cook, stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat and add drained corn.
Slowly add beaten eggs, stirring constantly.
Pour into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Top with buttered crumbs and sprinkle with paprika, if desired.
Place in a shallow pan of water.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
(Recipe may be doubled.)
In large mixing bowl, stir together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add egg, milk and cooking oil.
Beat until smooth, about 1 minute.
Place onions and cheese in well-greased 8-inch ring mold.
Tilt to coat all sides, reserving excess crumbs.
Pour batter into ring mold and sprinkle with reserved crumbs.
Microwave at Medium-high (7) for 9 to 11 minutes, until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Turn out on cooling rack or serving plate.
Serve warm.
Mix spinach, onion, eggs, crumbs, parsley, oil and cheeses in large bowl.
Melt butter.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan; dust with some bread crumbs.
Unroll phyllo and lay out 1 sheet into pan. Brush with melted butter.
Keep remaining phyllo covered with damp cloth.
Continue with 5 more sheets, brushing each with butter. Place mixture into pan; smooth top.
Arrange 6 more buttered sheets, one at a time.
Using razor blade, cut squares through top layers only.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Finish cutting squares through to bottom layers.
Boil macaroni as instructed on box.
Steam peas and carrots over boiling water in colander.
Drain noodles.
Stir in mayonnaise and sour cream.
Add veggies and tuna; mix well.
Salt and pepper as desired.
Serve on a bed of lettuce with tomato wedges on the side.
In a blender or food processor, process cottage cheese, milk and garlic until smooth.
Add flour, lemon juice, basil, mustard, pepper and salt, if desired; process until well blended.
Pour into a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until thickened.
Do not boil.
Serve over noodles; sprinkle with chopped tomatoes.
Yield: 4 servings.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Saute slivered pepper until soft. Add flour and stir until well blended with the butter.
Beat egg and milk together.
Combine with pepper-flour mixture and add sugar, salt and mace.
Fold in corn and drained, mashed squash. Turn into baking dish and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine the jellos and hot water; dissolve jello.
Place in refrigerator; let chill to a thin cream (20 to 35 minutes).
If overchilled, there will be lumps in finished salad.
Stir the remaining ingredients into the jello mixture.
Place in an 8 x 8-inch dish.
Put in refrigerator until firm.
Cut into squares. Garnish with red cherries and green citron for Christmas.
Cut
fish
in
small
pieces
and
place in large bowl. Cover with
equal
parts of
wine
and vinegar. Add dill to taste. Cover
and place
in refrigerator for 3 days.
Pickle onions
by slicing and placing in jar with Polish pickles for three
days also.
Remove
fish
from pickling and drain; dry well.
Chop both
pickled
and green onions and add to fish. Mix with salt and pepper, then add sour cream.
Serve as a dip with different kinds of crackers.

recipes.t: Martha Stewart'S Herb-Roasted Chicken With Baked Shallots
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Rub inside of chicken with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Fill cavity with half of the fresh herbs.
Truss bird firmly with kitchen string.
Put chicken, breast side up, in a shallow heavy roasting pan.
Put pan in middle of oven and roast for 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Chinese Fried Rice With Shrimp And Eggs
d: In a large skillet, heat 2 tablespoons oil and saute rice until golden brown.
Combine soup mix and water and stir into rice.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. In another skillet, heat remaining oil and saute shrimp quickly about 1 minute.
Add eggs, stirring constantly, and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Add salt, pepper and soy sauce.
Stir shrimp-egg mixture into soup-rice mixture; heat 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve topped with green onions.
Completely coat the pork chops by dredging them in a mixture of flour, cornmeal, salt, pepper and paprika.
Heat a heavy skillet (which has a lid) over medium-high heat.
Brush the pan with a thin coat of oil.
When the oil just smokes, add the coated pork chops and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for four minutes, then turn the chops.
Cover the pan and cook for 4 to 5 minutes. The pork chops should be juicy, but not pink at the bone.
Yield: 4 servings.
Brown meat. Add onion and cook until tender.
Add seasonings, tomatoes, soup and rice. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Spoon into casserole and top with cheese. Place in oven until cheese melts.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Dilute approximately 1/3 can of soup with about 1/4 cup milk and
blend.
Dip
breast into soup, coating well.
Press skinned side
into stuffing mix to which you have added onion and parsley flakes.
Place coated chicken, crumb side up, into shallow
baking dish.
Bake for 1 hour or until done at 350°. Serve
with
sauce made from heating (not boiling) equal parts of soup and sour cream.
Line bottom
and
2 long sides of a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan with
waxed
paper.
Cut cake into 3 even slices, put them in the pan and trim remaining slices to fit pan.
Pack sherbet into cake lined
pan; top with remaining slice of pound cake. Cover with waxed paper; freeze for at least 3 hours.
Combine cream, sugar and vanilla;
beat.
Put on top of cake;
freeze until ready to serve.
Makes 12 servings.
Clean mushrooms and remove stems.
Finely chop stems (about 1/2 cup) and set aside.
Do the same with red and green pepper. In large skillet, saute onion, mushroom stems and pepper until soft.
Keep mixture very moist adding more butter as you need it. Add bread crumbs until mixture holds together.
Season to taste with salt, pepper, sage and thyme.
Spoon on to mushroom caps. Bake on cookie sheet 20 minutes at 350°.
Saute onion in 1 tablespoon butter for 8 to 10 minutes, until limp and golden, but not brown.
In another skillet, saute bread crumbs in remaining 1 tablespoon butter, stirring until just golden.
(Dark crumbs will taste bitter, so be careful not to let them become too dark.)
Cook broccoli and cauliflower covered in a small amount of boiling water for 3 minutes.
Drain well.
Place in shallow 1-quart dish.
Add cherry tomatoes and onion; set aside.
Rub roast with brown sugar, salt and pepper.
Mix catsup, tomatoes and water with a dash of hot sauce and dash of Worcestershire sauce.
Pour mixture over roast and bake at 350° until tender.
Serve sauce over rice or noodles.
In
large
bowl
combine potatoes, beef, pickles, diced beets and herring (with sauce).
Cover;
chill several hours. Just before
serving, add mayonnaise.
Toss until ingredients are moistened.
Garnish
with diced egg white, sieved egg yolk and sliced beets.
Makes 25 servings.
Mix melted oleo, sugar, brown sugar, peanut butter, eggs and vanilla.
Sift flour, soda and salt into creamed mixture.
Blend in oats and chocolate bits.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Saute onion in margarine.
Mix squash, corn bread, soup, salt, pepper and sage.
Pour this mixture into baking dish.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Combine all ingredients, except chicken, in top of double boiler over simmering water; stir until smooth.
Cook until very thick, stirring frequently, about 20 minutes.
Cool at room temperature.
Discard ginger.
Place chicken in a large baking dish.
Brush sauce generously (both sides).
Cover and let stand 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spoon remaining sauce over chicken.
Bake approximately 20 minutes.
Cook sugar, eggs and vinegar until thick.
Dissolve jello in pineapple juice and water.
Combine with egg mixture.
Then cut up marshmallows and add crushed pineapple.
Cool.
Add nuts, whipped cream and cherries.
Serves about 8.
Saute hamburger and onion.
Add bacon and mix with rest of ingredients.
Put in 2-quart casserole and bake in a 350° oven for 50 to 60 minutes.

recipes.t: Broccoli And Cauliflower Casserole With Ham
d: Cook vegetables until crisp; drain well.
Saute margarine and finely chopped onion.
Blend cream cheese and mushroom soup.
Stir in ham dices.
Place cooked vegetables in a 10 x 13-inch dish. Pour sauteed onion, cream cheese, ham and soup over vegetables. Cover with grated cheese.
Crush crackers and sprinkle over the top.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Serves 10.
Saute celery, onion and bell pepper in butter or margarine. Mix corn bread in stock and soup.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add milk and pepper.
Add to bread mixture, then add chopped celery, poultry seasoning, bell pepper and chopped onion.
Bake in a well-greased pan at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes, or use for stuffing bird.
Peel and chop tomato.
Rinse chili peppers; discard seeds. Chop chili peppers.
Stir together chicken, chopped tomato and chopped chili peppers, vinegar and 1 teaspoon salt.
Chill mixture until ready to use.
Makes about 1 3/4 cups.
Drain beets, reserving 1/4 cup liquid.
In saucepan, stir beet liquid with cornstarch to make smooth paste.
Add marmalade, vinegar and salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens.
Add margarine, then add beets and stir gently over low heat until evenly glazed and heated through.
Serves 4.
Layer taquitos in baking dish.
Top with Ranch beans, enchilada sauce and grated cheese.
Bake at 325 degrees for 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Rice With Shrimp, Raisins And Walnuts
d: Cook rice.
Wash the rice once.
Add 4 1/2 cups water, 3 tablespoons butter and 1 teaspoon salt.
Cook on medium to high until water is mostly gone.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 1/2 hour until done.
Saute the onion in the vegetable oil until golden.
Add shrimp and let cook for a few minutes (shrimp cooks quickly).
Then add walnuts and raisins.
Continue to stir to avoid burning and add salt, pepper and saffron.
Remove from heat. Spread a layer of cooked rice on a large flat dish and top with a layer of the shrimp.
Gently mix.
Continue to layer and mix until everything is on the platter.
Serves 6 to 8 as a main dish.
Best if served fresh.
Brown bacon lightly.
Add onions; saute slightly.
In another pan, put the warm water, sugar and vinegar.
Heat and make paste out of the flour; add to mixture and stir until thick.
Add bacon and onion; stir well.
Pour over sliced potatoes; refrigerate overnight.
Bake the next day in a 325° oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Beat egg whites until stiff (set aside).
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix shortening with white sugar and add boiling water.
Alternate this with flour mixture and cold water. Add flavorings.
Fold in egg whites.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Makes 2 (8-inch or two 9-inch) cake layers.
Prepare rice as directed; mix sour cream, chiles and rice and seasonings together in bowl.
Mix it well.
Mix egg, cheese and onion.
Dip breasts in egg mixture, then flour.
Fry in 1/4 cup margarine for 3 to 4 minutes each side. Cook 1 1/2 cups cooked rice.
Place chicken over rice and cover with chicken soup (gravy).

Cream together the butter with the sugar. Add egg and molasses with soda. Stir in the buttermilk. Sift together the flour, allspice, baking powder and cinnamon. Stir into the mixture and beat well. Add the raisins and nuts. Bake in 3 layers. Allow layers to be thoroughly cold before icing.
Stem, wash and dry spinach.
Refrigerate.
Tear spinach into small pieces, then chop finely.
Sprinkle with salt.
Blend vinegar and Tabasco and mix with spinach.
Add celery, onion, chopped eggs and cheese.
Blend in mayonnaise and stir until well coated.
Serve on lettuce leaf.
Garnish with one tablespoon shredded egg.
Place 2 tablespoons horseradish on the side.
Stir sugar, syrup and milk together.
Add butter and start on low fire to cook.
Gradually increase heat as mixture starts cooking.
Cook until hard ball forms when dropped in cold water. This takes 1/2 to 1 hour.
Stir continuously.
Cooks down very thick.
Remove from fire, stir in nutmeats and spread on buttered tin.
Cut in small squares and wrap in waxed paper.
Combine the onion, beets and orange juice in a 2-quart casserole.
Cover tightly and cook on High for 8 to 12 minutes or until the beets are tender, stirring once or twice.
Add the lemon juice, broth, cucumber and pepper.
Cover again and cook on High for 3 to 5 minutes, or until heated through, but not boiling.
Put a layer of crumbled cornbread in bottom of a 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish (omit crust if hard).
Put a layer of apples over top of crumbs, then a layer of raisins over the top of the apples.
Repeat the procedure until all is used up.
You will have about 3 layers.
Put dabs of butter all over the top and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Add about 4 tablespoons of water.
Cover.
Bake at 375° to 400° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Take out and put in serving dishes and pour milk and sugar over the top.
Delicious.

Brown ground beef. Drain. Add tomato sauce and Italian seasoning. Simmer slowly for 20 to 25 minutes. Prepare lasagna according to package directions. Drain. Arrange 1 layer of lasagna in parallel strips in bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Top with 1/3 of meat sauce, 1/3 Mozzarella and 1/3 cottage cheese. Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before cutting.
Cook vegetables in 2 cups water.
Don't drain.
Melt butter and oleo in large kettle and add the chopped celery and onion. Saute until clear.
Add flour and stir until blended.
Add 4 crushed bouillon cubes.
Add 6 cups cold milk.
Stir until smooth, but don't boil.
Add vegetables and liquid from vegetables.
Add 1 cup diced ham, 1 teaspoon Accent, salt and pepper to taste.
Heat thoroughly, but don't boil.
Makes 3 quarts.
Beat eggs and milk, then add salt and onion flakes.
Spread bread cubes, sausage and cheese in a lightly greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Pour egg mixture over all items in the pan.
Cover pan with foil and either refrigerate overnight or bake now.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, then remove foil and continue baking for an additional 5 minutes or until eggs are completely cooked.
Cut into squares to serve 6 to 8.
Spread a large sheet of wax paper on a work surface.

In a pan, combine the sugar, corn syrup, milk and cream of tartar. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until sugar is dissolved. Increase heat to moderate and continue cooking, stirring constantly, until soft ball stage (238°).
Remove from heat and set aside for 3 minutes to cool slightly.
Beat in peppermint. Continue beating until creamy.
Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Parboil potatoes until tender.
Cut in half and put in baking dish.
Pour cranberry sauce over top.
Sprinkle with sugar and dot with butter.
Bake in 350° oven for 25 minutes or until heated through.
Brown meat with onion and drain.
In large pan add meat, juice, beans, Chili-O and tomatoes.
Let simmer 45 minutes.
While your pasta is cooking, saute the shallots in butter for about 2 to 3 minutes.
Now stir in the chicken broth.
Boil gently for about 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the heavy cream.
By this time the pasta should be ready to be drained.
The last step is to add the drained pasta, sour cream, cheese and chives.
Toss and heat through but don't boil.
Go get a nice glass of wine and mangia!!
Slice bananas and dip in lemon juice.
In a large bowl combine sweetened condensed milk and water.
Add pudding mix; beat well. Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon 1 cup pudding mixture into 2 1/2-quart glass serving bowl.
Top with 1/3 each of wafers, bananas and pudding.
Repeat layers twice, ending with pudding.
Chill.
Garnish as desired.
In a saucepan, combine Worcestershire sauce, water, catsup, pineapple juice, brown sugar substitute and pepper.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Combine sauce and margarine in a shallow baking dish.
Marinate chicken for 15 minutes, turning occasionally to coat all sides.
Grill or broil about 3 minutes on each side or bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
First fry chops until browned.
Add soup, seasonings and water; simmer, covered, for 45 minutes.
Place potatoes and onion in enough water to cover potatoes. Add salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer until potatoes are just done.
Do not drain.
Add bouillon cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add milk and cheese.
Continue to simmer until cheese is melted.
Add pepper and remove from heat.
Cook fresh broccoli; drain off any water.
Add cream of chicken soup, butter, cornbread, sage and beaten eggs.
Mix well. Pour into dish.
Cook about 1 hour at 300°.
Melt cheese on top (optional).
In blender, combine oil, vinegar, water, honey, poppy seed, salt, paprika and pepper.
Toss with lettuce, strawberries and onions and serve.
Combine water and garlic in a large saucepan; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes.
Wash broccoli thoroughly; trim off large leaves.
Remove outside layer of stem and the tough lower ends of broccoli stalks.
Separate into spears.
Add broccoli and salt to garlic mixture.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes or until tender.
Discard garlic and drain broccoli well.
Transfer broccoli to a serving dish.
Sprinkle with lemon juice and Parmesan cheese before serving.
Serves 6 (36 calories per serving).
Put chicken into baking dish.
Melt margarine.
Add brown sugar, mustard and mustard seed.
Stir well.
Pour over chicken. Bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes at 350°.
Pit plums and slice them fairly thin.
In a medium saucepan, stir together plums, sugar and 1 cup water.
Simmer about 15 minutes, until plums are soft.
Combine cocoa and sugar, add melted margarine, stir well, beat in eggs; mix well.
Blend in flour, vanilla, nuts and chocolate chunks.
Bake at 350° in greased 9 x 13-inch pan for 20 minutes or until done.
Toast pecans in 1/4 c. butter at 325 degrees for 25 minutes. Sift flour with baking powder and salt.
Cream one cup of soft butter.
Slowly add sugar to butter, until creamy.
Beat in eggs. Beat in dry ingredients, alternating with milk.
Beat well.
Stir in vanilla and pecans.
Pour into three 8 inch greased and floured cake pans.
Bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes.
Cool.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine 10 cups thin sliced pared apples and peaches, spices, sugar and flour into mixing bowls. Turn several times and allow the ingredients to rest and mingle while preparing the pastry.
Carefully place the ingredients into a pastry lined glass pie plate.
Build the mound from the rim up to the center.
Clip the excess pastry to within 1/2-inch of the pie plate.
Add lemon drops and butter.
Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise and sugar; mix well.
Stir in cranberry sauce, pineapple and pecans.
Fold in whipped cream. Spread in 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan; freeze until firm.
Remove from freezer 5 minutes before serving.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Brown beef and sausages.
Drain off excess grease.
Add spices and cheese.
Cook until cheese is melted, mixing well.
Spread mixture on split bagels.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Scrub cucumbers.
Place in bowl with salt and 3 cups water. Let stand 24 hours.
Rinse in cold water, then in boiling water. Drain.
Pack cucumbers in hot sterilized jars to within 1/2-inch of top.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Bring to rapid boil.
Pour over cucumbers.
Put on cap.
Screw band firmly tight.
Process in boiling water bath 10 minutes.
Yields 8 to 10 pints.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream butter.
Stir in honey, eggs and sour cream.
Sift in flours, baking soda and baking powder.
Add vanilla and mix well.
Pour half the batter into a greased and floured 9-inch Bundt pan.
Cover with a layer of blueberries mixed with half the sugar/cinnamon mix.
Pour in remaining batter.
Top with remaining sugar/cinnamon.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes.
Beat cream cheese with 1/2 cup sugar.
Gradually beat in whipping cream.
Add vanilla and beat until stiff peaks form. Set-aside.
Heat oven to 375°.
Beat margarine and sugars; add eggs, milk and vanilla.
Add flour, baking soda and salt.
Stir in oats and chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased pan.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes about 5 dozen (2 1/2-inch) cookies.
Mix shredded cheese and margarine.
Add flour and mix well. Add crisp cereal and mix well. Shape into small balls and place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Flatten each ball with a fork and bake at 375° for about 10 minutes.
Heat half and half with chili powder, stirring to blend.
Let simmer for few minutes.
Add salt, pepper and Tabasco sauce.
Put cheese in bowl.
Gradually add the hot liquid.
Stir until cheeses are mixed up good.
Soften sherbet and mix with pineapple juice.
Pour Sprite or ginger ale slowly over mixture to make a foam.
Dip spoonfuls of vanilla ice cream over top of punch after it's in the punch bowl. Serves about 50.
Using mixer, combine softened cream cheese, marshmallow whip, ginger and honey.
Remove beater.
Using spoon, fold in Cool Whip. Refrigerate until serving time.
Serve over assorted fresh fruit.
Peel and core fruit and place in baking dish.
Slice each piece of bread into 5 narrow strips and place over fruit.
Mix sugar, milk, flour, and lemon juice.
Stir in margarine.
Add egg and mix well.
Pour over fruit and bread strips.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until fruit is tender.
Serves 6-8.
Make peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
Butter each side of bread.
Place in skillet and brown it like a grilled cheese.
Combine
sugar, brown sugar, flour, cornstarch and salt in saucepan.
Add
milk
and
peanut
butter chips gradually. Cook and
stir on medium heat until thick and bubbly.
Reduce heat; cook
and
stir
2 minutes.
Beat egg
yolks
lightly in small bowl.
Stir
1 cup hot mixture into yolks gradually and
return egg
mixture
to saucepan. Bring to gentle boil. Cook
and
stir on low heat 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and vanilla.
Pour mixture into baked pie shell and sprinkle with peanuts.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Cool to room temperature before serving.
To make crust, cut 1 stick of margarine into flour (texture will be crumbly) and spread into bottom of ungreased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Cool completely.
Combine flour, wheat germ, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt in large bowl.
Add yogurt, butter, egg and raisins.
Stir just to moisten.
Fill paper lined muffin cups 2/3 full.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes 1 dozen.
Calories 125 each.
Brown hamburger and onion on medium heat; drain.
Add potatoes, garlic, salt and oil.
Mix good and cover.
Stir occasionally.
Turn on low heat until potatoes are tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine first 7 ingredients in a medium bowl; set aside. Combine egg and hot sauce; stir in buttermilk.
Pour into first seven dry ingredients, stirring just to mix.
Stir in onion and corn (do not overmix batter).
Drop batter by tablespoonfuls into deep, hot oil (350°); cook only a few at a time, turning once. Fry 3 minutes or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Yields 3 dozen.
Mix Jell-O, water, sugar and juice.
When syrupy from chilling, add whipped cream, folding until smooth.
Fold in angel food cake (pieces no bigger than 50 cent pieces).
Chill.
Can be made on the same day served, or the day before and let set up in refrigerator.
Should be fluffy.
Combine dry ingredients and sift.
Add egg just enough to blend; add melted butter and combine.
Combine milk and water; add to mixture, beating only until batter is smooth.
Combine coconut and pecans; spread on bottom of unbaked pie crust.
Fill with chocolate mixture.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes.
First 15 minutes at 375°, then drop heat to 375°.
Lightly brown meat in heavy skillet.
Sprinkle 1/2 of spaghetti sauce mix over meat.
Spread cottage cheese in layer over meat.
Next, arrange uncooked noodles in layer.
Sprinkle with remaining spaghetti sauce mix, basil, parsley flakes and salt.
Add tomatoes with liquid and water, being sure all is moistened.
Cover tightly and simmer about 30 to 35 minutes or until noodles are done.
Sprinkle cheese over top.
Return cover and let stand 10 to 15 minutes before serving.
Makes 8 servings.

Boil fresh sweet potatoes until tender; drain and remove skins, then slice. Mix brown sugar, margarine, orange juice, peels and salt in 8-inch skillet. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until smooth and bubbly. Add sweet potato slices; stir gently until glazed and heated through. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix all the cereals, pretzels and peanuts together in a large roaster.
Melt bacon fat and butter together and mix other seasonings.
Pour seasoned fat over the dry cereal and toss to mix the seasoning.
Bake in 200° oven for one hour.
Turn occasionally during the one hour so seasoning will be equally distributed. Cool.
Store in airtight container.
Saute onions in 4 tablespoons of butter until soft.
Stir in flour.
Add water and cook over low heat until thick.
Blend in cheese.
Combine sauce and thawed, well drained broccoli.
Add eggs and mix gently.
Pour into greased 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Cover with cracker crumbs and dot with 2 tablespoons butter.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
Melt chocolate with oleo over low heat; gradually blend in milk.
Mix sugar, flour and salt; beat in eggs and vanilla gradually.
Blend in chocolate mixture.
Pour into shell.
Mix coconut and pecans and sprinkle over filling.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until top is puffed.
Cool at least 4 hours before serving.
Fry rice in cooking oil until brown. Add chopped onion and green pepper. Fry about 1 minute.

Grind cumin and garlic in a spice grinder. Add ground spices, tomato sauce and chicken broth along with 2 1/2 cups boiling water. When all is boiling, cover and lower heat to simmer. Do not stir after this point. Cook until tender. Add peas for color.
Boil sugar and syrup for 1 minute.
Add butter and peanut butter.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and corn flakes.
Drop on wax paper.
Heat oven to 275°.
Combine oil, sugar and eggs; beat vigorously with spoon or electric mixer for 2 minutes.
Sift 2 cups flour with baking powder, salt and spices.
Stir into the oil mixture alternately with fruit juice.
Mix other cup flour with the fruits and nuts.
Pour batter over the fruit, mixing well.
Turn into 2 (8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch) loaf pans, greased and lined with brown paper.
I use a tube pan.
Place pan of water on lower oven rack.
Bake 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
After baking, let cake stand 15 minutes before removing from pans.
Place patties in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Chop onion and bell pepper and place on patties.
Pour cold and hot water into pan. Pour gravy mix into water; do not stir.
Cover pan.
Place in oven for 1 hour at 350°.
Heat oil over medium-high heat in Dutch oven.
Sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook in batches in hot oil until brown.
Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium and add garlic, onions, peppers and 1 teaspoon salt and cook until soft, about 10 minutes. Increase heat to high; add wine and cook until all liquid evaporates.
Add tomatoes, oregano, cayenne and chicken.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer until chicken is tender, 45 to 60 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
If sauce is too thin, remove chicken and cook sauce over high heat until thickened.
In saucepan, add milk, water and salt.
At boiling point, add rice and put on low heat.
Boil rice for 45 minutes, stirring often.
Let rice cool 15 minutes.
In a bowl, add sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Beat real well and add to the rice mixture and mix well. Put in serving cups, sprinkle top with cinnamon and refrigerate.
Drain and slice water chestnuts.
Add soup, stuffing mix and mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Add crab and mix lightly.
Pour into greased 2-quart casserole dish and bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Place cheese between bread.
Cook in margarine as would for grilled cheese, until bread is brown and cheese melted.
Open sandwich and put slices of bacon, slice of pineapple and close. You may use lettuce, mayonnaise and tomato, if you prefer.
Crumble ground beef into a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Add next 7 ingredients.
Microwave at High for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring at 2-minute intervals.
When meat is done, drain away grease.
Spoon 3 tablespoons meat mixture into each taco shell; top with lettuce, tomatoes and cheese.
Serve with taco sauce.
Brown pork chops in oil and salt; drain.
Combine other ingredients and reserve 1/2 cup of this mixture.
Pour remaining over chops and simmer, covered, on low heat for 25 minutes, basting a few times.
Place chops on sheet and put apple on each. Cover with reserved mixture.
Bake in oven at 350° for 15 minutes.
Remove chicken skin; cook chicken in 1 tablespoon margarine over medium heat until done on both sides.
Reduce heat; sprinkle with paprika, salt and dill weed.
Mix 1/3 cup water and dry bouillon; pour over chicken.
Add onion.
Cover and simmer until chicken is done, about 30 minutes.
Remove chicken; keep warm. Stir yogurt into liquid in skillet.
Mix cornstarch and 1/4 cup water; gradually stir into yogurt mixture.
Heat to boiling; stir constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Pour yogurt sauce over chicken; sprinkle with parsley.
Serves 4 people.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spread 1 tablespoon softened butter evenly over bottom of large pan.
Shell the shrimp.
Devein by making a shallow incision down their backs with a small, sharp knife and lifting out black vein with the point.
Drop the shrimp into lightly salted, boiling water and boil 3 minutes, until firm and pink.
Drain.
Chop coarsely and place in bowl.

recipes.t: Grilled Eggplant And Peppers With Fontinella Cheese
d: Cut eggplants in half lengthwise.
Cut peppers in quarters. Core and seed.
Combine oil and vinegar and salt and pepper to taste.
Marinate peppers and eggplant in oil mixture for 2 hours.
In buttered 9-inch square
Pyrex dish, spread pie filling. Spread cake mix over filling.
Pour margarine over cake mix. Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake in moderate oven until nuts are brown. Serve hot or cold with ice cream or whipped cream.
Heat oven to 325°.
Melt butter.
Add celery, onions and carrots.
Saute until vegetables are tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour in a 1 1/2-quart casserole and bake 30 to 45 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Melt oleo in large oblong baking dish.
Add peaches (slices and juice) to the oblong dish.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt; add milk and vanilla.
Pour batter over top of peaches; sprinkle 1/2 cup sugar over top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
In a bowl, stir together the cornmeal, 1 cup of cold water and salt.
In a medium saucepan, bring 3 cups of water to a boil. Over low heat, gradually stir in the cornmeal mixture and continue stirring until thickened.
Cover and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, for about 15 minutes.
Off heat, stir in Parmesan. Divide mixture evenly among three 12-ounce frozen juice concentrate cans.
Chill until set, about 2 hours.
Beat eggs on high speed for 5 minutes.
Beat granulated sugar, lemon juice and pumpkin.
Fold into pumpkin mixture flour, baking powder, cinnamon, salt and ginger.
Grease and flour a 15 x 10 x 2-inch cookie sheet.
Pour in batter and top with nuts.
Bake 15 minutes at 375°.
Turn out on powdered tea towel.
Roll up and cool 1/2 hour.
Unroll and spread with filling.

Cook chicken strips in skillet thoroughly. Pour off drippings, leaving approximately 1/4 cup in pan. Add onion and green chiles; cook over medium heat for 3 minutes longer. Add cream cheese and seasonings; mix well and continue to simmer 5 to 7 minutes.
Cut links into fourths; spread on bottom of ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan (glass).
Cover with scrambled eggs.
Cover with cottage cheese, then cover with Cheddar cheese soup.
Cover pan and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 325° for 50 to 60 minutes, uncovered.
Serve hot with toast, muffins or bread.
Simple and elegant.
Sift flour, half of salt and onion salt into butter.
Stir in milk.
Cook over hot water, stirring occasionally until thickened. Pour Minute rice into 2-quart shallow baking dish.
Combine broth, remaining salt and pour over rice.
Sprinkle half of cheese over rice.
Top with asparagus or peas, then turkey.
Pour on sauce.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake at 375° about 20 minutes.
Top with almonds.
Pour 1 envelope onion soup over meat; add preserves, then dressing.
Mix well on meat.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour in an aluminum foil covered pan, then uncover for 30 minutes or 1 hour until meat has browned.
Baste with juice from meat.
Soften gelatin in 1/4 cup water, then dissolve in 1 1/2 cups hot water.
Stir in next 3 ingredients and pour 1/4 cup into 1 1/2-quart mold.
Add about 1/4 cup apples and chill until firm. Chill rest of gelatin until thickened, but not firm.
Mix remaining apples and next 4 ingredients together.
Whip the cream and fold in.
Fold into gelatin mixture.
Pour into mold and chill several hours.
Unmold on lettuce.
Serves 4 to 6.
Saute bacon until crisp, remove from drippings and set aside to drain.
Parboil poke greens and drain.
Add poke and soy sauce to hot bacon drippings.
Simmer, tightly covered, until poke is wilted.
Drop eggs individually on poke.
Cook, covered, until eggs are firm.
Using spatula, cut around each egg and place on warm plates.
Crumble bacon pieces over eggs and serve.
Serves 2.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Melt oleo, put half in 9 x 13-inch dish.
Sift flour and baking powder.
Beat eggs; season with salt and pepper.
Add ham, cheese, flour mixture and other half of oleo.
Mix, pour into dish, bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350°, bake 30 minutes longer or until puffy and light golden brown.
Can be mixed and stored in refrigerator until ready to be baked.
Can also be baked and frozen.

recipes.t: Spicy Corn And Black Bean Relish
d: In a large bowl, combine corn, beans and pepper. Combine remaining ingredients in a small bowl; pour over corn mixture and toss to coat.
Chill. Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Mix butter, cheese, salt, pepper and flour.
Take a ball of the mixture and wrap around a pitted date.
Bake at 300° for 10 minutes.
Makes approximately 33 balls.
Boil raisins until puffy.
Cut cranberries in half and wash in colander to remove seeds.
Dissolve cornstarch in cold water and add salt.
Cook 5 minutes.
Add boiling water and cook 10 minutes longer.
Add raisins and cranberries.
Bake in unbaked pie shell. Make a lattice work top with pastry strips.
Bake about 40 minutes in a 350° oven.
Slowly brown slivered almonds in 2 tablespoons oleo; drain on paper toweling and salt.
Melt 1/2 cup oleo and add brown sugar while on stove.
Remove from heat and add coconut, Rice Chex and almonds.
Put 1/2 mixture into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Slice ice cream and place over mixture.
Put other 1/2 of mixture on top of ice cream.
Cover tightly and freeze.
Cook lima beans as directed.
Drain reserving liquid as part of the 1/2 cup water to the soup.
Combine onion, red pepper, soup and water in a saucepan.
Heat through.
Remove from heat.
Blend sour cream and curry powder into soup mixture.
Stir in lima beans.
Put mixture into a 6-cup casserole.
Combine bread crumbs with melted butter.
Stir in bacon crumbles.
Sprinkle over lima mixture.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 25 minutes until
crumb topping is browned.
Cut squash into 1-inch pieces and combine with onion in a greased 6-cup shallow, microwave casserole dish, covered with plastic wrap.
Microwave on full power for 7 minutes.
Drain all liquid from dish and save it for soup or sauce.
Beat eggs in a medium size bowl with
a wire whip until foamy.
Stir in cheese, salt, basil and pepper until well blended.
Pour over squash in casserole, stirring to mix well. Cover casserole with a paper towel.
Microwave at Medium power 5 minutes.
Remove the paper towel.
Microwave 3 minutes longer or until egg mixture is set. Before serving, garnish with parsley.
Very good.
Cut chicken into thin strips.
Heat oil in frypan.
Add chicken and garlic.
Cook, stirring constantly, until chicken turns white.
Add soy sauce and stir.
Add celery, mushrooms and stir-fry vegetables.
Cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch and water.
Add slowly to chicken mixture, stirring constantly.
Cook until ingredients are coated with a thin glaze, about 1 minute.
Serve with hot rice and extra soy sauce.
Combine pineapple juice, soy sauce and oil in a baking dish and marinate chicken in the mixture for 3 hours.
Alternate chicken with tomatoes, green peppers, onions and mushrooms on skewers.
Broil for 10 to 15 minutes, turning once, or until chicken is cooked through.
To barbecue, cook 5 inches from flame using marinade to baste.
Serve over rice or pasta.
Break salmon in bite size pieces.
Put in bowl.
Add celery and drained peas.
Combine other ingredients.
Pour over salmon mixture.
Toss lightly with fork.
Chill several hours.
Serve in lettuce cups.
Prepare cake according to directions.
Bake in 15 x 11-inch cookie sheet with edges at 350° for 15 minutes.
Combine pudding with cold milk and cream cheese.
Fold in frozen topping.
Spread mixture on cold cake.
Drain pineapple very well.
In layers, put on fruit and sprinkle with coconut and nuts.
Soak gelatin in 1/2 cup cold water; heat to boiling 1 cup water with sugar, vinegar and salt.
Add gelatin mixture to hot liquid and stir until dissolved.
Cool.
Add remaining ingredients including asparagus juice.
Pour into bowl, chill until set.
Cut into squares.
Garnish; mayonnaise and lettuce if desired.
Cut up chicken and season to taste; boil until done.
Remove chicken; let cool; debone.
Dip tortillas in the chicken broth to soften; line a 13x9 inch pan.
Place chicken on top of tortillas. In a bowl mix onion, bell pepper, soups, tomatoes, garlic salt, and chili powder.
Blend well, pour over chicken. Cook at 350 degrees for 30 minutes, put cheese on top; cook for additional 15 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Place crackers on cookie sheet.
Spread 1 teaspoon ketchup on each cracker and add pepperoni and any other desired toppings. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 400° for 3 to 5 minutes.
Easy for kids and a good healthy snack.
Bake cake according to package directions in a 9 x 12 x 2-inch pan.
Pour cream of coconut over warm cake.
Cool.
Add 2/3 can of full-cream milk for each can of soup.
Brown lobster meat in butter, add to soup mixture and warm slowly.
Add sherry to taste just before taking off stove.
Beat egg; add pineapple juice, lemon juice and sugar.
Bring to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes.
Refrigerate until cold. Serve over any combination of fruit.
I like the pineapple chunks that the juice was drained from, bananas, white grapes, peaches, etc.
Fruit can be fresh or canned.
Cook broccoli until just tender.
Drain and place in greased casserole dish.
Make a sauce with the butter, flour, salt, milk, pepper and cheese.
Sprinkle nuts over broccoli, then pour sauce over all.
Sprinkle top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbling hot and browned on top.
Yields 8 servings.
Cook lasagne according to package directions.
(Separate lasagne and lay out flat on wax paper or aluminum foil to keep pieces from sticking together as they cool.)
Combine Sargento cheese, the vegetables, 2 1/2 cups of the Ricotta and the egg. Place layer of lasagne on bottom of a 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Spread with 1/2 of the cheese mixture.
Repeat layers, ending with lasagne.
Mix
oil, melted margarine, buttermilk, eggs, honey and molasses.
Add Grape-Nuts and
bran.
Mix in separate bowl the flour, soda, baking powder, brown sugar and salt.
Make a well in middle of dry ingredients
and
add wet.
Stir until barely mixed. Bake at 400° for
20 to 25 minutes.
These are wonderful and sweet.
Brown sausage and onion in skillet.
Pour over cream cheese in bowl.
Mix until cream cheese is blended.
Add Ro-Tel tomatoes and mix well.
Spread tortillas with thin layer of refried beans, then place 1/4 cup meat mixture in center with a pinch of cheese and roll up.
Place in greased casserole.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes or until cheese melts.
Serves 6 to 8.

Place everything in 9 x 13 pan. Cover and put in the refrigerator for 1 hour. Turn chicken and leave sit for 1 more hour. Pour entire contents into saucepan and cook until approximately 1 cup of sauce remains. Serve over rice or noodles. Excellent flavor.

Mix cranberry sauce, sugar and gelatin together. Bring to a boil. Add the jellos and stir and cook for at least 5 minutes. Pour into 9 x 9 inch pan or glass dish. Cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate 12 hours. Cut into small 1/2 inch squares. Roll in sugar. Put on cookie sheet lined with wax paper. Leave air space around each piece. Let dry 24 hours. Roll again in sugar and return to cookie sheet. Repeat this every 24 hours until they stay dry. Do not refrigerate. Place in airtight container when dry.
Soften the peanut butter in a pan over low heat.
Gradually stir in milk, salt and pepper.
Chill.
Cold peanut soup for 8 people.
In medium saucepan over medium-high heat, melt butter and saute shallots lightly.
Stir in flour until creamy.
Add broth and sherry slowly; heat until boiling and gravy is smooth.
Season to taste with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in ham, chicken, asparagus and cream. Pour chicken mixture into ungreased 9-inch pie plate.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Fill cavity of turkey with celery stalks for moisture.
Place in large cooker.
Baste with a sauce of equal parts honey and lemon juice.
Add hickory chips that have been saturated with water for a hickory smoked flavor.
Cut eggplant, zucchini and potatoes in bite-size chunks (do not peel zucchini or eggplant).
Slice peppers, onions and dice tomatoes.
Saute the vegetables, except tomatoes, in olive oil. Place sauteed vegetables in baking dish.
Add tomatoes into the pan to saute with crushed garlic.
Add sugar, salt and pepper and simmer for another minute.
Pour tomato sauce on top of the vegetables and bake at 350° until the vegetables are tender.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix 1 egg, butter and dry cake mix until crumbly; reserve 1 cup.
Pat remaining mixture lightly into ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake until lightly browned, about 15 minutes.
Beat 2 eggs, sugar, baking powder, salt, lemon peel and lemon juice with rotary beater until light and foamy.
Pour over hot crust.
Sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture.
Bake about 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar, if desired.
Cool, cut into about 2 x 1 1/2-inch bars. Makes 32 bars.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 13 x 9 -inch baking dish.
In a large mixer bowl, beat brown sugar, butter and 1/4 cup peanut butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs.
Add combined flour, baking soda, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Beat until well mixed.
Stir in oats and mix well.
Set aside 1 cup of oat mixture.
Spread remaining oat mixture into pan.
Use spatula to spread evenly.
Prepare and cook green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces, as directed.
Cook beans, onion, olives and dressing, uncovered, over medium heat, just until onion is tender, about 3 minutes. Sprinkle with tomato.
Add pepper, celery, bay leaf, salt, pepper, butter and cayenne pepper to the tomatoes.
Simmer 20 minutes.
Saute onion in 1 tablespoon butter; add parsley.
Add this to mixture.
Add shrimp.
Cook until shrimp are pink.
Pour over fluffy hot rice.
Cut tortillas into thin strips.
Heat oil in 10-inch skillet until hot.
Cook tortillas and onions, turning occasionally until tortillas are crisp, about 10 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with cheese; heat just until cheese is melted.
Serve with sour cream.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Combine potatoes, mushrooms, celery and soup and 1/2 cup cheese.
Spoon into buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Arrange sausage on top of potato mixture.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar well.

Add ingredients in order listed. Chill dough for several hours before rolling out. Roll fairly thin and cut with a biscuit cutter, allowing two for each cookie. (Or, you may place filling on one side of the circle of dough and fold over and crimp together with a fork, making a crescent shape.) Put a generous teaspoon of filling on one cookie and cover with another, pressing edges together.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large roasting pan.
Combine margarine and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over cereal mixture, tossing gently.
Sprinkle with herb and spice blend.
Bake at 250° for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Stir in raisins and cool.
Store in an airtight container. Yields 11 cups, 151 calories and 5 g fat from 1 cup serving.
Coat 2-quart (9 x 13) baking dish with cooking spray or Crisco.
Add potatoes and some onion.
Dissolve bouillon in hot water and pour 1/2 cup over potatoes.
Combine meat, taco seasoning, milk, 1/4 cup salsa, oats, egg and remaining onion. Mix well and pour over potatoes.
Combine remaining 1 cup salsa and broth.
Pour over meat mixture.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
Empty all boxes in a mixing bowl.
Add Parkay (or butter), cream cheese and water.
Blend on medium speed of mixer until fluffy.
Blend well for about a minute.
Set aside.
Sift together in large bowl the first 4 ingredients.
Add shortening, milk and vanilla.
Beat vigorously by hand or with electric mixer.
Add 3 large egg whites.
Beat 2 minutes longer. Pour into 2 (8 or 9-inch) greased and floured round pans.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool and ice with Browned Butter Icing.
Mix together quick oats, wheat germ, coconut, cinnamon and brown sugar.
Add the honey and mix with fingers.
Add oil and vanilla and mix.
Spread on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Cream butter; add sugar gradually and beat until creamy.
Add other ingredients, except peanuts, to creamed mixture and mix well.
Add peanuts and mix again.
Chill at least 1 hour.
In a saucepan melt 1/2 stick butter.
Slice tomatoes to desired thickness and spread out in a saucepan; sprinkle with garlic, salt, pepper and other spices, if desired.
Turn tomatoes and sprinkle again with desired spices.
Place several slices of cheese (Provolone) on top of sauteed tomatoes.
When melted, put onto fresh or toasted Italian bread or rolls.
Drain pineapple, reserving 2 tablespoons of juice (discard the remaining juice).
Place pineapple and juice in a bowl; add remaining ingredients and toss lightly.
Yield: 4 servings.
Chop tomatoes and onion and set aside.
Heat soup with milk and mustard mixed in.
Toast bread.
Pile tomatoes and onion on toast and pour soup mixture over this.
Dissolve strawberry jello in boiling water.
Add 1 cup strawberry juice from thawed frozen strawberries.
Put in refrigerator until set.
Mix in sour cream, Philadelphia cream cheese and drained strawberries.
Pour into bowl.
Set and serve later.
Heat sugar, butter, syrup and milk to a boil; boil to soft ball stage.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and peanut butter. Beat until thick.
Pour into buttered pan and cool.
Combine oil, eggs and honey. Beat well. Add oatmeal, baking powder, salt and milk. Mix. Then add apples, raisins, pecans and cinnamon. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat together the cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, water, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in the sour cream, chocolate chips and nuts.
Pour into a greased bundt pan or angel food pan.
Bake at 350° for approximately 45 minutes.
Cool at least one hour and top with powdered sugar (use a strainer to shake it on).
Mix sausage, croutons and milk in a bowl. Fill mushroom caps and bake at 350° until hot on cookie sheet.
Crumble sausage into a heavy skillet.
Brown and drain.
Stir in onion and garlic; saute 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in remaining ingredients; cover and simmer mixture 60 to 90 minutes, stirring as needed.
Add a little more water during cooking if needed. Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Sprinkle yeast into very warm water; stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the sugar.
Stir until dissolved and let double in volume. Combine remaining sugar, milk, margarine and salt; heat just until margarine melts.
Pour into a large bowl; cool to lukewarm.
Stir in yeast.
Gradually stir in enough flour to make a soft dough. Turn out onto a floured surface.
Knead until smooth and elastic, adding flour as needed.
Place in a greased bowl.
Turn to bring greased side up.
Cover and set in a warm, draft free place to rise to double in bulk.
Punch down.
Knead a few times, cut in half.
Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Shape into 2 loaves. Place in 2 greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch pans.
Cover and let rise again. Bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until loaves are lightly browned and sound hollow when tapped.
Bring sugar and syrup to a boil.
Add peanut butter.
Mix Rice Krispies.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch buttered pan.
Melt chocolate chips and butterscotch chips together.
Pour over mixture in pan.
Peel and slice cucumbers.
Let stand overnight in brine made with 1/2 cup salt to 3 quarts water.
Next day, slice thin or chop onions.
Mix sugar and spices with flour and vinegar.
Add drained cucumbers, onions and pimento.
Cook, uncovered.
Turn down heat, stir and cook 10 minutes.
Seal in jars.
The night before serving, put potatoes, onion, tomatoes and cut up chicken in the crock-pot.
Cook on low overnight.
Next morning, take chicken out.
Remove skin and bones, then tear chicken into small pieces and return to crock-pot.
Stir in sauces and catsup.
Cook on low until one hour before dinner.
Add corn, stir well and leave on low until ready to serve.

Cream margarine and cream cheese together. Add sugar. Add eggs 2 at a time. Add all flavors together. Add flour slowly. Mix all ingredients on medium speed for 3 to 4 minutes. Bake in a 16 x 4 loaf baking pan for 1 hour at 300°. Be sure to flour and grease pan.
Mix cheese and juice real well.
Add marshmallows and stir well.
Cut up oranges; add to mixture.
Let set a few minutes until thickened.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Add nuts.
Pour into long baking dish; refrigerate until firm.
Fry onion, pepper and beef together in a skillet; drain.
Add salt, pepper, basil, oregano and onion soup mix to taste.
Add Worcestershire sauce.
Mix all together and cook 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Add all other ingredients.
Cover and simmer 20 to 45 minutes (until cabbage is tender).
Serve over rice, beans or pasta.
Cook stewing hen until tender in plenty of water to be used as broth later.
When cool, skin and debone.
Refrigerate.
Cook 1 large skillet of self-rising corn bread, using 3 to 4 eggs.
When done, remove from skillet to large mixing bowl.
Add 6 thick or 8 thin slices of bread.
Pour enough broth to cover. Dissolve the soup in more broth (1 can).
Pour this over bread.
Use poultry seasoning and 2 bouillon chicken cubes, if needed, to improve taste.
Set mixture aside for bread to soften.
Layer chicken in a greased casserole dish.
Pour soup over chicken.
Add milk.
Mix stuffing with butter and chicken broth. Spread over top.
Bake at 350° about 20 to 30 minutes.
Cook meat and onion together.
Drain and put in a baking dish. Top with potatoes and then corn.
Pour soup over this and bake until potatoes are done.
Melt half of margarine; add chicken with Tony's and brown slightly.
Add chopped onions and bell pepper.
Saute, then add rest of margarine and 1 cup uncooked rice.
Stir constantly until rice begins to brown slightly.
Add 2 1/4 cups of hot water, additional Tony's and mushrooms.
Cover.
Reduce heat and cook until rice is done, approximately 20 minutes.
Melt margarine in a large saucepan.
Add Worcestershire sauce, ketchup and hot sauce.
Stir in nuts.
Spoon into glass baking dish.
Spread evenly.
Toast at 400° for about 20 minutes. Salt when you remove.
In Dutch oven, fry bacon and onion.
Drain grease.
Add potatoes, carrots, chicken bouillon
and water to cover.
Boil and then simmer for 20 minutes (until potatoes and carrots are soft). Add half and half,
corn and pepper.
Heat until warm. Do not boil.
Add cheese
and
stir until melted.
Soup should be thick like a stew, if
not,
add in a small amount of flour dissolved in water to thicken.
Sprinkle salt in large skillet.
Add chops and brown over medium heat.
Sprinkle chili mix over chops.
Add rice, water and tomatoes.
Be sure rice is moist.
Cover and reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes.
Mix beans in a saucepan; add butter, seasoned salt and lemon pepper.
Let simmer for 10 minutes after coming to a hard boil. Wait for 2 minutes, cool down and place in bowl.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese on top.
Ready to serve.
Put chicken in pot with broth, water, salt and Tabasco.
Bring to boil and skim off foam.
Reduce heat; add carrots.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Mix Bisquick, onions, basil, egg and milk in medium bowl until stiff.
Drop by teaspoonful into rapidly boiling broth.
Reduce heat, cover and cook 10 minutes, until dumplings have puffed.
Pull chicken off bone in large pieces and serve with soup and dumplings.
Makes 4 servings.

Cook tomatoes, onions, celery, parsley and peppers until tender. Put through a sieve. Add sugar and salt. Make a paste of melted butter and flour. Blend with juice. Heat and add to jars. Process in hot water bath 2 hours or in a pressure cooker (pints 15 minutes or quarts 20 minutes).
Cook noodles according to box.
In large Pyrex, layer 1/2 of cooked noodles, hamburger and 1 jar of sauce; layer on slices of Velveeta and sprinkle Parmesan cheese.
Repeat process.
Bake at 350° for approximately 45 minutes.
Saute Spam, onion and green pepper in oil until vegetables are tender.
Spoon into lightly greased 10-inch deep dish pie plate. Sprinkle with cheese.
Mix remaining ingredients in blender or with hand mixer until smooth.
Pour evenly into pie plate.
Bake at 400° about 30 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting. Makes 6 servings.
Brown sausage and drain off grease.
(Roll sausage in a few paper towels for more removal of grease, if desired.) Return sausage to skillet and add carrots, celery, onion and pressed garlic.
Simmer in covered skillet until desired tenderness.
Add eggs and rice.
Season as desired.
Good with hot sauce.
Use your favorite veggies.
Spread 1/2 box of dry cake mix in a 9 X 12-inch pan.
Spread in canned pie filling.
Spread the rest of the cake mix on top.
Pour water slowly over top.
Bake 50 - 60 minutes at 350 degrees.
Cook macaroni; melt butter and blend in flour seasonings.
Add diluted milk gradually.
Cook over low heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Add shredded or thinly sliced cheese; stir until it begins to melt.
Scald dried beef and add to sauce.
Add macaroni and pour into greased baking dish.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
