recipes.t: Lemon-Snap Cookies(30 Calories Per Cookie; Lo-Cal)
d: In medium bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in egg, lemon juice and rind.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Add gradually to sugar and shortening.
Mix until smooth.
Refrigerate until firm (about 1 to 2 hours). Preheat oven to 400°.
Roll to 1/8-inch thickness; cut as you wish.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes on lightly greased cookie sheet or until edges are golden brown.
Makes 6 to 7 dozen.
Grease and flour 2 (9-inch) round cake pans.
Combine cake mix, pineapple juice, water and egg whites in a large mixing bowl. Blend with mixer on low speed 30 seconds.
Beat at medium speed 2 minutes.
Divide batter between pans.
Bake at 350° for 29 to 32 minutes or until pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, then remove from pan.
Combine crushed pineapple and cornstarch in small saucepan.
Blend until smooth.
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture boils.
Reduce heat and cook, stirring constantly, 1 minute.
Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Prepare Whipped Cream Frosting.
To assemble cake, place one cake layer on serving plate and spread top with frosting.
Spoon thickened pineapple sauce over frosting.
Top with second cake layer.
Frost sides and top of cake.
Refrigerate until serving time.
Cut up cabbage, onion and pepper.
Mix.
Put into a covered dish or pan and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Place fish into microwavable dish.
Cover with parsley, lime juice, salt and pepper.
Cover with plastic wrap and microwave 5 to 6 minutes.
Pour almonds with oleo over the fish to serve.
Serves 3 to 4.
Scald milk.
Add sugar, salt and margarine; set aside. Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water.
Add milk mixture.
Add 1 cup flour, beating well by hand.
Add eggs, vanilla and nutmeg. Beat well.
Add remaining flour and beat well until smooth.
Cover and let rise 1 hour.
Stir down.

recipes.t: My Mother'S Chicken Cacciatore (In A Pot)
d: Brown chicken in oil. Season with salt, pepper, garlic and basil. Cook for 10 minutes, turning frequently. Add the tomatoes which you have crushed by hand and sliced peppers.
Cook, covered, 45 to 60 minutes. Serve with plain or garlic bread.
Enjoy!
Combine cheese, bacon, chili sauce and honey in bowl.
Mix well.
Spread on muffins.
Place on baking sheet.
Broil for 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 12 servings.
Fry diced bacon almost crisp.
Then place in bowl with paper towels.
Once dry, add bacon, horseradish and garlic salt to cheese.
Mix well.
Add mayo.
Mix until creamy.
Brown pork loin well on all sides in kettle or Dutch oven; remove from pan.
(Or brown in a large, heavy roasting pan on surface burners.)
Saute onions and carrots in pork drippings until soft.
Stir in beer, salt, pepper and bay leaf (if substituting butter beans for carrots, add them at this point). Return pork to kettle and cover.
(If using roasting pan, cover tightly with aluminum foil.)
Braise in a 350° oven for 2 hours, or until pork is tender when pierced with two-tined fork.
Place pork on a platter and keep warm.
Cook the noodles as mentioned on the package.
Drain and rinse in cold water; drain again and cool the noodles.
Bring to a boil 1 cup pineapple juice.
Remove from the heat and add the orange Jell-O, stirring to dissolve the gelatin.
Then add the rest of the juice and let cool the mixture until it is half taken in Jell-O. Add the noodles, the orange sections and the diced cucumber.
Pour in an already buttered 1 1/2-quart mold and refrigerate.
To serve, unmold on lettuce.
Bon appetit!
Toss lettuce, tomatoes and peppers in a bowl with desired amount of vinaigrette.
Garnish with red onion rings.
Dissolve lime jello in hot water, then add the cold water. Pour into a 14 x 10 x 2-inch pan.
Chill until set, then dissolve lemon jello in water.
Over heat, dissolve marshmallows in jello. Remove from heat and add pineapple juice and cream cheese.
Beat until well blended.
Stir in pineapple.
When cooled, add whipped cream and mayonnaise.
Chill until thick, then pour over lime jello.
Chill until set.
Dissolve cherry jello in hot water, then add cold water.
Chill until syrupy.
Pour over pineapple layer. Chill until firm.
Mix butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla.
Place one can of "cut-up" biscuits in a Bundt pan.
Pour 1/3 of the sugar mixture over biscuits.
Repeat procedure with each can. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes and then turn out.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Into a 1 1/2-quart shallow baking dish, spoon peach pie filling.
Into a medium bowl, measure flour, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
With pastry blender or 2 knives used scissor-fashion, cut in butter or margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in coconut.
Crumble mixture evenly over peach pie filling.
Bake 15 minutes or until topping is golden brown and filling is bubbly.
Serve with half and half.

recipes.t: Marinated Carrot And Green Bean Salad
d: Combine carrots, green beans and onion in glass jar with good lid.
Combine oil, vinegar, honey and salt.
Pour over vegetables. Marinate several hours or overnight (turn jar upside down a couple times).
When marinated, drain well.
(Because of the honey, you may want to blot vegetables by pouring about a third at a time on a paper towel lined platter.)
Arrange on chopped lettuce.
Garnish with pickled beets, or put marinated vegetables in glass bowl and serve as vegetable dish.
Cut squash in half and remove seed.
Lay squash halves in baking dish.
Fill dish with 1/2 inch water.
Sprinkle inside of squash with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Cut apples into pieces 1 x 1/2 x 1/2-inch.
Fill opening in squash with pieces of apple, raisins, pieces of walnut (fill to almost overflowing).
Put a pat of butter on top and sprinkle with cinnamon, nutmeg and ground cloves.
Bake, covered, at 400° for about 1 hour.
Fill unbaked pie shell with sliced peaches.
Cream together sugar with margarine.
Add flour, egg and vanilla.
Spread this mixture over the sliced fruit and bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until top is golden and brown.
Combine eggs, sugar, syrup, butter, salt and lemon juice. Sprinkle nuts on bottom of each pastry cup.
Add filling and bake 20 to 25 minutes at 375°.
May be frozen.
Boil water, sugar and cream of tartar for 5 minutes.
While boiling, add one at a time, 20 Ritz crackers.
Do not stir; pour into an unbaked pie crust.
Sprinkle with nutmeg and dot with butter; cover with top crust.
Bake at 425° approximately 25 minutes.
Grease cookie sheet or pizza pan generously.
Layer ingredients in the order as shown, adding just enough tomato sauce to hold mixture together.
Place in 350° oven until cheese melts.
Rinse chicken; pat dry.
Combine paprika and pepper; rub into chicken.
Arrange chicken pieces in 1 2/3 to 2-quart microwave dish, with meaty portions toward edge.
Combine remaining ingredients; spoon over chicken.
Mix vanilla pudding as directed on the package.
Mix softened cream cheese with vanilla pudding.
Beat with beater until smooth. Beat the pint of whipping cream until fluffy.
(I sometimes add Equal or Sweet 'N Low as I beat it.)
Add the whipping cream to the pudding/cream cheese mixture.
In a 13 x 9-inch covered container, put graham crackers, then a layer of the pudding mixture.
(I chip up a banana on the first layer for added flavor or add a layer of crushed drained pineapple.)
Make another layer of graham crackers and another layer of pudding mixture and top with cherry pie filling.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Not good unless it is cold.
Enjoy.
Low-fat and almost sugar free!
Soak oats in 5 tablespoons warm milk until swollen, about 5 minutes.
Stir in yogurt, hazelnuts, honey and lemon juice.
Mix grated apples into yogurt mixture. Carefully mix in 1 pint mixed berries. Spoon mix into each of 4 goblets or bowls.
Garnish with thin apple slices and mint sprigs.
Serves 4.
For breakfast, brunch or dessert.

Prepare cake according to package directions and bake in greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Remove cake from oven and poke holes over surface with wooden spoon handle. Combine condensed milk and caramel topping; pour over hot cake. Cool and refrigerate several hours. Stir crushed candy bars into whipped topping and spread over cake. Store in refrigerator. Serves 10 to 12.

In a large pot, bring 5 quarts of water to a boil. Add salt and cook pasta according to package instructions. On low flame in a large skillet, add butter. Bring to simmer but not burn. Remove skillet from flame while adding vodka, then return to flame. Let vodka evaporate, 1 to 2 minutes, then add Ragu sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook until sauce is heated through. Drain pasta. Pour into skillet with sauce and mix until pasta is well coated. Serves 4 to 6.
Mix first five ingredients well.
Separate rolls.
Spread rolls with butter and add about 1 tablespoon salmon mixture.
Roll up, starting with wide end.
Place on ungreased baking sheet. Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve hot with Cheese Sauce.
Grease a 10 3/4 x 7 x 1 1/2-inch pan.
Add liquids to dry ingredients; blend in corn.
Add cheese.
Sprinkle cheese on top and add chili powder, also.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Saute the onions, celery and green peppers.
Add to the fried hamburgers.
Add 2 cups sliced cabbage.
Simmer a few minutes.
Beat sugar and butter until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Mix in sifted flour.
Add 7-Up and orange juice. Add flavoring last.
Melt butter in skillet; add finely diced onions and turkey cutlets.
Brown cutlets on both sides and remove.
Add sherry and let thicken, stirring constantly.
Slice mushrooms and add.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Add heavy cream as a final.
Serve over turkey cutlets.
Mix brown sugar, margarine, vanilla and egg yolk with fork in ungreased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Stir in baking
mix until moistened, mix will be crumbly.
Press mixture evenly in pan.
Bake until light and brown, about 16 to 18 minutes.
Immediately sprinkle chocolate chips over top.
Let stand until chips are softened. Spread evenly over top.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Cut into bars.

recipes.t: Mrs. M. L. Mahone'S Eggplant Casserole
d: Pour sauce over eggplant; put into 350° oven and cook until cheese melts well.
Cook in pan of water.
Dredge chicken with flour; shake off.
Heat oil and butter; saute onions and mushrooms 5 to 7 minutes until soft.
Remove with slotted spoon.
Brown meat on both sides and remove.
Add wine to deglaze, then broth.
Return meat and vegetables.
Cover and simmer 35 to 40 minutes.
Serve with sauce.
Place syrup, sugar, margarine, salt and water in two-quart pot.
Cook over low to medium heat to 300° (hard crack stage). Stir in nuts, add baking soda in hot water to hot syrup and stir well.
Pour hot syrup and nuts over popped corn in large greased pan.
Mix syrup and corn rapidly.
Spread thinly on cookie sheets or wax paper and let cool.
Store in closed container.
Wash clams; place in Dutch oven with 1/4 cup of wine and steam until clams open.
When opened, place clams and their juice in bowl and set aside.
Place oil and garlic in Dutch oven and cook garlic until brown.
Add all other ingredients except linguini and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add clams and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes. Cook linguini and serve with clam sauce.
Soften cream cheese in microwave on High 15 or 20 seconds. Beat cream cheese, milk and sugar in bowl with whisk.
Stir in lemon juice and 1 1/2 cups whipped topping.
Spread in bottom over crust.
Press strawberries into cream cheese.
Pour 2 cups milk into bowl; add pudding and mix with whisk.
Let stand 1 minute or until thick.
Add 1 cup whipped topping and spoon over strawberries.
Garnish with a few strawberries.
Refrigerate 4 hours.
Makes 8 servings.
Grind whole cranberries in the blender.
Pour in a bowl.
Add sugar and let set 1 hour.
Cream together butter
and
sugar.
Add eggs.
Sift dry ingredients.
Mix tomato sauce and water.
Add dry ingredients to butter mixture
alternately
with
tomato sauce.
Pour into greased pan; bake for 45 minutes in a 350° oven.
Mix jello and boiling water together.
Let cool some.
Add carrots and pineapple.
Put in mold or large bowl and refrigerate until congealed.
Add 1/4 cup caramel topping to a large coffee cup. Finish filling with fresh coffee.
Add creamer to taste. Top with Reddi-Wip and a sprinkle of cinnamon. Yum!
Combine sugar and syrup in large pan; heat until sugar dissolves.
Stir in peanut butter and margarine.
Mix well until melted.
Add cereals and peanuts.
Mix well.
Press into large cake pan.
Cool and cut into serving pieces.
Rub pan with 1/2 clove garlic.
Melt butter; stir in flour until blended.
Stir in bouillon and water; boil, stirring constantly.
Season to taste.
Put soy sauce in bowl.
Dip pieces of steak in soy sauce, then roll in flour.
Brown steak in oil over medium heat.
Add green pepper and saute a few minutes.
Add water and mushrooms.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serve with rice.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In medium-size bowl, mix eggs and potatoes together and set aside.
Spray bottom of an 8 x 8-inch pan with Pam.
Place chicken in single layer; add veggies and onions on top of chicken.
Take potato mixture and drop by spoonfuls on top of that.
Sprinkle bread crumbs over all.
Bake for 30 minutes, until top browns.
Very good low-cholesterol recipe.
Mix peanut butter, corn syrup, milk and sugar.
Add raisins and mix well.
Chill candy mixture.
Divide into 24 pieces, forming each into a small log.
Wrap individually in clear plastic wrap.
Keep refrigerated.
Combine apples with sugar and cinnamon.
In casserole dish, combine boiled noodles with apple mixture.
Dot with butter on top.
(Optional:
We usually add cooked, sliced sausage to mixture or you can serve sausage as a side dish.)
Cover and bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Shape beef into 4 (1/2-inch thick) patties.
Place patties on grill over medium coals.
Grill seven to nine minutes for medium, turning patties once during cooking.
Season with salt and pepper as desired.
Combine first 6 ingredients.
Beat egg whites until stiff. Add to first ingredients until mixed.
Then spread between 2 vanilla wafers until all used.
Place on trays.
Put trays in freezer until cookies are frozen.
Mix dry ingredients.
Mix milk, apple juice concentrate, egg whites and oil.
Add this mixture to dry ingredients.
Add chopped apple, raisins, nuts and mix all together. Line muffin tins with paper baking cups. Fill with batter.
Bake at 425° for 17 minutes.
After cooling, may store in plastic bag to retain moisture (in refrigerator).
Soften gelatin in lemon juice.
Add sugar, salt and boiling water.
Stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Let cool.
Whip milk until stiff.
Fold or beat in mayonnaise; add gelatin mixture. Stir in remaining ingredients.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Roll bread dough into 15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch rectangle.
Place in jelly roll pan.
With fingertips, firmly press into dough at 1-inch intervals.
Arrange tomato slices, fresh sage leaves and onion wedges on top of bread dough. Sprinkle with oil over vegetables.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until browned and crisp.
Cook broccoli as directed on package, drain.
Blend baking mix, milk, eggs, salt and onion with mixer until smooth.
Stir in broccoli and cheese.
Pour into greased 1 1/2 quart baking dish. Bake at 325 until knife inserted halfway between center and edge comes out clean, about an hour.
Finished dish resembles a souffle.
Dice approximately 1 pint of strawberries.
Crush cookies and sift through strainer.
Re-crush leftovers and sift until all cookies sift.
Mix pudding and Cool Whip; add diced strawberries. Mix well.
Pour mix into pie crust.
Spoon cookie crumbs over top and even out with fork.
Garnish with remaining strawberries and freeze.
Peel bananas and cut in pieces, roll in well beaten egg and flour them in bread crumbs.
Fry in hot shortening until golden brown.
Combine popcorn and chow mein noodles in a large bowl.
Place butterscotch morsels in a glass bowl.
Microwave on Medium (50%) for 5 minutes or until melted, stirring midway.
Pour over popcorn-noodle mixture.
Stir to coat well.
Drop by heaping tablespoonsful on wax paper until firm.
Store in tightly covered container.
Makes 24.
In a 3 quart saucepan, brown turkey.
Drain off any fat.
Stir in vegetables, soup, milk and thyme.
Bring to boil; reduce heat. Simmer 5 minutes.
Spoon into 8-inch round baking dish.
Unfold crust; cut decorative cutouts or slits in crust so steam can escape.
Place crust on top of dish.
Turn edge under; flute. Combine egg white and water; brush over crust.
Sprinkle sesame seed on top.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden. Let stand 5 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Thaw pastry 20 minutes.
On a floured surface, roll to a 15-inch circle.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Slice Brie in half horizontally and layer with almonds and parsley.
Reassemble and place in center of pastry.
Brush pastry edges with egg wash and pull up sides to enclose Brie.
Place seam side down on ungreased baking sheet.
If desired, decorate top with pastry scraps.
Brush with egg wash.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Makes 12 servings.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Cook and drain spinach. Combine spinach, sour cream, garlic, and 1/2 stick melted butter. Add artichokes and combine.
Melt the other 1/2 stick of butter and mix with the stuffing.
Place spinach mixture in the casserole dish and top with stuffing mixture.
Bake in preheated oven 30 minutes.
Drain clams into measuring cup.
Add boiling water to equal three cups.
In large pan, place potatoes, sauce mix and liquid. Heat to boiling.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in clams, milk and margarine and heat through.
Melt chocolate in a double boiler.
When melted add sugar, milk and cornstarch which have already been blended with water.
Remove from double boiler and place on direct heat, medium-high.
Cook until thick.
Remove from heat and add butter and vanilla.
Stir. Enjoy!
Combine water, potatoes, onion and garlic in large pot.
Cook on high heat for 15 minutes.
Lower heat.
Add cabbage, tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Cook 10 minutes.
Add catfish.
Cook 15 minutes. Remove from heat.
Serve over rice.
Makes 6 servings.
Set aside 2/3 cup of the pineapple juice.
Add remaining pineapple juice to unsweetened
orange juice to equal 1 cup.
In medium saucepan, combine the sugar, flour and pineapple/orange juice. Bring mixture to a boil, then stir for 1 minute or until mixture reaches pudding consistency.
Remove from heat, then fold in drained, crushed pineapple.
Heat Broiler.
Melt 1/4 cup unsalted butter in 5 quart saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add 4 large white onions, halved and thinly sliced; stir to coat with butter.
Cover and cook 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 tsp. sugar, cook uncovered stirring onions until slightly golden, about 6 minutes.
Add 1 Tbsp. flour, cook 1 minute longer.
Stir in 3 cans condensed Beef Broth, 1 can of water and 1/4 cup red wine, cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Arrange chicken in baking dish and sprinkle with curry powder. Spoon thawed orange juice and soy sauce over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes and serve with rice.
(For a special treat, cook rice with chicken broth, saffron, cardamon and white raisins.)
Cook chicken.
Pick from bones.
In the broth, add the egg noodles, salt and pepper to taste and cream of mushroom.
Cook on top of stove.
When done, cover with cheese.
Melt the margarine and cream cheese in microwave while cooking corn according to directions on bag. Drain corn and stir margarine mixture into corn.
Add sugar.
Put in crock-pot and cook for 4 hours.
You can let this simmer on top of the stove if you prefer.
Line aluminum foil on your cookie sheet.
Work the almond paste with your hands.
Then add sugar and egg whites.
Constantly knead.
Now add flour and powdered sugar.
Now add fruit.
Place 1/2 teaspoon of mix on the lined aluminum foil cookie sheet until all the mix is used.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Next day bake at 300° 25 to 30 minutes.
Decorate each cookie with a bright red cherry or green citron.
Brown meat.
Add water to roast in crock-pot.
Add onion and green pepper.
Cook 4 to 5 hours on high or 8 hours on low.
When cooked, shred meat and add seasonings to broth.
Serve on hoagie buns.
Use broth for dipping.
Flake crabmeat and cut shrimp into small pieces.
Mix crabmeat, shrimp and cream cheese together; spread into shallow pie plate.
Top with cocktail sauce to taste.
Mix cereal, pretzels and peanuts in a large roasting pan. Combine butter and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over.
Cover; bake in a 225° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Cut apples into small wedges and add a small amount of lemon juice to prevent browning.
Set aside and chill.
Cook fresh asparagus until crisp and drain water.
Chop when cool into 1-inch pieces.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Mix flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Add gradually, alternating with buttermilk.
Add vanilla and mix well.
Pour into well-greased tube pan and bake at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.t: Escalloped Sweet Potato And Apple Casserole
d: Scrub potatoes well.
Peel and slice.
Core and slice apples. Arrange potatoes and apples in alternate layers in buttered casserole dish, sprinkling each layer of potatoes with salt and each layer of apples with brown sugar.
Dot with butter.
Cover and bake at 375° until both potatoes and apples are very tender and flavors are well blended (about 45 minutes).
Combine fruit juices.
Pour over ice cubes or ice ring, adding ginger ale just before serving.
Serves 50 to 60.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Add mint, poppy seed and orange peel.
Mix well.
Stir dressing into rice.
Cover and chill several hours.
To serve, stir in fruits.
Makes 2 servings.
Cream together the butter, sugar and vanilla. Add the eggs, one at a time.
Sift together the flour, salt and soda. Add to the creamed mixture.
Stir in pecans and chopped dates.
Cover with wax paper and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Drop by tablespoons about 2-inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet. Bake 10 minutes at 375°.
Remove immediately from the baking sheet and cool on wire racks.
Makes 8 dozen.
Combine 1/2 cup of sugar, gelatin and half of the cream.
Stir over low heat until gelatin dissolves.
Stir a small amount of hot mixture into egg; mix well.
Return to remaining mixture.
Cook and stir until thick, about 1 minute.
Chill.
Add remaining cream, vanilla, almond extract and salt.
Combine peaches and 3/4 cup of sugar.
Add to chilled mixture.
Freeze in ice cream freezer.
Combine chicken and salt in a Dutch oven; add enough water to cover chicken.
Bring to a boil.
Cover; reduce heat and simmer 1 hour or until tender.
Remove chicken and cool slightly.
(Reserve broth for other uses.)
Bone chicken and chop.
Cook broccoli according to package; drain well.
Arrange broccoli in a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Combine soup with next 5 ingredients.
Spoon 1/2 sauce over broccoli.
Place chicken over this and pour remaining sauce over.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and paprika.
Bake 5 more minutes. Serves 8.
Cook pasta al dente in boiling water.
Drain.
Mix with half of the mayonnaise.
Add tuna, onion, olives and tomatoes.
Fold in remaining mayonnaise and season to taste with pepper and Season-All. Refrigerate, covered, at least 1 hour.
Serves 12.
Cut eggplant
into
8 parts lengthwise and fry in olive oil until brown
and
tender,
about 10 minutes for each part. Place tomato
sauce in casserole.
Add eggplant; sprinkle well with cheese.
Dot with butter and bake in moderate oven (375°) 15 minutes.
Serves 4.
Chill all ingredients for 1 hour.
Pour in soda and champagne last, then add ice.
Add cherries, lemons and orange slices for decorations.
Brown hamburger with onion and garlic.
Add salt and pepper. Add tomatoes, beans, tomato juice and chili powder.
Bring to boil, then simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Enjoy!

recipes.t: Cantonese Chicken In Black Bean Garlic Sauce
d: Combine black bean garlic sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and set aside. Heat oil in skillet over medium heat and saute garlic until light brown, about 2 minutes. Stir in red and green peppers, white onions and green onions. Cook until white onions start to turn translucent, 1 minute. Add chicken and cook until no longer pink, stirring occasionally, about 3 to 4 minutes. Add black bean garlic sauce mixture and pepper and mix well. Cook until chicken is cooked through, about 3 to 4 minutes more. Garnish with chopped green onions. Serves 3 to 4.
Put mustard on pieces of steak; salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with garlic powder.
Put slice of bread on steak and roll up; secure with toothpicks.
Brown and then add a little water and cook slowly for about 30 minutes.
Good served with a vegetable and salad.
In a large skillet (Teflon works best) saute onion, carrot and bell pepper until tender.
Add rice and heat thoroughly.
Stir in eggs and meat and fry on medium-high heat for a few minutes.
Add soy sauce and black pepper to taste.

Cream together the shortening, butter, peanut butter and sugars. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Combine flour, soda, baking powder and salt. Stir in creamed mixture and mix well. Shape the soft dough into balls.
Place on cookie sheet and flatten with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Soak dates in hot water, mixed with soda, until most of water is absorbed.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Add date mixture and mix well.
Add mayonnaise, vanilla and nuts.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake 35 minutes at 325°.

Combine the lemon juice, olive oil and seasonings in a bowl. Marinate the fish in this mixture for at least 1 hour or as long as 6 hours (if thin fillets are used, no longer than 1 hour). Place the fish, skin side down, in a baking dish.
Pour the marinade around the fillets and add enough water to cover 3/4 of the fish.
Broil the fish until it flakes easily with a fork.
Combine graham crackers, butter and sugar.
Press into bottom and sides of spring-form pan.
Combine whipped topping, pudding and sour cream in bowl.
Pour half of the filling over crust.
Slice bananas and layer on top.
Pour remaining filling over bananas. Finely chop pecans and sprinkle over top.
Refrigerate to chill.
Mix dill seed, celery seed, onion salt, garlic salt, onion flakes, parsley flakes, sour cream and mayonnaise together. Chill overnight.
Cut center out of rye bread and fill with dill dip.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease a 9x13 glass pan and set aside.
Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spices together.
Blend thoroughly and set aside.
Cream butter; gradually add the sugars, creaming until fluffy.
Add the beaten eggs in halves, beating thoroughly after each one.
Add 1/3 dry ingredients and 1/3 of the buttermilk, mix thoroughly and repeat until each is gone.
Spread evenly in pan.
Bake for 55 - 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted into center comes out clean. Try topping with a cream cheese icing or enjoy this treat just as it is.
Layer asparagus, cheese and chips; repeat layers.
Cook at 350° until light brown.
Cream together sugar and margarine.
Add eggs to creamed mixture.
Stir in flour, baking powder and salt.
Add melted chocolate and nuts.
Grease bottom of 8 x 8-inch pan.
Pour batter into pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
When cool, sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Place bacon in 1-quart casserole.
Cover and cook 5 to 6 minutes or until crisp.
Remove bacon and crumble.
Reserve 1 tablespoon of bacon drippings.
Add green pepper to bacon drippings and cook 1 minute or until pepper is tender.
Combine eggs and soup.
Pour into casserole with green pepper.
Cook, covered, on 70% power for 5 1/2 to 6 1/2 minutes.
Stir twice during cooking time.
Sprinkle crumbled bacon and cheese over top. Season with salt and pepper as desired.
In a skillet, brown chicken breasts and onions until brown. Prepare brown gravy mix by package directions.
Transfer to crock-pot; then add celery and mushrooms.
Cook in crock-pot on low (6 to 7 hours) or high (4 to 5 hours) or until chicken shreds easily with a fork.
Serve with rice.
Brown meat with onion, salt and bell pepper; drain.
Add tomatoes, tomatoes with green chilies, soup, cabbage and 1 soup can of water.
Cook slowly for 1 hour.
Stir brownie mix, water, oil and eggs until well blended. Spread in 9x13 pan and bake at 350°F oven for 28-30 minutes.
Cool about one hour.
Boil 4 cups water and 4 cups sugar until dissolved.
In large container, put strawberry and mixed fruit jello.
Add 9 cups cold water; mix.
Pour into hot sugar water.
Add lemon juice and pineapple juice.
Pour into 16 ounce containers and freeze.
When ready to use, take out of freezer and let thaw until you can break it up with spoon.
Put in punch bowl.
Add 7-Up.
Serves 100.
Mix orange juice, Hi-C, lemonade and 2 lemonade cans of water. Chill thoroughly.
Add ginger ale when ready to serve.
Add sherbet. Stir lightly and serve.
Makes 20 servings.
Beat egg yolks until fluffy.
Add 1 cup sugar gradually.
Beat until smooth.
Blend in lime and lemon juice, grated peel and salt. Stir over low heat until it thickens.
Soak gelatin in rum and stir into hot custard until it is dissolved.
Cool.
Beat egg whites until foamy; add 1 cup sugar gradually.
Beat until stiff.
Whip the cream until stiff.
Fold egg whites into custard, then fold in whipped cream.
Pour into pan and chill.
Can be served refrigerated or frozen.
Serve with strawberries.
Spread the anchovy paste and cheese on the pecan half.
Top with another pecan half to make a tiny "sandwich."
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add other ingredients and chill. Add 1 quart cold ginger ale at serving time.
Makes 1 gallon.
Fold drained bread into eggs and cook until soft set.
Fold into greased 8 x 8-inch baking dish and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cover with Swiss cheese slices and sprinkle with bacon. Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Can be made the day before. Doubling the recipe fills 9 x 13-inch pan.

In a mixing bowl, beat egg yolks until slightly thickened. Gradually add 3/4 cup sugar, beating until thick and lemon colored. Beat in vanilla. Combine the flour, cinnamon and salt. Add to batter and beat until smooth. In another mixing bowl, beat egg whites on medium speed until soft peaks form. Add remaining sugar 1 tablespoon at a time, beating on high until stiff peaks form. Fold 1/4 of the egg whites into batter. Fold in remaining egg whites. Fold in nuts. Spoon into a greased 10-inch tube pan. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until cake
springs back. Cool. Run knife around cake. Remove from pan.
Stir can of cranberry sauce in a large bowl.
Peel orange and remove all white pith you can.
Cut orange into small sections. Add to cranberry sauce.
Add raisins and nuts to the mix.
Pour into a pretty bowl and chill at least one hour.
Keeps in the refrigerator 2 weeks to 1 month.
I freeze leftovers from holiday to holiday.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Drain liquid off beans, peas and corn.
Mix all ingredients except oil, vinegar and sugar.
Mix sugar, vinegar and oil.
Heat to dissolve sugar.
When this has cooled, add Wesson oil and pour over mixture and other ingredients.
Place in refrigerator for 24 hours.
Drain off liquid and serve.
Preheat
oven
to
Line 10-inch pie pan with pie crust. Mix
apples
and cranberries and put half of the fruit in
the bottom
of the pie crust.
Mix water, apple juice and lemon juice. Drizzle half of the liquids over the mixed fruit in the pie crust.
Mix cornstarch, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon and apple
pie spice.
Sprinkle half of this dry mixture over the fruit
in the pie crust.
Repeat layers of mixed fruit, liquid and
dry mixtures.
Cube butter and distribute across the top. Put top crust in place;
crimp edges and using a fork or knife tip,
make multiple
punctures
in
the top to allow steam to escape.
Bake in 425° oven for 10 minutes; lower heat to 350° and
bake
for
50 additional
minutes.
Allow to cool before serving.
Makes 1 pie.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Drop from a teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes. Cut gumdrops in eight, omit licorice ones.
As you cut up gumdrops, mix with part of cake mix to prevent clumping together.
Pour pie filling into baking dish.
Crumble cake mix over filling.
Put finely crushed nuts over mixture and add melted margarine over top. Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Crumble bread into a glass baking dish. Whip eggs.
Layer on top of bread.
Brown sausage.
Sprinkle on eggs (add mushrooms now); then sprinkle top with cheese.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until brown.
Serve hot.
In heavy skillet on medium heat, melt butter.
Stir in cream and cheese until smooth.
Stir in nuts.
Cook and stir constantly for about 15 minutes, until it becomes a thick mass with a fine consistency.
Stir in dry milk, working it into the mixture.
Cook and stir another 15 minutes (should be well thickened by now). Stir in sugar until well absorbed.
Cook and stir 5 minutes more. Spread in 9 x 13-inch pan to 1/2-inch thickness.
Smooth out; let set.
Cool to fudge consistency.
Cut into squares.
Refrigerate to store.
Unroll dinner rolls.
Cut each one in half to form a triangle. Spread a little mustard on each triangle.
Add a small amount of ham and cheese near the longest side of each triangle.
Roll up and place, seam side down, on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serves 16.
In saucepan, cook dates, pineapple, sugar, eggs and butter until thick.
Remove from heat and add nuts.
Allow to cool. Spread mixture on a vanilla wafer, top with another wafer; roll in powdered sugar.
Store in airtight container.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Place potatoes in a saucepan and cover with water; cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes or until tender.
Drain and mash.
Add sour cream, butter, salt and pepper; beat until smooth and fluffy. Transfer to a greased 2-1/2 quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with cheese, bacon and chives if desired.
Bake, uncovered for 20 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted.
Yield:
8 to 10 servings.
Dice bell peppers, onions, parsley and 1 pound mushrooms. Saute vegetables in 1/2 of butter until transparent.
In a separate pan, saute mushrooms with other 1/2 of butter until almost done.
Add to vegetables.
Add cream.
Cook approximately 5 minutes.
Add crabmeat, bread crumbs and cheese until firm.
(Add more bread crumbs slowly if necessary.)
Salt and pepper to taste. Using mushrooms with stems, cut a tiny piece of top off mushrooms to let stand.
Cut a small piece of stem off.
Wipe mushrooms (do not wash).
Let stuffing cool for 10 to 15 minutes.
Form stuffing into small ball and stuff on stem of mushroom.
Place in baking dish.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes until warm.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add fruit juice.
Chop fruit and nuts into a mixing bowl.
Add crushed pineapple to jello mixture and semi-congeal with a lump of ice.
Mix cream cheese with mayonnaise to a smooth paste.
Add mayonnaise mixture to jello and stir well.
Oil salad molds with salad oil and line with whole grapes.
Whip cream and fold into the salad mixture.
Fill molds and congeal.
Serves 8.
Boil first 3 ingredients on medium-high heat for 5 minutes. Then add baking soda.
Mix in well.
Pour over popcorn.
Bake at 225° for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Melt margarine; add cut onion and saute.
Add ketchup.
Add kielbasa.
Stir in other ingredients and simmer 45 minutes.
This can be made in a crock-pot.
The longer you simmer it the better the flavor.
Heat sugar, water and salt. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Cool.
Mix cranberry juice, lemonade, orange juice, apple juice and pineapple juice; add sugar mixture. Add desired amount of food coloring. Chill for 1 hour.
Add ginger ale before serving. Serve with ice.
Prepare 4 to 6 meat patties.
In a large iron skillet, cook the meat patties for about 15 minutes.
Peel and quarter potatoes and onions.
Dice the bell pepper.
Combine the pepper, onions and potatoes in microwave-safe dish.
Cook on High in microwave for 7 to 8 minutes.
Pour off almost all of the grease in meat.
Add potatoes, onions and bell pepper to meat patties.
Cover and cook all together for about 10 minutes.
Uncover, then brown for about 2 to 3 minutes.
Cook potatoes in pan of water 13 minutes.
Add carrots.
Cook 5 minutes.
Add yellow squash.
Cook 2 minutes.
Add peas.
Cook 2 minutes.
Drain and put in dish.
Add melted butter or margarine. Sprinkle with scallions and parsley, cut up.
Serves 8.
Looks beautiful when served.
In a large bowl, combine the shrimp, lemon juice, lime juice, celery, onion, dill, mayonnaise, and pepper.
Mix well and refrigerate until chilled.
Cook carrots and green beans until tender and drain.
Place in 2-quart casserole.
In skillet, melt margarine.
Add onions, basil, garlic salt, pepper and mushrooms; saute until onion is tender.
Spoon onion mixture over carrots and green beans; top with tomato wedges.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Serves 12.
Combine ham, beef, pork, bread crumbs, egg and tomato puree. Form into a loaf pan.
Steam for 1 hour and bake in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Serve with tomato sauce or grilled pineapple slices. Makes 16 portions.

recipes.t: Buttermilk Pie In Corn Flour Crust
d: Sift cornmeal and flour together.
Cut in shortening.
Add cheese. Finish as any other pie crust.
Cook carrots and onion in butter until tender; combine with rice and flour.
Blend soup, egg and seasonings; add to rice mixture.
Turn into greased 8-inch ring mold.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) for 30 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before inverting on serving platter.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine sausage, flour, cheese, shortening and milk in bowl, mixing well.
Shape into long rolls.
Cut into slices. Place slices on baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes or until done.
Yields 24 servings.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add slightly beaten egg yolks and blend well.
Add crushed pineapple, juice also.
Sift baking powder with flour and add to mixture.
Add one-half of the coconut and the vanilla.
Fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Pour batter into two buttered cake pans.
Sprinkle the other half cup of coconut over the two layers.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Allow to cool and frost with your favorite frosting.
Soak apricots in sherry for 1 hour.
Drain and discard sherry. Sift flour, baking powder and baking soda twice.
Set aside.
Cream butter, lemon rind and sugar together.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Beat well after each addition.
Fold in fruits alternately with flour mixture.
Place mixture into a greased and lined 4 x 8-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until cooked.
Cool on wire rack.
Ice, if desired, with icing of your choice.
Makes 1 loaf.
Blend cream cheese with milk until smooth.
Stir in olives, nuts, pimento and pepper.
Cover bowl; chill 1 to 2 hours to blend flavors.
Serve as dip for potato chips, etc.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups.

recipes.t: Robert Redford'S Whole Wheat Quick Bread
d: Combine egg with buttermilk, molasses or honey and melted butter.
Mix together whole wheat flour, baking soda, salt and baking powder.
Stir into wet mixture.
Stir in walnuts and raisins.
Spoon into 2 small, greased loaf pans or 1 large one. Bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Slice white portion of leeks into 1/4-inch slices.
Separate rings (they'll look like mini-onion rings).
Mix flour, Bisquick, seasoned salt and cayenne pepper together in a bowl.
Pour half of a bottle of beer (or so) into another bowl.
Dip out 10 leek rings at a time into the beer, then into the flour mixture.
Shake off excess flour.
Fry rings in peanut oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Serve hot.
Melt the butter in a heavy 3-quart saucepan over moderate heat.
Add the onion, and cook, uncovered, for 5 minutes, or until soft.
Stir in the rice, green pepper, chili powder, oregano, tomato juice and tomato sauce; then add the water and salt.
Stir once; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook broccoli in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Cut rice according to directions; set aside.
Saute onions in butter, using large saucepan.
Add the can of Cheddar cheese soup and stir.
Cut other cheese in and add to soup mixture; mix until all is melted.
Add mushrooms, juice and all.
Drain broccoli.
Add it with rice to the mixture and mix well.
Pour into baking dish.
Place onion rings on top or mix them in the mixture.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes or longer.
Mix and bake the cake mix according to directions on box. Use a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cool.
Mix the pudding, milk and cream cheese.
Spread on cooled cake.
Spread 1 large can of drained pineapple over pudding mixture.
Spread cool whip over pineapple. Sprinkle coconut on top of cool whip.
Keep refrigerated.
Boil chicken and debone.
Spray a long deep baking dish (use a nonstick spray).
Break chicken up into pieces.
Place chicken pieces along with crescent rolls.
Add strips of thinly sliced cheese and roll one at a time.
Place in a baking dish.
Heat only to mix
soup and milk.
Pour over rolls and bake 25 minutes at 350° or until slightly browned.
Serves 8 to 10.
Melt margarine and cheese in saucepan over low heat, stirring frequently.
Combine confectioners sugar and cocoa together.
Add to cheese mixture, stirring to blend.
Add vanilla and pecans; mix well.
Pour into a 10 x 14-inch glass dish.
Chill in refrigerator. Cut into 25 squares to serve.
In skillet, heat deer or beef; let boil for 15 minutes.
May need to add water 1/2 cup to 1 cup.
Use enough liquid to keep from boiling dry but don't make it too soupy because the frozen vegetables will have their own liquid.
Add 4 or 5 shakes of Worcestershire sauce.
Turn down heat to low; add vegetables. Cook until vegetables are cooked yet still slightly crunchy. Serve over rice with soy sauce.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease and flour a loaf pan.
Beat oil and sugar.
Add eggs and banana; beat well.
Sift dry ingredients and add them to creamed mixture.
Add sour cream and juice; mix well.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into pan.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Snap ends off beans and break into 1/2-inch lengths.
If very young, leave whole.
Wash and place in pan.
Sprinkle onion, garlic, salt and pepper over beans.
Add water.
Cover tightly and cook on high until steaming; reduce heat and cook about 20 minutes until beans are crisp-tender.
Pour off excess liquid.
Sprinkle sunflower seeds and oregano over beans.
Mix lightly.
Pour roasted peanuts into a blender; add peanut oil and salt. Blend until mixture becomes spreadable.
In a large skillet, saute onions in 2 Tablespoons butter until tender.
Sprinkle with flour;
stir in salt and pepper.
Add the consome and sherry;
cook and stir until thickened, about 3 minutes.
Pour into a shallow 2-quart baking dish or individual baking dishes.
Spread remaining butter on both sides of bread; place on a baking sheet.
Bake at 350°F. for 10 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Place bread on top on onion mixture; sprinkle with cheeses.
Bake , uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Mix nuts, sugar and cinnamon together.
Melt butter.
Butter a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Place six buttered sheets in pan.
Sprinkle generously with walnut mixture.
Add three more buttered filo sheets.
Sprinkle with nut mixture.
Continue alternating buttered filo with nut mixture until nut mixture is used.
Top layer of filo should have 6 to 7 sheets.
Pour melted butter over assembled Baklava and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until golden brown.
Cream oleo and sugar together.
Mix in other ingredients. Pour into cake pans.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours at 300°, until done.
Saute onion. Add rice and lightly saute.
Add water, bouillon cubes, garlic and stewed tomatoes. Cook until tender and thickened.
Yummy.

recipes.t: Grandpa Vinnie'S Egg Drops For Soup
d: Have broth from chicken boiling.
Beat 1 egg.
Add salt.
Add water and stir to make a smooth paste.
Add flour and mix.
Take a real thin sliver off of spoon and drop into boiling broth.
It will come to top.
Cook just a little longer and serve.
If I don't have enough mix and if there is a lot of broth, I mix up another batch.
Brown ground beef; drain fat.
Add onion and garlic.
Drain tomatoes into 1-quart measure.
Chop tomatoes and add to tomato liquid.
Add enough water to make 2 1/4 cups liquid.
Combine tomato mixture, rice, A.1. steak sauce, green pepper, salt and celery in skillet.
Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes or until rice is tender.
Mix flour, butter, oil, mahlab, cinnamon, salt, anise seed and baking powder.
Add enough milk to blend together well.
Knead for several minutes until dough is soft and elastic.
Make dough into walnut size balls.
Roll dough into circles.
Place about a teaspoon of filling (ground walnuts, sugar and mahlab) into each circle.
Fold over the half moon shape and seal the edge by pressing with a fork.
Place on a cookie sheet about 1/4 inch apart and bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes until light brown and let cool.
Dip in syrup and drain in colander.
This can also be prepared by sprinkling hot sumboosic with confectioners sugar.
Blend 1/3 cup sugar, cornstarch, crushed pineapple.
Cook stirring constantly until thick.
Cool.
Blend cream cheese, 1 1/2 cups sugar, salt and eggs, one at a time.
Add milk and vanilla. Place cooled pineapple mixture in unbaked pie crust.
Pour cream cheese mixture over it.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 400°
for 10 minutes; reduce heat to 325° for 50 minutes.
Grease and flour large Bundt or angel food cake pan.
Cream butter and sugar together.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add lemon extract.
Mix baking powder and flour together.
Add flour a little at a time to creamed mixture, until well blended.
Fold in other ingredients.
Bake in 275° to 300° oven for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Dissolve the gelatin in hot water.
Beat together the soup, mayonnaise and cream cheese.
Add the gelatin water.
Stir in the remaining ingredients and pour into one large or two small molds. Refrigerate overnight.
Serve with crackers or cut up vegetables.
If turkey is frozen, soak in cold water overnight in cool place.
Take out of water; let drain about 30 minutes.
Rub 3 sticks of butter over turkey inside and out and salt.
Place apples inside turkey.
Line roaster pan 2 ways with tinfoil to seal turkey tightly.
Place turkey and 4 quarts water in roaster.
Seal and bake 5 hours at 350°.
Mix eggs, sage, bread and onions.
Add broth from turkey to moisten.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes, until soft crust forms on top.
Brown meat with onion, pepper and garlic.
Drain off the fat. Add in beans, water, sauce, bouillon and garlic powder.
Bring to boil.
Stir in the rice; remove from heat and cover.
Let stand at least 5 minutes, then stir again.
It's ready when all liquid is absorbed.
Saute shrimp in garlic and butter on high heat just enough to brown on both sides.
Take from skillet and saute red pepper and onion until translucent.
Pour in tomatoes and sliced squash and zucchini and cook vegetables until crisp.
Add shrimp long enough to heat, then add chili powder.
Cook rice as directed.
Serve over rice or rice as side dish.
Really good!
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook macaroni; set aside.
Cook onion, celery and pimento in a little butter until tender.
Add meat, cook until brown; drain. Put macaroni in a casserole dish with tomatoes, add salt and pepper.
Add meat mixture and mix.
Cook at 350° until thick.
Put cheese on top and let it melt.
Serve with Italian bread.
This will get you a big hug.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Follow directions on back of double box of pizza.
Add sliced olives, mushrooms and pepperoni.
Cook the hamburger and sausage.
Add green pepper and onion.
Add banana pepper, finely cut.
Add cheese.
Bake until cheese is brown.
Let cool.
Boil, cut and drain the spinach and add it to the clear soup. Broil the mochi.
Place the mochi and several slices of kamaboko and some spinach into the bottom of bowls.
Pour the clear, hot soup (over all) into each bowl and serve.

In large Dutch oven, make roux with flour and cooking oil. Cook roux until light brown. Add onions, green peppers, celery and garlic. Saute for 5 to 10 minutes until tender. Using a blender, blend tomatoes with green chili peppers until smooth. Add blended mixture, tomato sauce, chicken broth, salt, black pepper and red pepper to Dutch oven. Simmer uncovered for 45 to 60 minutes or until thick. Stir in fish pieces and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes. Season to taste. Serve over rice.
Dissolve gelatin in cold water.
Add boiling water, salt, lemon juice.
Add sugar to peeled and sliced peaches.
Combine whipping cream with cooled gelatin mixture and add peaches.
Fill pie crusts and refrigerate.
Cut cabbage in 6 slices and cook 10 minutes or until tender but crisp.
Pour in buttered 2-quart dish.
Saute onion, green pepper, sugar and butter.
Add tomatoes, salt and pepper. Pour over cabbage and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° until heated through.
Can cut hot dogs and put on top.
Mix ground meat, eggs, and bread crumbs and season.
Shape into balls,
Combine soup, cornstarch, and water
in a large bowl and microwave for 5 minutes.
Add meatballs to gravy and bake in a 350 degree oven for 1-1/2 hours.
Heat 1 cup of drink with candies, stirring constantly for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in sugar and add to rest of drink.
Chill. Combine with ginger ale just before serving.
Cut beef into 1/8-inch strips.
Toss with garlic and orange peel in medium bowl.
Set aside.
Pound cutlets as thin as possible. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat each cutlet first in flour (shaking off excess), then in egg and last in bread crumbs. Cook in 1/4-inch hot oil until golden brown on each side.
Pour off nearly all the fat from the pan. Add sour cream and heat gently, scraping up any brown bits from bottom of pan.
Pour over schnitzels.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; omit salt; drain.
Combine cream cheese, sour cream, cottage cheese, onions and parsley; mix well.
Layer half each of macaroni, cheese mixture and crabmeat in a lightly greased 2-quart baking dish. Repeat procedure and top with tomato slices.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Separate, and clean buds, drop in boiling salted water for 5 minutes, remove from water.
Chop onions and brown in butter.
Add tomato paste to browned onions.
Beat eggs, dip cauliflower in beaten eggs and brown in butter slightly.
Pour tomato paste and onions over cauliflower.
Cover and steam in 350° oven for 20 minutes.
Put cornmeal, drippings, sugar and salt into baking dish. Pour the boiling water over them gradually and beat well.
When the mixture is cool, add the beaten egg, milk, soda and 1 teaspoon cold water. Beat the whole mixture well.
Bake in a deep dish 20 minutes in oven at 350°.
Spread butter evenly over bottom and sides of 9-inch pie pan. Press 1 1/3 cups coconut into butter, forming a shell.
Mix 1 cup coconut, the eggs, sugar, cheese and lemon juice.
Blend until smooth, about 1 1/2 minutes.
Pour into coconut shell.
Sprinkle remaining coconut in a ring around top and in center.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Refrigerate any leftovers.
Mix margarine, brown sugar, vanilla and flour until well blended.
Chill dough for 30 minutes.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes.
Immediately press 1 whole peanut candy into top of each cookie.
Dust lightly with confectioners sugar.
Makes approximately 4 dozen cookies.
Combine flour, sugar and salt.
Blend in shortening until crumbly.
Combine water, vinegar and egg.
Beat lightly with fork. Pour into dry mixture.
Blend until sticky.
Chill 2 hours. Divide into 4 or 5 balls or roll out to fit pie pans.
Wrap securely and refrigerate or freeze.
Mix Jell-O in 2 cups hot water.
Drop in marshmallows, cut in fourths.
Stir until melted.
Let stand until set.
Beat in 1/2 pint whipping cream and the crushed pineapple with mixer.
Stir in nuts.
Let set until firm.
Keep refrigerated.

Slice sausage 1/4-inch thick slices. Brown in 12 or 14-inch skillet on medium heat. Brown both sides of slices approximately 10 to 12 minutes. Mince garlic and stir thoroughly into skillet as sausage browns. Slice pepper into 1/4 x 2-inch slices. Dice onion. When sausage is browned, add pepper and onion. Continue medium heat and stirring, cook 5 minutes. Add kidney beans, tomato sauce, stewed tomatoes and chili powder. Stir thoroughly and continuously approximately 5 minutes. Add and stir in water; reduce heat and let cook down, uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Result should be a nice thick dark brown sauce with sausage, peppers, onions and tomatoes visible. This is a fun one pan easy quick meal that can be adjusted to taste and will fill the kitchen with a wonderful fragrance. Serve with buttered hard rolls and a green salad or for a real treat with buttered sun-dried tomato bread.
Place bacon in 3-quart microproof casserole.
Cover with paper towels.
Cook on High 2 minutes, or until crisp.
Remove bacon; drain, cool and crumble.
Drain all but 1 tablespoon drippings from casserole.
Add onion.
Cover.
Cook on High 1 1/2 minutes, or until onion is transparent.
Stir in vinegar and sugar.
Add spinach; mix lightly.
Cover.
Cook on High 6 to 7 minutes, or until spinach is tender, stirring once during cooking time; stir. Drain.
Sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Serve hot.
Mix flavored jello, 1 tablespoon gelatin and boiling water and let harden in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
In a medium bowl, stir together the 1/2 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa powder and baking powder.

recipes.t: Quick, Easy And Healthy Pasta Sauce
d: Simmer all ingredients together in a pot.
Cook 1 pound of your favorite pasta.
When pasta is done, drain water halfway.
Pour sauce into macaroni.
Mix and serve.
Sprinkle gelatine onto cold milk, let stand 5 minutes.
Melt butter, stir in 1/3 cup sugar and cocoa.
Add gelatin mixture. Blend well, stir in beaten egg yolks.
Blend well.
Heat until mixture is hot, do not boil.
Beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually add 1/3 cup sugar and beat until stiff.
Pour into creme de cacao mixture.
Fold until mixed.
Chill until firm.
Cut sausage into bite size pieces.
Place in a large skillet; add water just to cover sausage.
Let simmer until all water is cooked out, then brown and drain grease.
Add Ro-Tel and 1 cup of water.
Add all other ingredients; let cook until potatoes are tender.
Serve over rice.
Add rice to boiling, salted water; boil 15 minutes, uncovered, stirring occasionally.
Drain water from rice.
In 2-quart casserole, beat eggs.
Add sugar, vanilla, raisins and lemon rind. Add 2 cups milk to drained rice.
Add to egg mixture.
Blend well.
Sprinkle nutmeg and bits of butter over pudding.
Place in deep pan and fill pan almost full of water.
Bake 1/2 hour; stir. Bake 1 more hour or until a silver knife comes out clean.
Cool. Bake at 325°.
Mix the eggs and butter together until smooth and creamy.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, celery seed, parsley, red pepper and salt.
Mix well.
Serves 12.
Sprinkle chicken heavy with paprika, lightly with salt and cayenne pepper.
Place in roaster; spread onions on top.
Add bay leaves.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Stir chicken once during this 45 minutes.
When chicken is browned, add enough water to just cover the chicken. Stir chicken so the paprika is blended into water.
Return to oven to blend flavors, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Blend together sour cream and flour and slowly add broth from chicken.
When blended, slowly add broth in roaster.
Stir to thicken for 15 minutes.
Serve with noodles.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 2 bread pans and flour; cream sugar, eggs, oil and spices.
Add remaining ingredients, except grape skins.
Mix well; fold in grape skins.
Bake 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin completely in boiling water in large bowl. Mix cold water and ice to make 1 3/4 cups.
Add to gelatin, stirring until ice is melted.
Refrigerate 10 minutes or until slightly thickened, if necessary.
Stir in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping and strawberries.
Spoon into 2-quart saucepan (about 3 1/2 inches deep) which has been lined with plastic wrap. Refrigerate 4 hours or until firm.
Invert saucepan onto serving plate; remove plastic wrap.
Spread top and sides of dessert with 1 cup of the whipped topping.
Press cut sides of ladyfingers into sides of dessert. Tie ribbon around dessert. Garnish with remaining whipped topping, strawberry halves and mint leaves. Store leftover dessert in refrigerator.
Makes 12 servings.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat.
Add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.

recipes.t: Moist Chocolate Fudge And Cherry Cake
d: In mixing bowl, add cake mix. Make hole in center. Add eggs and beat, then add cherry pie filling. Mix. Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan in a 375° oven. Bake for 24 to 33 minutes.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise.
Arrange in a shallow baking dish.
Combine orange rind, orange juice, sugar and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Pour over potatoes and bake in a 375° oven for 30 minutes, basting after 15 minutes.
Remove from oven; cover with cranberries and bake 15 minutes more.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.

Combine coconut, walnuts, flour, cinnamon and salt in large bowl. Mix in egg whites and lemon peel. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto lightly greased cookie sheets. Bake at 325° for 20 minutes or until golden brown. Dip macaroon bottoms in melted chocolate. Place on waxed paper to set.
Mix flour, brown sugar and baking soda.
In another bowl mix egg, plain yogurt and oil.
Combine the 2 bowls.
Add chopped apples and chopped dried cranberries.
Put mixture in pan; mix butter, oatmeal, chopped almonds and cinnamon.
Place on top of mixture in pan.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Cook zucchini, corn, pepper, onion and garlic in 10-inch skillet over moderately high heat, stirring constantly, about 2 minutes.
Sprinkle in salt.
Stir in picante sauce and cook, stirring constantly, until most of the liquid has evaporated and vegetables are crisp-tender, about 3 or 4 minutes.
Makes six servings.
Sift together the first 6 ingredients.
Stir in the nuts.
Set aside.
Combine the eggs, milk and cooking oil; add all at once to dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.
Fold in cranberries (chopped) and cereal flakes.
Fill greased muffin pans 2/3 full.
Combine 2 tablespoons sugar and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon; sprinkle atop.
Bake in a 400° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes 18.
Make
in
2 or 3 batches in food processor.
Put 1/2 or 1/3 of the
onion
and jalapeno in processor. With chopping blade, chop
fine.
Add
or 1/3 of the ham, cubed.
Chop fine.
Add 1/3 or 1/2 of the mustard and relish, and about 1/3 to
cup mayonnaise;
blend thoroughly.
Repeat. Then mix batches together, using enough mayonnaise to make spreadable.

In a heavy saucepan, combine sugar, butter, milk, sweet potatoes and spices; bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Continue boiling over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture reaches 228° on candy thermometer, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in butterscotch morsels.
Add Marshmallow Creme, nuts and vanilla, mixing until well blended.
Quickly pour into buttered 13 x 9-inch pan, spreading just until even.
Cool and cut into squares.
Store tightly wrapped in refrigerator.
In bowl, cream sugar and oleo until light and fluffy.
Add 4 eggs, one at a time, then add flour a little at a time.
Add lemon flavoring.
Pour into 15 x 10-inch pan.
Mark off batter into squares.
Place 1 heaping tablespoon of cherry pie filling into center of each square section.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes. While still warm, sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve.
Drain salmon.
Saute zucchini and green onion in 1 tablespoon butter.
Remove from skillet. Melt remaining butter.
Beat eggs, water and dill weed.
Cook omelet, lifting to allow uncooked eggs to flow to bottom.
When golden, spoon on vegetables and salmon. Fold omelet in half.
Slice in 2 pieces.
Serve with sour cream.

Combine cracker crumbs, eggs, onion, worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Add ground beef & mix well. Shape meat mixture into patties. In large skillet, brown patties on both sides. Pour soup over meat; top with beans & green peppers. Cook, covered, over low heat for 10 minutes. Sprinkle cheese over mixture; cover & cook 5 minutes longer. Makes 6 servings.
Put broccoli in casserole.
Saute onion in oleo.
Mix soup, milk and grated cheese.
Blend well.
Pour over broccoli.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 30 minutes.
Place butter inside baked potatoes. Add cut up chicken strips. Mix gravy according to package directions. Pour over chicken. Top with cheese.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, vanilla, flour, baking powder and cocoa; mix well.
Spread in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake 15 to 20 minutes in 350° oven.
Put marshmallows on top of hot bars.
Melt chocolate chips, peanut butter and stir in Rice Krispies.
Put on top of marshmallows.
Chill and cut in squares.
Make Jell-O; let cool for 20 minutes.
Add crushed pineapple and orange slices, drained.
Fold in Cool Whip or mound on top, if preferred.
Brown ground beef with garlic.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Simmer and put in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cover with sour cream and cheese. Top with unrolled (flat) rolls.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 350° until rolls are done.
Wash conch.
Dice into small pieces.
Chop onion and green pepper.
Dice tomatoes.
Mix conch, onion, green pepper and tomatoes.
Pour Old Sour or lime juice over the mixture.
Let sit in refrigerator for an hour or so.
Remove giblets from hens. Wipe hens with damp cloth; tie legs together with string.
Melt butter in Dutch oven over medium heat. Put hens in Dutch oven; brown well on all sides.
Remove hens; keep warm.
Place rice in Dutch oven; cook and stir until lightly browned.
Add mushrooms, salt, bouillon and red wine.
Place hens on top of mixture.
Cover with tightly closed lid.
Lower heat; simmer for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until rice is tender and hens are done.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook macaroni as directed.
Brown meat, onion and green pepper.
Add chili powder, corn, tomato sauce, salt and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes.
Pour mixture over drained macaroni and sprinkle with cheese.
Makes 6 (1 cup) servings.
Pick over crab meat.
Remove crust from bread and break bread into small pieces.
Mix bread with beaten egg.
Add remaining ingredients.
Form into cakes and saute quickly in a small amount of fat.
(Cakes can also be broiled.)
Serves 6 people.
Place raisins and water in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil.
Cover; remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Drain raisins, discarding water.
Combine flour and next 3 ingredients, stirring well.
Set aside.
Combine applesauce and next 3 ingredients in a large bowl.
Add flour mixture to applesauce mixture, stirring until blended; fold in raisins.
Pour batter into a 13 x 9-inch pan coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan on wire rack 10 minutes; remove from pan and let cool completely on wire rack.
Yield:
12 servings.
Melt butter and mix with crushed Ritz crackers.
Mix milk with pudding and beat approximately 2 minutes.
Add softened ice cream and mix.
Press 1/2 of the crackers in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour ice cream mixture on top of crust.
Spread entire tub of Cool Whip on top of ice cream.
Sprinkle rest of cracker crumbs on top and freeze.
Dissolve bouillon in boiling water; save 1/2 cup for later. Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl, except potatoes, 1/2 cup bouillon, cheese and mushrooms.
Pat the meat loaf into a 9-inch skillet to within 1-inch of the edge.
Pour remaining bouillon around the edge.
Place potatoes on meat loaf in a spoke fashion.
Cover with a tight fitting lid or foil and a lid.
Cook on low heat on top of the stove (not in the oven) 40 to 50 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Then arrange the cheese and mushrooms on top of the potatoes; continue cooking until cheese is melted.
Combine potatoes, beaten egg, sugar, margarine, milk and spices.
Beat until smooth.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Remove skin and all visible fat from chicken breasts.
Place in baking dish.
Combine orange juice, lemon juice, curry and salt. Pour over chicken and cover.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Sprinkle with paprika, if desired, and serve with brown rice.
Crush the cookies and add the melted butter.
Dissolve the Jell-O in the hot water.
Add the lemon juice and sugar.
Let stand while whipping the Carnation milk. Add Jell-O to milk.
Add the lemon rind and green coloring. Whip until stiff. Butter dish, putting half of cookies in bottom and half on top.

recipes.t: Charlott Knox Tuttle'S Beef And Kale Soup
d: Simmer beef soup bones, meat and onions to make a broth. Strain.
Remove and discard bones and spent meat.
Add barley to the beef stock and cook for 1 hour.
Add kale to stock and barley and cook 1 more hour.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Rub potatoes with cooking oil; bake in a 350° oven until done, about 1 hour.
Cut the top off each potato and scoop out the contents into a mixing bowl, saving the skins.
Add cheese, butter, milk and salt and pepper to taste.
Mix with electric mixer until well blended.
Pile potato mixture back into the skins and sprinkle with paprika.
Return to oven until browned.
Serves 4.
Bring sugar, butter and milk to a boil.
Boil for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Add remaining ingredients; stir to mix.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper.
Cool until set.
Mix pizza dough and let rise in warm oven.
Brown hamburger and sausage in skillet separately.
Follow directions on pizza mix.
Top pizza with hamburger, sausage and grated cheese.
Cook pizza and enjoy.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Stir in cranberry sauce. Chill until partially set.
Add celery or cauliflower and nuts or bananas.
Pour into a 4-cup mold and chill until firm.
In a 5 to 6-quart pan, stir ground beef over high heat until crumbly, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic; stir until onion is limp, about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium and stir in chili powder, cumin and allspice.
Stir until spices are very fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, green chilies and beans.
Simmer, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thick and beans are hot, 5 to 10 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
(If made ahead, cool, cover and chill until the next day.
Reheat to use.) Slice through each roll, about 1/2 inch from top.
Lift off cut portion and hollow out insides of base to make a shell 1/4 inch thick then pull soft bread from top to make lid about 1/4 inch thick; reserve scraps for another use.
To a quart of canned tomatoes, add extra salt, if needed, a dash of pepper, sugar and Worcestershire sauce. Heat to boiling point. Serve in bowls.
Boil noodles.
Open cans.
Mix in big dish.
Add bacon and cheese.
Heat for 15 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Um, it is good eatin'!!
Cook onion in butter until tender. Blend in soup.
Gradually stir in milk.
In 1 1/2-quart casserole dish, combine sauce and cooked macaroni. Sprinkle crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown and bubbly.
Sift flour and cornstarch, beat butter until creamy.
Add sugar and beat; gradually add flour.
Knead with hand, then pack in pan until it is 1/3-inch thick.
Mark in squares; prick with fork.
Bake about 30 minutes at 350° oven.
On a dinner plate, combine oil, Italian seasoning, paprika and salt.
Add potato wedges, turning to coat with mixture; arrange in a spoke-like fashion, cut sides down.
Cook, covered with wax paper, on High for 4 to 5 minutes, until tender; rotate each wedge halfway through cooking.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Let stand 3 minutes.
If you like, serve with catsup or tomato sauce. Makes 1 serving.
Cut smoked shoots into 1-inch lengths.
Soak shoots in cold water for 20 to 30 minutes to soften.
Drain water; rinse shoots in cold water.
Cover with water; boil, uncovered, for 30 to 45 minutes, or until tender.
Add baking soda (substitute for indigenous seasoning).
Add peanut flour or peanut butter; let boil for 1 minute, then simmer for 10 minutes, turning to avoid sticking to the bottom.
Avoid mashing shoots.
Add salt to taste. Tasty with boiled, mashed green bananas.
Also good as a dip with ripe bananas.
Saute round steak in butter.
Layer raw cut-up bacon, sauteed steak and sliced onion.
Mix tomato sauce, garlic cloves, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Spread over layered ingredients.
Cover with can of kidney beans.
Dot with butter.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serve on rice.
Line bottom of a 2-quart casserole with butter chunks.
Pour bag of fries on top.
Sprinkle with minced onion, salt and pepper. Cover with whipping cream and sprinkle with parsley.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Not recommended for cooking ahead and/or freezing.
Simple and delicious.
Serves 6 to 8.
Lightly mix ground beef, pecans, salt and pepper.
Shape into 4 patties.
Brown on both sides.
Drain.
Add wine and onion. Cover; simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove patties to platter.
Blend water and cornstarch.
Add to pan juices.
Cook and stir until boiling.
Pour over patties on serving platter.
Makes 4 servings.
Peel pears and slice in half rounds or spears.
Soak overnight in 1 gallon water and lime.
Next morning, drain, rinse and soak in clear water for 4 hours.
Melt butter in skillet; add onions and saute until golden brown.
Crumble bread into mixing bowl; add milk.
Let stand until bread is moist.
Add eggs and mix well.
Add onion, green pepper and salt.
Add meat and mix well.
Pile mixture lightly into greased 2 1/2-inch muffin pans.
Top each with thin onion slice. Bake in 425° oven until browned, about 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine first five ingredients; mix well. Form peanut butter mixture into 1-inch balls.
Press balls into miniature 1-inch baking cups with your thumb.
Top each with a 1/2 tablespoon melted chocolate.
Chill one hour.
Store in container with tight fitting lid.
Tastes like Reese's Peanut Butter Cups.
Drain pineapple and put aside.
Mix its juice with sugar, cranberries, raisins, spices, salt and cayenne in a heavy saucepan.
Cook to boiling.
Lower heat and simmer 20 minutes. Add pineapple; simmer 10 minutes more.
Keep either in deep freeze or refrigerate if paraffin sealed.
Prepare spaghetti according to box directions.
Drain and set aside to cool.
In a large skillet over high heat add sesame oil and meat.
Once done, remove from pan and set aside.
In same pan, add vegetable oil, crushed red pepper flakes.
Stir-fry the peas, onion, and bean sprouts for 1 minute.
Dump in drained, cooled pasta and toss.
Next add in the meat that was set aside, and fry the mixture until noodles and veggies are combined.
Drizzle with soy sauce and 1 tablespoons of sesame oil.
Dump into large serving bowl.
Fill a large mixing bowl with hot water from the faucet and let it sit for a minute or two.
Empty, then add 2 cups lukewarm water to the warm bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons sugar and yeast; mix well.
When dissolved, add the sugar (1 cup), Wesson oil, eggs and salt.
Mix well.
Add the flour 1/3 at a time and mix after each addition.
This should make a fairly thick dough.
Cover and let rise until double in bulk.
Grease 3 loaf pans.
Dip the batter by spoonfuls evenly in the pans.
Heat the margarine and spread evenly on top of dough.
Let rise until double.
Bake in 300° oven 30 to 45 minutes or until bread leaves the side of the pans and tests done.
If it browns too fast, cover with foil after the first 15 to 20 minutes.
When done turn out immediately on towel to cool.
Some ovens may take longer to cook.
Combine catsup, sugar and vinegar in skillet.
Simmer over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add chicken breasts.
Cover skillet with lid. Turn chicken once or twice while cooking.
Add a little water while cooking if needed.
Simmer for 40 minutes.
Chicken legs and thighs can also be used.
Just remove the skin first.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Cook macaroni until soft; drain.
Mix ham and onion together.
Mix macaroni with ham and onion.
Pour soup over the top of macaroni and ham.
Sprinkle top with celery salt.
Bake at 300° for 35 minutes or until bubbly.
Boil potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes with skins and cut in half. Layer cut side up in 8 x 12-inch pan.
Pour the milk over.
Chop green and red pepper and arrange peppers and chopped onion over the potatoes.
Melt butter and drizzle over top.
Sprinkle salt and pepper to taste.
Top with parsley and then spread grated cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
In a medium saucepan over very low heat, stir together semi-sweet chocolate and butter until melted.
Off heat, stir in cereal (without crushing) until coated.
Turn into buttered 8-inch glass pie plate and spread over bottom and side, not over rim. Chill until firm.
(Chocolate will seep through and make a shiny firm bottom.)
Spray 8-inch spring-form pan or 9-inch pie plate with Pam. Place cookies in bottom of pan.
Process cottage cheese and cream cheese in food processor or blender until smooth.
Add flour, sugar, salt, egg whites and vanilla.
Whirl until blended.
Remove 1/3 cup of filling; stir in cocoa, 2 tablespoons sugar and milk. Pour plain filling into pan.
Spoon chocolate mixture in mounds over top.
Swirl to create a marble platter.
Place on a baking sheet.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes.
Turn off oven.
Leave cheesecake in oven with door ajar 1 hour.
Cool.
Chill.
Soften the sherbet in a pitcher or bowl.
Blend in milk with a spoon or a rotary beater until sherbet is melted and thoroughly combined with the milk.
Add the vanilla.
Serve immediately in chilled glasses.
Combine first 5 ingredients; toss lightly.
Fold in eggs and mayonnaise; cover and chill 2 hours.
Serve on leaf lettuce. Sprinkle with bacon and almonds.
Makes 2 servings.
Can be easily doubled.
Combine oil, sugar and eggs; mix well.
Add flour and cinnamon.
Stir in apples and nuts.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle butterscotch morsels on top of batter and bake at 350° for 1 hour in preheated oven.
In a large skillet, brown meat, onion, rice, salt and pepper. Drain excess drippings.
In a 2 1/2-quart baking dish, layer the cabbage leaves, torn into 1-inch bits, meat, rice mixture and spaghetti twice.
Bake, covered, 30 minutes at 350°.
Uncover and bake for 30 minutes more.
Sprinkle salt on each cabbage leaf (unwashed).
Mix it well. Let it set outside overnight.
Next day, mix it again.
Wash it 3 times.
Taste it to see how salty it is.
Squeeze out the juice. Once it is salty enough, add garlic, ginger, onions, shrimp, hot pepper, black pepper, garlic powder and sugar.
Leave the Kim Chee out for two days, then put it in the refrigerator for one week or until sour.
Mix together dressing and butter.
Put half of this mixture in bottom of a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix together chicken soup and sour cream.
Spoon onto the dressing.
Sprinkle remaining dressing over the entire dish.
Pour broth over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Saute onion and chicken and add all other ingredients and simmer 45 minutes.
(Thicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch in 1 cup cold water; pour into mixture.)
Bake your own corn tortilla strips or buy as chips and crush into bowls; add soup and top with any or all of the following:
shredded cheese, chopped cilantro, diced tomatoes or diced onions.
Enjoy and expect lots of compliments!

recipes.t: Beefsteak Na Kyselo(Steak With Sour Cream Gravy)
d: Trim meat slices.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Heat shortening in heavy skillet.
When smoking hot, saute meat in it until browned on both sides.
Lower heat.
Sprinkle salt over meat and top with onion slices.
Pour water over meat.
Simmer, covered, for 50 to 60 minutes or until tender.
Check liquid; at the end of cooking time, there should be about 1 cup of it. Remove meat to hot dish.
Blend sour cream with flour.
Stir into skillet and mix thoroughly with pan juices.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and add ketchup, if desired.
Heat through and pour sauce over meat.
Serve very hot with boiled noodles or boiled potatoes.
Yields 4 servings.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Yams And Pineapple
d: Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Combine juice from pineapple, cornstarch and salt in saucepan; mix well.
Cook until sauce boils and thickens, stirring.
Stir in vinegar.
Add yams and pineapple slices; cover and simmer.
Stir-fry onions, celery and green pepper in oil for 4 minutes.
Combine with yams and pineapple.
Serve immediately.
Bowl 1:
Mix flour, salt and baking soda.
Bowl 2:
Beat sugar and butter; add eggs, one at a time.
Bowl 3:
Mix pineapple, yogurt, extracts and lime rind.
Add flour mixture and pineapple mixture to sugar mixture.
Bake in a greased and floured Bundt pan for 1 hour at 325°.
Glace with lime juice and confectioners sugar, mixed to a good consistency.
Pour over top.
Let sit to dry.
In a bowl, mix together egg, sugar, butter, sour milk or buttermilk and vanilla.
Add salt, nutmeg, soda, baking powder and flour.
Stir well. Roll out onto floured board to about 1/2-inch thick.
Cut with doughnut cutter. Fry in hot lard, turning as soon as they rise to surface. Turn often until done.
Makes 30 to 36 doughnuts.
Brown sausage until done, drain and set aside.
Lightly butter bottom and sides of dish.
Arrange bread cubes in dish to cover bottom; set aside.
Pour drained sausage over bread cubes; spread evenly.
Mix first 5 ingredients well.
Pour this mixture over sausage and bread cubs.
Cover to let settle overnight (meat and cheese will float to top).
In a mixing bowl, cream butter, sugar and vanilla.
Gradually add flour; mix well.
Stir in the nuts.
Shape into 1-inch balls; place 2-inches apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake at 300° for 18 to 20 minutes or until bottoms are lightly browned.
Cool on wire racks.
Combine confectioners sugar and nutmeg.
Gently roll cooled cookies in sugar mixture.
Yield: about 5 dozen.
In a large skillet saute bacon, remove and keep warm.
Add next 4 ingredients, saute 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove and add to bacon. Clean and wash livers.
Pat dry with paper towels.
In the palm of your hand place several livers.
With a sharp fork, prick them several times.
This prevents them from popping.
Repeat until all are done.
Dust with salt and pepper; dust with flour until all are covered.
Heat drippings.
Saute livers a few at a time, just until they are no longer pink in the center.
Do not overcook.
Add bacon, green onions, mushrooms and parsley.
Heat.
Add wine and simmer until wine has evaporated.
If too dry, adjust with hot water.
Serve on slices of hot buttered toast.
Enjoy.
Mix hamburger, bread crumbs, salt, eggs, milk, chopped onion and pepper well.
Mix brown sugar, vinegar and ketchup together. Add 1/2 of this mixture into the meat loaf mixture.
Baste the top with the remaining part.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 1/2 hours.
Simmer all ingredients 1/2 hour; add rice.
Continue to simmer until rice is covered.
Arrange on tray or Lazy Susan:
fresh chopped tomatoes, onions, avocado, lettuce and 2 cups grated Longhorn cheese.
Slightly crumble Fritos on plate.
Top with ground beef combo and favorite other toppings.
Top with lettuce, cheese and salsa.
In a mixing bowl, combine the sugar, flour, baking soda and salt.
Add mandarin oranges and egg;
beat on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into a greased 8 inch square baking pan.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 - 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack for 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease rectangular baking dish, 11 x 7 x 1 1/2-inch.
Layer chicken, onion, chilies, cheese and corn in dish. Beat Bisquick milk, salt and egg yolks.
Beat egg whites in large bowl until stiff; fold in egg yolk mixture.
Pour over corn.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, about 35 minutes. Makes 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt margarine in 9 x 13-inch pan (in oven) while preheating oven.
Add sugar and pineapple (include juice).
Mix well.
Rinse cranberries in colander and pick out mushy ones.
