Remove any stems.
Sprinkle cranberries over pineapple mixture (evenly).
Pour prepared cake mix over pineapple/cranberry mix.
Beat egg whites.
Mix butter or margarine with sugar.
Beat in egg yolks; mix well.
Mix flour, soda and salt together and add alternately with milk.
Add vanilla.
Fold in beaten egg whites. Bake in 4 layers at 350° for 30 minutes.
Pour liquid from beans; save it.
Lightly brown almonds in oil; add celery and saute 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup bean liquid, stock base, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar.
Cover; simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in beans and heat until hot.
Add cornstarch mixed with water; heat just until sauce thickens.
*Roast almonds with 1 tablespoon butter in frying pan until slightly browned, stirring constantly.
Beat egg whites until foamy.
Gradually add 1/4 cup sugar and continue beating until mixture will form soft peaks.
Mix tapioca, 1/4 cup sugar, salt, milk, egg yolks and gelatin in a saucepan. Let stand 5 minutes.

In a bowl, combine soup mix, salad dressing and cranberry sauce. Mix well. Place chicken in shallow 2 or 3-quart baking dish that has been sprayed with Pam. Pour sauce mixture over chicken. Cover with foil. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 20 minutes longer or until chicken is done. Serve over rice. Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Beat eggs with electric mixer until thick and lemon colored. Gradually add sugar, milk and vanilla.
Stir together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Blend these ingredients into egg mixture. Pour batter into a jelly roll pan (10 x 15-inch) sprayed with Pam or Baker's Joy.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until cake tester comes out clean.
While cake is still hot, spread peanut butter evenly over top of cake.
Let cool thoroughly, then spread melted Hershey bar over peanut butter.
Refrigerate until firm.
In a large, heavy skillet, brown chicken in hot oil and margarine until golden brown.
Add onion, potatoes, celery, salt, thyme, pepper, bay leaf and broth.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer about 30 minutes or until chicken and potatoes are almost tender.
Add cut green beans; cover and cook about 10 minutes or until chicken and vegetables are tender.
Serves 4.
Set oven to 375°.
Put onions and apples in a pan and cover with water.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Drain well.
Meanwhile boil swede for 10 minutes, then add potato and cook until both are soft.
Drain well and mash together until smooth.
Grease an ovenproof dish with the butter.
Place layers of meat, onion and apple in the dish, seasoning and sprinkling each layer with herbs as you fill up the dish.
Pour in the gravy and top with the mashed potato and swede mixture.
Dot top with butter and bake uncovered for 3/4 to 1 hour.
Serve with a green vegetable. Serves 4.
In medium saucepan, mix nonfat dry milk in water until dissolved.
Over medium heat, stir in sifted unsweetened cocoa powder and honey.
Cook and stir for 15 to 20 minutes, until mixture is thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Let cool 10 minutes, and frosting is ready to use.
Frosting will continue to harden as it cools.
Chop ham in blender or food processor (do not overchop or will be mushy).
Mix in large bowl with chopped eggs and remaining ingredients.
Add enough mayonnaise for good spreading consistency.
Can be kept in sealed container in refrigerator for several days.
Combine soup, onion, parsley and poultry seasoning in baking dish.
Blend well.
Add tuna, pimientos and peas to soup mixture. Mix gently.
Bake at 425° for 20 minutes.
Place biscuits on tuna mixture in slightly overlapping border.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes. Serves 6.
Freeze 2 cups cranberry juice cocktail in ice cube trays. Combine remaining cranberry juice, orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice and sugar in a large pitcher.
Stir until sugar dissolves. Chill until ready to serve.
Mix juice into condensed milk until thick.
Fold in Cool Whip. Add pineapple.
Refrigerate.
Prepare crust and set aside.
In small saucepan, soften gelatin in cold water.
Stir over low heat until gelatin dissolves completely.
Stir into yogurt.
Mash strawberries and fold into the yogurt.
Stir in Equal.
Pour into the graham cracker crust.
When pie is firm, whip dessert topping and spread on top of pie.
Chill. Serves 8. Contains 135 calories per serving.
Cook macaroni as directed on package.
Drain and pour into ungreased 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Stir soup, milk and Worcestershire sauce into macaroni.
Cut frankfurters crosswise into very thin slices and arrange on top of macaroni mixture. Bake uncovered 25 minutes at 375° or until hot and bubbly.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix flours and oats.
Combine 3 cups flour mixture, wheat germ, yeast and salt in large mixing bowl.
Add water, cottage cheese, molasses (or honey) and oil to flour mixture; beat until smooth, about 3 minutes on high speed of electric mixer.
Stir in raisins and enough more flour to make a soft dough.
Peel and cut mirlitons in small cubes.
Cook 25 minutes with garlic, 1/2 of onions, bell peppers and celery.
Saute shrimp and meat with remainder of vegetables in 3 tablespoons oil.
Cook 20 minutes.
Add can of gravy.
Combine with mirliton mixture, chopped tomato and seasonings.
Cook 15 minutes.
Season to taste.
Remove thick/tough peeling from potatoes leaving as much tender peeling as possible.
Cut into 1/2-inch slices & set aside.
Cut bacon into 1/4-inch bits and saute in a large saucepan until lightly crisped. Remove bacon bits with a slotted spoon leaving the drippings.
Set bacon aside.
Add onions and celery to drippings and saute until tender but not browned.
Add broth, water, pepper, salt and parsley flakes and bring to a simmer.
Stir in diced potatoes and allow to simmer for about 5-10 minutes.
Begin adding instant potato flakes to thicken if desired, adding 1 tablespoon at a time until you have a fairly thick consistency.
Allow to simmer for a few minutes to have the potato flakes absorb to their maximum.
When the consistency that you wish is reached, slowly add the cream, stirring constantly.
Allow to heat through but not boil.
Add reserved bacon bits, stir and serve.
Saute onions and bell pepper in butter, add Rotel, soups, and cool on low heat until smooth.
Add shrimp or crawfish and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Tear half of angel food cake into bite size pieces.
Place pieces into bottom of 3-quart glass bowl.
In bowl, combine pie filling and whipped topping.
Drizzle cake pieces with 1/4 cup fruit spread.
Then spread half of filling mixture over cake pieces.
Layer half of the pineapple, kiwi and strawberries over filling mixture.
Tear remaining cake into bite size pieces and place over filling.
Repeat layers with remaining ingredients. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 4 hours before serving.
Combine cabbage and marinade in resealable plastic bag. Refrigerate for 1 hour or overnight.
Layer 1/4 marinated cabbage, turkey and cheese on each of 4 rye slices. Top with additional slice of bread.
Makes 4 servings.
Lightly grease cookie sheet.
Separate rolls into 12 pieces, then 3 layers.
Mix together crabmeat, shrimp, cheese, mayonnaise, onion, parsley flakes and curry powder.
Spoon mixture on each dough piece.
Top with water chestnuts.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Heat 2 quarts water with salt.
Add beef; bring to a boil. Skim foam from surface until clear.
Partially cover pot; simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Cut leeks in 2-inch pieces, then cut in half lengthwise.
Add leeks, onion, carrots and celery to beef.
Cook until beef and vegetables are tender.
Cut beef into 1/2-inch slices.
Cut gherkins lengthwise in thin slices, leaving 1 end uncut.
Spread out slices like a fan; garnish beef with gherkins. Serve vegetables in a separate dish with 4 tablespoons cooking liquid spooned over the top.
Garnish with parsley.
Serve with Swedish mayonnaise.
In a 5 to 6-quart pan, break turkey into chunks; add onion, garlic and 1/2 cup chicken broth.
Stir often over medium-high heat until liquid evaporates and meat and onion start to brown.
Add another 1/2 cup broth.
Stir to release browned bits.
Boil dry as in preceding step.
Repeat, adding liquid and boiling dry until meat and onion are well browned, 2 or 3 more times.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups broth, kidney, lima and pinto beans, garbanzo, catsup, sugar, vinegar and mustard.
Cover and simmer gently until flavors are blended, about 1 hour.
Stir often.
If making ahead, let cool. Cover and chill up to 3 days.
Reheat to serve.
Serves 6.
Steam live crabs 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool and pick out crabmeat.
Melt butter, add flour.
Add milk and bring to simmer. Cook until a little thick.
Chop eggs, add with crabmeat.
Simmer a few minutes (3 to 5).
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to simmer and serve.
Yields about 6 servings.
Boil macaroni according to directions, adding tomatoes and juice during boiling time.
When done, make sure only small amount of liquid is present (may have to drain some).
Stir in browned ground beef.
Add salt and pepper.
Pour into lightly greased baking dish.
Top with shredded cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Sift flour with soda, baking powder, salt, spices and cocoa.
Blend into creamed mixture alternately with applesauce.
Fold in raisins and nuts.
Pour into 2 greased 9-inch pans.

Cube potatoes and cook in broth till tender.
Fry bacon crisp while potatoes are cooking.
Pour off most of bacon fat from pan, and cook onions till tender with the bacon.
When potatoes are tender; add bacon and onions and butter, salt and pepper to taste. Thicken soup with flour and water paste.
Simmer for 5 minutes till slightly thickened.
Add milk and sour cream mixture.
Stir in chopped parsley.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, eggs, lemon juice, and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Drop one vanilla wafer into the bottom of each cupcake liner.
Fill cups 2/3 full with cream cheese mixture. Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes until set.
Top with your favorite fruit topping.
Combine butterscotch pieces and butter in a 2-quart microwavable glass casserole.
Cook, uncovered, 2 to 3 minutes at power level 7 or until melted.
Stir in marshmallows.
Cook, uncovered, 3 to 4 1/2 minutes at power level 6 or until marshmallows are softened.
Stir twice.
Blend until smooth.
Stir rice cereal into marshmallow mixture.
Press into buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish; cool and cut.
Sort out red beans and wash.
Cover beans with water.
Add onions, garlic, green pepper, celery and wine.
Soak overnight.
In morning, add ham bone and bay leaf and few dashes of Louisiana hot sauce.
Cook until beans are tender.
More water may be added. Cook, simmering uncovered, but watch closely.
Mash a few beans to thicken.
When done, serve over rice and sprinkle with chopped green onions.
Salt and pepper to taste while cooking.
Peel potatoes and cube or cut up.
Brown potatoes and onion in 2 tablespoons of oil.
In separate boiler, cut up cabbage and cook in a small amount of water.
Slice sausage and add to potatoes and onion mixture.
After cabbage is tender, add to sausage, potatoes and onion.
Let simmer for 15 to 20 minutes over low heat.
Serve with cornbread and enjoy.
Melt chocolate chips over simmering water in top of double boiler.
Let cool.
Stir in salted peanuts, raisins and marshmallows.
Line cookie sheet with wax paper.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on paper.
Refrigerate overnight.
Combine sugar and milk, then add eggs and butter.
Sift dry ingredients and add, using just enough flour to make a fairly stiff batter, but not too stiff!
Drop by teaspoonfuls into 375° fat and fry like doughnuts.
When cool, shake in a sack with powdered sugar.
Powder again before serving.

recipes.t: Grapefruit, Avocado And Red Onion Salad
d: Peel grapefruit, being sure to remove all the white, then separate by removing the membranes from between the sections. Peel and slice avocado.
Mix with mayonnaise and garnish with red onion slices.
Cream butter until fluffy.
Add sugar, egg and cottage cheese. Fold in cranberries and raisins by hand.
Mix in flour and remaining ingredients.
Stir together well, then fill muffin cups 3/4 full.
Bake until puffed and lightly browned.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Makes 24 petite little muffins.

Drain salmon, discarding bones and skin. Flake and set aside. Combine celery, green pepper and onion in a 2-quart glass casserole dish. Cook uncovered in the microwave 2 minutes on high or until tender. Add flaked salmon, bread crumbs, lemon juice and a mixture of the evaporated milk and egg to the vegetables. Mix well. Carefully spoon the salmon mixture into a 5 1/2-6 cup microwave-safe ring mold. Cover with waxed paper.
Saute onions and celery in oil until tender.
Finely grind almonds or liquify with water in blender until very fine.
Combine all ingredients, except gravy.
Pack into greased loaf pan or ring mold.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Serve with mushroom gravy.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cut cauliflower into florets and cook in
boiling salted water for 5 to 8 minutes.
In skillet heat
oil and saute onions until slightly golden.
Add drained cauliflower, salt, pepper and parsley.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes on medium
heat. Beat
eggs and milk in a bowl with the Parmesan cheese
and
set mix with cauliflower mixture.
Grease 8-inch baking dish
with butter
and
pour
cauliflower mixture into dish.
Bake for approximately
35 to 45 minutes or until eggs feel set and
firm. To serve, sprinkle with a little Parmesan cheese.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
A great luncheon or sidedish.
Wash lettuce head and tear, not cut, into slices.

Place lettuce leaves in bowl; put half of peach and half of pear in bowl. Take ice cream scoop and drop two scoops cottage cheese in on lettuce leaves, pears and peaches, then place 1 or 2 cherries on top.
Wash chicken; skin and bones may be removed.
Put all in crock-pot in the order given.
Do not mix.
Turn on high for 1 hour, then turn on low for 2 to 3 hours.
Take chicken out first and put in a bowl very carefully.
Put vegetables and rice in another bowl.
Serve warm with rolls.
Pat chicken dry with a paper towel.
Heat butter and oil in skillet over medium high heat.
Coat chicken with flour and season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with a few drops of lemon juice. Cook chicken until brown on each side, about 15 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
To the pan juices, add the remaining juice.
Simmer about 5 minutes, then pour over chicken.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease bottoms of 12 medium muffin cups or line with paper baking cups.
Beat egg, stir in milk, oil and cherry syrup.
Mix in flour, 1/4 cup sugar, cherries, baking powder and salt just until flour is moistened.
Trim crust from bread; cut into 1/2-inch slices.
Line a 1 1/2-quart round bowl with bread, pressing firmly with fingers. Cook plums with 1 cup sugar and cinnamon, stirring constantly until plums are soft, about 10 minutes.
Cook peaches with 2/3 cup sugar, about 10 minutes.
Layer plums and peaches in bread-lined bowl.
Cover top with remaining bread slices.
Place a flat plate with a heavy weight on top.
Refrigerate overnight. Unmold and serve with whipped cream (Cool-Whip).
Saute the zucchini, sliced thin, in 1 tablespoon oil until tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper and cook 1 minute.
Add the fresh lemon juice and the grated lemon peel; heat through.
May add some sliced black olives.
Oil-cured olives are very nice.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Pour the melted margarine into an 8-inch square pan.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and line bottom of pan with crushed pineapple.
In a mixing bowl, sift together the flour, salt and white sugar.
Add the oil and 1/4 cup of the milk. Stir until flour is dampened, then beat 1 minute.
Stir in the baking powder and the remaining milk.
Stir in the unbeaten egg whites and the vanilla.
Beat for 2 minutes.
Pour batter over the crushed pineapple in the cake pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the cake comes out clean.
Remove from oven; cool slightly and invert onto a serving plate. Approximately 290 calories per serving.
Combine cheese, butter and sugar.
Combine flour, salt and blend into cheese mixture.
Shape dough into small balls.
Place on baking sheet.
Press pecan halves into each ball and flatten slightly.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes or until slightly browned.
Makes 100 wafers.
Brown and drain beef.
Combine beef, onions, cheese, oregano, cumin, garlic salt and chilies.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture on each won ton wrapper and follow package directions for folding and sealing.
Deep fry 1 1/2 minutes or until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Serve warm.
Yield: 6 dozen appetizers.
Stir instant pudding with milk.
Drain fruit cocktail.
Mix pudding and fruit together.
Add yogurt and whipped topping.
Add food coloring and marshmallows, if desired.
Chill for 2 hours.
Grate cheese. Put cream of mushroom soup in pot (undiluted). Put cheese into cream of mushroom soup and heat on low.
Add the chilies and stir. Do not boil.
Mixture will be thick when done.
Combine lime gelatin and pineapple in bowl; mix well.
Fold in whipped topping.
May be served immediately or chilled until serving time.
Mix flour, margarine and pecans.
Press in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Let cool.
Mix cream cheese and confectioners sugar until creamy.
Fold in 1 cup Cool Whip.
Spread on top of crust.
Mix both puddings with 2 cups milk.
Spread on cream cheese layer, then top with rest of Cool Whip.
Grate chocolate bar on top.
Beat eggs in small bowl.
Gradually beat in sugar and vanilla. Fold in flour mixed with baking powder.
Fold in apples and nuts.
Crust:
Moisten cookie crumbs with melted margarine.
Divide mixture in half, pressing into two pie plates.
Brown ground beef with taco seasoning mix.
Line a 9 x 9-inch baking dish with the rolls.
Pour 1/2 cup Fritos on the dough. Add meat mixture.
Spread sour cream over meat.
Sprinkle cheese over sour cream.
Sprinkle on remaining Fritos.
Sprinkle the water over all.
Beat cream cheese in medium bowl until fluffy.
Beat in mayonnaise, sour cream, chives and parsley.
Stir in clams. Serve with assorted vegetables.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
Use your favorite sweet dough recipe.
Cook beans, drain and mash; add salt and sugar.
When dough is ready to shape, form into balls the size of a large walnut.
Let rise about 30 minutes. Pull apart and place 1 rounded teaspoonful of bean mixture on dough and close by pressing edges together.
Place in greased pan and let rise about 30 minutes.
Bake in moderate oven for 25 minutes.
Serve with hot sauce.
(Dough can also be rolled out and cut into 3 to 3 1/2-inch squares and then filled.)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Layer in a 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish 1/3 of the hominy and 1/3 of the corn. Sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper.
Add 2 to 3 tablespoons chilies. Dot with butter and 4 more tablespoons sour cream.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup of both cheeses.
Repeat layers 2 times.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes. Serves 12.
In skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sprinkle with mix. Saute 4 minutes each side or until done.
Add lemon juice and stir, scraping brown bits from bottom of pan. Turn chicken and add parsley. Serve over rice or pasta.
Clean, wash and cut cutlets into bite-size pieces.
Dip into flour mixed with salt and pepper.
Using 2 large frypans, place 1/2 pound butter in each and melt on low heat.
Place chicken into frypans equally and cover.
Turn chicken as it simmers. Meanwhile, on medium speed, mix together heavy cream or half and half together.
Add wine.
Mix until bubbly.
When chicken looks golden and cooked, add cream mixture and stir thoroughly.
Cover. As mixture thickens, add black pepper and granulated garlic to taste.
Remove to large serving pan.
Top with orange slices for garnish.
Serves 25.
Mix the pudding and milk, then add Cool Whip. Mix together the cream cheese and condensed milk and then beat together with pudding mixture. Layer vanilla wafers, bananas and pudding, then chill.
Brown ham slightly in fat.
Cook well if uncooked ham is used. Stir in flour; add milk.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Stir in mustard, salt and celery salt; add eggs.
Heat just until hot; stir only to keep from sticking.
Serve over hot split biscuits. Yields 8 servings.

recipes.t: Saint Joseph'S Day Cream Puffs(Sfingi Di San Giuseppe)
d: Combine
butter,
salt
and water in saucepan; bring to boil. Add
flour
all
at
one time and mix well, until dough leaves side of pan.
Remove from stove and cool a little.
Add eggs,
one at
a
time, mixing well after each addition.
Add sugar, orange and lemon peel; mix thoroughly.
Dissolve yeast, sugar and warm water.
In a heavy saucepan, combine cornmeal, sugar, shortening, salt and milk.
Cook until thickened, stirring often.
Cool until lukewarm.
In a large bowl, combine corn and eggs.
Stir in yeast mixture and cooled cornmeal mixture.
Mix thoroughly; then stir in 5 cups flour.
Preheat oven
Spray a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan with nonstick
cooking
spray and set aside, or use tube pan. Into
a small mixing bowl sift together flour, baking powder, salt
and cinnamon.
Set
aside.
In
a
large
mixing
bowl, combine margarine and sugar.
Using electric mixer beat until creamy and light.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat until thoroughly combined.
Add sifted
ingredients alternately with
bananas, beating
gently after each addition.
(Do not overbeat as this will toughen bread.)
In a 9 x
13-inch pan, stir in melted butter and brown sugar. Add
flour and nuts.
Pack evenly over bottom and bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes until brown.
In large bowl, beat egg whites to a
soft
peak. Gradually
add sugar, berries, lemon juice and
vanilla.
Beat at high speed until triple in volume and stiff
peaks
form.
Fold
in
cream.
Spread over cooled crust. Freeze.
Mash avocados with lemon juice, taco mix, mayonnaise and sour cream.
In medium bowl, combine sour cream, mayo and seasonings.
Stir in chopped onions, spinach, chopped water chestnuts and red peppers.
Cover and refrigerate.
Serve with crisp or assorted crackers.
Makes 3 1/2 cups dip.

Add the sugar, light brown sugar and water. Important: do not stir mixture. Bring to 240°, then add the margarine. Do not stir. Bring to 265°. Add the vanilla. Pour on buttered marble slab; should be cold marble. Let cool enough to start pulling. Take outside and pull. When it has been pulled enough, cut with buttered scissors. Necessary to be cold weather and not raining or snowing.
Combine muffin mix with sour cream, eggs and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients and bake at 350° until browned lightly.
Beat cream cheese, chocolate, eagle brand milk, eggs, cornstarch and almond extract until smooth.
Pour into springform pan, bake 55 minutes to an hour or until center is set.
Chill. Top with cherry pie filling and cool whip before serving.

In a large skillet, brown hamburger and drain. Add onions and peppers. Cover. Stir. In 5 minutes, add garlic salt, zucchini, stewed tomatoes and lemon juice. Cover and simmer. Bring water to boil, add rice and cover. Shut off stove. Serve skillet mixture over rice.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Pour the uncooked rice in the bottom of a 9x13x2 inch baking pan. Layer the chicken over the rice.
Add the drained tomatoes and vegetables. Combine the liquid from the tomatoes and vegetables with enough chicken broth to make 2 1/2 cups of liquid.
Add this to the mushroom soup and heat. Pour this mixture over the vegetables.
Sprinkle the cheese over top of the casserole.
Bake for about 35 minutes.
Makes 10 generous servings.
Less than 4 grams of fat per serving.
Place peaches in medium size baking dish. Add lemon rind, if used. Crumble pie crust and sugar together, mixing well.
Dust onto peaches and dot liberally with butter or oleo.
Bake 45 minutes at 325°.
Serve warm with cream.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix together sugar and cinnamon and set aside.
Mix remaining ingredients and pour half into greased and floured Bundt pan.
Add sugar and cinnamon mixture.
Pour remaining batter over sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
After baking, let set 25 minutes before removing from pan.
In large saucepan over medium-high heat, heat water and milk almost to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Using a whisk, slowly stir in cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, garlic powder and black pepper until smooth.
Blend in remaining ingredients.
Spoon into lightly greased 2-quart souffle or baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes or until puffed
and golden brown.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.t: Grilled Fish Steaks With Ginger, Honey And Mustard
d: Combine mustard, mayonnaise, ginger and honey in bowl.
In a large, shallow dish, coat fish with mustard mixture on both sides. Cover with plastic wrap and marinate 30 minutes in refrigerator while preparing grill.
When coals are hot, grill fish on oiled grid, about 5 minutes per side, turning once.
Serves 4.
Wash rice, cover with water and bring to a boil.
Drain at once.
Combine with boiled milk, sugar, salt, butter, orange rind and vanilla extract.
Place in 2-quart ovenproof casserole.
Bring mixture to a boil over medium heat.
Remove from heat.
Cover and bake in 325° oven 20 to 25 minutes or until rice is cooked and liquid absorbed.
Remove from oven and remove orange peel.
Cool slightly.
Beat eggs well.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add Karo and pecans. Pour in uncooked pie shell and bake for about one hour in a 350° oven.
Thoroughly mix together almond, cardamon and powdered sugar. Set aside.
In a flat baking pan combine egg yolks, milk and melted butter.
Add flour little by little, until a dough is formed.
The dough should not stick to your hand.
Divide the dough into 5 equal portions and place each portion into a plastic bag.
Remove dough one piece at a time and make five sheets to fit the size of the pan.
Cover the bottom of a well-greased pan with 2 pastry sheets. Brush each sheet with melted butter before placing the next sheet on top.
Place 2 more sheets on top, grease each sheet.
Cut pastry into 1 x 1-inch squares.
Add 3 or 4 tablespoons melted butter on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until crust is golden. Immediately drizzle syrup on top.
Cover the pan with aluminum foil and let cool.
Sprinkle pistachios on top just prior to serving.
Cook rice in water and salt at medium heat until all the water is absorbed.
Add milk, vanilla and sugar until desired consistency (a little softer than you want to end up with).
Add egg and raisins and cook for 4 to 5 minutes longer.
Great served warm or cold!
Saute celery
and onion in corn oil.
Stir in liver and sherry,
cooking 3 to 5 minutes.
Avoid overcooking.
Add salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.
Mix oil, sugar, eggs, vanilla and milk.
Beat until smooth. Sift dry ingredients together.
Add slowly to first mixture and beat well.
Add apples and nuts.
Bake for 55 minutes at 350°.
Cook rice as directed; add a little salt.
When rice is cooked, put in a casserole.
Add tomatoes and mix.
Dice cheese over this mixture and bake in 300° oven for 15 minutes.

Lightly dredge the pork in flour, then brown lightly in olive oil in a large Dutch oven. Remove pork; lower the heat and cook the onion and garlic until quite fragrant. Return pork to the dish and add the canned chiles and tomatoes. If you like your chili really zesty, add some minced jalapenos or serranos too. Add additional liquid to almost cover the pork. Simmer covered until pork is just tender. Season with cumin and chili powder - be very generous with cumin as it is what really sets this chili apart. Three to four tablespoons is not unusual. Simmer about 30 minutes more and serve with heated tortillas and if you wish, some grated Jack cheese on top. This both reheats and doubles well. Serves 6 to 8.
Sift flour and sugar into bowl.
Pour berries into mixture and stir until every berry is coated.
Proceed as with any berry pie. Cook until juice bubbles out of crust.
Combine mustard, oil, wine, garlic, herbs and pepper.
Place lamb in shallow dish.
Spread lamb with mustard mixture.
Cover. Marinate 1 hour at room temperature or overnight in refrigerator. Grill over medium coals 50 minutes to 1 hour or until done.
Turn frequently.
Do not overcook.

Stir together green beans, wax beans and red kidney beans. Add onions, if desired. Combine remaining ingredients and toss together with beans. Chill overnight. Stir a couple of times to blend flavors.
Heat soup, milk and Velveeta in top of double boiler until cheese is melted. Add green chillies and pimentos. Combine Longhorn cheese, onions and meat.
Fill each tortilla with mixture and roll tightly.
Place in a long baking dish.
Pour sauce over the top. Cover. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Put 1/2 of cake mix into a 9 x 13-inch pan; bake a thin layer. (Make cupcakes out of rest.)
Cook the vanilla pie filling, or make a 3-cup cream pie filling recipe.
Stir into hot filling the cream cheese.
Pour over cooled cake layer.
Combine juices and lemonade and orange juice concentrate in a large punch bowl.
Blend well.
Pour in ginger ale.
Add ice cubes. Garnish with lemon slices.
Makes about 1 gallon.
Preheat
oven
to
Shake flour in 1 regular size Reynolds Oven
Bag,
place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Add picante
sauce, onion and garlic.
Squeeze bag to blend ingredients.
Trim
fat from roast, place in bag.
Turn bag to coat roast
with
sauce.
Place
pepper
and
carrots in bag around roast.
Close
bag
with nylon tie.
Cut six 1/2-inch slits in top of
bag.
Bake
until
roast
is tender, 1 3/4 to 2 hours. Let stand in bag 5 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Melt margarine in large saucepan.
Add onion and saute until limp.
Add clam juice, water and potatoes.
Simmer until potatoes are tender.
Add clams and milks.
Heat slowly over low heat about 45 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Makes about 6 servings.
Combine spinach, stuffing mix and sour cream.
Spread 1/4 cup of stuffing mixture down center of ham slice.
Roll up and place seam side down in single layer in 12 x 8 1/2-inch baking dish. Melt butter in saucepan, blend in flour.
Add milk.
Heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Add cheese, and stir until cheese melts.
Pour over ham rolls.
Sprinkle with paprika and Parmesan cheese.
Cover with foil.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Remove foil and bake 15 to 20 minutes more. Serve hot with sauce spooned over ham rolls.
Combine yogurt, vinegar and honey in a large bowl.
Add vegetables and mix well.
Cover and chill 15 minutes.
Spread quail open and wipe dry with paper towels.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and dredge in flour.
Fill a deep, heavy skillet half full of salad oil; heat to 350°.
Cook quail in hot oil 5 minutes; cover and continue cooking until golden brown, turning once.
Drain well.
Serve birds on a hot platter and garnish with lemon slices and parsley.
Yields 6 servings.

Brown meat; drain. Add taco seasoning mix and water. Bring to a boil; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat. Add desired cheese; mix well. Place 2 flour tortillas on bottom of an 8 inch square baking dish. Layer 1/4 of the meat mixture over tortillas. Repeat layers 3 times. Top with remaining cheese. Bake at 375 degrees for 15 minutes or until thoroughly heated. Makes 6 servings.
Lightly brush bread with 1 tablespoon of the dressing; place on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Brush bread half with half of the remaining dressing.
Top with processed cheese and desired pizza toppings. Drizzle with remaining dressing.
Bake 1 to 2 minutes or until cheese has begun to melt.
Cut into 6 wedges.
Makes 2 servings.
Melt butter in skillet. Add walnuts. Sprinkle with dill.
Stir over moderate heat for about 5 minutes or until walnuts are lightly toasted.
Arrange hot cooked vegetables and herbed walnuts on crisp lettuce on serving platter.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt. Heat dressing.
Serve separately with salad.
Yields 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease baking sheets.
Cream butter with sugar, egg yolk and vanilla.
Combine flour with salt and baking powder.
Add to creamed mixture.
Blend well and form into bars about 1-inch in diameter.
Beat egg white until slightly frothy.
Dip dough balls into egg white, then roll in coconut. Place on greased baking sheets.
Make a "thumbprint" in the center of each cookie and spoon 1/2 teaspoon of preserves into each. Bake at 375° for 8 to 9 minutes or until coconut begins to brown. Yields 2 dozen cookies.
Day ahead, mix margarine, cheese and salt until creamy.
Mix in flour. Shape into 14 balls.
Chill overnight.
Heat oven to 350°.
On lightly floured cloth covered board, roll each ball to 6-inch circle.
Cut each into quarters.
Mix nuts, sugar and cinnamon. Drop rounded teaspoonfuls onto each quarter.
Pinch together edges of dough. Form into crescents.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake for 12 minutes or until light brown.
Brown beef and onion.
Add both cans of soup and 1 can water. Add rice and soy sauce.
Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°. Sprinkle with chow mein noodles and bake 10 minutes more.
Serves 6 to 8.
Beat cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise and garlic salt. Hollow out rye bread (not too deep).
Put mixture in bread.
Wrap in foil.
Put on cookie sheet and put broken bread pieces around it.
Heat at 350° for 50 minutes.
Serve with the broken pieces and crackers to use with the dip.
Mix thoroughly the meat, bread crumbs, parsley, dill, egg, garlic and salt.
Shape mixture into 4 patties.
Wrap bacon slice around edge of each patty; secure with wooden picks.
Place patties on rack in broiler pan.
Broil for 15 minutes; turn once.
Combine mushrooms, shrimp, tarragon, garlic and dressing. Chill 1 hour.
Arrange lettuce leaves on individual salad plates. Peel, halve and pit avocados.
Place a half avocado on each plate and fill with salad mixture.
Garnish with cherry tomatoes.
Heat oil in pie plate until very hot, about 5 to 7 minutes. Place each tortilla in hot oil to make it more pliable.

Combine mixed cheeses, 1/2 cup green onions and chopped olives in a bowl. Place about 2 tablespoons of this mixture into each tortilla. Roll closed and place seam-side down in an 8 x 12-inch shallow baking dish.
Pour enchilada sauce over top and sprinkle grated Cheddar cheese and 1/3 cup chopped green onion on top.
Microwave at 80% power (Medium-high) for 13 to 15 minutes, turning dish once during cooking.
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Mushroom Appetizers On Toasted Batard Bread
d: Saute mushrooms in butter.
Stir in flour. When mushrooms are golden and tender, remove from heat. Stir in sour cream and dry onion soup. Sprinkle with grated cheese. Bake at 350° about 20 to 25 minutes.
Can be made the day before.
This is good served on Toasted Batard Bread.
Mix the 2/3 cup chopped nuts, flour and melted margarine until crumbly.
Spread in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool.
Cream the cream cheese.
Add the powdered sugar and peanut butter; cream until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip; spread on first layer.
Mix the pudding mixes with the milk; spread over second layer.
Spread the Cool Whip on third layer. Garnish with chopped nuts.
Refrigerate.
Grease 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Mix cake mix, 1 egg, 1 teaspoon vanilla, stick of melted margarine and nuts.
Spread into pan.
Mix 3 eggs, powdered sugar and softened cream cheese. Spread over mix and bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Heat refried beans in a pan (careful not to burn).
Add hamburger (I cook up
my
hamburger using salt, pepper, garlic powder and a little
chili
powder
to
taste or use hamburger made up with a
packaged
taco
seasoning).
Next, add cheese, salsa and a little onion.
All
you want to do is melt part of the cheese and mix
all
of the flavors.
Adjust seasonings to your taste.
Serve with chips.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream sugar, margarine and Crisco.
Add other ingredients, mixing well.
Make a small ball and press down with a fork.
Bake 12 minutes.
Allow to cool on pan a minute before removing.
Makes 3 dozen 3-inch cookies.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Spray 13 x 9-inch pan.
On waxed paper, combine bread crumbs, salt and pepper.
In shallow pan, beat egg whites and 1 tablespoon water.
Dip fillets in egg and water, then the crumbs.
Place in pan and spray butter Pam on top.
Sprinkle with paprika.
It is done when fillets flake when tested with fork.
Make shell first; soften margarine with hand.
Mix eggs, orange juice and vanilla.
Add sugar, flour and baking powder. Knead until dough holds together and forms a ball.
Roll dough out to make crust and place in 9-inch pie pan.
Cut chicken into bite-size pieces and coat with flour.
Heat shortening and garlic, then add chicken.
Stir until brown on high heat.
Separate whites of eggs.
Beat egg whites and add sugar gradually.
Fold in egg yolks into this mixture.
Add flour gradually, vanilla, lemon peel, lemon juice and oil.
Fold together and pour into pan.
Butter spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes until done.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Pour rice into a baking dish.
Add soups. Stir until well blended.
Add enough water to make rice mixture "soupy".
Place chicken breasts over top of rice mixture. Sprinkle with gravy mixes.
Bake 1 hour or until rice is thoroughly cooked.
Check after 30 minutes to make sure mixture is not getting too dry.
If needed, add more water.
Brown hamburger.
Add diced onion, bell pepper and mushrooms. Simmer for a few minutes.
Dice peeled potatoes and fry.
Then add fried potatoes to meat mixture and stir together.
Soften tortillas; then roll meat mixture in tortillas.

Chop prunes and soak in water for 1 hour. In large skillet, heat butter & oil; add chicken and brown 5-10 minutes on all sides. Arrange chicken in shallow baking dish. Add onions to skillet and saute' 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, tomatoes, salt & pepper, and nutmeg. Simmer 5 minutes. Pour over chicken and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Pour prune mixture over chicken and bake until chicken is tender. Serves six.
Season chicken breasts with paprika, salt and pepper.
Bake, covered, in an oven preheated to 350° for 35 minutes.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a pan.
Add the flour and stir well.
Cook for a couple of minutes; don't brown.
Add hot chicken stock and continue stirring until smooth.
Set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°. In a medium bowl, combine rice with 1 egg and 1 ounce Cheddar cheese. Press mixture firmly over bottom and sides of an 8-inch pie pan to form a crust; set aside.
Place butter in 1 cup glass measure; microwave on High 1 minute.
Set aside.
Break eggs into mixing bowl.
Beat with electric mixer until lemon colored.
Add butter, brown sugar, flour, baking powder and vanilla.
Blend well.
Stir in nuts and coconut.
Pour into 8-inch round microproof baking dish. Microwave on High for 6 minutes.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Cool completely before cutting into bars or wedges.
Allow pie crusts to thaw slightly.
Combine uncooked meat, soup mix, milk, pepper and allspice.
Mix gently.
Lightly pat into pie crust plate.
Top with thawed hash brown potatoes.
Salt and pepper hash brown potatoes to taste.
Add top crust.
Seal and flute edges.
Cover fluted edges to keep them from browning too much.
Cut slits in top crust.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour until golden brown.
Serve with warm ketchup, if desired.
Soak steaks in baking soda 15 minutes.
Change water.
Soak in clear water 1/2 hour.
Cut steak into 4 pieces.
Fry in butter. Turn heat to simmer.
Add salt and pepper to your taste.
Keep adding water.
If meat is cut thick, cook 1 hour.
Make sure it is tender.
Before serving, add 1/2 stick butter.
In a bowl, combine bread crumbs, garlic, parsley, cheese, thyme, lemon zest and salt; mix well.
Add 4 tablespoons of butter and toss lightly to coat; set aside.
Cook spinach in salted water.
Drain.
Cool.
Mix all ingredients.
Place in large buttered baking pan, spread reserved crumbs over top.
Pour melted butter over crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes, or until heated through.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Rub 1 tablespoon butter over the bottom and sides of a 9-inch diameter spring-form pan.
Mix bread crumbs with 2 tablespoons grated cheese.
Coat pan with crumb mixture. Using an electric mixer, beat cream cheese, Ricotta, remaining 1/2 cup Parmesan, salt and cayenne in a large bowl until light.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Transfer half of mixture to a medium bowl.
Mix pesto into remaining half. Pour pesto mixture into prepared pan; smooth top.
Carefully spoon plain mixture; gently smooth top.
Sprinkle with pine nuts.
Bake cake until center no longer moves when pan is shaken, about 45 minutes.
Transfer to rack and cool completely.
Cover tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Run small sharp knife around pan sides to loosen cheesecake, if necessary.
Release pan sides from cheesecake.
Transfer cheesecake to platter.
Garnish with fresh basil sprigs.
Surround with crackers and serve.
Cream butter, oleo, shortening and sugar for 5 minutes.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix flour and baking powder.
Add alternately with milk and flavoring to batter.
Bake for 1 hour at 325°.
Reduce to 300° for 30 minutes.
Cool in pan for 3 minutes; turn out on foil and wrap to cool.
Place onions in bottom of 1 gallon jar.
Top with cucumber slices.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over cucumbers. Cover jar and refrigerate for 1 week before serving.
The pickles keep 9 months.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in pineapple, cranberry sauce and juice.
Chill until mixture thickens slightly. Fold in pecans and turn into a two-quart mold or flat casserole. Chill until firm.
Beat the softened cream cheese until smooth. Gradually beat in sour cream until mixture is smooth.
Spread over gelatin.
Chill.
Dissolve lemon jello in hot water.
Add vinegar and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Pour a thin layer into mold and chill until firm. Chill remaining jello until slightly thickened.
Combine apples, celery, nuts and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and fold into slightly thickened jello.
Pour into mold over firm layer.
When jello is completely firm, take out of mold and serve on top of lettuce with mayonnaise.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease baking pan.
Place fish on bed of onions in prepared pan.
Combine mushrooms, tomatoes, green pepper and parsley.
Spread mixture over fish.
Combine wine, lemon juice, salt and pepper; pour over vegetables and fish. Cover pan with foil.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until fish flakes easily.
Serve with lemon slices.
Mix yeast and sugar in warm water; let stand until foam appears.
In a food processor, mix the dry ingredients.
Slowly add the liquid mixture.
Add the egg.
The mixture will form a ball.
Remove to a floured surface and knead briefly.
Let rise 1 hour.
Form into rolls or loaf.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 minutes for loaf or 20 minutes for rolls.
Heat oil in a skillet.
Add meat, spices and salt.
Cook for 20 minutes.
Add peas and cook for 10 more minutes, stirring often.
Add water.
Bring to a boil and add washed rice.
Brew a pot of coffee.
Add flavorings.
Pour into cups and add one teaspoon cocoa and one teaspoon sugar per cup.
Garnish with whipped cream on top, along with chocolate and red candy sprinkles and a chocolate-covered strawberry on top.
Slice squash about 1/2-inch thick.
Cook until done.
Drain well.
Mash with butter, salt, pepper and onion.
Add dressing, eggs and corn.
Put in casserole dish.
Sprinkle top with dressing and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine gelatin and water; chill until beginning to set.
Whip the cranberry juice; fold sauce and lemon juice into thickened gelatin.
Set aside.
Combine beef, soy sauce, carrots, celery, onion, rice and water.
Steam for 15 minutes (add no salt).
After steaming, add mushroom soup and cream of chicken soup.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°. Add chow mein noodles last 15 minutes.
Spread tortilla with refried beans.
Brown meat. Add chopped onion, celery and sliced water chestnuts.
Stir and cook until crisp and tender.
Add onion soup mix and pepper. Stir and add mushroom soup. Remove from skillet and put in casserole dish.
Top with Chinese noodles. Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
6 to 8 servings.
Soy sauce may be added if desired.
Line a 10 1/2x15 1/2-inch jellyroll pan with aluminum foil, extending foil over ends of pan; grease foil.
Melt butter in a heavy Dutch oven over low heat; stir in sweetened condensed milk and milk.
Add all of the chips; stir until smooth.
Remove from heat; stir in marshmallow creme and extracts.
Stir in walnuts. Spread mixture into prepared pan.
Chill 1 hour.
Use ends of foil to lift fudge from pan.
Cut into 1-inch pieces.
Store in an airtight container in refrigerator.
Yield:
12 dozen pieces.
In medium bowl cream the cream cheese, jalapenos, onion, garlic and chili powder.
Fold in chicken and 1 1/2 cups of Jack cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread mixture on insides of split pita bread.
Put on baking sheets.
Bake at 400° for 5 to 10 minutes, until very hot.
Cover with remaining cheese (Jack and Cheddar).
Continue baking until cheese is melted.
Cut each pita half into 3 wedges.
Serve with salsa (optional).
Makes about 72 wedges.
Cook vegetables until tender.
Drain well.
Put in casserole dish.
Combine soup and sour cream and pour on top of vegetables. Sprinkle with onion rings.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes or until bubbly hot.
Brown beef in 10-inch skillet; drain.
Stir in rice, water, salt and onion.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and cook on low heat until water is absorbed, 25 minutes.
Stir in cheese until it softens.
Combine tomato sauce and chili powder.
Pour over rice mixture.
Cover and heat 5 minutes, until hot.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Use 2 medium yellow summer squash or zucchini or medium eggplant.
Cut squash or zucchini into 1/4 inch slices.
Place in plastic bag.
Add the Italian dressing and shake to coat thoroughly.

In a separate bag place the cheese and bread crumbs. Add the coated vegetable slices, close bag and shake to coat. Using a nonstick pan sprayed with cooking spray, add the vegetables in a single layer.
Bake in preheated 450° oven for 5 to 7 minutes, just until tender and crisp.
If using eggplant, slice into 3/4 inch thick slices.
Moisten with the Italian dressing and roll in the cheese bread crumb mixture.
Bake for 5 to 7 minutes at 475°, turn and bake other side for another 5 minutes.
Yield:
4 servings.
Carbohydrate 7 g, protein 3 g, fat 3 g, calories 61.
Sprinkle yeast over warm water.
Allow to soften for 5 minutes. Stir onion soup mix into 2 cups water.
Simmer, covered, 12 minutes.
Mix in sugar, salt and shortening; cool.
Stir 2 cups flour into onion soup mix; add yeast and enough flour to make moderately stiff dough.
Knead on board sprinkled with flour and cheese until dough is smooth, about 10 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; let rise until doubled.
Divide into two parts.
Let rest 15 minutes.
Shape into long tapered loaves.
Grease baking sheet. Coat with cornmeal.
Arrange loaves so they do not touch.
Make 1/4-inch deep diagonal slice in tops at 3-inch intervals.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Brush loaves with a mixture of egg white and water. Continue to bake 15 minutes more.
Remove; place on wire rack to cool.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Put all ingredients into oven-going casserole and mix thoroughly.
Add fresh mushrooms last.
Cover and place in 325° oven for 3 hours.
Take to the table in casserole right from the oven.
I use this a lot on holidays.
Preheat oven to 425°.
In a 9 x 13-inch baking dish, layer the ingredients in the following order:
butter, crumbs, fish, salt and pepper, lemon juice, cheese and sour cream.
Bake 20 minutes. Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Makes 4 servings.
Place vanilla wafers in a cupcake paper in a muffin pan.
Mix cream cheese, eggs, sugar and vanilla.
Pour mixture over vanilla wafers; fill about 1/2 full.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes or until golden brown; cool.
Spoon pie filling over cooled cheesecake.
Soften yeast in warm water and set aside.
Heat milk and add brown sugar, oil, yeast mixture and soda.
Pour all at once over dry ingredients (wheat flour, gluten flour, salt and wheat germ). Stir until well mixed.
If too soft, add a little more wheat flour. Pour onto board with whole wheat flour and knead until it is elastic.
Set into oiled bowl and turn dough over in the bowl so top has been oiled.
Cover, let rise.
When double in size, shape into loaves and place into well-greased pans.
Let rise until double and bake in 350° oven for approximately 30 minutes.
Drain apricots, reserving 1 cup juice.
Drain pineapple.
Mix reserved apricot juice with pudding and cook until thick.
Cool. Add fruits and pecans.
Chill overnight.
In large bowl, combine cream cheese, sour cream, milk and Worcestershire sauce and beat until fluffy.
Stir in rest of ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve hot with crackers.
Makes 4 cups.
Fry hamburger, celery and onions together until done. Add remaining ingredients. Put into baking dish. Sprinkle top with chow mein noodles or potato chips, crushed. Bake an hour or more at 325°.
Fry bacon; drain fat.
Add onions.
Fry until onions sweat. Put potatoes in casserole raw.
Add apples and bacon-onion mixture.
Add 1 handful of sugar, a glug of apple cider vinegar and salt and pepper to taste.
Mix well.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Lightly spray baking pan or casserole dish with vegetable spray (like Pam).
In a small bowl, combine lemon juice, oil and garlic.
Set aside.
Rinse chicken; pat dry. Arrange chicken in prepared pan or dish.
Pour lemon juice mixture over chicken.
I lightly salt my chicken before pouring lemon juice mixture over it, then I sprinkle lightly with lemon pepper. Cover and bake about 40 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes or longer to brown.
Cream shortening and sugar. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well. Add buttermilk, alternating with flour, soda, salt and baking powder. Add orange rind. Bake 1 hour in tube pan at 325°.
In saucepan combine sugar, cornstarch, salt, water, syrup and raisins.
Cook and stir until bubbly.
Cook 2 minutes more. Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice and margarine.
Pour filling into pastry lined pie plate glass pie dish; filling will be thin.
Cover with top crust.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Reduce temperature to 375° and bake 30 minutes more or until crust is golden brown.
Makes 8 servings.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder together.
To this cut in the shortening.
To this add milk and egg mixture.
Stir until makes a soft dough.
Roll out very thin.
Spread softened butter over dough.

Sprinkle with brown sugar, raisins and cinnamon. Begin at edge nearest you and roll up like you would a jelly roll. Cream 6 tablespoons butter and 6 tablespoons brown sugar and spread thickly on bottom and sides of baking pan or skillet.
With sharp knife cut the dough in 2 inch pieces and place in pan with cut side up.
Let stand 20 minutes.
Cook at 425° for 25 minutes.
Remove at once, upside-down.

Fry onion and pepper slowly in butter until golden. Add tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes. Add seasonings and drained beans. Alternate layers of bean mixture and cheese in a greased 1-quart casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Cook jello according to package.
Chill until partially set. Add pineapple, cheese and nuts.
Fold in whipped cream.
Chill until firm.
Marinate breast several hours in milk.
Cut breast into fingers; salt and pepper to taste.
Roll or shake fingers in flour.
Heat oil in pan; fry until brown.
Allow 1/4 to 1/3 pound per person.
Put vegetables in 2-quart microwavable bowl.
Microwave on High for 3 minutes.
Add milk, white sauce mix, cheese and 1/2 can onions.
Microwave, covered, on High for 8 minutes.
Stir once and sprinkle remaining onions.
Microwave, uncovered, 1 minute. Serves 6.
Separate eggs. Beat whites separately until stiff.
Beat sugar and yolks until fluffy.
Add flour and baking powder.
Fold in by hand the walnuts (pecans) and vanilla.
Add to egg whites and fold.
Grease 3 round cake pans.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes. Allow to cool.
Ice with a good chocolate icing between layers.
Peel and dice potatoes.
Place in a Dutch oven; cover with water.
Boil until tender.
Drain and place in a very large bowl (or back in Dutch oven).
Add sour cream, milk, butter, salt and pepper to taste.
Beat on medium-low speed until light and fluffy. Stir in 2 cups cheese, the bacon and green onions.
Transfer to a greased 3-quart baking dish.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted.
Serves 14.
Remove core from fennel and slice.
Reserve some sprigs for garnish.
Peel potatoes and chop coarsely.
In medium soup pot, heat butter and oil over low heat.
Add leeks; saute, stirring occasionally until soft.
Add fennel and potatoes; continue sauteing for 10 more minutes, or until softened.
Add chicken stock; bring to simmer.
Partially cover and cook 30 minutes.
Cook squash and onion in salt water about 5 minutes.
Drain well; set aside.
Cook green pepper and ground beef until meat is no longer pink.
Stir in rice.
Blend eggs, soup, sour cream and seasoning and stir into meat mixture.
Fold in squash mixture and turn into a greased, shallow 2-quart baking dish.
Top with cheese.
Sprinkle with paprika, if desired.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Boil noodles to taste.
Add mushroom soup, chicken soup, sour cream and corn.
Add noodles when done.
Heat and eat.
Break cauliflower into flowerets and cook in small amount of boiling salted water until tender (8 to 12 minutes).
Meanwhile, place the cheese soup, milk, pepper, pimento and Tabasco in saucepan.
Cover and cook slowly until it starts to boil.
Drain cauliflower and pour the sauce over it.
Serve immediately. Yield: 8 servings.
Heat milk and add cabbage.
Simmer about 5 minutes.
Mix flour and butter; stir in a little of the hot milk.
Stir this mixture into the cabbage and cook 4 to 5 minutes or until thickened, stirring constantly.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot. Makes 4 servings.
Cream butter, gradually add sugar, beat until fluffy.
Add egg, beat in oil.
Combine flour, cream of tartar and soda and add. Stir in vanilla.
Chill dough 2 hours (I usually chill overnight). Shape in 1 inch balls, dip tip in sugar, flatten with fork.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Store in airtight container.
Layer with wax paper.
Makes 4 to 5 dozen cookies.
Heat oil in frying pan.
Sprinkle in wine and pour in soup stock immediately, then add sweet corn and mix well.
Cook until soup boils.
Season with salt.
Add mushrooms, tomatoes and lima beans.
When it boils again, reduce the heat to low and pour in the cornstarch paste slowly.
Stir well until thickened.
Beat egg white and sprinkle into soup carefully.
Turn off heat immediately.
Pour into soup bowl and serve.
Cook onions in butter until tender.
Add mushrooms and cook 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add other ingredients except fish. Mix.
Place fish in a single layer in well-greased baking dish. Cover fish evenly with stuffing mix.
Place in 400° oven for 25 minutes or until fish flakes easily.
Serves 6.
Combine crumbs and butter.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Save 1/4 cup crumbs.
Chill.
Combine Jell-O with water, sugar and orange juice.
Heat until Jell-O and sugar dissolve.
Chill until partially set.
Chill evaporated milk thoroughly.
Whip and fold into partially set Jell-O with orange peel.
Pile over crumb crust.
Sprinkle with remaining crumbs.
Chill until firm.
In blender, mash beans with liquid to make a paste.
Brown ground beef and onions.
Drain grease.
Add beans, ketchup, and tabasco.
Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.
Place in shallow casserole and cover with grated cheese and olives.
Serve with corn chips or tortilla chips.
Boil berries in water and sugar until all berries burst open. Remove from fire.
Add gelatin and marshmallows.
Stir until melted and dissolved.
Add all other ingredients.
Mix well. Chill.
Put rice in bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Top with game hens.
Add water and spices from rice package.
Add celery, green onions, water chestnuts, mushrooms and wine.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream butter in bowl; add sugar, molasses, spices and soda and mix well.
Stir in almonds. Sprinkle 1/2 cup flour onto work surface.
Add remaining 3 cups flour gradually, mixing well after each addition.
Turn onto floured surface.
Knead until smooth.
Shape into 2 long rolls; wrap each in wax paper.
Chill or freeze until ready to bake.
Cut with sharp knife into thin slices.
Place on greased 10 x 15-inch cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Mix dry ingredients.
Pour margarine over and form into balls. Dip in chocolate melted with wax in double boiler.
Heat oven to 350° (moderate.)
Arrange potatoes, bologna, green pepper, flour and seasonings in layers in 1 1/2-quart baking dish, dotting each layer with butter.
Pour milk over and bake 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.

recipes.t: Farmer'S Bread With Ham, Cheese And White Sauce
d: Arrange 8 slices of farmer's bread on cookie sheet.
Cover farmer's bread with 2 slices each of ham; top with 1/2 cup Monterey Jack cheese.
Salt and pepper all 8 slices.
Close sandwiches.
Spoon white sauce over each sandwich.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Broil for 4 minutes in oven until bubbly. Serve at once.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook potatoes until tender.
Melt 3 tablespoons of margarine in a large skillet.
Add onions and cook over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until translucent. Increase heat to medium and cook 5 to 7 minutes longer, stirring occasionally, until golden.
Drain potatoes, reserving 1 cup cooking water and return to pot.
Add reserved cooking water, remaining margarine, the salt and pepper.
Mash smooth with potato masher.
Stir in onions and parsley.
Place one package frozen vegetables in a cup of boiling water with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Boil just enough to thaw; drain.
Place in buttered 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Blend together chicken and celery soups.
Put half the butter, half the onions and half the soup on top of vegetables.
Proceed with second package and place remaining soup, onion and butter on top.
Place can of onion rings on top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour, or put in microwave for 20 minutes on Medium heat.
Serves 8.
Combine cake mix, oil and water.
Stir until moistened.
Add eggs and stir until blended.
Let stand while spreading pie filling in bottom of Tupperware 3-quart casserole with cone inserted.
Pour in cake mix.
Microwave cake 14 minutes on 100% power or until cake begins to shrink away from sides of casserole. Let stand for 20 minutes, then invert on serving plate.
You have a cherry topped chocolate cake.
Recipe can be used with apple pie filling and carrot cake mix (or spice cake mix).
Also German chocolate cake mix with coconut pecan frosting for a self frosted German chocolate cake.
Cream together butter and powdered sugar.
Add egg yolks, chocolate, salt, vanilla and nuts.
Fold in egg whites.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan and put graham cracker crumbs on bottom.
Pour on filling and freeze 2 hours.
Spread ice cream on top; sprinkle with crumbs.
Freeze.
Cream margarine and sugar until light and fluffy; add eggs, beating well.
Blend in flour, vanilla and nuts.
Spoon batter into well-greased and lightly floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Cool and dust with powdered sugar, then cut into squares.
Cookies will fall as they cool.
Yield:
2 1/2 dozen.
Place tuna and Fritos in layers in casserole dish. Heat mushroom soup and milk in saucepan. Pour over tuna mixture. Place cheese slices over top. Bake in 375° oven for 30 minutes. Makes 4 servings.
Saute onion, celery and green pepper in butter, adding more butter, if needed.
Combine with cooked rice, sour cream, salt and chilies (seeded and chopped).
Spread mixture in a greased casserole, saving half the mixture.
Sprinkle cheese and half the Monterey Jack cheese over top of mixture.
Add remaining rice mixture and top with remaining Monterey Jack.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In frying pan, use spray or a little oil to brown chicken. Turn down heat and simmer in its own juice until done (45 minutes to 1 hour).
Add a little water to pan if chicken gets dry cooking.
As chicken simmers, cook spinach; drain well.
Also make sauce.
(You can double sauce recipe if you want to have sauce to pour over rice or noodles as part of menu.)
Combine and whisk milk, cornstarch, bouillon, caraway seed and pepper until smooth. Cook and stir on medium heat until thickened and bubbly.
Add cheese and blend until melted.
Carefully watch because sauce may burn, so adjust heat lower if needed.
Use serving platter and arrange spinach on platter.
Place chicken on top and spoon sauce over chicken.
Slices of lemon added on each side makes a colorful presentation.
Good for when company comes.
Mix flour, sugar, and milk for the batter.
Melt butter in square baking dish (approximately 10 x 10 inches).
Pour batter mixture into the melted butter.
Add can of fruit pie filling. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Melt butter.
Pour into shallow baking dish.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix juice, honey and mustard in small bowl.
Sprinkle chops with salt.
Place in dish.
Arrange carrots and potatoes around chops.
Pour honey-mustard mixture over all. Bake 35 to 40 minutes or until chops are tender.
Combine the first 4 ingredients with wire whip.
Add onions. Gradually add oil while beating.
Add celery seed.
Refrigerate. Good on tossed salads (greens).
In a saute pan on medium heat, melt margarine, coconut, pecans and sugar.
Saute until slightly browned.
Cool.
Next blend cream cheese, sugar and Cool Whip until well mixed.
Make lime Jell-O; chill until it is the consistency of unbeaten egg white.
Beat with mixer until it gets foamy; gradually add bits of softened cream cheese and beat well.
Add sour cream and continue beating.
Blend in crushed pineapple; pour into mold and refrigerate.
Combine oats, coconut, nuts, sunflower seeds, sesame seed and wheat germ in a large bowl.
Heat together oil and honey in microwave or on stovetop until almost boiling.
Stir into dry mixture, mixing well.
Spread a third of mixture in shallow pan. Bake at 325° for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Repeat with remaining mixture.
In four separate bowls, dissolve each package of jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup cold water to each and stir.
Pour one bowl of blue jello into an oiled 10-inch fluted tube pan. Chill until almost set, about 30 minutes.
Set the other three bowls of jello aside, at room temperature.
Cook bacon and onion in a saucepan until bacon is lightly browned and onion is tender.
Blend in flour.
Add milk.
Cook and stir until bubbly.
Dice potatoes.
Add with thyme, 1 teaspoon of salt and 1/8 teaspoon of pepper.
Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes or until potatoes are done.
Stir in beans and heat completely. Top with your parsley.
In a large pan, melt butter over low heat (do not brown). Stir in mushroom soup/water mixture and mushrooms; heat until very warm.
Stir in gently the sour cream and heat (do not boil).
Stir in rice, ham and chicken.
Simmer gently.
(If mixture seems too thick, add water.)
Add cheese; combine all and heat until cheese melts.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle with parsley for decoration.
Dot with butter and thin with water to reheat leftovers in microwave.
Melt margarine. Add marshmallows. Stir until melted. Add dry gelatin. Mix and pour over popcorn.
In a large mixing bowl cream butter and sugar together until smooth.
Beat together eggs and milk and add to butter mixture. Blend well, then add flour and baking powder and mix lightly. Stir in corn syrup and vanilla.
Add pineapple, macaroons and macadamia nuts.
Blend well and pour into greased and floured loaf pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour and 40 minutes or until center tests done.
Bring tomatoes, water, salt and pepper to a boil in a large pot.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 to 10 minutes; then remove from heat and add baking soda, stirring constantly.
(It will overflow if you are not careful.)
After bubbling stops, return to low heat and add the margarine.
Stir well.
When melted and smooth, it is ready to eat.
(Good with oyster crackers or saltines.)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown meat, add salt.
Split English muffins and spread with margarine.
Place on baking sheet.
Spread pizza sauce on muffins, then add meat.
Put onion, pepper and mushrooms on top of this.
Cover with cheese.
Heat about 15 minutes, until cheese melts and muffins begin to brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift flour with salt; set aside.
In large bowl, beat margarine, shortening, sugar, cream and vanilla until smooth and fluffy.
Stir in flour mixture until well combined.
Stir in nuts.
Drop by teaspoonfuls, 2-inches apart, onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or just until light golden brown.
Remove to wire rack; cool.
Trim meat and cut into small chunks.
Place meat in a microsafe dish.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Add 1/2 cup water. Microwave at High power for about 12 minutes, turning meat over and around after 6 minutes.
Add vinegar, bouillon cubes, chili powder, onions and green pepper.
Add another 1/4 cup water. Microwave at High power for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring once during cooking.
Chop garlic very fine, chop basil, cilantro and parsley in food processor.
Add garlic and tomatoes; mix well.
Add olive oil and balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper.
Use as you would salsa as a dip or use with meat.
Cook filling until thickened and cool (raisins, sugar, water, 2 tablespoons flour and walnuts).
Mix together oats, 2 cups flour, baking soda and salt in one bowl.
Mix together brown sugar, melted oleo and vanilla in another bowl.
Combine the two mixtures.
Work with fingers until well mixed.
Put half mixture in 9 x 12-inch pan.
Pat firmly.
Put cooked filling on top.
Top with other half of mixture.
Pat firmly.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Drain sauerkraut.
Mix red wine vinegar and sugar in saucepan; bring to a boil.
Mix chopped vegetables.
Pour boiling liquid over vegetables and toss.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Mix all dry ingredients; add cocoa.
Mix applesauce, oil and nuts.
Stir well.
Bake in 10 x 13-inch aluminum foil lined pan. Bake for 1 hour at 325°.
Split, bone and quarter breasts.
Shake in bag with flour, salt and pepper.
Brown chicken in a little oil.
Take chicken out and set aside in casserole.
Add remaining ingredients to drippings.
Cook and blend for 1 minute.
Cool and pour over chicken.
This may be refrigerated or bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
In a saucepan, combine chili and salsa; simmer 15 minutes. Crumble chips into serving dish.
Spoon hot chili mix over chips. Top with lettuce and cheese.
Add more salsa, if desired.
Serves 6.
Simply peel, dice and boil potatoes until tender.
Boil your eggs for 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain water from potatoes while your eggs are cooling.
Peel eggs; dice and add to potatoes.
Use seasoned salt to taste, a dash of regular salt, 3 to 4 dashes of pepper and 2 to 2 1/2 tablespoons of mayo; stir.
Mix in 5 to 6 dashes of paprika.
Combine the first 3 ingredients and let cook until rice is soft, or until water is all cooked out.
Bring 2 cups milk to a boil.
Add the eggs, 2 cups sugar and 2 tablespoons flour to make a paste.
Add a little milk.
Add all of this to the rice, and cook until thick.
Keep stirring until done.
When finished, add 1 tablespoon vanilla.
Let cool.
Whip 1 can of Carnation milk and 2 tablespoons sugar.
Add to the rice.
Prepare spaghetti according to package instructions.
Rinse in cool water.
Add broccoli florets, cherry tomatoes and black olives to spaghetti.
Pour Italian dressing over pasta and vegetables.
Cover and marinate in refrigerator for at least 2 hours. Toss mixture occasionally.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese before serving.
Brown meat and onions until tender.
Drain; add corn and all other ingredients.
Mix well, then add cooked noodles.
Put in casserole dish; top with 1 cup bread crumbs.
Melt 1/4 cup butter and pour over top.
Sprinkle with paprika and bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Jack'S Favorite Cookies(President John F. Kennedy)
d: Cream butter, add sugar, egg, lemon juice and rind.
Mix well. Add dry ingredients and nuts.
Mix well.
Form into a roll about 2 inches in diameter; wrap in wax paper and chill in refrigerator until ready for use.
Slice and bake on ungreased cookie sheets for 10 to 12 minutes at 400°.
Makes 4 dozen.
Pour sugar over apples.
Mix thoroughly and let stand while preparing batter.
Sift together flour, soda, nutmeg and salt into large mixing bowl.
Beat eggs and corn oil together.
Add to dry ingredients and continue beating until smooth.
Stir in vanilla, apple-sugar mixture (including juice), raisins and nuts.
Continue stirring until evenly distributed through batter.
If apples are not real juicy, add a little water.
Pour batter into well-oiled tube pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour.
If preferred, can add a glaze for topping, although it's delicious plain.
Cook, debone and chunk chicken.
Saute broccoli and onion in margarine.
Cube the Velveeta cheese.
Cook the rice in the 2 cups of water and salt according to directions on box less 5 minutes. Combine all ingredients in large casserole dish and bake at 350° until cheese melts.
"My family likes crushed potato chips on top."
In medium size heavy saucepan, combine brown sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt.
Mix well. Stir in water; cook over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil and thickens.
Stir in vanilla. Serve warm.
Store in refrigerator.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
In wok or large skillet, heat the oil briefly.
If using fresh garlic and/or ginger, add and stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add the broccoli, carrots and onions, tossing the vegetables to mix them well.
Add the water, cover and cook for 3 minutes over medium heat.
Remove cover and turn the heat to high.
Cook the vegetables, stirring them 5 minutes longer or until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
If using garlic powder or ground ginger, add and mix in soy sauce.
Remove from heat and serve.
Boil the first 4 ingredients 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add the soda and vanilla.
Pop approximately 2 gallons popcorn. Cover popcorn with syrup mixture.
Bake on 2 cookie sheets at 250° for 1 hour.
Stir every 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with lemon pepper.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium heat.
Add chops; brown on each side until done.
Transfer to a platter and keep warm.
Add water to skillet, scraping to loosen browned particles.
Add preserves and onion soup mix. Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes.
Add peaches; cook 1 minute.
Spoon over pork chops.
Dump pineapple, fruit cocktail and oranges, undrained, in bowl and then add pudding mix and coconut.
Refrigerate.
Add bananas just before serving or omit if planning to keep for several days.
Saute
beef
and garlic in 2 tablespoons oil on medium-high heat.
Add bell pepper, onion, celery, carrots and beans; stir-fry for
minutes.
Add
tomato soup, tomato sauce and oregano flakes.
Add
water
is
sauce
is too thick.
Simmer until carrots and beans are tender.
Serves 4 to 5.
Cut chicken into bite-size pieces.
Mix with soups and water. Put in a 9 x 11-inch pan.
Sprinkle bread stuffing over this mixture; pour butter over it.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Put butter and oil in skillet over medium heat until butter melts and mixture bubbles.
Add wine, garlic, rosemary, oregano and onion.
Cook, stirring until wine evaporates and butter is golden.
Reduce heat and add tomatoes.
Cook until heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add shellfish, parsley, sugar and salt and pepper.
Stir until shellfish is heated through and serve over hot pasta.
Serves 6.
Brown beef; add celery and onion and brown slightly.
Add tomato sauce and cheese.
Cook on low heat about 20 minutes.
Cook macaroni in salted water; drain.
Add to meat mixture; add tomatoes.
Bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Add tomato juice if mixture dries a bit while baking.
Brown beef; add onion and salt and pepper to taste.
Stir until onion is tender.
Add sugar and tomato soup; mix well and set aside.
Cook and drain noodles.
Add chicken soup.
Place layer in casserole.
Place cheese layer on top.
Cover with meat mixture and then cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly and heated through.
Dissolve yeast in warm water and set aside.
Scald milk.
Add oleo, salt and honey.
Cool to lukewarm.
Add yeast mixture. Add whole wheat flour.
Add white flour, a cup at
a time.
Heat grill or oven to 375°.
In bowl, combine vegetables. Add oil and lemon juice.
Toss to coat evenly.
Place vegetables on grill pan or roasting pan.
Cook 20 minutes or until tender, turning occasionally.
Season with sea salt and pepper, if desired.
Cook mostaccioli according to directions.
Beat Ricotta cheese with milk until smooth. Drain pasta and return to pot.
Add Ricotta mixture.
Add Parmesan, sausage and tomato sauce.
Toss to combine.
Set aside for 5 minutes before serving.
Sift together 2 cups flour plus next 3 ingredients.
Stir in oats. Beat butter and sugar until creamy. Add lemon peel.
Beat in egg, egg yolks, cottage cheese and last 1/2 cup of flour.
Stir in raisins, candied fruit and nuts.
Dough will be stiff and biscuit like.
Divide dough in half.
Turn out on lightly floured board. With palms of hands, press each half into oval shape 1/2-inch thick. Fold in 1/2 lengthwise.
Lift to lightly greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Cool on rack. Decorate with frosting and candied cherries.
Cut onions into 1/4-inch slices.
This should be about 2-quarts. Separate the slices into rings.
Heat butter in skillet. Add onions, tossing them about with a wooden spoon until rings are coated with butter.
Add cloves and salt. Continue to cook over low heat until onions just start to brown. Add wine. Cover pan and simmer about 15 minutes.
Onions should be slightly crisp but tender.
Remove cover and cook until wine is reduced to a glaze. Serve at once. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
In blender, combine juice, extracts and ice cubes; blend until ice is coarsely chopped, about 1 minute.
Pour into chilled 16 ounce glass.
Stir in soda.
Calories: 54.
Heat olive oil and butter; add onion and garlic.
Cook until soft.
Add carrots; cook 4 minutes.
Add basil; cook 2 minutes. Add tomatoes; put sauce back into pan.
Add cream and curry.
Stir thoroughly.
Serve over pasta with freshly grated cheese.
Enjoy!
Make simple syrup by boiling sugar and water 5 minutes; set aside.
Combine tea and fruit juices.
Chill.
Just before serving, add ginger ale and syrup to taste.
Garnish with orange slices and mint sprigs.
Makes 12 servings.
Combine the sugar, cinnamon, butter and apples in a saucepan. Simmer this mixture until apples are tender.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine all ingredients, adding onions, bell pepper and mushrooms last (all chopped fine). Mix well.
Shape in a loaf pan.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Combine soup, milk and curry powder in 2-quart casserole. Stir in tuna, noodles, celery, raisins, almonds and 1/2 the onion rings.
Microwave at High 5 minutes.
Stir well.
Sprinkle on remaining onion rings.
Microwave 4 to 6 minutes until heated through.
Melt Velveeta cheese in microwave or saucepan.
Add soup, sausage and salsa.
Heat until hot.
Serve with tortilla chips or your favorite chips.
Preheat oven to 400°. In large bowl, combine potatoes, soup, 1/2 French-fried onions, sour cream and seasonings.
Spread potato mixture in 12 x 8-inch baking dish. Split frankfurters lengthwise, almost into halves. Arrange frankfurters, split side up, along center of casserole.
Bake, covered, at 400° for 30 minutes or until heated through. Fill frankfurter with remaining cheese and onions. Bake, uncovered, 1 to 3 minutes or until onions are golden brown. Yield: 6 servings.
Quarter, core and peel apples.
Cut into 1-inch cubes.
Spread evenly on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes until apples are tender but not mushy.
Remove from pan and cool.
Beat 1/2 cup margarine until creamy; add 1/2 cup sugar.
Beat well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Blend in sour cream.
Sift together 2 cups flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and 2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Fold into margarine.
Add apples, folding in gently.
Pour half of the mixture into a greased, wax paper lined and greased again 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Cut remaining margarine into remaining flour, sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg until crumblike.
Sprinkle half of the crumb mixture over the batter; pour in remaining batter.
Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes until browned, pulled away from the edges and a toothpick inserted near center has no sticky dough adhering to it.
Cool in pan on rack 10 minutes. Carefully remove from pan.
Bring first 3 ingredients to a boil and boil 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Then add 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1 cup coconut and 1/2 cup chopped nuts.
Pour over cake while still warm.

recipes.t: Baked Ziti With Ricotta And Sausage
d: In a medium saucepan,
melt 4 tablespoons of butter and add the flour. Stir and blend with a wire whisk and cook over medium heat for about
minutes.
Slowly
add
the
scalded chicken stock and wine
and keep whisking. Allow the sauce to simmer for about 15
minutes. Set
aside.
In
a medium bowl, combine the Ricotta with
half the
Asiago cheese, beaten egg and 1 tablespoon parsley;
add
salt and pepper to taste.
Mix well and set aside. In
a
medium
skillet,
heat the oil and saute the sausage over
medium-high
heat for a few minutes or until done; set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter a 10-inch spring-form pan.
For crust, mix cracker crumbs with melted butter and press into pan. In large mixer bowl, blend sugar and eggs until light and thick. Gradually add cream cheese.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in melted chocolate, Kahlua and cocoa.
Mix in sour cream.
Fold in melted butter, then add mini chocolate chips; pour into pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours; let cool, then refrigerate.
Remove outer rim of pan to serve.
Baking time can vary depending on oven.
Drain apricots and pineapple, separately.
Reserve 1 cup apricot syrup and 1 cup pineapple syrup.
Dissolve Jell-O in 2 cups hot water.
Stir in reserved apricot syrup; chill until partially thickened.
Stir in apricots, pineapple and marshmallows. Chill until firm.
Combine sugar, flour, egg and butter; stir in reserved pineapple syrup; cook over low heat until thickened. Cool.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spread over Jell-O mixture. Sprinkle with cheese.
In a 3-quart casserole, mix celery, stuffing and mushrooms. Layer turkey evenly over stuffing.
Combine and mix well the milk, eggs and soup.
Pour over turkey.
Sprinkle with almonds; sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.
Drizzle with butter.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes, until knife inserted in center comes out clean. Serves 8 to 10.
Brown pork steaks in large skillet, then remove pork to roasting pan.
Make gravy with flour, water, salt and pepper in skillet with meat drippings.
Add 1 teaspoon of instant coffee to gravy or enough to give gravy a nice brown color.
Place sliced potatoes and onion on top of meat; pour gravy over all.
Cover the roasting pan; bake at 300° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Combine salad dressing, curry powder, salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Add rice, chicken, celery, onions and peas; mix well. Chill for 2 hours minimum.
Makes 6 servings.
Dice onions, carrot and potatoes.
Chop garlic and saute in butter for about 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth.
Add fresh or canned tomatoes, chopped and seeded, and Ortega chilies.
Simmer until vegetables are done.
Add grated Monterey Jack cheese and Colby cheese, mixed together.
Add milk.
Bring to hot temperature, but do not allow to boil.
Your soup is ready to serve.
Enough for 4 cups.
