Peel bananas and place in a single layer in baking dish, just large enough to hold them.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine pineapple with juice, honey, lemon juice and cornstarch in a bowl; mix together.
Pour over bananas.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.
Sauce will bubble.
Cheap and kids will love it.
Using electric mixer, cream margarine, brown sugar, pudding mix and egg.
Sift flour, baking soda and spices.
Combine flour mixture with creamed mixture; chill.
Roll part of chilled dough out on a floured surface to 1/8 inch thickness.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove from cookie sheet to rack to cool.
Decorate.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Combine cream cheese and milk, mixing until well blended.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Chill.
Serve with veggies or chips or both.

Place 6 slices of buttered bread in buttered dish. Place 1/2 cheese and meat over bread. Add 6 slices of buttered bread, then rest of meat and cheese. Beat eggs. Add milk, onion and seasoning to eggs. Pour this over layered bread and meat. Place in refrigerator overnight. Bake at 350° in preheated oven 1 hour. Let stand 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove seeds from peppers.
Combine remaining ingredients; mix lightly.
Fill each pepper with approximately 1/3 cup rice mixture; place in shallow baking dish.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
In bowl, pour boiling water over gelatin.
Stir until Jell-O dissolves.
Gradually beat hot Jell-O into cream cheese until cream cheese melts and mixture is smooth.
Mix in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 8-cup mold, lightly brushed with salad oil.
Chill until firm.
Makes about 12 servings.
Saute onions over medium high heat in a Dutch oven until translucent, but not brown.
Add meat and brown until almost cooked.
Reduce the liquid in the pan until almost gone, being careful not to scorch.
Once reduced, add tomato paste, paprika, salt and pepper.
Simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Add remaining seasonings and cover with enough water to just cover the meat.
Simmer for 1/2 hour and adjust seasonings to taste.
Arrange sausage links in 8-inch square glass baking dish. Bake in preheated oven at 400° for 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Pour off any accumulated fat.
Drain tomatoes, saving juice.
Add tomatoes and corn to sausages, prepare muffin mix as directed on package, using eggs and 2/3 cup tomato juice for the liquid.
Pour over ingredients in baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for about 30 minutes or until corn bread is done. Cut into squares or spoon out to serve.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray a 4 x 8-inch loaf pan.
Combine both types of flour, brown sugar, baking powder and spices; mix well.
In separate bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Beat with fork until blended.
Blend together.
Place mixture in prepared pan.
Bake 35 minutes until center is done.
Cool on wire rack.
Prepare stuffing mix according to package directions.
Stir milk into soup.
In a greased 2-quart casserole, layer ingredients in the following order:
stuffing, broccoli, crabmeat and soup. Cover and bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Remove cover and continue baking for another 1/2 hour.
Spread cheese on top and bake another 5 to 10 minutes.
Mix together the vanilla pudding mix and the juice.
Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Cool completely.
Beat until fluffy.
Stir in 8 ounces "Cool Whip".
Refrigerate.
In a large bowl, beat bananas, sugar, oil, and egg.
In a medium bowl, combine both flours, baking soda and powder, and salt.
Add to banana mixture, stirring just until moist.
Stir in nuts or raisins.
Pour into a greased loaf pan.
Bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 45 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool on wire rack for 10 minutes.
Remove from pan to cool completely.
Crack eggs into bowl and stir until even consistency.
Pour bread crumbs onto a flat plate.
Pat dry pork chops with paper towel.
Dredge pork chop through flour to cover one side and turn over to cover the other side.
Apply medium downward pressure to the pork chops to improve adherence of the bread crumbs on the down side.
Flip pork chop once more in the bread crumbs and apply pressure again.
If the pork chop is thick, stand it on each edge in the bread crumbs to cover the sides as well as possible.
Heat oil in deep frying pan to 350° to 360°.
Place pork chops into the hot oil.
Turn after 2 to 3 minutes.
Continue frying until the outside is uniformly medium brown.
Total cooking time will be about 4 to 5 minutes.
Slice cooked pork chops into 1/2-inch thick strips and serve hot with tonkatsu sauce for dipping.
Dissolve lemon jello in boiling water and while still hot, stir in Grape-Nuts, raisins, walnuts, prunes and citron (all cut fine).
Also add cinnamon and cloves.
Salt to taste.
Mix and let harden in mold.
Turn out on large plate and garnish with holly. Serve with whipped cream or pudding sauce.
Blend butter, flour and nuts.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Cool completely.
Next blend cream cheese, sugar and Cool Whip.
Spread over the first layer, then mix pudding and milk.
Pour over the cake.
Top with Cool Whip and pecans.
Refrigerate.
Fry bacon until crisp; drain and set aside.
In bacon grease, fry onions with brown sugar (20 minutes; watch).
Before frying, add salt, garlic powder and mustard to onions.
Drain and add beans.
Mix together; put into casserole and add crumbled bacon to top.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 10 to 15.
Combine chicken with celery, grapes, pineapple, walnuts, onion and salt.
Add mayonnaise and toss lightly until mixed.
Whip cream and fold gently into chicken mixture.
Chill thoroughly.
Heat broth, onion, and broccoli to boiling.
Reduce heat. Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in potatoes until blended.
Stir in chicken, cheese and milk.
Brown sausage and drain.
Mix remaining ingredients together and then mix cooked sausage into ingredients; mix well.
Put in 9 x 13 casserole dish and top with a little grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
You can mix this the night before and put in the refrigerator and bake the next day.
If you put it in the oven cold, it will take longer to cook.
Combine steak sauce, brown sugar, lime juice and red pepper (reserve 2 tablespoons marinade).
Place beef steaks in plastic bag and add remaining marinade, turning to coat.
Close bag securely and marinate for 10 minutes.
Pour off marinade.
In medium bowl with fork, beat eggs and milk slightly.
Stir in shrimp, salt, pepper and mustard.
Meanwhile, toast English muffins.
Spread with butter; keep warm.
In an 8-inch skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tablespoon butter or margarine.
Add egg mixture and cook, stirring once or twice with fork, until eggs are set.
Spoon over muffin halves.
Marinate meat in vinegar, water, pickle spices and onion for 2 days, turning meat frequently.
Drain meat.
Brown all sides. Strain vinegar water.
Simmer meat in strained vinegar water until almost done.
Remove meat; carve in thin slices.
Mix ketchup, mustard, brown sugar and gingersnaps with vinegar water and flour to make gravy.
Put meat back in gravy.
Heat and serve over noodles or whatever.
Mix sugar and flour in a bowl.
In a boiler bring the oleo, cocoa, water and Crisco to a boil.
Boil for 1 minute and pour into dry ingredients.
Add buttermilk, vinegar, eggs, soda, vanilla and mix.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 11 x 16 pan.
Bake for 20 minutes at 400 degrees.
Melt butter in large saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in sugar, eggs and dates.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture leaves sides of pan, about 20 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add rice cereal, walnuts and vanilla.
Mix until well blended.
Let cool; shape into rolls about 3-inches long.
Roll in coconut.
Store in refrigerator.
Makes 4 dozen.
Cream together butter and
sugar.
Add
eggs one at a time. Beat thoroughly after each addition.
Sift flour before measuring and add a pinch of salt.
Alternate adding cream and flour, beating
all
the
time.
Add
almond
flavoring.
Use greased tube pan which has been sprinkled with flour.
Bake in 325° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Do not open oven door.
Cream the margarine or butter and Crisco together.
Add the sugar gradually, beating after each addition.
Beat the eggs until light and fluffy and add to the butter-sugar mixture, blending thoroughly.
Sift dry ingredients.
Add the flavorings to the milk.
Add dry ingredients alternately with the milk, beginning and ending with the flour.
When well blended, pour into a well-greased and lightly floured tube pan.
Bake at 350° for about an hour.
In a small bowl, use a spoon to stir together the melted margarine and cinnamon.
Put the popcorn in a large bowl.
Pour the margarine with cinnamon over the popcorn. Stir the popcorn to mix it with the margarine and cinnamon.
Crumble corn bread and bread.
Add onion soup mix, sage, pepper, salt and poultry seasoning.
Stir in eggs, celery soup, chicken soup and enough broth to make a very moist dressing. Place dressing in large roasting pan.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes, or until browned.
Stir once or twice during the first 20 minutes of baking.
Makes 12 to 14 servings.
Sift together flour, soda, cocoa and salt; set aside.
Cream butter and vanilla.
Add sugar gradually, creaming until fluffy. Add egg and beat thoroughly.
Alternately add water and dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Gradually add oats, stirring well.
Mix in chocolate chips.
Drop 2 inches apart on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° until done.
Don't overbake!

recipes.t: Gumdrop Coconut Cookies(Another Christmas Favorite Of The Seiter Children)
d: Cream sugar and butter or shortening.
Add eggs, water and vanilla.
Continue beating.
Add remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet and bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes until lightly browned.

recipes.t: Pasta Salad With Fresh Tomato And Basil Sauce
d: Cook pasta and drain.
In the meantime, cut up fresh tomatoes into eighths and saute garlic in olive oil.
Add tomatoes to olive oil and garlic.
Add dried spices, herbs and hot pepper.
Add green peppers and fresh basil.
Cook on low for about 15 minutes, stirring often.
Put cooked pasta in bowl; coat with olive oil and add hot pasta sauce, removing hot pepper first.
Serve at once and top with freshly grated Romano cheese.
If you add pine nuts, add them to pasta sauce at the last minute.
Put ham pieces in bottom of pan.
Place chicken on top of ham. Put bacon slices on top of chicken.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Mix sour cream and mushroom soup together and pour over chicken. Bake, covered, at 300° for 3 hours.
Stir and serve over rice.
Mix V-8 juice and Tabasco sauce.
Marinate chicken in this for 3 hours in refrigerator, then 1/2 hour at room temperature.
Drain and throw away the marinade.
Put cornflake crumbs and all seasonings in plastic bag.
Shake 1 piece at a time and place in a shallow baking dish that has been sprayed with Pam.
Sprinkle any leftover coating on chicken.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes. Sprinkle cheese and return to oven until cheese melts.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Measure juice and add water to make 2 cups.
Boil juice and pour over Jell-O.
Cool in refrigerator until thickened.
Beat the cream cheese into gelatin.
Whip the cream and fold into gelatin. Arrange oranges in mold and pour gelatin mixture over them or just mix oranges in.
Refrigerate until thickened.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Melt caramels with 1/3 cup evaporated milk in double boiler. Mix cake mix, margarine, 1/3 cup evaporated milk and nuts.
Press 1/2 of mixture in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 6 minutes. Sprinkle chips over this crust; pour the caramel mix on and dab the remaining cake mixture on top.
Bake an additional 15 to 20 minutes at 350°.
Let cool.
Cut in squares.
Brown ground beef and onion in skillet; drain grease.
Add can of chili, Cheez Whiz and kidney beans.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring as needed.
Place prepared ingredients on top of corn chips, lettuce and tomato; top with grated cheese.
Add optional ingredients, if you use (ripe olives and sour cream).
Cover chicken parts with broth in a 5-quart saucepot.
Add all remaining ingredients, except noodles.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Partially cover, reduce heat to low and simmer about 1 hour, until chicken is very tender, but not yet falling off the bones.
As chicken, cooks, skim fat off surface every 20 minutes. Remove from heat.

recipes.t: Chicken And Mushrooms With Wine Sauce
d: On top of stove over medium heat, put butter, onions and garlic in large skillet.
Saute until onions are soft.
Add chicken and broth and cover until chicken is cooked.
Add mushrooms and wine and simmer until soft.
Remove chicken breasts; add thickening to make sauce.
Serve chicken on rice with sauce ladled on top.
Sprinkle legs with salt and pepper.
Turn them in oil to coat. Arrange skin side down in one layer in a baking dish.
Place in a 425° oven and bake 50 minutes.
Turn skin side up and sprinkle with mixture of bread crumbs, onion, garlic, parsley, thyme and rosemary.
Bake 1/2 hour longer.
Baste and cook another 10 minutes longer.
Pour around (not over) 1/3 cup dry white wine and bake 10 minutes longer.
Total cooking time is 1 hour and 40 minutes.

Arrange chicken pieces in bottom of greased 9 x 13 pan. Mix soups and mayonnaise. Stir well. Pour over chicken. Sprinkle shredded cheese over all. Sprinkle stuffing crumbs over all. Drizzle melted butter over top. Cover and bake 1 hour at 350 degrees. Uncover and bake 10 more minutes.
Heat 1 cup cherry juice and Port.
Pour remaining juice over plain
gelatin.
Put
both gelatins together and dissolve in the hot cherry juice.
Stir and mix together.
Add cherries stuffed with pecan halves. Put in mold.
Serves 6.
Beat butter, sugar and eggs until light and fluffy.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Make into 2 rectangles of dough. Roll into waxed paper.
Chill overnight. Slice very thin (1/4-inch or less).
Bake in a 350° oven until golden on the edges.
Remove immediately from cookie sheet.
These freeze well.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water; set aside to cool.
Combine cream cheese and mayonnaise; blend well.
Stir into gelatin along with all remaining ingredients, except whipped topping.
Fold in whipped topping.,
Spoon into an 8-inch square pan; refrigerate until firm.
Cut into squares.
Yield: 9 servings.
Put butter and molasses over medium heat and bring to a boil. Remove and add soda; then beat well.
When cool add milk and well beaten eggs.
Add dry ingredients, sifted together.
Mix well. Bake in well-greased and floured pan in a 350° oven for 40 minutes. Serve warm with country butter or topped with whipped cream.
Place beef in a 3-quart microproof casserole; break up with a spoon.
Add onions and garlic.
Cook on High 5 to 6 minutes or until beef is no longer red; drain.
Stir again to break up beef. Stir in enchilada sauce and tomato sauce.
Cook on High 3 minutes. Stir in beans, 1 cup corn chips and 3/4 cup cheese.
Cover; cook on High 6 minutes; stir.
Spread sour cream evenly over top. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups corn chips and 1/4 cup cheese.
Cook on Medium-high for 1 to 2 minutes until sour cream is warm.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Microwave frozen green beans and water in a 2-quart casserole dish, 15 minutes, or until tender.
Stir once during cooking. Drain.

Place cream cheese, salt and garlic salt in a bowl and microwave approximately 1 minute or until cheese is very soft. Gradually add the milk to the cream cheese and stir until smooth. Microwave another 1 to 2 minutes, stirring once while cooking. Blend sauce until thoroughly mixed and pour over green beans. Stir lightly and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
In a medium saucepan off the heat, mix the brown sugar, cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and coffee to dissolve the sugar. Whisk in the ketchup and corn oil.
Bring sauce to a boil and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes to blend flavors; cool.
Soak tapioca in water overnight or a couple of hours.
In saucepan beat eggs.
Add sugar and continue beating until blended. Add milk.
Stir and add tapioca and water.
Stir.
Cook until it thickens, stirring constantly. Boil 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and almond or 1/2 teaspoon almond and 1/2 teaspoon lemon extract.
Cool and serve.
Serves 6 people or 2 servings for David.
Add boiling water to gelatin.
Stir to dissolve, then add ice milk and lemon juice.
Pour into crust and chill.
Combine sugar, corn syrup, water and salt.
Simmer 10 minutes. Cool.
In a large bowl, stir mixture into peanut butter and raisins.
Spoon over fresh fruit cup.
Yields 1 1/3 cups.
Combine the chicken, onion, celery and green pepper.
Mix the cream, mayonnaise, salt, pepper and vinegar for dressing.
Add the cashews.
Combine chicken mixture and dressing.
Heat in oven, if desired to serve hot, at 450° for 15 minutes.

In small saucepan, place butter and cream to boil. Simmer 1 minute and reduce to low to thicken slightly. In separate pan, bring water to a boil and follow pasta package instructions. Drain when finished. In another saucepan, boil small amount of water; boil spinach a few minutes and drain very well, squeezing out excess water. In same pan, rinse and dry, then add olive oil and chopped garlic. Saute briefly, then add drained spinach and mix well.
Melt sugar in heavy saucepan until medium brown.
Stir.
Scald milk with butter and blend with sugar.
Cook until smooth, remove from fire.
Add sugar and beat until all is used.
Add vanilla and sprinkle with nuts, if desired.
Slice carrots and celery together. Then slice onion and cabbage. Place in a 3-quart saucepan.
Saute onion and garlic in butter until golden brown.
Add pepper.
Cut cooked shrimp into 1/2-inch pieces and add to onion mixture.
Mix well and cool.
Cut each potato lengthwise into 4 equal wedges.
Set aside. Place butter in 10-inch square casserole.
Microwave on High for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes or until butter melts.
Add potatoes, turning to coat with butter.
In small bowl, combine remaining ingredients. Sprinkle over potatoes.
Cover.
Microwave on High for 14 to 18 minutes or until potatoes are tender, rearranging potatoes twice. Let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Have everything chilled.
Mix orange juice, lemonade, pineapple juice, vodka and soda together until frozen juice is melted.
Then add strawberries while still frozen.
Stir. Serves 35.
Place meat of choice in bottom of baking dish.
Add potatoes, beans and carrots.
Cover with soup.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain pineapple and mandarins.
Add enough water to make 1 1/2 cups liquid, heat.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot fruit water.
Add sherbet and the remaining water, mix.
Add softened cream cheese, carrots and pineapple.
Pour into a mold, top with mandarins, freeze.
Serves 6 to 8.
Reserve 1 cup dry cake mix.
In large mixing bowl, combine remaining cake mix, 1 egg and oil.
Mixture will be crumbly.
Press mix evenly on bottom and up 3/4 of the side of a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
In same bowl, blend the cream cheese and sugar.
Add 3 eggs and reserved cake mix.
Beat 1 minute at medium speed.
At low speed, add milk, lemon juice and food color.
Mix until smooth. Pour into crust and bake at 300° for 50 to 60 minutes, until center is firm.
Chill.
Spread topping before serving.
Partially freeze rolls, then cut them in half.
Melt margarine. Add rest of ingredients.
Saute on low heat for 5 minutes.
Spread on both sides of rolls.
Place slices of ham and cheese on rolls. Wrap in foil and heat for 10 to 15 minutes at 350°.
Mix sugar, margarine, milk and cocoa; heat over medium heat until sugar is dissolved.
Add to the sugar mix, oatmeal, coconut, peanut butter, salt, vanilla and marshmallows.
Remove from heat. Stir to mix all thoroughly as marshmallows will melt.
Drop by spoonfuls on cookie sheet.
Allow to cool.
Cook onion and green pepper in butter until tender.
Cut half of pepperoni slices into fourths.
Toss onion, green pepper, pepperoni and cheese with flour.
Add milk, eggs and seasonings. Pour into prepared pastry shell.
Gently place remaining pepperoni slices around edge of pie.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes at 350°, until set.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Makes 6 servings.
Form ground beef into patties.
Cook and drain patties.
Heat soup, milk and pepper together.
Place patties back into gravy mixture; cook on low heat.
Turn over patties and heat.
Serve with white rice.
For spicy barbecue sauce, omit Worcestershire, mustard and ginger.
Add:
Combine all cereal, nuts and pretzels in large baking pan. Melt margarine and bacon drippings.
Add all the spices and sauces.
Pour over cereal mixture and bake for 1 hour in a 250° oven.
Stir every 15 minutes.
Mix sour cream and seasonings.
Coat chicken breasts with mixture and place in buttered glass baking dish.
Marinate, covered, in refrigerator overnight or at least 8 hours.
Sprinkle thoroughly with crushed stuffing mix.
Drizzle with
melted margarine.
Bake, covered, 45 minutes at 350°.
Bake, uncovered, 15 more minutes or until meat is tender.
Microwave pecans, sugar, Karo syrup and salt on High for 8 minutes.
Stir once after 4 minutes.
Add butter and vanilla and microwave on High for 2 minutes.
Stir.
Add soda and stir until foamy.
Pour onto greased cookie sheet and cool.
Use any variety of fruit that you like.
Drain fruit, place in shallow casserole.
Add dry sherry and let stand in refrigerator several hours.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and dot with butter. Place in oven at 350° until thoroughly heated (about 30 minutes). Garnish with maraschino cherries.
Serve in decorative bowl.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa, baking powder and salt in an ungreased 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Mix in milk, oil and vanilla with a fork until smooth.
Stir in nuts.
Spread in pan.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and 1/4 cup cocoa.
Pour hot water over batter.
Bake 40 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes; spoon into dessert dishes or cut into squares and invert on dessert plates.
Top with ice cream and spoon sauce over each serving.
Yield: 9 servings.
In a mixing bowl, melt margarine in microwave.
(Use a large saucepan for stove top melting.)
Add cocoa and mix.
Add sugar and beat with mixer.
Add vanilla.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each egg.
Add flour and mix.
Cook in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cover pan tightly with foil while still hot.
Cook noodles.
Brown meat.
Add onions, celery and green pepper; cook until tender.
Season.
Alternate meat and noodles in greased casserole.
Pour over soup, mixed with Worcestershire sauce.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in moderate oven at 325° for 45 minutes.

recipes.t: My Sugar Free Banana Nut Ice Cream(Delicious, But Not Low Calorie)
d: Cook pudding according to directions.
When finished cooking, add condensed milk. Stir together and pour into freezer container. Carefully fry nuts in butter until just beginning to turn golden brown.
Do not burn.
Add nuts and mashed bananas along with other ingredients to pudding/canned milk mixture.
Add enough milk to reach fill line.
Add NutraSweet to taste.
Freeze and enjoy.
Place roast in deep baking pan.
Place potatoes around the sides and carrots all around top of potatoes.
Sprinkle onion and garlic over carrots.
Bake 2 hours at 350°, covered.
Uncover; add water.
Bake at 200° for one more hour.
Cool down for 20 minutes. Slice thin.
Serve with juice or make gravy.

Mix egg, saltines and beef together and form into balls. Roll balls in flour and brown in a skillet; set aside to drain. Mix soup, milk and catsup. Place meatballs in baking dish. Pour on soup mixture. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until soup mixture begins to thicken.
In sheet cake pan, dump can of pineapple, juice and all, and spread evenly.
Add apricots and juice.
Sprinkle cake mix evenly on top of fruit mixture.
Pour melted butter over the top of cake mix evenly.
Add nuts to top.
Do not stir!
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Keep refrigerated after it cools.
In small bowl, blend cream cheese and powdered sugar; stir in pineapple, nuts, orange peel and vanilla.
Separate dough into 8 pieces.
Place each piece in ungreased muffin cup; press dough to cover bottom and sides, forming 1/4-inch rim.
Spoon 1 teaspoon coconut into each cup.
Spoon 1 tablespoon pineapple mixture into each cup.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining coconut; bake an additional 3 to 8 minutes until crust is brown.

recipes.t: Cream Of Asparagus Or Zucchini Soup
d: Discard coarse ends from asparagus or trim and slice zucchini thickly.
In saucepan, bring the vegetable, onion, broth, salt, pepper and basil to a boil and simmer 20 minutes.
Empty all into blender; cover and blend on high speed.
Mix yellow cake mix according to box directions but cut water by 3 tablespoons.
Stir in poppy seed.
Pour half of batter into pan; sprinkle Vienna Revel over batter.
Spread remaining batter over Vienna Revel.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until toothpick test is done.
Place pie filling in a blender; cover and process until the apples are in 1/4-inch chunks.
Pour into a mixing bowl; add dry cake mix and eggs.
Beat on medium speed for 5 minutes.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2 baking pan.
Sprinkle with nuts and chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool and then cut.
Makes 12 to 15 servings.
Drain pineapple, reserving 1 Tbsp. syrup.
Beat cream cheese, dressing and syrup together until smooth.
Fold in banana, cherries and dates.
Arrange 1 pineapple slice on each of 8 lettuce leaves.
Top each slice with cheese-fruit mixture.
Top with cherry half.
Place 6 slices of buttered bread in greased dish.
Place 1/2 of cheese and meat over bread.
Add 6 more slices of bread, then rest of cheese and meat.
Beat eggs; add milk, onion and seasonings.
Pour over layered bread and meat.
Place in refrigerator overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 400°.
With sharp knife, make 13 evenly spaced deep vertical slits in loaf of bread, being careful not to slice all the way through.
Set aside.
In blender, process cottage cheese until smooth.
Add parsley, Parmesan cheese, onion, garlic and pepper.
Process until parsley and garlic are minced.
Press bread open between slices.
With small spatula, spread cheese mixture on surface.
Bake 8 minutes, or until hot and crispy. Serve hot.
Put cauliflower in a microwave-safe casserole dish.
Add 1 Tbsp. water and cover.
Cook in microwave on high for 5 to 7 minutes and let stand, covered, another 3 to 5 minutes.
You want the cauliflower tender, but not mushy.
Drain cooked cauliflower and combine with celery and onion in a large bowl.
Combine mayonnaise, vinegar, salt, Splenda and pepper.
Pour mixture over vegetables and mix well.
Mix in chopped eggs last; only stir lightly to preserve some small chunks of yolk.
Chill and serve. Serves 12.
Pour pineapple juice concentrate into punch bowl. Add water, lemon juice and sweet orange marmalade. Stir to combine.
Add seltzer.
Add sherbet and ice cubes.
Garnish with orange slices and maraschino cherries.
Makes 6 (12 ounce) servings each.
Combine sugar, cinnamon and brown sugar.
Thaw bread dough. Break small pieces of dough (about the size of golf balls.)
Roll in melted margarine, then in sugar/cinnamon mixture.
Drop in greased Bundt pan.
May sprinkle chopped nuts between layers. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Take out of refrigerator 30 minutes before baking.
Then bake 30 minutes at 350°; turn cake upside down onto plate and pull apart.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Add tomatoes, barbecue sauce, pepper, onions, rice and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover; reduce heat.
Cook at medium heat, simmer for 25 minutes.
Place cheese on top and set off stove to melt.
In a 2-quart casserole, heat butter 1 to 2 minutes on High until melted.
Stir in rice; heat 5 minutes on High, until rice is browned.
Stir once.
Add remaining ingredients.
Heat, covered, for 8 minutes on High.
Continue cooking on Defrost an additional 11 minutes, until rice is tender.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Melt butter in frying pan.
Add crushed garlic and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add carrots, stirring until hot.
Add salt to taste.
Combine the margarine or butter, sugar, egg substitute, molasses and vanilla extract in the bowl of a food processor or electric mixer and process until smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine the flour and baking soda. Add the flour mixture to the margarine mixture and process to mix well. Stir in the remaining ingredients.
Coat a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray. Drop rounded teaspoonfuls of dough onto the baking sheet, placing them 1 1/2-inches apart.
Bake at 300° for about 16 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool the cookies on the pan for 1 minute. Transfer the cookies to wire racks and cool completely. Serve immediately or transfer to an airtight container.
Remove cap and seeds from bell pepper.
Mix tuna, rice and mayonnaise to desired consistency.
Add salt or lemon pepper, celery salt, whatever tastes good.
Stuff pepper and enjoy.
May be chilled, if you prefer.
Serves one.
Dip chops in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Brown in hot fat.
Drain off fat.
Sprinkle with lemon juice and sugar. Top each chop with a slice of onion.
Pour ketchup over all.
Add water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 1 to1 1/2 hours or until tender.
Rub quail generously inside and out with a mixture of oil and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stuff each quail with 1/2 cup blueberries and 1/2 teaspoon sugar.
Close with skewers or thread.
Place each on square of aluminum foil, large enough to fold well.
Melt butter, add to minced garlic and bay leaves. Pour equal amount of mixture over each bird. Wrap loosely and fold edges to seal.
Roast, breast down, in 425° oven for 1 hour or until tender.
Serve with juice.
Serves 4.
Cut all crusts from bread.
Slice cut bread into finger slices and set aside.
Bake crust pieces in 300° oven until brown, slightly.
Put crust pieces in blender and make fine crumbs.
Add 1/2 cup sugar to crumb mixture.
In double boiler over hot water, mix peanut butter, oil, 1/2 cup sugar and vanilla.
Stir until warm, but not hot.
Dip bread slices in peanut butter mixture, then roll in crumb mixture.
Store in closed box or tin.
Melt
shortening,
saute
mushrooms
and
garlic.
Add tomato paste,
water
and
wine. Mix dry ingredients and add slowly to saucepan.
Stir in cheese and cook over low heat for 10 minutes. Layer
everything
and put in greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes at 350°.
Melt margarine in saucepan.
Add sugar and stir.
Break egg yolks and add vanilla.
Mix well; set aside.
Add dry ingredients to margarine mixture.
Mix well.
Will be thick.
Add egg mixture. Beat all together.
Pour mixture into a 9 x 9-inch cake pan that has been lined with plastic wrap.
Spread and cover mix with wrap. Refrigerate until firm.
Slice thin and bake on an ungreased cookie tin for 10 minutes.
Remove immediately.
Store in tight fitting topped cookie jar.
Melt over hot water the chocolate morsels.
Stir in sugar, corn syrup and orange juice.
Mix well.
Combine crushed vanilla wafers and nuts.
Add chocolate mixture; stir thoroughly.
Form into 1-inch balls.
Drop into granulated sugar and roll until well coated.
Seal tightly in heavy-duty foil.
Let stand several days to ripen.
(These keep well and improve in flavor upon storing.) Yields 4 1/2 dozen.
Grate cheese.
Combine with other ingredients in medium-size bowl.
Spread evenly on cocktail rye.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Slice onions and separate into rings.
Combine water, sugar and vinegar.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Pour over onion rings, cover and chill at least 3 hours.
Drain.
Stir in mayonnaise and celery seed.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Yield:
4 servings.
Brown chicken and chopped onion in olive oil.
When well browned, add salt, pepper and bay leaves.
Cook for a few minutes, turning pieces occasionally.
Add wine; cook until wine is almost evaporated.
Add your sauce.
Season with salt and pepper (onion and garlic if desired) to taste.
Simmer 1/2 hour or until tender. (I like to add a can or frozen package of peas for the last 10 minutes or so.)
Meanwhile, cook macaroni; pour on platter and cover with chicken and sauce.
Top with grated cheese, if desired.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Stir in soup and noodles. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve over toast.
Yield:
8 servings.
Cut ahi into steaks about 3/4-inch thick.
Salt and pepper steaks and lay in baking dish (touching each other).
Mix mayonnaise and onions together and spread over top of steaks. Next, spread bread crumbs on top, then spread crab on top of crumbs.
Add optional mushrooms.
Melt butter, garlic powder and lemon juice.
Dribble over fish.
Bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes.
Combine corn, peas, onion, celery, pimento and water chestnuts. Bring to boil the vinegar, sugar, oil, salt and pepper. Pour over vegetables. Stir. Cover and marinate a few hours or overnight.
Cook pineapple and sugar for 5 minutes, stirring; cool.
Add mayonnaise, grated cheese and cut up pecans.
Fold in the whipped cream.
Put in loaf pan and chill.
Core tomatoes; cut into thick slices, then cut into halves. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Peel onion; slice into thin rings. Add to bowl and turn gently with a spoon.
Add remaining ingredients except cheese and again turn gently.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Just before serving, transfer salad to a serving bowl and crumble cheese over all.
Makes 6 to 8 portions.
Cream oleo and sugar.
Add beaten egg and melted chocolate and mix well.
Sift the dry ingredients together and add alternately with the milk.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet. Bake in a 350° oven for 8 to 10 minutes.
Brown ground beef.
Mix refried beans and 1/4 of the jar of picante sauce.
Layer in 9 x 12-inch dish.
Grate 1/2 of cheese and layer over beans.
Mix 3/4 cup picante sauce, ground beef and tomatoes*, cumin and salt together.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Layer over cheese and beans.
Top with remaining grated cheese.
Cook in oven for 20 minutes.
Serve with side order of tortilla chips.
Mix shortening, sugar and eggs.
Sift flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Add oatmeal, Grape-Nuts flakes, raisins, nuts and vanilla.
Mix and drop on cookie sheet and bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Mix yeast and warm water together.
Blend well all of the ingredients.
Let rise.
Punch down and pinch off into rolls.
Let rise to desired size.
Bake at 350°
until browned.

Cut bread loaf into thirds, making cuts in the already-sliced bread. Lay the slices on a cookie sheet. Mix all the ingredients together and brush on bread. Sprinkle with paprika. Bake at 225° for 1 hour.
Beat egg yolks; add flour, cornstarch, salt and pepper and beat until smooth.
Add milk gradually, beating constantly.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry.
Fold into egg yolk mixture. Melt butter in a heavy 9-inch skillet.
Pour in egg yolk mixture and bake in a moderate oven (350°) for 20 minutes.
Fold onto hot platter.
Serve at once.
Drain fruit cocktail; gradually add salad dressing and sugar to softened cream cheese.
Mix in a few drops of food coloring until well blended.
Fold in drained fruit cocktail, marshmallows, nuts and whipped cream, then spoon mixture into two 1 pound coffee cans; cover and freeze.
Remove from cans onto lettuce leaves. Serves 10 to 12.
Microwave:
Cook broccoli on High for 2 minutes.
Stir in rice, chicken, soup, milk, cheese and onion.
Cook for 6 minutes. Stir.
Add remaining cheese and cook 5 minutes longer.
Melt cheese, soup and onion together.
Serve with corn chips.
Saute onions (cut up) in a very small amount of olive oil.
Add ground beef.
(If you use dried beans, cook in water in large pot for 1/2 hour or so.)
Otherwise, add beef mixture to large pot with 3 quarts of water.
Also, add the tomatoes, sugar and vinegar and beans.
Cook for 1 1/2 hours if using dried beans or cook for 1/2 hour and add canned beans and cook another 1/2 hour.
Skim off any grease and thicken with flour.
Serve.
In 2 quart microwave-safe casserole, stir soup and milk until blended.
Stir
in
cheese
and
macaroni.
Cover and microwave on High
for
10 minutes. Stir at 3 and 6 minutes. Remove and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

Line a baking sheet with waxed paper; set aside. Place nuts in a shallow dish. In a large microwave-safe bowl, combine caramels and water. Microwave, uncovered, on High for 1 to 2 minutes or until melted, stirring twice. Dip each marshmallow into melted caramel, then roll in pecans. Place on prepared baking sheet. Let marshmallows stand until set. Yield: 20 servings.
Brown beef and drain.
Cook noodles and drain.
Put beef, noodles and sauce in a 9 x 13-inch pan and mix.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for about 40 minutes or until brown and bubbly.
Peel the banana and cut in half.
Split the one-half, which is to be used in the recipe.
Soften the peanut butter and spread in between the two slices of banana.
Press two halves together. Place in dessert dish and sprinkle lightly with cinnamon.
Pour over it the evaporated milk, which has been slightly beaten.
Combine in bowl, flour, sugar, soda and salt.
Add dry ingredients.
Then fold in 1 cup drained fruit cocktail.
Pour in greased pan and sprinkle brown sugar and nuts over top.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Add orange jello to hot orange juice.
Soften cream cheese. Add whipped cream or Dream Whip and drained, crushed pineapple. Mix thoroughly with the cream cheese.
Then add the jello and orange juice mixture (which should be cool).
Add miniature marshmallows and pecans.
Then chill.
Blend by hand the cream cheese.
Add peanut butter and milk until smooth.
Fold in the Cool Whip.
Place in the cookie pie crust and freeze.
When firm, add a large jar of chocolate ice cream topping to cover the top of the pie.
Keep in the refrigerator until ready to cut.
Cream margarine and sugar in large mixing bowl.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Add lemon extract.
Sift flour and baking powder together, then add small amount of flour mixture to cake, beating well after each addition.
Then last, add the nuts, raisins, cherries and pineapple.
Mix thoroughly.
Saute mushrooms in butter.
Add soup and sour cream.
Mix well.
Add the rest of ingredients and simmer.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Mix brown sugar, corn syrup, peanut butter and salt. Microwave on High 1 to 1 1/2 minutes or until mixture begins to bubble. Stir. Stir in popcorn and peanuts until well coated.
Let stand for 5 minutes. Shape mixture firmly into four 3-inch balls with hands dipped in cold water.
Place onto waxed paper.
Let stand about 30 minutes or until completely cooled. Wrap in plastic wrap.
Yields 4 popcorn balls.
Contains 310 calories per ball.
In large bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in milk, egg and extracts.
Stir in flour, baking powder and salt until well blended.
(If using one one food coloring, add several drops when beating in liquids.
Otherwise, divide dough and knead coloring into dough portions if using more than one color.)
Then wrap dough or portions of dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate approximately 1 hour.
Next, roll dough on a floured surface to about 1/4-inch and use cookie cutters for desired shapes.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350° on ungreased cookie sheets for 10 minutes or until very lightly browned.
Cool on wire racks.
About 30 minutes before serving, preheat broiler if manufacturer directs.
Cut potatoes into 1/4-inch thick slices. Arrange potato slices in single layer at one end of rack in broiling pan.
In small saucepan over low heat, melt 2 tablespoons corn oil spread. Stir in pepper and 1/2 teaspoon salt. With pastry brush, lightly brush some light corn oil spread mixture over potato slices.
Place broiling pan in oven 5 to 7-inches from source of heat.
Broil potatoes 8 minutes.
Put syrup and sugar into saucepan; heat until sugar dissolves, then add vinegar.
Continue boiling, without stirring, until it reaches 260° (hard ball stage).
Add butter and continue cooking to 270° (soft crack stage).
Remove from heat.
Cook beans in water until tender.
Remove coconut from shell; rinse and grate.
Pour 1 1/2 cups warm water over grated coconut; mix and squeeze juice through sieve.
Repeat with 1 1/2 cups warm water.
Add milk and rice into 2 to 3-quart-sized pot.
Add all other ingredients.
Bring to boil and let simmer for about 1/2 hour.
Stir.
Cover and leave on turned-off stove for about 10 minutes.
Serves 4.
In 2-quart casserole, combine vegetables with water.
Cook according to package microwave directions.
Stir in the milk, bouillon granules, dry mustard, oregano and Worcestershire sauce. Cook, uncovered, for 3 to 5 minutes.
Line bottom of an 8 x 6 x 2-inch glass or metal baking dish with 3 honey graham crackers.
In medium saucepan, combine milk and pudding mix.
Cook over low heat until mixture comes to a full boil.
Cool 5 minutes.
Spread half of the pudding over crackers; top with second layer of crackers.
Place candy bars on crackers. Spread remaining pudding over candy bars; top with third layer of crackers.
Sprinkle with marshmallows; broil until golden brown, about 2 to 4 minutes.
Serve warm or chill in refrigerator.
Set oven at 400°.
Use a cast-iron skillet or baking sheet. Dip chicken in yogurt.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl and dip chicken in seasoning; coat well.
Bake for 1 hour, turning it every 20 minutes.
Blend cans of tomatoes (juice too).
Put in Dutch oven.
Add garlic powder, cumin and pepper.
Dice the jalapeno finely.
Add to mixture.
Bring to a boil.
Add the cheese (grated) until melted.
Remove from heat and cool.
Mixture will be thick and lumpy.
Add 1 cup of water and blend.
May freeze.
Makes a lot!
At least 4 hours before serving, chop green onions and tops very fine.
Combine mayonnaise, cheese and onion very well.
Store in a tightly covered container in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
Split biscuits and spread mix on top of each half.
Broil with or without paprika sprinkled on top until bubbly.
Keep a close eye, as these burn very quickly.
Serve at once warning guests that they are very hot.
Chop cabbage and onion.
Mix together. Cover and set aside. Break noodles in package. Saute noodles, sesame seed and almonds in butter or margarine until light brown.
Cool on absorbent paper. Bring last 4 ingredients to a boil and cool. Store 3 mixtures separately in refrigerator.
Combine them immediately before serving.
Cook shellroni until tender, then chill by running cold water over it. Flake tuna. Blend all ingredients with mayonnaise.
Cook rutabaga 25 minutes or until tender and drain well.
In a large bowl, beat rutabaga on medium speed of electric mixer until smooth.
Beat in margarine, salt, nutmeg and pepper.
Fold in thawed spinach souffle.
Turn mixture into 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake, uncovered, in a 375° oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Crumble and reserve 2 tablespoons drippings.
Combine drippings with vinegar, mayonnaise, salt and pepper.
Toss cabbage with onion, bell pepper and dressing.
Mix well, add bacon just before serving.
Serves 6.
Freeze angel food cake for easy slicing.
Put 1 cup milk in a bowl, add Dream Whip and vanilla.
Beat until it peaks.
In a medium bowl, beat cream cheese, sugar and 3 tablespoons milk until blended.
Fold Dream Whip mixture into cream cheese mixture.
Blend first three ingredients.
Batter will be stiff.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool.
Cream the cheese with sugar, fold in Cool Whip.
Spread cream cheese mixture onto cooled crust.
Mix together pudding and milk, spread onto cream cheese mixture.
Add rest of Cool Whip.
Use large container to spread over pudding.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts, if desired.
In a large (9 x 13 or larger) dish, layer all of the above ingredients beginning with the ice cream sandwiches and finishing with the Magic Shell. Put in freezer overnight and enjoy.
Combine chicken broth and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Add mixed vegetables.
Cook 15 minutes until tender. Saute onion and pepper in Dutch oven until tender.
Blend in flour, paprika and mustard.
Gradually add milk, vegetables and broth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Add cheese and pepper.
Stir until cheese melts.
Yield: 7 cups.

Preheat oven to 375°. Defrost peas and carrots and then drain. Add next 3 ingredients and pour into a buttered 3-quart baking dish. Mix flour and milk together and pour over top of dish. Dot with butter. Bake in preheated oven for 1 hour. Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In a medium bowl, combine Ricotta cheese, egg, Parmesan cheese and garlic powder.
Spread 1/3 of spaghetti sauce over bottom of a baking dish.
Cover with 3 uncooked noodles.
Top with half Ricotta cheese mixture and then sprinkle with 1 cup Mozzarella cheese.
Repeat steps until all noodles are used.
Cover with foil and bake 45 to 50 minutes or until noodles are tender.
Add celery, onion and nuts to milk mixture in mixing bowl. Add whole wheat bread crumbs.
Add salt and bake in oiled pan until done at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Peel and grate potatoes and onions.
Crumble crackers and soak in milk for a few minutes.
Add crackers to grated potatoes and onions.
Add cheese.
Beat egg yolks slightly and add to potato mixture along with seasonings.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry, and fold into potato mixture.
In a 1 1/2-quart mixer bowl, combine all ingredients except almonds.
Beat at medium speed, scraping bowl often, until well blended.
Shape mixture into large ball.
Roll in toasted almonds. Cover; refrigerate.
Remove from refrigerator 1/2 hour before serving.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Yield:
1 cheese ball.
In saucepan, cook bacon until crisp.
Remove and crumble. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon drippings.
Add onion, parsley and thyme.
Cook until onion is tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat, stirring occasionally.
Serve.
Mix sugar, Karo syrup and water; boil to 280° on candy thermometer.
Add butter.
Cook to hard crack stage and add soda and cashew nuts.
Mix well.
Pour into buttered jelly roll pan. Cool and break into pieces.
Butter a deep baking dish.
Then start at the bottom and arrange in layers.
First potatoes, then the ground beef, onions, green pepper if used, uncooked rice and tomatoes.
Season each layer, cover and bake for 2 hours at 300°.
Parmesan cheese may be used on top.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Brown hamburger with onion and bell pepper.
Add Worcestershire sauce after meat is browned.
Mix in soup.
Add salt and pepper for taste.
Pour meat and noodles in baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Slice cheese on top and leave in oven until cheese melts.
Combine sugar, flour and nutmeg.
Cut in butter until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Add nuts.
Arrange yams and peaches in 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with sugar mixture.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes, then sprinkle with marshmallows.
Brown lightly in oven.
In a large mixing bowl sift the dry ingredients.
Make a well and drop in the eggs, vanilla, buttermilk and cooled margarine. Mix well.
Add nuts and mix well.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with vegetable oil. Bake about 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Combine vanilla wafers and melted margarine.
Press into a 9 x 13 x 2-inch dish.
Slice bananas; spread on top of crumbs.
Mix Eagle Brand milk and lemon juice; pour on top of bananas.
Drain crushed pineapple; spread over top.
Spread Cool Whip over pineapple layer.
Sprinkle with coconut, pecans and cherries. Refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine Ricotta, 1 cup Mozzarella, Parmesan and eggs.
In 13 x 9-inch baking dish, spread 1 cup sauce; layer 4 uncooked noodles, 1 cup sauce and 1/2 of Ricotta mixture.
Repeat; top with remaining 4 uncooked lasagne noodles and 2 cups sauce.
Reserve remaining sauce.
Cover with foil; bake 1 hour.
Remove foil; sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake, uncovered, 10 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Serve with remaining sauce, heated.
Simmer applesauce gently 5 minutes.
Add sugar, butter, cocoa and salt.
Boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Immediately add oats, nuts, vanilla and almond.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoons on wax paper.
When cool, roll into balls and then in pecan meal. Store in airtight container.
Yield:
50 to 55 balls.
Heat margarine in small saucepan until melted.
Stir in flour, salt, sugar, pepper and onions.
Add sour cream; stir until smooth.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to just boiling point.
Fold in broccoli.
Pour into greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Toss together the cereal and cheese; sprinkle over broccoli.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for about 20 minutes, or until bubbly.
Cream shortening and sugar in large mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add flour alternately with milk, beating well after each addition.
Stir in 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and 1 cup pecans.
Fold in 4 ounces cherries.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 2 hours.
Cool in pan for several minutes.
Invert onto serving plate.
Beat cream cheese and margarine in mixer bowl until light.
Add confectioners sugar and remaining 1 teaspoon vanilla; beat until fluffy.
Fold in remaining cherries and 1/2 cup pecans.
Spread over cake.
Yield:
16 servings.
Set water for lasagne to boil.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in large skillet and saute garlic.
Add thawed spinach and let steam over low heat, covered, until limp.
Add sprinkle of salt or soy sauce if desired.
Set aside.
Add remaining tablespoon oil in large skillet and saute onion, add squash and stir until slightly cooked.
Brown hamburger, onion and garlic.
Drain off fat.
Add tomatoes, enchilada sauce and olives.
Bring to boil.
Cover and reduce heat to simmer for 15 minutes.
Cut 2 tortillas into quarters.
Crisp the quarters and the remaining 6 tortillas in the oil over medium heat.
Drain.
Set aside the quartered tortillas and break up the remaining 6.
Combine the cottage cheese, egg and cheese.
Spread 1/3 of the meat mixture in a shallow baking dish. Top with 1/2 of the cheese mixture, then 1/2 of the broken tortillas.
Repeat layers, ending with meat mixture.
Place quartered tortillas on top.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Spread all slices of bread with butter, then spread whole wheat slices with Thousand Island dressing.
Cover 1/3 of the area of whole wheat slices with lettuce, reserving a little.
Remove egg yolks from whites and arrange yolk slices over center area of bread, reserving a little.
Place 4 tomato slices over remaining area on bread.
Season with salt and pepper.
Using a small 3/4-inch plain or fluted rounded cookie cutter, cut out 6 holes from each slice of white bread. Place bread, buttered sides down, over filling and press together firmly.
Cut each sandwich neatly in half to form "traffic lights."
Chop the reserved lettuce and tomato and slice egg yolk; use to fill the relevant holes in sandwich.
Garnish with a few green onion flowers.
Makes 4.
Mix butter and margarine.
Add the following in order: sugar, brown sugar, eggs, sifted flour, baking powder, baking soda, vanilla and nuts.
Roll in wax paper; refrigerate for 24 hours. Slice and bake at 350° until set (10 to 15 minutes).
Spray 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam.
Place chicken in pan. Combine soup and wine and pour over chicken.
Cover loosely with foil and bake in oven at 350° for 50 minutes.
Remove chicken from oven; top each piece with a slice of cheese.
Put back in oven without the foil and bake another 10 minutes until cheese melts.
Scramble 2 dozen eggs, 1/4 pound butter and 1/4 milk.
Combine 2 cans cream of mushroom soup, wine and chilies together in separate bowl. Layer in a 9 x 13-inch pan, scrambled eggs, soup mixture and cheese.
Repeat. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook broccoli as directed on package (let water cook low). Pour into baking dish.
Sprinkle with onion and eggs.
Melt stick of margarine; pour over crackers.
Stir and put on top of dish. Combine soup, mayonnaise and cheese in small saucepan over low heat until cheese melts, stirring constantly.
Pour soup over all; bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix shortening, peanut butter, white sugar and brown sugar together.
Add and mix well eggs and vanilla.
Then add flour, baking powder, salt, soda and Raisin Bran; mix well.
Add raisins and nuts.
Make 1-inch balls; place on ungreased cookie sheets (I use parchment paper) and flatten with fork.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 350° until lightly brown.
Slightly cool before removing from pan.
This is a good nourishing cookie.
Add mushrooms, seafood, sherry and cheese to soup.
Bake in a 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix flour, salt, paprika, pepper, garlic and poultry seasoning.
Shake each pork chop in this mixture until there are no moist spots on the meat.
Place chops in greased shallow baking pan.
Add as many pear halves as pork chops, placing the pears between the chops.
Add 1/2 teaspoon mayonnaise to each pear center.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Ovens may vary. Bake until chops are thoroughly cooked and brown.

recipes.t: The Creamest Dreamest Cheese Cake Surprise
d: Mix well, cream cheese and sour cream.
Add sugar slowly.
Mix in whipped cream slowly (mix until smooth).
Pour mixture in pie shell, spread evenly and top with cherry pie filling.
*Chill 2 hours before serving.* Your guests will love your cool no bake surprise!
Brown hamburger meat; drain.
Add onions, pepper and remaining ingredients.
Cook 3 hours over low heat.
Salt and pepper dove breasts to taste and dredge in flour. Heat butter in a heavy skillet and brown dove breasts nicely. Sprinkle with thyme and add cream.
Cover tightly and simmer very slowly until tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Serve dove on a platter of wild rice.
Gravy may be thinned with milk, if necessary. Serve gravy separately.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Cool.
Whip Milnot thick and add vanilla.
Beat, then add 1 cup sugar.
Beat, then add cream cheese.
After jello is cooled, add to whipped mixture and beat until creamy.
Pour over cracker crust.
Place in refrigerator for 2 hours or overnight.
Cook and drain spaghetti.
Pour into ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over top of spaghetti.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1/2 hour or until cheese is melted.
Cut and serve with warmed sauce and garlic bread.
Serves 8.
In large skillet, fry hamburg and onion until meat is light brown.
Add salt, pepper, celery, onion and water.
Bring to a boil and cover.
Let simmer for 20 minutes.
Add rinsed bean sprouts and heat.
In separate bowl, combine 2 tablespoons water, soy sauce, sugar and gravy.
Add to meat and stir until thickened.
Season meat and brown in oil.
Remove any excess fat.
Peel and slice potatoes thinly.
Make alternate layers of potatoes, onions and meat.
Pour mushroom soup on top and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cover casserole with foil and remove the foil after 30 minutes.
Continue baking for 15 minutes or until potatoes are done.
Combine pineapple juice, orange juice, lemon juice and sugar. Stir to dissolve sugar.
Add crushed ice and milk.
Shake vigorously or beat until well blended and frothy.
Pour in tall glasses and garnish with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream. Serves 4.
Sprinkle salt and pepper on chicken and place in shallow baking pan.
Make sauce by mixing sugar and flour; add egg, orange juice and wine and cook over low heat until slightly thickened. Pour over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° about 1 hour or until done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. In bowl, beat together honey, brown sugar, vanilla, oil and egg until well blended.
Fold in undrained pineapple, whole wheat flour, 1/4 cup oats, raisins and nuts.
Turn into pan.
Sprinkle with remaining oats.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes or until center is just firm.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Yields 12 servings.
Cook
both
the
rice
and
the
broccoli
according to package directions.
Combine the cooked rice and broccoli with the Cheez Whiz, butter, water chestnuts, soup and pimento; mix well. Pour
into
a
3-quart (or 2 smaller) greased casserole dish. Bake
at
for 25 to 30 minutes.
Remove and cover the
top with
grated cheese.
Place back into the oven until cheese is melted.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Mix first 6 ingredients in pan.
Cover with water.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Add can of skimmed milk.
In large bowl mix gelatin and sugar; add boiling water and stir until gelatin is completely dissolved.
With electric mixer, beat in cream cheese until smooth.
Blend in sour cream and vanilla.
Pour into prepared crust.
Chill until firm, at least 2 hours.
Top, if desired, with fresh fruit.
Serves 6.
In saucepan, heat chicken broth, milk, thyme and bay leaves until simmering.
Remove from heat; let stand 10 minutes. Meanwhile, in skillet, heat butter until melted.
Add chicken. Cook and stir until tender 2 to 3 minutes.
Add remaining butter; heat until melted.
Add mixed vegetables and sprinkle with flour. Stir until vegetables are coated.
Add to milk mixture with salt and pepper.
Cook and stir until mixture boils and simmer a few minutes.
To serve, remove bay leaves and serve with croutons.
Rinse mussels well.
Place in a pot of boiling water to which a little lemon juice and onion has been added and boil about 5 minutes.
(Buy only mussels which are closed.
Store in refrigerator in open container.
Once they are boiled, they should be open; if not, throw away.)
Drain mussels, reserving 4 cups of the liquid.
Separate each mussel into 2 halves, discarding the half shell which has no meat. Meanwhile, saute onion and garlic until tender in plenty of olive oil in a paella pan or a very large skillet.
Rinse and drain shrimp, leaving on shells.
Add to pan and cook until pink, stirring frequently.
Then add the rice and saute a little.
Boil chickpeas for 15 minutes and mash like potatoes. Mash and add garlic cloves and other ingredients, mixing together well. Serve in a flat dish; decorate with parsley.
Sprinkle gelatin in water; let dissolve (about 10 minutes) over low heat.
Cool slowly, stirring occasionally, so it does not get on the bottom or around the edges of the pan.
Beat eggs and sugar about 7 minutes at high speed until thick and light.
Whip 1 1/2 cups of heavy cream into peaks; refrigerate.
Add lemon rind and juice to cooked gelatin and stir.
Juice and gelatin must be at the same temperature to avoid gelled lumps.
Pour mixture into egg-sugar mixture; blend well.
Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream until mixture is uniform.
Pour into a serving bowl by Malcolm Davis; chill 3 hours.
Garnish with remaining whipped cream and strawberries.
Melt the butter and saute the green onions and parsley.
Blend in flour slowly and smooth out with 1 pint of cream (or canned milk).
Add Swiss cheese and stir until melted and smooth.
Gently put in 1 pound crabmeat and salt and peppers to taste.
Add sherry and simmer 7 to 10 minutes.
Crumble sausage in large skillet.
Add mushrooms; cook over high heat, stirring frequently, until mushrooms and meat are lightly browned and all liquid from mushrooms has evaporated. Drain off any excess grease.
Stir in parsley.
Beat eggs with half and half and Parmesan cheese.
Blend in mushroom mixture and salt. Pour into unbaked pastry shell.
Arrange mushrooms so that any stems are turned down in liquid.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 25 to 30 minutes, or until crust is well browned and filling is set.
Let stand about 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.t: Sweet Orange Bread(Use A Bread Oven)
d: Do not use the delayed bake feature for this recipe.
Use the sweet bake program.
Glaze this bread if you like with powdered sugar and orange juice.
For garnish, prepare ice cubes by placing twisted lime slices in each cube compartment.
Fill with water and freeze.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Pour over ice cubes in glasses. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In large saucepan, melt butter or margarine over low heat. Blend in sugars, beaten egg and peanut butter; mix until smooth. Add oats, baking soda, raisins and chocolate chips.
Dough should be sticky.
If not, add several tablespoons water.
Drop by ice cream scoopfuls on greased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Remove to wire rack to cool.
Yields 2 dozen.
Cook sugar, salt, syrup, margarine and milk until it comes to a boil.
Add cut-up dates.
Stir all time.
Cook to soft ball stage. Remove from heat; cool.
Beat until very stiff and add pecans. Shape 6 to 8 inches long, 1/2-inch in diameter.
Place on wax paper.
Cut in slices when firm.
Slightly cook noodles.
Combine all ingredients.
The broccoli and cauliflower (10 ounces each) should be slightly thawed.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain peaches.
Add water, lemon juice and sugar.
Pour into large skillet.
Place biscuits over peaches.
Brush with melted margarine.
Sprinkle with 1/4 cup sugar and cinnamon to taste. Cover and simmer about 20 minutes.
Serve with cream.
Combine first 4 ingredients and stir.
Add 2 cups flour, oil and eggs.
Start adding additional flour.
Recipe will use approximately 6 cups.
Keep adding and kneading until dough is no longer sticky.
Put into an oiled bowl.
Cover and leave in a warm spot
until doubled in quantity (about 1 hour).
Remove from bowl. Punch and divide into sections for braiding.
Braid into one large or 2 small Challahs.
Allow to double in bulk.
Brush with egg yolks, thinned with one tablespoon of water and bake in preheated oven at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Mix shortening, sugar, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla until totally mixed.
Blend in soda and salt.
Add peanut butter, flour and milk.
Mix chocolate bits in by hand.
Drop by teaspoons on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Combine eggs, mayonnaise, onion, salt and pepper.
Add vinegar and mash to smooth paste.
Spread on bread.
Fasten two opposite corners of bread together with toothpicks forming lily shape. Decorate with carrot stick for center of lily and pickle slices for leaves.
Makes 4 servings.

recipes.t: Papaya Kiwi Fruit Salad With Orange Dressing
d: Peel and remove seeds from the papaya. Slice lengthwise into thin slices. Peel kiwi fruit and cut lengthwise into thin slices. Arrange papaya and kiwi fruit on 4 salad plates. Combine orange juice concentrate and honey in a small bowl. Stir in sour cream. Spoon dressing over salads; sprinkle with peels. Serves 4.
Rub oil on steak.
Coat all pieces with bread crumbs and place in baking dish.
Cook noodles; drain.
Add eggs and mix.
Add butter and salt; mix.
Add cottage cheese and sour cream; mix.
Add sugar, cinnamon and raisins/pineapple; mix.
Bake in 8 or 9-inch Pyrex dish at 350° for 45 minutes or until lightly browned.
Combine cream cheese and honey, mixing until well blended. Stir in sour cream.
Chill.
Combine cheese with lettuce; layer lettuce mixture, peaches, berries, grapes and cream cheese mixture in a large bowl.
Chill several hours.
Yield:
12 servings.
Combine water and salt in saucepan.
Bring to a boil and add beans.
Cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes; drain.
Toss beans with 1 tablespoon of butter, Blue cheese and pepper.
Spoon into a lightly greased 1-quart casserole dish and set aside.
Heat oil in large skillet; saute onion and Kasha until onion is transparent.
Add water and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Bring to boil; cover and reduce heat.
Cook about 15 minutes, until water is absorbed.

Cook spinach and put spinach, peanuts and one egg in blender and process on high until creamed (nuts should be coarse). Lightly beat one egg; add spinach mixture, Kasha, salt and pepper. Put into well oiled 9 x 5 x 3-inch pan.
Bake 55 minutes at 350°. Cool 5 to 10 minutes.
Serves 6.
Broil eggplant slices 3 to 5 minutes on each side.
Remove eggplant.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine cheeses.
In a 9-inch pie pan, arrange eggplant.
Overlap by pressing edges to form a "pie crust."
Spread vegetables evenly over eggplant; sprinkle with oregano and garlic powder.
Top with combined cheeses, then sprinkle Parmesan.
Bake until cheese is melted; brown 20 to 25 minutes.
Cut into 4 equal wedges and serve 2 wedges per portion.
Combine butter, peanut butter and confectioners sugar.
Mix well.
Add Rice Krispies and walnuts.
Chill.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Chill.
Dip in chocolate.
Melt chocolate bits and chocolate bar.
Dip balls into this using a fork to cover and remove to cookie sheet.
Chill.
Blend sour cream, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Add to remaining ingredients and toss.
Thaw and drain spinach in colander; squeeze out all water. Mix mayo, sour cream, soup mix, chopped water chestnuts, onion, salt and pepper.
Chill at least one hour.
Cut cabbage into small pieces and cook in salted water until tender.
Drain and put in casserole dish.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add sugar, cheese, soup and milk.
Mix in 1 cup of cracker crumbs.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup of cracker crumbs on top and dot with margarine.
Bake at 350° until brown and thickened.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In bowl, mix cheeses, green onions, olives and pimentos.
Add mayonnaise only enough to make spreadable.
Slice French bread, sandwich style and stuff with cheese mixture.
Wrap with foil and place on cookie sheet.
Bake until cheese has completely melted, about 20 minutes.
Slice and enjoy.
This bread goes well with most any meal, especially, spaghetti dinners and barbecues.
"Everyone will love it!"
Melt butter and stir in brown sugar and pecans.
Put in bottom of a greased 9-inch round cake pan.
Cream Crisco and sugar.
Add unbeaten egg yolk.
Sift together cocoa, flour, baking powder and salt.
Add alternately with a mixture of milk and vanilla.
Beat egg white until stiff.
Fold in egg white.
Pour on top of sugar and pecan mixture.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Turn out on cake plate while hot.
Serve with whipped cream.
In 2-quart capacity container, mix all ingredients.
Microwave on High for 10 minutes or until mixture boils.
Stir.
Strain into mugs.
Garnish with additional orange slices and cinnamon sticks. Yields 4 cups.
Drain mushrooms; reserve liquid.
Add enough milk to mushroom liquid to make 1/2 cup.
In mixing bowl, combine liquid, egg, Worcestershire sauce, seasonings and bread crumbs.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in beef and mushrooms.
Mix.
Shape into loaf in baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine ketchup and corn syrup.
Brush on meat top.
Bake meat loaf for 15 more minutes.

recipes.t: Shrimp With Capers And Dijon Mustard
d: In heavy skillet, heat oil.
Add shallots and cook slowly until softened.
Add shrimp and cook just until they turn pink and curl.
Add mustard, pepper and capers.
Toss to coat the shrimp. Remove shrimp to a serving dish.
Add wine to skillet, increase heat and stir rapidly, scraping the pan.
Pour sauce over shrimp.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add cumin seed; saute 1 minute.
Add rice and next 5 ingredients.
Reduce heat and cook, uncovered, for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add water and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed.
Remove pan from heat; let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in peanuts.
Serves 5.
Combine lamb, onion, catsup, Worcestershire sauce and pepper. Shape into 4 thin patties.
Place 1 tablespoon Bleu cheese on each of 2 patties.
Cover with remaining patties.
Seal edges.
Place on broiler rack 3 to 4-inches from heat.
Broil 6 minutes or until browned on 1 side.
Turn once and broil 3 minutes.
Don't overcook.
Line pie pan with pastry.
Brush shell with evaporated milk. Bake in preheated oven at 450° for 5 minutes.
Fill shell with tomatoes and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Mix remaining ingredients and spread on tomatoes.
Bake in preheated moderate oven at 350° for 40 minutes or until done.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix corn muffin mix as directed on Jiffy box, adding pepper, onions and corn.
Pour into an oiled pan and bake for about 30 minutes or until golden brown.
In a saucepan, melt the butter and Blue cheese over low heat. Unroll dough and cut each breadstick into 6 pieces; place in a foil-lined 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking pan.
Pour cheese mixture over dough.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until butter is absorbed and rolls are lightly browned.
Carefully lift foil out of pan; place on a serving dish.
Serve hot.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
To prepare dressing, combine the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, sugar, mustard, salt and pepper in medium bowl; stir to mix well.
In saucepan, softened gelatin in cold water.
Stir over low heat until gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in can of tomato soup and beat.
Heat thoroughly.
Gradually blend into softened cream cheese.
Add mayonnaise, horseradish and hot pepper sauce.
Beat until smooth with rotary beater.
Chill until partially set.
Fold in tuna, celery and onion.
Chill overnight.
Makes 4 or 5 servings.

Look over beans, discarding halves, discolored ones and stones. In large soup pot, cover beans with water. Bring to the boil; simmer for 2 minutes. Turn off heat and let stand for 1 hour. Drain and rinse. Add water, broths, onion and garlic. Bring to the boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours. Remove a cup of beans and liquid; mash and return to pot. Mix flour and butter; add it and the ham. Stir well and continue cooking for 10 minutes. Add hot sauce, salt and pepper to taste. If desired, spike each serving with a tablespoon of juice from jar of hot jalapeno slices. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Divide lettuce between 4 large salad plates.
Arrange palm, asparagus and red pepper pieces in pinwheel pattern over lettuce. Place 1/2 of the artichoke hearts in center of each pinwheel. Sprinkle each salad with olives and shrimp.
Spoon dressing over salad.
Cream the cream cheese until smooth.
Mix with rest of ingredients and refrigerate.
Serve with raw vegetables.
Sift dry ingredients.
Beat butter until fluffy and add sugar gradually, beating well.
Add egg and molasses; beat well and stir in dry ingredients.
Wrap in wax paper and chill overnight.
Roll out small amounts of dough on floured board.
Cut into animal or other shapes.
Bake at 350° for 8 minutes.
When cool, decorate with white royal frosting.
Sprinkle eggplant with salt and let stand 20 minutes in water. Gently squeeze out salt water.
Dip each slice in beaten egg and fry quickly in oil just until egg sets.
Lightly brown cube steak in olive oil on both sides. Sprinkle cube steak with the dry onion soup mix.
Mix mushroom soup with water and pour over cube steak with dry onion soup.
Cover and simmer 45 minute to 1 hour.
Spread mustard
on
both
sides of chicken and sprinkle with pepper.
Cover and refrigerate 2 to 4 hours.
Melt butter in a glass
measuring cup and then stir in lemon juice, garlic salt and tarragon.
Place chicken on a microwave roasting rack and brush with
butter
sauce
and
microwave
on High for 10 minutes. Rearrange
chicken
without
turning so the uncooked portions are on the outside of dish.
Again brush with butter sauce on High for
to 15 minutes or until chicken is done brushing with butter sauce every 5 minutes.
Combine flour and salt; set aside.
Cream butter or margarine and warm cheese.
Stir in flour mixture by hand just until blended.
Divide dough into fourths, wrap in plastic wrap and chill several hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400° and lightly grease baking sheets.
Combine apricot preserves, coconut and walnuts; set aside.
Working with one fourth of dough at a time, roll on floured pastry cloth or other floured surface into 8 x 10-inch rectangle.
Cut rolled dough into 2-inch squares. Spread each square with 1 teaspoon apricot mixture leaving edges of dough uncovered.
Moisten one corner of dough with water. Beginning at opposite corner roll toward moistened corner and press lightly to seal.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until edges begin to brown.
Cool on wire rack.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar. Makes 80.
Combine flour and salt in large mixing bowl.
Cut in shortening with pastry blender until mixture is of cornmeal consistency.
Beat egg; add 1 cup cold water and vinegar. Pour slowly into flour mixture, stirring with a fork until particles are moistened.
Divide pastry into 3 balls; wrap securely in plastic wrap.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
Whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch and clam juice.
Cut scallops in half.
Slice pepper thin.
Cut peas in half.
Chop tomato.
Heat oil and add shrimp.
Saute 30 seconds. Remove to warm dish.
Add scallops to pan and saute 20 seconds. Remove to dish with shrimp.
Add scallions, pepper, peas and tomatoes.
Return seafood to pan.
Add cornstarch mixture.
Cook and stir until sauce thickens.
Serve over rice.
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces.
Pound chicken to 1/4-inch thickness.
Place a slice of cheese on top of each chicken piece. Roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Dilute mayonnaise with milk in a small bowl.
Mix remaining ingredients together in another bowl. Dip chicken rolls in mayonnaise mixture, then roll in crumb mixture, covering completely.
Place chicken rolls in lightly greased baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 35 minutes.
Combine chopped pepper, garlic and shortening in frying pan. Add beef, chili powder and salt.
Boil briskly, then stir in corn meal, milk, mixed olives and mushrooms.
Pour into casserole and bake at 325° for about 1 hour until set.
Top with grated cheese before baking if desired.
Boil chicken in large pot for 1 hour, or sooner if tender. Remove chicken from pot.
Add remaining ingredients to boiled chicken broth.
Cut-up chicken and add to broth.
Add noodles. Homemade noodles are great with this recipe.
Simmer for 2 to 3 hours.
Add ingredients to suit taste.

recipes.t: Easy Cheese And Broccoli Soupeverton, Missouri
d: Melt butter in 3 qt. saucepan. Add onion and celery.
Cook and stir 5 minutes over medium heat.
Thoroughly cream the butter, sugar and vanilla.
Gradually blend in flour.
Chill dough.
Form logs about 1 1/2 inches long. Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° until delicately browned (about 15 minutes).
Cool cookies.
Melt chocolate chips and shortening.
Dip cookies in melted chocolate; coat with toppings.
Insert dough hooks in electric mixer.
Set aside 1 cup flour. In large bowl, mix remaining flour, sugar, salt and yeast.
Stir in hot water and margarine at speed 3.
Mix in only enough reserved flour to make soft dough.
Turn to speed 2; allow mixer to knead for additional 4 minutes.
Roll dough to 14 x 10-inch rectangle; place on greased baking sheet.
Spread dressing down center third of length of dough.
Top with layers of beef, cheese and sauerkraut.
Cut 1-inch wide strips along sides of filling out to dough edges.
Alternating sides, fold strips at angle across filling.
Cover with Saran Wrap; place over large shallow pan half filled with boiling water for 15 minutes.
Brush with egg white; sprinkle with caraway seed.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes or until done.
Cool slightly; serve warm.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Reheat to serve.
Cut quail in half down center back and breast.
Soak for 15 minutes or more in buttermilk.
Add salt and pepper to self-rising flour in a plastic bag.
Add quail and shake until birds are well coated.
Bake chicken, seasoned to taste.
Add chopped onions, garlic and bell pepper.
Add peas, mushrooms and potatoes.
Roast until tender 1 hour at 400°.
Cook onions in margarine in medium saucepan until tender.
Add tomatoes, 1/4 cup steak sauce and vinegar.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat; stir in parsley.
Broil steaks or grill until desired doneness.
Brush with remaining steak sauce.
Serve with vegetable mixture.

recipes.t: Mother'S Day Brunch Baked Spanish Eggs
d: Saute the onions and pepper in the butter until lightly browned.
Place evenly on bottom of a 9 x 12-inch baking pan. Carefully break the eggs, keeping the yolks intact, placing them evenly in the pan over the onion/green pepper mixture.
Mix all ingredients, except bread, tomatoes and cheese. Spread evenly over 1 loaf of French bread or 6 hot dog buns, split and toasted.
Cover edges completely.
Broil about 4 inches from heat for 12 minutes, then top with slices of tomatoes and sliced cheese.
Broil until cheese melts.
Serves 6.
Crush cookies and mix all ingredients together.
Refrigerate several hours.
If using a fresh pineapple, hollow out and pour dip in pineapple.
Refrigerate overnight (do not use extract).
Chill pie filling and pineapple.
In large bowl, combine all ingredients; mix well.
Spoon into individual serving dishes, if desired, or one large dish.
Chill 30 minutes.
Garnish with sugar wafer cookies.
Serves 8 to 10.
Tear bread into small pieces.
Add ground meat, onion, ketchup, salt and pepper.
Mix well on waxed paper.
Pat mixture into a 12 x 8-inch size.
Arrange salami slices to cover meat. Top with chopped spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) and cheese. Starting at narrow end, roll in jelly roll fashion, lifting wax paper to help shape roll.
Place in pan seam side down.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
When loaf starts to brown, cover loosely with tent of folded foil to prevent oven browning.
Saute onion and bell pepper in margarine.
Add ground beef and cook; drain off the fat.
In a bowl mix together sweet pickle juice (optional), salt and pepper, chili powder, Worcestershire sauce and chili beans.
Pour sauce in pot with ground beef and simmer for 30 minutes.
May need to add water to make it thinner.
Stir milk, 1 tablespoon at a time, into cream cheese.
Add mayonnaise, green onions, Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder. Blend well.
Stir in tuna.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour. Garnish with paprika and parsley.
In skillet, cook sausage over medium heat, stirring to crumble; drain and set aside.
Add eggs to skillet and scramble.
Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
When eggs are set, add sausage. Remove from heat and add cheese.
Warm tortillas, one at a time, in microwave, 10 seconds each.
Spread 1 tablespoon picante sauce down center of each tortilla.
Divide egg mixture among tortillas.
Fold bottom 1/3 of tortilla over filling.
Fold sides toward center and overlap.
Makes 6.
Crumble ground beef into a large skillet with the onion. Brown meat evenly; drain.
Stir in soup and ketchup.
Season with a dash each of garlic powder and chili powder.
Heat through, stirring occasionally.
Slice French bread in half lengthwise. Top the cut sides with the ground beef mixture.
Slice diagonally to serve open face.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.

recipes.t: Brazilian Cream With Lime And Rum
d: Halve avocados lengthwise; twist gently to separate halves. Remove seed.
Remove avocado pulp and put in blender with the sugar, lime juice and rum; whip in blender until smooth.
Mound in sherbet or champagne glasses.
Serve garnished with lime slices or wedges.
Cook and drain noodles.
Saute onion, celery and green pepper in butter.
Brown ground beef; drain, then mix in tomatoes and tomato sauce.
Then put all else in and mix.
Butter a roaster pan; put layer of sauce mixture, layer of noodles and end with sauce.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Mix together the two cans of soup and stew beef in a 2 quart oven dish (do not add water to soups).
Cut up potatoes and carrots and add to soup mixture.
Add peas, diced celery and diced onion.
Stir everything together and bake uncovered in 300° oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Turn off oven and leave stew in oven for another 45 minutes.
Stir before serving.
Combine butter and sugar; cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time beating well after each.
Combine dry ingredients; add to creamed mixture alternately with yogurt and vanilla, beating well after each addition.
In a deep skillet, brown ground beef on medium high.
Just before it is done, drain and put back in skillet.
Add cheese. Cover and turn down temperature to a low simmer.
(Be careful not to burn the cheese!)
When cheese is completely melted, add entire jar of salsa, stir well and serve with tortilla chips.
Cook pork in skillet until browned with garlic and some onion.
Add broccoli or spinach, fresh tomatoes and cornstarch mixture.
Cook until broccoli or spinach is done.
