Can add bean sprouts and water chestnuts, if desired.
Serve over rice; add soy sauce on plates and eat.
Takes about an hour.
Beat together cottage cheese, cream cheese and Blue cheese until they are smooth and creamy.
Gradually beat in whipping cream, beating until thickened.
Stand colander in a bowl and line with several thicknesses of cheesecloth.
Pour in cheese mixture. Tie cheesecloth at top.
Let drain overnight in refrigerator. Untie cloth and turn ball out onto a plate.
Remove cloth. Decorate top of cheese with lemon or mint leaves.
Surround cheese with assorted crackers, apples and pears.
Brush fruit lightly with lemon juice or ascorbic acid color keeper to keep from turning brown.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Drain liquid from pineapple and mix liquid with pudding.
Add powdered sugar, vanilla, crushed pineapple and Cool Whip.
Boil sugar, brown sugar, Carnation milk and Karo until soft ball stage reached.
Add butter and vanilla.
Cool slightly and beat until creamy colored and thickened.
Add pecans and drop by spoonfuls on waxed paper.

Peel and slice potatoes in french fry style. Pour milk and egg in a large bowl. Mix well. Add potatoes. Stir with hands to cover potatoes with egg and milk mixture. Sprinkle with flour to cover potatoes. Fry in vegetable oil.
Brown ground beef in skillet, stirring, until crumbly; drain. Saute green pepper and green onions with garlic salt in margarine in skillet until tender.
Mix in flour.
Add milk gradually, stirring constantly, until thick.
Stir in soup.
Simmer for several minutes.
Add ground beef and cheese, mixing well.
Cook over low heat until cheese melts, stirring frequently.
Mix in celery, salt and pepper.
Combine with spaghetti in baking dish, mixing well.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Combine blueberries, 2/3 cup sugar, lemon juice and 1/4 cup water.
In medium saucepan, cook over low heat until berries are soft.
Combine cornstarch and 3 tablespoons water in small jar.
Shake until dissolved.
Add cornstarch mixture to blueberry mixture; cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Set aside to cool.
Combine flour, margarine and pecans in a small bowl; mix well.
Press evenly into bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cool.
Combine cream cheese and 2/3 cup sugar. Beat until smooth.
Fold in whipped topping.
Spread mixture evenly over cooled crust.
Pour blueberry mixture evenly over all. Refrigerate.
Cut into squares to serve.
Yield: 15 servings.

recipes.t: K.I.S.S. Roast(Keeping It Simple And Succulent)
d: Insert slivered garlic into roast.
In frypan, brown roast in butter.
Mix together soy sauce, ginger, sherry, paprika, salt and water.
Pour over roast.
Arrange celery in large pot or Dutch oven; place roast on top.
Cover tightly.
Roast at 250° for 3 1/2 hours, basting occasionally.
Remove roast from pan; place on warm serving dish.
Discard celery.
While mixing cake, substitute 4 egg whites instead of whole eggs or use egg substitute.
Substitute equivalent applesauce instead of oil.
Follow baking directions as on package.
Melt 1 stick margarine.
Add crushed crackers and mix well; set aside.
Cook frozen vegetables until tender and drain.
Melt Cheez Whiz.
Add canned milk and 1/2 stick of margarine; set aside.
Saute chopped vegetables in olive oil in a large pot on medium-high heat for about 10 minutes.
Add turkey sausage and turkey and crumble; cook at medium heat, crumbling turkey and stirring until turkey loses pink color.
If using wine, add wine and cook at medium-high heat until most of wine liquid has evaporated.
Add the tomatoes (chop some of the tomatoes in the pot with a spatula, if whole) and lower heat to keep simmering.
Simmer one or two hours.
Serve over your favorite pasta.
More than enough sauce for one pound of pasta.
Combine sour cream and pudding mix. Add coconut and pineapple and stir. Spoon into 8 x 4 or 9 x 5 inch loaf pan and freeze 3 hours. To serve, dip pan in warm water to unmold.
Place potatoes in a saucepan of cold water with the sprig of basil.
Bring to boil, then cover and simmer until potatoes are tender.
Drain and remove basil.
Melt butter in a pan; add chopped basil and cook for 30 seconds, stirring, taking care not to brown the butter.
Toss the potatoes in the butter; spoon into serving dish and garnish with basil sprig.
Serve immediately.
Serves 4. Essential to use fresh basil or half a jar of pesto.
Mix egg white and salt with rotary beater until stiff.
Add 2 tablespoons sugar to this.
Whip cream and 4 tablespoons sugar; add flavors.
Mix cream and egg whites together.
Spoon into cupcake cups and freeze until firm.
Enjoy!
Arrange chicken in 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish.
Combine soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice, curry powder and mushrooms in a large bowl and set aside.
Boil sugar and milk for 3 minutes.
Stir to keep from sticking. Remove from heat.
Add peanut butter.
Stir to dissolve.
Add pecans, vanilla and crackers.
Beat until it starts to harden. Drop onto wax paper with teaspoon.
Makes 35.
Ground tomatoes, peppers, onions and cabbage and put into a container with glaze on it.
Put a layer of salt over it and let stand overnight.
The next morning wash and be sure all salt is out of mixture.
Put back in container and put 7 lb. sugar, 3 Tbsp ground allspice and 3 Tbsp turmeric and enough white vinegar to stir where you can cook it.
Cook until tender and put in jars and seal.
Saute the onion and celery in oil.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Transfer to a large casserole dish.
Top with 1 stack crushed Ritz crackers.
Drizzle 1 stick margarine over all.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Add sandwich spread, chicken broth and salt and pepper.
Add more pickles if you want to.
You can add eggs or anything else you want.
In double boiler, melt margarine.
Mix flour and sugar together and stir into butter. Add cream.
Cook over medium heat until thick. Cool and spread over cake.
Boil chicken 40 minutes or until tender.
Remove chicken and let cool slightly. Bone chicken, dice and set aside.
Cook spinach according to package directions and drain well. Reserve 1 cup spinach broth. Set aside.
Saute onion in butter until tender. Stir in spinach and chicken. Set aside.
Combine soup, reserved spinach broth, milk, green chiles, sour cream and half of the cheese in a bowl.
Mix well. Stir half of the sauce mixture into chicken mixture.
Reserve remaining sauce.
Spoon chicken mixture evenly down center of each tortilla.
Roll up tortillas and place, seam down, into 2 lightly greased pans. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 25 minutes. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake an additional 5 minutes.
Serves 16; you may halve the recipe, if you want.
Cut cloves of garlic and tomatoes.
Cover with Italian salad dressing in a bowl, such as a Tupperware.
Turn bowl upside down every hour or so for 8 to 24 hours.
Mix together the coconut and butter and line 8 (5 ounce) custard cups; refrigerate.
When ready to serve, fill cups with ice cream.
Top with any of the following: crushed pineapple, strawberries, chocolate or butterscotch sauce, chopped nuts, apricot or raspberry jam.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook sausage; save some sausage grease to mix in the pancake batter.
Mix pancake mix, egg, milk and oil in bowl.
Add cinnamon, vanilla extract and sausage grease.

Preheat oven to 350°. In large bowl, combine eggs, cottage cheese, flour and bouillon. Add squash; mix well. Turn into greased 12 x 7-inch baking dish. Top with Cheddar cheese and bacon. Bake 20 to 25 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Do not dilute juices.
Mix all together.
When ready to serve, put sherbet balls on top of juices.
Add ginger ale and mix.
Serve.
Fry bacon; drain and set aside.
Cook spinach; drain and set aside.
Boil potatoes; drain and mash.
Then add spinach to potatoes.
Tie in cheesecloth bag the 16 cloves, whole allspice and cinnamon stick, broken into pieces.
Stud 3 oranges with box of cloves; cover well.
In saucepan, combine apple juice or cider, cranberry juice, sugar and bitters.
Add bag of spices and oranges; cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add rum just before serving.
Garnish with slice of orange for each cup.
Serves 10 to 12.
Batter:
Mix the cake mix, eggs, water, 1/2 container sour cream and 1 1/2 mashed bananas (mashed by using bottom of a small glass).
Use mixer on batter until lumps of cake mix have dissolved.
Pour batter into two 9-inch round pans or 1 large oblong pan.
I use wax paper on round pans.
Bake as box directs.
Put the lime juice in a pitcher.
Add the honey, sugar and water.
Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Place in refrigerator until ready to serve.
Serve over ice.
Prepare crust. Mix graham cracker crumbs and sugar. Then mix in butter. Pack into a 9 inch pie plate and bake 375 degrees for about 8 minutes. Heat pineapple and add marshmallows allowing them to
melt. Add 2 Tbsp. jello powder. Stir until dissolved. Cool until it begins to stiffen then add cream. Add 2 Tbsp. powdered sugar to cream. Pour into graham cracker crust and refrigerate.
Slowly melt butter.
Mix together the milk and flour.
Add eggs; mix, leaving some lumps.
Pour into heavy baking pan which butter has been melted in.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar; squeeze fresh lemon over.
Add marmalade.
Combine applesauce, squash, brown sugar, nutmeg, salt, butter, eggs and milk.
Mix well.
Pour into buttered baking dish. Sprinkle with nuts and bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve hot.
Saute onion in butter in large fry pan and add Kielbasa. When heated or lightly browned, add cabbage and seasonings.
Cover until cabbage is cooked through.
Add noodles and sour cream. Heat and serve.
Combine spaghetti sauce, tomatoes with liquid and water in bowl.
Stir to blend and break up the tomatoes; set aside. Combine Ricotta cheese, 1/2 cup Mozzarella, egg and garlic powder in bowl; mix well.
Spread 1/3 spaghetti sauce mixture in bottom of microwave-safe baking dish (about 12 x 8 x 2-inch).
Place 3 noodles on top of sauce.
Spread half Ricotta mixture over noodles.
Layer with half of the spinach and 1 cup Mozzarella. Repeat layers (sauce, noodles, Ricotta, spinach and Mozzarella). Cover with the remaining noodles; pour on remaining sauce mixture.
Mix sugar, cocoa, milk, syrup and salt together.
Cook on medium heat until it forms a soft ball when dropped in cold water. Remove from heat.
Add margarine and vanilla.
Beat until cool.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Mix together 1/2 cup mayo, milk and seasonings.
Lightly dip chicken into mayo mixture.
Coat well with crumbs.
Place on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes.
Mix remaining mayo with salsa.
Serve with nuggets on toothpicks.
Beat egg whites; add baking powder, sugar, nuts (if desired) and Ritz crackers (crumbled coarsely).
Spread in butter lined long pan, then add egg mixture.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Add onion, garlic, bread crumbs, milk, beaten egg yolks, salt, pepper and nutmeg to hamburger.
Beat egg whites stiff; fold into hamburger mixture.
Pinch off small bits and roll into tiny balls, keeping hands well-greased with cooking oil to ensure smooth balls.
Place, uncovered, in greased casserole dish.
Cook at 375° for 35 minutes.
Pour mushroom soup over top; bake for another 10 minutes.
Crush cookies and spread on bottom of a
9 x 13-inch or larger baking dish.
Melt 1 stick butter; mix with cookie crumbs.
Cream 1 1/2 sticks butter; add sugar and egg yolks and beat until fluffy and light.
Beat egg whites until stiff, then blend into sugar-butter mixture.
Spoon over cookie crumbs.
Cover cream with pie filling.
Cover with whipped cream.
Chill several hours or overnight before serving.
Add boiling water to jello.
Add blueberries and pineapple with juice. Chill until firm.
Combine cream cheese, sugar and sour cream.
Add vanilla.
Spread on top of jello.
Sprinkle with pecans.
This recipe will serve 7 people.
Heat oven to 350°.
Lightly mix bread, meat, milk, egg, onion, Worcestershire sauce and salt.
Spread mixture evenly in 9-inch pie pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Drain fat from meat loaf.
Pile mashed potatoes on meat loaf as for meringue on pie.
Sprinkle cheese over potatoes and bake until cheese is melted.
Bake the pie shell at 450° for 7 minutes.
Remove from oven. Reduce temperature to 325°.
Crumble corned beef hash into pie shell.
Top with the cheese.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over hash and cheese.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until set.
Cool for 25 minutes before serving.
Set out ingredients, mixing bowl, measuring spoons and cups, fork, muffin tins and pot holders.
Set oven at 450°.
Beat egg in mixing bowl.
Add ground steak, 1 teaspoon of salt, 1/8 teaspoon of pepper, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, chopped onion, bread crumbs and vegetable soup.
Mix lightly with fork. Butter 12 muffin tins.
Spoon meat mixture into muffin cups. Round off tops.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.

Heat oven to 400°. In a large skillet, brown beef and onion. Drain off all fat from beef. Stir in mustard, salt, garlic powder and pepper. Spoon 1/2 of beef mixture evenly into crust-lined pan. Top with cheese cubes. Add remaining beef. Spread evenly and drizzle with ketchup. Sprinkle with shredded Cheddar cheese. Top with second crust. Seal edges and flute. Cut holes in top crust. Bake 30 to 40 minutes, until golden brown. Serves 8.
Melt butter.
Mix with cooked, mashed potatoes and vanilla. Add 10x sugar and salt.
Knead until smooth.
Roll out on wax paper sprinkled with 10x sugar.
Spread peanut butter on this mixture.
Roll up.
Chill and cut into thin slices.
Cream butter, shortening and sugar.
Add vanilla and eggs. add flour, soda and salt.
Mix well.
Add chips and nuts.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
In a Dutch oven, brown brisket in oil on both sides over medium-high heat; drain.
Combine hot water and soup mix; pour over brisket.
Cover and bake at 325° for 2 to 2 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
Remove brisket to a serving platter.
Let stand for 10 to 15 minutes.
Combine cornstarch and cold water until smooth; gradually stir into pan juices.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
Thinly slice meat across the grain; serve with the gravy.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Dissolve red hots in the hot water.
While still hot, add Jell-O.
Cool and add applesauce.
Pour 1/2 of the mixture in pan. Set until solid.
Mix cheese, cream and mayonnaise and spread over solid mixture.
Add remaining Jell-O and chill.
Put the dried fruit and sugar in a bowl.
Pour the tea over; soak overnight.
Grease and base-line a 2-pint loaf tin.
The next day, add the egg, flour, baking powder and mixed spice to the fruit and tea mixture.
Beat thoroughly with a wooden spoon until all ingredients are evenly combined.
Spoon into the prepared tin; level the surface.
Bake at 350° for about 1 1/4 hours, or until well risen and a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean. Turn out onto a wire rack to cool.
Serve sliced and spread with butter.
Serves 14.
Mix cake mix with dry lemon or orange flavored gelatin in a large bowl, then add all the other ingredients at once.
Mix with an electric beater for 2 minutes.
This is a thin batter.
Add salt and pepper to the flour and pound into meat.
In large skillet, add the olive oil and brown the meat.
Add the onion, green pepper, boiling water and ketchup.
Cover closely; simmer slowly until done.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Chill all liquid ingredients.
Pour into large punch bowl. Float sherbet on top.
Stir while serving.

Pour milk into shallow dish. Combine bread crumbs, cornmeal, sesame seed, seasoning, dry mustard, garlic powder and pepper in bowl. Dip fish into milk. Coat with crumb mixture. Spray a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with Pam.
Place fish in baking pan. Sprinkle with parsley. Bake at 450° for 4 to 6 minutes per 2-inches of thickness until fish is golden and flakes easily.
In a 10-inch skillet, combine frozen potatoes and milk.
Heat to boiling, stirring often to break up potatoes.
Cover, reduce heat to low and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until potatoes are thawed and tender.
Remove cover and stir in garlic, pepper, peas and carrots and tuna.
Cook until peas and carrots are tender and tuna is hot, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1 cup cheese mixing well. Sprinkle remaining 1/2 cup cheese over top.
Cover and cook over low heat until cheese is melted, 2 to 3 minutes.
Dissolve jello in 2 cups hot water.
Add ice cream and stir until melted.
Place in refrigerator.
When it starts to jell, add well-drained pineapple, marshmallows and pecans.
Chill until jelled.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray a 12-cup muffin pan with nonstick cooking spray.
In medium bowl, combine flour, sugar, cinnamon, salt, baking soda and baking powder.
In a large bowl with wire whisk or fork, mix fruit, yogurt, egg substitute, applesauce, raisins and vanilla until well blended.
With spoon, stir flour mixture into fruit mixture just until flour is moistened.
Spoon into pans.
Bake 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of muffin comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes.
Remove from pan. Makes 12.
These freeze well.
In medium bowl combine salmon, cream cheese, salsa, parsley and cilantro.
Add cumin if desired.
Spread about 2 tablespoons of salmon mixture on each tortilla.
Roll each tortilla up tightly and wrap individually with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
(Can also be frozen.) Slice each tortilla into bite size pieces.
Yields 48 appetizers.
Put juice of tomatoes into a blender or food processor set up to chop.
Add onions, garlic, salt and cilantro.
Process until smooth.
Add tomatoes.
Process just slightly.
Add Ro-Tel tomatoes; process just until mixed.
Do not overblend.
Preheat oven to 425°. Line 9-inch pie plate with bottom pastry crust.
Roll out top crust.
Combine apples, sugar, flour and cinnamon.
Arrange pears in 9-inch pie plate.
Top with apple mixture; dot with butter.
Adjust top crust.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes or until filling is tender and crust nicely browned. Serve warm or cold.
Makes one 9-inch pie.
Mix chili sauce, grape jelly and soup mix together in crock-pot.
Spray with Pam first.
Add wieners and stir until coated.
Cook on low for 4 to 6 hours.
Peel and cube potatoes; boil until very soft.
Drain water. Mix milk, butter, parsley, cheese and potatoes with electric beater until well mixed to a creamy texture.
Rub the butter over the bottom of a shallow flameproof casserole or skillet.
Trim off the bottoms and any damaged outer leaves of the endive and cut the heads into diagonal slices about 1-inch thick.
Put them in the pan with salt and pepper to taste, lemon juice and water.
Press a piece of buttered foil on top of the endive and cover with a lid.
Cook over low heat for 7 to 8 minutes or until the endive is tender.
Shake the pan occasionally. Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and serve.
Wash potatoes and rub with vegetable oil.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour or until done.
Split potatoes in half lengthwise.
Carefully scoop out pulp, leaving shells intact.
Mash pulp.
Add salt, butter, orange juice concentrate and pineapple to mashed pulp. Mix well.
Stuff potato shell with pulp mixture.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Cut each marshmallow in half.
Place 2 marshmallows (cut side down) on each potato half.
Place potato shells on baking sheet.
Bake at 400° until lightly browned on top.
Bake angel food cake.
Tear into bite-size pieces and put in bottom of 9 x 13-inch dish.
Mix large package sugar-free chocolate pudding with skim milk.
Mix well with 8 ounces light Cool Whip. Alternate layers with 1/2 cake topped with 1/2 pudding.
Sprinkle with chopped pecans.
Repeat layers.

recipes.t: White Christmas Mousse(In Honor Of Sep Palin, Along With Greyhound)
d: Melt the white chocolate with hazelnuts in double boiler, stirring occasionally.
Gradually add warm milk, stirring until smooth; allow to cool.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form; gently fold into chocolate mixture (the white chocolate mixture). Whip cream until stiff; fold into white chocolate mixture.
Add lemon juice; stir lightly.
Spoon into 1-quart glass bowl, or 6 individual stemmed dessert glasses.
Chill at least 2 hours; garnish with dark chocolate curls or shavings.
One may also want to place a maraschino cherry on the top to garnish.
Place chicken in casserole dish.
Mix Italian sauce (dressing) and lemon juice.
Pour over chicken; melt butter and pour over chicken, then salt and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix dry jello and water together. Chill until almost set. Whip until fluffy and fold in the Cool Whip. Then add all the other ingredients. Refrigerate for about 1 hour. Ready to serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in casserole.
Add peaches. Sprinkle with 1/4 cup sugar.
Combine remaining sugar, flour, baking powder, salt and nutmeg.
Stir in milk and vanilla.
Pour batter over peaches; bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown. Serve vanilla ice cream over cobbler.
Cream the butter and sugar together, adding milk in small amounts.
Add salt and vanilla.
Drain cherries.
Roll cherries in cream mixture to cover each cherry well.
Add nuts to what is left of mixture and roll in oblong rolls.
Melt chocolate and paraffin over boiling water.
Dip cherry and nut rolls, one at a time, in melted chocolate.
Place on wax paper to cool.

Cream butter, shortening and sugar. Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating after each addition. Sift soda, flour and cocoa together. Add alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with dry ingredients. Stir in coconut, vanilla and nuts. Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake in three greased and floured 9-inch layer cake pans at 325 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes.

Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic. Saut for 5 minutes. Stir in the lentils and bulgur wheat. Add the broth, tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes or until lentils are tender. Makes 6 (1 cup) servings.

Cream the sugar and margarine until fluffy. Add egg and combine. In a separate bowl, sift dry ingredients together, then add to creamed mixture. Stir in undrained pineapple just until all ingredients are moistened. Fill greased muffin pan 2/3 full and bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 12 to 14.
In a mixing bowl, combine cake mix, fruit cocktail and eggs. Mix for 2 minutes or until all the ingredients are blended well.
In a 1 1/2-quart bowl, microwave cream cheese, uncovered, on High for 1 minute; stir in sour cream, milk, mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce.
Add kolbassi, half of the onions and Parmesan cheese; stir.
Cook, uncovered, on High for 2 to 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining onion.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease an 8-inch square pan.
In a small saucepan combine soup and margarine.
Heat over low heat until butter melts.
Remove from heat and stir in milk.
In a large bowl combine flour, meal, sugar and baking powder.
Add soup mixture, egg, corn and cheese.
Stir until batter is just combined.
Do not over mix.
Scoop batter into prepared pan and bake 30 to 35 minutes.
I usually use an iron skillet instead of a pan.
Substitute applesauce for liquid called for on cake mix package and measure additional 1/4 c.
Mix cake as package directs, adding extra 1/4 c. applesauce in the first mixing.
Stir in walnuts and bake as per package instructions.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine ground beef, onion, bread crumbs, egg, mayonnaise and seasonings; mix well.
Keeping meat mixture one inch from edges; press meat mixture into the bottom of a 15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes; drain.
Top mixture with cheese and bake 5 to 8 minutes longer or until cheese is melted.
Remove from oven and allow to set (about 5 minutes).
Cut meat into 20 squares and place inside split rolls. Serve with mustard and mayonnaise.
Mix first four ingredients and set aside.
Cut up chicken in small pieces and grill.
Combine cooked chicken, green onions and olives.
Fill tortilla with meat mixture and Monterey Jack cheese and roll.
Cover enchiladas with soup mixture. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Line baking dish with peaches.
Combine all other ingredients and spread over top of peaches.
Combine 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water.
Pour over top of batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Shred lettuce in large glass bowl.
Sprinkle next 3 ingredients over top in layers.
Break peas apart and sprinkle over while frozen.
Spread mayonnaise like frosting.
Sprinkle sugar and enough cheese to cover top.
Cover and put in refrigerator for 24 hours or overnight.
Before serving, sprinkle top with eggs and Bac*Os and toss.
In small bowl, mix with beater the margarine, cream cheese and 10x sugar.
In another bowl, combine milk and pudding; beat until creamy and thick.
Add cream cheese mixture; continue beating until well mixed.
Now fold in Cool Whip.
Cook turkey breast in crock-pot overnight.
Spread breast and line a large pan with it.
Melt Velveeta, 1 1/4 cans cream of chicken soup and 1 1/2 cups turkey broth, stir until melted.
Pour mixture over the top of meat.
Next, in a large bowl crumble up biscuits and cornbread.
Add chopped eggs, onion, the rest of the soup and enough turkey broth to make moist.
Add sage and seasonings to taste.
Pour over meat and bake at 350° until dressing is done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, cream the margarine. Add sugar and mix well. Add eggs, vanilla and cocoa.
Mix well. Stir in flour, soda and salt. Add chocolate chips, white chocolate and nuts. Mix well. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Cookies will be soft and appear to be undercooked.
Don't overbake.
Chewy and good.
Yields 3 to 4 dozen.
Brown beef, onion and green pepper in butter until tender. Stir in gravy and cabbage.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes. Spoon 1/2 cup mixture on bottom half of each roll; top with cheese and cover with top half of roll.
Make 1 pie at a time.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Put spinach, cheese and onion into pie shells.
Pour eggs, milk, salt and pepper over spinach mixture.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes; turn oven down to 350°.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
These do not freeze well.
Boil whole sweet potatoes.
Let cool.
Peel and cut into quarters.
Place potatoes in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle on sugar, vanilla and water.
Dot potatoes and sugar with butter. Sprinkle lightly with nutmeg.
Bake at 325° to 350° until syrup thickens.
Serves 8 to 10.
Combine beef broth, tomato juice and water.
Heat to boiling. Reduce heat and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add parsley.
Serve.
Makes 6 servings.
Equals 14 calories or free exchange.
Cut potatoes into stew-sized chunks and boil until firmly cooked.
Brown hamburger and onion in large skillet; drain.
Add sauce, green beans and potatoes into skillet.
Cook on low heat approximately 15 minutes.
Top with grated cheese, if desired. Makes 4 servings.
In
saucepan,
combine rhubarb,
sugar and water. Cook over medium
heat
for 3 minutes until tender.
Cool;
drain, reserving syrup.
Add
enough water to syrup to equal 2 cups. Return
and bring
to a boil. Stir in Jell-O until dissolved. Add
cup cold
water
and
lemon juice. When set, add rhubarb,
cream cheese and banana. Turn into 6 cup mold or 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sift flour and baking powder, 2 or 3 times.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Mix flour and milk alternately.
Bake in layers.
Slice potatoes and onions on large piece of foil. Dot with butter. Combine cheese, parsley, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Sprinkle over potatoes; fold foil and seal. Grill 30 to 40 minutes.
Bake Jiffy cake mix in 9 x 12-inch loaf pan as directed on package.
Cool.
Beat cream cheese with milk until smooth.
Then add pudding (mix as you would to make pudding).
Pour over cooled cake.
Let set up.
Then put on a layer of fruit (strawberries or blueberries or whatever).
Then cover with Cool Whip. Refrigerate.
Place meat in plastic bag or shallow glass dish.
Mix soy sauce, sherry, 2 tablespoons honey and garlic.
Pour over meat. Fasten bag or cover dish securely.
Refrigerate 8 hours, turning meat occasionally.
Remove meat from marinade; reserve marinade. Lace ribs on spit rod; secure with holding forks.
Check balance by rotating spit in palms of hands.
Arrange medium-hot coals at back of firebox; place foil drip pan under spit area.
Cook ribs on rotisserie for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until done, basting with marinade.
Brush ribs with 1/2 cup honey during last 30 minutes of cooking.
Double aluminum foil and line a rectangular baking dish, leaving plenty extra to cover the entire roast.
Put the roast in pan and cut onion into small pieces on top of it.
Pour soup over the roast and onion.
Add A.1. sauce on top of soup.
Bring foil together to form a tent, covering the roast.
Bake at 350° for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Wash
tomatoes;
cut
stem
ends
off. Mix
flour
and seasonings.
Cut tomatoes in 1/2-inch slices; dredge in flour. Saute in salad oil until brown on both sides, turning once.
Crumble meat into casserole dish.
Stir in peppers and onion. Microwave on High for 5 to 6 minutes or until meat loses pink color when stirred.
Drain meat mixture well.
In a pan, bring pineapple and juice to a boil.
Add gelatin. Stir to dissolve.
Stir in marshmallows into cooled gelatin. Refrigerate 1 hour.
Fold into gelatin along with crushed mints. Spread into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish.
Refrigerate.
Top with whipped cream.
Makes 12 servings.
Mix sugar and nuts well.
Add margarine and flour.
Turn onto board.
Make a well and add yolks; mix.
Use about 2/3 of this dough to make bottom layer in jelly roll pan.
Roll to about 1/2-inch thickness.
Spread with jam.
Use remaining dough to make cross bars on top by making thin rolls of dough and place these crisscross to each other on top of the jam layer.
Bake in moderate oven until light brown.
Slice into rectangles.
Saute everything chopped.
Add chicken broth.
Boil until all is soft; add milk and potatoes until soft.
Shut off heat; let cool.
Add the sour cream.
Stir well and serve.
In a large saucepot, bring broccoli, water and bouillon to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes or until broccoli is crisp-tender.
Drain and place in a serving dish; keep warm.
In a skillet, saute almonds in margarine until browned. Add onion and salt; saute until onion is tender.
Pour over broccoli; toss to coat.
Yield: 6 servings.
Boil mustard greens in 1-quart water, covered, until tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in margarine and pepper and serve.
Brown chops and cut up meat.
Place in crock-pot.
Peel potatoes and slice.
Add onion, potatoes and tomatoes; cook until potatoes are tender.
White potatoes may be substituted for sweet potatoes.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Combine the soups and milk; heat to just below boiling point. Add the curry and mix well.
Just before serving, add cream and sherry.
Mix flour, mustard and salt.
Sprinkle one side of beef steak with half of the flour mixture; pound in.
Turn beef and pound in remaining flour mixture.
Cut beef into 6 serving pieces.
Mix lemon jello and hot water until jello is dissolved.
Add cream cheese and mix, then add pineapple and pecans.
Pour in a jello mold and chill. Mix strawberry jello and hot water until jello is dissolved, then add cranberry sauce, pour over chilled mixture and continue to chill until set.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add remaining shortening, vanilla and/or almond flavoring and pineapple juice. Beat for 3 minutes.
Then add eggs and water.
Beat 2 minutes longer.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes for 3 to 4 layers or 35 minutes if in a large flat pan.
Heat fruit in a 2-quart saucepan until hot.
Mix sugar and cornstarch together and add to fruit.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Mix Jiffy cake mix according to package directions.
In a hot skillet cook green pepper and onion until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in soup and milk and blend well. Stir in meat, cheese and pimentos.
Cook for 5 minutes until thoroughly heated.
Pour over split biscuits.
Yields 6 servings.

recipes.t: David Payne'S Strawberry Bowl(Sparkling Wine Punch)
d: Layer berries and sugar; let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
(Add Gran Marnier during layering if desired.)
Add wine and lemon juice; refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Add "sparkle" and serve.
Combine butter, condensed milk and bourbon in a large mixing bowl; add sugar and knead until mixture is well blended and does not stick to hands.
Knead in chopped pecans.
Shape in 1-inch balls.

Combine chocolate morsels and paraffin in top of a double boiler; place over hot water, stirring until chocolate is melted. Using a toothpick, dip each ball of candy into chocolate mixture. Place on waxed paper.
Remove toothpick and gently press a pecan half on each.
Yield:
About 6 dozen.
In saucepan, combine first 5 ingredients.
Bring to boiling. Place pears and orange slices in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Pour cranberry mixture over fruit.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until pears are tender.
Serve warm.
Makes 6 servings.
Drain pineapple.
Combine biscuit mix, milk, eggs, butter, mustard, onion powder and nutmeg in blender.
Stir in ham, cheese, onions and pineapple.
Pour into greased 9 x 9-inch or 12 x 7-inch pan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes at 350°, until set.
Cut flowerets off broccoli.
Peel stalk of broccoli.
Slice stalk.
Add sunflower seeds, raisins and onion to broccoli.
Mix Miracle Whip, vinegar and sugar.
Pour over broccoli
mix.
Add bacon and mix well.
Combine and mix ground beef, salt, onion, oatmeal, pepper and milk.
Form into small balls.
Place in baking dish.
Set aside. Mix together catsup, vinegar, sugar and water.
Pour over meat balls.
Bake at 350°
for 1 hour.
Serve over potatoes, noodles, rice, etc.
If you can't get capers and chow chow pickles, use 2 tablespoons Durkee dressing and 1/2 cup chopped sour pickles. Salt and pepper to taste.
Combine chocolate, 1/2 cup milk, whole egg and 2/3 cup sugar; cook over low heat until thick.
Cool.
Cream shortening and remaining cup of sugar; add egg yolks and mix well.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with 1 cup milk and vanilla extract. Stir in chocolate custard mixture.
Bake in 2 waxed paper-lined 8-inch layer cake pans in moderate oven (350°) for 25 to 30 minutes.
Put layers together with frosting of your choice (regular white seven minute frosting, ivory frosting or chocolate fudge frosting).
Cut
beef
into
bite
size chunks.
In a bowl, combine shoyu, ginger and sugar.
Add beef; marinate for 1 hour.
In a pot,
add oil
and heat.
Add beef;
cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Set
aside. Place onion, celery and green pepper in pot for 2 minutes. Stir cornstarch into remaining sauce.
Add marinated beef
and tomatoes
to vegetables; mix well. Cook for 3 minutes.
In a medium-sized mixing bowl, beat together butter, eggs, orange extract and apple juice.
Add flour, soda, baking powder and spices; beat well.
Stir in diced prunes and nuts.
Spoon into an oiled and floured 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Spread batter evenly in pan.
In a food processor or blender, combine garbanzo beans, yogurt, salad dressing, bread crumbs, lemon juice and red pepper. Cover and process until smooth.
Stir in olives.
Chill, uncovered, for at least one hour.
Serve with vegetable dippers or crackers.
Makes about 1 2/3 cups.
Mix oil, lemon juice, seasonings and sugar.
Add mushrooms and marinate 1 hour.
Stir in scallions and pimiento.
Serve in nest of shredded lettuce.
Heat oil
in
large Dutch oven.
Add cabbage and onion. Cook over
medium heat until slightly browned, stirring often. While cabbage
cooks,
remove
core
from tomatoes with tip of sharp paring
knife.
Quarter
2 tomatoes and place in blender jar
with garlic, tamari sauce and molasses.
Blend at medium speed until smooth.
Add blended mixture to cabbage and bring to
a boil. Chop remaining tomato and add to soup.
Add chili powder
and cumin.
Stir
in
cup water more, if needed. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Beat egg whites, cream of tartar, and salt until stiff. Slowly add sugar and flour.
Add vanilla.
Pour into angel cake pan.
Beat hot water, egg yolks, sugar, and salt for 3 minutes or until lemon yellow.
Add flour mixed with baking powder and beat well.
Add lemon flavoring.
Pour into pan on top of white mixture.
Bake in a very slow oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
In large bowl with an electric mixer, beat the cream cheese and the butter until the mixture is light and creamy.
Add the sugar, a little at a time, beating, and beat the mixture until it is combined well.
Add the vanilla and the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
In a bowl, stir together the flour and mace; stir the mixture into the cream cheese mixture and stir in the hazelnuts.

Pour batter into buttered and floured 10 x 4 1/2-inch tube pan with a removable bottom or a Bundt pan. Bake cake in the middle of a preheated 300° oven for 1 hour and 45 minutes or until tester comes out clean.
Cool.
Sift confectioners sugar over cake.
Pour the one cup of boiling water over half of the dates and add the soda.
Let this mixture stand while you mix the next batch of ingredients.
Sift (mix) flour, sugar and baking powder.
Mix into the date, soda and water mixture and add beaten egg, butter and 1/2 cup of nuts.
Blend well and spread mixture in a greased 10 x 15 x 1-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Spread over the top a sauce made by mixing the remaining 1/2 pound dates, 1/2 cup nuts and the 2/3 cup of boiling water.
The sauce should be mixed while the cake is baking.
The topping will remain moist and keep the cake moist.
Serve slices with whipped cream.
Take flat cookie sheet or jelly roll pan and cover with foil. Spread saltine crackers on pan to entirely cover pan.
In saucepan, melt and boil butter and sugar for 3 minutes.
Pour over crackers and bake at 350° for 7 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle chocolate chips over entire pan.
It will have a glossy look.
Let cool and then break into pieces.
This is a delicious treat for kids and kids at heart.
Butter both sides of bread.
Layer in pan.
Add Swiss cheese, ham and Cheddar cheese.
Add second layer of bread.
Mix eggs, milk, mustard and salt.
Pour over sandwiches.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake 1 hour at 350° in 9 x 13-inch pan.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, melt the margarine.
Sprinkle with crumbs, then sprinkle with coconut
flakes, next sprinkle with butterscotch bits, then chocolate
bits.
Pour
condensed
milk over all.
Sprinkle with chopped
nuts.
Do
not stir, ingredients should be layered. Bake about
25 minutes in a 350° oven. Do not overbake.
Blend apricots, yogurt and dried milk.
Put in tall glass and add club soda.
Heat oven to 400°.
Place biscuits on 2 greased cookie sheets.
Press each biscuit into a 5-inch round.
Spread 1 tablespoon pizza sauce on each round.
Top with shredded cheese and pepperoni.
Bake at 400° for 9 to 12 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Yields 10 pizzas.
In saucepan, cook noodles until tender. Drain. Rinse with cold water.
In a large kettle, brown hamburger and onion.
Drain off grease. Add corn, tomato soup, tomato paste and seasonings.
In greased casserole dish, alternate layers of noodles, meat mixture and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Serves 6.
Peel
eggs
and
cut them in half lengthwise.
Mash the yolks and
add
anchovies,
mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, pepper, parsley
and
lemon juice. Mix into paste and refill the whites. Serve slightly chilled.
Use as part of antipasto or as canapes.

Mix candy, coconut and nuts. Add milk and mix well. Pour mixture into baking dish and cook in oven for approximately 30 minutes at 350°. Remove from oven and add sugar and flavorings. Mix well and drop on wax paper. Let dry; turn over to dry on other side. Very good.
Boil noodles; drain and set aside.
Saute onion, green pepper and garlic in butter.
Add hamburger and brown.
Add cream corn and tomato sauce.
Cook for about 20 minutes.
Add Parmesan cheese.
Place pumpkin, milk, honey and cinnamon in blender jar; blend. Add ice cream and rum.
Blend until smooth.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Serve at once.
Makes about 1 quart.
Brown ground beef, onions and garlic.
Drain.
Add tomatoes, seasonings and paste.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Place in casserole.
Top with quartered biscuits and 1 cup Mozzarella cheese (or whatever cheese you happen to have).
Bake at 425° for 15 to 20 minutes or until biscuits are done.
Spread bean dip on a pie plate.
Pour picante sauce over bean dip.
Sprinkle chopped onions over mixture.
Blend together mayonnaise and sour cream.
In a food processor or blender, place the cottage cheese, sour cream, dill pickle and pepper.
Process until smooth, about 1 minute.
Mix all vegetables together. Combine sugar, salad oil, cider vinegar and water. Mix well and pour over veggies. Toss well. Cover and chill overnight. Drain well before serving.
Combine paste and sauce in large saucepan or Dutch oven.
Add salt and pepper.
Slice and dice garlic, onion and mushrooms. Saute garlic in butter until golden brown; mix with sauce/paste. Heat until it bubbles.
Stir.
Saute onions in butter until limp; add to pot and stir.
Saute mushrooms until limp; add to pot and stir.
Reduce to simmer.
Simmer for 3 hours, stirring every 15 to 20 minutes.
After 2 1/2 hours, add sugar and blend.
Stir well. Sugar will blend flavors and kill the acid.
Drain fruit cocktail, apricots and pineapple.
Reserve juices. Place fruit in large bowl.
Add marshmallows and set aside. Place juices in saucepan and stir in gelatin.
Place over medium heat.
Heat, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
Cool slightly. Pour over fruit.
Stir in diced cherries and cherry juice.
Pour boiling water over oatmeal.
Add margarine; cover and let stand 20 minutes.
Add brown sugar, sugar and eggs; mix well.
Mix dry ingredients together and add to mixture.
Pour into well-greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake in 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes.

recipes.t: Crock-Pot Meat Balls In Mushroom Gravy
d: Cut bread into very small pieces.
Combine meat, bread, salt, pepper and minced onion.
Using scoop or hands, shape into rounds about 1 1/2 to 2 inches.
Brown meatballs in hot skillet in small amount of oil.
Turn so all sides are browned.
Place in crock-pot.
Add soup and water.
Cook on low for 6 to 12 hours or on high 6 hours.
Drain pineapple and dissolve jello in boiling juice from pineapple.
Refrigerate until mixture just begins to jell.
Soften the cream cheese and add mayonnaise, garlic powder and nuts.
Serve with crackers.
Dredge fruit and nuts with half the flour.
Cream sugar until smooth.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Combine remaining flour and baking powder and add to creamed mixture.
Add fruit and nuts.
Bake in miniature muffin pans or in miniature paper baking cups at 275° for 30 or 40 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Section wings at joints, discarding wing tips.
Combine flour, salt, sugar, cornstarch, rice flour and ajinomoto.
Beat eggs until well-blended.
Add with onions and soy sauce to dry mixture and mix thoroughly.
In a small saucepan, combine the butter, thyme, rosemary, oregano and basil.
Heat over low heat until the butter is melted. Slice the bread and generously brush the butter mixture on each slice.
Sprinkle with minced garlic, Parmesan cheese and parsley. Bake in a 475° oven or under the broiler until lightly browned. Serves 6.
Melt chocolate and butter in double boiler on low heat until smooth. Hand beat eggs lightly.
Stir in brown sugar, salt, vanilla, syrup and
chocolate mix.
Mix 1/2 cup walnuts into batter.
Turn into pie shell.
Cover top of pie with remaining walnuts.
Bake at 350° in center of the oven until barely set in the center and pastry is light golden brown, approximately 45 to 60 minutes.
Cool and refrigerate.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Spread 1/2 of vegetables on sheet of heavy-duty aluminum foil. Top with butter and cheese, then spread the other 1/2 of vegetables on top.
Season to taste with salt and teriyaki sauce.
Close up tightly with more foil and grill until done.
Heat soup and cheese together.
Put vegetables in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Pour soup/cheese mixture over and bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Cut potatoes like French fries; place on heavy-duty foil and sprinkle with seasoning and generous amount of cheese.
Dot with butter; seal in foil and bake on grill, turning a couple times.
Boil apricots in water until tender.
Chop fine and mix with sugar.
Melt margarine and mix with grated cheese.
Add flour, salt and red pepper.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Remove cheese dough from refrigerator and put orange size ball in microwave for 5 to 10 seconds.
Place ball between two sheets of wax paper and roll thin.
Remove top paper and cut dough into 1-inch size squares. Using knife, lift each square and put small amount of apricots in center.
Fold over two opposite edges forming diamond shape.
Bake at 225 until slightly brown.

Rub outside of chicken with ingredients except salt and ajinomoto and let stand overnight in refrigerator. Rub inside with salt and ajinomoto. Place chicken on rack and roast at 300° for 1/2 hour. Cover with foil and continue for another hour. Remove foil and raise temperature to 400° for another 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a 12-inch
pizza pan
or cookie sheet.
With greased fingers, press dough into prepared pan, making a 12-inch round and pinching up edges to form rim. With fork,
prick crust several times.
Bake
minutes
or until crust just begins to brown.
Spread
sauce evenly over crust. Sprinkle with half of the Mozzarella and
half
of the Parmesan cheese.
Top with sausage, olives,
mushrooms, green pepper and pepperoni. Sprinkle with
remaining
cheese.
Bake 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain.
Saute onion and green pepper in butter until tender.
Add macaroni; season with salt.
Stir in cottage cheese.
Serve immediately.

Combine meat, onion, salt, catsup, mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Shape into 4 patties. Broil 3 to 4-inches from heat for 7 to 8 minutes or until brown on one side. Turn and broil other side 4 or 5 minutes or until brown. Top each patty with 1/4 cup cooked rice. Sprinkle with cheese. Return to broiler until cheese melts. Spoon drippings over.
Serves 4.
Boil and debone chicken. Saute onion and bell pepper.
Cook spaghetti.
In microwave dish, combine cheese, soup, Ro-Tel and mushrooms.
Heat until soupy.
Combine all ingredients in casserole dish.
Heat through and through in oven or microwave.
Alternate macaroni and apples in layers in baking dish. Combine cream and sugar and pour over macaroni and apples.
Pour half and half over macaroni and apples until they are covered. Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 325° until tender (about 30 minutes).
This dish can be used for breakfast, lunch or supper.
Cream shortening.
Add sugar, eggs and flavorings.
Beat well. Dredge raisins in 1/2 cup flour and add to mixture.
Sift remaining flour with other dry ingredients and add to mixture. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet and flatten with a fork.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 400°.
Makes 40 two-inch cookies.
Dip bananas, apples and pears in lemon juice.
Drain.
Combine with orange sections in glass bowl.
Chill for 1 hour.
Fold in coconut and yogurt.
Cream the cheese with mixer.
Add milk, baking powder, vanilla and sugar.
Mix well.
Fold in fruit. Sprinkle with pecans. Freeze until firm.

Saut onion and celery in margarine. Add broth, cream cheese and soup. Stir over low heat until melted. Add remaining ingredients, except Parmesan. Pour into 1 to 1 1/2-quart casserole. Sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Bring 3 cups
water to boiling point.
Soak tapioca in other cup of water while water comes to boil, stirring occasionally. Add tapioca to water and
bring to boil, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and add sugar, salt
and
orange
juice.
Just before serving, add 1 quart frozen peaches and 1 1/2 cups sliced bananas.
Makes 1/2 gallon.
Thaw dough and cut each loaf in half to make 4 pieces.
Let rise about 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until double.
Mix spices in oil. Brush on dough.
Bake at 350° about 10 minutes.
Remove, slightly flatten with a fork.
Brush with extra oil and spices.
Place sliced tomatoes and cheese on each pizza.
Return to oven about 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix together cake mix, margarine and 1 egg.
Press into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
In a separate bowl, combine cream cheese, 3 eggs and sugar.
Beat until smooth.
Pour over cake mixture and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of wax paper; flatten to 1/4-inch thickness.
Use meat mallet or rolling pin. Combine eggs and milk.
Brush side of chicken with milk.
Put a piece of ham and piece of cheese in center of chicken breast. Brush cheese with milk mixture.
Turn ends over cheese and ham. Roll up, beginning with long side.
Secure with toothpicks. Dredge chicken in flour.
Dip in remaining milk mixture.
Coat well with bread crumbs.
Cover
and chill 1 hour.
Butter Bundt pan.
Spread marmalade over bottom; sprinkle with nuts.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon.
Dip each biscuit in butter, then in sugar mixture and stand on side in Bundt pan.
Sprinkle any remaining sugar over ring and drizzle with any remaining butter.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Serve warm.
Cook chicken in a large cooker until fully cooked.
Cool and debone.
Discard and put back into broth.
Peel and dice potatoes. Place into broth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Line bowl with romaine leaves.
Place mixed greens in center of bowl.
Arrange apple slices around bowl.
Sprinkle coconut.
Add raisins, almonds and carrots in circle on top of lettuce.
Cover and chill.
Blend eggs, salt and sugar with wire whip.
Add vanilla and milk.
Break bread into medium-sized pieces in a bowl.
Pour the melted butter over bread and toss to coat.
Then arrange bread in a Pyrex baking dish and pour the egg mixture over it.
Place the dish in a larger pan of water with at least an inch of water in the pan.
(Water should be well up around the dish.)
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Serve with lemon sauce or whiskey sauce (below).

recipes.t: Sour Cream Rum Pound Cake And Icing
d: Cream butter, shortening and sugar until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Add flavoring and salt.
Alternate mixing flour and sour cream ending with flour. Bake at 325° for 1 hour 10 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool.
Ice with Rum Butter Icing.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In broiler pan, place 1/2 the butter on bottom and add 1/2 of the Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 the A.1. sauce.
Sprinkle 1/2 the garlic powder and place steak in the center of the pan.
Slice potatoes around the steak.
Pour the other half of the remaining ingredients over steak and potatoes. Cover with aluminum foil; bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Broccoli Almond Angel Hair Pasta Salad
d: Cook pasta; drain and rinse with cool water.
Combine oil, vinegar, sesame oil and garlic in a jar and mix well.
Toss pasta and dressing.
Add bacon, almonds, onions and cheese.
Chill overnight.
Melt butter in a skillet and saute mushrooms over medium heat. Combine ham, cream cheese and thyme; blend well.
Stir in sauteed mushrooms.
Cover and chill overnight.
Serve on party bread slices.
Wash pineapples; trim any bad leaves around edge and cut in half.
Hollow out, leaving at least a half inch of the pineapple meat.
Mix chicken, scallions, almonds, pineapple meat and grapes. Add mayonnaise (just enough to hold the ingredients together). Fill pineapple shells.
To serve, line platter with red lettuce leaves and lay pineapple with leaves out.
Top salad with a little fresh chopped parsley and a half a grape turned upside down.
Mix thoroughly 1/2 cup soup, tuna, bread crumbs, eggs, parsley and lemon juice.
Spread evenly in well-greased loaf pan, 8 x 4 x 3-inch.
Bake 40 minutes at 400°.
Loosen edges; unmold.
Combine rest of soup, water and basil.
Heat.
Pour over loaf.
Grind or chop very fine the Spam, onion and olives.
Mix well with cream cheese.
Add Worcestershire sauce and lemon juice.
Put in a greased gelatin mold and chill for 6 to 8 hours.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Boil fryer.
Debone and cut into chunks.
Reserve broth.
Cook noodles in broth for 4 to 6 minutes.
Chop and saute celery and carrot.
Heat together all soups.
Mix all ingredients together. Bake in a 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes or microwave on High for 4 to 8 minutes.
Brown beef with onions; drain.
Prepare Jiffy mix according to the package.
Place 1/2 of the corn bread mixture on the bottom of the 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer ground beef, chilies, creamed corn and grated cheese.
Top with remaining corn bread mixture and cover with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Test by inserting a knife in center.
If clean when removed, it's done.
Cook chicken until cooked off bone.
Cut into pieces.
Dilute soup with milk.
Pour over chicken.
Mix stuffing with butter and chicken broth.
Pour over chicken and soup mixture.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Cream the cheese with a little milk.
Fold into stiffly whipped cream.
After lemon jello has chilled, fold it into the cream cheese mixture.
Fold the fruit cocktail into the chilled strawberry jello.
For this, use about 1 cup hot water and 3/4 cup cold water or juice from fruit cocktail.
When finished, the light mixture should be on top.
These mixtures have been poured into a mold and then chilled.
Unmold onto plate for serving.
Sift flour; stir in cornmeal.
Combine egg and buttermilk; add shortening.
Pour into dry ingredients; stir just until mixed. Turn into hot 8-inch square pan (greased).
Bake in 400° oven for about 30 minutes.
Open cans.
T. C. loves to do this.
Drain chicken and chillies.
Saute onion in 1 teaspoon butter.
Empty all cans in a large bowl, mix and add onion.
Crush Doritos.

recipes.t: Extra Easy, Extra Good Potato Soup
d: Peel and cut up potatoes into small pieces.
Peel and cut up 1/2 onion (or more, if desired).
Place 2 cans of soup and 2 soup cans of water in sauce pan over low-medium heat.
Add veggies and butter, season to taste.
Put lid on pan and cook until potatoes are tender (30 to 40 minutes).
Stir to prevent sticking.
Put margarine, sugar, milk, cocoa and vinegar in a heavy saucepan.
Stir and let come to a boil and boil for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and add other ingredients.
Mix well and drop from spoon onto waxed paper.
Can be poured into pan and cut into squares.
No baking necessary.
Cream sugar and shortening until light.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in mashed bananas. Sift dry ingredients together and add to banana mixture.
Add vanilla and mix well.
Pour into two well-greased bread loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in middle comes out clean.
Cool in pans on rack for 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove from pans and continue to cool on rack.
Cover with dish towel or soft cloth while cooling.
Wrap in plastic wrap or foil if you plan to freeze.

recipes.t: Flat Armenian (Russia) Bread With Sesame Seed(Churek)
d: Sprinkle the yeast and 1 teaspoon of the sugar into 1/2 cup of lukewarm (110-115F) water in a small, shallow bowl.

Let stand for 2 or 3 minutes, then stir to dissolve the yeast completely. Set the bowl aside in a warm, draft-free spot (such as an unlighted oven) for about 5 to 10 minutes, or until the mixture almost doubles in volume.
In a blender, sprinkle gelatin over cold milk and let stand 4 minutes.
Add hot milk and process in blender 2 minutes. Gradually add fruit, sugar and vanilla.
Process until smooth.
Pour into bowl and chill, stirring occasionally, until mixture mounds slightly when dropped from spoon. Fold chilled gelatin mixture into whipped cream.
Pour into an 8-inch baking pan.
Freeze until firm.
In a deep dish (casserole or baking), chop up onion; add green beans, carrots and sliced up potatoes.
Stir.
Add 1/4 cup milk and 1/2 can soup to the mixture.
Place pork chops on top of mixture; add rest of soup on top of each pork chop.
Put in oven for an hour at least until pork chops turn brown and are done (350°).
Melt oleo; add vinegar, lemon, chopped fine garlic, salt and pepper to taste; simmer.
Add all other ingredients; continue to simmer.
If oleo comes to top, add 1/4 cup beer to emulsify while stirring.
Blend sugar, oil, eggs, vanilla and cinnamon.
Stir in pineapple.
Slowly add flour.
Beat well.
Fold in bananas.
Bake in heavy tube pan for 1 hour and 20 minutes at 350°.
Add rice and salt to boiling water.
Cook until water is absorbed.
Fix broccoli according to package directions.
Combine all ingredients (except cheese) in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place cheese on top and bake at 325° for approximately 1/2 hour.
Serves 10 to 12 people.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix ingredients.
Spread on flattened crescent roll dough. Fold corners over filling and press edges together to seal.
Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes until golden brown.
Cover cucumbers, onions, pepper and garlic with ice for 3 hours and drain.
Cook vinegar, sugar, salt, turmeric, celery seed and mustard seed together.
Remove garlic.
Add cucumbers, onions and pepper to vinegar and sugar mixture.
Bring to a boil.
Can.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Mix all remaining ingredients. Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Yummy and quick!
Into a saucepan saute onion in butter until lightly browned. Slowly pour in rice, stirring often.
Cook on very
low heat. Stir in chicken broth and marsala.
Put saffron in hot water. Also add to rice.
Cover with lid.
Allow to sit about 15 to 20 minutes until rice gets soft and absorbs liquid.
After 20 minutes, strain grated cheese.
If using mushrooms, saute when doing onions.
Take one can of croissants and layer it in 9 X 12 Pyrex dish. Dice up chicken - put it on

top of croissants. Bring the 2 cans of soup and whipping cream to a boil and let simmer until it thickens. Pour it over chicken. Then put the last can of croissants on top of that. Bake on 350° until the top browns - about 20 minutes.
Melt chocolate chips and butter, and add 1 beaten egg.
Cool. Fold in 3 cups miniature marshmallows.
Form into a roll.
Roll in nuts or coconut, and wrap in foil to refrigerate.
Slice when firm.
Mix cornmeal, eggs, milk, soda, salt, corn and butter; set aside.
Cook meat, onion and pepper.
Pour 1/2 of cornmeal batter into greased casserole dish.
Add meat mixture; sprinkle with cheese.
Pour remaining batter over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Cut shortening into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add milk and stir with a fork only until dough leaves sides of bowl.
Turn dough onto lightly floured board or pastry cloth and knead until smooth.
Roll dough to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut dough into 1/2-inch strips with floured knife. Cut strips into 3-inch sticks.
Dip sticks into melted butter and roll into mixture of Parmesan cheese, oregano and garlic salt. Place on lightly greased baking sheet, about 3/4-inch apart.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 3 dozen sticks.
Mix ground beef, onion, cheeses, 1/4 teaspoon salt, garlic salt and egg white.
Reserve.
Drain cherries; save juice.
Drain rhubarb.
Combine tapioca, sugar, salt, cherries, juice and rhubarb in saucepan.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil; remove from heat.
Combine sifted flour, baking powder, sugar and salt; sift together.
Cut in shortening.
Add milk gradually, stirring, until soft dough is formed.
Turn out on lightly floured board; knead 30 seconds or enough to shape.
Roll dough to fit dish; make several cuts near center.
Pour mixture into greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish; dot with butter.
Cover with dough.
Bake at 425° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Use cream, if desired.
Brown sausage and drain.
Add mushrooms and onion, sauteed in lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce.
Press dough in sheet pan. Spread with cream cheese.
Top with sausage, mushrooms, onion and Parmesan.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
In a small bowl, beat margarine and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add egg and beat at medium speed 2 to 3 minutes.
Blend in melted chocolate and vanilla.
Mix well.
Spread 1 cup chocolate filling evenly into Keebler extra 2 servings graham cracker crust.
Reserve remaining chocolate filling for top of pie.
Sprinkle with peanuts.
Pound chicken and put in large shallow baking dish.
Saute mushrooms in butter.
Mix them with sour cream, soup and sherry. Pour over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, in 350° oven for 1 hour. Serves 4 to 6.
Melt butterscotch chips and peanut butter.
Dip bananas in melted mix.
Roll in crushed candy.
Freeze.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In a small bowl, toss together 1 1/2 cups cheese, squash and flour.
Place in pie shell.
Spoon 1/2 cup salsa over top.
In medium bowl, whisk eggs and evaporated milk. Pour into pie shell.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes.
Cool 15 minutes before serving.
Make sausage into equal patties.
Take each patty and completely wrap 1 boiled egg.
Do all 6 patties in this manner. Roll each one in flour and fry on all sides until browned all over. Really tasty and different.
Mix vinegar, oil and sugar to a boil until sugar is dissolved over low heat.
Cool.
Mix all other ingredients together and pour dressing over.
Chill and serve.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a roasting pan.
Drizzle half of the margarine over cereal mixture.
Sprinkle with half of the seasonings.
Stir.
Repeat with remaining margarine and seasonings.
Bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Stir every 15 minutes. Yields 12 cups.
Mix all ingredients, chill.
Serve as a dip for fresh strawberries, peaches or pears or drained canned mandarin sections.
Cook onion in oil until done.
Add picante sauce, molasses and mustard.
Add beans.
Cook until well blended.
Thinly slice 1 cucumber and arrange in bottom of lightly oiled 4-cup ring mold; set aside.
Peel, seed and coarsely chop remaining cucumbers.
With food processor or electric mixer, combine cream cheese, 1 cup chopped cucumber, sour cream, dill, lemon juice and soup mix until smooth.
Stir in remaining chopped cucumber.
Cook and drain noodles.
Squeeze dry and chop spinach.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add picante sauce, onion, tomato sauce, salt and oregano; mix well.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 1 minute.
Remove from heat and mix in noodles.
Place 1/2 mixture into 13 x 9 baking dish.
Cover with spinach.
Top with remaining mixture.
Sprinkle with corn.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Cover with cheese and bake until cheese is melted. Garnish with sour cream.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook pasta following package directions; drain.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 2-quart casserole.
In large bowl blend Ricotta, 1 cup Mozzarella, egg, parsley, garlic, pepper and nutmeg.
Stir in ziti.
Spoon into prepared casserole and sprinkle with remaining Mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake until top is golden, about 30 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Heat
sugar
and
corn syrup to dissolve sugar.
Remove from heat.
Add salt, peanut butter and Rice Krispies.
Put in 12 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cool.
Arrange bread slices in lightly greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix sausage and mustard and spread on top.
Arrange cheese on top. Combine, beat and pour over sausage and cheese the remaining ingredients and refrigerate overnight.
Allow to come to room temperature and bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Serves 8.
In big frying pan, brown about 1 pound ground beef.
Put noodles on top. Beat together sour cream, tomato juice, water, minced onion, Worcestershire sauce, salt and hot pepper sauce. Pour mixture over noodles.
Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer about 25 minutes or until noodles are tender.
Cream butter and shortening until light and fluffy.
Add sugar, one cup at a time, then add eggs (one at a time); beat well.
Add flour, beat lemon and vanilla extract.
Add Seven-Up last.
Grease and flour pan, then bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, combine the cream, chocolate chips, cream cheese, sugar and butter.
Cover and microwave on high for 3-4 minutes or until chips are melted; stir until smooth. Add bread cubes; toss to coat.
On foil-lined baking sheet, lay out crescent rolls to form one large rectangle.
Pinch all perforations together.
Brown hamburger with onion.
Drain.
Add tomato paste, salt and pepper. Combine cottage cheese, egg and Parmesan.
Spread meat mix down center of crescent roll rectangle.
Top with cottage cheese mixture.
Spread Mozzarella slices to cover.
Combine flour, soda, sour cream, salt, sugar and beaten eggs in a large bowl.
Mix until smooth; set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine butter, water and chocolate; bring to a boil.
Add chocolate mixture to batter; mix together very well.
Batter will be thin.
Pour batter into greased 17 x 11 1/2 x 1 jellyroll pan. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cool in pan on wire rack.
Have pie crust ready.
Defrost blueberries for 2 to 3 hours at room temperature.
In mixing bowl, combine berries and lemon juice.
Blend flour, cornstarch, sugar and salt.
Sprinkle a little over bottom of crust.
Stir the rest into berries.
Dot with butter.
Seal crust good and press down.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes, then at 350° for 1/2 hour more.
Boil the chocolate, granulated sugar and water together until smooth. Add the vanilla.
Cream together the butter, powdered sugar and 4 egg yolks. Stir this into the chocolate mixture. Fold all into the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Line a jelly roll pan with ladyfingers. Alternate with chocolate mixture and ladyfingers, ending with chocolate. Leave in refrigerator overnight. Serve with whipped cream.
Soften butter and cheese 1/2 hour before starting.
Blend all ingredients, adding cream a small amount at a time.
When adding cream, add small amount if dip is desired as a spread or larger amount if the dip is desired for vegetables.
Scoop into bowl. Garnish with paprika or parsley.
Serve with crackers or vegetable strips.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add honey, salt and sugar. Stir well.
Add flour and mix well.
Knead.
Roll into long sticks and shape into pretzels.
Brush with beaten egg for crisp pretzel. Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes.
Boil and mash potatoes.
Combine bouillon cube, hot milk, butter, salt and pepper.
Beat into potatoes.
Reserve 1 1/2 tablespoons of the beaten egg and beat the remainder into the potatoes.
Pile into a buttered 9-inch cake pan and brush with reserved egg.
Sprinkle with paprika and broil until the top is browned.
Cut into wedges to serve.
Serves 8.
In a large bowl, break noodles into small pieces:
set seasoning packet aside.
Add coleslaw mix almonds and onions.
In a small bowl, combine the oil, vinegar, sugar and contents of seasoning packet.
Pour over coleslaw mixture and toss to coat; serve immediately. Refrigerate leftovers. Yields 6 servings.
Place baking sheet in freezer until it's cold.
Then use ice cream scoop to form frozen yogurt into balls; place balls on baking sheet.
Return to freezer until serving time.
Cover yogurt balls and baking sheet with foil.
Use vegetable peeler to peel fresh peaches.
Cut peaches into thin slices on cutting board. Place peach slices and lemonade concentrate in food processor or blender.
Cover and whirl until smooth.
Pour peach mixture into punch bowl and add pineapple-orange juice, sparkling water and frozen yogurt balls.
Stir gently.
Makes about 17 cups.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large skillet, saute asparagus and onion in butter 2 to 3 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes.
Stir in next 7 ingredients and 1 beaten egg.
On floured surface, roll out pastry to a 10 1/2 x 11 1/2-inch rectangle.
Place asparagus mixture lengthwise along center of pastry.
Brush 1/3 of beaten egg along empty edges.
Overlap sides to cover filling.
Seal.
Place seam side down on baking sheet.
Brush with remaining egg.
Cover with dill sprigs.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes until golden.
Cool 5 minutes.
Place chicken breasts between plastic wrap.
Pound lightly until 1/4-inch thick.
Place ham and Swiss slices in middle of each chicken breast.
Roll and place in casserole.
Mix cream of chicken soup with sherry.
Pour over chicken.

Cook rice. Blend in soup, mushrooms, soy sauce, chicken, broth, celery, onions and water chestnuts. Spread in 13 x 9 baking dish. In small bowl, combine dry stuffing mix and melted butter. Sprinkle on top of casserole. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Sort beans in bowl; rinse.
Put beans in a large pan; cover with water.
Boil rapidly for 10 to 15 minutes.
(This swells the beans.)
Rinse and put in crock-pot with the ham chunks.
Add a little salt.
Cover with water.
Cook on high for 8 to 10 hours.
Preheat oven
to
350° (325° if using glass pans).
Mix yeast in warm
water.
Stir
in
of
flour to make a thin mixture and
let
stand
in
warm
place
minutes or until mixture starts to get light and frothy.
Cream the butter; add sugar gradually
and
beat until fluffy.
Set aside 1/8 cup of flour. Mix
together
remaining flour, baking
powder, spices and salt. Add
to
butter
mixture alternately with the milk, beginning
and ending
with
dry
ingredients.
Add
to yeast mixture.
Dredge raisins in 1/8 cup flour and stir into batter which should
be like thick, whipped
cream; if too thick, add a little milk. Spread batter in greased and floured loaf pans (two).
Bake
about 50
minutes or golden brown.
Remove from pans after 10 minutes. Cool on racks.
In a large pan, add rice, water, butter, onion soup, bouillon and mushrooms.
Cook at 350° for 25 minutes.
In separate pan, saute shrimp with garlic and parsley.
When rice is cooked, add in sauteed shrimp and mix.
Enjoy.
In a pie plate or on a sheet of waxed paper, combine bread crumbs and 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese.
Rinse chicken; pat dry. Brush chicken with milk.
Coat with crumb mixture.
Spray a cold large skillet with nonstick spray coating.
Preheat skillet, then add chicken.
Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or until tender and no longer pink, turning the pieces occasionally to brown evenly.
Transfer to a platter; cover to keep warm.
Wipe skillet with paper towels.
Disjoint pheasant and marinate in wine for 3 hours.
Add spices.
Brown meat in butter in a hot iron skillet, turning often. Combine mushroom soup, cream, sour cream and onion; cook over low heat.
Add 1/2 cup wine and mushrooms.
Combine with meat and bake at 275° for 1 hour.
This is also excellent using wild duck.
Brown ground beef and onion in skillet; drain grease from skillet.
Add Ro-Tel, chili beans, taco seasoning and cooked rice. Simmer 10 minutes with lid on pan.
Pour into baking dish.
Top with chips and then cheese.
Heat in oven until cheese melts.
Place spices and tea in saucepan.
Cover with boiling water; cover and steep 3 minutes.
Add sugar.
Cool.
Add remaining liquids and chill.
Serves 18 to 24.
Heat oven to 375°.
Beat margarine and all sugars until creamy.
Add eggs, milk and vanilla; beat well.
Add flour, baking soda and salt; mix well.
Stir in oats and chips; mix well.
Drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 9 to 10 minutes for chewy or 12 to 13 minutes for crisp cookies.
Cool 1 minute on cookie sheet; remove to wire rack.
Cool completely. Makes approximately 4 1/2 dozen.

The syrup is a cold pack. Mix sugar, vinegar and spices together. Sterilize jars of various sizes with lids. Pack into sterile jars the slices of cucumbers with onion slices. Pack tight. Pour cold syrup over cucumbers. Seal jars. Refrigerate. No hot water bath! Every day for 1 week, turn jars upside down, blending ingredients. Cucumbers will shrivel up in this process. Ready to eat after 1 week. Will keep 6 months in refrigerator. This recipe can be made all year round. Good for gift giving. Serves many.
Pickles are crisp and delicious. Great for picnics!
In a bowl of a food processor or the small bowl of an electric mixer, break almond paste into small pieces.
Add cocoa and two of the eggs.
Whirl or beat until mixture is smooth.
Pour into a 10-inch spring-form pan.
Bake in 375° oven for 15 minutes or until cake springs back when lightly touched.
Cool on a wire rack.
Wash and chop the endive.
Fry bacon until crisp; remove from drippings; crumble.
Mix salt, sugar and flour; add vinegar.
Stir until well blended.
Cook sauce in 2 tablespoons bacon drippings until thickened, adding cream gradually.
Pour mixture over endive and mix together lightly.
Garnish with chopped eggs and crumbled bacon.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Alternate layers of noodles, beef mixture, olives and cheese and large can of mushrooms. Repeat layers, ending with beef mixture.
Pour mushroom soup (diluted with milk or water) over casserole.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Uncover.
Sprinkle chow mein noodles and nuts over mixture.
Bake 30 minutes longer.
Serves 16 to 18.
Melt bits with condensed milk over boiling water until mix begins to thicken.
Remove from heat.
Add chopped nuts and vanilla; blend well.
Chill about 1 hour.
Line bottom of a 9-inch pie pan with foil.
Place nut halves in the bottom.
Spread chocolate mix over nuts to form ring.
Put nuts on top.
Chill.
Coat potatoes with oil.
Place raw potatoes and remaining oil if any in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle onion soup mix over potatoes. Bake at 450° until done, about 40 minutes, mixing occasionally. Smells and tastes heavenly.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream butter and sugar well.
Add egg yolk and flavoring.
Combine dry ingredients and add alternately with the juice and rinds.
Mix thoroughly; cover and refrigerate for easy handling.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat egg white slightly.
Spread nuts on waxed paper.
Roll dough into tiny balls; dip in egg white and roll in nuts.
Place on greased cookie sheet 1 inch apart.
Press cherry on top of each and bake 25 minutes.
Makes 40.
Cook sugar, Karo, cocoa, butter and milk together.
Stir until it starts to boil and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and put in pan of cold water to cool.
Pour into buttered pan.
When cool, cut and serve.
Mix chili powder and flour.
Add the meat.
Fry a small piece of tallow in shortening.
When very hot, fry in the garlic and the onions until very clear.
Add meat mixture and stir constantly until well browned.
Add tomatoes and chillies.
Pour into meat mixture 1 1/2 quarts boiling water and simmer until done, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

recipes.t: Grandma'S Coleslaw 'N' Dressing(In Honor Of Hasty Grand Slam)
d: Shred cabbage (coarsely); it will make 4 to 5 cups.
Shred carrot.
Combine both in a large bowl.
Remove seeds and stems from green pepper (chop or dice), and add to the cabbage-carrot mixture.
Add celery seed.
Combine well.
Pour chilled coleslaw dressing (about 1/2 cup) over the cabbage mixture and mix well.

Lay out 6 of the tortillas and sprinkle with cheese, onions, peppers and baked beans. Add another layer of cheese and top with remaining tortillas. Cook on warm grill for 3 minutes on each side or until warm throughout. Serve with sour cream and salsa.
Chop onion; cook in oil until tender.
Add water or broth. Heat to boiling; add rice.
Lower heat; cover and cook slowly 20 minutes.
Add chicken, cheese, salt and pepper and cook over very low heat until cheese melts.
Makes 6 servings, about 2/3 cup each.

recipes.t: Checkerboard Masterpiece(Fun To Make, But A Little Tricky)
d: Sift flour.
Measure
and
resift
times with baking powder and salt.
Cream butter.
Mix in sugar thoroughly.
Add eggs and beat
until
smooth and fluffy.
Add vanilla and stir in flour mixture
in
several
portions until smooth.
Divide mixture in 2 portions
and mix melted cooled chocolate with 1 portion.
Line a small bread loaf pan or refrigerator freezing tray with wax paper.
Pack
the chocolate dough into the bottom in a uniform
layer.
Place in refrigerator until very firm, then cover this
with half the plain dough, then repeat chilling and add another
layer
of chocolate and finally the last of plain
dough. Try
to
keep
the
layers
uniform
in thickness and
smooth. Cover
with
wax paper and chill overnight in the refrigerator. Turn the layered loaf out onto wax paper on a
molding
board
and cut into uniform thick slices, using a
thin
sharp
knife.
Divide Jack cheese evenly among chilies, folding or tucking cheese inside.
Arrange chilies side by side in bottom of greased shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
With electric mixer, mix eggs until thick and foamy; add milk and baking powder.
Beat until smooth as possible.
Pour egg batter over chilies, moistening evenly over all chilies.
Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for about 30 minutes.
Garnish with black olives.
Just before serving, top with heated marinara sauce or set sauce aside at table to be added when eaten.
Cream butter and sugar, add eggs one at a time.
Mix flour and spices, add to butter mixture alternately with milk.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Mix well.
Bake in tube pan for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 325°.
Sift together 3 cups flour, salt and baking powder.
Cream together 1/2 cup butter and eggs, beating well after each addition.
Add dry ingredients alternately with milk, blending well after each addition.
Spread 1/2 batter in greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Sprinkle 1/2 of mixture over batter.
Spread with remaining batter; top with remaining crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes (glass dish 35 to 40 minutes) or until golden.
Makes 12 servings.
Beat eggs until thick and lemon colored.
Add sugar gradually while continuing to beat.
Melt butter, unsweetened chocolate and semi-sweet bits together in microwave and add with vanilla to egg mixture.
Fold in flour. Stir in marshmallows and nuts. Bake in greased 9-inch square pan at 350° about 30 minutes. The batter is thick. Cool before cutting into squares.
In saucepan, heat cubes of butter until melted.
Add flour and mix with wooden spoon.
Mix until pale gold in color.
Remove from heat and stir in milk.
Put back on heat to thicken.
Add Cheddar or Muenster cheese to taste, starting with 1/2 cup.
Add 2 eggs to Ricotta cheese and blend well.
In baking dish, alternate Cheddar cheese sauce, noodles, and Ricotta mixture, top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Bake chicken and dice.
Halve grapes.
Chop celery and mix together.
Add raisins and walnuts.
Stir in just enough mayonnaise to moisten and blend.
Ingredients may be varied according to taste. Serves 6 to 8.
In a small bowl, mix cream cheese, peanuts and chutney until well blended.
Stuff each rib of celery with 1 tablespoon of cheese mixture.
Cover and chill.
Cut into 2-inch pieces.
Combine first seven ingredients in medium saucepan.
Bring to boil, cover, lower heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Set aside to cool, 1/2 hour.
Press mixture through fine mesh strainer.
Chill until ready to use.
Then combine yogurt, sour cream and blackberry puree until smooth and silky.
Garnish with reserved berries or top with Creme Fraiche.
Cook bacon until
crisp,
drain.
Add onions and thyme. Cook until tender.
Stir in vegetables and heat through.
Combine butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar and sifted 1 1/4 cups flour.
Place in greased 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
In a 3-quart saucepan, combine broccoli and water over high heat; heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low; cover.
Cook 8 minutes or until broccoli is tender, stirring occasionally.
Drain in colander.
Use large mixing bowl.
Soften sherbet.
Gradually add fruit juices.
Add milk.
Beat until frothy.
Serve in chilled bowl. Serves 30.
Combine first 4 ingredients and boil until clear; add dry jello, lemon juice and food coloring.
Cool and pour over strawberries that have been placed in a baked pie shell.
Chill. May garnish with whipped topping, if desired.
Bake cake by directions on box in oblong baking pan.
Cool and split lengthwise.
Place 1/2 of cake in serving dish.
Place chipped potatoes into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Crumble ground beef over potatoes.
Add mixture of onions and rutabaga on top of ground beef.
Season and slice margarine over all.
Cover with foil and bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour. Remove from oven; drain off grease.
Add mixture of soup and water, pouring evenly over surface of casserole.
Cover with foil and bake an additional 15 minutes.
