Remove, uncover, and add crescent rolls on top, unrolling each section to make a flat crust.
Bake uncovered 10 to 15 minutes or until brown.
Brown bacon; break in large pieces.
Cook onion in 2 tablespoons drippings.
Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in corn, milk and seasonings.
Bake 10 minutes.
Mix first 4 ingredients together.
Slice lemon and lime and put them in punch.
I freeze some of the apple and cranberry juice into cubes ahead of time so punch is not diluted by ice.
Mix together the first 3 ingredients and let set while mixing the other ingredients.
Beat eggs; add oil, water, sugar and salt. Add yeast mixture.
Add 4 cups flour and mix with mixer.
Then add rest by hand.
Let rise; knead down.
Put in pans to rise again. Makes 3 loaves or 2 loaves and 10 to 12 rolls.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes (less for rolls).
Can put in fridge before first rising and use as needed.
Will keep about a week.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt morsels in a double boiler or microwave.
Remove from heat and set aside.
In a large bowl combine corn syrup, eggs and salt; beat well.
Gradually blend in melted butterscotch and beat until smooth.
Stir in pecans.
Pour into large unbaked pie shell.
Place on cookie sheet.
Bake for 50 minutes.
Cool and garnish with whipped cream.
(This recipe does not need sugar because the butterscotch replaces it.)
Cook peas, butter, mushrooms and onions until onion is done. Mix flour with a little milk and add slowly to peas. Cook to a little thickness.

Thaw shrimp, if frozen. Peel and devein shrimp. Cook linguine according to package directions. Chop jalapeos finely. In a large skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add jalapeos, garlic, salt and pepper; cook and stir for 1 minute. Add shrimp; cook and stir about 3 minutes more or until shrimp turn opaque. Stir in tomatoes; heat through. Drain linguine; toss with shrimp mixture. If you would like, top with Parmesan cheese.
Mix all and get soup hot enough to melt frozen broccoli and cheese.
Serve hot.

recipes.t: Braised Chicken Thighs With Spicy Tomato And Ginger Sauce
d: In a medium frying pan, heat oil over moderate heat.
Brown thighs on both sides, skin side first.
Salt and pepper while browning second side.
Drain thighs on paper towels and set aside. Drain fat from frying pan except for 2 teaspoons.
Add tomatoes, garlic, ginger, chili and sugar and cook over moderately high heat for about 8 minutes.
Reduce to a low simmer.
Return thighs to skillet.
Cover and braise slowly for 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 500°.
Place cracked crab in roasting pan. Drizzle olive oil over crab.
Drizzle melted sweet butter over crab.
Add peeled garlic cloves, salt and pepper.
Squeeze half a lemon over crab.
Toss everything and roast for 15 minutes. Squeeze the other half lemon and add parsley.
Strip the skin from the chicken; remove the seeds from the green peppers and slice them into thin rings.
Place chicken in skillet.
Cover with pepper rings and pour in V-8 juice (or similar vegetable juice mixture) until chicken is submerged. Cover skillet; cook at 250° (low heat) until chicken is tender (about 2 1/2 to 3 hours).
Cook spaghetti as directed on package; drain.
Cook broccoli, tomatoes, garlic, bell pepper and onion in broth in skillet over medium heat about 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken.
Cook 2 or 3 minutes, stirring constantly until broccoli is crisp-tender and chicken is no longer pink in center.
Stir in spaghetti and remaining ingredients.
Toss until heated through.
Yields 6 servings.
Melt brown sugar and butter in 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Add pineapple and cinnamon; mix well. Place biscuits on top. Bake at 425° for 10 minutes or until browned. Yield: 6 servings.
In skillet, brown meat and onions in hot oil.
Transfer meat and onions to slow cooker and add remaining ingredients to skillet, scraping browned bits from bottom.
Pour over pork.
Cook on high heat for 4 to 6 hours.
Thicken gravy.
Serve over hot rice.

recipes.t: Deviled Ham And Mushroom Stuffed Tomatoes
d: Saute mushrooms in margarine over low heat for 5 minutes, let cool. Mix remaining ingredients (except tomatoes) in a medium side bowl.
Stir in mushrooms.
Chill.
Cut top fourth off each tomato and scoop out insides.
Fill with ham mixture, keep chilled until serving.
Garnish with snips of parsley, if desired.
Makes approximately 20 appetizers.
Place rice in a greased loaf pan.
Top with chicken and mushrooms.
Mix water, soup and sherry.
Top with cheese.
Cover snugly with foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until chicken and rice are done.
Mix gelatin, sugar and salt in small saucepan.
Add water. Place over low heat, stirring constantly until gelatin dissolves. Remove from heat and stir in mayonnaise, lemon juice and rind. Blend with a rotary beater.
Pour into a refrigerator tray.
Quick chill in freezer 10 to 15 minutes or until firm about 1-inch from edge but soft in center.
Beat until fluffy.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Turn into 4-cup mold or individual molds.
Chill until firm.
Unmold on serving plate.
Garnish with salad greens and mayonnaise.
Combine cream cheese and sugar; beat until creamy.
Fold in peanut butter, milk and vanilla; beat until smooth.
Fold in 2/3 of Cool Whip.
Pour into pie crust.
Top with remainder of Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with finely chopped peanuts.
Chill well before serving.

recipes.t: Paul'S Stir-Fried Rice With Ground Beef
d: Heat the wok, then add oil.
Put the mixed vegetables in the hot wok.
Stir-fry the mixed vegetables for about 5 minutes.
Add the beef and stir until it's cooked.
Then add the rice, salt, ketchup and sugar.
Stir-fry until the rice is fried.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Blend milk, honey, sassafras powder and sugar thoroughly.
Combine with sifted flour, baking powder and salt.
Add eggs and shortening and mix very lightly and quickly. Bake in well-greased muffin pans for about 20 minutes.
Makes 18 to 20 muffins.
Cook spinach and drain well. Saute onion in butter.
Mix milk and eggs.
Add to spinach.
Place ham and cheese on bottom of pastry shell.
Pour other ingredients on top.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes.
Slice meat into 1/4 x 2-inch strips.
In electric skillet on high heat, add seasoned meat to hot oil.
Cover, braise for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Do not scorch.
Add drained mushrooms and saute 5 more minutes.
Add beef broth, simmer 20 to 30 minutes, covered.
Stir often.
Add flour, milk and Kitchen Bouquet mixture to thicken broth.
Stirring frequently, cook until desired consistency.
Serve tips and gravy over rice or egg noodles.
Mix hamburger, onion, bacon and parsley.
Mix in other ingredients and shape into balls, then brown in shortening.
When browned, add the soup and tomato juice.
Bake in a slow oven or covered skillet for 1 1/2 hours.
When done, the rice will stand out like the quills of a porcupine.
Drain liquid from hominy.
Reserve liquid and add enough milk to make 2 cups of liquid.
Add grits; cook, stirring constantly, for 2 or 3 minutes.
Mix in hominy, cheese (reserve some for top), peppers and olives.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole and cover with remainder of cheese and crushed Fritos on top.
Bake at 300° for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Do not brown cheese on top. Serves 6 to 8.
Combine buttermilk and dressing; mix.
Cover and refrigerate. Combine vegetables; cover and refrigerate.
Toss together cabbage mixture, dressing and almonds just before serving.
Makes 8 servings.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks and vanilla.
Beat until well blended.
Alternately add flour an milk to batter a little at a time until blended.
Beat the egg white until stiff and gently fold them into the batter.
Take 1/3 of the batter and stir in chocolate syrup.
Layer batter in tube or bundt pan as follows: Pour 1/2 of white batter into the greased pan.
Pour in chocolate batter and then pour in remaining white batter.
Bake at 300 degrees for 1 1/2 hours.
When cool, turn out and dust with confectioners sugar.
Rinse chicken breasts thoroughly and cut into 1-inch pieces. Cut sausages in small slices.
Cook in water for about 5 minutes and drain.
In a large gumbo pan, dissolve mix in water.
Saute vegetables in 2 tablespoons of oil; add to boiling water.
Add chicken and sausages, Ro-Tel tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Simmer for about 30 minutes.
Serve with crackers or corn bread. Grandchildren will love this.
Soak steaks in vinegar and water for 1 hour.
Wash and sprinkle with meat tenderizer.
Roll in flour.
Place in skillet with hot grease.
Brown both sides on high.
Reduce heat to medium.
Cut up onions in slices and place over steaks.
Add a pat of butter to each steak.
Add salt and pepper.
Cover and cook until done, turning once.
Worcestershire sauce may be sprinkled over steaks while cooking to add more flavor.
Combine flour, sugar, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
In another bowl, combine eggs, oil and vanilla.
Add to flour mixture and mix well.
Stir in cherry pie filling, chocolate chips and nuts.
Pat into greased and floured 10-inch tube or Bundt pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool in pan or wire rack for 15 minutes. Remove from pan.
Cool; sift powdered sugar on top.
Place each chicken breast half between two sheets of heavy plastic wrap and flatten with a mallet or rolling pin.
Sprinkle both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper and place breasts in a shallow glass baking dish.
Combine the lime juice and oil.
Pour over the chicken.
Turn breasts to coat.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 hours, turning occasionally.
Put sliced cucumbers and onions in large jar, bowl or crock. Cover with weak salt water solution.
Let stand overnight.
Drain and rinse.
Heat vinegar, sugar and spices to boiling point.
Add cucumbers and onions.
Simmer until good and hot - about 1/2 hour. May be kept in jar in refrigerator or canned.
In a 5-quart Dutch oven, saute ground beef, mushrooms and onions in hot oil until browned; drain and add bouillon, water, wine, catsup and mustard.
Cover; simmer 15 minutes.
Combine flour with cold water.
Slowly stir into meat mixture.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to
a boil.
Reduce heat; stir in sour cream.
Heat, but do not boil.
Serve over noodles, rice or mashed potatoes.
Makes 6 servings.
Saute the onion and hamburger in fat and add the remaining ingredients.
Put in a greased casserole and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Beat egg whites in small bowl until stiff. Place chocolate chips in blender.
Whirl until broken apart.
Add water.
Whirl until smooth. Add egg yolks and vanilla.
Whirl 1 minute until blended.
Combine all ingredients in large saucepan and heat until cheese is melted.
Add chicken and pour in Pyrex dish.
Bake at 350° for approximately 25-30 minutes.
Serve hot with scoop Fritos.
Drain beans; empty into bowl.
Add onions and garlic.
Combine all other ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Pour over beans; stir to coat.
Chill at least 12 hours, 24 hours is better.
Melt together Eagle Brand milk and caramels.
Then dip marshmallow (one at a time) into this mixture and roll in chopped pecans.
Pare, core and slice apples.
Arrange in an ungreased shallow 2-quart baking dish.
Combine oats, brown sugar, flour and salt. Cut in butter and sprinkle mixture over apples.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until brown and bubbly and apples are tender.
Serve warm with milk or ice cream.
Dissolve gelatin in 1 cup boiling water.
Drain pineapple; reserve syrup.
Add cold water to reserved syrup to make 2/3 cup. Stir syrup into gelatin; cool.
With rotary beater, beat yogurt into gelatin; chill until partially set.
Fold in fruit and cucumber.
Pour into 4-cup mold; chill until firm.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix together flours, sugar, spices and margarine until crumbly.
Take out 1 cup of these crumbs and reserve for topping. Dissolve soda in milk or yogurt.
Add to mixture, stirring until blended.
Put batter into 2 greased 8-inch pans and top with crumbs.
Bake 35 minutes at 350°.
Chop or slice first 4 ingredients.
Add raisins and walnuts. Toss and add Russian dressing.
Let set overnight.
Cook beef in oil until gray in color.
Add onion and celery and cook until onion is soft.
Add catsup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, mustard and oregano; mix well.
Stir in macaroni and cover.
Simmer to blend flavors, about 25 minutes.
Just before serving, fold in cheese.
Serve hot in the skillet.
Melt chocolate in a saucepan or double boiler over simmering water.
Cool slightly.
Cream butter, peanut butter and brown sugar.
Beat in eggs and chocolate extract.
Mix in melted chocolate.
Blend in flour and peanut butter chips.
Pour batter into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top evenly with peanut butter cup candy pieces, pressing them lightly into the batter.
Grease a large "horn cake pan" or Bundt pan with oil or margarine.
Line the bottom with brown paper and grease again. Cream butter, salt and sugar by hand for approximately 3/4 of hour (having butter at room temperature to begin with).
After the 3/4 hour hand mixing, start the balance of recipe mixing with the electric mixer.
Add egg yolks, beaten until thick and lemon colored.
Add beaten egg whites (beaten until stiff).
Turn the mixer down.
Add the flour, a little at a time.
(It will seem like too much flour, but it is not.)
Beat for 5 minutes; add flavoring. Bake in the deep pan, slow oven at 250° to 300° for approximately 2 1/2 hours or until a straw inserted comes out clean.
Do not fill the deep baking pan more than 2/3 full.
Would be a good idea to prepare a medium size pan for the balance of cake.
Place eggs in large saucepan; cover with cold water.
Bring to boil over high heat.
Remove from heat; cover.
Let stand 15 minutes.
Cool eggs under cold water and peel.
Slice eggs in half lengthwise; remove yolks.
Refrigerate 6 half yolks for another use.
Arrange 18 of the egg yolk halves on serving platter.
Place the remaining 6 egg white halves and 18 egg yolk halves in a large bowl.
Using fork or pastry blender, mash eggs. Blend in remaining ingredients.
Spoon or pipe mixture into 18 egg whites halves.
Sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Refrigerate for up to 6 hours.
Mix the oleo, sugar, syrup and salt together.
Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring all the time.
Remove from fire and add soda and the pecans.
Then pour over the popcorn and stir real good. Put in a roaster pan and cook for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes, at 250°.

Preheat oven to 425°. Whisk together slightly, eggs and whole milk; add melted butter, flour, salt, pepper, blue cheese and chopped fresh thyme. Whisk all together. Chill batter for at least two hours or overnight. Butter small muffin pans. Bake at 425° for 18 to 20 minutes.
Note:
You can use another can of vegetable soup instead of chili without beans.
On bagel, put 1 teaspoon dressing.
Spread.
Sprinkle with bacon and onion.
Put in pan.
Broil until hot and bubbling. Serve hot.
In a large saucepan, mix pie filling and water.
Add all remaining ingredients, except cream, and stir well.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Cool to room temperature and add cream.
Stir and refrigerate.
Serve cold.
Serves 6.
Put ranch dressing in bottom of a large container.
Add the remainder of ingredients (except crackers) and mix well.
Add crackers, gently toss to coat.
Refrigerate.
Gently combine liquid and thawed ingredients.
While facing north and standing upright, add banana slices.
While sitting with knife in hand, add orange slices.
Grip firmly a large spoon and stir briskly all ingredients in a large punch bowl or small wash tub.
Serve while still swirling.
If swirling stops, well, stir it again!
Boil noodles until done and drain.
Add cheese, milk and margarine.
Pour into casserole dish.
Cover with foil and bake at 425° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cream butter, sugar and egg yolk.
Add flour gradually, stirring until well blended.
Spread dough in a lightly greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° in a preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until medium brown.
After removing from oven, lay chocolate bars on top.
When melted, spread.
Sprinkle with nuts. Press down nuts slightly.
Cool and cut into bars.
Place pineapple in punch bowl.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Add rum; let stand for 2 hours.
Add wine and champagne or soda water. Strawberries can also be used.

Mix beef, crumbs, egg, onion and salt. Shape into meatballs. Brown in skillet. Drain off fat drippings. Add remaining ingredients and simmer over low heat 20 minutes or until meat is done, stirring occasionally. If desired, some cheese may be added. Makes about 4 servings.
Place roast in Dutch oven.
Slice onion in thin slices and put on top.
Put onion soup mix in and then pour consomme and sherry over all.
Bake (uncovered) at 325° for 2 hours.
Remove roast from pan and thinly slice.
Put slices back into the pan and cook in oven an additional 45 minutes.
Slice rolls and butter them. Broil until toasted.
Place cheese slices on bottom, then put meat slices and onion on top.
Serve with a cup of sauce for dipping.
In a 1-quart saucepan, combine cream cheese and milk.
Add soup and cook over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth and thoroughly blended and heated.
Add lemon juice and cook 2 minutes longer.
Serve over cooked vegies.
Garnish with chives and slivers of almonds.
In a large skillet, melt butter; saute onions until lightly brown.
Stir in celery; cook 1 minute longer.
Remove vegetables with a slotted spoon to a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
In same skillet, stir in flour; cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat; gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Stir in wine and Tabasco sauce. Return to heat.
Cook over low heat, stirring until mixture boils and thickens.
Stir in cheese; then pour sauce over onions.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes, until onions are tender.
Serve.
Split cake horizontally into 3 layers.
Drain strawberries and combine juice with gelatin.
Let stand 1 minute.
Add sugar and lemon juice.
Microcook 2 minutes until sugar and gelatin are dissolved.
Refrigerate for 25 minutes.
Combine gelatin mixture, strawberries and vanilla.
Beat at high speed of electric mixer until light and frothy.
Whip cream and fold into strawberry mixture.
Blend well.
Put crushed pineapple, 1 1/4 cups sugar, flour, egg, soda and salt in a bowl; mix with a fork.
Pour into ungreased 13 x 9-inch pan (batter will be thin) . Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Remove from oven.
While still hot, sprinkle with coconut and chopped nuts.

Chop onion and water chestnuts; mix all ingredients together and place 1 teaspoon in the center of a Won Ton skin. Moisten edges with water and seal to form a triangle. Deep fry in 4 cups oil until golden brown. Serve with Won Ton Sauce.
Prepare mashed potatoes as you normally do.
Place potatoes in casserole dish.
Make a well in center of the potatoes.
Take whipped cream (whip as directed on carton) and cheese.
Fold into the whipped cream and spoon into the well.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts.
Will run over top of the potatoes.
Combine coleslaw mixture, almonds and green onions in large bowl.
Sprinkle uncooked broken Ramen noodles, reserving seasoning packets.
Combine sugar, oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and seasoning packets in small bowl.
Mix well.
Spoon over salad and toss to coat.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cook lobsters in boiling salted water for 10 minutes.
Remove and let cool.
Saute peeled shrimp in butter.
Add cooked meat from 1 pound lobster, crab and scallops and heat through.

recipes.t: Party Bread("What Do You Do With A Kumquat?")
d: Put kumquats in a heavy pan with the sugar.
Stir until sugar is dissolved and boil 3 minutes.
Cool.
Add beaten eggs and
oil. Sift together the flour, salt, baking powder, soda and spices. Stir in nuts.
Stir gently into kumquat mixture.
Cut a piece of wax paper to bottom of each of 2 loaf pans.
Grease and add batter.
Bake in a 350° oven until done, about 45 minutes.
In medium bowl combine cream cheese, horseradish, mustard, salt and pepper.
On a work surface, overlap 2 slices of roast beef to form a rectangle, about 8 x 4-inches.
Spread about 2 tablespoons of horseradish mixture over beef.
Beginning with long side, roll tightly.
Cover in plastic wrap.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours.
To serve, slice crosswise on the diagonal.

Melt bacon drippings in large skillet. Add rice and brown. When the rice is a golden brown, reduce heat and add onion, bell pepper, tomatoes, garlic and pepper. Mix well and add 1 1/2 cups of warm water or enough to just cover rice. Add salt. Cover and let simmer until almost dry. Add remaining water, cold a little at a time, cooking over low heat until fluffy. This is the secret to fluffy rice.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
Pour pineapple in pan.
Spread fruit over pineapple.
Pour 3/4 cup sugar over fruit.
Sprinkle box of cake mix over sugar.
Melt oleo and pour over cake mix.
Sprinkle 1/4 cup sugar over oleo.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Bake 38 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Cut through cake and let juice rise up.
Cook 15 minutes more.
Place chicken breasts between 2 sheets of waxed paper; pound until 1/4-inch thick.
Place clam juice with garlic into casserole dish.
Place pounded breasts into juice.
Cover with foil and refrigerate for 36 hours.
Dredge each breast into flour and fry in butter about 3 minutes on each side.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
In large bowl, combine sugar, salt and 3 tablespoons butter.
Pour in hot milk.
Stir until butter is melted and sugar dissolved.
Stir in yeast.
Beat in egg.
Gradually add flour, mixing well.
Cover and let stand 15 minutes.
Roll out dough to an 18 x 12-inch rectangle.
Spread with butter.
Place crushed cookies in the bottom of a square container that can be sealed.
Spread softened ice cream on top of cookies.
Seal and freeze.
Before serving, ice with Cool Whip.
Dribble with chocolate syrup and garnish with walnuts/pecans and cherries.
Saute onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add chicken broth, tomato and basil.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice and olives. Cover.
Remove from heat and let stand for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork.
Brown sausage.
Add tomatoes, onions and bell peppers.
Cook until thick.
Add 3 cups of water (more if needed), salt and pepper.
Cook 15 minutes.
Add shrimp and crabmeat; cook another 15 minutes.
Serve over cooked rice.
Grease 9-inch pie plate with 1/3 cup melted butter.
Press thawed hash browns into butter.
Brush butter over tops of hash browns.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Remove.
Fill with cheese and ham and onions.
Beat eggs and salt and milk.
Pour over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Bake until knife comes out of center clean.
Have kids cut cheese with cookie cutters and then paint with favorite condiment.
Put on top of cracker and enjoy!
In a heavy pot, melt the chocolate chips, butter and Kahlua on medium, stirring constantly, until all is melted and well blended. Add walnuts and pour into a buttered 8-inch square pan. Refrigerate.
Cut when cold.
Mix butterscotch morsels and 1/3 cup of sweetened condensed milk in microwave-safe bowl.
Set aside.
Line 8-inch square pan with foil.
Mix chocolate morsels, vanilla and remaining milk in microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave on High for 1 minute.
Spread in pan.
Microwave butterscotch morsels 45 seconds on High.
Spread on chocolate mixture.
Chill.
Turn out on plate and cut into squares.
Combine the eucalyptus leaves, rose petals, rose leaves, tonka beans and orrisroot.
Sprinkle with refresher oil.
Place the mixture in a bowl or other decorative container, then arrange the cockscomb, roses and pansies on top.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix sugar and cornstarch.
Beat in egg yolks.
Stir in milk.
Cook over double boiler until thickened. Add margarine, coconut and vanilla.
Pour into an 8 or 9-inch baked pie shell.
Cover with meringue.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Fry hamburger with onion, carrot, celery and green pepper. Make sure that you keep stirring the mixture so it doesn't burn or get too hard.
Add tomatoes and let simmer about 20 minutes. Using mashed potato mix, follow directions for making mashed potatoes, however, use 1/3 less milk or water.
Pour hamburger and veggies into a buttered baking dish and spoon the mashed potatoes over the top, keeping it evenly spread.
Put under broiler for about 3 minutes or until potatoes brown a little. Serve immediately.
In a heavy skillet or wok, heat sesame oil.
Quickly saute green beans and asparagus until skins wrinkle.
Add sherry, soy sauce and chicken stock and simmer until tender.
Toss with toasted sesame seed.
Combine soups and water.
Put meat in large casserole pan; cover with liquid.
Cover tightly.
Bake at 325° for 3 hours, no peeking.
Serve over rice or noodles with vegetables as desired.
Stir flour, salt, pepper & shortening over medium heat until lightly browned.
Add liquids and stir until thickened.
Pour over swiss steak.
Serves 6.
Make a roux with flour and butter.
Poach salmon in wine and chicken broth.
Remove and place on a platter; keep warm.
Reserve broth.
Using roux, add broth.
Then add sour cream, salt, pepper, dill weed and Worcestershire sauce.
Serve salmon and pass sauce to pour over each portion.
Serves 4.
Soften dry yeast in 1 cup lukewarm skim milk.
Mix 1 1/3 cups flour and 2 egg whites in the yeast/milk mixture and beat for 100 strokes.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes.
Mix in salt and 1 2/3 cups flour.
Mix well until dough pulls away from sides of bowl.

recipes.t: Jalapeno Cheese And Onion Bread(Yields 1 Loaf)
d: In mixer, place water, honey and yeast.
Let yeast soften. Add at once all the rest of the dry ingredients, making sure salt is mixed into flour before adding to yeast mixture.
(Use dough hook on mixer.)
Add jalapeno and onion.
Continue to mix for 10 minutes on medium speed or knead by hand until it becomes elastic in consistency.
Grease and line bottom and sides of a 9 or 10-inch spring-form pan.
Beat cream cheese, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Add beaten egg yolks and melted chocolate.
Mix.
With a clean bowl and beaters, beat egg whites until stiff. Fold in chocolate mixture and whipped cream.
Pour into pan and chill until firm. Serves 10 to 16.
Beat Crisco and sugar in large bowl until fluffy.
Beat in eggs, vanilla and peanut butter.
Stir in oats and mix dough until stiff.
Stir in candies, etc.
Make into large balls spaced apart to allow cookies to spread to their "monster" size.
Bake in 350° oven for 12 to 13 minutes until edges are lightly browned.
Cool on sheets 5 minutes, then remove.
Combine sugar, chocolate and milk in a heavy bottomed saucepan.
Cook over medium-high heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Cook to soft ball stage.
Remove from heat; put in butter and vanilla.
Beat with spoon to remove shine from mixture. Pour into buttered platter and cool.
Cut into squares.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Using 9 x 13-inch pan lined with aluminum foil, cut meat.
Add salt and pepper.
Place the onion on meat.
Layer potato slices and arrange mushrooms on top.
Mix the soup, sour cream, catsup, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper in a bowl and spread over top of pan ingredients.
Now wrap with aluminum foil.
Bake 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours at 350°.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Make a well and add, in order, oil, egg yolks, cold water and vanilla.
Beat until smooth. Measure egg whites into large bowl along with cream of tartar. Beat until very stiff.
Pour egg yolk mixture gradually over whipped egg whites, gently folding with rubber spatula just until blended.
Sprinkle chopped walnuts over the top and fold in gently with a few strokes.
Pour into ungreased tube pan and bake at 325° for 55 minutes, then at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Invert until cool.
Frost with a butter frosting and sprinkle chopped nuts all over top.
Peel and quarter potatoes.
Put in a 4-quart kettle along with the water.
Add the salt and pepper, butter and milk.
Boil until potatoes are tender.
Roll biscuit dough 1/4-inch thick.
Cut into 2-inch squares and drop into rapid boiling potato broth.
Cook dumplings 2 minutes.
Best served while hot.

recipes.t: Beefaroni Casserole(This Is Good And Easy)
d: Cook ground beef with celery and onion until beef is done. Drain off all grease.
Add tomato sauce, salt and pepper and stir well.
Cut heat to low; cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Cook macaroni according to package directions and drain well.
Combine macaroni, sauce and 1 cup cheese and mix well.
Put in casserole dish and top with other 1/2 cup cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes until bubbly and cheese is melted.
Serves 4 to 6.
Boil lima beans until tender.
Rinse in cold water.
Mix in mayonnaise, green onions, celery and 3 diced eggs.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with parsley and sliced egg and paprika. Better flavor if made the day before.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix sugars, butter, shortening, egg, vanilla and almond extracts.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls about 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
When removing cookie sheet from oven, gently place sheet on surface to keep cookies from falling.
Makes 3 1/2 dozen cookies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt margarine; add cake mix and nuts. It will be lumpy; set aside.
Spread pie filling in a 9 x 9-inch Corningware dish.
Sprinkle on lemon juice.
Sprinkle cake mixture on top.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes until brown.
Fry bacon in skillet.
Remove and crumble and set aside.
Add bread cubes to bacon drippings.
Stir.
Cook on medium heat 5 minutes.
Drain and set aside.
Combine beans, bacon and soup in 1-quart casserole.
Mix well.
Top with bread cubes.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Cream together the shortening and sugar.
Add the eggs and vanilla.
Sift together flour, salt, soda and nutmeg.
Alternate with the sour milk.
Mix well.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle the brown sugar on top of batter.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 minutes.

recipes.t: Winter Vegetables With Horseradish And Dill
d: Steam all vegetables separately for 8 to 12 minutes or until tender.
Melt butter; stir in horseradish, vinegar, dill, salt and pepper to taste.
In a large pan, toss vegetables with butter mixture.
Keep vegetables warm, covered, in a 200° oven.
Place in casserole to serve.
Yield:
10 to 12 servings.
Mix the 4 big spoonfuls of applesauce with alot of red food coloring.
Put on the raisins, gummy fish and pretzels, then eat.
Cook noodles until done, drain.
Wash noodles with cold water until cool, then drain.
Set aside noodles.
In separate bowl, dice the tomatoes, and add balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper. Pour 1 cup of the cheese into mixture.
Pour mixture over noodles; stir.
Pour into serving dish; sprinkle the remainder of cheese over the top of the salad.
Heat oven to 350°.
Generously season the flour with salt and pepper; coat the trout with the mixture.
Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a shallow, flameproof roasting pan.
Add the fish and cook over high heat for 1 minute on each side.
Transfer to the heated oven and cook just until fish is cooked all the way through, 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix the first four ingredients in pan you are going to make your dough. Mix yeast in water and add to above mixture.
Start adding flour about 3 or 4 handfuls at a time.
Mix in well each time until it forms a soft dough.
Knead well for 4 or 5 minutes. Place dough in a large greased bowl, turning once to coat dough on top.
Let rise 50%.

Punch down and let rise again till it doubles in size. Make into rolls or biscuits and let rise till double in size. Bake at 325° to 350° for 30 or 35 minutes, according to oven. This dough is good for sugar cake and will keep in refrigerator if tightly covered.
Saute meat and onions in oil.
Add salt, tomatoes and juice. Cook noodles until tender and add to meat mixture.
Add diced cheese and mushroom soup.
Heat and serve.
Dissolve jello in water.
Let partially congeal.
Place this in mixer and whip in cream cheese, which has been partially broken up.
Add pineapple and nuts, then fold in Dream Whip or Cool Whip. Pour in 13 x 8 x 2-inch glass or Tupperware dish.
Chill overnight.
Combine eggs, milk and seasonings; set aside in bowl.
In deep, well-greased covered baking dish alternate bread and cheese layers.
Pour entire liquid mixture over bread layers.
Cover and let stand 4 hours or overnight in refrigerator.
Bake uncovered for 1 hour at 350°.
It's great with kielbasa and stewed tomatoes on the side.
In medium saucepan, combine sweetened condensed milk, cocoa, butter and coffee.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until butter melts and mixture becomes smooth.
Remove from heat and cool.
Put the scant cup of white sugar, the butter and the salt into a heavy saucepan or iron skillet and brown (scorch) lightly, until sugar, etc. is melted.
Then pour in the hot water over the sugar mixture.
Let boil for a short time until all is well dissolved. Next, take the flour and mix in with the milk and the beaten egg yolk.
Pour this slowly (so will not curdle) into the sugar-syrup mixture.
Cook over low heat until pudding is thick and pour into an 8-inch baked pie shell.
Cover with meringue made from one's favorite recipe.

In a large skillet, cook bacon in butter until lightly browned. Add the peas, onions, water, sugar, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over medium heat until vegetables are tender, about 10-15 minutes; drain.
Cut veal cutlets in half and pepper into strips.
Saute scallops in lemon juice and butter for five minutes.
Place veal, scallops, pepper and half of the peeled tomatoes (you may want to cut the tomatoes in half) in crock-pot.
Sprinkle basil, garlic to taste and Parmesan cheese on top.
Add a splash of wine, if you desire.
Cook on low for 6 hours.
Soften gelatin in cold water.
Beat cream cheese and sugar. Gradually add gelatin and eggnog.
Refrigerate until slighlty thick.
Beat whipping cream until peaks form.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour into prepared graham cracker crust.
Refrigerate until firm.
Garnish with whipped cream and grated nutmeg.
Roll dough to fit into a 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake in 425° oven for 15 minutes or until crisp around edges.
Let cool.
In small bowl, combine zucchini, refried beans and taco seasoning.
Spread bean mixture and sour cream on baked crust.
Drizzle on salsa, top with cheese, green onions and olives.
Return to oven to melt cheese.
Cut into squares.
Makes 1 dozen appetizers.
Mix first three ingredients in bowl.
Leave in warm place until frothy.
Mix next four ingredients in another bowl.
Add yeast mixture and onion to flour mixture, kneading to make soft dough. Knead lightly on floured surface for 10 minutes until dough is smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a bowl, cover with damp cloth and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 1/2 hours, until doubled in size.
Turn dough onto floured surface and knead 5 minutes.
Shape into rolls or loaves and place on baking tray or greased loaf pans.
Brush dough with a little water and sprinkle with the lovage seeds.
Leave for 20 minutes.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes, then reduce oven to 400° for a further 5 to 20 minutes. Remove from pans to wire racks.
Yields 14 rolls or two (1 pound) loaves.

Season beans with salt, pepper, garlic powder and basil to taste. Wrap 10 to 12 beans with strip of bacon. Place in baking dish. Cover with liberal coating of brown sugar. Sprinkle with Worcestershire sauce, using a good bit, but do not make brown sugar watery. Bake at 350° approximately 20
minutes until bacon is done.
Combine sugar, butter
and milk in a saucepan and bring to boil for
minutes.
Put oatmeal, coconut, cocoa, vanilla and nuts in mixing bowl.
Pour hot mixture over these ingredients. Drop from a teaspoon onto waxed paper and allow to cool completely.
Fry bacon.
Add hot sauce, spices and onion.
Bring to boil; simmer with beans.
Beat egg yolks with sugar, vanilla, salt and water until light and fluffy.
Add flour and stir in pineapple.

Spread out crescent rolls on bottom of greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Place Canadian bacon over crescent rolls, followed by 1 cup Swiss cheese. Carefully drop eggs one at a time onto cheese and bacon layer. Be careful not to drop yolks. Pour cream over eggs and sprinkle remaining cup of Swiss cheese. Bake at 400° for 25 minutes. Slice into squares and serve.
Quarter the unpeeled cucumber and then cut each quarter into 1/4 inch slices.
Fry the spring onions and cauliflower in the butter for 5 minutes.
Put the cucumber in the bottom of an ovenproof dish.
Put the fried mixture over the top and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Mix the cheese with the breadcrumbs and put over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Fix jello as directed (omit 1 cup cold water).
Chill until set.
Add cranberries, pecans and celery.
Chill until firm. Yields 8 servings.
Allow Camembert, Swiss and Blue cheeses to stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
In large mixer bowl, combine the 3 cheeses with 2 packages of cream cheese.
Set aside.
Remove grapefruit
sections.
Cover
grapefruit shells with water
in
saucepan.
Bring
to a boil.
Boil 15 minutes. Drain. Carefully
remove any remaining pulp or membrane.
Cut peel into thin
slices,
about
1/4-inch
wide.
Again
place grapefruit peel
in
saucepan, cover with water and boil until tender.
Mix Jell-O
with 2 cups water in heavy skillet.
Add prepared peel and
spices.
Bring
to a boil, reduce heat and continue stirring occasionally until peels are translucent and syrup is
almost absorbed 30 to 45 minutes. Remove from heat; lift peels
from skillet with slotted spoon.
Sprinkle with 1 cup sugar;
toss lightly.
Arrange
pieces in single layer on waxed paper-lined trays.
Let dry about 12 hours or overnight. Store in tightly covered container. Makes about 1 pound.
Stir together flour, baking soda and salt.
In saucepan, combine sugar, butter and water.
Cook over low heat until mixture comes to boil.
Remove from heat; add 1 cup chips, stirring until melted.
Stir in eggs and vanilla.
Add flour mixture.
Stir in remaining chips and nuts.
Pour into 9-inch greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cook noodles and cool.
Cook pepper, onion and hamburger in a small amount of butter until tender.
Add soup and mushrooms and fold in noodles.
Place in casserole dish and put cheese on top. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix sugar, salt, yeast, and some flour.
Add water, vinegar, and oil.
Add more flour.
Knead to make a dough that is soft and easy to work with.
Let rise for 15 min.
Punch down.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Form into buns.
Let rise for 1 hour or until almost doubled.
Bake at 400°F for 15 - 20 min.
Combine sugar, cornstarch and salt in pan.
Gradually add water.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Cook 1 minute until mixture is clear and thickened.
Stir small amount into beaten egg yolks.
Return to hot mixture.
Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice, butter and rind.
Pour into shell.
Combine cream cheese and pineapple.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Chill.
Shape into log.
Slice and serve.
In a skillet, brown chops on both sides in 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
Drain grease.
Mix the water and catsup and put on chops.
Sprinkle with red pepper flakes.
Put sliced lemons on top of chops.
Cover and simmer, about 35 to 45 minutes until done.
Spread crescent rolls in baking pan to make a crust.
Bake according to directions on package.
Let cool.
Mix cream cheese, mayonnaise and taco seasoning together.
Spread mixture over cooked and cooled crust.
Spread chopped tomato, green pepper and olives over top of mixture.
Sprinkle entire pizza with shredded cheese and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.
Saute onions and garlic in oil until translucent.
Add celery and saute.
Add pea juice, tomatoes and spices; simmer 10 minutes. Add peas.
Serve with cooked pasta shells.
Melt 2 tablespoons shortening in large kettle, but do not brown chicken.
Put sliced onions on top and paprika, salt and pepper. Cook about 1 hour.
Add soup and vegetables.
Add cream just before serving.
May be thickened (with flour and water); serve with dumplings or hot rice.
Melt margarine in a baking dish.
Sprinkle in pretzels; then add 1/4 cup sugar.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Refrigerate until chilled.
Cream the cream cheese with 1/2 cup sugar.
Drain pineapple mixture into Dream Whip and pour over pretzels. Refrigerate.
Brown onion in skillet.
Add dried beef, soup and peas.
Cook a few minutes until peas are done.
(May need to add some water, if necessary.)
Serve in French pastry shells.
Serves 4.

recipes.t: Aunt Pee Wee'S Sweet Potato Pones
d: Cut up enough sweet potatoes to measure 1 gallon and 1 quart. Shake potatoes down a little when measuring.
Cook potatoes until tender.
Drain.
Add butter to cooked potatoes while hot so butter will melt.
Beat well with mixer.
Combine sugars, spices and flour in another bowl.
Let potatoes cool, then gradually add flour mixture to potatoes, alternating with Pet milk.
Mix well. Pour into 4 to 5 greased iron skillets.
Melt some margarine and pour on top; then sprinkle with sugar.
Bake about 45 minutes at 350° to 400°.
Boil chicken breasts for 25 minutes, then cut up in bite-size pieces.
Spread cottage cheese in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top of cottage cheese.
In 1-pint jar with tight fitting lid, combine oil, ReaLemon, garlic, salt and pepper.
Shake well.
In narrow 1-quart glass container, layer 1/2 each of the green pepper, tomatoes, cucumber and onion.
Repeat layering with remaining vegetables.
Pour dressing over salad.
Chill 4 hours to blend flavors.
Makes 8 servings.

Brown ground beef and drain. Cut cheese into chunks and add to browned beef. Pour tomatoes and green chilies into cheese and beef mixture. Add Worcestershire sauce and chili powder to mixture. Cook until all the cheese has melted. Serve with tortilla chips.
Mix
sugar and cream together;
add soda; stir in flour and rhubarb.
Spread
in
a
greased 8 x 8-inch pan.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake
at
350° for about 25 minutes.
Serve warm with cream, if you'd like.
In bowl, combine sugar and turmeric; add eggs and vinegar. In large skillet, melt butter.
Let cool to room temperature.
Add egg mixture and cook on low heat until thick, stirring constantly. Add mayonnaise, mustard and salad dressing.
Combine remaining ingredients and mix with dressing.
Chill and serve.
Add Roquefort cheese to cream cheese.
Add salt, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix and add mayonnaise and light cream. Refrigerate.
Slice potatoes but leave together.
Place on a piece of heavy-duty foil.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and garlic. Sprinkle with onion.
Dot with butter.
Wrap up tight.
Place on grill at medium-high heat.
Cook for about 40 minutes.
When done, open and place cheese cubes inside.
Reclose and melt cheese. Remove from heat.
Individual potatoes may be done.
Beat egg yolks.
Add sugar, cornstarch and salt.
Add pineapple and water.
Cook in double boiler until thickened.
Fold in beaten egg whites while mixture is still hot.
Cool.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Cover with whipped cream; sprinkle with coconut or nuts.
Squeeze lemon juice into large pot of cold water.
Add lemon wedges, artichokes, onion, bay leaves and salt and pepper.
Allow to come to a boil, then cook at a simmer until artichokes are tender.
This is low-fat, low calorie and very flavorful.
Roast turkey.
Cool, bone and cut into small bite size pieces. To turkey broth add garlic salt, seasoned pepper, thyme, onion, spinach, turkey meat and rice.
Add enough water to a little more than cover rice.
Cook until rice is just done (10 to 20 minutes). Add soup, mix well.
Put grated cheese on top.
Mix bacon, pecans and bell peppers together.
Add enough mayonnaise to bind the mixture together and make it spreadable on bread.
Portions can vary according to the individual.
Yields 10 to 12 sandwiches.
Heat butter in saucepan.
Add flour; cook over low heat, stirring constantly for 8 to 10 minutes.
Do not allow mixture to brown.
Slowly add hot milk to butter-flour mixture, stirring constantly with a whisk until sauce is thickened and smooth; simmer for 5 minutes.
Strain and keep warm.
Bake cornbread; cool.
Then cut or crumble into bowl.
Chop tomato, onion and bell pepper into bowl with bread.
Add jalapeno and cheese and crumble bacon.
Mix well with plenty of mayonnaise (about 1 pint) and chill.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Place 50 (1 1/2-inch) paper baking cups on cookie sheet.
In a medium size mixing bowl, combine the peanut butter, sugar and egg; stir until well blended.
Press 1 1/2 teaspoons of mixture into each baking cup.
In small bowl, combine milk and coconut; mix.
Put 1 teaspoon of the peanut mixture. Bake for 20 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Combine cereal, milk and molasses.
Let stand until most of the moisture is absorbed.
Melt butter. Combine egg and butter with the cereal mix and beat well.
Stir in raisins.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Add to cereal mixture, stirring only until combined.
Fill greased muffin pan cups 3/4 full.
Bake at 400° about 20 minutes or until muffins are lightly browned.
Serve hot.
Cook and drain sausage and beef separately.
After draining beef and sausage, combine them and add grated cheese.
Cheese must melt and blend with meat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Spread on "party rye"; quick freeze on cookie sheets 10 to 15 minutes.
When ready to serve, put into 400° oven (frozen) for 15 minutes.
One recipe uses 1 1/2 loaves of rye.
Makes 48.
Cut chicken up and skin it.
Turn chicken pieces over in melted butter and then in bread crumbs that are seasoned with salt and pepper.
Put on a baking sheet.
Bake for 45 minutes at 450°. Pour the rest of the melted butter over it when done.
Cook spinach; drain.
Add cream cheese, onion and 1/2 sick of butter.
Put in small baking dish.
Put bread crumbs and melted butter on top.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes at 350°.
In blender, place cottage cheese, pineapple juice, sweetener and the extracts.
Process until smooth.
Place banana strips in bottom of medium size dessert dish.
Pour cottage cheese mixture over the bananas.
Top with crushed pineapple.
Refrigerate one hour before eating.
Boil and bone chicken; save broth.
Mix soups and Ro-Tel tomatoes together.
Saute bell pepper and onion in oleo.
Add 1 cup of broth to soup and tomatoes; set aside.
Line casserole dish with flour tortillas that have been dipped in boiling chicken broth.
Lay chicken on tortillas, then add a layer of soup mixture.
Top with cheese.
Put in another layer of tortillas. Add remaining soup mixture and top with cheese.
Bake at 350° until mixture is bubbling and cheese melts, about 20 or 30 minutes.
Thaw carrots, cauliflower, green beans and drain.
Pour dressing over thawed vegetables.
Add pimentos.
Cover; marinate in refrigerator several hours or overnight.
Drain.
Combine vegetable mixture with cheese and mix lightly.
Sprinkle with additional cheese before serving.
Makes approximately 6 servings.
On each piece of chicken, spread pepper, Italian seasoning and Dijon mustard.
Top each piece of chicken with a slice of cheese; roll up, secure with toothpick and then flour.
Saute in olive oil or butter over medium heat.
Cover with vegetables and cook slowly until tender.
Whip cream, add sugar.
Mix with cottage cheese.
Add marshmallows, cherries and pineapple.
Chill.
Serve as a salad or dessert.
Mix preserves, juice and soy sauce.
Coat chicken.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Top with melted butter.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Melt butter in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese in butter (to taste).
Turn potatoes upside-down in this mixture.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350°.

Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon. Cut in butter with pastry blender until crumbly. Stir in chopped walnuts. Press 1/2 of mixture in 8 x 8 pan. Stir almond extract into blueberry pie filling. Pour over crumb mixture. Spread to edges. Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serve warm or cold with ice cream.
Boil sugar, lard, raisins, water, cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt for 3 minutes.
(Boil 3 minutes after it starts to boil.) Take off the stove and let cool (real cold).
Then stir in flour, baking powder and soda.
Bake in a slow oven for 1 hour at 300° or until done.
Put cereal and nuts on a cookie sheet.
Boil margarine and brown sugar for 2 minutes.
Drizzle over cereal mix.
Bake 8 minutes at 325°.
Stir and bake 8 minutes more.
Cool and put in container.
Preheat broiler.
Line broiler pan with foil.
Melt butter on stovetop.
In a small bowl, combine melted butter, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 teaspoon lemon zest, 1/2 teaspoon tarragon, salt and pepper.
Place fish on prepared pan.
Brush lemon-butter mixture on fish.
Broil fish 4 inches from heat about 7 minutes until fish is cooked.
In mixer bowl, combine remaining 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 teaspoons lemon zest, 1/2 teaspoon tarragon, Dijon mustard and dry mustard.
Beat cream into mixture in a thin stream. Continue beating until cream forms soft peaks.
Serve fish topped with a dollop of the lemon cream.
Heat pineapple in saucepan and add jello; stir until dissolved.
Pour over softened cream cheese and mix well.
Place in refrigerator until mixture begins to thicken.
Mix in whipped cream, chopped cherries, nuts and oranges.
Return to refrigerator to congeal.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles until half done.
Layer noodles, cottage cheese, cheese, mushrooms and sauce.
Reserve a little cheese to sprinkle on top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until cheese is browned.
Serves 4.
Contains 325 calories per serving.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and blend thoroughly.
Add oats, pecans, raisins and vanilla.
Add flour which has been sifted with cinnamon, soda and salt.
Roll into teaspoon size balls and place on cookie sheet.
Press down ball with a flour coated fork.
Crush cookies; pat down with melted butter in a 9 x 13 pan. Stir ice cream until creamy. Spread over cookie layer.
Add peanuts. Freeze.
Boil fudge topping 8 minutes, stirring constantly until thickened.
Cool. Pour cool fudge sauce over ice cream.
Top with Cool Whip. Freeze.
Sift flour with baking soda and salt.
Mix with electric mixer cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, sugar, oil, molasses and eggs.
Add dry ingredients alternating with the buttermilk.
Pour into two 9 x 13-inch pans (not loaf type).
Bake at 350° to 375° until done. Tester will come out clean.
Heat milk and sugar together.
Stir in soda; mix.
Set aside and cool.
Put in dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Then stir in milk; mix again.
Chill.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Roll out on bread board with flour.
Cut out cookies with cutter.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Measure 1/2 cup tomato sauce.
Mix beef, bread crumbs, tomato sauce, salt and crumbs.
Divide in 4 parts.
Make 4 1/2-inch circle and 1/2-inch thick.
Pinch edge of circle to stand up rim. Pour 2 tablespoons sauce in center.
Bake at 425° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Sprinkle pizza with cheese.
Put in oven just long enough for the cheese to melt.

Remove stems from mushrooms and chop finely. In medium pan, melt butter or margarine. Add stems and cook until tender. Add soup mix, bread crumbs, sherry and nuts; mix well. Fill caps and place on greased pan; sprinkle with cheese. Broil 5 minutes. These can be made ahead and frozen. Defrost slightly before broiling.
Boil unpeeled potatoes until done.
Cool, peel and mash.
Add flour and salt.
Roll out on floured board about 1-inch high.
Cut into 1-inch wide strips.
Cut each strip into 2-inch pieces.
Place in greased pan and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
In glass measure, combine broth and corn meal.
Blend until very thick, stirring occasionally.
Add butter or margarine, Mozzarella cheese, salt and pepper.
Stir.
Whirl orange juice concentrate, yogurt and milk in blender container until smooth.
Pour into 2 tall glasses. Top each with a large scoop of orange sherbet.
Garnish with strawberries, if desired.
Combine coconut, marshmallows, pineapple, oranges and blueberries in a bowl; mix well.
Fold in yogurt.
Yields 8 servings.
Per serving:
127 calories, 4 g fat, 0.5 mg chol, 56 mg Na.
Cook bacon until most of the fat is removed.
Add onion, tomato and celery.
Cook over medium heat until onion is tender. Stir in salsa and salt.
Add cheese and heat until cheese is melted.
Do not let boil.
Keep warm for dipping.
Heat oven to 350°.
Spray casserole dish with vegetable cooking spray.
Combine soup, milk, pimientos and pepper.
In the casserole dish, layer half of each:
cubed Spam, onions, combined soup mixture, peas, potatoes; repeat layers.
Cover.
Bake 60 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Combine bread crumbs and parsley. Sprinkle over casserole.
Bake, covered, 15 minutes longer.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Serves 6.
Slice a thin slab off each side of baked potato.
Slice the slabs like thin French fries.
The remaining block can be cut in half, then quarters and eighths.
Cut to size of small French fries.
Put 2 cups water in bowl and add sugar.
Soak French fry size potatoes for 1 hour or more.
Pour off water and place potatoes in a flat baking dish.
Melt butter or margarine in a small pan.
Add chives, parsley and garlic powder.
Mix and pour over potatoes; cook in a 350° oven for 30 minutes or until done. Leave skin on potatoes.
Mix crackers, nuts and baking powder.
In a large mixing bowl, beat egg whites, adding sugar gradually until thick.
Add vanilla. Fold in cracker mixture.
Bake in a greased 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan at 300° until lightly brown, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool completely.
Prepare jello according to directions and chill until slightly thickened.
Drain pineapple and save juice.
Add all ingredients (including jello) and chill until firm.
(I substitute pineapple juice for water in jello.)
Steam broccoli until just tender, then chop.
You should have about 2 1/4 cups.
Melt butter in a large skillet; add garlic, green onions and broccoli.
Saute for 3 minutes.
Stir in cream, salt and pepper and cook to a gentle boil until sauce thickens slightly.
Toss sauce with hot pasta in a serving bowl.
Add Blue cheese and toss to distribute evenly.
Add Parmesan cheese and toss again.
Serve immediately with extra grated cheese and pepper on the
side.
Serves 4.
Mix sour cream and taco mix thoroughly.
Spread evenly in long cake pan.
Put a thin layer of lettuce, then a thin layer of tomatoes and top it with a thin layer of Cheddar cheese.
In a large kettle or covered pan, bring the first 5 ingredients to a boil.
Reduce heat and add turkey breast.
Cover and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until turkey is fork-tender. Remove and let stand 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook liquid down or thicken with flour for sauce.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Cook broccoli until tender.
Drain
well.
Arrange in a single layer in an oblong Pyrex.
Mix bread crumbs and cheese. Sprinkle over broccoli.
Season
with
salt
and pepper.
Melt butter with pressed garlic
in
a
small saucepan.
Spoon over crumbs.
Top with paprika.
Put under broiler until crumbs are golden brown.
Cook whipping cream over medium heat until it comes to a boil (6 to 8 minutes).
Remove from heat.
In a medium bowl, gradually whisk sugar and cornstarch into egg yolks.
Whisk until mixture is light and creamy (3 to 4 minutes).
Gradually whisk hot cream into beaten egg yolks.
Return mixture to same saucepan; stir in vanilla.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until custard is thick enough to coat back of metal spoon (3 to 4 minutes).
Do not boil because egg yolks will curdle.
Serve warm or cool over fresh fruit.
Mix together in stainless steel bowl the peas, celery, peanuts, bacon and onion.
Cook rice and chicken broth.
Let sit for 20 minutes.
Add next five ingredients.
Whip curry powder into artichoke marinade. Add mayonnaise.
Mix all ingredients (except shrimp) together. Make the day before and refrigerate.
Cut circle from center of bread, keeping sides intact; trim inside of bread to form bowl.
Set aside.
Cut bread removed from center into bite size pieces.
Combine sour cream, mayonnaise and dill dip.
Refrigerate dip overnight.
Just before serving, fill hollow portion of bread bowl.
Place bread bowl on serving platter and surround it with cut bread pieces.
Use bread as dippers.
This dip is also good with assorted raw vegetables.
Trim crusts from bread.
Flatten each slice by rolling lightly with rolling pin.
Beat together cream cheese and mustard; stir in Cheddar cheese and salami.
Spread on bread.
Roll up each slice, starting with one of the corners; cut in half.
Roll half slice bacon around each pinwheel and fasten with a toothpick.
Place on broiler pan and bake in 425° oven for 20 to 25 minutes until bacon is crisp.
Makes 40 to 60 pinwheels.
Melt butterscotch bits and butter in saucepan, stirring constantly.
Cool and add flour, brown sugar, baking powder, salt, flavorings and egg.
Fold in marshmallows, chocolate bits and nuts. Spread into 9-inch square pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Do not overbake.
The center will be jiggly, but becomes firm with cooling.
Cook potatoes in salted water, when soft rub through a strainer. There should be 2 1/2 c.

Scald milk with onion, remove the onion and slowly whisk milk into potatoes. Melt half of the butter and add flour, salt, celery, salt and pepper. Stir until well mixed in seperate pan, then stir into the hot soup. Boil for 1 min. then add remaining butter.
Serves 4-6
Dissolve gelatine in water.
Combine with pineapple, sugar and lemon juice.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add cream cheese and pineapple cheese spreads.
Stir until dissolved and blended.
Add whipping cream.
Pour into 13 x 19-inch dish and refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
May garnish with red or green maraschino cherries if making for Christmas.
In 1 1/2-quart casserole, crumble beef.
Add onion, celery and green pepper.
Cover.
Microwave on High for 6 minutes.
Stir after 3 minutes.
Drain meat well.
Add to cooked mixture, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Cover.
Microwave at High 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir after 3 minutes or until hot.
To serve, spoon on buns.
Thinly slice carrots and mix with white wine or champagne. Add butter, dill, pepper and (if desired) salt.
Cover tightly and microwave until crisp-tender.
Season with additional pepper and garnish with parsley.
Preheat oven to 325°.
In a mixing bowl, beat margarine or butter with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds.
Add about half of the flour, the sugar, egg, baking powder and almond extract.
Beat until thoroughly combined.
Beat in remaining flour.
Divide dough into 4 portions.
Shape each portion into a 12-inch long roll.
Place 2 rolls 4 to 5-inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Using your hand, flatten each to 3-inches wide.
Repeat with remaining rolls.
Brush flattened rolls with milk and sprinkle with almonds.
Bake in a 325° oven for 12 to 14 minutes or until edges are lightly browned.
Cut warm cookies diagonally into 1-inch strips.
Cool cookies on a wire rack.
Drizzle with icing.
Makes about 48.
Pan-fry chicken, coated in flour mixture (flour, salt, paprika and pepper).
Mix soup, sour cream and mushrooms together well. Place cooked chicken in a casserole dish and pour soup sauce all over.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Sprinkle on grated cheese and just put back in oven until cheese bubbles.
In a hot pan, pour vegetable oil and stir-fry the leek and shiitake mushroom.
Add beef, and cook until done.
Mix sugar, soy sauce, and butter until well blended.
Pour over beef mixture. Serve cooked rice in a bowl and pour this over the rice.
You can also put 1 tablespoon butter on top too.
Combine juice, pudding and sugar in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil. Simmer 5 minutes or until slightly thick.
Add orange slices, lemon slices and spices.
Simmer 10 minutes more, stirring occasionally. Discard citrus slices, cinnamon sticks and whole cloves.
Add fresh fruit and simmer 10 minutes longer. Serve hot or cold. Garnish with sour cream and/or ground cinnamon.
Combine sugar, cocoa, nuts and salt in mixer bowl; mix at low speed until thoroughly blended.
Add unbeaten egg whites; mix just to moisten.
Do not overmix.
Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Drop by heaping tablespoonfuls, 2 to 3 inches apart, onto parchment paper.
Bake at 300° for 20 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen.
Cover beef with
water;
add
salt
and slice of onion. Cook under pressure slowly 1 hour.
Debone and chip lean meat. Skim off fat and
add
other
ingredients.
Bring
to boil and cook slowly about
minutes,
until
celery and carrots are done.
(If soup is
too watery, add another can of potato soup to thicken.)
In saucepan, blend butter (1/2) with heavy cream, pepper and cheese.
Apart, in skillet, melt garlic in butter until brown. Add shrimp and stir-fry.
Add parsley, basil and lemon on low heat.
Remove from heat.
Apart, prepare pasta.
Drain.
Pour cream sauce on pasta.
Garnish with shrimp.
Place raw chicken in 8 x 8-inch glass pan.
Cover with vegetables.
Pour spaghetti sauce over all.
Sprinkle with cheese. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serve over spaghetti.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Clean mushrooms; remove caps and chop stems.
Mix cracker crumbs with salt, pepper, parsley, onions and melted butter.
Add chopped stems.
Cook chicken in water until tender, adding salt to taste. Remove from heat; let cool.
Shred the meat from the bones.
Put broth in a pan and add the mole and garlic.
Make sure it is not too thick, if it is keep adding chicken broth, then add the chicken and let it cook with mole for 10 to 15 minutes over low heat.
In a large saucepan, combine sugar and corn syrup; bring to boiling.
Remove from heat.
Add peanut butter, stirring until melted.
Stir in cereal, coconut and peanuts.
Drop from teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Cool thoroughly.
Do not refrigerate.
Makes 6 to 7 dozen.
Warm in pan the thin cream.
Add beaten yolks and pinch of salt.
Cook until thick.
Cool.
Stir soup, water and gelatin together and let stand for 10 minutes.
Heat and stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Cool.
Beat in mayonnaise and cottage cheese with rotary beater.
Fold in shrimp, eggs and onion.
Pour into 6-cup mold or individual salad molds sprayed lightly with Pam.
Chill until firm.
Cook cranberries in all but 1/4 cup water until very soft; rub through fine sieve.
Soften gelatin in remaining water.
Heat sugar and corn syrup to boiling; add gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Combine all ingredients and beat well for a few minutes to cool and slightly thicken.
Pour into automatic refrigerator tray and freeze quickly, stirring several times during freezing.
In a double boiler, melt caramels in water.
Dip half of each pretzel into the hot caramel.
Place on a greased sheet of foil to cool.
Dissolve yeast in water; add sugar, salt, oil and egg; stir. Add flour, half
at
a time (may not need all).
Knead until smooth
and
elastic.
Let rise
until
doubled.
Punch down, divide
in half;
divide
each half into quarters.
For each loaf, divide
one quarter
into
3 pieces.
Take 3 large pieces, roll
into long
"snakes."
Braid.
Take
smaller pieces, repeat process.
Put small braid on top of large braid and tuck ends
under.
Repeat for second loaf.
Let rise until doubled (or almost);
oil
lightly
to keep from drying out. Glaze with beaten
egg
yolk
and bake at 400° for 10 minutes, 350° for 40 minutes.
Best eaten warm and broken off loaf with fingers and buttered.
Dip veal into egg, then into flour to coat.
Brown in oil in skillet; remove and keep warm.
Add broth to pan juices, stirring to blend in meat particles.
Combine cornstarch and wine and stir into broth with remaining ingredients.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Pour over veal and garnish with lemon slices.
Combine tuna, celery, green pepper, relish, lemon juice, mayo and cheese.
Spread evenly on 6 slices bread and cover with remaining slices.
Combine eggs and milk.
Melt butter in skillet. Dip sandwiches in egg mixture.
Turn so both sides are coated. Cook sandwiches until golden brown on both sides.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix sugar with shortening and salt.
Add egg.
Beat with electric mixer 1 minute or until well blended.
Dissolve yeast in warm milk.
Add flour, then milk-yeast mixture and vanilla to dough batter.
Mix 3 minutes with electric mixer (use dough hook if available).
Turn dough out on floured board and knead for 1 minute.
Place in a lightly greased bowl; cover with a towel and set in a warm place to rise for 1 hour.
Split fresh jumbo shrimp (cleaned and headed).
Layer 1/4 sliver of jalapeno pepper and sliver of Colby cheese inside.
Wrap shrimp with piece of bacon and hold together with toothpick. Season with a little salt, if desired.
Cook for a few minutes on outdoor grill until done.
Puree the fruit with the grape juice and ice in the work bowl of a food processor or blender.
Combine in a pitcher with seltzer.
Serve in 12 ounce glasses filled with ice.
Squeeze a wedge of lemon or lime into each glass.
Makes four servings.
Cream butter and sugar; add flour and mix well.
Add nuts
and chips or bits (or add all three).
Roll into balls.
Place on cookie sheet sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Let cool.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Mix gelatin, mayonnaise and cream cheese until light in color. Add hot water and juice from fruit cocktail and allow to cool. When gelatin mixture begins to set, add remaining ingredients. Chill.
Yield:
6 to 8 servings.
Bake pie crust.
Mix peanut butter and cream cheese until well blended. Add sugars and milk.
Continue mixing until fluffy. Fold in whipped topping and mix thoroughly.
Pour into cooled pie crust and chill in freezer for 2 hours (or until set). Refrigerate leftovers.
Makes 1 pie.
Combine corn and milk.
Add eggs, crumbs and the other ingredients in mixing bowl.
Pour into well-greased casserole. Dot with butter.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes in 350° oven.
Top with paprika, if desired.
Add approximately 1/2 amount of water to canned juices.
Add 1/2 amount of water to fruit punch.
Fry flour tortillas (or brush with butter and bake) until crisp.
Sprinkle with cheese while hot.
Add warmed refried beans with onion, chilies and garlic seasoning added.
Fry hamburger; drain and add mushroom soup and rest of green chilies.
Add second layer of cheese to tortilla.
Top with meat mixture.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes and sour cream.
Brown beef and drain.
Mix soups, milk and tomatoes in micro-safe dish and heat until hot.
Spray casserole dish with Pam and layer with half Doritos; layer half of meat, onions and cheese.
Pour 1/2 soup mixture over and repeat layers.
Pour rest of soup mixture over top.
Bake at 350° until hot and cheese is melted.
Put in double boiler the egg yolks, 1/2 cup sugar and lemon juice.
Cook until thick; set aside and cool.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 1/4 cup sugar, beat well.
Add half egg white mixture to first mixture; mix well.
Pour into baked pie shell. Top with remainder of egg white mixture; put in oven and brown as desired.

recipes.t: Baked Leeks With Bechamel Sauce And Chopped Ham
d: Discard any withered leaves from the leeks and chop off the green tops.
Cook in salted boiling water for about 10 minutes, until leeks are cooked al dente.
Prepare the bechamel (with nutmeg) and leave to cool.
Drain the leeks and saute for 5 minutes in a skillet with the butter, salt and pepper.
Transfer to an ovenproof dish.
Combine the egg yolk and 3/4 of the ham with the bechamel, mix well and pour over the leeks.
Sprinkle with the cheese and the remaining ham.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 20 minutes.
Serves 4.
Prepare linguine according to package directions; drain.
In large skillet, heat oil.
Add chicken; stir-fry until no longer pink.
Add vegetables; stir-fry just until tender-crisp.
Stir in parsley flakes, Italian seasoning, salt, garlic powder and pepper. Add to linguine; toss to mix.
Garnish as desired.
Serve immediately or cover and chill.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Soften gelatin in water in bowl.
Bring picante salsa to a boil in saucepan.
Stir in gelatin until dissolved.
Beat in cream cheese.
Cool to room temperature.
Add onions, bell pepper, celery, crab, shrimp and Tabasco sauce.
Mix well.
Fold in mayonnaise.
Chill until partially set.
Spoon into greased mold. Chill overnight.
Unmold onto serving plate.
Serve with crackers.
Cut meat into steaks (approximately 8 portions).
Coat meat with beaten egg; then flour.
In electric skillet, season meat while browning on both sides.
(Use high heat - do not scorch.) Pour meat and drippings into 8-quart stew pot.
Add tomatoes, carrots, onions, black pepper and 2 cups water (more as necessary). Salt, pepper and garlic to taste.
Cover and stew on medium heat for 2 1/2 hours; stir frequently.
Do not allow all water to cook out.
Serve over or with mashed potatoes.
Line a 9 x 13 greased pan with bread.
Put cheese over bread. Combine eggs, milk, onions, mushrooms and green peppers and pour over top.
Crumble bacon and spread on top.
Refrigerate overnight. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour, uncovered.

recipes.t: Homemade Style Done Easy Chicken Noodle Soup
d: Cook chicken, onion, salt and pepper in a crock-pot.
When chicken is done, remove and pick chicken from bones.
Add to crock-pot the picked chicken, mushrooms, egg noodles and more salt. Cook until egg noodles are done, usually about 20 to 25 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease jelly roll pan (15 1/2 x 10 x 1-inch).
Beat margarine and sugar in large bowl.
Beat in syrup, eggs and flour thoroughly.
Stir in nuts.
Next a true chocoholic will wish to stir in chocolate chips; these are optional.
Pour in pan.
Bake until toothpick comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Make 48 squares.
Filling Preparation:
Cook meat, onion, garlic, salt and pepper for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, then add the rest of the ingredients.
Cook about 25 to 30 minutes, until potatoes are done; ladle off any excess oil.
Let cool.
Combine juice, whiskey and sugar to dissolve.
Chill.
Add tea and put mixture into a large punch bowl with a ring or block of ice.
Add soda and fruit.
Makes about 25 servings.
Saute onion until done.
Add butter and mustard.
Place cheese between bread slices.
Spread with some of sauce.
Spread rest of sauce over bread.
Sprinkle poppy seed over top.
Bake at 275° about 45 minutes or until done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place 1/2 pound butter in a small pan, then melt in the oven.
Sift the flours (at least once) and mix them thoroughly in a large bowl.
Place some extra white flour (several cups) in a medium bowl.
Measure the baking powder, salt, butter and honey.
Add to the 1 3/4 cups of warm water and stir well.
Grease baking pan with butter and dust with white flour.
Place chocolate in a small bowl.
In small saucepan, bring 1/2 cup of the cream to a simmer.
Pour over the chocolate.
Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then stir until smooth.
Dry soft crabs with paper towels.
Remove all cartilage from crabmeat.
Place soft crabs in shallow baking pan.
Remove top shell from crabs and stuff each crab cavity with about 3 tablespoons crabmeat.
Replace top shell.
Melt butter and pour evenly over crabs.
Bake at 400° until shells turn red and crabs brown slightly, about 15 minutes.
Makes 6 servings, 2 crabs each.
Combine 1/2 of chickpeas in Cuisinart.
Add all other ingredients except parsley.
When pureed, add rest of chickpeas and mix until pureed.
Stir in parsley, leaving a few tablespoons to sprinkle on top before serving.
Serve with pita bread.
Mix oil, vinegar, lemon juice, dry mustard, egg, garlic and Worcestershire sauce well.
Put lettuce and bacon in a salad bowl. Add dressing and toss.
Top with cheese and croutons.
Separate eggs.
Beat whites stiff and sit in refrigerator. Reserve 2/3 cup sugar
(from
original 2 2/3 cups).
Add to whites.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks.
Gradually add flour.
Fold in egg
whites, cream and flavoring.
Bake in tube pan 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Sprinkle lobster meat with lemon juice.
Add celery, onion and pickle relish.
Moisten with mayonnaise.
Season with salt and pepper.
Fold in egg slices.
Serve over lettuce.
Bring pepper, sugar and vinegar to a rolling boil.
Take off stove and let set 5 minutes.
Then stir in Certo, mixing well. Pour into glasses and seal.
Cream sugars and margarine; add oil, egg and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add coconut and rolled oats.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar and salt and add in parts to other mixture.
Mix in Rice Krispies.
Drop by teaspoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes in 350° oven.
Mix 50-50 water and vinegar together.
Add onion, garlic and salt and pepper.
Add fish to marinade and leave for 1 hour. Remove from marinade and dry with paper towels.
Dredge in flour and cook in hot oil.
In blender or food processor, combine cream cheese, yogurt, garlic, chives, parsley and pepper to taste.
Process until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for several hours to let flavors blend.
Yield:
1 cup.
Saute noodles in vegetable oil until lightly brown (don't burn).
Bake almonds and sesame seed at 350° about 5 minutes. Combine lettuce, onions, noodles, almonds and sesame seed.
Mix thoroughly the oil, sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper and pour over salad when ready to serve.

recipes.t: Orange Roughy With Creamy Mushroom Sauce
d: Coat a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray; place over medium heat until hot.
Add the next 3 ingredients; saute for 3 minutes.
Set aside and cool.
Combine mushroom mixture, cheese and yogurt in a bowl; stir well.
Place fillets in an 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with mushroom mixture; sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes, or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Garnish with paprika and parsley, if desired.
Drain pineapple and
peaches.
Mix
juice with pudding, using wire whisk.
Pour over fruit and chill.
Stir together onions, cheese, crabmeat and mayonnaise.
Toast the cocktail slices and spread the cheese mix on top.
Arrange on baking sheet and place in broiler. Broil until the cheese melts and becomes bubbly and browned, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Form the meat into extra large meatballs (about 6-inch). Brown well in heavy skillet.
Remove from pan.
Add cold water to the pan and scrape all the brown bits from the bottom of the pan while still very hot.
Turn heat to low and add as much water as needed for gravy to cover all meat, potatoes and onions.
Make your gravy with flour, salt, pepper and crushed gravy to taste.
Put meatballs back in skillet, cover with thinly sliced onions and peeled potatoes (cut in half).
cover completely with gravy. Cover and simmer 2 or 3 hours.
The longer, the better.
Peel the green from rind. Cut into cubes. Soak rind in salted water with alum overnight.
Drain. Cover with fresh water and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and drain.
Mix sugar into 8 cups water and add remaining ingredients.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until mixture becomes syrupy.
Add rind and bring to a slow boil. Cook until rind is tender.
Pack in jars and seal.
Do water bath for 10 minutes.
Makes 3 to 4 quarts.
Put apples, cranberries, water, sugar, cinnamon and salt in saucepan; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until apples are tender.
Bake shortcake in two 8-inch layers.
Put hot apple mix between layers and on top of hot shortcake.
Cut into wedges and serve with whipped cream, if desired.
Serves 6.
Cook broccoli and drain. Beat eggs, yogurt, milk and cornstarch. Stir in remaining ingredients except broccoli.
Spray a 9-inch baking pan with Pam.
Put broccoli in pan and pour mixture over it. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown chops in oil 3 to 5 minutes on each side; arrange chops in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish.
Combine soup and remaining ingredients; spoon over chops.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Yields 6 servings.
Mix eggs and low-fat milk into a square dish.
Stir until blended.
Dip slices of dry bread into batter.
Fry toast in a lightly buttered nonstick skillet until golden brown.
Sprinkle toast with cinnamon and top with syrup.
Serve with a cold glass of milk.
Place 4 scoops (about 1/2 cup each) of ice cream in a small pan; freeze for 1 hour or until firm.
In small mixing bowl, stir together egg and vanilla.
In pie plate, stir cereal and cinnamon.
Combine cabbage and carrots.
Add drained pineapple, reserving juice.
Make dressing by adding sweetener and small amount of pineapple juice to the yogurt to suit your taste.
Add yogurt mixture to slaw, combining well and refrigerate before serving. Yields 6 servings.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Place 1/2 of tomatoes in baking dish; cover with bread crumbs and 1/2 of the cheese.
Dot with butter.
Add remaining tomatoes and top with cheese formed into a circle.
Bake in a moderate oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 5.
Saute onions in fat.
Mix all ingredients and stuff chicken. Bake as usual.
Remove meat from casing and break apart and brown meat; remove and saute chopped green pepper, onion and mushrooms.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Cook and drain pasta.
In Dutch oven, mix pasta sausage, sauce and chilies.
Put into large baking dish.
Cover with more Mozzarella.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
(Makes enough for a small army.)
Toast Eggo.
Spread butter over Eggo.
Sprinkle powdered sugar, then cinnamon sugar.
Top with candied sprinkles.
Good with chocolate milk.

Grease and flour a 15 x 10 x 1-inch jellyroll pan; set aside. In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs, salt and vanilla with an electric mixer on high speed about 4 minutes or until thick. Gradually add the 3/4 cup granulated sugar; beat on medium speed for 4 to 5 minutes or until light and fluffy.
Add the pancake mix; beat on low speed just until combined.
Spread batter in pan that's prepared.

Bake in 400° oven for 8 to 10 minutes, or until golden and cake springs back when lightly touched near center. Immediately loosen edges of cake from pan and turn cake out onto a towel sprinkled with powdered sugar.
Roll up towel and cake, jellyroll style, starting from one of the short sides.
Cool on a wire rack.
Cream butter, shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour and 7-Up, beginning and ending with flour.
Add flavoring.
Pour into a large tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes and remove.
Sprinkle yeast into warm water; stir until dissolved.
Sift together flour, sugar and salt.
In large bowl, combine potatoes, butter, cheese, eggs and milk.
Beat until well blended.
Add yeast mixture and dry ingredients; mix thoroughly.
Turn dough onto well floured surface.
Knead about 8 minutes or until smooth and satiny. Place in greased bowl.
Cover.
Let rise in warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Punch down dough.
Knead gently on floured surface for 2 minutes.
Shape into a 20-inch roll.
Place in a well-greased 9-inch ring mold.
Pinch edges to seal.
Cover.
Let rise until almost doubled, about 30 minutes.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 35 minutes.
Yields 1 ring.
Cook sprouts according to package directions; drain.
Combine vinegar, oil, garlic, sugar, salt and Tabasco.
Add sprouts and onions.
Toss; cover and chill 8 hours or overnight.
Arrange on appetizer tray, with toothpicks, to serve.
Mix together
butter, sugar and syrup.
Cook to 305° or hard crack.
Add
2 teaspoons vanilla extract.
Pour over 4 to 5 quarts popped
popcorn.
Add nuts and stir to cool.
Spread on waxed paper and cool.
Cook and stir bacon and onion until bacon is crisp.
Add enough water to clam juice to make 1 cup.
Stir clams, liquid, potatoes, celery and spices in bacon and onion mixture.
Heat to boiling.
Cover and reduce heat.
Simmer until potatoes are tender.
Stir in milk; heat, but do not boil.
Cook sausage and drain on towels.
Melt cheese and add all ingredients.
Place in casserole.
Grill to keep warm.
Serve with chips.
Beat eggs, then add sugar, milk and vanilla.
With a wooden spoon blending dry ingredients.
Pour into large greased and floured cookie sheet.
Bake at 300 degrees for 20 minutes.
