Right from oven, spread on peanut butter, allow to cool, melt chocolate bars and spread on top.
Melt butter in Dutch oven.
Add kielbasa chunks, saute until lightly browned.
Add onions and garlic.
Saute briefly and add carrots, broth and rice.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Add spinach strips, zucchini, green beans and corn.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes or until carrots and beans are done.
Season to taste.
I usually like to make it a day before so it blends.
Combine tomatoes, celery, salad dressing, green peppers and onion.
Toss lightly.
Chill 1 hour.
Add bacon; toss lightly. Spoon vegetable mixture over shredded lettuce.
Garnish with additional cherry tomato halves and bacon crumbs if desired. Yields 6 servings.
In a large bowl, combine hot sauce, dressing mix, margarine, Worcestershire sauce and honey. Set aside.
Cut off and discard bony wing tip from wings.
In a Dutch oven, heat oil for deep fat frying to 350°.
Fry wings until crispy. Dip wings in sauce and serve.
Boil pears, pineapple and sugar for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and add 1 large box of orange jello.
Pour into jelly jars.
Put all beans, onions and Ro-Tel in large pot.
Bring to a boil with 3 cups water.
Turn down heat to simmer for 30 to 45 minutes. Add ground beef, all cut up hot dogs and smoked sausage.
Add to pot and cook on low heat for 30 more minutes.
Salt and pepper to taste.
I don't add salt and pepper until it's done for the dogs and sausage are already salty.
Combine ingredients in bowl.
Sprinkle cheese mixture on a non stick cookie sheet into 1 1/2 inch rounds.
16 circles on a sheet.
Bake in 350 degree oven for 9 to 10 minutes until golden. Cool on rack. Makes 96 rounds. Store in air tight container.

Cut chicken in quarters. Boil in large pot, covering chicken with water. Add salt and pepper. Boil until tender and well cooked. Remove chicken to cool on large cookie sheet. Place broth in large roaster pan and continue to simmer while chicken cools. Add margarine, soup and enough water to fill roaster pan about half full. Taste to see if seasoned enough. Add chicken (picked off bone). Add evaporated milk just before you begin to add dumplings.
Combine cocoa, sugar and salt in a saucepan.
Add syrup and milk.
Cook over slow heat until mixture forms soft ball when dropped in cold water.
Remove from heat and stir in peanuts, oatmeal and coconut.
Combine soy sauce, oil, water, garlic, oregano and brown sugar.
Arrange chicken breasts in baking dish.
Pour wine mixture over breasts. Cover. Bake at 375° for
1 hour and 30 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Dice avocado into a bowl.
Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
Blend cheese with remaning lemon juice, sugar, mayonnaise and salt.
Add fruit.
Fold in whipped cream.
Put in freezing tray and freeze 6-8 hours.
Let stand a few minutes before cutting.
Cut in squares to serve.
Pretty and good!
In Dutch oven, brown beef chuck slowly in cooking oil.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add water.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour. Add water, if necessary.
Add carrots, onions and potatoes to meat.
Simmer 45 minutes or until tender.
Serve with skimmed juice.
Place orange slices on a greased wire rack.
Place rack on baking sheet.
Bake at 200° for 5 to 6 hours, removing slices as they dry.
Cut slices into eighths with shears.
Place 1/4 cup orange pieces, 1 teaspoon cloves, 1 teaspoon allspice and 1 cinnamon stick in 7 to 8 Ziploc plastic bags.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Saut onion in bacon drippings (or oil) until golden brown.
Combine with beans, brown sugar, chili powder, oregano, salt and pepper and tomato sauce. Mix lightly and place in 2-quart dish.
Arrange bacon on top.
Cover.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Remove cover and bake 10 minutes to brown bacon.

Grease a shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish with butter. Set aside. In a saucepan, combine cream, milk, salt, pepper and garlic. Cook just until bubbles begin to form around sides of pan. Remove from the heat; cool for 10 minutes. Peel and thinly slice the potatoes; pat dry with paper towels. Layer half of the potatoes in prepared baking dish. Top with half of the cream mixture and half of the cheeses. Repeat layers. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 55 to 65 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Let stand for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
Combine the first 6 ingredients.
Add the spinach; cover pan and cook until thawed.
Add the soup and sour cream; mix thoroughly.
Transfer to buttered casserole.
Arrange sliced cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brown meat and drain.
In large skillet, add cabbage, carrots, onion, beans and soy sauce.
Cook until vegetables are tender. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Place 2 tablespoons of vegetables per wrapper.
Roll up and deep fry eggroll until they slightly brown.
Grease 13 x 9 pan, line with wax paper.
Grease again.
Sift Flour, baking powder and salt and set aside.
In another bowl, beat eggs and add sugar and extracts.
Scald milk and add to dry ingredients.
Add egg mixture.
Pour into prepared pan and bake at 350° for 35-40 minutes.
When done, let cool in pan at least 30 minutes.
Whip the cream and add confectioners sugar and vanilla. Slice the strawberries.
Slice cake lengthwise.
Take 1 1/2 cups of frosting mixture and add strawberries (reserve enough for garnish) and spread for filling.
Add top layer and frost with remaining cream.
With remaining strawberries, make 4 rows to form stripes and the 50 blueberries to form starts.
Wash and boil cleaned string beans in a pot with about 4 quarts of water and salt for about 15 minutes until tender, but not completely done.
Drain in a colander.
Combine 1 ounce of butter and chopped onion in a pan.
Heat for about 2 minutes, without browning, then add beans, pepper and nutmeg.
Stir for 2 more minutes and pour in a buttered baking pan.
Beat eggs slightly and blend in cream and grated cheese.
Pour mixture over beans and bake until gratin is formed.
Serves 6 persons.
Beat egg yolks and sugar until fluffy, and add vanilla.
Mix flour with baking powder.
Add sour cream, rum and beaten egg yolks.
Knead well.
Cut off a little part of the dough (cover the rest with plastic) and roll very thin.
Cut in 2 x 4-inch strips. Cut a hole in the middle of each strip, then pass one end of each strip through it to make a knot.
Fry until golden brown in hot Crisco shortening.
After cooling, sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Brown meat and drain fat.
Mix soup, beans, sauce and tomatoes.
Place tortillas in a long shallow casserole dish.
Pour meat over tortillas.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 250° F.
Beat cream cheese at medium speed with an electric mixer until creamy.
Add ricotta cheese; beat until well blended.
Gradually add Splenda No Calorie Sweetener, Granular, beating until blended.
Add eggs gradually, beating until blended.
Add egg white and beat until blended.
Add vanilla and half and half, beating until blended.
Pour mixture into 8 (8 ounce) ramekins; place ramekins in a roasting pan.
Add hot water to pan to a depth of 1 inch.
Bake at 250° F for 45 minutes or until custards are set.
Custards will puff slightly and remain white. Remove from water bath and cool on a wire rack.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
Garnish, if desired.
Makes 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Toss together crumbs, cheese, butter and mustard.
Turn tomatoes, stem end down, and cut tomatoes into 5 slices, cutting to (but not through) the base.
Spread apart slightly and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Spoon 2 tablespoons crumb mixture between each slice.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Combine with undrained sauerkraut and remaining ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Makes 6 servings.
Cut the chicken breasts in half.
In one dish, mix the bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, salt and parsley.
In another dish, melt the butter, plus 1 clove garlic (minced).
Take chicken pieces and white pepper both sides.
Put in butter and garlic. Roll in bread crumb mixture.
Roll up and toothpick together.
Put all rolled chicken in casserole dish.
Pour remaining butter
and garlic in casserole.
Squirt lemon juice over all chicken. Sprinkle paprika over it.
Put in oven at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.t: Grilled Honey Mustard Chicken With Vegetables
d: Mix honey and mustard in a gallon Ziploc bag to make marinade. Add cutlets.
Marinate 3 to 4 hours or overnight.
Mix olive oil, salt and garlic powder; coat vegetables with this mixture.
Heat barbecue.
Grill vegetables until slightly charred.
Grill cutlets until done.
Pound chicken breast.
Put on ham and cheese.
Roll and fasten with picks and fry until brown in hot fat.
Put in casserole and pour soup and cooking wine.
Bake about 1 hour.
Brown beef, onion and garlic in Dutch oven.
Add spices, tomatoes and water.
Bring to boil; reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes to 1 hour.
(I add kidney beans and some spaghetti.)
It's optional.
In saucepan, saute mushrooms in 1 tablespoon butter until lightly brown, stirring occasionally; remove from heat.
Stir in ham, sour cream, mustard and pepper; mix well.
Spread evenly on 4 slices bread.
Top with remaining bread.
Brush both sides with melted butter.
Broil in preheated oven until browned and filling is hot, turning once.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spray 6 large, 3-inch muffin cups with nonfat, nonstick spray and set aside.
In a large bowl, stir together both flours, sugar, baking powder and lemon peel, making sure all is evenly distributed.
Make a well in the center of the mixture.
Blend the flour, butter, pecans and brown sugar.
Press into pan (13 x 9-inch) and bake for 20 minutes at 325°.
Cool.
Cream the shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well. Combine flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk, beating well after each addition.
Stir in the raisins.
Spread batter in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Top with apples.
Combine sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over the apples.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until cake tests done.
Serve warm.
Yields 12 servings.
In a large saucepan, saute onion, celery and caraway seed in 2 Tbsp. butter or margarine until slightly soft.
Add chicken stock or chicken broth and bring to a boil.
In a small saucepan, melt 1/2 c. butter or margarine, stir in flour.
Mix well and add to the boiling soup, stirring to combine thoroughly.
Reduce heat to a simmer.
Stir in sauerkraut and corned beef.
Add salt and white pepper to taste.
Just before serving, add half and half or light cream. Heat, but do not let soup come to a boil.
Serve immediately.
This holds well in a Crock-Pot.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks, flour, salt and peaches.
Turn into unbaked pie shell.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°. Add meringue and brown.
Cover bottom of casserole dish with bacon slices.
Press the ground beef on top of bacon followed with sliced onion, carrots and sliced raw potatoes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour on one can of soup.
Cover and bake until vegetables are tender at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
In buttered casserole dish, layer thin sliced potatoes, layer of sliced onions, layer of shredded cabbage, layer of corned beef. Top with 1 can golden mushroom soup.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes. Bake according to number of servings.
Cut 4 pieces of aluminum foil, each about 12 x 15-inches and set aside.
Cut unpeeled potatoes into slices about 1/16-inch thick.
Toss potatoes with onion, bell pepper, oil and seasonings. Distribute mixture evenly between 4 pieces of foil.
Drizzle with lemon juice.
Wrap each securely but loosely to form a flat package.
Place seam side up on baking sheet.
Bake at 450° about 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Serve hot.
Serves 4.
Combine ground beef, evaporated milk, tomato sauce, bread crumbs and onion in large bowl.
Mix well.
Spread evenly in pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 5 more minutes.
Makes 6 servings. Each serving contains:
3 1/2 protein, 1 bread and 65 optional calories.
In medium bowl, toss peach slices, 1/4 cup sugar and mace to mix well.
Set aside.
In second bowl, combine flour, remaining 1/2 cup sugar and baking powder.
Stir in milk and eggs, mixing just until blended.
Place butter in a 9-inch square baking pan and place in 375° oven until melted and hot.
Remove pan from oven and immediately pour batter over butter.
Spoon peach mixture evenly over batter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until puffed and brown.
Serve warm, topped with vanilla ice cream, if desired. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Combine raisins, brown sugar and nuts.
Stretch biscuits to a 4-inch circle.
Butter generously.
Press raisins, sugar and nut mixture on top.
Bake at 450° for 8 minutes.
Sift flour, salt and baking soda into mixing bowl.
Blend in brown sugar and oatmeal. Cut in the shortening until particles are the size of small peas.
Press 1/2 oatmeal mixture into bottom of ungreased 12 x 8 x 2 or 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Spread with cherry pie filling. Add balance of oatmeal mixture on top.
Press gently with spoon.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes at 350° until golden brown. Cut into squares.
Serve with cream, warm or cold.
Place meat into a large saucepan or wok after heating oil. Cook on medium heat until cooked through. Add flavor packets from the noodles with about 4 teaspoons soy sauce.

Add the vegetables and squirt lemon juice and more soy sauce onto the mixture. Continue stirring until all vegetables are cooked. Boil noodles and drain. Add noodles to meat and vegetables, along with 2 teaspoons lemon juice and soy sauce. Stir together until all noodles are covered with "sauce."
Place on a serving platter with wedges of lemon.
In a shallow glass dish, combine soy sauce, honey, ginger, garlic, lemon peel and red hot pepper flakes.
Mix well.
Add beef.
Stir to coat.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Stir occasionally.
Cook macaroni per package directions.
Stir together eggs, evaporated milk, salt and pepper; set aside.
Grate Cheddar cheese.
Cut up Velveeta in small blocks or slices.
In large dish or several small casserole dishes (loaf pans), layer macaroni and cheese
2 or 3 times.
Pour milk-egg mixture over Mac-N-Cheese. If more than 1 casserole dish is used, pour equal amount of milk-egg mixture over each dish of Mac-N-Cheese.
Bake at 350° to 375° for 45 minutes to 1 1/2 hours.
Mix corn muffin mix and biscuit baking mix in large mixing bowl.
Blend in milk and egg.
Spray inside of 9 x 2-inch round glass dish and outside of 6-ounce glass cup with spray-on vegetable coating.
Cook in oven on full power for 3 to 4 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

Stir together the first 5 ingredients in a 1-quart microwave-safe dish. Microwave at High 3 minutes or until cheese melts, stirring after each minute. Serve immediately with tortilla chips. Yield: 3 1/4 cups.
On a large platter, place a layer of chips, followed by lettuce, quartered tomato and sliced onion.
Slice and saute one onion and the green pepper; set aside.
Brown and drain the hamburger.
Mix the hamburger with refried beans and heat.
Spoon the hamburger-refried bean mix over the chips and vegetables. Place the sauteed onion and green pepper over the hamburger-refried beans.
Cover with green chilies, black olives and cheese.
Broil until the cheese melts.
Garnish with hot peppers; start dipping into your favorite salsa (mine is made with habanera peppers).
Be sure to have plenty of Mexican beer around!!
Mix pancake mix and 1 package salad dressing (both dry); set aside.
Beat egg with water; stir in second package salad dressing (dry).
Coat evenly each piece of cut up chicken with egg-water-dressing mixture, then roll in pancake-dressing mix. Let dry on toweling.
Heat 1-inch deep oil in a heavy skillet (400°).
Fry 4 to 5 minutes on each side.
Place on cookie sheets in 350° oven for 30 minutes for crispy coating.
Bring all refrigerated ingredients to room temperature by letting them stand on counter about 30 minutes.
Place yeast in bread machine pan according to directions in manual.
In medium bowl, combine flour, oats, cheese, sugar, salt and seasoning; mix well.
In separate bowl, combine buttermilk and oil; mix well. Place dry ingredients and buttermilk mixture in bread machine pan according to manual.
Select white bread and light crust settings. Remove bread from pan to wire rack.
Cool completely before slicing.
Yield:
1 1/2 pound loaf (16 servings).
Cool cake after baking.
Pull cake apart into small chunks. Spread in a bottom layer of bowl.
Pour caramel sauce generously over cake.
Sprinkle crushed nuts over sauce.
Spread Cool Whip over that.
Repeat with chocolate cake, caramel, nuts and Cool Whip until it reaches the top of the bowl.
(Sometimes I add crushed Oreos or Heath Bar bits.)
Stir together pie filling, ice cream and lemon juice.
Stir in bananas and nuts.
Turn into 8 individual molds.
Freeze firm several hours or overnight.
Place in refrigerator 15 minutes before serving.
Unmold onto lettuce-lined plates.
Makes 8 servings.
Grease foil-lined pan.
Heat oven to 375°.
Place oats, paprika, oregano, salt and pepper in the blender container and mix well.
Stir in parsley.
Coat chicken in oat mixture.
Dip into milk and coat again with oat mixture.
Place on rack.

recipes.t: French Fried Cream Cheese And Jelly Sandwich
d: Spread cream cheese on one slice of bread.
Spread jelly on second slice of bread.
Put sandwich together.
Heat oil or oleo in frying pan.
Fry sandwich on both sides until lightly browned. Put on plate; sprinkle with confectioners sugar and enjoy!
Drain pears, saving the juice. Add water to pear juice to make 1 cup.
Bring to a boil. Add lime Jell-O and mix for 2 minutes.
Cream together first 3 ingredients; add milk, flour, baking powder, almond extract and vanilla.
Mix with electric mixer. Grease 2 (7-inch) cake pans.
Flour inside.
Whip egg whites with sugar and cream of tartar until stiff.
Divide batter into cake pan; cover with whipped egg whites to form peaks.
Sprinkle chopped nuts over both layers.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes in 350° oven until tester comes out clean.
Cool on rack.
Assemble cake. Place first layer with meringue on bottom.
Put strawberries (frozen) and juice in center with whipped cream.
Add upper layer with meringue up.
Put rest of cream over cake.
Garnish with fresh strawberries.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Combine everything but pork chops. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Dip each chop into sauce.
Bake, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes, until done.
Pass sauce separately.
Serves 5 or more.
Cut orange slices in quarters.
Arrange fruit in serving bowl. Combine sugar and coconut.
Sprinkle over fruit.
Add pineapple juice.
Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cook vegetables as directed on package.
Stir-fry onion and olives in 2 tablespoons margarine.
Mix in vegetables and stir together.
Pour mixture into flat casserole dish.
Place sheets of Swiss cheese on top.
Microwave until cheese melts.
In a large pitcher, mix together one 24 ounce can unsweetened frozen apple juice concentrate, 2 (24 ounce) cans cold water and one (32 ounce) bottle club soda.
Stir well and pour into plastic glasses.
Makes 17 small servings.

Cut sliced ham and sharp cheese into 1/4-inch cubes. Combine with onions, hard-boiled eggs and sliced peppers (or stuffed olives). Mix salad dressing and chili sauce and add to ham and cheese mixture. Mix well and spread on hot dog buns. Wrap each in foil. Twist ends securely. Bake for 10 minutes in 400° oven or until buns are hot.

recipes.t: Blueberry, Maple And Walnut Quick Bread
d: Combine and beat eggs, sugar, sour cream, syrup and vanilla. Stir in bran flakes.
Add sifted flour, salt and baking soda. Add 1 cup blueberries.
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until done.
Combine consomme and water and bring to a boil.
Add remaining ingredients and let stand overnight at room temperature.
Makes 2 quarts sauce.
This is used for basting meats for barbecue.
It is applied with a wooden handle dish mop soaked in sauce.
Combine peanut butter, egg, butter, dates, coconut and confectioners sugar in large bowl and mix thoroughly.
If sticky, add more confectioners sugar.
Shape in 1-inch balls and refrigerate while preparing chocolate for coating.
Melt chocolate chips, semi-sweet chocolate and wax in top of a double boiler.
Use spoon or fork and dip balls in melted chocolate.
Place on foil to set.
Store in a cool place in a covered container.
Beat margarine; gradually add sugar, beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer.
Add cocoa mix, egg substitute and vanilla, beating until well blended.
Combine flour, soda and salt; add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Stir in cereal.
Place chicken in a 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Lay cheese over chicken.
Mix celery soup and sherry.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle generously with seasoned croutons and butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a large pot melt margarine and marshmallows over low heat. Add Rice Krispies, nuts and raisins; mix well.
Press into an 8 x 12-inch greased pan.
Let cool.
Cut into squares.
Combine rice, milk and sugar.
Cook until thick and creamy, about 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cool and fold in remaining ingredients.
Spoon into serving dishes.
Chill.
Makes 12 servings, about 1/2 cup each.
Add cherries on top if desired.
In blender or food processor container, combine cottage cheese, lemon juice and rind.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Coarsely chop orange sections.
Stir chopped oranges and almonds into mixture.
Chill at least an hour.
Serve spread with Triscuit wafers.
Wash the nasturtium flowers in ice water. Dry. Spread 1 slice of bread with mayonnaise.
Place a thick layer of nasturtium petals on top.
Place a slice of buttered bread on top. Cut the sandwiches into triangles and serve on a large platter with blossoms strewn over the top.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat margarine, sugar, egg and vanilla until light and fluffy. Add flour, baking soda, cinnamon and nutmeg, mixing until thoroughly combined. Stir in Maypo, raisins and walnuts.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until desired brownness.
Allow cookies to cool 1 minute on cookie sheet. Remove to wire rack to cool completely.
Makes 4 1/2 dozen.
Cook onions and green pepper in oil until soft.
Add sauce, wheat germ, soy grits, cheese and parsley.
Simmer several minutes until hot, stirring often.
Cook spaghetti about 7 minutes, but do not overcook.
Drain well.
Spoon over spaghetti.
Be generous. Top each portion with extra cheese.
Serve with a salad and whole wheat or rye bread for a tasty change.
Add sugar to Jell-O prepared in usual way except leave out 1 cup of water.
Use 3 cups for 2 packages.
While Jell-O is still warm, add strawberries, cut fine.
Let stand until it begins to thicken.
Break angel food cake into bite-size pieces.
Place in a tube pan.
Pour part of Jell-O mixture and another layer until all mixture is used.
Let stand until congealed or overnight in refrigerator.
Remove from pan or mold and ice with whipped cream.
Combine first 4 ingredients and heat gently.
Add cinnamon sticks and orange slices and heat 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat butter in a large pan.
Saute the first 2 ingredients in the butter for about 10 minutes.
Stir in croutons; add the chicken broth, poultry seasoning, salt and pepper, stirring constantly on low flame.
Saute diced green pepper and onion in large pan.
Add diced potatoes and cut up broccoli and cauliflower and barely enough water to cook until vegetables are done.
Add 2 cups of milk to cooked mixture.
Add 1 1/2 to 2 cups grated cheese (any kind). Thicken with 2 teaspoons cornstarch and water mixture if needed.
Blend together 10x sugar, margarine and peanut butter.
Add coconut, graham cracker crumbs and pecans.
Mix together well. Form into eggs or ball shapes.
Coat with chocolate.
Melt Hershey milk chocolate candy bars in double boiler.
Add 1/4 cake grated paraffin.
Coat candy when chilled.
Crumble ground beef into 3 quart casserole.
Cover and microwave on High 8 to 9 minutes.
Break up and stir after 4 minutes.
Drain.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and microwave 10 minutes.
Stir.
Cover and microwave 10 to 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes until macaroni is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Mix first three ingredients
and press into a 9 x 13 cake pan.
Bake 12 - 18 minutes at 350° or until golden.
Remove from oven and cover with miniature marshmallows.
Return to oven until they puff up. Remove and let cool.
In a large mixer bowl, stir together flour, brown sugar, coconut, baking powder and soda.
Add peanut butter and softened margarine.
Beat on low speed of electric mixer just until crumbly.
Set aside 1/2 cup of mixture.
Quarter the plums. Arrange on pie crust.
Mix eggs, sour cream, sugar, Cream of Wheat and vanilla.
Pour over plums.
Bake in a 375° oven for 60 to 70 minutes or crust is brown and filling set.
Mix and press crumbs, sugar and butter into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle with chips, nuts and coconut.
Pour milk over all and bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until lightly brown on the edges.
Thin cream cheese with a little salad dressing and French dressing.
Add garlic salt and onion salt.
Add shrimp.
I use electric mixer to mix all.
Pull petals from flowers.
Combine vinegar with honey, tarragon and lemon juice in small bowl.
Marinate petals in mixture for 30 minutes.
Drain petals and reserve marinade.
Mix petals with lettuce, watercress and olives in large bowl.
Line an 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan with buttered foil.
Combine sugar and milk in large saucepan.
Cook over medium heat stirring constantly until mixture boils.
Boil stirring constantly 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Beat in chocolate chips and marshmallows until melted and mixture thickens.
Stir in nuts and vanilla.
Pour into pan and cool until firm.
Store in tightly covered container.
May be frozen for a few weeks.
Cook macaroni by package directions; drain.
While macaroni cooks, brown beef and onion.
Stir in macaroni and remaining ingredients.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Serve.
Blend egg and
margarine
in
mixer
bowl.
Add
orange juice and orange rind; mix
well.
Add mixture of dry ingredients; beat until smooth.
Stir in pecans and raisins. Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls 2
inches
apart onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20
minutes
or
until brown.
Makes 2 dozen cookies.

recipes.t: "I Can'T Wait For Puerto Rico" French Toast
d: Crush corn flakes.
Dip bread in eggnog, allowing to soak.
Put bread on plate of corn flakes and flip to cover other side. Lightly brown in margarine on both sides.
Heat oven to 350°.
Place 1 cut-up fryer chicken in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Pour barbecue sauce over chicken.
Bake uncovered 1 hour or until tender.
Makes 3 to 4 servings.
In mixing bowl, combine sugar, egg, molasses, oil, baking soda and salt.
Add flour and buttermilk, mixing thoroughly.
Spoon mixture into greased and lightly floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Let stand, covered, for 15 minutes.
Cool before slicing.
Place macaroni in a baking dish and set aside.
Make sauce by adding flour, water, milk and Egg Beaters; mix until smooth.
Dice 2 slices cheese in sauce and flour over macaroni.
Place remainder of cheese on top and bake until firm.
Less than 1 gram fat per serving.
Serves 4.
Brown beef and add garlic powder, nacho sauce mix and tomato sauce.
Place nacho chips on cookie sheet or baking pan and heat in oven 5 minutes at 400°.
Place 12 to 15 chips on plate.
Top with hamburger mixture.
Sprinkle tomatoes, shredded lettuce and onion on top.
Top with squeeze cheese and jalapeno peppers. Makes 8 servings.
In
large
pot,
boil
Portuguese
sausage in water and tomato sauce.
Dice
carrot, celery and potatoes; add to pot. Add kidney
beans
and string beans; bring to boil.
Boil on medium heat until vegetables are tender.
Add cabbage.
Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
Cook pasta; drain.
Chop bell peppers, onion, cucumber and tomato.
Mix all in big bowl; add Mrs. Dash and Italian dressing and stir together thoroughly.
Refrigerate overnight so it can marinate.
It is fantastic and has become a July 4th tradition!
Melt butter in heavy skillet.
Add pecans; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 3 to 4 minutes or until toasted.
Stir in cereal crumbs, brown sugar and nutmeg.
Press half of crumb mixture into 8-inch square baking pan.
Put pan into freezer for 15 minutes.
Crumble sausage in skillet and saute until brown.
Add onions, celery, bell pepper and saute lightly.
Add salt and pepper and water; bring to a boil.
Add rice; stir in well.
Cover and remove from heat.
Let set for 5 minutes fluff with fork and serve.
Cook rotini until tender.
Add carrots last minute or so of cooking.
Cool; toss rest of ingredients in and pour dressing over.
Toss again.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Let chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Add chopped basil as garnish.
In 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish, place bacon between layers of paper towels.
Cook full power for 4 1/2 minutes.
Crumble bacon and set aside.
Place croutons in same baking dish.
Sprinkle with Cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses.
In large bowl beat eggs.
Add milk, mustard, onion powder and pepper and pour over croutons and cheese.
Cook at 50% power for 8 minutes.
Sprinkle with bacon. Cook at 50% power for 12 minutes.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes.
Pat out crescent rolls onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 9 to 11 minutes until lightly browned.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese, dressing and mayonnaise.
Spread over rolls.
Spread vegetables over mixture (use any vegetables desired).
Chill well.
Cut into wedges and serve.
Nice alternative to sweet appetizer/snack.
Boil 2 cups water and 2 cups of sugar for 10 minutes.
When cold add 3 cups cold tea, 1 cup lemon juice, 1 cup orange juice, 1 can crushed pineapple, juice and all, 1 small bottle maraschino cherries and mix well together.
When ready to serve, pour over ice cubes and pour in 2 large bottles ginger ale.
Combine first five ingredients and chill in refrigerator. Serve with poppy seed dressing.
You can omit the blueberries since they are hard to find.
Saute the onions and celery in margarine.
Add chicken broth and all ingredients (except croutons).
Simmer for 10 minutes, then pour over croutons.
(If mixture seems too dry, add a little milk.) Bake in a 9 x 13-inch uncovered pan for 30 to 45 minutes at 350°.
Grate potatoes; add salt, egg and flour to make a soft dough. Have a pot of water (3-quart) boiling.
Put dough on plate and scrape off with teaspoon into water.
Stir often and gently.
Cook about 10 minutes.
Drain.
Place sugar, syrup, water and salt in pan. Cook over medium heat until a little dropped in cold water will form a hard ball. Beat egg whites until stiff while syrup is cooking.
Pour mix into egg whites, beating continuously.
Add vanilla and beat until it loses its glossy look. Add pecans and pour onto buttered platter or drop by spoon on waxed paper. Garnish with pecan halves.
Mix cream cheese and deviled ham. Chill until firm. Form into bite size balls and roll in paprika, then in chopped nuts. Serve on toothpicks. Makes 40.
Cook pasta according to label directions; drain, rinse and drain again.
Combine cole slaw dressing, onion and mustard; add pasta, stirring to coat.
Cover tightly and refrigerate at least one hour.
Just before serving, add cabbage, green pepper and carrots to pasta mixture, stirring to coat.
Makes ten 1/2 cup servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease baking sheet.
In a large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder and soda.
Cut in margarine/butter.
Stir in pecans and currants.
Stir in eggs and enough buttermilk/sour milk to make soft dough.
Knead on floured board until smooth, about 1 minute. Shape into ball and place on greased baking sheet. Flatten to a 6-inch diameter.
Cut a deep "X" into top of loaf.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes. Cool on rack.
Toast bread; trim crusts.
Spread bread with cream cheese. Cut each piece into quarters.
Cut salmon slices to fit on top of toast.
Top toast with slices.
Garnish with strips of lemon peel.
Mix flour, salt and shortening, cut enough milk in to moisten so it will hold together.
Roll out as thin as possible and cut to make noodles.
In large kettle, alternate noodles, potatoes and chicken until used up. Pour hot broth from chicken over all layers and boil until done, about 15 minutes.
May season with onion, salt, celery seed or parsley flakes.
Cream lard, sugar and eggs.
Sift 2 cups flour with soda, salt and nutmeg.
Add to creamed mixture, alternating with milks.
Add enough more flour to make a dough as soft as can be handled.
Roll out rather thin.
Cut with a large cookie cutter.
Bake at 400° until just firm to touch.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Combine flour, seasoned salt and paprika.
Coat pork chops. Brown chops in a lightly greased skillet; drain.
Combine gravy mix and water as called for on package.
Pour over chops.
Add onions.
Simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 15 minutes longer.
Remove pork chops to serving platter.
Add mushrooms and sour cream to gravy.
Combine thoroughly.
Heat through; pour over chops.
Yield:
6 servings.
In large pot, combine potatoes, chicken and broth or water. Boil, skimming as necessary.
Cook at slow boil for 13 to 15 minutes or until tender.
Add olive oil, carrots, scallions, kale, beans, bay leaf, basil and parsley.
Add dash or two of Tabasco sauce if desired.
Boil, stirring occasionally, 5 to 6 minutes or until flavorful.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Serves 4 to 6.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Stir in grated orange rind and chopped nuts.
In a separate bowl cream butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs and molasses.
Stir egg mixture into first mixture to make a smooth dough.
Roll into balls in size of walnuts.
Bake in 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes.
Roll in confectioners sugar upon taking from oven.
In a large skillet, cook turkey until brown.
Drain off fat. Stir in tomato sauce, basil, sugar, salt, garlic salt and pepper. Bring to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes.
Soften the gelatin in the cold water for 5 minutes.
Place in top of a double boiler over water; stir until completely dissolved.
Add chopped cherries with juice, sugar and salt. Chill until slightly thickened.
Whip cream.
Add almonds, vanilla and almond extract.
Fold into gelatin mixture.
Frost white layer cake or angel food cake.
Layer in glass bowl:
All cupcakes (quartered), then sprinkle Kahlua over them.
Add 1/2 pudding mixture; sprinkle 1/2 Heath bars (broken up), then 1/2 Cool Whip mixed with nuts and marshmallows.
Then repeat with pudding, Cool Whip mixture and sprinkle with rest of broken Heath bars.
In mixing bowl, stir together cornmeal mix, flour and garlic powder.
Cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in cheese.
Blend in enough milk to make a soft dough.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Oil a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish.
On each tortilla, place one slide of each kind of cheese near edge. Top with a teaspoon each of onion and chilies.
Roll tortillas up; fold ends under to form a small package.
Place in casserole dish, overlapping.
Mash tomatoes in bowl with jalapeno sauce. Pour over quesadillas; garnish with green pepper rings.
Bake in a 425° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
In a medium bowl, mix all of the ingredients together.
Make sure the banana is mixed thoroughly with the other ingredients. Roll into a log shape or into balls and place in freezer for 30 minutes.
Arrange vegetables on tray.
Place veggie dip, peanut butter and cheese spread in separate bowls.
Add dry orange Jell-O to Cool Whip. Then add cottage cheese and drained Mandarin oranges. Top with chopped pecans (optional). Let set in refrigerator for 15 to 30 minutes, then serve.
Mix cheese, mayonnaise, chilies, half of olives, garlic powder and half of green onions together.
Add several drops of Tabasco sauce to taste.
Pour into 9 inch pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Let sit for a couple of minutes.
Sprinkle remaining olives, green onions and tomato on top.
Serve with tortilla or corn chips.
In a large kettle, fry the bacon over medium heat until very dark and crisp.
The bacon should not produce more than 1 tablespoon of fat, if so, drain off all but 1 tablespoon.
Add the onion and fry until soft.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions, stirring well, and cook for about 1 minute.
Stir in the water, juice from the clams, potatoes, evaporated skim milk, salt, pepper and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer and cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add the clams and skim milk (1 cup) and simmer over low heat 10 minutes until hot. The soup will continue to develop flavor for up to 3 days and it freezes well.
Pour oil in skillet.
Saute onion.
Drain spinach (squeeze if necessary to get out liquid).
Mix beaten eggs, salt, pepper, spinach and onion.
Add flour to thicken.
Pour into remaining oil in skillet.
Spread evenly.
Cook slowly one side, then turn to cook other side.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese before serving.
Put pears in microwave dish at least 1-inch deep.
Put 1 tablespoon butter, 1 tablespoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in each pear.
Pour 1/2 cup rum over pears.
Cook on High for 3 minutes.
Spoon sauce over pears.
Add more rum, if needed.
Cook on High for 3 more minutes or until almost tender.
Spoon sauce over pears.
Serve with whipped cream.
Soften 1 package active dry yeast in warm water.
Add salt. Blend in 3 cups flour and garlic cloves, mashed well.
Add 2 to 2 1/2 cups more flour.
Knead until smooth.
Put into a greased bowl. Cover and let stand 2 hours until doubled.
Punch down.
Let stand 10 minutes, covered.
Roll sections of dough into long sticks (about 8 or 10).
Place on greased cookie sheets.
Brush with 1 egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon milk.
Let rise in warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Again brush with egg and sprinkle on garlic salt.
Bake at 400° for 18 to 20 minutes.
Hollow out round bread (save pieces).
In large bowl, cream cream cheese.
Add clams.
Reserve juice add 1/4 cup liquid.
Add onion, beer, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, hot pepper sauce and salt.
Put mixture into hollowed out bread.
Cover entire loaf with foil.
Bake at 250° for 3 hours.
Serve with veggies and bread pieces.

recipes.t: Sauteed Turkey Sausage(With Peppers And Herbs)
d: Put the sausages into a medium size saucepan and cover with water.
Bring just to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer 8 minutes.
Remove the sausages from the water and cut into 1 inch slices.
Heat the olive oil over medium heat in a large nonstick skillet.
Add the sausage slices and saute for about 3 minutes, just until lightly browned.
Remove from the pan.
Add the garlic and onion to the pan, sauteing 3 minutes.
Add the bell peppers; saute 10 minutes.
Stir the sausages back into the pan with the salt, pepper, milk, basil and vinegar.
Stir 2 minutes and serve.
Bake yellow cake mix in 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool cake.
Blend in vanilla instant pudding with 1 1/2 cups milk; add this to cream cheese and 1/2 cup of milk.
Add large can of crushed pineapple, drained and spread on cake.
Spread Cool Whip on top of that and sprinkle almonds on top.

In separate bowl, mix flour, nuts and raisins. Cream butter, sugar, and the eggs, mixing well. Add to dry ingredients. Add vanilla to taste. Batter will be stiff. Bake at 350 degrees in tube cake pan for 1 hour 15 minutes or until done.
Cook chicken in enough liquid so that there can be at least 3 to 3 1/2 cups of liquid to cook spaghetti in and 1 cup of broth to use later.
Cook spaghetti; add soup, 1 cup of broth, salt and pepper to taste and rest of ingredients.
Bake in greased casserole dish in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Cream sugar, flour and butter until crumbly; set aside 1 cup. Mix soda and spices into mixture.
Add eggs and milk.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with reserved mix.
Bake in preheated 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Serve with Lemon Sauce.
In a large bowl, combine together butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg and stir in zucchini.
Add baking powder, spices and flour.
Mix well and then add two of the following 3 ingredients:
either raisins, chocolate chips or the chopped walnuts.
I prefer 1 cup of the chocolate chips and 1 cup of the raisins.
Bake approximately 10 minutes or until cookies are firm to touch and the edges are brown at 375°.
Thaw frozen fruit or slice banana.
Puree in blender.
Force puree through a sieve to remove berry seeds.
Put 1/4 cup puree in a tall glass.
Add milk and vanilla ice cream or matching fruit ice cream.
Almost fill with chilled soda water.
Fry and drain ground beef.
Stir in beans, salsa and chili powder.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle with green pepper.
Serve warm with chips or vegetable sticks.
Makes about 3 cups of dip.
Cream sugar and butter until fluffy.
Add meal, salt, creamer and eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Add pumpkin and spices and mix well.
Pour into unbaked 9-inch pastry shell.
Bake at 350° for about 50 minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.

Mix together well the sugars, shortening and eggs. Add dry ingredients with nuts and divide dough into 2 pieces. Make long rolls; wrap in waxed paper and refrigerate overnight. Slice cookies 1/4-inch thick and bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

Set oven at 400°. Sieve the flour. Cut the fat into pieces; add to the flour and rub in with fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs. Add raisins and sugar and mix well. Mix the eggs and milk together in a measuring cup or anything. Using a wooden spoon, add the egg mixture gradually as you mix quickly by cutting through the dough and up from the sides; do not beat or overmix. Mix to a sticky consistency and not too wet. Add a little milk if needed. Better too stiff than wet!!

Place 1 bag of frozen bread rolls in bottom of Bundt pan (no greasing is necessary). Sprinkle on top of the rolls: 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 package of butterscotch pudding and pie filling. Pour or sprinkle on top: 1/2 cup melted butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon cinnamon and 1/2 cup pecans. Prepare the night before. Cover Bundt pan with tin foil and set aside overnight.
Mix sour cream and dressing. Put on on glass tray and refrigerate overnight. Just before serving put chopped tomatoes and onion on top of mixture. Then add the cheese. Serve with chips or crackers.
Remove crust from loaf of bread.
Cut 4 lengthwise slices. Spread each bread slice with softened butter.
Spread chicken salad first and second slice of bread.
Put cheese spread between second and third slice.
Put ham salad between third and fourth slices.
Press loaf together; wrap in wax paper.
Chill 1 hour. Frost top and sides of loaf with cream cheese, softened with cream.
Arrange chopped parsley, sliced green pepper or sliced tomatoes on top.
Cut into thick slices when serving.
Warm all ingredients in saucepan.
Place ribs in 475° oven for 30 minutes.
Put slices of onion and lemon juice on ribs.
Put oven at 350°. Pour sauce over ribs.
Bake 45 minutes to 1
hour, basting ribs every 15 minutes.
Cook apples until done.
Add raisins, nuts and half the sugar. Cream remaining sugar, butter and eggs.
Sift flour, soda and spices and add last.
Bake 1 hour in loaf pan at 325°.
Cream butter, shortening and sugar.
Add sour cream alternately with dry ingredients.
Stir in the nuts.
Knead dough into rolls.
Wrap the rolls in wax paper and chill in refrigerator overnight.
Roll dough very thin; cut into shapes (St. Nicholas, birds, fish, animals, etc.).
Bake in moderate oven at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Combine first 3 ingredients; press into bottom and 1-inch up sides of a 10-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack.
Beat cream cheese at medium speed until smooth.
Gradually add 3/4 cup sugar, beating well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each addition.
Stir in sour cream and next 6 ingredients.
Spoon into crust.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 20 minutes; turn off oven.
Leave cheesecake in oven with door closed 1 hour, then cool to room temperature on a wire rack.
Chill.
Yield:
10 to 12 servings.
Mix garlic with oil, then all other items.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese onto lettuce as you mix other ingredients.
Toss and serve at once.
(Dry lettuce or romaine with towel until dry.)
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and chocolate.
Add flour alternately with milk, mixing well.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Soften yeast in warm water and mix.
Add to batter and mix well.
Let stand, covered, overnight.
Add mixture of soda and water; mix very well.
Bake in a tube pan for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 325°.
Dissolve yeast in milk.
Add salt to flour, then work in cracklings as for pie crust.
Combine egg with sour cream and add to flour mixture with dissolved yeast.
Mix quickly.
Shape into ball and refrigerate a few hours.
Roll out on floured board and fold up like a handkerchief.
Chill.
Repeat rolling and folding and chill again, about 3 times.
Roll out on floured board to 1/2-inch thickness and cut with round cutter.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Let raise until about double in size.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
In skillet, brown beef and cook sausage, onion and oregano until done.
Stir to separate meat.
Pour off fat.
Add soups and water and mix.
Set aside.
Cook noodles as directed and drain. In separate containers refrigerate meat mixture and noodles overnight.
Combine meat mixture and noodles and pour in 2 qt. shallow baking dish (12 x 8 x 2) and cover.
Place in cold oven. Bake at 400 degrees for 40 minutes.
Stir.
Top with cheese and bake until cheese melts.
Wash dried limas and cover with water.
Add salt and onion powder to taste.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and let set for 1 hour.
Add sausages and bring to a boil again.
Lower heat and simmer covered for 1 to 2 hours until beans are tender, stirring only once or twice.
Frequent stirring causes beans to loose shape and turn to mush.
Brown onion and beef in shortening in skillet.
Add tomatoes, ketchup, steak sauce, pepper and parsley.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Cook macaroni.
Mix macaroni with beef in baking dish.
Season to taste. Gently spoon soup into mixture.
Mix lightly and sprinkle grated cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Into a large mixing bowl of an electric mixer, place egg whites and syrup.
Start beating on low speed; then increase to high speed.
Add vanilla.
When mixture holds a peak, spread on cake.
Melt butter and saute onion until soft.
Add spices and broth; bring to a boil.
Add pumpkin and return to boil.
Lower heat and slowly add cream.
Do not boil.
When thoroughly heated, add brandy.
Adjust seasoning.
Pour into pumpkin to serve.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Melt oleo in 2-quart oblong casserole in 350° oven.
Remove from oven.
Stir in curry powder and ginger.
Place 6 chicken pieces (thick side down) in pan.
Season with salt and pepper. Top with onion, apple and raisins.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Turn chicken and cook, uncovered, until tender.
Remove from pan.
Add rice to sauce in pan.
Put chicken on top of rice. Makes 6 servings.
Place chicken in one layer in a 9 x 12-inch greased pan, skin side down.
Season with salt and pepper.
In a separate bowl, mix tomato, seasonings and oil.
With a spoon, spread 1/2 the tomato mixture over chicken.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 30 minutes. Turn chicken pieces over, salt and pepper and spread on remaining tomato mixture.
Continue baking, uncovered, for 45 minutes.
Beat eggs.
Add other ingredients and mix.
Follow instructions for your ice cream freezer.
Sprinkle steak with meat tenderizer and let sit 1 hour.
Cut steak into single portion pieces and dredge each in flour.
Brown on both sides in oil.
Season meat with seasoned salt and pepper as it cooks.
Remove meat and drain on paper towel.
Put soups and milk into frying pan and mix with crusties from meat.
Stir well. Grease a 3-quart casserole and layer meat, potatoes and gravy, ending with gravy.
Bake, covered, at 300° for 3 to 4 hours.
Cook chicken and dice.
Cut tortillas in 1-inch squares.
Mix liquids, onion and SALA together.
Butter a large, shallow baking dish.
Add juice to bottom of dish, then a layer of tortillas and a layer of chicken.
Make 2 or 3 layers, ending with the liquid on top.
Cover with cheese and let stand 24 hours in refrigerator. Bake at 300 degrees for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Brown and drain hamburger meat.
Add all ingredients to drained kidney beans.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Let simmer for 1 hour and 30 minutes after bringing it to a slow boil, stir occasionally.
Serves many!
You may freeze servings of your choice.
Mix crumbs, oleo and 1/2 cup powdered sugar.
Press into bottom of cake pan.
Mix cream cheese, 1 cup powdered sugar and Cool Whip.
Place over crumbs.
Top with pie filling.
Heat sauce and jam until jam melts.
Stir in sesame seed. Remove from heat.
Season chops with salt and pepper.
Bake pie shell for 10 minutes at 400°.
In butter saute onion, mushrooms and broccoli until soft.
Spoon into pie shell. Sprinkle cheese over vegetables.
Beat eggs in small bowl until frothy.
Stir milk into eggs and pour over vegetables and cheese. Top with bacon.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes, then lower to 350° and bake an additional 20 minutes.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes.
Cook green beans as directed.
Mix together cream of mushroom soup, egg, sour cream and mayonnaise and mix with green beans. Put grated cheese over top, bread cubes over cheese and Parmesan cheese over bread cubes.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Cook ground beef in the melted butter.
Drain.
Stir in soup mix, beans, ketchup, water, mustard and vinegar.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Top with Cheddar cheese.
Serve with bread sticks.

recipes.t: Red, White And Blue Jello Mold
d: In four separate bowls, dissolve each package of gelatin in 1 cup of boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup cold water to each and stir. Pour one bowl of blue gelatin into an oiled or sprayed fluted tube pan.
Chill until almost set, about 30 minutes.
Thaw pastry sheets for 15 minutes.
Separate sheets.
Slice cheeses in approximately one-inch thick slices horizontally. Alternate cheese slices on thawed pastry sheet (making a long block of cheese), first Monterey Jack and then cream cheese slices.

Marinate chicken in Italian dressing. In separate bowl, mix dry ingredients. Dip chicken in mixture, covering each completely. Place on baking sheet. Pour remaining dry ingredients on top. Bake at 350° to 375° for approximately 40 minutes.
Season duck cavity and outside of bird with salt and pepper. To your favorite bread stuffing, add 1 cup oysters, drained and chopped.
Use oyster liquor as a part of liquid to moisten stuffing.
Lightly stuff duck; put the remainder of the stuffing in a pan to bake with duck (baste with duck drippings).
Place duck on a rack in a roasting pan; cover and bake in a slow oven (325°) about 2 1/2 hours.
Remove cover to brown.
Baste often with mixture of butter, lemon juice, paprika and thyme.
Peel and slice tomatoes (submerge in boiling water for 1 minute, then peel).
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and basil.
Add garlic to oil; drizzle half of oil over tomatoes.
Sprinkle sparingly with 1 to 2 teaspoons of vinegar.
Rinse mushrooms; do not remove stems.
Slice lengthwise.
Arrange over tomatoes. Season with salt, pepper and remainder of oil.
Sprinkle with remainder of vinegar.
Cover with plastic wrap and chill well. Garnish with black olives.
Serves 10.
Great for a cookout!
Simmer first seven ingredients.
Strain out cloves.
Add sugar. While mixture is still quite hot, pour over jello.
Add gelatin. Put in beets.
Mold in ring mold or individual molds.
Garnish with lettuce, cheese balls (small), artichoke hearts, etc.
Mix Ricotta, milk, eggs, salt, pepper and some tomato sauce together.
Cook shells and drain; put in pan.
Add cheese mixture. Mix together.
Cover with sauce.
Sprinkle with extra grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cook Brussels sprouts.
Drain off liquid.
Mix Italian dressing, pimentos and mushrooms together and heat.
Pour over cooked Brussels sprouts.
Fry bacon until crisp and crumble on top of Brussels sprouts.
Can be served warm or cold.
Melt margarine.
Add to mixture consisting of:
warm milk, egg yolks and flour.
Mix together and divide dough in 6 portions. Chill for at least 3 hours.
Soften yeast cake in water.
Pour hot milk over sugar, shortening (melted) and cool to lukewarm.
Beat in 1 cup of the flour to make a stiff dough.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups candied fruits, reserving remainder to decorate cake ring.
Over low heat, melt margarine.
Add cocoa, milk, Karo and sugar.
Mix well.
Let come to rolling boil and boil for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.
Add vanilla.
Beat until right consistency to spread.
Cream butter and set aside.
Grind dates.
Blend with eggs and vanilla to make a paste.
Stir in dates and butter into batter. Add flour, milk powder, oats, raisins, chips, sunflower seeds and pecans.
Mix and drop by spoonfuls 1/2-inch apart on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° in regular oven for 10 to 15 minutes or conventional oven for 7 1/2 minutes to 10 minutes, until peak begins to brown.
Makes 5 dozen.
Clean and cut up into bite-size pieces the cauliflower. Microwave.
In skillet, melt 1/2 stick margarine.
Stir in 3 heaping tablespoonfuls flour.
Add liquified cream cheese (adding milk with mixture).
Add garlic salt and pepper to taste.
Keep adding milk to gravy consistency.
Cook until thick.
Pour over cooked cauliflower.
Cook vegetables in salted, boiling water until barely tender. Drain.
Add onion, tuna, salt, pepper, soup and milk.
Heat to boiling.
Mix beef, seasonings, eggs and cornflakes together thoroughly. Divide into 16 portions.
Wrap a portion around a green stick (thumb size) that has been peeled about 3 inches on the end.
Make meat long and thin (not in a ball); be sure there are no air spaces.
(Watch out for big pieces of cornflakes.)
Cook slowly over coals, turning frequently so all sides are evenly cooked. Twist slightly to remove from stick and serve in a roll.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine liverwurst spread, 1 tablespoon sour cream, lemon juice and crumbled onions.
Unroll dough and cut into 4 rectangles.
Cut each rectangle into 6 equal pieces, then roll each piece into a ball.
Place 1 ball of dough in each of 24 gem-size (1 1/2-inch) ungreased muffin cups.
Press dough to evenly cover bottom and sides of muffin cups.
Fill each with 1 generous teaspoonful of liverwurst mixture, keeping level with edge of dough.
Top each with 1 teaspoon of sour cream and bake until crust is golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Combine broth, water, rice, celery and carrots.
Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes or until vegetables and rice are tender. Add remaining ingredients.
Stir until process cheese spread is melted.
Makes 5 (1 cup) servings.
Cooking time:
30 minutes.
Cook
onions
in
margarine.
Boil
rice in water for 5 minutes.
Drain. Mix well with onions, cheese and cream.
Bake in greased casserole at 300° for 1 hour.
Serves approximately 8.
Combine lime juice, steak sauce, salsa, oil, garlic and pepper in small saucepan.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cool.
Place steak in a plastic bag or marinating container; add cooled marinade, turning to coat.
Close bag or container and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight. Remove steak from marinade and discard marinade.
Place steak on medium heat grill.
Grill steak 12 to 14 minutes for rare to medium, turning once.
Cook macaroni; drain.
Meanwhile, cook bacon in oil until crisp.
Add wine.
Cook and stir until it has evaporated.
After draining macaroni, return to hot saucepan.
Mix remaining ingredients, including hot bacon fat.
Because this mixture will attach itself to the macaroni and be cooked by the heat of the pot and macaroni.
If eggs are not thoroughly cooked, stir over low heat for an additional minute.
Cut cabbage into pieces; boil until tender and drain.
Fry bacon in large skillet until crisp; drain and set aside.
Pour bacon grease into container (keep).
Wipe pan with cloth or paper towel.
Pour 2 or 3 tablespoons grease back into pan and add 1/3 of bread crumbs.
Turn crumbs until toasted; repeat with the rest of crumbs.
Mix cream cheese with powdered sugar until desired sweetness. Add a few drops of lemon extract.
Chill.
Remove core from strawberries.
Place cream in plastic bag.
Cut off corner and squeeze to pipe cream in strawberries.
Chill until ready to serve.
In a small bowl, combine yogurt and orange juice concentrate. Place fruit in individual dessert bowls.
Drizzle each serving with yogurt sauce.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Yields 6 servings.
Cut raisins and figs into small pieces.
Cream shortening with honey until fluffy.
Add beaten egg; sift dry ingredients with
milk;
add
nuts
and fruits.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Makes 1 loaf.
Mix milk and pudding together.
Add cream cheese and powdered sugar until smooth.
Crumble just enough Oreos to cover the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour in mixture.
Crumble rest of Oreos and top with whipped cream.
I have even saved enough of the Oreos and sprinkled them on top of whipped cream.
Mix lemonade, milk and salt together.
Fold in Cool Whip. Put in vanilla wafer pie crust.
Top with pecans.
Refrigerate 6 to 8 hours before serving.
Combine ketchup, cream cheese, lemon juice, dill, lemon peel and garlic powder.
Cover and chill to blend flavors.
Spoon small amount of dressing on each zucchini slice.
Top with shrimp. Garnish with fresh dill, if desired.
Cream shortening, margarine and 8 ounces of the cream cheese. Add the 3 cups sugar and beat until fluffy.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, and beat well after each egg.
Add 4 teaspoons of the lemon flavoring.
Fold in flour.
Reserve 1/4 cup.
Combine 1/4 flour with grated cheese and add to batter.
Pour mixture into greased and floured tube pan.
Place pan in cold oven.
Bake at 275° for 1 1/2 hours.
Do not open oven door while cake is cooking.
Remove from oven and cool.
While cake is cooking, combine the powdered sugar, remaining cream cheese and flavoring.
Use enough evaporated milk to make icing of spreading consistency.
Beat well.
Frost cake when completely cooled.
About
hours
before
serving, or a day ahead:
In a large bowl, combine salt, yeast, 2 cups whole-wheat flour and 1 cup flour.
In a 2-quart saucepan over low heat, heat water, honey and
butter until very warm (120° to 130°).
(Butter or margarine does not need to melt completely.) With mixer at low speed, gradually
beat liquid into dry ingredients just until blended. Increase
speed to medium; beat 2 minutes, occasionally scraping bowl with rubber spatula.
Gradually beat in egg and
1 cup whole-wheat flour to make a thick batter;
continue beating
2 minutes, scraping bowl often.
With a wooden spoon, stir in oats, 1 cup whole
wheat flour and 1 cup flour to make a soft dough.
Slice biscuits twice.
(Save center slice for top of pie.) Arrange bottom layer of biscuits into dish and cover with apple mixture.
Add next layer of biscuits and apple mixture.
Put third layer of biscuits and top with apple mixture.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Spread half the cranberries in the bottom of a well greased 10-inch pie plate.
Spread the nuts over the cranberries.
Add the sugar to the eggs, beating well.
Beat in the flour, butter and shortening.
Pour over the cranberries and nuts.
Top off with remaining cranberries.
Bake about 1 hour or until crust is golden brown.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread evenly and make a thin layer of graham crackers across bottom of pan.
Add coconut, nuts, chocolate chips and butterscotch chips.
Pour milk evenly over everything.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes, or until chips start to melt.
Cool and cut into squares.
Mix 1 cup warm water and yeast.
Mix 1 cup sugar, instant potatoes and 1 cup warm water together.
Add first mixture to second mixture, then add 1/2 cup oil.
Mix dry ingredients and add to yeast mixture.
Work together.
Pour 4 to 5 Tbsp. oil into big bowl.
Pour dough into bowl; form into ball coated with the oil. Cover with towel overnight.
The next morning, punch down dough. Knead on flour surface; cut out rolls and put on greased baking sheet (spray sheet with Pam cooking spray).
Put oil on top of rolls.
Allow to rise at least 4 hours.
Cover with paper towel or regular towel while rising.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Makes about 40 rolls.
Heat milk, fat, sugar and salt; cool to lukewarm.
Sprinkle yeast over warm water in a large mixing bowl; stir until dissolved. Add milk mixture, egg, chives, parsley and oregano.
Stir in 2 cups flour, beating until smooth.
Add enough additional flour to make a stiff dough.
Turn dough onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease dough completely.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in bulk, about 1 to 1 1/4 hours.
Heat olive oil and butter (approximately 1 1/2 teaspoons each is plenty).
Add shrimp and saute briefly.
Add shallots, cognac and flambe.
Add tomatoes, peas, wine and spinach leaves and reduce heat to low for a few minutes.
Sprinkle on raspberry vinegar. Season with salt, pepper and cayenne.
Serve over saffron rice or spaghetti.
Combine 1 1/3 cups of sugar, flour and salt in saucepan. Gradually add water and lemon juice.
Cook over medium heat until thick, stirring constantly.
Stir a small amount of hot mixture into beaten egg yolks.
Stir mixture back into hot mixture.
Cook, stirring for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add food coloring, lemon rind and butter.
Cook rice according to directions on package.
Spray skillet with Pam cooking spray or heat 3 tablespoons cooking oil in skillet on medium heat.
Sprinkle chicken strips heavily with fajita seasoning and fry in the skillet until lightly browned. Place onion on top of chicken fingers and put a lid on the skillet.
When onion is tender (not soft), remove lid and turn over chicken fingers.
Place tomatoes on top.
Replace the lid on the skillet until tomatoes are slightly soft.
The fajita seasoning sometimes makes the chicken appear blackened.
This is okay.
Place rice on plates and put chicken, onion and tomatoes on top.
Cook cavetelli in 4 qts. boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Set aside.
Place oil and garlic in large frying pan. Saute until golden brown,
Remove garlic and discard. Add tomato and basil sauce and beans. Saute until hot.
Add the cooked cavetelli.
Stir and let simmer 2-3 mins.
Top with cheese and fresh basil.
Prepare stuffing according to package.
Lay steak flat and spread stuffing on top.
Combine cheeses and sprinkle on top of stuffing.
Top with mushrooms.
The night before making vegetable bar, mix together the first 4 ingredients and place in refrigerator until ready to make the bar.
Place crescent rolls onto a cookie sheet and press together with edges up.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Let cool. Spread the cheese mixture on cooled rolls and layer with next 6 ingredients.
Sprinkle top with shredded cheese.
In a large salad bowl, combine lettuce, apples, oranges, tuna and nuts.
Toss together.
Boil noodles and drain.
Beat eggs, Ricotta cheese and parsley.
Cook and crumble hamburger; drain off grease.
Cook peas.
Mix eggs and Ricotta cheese mixture into noodles and add 2/3 spaghetti sauce.
Add Mozzarella cheese, cooked peas and cooked hamburger.
Put into a large casserole dish; top with remainder of sauce, Parmesan cheese and olives.
Cover.
Bake for 1/2 hour at 350°.
Combine syrup, sugar and cream.
Cook until "clicks" in cold water.
Mix corn flakes, coconut and nuts and pour syrup mixture over.
Spread in buttered dish.
Cool and break into pieces.
Cut eggs in half lengthwise; remove yolks.
Mash.
Stir in ham, celery, mayonnaise, salt, garlic salt and pepper.
Stuff whites with mixture.
Chill.
Yields 24 appetizers.
Melt butter over medium heat and season with the garlic cloves.
Place onion rings in bottom of pan.
Season both sides of fish with garlic salt, onion salt, paprika and pepper.
Place fish into pan on top of onion; pour butter over fish and onion.
(Cover approximately 1/2 fish fillets with butter).
Baste with butter. Broil 15 to 18 minutes.
After about 5 minutes of cooking, baste approximately every 2 to 3 minutes.
Check fish by using fork and see if fish flakes apart easily.
If desired, sprinkle Parmesan cheese over fillets.
Bake fish on rack in middle of oven.
Heat oven to 350°.
Use sheet cake pan.
Mix 1/2 cup of boiling water with chocolate until chocolate melts.
Mix flour, salt and baking soda.
Beat margarine and sugar until smooth; add one egg yolk at a time and beat.
Stir in chocolate mixture with vanilla; add flour mixture, alternately with buttermilk, beating after addition until smooth.
Beat egg whites until they form a stiff peak.
Gently stir in egg whites into batter.
Pour batter into pans and bake about 30 minutes or until done.
Boil a saucepan full of water and add ziti.
Cook until soft. Heat large skillet with 1/2 pound butter until burnt.
Add ziti, salt, pepper, garlic, parsley and grated cheese.
Mix well and serve.
Preparation time:
30 minutes.
Cooking time: 30 minutes.
Mix cream or milk, sugar, shortening, eggs, and salt.
Next, beat in flour, cocoa, vanilla, and nuts.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes. Spread marshmallow cream evenly over top and bake another 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Melt
morsels
over
hot water.
Stir in sweetened condensed milk
and
vanilla.
Add
chopped pecans and mix well. Chill until firm.
Roll
into a log and place on waxed paper. Brush with beaten
egg white and press pecan halves into log. Keep refrigerated.
Saute garlic and basil in olive oil in large saucepan until golden.
Add tomatoes; season to taste with salt and pepper. Cook, breaking up tomatoes with a fork.
Soak bread in water to cover; squeeze dry.
Add bread, broth and half the cheese to tomato mixture; bring to a boil.
Simmer slowly 1 hour or until most of liquid is absorbed.
Add butter and remaining cheese.
Soup should thicken to consistency of porridge.
Put evaporated milk in freezer overnight or for several hours. Make jello, using pineapple juice with water equal to 2 cups. Chill until firm.
Make whipped cream using evaporated milk, lemon juice, drained pineapple and sugar.
When jello is firm, fold in cream mixture.
Crush vanilla wafers and cover bottom of large cake pan.
Pour mixture over crumbs.
Garnish with a few crumbs.
Put whipping cream and marshmallows in a bowl in the fridge overnight.
Beat the next day until thick, then add fruit.
Cover it and refrigerate.
Season hot sweet potatoes with butter, cinnamon and nutmeg. Add cornflakes and sugar.
Shape into 8 balls; roll in chopped pecans.
Chill at least 30 minutes.
Arrange on pineapple slices in buttered baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Combine butter, honey and water in small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring frequently until boiling.
Boil 1 minute.
Spoon over potato balls.
Bake 5 minutes longer.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine butter, sugar, vanilla and salt; cook over high heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon till butter is melted. Continue 5 to 7 minutes longer or until candy is the color of almonds.
Arrange almonds in a single layer in a 12-inch by 7-inch pan, and pour candy mixture over almonds.
When cool, melt chocolate pieces; dip pieces of candy into the chocolate allowing excess to drip off, then dip into the ground walnuts.
Cut zucchini into halves, lengthwise.
Scoop out seeds.
Line 8 x 11-inch baking pan with aluminum foil.
Place into zucchini halves pinch of seasoned salt, layer of sour cream and layer of grated Cheddar cheese on top.
Sprinkle paprika.
Place zucchini slices, side by side, in pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes (until cheese melts).
Separate the sliced onions into rings and put into greased crock-pot.
Sprinkle onions with salt and pepper and half the crushed crackers.
Add cream and dot with butter.
Sprinkle remaining crushed crackers over top.
Top with cheese slices. Cover and cook on high 1 hour, then low 2 to 4 hours.
Mix margarine, milk, cocoa and sugar in saucepan and bring to a boil.
Boil for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Add remaining ingredients. Stir and drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Brown and crumble hamburger.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Prepare macaroni and cheese according to box directions.
Stir in hamburger and shredded cheese.
Melt together chocolate and butter. Add salt and cool. Add egg, flavoring and sugar.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Mix in nuts.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups or enough to cover sides and top of 10-inch tube cake.

Combine sweet potatoes, orange juice and sugar. Blend well. Shape into 12 sweet potato balls. Insert 1 large marshmallow inside each ball. Roll the sweet potato balls in chopped pecans. Place on a cookie sheet and heat in a 350° oven 15 to 20 minutes or until heated through.
Saut celery, onion and green pepper in butter.
Cook celery and onion down until all celery juice has evaporated.
Cook wild rice in chicken broth.
Add cooked white rice.
Mix all ingredients and put in a casserole dish.
Be generous with almonds on top. Bake in 325° oven about an hour.
Pare, core and cut apples into small wedges.
Melt margarine. Add brown sugar in saucepan over low heat.
Remove saucepan from heat.
Stir in apples; coat with brown sugar and margarine mixture.
Add water and nutmeg.
Cook apples over medium-high heat to boiling.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer on low for about 20 minutes, or until apples are tender.
Serve warm or cold.
Brown 1/4-inch thick cutlets in hot butter over medium heat. Set aside.
Add green onions and garlic to skillet.
Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Add broth and lemon-pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Add cutlets.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 15 minutes or until cutlets are tender.
Stir occasionally. Add broccoli and water chestnuts. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove cutlets and vegetables to platter.
Keep warm.
In a cup, stir together cornstarch and water. Stir into juices in skillet.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Allow to cook about 1 minute.
Pour over cutlets and vegetables.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Spread pineapple into bottom of pan.
Pour cherry filling evenly over pineapple.
Sprinkle cake mix over fruit.
Sprinkle walnuts and coconut next.
Cut margarine into slices and cover top.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Place lettuce in 9 x 13-inch dish.
Sprinkle next 3 ingredients in layers on top of lettuce.
Break peas apart and sprinkle on top while frozen.
Spread mayonnaise on top of peas and sprinkle with sugar.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Before serving, add layers of bacon, eggs and tomatoes.
Sprinkle generously with cheese.
Do not toss.
Cut into squares.
Fold pistachio pudding into the whipped cream.
Add cherries, pineapple and marshmallows.
Chill and serve.
Heat milk. Add salt, brown sugar and eggs.
Stir vigorously. Add vanilla and
remaining sugar. Butter sides and bottom of glass baking dish or casserole.
Put cubed bread in dish.
Pour milk mixture over bread and level off.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

Cream shortening and sugar. Add lemon juice and rind. Beat well. Add sifted dry ingredients. Mix well. Stir in nut meats. Shape in rolls. Wrap in waxed paper and chill thoroughly. Slice very thin. Bake on greased cookie sheet in oven (350°) for 12 to 15 minutes.
Pour 3 cups of sugar over pumpkin and let stand, covered, overnight.
The next day, add remaining sugar and bring to boil in a heavy kettle.
Reduce heat and simmer 1 1/4 hours.
Add lemon slices and ginger.
Simmer 1 hour more.
Pack into hot, sterilized jars, leaving 1/2-inch space at top.
Wipe any spills from jar rims and immediately pour 1/8-inch hot paraffin on preserves.
Yield: 8 half-pint jelly glasses.
Add water if needed.
Over medium heat, saute vegetables until cooked.
Peel and devein shrimp.
Cut in pieces.
Mix with vegetables until shrimp are pink.
Add soups.
Add Old Bay and pepper.
Let simmer 5 minutes.
Add wine.
Serve over rice or grits.
Serves 10.
Drain tuna.
Add softened cream cheese, onion, lemon juice and horseradish.
Mix well.
Roll into ball and cover with nuts. Serve with crackers.
Mix flour, salt, paprika, garlic powder and pepper in a large plastic bag; set aside.
Pour evaporated milk in bowl.
Dip chicken pieces in evaporated milk.
Add a few pieces chicken to bag.
Shake to coat.
Remove chicken from
bag.
Repeat with remaining chicken.
Heat Crisco oil in a large skillet.
Add chicken; brown over medium-high heat.
Cook over moderate heat about 25 minutes or until meat near bone is no longer pink and juices run clear, turning pieces over frequently.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a 6- to 8-quart Dutch oven brown meat on both sides in hot oil.
Drain off excess fat.
In a small bowl stir together Marsala wine, 1/3 cup water, basil, garlic salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper; pour over meat.
Cover and bake for 2 hours.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking soda and salt.
Add eggs and undrained fruit cocktail and mix well.
Turn batter into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour or until wooden pick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.
Cool 10 to 15 minutes and remove from pan and place on wire rack.
Place butter, sugar, milk and egg yolk in heavy saucepan.
Bring to boil and cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add vanilla to taste, coconut and nuts, mixing well.
Cool icing slightly and spread on top of warm cake.
Makes 16 servings.
Mix honey and lemon juice; pour over fruit. Cover and chill until serving time. Serves 6 to 8.
Saute ground beef, onion and celery in melted butter until meat is well browned.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Bring to boil; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Yield:
2 quarts.
First Cooking Pan:
Melt 1/4 stick margarine.
Mix raw eggs with salt, pepper and milk.
Scramble eggs until done.
Set this pan to the side.
Put beef in 2 quarts warm water and stir well to separate beef.
Salt to taste.
Boil on medium heat until beef is well done.
Add potatoes, onion, carrots and peas.
Stir occasionally to keep beef separated.
Add tomato paste and simmer 15 minutes. Serve with toasted cheese sandwiches, cheese toast, cornbread or crackers.
Place cut up chicken in cake pan (9 x 13-inch).
Salt and pepper.
Place cheese over all.
Mix soups and pour over chicken, then sprinkle with rice.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 3 hours or until chicken is done.
Sprinkle hot skillet with salt and brown meat.
Stir in flour. Cook for a few minutes.
Add undiluted onion soup and cook for a few minutes more.
Serve on dollar size egg bun.
Mix salt, pepper and flour together and coat beef cubes with this mixture.
Brown the beef cubes in a small amount of oil.
Add beef bouillon cubes and 2 teaspoons onion flakes and cook for 1 1/2 hours.
Check seasoning to taste after 1/2 hour.
Add flour, if necessary to thicken gravy.
Add Kitchen Bouquet.
Cook egg noodles as directed on package and drain.
Add butter and mix through noodles. Top noodles with meat and gravy.
Melt margarine in
large saucepan.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Pour
in
rice
and
beef consomme.
Add more water, if needed, to cook rice.
When rice is done, add shrimp and continue to cook until shrimp are pink.
Salt and pepper to taste.
I use boned chicken breasts and cook in the stick of oleo in a skillet.
Mix the other ingredients and add to chicken and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Remove from oven and add 1/2 cup chow mein noodles on top.
Water chestnuts are optional but they give the casserole a nice "crunch." Serves 10 to 12.
In large bowl mix graham cracker crumbs, cinnamon and sugar; mix by hand.
Melt butter; pour butter over mixture.
Mix until moistened.
Spread over sides and bottom of 13 x 9-inch oblong cake pan.
Bake crust at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Beat instant pudding with milk until smooth.
Add soft cream cheese to pudding mixture.
Beat 1 1/2 minutes.
Pour mixture over crust.
Spread blueberry pie filling over pudding mixture.
Spread whipped cream over top of blueberries.
Refrigerate 2 hours.
Cook broccoli. Combine eggs, soup, water and mayonnaise. Place layer of broccoli in 2-quart casserole.
Add layer of cheese.
Pour a small amount of soup mixture on top. Repeat layers until all are used. Toss stuffing mix with margarine.
Put on top of casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Beat egg yolks well.
Add water, sugar, baking powder, salt and flour.
Beat egg whites stiff.
Add cream of tartar to egg whites.
Fold into batter and pour in angel food pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a saucepan, mix the first 5 ingredients and heat until margarine is melted.
Remove from heat.
Separate eggs; set aside the whites in a grease-free bowl.
Maintain them at room temperature.
Slowly add 8 tablespoons of heated liquid to the egg yolks.
Stir constantly.
Pour yolks into remainder of heated mixture.
Dissolve cornstarch in the 1/2 cup of water.
Then add to the milk and egg mixture.
Over medium heat, bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Cover with Saran Wrap and refrigerate until cool.

Mix first 4 ingredients and place in baking dish. Place oleo in chunks on top. The salt and pepper should be stirred in first. Bake in a 350° oven, uncovered, 1/2 hour and covered for 1/2 hour longer.
Use a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Mix eggs, molasses, milk and spices together.
In a pan of self-rising flour, work in shortening, then add combined ingredients.
Roll out thin and cut with pie pan.
Makes 14 to 16 layers.
Cook at 400° until brown.
Mix margarine and crumbs.
Put in bottom of 7 x 11-inch pan. In blender, put in hot water and gelatin.
Process at low speed until smooth.
Add cheese one cup at a time.
Process until smooth.
Pour in large bowl of mixer.
Add Cool Whip and mix until smooth (low speed).
Pour over graham crust.
Chill until set (about 1 hour).
Top with filling.
Ready in 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Sift together first 4 ingredients and set aside.
Put water, margarine, oil and cocoa in sauce pan and mix well.
Bring to a boil;
pour over dry ingredients, mix well and set aside.
Mix buttermilk, eggs and vanilla.
Gradually add to the chocolate mixture.
Pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13 ijnch pan.
Bake at 350 degrees until done Test with a toothpick for doneness. Frost while warm.
Cool and cut into squares.
Fry ground beef with onions.
Cook beef, onions, bouillon and celery with soups and hot water.
Wash rice in cold water and dry. Add to other ingredients.
Rice is uncooked.
Bake about 1 hour in 350° oven.
Brown beef and sausage.
Don't drain grease.
Dice vegetables and saute with meat.
Turn often.
Serve when potatoes are done. Season to taste.
Can add Tabasco when cooked.
Serves 8 to 10. Grated cheese on top and eggs on side go great with this.
Use 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Mix graham cracker crumbs with sugar and butter until well mixed.
Line bottom of pan with graham cracker mixture.
Save about 1/2 cup for topping.
Sprinkle walnut pieces over crackers as desired.
Save a few for top.
Mix Dream Whip as directed on package (mix in large bowl).
Soak beans overnight.
Drain and rinse.
Cover with water and boil until when you blow on the beans the skins come off.
Add soda.
Let bubble; drain and rinse.
Put in baking dish.
Add other ingredients.
Cover top with bacon.
Bake at 400° until it boils.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Finish baking 2 more hours at 300°.
Heat butter in pan and saute mushrooms until light brown. Strain out mushrooms and set aside.
Heat cooking liquid; add flour and cook until thick.
Gradually stir in broth until blended.
Add onion, bay, basil, salt and pepper.
Cook until thickened.
Turn down heat and add half and half.
Cook on low for 15 minutes.
Strain.
Add mushrooms to broth.
Heat and serve.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Cut in butter and add 1 egg.
Mix well.
Pat mixture into 9 x 12-inch cake pan which has been well greased.
Press into this 1 cup chopped nuts.
Beat together the egg whites, brown sugar and vanilla.
