Pour this mixture over the nuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cut into small squares before cool.
These improve with age.
Cream sugar and butter until fluffy.
Add eggs, fruit and nuts and stir.
Add soda dissolved in buttermilk.
Sift dry ingredients and blend into batter.
(This is stiff so you'll have to mix with hands.)
Chill until real stiff.
Rol lout into small logs about the size of your finger.
Chill again, then cut and place on sheet, cut side up and bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool and store in airtight container.
Combine peanut butter and margarine, stirring until smooth. Stir in corn syrup.
Mix well.
Use on rice cakes, toast or waffles.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, molasses and salt mixing well.
Add flour, raisins and pecans.
Beat shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, dry ingredients, milk and raisins.
Add vanilla.
Drop by teaspoon; press down with floured fork.
Bake for about 10 minutes at 350°.
Saute onions in butter until tender; remove from heat.
Add sour cream and 1/2 cup of cheese; set aside.
Stir together cornmeal, sugar and dill weed.
Mix flour, soda and shortening together.

Take out 1 cup of mixture to put on top of cake. Combine all other ingredients to remaining flour mixture and mix well. Put batter in prepared pan and sprinkle top of cake with the 1 cup of flour mixture.
Bake at 350° until done when tested.
Heat oven to 200°.
Place cereal and peanuts in large bowl. Set aside.
In 1-cup glass measuring cup or small microwavable bowl, combine peanut butter and honey.
Microwave at High 30 seconds.
Stir until smooth.
Stir in water and vanilla.
Mix well. Pour over cereal.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Combine first three ingredients.
Toss with salad dressing and mustard.
Add more salad dressing, if desired.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce.
Serves 10.
Mix popcorn, peanuts and coconut.
In heavy saucepan, combine sugar, syrup and water.
Cook and stir until sugar dissolves, then cook at 270°, soft crack stage.
Remove from heat; add butter and vanilla.
Pour mixture over popcorn, stirring well.
Press into buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Immediately cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Melt chocolate and shortening together.
Drizzle over top of squares.
Put into a 3-quart saucepan 2/3 cup Pet milk (1 small can), 2 cups miniature (or cut up) marshmallows and the undiluted frozen orange juice.
Stir over medium heat until marshmallows melt; take off heat.
Stir in the 3/4 cup nut meats, 1 cup mixed candied fruit and 1/4 cup candied cherries.
Stir in well a mixture of 4 cups finely crushed graham cracker crumbs, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and 1 teaspoon cloves.
Press firmly into a loaf pan (or pans) lined with wax paper.
Cover tightly.
Chill 2 days.
Brown meat.
Add potato, water, tomato sauce, dry soup mix, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Simmer until done (about 10 to 15 minutes).
Serves 4 to 6.
Make a little or a lot; depends on amount needed. Add onion, mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar to taste.
Cook broccoli in salted water until almost done.
Drain and arrange in buttered baking dish about 11 1/2 x 7 1/2-inches. Place
cooked
chicken on top of broccoli. Combine soup, milk, lemon
juice, curry powder and mayo.
Mix well and pour over chicken.
Sprinkle cheese over all.
Combine bread crumbs with butter and sprinkle over top.
Cook in preheated oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Grind the chicken through a meat grinder or chop very fine. Combine with softened bread (squeezed dry), butter, salt and pepper and beat until smooth.
Shape into oval patties and roll in bread crumbs.
Fry 5 minutes on each side.
Drain all canned fruits and cherries of all juice.
Add apricot pie filling and sliced bananas.
Stir well.
Chill.
(Bananas will not turn brown.)
In saucepan, combine water, cornmeal and salt; bring to boil. Cook and stir until thickened.
Remove from heat.
Stir a moderate amount of the hot mixture into 1 beaten egg.
Return to hot mixture.
Stir together the flour, baking powder and pepper.
Add to the cornmeal mixture; beat well.
Stir in the corn.
Drop batter by rounded tablespoons into boiling stew mixture.
Cover; simmer until dumplings are done, 10 to 12 minutes.
Put liver and 1/4 cup salt in pot.
Cover with water and soak for 5 to 10 minutes to remove blood.
Drain and rinse 2 or 3 times.
Place liver in cooking pot.
Cover with water.
Add olive oil, garlic powder and thyme.
Bring to boil and boil for 20 minutes.
Remove from pot and drain.
Freeze or store in refrigerator until needed.
Melt margarine in a pan.
Add leeks and stew for 5 minutes. Add hot water and bring to a boil.
Stir in macaroni and cook 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper.
Just before serving, sprinkle some grated cheese over soup.
Mix sugar and hot water, stirring until dissolved.
Let cool. Add orange juice, lemonade and apricot juice.
Freeze.
To serve, spoon the desired amount of this slush into your glass filled with 7-Up and enjoy.
This can be kept in your freezer and used to make individual servings of punch.
Brown meat in skillet. Pour just enough spaghetti sauce to cover the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Add the rest to the browned meat with the water to heat on low.
Spread 1 layer of uncooked noodles with Ricotta. Add a layer of grated Mozzarella and then a layer of meat sauce.
Repeat until you have filled the baking dish.
Finish with a layer of noodles and a light covering of sauce.
Cover tightly with aluminum foil. Bake in a 400° oven for 1 hour.
Let set, uncovered, for 10 minutes before serving.
In cup dissolve baking soda in water.
In bowl mix flour, salt and spices.
In another bowl blend butter, sugar and eggs.
Add dissolved baking soda.
Blend thoroughly with flour mixture.
Add raisins and nuts.
Using a teaspoon, form individual cookies on greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Yields 5 1/2 dozen.
Cut cake into 2-inch strips.
Cut each strip into 4 equal pieces.
Cut each piece into 2 triangles.
Combine corn syrup, water and butter in saucepan; bring to a boil.
Heat until butter melts.
Remove from heat.
Stir in chocolate chips until they melt.
Cool to room temperature.
Place each cake triangle onto 2 prong frying fork.
Spoon cooled chocolate glaze over cakes until well covered.
Place on cooling rack to allow excess chocolate to drip from cake.
Combine all ingredients except lemon slices in large punch bowl; stir until concentrate is dissolved.
Add ice cubes and lemon slices.
Makes about 2 1/4 quarts or enough for 18 (4 ounce) punch cup servings.
Cream sugar and margarine.
Add yogurt and Egg Beaters. Combine flour, soda, baking powder and salt; set aside.
Combine orange juice concentrate, water and orange rind.
Gradually add dry ingredients to creamed mixture and orange juice mixture.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoons onto slightly oiled baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Quickly remove from baking sheet.
When cool, frost.
Shred cabbage and set aside.
In a frying pan, brown ground beef and drain off fat.
Add onion, celery, tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Food processor method:
Place flour, sugar, salt and baking soda in bowl.
Process 3 seconds.
Stir yeast with 1/2 teaspoon sugar and 1 tablespoon of water to a smooth mixture and let proof. Melt butter and let cool.
Put the eggs, butter and buttermilk on top of dry ingredients.
Process a few seconds.
Add proofed yeast. Process 30 seconds.
Combine rice, butter, 1 egg, 1 tablespoon onion and 1/4 tsp. marjoram.
Press onto bottom and sides of lightly buttered 10-inch pie plate or 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle tuna evenly over rice shell.
Combine remaining ingredients; pour over tuna.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Serves 6.
Mix well the vanilla wafers, peanuts and margarine and press into the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cream together first 3 ingredients.
Put in a low dish.
Layer next 5 ingredients.
Top with Mozzarella cheese.
Serve with corn chips or potato chips.
Cut orange into 7 to 8 pieces and remove seeds.
Combine orange pieces and juice in blender.
Puree.
Add dates, egg and butter to blender, blend and then pour into mixing bowl.
Measure dry ingredients into separate bowl and mix well.
Pour dry ingredients into orange mixture and stir gently to combine.
Fill muffin tins (greased or filled with paper liners) and bake at 400° for about 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Eye Of Round Pot Roast(Makes 4 Servings)
d: In heavy casserole with lid, brown roast in oil with garlic; add onion.
Pour in wine or broth.
Stir coffee powder into liquid.
Cover and roast at 325° for 1 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
Remove meat onto heated platter and keep warm.
Lift onions on top of meat and strain remaining juices.
Heat to boiling.
Simmer until juice are reduced to about 1/3 of the original volume, whisking all the time.
Add salt to taste.
Whisk in mustard, then margarine, one piece at a time.
Do not let sauce stand without whisking or it may separate.
Remove from heat; spoon sauce over meat.
Cut into 1/2 slices to serve.
Cut bell peppers into thin strips and pack into pint jars. In each jar, add one red pepper, 1 clove garlic and 1 teaspoon dill seed.
Combine salt, vinegar and water. Bring to a boil and pour over peppers.
Seal.
Let stand a few weeks before serving.
Wash, dry and rub potatoes with vegetable oil.
Bake at 425° for 40 to 60 minutes.
When potatoes are close to done, cook broccoli in water until still slightly crunchy.
Do not drain. Mix in sour cream and cheese and heat thoroughly, but do not boil. Cut potatoes in half (lengthwise) without cutting all the way through.
Open potatoes and fluff inside with a fork.
Spoon broccoli mixture over each potato and serve immediately.

recipes.t: Turkey Appetizers(Good Way To Use Leftover Turkey)
d: Combine first 4 ingredients; cut in butter with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Sprinkle milk (1 tablespoon at a time) evenly over surface; stir with a fork until dry ingredients are moistened.
Stir in turkey, cheese and green pepper.

recipes.t: Corned Beef And Cabbage With Vegetables
d: Melt butter in a large pan. Cut cabbage into large pieces. Place in pan. Add carrots, onion and potatoes. Add salt and pepper.
Break corned beef on top.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours on low heat.
Beat egg, mustard and water in shallow pan.
Combine meal, flour and cheese in another dish.
Dip fillets first in egg mixture, then meal mixture.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes on each side. Salt and pepper.
In large skillet, simmer oil, garlic and anchovies, stirring gently.
Remove from heat when garlic is golden and set aside. Add beets with its juice, parsley, chopped escarole, salt and pepper.
Let all ingredients marinate while cooking spaghettini.
Mix
cheese,
mayonnaise
and
seasonings.
Add
onion, almonds and bacon. Spread on slices of crustless bread, which has been cut into quarters.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Chop onions and peppers and saute in large skillet.
Add peas and tomato juice;
simmer 15 minutes.
Dilute each can of soup with a can of water.
Add rice.
Saute onion in 2 tablespoons of butter.
Add to soup mixture.
Slice sausages and add to mixture; bring to a boil.
Cover and reduce heat.
Simmer for 20 minutes or until rice is tender.
Cover entire round of bread with cream cheese.
Spread hummus over 3/4 of the cream cheese, leaving about 4 inches at one end with cream cheese only.
Cover hummus with fresh spinach leaves. Continue to layer ingredients and roll bread into jelly roll. Chill for one hour.
Cut roll on bias and serve.
This should be served the same day it is made.
Cream margarine and Crisco for 10 minutes.
Add sugar and cream.
Add eggs one at a time.
Add flour alternately with milk. Add flavoring.
Fold in nuts and coconut.
Bake in large tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 25 minutes.
To mayonnaise, add prepared mustard, dry mustard, vinegar, garlic salt, curry powder, grated onion and horseradish.
Mix all ingredients and chill.
Combine all ingredients in order given in very large bowl. (I beat with mixer, sugars, oil and eggs.)
Mix soda, baking powder, salt and flour in separate bowl, then add to first mixture; mix well.
Add oatmeal, coconut and corn flakes; mix well.
Add chips.
Drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Yields 14 dozen.
Pick over cranberries; wash. Add raisins.
Peel oranges; remove seeds.
Combine fruits and chop.
Add sugar, salt and water; cook until thick, about 30 minutes, stir often.
Pour into hot sterile jars; store in cool place.
Boil peas, water, celery and bouillon cubes together for 4 or 5 minutes.
Make a paste of the cornstarch and 1/2 cup of water. Add to hot vegetable mixture.
Cook until thickened.
Just before serving, add sliced water chestnuts and slivered almonds to suit taste.
Serves 6 to 8.
Dee-licious!
Heat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in a 15 x 10 x 1-inch pan. Sprinkle and pat dry cake mix over butter.
Sprinkle marshmallows, chocolate chips and cereal.
Drizzle milk over top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
While warm, run knife around edge.
Cool 2 hours.
Makes 48 bars.
Cut 1 and 1/2 pounds of fish into 2-inch strips.
Cover with sherry and let stand for 30 minutes.
Cut remaining fish in pieces, put in kettle with water to cover.
Add thyme, cloves, salt and pepper.
Simmer 30 minutes and cook vegetables in the fish broth until tender.
Melt butter in frying pan and brown onion in it.
Add chopped green pepper, tomatoes, sugar and salt.
Cook until green pepper is tender. Make the sausage into small balls and roll in the uncooked rice. Place in greased baking casserole and pour the tomato mixture over sausage balls.
Cover baking dish and bake for 1 1/2 hours in a 350° oven.
Heat oven to 350°.
Blend flour, oleo and 1 cup of nuts. Crush in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan, forming a crust.
Bake crust for 20 minutes.
Mix the cream cheese with sugar.
Blend in 1 cup of Cool Whip.
Spread on top of crust.
Mix package of pudding with milk.
Spread on top of cheese mixture.
Top with more Cool Whip.
Sprinkle the top with nuts and shaved chocolate.
Freeze before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9-inch pie pan.
Mix together gingersnap crumbs, melted butter and sugar.
Press into bottom and up sides of prepared pan.
Bake crust until slightly darkened, 9 minutes.
Melt butter in water in saucepan. Remove from heat. Stir in stuffing. Add remaining ingredients (except bacon).
Chill 1 hour. Roll or shape into balls.
Wrap bacon pieces around dressing balls.
Place on aluminum foil lined shallow baking pan with bacon touching foil.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes, turning once.
Yields 4 dozen.
Brown and degrease sausages.
Cut bread, cheese and sausage into bite-sized pieces.
(I grate the cheese.)
Layer in 2-quart casserole, bread, cheese and sausage.
Best if you repeat once. Pour butter over.
Beat eggs.
Add salt, mustard and milk.
Pour over casserole.
Refrigerate overnight, covered.
Bake 1 hour at 350° after it is at room temperature.
For double recipe, bake 1 hour and 45 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine milk, coconut, 3 tablespoons gelatin, almond flavoring and food coloring (to tint).
Form into small balls (about 1/2 tablespoon).
Sprinkle remaining gelatin into dish; roll each ball to coat.
Place on waxed paper.
Chill. Cloves can be stuck on balls.
Top 1 bread slice with cheese single, salsa, chicken and second bread slice.
Spread sandwich with margarine.
Cook in skillet on medium heat until lightly browned on both sides.
Makes 1 sandwich.
Cook grits in water according to package directions. Stir small amount of hot grits into eggs. Add egg mixture to remaining grits. Stir in margarine, cheese, garlic and salt.
Spoon mixture into a greased 2-quart dish. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Blend biscuit mix and 2 tablespoons sugar with raisins.
Add milk slowly, mixing lightly with a fork.
Roll out dough to 3/4-inch thick.
Cut with a 1-inch cookie cutter.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes at 425°, or until light brown.
Mix remaining sugar and cinnamon; blend in butter and cream.
Brush tops.
Place under broiler about 4 inches until bubbly and light brown.
Serve hot.
In bottom of large bowl, put one layer of grated apples with sugar to taste, then some ground walnuts.
Then spread Cool Whip over nuts.
Put one layer of crushed pineapple with sugar to taste.
Layer ground nuts, then Cool Whip.
Put one layer of raisins, ground nuts and Cool Whip.
Top with sliced bananas with sugar to taste.
Cut chicken into small bite sized pieces.
In skillet brown onion and garlic lightly in oil.
Add 1/4 to 1/2 can enchilada sauce to skillet.
Add chicken, olives and green chilies.
Let mixture simmer a few minutes.
In a 13 x 9-inch greased baking dish, layer one layer of tortillas that have been dipped in remaining enchilada sauce, a layer of meat mixture and a layer of cheese.
Repeat layering process until all ingredients have been used up.
(End with a layer of cheese.)
When all layers are finished, pour remaining green sauce over enchiladas.
Bake covered in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Ole!!
Grease pan with unmelted margarine.
Mix popcorn, candy and nuts.
In saucepan, mix oil, melted margarine and marshmallows. Cook over low heat until marshmallows are melted.
Pour over popcorn mixture; mix well.
Press into pan.
Cover and chill.
Cut into squares when ready to serve.
Drain fruit cocktail.
Pare and dice apple.
Peel and slice bananas.
Mix fruit in bowl with marshmallows, coconut and walnut pieces.
Cook beef and onion in a large skillet until lightly browned. Add salt, water and tomatoes.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Wash and dry chicken.
Salt and pepper inside and outside and sprinkle with fine herbs.
Cut potatoes (scrubbed and unpeeled) into large pieces.
Coarsely chop onion.
Place chicken, back side down, into a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Arrange potato and onion around bird and sprinkle with salt, pepper and fines herbes. Drizzle lightly with olive oil.
Bake for 40 minutes at 400°.
Turn bird over (use large wooden spoon in cavity and flip).
Pour white wine over all (about 2 cups) and bake 40 to 45 minutes, basting now and then.
Oil a 9 X 13 pan and cover the bottom with cubed bread.
Fry the sausage, drain and sprinkle it over the bread.
Add the grated cheese and cut up mushrooms.
Combine the seasonings and milk with the slightly beaten eggs.
Pour over the bread and cheese mixture and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine chocolate chips and half and half in medium bowl. Microwave on Medium-high (70%) until chips are melted, 1 to 3 minutes, stirring once.
Stir in vanilla and remaining ingredients until coated.
Press into a greased 8 x 8-inch square dish. Chill.
Boil
macaroni until
tender, drain. Brown
meat
in skillet, pour off
fat,
add
onions,
green pepper and sauce. Simmer about 5
minutes.
Add
1/3 macaroni in casserole dish. Add 1/3 sauce, 1/3 of both cheeses, continue in layers ending with cheese on top.
Bake
in
oven at 350° until cheese melts and mixture bubbles.
Mix ingredients (except for extra sugar) together, adding chocolate chips last because dough will be stiff.
Spread onto a greased cookie sheet (12 x 24-inch).
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Cut into bars.
Turn bars onto side and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon; bake at 350° for an additional 10 minutes.
Turn bars on other side and repeat process.
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon and bake another 10 minutes.
Makes about 7 dozen cookies. Goes great with a cup of coffee.
In skillet, melt margarine.
Add scallions and ham; saute for 1 minute.
Add kidney beans and rice.
Season with salt, pepper and hot sauce to taste.
Toss until heated through.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Place breast, skin side up, in roaster. Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Lower oven to 325°.
Combine 1 1/2 cups cider and soy sauce.
Pour over turkey breast.
Cover and bake 1 1/2 to 2 hours, basting frequently, with the cider mixture.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Set aside.
Cream together shortening and the sugars.
Add 1 beaten egg, the vanilla, then add dry ingredients.
Add the can of pineapple with juice and stir in the butterscotch chips.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Break or chop the chocolate into medium size pieces.
Place it in the top of a small double boiler over hot water on low heat. Cover and let stand until partially melted.
Uncover and stir until completely melted.
Remove the top of the double boiler temporarily.
Add the butter, a few pieces at a time and stir with a small wire whisk after each addition until smooth.
Brown ground beef with chili powder and garlic.
Pour off excess drippings.
Stir in soups; gradually stir in water.
Add corn.
Heat, stirring now and then.
Mix together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut in shortening.
Add milk to make soft dough.
Add a little more milk, if necessary.
Turn out onto floured board; knead gently for 2 minutes.
Roll out 1/4-inch thick and brush with melted butter. Cover with apples; sprinkle with brown sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg. Roll up like jelly roll; form into semi-circle on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 425° for 35 to 40 minutes.
While warm, frost with icing made of confectioners sugar, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and a few drops of hot water.
Mix vinegar, oil, salt, pepper and chip of garlic.
Chill overnight.
Break lettuce.
Add 1/2 jar parsley.
Pour vinegar mixture over lettuce and mix well.
Beat cream cheese.
Add egg and sugar; mix.
Add chocolate chips; stir and set aside.
In Dutch oven, brown beef in oil; drain fat.
Add stewed tomatoes, bell pepper, taco spices and seasonings and cornmeal. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 20 minutes. Add kidney beans.
In a 10-inch pie plate, unfold one crust and fill with chili mixture and 1/4 cup cheese.
Top with remaining crust and flute edges.
Bake, uncovered, in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over crust, return to oven and bake 10 minutes longer.
Makes 6 servings.
Take the pieces of chicken; sprinkle Lawry's salt and pepper on each one.
Arrange chicken in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Mix the 3 cans of soup together; then pour over chicken.
Cook in oven for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Cook with pan, covered.
Mix onions, taco seasoning and peppers with meat and divide into 8 patties.
Cook until done.
Top with cheese, sour cream and salsa.
May serve open-faced on Texas toast or on hamburger buns.
Heat oil.
Add onion, green pepper, meat and rice.
Stir over high heat until slightly brown.
Add rest of ingredients and mix well.
Bring to boil.
Cover tightly and simmer for 25 minutes.
Butter baking dish.
Set oven for 350°.
Drain juice from pineapple.
Mix sugar, flour and just enough juice to make sugar and flour into a paste.
Add pineapple to mixture.
Melt margarine and add crushed crackers.
Pour over pineapple mixture and bake about 30 minutes.
Put the spices, sugar and orange peel in a small pan and pour over the rum.
There should be enough to cover them.
Heat gently, shaking pan until the sugar has melted.
Pour in the hot coffee. Strain and serve.

Combine Crisco, salt, lemon rind and nutmeg. Add sugar and cream well. Add beaten eggs and milk, mixing well. Sift flour with baking powder and soda. Add to creamed mixture. Mix well. Drop by teaspoons on greased cookie sheet. Flatten cookies by stamping with bottom of flat glass dipped in water. Sprinkle cookies with sugar. Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes. Makes 4 to 6 dozen cookies.
Melt butter in large pot.
Add onion and garlic.
Cook about 5 minutes (do not brown).
Add leeks; cook 5 minutes more.
Add potatoes; add flour.
Add seasoning and hot beef broth.
Bring to boil and simmer until done.
Add chopped chives and parsley when serving.
Makes 8 servings.
Brown chops on both sides.
Place into shallow baking dish. (Sometimes I do mine in electric skillet.)
Lightly mix together bread cubes, onion, butter, 1/4 cup water and poultry seasoning. Place a mound of stuffing on each chop.
Blend soup and 1/3 cup water.
Pour over chops.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour or until tender.
Makes 4 servings.
Meanwhile, wash and drain blueberries.
Combine blueberries, water, sugar and cornstarch.
Boil until clear, stirring constantly.
Add butter and mix until smooth.
Cool slightly. Pour over baked mixture.
Allow to cool.
Refrigerate.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Set aside to cool. Mix the cream cheese with pineapple juice, then add remaining ingredients.
Pour into mold.
Chill until set.
After set, pour a little warm water over mold to empty.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt margarine and pour into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle graham cracker crumbs over margarine.
Mix together and press evenly into pan.
Sprinkle chips evenly over crumbs; then nuts and coconut.
Pour Eagle Brand milk over all. Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Cut potatoes lengthwise into 6 spears.
In a large bowl, combine mayonnaise, seasoned salt, pepper and hot pepper sauce. Add potatoes, coating each well. Spray a cookie sheet with nonstick coating.
Place all the potato spears on the cookie sheet, cut side up.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes or until golden brown and potatoes are slightly blistered.
Brown ground turkey and dry onions in a large pan.
Add mashed beans, catsup, chili powder and hot sauce and heat.
Add chopped onion and cheese and heat until cheese is melted.
Serve with tortilla or nacho chips.
Wash and tear lettuce, making a bed on the bottom of the tray. Layer the tomatoes in.
Next, add the peppers and beans. Top them with the onion slices and cover them with the shredded cheese. Top with dressing.
For a finishing touch, just before serving add the crushed Doritos.
Combine 2/3 caramels and both packages cream cheese in a mixer or food processor.
Mix until well blended, pour into decorative bowl.
Dribble remaining caramels on top and sprinkle with chopped peanuts.
Serve with apples.
A little lemon juice on the apples will prevent browning.
Combine mayonnaise, honey, sour cream and white pepper in a large bowl; mix well.
Add chicken, green onions, celery, raisins and almonds.
Toss gently to coat chicken well.
Chill well before serving.
Makes 12 servings.
Score the surface of the loin with a knife.
Mix the salt, pepper, sage and garlic; rub the surface with the spice mixture. Stand the loin on end.
Using a large 10-inch knife, skewer the roast lengthwise.
Remove the knife and begin stuffing prunes into the slot.
Pack the prunes in as tightly as possible.
When you can't stuff any more into the roast, secure both ends of the opening with toothpicks.
Place the pork in a pan, add about 1/2 cup water and cover with foil.
Put in a 375° oven and roast for about 1 hour and 45 minutes or until the internal temperature is over 180°.
Remove from oven and let stand for 15 minutes before carving.
Fry sausage slowly until brown; drain and put in 8-inch cake pan or casserole dish.
Fry apples and onions in sausage fat. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat.
Brown flour in remaining fat with apples and onions.
Add seasonings and stock and stir until thickened.
Pour over sausage.
Mix lightly with fork.
Top with mashed potatoes.
Bake at 350° in oven until potatoes are brown. Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spray a cookie sheet with nonstick oil spray.
Arrange eggplant on cookie sheet and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over eggplant.
Layer one slice of tomato on each eggplant round.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes. Makes 3 to 4 servings.
Beat cream cheese until creamy.
Melt chips in double boiler. Mix with cream cheese.
Stir in nuts.
Chill and shape into balls. Roll in nuts.
May serve with butter cookies or other cookies of choice.
Shape meat into small patties, adding a few green chilies to each.
Cook to medium done in a large frying pan coated with a smidgen of oil.
Add stewed tomatoes and heat.
Put a slice of cheese on each patty and cover so the cheese melts a little.
Have mackerel split and cleaned and have heads and tails removed, if desired.
Rinse fish with cold water and dry well. Saute onions lightly in 1 tablespoon olive oil for about 5 minutes.
Coat flat baking dish with oil and arrange fish in one layer so it will cook evenly.
Cover fish with onions, remaining oil, herbs, seasoning and lemon juice.
Top with olives.
Cover dish with double layer of foil.
Bake in a 375° oven for about 1/2 hour or until fish flakes.
Serve with plain boiled potatoes. Makes 4 servings.
Put soup in boiler
undiluted; add
gelatine and bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Put cream cheese and soup mix in blender (better to do half portions
at a time) and blend. Put all in big bowl and
add
cooked shrimp, onion and celery. Fold together and put in mold.
Mix cream of celery soup, mayonnaise, milk, cheese, turkey, and peas.
Cook noodles and fold in the above ingredients.
Bake at 350°, covered, for 20 to 30 minutes.
Sift
flour,
soda,
salt and cinnamon together.
Place eggs and
sugar in
mixer
bowl.
Beat at medium speed until mixed. Beat in
oil, a small amount at a time.
Stir in flour mixture, carrots, pineapple, vanilla and peanuts.
Pour batter in two greased loaf pans. Makes 2 small loaves.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes.
Mix sugar, oil, eggs and plums.
Sift flour, cinnamon and cloves.
Add the two mixtures together; then add vanilla, raisins, nuts and coconut.
Bake in a well-greased pan at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Beat sugar and butter together; add egg yolk.
Mix flour and baking powder and spices.
Alternate mashed potato and flour mixture and milk in with butter, sugar and egg mixture.
Add nuts and vanilla.
Last, fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake in two 9-inch layer pans at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Rinse, drain and dry raisins.
Chop or grind chop walnuts. Beat eggs until foamy and gradually beat in sugar and vanilla. Sift flour, baking powder, salt and spices into first mixture. Blend in raisins, nuts and orange rind.
Spread in well-greased and floured 8-inch square pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes until lightly crusted on top.
Cut into squares while warm.
Cool; remove from pan.
Makes about 16 to 20 squares.
Brown chicken in butter and steak sauce.
Mix remaining ingredients (except fruits).
Pour over chicken; simmer 30 minutes.
Arrange in greased casserole with fruits.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes until well browned and glazed.
Serves 4.
Place stuffing mix on bottom of 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Add cooked rice over top of stuffing.
Next, layer cream of mushroom soup and sour cream, mixed together.
Then add layer of sliced mushrooms.
Brown hamburger well.
Add oregano, salt and pepper.
Add chili beans.
Start with handful of Fritos on your plate, then hamburger mixture, cheese, onion, green peppers, lettuce and tomato.
Pour taco sauce on top.
Saute onion in butter until soft.
Combine with ham in 8 x 10-inch greased casserole.
Mix beaten eggs and milk.
Add cheese and crackers to casserole, then milk and egg mixture.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.

Cut cabbage into 12 wedges. Heat water and salt to boiling in 10-inch skillet; add cabbage wedges. Heat to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer until cabbage is crisp-tender, 10 to 15 minutes; drain.
Sift together the flour and salt.
Cream the butter. Gradually add powdered sugar, creaming well.
Blend in eggs and extracts.
Add dry ingredients gradually.
Mix thoroughly.
Press through cookie press onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with colored sugar or sprinkles before baking.
Bake at 400° for 6 to 8 minutes.
Combine flour, teff, baking powder, baking soda and cinnamon. In a separate dish combine egg, milk, honey, oil and lemon juice. Combine dry and liquid ingredients.
Add lemon rind and vanilla. Stir vigorously until smooth.
Pour into lightly oiled muffin tins.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Beat cream cheese and 1 tablespoon milk until smooth.
Stir in lemon peel and juice.
Stir in 1 package Sweet 'N Low.
Fold in 1/2 of yogurt.
Spread evenly in bottom of crust.
Press strawberries into cream cheese layer, saving several for garnish.
To make dumpling gravy, cook chicken, bone and dice it.
Save broth and add water to make 2 quarts.
In a large kettle, place broth.
Add coloring and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Make a thickening by mixing well melted oleo to flour.
Add to boiling broth.
Slowly add diced chicken and stir.
Ready for dumplings.
Combine flour, sugar, oats and cinnamon, cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Arrange yams and cranberries in a 10 x 6-inch baking dish; sprinkle with crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with marshmallows and broil until lightly brown.
First - In a small pot, cook fresh (or approximately 2 cups frozen blueberries), syrup, spices and cornstarch over medium to medium high heat until thickened.
Set aside.
Trim excess fat from chicken.
Cut chicken into 4 x 1-inch strips.
Combine egg and milk, stirring well.
Combine breadcrumbs and next 5 ingredients; stir well.
Dip chicken strips in egg mixture; dredge in breadcrumb mixture.
Saute onion, bell peppers, celery, garlic, and butter. Add shrimp and tomatoes. Cook for 30 minutes, serve over rice.
In a large bowl, combine buttermilk, sugar and salt.
Soften gelatin in cold water.
Dissolve in hot water.
Add to buttermilk mixture.
Mix well.
Mix in pineapple and lemon juice.
Pour into ice cream machine and freeze according to directions.
If using freezer method, pour into pans or undivided ice cube trays.
Cover and place in freezer.
When mixture reaches mushy stage, transfer to bowl and beat with mixer to minimize ice crystals forming. Return to trays, cover and freeze until frozen.
Makes 1 1/2 quarts.
Beat eggs with all other ingredients.
Pour in a casserole dish and place in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Grate cheese and place on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

With mixer, beat cream cheese, lemon juice and condensed milk. Use a large bowl for mixing ingredients. Beat until smooth. Drain pineapple chunks. Mix in Cool Whip and nuts. Mix all the ingredients well. Chill in the refrigerator a few hours before serving.
In a 2 to 3 quart saucepan, combine brown sugar, 2 1/2 cups blackberries and salt over medium heat until berries make sufficient juice, then cook over high heat when mixture comes to full boil.
Have cornstarch
dissolved in 1/2 cup water; add to boiling berries, stirring constantly.
Cook until thick.
Remove from heat; stir in margarine and lemon juice.
Cool slightly; fold in 2 cups berries.
Pour evenly into pie crust.
Sprinkle remaining fresh berries over top, pressing in lightly.
When served, top with whipped cream.
Cut
steak
across
grain.
Set aside. Place mushrooms and next 4 ingredients in 2 quart casserole.
Cover dish with wax paper.
Microwave
on
High 3 1/2 to 4 1/2 minutes.
Stir once. Drain
well.
Stir in meat.
Cover.
Microwave 3 1/2 to 4
1/2 minutes.
Stir twice.
Meat will be pink.
Blend cornstarch
into soy sauce. Combine with gravy and ginger. Stir in
meat mixture.
Cover;
microwave on High, 4 to 6 minutes. Serve over rice or noodles.
Mix lemon Jell-O, lime Jell-O, hot water, pineapple and lemon juice, if desired, in large bowl. In another bowl, mix cottage cheese, milk, salad dressing and nutmeats (optional). Combine and chill.
Cut pound cake into 1/2-inch cubes.
Arrange in a 2-quart bowl.
Prepare pudding mix according to package directions; pour over pound cake.
Spoon blueberry pie filling over the pudding, then spread whipped topping over the blueberry pie filling. Chill.
If you wish, you may top with toasted almonds.
Mix sugar, lard, oatmeal and flour well.
Add water and soda and add to mixture.
Add 1/2 cup milk.
Spread 3/4 mixture in pan. Boil dates or raisins with 1 tablespoon sugar.
Top with salted peanuts and remaining dough.
Bake at 350° until done (35 to 50 minutes).
Preheat oven to 350°.
Roll pastry to 13-inch circle on lightly floured surface.
Place in 10-inch pie plate or casserole dish.
Turn under edge; flute.
Sprinkle cheese, crab or Sea Legs, onion, flour and seasonings in pie plate or dish.
Beat together eggs and half and half.
Pour over cheese mixture.
Bake 55 or 60 minutes or until set.
Yields 6 servings.
Spray baking rack and place on a baking sheet. Combine corn flake crumbs and cheese. Cut chicken into finger size pieces. Dip into milk, then roll in crumbs, coating completely.
Place on rack.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 12 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Scrub potatoes; arrange on a baking sheet and bake 45 minutes until tender; remove from oven.
While potatoes cook, in a small bowl, combine the ham, mushrooms, bacon, cream cheese and 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese.
Let potatoes cool 15 minutes or until you can handle them.
Slice 1/4 off the top of potato; scoop out a few teaspoons of flesh.
Fill cavity of each potato with the cream cheese mixture; sprinkle tops of potatoes with remaining Cheddar cheese.
Put back in oven to warm, approximately 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve with dollops of sour cream. Makes 10 to 15 servings.
In a large skillet, place 2 tablespoons oil. Season strips of steak and cook in oil until browned.
Cover steak with bell peppers and onions.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring as needed. Add the tomatoes and Ro-Tel tomatoes.
Let mixture simmer for another 30 minutes.
With pastry blender, cut butter into flour until mixture is like coarse meal.
Mix in sugar, ground almonds, egg yolk and almond extract.
Blend to a stiff paste, using hands if necessary. Press half of the mixture in a 9-inch square pan.
Spread with jam.
Roll out remaining dough (chill first if necessary) to a 9-inch square.
Arrange carefully and evenly over the jam. Sprinkle with chopped almonds.
Bake in 350° oven for 15 minutes. While still warm and in pan, cut into fingers.
Makes 27.
In a heavy saucepan, add brown sugar and butter.
Boil 1 minute.
Top dough mixture with chopped pecans.
Pour mixture over pecans.
Put chocolate chip pieces over top.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 18 minutes.
In large bowl, combine oats, coconut, almonds, sunflower seeds and wheat germ.
Combine honey and oil; stir into oat mixture. Spread in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Cook oat mixture at High for 10 minutes, stirring 3 times.
Stir in fruits.
Remove to another pan to cool.
Stir occasionally during cooling to prevent lumping.
Store in tightly covered jars or plastic bags.
Makes 6 cups.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add molasses.
Beat until creamy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add milk and vanilla to creamed mixture.
Cut chicken into chunks.
In frying pan, combine sesame seed and oil; cook until golden.
Cool.
Stir in soy sauce, sugar, ginger, pepper, garlic and 1/2 the green onions.
Mix in chicken. Cover and chill 1 to 4 hours (I have chilled overnight).
Pour meat and marinade onto cookie sheet in a single layer.
Broil until golden; stir often.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Boil chicken in broth with onion and celery for 30 minutes. Remove chicken.
Put vegetables in broth; simmer 20 minutes.
Dice chicken; add soup and peas.
Drain vegetables.
Add to mixture. Pour in crust (only liquid is soup).
Invert other crust and place on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook hamburger and onion.
Drain grease.
Add eggs, tomato paste, ketchup or barbecue sauce, milk and seasoning to taste. Press down crescent rolls into a pie pan.
Put hamburger mixture into the pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for at least 30 minutes.
Put cheese topping on
for the last 15 minutes.

Combine ground beef, sausage and onion in a Dutch oven. Cook until beef is browned, stirring to crumble; drain. Drain pinto beans. Add liquid to Dutch oven. Stir in remaining ingredients except beans. Cover and simmer 45 minutes. Stir in beans. Cook an additional 15 minutes. Yields about 3 quarts.
Sprinkle onion with sugar, juice of a lemon and herring liquid.
Mix in the drained herring and sour cream.
Let stand overnight.
Heat oven to 400°.
Trim fat from chops.
Sprinkle both sides generously with pepper, seasoned salt and garlic powder.
Place on large piece of heavy-duty foil.
Put squash on top of chops.
Fill hollows with brown sugar, honey and oleo.
Put mushrooms on top of chops.
Wrap tightly in foil.
Put on baking sheet and bake about an hour or until tender.
Serves 2.
Grease a baking pan (8 x 8 x 2-inch) or a 2-quart baking dish. Preheat oven to 350°.
Measure the oats, flour, salt, cinnamon and brown sugar into a bowl.
Remember to pack the brown sugar. Measure the margarine.
Cut it into the dry ingredients until it is like small peas.
Adjust the oven racks so that the pan is in the center of the oven.
Peel and slice the apples.
Arrange in the baking pan or dish.
Spread the oatmeal mixture on top of the apples.
Press lightly.
Bake 30 minutes until topping is light brown and the apples are tender.
Serve warm with milk or ice cream.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add marshmallows and cream cheese and stir until slightly melted.
Add oranges and pineapple with syrup.
Chill until partially set.
Then fold in Cool Whip until small, then pour in mold or dish.
Refrigerate until set.

recipes.t: Sippin' Cider Salad(In Honor Of "Washpa Eagle")
d: Bring juice or cider to a boil.
Pour over jello to dissolve. Drain cherries, cut in halves, and save juice.
Measure cherry juice and add water to make 1 1/2 cups.
Stir into gelatin.
Set aside 2 cups of gelatin.
Keep at room temperature.
Chill remaining gelatin until partly set.
Fold in cherries, celery and nuts.
Pour into mold or 8 x 8-inch dish.
Chill until firm.
Microwave bacon (5 strips) approximately 4 1/2 minutes. Microwave egg 1 minute and 15 seconds in a cup covered with paper towel.
Place egg on toasted English muffin, top with cheese (Cheddar and Swiss).
Microwave for 45 seconds or until cheese is melted.
Amounts depend on how many there are to serve.

recipes.t: Green Vegetables In Mustard Sauce(Makes 4 To 6 Servings)
d: Cook zucchini and shallots in butter in large heavy skillet until tender.
Stir in green beans, marjoram, thyme, salt and pepper.
Heat, stirring occasionally, until hot through.
Combine sour cream, mustard and flour; stir into vegetables.
Heat and stir until hot and thickened.
Serve garnished with tomato wedges.

recipes.t: Hash Brown Pie(Diabetic And Heart Healthy)
d: Press thawed hash browns between paper towels to remove excess moisture.
Press into bottom and up sides of ungreased 9-inch pie plate.
Drizzle with melted margarine.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Combine ham, cheese and green pepper; spoon over crust. Mix eggs, milk and pepper.
Pour over hash browns.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake for 20 to 30 minutes.
Allow to cool 10 minutes before cutting.
Serve with salsa.
Serves 6.
Cover bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch dish with hash browns. Brown onion and sausage; drain.
Spread over potatoes.
Cover with cheese.
Mix eggs and milk; season to taste.
Pour over mixture in dish.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° uncovered for 50 minutes.
Combine oil and sugar; mix well.
Sift together remaining dry ingredients.
Sift half of dry ingredients into sugar mixture; blend.
Sift in remaining dry ingredients alternately with eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Add carrots and mix well, then mix in pecans.
Makes 4 layers.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Frost with cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Saute onions and pepper, then put in hamburger and brown.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Place in preheated 425° oven and bake covered 1/2 hour and uncovered 1/2 hour.
Clean and wash turnip tops thoroughly (3 or 4 washes).
After last wash, take small bunches of leaves at a time and chop into small chunks.
Place leaves in a large pot with about 1/2 quart water and whichever seasoning you choose (bacon, etc.).
Add salt and cook at least 1 hour.
If your turnips have roots, wash, peel and cut into pieces.
Add to cooking turnip tops and cook until tops and roots are tender.
Add water as needed.
Start cooking on high and lower to medium high when they come to a boil.
If you don't add roots, cook greens until tender.
Follow same recipe for rutabaga tops and roots.
Combine Miracle Whip, salt, sugar and pepper.
Add vinegar and milk.
Whip with a wire whisk until sugar is dissolved.
This is enough dressing for 1/2 head cabbage.
In a large mixing bowl, gradually beat the sugar into the softened butter with an electric mixer, beating until mixture is well blended.
Beat in the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine the all-purpose flour and the salt. Gradually beat these dry ingredients into the butter mixture. Beat in the buttermilk until mixture is well blended.
Pour the egg and buttermilk filling into the pie crust.
Sprinkle the toasted pecans over the top of the filling in the pie crust.
Brown and drain hamburger.
In casserole dish, layer hamburger and onion soup mix, then frozen Tater Tots.
Mix soups and milk. Pour on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Top with cheese. Bake 15 minutes longer.
Sift flour, soda, nutmeg and salt together.
Cream shortening and gradually add sugar.
Cream until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add lemon extract. Combine vinegar and milk and add to creamed mixture alternately with dry ingredients.
Roll about 1/8-inch thick on floured board. Cut and place on cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 370° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen cookies.
Place frozen broccoli and water in a 2-quart casserole.
Cook, covered on High for 10 to 11 minutes or until tender.
Drain.
Stir to break up.
Stir in onions and soup.
Top with cracker crumbs. Cook on High 5 to 7 minutes or until heated through.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Cook on High 45 seconds to 1 1/2 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Dissolve lemon gelatin with 3/4 cup boiling water.
Cool slightly and beat until light and fluffy.
Fold in whipped topping and cottage cheese.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan; chill until firm.
Dissolve lime gelatin in 1 1/2 cups boiling water and pineapple juice.
Add pineapple, olives and chopped pecans.
Spoon carefully on top of first layer.
Refrigerate and chill overnight.
Combine gingerbread mix and applesauce.
Beat 2 minutes at medium speed with electric mixer or 2 minutes with spoon.
Stir in raisins and fruits and peels.
Spread in greased 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Prepare frosting according to package directions, substituting the lemon juice for half the liquid.
Spread on cooled cookies.
Cut in 1 x 1 1/2-inch bars.
Decorate with candlesticks made from gumdrops.
Makes about 8 dozen.
Grease and flour 9-inch baking pan.
Heat oven to 325°.
Melt butter in saucepan over low heat.
Remove from heat and add 1 cup chopped white chocolate.
Do not stir.
Set aside and let it stand.
Combine water and raisins and bring to a slow boil (approximately 20 minutes).
Add dates and cool.
Cream butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Add fruit and liquid.
Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Combine mixtures.
Do not overmix.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Drain juice from cherries.
Add enough water to make 2 cups of liquid.
Add cornstarch; cook until clear.
Remove from fire.
Add Jell-O, sugar, pineapple, cherries, food coloring, bananas and nuts.
Pour into baked pie shell and chill.
Serve with whipped topping.
Put spoonfuls of peanut butter in a bowl.
Put in 2 teaspoons of milk.
Beat together, putting milk in 1 teaspoon at a time. Beat each time until peanut butter is creamy.
Spread on bread. Sliced fruit such as strawberries or bananas can be added for extra special taste.
Also a jam or jelly spread would be nice for change of taste.
Mix lemonade, Kool-Aid and pineapple juice.
Add ginger ale and ice cream just before serving.
Serves 50.
Saute mushrooms, carrots and onion in corn oil.
Spread until lightly browned in Dutch oven over medium-high flame.
Stir in barley, salt, garlic salt, pepper, bay leaves, water and broth. Bring to a boil; reduce flame, cover and simmer 45 minutes or until barley is tender.
Stir in spinach and cook, covered, an additional 10 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.

About 2 1/2 hours before serving, in skillet over medium heat in hot butter, cook onion, garlic, 1 teaspoon salt, 3/4 teaspoon rosemary, 3/4 teaspoon thyme and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper until onion is tender.
Bring half and half, cream and sugar to boil, then remove from flame.
Let cool.
In bowl, lightly whisk yolks while slowly adding sugared creme.
Add Kahlua; remove any froth from the top.
Ladle mixture in ramekins and bake approximately 20 to 25 minutes at 325° in water bath, lightly covered with foil (they are ready when bounce to touch).
Refrigerate until completely cooled.
Cover top with coating of sugar and caramelize.
Serve immediately.
Serves 6 to 8.
Prepare cake mix as directed.
Pour into greased pan, brownie size.
Dot with pieces of margarine.
Pour water over the batter. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serve warm with whipped topping (optional).
Brown and drain ground beef; leave in skillet.
Add soup, ketchup, and mustard.
Mix well and simmer until well heated. Serve.
Can also make larger quantities and keep warm in a crock-pot.
Stir salad dressing mix and mayonnaise together with whip; fold in yogurt and mix well.
Chill.
Makes 1 1/2 cups of dressing, approximately 16 to 19 calories per tablespoon.
Mix together ingredients, except chicken. Marinate chicken several hours. Sprinkle generously with lemon pepper while barbecuing over low heat. Turn chicken often to prevent burning.
Drain over bowl: oranges, pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Use juice plus water to make 1 1/2 cups liquid.
Mix liquid and pudding mix.
Cook until thick.
Cool.
When cool, add fruit plus marshmallows and whipped cream.
Stir all together.
Refrigerate overnight.
Add bananas before serving.
Mix sour cream, cream cheese, Ranch dip, olives and onion. Cover burrito skin; roll up and chill.
Cut in one-inch pieces. Serve with taco sauce.
Can be made ahead and kept in refrigerator.
Mix flour, melted butter and 3/4 c. nuts.
Press into a 9 x 13 pan.
Cook 15 minutes at 300.
Cool.
Mix 8 oz. cream cheese (softened), sugar, and cool whip.
Spread over cooled flour crust. Mix pudding and milk, spread over cream cheese mixture.
Top with remaining nuts.
In a skillet, melt 1/4 cup butter. When hot, add 1 cup drained oysters. Watch out, they pop and spit a little. Turn until done (they will harden). Then dice. Add to prepared stuffing. Mix well.

Fry bacon crisp and set aside. Saut one medium chopped onion in bacon grease. Add 1 finely chopped tomato. Add diced jalapeno to mixture. Let simmer; add beaten eggs, stirring until eggs are done. Serve with tortillas and cheese. Great for camping!
Melt butter in saucepan; add apple pie filling and sugar. Continue heating, stirring occasionally, until sugar melts. Cool.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Mix raisins, currants, pecans, candied fruits and cherries with dry ingredients.
Combine apple mixture and dry ingredients.
Pour into foil-lined 9-inch tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 90 minutes or until done.
Cook broccoli and cauliflower according to package directions. Drain and put in a large casserole dish.
Steam bite size pieces of German sausage; add to broccoli and cauliflower.
Add carrots. Pour Cheez Whiz over top and warm in a 250° oven until Cheez Whiz is melted over all.
Stir and serve.
Put icing on the bottom of the peppermint patty and place on the flat side of a vanilla wafer.
Ice the flat side of the second vanilla wafer and sprinkle outer edge with green coconut.
Place on top of peppermint patty.
Using a new paint brush, dab with light Karo and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Combine and mix cream cheese, green chilies, green onions, garlic and salt. Spread a layer of cream cheese mixture on each tortilla. Roll up and slice into bite size pieces.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Brisket(Taste It, It'S Great!)
d: Place brisket on onions and garlic.
Mix other ingredients; pour over brisket.
Cover and roast in 350° oven until tender (approximately 4 hours).
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Thicken gravy with flour and water mixture.
Preheat the oven to 300°.
In a double boiler, melt the semi-sweet chocolate over hot, not simmering, water.
Set aside to cool to room temperature.
In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda and salt.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the brown and granulated sugars, then add the butter and beat until well combined.
Add the peanut butter; beat until smooth.
Add the eggs and vanilla; beat until just combined.
Add the flour mixture and the milk chocolate chips; beat until no streaks of flour are visible.
Pour in the melted chocolate; mix partially with a wooden spoon until marbled.
Drop the dough in 3 tablespoon mounds, 2 inches apart, on an ungreased baking sheet.
Top with 1 whole peanut.
Bake for 23 minutes, or until just set but still soft.
Cool on the cookie sheet for 30 seconds, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Season fish with salt and pepper and dip in flour.
Fry in oil until golden.
Add chopped onion and thin strips of pepper
and fry until soft.
Add skinned and chopped tomatoes.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Thicken with remaining flour and serve.
Wash chicken, pat dry and split chicken breasts in half.
Beat eggs with 1/2 cup milk.
Dip chicken into mix and then into bread crumbs, coating well.
Put breasts in well-buttered baking dish with a pat of butter under each one.
Sprinkle each breast with garlic and onion powders.
Cover well with Mozzarella, then salami, then pepper.
Combine remaining milk with rest of beaten milk and eggs.
Add 3/4 cup bread crumbs and Parmesan to create thick batter.
Mix well and pour over each breast.
Top each with a pat of butter.
Bake at 400° to 450° until golden brown (20 to 25 minutes).
Yields 4 servings.
Bake cake as directed on package.
Cool 20 minutes, then poke holes with handle of wooden spoon.
Drizzle milk on cake.
Now drizzle topping and refrigerate.
When cake is cool, spread on whipped topping, then sprinkle candy.
Keep refrigerated.
Remove stem ends from tomatoes.
Scoop out pulp and seeds.
To stuff each tomato, fill each with 1/4 cup frozen peas.
Dot with 1/4 oleo.
Sprinkle basil on each and top with cheese.
Place tomatoes in pie plate in circular form.
Microwave on medium 6-10 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Serves 4.
Sift flour before measuring.
Blend 1 cup flour and the butter to a smooth paste.
Spread this mixture in a 9 x 12-inch pan; bake in a 350° oven for 12 minutes.
Spread the baked dough with the following mixture:
combine beaten eggs, brown sugar, pecans 2 tablespoons flour, coconut (if desired), baking powder, salt and vanilla.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Stir lemon juice into confectioners sugar a little at a time, until spreading consistency, then ice cookies after they have cooled.
Cut into squares or bars.

recipes.t: Christiana Campbell'S Tavern Sweet Potato Muffins
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease muffin tins that are 1 1/2-inches in diameter.
Puree sweet potatoes in blender.
Cream butter and sugar.
Beat egg into the potatoes.
Sift flour with baking powder, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Add the dry ingredients alternating by hand with milk, chopped nuts and raisins, mixing just until blended.
Do not overmix.
Spoon into greased muffin tins, filling each tin completely full.
A little sugar and cinnamon may be sprinkled on top of each muffin.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes. Yields 2 1/2 dozen.
Dissolve strawberry and lemon gelatins in boiling water.
Add cold water, pineapple juice and ginger ale.
Refrigerate until partially set.
Stir in cranberry sauces, crushed pineapple, applesauce and walnut meats.
Pour into a 7 1/2 x 11-inch pan or 10-cup gelatin mold.
Allow to set until firm.
Pour pie filling evenly in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle cake mix evenly over pie filling (do not stir).
Put butter in rows over entire cake mix.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Enjoy!
*Semi-sweet chocolate may be substituted if you prefer the taste.
Melt margarine in a 2-quart pan over low heat.
Add chopped onions.
Saute 3 to 4 minutes over moderate heat.
Add next 3 ingredients.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered about 20 minutes; stir occasionally.
Cook rice according to package directions.
When sauce and rice are ready, poach eggs until all whites
are cooked but
yolks are soft.
In each of 2 small au gratin dishes, spoon 1/2 cup to 1 cup of rice. Add 1/2 cup to 1 cup of sauce to each.
Place 2 eggs in each dish. Top with shredded cheese.
Melt cheese, as in a small electric toaster oven
on broil, but do not cook eggs further.
Pass salsa for topping.
Yield 2 servings.
There will be excess sauce which will refrigerate.
In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar.
Add the egg and the remaining ingredients.
Drop by the spoonful onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in a 375° oven for 10 minutes.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in large skillet; blend in flour, salt and pepper cook until smooth and bubbly over low heat. Remove from heat add chicken broth and milk.
Return to heat, bring to boil, stirring constantly one minute or so.
Add remaining ingredients pour into 9 by 13 pan or two small casseroles.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serves 12.
May be doubled for serving 24.
Combine crumbs, walnuts, 2 tablespoons sugar and oleo; mix well.
Firmly press mixture into bottom and sides of an 8-inch spring-form pan.
Break candy into several pieces; melt in double boiler or microwave.
Set aside.
Beat cream cheese with electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Combine 3/4 cup sugar, cocoa and salt; gradually add to cream cheese, mixing well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add melted chocolate; beat until blended.
Stir in sour cream and vanilla, blending well.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes.
Turn off oven; let cheesecake stand in closed oven 30 minutes.
Let cool at room temperature, then chill.
Remove sides of spring-form pan; spread Sour Cream Topping and sprinkle with walnuts.
Yield:
1 (8-inch) cheesecake.
Arrange grapes and cucumber on lettuce in salad bowl.
Mix the next five ingredients.
Stir into yogurt and spoon over salad. Yields six servings.
Steam green beans 5 minutes.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam.
Place half the beans in pan.
Cover with half of the onion and garlic.
Place other half of beans on top and cover with rest of onions and garlic.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour wine and tomatoes on top of beans.
Sprinkle half the herbs on top. Wash and dry chicken.
Place skin side up on top of beans.
Spray chicken with Pam.
Sprinkle with chicken spice and the rest of the herbs.
Bake uncovered at 375° for about 1 hour and 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked.
Place raw hamburger in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Combine celery, onion, butter and water in pan and cook until celery is tender. Add croutons and toss until moistened.
Spread over hamburger.
Pour soup over mixture. Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Remove from oven and let set 15 minutes, cutting into squares.
Heat oven to 425°.
Lightly grease a cookie sheet.
Mix chicken, mushroom soup and 1 cup shredded cheese.
Mix baking mix and 1/2 cup cold water until soft dough forms.
Beat about 25 strokes and form dough into ball on floured surface.
Knead 5 to 10 times.
Roll dough into 14 x 11-inch rectangle and place on cookie sheet.
Spoon chicken mixture lengthwise down center of dough and fold sides over mixture.
Cut small slits in top and seal the ends together.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until light brown. Mix cream of chicken soup, milk and 1/2 cup cheese together and simmer.
Use as gravy over slices of chicken loaf.
Serves about 6 smaller portions or 4 "hungry man" portions.
Cook pie cherries, pineapple, sugar and flour, stirring continuously.
Remove from heat and add orange jello.
Chill.
Then add nuts, bananas and brandy flavoring.
Makes two pies.
Use regular pie crusts and top with Cool Whip.
Mix cheese and chili and beef.
Microwave 4 to 5 minutes, stirring once.
Serve with chips.

recipes.t: Kay Hill'S Best Brownies In The World
d: Combine caramels and 1/3 cup evaporated milk in a glass bowl. Cover with wax paper.
Microwave on Roast (Medium, 60%) for 3 minutes.
Stir.
Continue microwaving at the same speed for 2 or 3 more minutes or until melted.
Spray a 9-inch pan with nonstick cooking spray (Pam). Sprinkle coconut over bottom of pan.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice; sprinkle pineapple over coconut.
Set aside.
Put eggs and Sweet 'N Low in a blender and blend well.
Add milk to reserved pineapple juice and pour into blender.
Add baking mix and vanilla to ingredients in blender.
Blend at medium speed until well mixed.
Pour mixture over pineapple in pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes, or until a knife inserted into middle of the pie comes out clean.
You can microwave 22 minutes, but is not as brown as when done in the oven.
Add yeast to 1/2 cup water and stir until dissolved.
In a large bowl, dissolve sugar and salt in other 1 cup of water.
Add shortening and yeast.
Mix well.
Add flour and mix well.
Work through dough with a spoon at 10 minute intervals for 5 consecutive times.
In a small bowl, combine oat bran, whole wheat flour, salt and baking soda; set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs; stir in molasses.
Mix in olive oil, apple juice concentrate and skim milk.
Gradually add flour mixture using a wire whisk.
Mix ingredients just until moistened.
Stir in chopped apples and raisins.
Pour into paper-lined muffin pans.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until toothpick inserted into center comes out dry.
Place chicken and onion in a heavy saucepan. Sprinkle with salt. Chop tomato, chili peppers and ginger very fine.
Add to chicken.

Pour in water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for about 20 minutes or until chicken is barely tender. Add okra. Stir in tomato paste. Continue simmering until chicken and okra are tender. Serve over cooked rice.
Remove the stems
and
slice
the
mushrooms into thick slices.
In a skillet, saute the mushrooms in the butter until they are barely
tender.
Transfer them
to
a
well-buttered baking dish, arranging them
in
neat, overlapping rows.
In a saucepan, combine the sour cream and flour; salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer until heated,
but
do not let boil.
Spoon the sauce over the mushrooms and top with the cheeses and cayenne. Bake for 15 minutes.
Serves 4.
Cook chicken breasts in broth until tender, about 20 minutes. Remove breasts and set broth aside.
Bone and skin breasts.
Cut meat into 1/4-inch strips; set aside.
Saute onion and garlic in lard until onion is transparent.
Add tomato and cook, uncovered, stirring frequently, until mixture is somewhat dry, about 5 minutes.
Remove mixture from heat.
In food processor, puree chipotle chiles with 1/2 cup reserved chicken broth.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Divide chicken strips, radishes, green onions, garbanzo beans, avocados and cheese among 12 warmed soup bowls. Ladle chicken stock into bowls.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.
Serves 12.
Combine strawberries, water and sugar in 3-quart saucepan. Cover; bring water to a boil.
Lower the heat, remove the cover and simmer, uncovered, until the berries are very soft, about 15 minutes.
Puree the mixture in a blender or food processor, then strain it through a sieve or cheesecloth to remove the majority of the seeds.
Return it to the pan.
Stir the cream mixture into the strawberry mixtures and heat or simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly thick.
Remove from heat; chill for 2 hours.
Add and mix in champagne, if you would like.
Top each serving with sour cream.
Break lettuce in bite-size chunks.
Add cheese, olives, pimientos and anchovies.
In jar, combine oil, vinegar, salt, pepper and garlic for dressing.
Shake well.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss lightly.
Serves 10.
Shake chicken, flour,
salt
and pepper in plastic bag. Arrange in single layer
in
baking pan.
Melt butter and pour over chicken.
Bake 1/2 hour at 400°.
Flip chicken over.
Mix lemon juice, soy
sauce,
oil
and garlic. Pour over chicken. Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Flip chicken and bake 1/2 hour more at 350°.
Boil potatoes to done.
Peel while still hot and cut into thin slices.
Mix together oil, vinegar, sour cream, onion, salt, pepper, sugar and parsley.
Beat to a thick sauce.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes and mix gently so potatoes are not mashed.
After mixing, cool overnight.
Beat egg whites in a small, chilled bowl until stiff and glossy.
Whip 2 cups cream with sugar in medium bowl until stiff. Whisk strawberry puree into cream until mixture is very thick. Gently fold in egg whites, blending well.
Spoon into small dessert bowls.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Garnish each with whipped cream just before serving.
Boil green chiles, Ro-Tel, onion and garlic until onion is tender.
Add milk and stir continuously.
Add cheese and stir over medium heat until cheese melts.
Serve hot or cold.
Yields 10 servings.
Brown meat.

Bring tomato sauce and Sloppy Joes mix to a boil; add meat and simmer 30 minutes, stirring often (prevent sticking). Just before serving, remove from heat and stir in sour cream. Garnish with parsley.
Serve on noodles.
Scrape carrots; remove ends.
Cut into julienne strips.
Add carrots and onions to 1 inch of salted boiling water.
Cover and simmer until tender, about 25 minutes.
Drain; toss with butter and walnuts.
Season to taste.
In 1-quart casserole, combine corn and 2 tablespoons of water; cook, covered, at High for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring once.
Drain in colander.
In same casserole, mix sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in vinegar and 1/3 cup water.
Add corn, celery, green pepper, pimento, onion and seasonings.
Cook, uncovered, at High for 5 minutes until mixture is thickened and bubbly, stirring after each minute.
Cook, covered, at High for 3 minutes more.
Cool.
Chill thoroughly.
Stir before serving.
Makes 2 cups.
Add yeast to warm water.
Mix in sugar.
Let set until dissolved. Blend dry ingredients.
Mix in yeast mixture.
Knead for 5 minutes. Cover and let rise.
Knead again. Roll out and add anything you want, such as raisins, nuts, cinnamon and sugar.
Let your imagination go!
Fold into loaves. Place in greased pans and let rise. Bake at 350° for 35 to 60 minutes, depending on size of loaf.
Drain fruit; save juice.
Dissolve jello in boiling water; add ginger ale.
Add cold water to fruit juice to make 1 3/4 cups; stir in jello.
Chill until partially set, then add fruit.
Pour into 2-quart container or mold.
Chill until firm.
Fold marshmallows into Cool Whip and then add Miracle Whip.
Spoon over jello mix and chill.
Garnish with toasted, shredded coconut, if desired.
Cook chicken; remove from stock and cut into bite size pieces. Brown bacon in large kettle.
Add potato cubes and stir until coated with bacon drippings.
Add water and stock, tomato sauce, onion and salt.
Simmer for 1 hour.
Place green chilies and grated cheese in 6 soup bowls.
Add chicken.
Spoon hot soup over chicken and garnish with crisp tortilla strips and avocado. Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Toss cranberries, sugar and walnuts in 1 1/2-quart baking dish. In another bowl, combine flour, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Cut in butter with pastry blender.
Cover cranberries with flour/sugar mix.
Bake 45 minutes.
Serve with ice cream.
Yields 6 servings.
Combine
tomatoes,
onion,
garlic,
1 cup water, salt, pepper and dill in large saucepan. Bring to boil and simmer 30 minutes. Stir
remaining
water
slowly into flour and add to hot soup. Cook
minutes, stirring.
Pour soup into blender and
blend
in batches.
Strain.
Refrigerate when cooled.
To serve, stir in cream and garnish as desired.
Serves 8.
Mix pie filling, water and sugar together; bring to boil.
While boiling, add gelatin.
Remove from heat, stir until dissolved. Pour into a bowl and refrigerate until syrupy.
Add cola slowly; chill until set.
Add topping if desired.
To make topping combine melted marshmallows and cream cheese.
Mix well.
Fold in whipped topping.
Layer cucumbers in small bowl; sprinkle with salt. Refrigerate, covered, for 30 minutes.
Saute bacon in large skillet until crisp; drain well.
Add cucumbers, drained thoroughly, and remaining ingredients.
Stir to mix well.
Cook, covered, over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Slice croissants in half.
Spread mustard very lightly on one side of croissant.
Evenly divide ham and cheese between sandwiches.
Put tops of croissants on ham and cheese.
Microwave for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Very tasty.
Serve with chips or raw veggies.
Serves 4+.
Saute green pepper in margarine. Blend in flour and herb spice mix from spaghetti mix.
Gradually add milk. Stir constantly until thickened.
Add chicken.
Cover.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Put crumbled Oreos in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Combine cream cheese, 10x sugar, peanut butter and milk in a large mixer bowl.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour mix over Oreos.
Put chopped nuts (or crushed Oreos) on top.
Freeze it.
Defrost slightly before serving.
Chop squash and onion.
Boil until tender and drain.
Combine all other ingredients.
Top with crackers and melted margarine. Bake for 20 minutes in a 350° oven.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Add all ingredients, except cheese and cracker crumbs.
In a 2-quart casserole, alternate mixture, cheese and crumbs.
Finish with crumbs on top.
Cook at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes, covered with foil, or until bubbly.
Remove foil and brown crumbs.
Mix together cake mix, water and icing.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Beat well.
Add oil and mix well.
Bake at 350° for at least 1 hour in Bundt pan.
To test, insert toothpick into cake. Cake is done when toothpick comes out clean.
Cook, cool and squeeze to drain the spinach.
Combine mayonnaise and milk.
Beat until smooth with wire whisk.
Stir in and blend sour cream.
Add spinach and remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours to blend flavors. Serve with fresh vegetables.
Makes 3 2/3 cups.
Peel and slice banana.
Cut peaches in chunks.
Combine ingredients in electric blender.
Whirl until smooth and fluffy. Yields 10 (1/2 cup each) servings; 44 calories per 1/2 cup serving.
Combine spices in a large pot.
Add duck and enough water to cover.
Simmer 45 minutes.
Remove duck from pot, reserving 2 cups broth.
Heat 1/2-inch oil in a
large frying pan and fry duck on each side about 5 minutes until well browned.
Cool duck.
Remove meat from the bones in as large pieces as possible.
Dip the duck in egg and then in crumbs before frying in the same oil.
Cut duck into 2-inch pieces and serve over Chinese vegetables.
Top with lettuce and onions.
If desired, make gravy with the reserved duck broth and 4 tablespoons flour and serve on the side with rice. Serves 3 to 4.
Pour the mush, while hot, in a small deep pan, first rinsed with cold water.
When cold, turn out, slice crosswise and then in halves.
Dip each piece in fine dry crumbs, then in the egg slightly beaten with one-fourth cup cold water, then in crumbs again.
In the meantime, heat enough Mazola in a deep fat frying kettle to half fill it.
Put slices in a frying pan and fry until golden brown in the Mazola which should be hot enough to brown a bit, 375° by the frying thermometer.
Pour 2 tablespoons of butter into a shallow baking pan; arrange scallops in single layer.
Combine breadcrumbs, garlic salt, mustard, paprika and remaining butter; sprinkle over scallops.
Broil 4 inches from heat until lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes.
Drizzle sherry over scallops; serve hot with lemon wedges.
Serves 6 to 8.

Place the potatoes and 1 teaspoon salt in a heavy 4-quart saucepan and cover with water by 1-inch. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain in a colander and return to the cooking pot. Add the cream, butter, remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt and black pepper. Place the pan over medium-low heat and mash with a potato masher to mix the ingredients and get a light texture, about 4 to 5 minutes. Add the bacon, grated cheese, sour cream and chopped chives and stir until thoroughly combined. Season to taste. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350.
grease an 8 inch square pan.
In bowl with electric mixer on medium speed, cream together butter and sugar.
Add molasses, corn syrup, egg, and salt and beat until smooth.
In skillet, brown hamburger meat, onion, mushrooms and salt and pepper to taste.
Drain meat mixture.
Mix in large serving bowl, prepared macaroni and cheese and hamburger meat.
Serve with salad or vegetable.
Place drained beans on a large double thick square of aluminum foil which has been sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Top with tomatoes.
Cream together onion, butter, brown sugar, salt, mustard, horseradish and pepper.
Dot mixture over tomatoes.
Wrap securely in foil, sealing edges.
Place on grill and heat with cover down for 30 to 40 minutes on low flame setting.
Heat oven to 350°.
Melt chocolate and margarine in a pan. Beat in sugar and eggs.
Add dry ingredients plus nuts.
Spread in 9 x 12-inch greased pan.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool slightly and frost.
Combine whole eggs, yolks, sugar and lime juice in large mixing bowl.
Whisk vigorously over simmering water until mixture is ribbony and pale in color.
Remove from heat and whisk in softened butter.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Whip heavy cream until stiff.
Whisk approximately 1/4 of cream into Key lime mixture to lighten it.
Fold in remaining cream.
Crumble bread in bowl.
Add water and egg and mix until bread is moist.
Add hamburger, onion, salt and pepper to taste and a dash of garlic salt.
Mix and shape into patties.
Put on wax paper.
Stack and store until ready to cook.
Sift flour and salt together.
Add milk gradually while beating with rotary beater, then beat in eggs.
Beat 2 to 3 minutes.
Split chicken breasts in half.
Dredge in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in skillet.
Brown chicken breasts in butter.
Remove to a shallow, covered, baking dish.
Saute peppers until limp.
Add to chicken.
Add wine to skillet and cook for a minute, scraping bottom of pan with a wooden spoon.
Remove skillet from heat, add herbs to wine and pour over chicken.
Cover baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes, basting once or twice during cooking.
Yield:
4 servings.
Carbohydrate 4 g, protein 15 g, fat 18 g, calories 270.
Chill a 2 1/2-quart mold in freezer.
Stir sherbet to soften. With spoon, spread sherbet thickly over the sides and bottom of the mold.
Freeze firm.
Spread ice cream into the mold over top of the sherbet, covering completely.
Freeze firm.
Mix the Cool Whip, sugar and salt, then add the fruits, nuts and flavoring. Pile into the center of the mold, smoothing the top.
Cover with foil and freeze.
Peel off foil and invert mold onto a plate. Serve cold.
Mix mincemeat, egg, Equal, coffee, syrup and Crisco; beat well.
Add soda and flour.
Bake in a greased and floured pan at 350° for about 1 hour.
Cook and drain ziti; set aside.
Brown hamburg.
Remove from heat and add Ricotta, Parmesan, parsley, egg, salt and pepper and half of sauce.
Add ziti.
Spread in greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Add the remaining sauce and cover with Mozzarella.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 minutes, or until bubbly.
Divide bread dough in half.
On lightly floured surface, roll each half into an 8-inch square.
Spread each square with 1 tablespoon of butter.
In a bowl, combine brown sugar, flour and cinnamon.
Add apples.
Toss to coat.
Spread half of this mixture down the center of each square.
Cutting from the right edge towards the filling, make 2 1/2-inch long cuts in the dough at 1-inch intervals.
Repeat from the left edge.
Fold strips alternately over filling.
Fold under ends.
Place loaves on a greased 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan.
Brush with milk.
Combine flour and sugar, cut butter into flour and sugar until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle half the crumb mixture over each loaf.
Top with almonds.
Cover and let rise until nearly double (45 to 60 minutes).
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until golden. Serve warm.
Makes 2 loaves.
Mix soft margarine with sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Stir in flour, baking soda, orange rind, buttermilk and bananas.
Mix until batter is moistened.
Fold in nuts and chocolate chips. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Makes 18 regular muffins or 9 Texas size muffins.
Mix Bisquick, butter and milk.
Spread in an 8 x 8 x 2-inch square cake pan (ungreased).
Spoon cherry pie filling over top of Bisquick mixture.
Bake at 425° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream or with ice cream on top.

Prepare cake mix according to package. Pour 1/2 batter into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Unwrap caramels and melt with evaporated milk and butter/margarine in saucepan over low heat. Pour caramel mixture over hot cake spreading evenly. Sprinkle chocolate chips and chopped pecans on caramel mixture. Top with remaining cake batter and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Marinate chicken strips in picante sauce, oil and lemon juice for several hours. Chop onion and pepper and add to the chicken marinating
and either cook on the grill on top of foil or stir-fry in pan on stove.
Can be served with chopped tomato, shredded cheese, guacamole and sour cream.

Brown beef. Pour off excess liquid. Add onion. Cook beef well and onions softened. Add tomato paste, chili beans, diced tomatoes and water to desired consistency. Add pepper, salt, chili powder and sugar. Simmer on low for at least 30 minutes.
Put liver in a pot with enough water to cover it.
Add onion, bouillon cubes, salt, pepper, and garlic.
Bring to a boil and cook over medium or medium low heat until liver is falling apart and most of the liquid is cooked out.
Drain and put into a food processor.
Add eggs and mayonnaise.
Blend until smooth.
You can add more salt, pepper, or mayonnaise to suit your taste.
Place cabbage and water in large bowl.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Microwave for 5 minutes on High to soften.
Mix ground beef, rice, onion, egg, salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons soup. Divide among cabbage leaves.
Fold in sides.
Roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Place cabbage rolls, seam side down, in 12 x 18-inch baking dish.
Mix remaining soup and sauerkraut; pour over cabbage rolls.
Cover dish loosely with plastic wrap.
Microwave 12 to 17 minutes on High, turning dish once.
Yields 4 servings.
Finely chop walnuts, then toast.
Chop mushrooms and scallions.
In heavy skillet, cook in butter the mushrooms, scallions and thyme for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add salt and sherry. Cook until all liquid is gone.
Cool.
Fold in soft cream cheese. Add walnuts, parsley and Tabasco.
Place in a dish and refrigerate.
(Use 1/4 fresh chives to garnish, if desired.)
Slice eggs in half lengthwise and carefully remove yolks. Mash yolks with mayonnaise.
Add remaining ingredients; stir well. Stuff egg whites with yolk mixture.
Garnish eggs with paprika.
Remove and discard stems and any discolored spots from greens. Wash thoroughly and drain.
Tear into bite size pieces.
Set aside.
Combine olive oil and butter in a large stockpot.
Add garlic and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until tender.
Add greens; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, 35 to 45 minutes or until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in salt and pepper.
Cook cauliflower and carrots in boiling water for 8 minutes. Add peas and cook for 4 minutes.
Drain and keep warm.
Melt margarine in a pan; remove from heat and stir in flour.
Blend in the milk and salt and pepper.
Return to boil, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Cook for 2 minutes, then mix in half of the cheese and cooked vegetables.
Turn into large ovenproof dish and sprinkle with bread crumbs, remaining cheese and sesame seed.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown.
Combine in a double boiler the sugar, fruit juices, egg yolks, wine and rum.
Place over heat and beat continuously with an eggbeater until foamy and thickened.
Remove from the heat and add the gelatin which has been softened in the cold water.
Cool until it is syrupy.
Fold in the whipped cream.
Pour into a well-oiled quart mold and chill for at least 3 hours.
Serve with small dish of whipped cream.
Serves 6.
Cut potatoes lengthwise into thick slices.
