Cut slices into strips.
Brush with salad dressing.
Place on greased 15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch jelly roll pan.
Season to taste.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until tender and golden brown.
Makes 4 servings.
Brown garlic, sesame seed and onion in oil.
Let cool.
Add salt and pepper, sugar and sauces.
Soak chicken overnight.
When you put chicken in sauce, put in one piece at a time.
When all pieces have been coated, pour remaining sauce over chicken.
Great for grilling!
You can double recipe for larger amount of marinade.
Grease or spray a cake pan real good.
Pour in sweetened applesauce.
Pour in crushed pineapple on top of the applesauce. Sprinkle cake mix over pineapple.
Sprinkle coconut over cake mix. Pour melted butter on top.
Finish with sprinkling chopped nuts over top.
Do not stir.
Add mustard and Worcestershire sauce to softened cream cheese. Add onion, parsley and mayonnaise.
Mix until well blended.
Mash in shrimp.
May need to be thinned a little for right consistency; little more mayonnaise can be added.
Serve with potato chips. Serves 8.

Peel potatoes; cut into 1-inch cubes. Cook in boiling water to cover 15 to 20 minutes or until tender; drain and place in a large mixing bowl. Add cream cheese, sour cream, margarine, milk, onion salt, pepper and salt.

Beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth and fluffy. (Do not overbeat.) Spoon into a lightly greased 13 x 9-inch or 3-quart baking dish. Bake, covered, at 325° for 50 minutes or until thoroughly heated; garnish, if desired. Makes 10 servings.
Scrub potatoes and cut into lengthwise wedges.
Coat with olive oil by dipping both cut sides in the oil.
Arrange on a nonstick baking pan.
Sprinkle all potatoes with a dash of salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder.
Bake at 375° for about 20 minutes or until crispy and lightly browned.
Heat skillet to 325° with oil in it.
Place chicken in.
Cook until white on both sides.
Mix jelly and Port wine in pot on stove.
Simmer until berries are gone.
Pour over chicken in skillet and simmer 30 to 40 minutes or until chicken is tender. Turn chicken often to keep flavor on both sides.
Melt chocolate morsels, peanut butter and margarine on low heat until smooth.
Add cereal gradually; mix well in a large Ziploc bag (do in 3 or 4 parts).
Add 1 cup of powdered sugar and 1/3 or 1/4 of chocolate cereal mixture; mix well.
Repeat (use full box of sugar).
Spread on 2 baking sheets.
Let dry approximately 1 hour.
Separate with a fork or break apart.

Preheat over to 325°. Put sunflower seeds and parmesan cheese into the food processor (with S blade) until it forms a fine meal with almost a flour consistency. Add the water and pulse until dough is well blended, soft, and sticky. Cover your cookie sheet with a piece of parchment paper. (You must use parchment paper - see note.) Turn dough out onto parchment paper, and tear off another piece of parchment paper to cover dough. Through the top sheet of parchment, use your hands to press the dough as thin as you can (the thinner the better). Peel off the top layer of parchment paper. Use a thin, sharp knife or a pizza cutter to score the dough into squares. (Hint: spray knife or cutter with Pam and the dough will not stick to it.) Bake for 30 minutes or until evenly browned. Break along the scored lines and store in a container with a tight lid. For those counting carbs you'll love this recipe. Each cracker contains just a trace of carbohydrates, a trace of fiber, and 1 gram of protein.
Brown and drain ground beef. Add salt, sugar, pepper and spaghetti sauce.
Simmer 15 minutes. Cream together the cream cheese, Ricotta cheese and onion salt. Stir well until smooth and softened.
Using a 9 x 12-inch baking dish, layer noodles, meat mixture and cream mixture.
Repeat until all gone. Top with shredded cheese. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Shred cabbage in large skillet.
Put water, margarine and seasoning and let come to a boil.
Add cabbage and diced sausage along with shredded apple and onion.
Cover and reduce heat.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Layer one layer of crackers in an 11 x 13-inch casserole dish. Mix pudding with milk; let stand until set.
Add jello; mix well. Fold in Cool Whip.
Cover first layer of crackers with 1/2 of filling.
Add another layer of crackers.
Top with last of filling; end with last layer of crackers.
Spread lemon icing over crackers.
Refrigerate for 24 hours.
In a bowl, mix the egg yolks, sugar, maple syrup, milk and the butter.
In another bowl, mix the egg whites until they make firm peaks and incorporate into first mixture with a spatula.
You have to gently fold the egg whites to incorporate air in the mixture. Put the preparation in pie crust and cook at 350° for 30 minutes.
Saute onion in margarine.
Salt chopped onion.
Place colander inside mixing bowl.
Chop tomatoes with pastry cutter or knife, letting juice fall into bowl.
Add chilies to tomatoes and stir. Place chilies and tomatoes in 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Add onion and cheese.
Bake until cheese melts (about 1 hour).
Baking can be sped up by preheating in microwave.
Dip or spoon mixture onto tortilla chips or pita bread and top with sour cream.

In a large pot, put enough water to cover pork and hominy. Place garlic (whole cloves) in pot. Bring to boil, then reduce heat to medium and continue cooking until cooked. Add the seasonings. Cook 5 minutes more, stirring frequently to blend flavors. Serve with sliced radishes, diced onions, chopped lettuce, a dash of oregano or lemon and salt for extra flavor. Can also be served with tostadas. Serves 2 to 4.
Combine first 5 ingredients; stir well.
Add squash, red pepper and zucchini; toss gently.
Arrange vegetables in a wire grilling basket coated with cooking spray.
Place on grill over medium-hot coals.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes or until tender, turning once.
Serves 6.
Melt together margarine, marshmallows and butterscotch pieces in top of double boiler over boiling water.
Remove from heat and stir in uncooked oatmeal and coconut.
Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Press pecan half on top of each cookie.
Refrigerate. Makes about 3 1/2 dozen.
No need to bake.
Saute onion and celery in butter and add to cooked rice.
Add mushrooms and pecans.
Just before serving, add whipping cream.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease large cookie sheet.
Unroll dough; separate into strips.
Cut each strip in half crosswise.
Twist strips; place 1 inch apart on greased cookie sheet.
Brush strips with margarine; sprinkle with cheese and pizza seasoning.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes or until golden brown.
Pound steak.
Spread with stuffing to which egg has been added.
Roll and skewer.
Dredge with flour, salt and pepper. Place in baking pan.
Add water and strips of pork.
Cover.
Bake at 375° until meat is tender.
Baste frequently.
Serves 8.
Mix 2 1/2 cups flour, sugar, salt, pepper and undissolved yeast.
Mix milk, water and bacon grease to 120° to 130°. Gradually add to dry ingredients and beat 2 minutes at medium speed of mixer.
Add egg and 1 cup of flour.
Beat at high speed for 2 minutes.
Stir in bacon and enough flour to make soft dough.

recipes.t: Blue Bird Cake For The Birds
d: In a medium-size bowl, put flour, baking powder and baking soda.
Set aside.
Boil sugar, raisins, shortening and water for 5 minutes.
Add this liquid mixture to the dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Add nutmeats.
Spoon into well-greased 8 x 8-inch cake pan. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Serve in pieces on feeder tray or ground feeder.
Boil turkey wings with seasonings for 45 minutes.
Place turkey wings in a pan.
Add Maurice's Meat Sauce.
Saute sausage until brown.
Mix crab meat with sausage. De-seed peppers and stuff sausage.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Place canned fruit in large bowl.
Mix allspice with plum syrup.
Add to fruit in bowl.
Refrigerate.
Just before serving, add apples, bananas and cold ginger ale.
Precook beans in a small amount of boiling water for 4 minutes; drain.
In a small dish combine butter (melted), basil, dill, salt and pepper; set aside.
Pour olive oil into large skillet (add more oil if necessary).
Heat over medium-high heat. Add partially cooked beans; stir-fry about 3 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Add tomato wedges and butter herb sauce; heat through.
Put in serving dish and sprinkle with Feta cheese.
Shell and devein shrimp.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Remove from heat; stir in flour and onion, blending until smooth.
Return to heat.
Add milk slowly.
Bring to boil, stirring until thickened.
Stir in coconut milk, salt, curry powder, ginger root, lemon juice and shrimp.
Simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Soften cream cheese with the juice from cherries.
Add powdered sugar and salad dressing.
Cream well. Add undrained crushed pineapple, slice cherries and Cool Whip.
May add other fruits, such as, mandarin oranges etc.
Pour boiling water on gelatin, add sugar in large bowl, stir until gelatin and sugar is dissolved.
Beat in cream cheese until smooth.
Stir in pineapple (with syrup), Cheddar cheese, cottage cheese and lemon juice.
Pour into 12-cup mold.
Refrigerate until firm, about 8 hours.
Unmold onto salad greens and serve with Honey Dressing and crackers.
In a
5-quart
Dutch
oven,
add
2 layers of potatoes, sliced onions and a portion of cream of mushroom soup.
Add 2 more layers
of
potatoes,
sliced
onions and a layer of the Cheddar cheese soup.
Alternate until 1-inch from top or less. Add
beer. Cook
at
325° until tender.
A little crushed red peppers in some of the layers is a treat.
In medium bowl, stir together mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt and pepper until smooth.
Add rest of ingredients; toss to coat well.
Cover and chill.
Makes about 5 cups.
Soften gelatine in cold water; dissolve over hot water.
Cool slightly; combine mayonnaise, whipped cream, and salt.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Chill in molds until firm.
Unmold on lettuce.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cook garlic in olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add peas and peppers; cook, stirring constantly, 5 minutes or until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Combine milk, sugar, biscuit mix, eggs, butter and vanilla in blender.
Blend on low speed for 3 minutes.
Pour into greased 9-inch pan.
Let stand about 5 minutes, then add fruit.
Bake at 350°
for 40 minutes.
Cool.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Mix in sugar, salt, butter, wheat germ and oats.
Stir in 2 cups flour or just enough to make dough leave sides of bowl.
Turn out on floured surface.
Knead 5 to 10 minutes until dough is smooth and elastic.
Place in greased bowl, turning to coat all sides.
Cover and let rise until doubled in bulk, about 2 hours.
Punch down.
Cut off 1/4 of dough.
Shape remaining dough and place in 8 or 9-inch spring-form or layer pan. Roll remaining dough in 1/4-inch ropes.
Arrange in lattice fashion on dough in pan.
Brush with egg wash.
Sprinkle with additional wheat germ and let rise in warm place until doubled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Remove from pan immediately and cool on rack.
Heat ingredients to boil and simmer.
Prepare, 3 to 4 hours earlier, 2 oranges with cloves.
Boil in water.
Add this juice to punch.
Slice oranges and float on punch.
Makes 16 1/2 cups.
Fry tortillas lightly in oil and drain.
Wilt onion in oil. Add tomatillo, garlic and dash of salt.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes.
Set aside.
Mix sour cream and chilies.

Set aside. Butter 2-quart casserole dish and arrange alternate layers of tortillas, tomatillo sauce, pork, zucchini and sour cream mixture and olives until all ingredients have been used, ending with a layer of sour cream mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Serves 6.
Wash
lettuce
thoroughly and shred. Add tomatoes, bell pepper rings, onion, radishes, carrots, sugar and cheese.
Mix with mayonnaise and salt.
Serve in individual bowls.
Yields 6 to 8 (6 ounce) bowls.
Steam pea pods or cauliflower head until done.
Drain and season to taste with butter and salt.
Brown mushrooms in 1/4 cup butter and then add tomatoes and olives.
Cover and steam through. Remove from heat just before tomato skins pop.
Salt to taste.
Boil ham hock in 4-quart pot about 30 minutes.
Add greens, salt, pepper, bacon drippings and sugar.
Cook 45 minutes or until greens are tender.
Remove from pot and cut into bite size pieces. Liquid is very good with hot cornbread and onions.
Thicken egg yolks, lemon juice and sugar in top of double boiler.
Dissolve 1 package of Knox gelatine in 1/2 cup water. Add to hot lemon mixture.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 3/4 cup sugar to egg whites.
Fold egg whites into warm lemon mixture. Tear angel food cake into bite-size.
Alternate layers of lemon mixture and angel food cake in a spring mold.
Set in refrigerator overnight.
Ice with Cool Whip or serve with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle breasts with parsley and garlic powder.
Roll in butter, then dressing mix.
Place in a greased baking dish. Sprinkle remaining crumbs over chicken and moisten lightly with water.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat.
Add flour and beat well.
Add nuts and fruit to mixture.
Stir with a spoon. Grease a cake pan.
Pour batter in and bake at 250 for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

Sift all dry ingredients together in a bowl. Beat the yolks of eggs and add to the milk. Stir into the dry ingredients and mix well. Add cheese. Beat the egg whites until stiff and fold into the batter. Drop by spoonfuls into hot deep fat and cook until golden brown. Drain on brown paper before serving.
Microwave (Medium) cream cheese in 1-quart casserole or serving dish 30 to 45 seconds or until soft.
Blend in remaining ingredients.
Microwave (Medium) 5 to 6 minutes or until hot, stirring after 3 minutes.
Garnish with finely chopped nuts or parsley.
Serve with vegetables (cut for dipping), crackers or chips.
Makes 2 cups.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Peel and slice Granny Smith apples. Place in Pyrex dish, covering bottom.
Add water to cover apples. Sprinkle with cinnamon and 2 tablespoons of sugar.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over apples. Melt margarine and pour over cake.
Sprinkle more cinnamon on top.
Bake until golden brown, about 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Apple Or Peach Pie In A Jar
d: In a large saucepan, blend the first 5 ingredients well.
Stir in 10 cups of water; cook on medium-high and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Cook an additional 2 minutes.
Add lemon juice and, if desired, food coloring, but I don't.
Add apples or peaches to sauce.
Stir constantly; bring to a rolling boil.
Cook for 1 minute at a rolling boil.
Keep saucepan on burner and ladle mixture into sterile, hot jars; leave 1/2-inch headspace.
Process in boiling water bath 25 minutes for pints or quarts.
Early in day or day before serving, prepare strawberry gelatin as label directs; pour 1/8-inch layer in bottom of 8 cup mold. Refrigerate until set, about 20 minutes.

Arrange 6 strawberry slices on gelatin layer, then carefully pour a 1/4-inch thick layer of gelatin over strawberries; refrigerate until almost set. Refrigerate remaining strawberry gelatin until mixture mounds when dropped from spoon.
Fold in remaining strawberry slices; carefully spoon over layer in mold.
Refrigerate until almost set.
Combine pineapple, apples, lemon juice and lemon peel. Combine sugar, flour, cinnamon and nutmeg;
add to fruit and mix well.
Spoon filling into 1 pie crust.
Dot with
butter.
Cover with second crust.
Make 6 slits in top crust.
Bake at 450 degrees for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350 and bake another 50 minutes.
Soften gelatin in cold water while heating other water. Combine with sugar and salt.
Bring all to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Watch carefully that it does not boil over.
Divide into 2 batches.
Color and season.
Rinse metal cake pans with cold water and shake out.
Put candy in pans and allow it to set for several hours.
Loosen and roll in granulated sugar or sifted confectioners sugar.
Cut into small squares.
Preheat oven to 350°. In saucepan, melt butter and dry dressing. Mix well. Add wine and mushroom soup. Mix well. Add cream cheese and mix until melted.
Blend vinegar, sugar, oil, salt and pepper and pour over vegetables.
Let sit overnight.
Do not drain vegetables before serving.
Make a mountain of potatoes with a crater on top.
Put cheese in crater and drizzle on sides.
Drop bacon pieces all over.
Dice squash; cook in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Dice onion and green pepper; brown in butter.
Add tomatoes; thicken with flour.
Add sugar and salt.
Pour over drained squash.
Place in casserole; cover with grated cheese.
Top with bread crumbs that have been browned in butter.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Soak the raisins in a bowl with a bit of wine.
Boil the potatoes and mash them, use a little bit of milk.
Put the sauerkraut in a pan and add the pineapple juice or white wine (not too much, it doesn't need a lot of moisture, like potatoes).
Boil 10 minutes, then drain all the moisture from the sauerkraut and mix with mashed potatoes.
In the meantime, you cut the onion, apple, pineapple and sausage in pieces.
Fry the onion and sausage in the pan; add the raisins, apple, pineapple, some pepper and ginger powder and simmer for 10 minutes.
Drain moisture and add to the sauerkraut and potato mix.
If everything is hot you can eat it right away.
If you want to heat it, put it in the oven for 30 to 40 minutes on 300°F/175° C.
Fill baked pie shell with blueberries.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and cover with whipped cream.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Rub margarine in flour.
Add enough water to form a firm dough.
Roll out and line 10-inch tin. Toast nuts under grill; chop and sprinkle over pastry case.
Peel, core and slice apples.
Arrange overlapping in 2 concentric circles over nuts.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of measured sugar. Cook in center of oven for 15 minutes.
Blend cornflower with milk in a basin.
Add rest of sugar and eggs.
Whisk together; add sour cream.
Whisk again and pour over apples.
Return tart to oven for approximately 20 minutes, until mixture has set.
Cook sausage over low heat until done and a crumbly consistency.
Drain and set aside.
Cut bread in cubes and place in a 13 x 9-inch Pyrex dish.
Melt butter and pour over bread. Spread sausage over bread and cheese over this.
Combine the remaining ingredients; beat well and pour over the cheese.
Cover and store overnight.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes, until brown.
Let cool about 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Serves 8 to 10.
Brush quick frozen waffles with melted butter or margarine. Sprinkle with coarsely chopped toasted pecans, almonds or walnuts. Set in hot oven just long enough to heat thoroughly at serving time.
Serve hot with honey or syrup with whipped cream or soft vanilla ice cream as a dessert.
Bring the vinegar, salt, coriander and peppercorns to a full boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Cool completely.
Combine apple, orange, grapes, bananas, pineapple, kiwi and strawberries in bowl.
Add half the yogurt, mixing well.
Spoon into serving bowl.
Top with remaining yogurt.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Yields 12 servings.
In a shallow glass dish, mix 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce, 4 tablespoons of the lemon juice, oil, garlic and salt.
Add pork and toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Drain marinade from meat; reserve marinade.
Combine soup, milk and lime juice in a saucepan.
Blend thoroughly.
Heat through, stirring occasionally.
Chill for at least 6 hours.
Before serving, blend in banana and grapes. Garnish with lime rind and nutmeg.
Mix
cake
mix,
pudding mix, oil and eggs.
Add water. Mix well.
Add poppy seed.
Pour in greased pan.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Brown hamburger and some onion.
Drain grease.
Add remaining ingredients.
Sprinkle fillets with salt and pepper.
Arrange in a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Remove fillets with a slotted spatula; place on a heated ovenproof platter and keep warm.
Prepare 3 flavors of jello separately, using 1 cup of boiling water and 1/2 cup cold water for each.
Pour each flavor into an 8 or 9-inch square pan or 7 x 11-inch rectangle.
Chill overnight.
Saute onion in margarine.
Cook broccoli as package directs. Combine all ingredients together in large casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook vermicelli per package directions.
Drain and rinse in cool water.
Mix with oil, lemon juice and Greek seasoning. Marinate overnight or at least 4 hours.
Chop black olives, green onions and pimento.
Mix with vermicelli and chill.
Cream sugar, margarine, salt, eggs and milk, mixing slowly. Sift dry ingredients.
Add to bowl.
Add next 4 ingredients.
Mix until blended.
Bake at 425° for approximately 20 minutes.
Cook mushrooms until tender; add margarine until melted.
Add flour with about 2 tablespoons of water slowly until mushrooms thicken.
Clean and cut livers in half.
Mix crumbs and seasoning salt. Dip livers in oleo, then roll in crumbs.
Arrange in buttered casserole.
Pour rest of oleo over all.
Bake at 350° until brown, about 35 minutes.
Turn each one over after 15 minutes.
Rinse, pat dry and slice mushrooms (about 5 1/2 cups).
In a large bowl, place greens.
Arrange onion rings, olives, radishes and reserved mushrooms on top of greens.
Combine oil, vinegar, salt, thyme, garlic powder and black pepper; pour over salad just before serving.
Toss gently to coat completely.
Sprinkle with parsley, if desired.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Saute onion in butter; add flour and mix until blended.
Add milk gradually, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add seasonings, peas and mushrooms.
Cook until hot.
Cut tomato in slices 1/2-inch thick.
Mix flour and 1/2 of sugar.
Sprinkle on both sides of the slices the remaining sugar and salt.
Dip the slices in the flour and sugar mixture.
Let stand for 5 minutes and dip again.
Mix pecans, brown sugar, flour and margarine together.
Place into 13 x 9-inch pan and bake until brown.
Let cool.
Mix together the confectioners sugar, the Cool Whip and cream cheese and spread over cooled crust.
Next, spread 1 can of peach pie filling over the top.
Drain artichokes.
Cut in bite size pieces. Drain olives. Drain peppers and cut in strips. Cut cheese in squares.
Cut salami in strips.
If too long, cut in half.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl. Season with oil, vinegar, salt, pepper and garlic salt. (Don't use too much oil and vinegar.)
In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, drained and rinsed garbanzos, green peas and 6 thinly sliced green onions.
Cover and refrigerate.
Peel, pit and slice avocados, then combine in a food processor or blender with oil, mayonnaise, yogurt, lime juice, salt, pepper, cumin and chili.
Process until smooth. Transfer dressing to a bowl; cover and refrigerate.
When ready to serve, combine the salad and dressing.
Garnish with remaining green onion, thinly sliced.
Spread each muffin half with 1 tablespoon pizza sauce.
Top each muffin with 3 slices of pepperoni, a few of the mushroom slices and 1 tablespoon of the Mozzarella cheese.
Arrange muffin halves on a paper towel lined plate.
(If desired, sprinkle pizzas with grated Parmesan cheese, chopped onion and chopped black or green olives.)
Microwave on High for 1 1/2 to 3 1/2 minutes or until the cheese melts, rotating the plate once during cooking time.
Cream butter and sugar and add yolks and vanilla.
Beat.
Add Cool Whip to custard.
Put wafers or cake into 9 x 13-inch pan. Spread mix over.
Crush candy and sprinkle on top.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Onion Ring Loaf Tony Roma Style
d: Slice onions crosswise and separate into rings.
Soak rings in mixture of milk, eggs and salt to taste in a bowl for 30 minutes.
Dip each onion ring in pancake mix and fry in oil heated to 375° until golden brown.
Pack fried onions loosely, without pressing (do not pack firmly), into an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan and bake at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Turn onto serving plate. Garnish with parsley.
Serves 4.
Mix together in a large pan, Cheerios, Chex, pretzels, Kix and nut meats.
Melt oleo; add Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder and onion powder.
Mix well and pour over first mixture.
Preheat oven to 300° and bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Combine water, salt, carrot, ginger, rice and green onion and bring to boiling; stir well.
Lower heat.
Cover and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally 45 minutes.
Stir in chicken.
Cover and cook over low heat 15 minutes.
Do not boil.
Remove carrot from saucepan and cut into thin slices.
Return to saucepan. Remove and discard ginger.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift sugar.
Beat eggs until light. Add the sugar, gradually beating until well blended.
Grate and add chocolate.
Combine flour, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, baking soda and salt; sift.
Add sifted ingredients to egg mixture alternately with honey or molasses.
Add chopped ingredients. Spread dough with a spatula into two 9 x 13-inch greased pans. Bake about 20 minutes.
When cool, ice with chocolate icing or melted chocolate chips and decorate with blanched almonds.
Cut into bars.

In large non-stick skillet, prepare hash browns according to package directions. After turning once, sprinkle 2/3 cup cheese over potatoes. Transfer to a platter. In bowl, beat together eggs and milk. Add ham, chopped pepper, onion and remaining cheese. Add egg mixture to skillet. Cook over medium heat, sirring occasionally, 5 minutes or until eggs are set but still moist. Spoon egg mixture over center of hash browns. Serve with sour cream and salsa. This is great!
Layer items in order given.
Use 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle top with brown sugar and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix sour cream and cream cheese together; set aside.
Boil noodles or cook rice.
Brown hamburger, add onion, salt, garlic, salt and tomato sauce.
Pepper or other appropriate spices may also be added.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.

recipes.t: John'S Apple Cake(From John Kram'S Bakery Back In 1930)
d: In a bowl, combine well the apples and 1/4 cup of the sugar. Add the cinnamon.
In a large bowl with an electric mixer, combine the oil and the 1 3/4 cups of sugar and beat for 2 minutes.
Add eggs.
In a bowl, sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Add the flour mixture to the oil and add orange juice and beat in the vanilla.
Pour 1/3 of the batter into a buttered and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Arrange 1/2 the apple mixture over it.
Pour half the remaining apple mixture.
Bake the cake on 350° for 50 minutes to an hour.
Let the cake cool for 10 minutes.
Place layer of potatoes sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add layer of onions and bell pepper.
Repeat until casserole is filled.
Mix soup and milk.
Put in about 1/2 stick of margarine. Pour mushroom mixture over potatoes and bake in 325° oven for 1 1/2 hours (or until tender).
Pressure meat with onion, salt, pepper and jalapeno pepper for 10 minutes after steam comes up.
Add corn, green beans, peas, celery, carrots and potatoes.
Pour meat juice over vegetables into roaster pan.
Add tomatoes and Snappy Tom.
Add catsup to taste.
Simmer until done or gone.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In large bowl, combine egg, sugar, butter, milk, rum, raisins and vanilla.
Stir until combined.
In skillet, brown beef and onions.
Drain fat.
Stir in flour, salt and garlic salt.
Add milk and softened cheese.
Cook and stir until smooth and bubbly. Stir 1 cup of hot mixture into beaten egg, return to mixture in skillet.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture is thickened (1 to 2 minutes).
Stir in cooked broccoli; set aside.
Prepare pastry.
Spoon mixture in bottom crust.
Arrange cheese slices on top.
Cover with remaining crust.
Cut slashes on top and brush with milk.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar and egg.
Cut in 1/2 cup of butter until crumbly.
Stir in nuts. Reserve 2 cups.
Press remainder firmly on bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes.
Meanwhile in saucepan over low heat, melt caramels, milk and remaining butter.
Pour over prepared crust.
Top with reserved crumb mixture.
Bake 20 minutes.
Cool.
Cut into bars.
Store loosely covered at room temperature.
Mix Jell-O with hot water to dissolve. Let cool. Mix all ingredients together, then divide into 2 gallon jugs. Add water to each to make a full 2 gallons.
Cook macaroni and drain.
At same time, brown 1 pound hamburger with a little onion.
When browned, add tomato soup, water, beef bouillon, molasses and A.1.
Stir and add corn and macaroni when cooked.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or microwave on High for 20 to 25 minutes.
Wash and dry spinach; discard stems.
If leaves are small leave whole.
Toss spinach, mushrooms and eggs together in a salad bowl.
In a small bowl, mix oil, sugar, lemon juice, mustard, pepper and salt; beat well.
Pour over salad and toss until all leaves are coated.
Serves 6.
Pour chips into crust, then pecans.
Top with coconut.
Pour Eagle Brand milk over all.
Let set for 30 minutes.
Bake at 325° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Combine salt, pepper and flour.
Dredge chops in seasoned flour.
Brown in oil.
Add 1 1/2 cups water; simmer, covered for 30 minutes.
Add carrots and cook, covered, for 15 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook, covered, until potatoes are tender.
Add water, if necessary.
Makes 4 servings.
Before slicing onions, put all bouillon cubes in 2 quarts of hot water and let sit; stir occasionally to encourage cubes to dissolve.
Spread cream cheese and top with cocktail sauce.
Cover with onion, green pepper, tomatoes and black olives.
Top with cheese. Serve with crackers.
Best when refrigerated overnight.
Prepare and bake cake in two 9-inch round cake pans according to package directions.
Remove from pans and cool as directed. Place unpeeled bananas on baking sheet.
Bake in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until very soft.
Remove bananas from peel and place in container of electric blender. Add butter, sherry and sugar. Blend until smooth.
Cool slightly. Slice each cake horizontally.
Place one layer on plate; spread with 1/3 banana filling. Repeat with two more layers and remaining banana filling.
Top with remaining cake layer.
Frost top and sides of cake with Whipped Cream Frosting. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Pat rolls into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle sausage over.
Beat eggs and remaining ingredients.
Mix well and pour over sausage. Bake in 425° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Put all ingredients in large bowl (ground beef, tomato sauce, diced onion, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, egg, bread and seasonings).
Mix thoroughly.
Put into baking dish and cover top of meat loaf with thin layer of ketchup. Cover with foil.
Bake for about 1 hour or until done clear through.
Serves 5 people.
Remove crust from bread; cut each bread slice into 4 triangles. Set aside until shrimp mixture is complete.
Chop shrimp, water chestnuts and bacon fat very finely.
Add all remaining ingredients and mix well.
Refrigerate mixture until firm.
Heat oil in wok or deep skillet.
Spread shrimp mixture on each bread triangle, covering edges.
Place in hot oil, shrimp side down, first.
Cook until shrimp mixture is light brown (does not take very long so keep an eye on it).
Flip sides and immediately remove from oil. Drain on paper towel and serve.
Cook broccoli until tender.
Drain; place in casserole dish. Pour Cheese Sauce over broccoli.
Top with bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes, or until bubbly. Let cool for 1/2 hour.
Sprinkle gelatin on cold water in small bowl to soften.
Stir until dissolved.
Beat eggs in large bowl until thick.
Add sugar gradually and blend well.
Stir in milk, gelatin mixture, salt and flavoring.
Chill until thick and syrupy.
Whip cream enough to hold soft peaks.
Fold into chilled mixture.
Pour into 8 to 10 paper cups.
Sprinkle crumbs on each and top with a maraschino cherry.
Cover well and freeze until firm.
May be kept frozen for some time.
Beat eggs; add flour, meal and sugar.
Beat to remove lumps. Add oil, buttermilk and eggs last.
Pour into a greased pan.
Bake at 375° until brown.
(I use muffin pans.)
Cream butter and cheese; gradually add sugar and one egg at a time.
Beat after each one.
Add flour, one cup at a time.
Then nuts, vanilla and salt.
Bake in a floured and greased Bundt pan at 325° for one hour and 20 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes and turn out.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Peel, slice and arrange in single layer in baking dish.
Mix together brown sugar, sugar, flour and salt.
Sprinkle sugar mixture over potatoes.
Sprinkle cinnamon over sugar mixture.
Combine water and vanilla.
Pour into pan. Dot potatoes with pats of margarine.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In medium skillet, heat tomato soup with water to boiling. Stir in rice, onion, green peppers, salt and marjoram.
Remove skillet from heat; cover and let stand 5 minutes.
Remove cover; fold in tuna.
Top with cheese slices cut into thin strips and olive pieces.
Cover.
Heat gently until cheese melts.
Nice with green beans with mushrooms.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.

recipes.t: Broccoli, Cheese, Rice And Chicken Casserole
d: Heat together the water, cheese, margarine, milk and soup. Add the remaining ingredients; bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes in a greased 2-quart casserole.
Brown beef until red disappears.
Add onions, garlic and celery and saute until tender.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 20 minutes.
Skim off fat.
Freeze.
Reheat and serve on hamburger buns when needed.
Makes 10 cups.
This is good to have in freezer for unexpected company.
Beat the following until fluffy:
brown sugar, white granulated sugar and eggs.
Mix these and add in order:
evaporated milk, pudding, vanilla and pecans.
Use milk to fill container.
Bring to a boil the salad oil, sugar, salt, vinegar, celery seed, turmeric and mustard seed.
Boil 1 minute.
Cool.
Pour over cabbage, green pepper, onion and carrot mixture.
Mix and place in refrigerator up to 30 days.
Always crisp.
Let stand at least 24 hours before serving.
Bake potatoes for approximately 1 hour in 450° oven.
Slice lengthwise and scoop out potato pulp.
Mash potato pulp well.
Add while potato is hot; corned beef hash, onion, salt, pepper, milk and cheese.
Mix well and restuff potatoes.
Bake until hot or microwave for approximately 3 minutes.
(May freeze and cook individually as needed.)

Drain beans, Chinese vegetables and water chestnuts. Combine soup, milk and soy sauce. Add soup mixture to vegetables in casserole. I add a few onions (French fried), also. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Add rest of French fried onions last 10 minutes of baking time. Serves 8 to 10. Can freeze. Can do ahead.
Combine orange juice, milk, strawberries (washed and hulled), pineapple, banana and coconut extract in container of an electric blender; process until smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 500°.
Halve potatoes lengthwise; then slice crosswise into 1/8-inch slices.
Immediately line up in a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan with slices overlapping.
Pour butter and onion over potatoes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Bake 20 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 5 to 7 minutes more, until cheese melts and is slightly brown.
Let dough rise.
Roll out to form an oblong.
Layer cheese down the center of the dough.
Add drained, roasted peppers and then pepperoni on top.
Fold over one side and then the other side, like wrapping a package.
Pinch ends and along the seam.
Soak onion in water for 5 minutes.
Add next 6 ingredients. Mix until well blended.
Spread on buns.
Beat eggs, sugar, rum or brandy and vanilla together until creamy, then add the Ricotta cheese, a little at a time.
This you use creamy and not beating until all is creamy.
Butter a lasagna pan.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour or until golden brown.
Cool and put in refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Line baking sheet with foil.
Spray with nonstick cooking spray.
In medium bowl, combine potatoes, oil, tomato paste, vinegar, chili powder and salt.
Toss well to thoroughly coat.
Arrange potatoes in a single layer on baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
Break pasta into bite-sized pieces.
Saute in margarine in skillet over medium heat until light brown.
Add rice, bouillon cubes and water to cover.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat.
Simmer, covered, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Season with salt and pepper.
Combine lemon juice, butter, Worcestershire, salt and pepper. Add juice from asparagus.
Simmer about 5 minutes.
Pour over asparagus.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In oven, melt margarine in 8-inch or 9-inch round cake pan, tilting pan to cover.
Sprinkle seeds evenly.
Separate biscuits and cut in quarters.
Place biscuits, cheese and onion in plastic bag; shake to coat.
Place coated biscuits in pan.
Sprinkle remaining cheese (in bag) on top.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 18 minutes.
Turn out onto serving plate immediately.
Saute onion, green pepper and mushrooms in butter about 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes. Add paprika until deep red.
Lay chicken on top and cover.
Cook for 45 minutes to 1 hour on medium heat.
Remove chicken and add sour cream.
Pour over chicken. Garnish with parsley and serve with rice.
Bake yellow cake according to box directions.
Let cool. Spread pudding mix (after preparing pudding according to box directions) on cake.
Spread pineapple over the pudding.
Slice bananas over pineapple.
Spread Cool Whip and sprinkle coconut on top.
Let stand for 2 hours before serving.
Spread chili
on
bottom
of
an 8-inch casserole dish. Spoon rice on
top
of chili. Blend muffin mix, cheese, pepper and milk. Layer over
rice. Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until brown.
Place a heavy wok or pan over high heat.
Add oil.
When hot, add the game hens, breast down.
Reduce heat to medium.
Cover and cook 6 minutes, turning at half time.
Add remaining ingredients. Combine well.
Cover and simmer over medium heat 40 minutes, turning at half time.
Remove hens and halve them.
Sauce should be thick and syrupy.
If not, cook, uncovered, for few minutes to reduce.
Tear leaf lettuce.
Cut cabbage into strips and chop on diagonal.
Put in large bowl.
Chop green onions and add to lettuce mix.
Crumble Ramen noodles and add to mix.
Refrigerate for several hours.
Saute almonds and sesame seeds in oil; drain and add to lettuce just before serving.
Cook squash with salt, pepper and sugar in water in saucepan until tender; drain.
Saute onion and carrot in butter in skillet. Add to squash 1 cup cheese and remaining ingredients, mixing well. Pour into greased 2-quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes. Top with remaining cheese and bake until cheese melts.
Spread bread with butter; place on broiler-proof pan.
Top each slice with sliced hard-cooked egg, then with mushrooms. Spoon 1 tablespoon salad dressing over each slice of bread; top with 3 half slices of bacon.
Broil 3 to 4-inches from heat, 4 to 5 minutes or until bacon crisps.
Makes 2 servings.
Mix together into patties.
Fry in a flat frypan.
Put in hamburger buns with mustard, ketchup, onions and chili sauce. Makes a delicious hamburger.
Sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg into a bowl.
In a separate bowl, blend the oil and sugar.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients alternately with applesauce to the creamed mixture, beating well after each addition.
Pour mixture into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Place beef, onions and potatoes in pressure cooker with enough water to maintain pressure.
Cook under pressure for 15 minutes. Release pressure and remove cooking rack, if desired.
Drain mixed vegetables and peas and add corn and tomatoes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add sugar, if desired.
Bring almost to a boil and reduce heat.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
This makes a fairly thick soup.
If a thinner soup is desired, the water from the mixed vegetables and peas may be used as needed.
Yields 12 servings.
Place the sugar, mustard, salt, onions and vinegar in a blender or food processor; blend until smooth.
In a steady stream, pour in vegetable oil and continue to blend until thick. Add poppy seed or pecans.
Keep covered in refrigerator.
Makes about 4 quarts.
(This dressing will keep indefinitely.)

Trim crusts from bread and flatten with a rolling pin. Blend cheeses with egg. Spread evenly on bread and put 1 asparagus spear on each slice. Roll up bread. Roll in butter to coat well. Place on cookie sheet, making sure seams stay closed. Freeze. Cut into thirds. Sprinkle with garlic salt and Parmesan cheese. Bake at 400° for 15 minutes or until golden.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Coat fillets with flour, seasoned with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat butter in medium skillet and lightly saute fillets on both sides, two at a time, adding more butter as needed.
Place fillets in individual casserole dishes. Divide sauce and then cheese among them.
Bake about 12 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley.
Use carrot peeler to remove thick skin from outside of stalks. Cut stalks lengthwise in thin slices.
In large skillet, heat oil.
Add garlic, sauteing briefly.
Add broccoli.
Saute 3 to 5 minutes over medium-high heat, until tender.
Toss in tamari and lemon.
Serves 3.
Sift the flour, salt and soda together and mix in broken nut meats.
Add to vinegar enough boiling water to make 1 1/2 cups. Add shortening.
Pour over dates and let stand 10 minutes. Combine egg and brown sugar.
Add to dry ingredients.
Add dates and water-vinegar mixture.
Mix well.
Pour into greased loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Dissolve jello in
3/4 cup boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup cold water.
Set aside. Mix and bake cake as directed in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch
pan.
Cool 20
to 25 minutes.
Poke deep holes about 1 inch apart in cake,
still in
pan, with a meat fork. Pour
jello mixture
into
holes.
Refrigerate
cake
while preparing topping.
In
a
chilled bowl blend and whip topping mix, instant pudding, cold milk and vanilla until stiff, 3 to 8 minutes. Immediately
frost cake and store in refrigerator. Serve chilled.
Simmer all ingredients in a large pan except for the orzo (shells or macaroni).
After beef shank is fully cooked, remove it from the pan.
Let it cool. Cut off meat into bite size pieces and return to pan.
Cook orzo (shells or macaroni) separately until almost done. Add to soup stock and simmer 1/2 hour.
Serve with warm French bread.
In large skillet break up the ground beef.
Let beef get brown. Add tomato juice, then add tomato paste.
Add chili powder, garlic salt, sugar, oregano and minced onions.
Cover and bring to a boil. Cook spaghetti noodles.
Serve noodles with sauce.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Semi cook broccoli according to directions on package.
Cube cheeses.
In bottom of pie shells, arrange broccoli and cheeses. Mix eggs and cream until foamy.
Pour into pie shells.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Enjoy!
Makes 2 quiches.
Combine chocolate, corn syrup and water in saucepan.
Heat over low heat until chocolate is melted.
Gradually add milk. Remove from heat.
Stir in orange juice.
Top with whipped cream. Sprinkle with orange rind.
Brown the beef until done.
Drain grease off hamburger.
Add 1/4 cup of water, seasoning, beans and mix all together.
Mixture should not be too thick or too thin.
If it's too thick add more water.
Let simmer until warm meanwhile, get out another pan, put it on stove and warm the pan.
Place tortilla shells one at a time in the pan.
Warm the sides of the shells.
Take the shells and place it on a plate, and put the taco mixture on the shell.
Roll the shell up, repeat until you run out of meat or shells.
Add lettuce, cheese, onions, etc. if you like.
Blend 2 cups strawberries, bananas, orange juice and ice cubes in a blender until thick.
Add remaining ingredients and enjoy a healthful breakfast.
As an added plus you have a fiber filled meal with Vitamins A and C.
Dissolve the brown sugar in the Wesson oil, then add vanilla, eggs and sugar.
In another bowl, add the remaining ingredients. Add ingredients of the first bowl to the second bowl; mix well with a spoon or fork.
Roll into large, marble size balls and place on cookie sheet (ungreased).
Bake at 357° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Drain and chop artichoke hearts and water chestnuts.
Then combine all ingredients in an oven or microwave-proof 11 3/4 x 7 1/2 x 1 3/4-inch pan.
Bake for 20 minutes or until mixture bubbles.
Microwave on High 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve hot with cocktail bread or crackers.
Dissolve jello and sugar in boiling water.
Cut cream cheese in pieces and add to jello while hot.
Beat with beater.
Set until it reaches a liver stage, then mix in undrained fruit and fold in Dream Whip.
Refrigerate.
Mix the first 4 ingredients in a double boiler.
Cook until mixture thickens.
Pour over bananas, layered with vanilla wafers in a casserole dish.
Make meringue from egg whites.
Top and brown.
Combine sugar, white vinegar, pickling salt and celery seed in a saucepan and bring to a boil until syrupy.
Let cool.
Mix the cucumber, onion and green pepper in a glass or plastic bowl.
Pour the syrup over all.
Cover and refrigerate.
Stir once a day for 5 days. Put into smaller containers and freeze.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, mix first 4 ingredients. In small bowl, mix the sugar, shortening and vanilla.
After stirring ingredients well, add sugar and shortening to flour mixture and stir.
Grease square cake pan.
Put 1 1/2 cups canned peaches in pan.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Sprinkle flour mixture over peaches and bake for 25 minutes.
In a skillet, saute chicken (cubes or tenders) in the butter until just barely cooked through. In a small mixing bowl, combine the cream of mushroom soup and the half and half.
Place the chicken on the bottom of a casserole dish.
Add the soup mixture. Stir to coat the chicken.
Pour the bread crumbs from the stuffing box on top of the chicken.
Cook the seasoning packet from the stuffing as directed on the box and pour on top of the bread crumbs.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 6.
Heat the butter in a 10-inch frying pan.
Stir in the onions and paprika and saute over a moderate heat until the onions are soft.
Add the tomatoes and season to taste.
Cook for about 5 minutes until the mixture is thick and well blended.
Add the potatoes and cook for a few more minutes.
Beat the egg yolks until they are thick and creamy.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg whites until they stand in firm peaks.
Fold the whites and yolks together with a spatula.
Return the frying pan to the heat.
Fold in the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Fold in the eggs, mixing well. Cook until the eggs are lightly set.
Serve with a green salad.
Preheat
oven to 350°. Lightly grease a 1 quart casserole. Melt butter in medium saucepan; remove from heat.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper and sugar until smooth.
Blend in cream and
milk. Cook,
stirring
over
medium
heat, until mixture boils and is thickened and smooth.
Stir corn into sauce until well-combined and thoroughly blend in eggs.
Turn mixture into prepared casserole. Set in pan containing 2 inches of water. Bake, uncovered, 1 1/2 hours or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Place apples in a 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and almond extract.
Dot with 2 tablespoons butter.
Mix flour, baking powder, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar and salt into a mixing bowl. Cut in 1/4 cup butter until the mixture is slightly coarser than cornmeal.
Combine egg and milk, pour over the dry ingredients, stir just enough to combine and spoon it over the apples in the baking dish.
Stir first 4 ingredients until blended.
Stir in flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Blend well.
Spread batter in prepared 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan (well-greased).
Bake 50 to 55 minutes or until they pull from side of pan.
Heat chocolate topping and pour over brownies.
After cutting, spoon ice cream onto brownies and sprinkle with cocoa.
Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil.
Add salt, oil and pasta; mix well.
Return to boil.
Add veggies on top.
Don't mix; return to boil.
Put on lid.
Turn off the heat for 10 minutes.
Take off stove.
Drain in colander.
Place on platter and serve!
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Stir in frozen concentrate. Place in a punch bowl two trays of ice cubes or a molded ice ring (molded ring is good made with cranberry juice).
Pour punch over ice.
Slowly pour in chilled ginger ale.
Fruit flavored sherbet may be added if desired.
Cut sausages into bite-sized pieces and brown in Dutch oven. Remove sausage from pan and set aside.
Remove all but 3 tablespoons of oil from pan.
Add onions and beans.
Saute until onions are clear and yellow.
Add mushrooms, basil, savory, seasoned salt, pepper, potatoes, beef bouillon and sausage.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
In a large pitcher, combine instant tea powder, sugar, water, cranberry, orange and lemon juices, cinnamon and nutmeg; chill. Garnish, if desired, with orange slices.
Serve with ice.
Makes about 2 quarts.
Melt chips, peanut butter and butter in microwave 3 to 4 minutes.
Cool.
Add nuts and marshmallows.
Pour into buttered pan 9 x 13-inches.
Cool and refrigerate.
Cut into squares.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease two 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
In a large bowl, cream butter or margarine and sugar until fluffy. Stir in eggs, pumpkin and water.
Blend in flour, soda, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and cloves.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into pans.
Bake approximately 70 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of bread comes out clean.
Dissolve lime Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup cold water.
Pour into sprayed 13 x 9-inch glass casserole.
Bring milk to boil in a saucepan.
Add sugar and mix until dissolved. Add unflavored gelatin which has been dissolved in 1/2 cup cold water.
Add sour cream and vanilla and beat until blended.
Cool. When lime Jell-O is set, pour 1 1/2 cups of white mixture over. When white layer is sticky, add red Jell-O, prepared in sme manner as the lime.
When set, add another 1 1/2 cups of the white mixture.
Follow with lemon layer.
Top with final white layer.
Tear or chop lettuce, cut celery diagonally.
Place lettuce, celery and onion rings in layers.
Combine sour cream and sugar; drizzle over the layers.
Combine mayonnaise and vinegar, drizzle over layers and sour cream.
Crumble cooked bacon over salad. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Mix together beef, egg, onion, rice, salt and pepper.
Shape into balls.
Brown meat balls on all sides in a skillet.
Pour off fat.
Cook candies in 1 cup water, stirring frequently, until candies melt.
Heat to boiling; pour over gelatin in large bowl, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in applesauce and vinegar.
Pour into 6 cup mold.
Refrigerate until firm.
Unmold onto serving plate.
Garnish with endive and orange slices of desired.
Mix together ground beef, onion, egg, salt and potatoes and shape in small balls.
Bake on cookie sheet 4 to 5 minutes at 450°. Mix brown sugar, tomato sauce, lemon juice, garlic salt and wine. Simmer, uncovered, until thickened, about 20 minutes.
Add meat balls to sauce and let simmer.
Great for cocktail food or served over rice.
Dissolve the gelatin in boiling water.
Break up the cranberry sauce in a bowl.
Sieve the cottage cheese or, preferably, puree it in a blender.
Put half the cooled gelatin mixture in the cranberry sauce and the other half in the sieved cottage cheese.
Cut flour into softened lard.
Pour vinegar into milk and let stand for a few minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and shape in a ball.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Separate into small balls and roll into pie crusts.
Dough may be frozen or kept in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
Saute broccoli, onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds.
After 5 minutes, add Worcestershire sauce and soy sauce, then simmer for 30 seconds. Serve over rice.

recipes.t: Fruit Punch For Fifty, Island Style
d: Combine frozen juices, water and tea in a large punch bowl, stirring well.
Add chilled ginger ale and ice and serve immediately.
Makes over 6 quarts or 50 servings of 1/2-cup each.
Cook pasta until al dente and drain.
Cut chicken into strips. Heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Add broccoli and saute for 2 minutes, then transfer to a heated dish.
Add chicken to the skillet and saute until no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Toss pasta with broccoli and chicken.
Garnish with parsley.
Sprinkle with pepper and serve.
Coat both sides of pot roast with flour and brown in butter in an electric frying pan and turn temperature to low.
Fill pan with water to top edge of meat.
Generously sprinkle meat with salt, pepper and chargrilled seasoning and then coat top of meat with horseradish.
Cover and simmer for 2 to 3 hours, adding water so water doesn't completely evaporate.
Flip meat; add carrots and onion and simmer 20 minutes.
Add potatoes.
Serve when meat is tender and gravy is desired consistency.
Melt butter in heavy saucepan.
Add marshmallows.
Cook over very low heat, stirring until marshmallows are melted.
Pour over mixed raisins, peanuts and cereal.
Mix thoroughly.
Form into balls.
Place on tray.
Refrigerate about 10 minutes.
Cook frozen mixed vegetables with salt.
Drain and let cool. Mix sugar, vinegar and cooking oil.
Mix with vegetables and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Blend in egg and vanilla.
Blend in flour.
Stir in pecans and pineapple.
Shape into 2 rolls about 1 1/2 inches in diameter.
Chill in refrigerator several hours. Slice into 1/4-inch slices.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 325° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Cook noodles according to instructions on package.
Beat together eggs, cream cheese, 6 tablespoons sugar, butter, cottage cheese and milk.
Add cinnamon.
Mix cooked noodles into the mixture and toss well.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Roast
the peanuts lightly in the oven; cool and grind. Boil the sugar with 2 cups of water until mixture forms a hard ball in cold water (240°). Add the ground peanuts and continue
cooking, stirring constantly, until bottom of the pan can be seen in the wake of the spoon. Remove from flame.
Add the egg
yolks, cinnamon,
salt
and vanilla and beat the mixture into
a
paste. Press
mixture
into
small balls with wooden paddles
moistened in cold water.
Arrange on wax paper lined tray and dust with powdered sugar.
Serve when dry.
Saute bacon until almost crisp.
Add onion and cook until clear and soft.
Drain off fat.
Add corn, seasoning and chicken broth. Lastly, add hot milk.
Enjoy.

recipes.t: Slow Cooker Chicken, Broccoli, Rice Casserole
d: Saute onion in oil in skillet. Add chicken and saute until chicken is no longer pink. Combine all ingredients in slow cooker. Cover and cook on low 2 to 3 hours. This is delicious!
In large bowl, combine 2 1/2 cups flour, cheese, salt and undissolved yeast.
Add water, milk and 1/4 cup oil to dry ingredients; beat 2 minutes at medium speed of electric mixer, scraping bowl occasionally.
Beat 2 minutes at high speed.
With spoon, stir in enough remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Knead on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Place in greased bowl, turning to grease top.
Cover; let rise in warm, draft-free place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
(For rapid rise yeast, cover kneaded dough; let rest on floured surface 10 minutes.
Proceed with recipe.)
Mix ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, salt and pepper for sauce.
Place serving size pieces of steak in greased casserole dish.
Pour sauce over steak.
Top with onion slices. Sprinkle with garlic flakes.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a small saucepan, heat the syrup and 1 cup of the corn kernels over low heat until the corn is tender and the mixture is heated through, 10 to 15 minutes.

Brown 1 cup white sugar to a darkened color in an iron skillet. Do not burn, then set aside. Mix together 1 cup unbrowned sugar, egg, cornstarch and milk. Slowly add this mixture to browned sugar in the iron skillet and stir until mixture is thick and smooth. Pour in crust and top with meringue. Bake at 325° until golden brown. Makes 2 small pies or 1 large pie.
Combine ingredients.
Use enough milk to make a medium-thin batter.
Mix well.
Bake in a 9-inch iron skillet, dusted with cornmeal.
Bake at 450° for 30 minutes or until done.
Melt together soups and cheese.
If using fresh vegetables, parboil until fork-tender.
Mix all ingredients together. Bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes or until bubbly.
Mix together thoroughly the sugar, Crisco, salt and nutmeg. Add the milk and vanilla.

Mix thoroughly. Next, add 1 cup sifted flour to which baking powder and soda have been added. Beat thoroughly making a soft dough. Now add gradually 4 more cups sifted flour, beating well after addition.
Roll out on floured board and cut into desired shapes.
Bake in a 400° oven. Bake small cookies 6 minutes and large cookies 8 minutes. Frost and decorate as desired.

recipes.t: My Favorite Snack:  Peanut Butter Coffee
d: You toast the bread.
Then you put peanut butter on the bread. Then make the coffee. Then, dip the peanut butter bread in the coffee and taste.
Enjoy!
In medium bowl combine yogurt, coconut and cinnamon; mix well. Add celery, raisins and nuts.
Mix until well blended.
Gently stir bananas into yogurt mixture.
Chill several hours.
Combine wine, meat extract and lemon juice.
Simmer until liquid is reduced to 1/2 of amount.
Add parsley and butter.
Melt over low heat.
(Very important.)
Combine sugar, milk, butter and cocoa.
Bring to a boil for 1 1/2 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients; blend well.
Take spoon and dip small clumps onto wax paper.
Let cool.
Cover mushrooms, celery, carrots and onion with water in 2-quart saucepan.
Simmer, partially covered, for about 45 minutes.
Add stock to make 6 cups of liquid.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Heat through.
Prick the potato with a fork.
Bake at 400° until done.
Cut potato in half lengthwise when cool enough to handle.
Scoop the potato center into a bowl.
Be careful not to break the potato skin!
Mash the potato with fork or mixer.
Stir in the shredded cheese and milk.
Spoon the mixture back into the potato skins. Then put the potato back into the oven for another 15 minutes. Makes 2 potato boats.
Make boats using a cheese slice for a sail and a toothpick for the mast.
Or, happy faces can be made with olives as the eyes and pimiento pieces for a mouth.
Mix dry ingredients.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add oil to yeast and water; pour into flour mixture.
Mix well.
Knead slightly, cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Knead a few times and divide dough.
Roll into "snakes" about the size of a pencil approximately 18 inches long.
Cut in half and twist together. Pinch into a circle.
Let sit 15 minutes.
Place on baking sheet sprayed with Pam and bake at 400° for 30 minutes or so.
If baking two sheets together, alternate at "half-time". Enjoy!
Combine pineapple juice, apple, sugar and cinnamon in large saucepan.
Bring to a boil for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add tea bags; steep 5 minutes.
Serves 6.
Cut thawed dough into 16 pieces.
Mix sugar, cinnamon and nuts.
Dip each marshmallow into margarine and then into cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Wrap each marshmallow with a piece of dough and seal edges.
Dip into margarine and then into cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Grease Bundt pan or cake pan.
Sprinkle a few nuts.
Arrange marshmallow balls in 2 rows in pan.
Sprinkle any remaining cinnamon-sugar mixture on top.
Let rise until doubled in size (45 minutes to 1 hour).
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Let cool 5 minutes.
Turn out onto serving plate.
Melt almond bark in the microwave.
Mix in the nuts, cereal and pretzels.
Stir until covered.
Pour out on waxed paper and break up when the bark is hard.
Boil sugar, maple syrup and milk together until it forms a soft ball in cold water.
Add butter and cream of tartar.
Beat until creamy.
Add pecans and vanilla.
Drop by spoonfuls on waxed paper.
Cut meat into 1 x 1/4-inch strips.
Coat with flour.
Brown in cooking oil.
Cut pepper and onion in thin strips and add to meat. Add pepper, onion, tomato sauce, chili powder and salt.
Add water and hot sauce.
Simmer until meat is tender.
Serve in warm tortillas.
Dissolve jello in hot water. Add grated lemon rind and salt. Add pineapple. When it starts to thicken, add cheese, whipped cream and lemon juice.
Cook spaghetti by directions on package; drain.
Brown sausage; drain.
Add Ragu sauce, tomatoes and Parmesan cheese; mix well.
Add spaghetti.
Grate all cheeses; keep separate.
Put 1/3 of spaghetti in a 12 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle 1/3 of each cheese on spaghetti; repeat 2 more times.
Sprinkle a little more Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°, until bubbly and brown.
Best if made the day before serving.
Store in refrigerator until cold.
Cut into squares.
Reheat for 20 to 25 minutes at 250°; serve hot.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add ice cream and mix thoroughly.
Add rest of ingredients one at time.
Mix until evenly combined.
Refrigerate.
Brown beef with onion; drain fat.
Add soup, water and noodles; blend well.
Cover and bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add salt and pepper and 1/2 cheese.
Blend well.
Pour into greased 2-quart casserole.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 minutes or until heated through.
Pour a quart of washed berries into pastry lined pie plate. Also pour brown sugar, flour, salt and a little nutmeg over berries.
Add top crust, slitting the center of top crust.
Press edges together.
Trim and rub cream over top crust.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake until browned in 350° oven, about 30 to 35 minutes. You may use huckleberries, raspberries, blueberries, gooseberries, increasing sugar to desired sweetness.
(White sugar may be used instead a of brown.)
(Butter instead of cream may be rubbed over top crust.)
Yield:
8 - 10 servings.
To each box of Jell-O, add 1 teaspoon sugar and 1 cup boiling water.
Prepare each box separately and refrigerate in separate bowls.
Heat milk, sugar and gelatine almost to a boil.
Cool thoroughly.
Cut the flavored Jell-O into pieces and place in pan (9 x 13-inch pan).
Pour the milk mixture over the Jell-O. Refrigerate until firm.
Cut in squares and serve.
Wash potatoes and rub skins with vegetable oil. Bake at 400° for 1 hour or until done. Allow potatoes to cool to touch. Cut a 1-inch lengthwise strip

from top of each potato; carefully scoop out pulp, leaving shells intact. Combine potato pulp and remaining ingredients except bacon in a medium mixing bowl. Beat at medium speed of an electric mixer until light and fluffy; stuff shells with potato mixture. Bake at 400° for 30 minutes; top with crumbled bacon. Serve hot. Yield: 4 servings.

recipes.t: Asparagus Saute With Butter And Garlic
d: In a large skillet, melt the butter over high heat.
As soon as it foams, add the garlic and saute until it turns light golden, about 1 minute.
Add the asparagus and saute until it is tender-crisp and the garlic is nicely browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Serve immediately over cooked pasta.
Let each guest add a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper to taste and plenty of Parmesan.
Combine steak, onion quarters and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer for one hour or until meat is tender.
Drain; reserve 1 1/2 cups of liquid.
Cool.
Shred meat or cut into small pieces; set aside.
Cook peppers, onion strips and garlic in 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet for 3 minutes. Stir in meat and reserved liquid (1 1/2 cups).
Cook 10 minutes. Add peas.
Remove bay leaves.
Stir well and cook 10 minutes. Toast garlic bread and serve with meat mixture.
Dissolve Kool-Aid in water. Add to Cool Whip and milk.
Stir in lemon juice.
Pour into graham cracker or vanilla wafer crusts. Makes 2 pies.
Mix cream cheese and sour cream together.
Layer cream cheese mixture on a plate.
Add taco sauce, 4 ounces Cheddar cheese, chopped tomato and chopped pepper.
Then add remaining Cheddar cheese on top.
In a screw-top jar, combine olive oil, vinegar, garlic and salt.
Cover.
Shake until well blended.
Chill until serving time.
Bake shell at 375° for 15 minutes.
In mixer bowl, beat sour cream, sweetened condensed milk, juice concentrate, egg, vanilla and cinnamon; pour into shell.
Bake 30 minutes or until set. Cool.
In skillet, cook apples in margarine until tender.
Arrange on pie; top with glaze.
Refrigerate leftovers.
In saucepan, just cover squash and onion with water.
Cook until tender and drain.
Mix with cheese, eggs, sugar, salt and pepper.
Pour into greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Blend butter, crumbs and almonds and sprinkle on squash.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until done.
May be prepared ahead.
Serves 8.
Heat oil in frying pan. Add garlic and chili.
Saute for 1 minute. Add shrimp and cook over medium-high heat until shrimp turns pink, about 3 minutes. Add basil and salt.
Cook pasta in boiling, salted water following package directions.
Drain.
Place fettuccine in heated serving bowl.
Pour shrimp and oil remaining in pan on top. Toss and serve.
Line a 9 x 13 pan with graham crackers.
In a saucepan, mix together the egg, brown sugar, oleo and water. Cook until it comes to a boil, stirring constantly.
Add the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, nuts, salt and vanilla.
Mix well and spread over graham crackers.
Place a layer of crackers on top.
Mix together the 1/3 stick oleo, milk, vanilla and enough confectionary sugar to make a frosting.
Frost the bars.
Brown beef and onion.
Drain off fat.
Add uncooked noodles, water, bouillon cubes, carrots, potatoes and mushroom soup.
Bring to boil.
Cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes.
Add salt, pepper and Worcestershire sauce.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Brown hamburger.
Cook onion and celery ribs until tender. Combine with tomatoes, tomato paste, chili seasoning, chili (no beans), kidney beans, sugar, salt, pepper and chili powder to taste.
Simmer until you can't stand it any more.
Enjoy.
Spread tomato sauce on crust of your choice. Top with meatball slices. Sprinkle with cheese. Bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Serves 2.
Bring all ingredients to a boil, except onion and eggs.
Slice onion thinly and separate into rings.
Pour beet mixture into a deep bowl.
Remove bay leaf and cloves.
Add onion; stir.
Add eggs, making sure they are submerged.
Refrigerate at least 24 hours.
(The longer the eggs stay in the pickle, the deeper color they will develop.)
Brown sausage; remove from pan and drain.
Saute mushrooms and onion; drain.
In a large bowl, mix together milk, eggs, mustard, chives and soup.
Add bread and 1 cup cheese; mix.
Add sausage, mushrooms and onion; stir.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Refrigerate overnight.

recipes.t: Cheesy Breakfast Casserole(Makes 12 Servings.  Prep Time:  20 Minutes.)
d: In a large skillet, prepare hash browns according to package directions. Sprinkle with garlic salt and pepper. Transfer to a large greased baking dish. Top with soup. Sprinkle half of the meat over soup.
Brown beef in skillet and drain.
Add next 5 ingredients and let it come to a bubbly boil.
Pour in casserole dish.
Cut biscuits in half and place around edge of dish.
Sprinkle cheese on top and bake in preheated oven at 350° for about 25 minutes.
Cut sausage into 1-inch pieces.
Put in large pot with 1 cup of water and boil until water evaporates and sausage browns in its own grease.
Add onion and saute 1 or 2 minutes.
Add potatoes and 5 cups of water.
Season with salt, pepper and parsley flakes to taste.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for about 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Serve over rice.
Wash, cut up and press persimmons through sieve.
Measure pulp.
To each cup of pulp, add one cup sugar and cook slowly 20 minutes, stirring constantly.
(Do not boil as jam will become bitter.)
Pour in sterilized jelly jars to within 1/4-inch of top. Put on scalded caps and screw bands firmly tight.
Process 10 minutes in boiling water bath.
Each cup of pulp makes about 1/2 pint jam.
Make a skillet of cornbread (do not make thick).
Boil hen in 1 1/2 quarts water.
Crumble corn bread and slices of bread.
Add vegetables that have been simmered for about 5 minutes in 1/2 cup of broth.
Make sure everything is cool that goes into the bread crumbs.
(If hot water is used, bread will gum together.)
Add seasonings, chopped eggs, beaten raw eggs and meat, if desired. Pour broth over mixture, stirring lightly so as not to mash up crumbs.
Bake in a 400° oven until brown.
Stir one time while baking.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Lightly coat cookie sheet with spray; dust with flour.
In a small bowl, whisk together egg whites and honey; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine flour, brown sugar, anise, baking powder, soda and salt.
Make a well in center and pour in egg white mixture and apricots.
Mix until smooth and well combined (about 1 minute). Transfer dough to lightly floured work surface.
Divide in half. Shape each portion into a 12 x 2-inch log.

Arrange logs on baking sheet about 6-inches apart. Bake until logs are golden brown (about 40 minutes). Reduce heat to 300°. Transfer logs to work surface and cool about 3 to 4 minutes. Use a serrated knife and slice each log diagonally into 1/2-inch thick slices.
On baking sheet, arrange slices upright and slightly apart. Bake 15 to 20 minutes more until crisp.
Cool completely. Store in airtight container. Will keep fresh up to 3 weeks.
Cook rice until tender.
Lightly brown meat, onion, salt, pepper and garlic powder in butter.
Add rice to meat mixture. Spread 1/2 of the cabbage in a 2-quart casserole.
Cover with meat mixture.
Top with remaining cabbage.
Pour soup over the top.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter a 2-quart casserole dish.
Stir in cheese, butter, nutmeg, salt, peppers and garlic into hot grits.
Beat eggs; mix into grits.
Pour into dish.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes.
Saute onion in butter. Add carrots and chicken stock.
Simmer until carrots are tender.
Puree in blender.
Add orange juice concentrate and cream.
Add 2 or 3 dashes of powdered cloves. Wonderful served hot or cold.
Serves 4 to 6.
Fry bacon and
remove
from grease.
Saute onions until tender and
remove
from
grease.
Brown
tomatoes
lightly. Combine all ingredients and cover and cook over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
De-bone chicken and cut into smaller pieces or use canned chicken.
Mix all ingredients together in a medium pot and bring to a boil.
Place 2 pie crusts on a foil-lined large cookie sheet and pour mixture into crusts, dividing amounts evenly.
Top with remaining pie crusts.
Cut a slit at the top of each crust.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until tops are brown.
Leftovers heat up well in microwave!
Day before using in large mixing bowl with lid, chop broccoli and cauliflower flowerets into bite size pieces.
Slice carrots very thin.
Thick slice the red or sweet onion; cut across slices to make small chunks.
Slice celery ribs and black olives.
Add Italian dressing, rinsing bottle with water and add to vegetables. Stir until well mixed.
Refrigerate, stirring occasionally.
Two to three hours before serving, chop into chunks the Italian tomatoes and add to vegetables, stirring well.
This keeps well for several days.
Beat eggs.
Add baking powder, vanilla and anise flavoring; blend all these.
Add sugar and oil; blend.
Add flour.
Mix all of these ingredients.
In large mixing bowl, combine all ingredients together; mix well.
Pour single layer mixture on cookie sheet.
Bake in 300° oven for 10 to 15 minutes.
Take mix out of oven and stir; cook 30 minutes longer.
Allow to completely cool, then place honey-munch mix in an airtight container.
Heat 1 quart milk until steaming.
Add 1 stick oleo.
Heat to boiling point, then gradually add 1 cup grits, stirring all the while.
Cook milk, oleo and grits until thick, like mush.
Keep stirring.
Remove from heat.
Add diced Swiss cheese (I usually grate) and 1 teaspoon salt.
Beat with electric mixer for 5 minutes.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Pour melted oleo over (1/3 cup).
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes until golden brown, uncovered.
Mix together the shortening, sugar and peanut butter.
Add flour and vanilla extract.
Knead until dough will no longer adhere.
Add boiling water; knead until dough is completely adhered, smooth and shiny.
Make into balls; place 12 balls of dough onto cookie sheet.
Press each cookie with a fork.
Do not grease cookie sheet.
Place into preheated oven and bake at 300° for approximately 20 minutes, or until light golden brown.
Yields approximately 8 dozen cookies.
Cool before removing from pan.
Cut French bread into 12 slices.
Combine cheese, olives, onion, mushrooms, oil, tomato sauce and oregano in bowl.
Mix well.
Spread on French bread; place on baking sheet.
Bake at 350° to 400° just until bubbly.
In a large bowl, combine beans, rice, tomato, bell pepper, cilantro and green onions.
Combine cheese, caraway seed and mayonnaise.
Cut 1-pound loaf bread diagonally almost through to bottom crust, into 1-inch slices.
Spread butter or margarine between slices.
Spread cheese mixture between each slice of bread.
Wrap loaf in aluminum foil. Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Brown meat and onion; drain.
Add barbecue sauce and simmer until done.
Boil the potatoes with skins on; let sit for 48 hours in refrigerator.
Shred the potatoes.
Add grated cheese in layers. Pour melted oleo, salt and evaporated milk over all.
Save a little cheese for the top.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, uncovered, in a greased glass 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish at 350°.

recipes.t: Baked Chicken Breast With Apricot Sauce
d: Melt oleo and oil in shallow pan.
Coat chicken with flour and salt.
Roast for 25 minutes at 375°.
Combine apricot jam, mustard and yogurt.
Spread on chicken.
Bake 25 minutes at 350°. Brown almonds.
Sprinkle on top.
Serve with rice.
Serves 8.
Brown turkey with onion flakes; set aside.
Saute onion, green pepper, mushrooms, onion powder and lawry seasoning all together. Add meat back in.
In big fry pan add the tomatoes, paste and water.
Then simmer all together for 15 minutes.
In a 13x9-inch pan put a little sauce in bottom and add 8 oz. egg noodles, then pour sauce over all.
Sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cover with foil.
Dissolve sugar in hot water.
Cool.
Mix lime Kool-Aid and pineapple juice into sweetened water.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Store in refrigerator.
Makes 1 gallon.

recipes.t: Too Good To Be True Cake
d: Bake cake according to box in an 11 x 14-inch cake pan.
When done, poke holes in top of cake with wooden spoon handle.
Mix Eagle Brand milk and butterscotch; heat in microwave oven until thin.
Pour over cake; sprinkle Heath Brickle Bits and pecans over cake; let cool.
Combine pie filling mix and 2 1/2 cups milk in saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil.
Remove from heat. Add coconut extract and 1 cup coconut flakes.
Pour mixture into a bowl.
Cover with plastic wrap and let cool completely.
Reserve five berries for garnish.
Mix remaining berries, sugar and liqueur.
Cover and refrigerate for two hours, stirring occasionally.
Just before serving, mix whipped topping and ice cream.
Fold into berry mixture.
Garnish with berries.
Wash turkey thoroughly.
Pat dry inside and out with paper towels.
Make paste of oil and salt.
Rub 1/4 cup of the mixture in cavities of turkey.
Place turkey on roaster rack.
Brush with plain oil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix liquid smoke, pepper and vinegar into salt and oil paste.
Baste turkey every 20 or 30 minutes, more often, if needed.
Cook about 3 1/2 hours longer or until drumstick moves easily.
Do not cover turkey.
Fry bacon till crisp and drain.
Cook celery and onion with meat.
When meat is done, drain and add all ingredients and heat on low so it won't burn on.
Combine margarine and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in eggs, three at a time.
Add 1/2 of sour cream and flour.
Blend.
Add remaining flour, soda, lemon and sour cream.
Beat until well mixed.
Fold in blueberries.
Grease and flour Bundt pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the sour cream and mayonnaise.
Add chopped tomato.
Cook bacon until extra crispy.
Crumble and add to mixture.
Stir.
Chill well.
Serve with toasted bread cut into triangles for dipping.
Place the corn, peas, celery, onion, green pepper and pimiento in a bowl.
Mix the Italian dressing and sugar and add to vegetables.
Chill.
Mash overripe bananas.
Add NutraSweet and butter.
Mix well and add remaining ingredients.
Spray loaf pan with Pam and pour in batter.
Bake in a 325° oven.
Sweet 'N Low does not work as well as NutraSweet.
I use Weight Watchers butter.
Mix sugar and cornstarch.
Add chocolate and salt.
Add water. Cook until mixture is thick.
Remove from heat.
Add butter and vanilla.
Spread on cake while hot for a glossy frosting which remains soft and smooth.
Brown ground beef. Add onions and celery. Cook until tender. Add remaining ingredients, except noodles. Bake at 350° for 60 minutes, stirring once or twice during baking.
Serve over Chinese noodles.
Cut chicken breasts in approximately 2 x 1/2-inch strips.
Cut diagonally.
Melt butter or margarine in large skillet; add chicken and brown on all sides.
Remove chicken from skillet, saving the drippings.
Add green pepper and mushrooms.
Saute until tender-crisp.
Return chicken to skillet.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Beat butter and sugar in a large bowl with mixer on high speed for 5 to 7 minutes.
Scrape down sides of bowl and beat in eggs, one at a time.
Then add orange peel.
Scrape bowl again.
In a 4-quart saucepan, brown ground turkey; drain.
Add tomato wedges, tomato sauce and tomato sauce cans filled with water. Bring to a boil; add frozen vegetables and cook until vegetables are done.
Chop fresh spinach and steam in 2-inch water until tender; set aside.
Saute onion and celery in melted margarine.
Stir in flour. Add spinach (do not drain).
Simmer 15 minutes with onion and celery.
Add milk, cheese and seasonings; allow to heat.
Slowly stir in cream.
If thicker soup is desired, add 2 tablespoons cornstarch, dissolved in 4 tablespoons cold water.
Serves approximately 8.
Melt butterscotch morsels and butter together; stir in graham cracker crumbs and walnuts until mixture resembles fine crumbs. Reserve 2 cups crumb mixture for topping.
Press remaining mixture into ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Place foil on cookie sheet.
In small mixer, blend milk, topping mix, vanilla and cocoa; whip at high speed until topping peaks, about 2 minutes.
Continue beating 2 minutes longer until topping is light and fluffy.
Spoon mixture into 5 mounds onto prepared cookie sheet with spoon.
Shape 4-inch shells.
Freeze. Fill center of each shell with fruit.
Combine sugar, syrup and salt in large heavy saucepan.
Boil, stirring occasionally until syrup is very thick (310° on a candy thermometer).
Add margarine and slowly stir in evaporated milk. Stir constantly.
Cook rapidly to firm ball stage (246°).
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla.
If mixture curdles, beat a minute or two. Add nuts and pour into buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch square cake pan. Let stand until cool.
Cut and wrap individually in wax paper. Keeps well for 3 months.
Arrange haddock on foil in a greased baking pan.
Mix sour cream, lemon juice, salt, maple syrup and corn flake crumbs and spread over the haddock.
Bake in moderately hot oven (425°) for about 35 minutes or bake in a small toaster oven to save power.
Cream butter and shortening; gradually add sugar.
Add egg yolks, soda, cream of tartar and vanilla, beating well. Gradually add flour, mixing well.
Divide dough into 4 equal portions.
Color one red, one yellow, one green and leave one plain.
Wrap each separately in plastic wrap; chill at least one hour.
Mix butter, sugar and coconut into mashed sweet potatoes while hot.
