Place in casserole dish.

recipes.t: How To Cook Greens(Mustard, Collards And Turnips With Roots)
d: Heat on medium-low.
Custard mustard into the boiler on top of the oil.
Start with low heat.
Add seasoning; cover and cook slowly for 30 to 45 minutes.
I don't add any water, they will make enough liquid.
Stir them occasionally.
Bring water to boil; add salt and vegetables in order.
boil until tender, 5 to 10 minutes.
Add sugar, pepper and hot milk; mix.
Add butter and serve.
Cut zucchini lengthwise.
Scoop inside out with a teaspoon. Set aside.
Boil shells for 3 minutes.
Fry onion, zucchini scoopings and drained mushrooms in butter or oleo.
Remove from oleo into a bowl.
Add egg and bread crumbs.
Mix. Sprinkle cheese over top and bake at 400° for 1/2 hour.
Bake in a long Pyrex dish.
Cook frozen vegetables in 2 cups of water until tender.
Mix oleo and butter.
Add celery and onions.
Saute until onions are clear.
Add flour and stir until blended.
Add bouillon and milk. Stir.
Add the vegetables, ham, pepper and Accent.
Salt to taste. Stir until thick and smooth.
Makes 3 quarts of soup.

Arrange bread slices on foil lined 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan. Broil bread about 4-inches from the heat until lightly toasted. Sprinkle half the cheese and half the onion evenly on the bread slices. Top with pepperoni. Sprinkle remaining cheese and onion evenly over the pepperoni. Broil 1 minute or until cheese is melted. Makes 15 appetizers.
Combine all ingredients except the chicken and oil.
Place chicken pieces in yogurt marinade.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Drain well.
Brush with oil and cook in 375° oven for about 1 hour or until tender.
Serve with rice.
Makes 4 servings.
Step 1:
In a small mixer beat egg yolks at high speed on electric mixer until thick and lemon colored, about 5 minutes. Gradually add 1/3 cup of granulated sugar, beating constantly. Stir in peel and juices.
Blend soup mix, sour cream and mayonnaise.
Stir in spinach, cheese and water chestnuts.
Cover.
Chill 2 hours.
In a 3-quart saucepan over medium heat, in hot oil, cook onion and garlic until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in soup, beans with their liquid, sausage, chilies, tomatoes with their liquid and water; heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover; simmer 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Cook noodles. Cook, but do not brown celery and onion in butter.
Add meat, soup, salt and pepper; heat thoroughly.
Pour half of noodle in 1 1/2-quart casserole and top with half mixture. Repeat layers with the rest of noodles and mixture.
Top with cheese and bake at 375°
for 30 minutes until bubbly hot and brown.
Serves 6.
Stir soup mix in package before measuring.
Lightly brown ground beef, drain off excess fat.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, frozen vegetables, celery, onion soup mix and sugar. Reduce heat. Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cut steak into strips; dip in seasoned flour and roll up. Wrap a strip of bacon around each roll and secure with a toothpick.
Brown steak rolls over medium heat in hot oil.
Pour off excess grease.
Add soup and water.
Cover; simmer for one hour.
Combine first 3 ingredients in blender until smooth.
Float chocolate sprinkles on top of each serving.
Place flour and milk in small pan.
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly,
or until a thickened paste.
Cool for 15 minutes in refrigerator.
Transfer to small electric mixer bowl. Add margarine, Crisco and sugar to bowl.
Mix on medium to high mixer speed until light and fluffy.
Will ice an 8 or 9-inch layer cake.
Quite different.
Melt Hershey bar in top of double boiler over hot water.
Cool. Cream margarine with sugar.
Beat until smooth.
Add eggs one at a time beating well after each.
Sift dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Stir in nuts.
Bake in 2 greased and floured 9-inch square cake pans in 350° preheated oven for about 35 to 40 minutes.
Frost cake with your favorite frosting.
To the hot roll mix add the yeast and sugar.
Mix according to directions on package.
Raise double.
Roll out into 9 x 13-inch rectangle.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Add it to sugar.
Roll; cut into 3/4-inch slices.
Cook all ingredients in a large saucepan for about 20 to 30 minutes over medium heat.
Prepare approximately 12 ounces of rice according to package directions.
(Cooking time is usually to minute.)
When rice is cooked and drained, add about 2 tablespoons of margarine.
Spoon rice onto plates and top with shrimp sauce. Served with a sprig of parsley, this dish makes an attractive main course for any meal.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Combine rice, sugar, salt and milk in a saucepan.
Simmer for 1 hour.
Stir occasionally.
Combine egg yolk, cornstarch and water.
Stir into the rice mixture along with the raisins about 15 minutes before cooking time is finished.
Pour into serving dishes and sprinkle with cinnamon.

Mix 1/4 cup peanut butter with 1/4 cup skim milk. Gently stir in whipped topping. Pour 4 cups milk into large glass bowl. Add pudding mix. Beat 2 minutes or until well blended. Spread crushed graham crackers on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan. Spoon pudding on top of crumbs and carefully spread over pan. Slice bananas on top of pudding. Layer Cool Whip mixture on top. Makes 12 servings. Each serving contains 176 calories and 5.8 g fat.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the oats, sugar, cocoa, cold coffee and vanilla.
Add 1 stick margarine (melted); blend well.
Shape into balls and roll in powdered sugar.
Mix crumbs and butter.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Then place ice cream over crumbs.
Pour the jar of hot chocolate sauce over ice cream and layer the peanuts.
Next put Cool Whip on and sprinkle a few cookie crumbs on top of the Cool Whip (then freeze).
Cut into squares.
In a large bowl, place wine, meat, green peppers, celery, onion and beans.
Soak these overnight.
The following day, empty this into a large cooking pot.
Fill pot half way with water. Cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 hours or until beans and meat are tender.
Add salt and pepper to desired taste.
Serve hot over cooked rice.
Combine cornmeal, milk, beaten eggs, salt, soda, bacon drippings and corn.
Mix well and set aside.
Brown ground beef and drain well.
Pour half of batter into well-greased cast-iron skillet that has been dusted with cornmeal.
Sprinkle cheese evenly over batter.
Sprinkle meat over cheese.
Sprinkle chopped onion and jalapenos evenly over meat.
Top with remaining batter and bake at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Serve hot.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine cookie crumbs, 2 tablespoons sugar and butter.
Press 1 cup of mixture into buttered pan.
Chill.
Save remaining crumbs for top.
Beat egg yolks until thick; add condensed milk.
Add lemon rind, juice and almond extract; stir until thick.
Beat egg whites; add remaining sugar, beating until stiff.
Fold into condensed milk and lemon mixture.
Pour into pan; top with crumbs. Freeze for 4 to 6 hours.
In ovenproof skillet saute beef, onions and peppers with seasonings until meat is no longer pink and vegetables are tender. Stir frequently to crumble meat.
Add tomatoes and rice.
Top with cheese and bake at 350° until cheese melts.
Broil eggplants until tender.
Peel and mash.
Set aside. Chop garlic finely and add to mashed eggplant.
Add vinegar and salt and pepper to taste.
Cut tenderloin into strips.
Sprinkle with soy sauce and lemon pepper.
Roll tenderloin into a roll and wrap with one strip of bacon.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until tender.
Sift 3 1/2 cups flour with salt.
Soften yeast in half the water, stir into flour.
Beat egg whites lightly.
Add sugar, eggs and oil to remaining lukewarm water.
Blend with flour mixture. Beat to make dough, adding more flour if needed.
Add raisins and cinnamon.
Knead until smooth.
Place in oiled bowl.
Cover with damp cloth.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Punch down until air is out.
Pull off pieces of dough and roll into ropes.
Moisten ends and squeeze slightly to seal.
Let stand for 10 minutes. Slide a few at a time into boiling water.
Turn after one minute. Cook one minute on other side.
Remove.
Mix egg yolk with 1 teaspoon cold water.
Brush on top of bagels.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 425° to 450° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Salt and pepper and brown pork chops, then put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt margarine.
Add 1/4 cup of water.
Pour over bread, onion and poultry seasoning.
Put bread dressing on top of chops. Mix 1 can of cream of mushroom soup and 1/2 soup can of water. Pour over chops and dressing.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cover with foil.
In large bowl combine 3 cups flour, undissolved yeast and salt.
Stir very warm water and olive oil into dry ingredients. Stir in enough remaining flour to make soft dough.
Knead dough on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Cover and rest on floured surface for 10 minutes.
Dissolve jello and salt in boiling water.
Break up jellied cranberry sauce with fork; add to gelatin mixture.
Chill until very thick before folding in apples.
Peel apples and finely grate.
Fold apples into mixture.
Pour into an 8 x 8-inch pan. Chill until firm.
Serves 6.
Mix together the water and iced tea mix, then add orange and cranberry juice.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In medium mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar and baking powder.
Cut in oleo with pastry blender or 2 knives until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Add remaining ingredients and stir just until mixture forms a sticky dough and leaves sides of the bowl (do not overmix).
Spray 12 muffin pan cups (2 1/2 inches) with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon an equal amount of pineapple mixture into each cup.
Bake until muffins are golden brown, 30 to 35 minutes.
Remove muffins to a wire rack and let cool.
Serve immediately or wrap individually and freeze until ready to use.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Cool and add other ingredients, stirring to blend them in.
Put in refrigerator until firm.
May be served on lettuce leaf with mayonnaise and paprika as a garnish.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine All-Bran, milk and molasses.
Let stand until most of the moisture is taken up.
Add egg and oil; beat well.
Stir in raisins.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Sift together the dry ingredients.
Add to wet mixture, stirring only until combined.
In saucepan, cook apple, coconut and onion with curry in butter until tender.
Add soup; pour into blender and blend until smooth. Return mixture to saucepan; gradually stir in milk and yogurt. Heat and stir occasionally.
Garnish with sliced apple.
Makes about 3 cups or 4 servings.
On wax paper, sift together first 5 ingredients.
In large bowl, beat eggs on high speed until yolks and whites are combined. Gradually add sugar, beating until lemon color (thick).
Beating continually, pour in corn oil.
With mixer at low speed, blend in sifted dry ingredients alternately with pumpkin, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Beat until smooth after each addition.
Stir in nuts.
Turn into ungreased angel food pan. Bake in 350° oven for about 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar if desired.
In large
skillet over low heat, cook vegetables in oil with seasonings for about 5 minutes, tossing frequently.
Add kielbasa slices
and
water.
Cover and
cook over medium low heat, 15
to 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender, tossing occasionally.
Dissolve yeast in warm water in large warm bowl.
Add sugar, salt, warm milk, butter, 3 eggs and 1 cup flour.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in enough more flour to make a soft dough.
On floured board, knead 8 to 10 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; turn to grease top.
Cover; let rise in warm, draft-free place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Punch dough down; cover bowl tightly. Refrigerate 5 hours.
Cut elephant into bite size chunks.
This should take about 6 months.
Cook over bonfire about 6 weeks.

Add potatoes, onions, carrots, salt and pepper. Stew the tomatoes, then add those. Serves about 5,000, but if more are expected, add the rabbits but only if necessary since most people do not like hare in their stew.
Dissolve jellos in hot water.
Add and stir in cottage cheese, pineapple, mayonnaise, lemon juice and horseradish mustard.
Pour into mold and chill.
Serves 8 to 10.
Mix white cake mix as directed on box. Bake. After cake has baked, poke holes in it with a fork.
Dissolve the Jell-O in the hot water and then add the cold water.
Pour over cake. Chill awhile.
Make vanilla pudding as directed on box. Spread over cake. Spread whipped topping over that.
Wash beans.
Put in pot.
Bring to a boil.
Cook until beans are swollen.
Drain water off.
Put beans in a baking pot and add water to cover.
Add molasses, pork, salt and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 6 1/2 to 8 hours in oven.
Check often and add more water, if needed.
Measure the tomato juice and pour into large bowl.
Sprinkle yeast over juice and stir to dissolve.
Add honey.
Beat in one egg.
Add the first 4 cups of flour, one cup at a time, stirring briskly after each addition.
After adding flour, beat the mixture 100 strokes, until very smooth.
Cover bowl and let dough rest 45 minutes in warm place.
Combine dry ingredients in large mixing bowl.
Add eggs, syrup, vanilla and margarine.
Beat with electric mixer until blended.
Stir in pecans.
Pour mixture in pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
Slice watermelon lengthwise 1/3 from top.
Cut the edge with a sharp knife.
Scoop the watermelon out in balls* removing all visible seeds.
Scoop out the scraps inside the watermelon and chill the "bowl".
Cut balls* from other melons.
Prepare grapes. Combine juices and sugar.
Pour over fruit in a large bowl.
Stir occasionally.
Just before serving, fill the melon bowl with fruit.
Chop onion into moon shapes.
Put 1 Tbsp. olive oil into skillet and add onion.
Cover and cook until clear.
Add black pepper, cinnamon, saffron and salt.
Cook uncovered; add raisin and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add sugar and simmer until begins to thicken and sauce is golden.
Stew and debone chicken.
Cool and cut into bite size pieces. Saute onions in margarine.
Drain both cans of tomatoes and reserve the liquid.
Add drained tomatoes to onions and simmer until liquid is reduced, about 10 minutes.
Add cheese, stirring until melted.
Add chicken; mixture should be thick.
Fry tortillas in oil over medium heat to soften.
Drain.
Place a heaping tablespoonful of chicken mixture on each tortilla and roll up.
Place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Thin remaining chicken mixture with some of the reserved tomato juice from both cans of tomatoes and pour over the enchiladas.
Spread with sour cream. Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine softened cream cheese, ground fine shrimp, eggs, sauces and salt.
Shape into roll about 2-inches in diameter. Combine chopped parsley and pecans and place in tray.
Roll shrimp mixture in parsley and pecans until well covered.
Chill.

Combine cream cheese and whipping cream in a little crock-pot. Cover and heat until cheese is melted (approximately 30 to 60 minutes). Add remaining ingredients. Cover and heat for 30 minutes. Serve with raw vegetables, crackers or bread pieces.
Brown beef and drain.
Add taco seasoning, water and beans. Cook for 15 minutes.
Let guests build their own sundae in the following order:
steamed rice, meat-bean mixture, corn, lettuce, tomatoes, olives, cheese and salsa.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Place peeled and diced apples in baking dish topped with sugar.
Combine other ingredients; mixture should look crumbly. Pour on top of apples. Bake at 375° for 35 minutes. Cool. Serve with Cool Whip.
Combine seafood, vegetables, mayo, Worcestershire, salt and 3/4 cup bread crumbs.
Put into a large casserole dish.
Mix remaining crumbs with melted butter and sprinkle on top of seafood mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes or until crumbs are browned.
Arrange chicken,
meat
side
down,
in a well buttered casserole
dish
or
Dutch
oven.
Cover
with
carrots,
then potatoes.
Sprinkle
with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over all.
Cover and bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Remove and turn chicken.
Add
broccoli and cauliflower;
cover again and bake 30 to 35 minutes more, adding green pepper, mushrooms and zucchini during the last 10 minutes.
Mix eggs, oil, water, pudding and cake mix together.
Pour in cake pan.
Bake at 350° until done.
Brown meat in medium saucepan.
Add water, bouillon cubes, tomatoes, vegetables, onion and garlic powders.
Bring to boil and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in rice, simmer 5 minutes longer.
In medium bowl, blend egg yolks, syrup, ginger, cloves, cinnamon and nutmeg until spices have dissolved.
In another bowl, beat egg whites until a little stiff.
Add sugar and continue beating until stiff.
Pour lemon and orange juice in punch bowl. Add egg yolk mixture, then fold in stiff egg whites.
Add ice cream (in chunks).
Pour ginger ale over eggnog mixture.
Stir and serve.

recipes.t: Pennsylvania Dutch Cinnamon Flop(Breakfast Bread Or Dessert)
d: Cream tablespoon of butter and sugar together.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder together.
Alternate milk and dry mix as you mix into creamed butter and sugar.
Mix until smooth.
Drain potatoes and apricot juice (save enough to make 1 1/4 cup liquid).
Dice potatoes into bite size pieces.
Arrange in layers of potatoes, apricots and nuts.
Mix dry ingredients in saucepan.
Over low heat, slowly add apricot juice.
Stir until thick.
Add margarine and pour over layered ingredients.
Heat 25 to 35 minutes at 375° (9 x 13-inch casserole).
Serves 10 to 12.
Chill lemon-lime beverage and fruit juice in advance.
At serving time combine pineapple, orange and cranberry juices in punch bowl.
Gently pour in lemon-lime.
Add scoops of sherbet and serve.
Yields 24 cups.
Wrap bacon around chicken and line a dish with chipped beef. Mix the rest of the ingredients together and pour over top.
Bake at 275° for 2 hours.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Peel, cube, and boil potatoes in salted water until done. Drain well and mash potatoes; add butter, salt, pepper, and 1/2 cup cheese; stir.
Add bacon bits and sour cream; stir well and pour in a Pam sprayed casserole dish.
Top with remaining cheese and bake at 350 degrees until cheese melts.
Spread raisins directly into uncooked pie shell.
Mix together flour, sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle over raisins.
Pour milk over raisins.
Dot with the margarine.
Bake at 400° until set, 40 to 60 minutes.
Measure water into large mixer bowl.
Sprinkle yeast over water.
Add cereals, sugar, salt, oil, bouquet sauce and 2 cups flour.
Blend well.
Beat 3 minutes at medium speed of mixer.
By hand, gradually add remaining flour to form a very stiff dough, beating well after each addition.
Cover dough with waxed paper or plastic wrap; let rest 15 minutes.
Fry bacon crisp.
Drain on paper towel and crumble.
Saute onion in drippings.
Drain beans; add to onions.
Add crumbled bacon and the chili sauce.
Add the water, salt and pepper. Simmer until done.
The longer you simmer, the better the flavor. Serves 8 to 10.
Put chicken pieces into 9 x 13-inch
dish.
(I usually melt about 1/2 stick oleo and pour over this to keep it from being so dry, but it isn't necessary.)
Mix together the soup, sour cream and lemon juice and spoon on top of chicken.
Sprinkle buttered Ritz crumbs over top.
Bake at 350° about 30 to 45 minutes until bubbly.
Stir together sugar, flour and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg. Stir in juice or water; toss to coat. Add 2 cups bread cubes. Toss until mixed. Transfer to an ungreased 2-quart square pan.
In skillet, saute in oil the garlic and spices for about 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in remaining ingredients except chicken.
Bring this to a boil, then cover and turn down heat to simmer for 50 minutes. Thicken with cornstarch and water, if
desired.

Saute onions, green pepper and tomatoes in stewer. Then add your stew meat, bouillon cube and potatoes. Fill stewer with enough water to cover potatoes. Add any seasonings you like. Cover and let simmer.
Fry beef, bacon and onion until tender.
Drain and add remaining ingredients.
Simmer at least 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Melt
butter
and cocoa.
Mix all ingredients together. Fills two pie shells.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Grease lightly a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Put in thick layer of cabbage.
Brown meat and onion in skillet.
Drain.
Spoon mixture over cabbage along with rice.
Heat soup and water just to boiling.
Pour over all ingredients.
Sprinkle cabbage over top and sprinkle cheese over top of cabbage.
Cover with foil.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Mix jello, milk, coconut and extract.
Shape like strawberries.
Make red sugar by dropping 1 to 2 drops of red food color into white sugar.
Roll strawberries in sugar.
Color almonds green with green food coloring.
Put 2 almonds into top of strawberry for leaf.

Wrap tortillas in foil; bake at 350° about 12 minutes or until heated through. In 10-inch skillet, cook onion and garlic in oil 5 minutes or until softened, stirring occasionally. Add bell peppers; cook 2 minutes. Partially mash one can of beans with wooden spoon or potato masher.

Add mashed beans, remaining can of beans, salsa and cumin to skillet; cook over low heat 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sprinkle 1/2 cup shredded cheese down center of each warmed tortilla. Spoon bean mixture over cheese. Top with cilantro, if desired, then roll up. Makes 4 servings.
Place peppers on towel and pat dry.
Combine cream cheese, sour cream and mayonnaise.
Then combine parsley and green onions. Spread very thin layer of cheese mixture on tortilla.
Then layer with roasted peppers.
Wrap up like jelly roll.
Wrap up roll in plastic wrap for about 2 hours in fridge.
Unwrap, slice and serve. Time Saver Alternative:
Substitute cream cheese, sour cream and mayo for (onion/chive Weis brand cream cheese).
Cook rice; chop peppers and mix with sour cream in top of food processor, then stir in rice, sour cream and pepper mixture with shredded Monterey Jack cheese.
Put in 9 x 13-inch pan and spread top with shredded Cheddar cheese.
Saute celery, pepper and onion until tender, but not brown. Add meat and stir until blended.
Add chicken broth and thicken with cornstarch.
Add salt and pepper and simmer about 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, arrange tomato wedges on top.
Serve over hot, cooked rice.
Chop mandarins into small pieces, mix in 1 tablespoon of the reserved syrup and the marshmallow cream.
This is great served over pound cake or sponge cake.
Cut small rounds of thin white bread with 1 to 1 1/2-inch cutter.
Butter one side of bread; spread other side with Durkee sauce.
Put into large frying pan.
Top sauce with small canned shrimp or fresh cleaned shrimp (cooked).
Top with another tiny dab of Durkee sauce and tiny parsley leaf.
Can refrigerate until ready to cook or fry until golden brown on bottom.
Serve immediately after heating.
Lightly brown nuts in oil in large nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Remove with slotted spoon.
Saute onion and garlic in skillet 2 minutes.
Add chicken.
Saute until golden brown, about 8 minutes.
Add broccoli, 3/4 cup broth and soy.
Simmer, covered, 5 minutes.
Dissolve cornstarch in remaining 1/4 cup broth.
Stir into skillet.
Simmer, stirring over medium heat until thickened.
Boil 1 minute.
Return cashews to skillet with salt and pepper.
Combine orange juice, ice water, lemon juice and pineapple juice.
Mix thoroughly and chill.
To serve, pour half the mixture into a large punch bowl and add 2 quarts of ginger ale.
Use the rest of the mixture and ginger ale as needed to keep the punch alive.
The punch may be sweetened with sugar dissolved in water, if desired.
Serves 100.

recipes.t: Bacon Stuffed Mushrooms By Mom Morrison
d: Clean mushrooms.
Remove stems and set them aside to use later.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Chop mushroom stems and saute with onion in butter.
When golden, add cream cheese, parsley, lemon pepper seasoning and onion salt. Cook only 1 minute or until cream cheese melts.
Crumble bacon and add to mixture.
Place 1 teaspoon of mixture into each mushroom. Bake mushrooms at 375° for 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
Turn kraut into colander and drain, pressing out all liquid. Combine in bowl the kraut, pimentos, onion, celery, carrots and green pepper.
In small bowl mix vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper, then stir until dissolved.
Then pour over vegetable mix.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Keeps well in refrigerator.
Cream butter and 3/4 cup sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the egg yolk and vanilla, beating until thick and silky.
Stir flour, cocoa and salt; mix thoroughly.
Add this butter-sugar mixture and stir until moistened.
Spread dough in ungreased 8 x 8-inch baking pan and put in the freezer to chill for 10 minutes. Heat oven to 325°.
Stir raspberry jam to make it smooth.
Spread over chilled dough and freeze for 5 minutes.
Beat egg whites until frothy and brush about 1/2 over cold raspberry jam.
Scatter walnuts on top and press into place.
Bake at 325° for 35 minutes. Remove from the oven and sprinkle with sugar.
Makes 16 small squares.
Mix cornbread mix, oil and eggs.
Add remaining ingredients and bake at 400° for 45 minutes in casserole dish.
Heat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease 2 cookie sheets.
Mix flour and baking soda.
In a large bowl beat butter, sugar and vanilla with electric mixer until fluffy.
Stir in oats, flour mixture and 1/3 cup chocolate chips until blended.
Divide dough in half. Place half in middle of each cookie sheet and spread into an 8-inch circle.
Sprinkle one with remaining 2 tablespoons chocolate chips, then score into 8 wedges with a sharp knife.
Bake both 15 minutes, turning cookie sheets and switching over positions once, until light brown and crisp looking.
Cool on sheets 10 minutes before removing to racks to cool completely.
Brown hamburger mixture in large pan.
In separate pan, cook spaghetti until tender.
Drain both.
Add tomato juice and remaining ingredients; stir occasionally.
Continue to heat until hot.
Serve with cheese topping.
Dredge fruit in some flour.
Cream sugar and margarine.
Add eggs, then other ingredients.
Mix well and put into miniature paper baking cups.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Makes 11 to 12 dozen.

recipes.t: Roast Wild Goose With Baked Apple
d: Cook goose giblets until tender.
Chop and add to stuffing made by mixing bread crumbs, onion, fat, sage, salt and pepper. After blending and washing the goose thoroughly, stuff, sew the neck and back closed.
Roast for 15 minutes at 500°.
Reduce the heat to 350° and cook about 1 1/2 hours.
Wash and core apples; sprinkle with brown sugar.
Stuff with seasoned sweet potatoes. Bake until tender; serve hot with goose.
Drain and flake salmon.
Saute onion in 2 tablespoons butter. Combine with other ingredients using 1 cup crumbs.
Put in casserole and cover with 1/4 cup crumbs and dot with 1 tablespoon butter.
Bake at 350°
for 45 minutes.
Melt butter in a skillet.
Add shallots and cook gently 3 minutes.
Add brandy to pan and allow to heat through a few seconds, then flame.
When flames subside, add wine to shallots. Stir in stock and peppercorns and boil rapidly 2 to 3 minutes or until slightly reduce.
Remove from heat and stir in cream and chopped parsley.
Return to medium heat and heat through 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Garnish with parsley sprigs, if desired.
Makes 3/4 cup.
Discard seeds from melon and with melon baller, cut out balls. Combine melon balls with chicken, grapes, celery and almonds.
Mix together remaining ingredients and gently fold into chicken mixture.
Fill melon shells.
Serves 2.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove from drippings, drain, crumble and set aside.
Add vegetables and chili powder to drippings. Stir, cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes or until corn is tender.
(Stir occasionally to keep from sticking.)
Add salt and pepper; mix well.
Pour into serving dish; sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Serve hot.
Yield:
6 servings.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Cool slightly.
Pour over ice cream and stir well (use hand mixer to blend thoroughly).
Add fruit cocktail and crushed pineapple including the juice from both. Stir and chill until set.
You can add some chopped pecans to this recipe if you desire.
Add yeast to lukewarm milk; let stand until dissolved.
Add sugar, salt and shortening; mix well.
Add 2 whole eggs and beat again.
Add flour (1 cup at a time), beating after each addition.
Peel and slice eggplant.
Boil in water until tender, then drain.
Cook beef in skillet with oil (if needed).
Add onions and bell pepper.
Cook, stirring, until nicely browned.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper and oregano.
Blend, then add tomato sauce. Arrange slices of eggplant in baking dish alternately with meat sauce and cheese.
Repeat in layers with cheese on top.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Place chicken in crock-pot.
Drain corn and peas.
Add to crock-pot.
Peel potatoes and cut in cubes.
Add to chicken and vegetables.
Pour tomato sauce over chicken, potatoes and vegetables.
Cover and cook on low setting 4 to 6 hours.
Can also be baked at 350° for an hour.
Parboil potatoes and
carrots
in
salted water 20 minutes. Drain.
Combine
soup, milk and catsup.

Butter a 13 x 9 x 2-inch cake pan.
Line with marshmallows. Mix cake mix as directed on box.
Pour over marshmallows.
Pour pineapple over cake batter.
Bake as directed on box.
No need to ice. Makes very moist cake.
In large bowl, combine the 6 cups milk with 2 boxes pudding mix.
Mix thoroughly and place in fridge to firm up.
In another large mixing bowl, mix the cream cheese (softened) with mixer. Add Eagle Brand milk until smooth and stir in vanilla.
Fold 1 container Cool Whip into pudding mix, then follow with cream cheese mixture and sliced bananas.
Stir bananas in well.
Arrange vanilla wafers in a big, big or two regular bowls and alternate with layers of pudding mixture.
Top with other container of Cool Whip.
Melt margarine over low heat.
Add flour.
Stir until smooth. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add milk.
Cook on medium heat.
Stir constantly until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in turkey, mixed vegetables, bouillon granules and pepper.
Cook until heated well over medium heat.
Spoon into 9-inch dish.
Cover with crescent rolls or pie crust.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes or until brown.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Take roast and cut in small pieces.
Put in large skillet and cook with lid on for 20 minutes.
Then add sliced mushrooms, onions and green peppers.
Add as much as you like.
Take your potatoes and quarter them, then slice them in small pieces and add to meat and other vegetables.
Cook until tender.
Brown rice slowly in skillet.
Add 2 3/4 cups hot water.
Stir in contents of flavoring packet.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes. Add olives, green pepper, celery and onions.
Cook until liquid is gone.
Chop artichokes, saving liquid.
Combine mayo and artichoke liquid.
Add curry, salt, pepper and garlic.
Combine with rice.
Add chicken.
Refrigerate.
Scrape carrots; cut into diagonal slices, about 1/4 to 1/2-inch thick.
Place in ungreased baking dish.
Stir together butter, juice, sugar, mustard and salt.
Pour over carrots.
Cook, covered, 30 to 40 minutes at 375° until carrots are tender.
If using microwave, cook carrots with small amount of water until almost done, add sauce and cook 2 or 3 more minutes.
Garnish with toasted almonds or pecans.
Serves 4.
Chop green onions and mince until fine.
Combine with sour cream, mayonnaise and salts. Set overnight prior to serving.
Pour water over hoarhound.
Allow to stand 10 minutes. Strain.
Combine sugar, salt, syrup and water from hoarhound. Boil to soft crack stage.
Pour in thin sheet into well buttered baking sheet.
Mark into squares before candy hardens.
Blend cream cheese, butter and flour.
Chill 1 hour.
Shape into small balls and place in ungreased 1 3/4 inch muffin cups. Press dough on bottom and sides.
Mix mayonnaise, chilli sauce, kraut, corn beef and Swiss cheese and fill cups.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 300° until brown.
Yields about 5 dozen.
Mix cake and bake as directed. Cool. Mix vanilla pudding as directed. Spread on top.
Mix chocolate pudding as directed and spread on top of vanilla. Top with Cool Whip and sprinkle pecans on top.
Leave in pan and refrigerate.
Place meat strips in plastic bag or bowl; add Italian dressing, turning to coat strips.
Tie bag securely or cover bowl and marinate in refrigerator 3 hours or longer.
Tear spinach into pieces and place in large salad bowl.
Drain marinade from meat, reserving marinade.
Add meat, artichoke hearts, onions and olives to spinach; toss lightly.
Add tomatoes and reserved marinade, as desired, and toss lightly to combine.
Makes 6 servings.
First, prepare to steam lobsters as follows: Combine the wine, water, garlic, lemon juice, sherry and salt in a pot large enough to hold the lobsters.
Bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Quickly place the lobsters in the pot and cover with a lid.
Cook until lobsters turn bright red (about 12 minutes).
Remove the lobsters from the pot and set aside until cool enough to handle. Now prepare ingredients for chowder.
Mix jellos and hot water and cold water.
Let set.
After this is set, add cream cheese, sugar, vanilla and cream.
Mix jello and cream cheese mixture well, then pour into an 8 x 12-inch pan lined with slices of angel food cake.
Refrigerate until well set.
Saute butter and garlic, then add shrimp and mushrooms.
Saute for approximately 5 minutes, or until shrimp are pink.
Add half and half, Velveeta cheese, and pepper.
Saute for a minute or two, then add Parmesan cheese and saute approximately 10 minutes. Serve over angel hair pasta.
Makes about 6 servings.
Boil and debone chicken.
Place chicken in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Place sliced eggs on chicken; add soup and chicken broth. Combine other ingredients and pour over chicken.
Do not stir! Bake at 400° for 30 to 40 minutes or until brown on top.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Drain well and crumble into small pieces.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine bacon, cheese, green onions, mayonnaise and cayenne.
Mix thoroughly.
Place almonds in the bottom of an oiled 7-cup ring mold.
Press cheese mixture into mold. Refrigerate overnight.
Unmold cheese ring onto platter. Place a small custard cup filled with strawberry preserves in the center of the ring.
Serve with crackers or French bread slices. Yields 20 to 25 servings.
Cream together sugar, shortening and eggs.
Add cooked cereal, then add all dry ingredients.
Bake 12 minutes at 375°.
Sift together into bowl, Softasilk, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add shortening, 2/3 cup milk, extract and vanilla.
Beat vigorously with spoon for 2 minutes by clock (about 150 strokes per minute).
Or mix with electric mixer on medium speed (middle of dial) for 2 minutes.
Add the rest of milk and egg yolks.
Beat 2 more minutes.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Pan size:
2 round layers, 8 x 1 1/2-inch.
Temperature:
350° (moderate oven). Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool.
Frost with White Mountain Icing.
Rinse lentils; drain.
Combine in saucepan lentils, onion and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Stir in brown sugar, catsup, molasses and oil.
Turn into 1-quart bean pot or casserole dish and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 1/4 hours.
Thaw frozen unbaked bread in microwave.
Spread on greased and floured pizza pan or cookie sheet.
Spread to 1/2-inch of edge. Spread 4 to 6 cloves garlic steeped in 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Top with Parmesan cheese and oregano.
Bake at 450° for 10 to 15 minutes.
In a medium bowl, dissolve the sugar in 1/2 cup of the water. Sprinkle with yeast on top; set aside until it starts to foam, about 5 minutes.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large mixing bowl. Beat at medium speed until well blended.
Fold in whipped topping.
Spoon mixture into pie crust and sprinkle with peanuts. Chill 8 hours. Makes 1 pie.
Cream
together with mixer the cream cheese and butter. Add 1 box confectioners sugar and mix well. Add the second box of confectioners
sugar
and
1/4 cup warm water and mix well. Add the
melted
German
chocolate. Take out 2 1/2 cups of the mixture and
reserve
it
for
frosting. Add to the remaining mixture the shortening and eggs (one at a time) and mix well.
In a 3 1/2-quart saucepan, heat oil and brown ribs.
Turn burner to low-medium heat.
Layer potatoes, sauerkraut and onion. Continue layers until finished. Garnish with scallion.
Salt and pepper. Cover and cook for 2 to 3 hours until pork is tender.
Make a cream sauce of butter, flour and milk; add horseradish, mustard, salt and pepper.
Saute mushrooms, onion, celery, green pepper and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder to taste.
When sauteed lightly, add the mayonnaise.
Butter six slices of bread on both sides and cut in 1-inch squares.
Put half of bread in casserole; add sauteed vegetables.
Add rest of buttered bread.
Beat eggs and milk.
Pour over all and refrigerate a few hours or overnight.
Take raw fresh artichokes and wash and core centers.
Break middle and remove, leaving cup like artichoke.
Set aside.
Mix together thoroughly the shredded crab, diced onion and the cheese. Mix to consistency with mayonnaise.
Add salt, pepper, Italian seasoning and garlic salt to taste.
Mix well to consistency of salad dressing.
Stuff center of artichokes with mixture.
Set in deep baking dish.
Fill 1/2 of the way with water.
Cover and bake for 1 hour or until tender.
Remove and serve; pull hot leaves off and dip in melted center.
Enjoy.
Slice carrots and cook in water until tender, drain.
Remove carrots, set aside and keep warm.
In the same saucepan;
combine sugar, cornstarch, salt and ginger.
Gradually stir in orange juice;
bring to a boil.
Cook and stir 2 minutes, add butter, return carrots to pan;
heat through.
Sprinkle with parsley, if desired.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water, stirring well.
Put in refrigerator until it starts to set, then add pineapple, lemon juice and salad dressing.
Fold in whipped cream.
Put into mold and chill until firm.
Nuts can also be added.
Wash and peel potatoes.
Grate or put in food processor set for coarse.
Pour into mixing bowl.
Add sugar, eggs, nutmeg, vanilla flavoring and orange juice. Baked in a glass pan or your favorite baking pan, 1/2 hour, then add margarine.
Cook about 1 hour at 375° or until potatoes are done.
Dredge livers in flour.
Heat oil and butter in large frying pan.
Cook livers 4 minutes over high heat, stirring once.
Add onion and mushrooms; season and continue cooking 4 to 5 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in chicken stock; mix and cook 4 minutes over low heat.
Mix cornstarch with water; stir into sauce and bring to boil.
Simmer 2 minutes over low heat and serve with noodles.
Trim fat from turkey and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Cook turkey, onion and mushrooms in vegetable oil until turkey is slightly brown and vegetables are tender.
Add remaining ingredients; cover and simmer for 1 hour or until vegetables are barely tender. Uncover and continue to simmer until most of liquid has evaporated.
Remove bay leaf.
Makes 4 servings.
One-thousand calorie recipe.
Cook peas according to package directions.
Meanwhile, combine soup, sour cream and milk in a
1 1/2-quart casserole.
Carefully stir in noodles, peas, ham and mushrooms; cover.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes, or until hot.
Serves 4 or 6.
In a small pitcher, stir together tomato juice or vegetable juice, lime juice or lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish and hot pepper sauce.
Pour tomato mixture into an 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Cover and freeze for 1 to 2 hours or until slushy.
Spoon into glasses. If desired, garnish with celery sticks.
Makes 2 (8-ounce) servings.
Boil black-eyed peas until tender.
Fry up chicken, onions, garlic, thyme and scallions until chicken is cooked.
Combine eggs, peas, onions and water chestnuts with mayonnaise, mustard, salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or more.
Just before serving, lightly toss in noodles. Reserve a few to sprinkle on top.
Stir together egg, sugar and vanilla.
Add flour, salt and soda.
Add pecans and raisins.
Bake in an 8 or 9-inch square pan for 20 minutes at 350°.
Cookies are soft when taken from oven. Cool in pan.
Cut in squares.
Combine tomatoes and cornstarch.
Cook over medium heat until clear and thickened.
Stir in onions.
Pour vegetables into 1 quart casserole dish.
Combine cheese, egg and salt; mix well. Spoon rounded ??? of cheese mixture around edge of the casserole. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
In small bowl combine crumbs and seasonings.
Dip chicken strips in water, then crumb mixture.
Press crumbs to thoroughly coat.
Spray baking sheet with Pam.
Arrange chicken on sheet and sprinkle evenly with remaining crumbs.
Bake at 350° until tender, about 20 minutes.
Clean zucchini; peel lightly and cut off stems.
Cut in 3-inch lengths.
Run apple corer through center of the zucchini lengthwise and pull out the center.
Chop the centers very fine and add bread crumbs, then cheese, egg, onion, parsley, salt and pepper.
Mix well and pack in hollow zucchini.
Roll any remaining stuffing into small balls.
Place balls and zucchini in baking dish and pour spaghetti sauce over all; cover.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake 1/2 hour longer.
Wash quail.
Pat dry and split each down the back.
Salt and pepper each quail half and coat with flour.
Heat oil in a covered skillet and brown quail on all sides.
Reduce heat to low and add light cream.
Cook 25 minutes or until quail is tender.
Serve with hot homemade biscuits.
Cook
onion and garlic in butter until tender. Stir in rice until
thoroughly
coated. Add parsley, salt, thyme and pepper; stir
well.
Combine
broth
and water in a saucepan. Bring
to
a boil
and pour
over rice mixture.
Pour entire mixture then into a large rectangular baking dish.
Cover with foil
and
bake at 350°
for
minutes or until liquid is absorbed.
Serves 8 to 10.
Fill pan with tender poke greens; add 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Drain and add another cup of water.
Cook on low heat about 10 minutes; drain well.
Add butter and cream cheese; stir.
Add eggs and stir.
Cook in same pan until eggs are cooked. Season to taste with salt.
Cook macaroni as to directions.
Brown onion in oil.
Add meat.
Cook until lightly browned.
Drain fat.
Add remaining ingredients except macaroni, parsley and cheese.
Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes or until celery and peppers are tender.
Stir in macaroni and cook 10 minutes longer.
Garnish with parsley and cheese.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 1-quart loaf pan; set aside. In medium bowl, with fork, shred salmon.
Add butter and eggs; mix until well blended.
Stir in crackers.
In small glass measuring cup, mix buttermilk with baking soda; stir in salmon mixture. Blend.
Spoon mixture into prepared pan.
Bake 30 minutes until set.
Serves 4 to 5.
Very good!
Chop onion fine.
Shred cheese.
Mix onion and cheese together.
Add mayo and Lea & Perrins until spreadable.
Spread on bread.
Broil 1 to 2 minutes, until golden brown.
These cook easy and quick so keep an eye on them.
Cook tomatoes, onion, salt, sugar, paprika and pepper in pan for 5 minutes.
Arrange tomatoes, eggs, cheese, crumbs and butter in alternate layers in an uncovered casserole.
Top with cheese and bread crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes in 375° oven.
Arrange fruit on lettuce lined plates; serve with Peachy Dip. Yields 12 servings.
Peel and cube rutabaga.
Cook in salted water until tender. Drain, then mash rutabaga.
Melt butter; add flour and mix.
Add milk slowly and stir until thick.
Add rutabaga to white sauce and serve.
Rutabaga may also be served without mixing into white sauce.
After mashing, add a little of the salted water and serve.
Cut cabbage in small pieces, dice onion and mince garlic. Chop bacon into very fine pieces and fry until brown.
Then add onion, garlic, salt, pepper and paprika; let saute a few minutes. Now add cabbage and let saute until cabbage is wilted.
Cook noodles as directed on package, then drain and add to cabbage and bacon mixture.
Put into a baking pan and place in oven on low heat for 45 minutes.
Crumble vanilla wafers 1/4-inch thick in bottom of pie pan or oblong baking dish.
Melt margarine and mix with powdered sugar, beaten eggs and vanilla.
Mix well and cook until it thickens, about 12 to 14 minutes.
Stir constantly.
Pour cooked mixture over cookie crumbs.
Spoon thawed strawberries over that.
Top with whipped cream or whipped topping.
Sprinkle a few cookie crumbs on top.
Freeze.
Slice salt pork almost through in several places; place in large kettle.
Add 2 quarts boiling water, beans, tomatoes, onion, salt, pepper and sugar.
Cook for 30 minutes.
Add corn, cook for 3 minutes longer.
Yields 6 servings.
Beat eggs lightly; add sugar and beat.
Add flour, salt, baking powder, vanilla (little lemon extract added is good) and 1/2 cup water.
Grease and flour small muffin tins; 1 teaspoon batter in each tin.
While hot, dip in 1 pound powdered sugar, juice of 2 oranges and 1 lemon with rinds (or small can of frozen orange juice and 1 can of water; use about 1/2 cup of juice).
Add dash of salt. Place on wax paper to set.
In food processor bowl with metal blade or blender container, combine chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, basil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Process until smooth.
Score edges of ham slice to prevent curling.
Place ham in glass baking dish.
Arrange yams over ham.
Spoon on pineapple and marmalade.
Cover loosely with plastic wrap.
Cook for 13 minutes.
Let stand for 5 minutes, then serve.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Mix all cheeses, onion flakes, garlic salt, and dried parsley flakes.
Form into 2 balls and roll in chopped pecans.
Bread and fry chicken cutlets 2 minutes on each side (cut cutlets in half).
In saucepan, melt butter; blend in flour.
Add salt, pepper and milk until bubbly and thick.
Remove from heat. Stir in wine.
In large saucepan over low heat, melt the chocolate and butter.
Remove from heat and add sugar, flour, salt, vanilla and eggs.
Mix well.
Spread half of batter in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Reserve remaining batter.
In a medium bowl, combine coconut, milk, vanilla and almond extract.
Mix well and spread evenly over chocolate batter.
Spread remaining chocolate batter evenly over coconut filling.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Sprinkle chocolate pieces over hot bars and let stand one minute.
Spread evenly over bars.
Toss crabmeat with juice of lemon and set aside.
Saute garlic cloves, parsley and oregano in 4 tablespoons of butter.
Add crabmeat and saute just until well heated.
Serve on rounds of toast with a tossed salad and parslied noodles.
Combine soup and sour cream in a flat bowl large enough to hold a flat corn tortilla.
Combine olives, onion and cheese.
Pour enough sour cream mixture to sparsely cover bottom of Pam-sprayed 9 x 13-inch pan.
Fry each tortilla soft, blot on paper towels.
Dip each tortilla, both sides, in soup/sour cream mixture and place 2 tablespoons of cheese/onion/olive mixture in middle.
Roll and place in pan.
Bake at 350° until bubbling (about 30 minutes).
Mash Feta cheese with a fork.
Add egg yolks, egg, parsley and pepper.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Keep warm, but do not allow to brown.
In bowl, add sugar, salt and 1/2 of flour; mix well.
Use the rest of flour for kneading.
Cover with a dough cloth and let rise until double in size.
Roll out 1/4 to 1/2-inch thick.
Cut in squares.
Brown ground beef, onions, salt and pepper.
Cook until done.
Drain off fat.
Cook cabbage until color turns.
Drain and add to meat mixture.
Add 1 tablespoon mixture to each square and bake in a 350° oven until brown.
Good to serve with a cheese sauce.
Place macaroni, soup, milk, water and chopped onion in a 2-quart ovenware casserole dish, covered.
Cook for 15 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Add corned beef and cheese.
Cover with onion rings.
Cook 3 to 5 minutes or until mixture bubbles along edges.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Brown ground beef and sausage in skillet.
Drain.
Place in an 8-inch square casserole dish.
Top with pizza sauce and cheese. Combine Bisquick, milk and eggs.
Beat until smooth.
Pour over casserole.
Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serves 6.
Prick pastry shells with fork.
Sprinkle pecans in bottom of shells and bake at 425° until golden brown.
Mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip together.
Spread half of this mixture over the bottom of each cooled pie shell.
Mix first six ingredients and pour into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Lay the pieces of chicken on top of mixture.
Sprinkle the dry onion soup mix over this.
Seal tightly with foil.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Add almonds over top after baking.
Rub salt and pepper over breast.
Make cuts 2-inches apart through meat.
Place in crock-pot.
Melt cubes in hot water and mix with soup and mushrooms.
Pour over turkey and cook on high 3 to 4 hours.
Lower heat and cook 4 to 5 more hours. Turn halfway through cooking time.
In a 9-inch skillet, heat oil.
Add onion, garlic and basil; cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and dill.
Reduce to low and add scallops.
Cook until they turn opaque.
Spray a large casserole dish with Pam.
Layer potatoes, onion, carrots and pepper.
Pour tomatoes and water over ingredients in a dish.
Place sausage on top and add salt and pepper to taste. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a medium bowl, combine bran, cereal, oats and boiling water.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Add melted butter, eggs, buttermilk, molasses, honey, vanilla and raisins.
In a large bowl, blend flours, soda and salt.
Add liquid to dry ingredients; mix lightly just until blended.
Spoon into muffin cups.
Bake in a 400° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes one dozen regular or 6 large muffins.
Dilute cream of mushroom soup with milk.
Put in double boiler and stir in Velveeta cheese and Worcestershire sauce.
Have water boiling and stir until cheese melts.
Add tuna.
Serve on bread, toast or crackers.
Melt chocolate.
Stir in peppermint oil.
Dip crackers in chocolate and put on cookie sheets covered with waxed paper. Refrigerate until chocolate is solid.
Then remove to a container and store in refrigerator.
Cut chicken into thin slices.
Heat several tablespoons of oil in bottom of wok.
Add pineapple, several dashes of salt and enough broth to cover.
Cook for 11 minutes.
Add chicken and cornstarch, diluted in water to make a thick paste, sesame oil, brandy, soy sauce and sugar.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly. Serve.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook noodles in boiling salted water about 5 minutes; drain. Meanwhile, in large saucepan, combine cream, butter, ham and peas. Heat to melt butter.
Stir in noodles.
Cook about 5 minutes until noodles are tender.
Stir in cheese and egg yolks.
Cook and stir until thickened slightly.
Cut chicken breasts into uniform squares about 1 1/2-inches thick.
Mix cornstarch, sugar, salt, 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 2 tablespoons oil.
Add chicken and stir to coat evenly.
Saute walnuts in 1 tablespoon oil until golden.
Sprinkle with salt. Heat remaining oil.
Add chicken mixture and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add ham and walnuts and stir-fry about 5 minutes.
Stir in remaining soy sauce and broth, scraping up brown bits from bottom of pan; cook for one minute longer.
Makes 6 servings.
Skin and debone chicken.
Combine rice, cream of chicken and mushroom soups. Add the extra mushrooms. Place in baking dish. Arrange broccoli over rice mixture.
Pour diluted cheese soup over broccoli.
Puree 4 cups corn in food processor.
Beat butter in mixer until fluffy.
Beat in cornmeal, sugar, cream cheese, and salt. Stir in corn puree and 1 cup whole corn.
Blend in cream.
Pour half of mixture in buttered ceramic baking dish.
Sprinkle with half of cheese and chopped chilies.
Pour in rest of mixture and cover with remaining cheese and chilies.
Cover with foil.
Bake one hour at 375°.
Cook 20 minutes before serving.
Serves 8.
Mix both cheeses in 9-inch pie pan or glass pie plate.
Pour tomatoes over top of cheese evenly.
Beat egg in can of tomatoes to get remaining sauce out.
Pour egg over top of mixture in pan evenly.
Bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes.
Stir when removed.
Serve hot with Fritos or dipping chips/crackers.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Melt butter in a medium saucepan.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper until blended; gradually stir in milk and dry milk powder.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture boils and thickens.
In a 2-quart greased casserole, layer half the potatoes, ham cubes and sauce.
Repeat layers and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake, covered, 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 to 20 minutes longer or until potatoes are done.
Fill canner with tomatoes which have been run through the blender; simmer for several hours, removing water as it gathers. Then add peppers, onions and onion salt.
Mix remaining ingredients together, then add tomatoes and continue to simmer until reduced to about 1/2 the beginning size or until desired thickness is reached.
Ladle into hot sterilized jars; seal. Makes 4 to 5 quarts.
Combine graham cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup sugar and butter; mix well.
Lightly butter a 10-inch round, 2-inch deep cake pan. Press crumb mixture evenly into bottom of pan.
Beat cream cheese with remaining 1 1/4 cups sugar until smooth, scraping sides of bowl often.
Add eggs, one at a time beating well after each addition.
Add sour cream, lemon juice and vanilla, beating well until smooth.
Melt Tootsie Rolls in top of a double boiler.
Stir in cream, then add to cream cheese mixture, mixing well.
Pour over crust.
Bake in a 300° oven for about 2 hours or until center is set.
Cool, then chill several hours before serving.
Combine cabbage, apple and raisins.
Sprinkle with salt.
Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice and sugar together.
Stir into cabbage mixture.
In blender, put water, liquid from pumpkin and oil.
Add chopped dates and let stand 30 minutes or longer.
Blend ingredients.
Gradually add nuts, raisins and egg whites.
When completely blended, pour in large mixing bowl and add other ingredients.
Mix thoroughly.
Bake at 250° for 75 minutes or until done.
Combine dry dressing mix, Parmesan cheese and dill weed; set aside.
Put cereal, nuts and pretzels in 2-gallon bag.
Pour oil over cereal mixture.
Close bag and toss gently.
Add salad dressing mixture.
Toss gently until coated.
Store in airtight container.
Slightly beat eggs.
Blend in sugar and flour.
Heat milk.
Do not boil.
Add small amount of warm milk to sugar mixture, enough to make the mixture thin.
Then pour the mixture back into the heated milk.
Heat to a scald, stirring constantly, on medium heat for about 35 minutes.
Let cool at room temperature.
Add vanilla while cooling.
Freeze in 4-quart freezer.

recipes.t: Coquille St. Jacques In Cheese Sauce
d: Simmer scallops in wine until tender, about 5 minutes.
Drain, reserve liquid; rinse scallops in cold water.
Melt margarine in medium saucepan.
Stir in flour and salt; cook, stirring 1 minute. Gradually whisk in reserved liquid; whisk over heat until smooth. Remove from heat; stir in cheese until melted.
Stir scallops into sauce.
In shallow glass ovenproof bowls or dishes with raised lips, spread mashed potatoes over bottoms and up sides to form a cup.
Fill with scallop mixture.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 375° until sauce bubbles, 8 to 10 minutes.
Boil water, sugar and Karo for 50 minutes.
Take off heat and add coffee.
Cool to room temperature and add grain alcohol, almond extract and vanilla extract.
Pour into smaller bottles when cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream Crisco, butter and sugar; beat in the whole egg and two egg yolks.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together; combine the two mixtures and blend thoroughly. Spread batter in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle nuts, chocolate chips and marshmallows over batter.
Beat 2 egg whites stiff; fold in brown sugar.
Spread over top of cake.
Bake 35 minutes.
Cool, then cut into bars.
Great warm or cold.
Spray oblong baking dish with cooking spray.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Mix chicken soup and sour cream together.
Pour over chicken (do not dilute).
Bake for 2 hours at 250°, uncovered. Sprinkle grated cheese on top, then sprinkle crackers over top. Pour on margarine.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes longer at 350° or until lightly browned.
Combine Vegeburger, milk, onion, green pepper, salt and chili powder in a heated microwave skillet.
Cover and cook 3 minutes on full power.
Add tomato sauce and chili beans.
Mix well.
Boil first 3 ingredients together to the soft ball stage. Pour over gelatin and cold water that has soaked while syrup boiled.
Beat for 10 minutes.
Add egg whites and salt.
Pour into a pan lined with nuts, coconut or powdered sugar.
Cool in refrigerator.
Cut into squares and roll in the nuts.

Drain and flake salmon into a bowl. Fold in eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Melt butter in skillet over low heat. Slowly pour salmon mixture into skillet. Continue stirring until eggs are done, but not dry. Add paprika.
Mix cake mix, butter, egg and water.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Batter will be stiff.
Stir together pineapple, coconut and pecans.
Press onto first layer.
Mash cream cheese.
Stir in eggs, powdered sugar and pour over first two layers.
Bake
at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until top is golden brown.
Cool and cut into squares.
Drain pineapple; measure juice and add hot water to make 4 cups.
Pour over Jell-O and stir until dissolved.
Add sugar, vinegar and salt.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Add pineapple, apples (cut fine) and celery.
Serve with salad dressing topping.

Combine sugars, water and syrup in a large, heavy saucepan over medium heat. Stir to dissolve. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Continue cooking, without stirring, until candy thermometer registers 300° (a teaspoonful of syrup will separate into hard brittle threads when dropped in cold water).
Wash spareribs in cold water.
Place ribs in a pot and cover with water.
Add onions, garlic, bay leaves, salt, pepper and thyme.
Bring to a boil; lower heat and cover pot.
Simmer meat for 40 to 50 minutes or until fork-tender.
Heat oven to 450°. Remove meat from pot and place in a baking pan.
Add cabbage and potatoes to the pan that the meat was cooked in.
(Do not throw away the juices.)
Mix cream cheese and sour cream.
Grind olives, onion, shaved ham and cheese (as much of each as you'd like).
Blend both mixtures together.
Spread on tortillas.
Roll tortillas and cut into 1-inch slices.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Saute garlic and onion in olive oil until onion becomes somewhat transparent.
Add Vegeburger and continue sauteing until Vegeburger is browned.
Transfer mixture to large kettle.
Add drained kidney beans and pinto beans with liquid.
Peel and blanch tomatoes; chop and add to kettle.
Next, include tomato sauce and water and cook on medium heat until tomatoes are semi-cooked. Season as desired with suggested seasonings.
Melt butter in large Dutch oven; add onion, garlic and pepper. Saute until tender.
Stir in soup, milk, cream cheese, Cheddar cheese, corn and bouillon cubes.
Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.* Add shrimp; cover, reduce heat and cook 5 to 7 minutes.
Serve hot.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Fry crackers in margarine until golden.
Mix in macaroni, salt and pepper and stir.
Kids like a little catsup over top when served.

Combine pumpkin and sugar, mixing thoroughly. Add milk, egg and melted margarine. Stir; add remaining ingredients and pour into a greased casserole dish. Cover with Crunch Topping (see following recipe) and bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cut deer meat in pieces and brown.
Place in crock-pot.
Cover with water and then add remaining ingredients.
Cook overnight, then serve over rice.

Preheat the oven to 375°. In a stockpot, bring 4 quarts of water to a boil. Partially cook noodles in the boiling water for half the time given in the package direction. Meanwhile, grease a 1 1/2-quart casserole. In a large bowl, combine cream cheese, sour cream and milk until smooth and creamy. Stir in flaked tuna, chopped green onions and chopped bell pepper. Season with salt and pepper. Drain the noodles thoroughly and stir them into the tuna mixture. Place the noodles in the prepared casserole and sprinkle with cheese. Bake until the mixture is bubbly and the top is browned, about 25 minutes and serve.

In a medium saucepan, melt margarine over medium heat. Add onion; cook 2 minutes. Stir in flour, salt and pepper. Stir in broth and milk. Cook, stirring constantly, until bubbly and thickened. Add chicken and vegetables. Remove from heat and spoon into crust. Bake at 425° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Prepare cake mix per box instructions.
Bake and cool. Combine the cream cheese, lemon juice and Cool Whip until folded smoothly together.
Cover first cake layer with the cream cheese mixture, then evenly place prepared blueberries.
Stack second layer; cover with cream cheese mixture, then evenly top cake with prepared strawberries.
Melt butter in a 2-quart pan.
Stir in oats and brown lightly over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Set aside and cool.
Blend flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into cooled oats.
Blend egg, vanilla and nuts.
Drop by rounded teaspoonful 3-inches apart onto lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
If using canned cherries, be sure to use the cherry syrup in the liquid.
You'll get a richer color and flavor plus requests for seconds.
Cook whole potatoes in salted water until done.
Drain.
Drain peas.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Drain.
In saucepan, melt butter. Add flour, salt, pepper, paprika and milk.
Cook until thickened. Add cheese and stir until melted.
Combine potatoes and peas in greased casserole.
Pour on sauce.
Sprinkle crumbled bacon on top.
Bake in oven at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Sally'S Jelly Roll Or Ice Cream Cake
d: Beat egg whites stiff, but not dry.
Beat in 1/2 cup sugar and set aside.
Beat egg yolks with water until thick and add 1/2 cup sugar.
Combine mixtures.
Mix and sift dry ingredients.
Fold into egg mixture.
Line jelly roll pan with waxed paper and grease well.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Turn onto a sugared dish towel. Spread with jam and roll immediately.
If using ice cream, roll immediately in towel and let cake cool.
Unroll gently; fill with softened ice cream and carefully roll.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar from the sifter.
Brown meat; to the browned meat add chopped celery, onions, green peppers and garlic.
Add 2 tablespoons water; cover and steam until vegetables are tender.
Cook noodles in water and drain.
Mix all together with soup, mushrooms, salt and pepper. Spread into baking dish 2 inches deep (several, depending on size of the dish).
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Refrigerate for at least 12 hours before baking.
To heat, place casserole in a cold oven at 250° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: I Can'T Believe It'S Cauliflower Salad
d: Combine bacon, lettuce, cauliflower and green onions. At serving time, mix together mayo and sugar and pour over lettuce; mix well and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Salt and pepper chicken.
In a large skillet, heat the butter and oil; brown the chicken on both sides.
Add Jack Daniels and carefully ignite, shaking the skillet until flames go out.
Add the shallots and cook for 1 minute.
Add thyme, parsley and water; cover skillet and cook over low heat, turning occasionally, 25 to 35 minutes.
Cream together cream cheese and sour cream.
Stir into mixture the bacon bits and chopped tomatoes.
Serve with toast (one piece of bread, cut into 4 triangles).
Mix cake mix, butter, milk and egg in a bowl.
Add 3/4 c of peanuts.
Spread into greased 13x9 inch pan.
Beat egg, fold in Ricotta.
Add milk, salt and pepper.
Cook in Teflon frypan.
In a six-quart pan, saute the garlic in oil at medium heat for one minute (not until golden).
In a separate pan, cook the broccoli in three quarts of water for 5 or 6 minutes.
Remove the broccoli from the water.
Take the water from the broccoli and pour it into the pan that has the garlic and olive oil.
Season the water with salt, pepper, garlic powder, parsley and oregano.
Put the broccoli in the pan and cook again at medium to low heat for 30 minutes.
At that point, start cooking the pasta in salted water in a separate pan.
Cook both for 15 minutes (the pasta will be al dente).
Drain the pasta.
Pour the broccoli and broth over the pasta and serve.
Serves eight.
Empty pudding into bowl.
Mix juices together and use quantity as required on pudding package (in place of milk).
Mix pudding and juices together and add fruit.
Refrigerate overnight.
Fry bacon crisp; add celery, green peppers and onions.
Cook until tender. Add flour and brown. Add enough water to make adequate gravy. Pour in tomatoes and season to taste.
Simmer 30 minutes. Great over grits at a fish fry.
Melt margarine in skillet.
Sprinkle brown sugar over margarine.
Arrange pineapple slices over sugar mixture, filling center with cherries and filling in between circles of fruit with pecans.
Sprinkle coconut over all.
Pour cake batter over all. Bake in a 10-inch heavy skillet at 350° for 45 minutes.
Wash beans; remove strings.
Cut beans into 1-inch pieces. Place in a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Add water; cover and microwave at High 16 to 17 minutes, or until crisp-tender.
Drain; keep warm.
Place butter in a pie plate.
Microwave at High 50 seconds, or until melted.
Add pecans and remaining ingredients; microwave at High 2 to 3 minutes, or until onion is tender, stirring after each minute.
Pour butter mixture over beans, tossing to coat. Yields 4 servings.
Combine biscuit mix and brown sugar.
Stir in remaining ingredients until the batter is moistened; do not overbeat. Grease bottoms of 12 muffin cups.
Divide batter evenly among cups.
Bake at 400° for about 15 minutes or until golden brown.
In a saucepan, combine vinegar, oil, celery seed and salt; bring to a boil.
Stir in sugar.
Melt butter in shallow pan.
Mix in lemon juice.
Dip fish in butter mixture and lay in single layer in pan.
Sprinkle with garlic salt and pepper.
Bake about 10 minutes in a hot oven basting several times.
Finish by putting pan under broiler until fish browns slightly but is not too dry, about 5 minutes.
Scald milk in double boiler.
Soak gelatin in cold water.
Mix together sugar, cornstarch, salt and egg yolks.
Gradually pour milk into this mixture and return to double boiler.
Cook until thickened.
Remove from heat.
Add gelatin, butter and vanilla. Chill.
When mixture is cool, add beaten egg whites and pour into baked pie shell.
Sprinkle with nutmeg and chill for several hours. Spread with whipped cream and chocolate curls.
Mix first four ingredients.
Fill hamburger buns; top with tomato slice and cheese.
Wrap in aluminum foil and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix butter, mustard and basil.
Brush fish with oil.
Season with salt and pepper.
Grill fish 5 minutes on each side.
Top with a spoonful of butter.
Garnish with basil sprigs.
Pare and core apples.
Mix flour, baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Cut in shortening.
Add milk; mix to form soft dough.
Roll dough into 12 x 8-inch rectangle; cut into 6 squares.
Saute garlic in oil.
Add chicken and cook until tender.
Add cooked sausage (cut into bite sized pieces) and broccoli and saute until broccoli is tender.
Add dried tomatoes, seasonings, wine, broth and butter.
Simmer 5 minutes and toss onto cooked pasta. If desired, sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Serves 4.

recipes.t: Old-Fashioned West Virginia Blackberry Jam Cake
d: Blend sugar, spices, salt, soda, baking powder and flour. Add milk, shortening and eggs after well blended. Blend together until creamy. Add jam (or preserves). Turn into lightly greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° until cake has slightly left the pan around the sides. Nuts may be added if you wish.
Cook potatoes, covered, in boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes or until tender.
Drain.
Rinse with cold water.
Drain again.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together condensed soup, sour cream, cream cheese and butter-flavored mix.
Add 1/4 cup of the shredded Cheddar cheese, 3 tablespoons of the green onion, the skim milk, parsley, garlic salt and pepper.
Stir to combine.
Stir in the cooked potatoes.
Transfer to a 2-quart shallow casserole or rectangular baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until heated through.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted.
Sprinkle with remaining green onion.
Makes 10 side dish servings.

recipes.t: Appetizer Avocados With Hot Bacon Sauce
d: In a small saucepan over medium heat, cook 2 tablespoons water and the first 5 ingredients to boiling.
Reduce heat to low; simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Arrange avocado slices on 6 small plates.
Spoon on hot sauce; sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Pour olive oil into large oblong baking dish.
Add thick sliced potatoes, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Toss well until well coated.
Bake in hot oven 15 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Add sliced kielbasa, stirring well.
Put back in oven and bake 15 minutes longer.
Serve hot.
Beat egg yolk, then add Wesson oil, a few drops at a time, beating until mixture begins to thicken.
Then add oil more rapidly alternating with the lemon juice.
Add remaining ingredients while beating.
Pour into a covered jar.
Refrigerate. Makes about 1/2 pint.
Keep refrigerated.
Soften cream cheese and add remaining ingredients.
Roll into a ball.
Roll ball in chopped pecans.
Serve with crackers.
Soak doves in vinegar and sugar mixture.
Boil doves for 35 or 40 minutes.
Wrap each dove in bacon and secure with toothpick. Coat dove in barbecue sauce.
Cook on grill until bacon is done.
In a blender or
food processor, whirl garlic and green onion with spinach until finely chopped.
Add rest of ingredients and blend to mix well.
Taste and adjust seasonings.
Combine margarine/butter with sugar.
Add eggs one at a time. Add sour cream, vanilla, baking powder and flour.
Beat 2 minutes. Pour half of batter into a greased and floured tube or Bundt pan. Spread one 8 ounce can of whole cranberry sauce over batter.
Add the other half of the batter.
Chop dried beef, onion and nuts in blender, then mix everything with mixer.
Chill until ready to serve.
Toss together the chopped tomatoes, parsley, olive oil, garlic, basil and pepper; cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours. Cook fettuccine in boiling water until al dente; drain.
Gently toss tomato mixture with fettuccine until well combined.
Makes 8 side-dish servings.
Cook sugar, syrup and milk until mixture spins a thread.
Pour over corn flakes, nuts and coconut.
Pour onto wax paper until cool, then roll into balls.
In a heavy 9-inch skillet (with lid), cook ground beef, onion and green pepper until meat is browned.
Stir in seasoning packets.
Break up noodles in packages; pour over meat mixture. Add tomatoes with liquid.
Arrange mushrooms on top; simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat; sprinkle with cheese.
Cover; let stand for 5 minutes.
Combine flour, salt and baking powder; stir in eggs and milk. Add shortening; mix well.
Stir in ham.
Drop batter by tablespoon into deep oil heated to 375°.
Fry until golden.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with Creamy Sauce.
Yields about 2 dozen.
Boil chipped beef in pressure cooker until done (in seasoning).
Put into large container on stove and add the tomatoes, rice, salt and pepper.
Cook until ingredients are done to taste.
Cream together butter and powdered sugar.
Blend in egg yolks. Spread 1 cup
graham cracker crumbs on bottom of 9 x 5 x 3-inch dish.
Pour egg yolk mixture over crumbs.
Cover with another light layer
of
crumbs
cup).
Whip heavy cream until stiff.
Add
pineapple,
walnuts,
sugar
and
vanilla. Spread whipped cream
mixture over top layer of crumbs.
Chill 4 hours before serving.
In a large saucepan, saute onion and celery in margarine until tender.
Stir in flour and salt until blended.
Gradually add milk.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened and bubbly.
Reduce heat.
Add potatoes, parsley and paprika; heat through. Yield: 5 servings.
Mash hot sweet potatoes.
Add butter, sugar, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Add egg and 1/2 cup graham cracker crumbs.
Continue mashing until completely mixed.
Chill if not firm.
Form mixture into ball using 1/3 cup for each ball and placing 3 miniature marshmallows in center of each.
Dredge balls in graham cracker crumbs.
Place in baking pan and bake in hot oven at 400° for about 10 to 15 minutes.
Yield:
8 sweet potato balls.
Drain and flake tuna; mix with potatoes.
Stir in egg yolks. Add salt, pepper and onion; fold in egg whites.
Pour mixture in greased custard cups or casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Break up sausage and brown in skillet.
Drain grease when no longer pink.
Mix Bisquick, cheese and sausage with a fork.
Beat together remaining ingredients and add to sausage and Bisquick. Blend well with your hands.
Shape into balls.
Place on baking sheet and flatten slightly.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Good party hors d'oeuvre or breakfast item.
Thaw puff pastry sheets.
Cut each sheet into 6 pieces.
Roll each piece into a square.
Saute chicken and onions in butter.
On each piece of dough, place a slice of ham, some of the chicken and onion mixture and the 2 cheeses.
Roll each square, sealing the edges.
Bake on an ungreased baking sheet at 450° until puffed and golden brown.
In a food processor, mix cheese, yogurt, jam and vanilla extract until smooth; add blackberries also.
Then chill until thick.
Cut chicken breasts into pieces and cook.
Break spaghetti into pieces and cook.
Cut cheese into cubes.
Saute onions and pepper in butter; add broth, soup and mushrooms.
Stir; then add cheese and stir over a low heat until cheese is mostly melted. Add chicken and spaghetti.
Mix well.
Pour into large Pyrex dish. Heat for 30 minutes at 350°.
This freezes well.
This recipe will serve 12 people.
Stir all ingredients together except whipped cream and 1/4 of cracker crumbs.
Shape into a pillow or a roll and roll in reserved crumbs.
Wrap in several thicknesses of wax paper and store in refrigerator.
Good topped with whipped cream when served.
Soften cream cheese and mix 1 cup powdered sugar until well blended. Add each ingredient separately and mix well. After all ingredients are mixed, top with chopped pecans
In a saucepan, cook vegetables in margarine until tender. Combine with soup, milk, macaroni, tomato and tuna in a 1 1/2-quart buttered baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix first 6 ingredients in saucepan and bring to a boil.
Mix cornstarch with 4 teaspoons water.
Stir cornstarch mixture into saucepan, stirring until sauce is clear and smooth.
Melt butter; add horseradish, Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce.
Put langostino in casserole dish on bottom.
Add butter and other ingredients (except crackers, mushroom soup and bread crumbs).
Put crushed crackers on top, add cream of mushroom soup, as is, and sprinkle with Italian bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Serves 4.
Place pork chops, celery rib, salt and onion in large saucepan with 4 cups water and butter.
Let come to a boil; then reduce heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Preheat broiler. Brush eggplant with olive oil. Sprinkle each slice with a pinch of salt and pepper. Put on baking sheet and broil until cooked through and tender, about 2 to 3 minutes on each side.
Cream shortening and sugar well.
Add milk and flour alternately, last portion of milk last.
If it is too stiff, thin with cream.
Drop by teaspoon on hot iron.
When baked, place roller on top of rack and roll up in rolls.
Combine water, sugar, bread, milk, salt, gelatin and vanilla in blender.
Pour mixture into saucepan and simmer slowly until smooth.
Cool.
Return mixture to blender.
Add buttermilk and cinnamon; blend until smooth.
Refrigerate until firm.
Serves 1.
Combine first 3 ingredients; stir well. Beat egg whites and cream of tartar at high speed of an electric mixer until foamy. Add sugar; beat until stiff peaks form and sugar dissolves.
Add vanilla; fold in cracker mixture. Spread in a 9-inch pie plate. Bake at 250° for 40 minutes; cool.
Drain shrimp; cook macaroni.
Chop onion and celery; slice olives and shred cheese.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add Miracle Whip to coat well.
Refrigerate.
Top with additional sliced olives and paprika for garnish.
Mix orange juice, beer and Italian dressing.
Pour over meat. Cover and marinate for 2 days.
Add barbecue sauce to marinade and brush on meat.
Seal in foil and cook for 1 1/2 hours.
Turn and cook for 1 1/2 hours more.
Remove from foil and continue to cook until slightly crusty.
Mix together in a large bowl the turkey, water chestnuts, grapes, celery and almonds.
Mix the curry powder, soy sauce and mayonnaise in a separate bowl.
Add to the other ingredients.
Beat egg yolks, sugar and water until very light and foamy. Whip egg whites to which you have added 1 pinch of salt and 1 teaspoon of water until stiff.
Beat 3 teaspoons of confectioners sugar, one at a time, into egg whites.
Pound chicken breasts to 1/2-inch thickness.
Mix eggs and milk together.
Dip each chicken breast into egg mixture and then roll in bread crumbs.
Spray olive oil on both sides of chicken breast.
Sprinkle garlic powder and Italian seasoning on one side, then add a layer of shredded cheese.
Tightly roll up and place into a casserole dish with seam down.
When finished placing all the chicken breasts in the dish, spray olive oil on all of the chicken rolls very well.
Bake in oven at 400° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Brown hamburg; add next 9 ingredients.
Rinse each can from soup with 1/4 can of water.
Mix all and put into casserole.
Top with chow mein noodles.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes at 350°.
Trim crust
off
bread;
cut
bread
in strips, about 5 strips per slice. Put
strips of bread and crust in 200° oven and dry out until crisp (1 to 2 hours).
Mix peanut butter and Wesson oil together
until it makes thin paste-thin enough to dip the crisp bread strips in.
Put bread crust in blender to make crumbs
or crush with rolling pin.
Mix bread crumbs with sugar, about
half and
half. Roll
dipped
peanut strips in bread crust
crumbs and
sugar (or graham cracker crumbs and sugar).
Store in tight container. Keeps well.
Combine peanuts, flour and butter.
Press into the bottom of a 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes. Cool.
Marinate roast with Italian dressing, turning occasionally and make sure it stays moist.
Next day, place roast in oven cooking bag and add potatoes, carrots, onion, salt and pepper to taste. Add 1/4 cup Italian dressing mixed with 1/4 cup water.
Close bag and cook according to directions on box or any any other roast cooked in oven bag.
Drain off pineapple juice and save 1/4 cup, adding lemon juice, sugar and salt to this and set aside.
Spread pineapple out onto paper towels in a pie plate.
Quarter, core and chop apples, leaving peel on, and put into a large bowl; toss with juice (will keep from turning dark) and let stand while you prepare rest of the fruit.
Peel and slice bananas into the apple mixture, tossing gently.
Drain off excess juice.
Using a wooden spoon (won't mash bananas), gently stir all ingredients together.
Chill 30 minutes, gently toss again; sprinkle a few pecan pieces and a little coconut on top and serve.

Mix fruit and drained chestnuts. Dissolve jello in water. Mix with fruit. Pour 1/2 of mixture in 9 x 13-inch pan and refrigerate 1 hour, then spread yogurt over all. Put other 1/2 of jello on top. Refrigerate. Makes 16 servings.
Mix together oil, cooked prunes, chopped apples, eggs and sugar.
Add orange rind and mix well.
Add salt, soda, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg, mix well then add flour and mix.
Add nuts, coconut and raisins.
Mix well, take a teaspoon of mixture and drop on lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes, more or less depending on thickness.
Makes 9 to 10 dozen. These cookies freeze well.
Cook onion in fat until soft.
Add cabbage and steam on medium with needed water for 15 minutes.
Add apples, vinegar, sugar and salt.
