Layer half of the rice, Ortega chilies, sour cream and cheese, then layer again with the other half.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Combine the brown sugar, oil, eggs, bananas and yogurt; mix well.
Sift the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
Stir into first mixture.
Add the coconut and pineapple and stir.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cube tomato and place in a bowl with shrimp, crabmeat, black olives, capers and a pinch of salt and pepper.
In frying pan, place garlic and olive oil and saute until garlic is golden brown. Then add ingredients and saute for about 10 minutes.
Cook fusilli; drain and pour puttanessca sauce over top.
Serve.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and nutmeg together.
Mix softened margarine and sugar real well.
Add eggs.
Add dry ingredients.
This is a hard dough but delicious to make small pies for figs, pears and peaches.
Refrigerate dough overnight. Use one rounded tablespoon dough.
Roll in hands to make a ball. Flatten on floured paper.
Fill one part and fold in half.
Cook at 375° until light brown.

Mix slaw and 1/2 cup of the salad dressing. Spread bread halves with remaining salad dressing. Layer bottom half of bread with slaw mixture and remaining ingredients. Cover with top half of bread. Makes 8 servings.
Chop cabbage coarsely into large pan; add 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cover with boiling water; boil for 7 minutes and drain.
Place half of cabbage in shallow baking dish.
Make white sauce with butter, flour, salt, pepper and milk.
Pour half of sauce over cabbage.
Sprinkle with half the cheese and half the bread crumbs. Layer with the remaining cabbage, cheese and crumbs.
Pour remaining white sauce over top.
I sprinkle can of Durkee onions over the top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Place apples in large bowl.
Coat apples with flour.
In small saucepan combine apple juice, cornstarch, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir until smooth.
Cook until thickened.
Pour mixture over apples, mixing gently.
Line pie pan with bottom half of crust.
Add apple mixture to pie pan.
Place top crust on top and crimp edges.
Cut several slits in crust. Bake for 10 minutes at 425°.
Reduce heat to 375° and bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Peel and slice the apples and put them into a pie dish with 2 ounces of sugar, cinnamon and the water.
Cream the fat and remaining sugar and beat in the egg.
Stir in flour and baking powder. Spread this mixture on top of the fruit.
Bake in a moderately hot oven at 400° for about 1/2 hour until the fruit is cooked and the cake mixture well risen and golden.
In a 2-quart bowl, mix with a fork 1 cup sugar, 3/4 cup sifted flour, baking powder and soft shortening.
Stir in evaporated milk and vanilla until well blended.
Stir in broken nuts and apple until coated with batter.
Spread evenly in a greased 9-inch square pan.

Mix together the first 4 ingredients until crumbly. Press half of the crumbs into an 8-inch square dish. Reserve other half. Microwave sugar, cornstarch and water on High for 2 to 4 minutes, stirring several times until thick and clear. Stir in blueberries, vanilla and lemon flavoring until well mixed. Pour the mixture over crumbs in dish. Sprinkle reserved crumbs over the top and microwave on High for 8 to 10 minutes. Let set 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.t: Colorful Pasta Salad(Also Suitable For Diabetic Food Plans.)
d: In a large bowl, combine oil, vinegar, pepper, garlic, salt, oregano, onion and sweetener.
Cook macaroni according to package instructions. Add cooked macaroni, beans and mixed vegetables. Toss well. Cover and chill.
Take out of refrigerator and toss 2 or more times and again before serving.
Makes 16 servings.
In a small bowl, combine first 7 ingredients.
Place 1 tortilla in an 8-inch round cake pan, sprayed with vegetable cooking spray.
Spread 1/4 of bean mixture over tortilla.
Repeat with second tortilla and bean mixture.
Sprinkle 1 cup cheese over bean mixture. Repeat with remaining tortillas and bean mixture. Sprinkle remaining 1 cup cheese over top.
Melt 1 stick margarine.
Add 1 cup of uncooked rice and 1/2 large onion (chopped).
Cook until rice is golden brown.
Add 1 can of beef consomme and 1 can of water to mixture.
Stir well and add 1 can of sliced mushrooms, drained.
Salt and pepper to taste. Pour in 2-quart casserole and cover.
Bake at 300° for 50 minutes.
Remove cover and bake additional 10 to 15 minutes. Serve with any meat or fish dishes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Steam carrots, zucchini, corn and green beans until tender; put aside to cool.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and set aside to cool.
Using blender or food processor, puree cottage cheese until smooth.
Blend in skim milk, basil and parsley.
Combine vegetables and pasta.
Pour sauce over vegetables and pasta; mix thoroughly.
Serve at room temperature. Serves 6.
Sift flour, measure and sift again with salt and baking powder. Add corn meal.
Combine eggs, milk, syrup and shortening; add to dry ingredients.
Beat until smooth.
Bake in greased pan 9 x 9-inch in hot oven, 400°, for 25 to 30 minutes.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Add peas and ham; heat through.
Cook and drain pasta; add to peas and ham.
Pour in whipping cream; heat until boiling.
Remove from heat.
Stir in cheese and nutmeg.
Serve immediately.
Stir water and sugar, bring to a boil and cool.
Mix all juices and fruit into this syrup and freeze in plastic containers. When ready to serve, remove to punch bowl and add ginger ale or 7-Up.
It is best for mixture not to thaw too much; it tastes better a bit thick and requires no ice.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease a 9-inch square metal pan or 10-inch cast-iron skillet; place in hot oven.
Combine cornmeal, baking powder and salt.
Add eggs, sour cream and oil; blend well. Stir in corn.
Pour 1/2 of batter into heated pan.
Cover with cheese.
Spoon remaining batter on top; sprinkle top with chili powder.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cut in squares.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine milk, marshmallows and orange juice in top of double boiler, let marshmallows melt.
Blend cracker crumbs and spices in large bowl.
Then add raisins, dates, nuts and candied fruit.
Stir in mixture of marshmallows with large spoon and hand until all crumbs are moistened.
Then pack tightly in greased pan and store in refrigerator for at least 12 hours.
Run knife around pan and take cake out.
Wrap in wax paper, then in foil and store.
Pour boiling water over jello and marshmallows.
Stir until dissolved.
Chill.
Mash cream cheese with vinegar until smooth. Add pineapple and juice; blend well.
Add nuts.
Chill.
Combine two mixtures when jello mixture begins to thicken.
Blend thoroughly.
Pour into desired mold and chill.
Saute onions and green peppers in butter for 3 minutes.
Stir in flour. Add chicken broth gradually.
Stir and cook over medium heat until thickened.
Add pimento, almonds, pepper, turkey and rice. Stir to combine.
Pour into 2-quart casserole dish. Top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cream cheese and margarine.
Add salt, onion powder, garlic and Worcestershire.
Blend thoroughly.
Add oysters and blend well.
Round mixture into ball and refrigerate until hard enough to roll in chopped nuts.
Refrigerate.
Cook macaroni.
Place in bottom of buttered 6 quart casserole dish.
Brown beef with onion and garlic.
Add mushroom soup. Simmer.
Place meat mixture on top of pasta.
Layer green beans and corn over meat mixture.
Pour mushrooms over all.
Top with cheese.
Bake about 30 minutes at 350°.
Serves 10.
Wash spinach carefully and drain it.
Beat eggs and add the cornstarch.
Season according to taste.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and when it is hot and ready, deep-fry the spinach one by one. Wait until it is golden brown.
Drain the excess oil in paper towel before serving.
In a 2-quart saucepan, stir milk and cornstarch until smooth. Add oleo and salt, stirring constantly.
Bring to boil over medium-high heat.
Boil 1 minute.
Stir in corn, ham pieces and cheeses.
Remove from heat.
Stir until cheeses melt; toss with cooked pasta and corn chips.
Makes 4 servings.
Melt chocolate in the microwave.
Add a couple drops of cooking oil and add peanut butter.
Place over heat and stir.
Add other ingredients.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cool and cut.

recipes.t: Weight Watcher'S Chicken Breasts With Raisin Sauce
d: Heat oven to 350°.
Season chicken with dash each of salt and onion powder.
Tuck ends of each breast under to form rounded mound.
Cover with skin and place in nonstick baking pan and bake about 25 minutes or until done.
Remove and discard skin.
While chicken is baking, prepare fruit sauce.
Dissolve yeast into lukewarm water.
Add sugar, salt and shortening to hot milk.
Cool to lukewarm, then beat in eggs.
Add 2 cups of flour and beat thoroughly.
Stir in dissolved yeast. Add just enough flour to make a soft dough.
Dissolve Jell-O, marshmallows and salt in 2 cups hot water. Chill until partially set, then beat until fluffy.
Whip cream until stiff peaks form.
Beat the cream cheese and pineapple together.
Fold in whipped cream.
Beat into jello mixture.
Cover top with chopped pecans.
Chill.
In large bowl mix together beef, bread crumbs, pepper, garlic salt, salad dressing mix, milk and egg.
Roll the mixture into balls about 1 inch in diameter.
Place 20 meatballs on microwave-safe tray.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave on High for 3 1/2 to 4 minutes until meat loses its redness, turning once.
Continue this procedure with remaining meatballs.
Serve with toothpicks.
Makes about 40 meatballs.
Dissolve jello in hot juice from pineapple with enough water to equal 1 cup.
Whip chilled milk and cream cheese until smooth and creamy; add jello after it is cooled.
Add vanilla, sugar and pineapple.
Put half of crumbs in bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Pour in mixture; cover with rest of crumbs and refrigerate overnight. Any flavor jello may be used but I prefer orange.
Beat egg whites until frothy; slowly add sugar and baking powder.
Beat until stiff.
Fold in nuts, graham crackers and vanilla.
Pour into well-buttered pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Top with whipped cream.
Spread 1 teaspoon margarine on each side of each frozen hash brown patty.
Place patties on ungreased cookie sheet.
Broil 4 to 6 inches from heat for 11 to 13 minutes or until brown.
Turn patties over; broil 4 to 6 minutes or until brown.
Place ham slice on each hash brown patty; broil for 1 to 2 minutes or until hot.
Sprinkle cheese and parsley over ham.
Makes 6 servings.
To soup, add 1 can water and sugar to taste.
Stir until smooth.
Bring to boil.
Core out seeds of peppers; wash and set aside.
Parboil rice for 10 minutes.
Rinse and strain.
Add to meat, onion, garlic, egg, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Stuff into peppers.
Place peppers into tomato soup and when it starts to boil again, lower heat and let slowly boil for 1 hour.

Cook onions in water for 4 minutes. Mince ground beef and add to onions and water in Dutch oven. Add chili beans, chili powder and tomato sauce. Mix thoroughly on high until boiling; reduce temperature to low and stir until satisfied chili will not stick to
pan. Serve with rice, cornbread, hot dogs or hamburgers. If you have some leftover, freeze and use for a later date.
Crumble and brown ground beef in heavy skillet (no fat added). Add onion and green pepper; cook until almost tender.
Add tomatoes and seasonings.
Cover.
Simmer gently 2 hours, adding bean liquid and water, a little at a time if needed, to keep consistency of thick soup.
Add kidney beans; heat through.
Remove bay leaves. Serve in small bowls.
Yields 6 servings.
Boil
chicken
in water until tender along with celery, onions,
carrots, salt and pepper.
Strain chicken and vegetables reserving broth.
Bone chicken.
Heat oven to 350°.
Melt oleo in 11
x
13 x 2-inch dish; place chicken in.
Add cooked vegetables and
peas.
Combine
baking
mix
with milk and mix until smooth. Pour baking mix over top of chicken and vegetables.
Pour
chicken broth over all.
Bake until golden brown about 35 minutes.
Pat chops dry.
Mix together thyme, pepper and salt and season both sides of all chops.
Set chops aside.
In a large, heavy skillet, melt the butter with the sugar over moderately high heat; add the apples and saute the mixture for 30-40 minutes, or until they begin to brown.
Turn the apples, cook them for 5 minutes more, or until golden brown and the sauce is thickened. remove from heat and keep warm.
Heat another heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Brush with a little vegetable oil.
Add chops and brown on one side about 4 minutes; turn and brown the other side 4 minutes more.
Keep turning chops every couple of minutes until just done (internal temperature measured with a meat thermometer will reach 160°).
Total cooking time for chops will be around 12 to 15 minutes.
Serve chops immediately with caramelized apples.
Place hot water in 2-cup measure.
Microwave at High for 2 to 2 3/4 minutes or until water boils.
Place gelatin in medium mixing bowl.
Stir in boiling water.
Stir to dissolve gelatin. Mix in cold water.
Chill until gelatin is soft set, about 1 hour. Place raspberries in 1-quart casserole.
Cover.
Microwave at 50% (Medium) for 3 to 5 minutes or until raspberries are defrosted, stirring once.
Reserve 6 whole berries for garnishing, if desired.
Stir raspberries into gelatin.
Set aside.
Place egg white in small mixing bowl.
Beat at high speed of an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
Fold into gelatin mixture.
Fold 1 cup whipped topping into gelatin mixture.
Spoon into each of 6 stemmed glasses or dessert dishes.
Top evenly with remaining 1/2 cup whipped topping.
Garnish with raspberries.
Serve immediately or chill for 1 hour for firmer texture.
Makes 6 servings.
Break up cauliflower into small flowerets.
Mix with peas, onion and mushrooms.
Combine oil, lemon juice, salt and mustard. Pour over top and mix together.
Mix peanut butter, honey and Rice Krispies; pour in pie pan. Use a greased cup to press crust.
Slice 1 banana and place them on the crust.
Mix chocolate pudding according to directions and pour over bananas and crust.
Refrigerate 1 hour until set.
Top with chocolate Cool Whip.
Combine cream cheese, green chilies, green onions, black olives, Cheddar cheese and garlic salt in a bowl.
Spread a heaping tablespoon (or more if you like) of cream cheese mixture on each tortilla.
Roll up the tortilla in jellyroll fashion. Place seam side down on a baking sheet.
Cover and chill for 2 hours.
Slice each tortilla into 4 pieces and serve with picante sauce on the side for dipping.
This recipe makes about 4 dozen.

recipes.t: Wild Bird Seed Cookies For Birds
d: Sift together dry ingredients into a large mixing bowl.
Cut in shortening with a pastry blender or knives until crumbly. Add eggs and mix to make firm dough.
Add bird seed and knead until smooth.
Wrap in waxed paper and plastic bag and chill thoroughly.
Beat egg slightly.
Add sugar, vinegar, celery seed, dry mustard and salt.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Let cool.
Add desired amount to slaw.
Store remaining amount in refrigerator for later use.
Season pork chops with salt, pepper and paprika.
In skillet, brown pork chops slowly on both sides.
Drain off excess fat.
Add the cup of water, celery and soup mix.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
Turn chops and cook 20 minutes more (or longer).
Remove chops from skillet.
Mix crumbs and margarine; press into pan and bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix milk and coconut and spread over crumb mixture. Bake 15 minutes longer.
Cook onion, red pepper flakes and salt pork in water in a very large Dutch oven.
Wash all greens carefully and add to pot.
Cook until greens are tender.
Break up lettuce; place in serving bowl.
Layer the following ingredients in order: celery, onions, green pepper, green peas, cheese and bacon.
Mix mayonnaise and sugar and spread on salad like frosting.
Be sure to spread dressing all the way to the edge of the bowl so the salad is sealed.
You can top with some reserved shredded cheese and a little bacon.
You can also add sliced hard-boiled eggs either in the salad or use as a garnish. Chill several hours or overnight.
Good for potlucks.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter 8-inch cake pan.
Combine Chex, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Add butter.
Mix well.
Sprinkle half over bottom of pan.
Arrange biscuits over crumb mixture.
Top with fruit and then with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve immediately.
Cook and stir ground beef and onion in Dutch oven until beef is brown; drain.
Stir in sauce mix, water, beans (with liquid), corn (with liquid), mustard, salt, pepper and tomatoes (with liquid).
Break up tomatoes with fork.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Stir in margarine.
Cover and cook 10 minutes longer.
Brown ground beef and onion in a frying pan.
Drain.
Combine all ingredients in a casserole dish.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with nonstick spray.
Skin chicken pieces.
Place in pan.
Sprinkle with salad dressing.
Put under broiler and broil until brown.
Turn pieces over; sprinkle again with salad dressing and broil until brown (approximately 5 minutes each side).
Reduce oven temperature to 400°.
Sprinkle chicken with paprika.
Quarter zucchini the long way and lay across top of chicken.
Cover with foil and return to oven for 30 minutes. Reduce heat to 300° and bake 1 1/2 hours more.
Makes very tender chicken with plenty of juices to serve over rice or potatoes.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients except sugar and cinnamon.
Blend at low speed.
Beat at medium speed 3 minutes. Mix sugar and cinnamon and swirl through batter.
Do not mix completely.
Pour batter into a greased 10-inch tube pan.
Bake in preheated oven at 325° for 60 to 70 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool on rack for 1 hour, then turn cake out of pan to cool completely, then frost with cream cheese icing and toasted coconut. Can be baked in 2 round cake pans.
Rinse tenderloin.
Place on foil covered baking sheet. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl combine onion, barbecue sauce, soy sauce and butter.
Place in microwave for 30 seconds.
Pour over tenderloin and bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Save juice from pineapple and to 4 tablespoons pickle juice, add enough water to make 1 cup.
Dissolve Jell-O in second cup of hot water.
Add shredded carrots, if desired.

recipes.t: Mrs. Leigh'S Hamburger With Barbecue Sauce
d: Handling as little as possible, mix beef, egg, bread crumbs, milk, salt and pepper; shape into balls.
Brown in the oil until brown on both sides.
Mix the tomatoes, sauce, vinegar, chili powder and onion well; pour over hamburger balls and let simmer for 30 minutes.
Slice cucumbers very thin.
Sprinkle with salt; cover and chill several hours.
Drain cucumbers well.
Combine with radishes.
Combine remaining ingredients; blend into cucumbers and radishes.
If desired, pile mixture into the center of a tomato aspic ring.
Dust with a little ground pepper.
May also be served on lettuce leaves.
Sprinkle lemon juice on apples as they are cut.
Mix apples, celery, walnuts and 15 to 20 grapes.
Make dressing of mayonnaise, sour cream and sugar; pour over apple and celery mixture.
Mix until covered.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Line a roasting pan with a large piece of foil.
Place vegetables in foil and arrange chicken on top.
Empty can of tomatoes over all and season with salt and pepper.
Wrap foil around chicken tightly.
Roast at 375° for 1 hour.
Turn back foil and baste chicken with pan juices.
Brush chicken with margarine and sprinkle with paprika.
Roast 45 minutes longer, uncovered.
In a large pot, heat water and crumbled bouillon cubes.
When boiling, add macaroni.
Cook according to package instructions until tender.
Drain well.
Cut ham into small strips.
Place a layer of pasta over bottom of a lightly greased pan.
Sprinkle with some ham.
Repeat last step.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs, half and half, salt and pepper.
Pour mixture over macaroni.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until lightly brown on top.
Melt margarine in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Stir in graham crackers and sugar.
Press down and sprinkle coconut on top of crust, then sprinkle chocolate chips and butterscotch chips on top of coconut. Then, pour nuts on.
Pour milk over top of nuts and bake at 350° for 20 minutes covered with foil.
Remove foil; bake 10 more minutes uncovered.
Cut meat into 1-inch cubes.
Remove mushroom stems and cut up. Combine with mushroom soup and water; set aside.
For each serving, cut a 40-inch length of aluminum foil and fold in half. Arrange meat, potatoes, carrots, onion, green pepper slices and mushrooms in center of foil. .
Spoon the mushroom soup mixture over all.
Top with a tablespoon of margarine.
Double fold top and edges to seal securely.
Place in center of grill and cook for 1 1/4 hours or until meat is tender.
Serve in foil.
May be cooked in conventional oven at 350°, but the flavor is better if cooked on the grill outside.
Place meat cubes in a shallow dish.
Combine marinade of wine, vinegar, onion, sugar, garlic and oil.
Pour over meat cubes; marinate overnight.
Remove meat from marinade and place on skewers, alternating with meat, small onions and green pepper strips.
Broil over charcoals or in oven, basting often with marinade sauce.
Serves 8 to 10.
Blend mango and cream cheese.
Heat water and juice to boiling; add gelatin and stir to dissolve.
Add lime juice. Combine with mango-cream cheese mixture and blend well.
Chill until set in mold or glass casserole dish.
Serves 8.
In a frying pan over medium heat, cook ground turkey with garlic.
Cook elbows according to package directions.
Drain. Pour cooked elbows into deep 3-quart casserole dish.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Cover and bake 30 minutes at 350°.

Preheat oven to 350°. Combine flour and sugar. Cut in butter. Set aside 1 cup of this mixture for topping. Add cinnamon, baking soda, nutmeg and ginger to the remaining flour mixture. Stir in eggs and buttermilk. Do not use electric mixer. Pour the batter into a greased 9 x 12 pan. Sprinkle reserved topping over batter and bake for 45 minutes or until done.
Split breasts into halves; bone halves.
In skillet, place boned breasts, skin side up.
Add wine, water, onion or shallots and bouillon cubes.
Heat to boiling.
Cover; cook over low heat for 15 minutes, or until fork-tender.
Beat batter until creamy; gradually add sugar, beating well. Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each addition.
Stir in banana and orange rind.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; add to butter mixture alternately with orange juice, beginning and ending with flour.
Mix at low speed.
Stir in pecans and raisins. Spoon batter into two greased and floured 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool in pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes.
Remove from pans and cool on rack.
In a large saucepan, heat oil and add carrots, onion, celery, potato, garlic and sugar.
Cover and cook vegetables over low heat for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the cloves, pepper and broth and bring the soup to a boil.
Reduce the heat and cook the soup, partially covering the pan for about 20 minutes or until the vegetables are soft.
Remove and discard the cloves. Puree the soup in batches in a blender or food processor.
Prepare grill.
Rinse fish in cold water.
Pat dry.
Sprinkle inside and out with salt and pepper.
Drizzle cavities with oil and stuff with lemon slices and herbs.
Grill, turning once, until just opaque at backbone, about 15 minutes.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Makes 4 servings.
Beat sugar and butter together.
Beat eggs separately (whites and yellows).
Stir them into mixture.
Add 3 cups flour, which has been sifted only once.
Take the remaining cup of flour and dredge nuts and raisins.
Line bottom of the cake pan with waxed paper.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Combine biscuit mix, milk and mayonnaise; stir well.
Spread mixture in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; set aside.
Mix oil,
margarine,
sugar and vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time,
beating well after each.
Slowly add flour, salt, baking soda and mix well.
Chill dough 1 to 2 hours in refrigerator. Preheat oven to
Shape
dough in 1-inch balls, space 2-inches apart
on
ungreased
cookie
sheets.
Flatten cookies with glass dipped
in
sugar.
Bake
about
15 minutes until lightly browned at the edge.
Cool and store in airtight container.
Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer.
Cut papaya and banana into chunks.
Combine papaya, banana, yogurt and orange juice in blender container.
Whirl on high for 30 seconds.
Add ice.
Blend for 30 seconds more.
Pour into chilled glasses.
Float 1 tablespoon of grenadine on each, if desired.
Debone and pound flat possum breast.
Press garlic mixed with olive oil and rub on upper side of breast.
Layer thinly on breast Mozzarella cheese, Prosciutto ham, sauteed peppers, onions, brown sausage or scrapple.
Fold over and seal edge by sewing together with half stitches using meat twine.
Place 1-inch of rock salt in large clay roasting pot.
Place stuffed breast on salt.
Fill pot and bake at 500° for 1 hour.
Three more hours at 300°.
Heat oil.
Saute garlic.
Slice peppers and mushrooms.
Cut up or dice tomatoes.
Add peppers, tomatoes and mushrooms to garlic and saute a few minutes.
Add basil, picante sauce and shrimp.
Cook just until shrimp is done.
Add cooked rigatoni and freshly grated Parmesan cheese; toss and serve.
Seres 2.
Mix soft margarine, sugar, egg and vanilla in a large bowl. Sift together flour, baking powder and salt. Add to mixture.
Add pineapple and oatmeal.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoonful onto ungreased cookie sheet 2-inches apart.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Cook 1 cup noodles until done.
Set aside.
Brown ground meat and drain.
Add soup, tomatoes, flour and water to meat.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add noodles.
Add cheese on top.
Bake in casserole for 15 minutes at 400°.
Melt cheeses together in the top of a double boiler over simmering water 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir in green onions, red pepper and jalapeno pepper.
Serve hot with chips.
Saute green pepper, onion and celery; add to boiling stock, chicken and tomatoes, then add orzo and dried parsley.
Cook about 15 minutes or until orzo is done.

Mix bread crumbs and seasonings well and place in pie pan. Mix egg white and water well and put into an individual salad bowl. Spread a small rimmed cookie sheet with aluminum foil and spread the margarine on the foil.
Dip each piece of chicken in the egg white mixture and then dredge it in the bread crumb mixture.
Place on the aluminum foil.
Dribble 1/2 teaspoon oil on top of each piece of chicken. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Remove from oven. Turn chicken over and continue to bake for another 30 minutes.
Serves 4.
Contains 215 calories, 7 gm.
cholesterol, 23 gm. protein, 10 gm. fat and 435 mg. sodium per serving.
In a glass 8 1/2 x 11 x 2-inch dish, layer soaked until soggy chocolate chip cookies and soaked coconut macaroons.
Then apply layer of Cool Whip.
Keep layering until all ingredients are used. Apply layer of Cool Whip over top.
Chill 2 hours or overnight.
In pitcher, combine bourbon, lime juice and creme de menthe. Stir in lemon-lime soda.
Serve over ice.
Garnish with mint.
In medium bowl, combine ground beef, taco spices and ketchup; blend well.
Shape into patties.
Grill or broil burgers 5 to 7 minutes on each side or to desired doneness.
Top each burger with a slice of cheese.
Return to heat until cheese melts.
Top with salsa, if desired.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Brown chicken in oil.
Whip egg and add to chicken.
Stir constantly until cooked.
Add in vegetables and soy sauce.
Stir constantly.
Add in ginger, sesame and water chestnuts.
Stir. Serve over rice.
Preparation time: 15 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6, depending on actual quantity of rice and vegetables.
Heat oven to 350° (moderate).
Work butter until creamy in bowl.
Add sugar; beat until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks and extracts; beat well.
Add flour gradually; mix until smooth. Shape level tablespoonfuls of dough into balls.
Place on greased cookie sheets; press each ball with thumb.
Drop a little jam in each depression.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cool on racks.
Makes about 4 dozen.
Mix all dry ingredients together, then mix with melted butter. Press 1/2 of mixture into 13 x 9-inch pan and bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Sprinkle boxed crust with chocolate chips, chopped nuts and ice cream topping.
Sprinkle the rest of the crumb mixture over this.
Return to oven and bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
Chill 1 to 2 hours before cutting.
Unroll crescent roll dough and shape into 8 triangles with equal sides.
Combine cream cheese, egg yolk, sugar and almond extract; blend well.
Place 1 tablespoon cream cheese mixture in center of each triangle.
Top with kiwi fruit slice.
Pull points of triangle to center and pinch to seal.
Bake on greased baking sheet at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Cook on rack.
Heat jam.
Top each Danish with another kiwi fruit slice; brush with jam.
Yield: 8 servings.
Wash, pare and dice rutabagas in tiny squares.
Add salt, pepper, onion and enough water to cover.
Boil 25 to 30 minutes. Drain water.
Sprinkle with sugar and paprika.
Add butter and parsley.
Steam 10 to 15 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix graham crackers and butter and set aside.
Mix Dream Whip according to directions on box.
Add cream cheese and sugar; mix on high.

recipes.t: Sunshine, Hi Ho Apple Pie(No Apples Required)
d: Bring sugar and cream of tartar and water to rolling boil. Add crackers and boil 2 minutes.
Do not stir; add spice.
Put pie in unbaked pie shell and bake until brown.
Cream butter and sugar until light.
Add egg and vanilla; mix well. Stir together flour and cornstarch; gradually add to creamed mixture.
Wrap dough and chill at least 1 hour.
Coarsely chop cranberries.
In a 2-quart glass jar with lid, combine all ingredients; stir until sugar is dissolved.
Cover tightly with lid.
Allow to stand at room temperature 2 weeks, inverting jar everyday.
Strain through cheesecloth.
Pour into decorative bottles; cap tightly.
Serve in chilled glasses. Serving size:
1/2 cup.
Servings:
In large bowl, combine salt, 3 cups flour and yeast. Heat margarine and the milk (125-130°). hot to the touch. Add to dry mixture, then add water. Add egg.
Knead by hand, adding remaining flour, until dough is no longer sticky.

Dough must be smooth and like elastic. Cover and let rest for 10 min. Cut dough in half, press each down. Prick with fork 3 times. Cover and let rise for 1 hour. (On top of refrigerator). Place breads on oven racks. Bake at 350° for 20 min.
Dissolve 1 tablespoon brown
sugar
in warm water.
Add yeast and stir;
let
stand.
Combine
cups flour, powdered milk, 1/3 cup brown sugar and
salt
in bowl.
Mix on speed 2, using dough hook; slowly add
yeast
mixture
to
flour for 30 seconds.
Add oil and
mix
for
seconds.
Add
remaining flour, 1/2 cup at a time,
until dough clings to hook, about 5 minutes.
Clean hook and bowl.
Knead on speed 2 for 7 minutes or until smooth and elastic.
Blend sugars, margarine and oil until well mixed.
Add almond extract and eggs; mix well.
Mix dry ingredients together. Gradually blend in at low speed.
Stir in brickle chips and almonds.
Shape large tablespoonfuls of dough into balls; roll in sugar.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. With fork dipped in sugar, flatten in crisscross pattern.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes or until light golden brown around edges.
Cut chicken breasts into strips or pieces.
Dredge in flour, then egg and then in bread crumbs.
Brown these in oil.
Slice some mushrooms and onions (to taste).
Simmer chicken, mushrooms, onion, bouillon cubes, water and margarine until done.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Delicious!
Brown beef and onion until done.
Remove from heat and cut up tamales and add to browned beef and onion.
Mix rest of ingredients holding out 1/4 of the cheese.
Place into a 9 x 13-inch tall sided baking dish and sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top.
Place into a preheated 350° oven and bake for 40 minutes.
Serves 10 to 12 people.
Saute garlic, green pepper and onion rings in hot oil.
Add tomatoes and seasoning; simmer 15 minutes.
Cook green beans and drain.
Place beans in center or round, flat vegetable serving bowl.
Spoon tomato mixture around beans.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions.
Separate tuna into flakes.
Mix with cream of mushroom soup, milk, salt and pepper.
Combine cooked noodles and tuna mixture in baking dish. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in moderate oven (375°) for 25 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.

Heat oil in large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and garlic and saut for 3 minutes. Add broth, tomatoes and picante sauce. Bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes. Sprinkle chicken with cumin and coriander. Add chicken, beans and corn to soup. Cover and simmer at least 15 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Beat cranberry sauce and apples; fold in bananas, sugar, vanilla, 1/2 nuts and whipped cream.
Freeze until firm and then serve.
Sprinkle remaining nuts on top.
Brown pork and beef separately.
Mix together with cheese in pan until cheese melts.
Add oregano and Worcestershire sauce. Spread on rye and freeze immediately.
Soften cheese with just enough milk to spreading consistency. Add mayonnaise, onion and seasoning.
Cut bread in circles, about the size of a silver dollar.
Spread mixture on bread, then spread another round of bread and place on top of first round. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Yields 75 puffs.
Mix together egg yolks and sugar. Add Marscapone cheese and mix.
Add lemon rind. Fold in egg whites.
Separately combine Espresso and rum.
Lightly toast ladyfingers. Dip ladyfingers into Espresso and cover bottom of baking pan.
Cover with layer of cheese mixture.
Continue to layer cheese mixture and coffee dipped ladyfingers. Cover and put in refrigerator overnight. Garnish with cocoa powder.
Drain salmon.
Remove skin and large bones.
Break in pieces. Saute artichokes in melted butter 5 minutes.
Place artichokes and salmon in casserole.
Mix sour cream, salt, pepper and Tabasco sauce.
Pour mixture over salmon.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Sprinkle with parsley before serving. Serves 4 to 6.
Prepare and cook broccoli. Place the oil, butter or margarine in a saucepan. Add broccoli. Cook and stir until broccoli is delicate brown. Sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese.
Cook cannelloni according to box.
Drain well.
Melt 1 ounce butter in a pan and saute onion until tender. Add veal and cook gently for 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add spinach, nutmeg and seasonings.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Brown meat in large skillet.
Remove excess fat.
Add celery, onions and garlic with 1 tablespoon water.
Cover and steam until vegetables are tender.
Cook the noodles and add to beef mixture. Mix in all other ingredients except cheese.
Spread mixture in 2 1/2 or 3-quart casserole.
Top with cheese.
Put in a cold oven set at 350°.
Bake, uncovered, about 1 hour or until bubbling. (Freezes well.)

Cut chicken breast meat into small pieces and dip into a mixture of the flour, salt, white pepper, marjoram and nutmeg. Then dip into the egg and water. Then dip into the bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese. Fry in olive oil and margarine mixture. You will probably have to make larger quantities of everything. This is a very tasty dish.
Add 1 cup boiling water to jello.
Chill until partially congealed.
Whip with mixer until fluffy.
Add cottage cheese; continue beating until smooth.
Add salad dressing, horseradish, lemon juice and evaporated milk.
Continue beating; add pineapple and mix well.
Pour into mold and chill until firm.
Cut sausage into small chunks.
Cut peppers and onions into small pieces.
Steam in electric skillet until peppers and onions are tender.
Remove with a slotted spoon onto serving dish.
This makes a good, quick and easy dish for potluck dinners.
Cook macaroni according to directions and drain.
Set aside. Combine egg, cottage cheese, sour cream, seasonings and shredded cheese, reserving 1/2 cup to sprinkle on top.
Mix in macaroni. Put in 3-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with cheese and paprika. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 8.
Mix crumbs, melted margarine, 1 cup powdered sugar, nuts, orange juice and Grand Marnier.
Shape into small balls.
Mix soft margarine and remaining powdered sugar; add enough milk for spreading consistency.
Beat eggs with milk.
Melt butter in skillet.
Scramble eggs. Spread in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with bacon, peppers, onions and mushrooms.
Warm soup with sherry (or water).
Spread over top. Top with grated cheese.
Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 250° for 50 minutes.
Mix beans, 1/2 can onions and soup until moistened.
Bake, uncovered, in a greased casserole dish for 30 minutes at 350°. Top with 1/2 can onions and bake for 5 minutes, uncovered.
Beat egg.
Mix flour and sugar, then add to egg along with lemon juice and juice from small can of pineapple.
Mix well. Cook over low heat until smooth and thick.
Set aside to cool completely.
Wash, drain and chop fruit.
Beat whipped cream until stiff; add to cooled dressing.
Pour over fruit and mix well. Refrigerate.
Can add pecans, if desired.
In large skillet, brown onion and meat.
Drain.
Add seasoning mix and 3/4 cup water.
Then add kidney beans, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain canned vegetables and pimientos well.
Mix all vegetables together.
Toss gently.
In a saucepan, combine oil, sugar, vinegar, water, lemon juice and paprika.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat; allow to cook 5 minutes.
Pour over top of vegetables and allow to marinate at least 24 hours.
Gently turn over with a slotted spoon.
Drain well before serving.
Makes 18 to 20 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine flour, sugar, cocoa and baking soda; cut in oleo until crumbly.
Press firmly on bottom of
13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes.
Melt butter in a large saucepan.
Add cabbage, using only the water which still clings to the leaves.
Cook, covered, over low heat until tender, stirring occasionally, to prevent sticking. Add onion rings, water, vinegar and Sucaryl.
Cover and cook about 10 minutes longer.
Yields 6 servings at 68 calories per serving.
Into a large pot, put rice, lentils, salt and water.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, turn heat to low and steam until tender.
Cook ziti and drain.
In small mixing bowl, mix the chopped onion, green pepper, salt, pepper and garlic powder.
In small pan, stir the meat until brown and then strain.
In the same small pan, mix the Spatini and paste according to the directions on the packet of Spatini.
Add the meat and let simmer.
In small casserole dish or oblong pan, place the ziti, top with meat, then with cheese, until all of the ingredients are gone (this can be layered if preferred).
Bake in the oven at 350° for approximately 20 minutes or until cheese is nice and golden.
Saute bacon.
Add onion and garlic, saute 3 to 4 minutes. Add peppers and tomatoes. Cover and saute 5 minutes.
Add salt. Cook, uncovered, 10 minutes on low.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Brown sausage as directed on package.
Beat Bisquick, cinnamon, milk and egg with a spoon until smooth.
Stir in apples.
Pour into baking dish.
Arrange sausage on top.
Bake until lightly brown, 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve with maple syrup.
Season roast with salt, pepper and garlic salt.
Dust with flour and brown in roaster in 1 or 2 Tbsp. of hot vegetable oil. Mix onion soup with hot water and pour over roast.
Add beef broth and carrots.
Cover.
I put this in a 300 degree oven before I go to church and let it bake until I get home (approximately 4 to 5 hours).
Slice onions about 1-inch thick.
Separate into rings.
Place in a large bowl of ice water for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix 1 cup flour, baking powder, egg, buttermilk, vegetable oil, paprika and red pepper to form batter.
In deep fryer, heat oil to 350°. Place remaining 1 1/2 cups flour in small bowl.
In small batches, remove rings from water, dredge in remaining flour, then dip in batter.
Place in hot oil.
Fry for 3 to 5 minutes, until golden brown.
Drain onto paper towels.
Repeat process with rest of rings.
Season with salt.
Serve immediately.
Serves 4.
Beat oleo (use Blue Bonnet) until fluffy; add sugar slowly. Beat well.
Add eggs (one at a time), beating well after each egg. Slowly add flour, pecans and vanilla flavoring.
Mix well.
Place 1/2 of batter in well-greased, floured, oblong baking pan.
Add 1 1/2 cups of chocolate frosting to batter in pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 40 minutes (do not overbake).
Heat oven to 375°.
Cut off stem end of zucchini.
Cut each in half lengthwise and scoop out pulp and seeds (reserve pulp), leaving 1/4 inch shell.
Brown ground beef, onion, garlic and oregano.
Drain fat.
Add chopped zucchini pulp, Parmesan cheese, 1/4 of soup, salt and pepper.
Arrange zucchini shells in 9 X 13 pan.
Spoon mixture into shells.
Spoon remaining soup over top. Sprinkle with additional Parmesan cheese.
Bake, covered with foil, at 375° for 30 minutes or until zucchini is tender. Sprinkle grated Mozzarella cheese over boats.
Return to oven for 5 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.

recipes.t: Sugar Snap Peas And Peppers(6 Servings)
d: Heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat. Add veggies and saute for 5 minutes. Sprinkle with soy sauce and lemon juice. Add pepper and salt to taste.
Combine gelatin with boiling water.
Drain pineapple, measure juice and add water to make 1 cup; then add to gelatin.
Chill until partially set.
Soften cream cheese and add mayonnaise or salad dressing.
Add to gelatin and stir well.
Add other ingredients.
Pour into mold and chill until firm.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
In mixing bowl, combine butter, cheese, sausage and seasonings.
Mix in flour.
Shape dough into balls and place on cookie sheet.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 350°.
Serve hot.
Cut ice cream into large chunks and place in a well-chilled bowl.
Stir quickly until smooth.
Stir in almonds, cherries, extracts and nutmeg.
Fold in candies.
Spoon into 2 1/2-inch fluted paper or foil baking cups in muffin pan.
Freeze.
Serve plain or top each serving with a dollop of whipped cream and a few additional candies.
Makes 8 servings.
Place fish fillets in ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Mix catsup, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, sugar, onion, salt and pepper sauce.
Pour on fish; turn until both sides are coated. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 400°.
Bake, uncovered, until fish flakes easily with fork, 15 to 20 minutes. Garnish with lemon wedges.
Serve with pan juices.
Serves 3 or 4.
In bowl of electric mixer, combine eggs, sugar, butter, flour, cocoa, vanilla, and salt.
Beat on high speed 4 minutes, stopping once or twice to scrap down sides of bowl.
Stir in almonds.
Pour mixture in greased 8-inch square baking pan.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until cracks appear on surface and edges begin to pull away from pan.
Cool in pan, then cut into squares.
Makes 16 servings.
Grind meat, pickles, cheese, pepper and onion. Add remaining ingredients.
Spread on bread, hamburger bun, hot dog bun, eat cold or put on an English muffin and bake for 15 minutes at 350°.
In blender, combine the yogurts, pineapple juice concentrate, coconut and rum extracts; add a few cubes of ice and pulse several times until ice is coarsely chopped.
Continue adding ice, pulsing after each addition, until mixture is smooth and creamy.
(If thicker colada is desired, add more ice.)
Pour into two 12 oz. glasses and garnish each with lime slice.
Trim excess fat from meat.
In a large Dutch oven, heat cooking oil.
Brown meat in the hot oil.
Spoon off fat.
Add orange peel, orange juice, onions, fines herbes and bay leaf. Bring to boiling.
Reduce heat.
Simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
Cut grapefruits crosswise; scoop out fruit with spoon.
Save the juice.
With sharp knife and clean hands, carefully remove membranes and lining from grapefruit hulls.
Set aside.
Peel cooled potatoes and cut into halves or thirds lengthwise. Add salt, if necessary.
Place in shallow baking pan.
Combine remaining ingredients, heat slowly and pour over potatoes.
Bake 20 minutes in 400° oven, basting frequently with sauce in pan. Serves 6.
Season chicken.
In large skillet, saute onion and garlic 2 minutes.
Add picante and broth; bring to boil.
Add rice.
Place chicken on top of rice.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Remove from heat; let stand until liquid is gone.
Serve with avocado, tomato and cheese on top.
May serve with olives and sour cream, if desired.
Combine sugar, salt, vinegar and oil to make dressing.
Cook and stir bacon, onion and garlic in large saucepan until bacon is crisp.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat.
Simmer uncovered until vegetables are tender; 15 to 20 minutes.
Pour mixture into blender and cover.
Blend on high until smooth.
If thinner consistency is desired, stir in water or chicken broth.
Garnish with sour cream, snipped parsley or shredded carrot, if desired.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cut potatoes crosswise into 1/2-inch thick slices.
Place in 1 1/2-quart baking dish; top with raisins, ginger and margarine.
In a saucepan, combine honey, apples or pineapple juice.
Heat over low heat 2 to 3 minutes, stirring to blend well.
Pour honey mixture over potatoes and bake 20 minutes. Spoon liquid over potatoes.
Serves 6.
Slice zucchini lengthwise.
Parboil 5 to 8 minutes.
Chop onions, peppers and mushrooms.
Saute in skillet with meat.
Add salt and pepper.
Scoop out centers of zucchini.
Chop up centers and combine with meat.
Mix zucchini, centers, meat, stuffing and tomato paste.
Place lengthwise zucchini on a greased pan.
Stuff zucchini.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.

Bake roast in 2 cups water 1 hour at 450°. Take from oven and add sweet and Irish potatoes, carrots, salt, pepper and onions. Dilute mushroom soup with 2/3 cup water. Stir well and pour over other ingredients. Sprinkle with parsley flakes. Return to oven and bake 30 minutes.
Mix cake batter according to directions on box.
Pour into two greased 13 x 9-inch pans.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until done.
Cool completely.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pudding mixes, milk and coconut extract.
Beat 2 minutes; add cream cheese and beat well.
Stir in pineapple.
Spread over cooled cakes.
Top with whipped cream; sprinkle with coconut.
Chill for at least 2 hours.

Place asparagus in a baking dish. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon salt. Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes or until tender. Cook pasta according to package directions and drain. Combine onions, vinegar and soy sauce in blender. Gradually add 1/2 cup olive oil. Pour dressing over spinach, pasta and asparagus. Sprinkle cashews and Parmesan cheese on top. Serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Rub pork with liquid smoke and 1 1/2 tablespoons of salt.
Wrap with foil.
Place in roasting pan and bake 5 hours.
After baking, shred pork.
Sprinkle with remaining salt.
Serves 12.
Mix all liquids.
Slice oranges and limes and add to liquid. Add cherries.
Stir well, then add sherbet.
Stir lemon juice into Carnation milk until milk thickens.
Add salad dressing, pepper and mustard; mix well.
Combine salad dressing and remaining ingredients in large bowl.
Toss lightly; chill.
Brown beef with scallions in a large skillet, breaking beef into small pieces.
Stir in tomato sauce, water, olives and chili powder.
Bring to a full boil.
Stir in rice.
Cover, remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Stir with a fork.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Makes 4 servings.
Dredge strips in flour, salt and pepper.
Fry in Crisco or butter until browned.
Place in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Melt 1 stick of margarine.
Add garlic and pour over strips.
Pour in broth.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, garlic powder and parsley. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serve over noodles.
Dissolve jello in hot water. Add cream cheese and Marshmallow Creme. Place over low heat until Creme is melted. Remove and let cool. Add other ingredients. Chill and serve.

recipes.t: Beef And Noodles And Sour Cream
d: Cook onion in margarine until soft, add ground beef and cook. Place noodles in layer on top of cooked meat.
Mix tomato juice, salt, celery salt, pepper and Worcestershire.
Pour over noodles and beef.
Do not stir.
Cook 30 minutes.
Add sour cream and mix thoroughly.
Combine buttermilk, yolks and shortening.
Sift together dry ingredients and add other mixture.
Fold in egg whites.

recipes.t: Bakeless Pudding(Given To Clo Fletcher By Clara Hollingsworth)
d: Cream sugar and oleo.
Add crushed pineapple.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites and chopped pecans.
Layer with vanilla wafers in serving dish.
Top with whipped cream.
Refrigerate several hours.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease a muffin tin.
In a small saucepan, combine apple juice, 1/2 cup sugar and the cinnamon. Heat to boiling. Stir in crushed crackers.
Reduce heat to medium and continue cooking until mixture is the consistency of apple sauce. Remove from heat and stir in raisins.
Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl combine beef, tomato paste, sage and crackers or oatmeal.
Finely chop your onions and add to the mixture. Select the type of pepper you would like to use, making sure you test for hotness.
Add to the mixture.
Firmly press into a loaf pan and bake at 350° for about 2 hours.
About 5 minutes before being done top with the cheese and let melt on top.
Serve with a little salsa.
Bake
pie crust per directions, perforating bottom with fork and sprinkling with chili powder.
Grate and mix cheeses and combine with eggs, chili, olives, cottage cheese and green onion. Mix
well. Pour
mixture
onto
pie crust and bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Mix brown sugar, sugar, flour, nutmeg, salt and oil.
Take 1/2 cup and add 1 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/2 cup chopped nuts.
Set aside topping.
To the rest, add sour cream or buttermilk, baking powder, soda and eggs.
Beat with mixer.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle topping over all.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cook and drain sausage.
Add paprika, garlic powder and catsup.
Put mixture on rye bread and top with cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts.
Makes about 28 slices.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix brown sugar, shortening, molasses, water, egg and anise oil in large bowl.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Knead dough until stiff enough to mold.
Shape into 3/4-inch balls.
Place 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake about 12 minutes or until bottoms are brown.
Makes 8 dozen.

recipes.t: Watauga Medical Center Low-Fat Chocolate Cake
d: Mix water, puree, egg whites and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Sift together flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add sugar.
Mix dry and wet ingredients until well blended and smooth.
Saute shrimp in margarine and garlic.
Toss over high heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over cooked pasta.
Top with fresh diced tomatoes and parsley.
Heat oil in skillet.
Add onion and cook gently about 5 minutes.
Blend in flour; stir in tomato sauce and heat to boiling.
Mix in lemon juice, salt, pepper, sugar, horseradish, mustard and chicken.
Cover and cook gently, about 15 minutes. Serve on warmed hamburg buns.
In a blender container, combine buttermilk, orange juice concentrate, brown sugar and vanilla.
Cover and blend until smooth.
With blender running, add ice cubes, one at a time, through opening in lid.
Blend until smooth and frothy.
Makes 2 (about 10 ounce) servings.
Brown hamburger in oil with onion and bell pepper.
Add sauce, beans with liquid and tomatoes.
Add spice, then simmer about 45 minutes.
Mix oleo and the cheeses together.
Combine flour, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle
over
this,
mixing
well.
Roll pieces about the size of walnuts
with
your hands and press down the center of each with a
pecan half.
Bake at 325° for about 20 to 25 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 10-inch tube pan.
In small bowl, beat 2 egg whites until foamy.
Gradually add brown sugar.
Beat until stiff peaks form.
Fold in coconut and 1/2 cup ground pecans.
Spread meringue on bottom and up sides of pan to within 1 inch of top.
Blend cake mix, sour cream, Amaretto, 1/2 cup water, eggs and 2 egg yolks at low speed until moistened. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 65 minutes. Cool completely.
Blend powdered sugar, cocoa, Amaretto, butter, corn syrup and water until smooth.
Spoon over top of cake. Sprinkle with 2 teaspoons ground pecans.
Garnish with cherries.
Peel potatoes and cut into small cubes.
Place in large bowl and cover with water; set aside.
Slice sausage and cut slices in half or fourths.
Dice pepper and onion.
Heat oil in a large skillet.
Drain water off potatoes and carefully place in skillet. Cover skillet and turn potatoes about every 7 to 10 minutes to avoid sticking, but not too often or they will be mushy.
When potatoes begin to brown, add remaining ingredients.
Cook about 20 minutes.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Brown pork chops in oil.
Use the lid of your skillet to drain them in while you cook onion, bell pepper and soy sauce in skillet for 3 minutes.
Add water; bring to boil.
Add rice; lower heat and place pork chops in skillet.
Cover and cook on low about 20 minutes or until rice is done.
Cook beef, onion and taco seasoning until brown; drain and cool.
Toss lettuce and tomatoes and cooled meat.
Add cheese and crushed Doritos just prior to serving.
Use enough dressing to make salad moist.
Serves 6 to 8 as main meal, 10 to 12 as side dish. May add kidney beans, pinto beans or any other flavored beans to stretch the meal.
Heat a cast-iron frying pan on medium-high and add margarine. Saute onion and jalapenos for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add garlic and saute for 1 minute.
Add the beans and herbs.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Mash bean mixture in pan until pastry.
Stir in cheese and continue heating for 1 minute.
Serve hot with warm tortillas and salsa.
Drain cherries and set aside.
In medium saucepan, combine chocolate chips and evaporated milk.
Stir lightly.
Cook over very low heat, stirring constantly, until melted.
Remove from heat. Add almond extract. Pour into fondue pot or chafing dish.
Dip cherries into warm fondue.
Um Um! Makes 1 1/2 cups fondue.
Proceed as for Cucumber Salad I, but omit olive oil and sugar and substitute sour cream and dill.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In large bowl, beat cheese until fluffy; gradually beat in sweetened
condensed milk until smooth.
On low speed, beat in water
and
pudding mix until smooth. Fold in whipped cream and coconut.
Pour
into prepared pastry shell.
Chill 2 hours or until set.
Garnish as desired.
Refrigerate leftovers.

Brown the onion in butter in a large saucepan. Put the meat (cut into small pieces) over the onion. Sprinkle with salt. Add each vegetable by layers over the meat, sprinkling each layer with salt and a few tomato pieces. First add a layer of eggplant pieces. (The eggplant should be peeled and cut into large pieces), then a layer of green beans, then the squash (cut large) and then the okra. Finish by adding a last layer of quartered green peppers. Cover and cook on a very low heat for 2 hours, until meat is tender. Serve with cooked rice.
In mixing bowl, combine crackers, sugar, and margarine, mix well.
Press into 9-inch deep dish, pie pan plate.
In another mixing bowl, combine cream cheese, milk, lemon juice, vanilla flavoring and mix well.
Pour mixture into pie plate evenly.
Top pie with cherry pie filling and chill overnight.
Mix wet ingredients with sugars.
Add flours and baking soda. Mix well.
Add oats and chocolate chips.
Scoop with ice cream scooper onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
For chewy cookies, do not overbake.

Mix rice that has been cooked by directions. Saute in a little oleo before mixing. Add mayonnaise with soup. Add 1 cup cheese to mixture and mix all ingredients. Put in buttered dish. Top with cheese. Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°. This recipe freezes well.
Mix first 3 ingredients; let stand while next ingredients are mixed.
Mix next 4 ingredients and add yeast mixture.
Add flour and egg.
Mix well.
Add 3 to 4 cups flour and milk.
Mix well. Dough will be sticky.
Knead on floured surface and let sit for 10 minutes; pinch dough off for rolls.
Place in greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Place spinach in sieve and press out as much liquid as possible.
Combine spinach, cottage cheese and coconut.
Combine eggs, sour cream, flour and soy sauce in blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth; fold into spinach mixture.
Spoon into ungreased 2 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes. Allow to stand 10 minutes before serving.
Yields 12 servings.
Brown ground beef; add chili powder and tomato sauce to make a chili mixture to your own good taste.
In a separate saucepan, cook rice.
In a casserole dish, place a layer of the chili mixture, then a layer of the rice.
Sprinkle with chips and lastly, sprinkle on some of the grated cheese.
Repeat until all ingredients are gone.
Place in oven and bake until cheese is melted (about 15 minutes).
Cook milk, flour and salt until thick; let cool.
Then cream in the sugar, Crisco and vanilla flavoring, using mixer, until fluffy.
If too thick, add small amount of water.
Saute onion and pepper in 2 tablespoons oleo.
Add soups and tomatoes and heat.
Layer tacos, chicken, cheese and sauce.
Make 2 layers in 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Bake in 350° oven for 25 minutes or until bubbly all over.
In medium bowl, combine all ingredients except bread and margarine; mix well.
To assemble sandwiches, spread 1/2 cup of tuna mixture on each of 5 slices of bread.
Cover with remaining bread slices.
Spread margarine on outside of each sandwich.
Heat large skillet over medium-high heat or heat griddle to 375°.
Add sandwiches; cook 1 to 2 minutes on each side or until bread browns and sandwiches are hot.
Yields 5 sandwiches.
Cream butter well.
Add eggs, sugar, baking powder and whiskey.
Mix well.
Add almonds.
Add enough flour to thicken and roll (about 3 cups).
Roll into size and shape of small finger. Bake in 350° oven 15 to 20 minutes.
Dip cold cookies into powdered sugar until well coated.
Makes about 30 dozen.
Prepare pudding according to package directions. Add all fruit. Fold in 1/2 cup whipped cream. Serves 10.
Cream butter and sugar until light; beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add vanilla.
Sift together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cocoa powder; add to creamed mixture alternately with sour cream and water, beating after each addition.
Stir in sauerkraut and chopped nuts.
Pour into greased and floured 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool in pan.
Frost with favorite chocolate frosting.
Combine cream cheese and milk; beat until smooth.
Spread over bottom of 10-inch round dish.
Spread cocktail sauce evenly over cream cheese mixture.
Top with shrimp, cucumber and onion. Refrigerate until serving.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
(110 calories per serving.)
In medium mixing bowl, toss 3/4 cup of croutons with 2 tablespoons melted butter; set aside.
In large saucepan, cook zucchini in lightly salted water until barely tender (5 minutes). Drain.
Cook carrots and onions in 1/4 cup butter until tender. Add remaining croutons, soup, sour cream, pimento, salt and pepper.
Mix thoroughly.
Stir in cooked squash.
Spread in ungreased 1 1/2-quart glass baking dish.
Top with more croutons. Bake at 350° about 35 minutes or until hot and bubbly.

recipes.t: Gayle'S Oat Bran Applesauce Muffins(12 Muffins)
d: Combine wheat flour, oat bran, fructose, wheat germ, soda, baking powder, salt, cloves, nutmeg, allspice and cinnamon together.
Mix butter, oil, applesauce, buttermilk, egg and vanilla in mixture well.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Fill greased and floured muffin tins (paper cupcake liners may be used in muffin tins).
Also, if you don't have muffin tins, place cupcake liners in a 2-inch deep pan before filling.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, until lightly browned.
May be frozen.
Pour half the oil into a large skillet to coat bottom.
Place salmon in pan.
Pour remaining oil over top and add onion, olives and pepper.
Saute about 15 minutes, covered.
Serve alongside boiled potatoes, yucca or rice.
Brown ground beef, onions and green pepper in oil.
Add all remaining
ingredients,
except cheese and noodles.
Cook slowly for
hour.
Add cooked,
drained noodles.
Put in a large baking
dish.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°. Makes about 10 servings.
In a bowl, combine first four ingredients.
Spread mixture over toasted bread.
Place on foil-lined baking sheet; top with cheese.
Broil 4 inches from heat for approximately 2 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Cream butter. Add sugar, 1 cup at a time.
Beat at high speed after each cup.
Add whole eggs, one at
a
time.
Beat well after each at medium speed.
Add sour
cream;
beat well. Add soda, baking powder and salt to flour.
Add
dry
ingredients
1 cup at a time, mixing well after
each
addition.
Add flavorings.
Pour into
well-greased tube pan.
Bake
1/2 hours at 300°.
Let stand 10 minutes;
remove from pan.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease a 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie plate.
Mix Bisquick, water and refried beans.
Spread in pie plate.
Layer remaining ingredients on bean mixture.
Bake for 30 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

recipes.t: Oven Baked Catfish With Pecan Sauce
d: Preheat oven to
450°. Rinse fillets in cold water and pat dry.
Mix
cornmeal, bread crumbs, paprika, red pepper and salt. Dip fillets
in
milk,
shaking
off
excess, then into cornmeal mixture, coating well.
Place fish in single layer in greased baking pan and
drizzle with oil. Bake 10 minutes or until fish is golden brown
and
pulls apart easily with two forks at thickest point.
Serve with Pecan Sauce.

Combine cream cheese and onion. Add sauerkraut, corned beef, and 1/4 c. bread crumbs; mix well. Shape into 1 inch balls, roll in flour, dip in milk then into the remaining 3/4 c. bread crumbs. Pour salad oil into fryer to depth of two inches. Fry in hot oil for 1-2 minutes or until brown.
These can be made ahead and reheated. Makes about 50 appetizers.

recipes.t: Cornish Game Hens With Rice And Vegetables
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Rub hens with olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper.

Place in an oiled roaster. Cover and put in the oven. After 30 minutes, add the parsley, mushrooms and zucchini to the pan drippings and stir to coat. Cover and return to oven for 5 minutes. Add rice, 2 cups of stock or water and bay leaves.
Add additional salt and pepper to season rice, if needed.
Continue baking for about 30 minutes more.
Hens are done when golden brown and the wings separate from the body. Remove hens and rice to serving platter and garnish with fresh parsley. Serves 8.
Pat fish dry with paper towels.
Cut fish into serving size pieces.
In deep fryer or heavy saucepan, heat 2 to 3 inches oil to 375°.
In shallow dish, combine pancake mix, lemon pepper, beer and egg; mix until smooth.
Place crumbs in another shallow dish.
Dip fish into batter then into crumbs, covering completely.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and fish flakes with fork.
Keep fish warm until all pieces are cooked. Serve with lemon wedges or tartar sauce, if desired.
Yields 4 servings.
Melt butter in a large saucepan.
Remove from heat. Add sugars and Pet milk.
Blend well. Add eggs and beat well.
Stir in dry ingredients and lemon rind.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour into a 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan, well-greased and floured.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool and spread with the following.

recipes.t: Crock-Pot Chicken With Wine And Mushrooms
d: Combine salt, pepper, paprika, wine, cream of mushroom soup and mushrooms.
Add chicken and mixture to crock-pot.
Cook on low for 7 to 9 hours.
During last 30 minutes, stir in combined sour cream and flour.
Great served with noodles or rice.
In blender, combine banana, juice, ice and milk.
Cover and blend well.
Serve frothy and cold.
Mix eggs, butter, sugar and sour cream.
Sift dry ingredients together and add blueberries to the mixture.
Fold blueberry flour mix into egg mixture until blended.
Fill greased muffin tins 3/4 full.
Bake at 375° about 25 minutes.
Makes 12 to 14, depending on size of tins.
Sprinkle bits of topping on each muffin.
Butter a 2
1/2 quart casserole dish and add the ingredients in order
given:
potatoes,
onions, hamburg, noodles, tomatoes, salt, pepper, oregano and parsley.
Mix Jell-O with hot water.
Put 3 cans of cherries in a colander (you need the juice).
Substitute the juice for cold water and add more cold water (as much as Jell-O directions call for). Add lemon juice.
In a large skillet, saute onions in oil.
Remove onion; set aside.

On wax paper, mix salt, pepper and about 1/4 cup flour. Sprinkle steak seasoning on steaks and lightly flour; with skillet over medium heat, brown steaks for about 5 minutes on each side. Remove steaks.
Brown remaining flour.
Add water; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add onions and steak; simmer about 5 minutes.
Serve steak topped with onions and gravy.
Beat egg whites at room temperature until soft peaks form. Gradually add sugar and vanilla, beating until stiff peaks form. Fold in cracker crumbs and pecans.
Spread mixture into buttered 10-inch pie plate, spreading sides slightly higher.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool shell completely. Beat cream until foamy.
Gradually add powdered sugar, beating until soft peaks form.
Fold in berries.
Spread mixture evenly into pie shell.
Chill about 3 hours before serving.
Makes 1 pie. Similar to Strawberry Fluff at Cheese Barn.
Melt
margarine
over
low
heat.
Add chocolate. Stir until just
melted.
Remove
from heat. Stir in sweetener and vanilla. Combine with cream cheese. Beat until smooth. Stir in nuts and spread in lightly greased 8-inch square pan.
Refrigerate
until firm.
Cut into 1-inch squares.
Store in refrigerator.
(I use walnuts.)

recipes.t: Carrot Muffins With Cream Cheese Filling
d: Stir together flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. In separate bowl, combine egg, milk and oil.
Add to flour mixture; stir until moistened.
In covered pot, boil 6 inches of rib end pork loin cut into 3/4 to 1 inch slices in water, 1/2 up the level of the meat, 2 to 3 hours until it falls apart.
Add 1 teaspoon salt and pepper to taste to the pot during the cooking.
Strain pot liquid, cool and remove fat from the top.
Reserve it for adding as necessary to keep the meat moist.
Pick meat apart into slivers, put into pot with cider vinegar and Tabasco sauce.
Blend flavors over low heat at least 20 minutes adding pot liquor as needed to keep meat moist and from sticking to bottom of pot.
Serve hot on buns or rolls with cole slaw and extra Tabasco.
Makes 8 to 12 sandwiches.
Combine the marshmallows, cooked pumpkin, salt, cinnamon and ginger in the top of a double boiler.
Heat the mixture over half a pot of boiling water until the marshmallows are melted, stirring as the mixture melts.
Let cool to room temperature.

Mix caramel ice cream topping and Eagle Brand milk; pour over cooked cake (punch holes in top of cake so it will run down into the cake). Crumble Butterfinger candy bars on top of mixture; top with Cool Whip.
Crumble more Butterfinger candy bars on top of Cool Whip. Refrigerate.
Cook broccoli, drain and cover bottom of greased large casserole.
Add chicken.
Mix soups, mayonnaise, egg and lemon juice; spread over chicken.
Cover with cheese.
Melt butter and add to dressing.
(I also add some chicken broth.)
Spoon over soup mixture.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Saute oil and spaghetti until light brown.
Add broth, bouillon and chicken and cook 15 minutes.
Add vegetables and cook 15 minutes.
In 1-quart saucepan over low heat, heat chocolate and butter or margarine until melted and smooth.
Remove from heat.
Let stand 15 minutes to cool chocolate mixture slightly.
Stir together cream cheese and salad dressing.
Add olives, nuts, olive juice and pepper.
Mix well.
Refrigerate 24 hours. Mixture will be soft but hardens as it chills.
Spread on thin sliced whole wheat bread.

recipes.t: Dick Spencer'S Banana Bread(Changes For Zucchini Bread)
d: Beat eggs until frothy.
Beat in sugars, oil and vanilla. Continue beating until thick.
Stir in loosely packed bananas (or zucchini) and flour, sifted with cinnamon, soda, salt and baking powder.
Fold in nuts.
Pour into 2 oiled and floured 8 x 4 1/2 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour.
Glass loaf pans are preferred.
(If you reduce heat the last 10 to 15 minutes to 325°, the loaves won't burn on top.)
Brown hamburg, bacon, onion and garlic in skillet.
Add other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or simmer in crock-pot.
Spread brown sugar on each 1/2 strip of bacon.
Roll bacon strip around sliced water chestnuts and pineapple chunks and put toothpick through.
Bake at 350° until crisp.
Combine first 6 ingredients in shallow bowl; beat well.
Melt butter (2 tablespoons) in skillet; dip 4 bread slices, 1 at a time, into egg mixture, coating well.
Let drain; arrange in skillet and cook 4 minutes on each side or until browned.
Repeat procedure with remaining bread, adding butter as needed.
Serve toast with Orange Sauce.

In a large non-metal punch bowl or pitcher, combine pineapple juice, concentrates and water. Just before serving, add ginger ale, stirring gently. Serve with ice ring or ice cubes and fresh fruit slices. Makes 19 (1/2 cup) servings.
Drain peas and pimento.
Cook white sauce according to directions.
Combine all ingredients with white sauce.
Top with bread crumbs and bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir together the flour and salt.

Beat the butter. Add cream cheese, orange rind and sugar. Beat thoroughly until fluffy, texture of mayonnaise. Beat in egg yolk. Stir in flour mixture, all at once, until blended, then chocolate and walnuts. Drop by level tablespoonfuls 1-inch apart on lightly greased cookie sheets.
Flatten slightly with a small spatula. Bake in a moderate 350° oven about 15 minutes or until cookie edges are brown. Tops will be cream color.
Makes 3 1/2 dozen.
In a large saucepan, combine sugar, honey, vinegar, water, salt, celery seed, mustard seed and onion.
Bring to boiling and boil 2 minutes.
Add corn pieces.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until corn is tender.
Remove from heat.
Cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate until well chilled.
In a large buttered baking dish, mix all ingredients, except margarine. Salt and pepper to taste. Dot top of potatoes with margarine.
Sprinkle top with parsley. Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Brown the meat.
Add onions and peppers, cook.
Dump in the tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Mix everything else in.
Cook over medium-low heat.
Add chili powder to taste.
Brown sausage in medium skillet over medium heat; drain on paper towels.
Combine sugar and cornstarch in a medium saucepan. Add reserved pineapple juice and soy sauce; stir until well blended.
Cook over medium heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Add vinegar, pineapple, green pepper and sausage. Heat until hot.
Serve in a chafing dish.
Makes about 36 pieces.
You will need 4 soup bowls (bread).

Place broccoli flowerets in a 2-quart bowl. Stir in onion. Microwave (covered) for 7 minutes. Let rest for 2 minutes. Add chicken and soups (x 3). Microwave (covered) for 5 minutes. Pour in milk to desired consistency. Microwave (covered) another 5 minutes. Serve in bread bowls.

Melt 1 cup butter, sugar and cocoa over hot water. Remove from heat. Add 2 eggs, beaten with a fork. Mix. Pour over cracker crumbs and coconut. Mix and press into large 12 x 18 pan (or cookie pan). Freeze.
Mix milk and oats.
Add turkey, eggs, garlic, pepper, chili powder and chopped onion.
Form into meat loaf.
Place in baking dish.
Bake at 350° 1 1/2 hours until done.
Cream the butter and cheese.
Use at room temperature.
Sift in 10x sugar to creamed mix, then add coconut, salt and vanilla. Refrigerate batch for 1 hour.
Remove from refrigerator and shape into small size, about 1 1/2-inch size eggs.
Place on wax paper tray and refrigerate again for 1 hour.
Melt wax in a double boiler, then melt chocolate. Dip eggs in chocolate.
Use icepick or skewer.
Place on wax paper.
Makes about 120 eggs.
Place in plastic bag olive oil, basil and garlic powder.
Peel and slice zucchini lengthwise in thick pieces.
Place zucchini in bag with other ingredients and shake.
Cook zucchini on grill until nicely browned.
Brown bacon lightly with diced onion.
Add liquid drained from beans.
Cook down to about 1/2 cup liquid.
Add remaining ingredients and beans.
Cook until soft.
Serves 4.
Mix together first 7 ingredients.
Cook potatoes in salted water with bay leaf.
Cool.
When cold, peel and grate coarsely. Mix potatoes with mixture of first 7 ingredients and place in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Sprinkle top with mixture of grated cheese and potato chips.
Bake a few minutes more to melt cheese.
Heat corn syrup and sugar to boiling in heavy saucepan, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter. Pour over cereal and raisins (optional) and stir until well coated.
Press into ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan and cool.
Melt chips together and spread over top.
Cool, then cut into bars.
Melt chocolate morsels in top of double boiler; pour into bowl of electric mixer.
Add butter, egg yolks, sugar and flour; beat until light and fluffy.
Beat egg whites until stiff, not dry. Fold into batter.
Reserve one cup of batter.
Spread remainder in greased and floured 9-inch square baking pan; bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cool in pan.
Cream sweet butter; fold into reserved batter and beat in electric mixer until thick and light.
Spread butter cream on cake and sprinkle with grated chocolate.
Chill until firm.
The cake sinks as it cools, leaving a high rim of cake around edges.
When you frost the cake, do not attempt to cover the rim; spread frosting evenly, leaving rim exposed.
Dip sharp knife in hot water; cut 25 squares.
Refrigerate.
Heat milk butterscotch chips and marshmallows in double boiler until melted; mix well.
Cool until thick.
Mix margarine, coconut, graham cracker crumbs and pecan pieces together to make crust.
Put half of crumb mixture in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan, keeping the other half for the top.
Cut 1/2 to 1 gallon of softened ice cream into thin slices.
Place 1/2 of the thin sliced ice cream on the crust.
Pour the sauce over the frozen solid ice cream.
Set this in freezer to set up so you can repeat ice cream layer.
Repeat ice cream layer.
Top with rest of crumbs.
Saute onion in margarine. Stir in Beau Monde and next 4 ingredients. Cook, stirring constantly, until it begins to boil. Combine cornstarch and 2 cups skim milk gradually.
Add to hot mixture. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Cook 1 minute. Reduce heat and stir in crabmeat and sherry. Yields 5 cups.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Cool slightly.
Stir in buttermilk; chill until thick.
Fold in pineapple, lemon juice, cottage cheese, nuts, celery and mayonnaise.
Chill.
Serves 6 to 8.
Arrange veggies on microwaveproof platter in rings.
Lay pepper strips on top in a circle.
Place mushrooms and onions over top.
Sprinkle onion mix evenly over all.
Cover with plastic wrap and microwave on High for about 8 minutes or until done.
Do not add water.
Serve from same dish.

recipes.t: Ham And Scalloped Potatoes In The Crock-Pot
d: Layer potatoes, ham, onion and cheese twice.
Spoon soup over top (undiluted). Cook 8 hours on low.
You may add sweet peas or green beans.

recipes.t: Corn On The Cob With Herb Butter
d: Line bottom of large kettle with clean corn husks.
Top with corn.
Add 1-inch boiling water.
Cover tightly and steam 6 to 8 minutes.
Serve immediately.

recipes.t: Easy And Delicious Upside-Down Pineapple Cake
d: Melt butter and brown sugar in a large skillet.
Place pineapple slices in the bottom of the skillet.
Place the cherry halves in the center of the pineapple.
Mix the other ingredients together and pour into the skillet.
Bake at 350° until done, approximately 35 minutes.
Turn cake out of skillet.
Brown meat lightly in skillet. Add onion and pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are soft but not brown. Stir in flour, salt and pepper.
Add tomatoes. Cook until blended.
Stir until smooth and thickened. Add vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour into hot scone shell.
Place chard in a large bowl; set aside.
Cook turkey bacon until crisp.
Drain, crumble and set aside.
In same skillet, cook onion until tender, but not brown.
Blend in sugar, flour and salt.
Stir in water and vinegar.
Cook until thick and bubbly. Pour the hot mixture over the chard, tossing to coat.
Sprinkle with bacon.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Thaw pastry for 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°.
On a floured surface or between two sheets of waxed paper, roll the sheet of puff pastry into a 14-inch square.
In the center of the sheet, place chocolate chips, walnuts and butter.
Pull pastry edges together.
Twist and turn the ends together to seal "package".
Smooth folds in dough.
Place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20 minutes at 425°.
Let stand 10 minutes at least before cutting.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Cook wild rice.
Crumble sausage in frying pan and cook until done.
Mix together with can of mushroom soup.
Cook in preheated 350° oven for about 20 to 25 minutes.
In large bowl, mix
together
chicken, water chestnuts, grapes, celery and almonds.
(Can be prepared up to 8 hours in advance.)
Blend cake mix, pudding, water, eggs and oil.
Stir in coconut and pecans.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch layer pans. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

Cook brown sugar, margarine and light corn syrup in a small saucepan, just until margarine is melted. Pour mixture into 13X9 pan. Arrange bread slices in a single layer, but snugly packed on top of caramel syrup. In medium bowl mix, eggs, milk, cinnamon until well blended. Pour over bread in baking dish. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Remove cover. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes. or until center appears set and top is slightly brown. Let stand about 10 minutes before serving. Serve two slices on plate topped with fresh fruit and whipped cream or powdered sugar.
Saute pieces of Kielbasa in butter; add onion and green pepper and continue to saute until done.
Add tomatoes and juice.
Add all remaining ingredients and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Split an angel food cake into 4 layers.
Whip cream with confectioners sugar until stiff.
Combine pineapple with 1/2 cup whipped cream.
Combine mashed apricots with 1/2 cup whipped cream.
Combine jam with 1/2 cup whipped cream.
Spread one filling on each layer.
Use the rest of the whipped cream to frost the cake.
Decorate with chopped nuts, if desired.
Refrigerate 12 hours before serving.

Mix ground beef, soup and eggs together. Shape into small meatballs. Place in a 9 x 13 pan. Cover with sauerkraut. Mix together the rest of ingredients and heat to dissolve cranberry sauce a little. Spoon mixture over sauerkraut and bake, covered, at 350° for 1 hour. Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.
Peel bananas and press through sieve.
Put pulp into saucepan with sugar, salt and butter.
Stir and cook until mixture starts to boil.
Remove from fire and cool.
(If firmer mixture is desired, 1 teaspoon gelatin may be added at this point.)
When it is cool, whip in the wine or lime juice and nutmeg.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Top with whipped cream.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
