Combine cabbage, peppers and onion in a large bowl.
In a one quart saucepan, combine vinegar, oil, sugar, mustard, celery seed, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil over moderate heat, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Boil 3 minutes.
Pour hot dressing over cabbage mixture and toss well.
Stand at room temperature 30 to 60 minutes, tossing occasionally.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 to 2 days before serving.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine first 7 ingredients.
Mix well.
Spread into a 8 1/2 x 4 1/2
x 2 1/2 inch loaf pan. Bake 1 hour.
Drain excess drippings.
Spoon chili sauce over cooked meat loaf; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake an additional 15 minutes. Serves 6.
Cut chicken breasts in half and pound lightly.
Mix flour, salt, pepper and parsley.
Dredge chicken into seasoned flour. Heat olive oil and butter.
Add chicken; saute quickly to a golden brown.
Lightly sprinkle with garlic salt.
Remove from heat and layer with Prosciutto and cheese slices.
Sprinkle grated cheese and pour chicken stock into skillet.
Bake, uncovered, for 10 minutes, until cheese is melted and lightly browned.
In large skillet over medium heat, slowly saute the almonds in butter about 6 to 7 minutes or until golden; drain off excess butter.
In small bowl, combine celery salt, chili powder and ground red pepper; toss almonds in mixture until well coated. Spread almonds on foil to cool.
Store in airtight container.

recipes.t: Angie'S Texas Size Chocolate Chip Cookies
d: Cream the butter and shortening.
Add sugar, eggs, corn syrup and vanilla; beat well.
Combine dry ingredients and add to mixture.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Line 2 pizza pans with foil; spread batter in pans.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 17 minutes or until light brown.
Remove from oven.
Let cookies cool in pans.
When cool, remove foil and place back in pan or on a plate.
Cut potatoes in half; slice approximately 1/4-inch thick, leaving skin on.
Cut margarine in slices; place half on bottom of an 8 x 10-inch aluminum pan.
Spread potatoes out.
Sprinkle with onion and peppers; place rest of margarine over it.
Cover with tinfoil and place on grill.
Occasionally remove foil and gently roll potatoes over until slightly brown.
Mix sugars in heavy pan.
Add Karo, milk and salt.
Stir in butter until melted.
Add pecans.
Place pan in cold water and stir until mixture begins to lose gloss.
Drop by spoonfuls onto buttered foil.
Let harden, then they are ready to eat.
Easy, foolproof and wonderful!
Beat sugar and margarine until it is very smooth.
Add the egg and beat just a little.
Add flour and flavoring.
Knead or pull and mash the dough with your hands until it is smooth.
In 2 quart saucepan, melt butter.
Saute onion over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add garlic.
Cook 3 minutes more.
Add potatoes, broth and milk.
Stir over medium heat until smooth.
Simmer an additional 8 minutes.
Add cheese and Tabasco sauce.
Stir gently until cheese melts and soup is hot.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Sprinkle with parsley.
In a stainless steel or aluminum pan (do not use Teflon or nonstick) put first 4 ingredients.
Cook on high heat, stirring until mixture is the color of brown sugar.
Spread on a cookie sheet.
Cover with chocolate chips, spreading evenly with spatula as they melt.
Sprinkle on almond slivers.
Cool.
This candy is like a Heath bar.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Scald milk and pour over bread crumbs. Cool; add sugar, beaten eggs, salt and nutmeg.
Mix and fold in sliced peaches.
Turn into buttered baking dish.
Bake for 1 hour.
In large bowl, combine first 5 ingredients.
Stir in sour cream.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Stir in peach halves and sprinkle with almonds.
Serves 10 to 12 people.
Soften cream cheese.
Blend in mayo and sugar.
Add fruits and nuts.
Fold in whipped cream to which the powdered sugar and vanilla has been added.
Pour into Pyrex pan that has been lined with waxed paper.
Freeze 6 hours before serving.
Let juice stand at room temperature for 10 minutes.
In bowl, mix peanut butter and sour cream.
Stir in juice until smooth. Serve with fruit or toast.
Makes 2 1/4 cups.
Sift together first six ingredients.
Toss walnuts into dry mixture.
Cut
in
butter; add milk, egg and carrots.
Mix lightly, being
careful
not
to
overmix. Spoon into greased muffin tins until almost full.
Bake in preheated 400° oven 20 minutes.
Makes one dozen muffins.
In a medium sized skillet, heat oil, adding celery, onion, green pepper, garlic, salt and meat.
Cook until the onion is tender.
Drain off fat.
Stir in the pork and beans, lima beans with liquid and chili sauce.
Do not cover.
Simmer about 10 minutes.
Serve while hot.

Mix hamburger, rice, onions and green pepper. Make into meatballs. Brown in a deep skillet. Once they are brown, pour in ketchup and water. Simmer about 45 minutes. More water may be added while simmering.
Heat oil in saucepan 1 minute.
Saute onion.
Stir in garlic, marjoram and rosemary and saute 2 minutes longer.
Add spinach; cover.
Cook over moderate heat until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add chickpeas and stock and bring to a simmer over moderate heat.
Add pasta and cook uncovered 10 minutes until pasta is tender.
Stir in salt and pepper.
Serve with Parmesan cheese.
Saute butter, shallots and garlic, stirring frequently for 5 minutes.
Add basil, parsley, wine, cream, lemon juice, pepper and salt.
Cook over medium heat until mixture is reduced to about 1/2 (stir frequently).
Taste for seasoning, adding pepper and salt as needed.
Mix lemon (juice and pulp), soy sauce, vinegar, seasoning and mustard.
Marinate salmon 1 hour.
Fry 7 to 10 minutes per side in hot oil in frying pan.
Dice pickles and onion as fine as possible.
Add juice and mayonnaise.
Serve.
Bake angel food cake mix according to directions in 9 x 13 x 2 pan.
Let cake cool.
Cut cake in 2 pieces that are about 1 inch thick (9 x 13 x 1) Combine cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Add condensed milk.
Add dry pudding mix. Add 1 1/2 cups of Cool Whip. Line bottom of 9 x 13 x 2 pan with 1 piece of angel food cake. Spread cream cheese mixture evenly over cake.
Top with 2/3 of the strawberries and all but 50 of the blueberries.
Place 2nd piece of angel food cake on top. Spread remaining Cool Whip on top. Place remaining strawberries & blueberries on Cool Whip to create a flag design.
In a large bowl, cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, one at a time; mix well.
Combine dry ingredients; add alternately with milk to creamed mixture.
Stir in oatmeal,
raisins (soak raisins in hot water, then drain if you like moister raisins) and nuts. Drop dough by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for about 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool on wire racks.
Makes 5 dozen.
Sift flour once, measure and sift 3 times with other dry ingredients.
Add oats.
Cream butter; add sugar and mix well. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Add nuts, raisins and milk.
Add flour mixture in small amounts at a time and blend.
Drop from teaspoon on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake in moderate oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 6 dozen.
Combine soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and pepper in small bowl. Dredge chicken in cornstarch.
Heat oil in wok over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and garlic; stir-fry until chicken is opaque, about 5 minutes.
Add soy mixture and stir-fry 30 seconds.
Mix in green onions.
Serve over rice.
Sort through and discard any foreign material.
Thoroughly wash and drain beans.
Combine beans, water, 1/3 cup of picante sauce, onion, salt and garlic in a Dutch oven.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and cover; simmer 3 to 4 hours or until beans are tender and mash easily.
Stir occasionally.
Drain beans, reserving liquid.
Return beans to Dutch oven or large mixing bowl.
Add butter and remaining picante sauce.
Beat at low speed with mixer, adding liquid as necessary, until desired consistency.
Spray baking dish with Pam. Layer apple slices. Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon. Add water and bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes.
Brown the roast in oil, searing the outside.
This will make a dark, rich gravy.
Add to this the other ingredients, especially the Kitchen Bouquet seasoning.
The Kitchen Bouquet gives the meat a wonderful flavor.
Cook in a pressure cooker for 30 minutes at 15 pounds pressure or cook in a Dutch oven for 2 hours on a medium heat.
Keep covered.
In a saucepan, mix the soup, water, milk and nutmeg.
Heat to boiling.
Serve hot, sprinkled with cheese.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Boil yams until tender, then drain and mash well.
Set aside.
Sift flour, baking powder, nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, allspice and salt.
Set aside.
Next, cream butter and brown sugar in a large bowl until light.
Add eggs one at a time to mixture, beating well after each addition.
Add half of dry ingredients and stir well, then add half of the half and half and stir well.
Repeat the same steps with the rest of the dry ingredients and half and half.
Add mashed yams and vanilla and beat well.
Pour into buttered 8 x 11 1/2-inch baking dish and bake in middle shelf of oven for 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Serves 8.

recipes.t: Glazed Carrots With Onion And Bacon
d: Boil carrots, covered, in a small amount of water until crisp-tender and drain.
Cook bacon in a skillet until crisp, drain, reserving 1 tablespoon drippings in skillet.
Crumble bacon and set aside.
Saute onion in reserved drippings, until tender. Add pepper, brown sugar and carrots.
Cook until thoroughly heated.
Sprinkle with bacon.
Serves 4 to 6.
Dissolve Jell-O in one cup boiling water.
Add thawed strawberries, undrained rhubarb and pineapple.
Set in refrigerator till thickened.
Mix Dream Whip as directed.
Blend in softened cream cheese to topping.
Pour onto top of Jell-O mixture and sprinkle with chopped nuts if desired. Let set for 3 hours.
Parboil potatoes which have been peeled and cut in 1/2-inch strips the length of potato or 1/2-inch rounds.
Drain and set aside (don't overcook).
Combine sugar, Karo and water.
Bring to light boil.
Add butter and potatoes.
Cook on simmer until done. Be sure you don't overcook.
Sift sugar and spices three times.
Spread half the mixture in 1/4-inch layer on a baking sheet.
Beat egg white, honey and salt together until mixed thoroughly.
Add nut halves; stir until coated well.
Place nuts on sugar mixture one at a time; cover with remaining sugar mixture.
Bake at 275° for 1 hour.
Cool and store in covered jar.
Cover carrots with salted boiling water in a skillet.
Cover and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes.
Drain carrots and return them to the skillet.
Add butter, sugar and vermouth.
Cook uncovered for 5 minutes or until wine has evaporated and carrots are glazed and shiny.
Garnish with parsley.
Serve hot.
Serves 4.
In roaster (to fit bird) put clean and seasoned turkey.
(Rub with butter and seasonings.)
Add onions, cleaned and cut into wedges.
Pour broth over all.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour. Reduce heat to 300° and cook 15 minutes per pound of meat, usually about 1 to 1 1/2 hours (no basting).

Add strawberries to jello and pour into the crust, let it stand for 30 minutes. Make the pudding while jello is setting. Pour over jello layer, let it stand for another 30 minutes, until set. Spread "La Creme" on top and decorate with slivered almonds.
Put green beans in bottom of pan.
Mix soup, cheese, sour cream, onion and water chestnuts. Pour over green beans.
Pour creamed corn on
top. Cover with Ritz cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until bubbly.
Great for diabetics.
Sift together first 4 ingredients.
Stir in next 3 ingredients.
In another bowl, beat eggs until light.
Add milk and oil.
Stir into flour mixture.
Pour into a greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes.
Remove to rack and cool completely.
Saute onion in butter until transparent.
Add pimientos, water chestnuts and soup and mix well.
Pour mixture over frozen peas in baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Prepare macaroni according to package directions; drain.
Beat egg, milk and salt together.
Blend into macaroni and spread on greased 10 x 15-inch jelly roll pan.
Spoon on spaghetti sauce. Top with pepperoni, onion, mushrooms, olives and cheese.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Stick cloves in peeled orange.
Place on foil lined pan and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix remaining ingredients in large pot and bring to a simmer. Remove orange from oven.
Discard cloves and add orange to punch.
Serve.
Cut green and red peppers into quarters; remove seeds.
Peel and quarter onions; grind carrots, green and red peppers and onions through food chopper (coarse).
Place in kettle.
Cover with boiling water.
Stir in sugar, salt and vinegar.
Bring to boiling point.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally for 5 minutes.
Ladle into hot sterilized jars and seal.
Yield: about 8 to 8 1/2 pint jars.
Mix seasoned bread cubes as directed on package; set aside. Brown and drain beef; season with pepper and onion to taste. Spread meat in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Add 1/2 can water to 1 can soup; pour over meat.
Pack bread crumbs over meat; poke holes (using long-tined fork) in stuffing mixture.
Add 1/2 can water to second can of soup; pour over stuffing.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix crushed crackers, Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, parsley and pepper.
Dip chicken pieces in butter, then dredge in cracker mixture.
Arrange in single layer in shallow baking dish.
Drizzle any remaining butter over chicken. Bake 15 to 20 minutes, then turn pieces and bake an additional 15 to 20 minutes (depending on thickness of pieces).
Saute mushrooms and onion in butter with juice of 1 lemon. Saute cauliflowerets in butter with garlic, basil, salt and peeper to taste.
Mix all ingredients and put in greased casserole dish. Cover and bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Saute onion and green pepper in margarine in a large skillet 2 minutes.
Add frozen okra, garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat 4 minutes, stirring gently.
Add corn and cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomato and squash to skillet; continue to cook over medium heat 5 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and let stand 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove garlic before serving.
Yields 8 servings.
Serving size:
1/2 cup. (Low cholesterol recipe.)
Heat oven to 350°.
Generously butter 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan. Combine cocoa, Splenda and flours stirred to evenly distribute. Combine melted butter with beaten eggs; stir in vanilla and almond extracts.
Add flour mixture and stir until well-combined.
Stir in almonds, if using.
Spread in pan and bake in center of oven for 25 minutes.
Cool in pan; cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Cut beef into small pieces.
Place in casserole dish.
Cover with undiluted soup.
Rinse can with about 1/4 cup water.
Season. Cover and bake in slow to moderate oven for 2 hours or until cooked (should break apart easily).
Serve with mashed potatoes.
Mix chilled fruit juices and water in punch bowl.
Just before serving, add slightly softened sherbet and stir briefly.
Add chilled Sundrop and serve.
Serves 16.
Dissolve gelatin in cold water and set aside.
Combine egg yolks, sugar, salt and milk.
Cook in double boiler until mixture coats the spoon. Stir in gelatin.
Cool.
Fold in 1/2 pint whipping cream.
Butter a 9 x 13 pan.
Crumble or slice cake and line pan with half.
Spread half of custard on top.
Cover with remaining half of cake and custard.
Whip other 1/2 pint of cream; spread over filling.
Garnish with cherries or shaved chocolate. Refrigerate.
Keeps well.
Serves 12.
Cook rice.
Saute butter, celery and onion; set aside.
In large saucepan, melt soup, cheese and Pet milk.
Combine broccoli and cooked rice; salt and pepper to taste.
Add liquid mixture to broccoli and rice mixture, then add celery and onions.
Pour into 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Top with shredded Cheddar cheese and pimento slices, if desired.
Bake at 325°, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Cover cucumbers, onion, peppers, garlic and salt with ice cubes and mix, let stand 3 hours then drain.
Add sugar, turmeric, celery seed, mustard seed and vinegar - bring to a boil.
Seal in hot jars.
Layer a 9 x 13-inch casserole pan.
First, layer sauce. Second, layer cabbage.
Third, Mix uncooked rice and uncooked meat.
Continue layering until pan is full.
Top with crushed tomatoes.
Cover and cook at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or until cabbage is cooked.

Roll beef in flour. Brown in oil in Dutch oven. Add onion, garlic and salt. Saute. Add beer, mushrooms, carrots and bay leaf. Cover and simmer slowly 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Add potatoes and peas last 1/2 hour.
Combine chocolate chips and walnuts or pecans.
Remove a spoonful of cake mix and toss it with chips and nuts.
In a mixing bowl, combine all ingredients, except the chips, nuts and confectioners sugar.
Mix well.
Fold in chips and nuts.
Pour into greased and floured tube or Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done.
Remove from pan and cool on wire rack.
Dust with confectioners sugar to serve.

Cut tops off green peppers and remove seeds and membrane. Mix beef with rice, onion, salt, pepper and garlic. Fill peppers with meat mixture. Arrange snugly in 3-quart casserole, with one pepper in the center of the dish. Mix together soup and water. Pour over and around peppers. For the microwave, cover with plastic wrap, leaving a vent. Cook 28 minutes on high. For the oven, cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Peel, halve and pit peaches.
Reserve 1 peach half for garnish.
Cut remaining peaches into chunks.
In blender at medium speed, blend peach chunks and sugar until smooth.
In small bowl with mixer at medium speed, beat heavy or whipping cream and almond extract until stiff peaks form.
With rubber spatula or wire whisk, fold peach puree into whipped mixture.
Arrange cauliflower, broccoli, and zuchinni on plate and cover with saran wrap.
Microwave approximately 8 minutes.
Let stand for 2 minutes with the wrap still on it.
Drain liquid off. Pour 3 Tbsp. butter with 1/2 tsp. garlic powder over top.
Cover with cheese and add tomatoes.
Microwave uncovered for 1 1/2 minutes.
Grind together the linguica, onion and cheese using food grinder or food processor.
Cut crust off bread and quarter each slice.
Top each piece of bread with linguica mixture.
Bake on cookie sheet at 425° for 10 minutes or until top browns and cheese melts.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook potatoes until tender but firm, about 15 minutes. Drain potatoes and transfer to a medium bowl.
Mash together with milk.
Place leeks in a medium saucepan with enough water to cover and bring to a boil.
Cook 10 minutes or until tender.
Drain and set aside.
In a medium skillet over medium heat, cook and stir the ground beef until evenly brown.
Mix in the onion, red and green bell peppers.
Season with green chile peppers and soy sauce.
Continue to cook and stir until vegetables are tender.
In a medium baking dish, mix mashed potatoes, leeks and ground beef mixture.
Sprinkle with cheddar cheese and top with ham.
Bake 25 minutes in preheated oven until bubbly and lightly browned. Serves 8.
Cream vegetable shortening with the sugar.
Add the eggs and mix well.
Add the milk and mix well again.
Sift into the first mixture the flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix by hand.
Fold in the blueberries very gently.
Fill muffin tins to the top. Sprinkle each muffin with sugar.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Wrap the chicken in one piece of bacon. Mix together the golden cream of mushroom soup, sour cream and milk. Pour over chicken breasts. Bake at 300° for 2 hours, covered, or 1 hour, uncovered.
Beat butter 30 minutes or until light and fluffy; add 1/2 cup powdered sugar and beat well.
Add the egg yolks and continue beating.
Add vanilla and enough flour to make a soft dough.
Roll into small balls.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Have powdered sugar sprinkled on a large sheet pan or paper.
Sprinkle powdered sugar on top while still warm.
Saute chopped onion and green pepper in a tablespoon of butter.
Brown hamburger meat and drain.
Add 2 packages of spaghetti sauce mix.
Add diced tomatoes, Ro-Tel and tomato sauce. Add water if needed.
Stir.
Bring to a boil.
Slowly add the uncooked spaghetti noodles and stir.
Let simmer on low until noodles are cooked.
Stir frequently.
After noodles are cooked, cover and let simmer on low, stirring occasionally.
The longer it simmers, the better flavor it will have.
May be refrigerated overnight.
In a medium saucepan, simmer sugar, coffee, shortening, raisins and apple together for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Cool 10 minutes.
In a large bowl mix together flour, baking soda, baking powder, all the spices and the nuts.
Pour sugar-raisin mixture into dry ingredients; mix well.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until center of cake springs back when lightly pressed with fingers.
Brown hamburger in large skillet.
Blend next 6 ingredients. When hamburger is brown, drain and mix dry ingredients with beef. Add the water and noodles.
Cook covered over medium heat approximately 10 to 12 minutes or until noodles are tender.
Serves 5 or 6. (One cup uncooked rice may be substituted for the noodles.) Cook 15 to 20 minutes.
Melt in microwave on High, the first three items for 1 1/2 minutes. Stir in the flour and nuts.
Let dough set for 5 to 10 minutes.
Drop by teaspoon and bake for 7 minutes.
Drain pears, save 1 cup pear juice; set pears aside.
In 2-cup measure, combine cornstarch, brown sugar, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Blend in pear juice.
Microwave on High 2 to 5 minutes, until thick, stirring 1 or 2 times.
Set aside.
Put pears in 9-inch pie plate.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave on High 2 to 3 minutes, until hot.
Line salad plates with lettuce leaves, put pears on lettuce, top with walnuts.
Put 2 to 3 tablespoons juice on top.
Stir and brown ground beef and 1-1/2 tsp. of salt.
Chop course in food grinder or food processor potatoes, carrots and onions and add to browned meat mixture.
Add 1 tsp. salt, pepper and milk.
Cover and cook slowly 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Stir occasionally, adding more milk if needed. Continue cooking uncovered about 3 minutes longer or until thick.
Mix flour, sugar, baking soda and salt.
Stir in yogurt and milk until moistened.
Fill muffin cup 3/4 full.
Bake 18 minutes until brown at 400°.
Makes 12.
Mix cake mix, jello and flour.
Add water and oil.
Beat well. Add eggs, one at a time.
Add vanilla and strawberries.
Bake in layers for 25 minutes in 350° oven.
Unroll crescent rolls to form a long rectangle on an ungreased cookie sheet; pinch perforations together.
Add soup, pepper and onion to beef.
Place mixture down the middle of pastry.
Pull up edges to form a rim.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until light brown.
Place cheese on top and bake an additional 5 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Sift flour, sugar, salt and baking powder into a large bowl. Cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Mix in raisins, walnuts and nutmeg.
Stir in eggs and vanilla until well blended (mixture will be dry).
Turn out onto a lightly floured board and pat to a 1/4-inch thickness.
With a floured cutter, cut into 2-inch rounds.
Cream butter, Crisco and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Mix well.
Alternately add milk and flour.
Add flavorings.
Cook at 325° for 1 hour.
Test with straw.
If not done, cook 15 minutes longer.
Boil stew meat for 2 to 3 hours, or until tender, adding water as needed.
Add carrots and green peppers.
Cook for 15 minutes. Add potatoes, onions, salt and peppers; cook for 20 to 30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Add tomato sauce.
Heat through.
Saute bacon and onion until bacon begins to crisp; remove excess bacon grease, if desired.
Add milk, broth and thyme; bring to a boil.
Stir in potatoes; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in parsley, salt and pepper.
Makes 6 servings, each with 175 calories, 14 g fat and 24 mg cholesterol.
Soften yeast in warm water and set aside.
Into mixing bowl, sift together flour and salt.
Cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored.
Mix in sour cream, vanilla and yeast.
Add to flour mixture.
Stir until thoroughly blended.
Cover and chill for at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle several tablespoons of sugar on board and place dough on sugar.
Roll into 12-inch square.
Fold dough over at ends to measure 12 x 4-inches, working quickly.
Re-roll in similar way three to six times more, using 2 to 4 tablespoons sugar each time.
The last time roll dough 1/4-inch.
Brush with egg white and sprinkle with remaining sugar.
Cook chicken.
Remove; keep warm.
In same skillet, cook spinach and mushrooms; stir for 3 minutes.
Stir in Lipton mix that has been blended with water.
Bring to a boil until sauce thickens. Pour vegetable mixture over chicken.
Serves 4.
Saute garlic and onion in olive oil until golden.
Add cubed chicken.
Aside, mix cool bouillon, water, cornstarch and wine and add to chicken mixture.
Cook, uncovered, on low heat at first, and then for 3 minutes on medium heat.
Serve over rice or angel hair pasta.
(Green beans may be added as last step while on medium heat; optional.)
Mix sugar and flour; add eggs and then butter.
Add English walnuts, chocolate chips and vanilla.
Pour into unbaked pie shell and bake 30 minutes in a preheated 350° oven.
You may have to bake it longer because ovens vary.
Test with a toothpick.
It should be chewy but not runny and is traditionally served warm.
Peel cucumber, cut in half and seed.
Dice the seeded cucumber.
In pan cook cucumber and water (shaking or stirring to prevent burning) for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cool slightly.
Put cucumber in bowl and add rest of ingredients.
Stir and cool.
Cook salmon in your favorite way.
Serve with sauce.
Cream together cream cheese and Cool Whip. Set aside.
Drain mandarin oranges, pineapple chunks and cherries. Mix all ingredients together in large bowl.
Add mini-marshmallows.
Add 1/2 cup walnuts if desired.
Chill 1 hour.
Bake potatoes at 400° until tender.
Cool.
Remove skins. Mash or whip potatoes in large mixing bowl.
Add butter, sugar, salt and extracts.
Set aside.
In small bowl, beat egg yolks slightly.
Add to potato mixture with milk/cream.
Set aside. Whip egg whites until soft peaks form.
Fold gently into potato mixture.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes; reduce temperature to 350°.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until center is cooked.
Combine soups and cream.
Do not boil.
Add crab meat and simmer 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add cooking sherry and sprinkle paprika on top of each bowl.
Combine juices and sugar; chill several hours.
Place ice in a punch bowl and add juice mixture.
Slowly pour in ginger ale and carbonated water.
Float fruit slices on top.
Serves 75.
In mixing bowl, cream together shortening, brown sugar and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Add applesauce; mix well.
Sift together flour, salt, cinnamon, baking powder and baking soda.
Add dry ingredients to applesauce mixture, mixing well.
Stir in oats and raisins.
Drop by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Yields 7 dozen cookies.
In Dutch oven over medium heat, cook spuds and onion in butter, stirring occasionally, 10 minutes.
Stir in salt, pepper, bay leaf and water.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add milk and fish; bring just to boil.
Reduce heat and cover.
Simmer very gently for 15 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork. Sprinkle with dill weed (optional).
Combine all ingredients except chicken and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cool slightly.
Put chicken in 9 x 13 pan.
Pour sauce over and marinate several hours in refrigerator.
Bake in oven at 350° until done or can be grilled on pit.
Melt margarine in saucepan.
Add celery and onion.
Cook over low heat about 5 minutes.
Do not brown.
Stir in flour.
Add milk (all at once).
Cook, stirring until thick and boiling.
Remove from heat and stir in tuna and salt.
Quickly add egg yolks.
Fold in egg whites.
Turn into greased 9-inch pie pan.
Bake at 325° for 45 to 50 minutes, until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Serve hot.
Stir 1 cup of hot water into loaf mix.
Add tomato sauce, tomatoes, oregano, basil and garlic powder.
Grease or spray a 9 x 12-inch or equivalent baking dish.
Cover bottom of dish with a thin layer of sauce mixture.
Arrange 3 noodles on top of sauce. Top with a little sauce and part of cheese mixture.
Repeat process 2 more times, ending with Mozzarella cheese on top.
Top with separated frozen Saucettes.
Cook at 325° for 1 hour.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Cream together oleo, brown sugar and egg.
Add flour, baking soda and salt.
Mix good.
Then add pineapple and nuts.
Drop on greased cookie sheet by teaspoonful.
Bake 12 minutes at 350°. Cut marshmallows in half.
Have them cut and ready as soon as you bring cookies out of oven, put a 1/2 marshmallow on top.
Cook sugar, butter or oleo and pet milk to soft ball stage. Remove from fire and add marshmallow cream, chocolate chips, vanilla and nuts.
Pour into well greased 9x13 pan.
Stem and seed pepper halves.
Cook in boiling salted water for 3 minutes; drain.
Place cut side up in shallow baking dish. Brown beef, onion and garlic in skillet.
Add tomatoes, water, barbecue sauce and salt; bring to a boil.
Stir in pasta.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Mix in corn.
Spoon mixture into pepper halves.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 400° for 8 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add sugar, juices, and enough water to make a gallon.
Add ginger ale when ready to serve.
Place cucumber slice on a round toast bed or Wheat Thin.
In the center of the cucumber, squeeze a small circle of anchovy paste.
Press a stuffed olive slice into the paste.

Cut the pear and apple into 3/4 inch pieces. Toss with raisins. Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet. When it sizzles, add the fruit and cook, stirring gently, for 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in maple syrup and cinnamon; cook until the fruit begins to soften and the sauce is slightly thickened, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from heat and gently stir in the vanilla. Serve over pancakes or waffles. Also good with yogurt or ice cream.
Slice apples into frying pan; add butter.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon together.
Add to apples and butter; heat until good and hot.
Pour into pie crust; add top crust or strips across.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Stir in sugar, salt and beaten egg.
Add vanilla.
Place shortening in bread bowl.
Pour yeast mixture over and mix with spoon.
Gradually add flour, 1 cup at a time and mix until somewhat sticky dough is formed.
Turn out onto floured surface.
Roll out to 1/4-inch.
Cut with biscuit cutter. Place in baking sheet.
Pat with melted butter and fold in half. Pinch closed.
Let rise until double, about 1 hour.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix together and spread on small platter the cream cheese, curry powder, mayonnaise and milk.
Sprinkle on cheese mixture in this order the olives, shrimp and hard-boiled eggs.
Serve on crackers.
In a metal tray, stir together 1 cup of the grapefruit juice and the sugar until the sugar is dissolved; fit the tray with the divider and freeze the mixture until it is frozen solid.
In another metal ice tray fitted with the divider, pour 1 cup of the pineapple juice and freeze it until it is frozen solid.

(The fruit mixtures may be prepared up to this point 1 day in advance.) In a blender, blend the frozen grapefruit juice mixture with 1 1/2 ounces of tequila and the remaining 1/4 cup grapefruit juice, scraping down the sides occasionally, until the mixture is smooth but still frozen and divide the mixture between 2 stemmed glasses. In the cleaned blender, blend the frozen pineapple juice with the remaining 1 1/2 ounces tequila and the remaining 1/4 cup pineapple juice, scraping down the sides occasionally, until the mixture is smooth but still frozen.
Pour over grapefruit mixture.
Makes 2 drinks.

Rinse cabbage and tear into pieces. Set aside to drain. Saute the meat, onion and garlic in olive oil. Drain off any grease. Add tomato sauce, salt, thyme and pepper. Stir to blend. In a casserole sprayed with PAM, place half of the cabbage and then half of the meat sauce. Repeat the layers and then top with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan.
Cook the garlic and onion over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes or until soft but not brown. Add 2 cups water and bring to a rapid boil.
Bring water to boil with salt, onion powder and sugar.
Turn off electric burner.
Stir in corn meal vigorously.
Dip hands in water and roll out about 1 tablespoon at a time in cocoon shape. Deep fry.
Drain
pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Mix in pecans and Eagle Brand milk.
Mix marshmallows in last.
In a large saucepan, heat margarine over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and saute for about 5 minutes, or until softened. Add stock, potatoes and red pepper flakes and simmer, covered, for about 20 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
Transfer half the potatoes and 1 cup cooking liquid to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
Return to saucepan.
Meanwhile, steam kale for 5 to 10 minutes or until tender.
Stir it into the soup.
Heat through and season with salt and pepper.
Yield:
4 to 6 servings.
In 5 quart Dutch oven over medium heat saute bacon for 3 minutes or until crisp.
With slotted spoon, remove bacon and set aside.
Remove all but 2 tablespoons fat.
Add onion and green pepper; saute 3 minutes longer.
Stir in potato soup, the broth, cream and milk; bring to boiling.
Add broccoli, cauliflower and corn.
Simmer covered 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper and the bacon.
Brown sausage.
Remove from skillet and brown diced onion in 3 tablespoons of the drippings.
Add flour and stir to a paste.
Add salt, pepper, chili sauce, Worcestershire sauce and juice drained from the green beans.
Cook until thick, stirring well.
Add the drained green beans.
Pour mixture into a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Top with the browned sausage.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in a hot oven (400°) for 20 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Melt cheese in with butter and milk.
Mix slightly beaten egg yolks with macaroni.
Add bread crumbs and onion, then milk ingredients.
Beat egg whites and fold in last.
Bake for 45 minutes in moderate oven (350°).
Wash cucumbers.
Pack into hot jars.
Put 1/8 teaspoon of alum on top.
Add 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon pickling spice, 1 garlic button, 1 hind dill and 1 little green strong pepper.
Into each quart, use 1/4 vinegar to 3 parts water (more vinegar if desired).
Seal.
Mix cake mix according to directions on package and bake.
Cook lemon pie filling and cool completely.
Set aside.
After cake has completely cooled, spread lemon pie filling between layers. Reserve about 1/3 of filling for topping on cake.
Cover entire sides and about an inch on top with Cool Whip.
Pour lemon pie filling around the top of cake.
Fill center of top with Cool Whip. Garnish with thin lemon slices twisted.
Lemonicious!

recipes.t: Seared Shrimp With Spicy Mango Salsa
d: In large skillet, heat oil until very hot.
Add shrimp; cook 2 minutes.
Add onions and cook until shrimp are done.
Add peppers, pear and pineapple juice and cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Add red onion, tomato, mangos and mint.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Squeeze lemon over and serve.
Garnish with mint.
Serves 4.
Prepare and bake cake as directed on package in a 9 x 12-inch pan.
While cake is baking, bring milk, sugar and half of coconut to a boil but do not continue to boil.
When cake comes out of oven, punch holes in cake and pour milk-sugar-coconut mixture evenly over cake, spreading coconut carefully.
Let cool completely at room temperature.
When cake is cool, spread with the whipped topping and top with remaining coconut.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Grilled Cheese And Ham On Rye Bread
d: Spread 4 slices of bread with butter or margarine and 4 slices with mustard.
Place cheese, then ham on buttered bread.
Top with remaining bread.
Cut in halves diagonally.
Grill sandwiches in small amount of butter in skillet or on a griddle over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes on each side.
Our favorite.
Boil cauliflower 10 minutes and drain.
Place in 9-inch pie plate.
Spread with onion, green pepper and cheese.
Put eggs, Bisquick, salt, pepper and milk in blender; process.
Microwave Directions:
In a 2-quart casserole, combine all ingredients, except salmon and green onions.
Microwave, uncovered, at High (full power) for 13 minutes, or until noodles are tender.
Stir in salmon and green onions.
Cover; let stand 2 minutes.
Makes about 2 servings.
This makes about eight 2-cup packages of beans.
Any dried peas or beans may be added to the mix.
Pat out desired size of hamburger patty.
Place on small sheet of tinfoil.
Place slice of onion on hamburger.
Then place the amount of frozen French fries you desire.
Last, you place string beans and salt and pepper to taste.
Roll up and crease the tinfoil to hold in juices from hamburger.
Cook at 350° until the hamburger is done.
Brown meat and onion in shortening.
Add seasonings and tomatoes.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add kidney beans.
Pour meat mixture into 1 or 1 1/2-quart casserole. Grease casserole.
First, top with corn bread batter; spread carefully with wet knife.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
In a 3-quart saucepan, melt the butter.
Add mushrooms, onions, celery and carrots.
Cook over moderately low heat, stirring often for about 15 minutes.
Stir in flour, then add broth.
Cook, stirring constantly, until boiling.
Prepare barley separately and drain.
Add barley to pot and stir in milk, chicken, salt and pepper.
Simmer.
Enjoy with a fresh loaf of bread.
Mix jellos with water.
When well dissolved, add sherbet and mix well.
Chill a few minutes in freezer or refrigerator.
Take out and add fruit and sour cream, folding them gently.
Put in molds or whatever.
Serves 12.
Stir together melted butter, crumbs and almonds. Set aside. Combine all vegetables and stir well with soup to coat. Pour into greased 1 1/2 to 2-quart baking dish.
Spread crumb mixture evenly over top of vegetables.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until heated through.
Melt butter in 10-inch skillet.
Add steaks and cook lightly over moderate heat.
Add wine, lemon juice and pepper.
Bring to a boil and then simmer, uncovered, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and is opaque.
Transfer to a heated plate in low oven.
Place the pork chops in a single layer in a baking dish.
Salt and pepper.
Chop onion and green pepper and put over chops.
Pour juice over and cover.
Bake at 350° until tender, approximately 1 1/2 to 2 hours, depending on size of chops.
Uncover the last half hour.
Boil frankfurters 10 minutes and drain.
Split lengthwise nearly through.
Spread cut surfaces with prepared mustard and lay a half inch strip of cheese in each.
Fasten together with toothpicks.
Make a fritter batter.
Coat dogs with this and fry golden brown in 1 inch of Crisco oil in skillet.
Serve hot.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large mixing bowl, combine meats with garlic, onion and bread crumbs.
Add tomato paste, egg and spinach to meat mix and mix well.
Transfer mixture to an 8 1/2 x 4 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Cover with aluminum foil and seal tightly. Bake for 45 minutes, then remove foil and bake for 30 minutes longer.
Let meat loaf sit for 15 minutes before cutting.
Enjoy!
Fry salt pork; saute onion.
Boil potatoes in shallow water. Add margarine; mix all ingredients.
Add scallops and fish.
Add milk and bring to boil.
Turn off.
Cover and let set for 3 hours.
Blend milk, water, sugar and syrup.
Dissolve thoroughly. Heat slowly to boiling point.
Cook slowly so soft ball stage when tested in cold water.
In a bowl, stir together pineapple and pudding mix.
Allow to stand about 5 minutes or until slightly thickened.
Whip the cream until stiff; fold into pineapple mixture.
Cut cake in 3 equal layers. Fill and frost with pineapple and whipped cream mixture. Chill at least 1 hour. Can use 1 cup whipping cream and 1 cup Cool Whip.

On a plate combine flour, salt and pepper. Dredge your scallops in flour mix. In a large heavy skillet, heat butter and oil and saute scallops very quickly to golden brown. Move scallops with slotted spoon and put in warm serving dish. Saute scallions in same pan, but don't brown. Saute them lightly, then remove and sprinkle over scallops and keep warm. (IT IS IMPORTANT TO KEEP THEM WARM.) Pour off excess oil from pan. Add white wine. Cook down halfway. Put sauce over scallops and scallions. Serve meal with lemon wedges.
In medium bowl combine flour, baking powder, and salt; set aside.
In a small heavy saucepan or double boiler, heat the chocolate over low heat until melted, stirring constantly.
Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl beat butter with electric mixer on medium speed for 30 seconds.
Beat in sugar until fluffy.
Beat in melted chocolate, egg, and vanilla until combined.
Gradually beat in the flour mixture.
Divide dough into 4 equal portions.
Wrap each portion in plastic wrap and chill in freezer for 20 to 30 minutes (or in refrigerator for 1 hour) until firm enough to handle.
Line 2 jellyroll pans with wax paper.
Mix angel food cake according to box.
Spread cake in pans and bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Turn out onto wet tea towels. Roll lengthwise like jellyroll; cool.
Cook milk and flour until thick; cool.
Cream oleo, Crisco and sugar.
Add milk and flour, nuts and cherries.
Unroll cakes and spread with filling.
Roll up and wrap loosely in foil.
Freeze; slice while still frozen.
Soften cream cheese.
Add mayonnaise and mix well.
Add imitation crab, chopped green onion and chopped round onion.
Mix together well.
Spread on crackers and serve.

Preheat oven to 350°. Melt 1 cup chocolate and butter in double boiler (or heavy-duty saucepan) over low heat, stirring constantly, until smooth. Remove from heat. Mix in eggs, one at a time. Add vanilla. In another bowl, mix flour, sugar and baking soda. Add flour mixture to chocolate mixture a little at a time. Spread batter into a greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Sprinkle with remaining chocolate and pecans. Bake at 350° about 30 minutes.
In a Dutch oven or any large pot, simmer pepper and onion until soft.
Add ground beef, salt and pepper and brown until all pinkness is gone.
Add tomatoes and water and simmer on low heat around 2 hours.
Add mushrooms after 1 hour.
Add Minute rice after 2 hours and simmer 1/2 hour longer.
Good one pot meal.
Can also be used for stuffed peppers.

Blend cake mix, water, oil and eggs in mixing bowl until moistened. Pour batter in lightly greased pan and sprinkled flour. Bake. Take toothpick and insert in mixture. If toothpick comes clean, allow it to cool. If cake mix is not clean, allow it to bake five additional minutes.
Repeat until toothpick comes clean. Pour lemon flavoring in chocolate icing and blend with spoon until smooth. When cake is completely cool, frost the cake.
Mix potatoes, onion, egg, flour, salt and pepper in mixing bowl.
Mix well.
Heat oil in large skillet.
Spoon 1/4 cup potato mixture into skillet for each of 4 pancakes.
Flatten with spatula.
Cook over medium heat 10 to 15 minutes, or until golden brown, turning over once.
Drain on paper towels.
Add additional oil, if needed.
Repeat with remaining potato mixture.
Makes up to 6 servings.
Combine yogurt, mayonnaise, cream cheese and seasonings.
Mix well.
Then, stir in Cheddar cheese and crab.
Cover and chill 2 hours.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Serve with crackers, bread sticks or vegetables.
Makes approximately 20 servings.
A 3 tablespoon serving equals 44 calories and less than 1 gram fat.
Thoroughly cream butter with sugar and rind.
Add egg yolks; beat until light and fluffy.
Blend in lemon juice, flour, cereal and milk.
(Mixture will look curdled, but this will not affect finished product.)
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour into greased one quart baking dish; place the dish in pan of hot water.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until top springs back when lightly touched.
When done, pudding has a cake-like layer on top with custard below.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Line with bread.
Layer on cheese, ham, onion and mushrooms.
Beat milk, eggs, mustard and salt and pour over ingredients in pan.
Let stand overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Place rack in lowest position in oven; preheat oven to 425°. Combine pie filling with 1/2 teaspoon lemon rind.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake 15 minutes.
In large mixer bowl, beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk, then eggs, ReaLemon juice, vanilla and remaining 1/2 teaspoon lemon rind.
Spoon over blueberries.
Reduce oven temperature to 350°. Bake 25 minutes or until set.
Remove seeds and rind.
Cut melon into chunks.
Combine melon, limeade and ginger ale in blender.
Freeze for several hours. Thaw partially to serve.
Spoon into glasses and garnish with lime or lemon slices.
Makes 1 gallon.
Crumble beef and chorizo into a large skillet.
Add onions and cook until meat is browned; drain and add several drops of hot pepper sauce.
Spread beans in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Spread meat mixture on top.
Sprinkle with green onions, chiles and cheeses. Drizzle salsa over all.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve with guacamole and sour cream.
Garnish with black olives.
Tuck tortilla chips around edges and serve.
Good hot or cold.
Serves 12.
Mix all ingredients together in a bowl.
Add enough Miracle Whip to moisten salad to desired consistency. Can thin out salad dressing with a little milk.
Add sugar, salt and pepper to taste.
In a 12-inch skillet, bring 2 inches of water to a simmer with bay leaf and lemon slices.
Add the fillets; cover and simmer for 4 to 6 minutes, or until fish is flakey.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cut celery leaves from the choicest pieces of celery.
Put in mixture for good taste.
Add more sandwich spread if you want a creamier salad.
Sift together the flour, salt and baking powder.
Add sugar, walnuts, pumpkin pie spice and apples that have been peeled, cored and chopped.
Mix to a rather stiff batter with eggs and milk. Drop by spoonful into hot oil and cook until puffs are golden brown and apples are tender.
Drain and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Rub inside with lemon juice and salt.
Saute celery, celery leaves and onions in butter.
Put bread in bowl; add vegetables. Add beaten eggs, herbs and salt and pepper.
Stuff fish and sew shut.
Bake at 375° to 400° for approximately 10 minutes per inch at thickest part.
Serve with a sauce made of equal parts of butter and lemon juice.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and salt together.
Add milk and egg yolks and cook.
Add margarine, vanilla and marshmallows and beat until marshmallows are dissolved.
Add this to Cool Whip.
Brown ground beef and onion in large saucepan or skillet.
Add salt, pepper, chili powder and seasoning mix.
Pour into extra large saucepan.
Add tomato paste and water.
simmer 30 minutes. Stirring occasionally, add beans and continue cooking on simmer another 15 minutes.
Feed the crowd or place in airtight containers and freeze for later use.
Brown chicken in butter and oil in large skillet until golden. Remove and set aside.
Saute mushrooms and onions in drippings for 2 minutes.
Add chicken, skin side up; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add wine, cover and simmer 20 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Serve at once over rice or noodles or refrigerate or freeze.
Makes 6 servings.
Clean, cut and boil potatoes.
Mash potatoes, adding milk and margarine to consistency desired.
Cook lasagne noodles; drain. Saute onions in butter; drain.
In a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, layer noodles, potatoes, onions and cheese, ending with cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Mix yellow cornmeal, salt and red pepper.
Roll fish in cornmeal mixture.
Heat 4 to 6 inches of oil.
Using caution, test oil or grease by dropping a match in pan.
If it ignites, it's ready.
Fry fish until it rises to surface.
Flip and wait until golden brown.
Mix
juice
and
jelly; baste chicken while grilling or broiling.
Boil remaining marinade and serve with chicken.
Remove stems from 18 mushrooms.
Rub the caps with a lemon half and place in baking dish. Set aside.
Mince stems and remaining 6 mushrooms.
Heat butter in skillet and add shallots and garlic.
Cook 2 minutes.
Add minced mushrooms.
Cook slowly 8 to 10 minutes. Add sherry and stir in crabmeat, parsley and bread crumbs; should be moist.
Add salt and pepper. Fill each cap with crab mixture. Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Makes 18 appetizers.
Arrange artichokes in greased casserole or 8 individual ramekins.
Add crushed garlic cloves to olive oil and heat. Drizzle oil mixture over artichokes. Spread chicken on top. Combine mayonnaise, soup, lemon juice and curry powder.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle with cheese and top with bread cubes that have been tossed in the melted butter.
Bake at 350°
for 25 to 35 minutes.
Serves 8.
Stir apples, cinnamon, tapioca, oil and apple juice concentrate together and place in a 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Mix flour, oats, margarine and cinnamon.
Sprinkle on apple mix.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix cheese, bacon, olives, onion, Worcestershire sauce, salt and mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Place 1 teaspoon on each bread square. Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cream first 3 ingredients together.
Fold in chopped pecans. Spoon topping over frozen pie.
Bake at 400° for 35 to 40 minutes until lightly browned and bubbly.
Wash okra; cut off tops of stem.
Fry or broil okra in a small amount of butter or oil.
Brown lamb in butter.
Add water, spices, tomato sauce and garlic.
Cook slowly in covered saucepan until meat is tender, stirring occasionally.
Add browned okra, juice of lemon and cook slowly 5 minutes.
Serve with rice (Shiriah).
Chop fine the bell peppers, onions, green onions, parsley and garlic.
Fry in margarine until transparent.
Add cleaned shrimp. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add pulp from cooked meliton (about 8 cups). Continue to cook.
Add Progresso bread crumbs.
Pour in baking dish and bake at 400° until done.
Boil melitons before peeling, until a fork can pierce.
Drain, flake and remove skin and bones from salmon. Add the remaining ingredients (except pecans); mix thoroughly.
Form into a log or a ball.
At this point, you can either roll it in the pecans or garnish with some parsley sprigs.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
The longer it has to blend, the better.
Using a fork, combine graham cracker crumbs, sugar and butter. Lightly press 3/4 of the graham cracker mixture on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add peas, carrots, onion and garlic. Cook for about 5 minutes until soft.
Add stock.
Simmer for about 20 minutes.
Put through blender until smooth.
Add cream and serve.

Drain juice from the cherries and measure out 1 1/2 cups juice. Sift sugar, salt and cornstarch and mix with the juice. Place mixture in the top of a double boiler and cook for 5 minutes to thicken. Stir to prevent sticking.
Add the butter and almond extract. Remove from the heat. Add the cherries. Pour the mixture into the pie shell and top with the other pie crust.
Sprinkle the top with 1 1/2 tablespoons of sugar. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes. Serves 8.
Brown hamburger, onion and celery.
Put all ingredients (except chicken) into crock-pot.
Cook on low for a couple of hours.
Add diced chicken one hour before serving.

recipes.t: Brownie Camp-Out Coffee Can Ice Cream
d: Mix first 3 ingredients together and pour in 1-pound coffee can.
(You will probably have enough liquid for two (1-pound) cans.)
Place lid on can and secure with duct tape.
Put this can inside of a 3-pound coffee can.
Place ice all the way around the smaller can.
Sprinkle a little rock salt on top of ice.
Close can.
Roll the can back and forth between several friends for about 10 minutes.
Open the can and drain the water.
Add more ice and salt.
(Pour melted salt water outside on gravel.)
Roll until the ice cream is frozen (30 to 40 minutes).
Cook cranberries in 2 cups water for 10 minutes, or until berries pop.
Press through sieve.
Combine cranberry juice, sugar and lemon juice; stir in milk.
Add walnuts.
Place in freezer. Freeze until firm, stirring occasionally.
Dissolve yeast in warm water in a large mixing bowl; let stand 5 minutes.
Stir sugar, oil and salt into yeast mixture.
Add eggs, lemon rind and 2 cups flour; beat at low speed with an electric mixer until mixture is smooth.
Stir in enough remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface.
Add raisins; knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 to 10 minutes).
Place in a well-greased bowl, turning to grease top. Cover; let rise in warm place (85°) free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.
Prepare the lasagna noodles.
Brown the hamburger and add to the sauce.
Simmer 20 minutes, then cool.
Mix the Mozzarella cheese and the Parmesan cheese together.

Grease pan; layer noodles, 1/3 meat sauce, 1/3 of cheese and 1/3 cottage cheese. Put 4 more noodles in the opposite direction (1/3 cheese, 1/3 meat sauce) and final 4 noodles, then meat sauce, then cheeses, ending with cottage cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Let cool 5 minutes before cutting.
Early in the day, or up to one week before serving, combine vegetables in medium bowl; mix sugar, vinegar, pepper and salt; mix with the vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours. Serve on lettuce leaves or cup.
Decorate as desired; can also be served as a relish.
In a medium saucepan, combine egg yolks, sugar, lemon juice and lemon peel. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Add cream cheese.
Beat until smooth. Stir in pecans.
Refrigerate, covered, until well chilled.
Roll cleaned shrimp in olive oil, then in bread crumbs with the parsley, garlic and cloves (3 cloves is not too much!).
Place shrimp on skewers (if using bamboo skewers, be sure to dampen them first).
Chill until ready to grill.
Grill quickly and enjoy. Allow about 8 shrimp per person.

recipes.t: Pan Broiled Liver Slices With Soy Sauce(Servings:  8)
d: Slice the liver thin and drain well after soaking it for 20 minutes.
Mince green onion, garlic, ginger and red pepper. Combine seasonings for them.
Marinate the above together for 30 minutes.
Pan broil over medium heat on both sides.
Place lettuce leaves on the plate and boiled liver in the center of it.

recipes.t: Icy Pear Soup(Anjou Pears Are Wonderful In This Recipe.)
d: In a large saucepan, melt butter over low heat.
Add leeks and celery; saut for 5 minutes or until soft. Add potatoes, stock and pepper. Bring to a boil.

Reduce heat and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes or until vegetables are soft. Cool slightly. Carefully puree in a food processor or blender until smooth. Add pears and puree. Pour into a large bowl. Stir in milk and nutmeg. Chill thoroughly, at least 2 hours. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix first 3 ingredients, then add eggs, a little at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Add salt, baking powder, lemon flavoring and vanilla.
Alternate milk and flour; mix well but do not overbeat.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 300° in a greased and floured tube pan.
Do not open oven door until cake is done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a heavy saucepan, combine 1 1/3 cups sugar and cornstarch; beat egg yolks and add to lemon mixture. Gradually add water, stirring constantly.
Over medium heat, cook and stir until mixture boils and thickens, about 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add margarine; stir until melted.
Pour into prepared shell.
Microwave (High) the butter in uncovered glass mixing bowl for 20 to 30 seconds or until softened.
Blend in brown sugar until creamy.
Mix in flour with fork until crumbly.
Stir in pecans. Set aside 1/2 cup mixture.
Press remainder into bottom of 8-inch square microwave-safe dish.
Microwave (High), uncovered, 2 to 2 1/2 minutes or until mixture is puffed and has a dry appearance, rotating dish once.
Set aside.
Microwave (High) the remaining crumb mixture in uncovered dish for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes or until lightly toasted, stirring once or twice.
Set aside.
Put in a 12-quart pot the bacon cut in small pieces.
Fry until done.
Add onion and cook brown.
Put water 3/4 full.
Add chicken; boil 15 minutes.
Add sausage, salt and pepper; boil 30 minutes.
Add rice; cook until done.
Stir after.
Well feeds 12 to 25 people.
Beat eggs.
Add salt, sugar and coconut.
Add hot milk while stirring.
Pour over pie filling.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Heat butter in a large skillet.
Add garlic, Cajun seasoning and Worcestershire sauce.
Add shrimp and cook just until shrimp are pink and firm to touch.
Add stock and white wine and heat just to boiling point, scraping bits from the sides of the pan. Serve on heated platter with warm sourdough bread.
Great with rice.
Mix together oatmeal, bran, baking powder, cinnamon and sweetener with a fork.
Add
to
this
mixture the egg whites, milk and vegetable oil
which
has been
mixed together.
Mix until moist.
Add remaining ingredients and mix with a fork or spoon.
Spoon into muffin pan
which
has
been
lined
with Baker's paper cup liners.
Bake at 425° for 20 minutes.
Store in tightly covered container
in
freezer or refrigerator.
No cholesterol, no fat and
low
in calories! Yields 12 muffins. Doesn't rise.
Brown beef with onion and garlic; drain and add salsa, tomato sauce, Ro-Tel, water, salt and seasoning pouch.
Bring to
a boil; reduce heat and simmer 30 to 45 minutes.
Serves 8 to 18.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Put 2 tablespoons olive oil in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Heat in oven for 3 to 5 minutes. Add potatoes. Toss to coat. Roast potatoes, turning occasionally, for 30 to 35 minutes or until tender.
While potatoes are baking, prepare garlic.
In a small skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil. Add the garlic.

Cover pan and cook over very low heat for 5 to 8 minutes until garlic is tender. Sprinkle with sugar and stir until garlic is golden. Add vinegar, wine and basil. Simmer 2 minutes. Spoon over roasted potatoes. Sprinkle with pepper and parsley. Serve.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix All-Bran and milk.
Add egg and oil and beat well.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder together.
Add to first mixture. Add honey and stir until combined.
Fill muffin tins 2/3 full. Bake in 400° oven for 30 minutes (approximately).
Lay chicken breasts in 8 x 12-inch pan.
Cover with foil; bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
While chicken cooks, mix cheese and chili.
Cover each breast with mixture; pat to hold in place. Sprinkle evenly with green onion and bacon.
Return to oven, uncovered.
Bake until chicken is white in center of thickest piece and cheese melts, about 10 minutes.
Scatter avocado over top.
Serve with sour cream to taste.
Cook ground beef, removing fat.
Mix together onion soup mix, egg and bread crumbs.
Pat evenly the ground beef on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add French-style green beans next.
Spread soups on top and then place Tater Tots on top of all just before baking. Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
In large Tupperware mixing bowl, dissolve yeast in water; stir in sugar, salt and half the flour.
Beat until smooth.
Add egg and shortening.
Beat in remaining flour until smooth.
Scrape down the sides of the bowl with paddle scraper.
Seal.
Let rise in a warm place until double in size.
Punch down dough.
Turn out on pastry sheet.
Press dough flat.
Cut with cutter or shape cloverleaf. Place in tins.
Let rise again.
Brush with melted butter. Sprinkle with seed if desired.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine the first 4 ingredients.
Make into meat balls and brown.
Layer the cabbage, onion, rice and browned meat balls. Top with the soup and milk.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Fry pork chops until brown on both sides.
Add onions, bell pepper and celery.
Cook until onions are soft.
Add water and let come to a boil.
Add green onions, pimentos and uncooked rice. Lower heat and simmer for about 30 minutes with the lid on until the rice is done.
You will need a 4-quart stockpot to start.
Chop garlic and saute in oil.
Add turkey and brown with Worcestershire.
When meat is done, add cabbage and onion and saute for 5 minutes.
Add bouillon and dissolve.
Add tomatoes.
Add pepper and basil.
Add water and simmer 20 minutes.
Makes good soup for a cool day!
In a large Dutch oven, saute chopped onion, bell pepper, celery and garlic in oil until wilted.
Peel and chop eggplant and add this, plus the sausage (chopped in small pieces) to wilted vegetables.
When eggplant is well smothered, add salt and pepper to taste.
(This should be a peppery dish, so don't spare the seasoning.)
Add rice and water next.
Cover and cook Jambalaya until rice is tender, about 25 to 30 minutes over low heat.
Heat oven to 375°.
In a large bowl, toss berries with 1/4 cup sugar and cornstarch.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add egg, milk and butter; mix until well combined.
Prepare six 8-ounce custard cups with nonstick cooking spray.
Divide berry mixture among the custard cups.
Top each cup with batter.
Sprinkle each with sugar and nutmeg.
Place cups on baking sheet; bake for 30 to 40 minutes, or until tops are golden.
Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Peel and slice potatoes round and thin.
Lightly grease casserole dish.
Layer potatoes in dish, sprinkling each layer with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Press garlic over mixture.
Add cream and milk.
Bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until potatoes are soft and creamy.
Beat sour cream and cream cheese until blended.
Add hot potatoes gradually, whipping constantly, until light and fluffy. Season with onion and garlic salt.
Spoon into 2-quart ungreased casserole dish.
Dot with butter.
Sprinkle with paprika and brown in 350° oven for 35 to 45 minutes, until warm.
Prepare mixed vegetables and macaroni separately according to package directions; drain.
Lightly brown onion in oleo in large frying pan.
Add soup and water, stirring to combine.
Stir in ham, vegetables, macaroni, Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Cook over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes or until heated through, stirring occasionally.
Makes 4 servings.
Pre-Kick Off:
Brown beef with pepper.
Drain.
Stir in onion mix, chili powder and tomato sauce.
Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in cheese and chili.
Melt butter; add sugar.
While mixing, beat in eggs.
Add vanilla and other ingredients.
Mix well and pour into pie shell. Bake at 300° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Combine cracker crumbs and butter.
Mold into 9-inch pie plate.
Beat egg whites until stiff, adding vinegar, sugar and vanilla gradually.
Beat for 5 minutes.
Pour into cracker crust. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool.
Place strawberries on top of pie; cover with whipped cream and walnuts. Garnish with strawberries.
Chill overnight.
Yield: 8 servings.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease jelly roll pan with shortening. Heat in saucepan, stirring a few times, margarine or butter, water and cocoa.
Remove from heat.
Stir in remaining ingredients. Pour batter into the pan (batter will be thin).
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.
Cool on wire rack.
Frost cake when cool.
Cut up chicken and cook in salt and pepper until meat is almost done.
Add celery (cut up) and green pepper.
Simmer for 5 minutes; add can of mushroom soup.
Cover 5 minutes more.
Cook until rice is done.
Separately follow instructions on rice box, preferably Uncle Ben's wild rice.
Serve chicken over rice.

Slice jalapenos from stem to tip; open and scoop out seeds. Soak cleaned peppers in cold water. Brown ground beef with salt, pepper, garlic salt and chopped onions. Stuff peppers with ground beef mixture and press in grated Cheddar cheese. Wrap the whole pepper with 1 slice of bacon and secure with toothpick. Place peppers on grill and cook until bacon is done.
Cream soft butter, sugar and cornmeal.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Add juice and rind.
Pour into unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 300°, until firm and slightly brown.
Test with point of knife.
Mix preserves, mustard and black pepper in a bowl; set aside. Heat olive oil, in a large skillet, over medium-high heat.
Add pork chops and brown 3 minutes on each side.
Spoon preserves mixture on top of pork chops, cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
In a 2-quart casserole, melt butter on High for 45 seconds or 1 minute.
Add onions and toss to coat.
Cover and cook on High for 4 to 6 minutes (microwave), stirring once.
Combine crumbs, cheese and paprika.
Spoon onto onions, cover with paper towel and microwave on High for 1 to 2 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cream butter and brown sugar.
Add pumpkin and baking soda and stir together.
Add egg, flour, spices, salt, nuts and raisins. Mix thoroughly.
Drop by rounded teaspoons on greased baking sheet. Bake in preheated oven at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes approximately 4 dozen cookies.
Roll out half of the dough and cut in 2-inch strips.
Line a 2-quart ovenproof dish with the strips.
Put chicken, broth, eggs, salt and pepper in dish.
Roll other half of dough and cut in strips.
Place on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Combine crumbs and butter and press into bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan. Place in freezer for 15 minutes.
Heat cheese and margarine in 3-quart saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally until melted.
Gradually add combined sifted sugar and cocoa, stirring until smooth.
Add pecans and vanilla. Mix well.
Spread into greased 11 x 9-inch pan.
Cover and chill. Cut into squares.
Sift together the flour, cinnamon, baking soda, salt, nutmeg, cloves and pepper.
Stir in anise seed, cardamon, citron and orange rind until well mixed; set aside.
Beat butter and 1 cup confectioners sugar until well mixed.
Beat in egg.
Add flour mixture just until blended.
Chill overnight, or until firm enough to handle.
Roll dough (about 1 teaspoon) at a time into small balls.
Place 2 inches apart on cookie sheets.
Top each with a piece of candied cherry.
Stir milk into remaining 1/4 cup confectioners sugar until smooth.
Drizzle very lightly over top of each cookie.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° for 8 minutes, or until very lightly browned.
Remove from cookie sheets at once with spatula.
Cool completely on wire rack.
Grate Cheddar cheese and cream together cheese and cream cheese.
Add all other ingredients, mixing well.
Roll into ball. Roll cheese ball in paprika.
Stir together cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup cocoa, 1/4 cup sugar and butter.
Press mixture firmly onto bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan.
Beat cream cheese, sour cream and 1 1/4 cups sugar until smooth.
Add 1/2 cup cocoa, eggs and 2 teaspoons extract; beat just until blended.
Pour over crust.
Sprinkle both sides of chops with pepper; set aside.
Spray an unheated, large nonstick skillet with nonstick spray.
Heat the skillet over medium heat.
Add the chops and cook for 3 minutes. Turn and cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until no longer pink.
Transfer to a plate and set aside.
In a small bowl, stir cornstarch into the apple-cranberry juice until dissolved.
Then add the juice mixture to the skillet, stirring and scraping to loosen any brown bits from the bottom.
Stir in the cranberries, tarragon, parsley and honey.
Cook and stir until slightly thickened.
Add the chops to the skillet.
Spoon the sauce over the chops; cook for 1 to 2 minutes more or until heated through.
Serve over rice.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet.
Add the cumin seed and cayenne or red pepper, starting with 1/4 teaspoon.
Allow to sizzle for a moment.
Add the onion and garlic.
Saute until relatively soft.
Add the tempeh and continue to cook, stirring frequently for another 5 minutes.
Combine crabmeat, oysters or mussels and eggs.
Melt butter and then saute the onion, celery, bacon and bread crumbs in it. Combine this mixture with seafood and season to taste.
Add Worcestershire sauce.
Mix water, bouillon and consomme. Heat to boiling.
Add vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, beets and beet juice.
Mix sour cream with 1 tablespoon water.
Add to stock, a little at a time. Reheat, but do not boil.
This can also be served cold.
Add sour cream just before serving. Sprinkle a little chopped parsley on top.
Combine onion, oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper in a large shallow dish.
Add scallops, stirring gently to coat. Refrigerate 2 hours.
Thread scallops on skewers.
Place kabobs 4 to 5 inches from hot coals; grill 10 to 12 minutes, turning and basting occasionally with leftover marinade.
Yield:
6 servings.
In skillet, cook onion in oil until tender; drain peas, saving liquid.
Add liquid, tomatoes, potatoes, green pepper and herb seasoning to skillet.
Cover and cook until potatoes are tender. Reduce heat; add peas and simmer until peas are hot.

Combine cooked penne, sausage, 2 c. cheese, pasta sauce and olives. Put in a greased 13 x 9 pan. Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes until bubbly. Uncover and top with remaining 2 c. cheese. Bake 10 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring until sugar is dissolved, then increase heat to medium and boil
Pour into well-greased platter.
When cool enough to handle, butter hands and pull candy until light in color and can't pull any further.
Stretch and twist into long rope. Cut or break into 1-inch pieces.
Wrap in waxed paper.
Melt butter in a glass custard cup or glass measuring cup in microwave about 15 seconds on High.
Put fish into a 2-quart glass baking dish, brush with melted butter and sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Cover with waxed paper.
Cook for 3 minutes on High or until fish flakes when tested with a fork.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Brown sausage in skillet; drain.
Mix pancake mix, eggs, milk and oil together.
Add sausage to pancake mix.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer apples on top and sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with maple syrup.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Pare, core and thinly slice apples and pears.
Place sliced fruits and pineapple in 9-inch square baking dish.
Set aside.
Combine sugar and flour; stir in egg, lemon rind and juice and water.
Cook over boiling water until slightly thickened.
Pour over rhubarb in pie shell.
Top with a lattice crust.
Bake at 425° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Makes a 2 crust 9-inch pie.
Mix eggs, milk, salt and dry mustard.
Pour mixture over bread, ham and cheese.
Cover.
Let set overnight in refrigerator.
In the morning, cover with crushed cornflakes and melted margarine.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Season chicken breast.
Grill.
Cool and cube.
Add mayonnaise, sandwich spread, grapes and almonds.
Mix well and refrigerate.
Brown the ground beef.
Add taco mix, chives and mushroom soup, then put in baking dish.
Add the Tater Tots on the top; cook until golden brown.
Add cheese until melted.
Bake the dish at 350°.
Cover bread slices with cheese; broil until cheese bubbles. Remove from oven; top with kiwi slices in decorative manner in center of each sandwich.
Combine mayonnaise and shrimp; spoon on top of kiwi slices.
Serve at once.
Cut green pepper into strips.
Chop celery and carrots thin and slanted.
Slice onions into rings.
Melt butter and add vegetables in large skillet.
Cover and cook 10 minutes or until vegetables are as tender as you like.
Stir in milk and heat thoroughly.
Add salt, pepper and sugar to taste.
Boil potatoes in skins until soft.
Remove skins.
Mash potatoes well, adding orange juice until they have the consistency of applesauce.
Chill.
Just before serving this dessert, fold in fruit and nuts.

Combine flour, sugar, oats, baking soda and melted butter. (If you substitute margarine for butter, use 2 tablespoons less.) Press 2/3 mixture onto bottom of 15 x 10 x 1-inch cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cream eggs, butter, sugars and vanilla; add remaining ingredients. Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 325°.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Combine flour, baking soda and salt. In a saucepan, combine butter, sugar and water.
Heat just to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Add semi-sweet chocolate chips and vanilla.
Mix until smooth.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Gradually blend in flour mixture.
Stir in white chocolate and milk chocolate chips.
Spread in a greased brownie pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Spread each round of bread with prepared mustard and heap some of the cheese on each round.
Sprinkle each with salt, pepper, paprika and 1/8 teaspoon of the Worcestershire sauce.
Boil potatoes in jackets.
When cool, peel and grate.
Melt oleo, add soup, onions, sour cream, cheese and chives.
In large mixing bowl, grate potatoes, and add the sauce; add desired amount of salt and pepper.
Put potato mixture in a large casserole dish. Melt oleo and stir in cracker crumbs, enough crumbs to be coated with oleo.
Top potato mixture with cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Beat until fluffy. Fold in whipped cream or whipped topping and vanilla.
Spoon into pastry shells.
Top with fruit.
Makes 6 servings.
Sift flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt several times.
Add melted butter to sugar and stir in egg and milk.
Put berries in pie plate and dredge with flour mixture.
Sift flour into liquid mixture; mix.
Fold in berries.
Pour into buttered steamer; cover and steam for 1 hour.
Serve warm with foamy pudding sauce.
Pound steak with flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Brown in oil; drain.
Mix remaining ingredients and add to steak.
Cover and simmer over low heat 2 hours or until meat is tender, stirring often.
Add water as necessary.
Cut shortening into dry ingredients.
Add water and vanilla. Roll out.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Sprinkle on top of cream cheese mixture.
Pat down and chill overnight.
Cut into squares and serve.
Dissolve jello in water.
Add ingredients in order.
Pour into mold.
Saute green pepper and onion in butter.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Cream sugar, cocoa and margarine. Add eggs and flour and beat well. Stir in the nuts. Mixture will be thick. Place mixture into a 9 x 13 x 2-inch greased cake pan. Bake 30 minutes at 350°. While hot, cover the cake with 1 package of miniature marshmallows. Cover the pan with a dish towel to retain the heat.
Heat water with salt to boiling in 2-quart pan.
Cube potatoes and cook in salted water.
Cook bacon, saving grease.
Cook potatoes until tender, then drain, saving the water.
Then brown the potatoes in the bacon grease.
While the potatoes are browning, mix the flour and beaten egg.
Add these to the potato water, stirring to separate and make riviets.
Cook until thick.
Combine cheese, tomato sauce, beef and garlic.
Heat over water in double boiler until cheese is melted.
Remove garlic. Remove mixture from heat and add beaten egg.
Age for several days in refrigerator.
Reheat and serve as hot dip with crackers. (Chafing dish works well.)
Makes 3 cups.
Line a large roasting pan with foil.
With sharp knife, score top of ham.
Combine garlic (mashed), mustard, chili sauce, brown sugar (packed) and rum in small bowl.
Mix well. Spread evenly over top and sides of ham.
Place shrimp, 1/2 of the garlic and fish sauce in bowl.
Mix and marinate 10 to 15 minutes; set aside.
Pour 1 teaspoon oil in wok or frying pan on medium-high heat.
Place remaining garlic in pan.
Stir couple times and add long beans, sprinkle sugar and shoyu sauce.
Stir; lower heat and simmer 7 to 10 minutes.
Remove beans from pan.
Return heat to medium-high, add remaining oil and place marinated shrimp in pan.
Stir and add onion.
Add long beans to partially cooked shrimp, stir and turn off heat.
Serve immediately.
Mix sugar and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.
Combine sugar, water, pineapple juice and rum extract and freeze.
Spoon mixture into glasses and pour lemon-lime soda over ice.
Stir and serve when it becomes slushy.
Add flour to beans and onion mixture until doughy.
Fry in skillet with cooking oil until golden brown.
Just use about 2 tablespoons mixture at a time for each cake.
Heavily coat a baking pan with butter or margarine.
Spread out oysters in the pan.
Cover with slivers of ham.
Broil until oysters curl and are hot through.
Soak onion in wine vinegar, sugar, salt ,pepper, oil and cider vinegar.
Pour over vegetables; mix well.
Marinate in covered dish for
6 hours or overnight.
Drain and serve.
Chopped black olives may be added if desired.
Makes 12 servings.
A good dish for a brunch.
Heat juice and butter together until butter melts.
Add sugar, salt, herbs, ketchup and cheese.
Let cool to lukewarm. Sprinkle yeast on warm water and
stir.
Add
tomato mix and 3 cups of flour to yeast.
Beat
with
electric
mixer at medium for 2 minutes until smooth.
Mix
in enough of remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Knead
by
hand
or
machine
to
10 minutes. Place in greased bowl.
Cover
and
let
rise 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Punch down and
divide
in half.
Place in greased loaf pans. Cover and let rise about 1 hour.
Bake at 375° for about 25 minutes.
While still
hot,
brush
top
with oil and cool.
Beat butter at medium speed until fluffy; gradually add sugar and beat well.
Add egg whites, sour cream,
milk and vanilla. Beat well.
Combine flour and next 3 ingredients.
Stir well. Add flor mixture to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Pour batter into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pan.
Frost.
Mix yeast in 1/2 cup warm water.
Add oatmeal, honey and milk; mix well.
Stir in white flour.
Let rise 45 to 60 minutes.
Stir in eggs, salt and cooking oil.
Work in wheat flour and wheat germ.
Let rise double; knead 5 minutes.
Divide into 2 loaves. Place in 2 greased loaf pans.
Cover with clean cloth; let rise in warm place until double again.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes. Remove from pans to cool.
Heat bacon fat in 10-inch skillet.
Add cabbage.
Cook over low heat, stirring frequently, until light brown.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Makes 4 servings.
Blend flour, salt and pepper into mayonnaise; gradually add milk.
Heat, uncovered, on Roast for 3 to 4 minutes or until thickened.
Stir occasionally.
Add cheese and heat, uncovered, on Roast for approximately 1 1/2 minutes, or until cheese has melted. Add onion, pimiento, ham and eggs.
Heat, uncovered, on Roast for 3 to 5 minutes or until heated to 140°.
Serve on muffins.
Brown meat and drain.
Layer corn tortillas, beans, meat, lettuce, tomato and cheese.
Repeat.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Combine popcorn, cereal, pretzels, and pecans.
Mix oil, sugar and eggs, then add baking soda.
Add dry ingredients.
Add pumpkin.
Bake in a 14 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch cake pan at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Saute garlic and mushrooms in oil.
Add tomatoes and spices. Simmer for at least 2 hours.
Cook spaghetti according to directions.
Serve sauce over spaghetti.
Top with cheese and dip Italian bread in sauce on side.
Enjoy!
Peel and cut potatoes into 1/4-inch slices.
Place in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Slice margarine over potatoes.
Bake for 1 hour at 375°.
Remove from oven; sprinkle with cheese and replace in oven to melt cheese.
Drain juice from cherries into saucepan.
Add cornstarch and water; cook until thick and clear.
Remove from heat and add jello.
Dissolve jello and add sugar.
Add cherries, pineapple and coloring.
Let cool and add bananas and pecans.
Let cool until jello starts to jell.
Pour into crust and top with Cool Whip or whipped cream.
Chill.
Brown and crumble hamburger and sausage; drain fat.
Cut cheese into chunks and add to skillet.
Stir until melted; add seasonings.
