Spread on party rye bread (you will use almost the whole package).
Place on cookie sheets.
Place under broiler, not on the nearest rack.
Broil for 5 to 10 minutes.
Watch, because they brown quickly.
Brown wurst on grill.
Cook onion, pepper and wurst in beer. Cover and cook 30 minutes.
Serve on buns.
Remove tails from shrimp.
Combine shrimp, oils, vinegar, peppercorn, parsley, tarragon, onion and lemon slices in large bowl.
Marinate in refrigerator at least 3 hours, tossing frequently.

recipes.t: Angel Hair Pasta With Lemon And Garlic
d: Bring large pot of water to boil.
Put olive oil and garlic in pan and cook over medium heat until garlic starts to brown. Remove pan from heat and add wine.
Return to heat.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes until wine is reduced by half.
Stir in lemon juice and tomato.
Remove pan from heat.
Cook pasta in water until done (30 seconds to 1 minute).
Drain pasta and put in warm serving bowl. Add the basil, Parmesan cheese and black pepper, along with the tomato mixture.
Toss and serve immediately.
Serves 4.
Contains 4.1 grams fat and 291 calories per serving.
Layer first four ingredients and heat until bubbling in oven or microwave.
Add avocado and sour cream.
Sprinkle with green onions and black olives.
Put the cookie dough onto pizza pan and roll out.
Bake according to directions; cool.
Mix together the cream cheese, peanut butter, brown sugar and vanilla flavoring and spread on top of cooled cookie crust.
Slice the apples and put on top of mixture. Sprinkle a little cinnamon on top.
Pour the ice cream topping over the apples. Sprinkle top with peanuts.
Brown beef.
Add onion.
Saute and drain fat.
Blend tomato sauce, water, oregano and salt with meat and onions.
Simmer 10 minutes.
In casserole dish layer macaroni, half beef and sauce and half cheese.
Repeat.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Bring 2 cups water to a boil.
Mix with Jell-O.
Add lemon juice with milk and juice from pineapple.
Total out liquid to 4 cups total with water.
Chill Jell-O.

Preheat oven to 350°. In medium saucepan brown ground beef until no longer pink; drain. Stir in spaghetti sauce spices and seasonings, tomato paste, water, butter, basil and thyme. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 10 minutes. In small bowl, combine ricotta cheese with egg; set aside. In medium saucepan, bring 1 quart water to a boil. Add zucchini and cook 2 minutes; remove and rinse under cold water. In 12 x 8 inch casserole, layer half the zucchini, ricotta mixture and meat sauce. Repeat layers. Top with mozzarella cheese and bake uncovered 30 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a medium bowl with an electric mixer, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy; beat in egg and vanilla and stir in 1 1/4 cups of the cornmeal and the flour. Mix well.
Place the remaining 1/4 cup cornmeal in a small bowl or plastic bag.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls; coat with cornmeal and place on ungreased cookie sheets 2 inches apart.
With the floured bottom of a glass, flatten balls to 1/4-inch thickness; top each with almonds.
Bake until cookies are pale gold around the edges, about 8 minutes.
Cool on sheets for 1 minute before removing to wire racks.
Save juices from oranges and pineapple cans.
Slice bananas and combine with all other ingredients, including juices.
Mix well and serve.
Cut meat in 1 1/4-inch pieces, roll in flour and brown in large pan with margarine.
Saute onions and mushrooms in drippings; add to meat with undiluted soup.
Place in casserole dish and bake at 350° until meat is tender, approximately 1 hour. In small pan, mix gravy mix, sour cream and wine.
Stir over low heat until well combined.
Add to casserole and serve over noodles, rice or mashed potatoes.
Combine sugar, mustard, salt and flour.
Stir dry ingredients into eggs.
Heat vinegar, water and butter.
When butter is melted, remove from heat.
Quickly pour in egg mixture, stirring constantly.
Return to heat, cook, stirring constantly, until smooth and thickened (about 3 minutes).
Cool and keep refrigerated until ready to use.
Cream the sugar and oleo. Add eggs and cream.
Add flour, vanilla and nuts.
Put 3/4 of the batter in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Spread fruit over top of batter.
Drop rest of batter by spoonfuls over cherries.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes until browned. When cool, sprinkle with powdered sugar or powdered sugar and milk glaze.
Toss hot cooked rice with melted butter or margarine and coconut, which has been toasted on a cookie sheet under your broiler to a medium brown.
Mix eggs
and
sugar
in
electric mixer for 5 minutes. Slowly add oil.
Then
add
the lemon rind and finally add the flour and keep
mixing until blended well.
Pour into shallow pan, which has been lined with oiled wax paper.
The uncooked mixture should be 3/4-inch
thick;
it will rise when baked. Bake in a
350° oven
for
minutes or until golden brown. Remove pan
from oven and slice each piece into strips, about 3/4-inch wide.
Place each
piece
on
its side and return to oven for about 5 minutes until golden brown.
Mix the teriyaki sauce with barbecue sauce.
Add garlic. Marinate chicken overnight in mixture, then grill using the leftover mixture to baste the chicken.
Peel potatoes and cut into chunks.
Boil until tender.
Mash and leave to cool.
Combine mashed potatoes, ground beef and all other ingredients, except bacon.
Mix well and shape into thick, rectangular loaf.
Wrap slices of bacon around hamburger roast, tucking ends under loaf.
Place in roasting pan.
Bake at 400° for 1 1/2 hours.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
Serves 10.
Cut cabbage into quarters.
Allow to stand in cold water 1 hour.
Drain.
Shred fine, cover with the following dressing.
Mix flour, sugar and mustard and set aside.
Bring one cup water to boil, add vinegar and oil, add dry ingredients.
Mash egg yolks with dressing.
Chop egg whites with cabbage.
Pour dressing over and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bake cornbread in 3 cake pans; cool.
Brown sausage; add chopped onions, pepper, Ro-Tel tomatoes and jalapeno cheese.
Cook until consistency of icing.
Spread on each layer of cornbread. Will look like an iced cake.
Cut in wedges to serve.
Simmer vegetables until tender in chicken broth.
In medium bowl, combine milk, cornstarch, salt, pepper and thyme.
Add milk mixture to vegetables; cook until soup is slightly thick, stirring constantly.
Makes 4 servings.

recipes.t: Sopas De Espiritu Santo(Holy Ghost Sopas)
d: Bring water to boil, add meat, and spices tied in a clean cloth, wine, onion, tomato sauce, mint and salt.
Cover and cook until meat is tender, about 3 hours.
Cut cabbage into wedges and add to pot.
Cook until tender.
Put boiling water on top of jello and cream cheese and stir until blended, add remaining ingredients.
Chill and serve. Change with orange jello and orange soda.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, bananas and sourdough. Mix after each addition.
Add flour, soda, baking powder, salt and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Stew celery in stock until very tender.
Add salt and nutmeg. Blend flour and milk and add, stirring constantly, while heating to boiling.
Do not boil.
Pour into soup cups and sprinkle with cheese.
Serves 4.
Arrange peach halves, cut side up, in pie shell.
Combine brown sugar and cornstarch.
Cut in butter.
Sprinkle over peaches.
Bake, uncovered, 10 minutes at 425°.
Cover with foil and bake at 375° for 35 or 40 minutes.
Cool before serving.
Cream butter and add sugar.
Mix well and add vinegar and egg yolks.
Mix together flour, spices, nuts and raisins and add to first mixture, mixing well.
Fold this mixture carefully into beaten egg whites and pour into two unbakes pastry shells.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until filling is browned.
Melt butter in saucepan; add flour and blend.
Saute onions in this until soft.
Add stock and cook until thick and smooth.
Stir in cream, crawfish tails, corn and seasonings.
Cook until tender. Adjust seasonings to taste.
Makes 2 1/2 to 3 pints.
Cut chicken breasts into four pieces.
Sprinkle with pepper, dill and garlic.
Saute in skillet until brown.
Arrange in casserole dish.
Slice potatoes and onions and arrange over chicken.
Cut broccoli into bite size pieces and put over potatoes. Mix soup and milk and pour over entire casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes until potatoes are soft.
Serves 6.
Cover apples with water.
Cook until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain.
While apples are hot, add remaining ingredients.
Stir well until sugar dissolves.
Place shredded lettuce in 9 x 13 inch dish. Top with pepper, celery, red onion and peas.
Mix mayonnaise sugar and cheese together.
Spread on top of salad. Top with broken bacon pieces. Refrigerate overnight.
Serves 12-15.
Prepare Basic Creole Sauce according to recipe.
How much you need depends on how many you are going to feed.
For one gallon, you need approximately 2 pounds smoked sausage (sliced thin), the meat from 1 medium fryer (boil and pull meat) and 1 1/2 pounds (70 to 90) peeled and deveined shrimp.
Cook 2 pounds rice.
Freeze what's left.

recipes.t: Like Grandma'S Soft Spicy Raisin Hermits
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine flour, cinnamon and nutmeg. Set aside.
Cream sugar and butter.
Beat in sour cream and eggs until blended.
Blend in flour mixture.
Stir in raisins and nuts. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack.

Mix the tomatoes and green chiles with the soup in a large skillet. Add the cheese and chicken. Cook until the cheese melts, stirring constantly. Place the vermicelli in a greased casserole dish. Pour the chicken and cheese mixture over the vermicelli. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
In a 1 1/2-quart buttered casserole dish, alternate 2 layers each of chicken, onions and noodles.
Combine soup, milk and seasonings.
Pour over layers.
Combine pecans and margarine and sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for about 25 minutes.
Saute sliced green onions and mushrooms in butter until tender.
Meanwhile, slice cheese and avocado.
Spread outside of slices of sourdough bread with a small amount of butter.
Heat griddle and place bread on griddle with the buttered side down and place onion/mushroom mixture and sliced cheese and avocado on bread.
Top with another slice of bread and lightly brown both sides of sandwich. This sandwich is best served hot.
Mix
salt,
pepper,
ginger and flour.
Dust chops with mixture.
In
heavy skillet, brown chops lightly on both sides in hot oil.
Lower heat and cook until done, about 20 minutes.

In Dutch oven, saute onions, green peppers, carrots and garlic in oil until tender. Add chicken broth, tomatoes, kidney beans, cooked chicken and basil. Cook 10 minutes. Stir in shell pasta. Cook 10 more minutes. Serve with shredded Parmesan. Serves 4.
Mix together thoroughly.
Stir over low heat until shortening and chocolate are melted, stirring constantly.
Bring rapidly to a full rolling boil; boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat and beat until lukewarm.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla flavoring and continue beating until icing begins to lose its gloss.
(Considerable beating is required.)
If icing does not stiffen after 30 minutes, add 1 teaspoon confectioners sugar.
If too stiff, add 1 teaspoon of milk.
Drain pineapple. Add water to juice to make 2 cups.
Bring liquid to a boil and add Jell-O to dissolve.
Add 1 cup cold water, blueberry filling and pineapple.
Place in refrigerator until firm.
Beat sour cream, sugar and cream cheese together and add to top of Jell-O. Chill until firm.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Combine cheese, onion, chilies and 3/4 cup tomatoes.
Spread on half of each tortilla.
Fold over tortilla and wrap tightly. Brush inside edges of flap with beaten egg to seal.
Brush tortilla with oil and place on grate over medium-low coals.
Grill for 5 to 7 minutes, or until golden on one side.
Turn and brown. Remove from heat.
Place on platter.
Top with lettuce, olives and remaining tomatoes.
Serve with bottled sauce.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Saute onion and celery in butter until soft.
Stir in flour.
Add milk all at once and simmer until thickened, stirring constantly.
Stir in parsley, pepper and 1 1/2 cups of shredded cheese.
Combine cooked wild rice and potatoes in a 3-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with salt.
Pour sauce over top; top with remaining cheese and bacon pieces.
Bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes.
Serves 8.
Soften margarine and cheese; mix well.
Add flour; work into ball.
Add Tabasco.
Add Rice Krispies.
Roll small balls. Flatten on cookie sheet with thumb.
Bake at 350° for 17 minutes.
Crush Oreos and line dish (bottom only) saving about 1/4 cup for topping.
Pour 1/2 cup melted butter on top, distributing as evenly as possible.
Freeze for 15 minutes.
Add softened ice cream, spreading evenly, and place in freezer for a minimum of two hours, overnight preferably.

recipes.t: Peanut Butter Topping For Ice Cream
d: Cook flour, cocoa, sugar and water together until thickened. Remove from heat and add vanilla and peanut butter.
Trim all fat and gristle from steak.
Cut meat into small cubes.
Drain mushrooms, saving broth.
Chop into small pieces. To cook, heat 2 tablespoons butter or drippings in large frying pan.
When hot, add cut up beef.
Cover.
Brown and cook slowly for 15 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add mushrooms to beef and cook 10 minutes longer.
Push mixture to one side of pan; add sour cream, stirring.
Add meat mixture and mix well.
Add salt and paprika to taste.
Cover and simmer slowly for 10 minutes.
Serve on top of toast, torn into bits.
Grease
and
flour
a
9-inch
cake pan.
Combine blueberries and 2 tablespoons sugar.
Cream margarine with sugar. Beat egg well.
Combine flour, baking powder, soda, nutmeg and cardamon; stir into creamed mixture, alternately with yogurt. Spoon carefully over blueberries and sugar in cake pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes when done. Serve warm.
Sprinkle chicken with poultry seasoning and sage.
Melt margarine in skillet.
Brown chicken in margarine with mushrooms and onion.
When chicken is almost fully cooked, add soup and water.
Stir well and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add rice and simmer for an additional 20 to 25 minutes.
Once dough has risen for the second time, punch down and knead lightly.
Pat and stretch dough to cover bottom and about 1 1/2 inches up sides of a greased, heavy 10-inch cast-iron frying pan or deep dish pizza pan or a 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Dough will shrink back at first but keep working it.
Cover with tomato sauce, Mozzarella and the vegetables.
Preheat oven to 500°.
Bake on bottom rack for 10 minutes or until crust is browned.
Brown hamburger and onions.
Drain.
Add dry taco seasoning mix.
Let cool.
Cream together cream cheese and sour cream.
Add olives, cheese and chilies; mix well.
Add cooled hamburger and mix.
Spread mixture over tortilla shells.
Roll up and wrap in Saran Wrap.
Refrigerate.
Cut into slices.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add powdered sugar slowly.
When mixed, add tartar and vanilla.
Use icing to put graham crackers around a milk carton.
Decorate with candy canes, M&M's, etc.
Mash sweet potatoes in a large mixing bowl.
Blend in margarine, salt, flour and sugar.
Form into logs and roll in chopped pecans.
Place in a greased, shallow pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.

In a skillet, saute red pepper and onion in butter until tender. Add soup, milk, Worcestershire sauce and hot pepper sauce, stir until smooth. Stir in beans and chestnuts. Pour into an ungreased 1- 1/2 qt. baking dish. Sprinkle with cheese. Bake uncovered, at 350° for 15 minutes or heated through.
Drain salmon and reserve liquid.
Flake salmon.
Soften gelatin in cold water.
Combine salmon liquid, catsup and vinegar; heat to boiling.
Add softened gelatin to hot mixture.
Gently blend salmon, celery and onion with hot mixture.
Stir in mayonnaise.
Pour into fish-shaped gelatin mold.
(Crown with a foil crown!)

recipes.t: Impossible Calico Corn And Bacon Pie
d: Grease 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie plate.
Reserve two tablespoons of the bacon.
Mix remaining bacon, the onion, green pepper, corn and pimentos in plate.
Beat remaining ingredients, except sour cream, until smooth, 15 seconds in blender on high or 1 minute with hand beater.
Pour into plate.
Bake in 400° oven uncovered until knife inserted comes out
clean, about 35 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes. Garnish with sour cream and reserved bacon.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix shortening, sugar, egg, water and vanilla until creamy. Add rest of ingredients.
Drop rounded teaspoonful onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes about 5 dozen cookies.
Mix biscuit mix with honey and pecans.
Add water to form soft dough.
Knead on lightly floured surface until smooth.
Roll out to desired thickness.
Cut with floured cutter.
Place, lightly touching, on greased cookie sheet.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 450°.
Top with glaze.
Brown beef in small amount oil.
Add water, tomatoes and beef and vegetable bouillons.
Simmer 1 hour, more if needed.
Add vegetables and seasoning.
Simmer 1 hour or until vegetables and meat are done.
Great for unexpected company and nourishing too.
Mix butter, Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce with garlic salt.
Coat pecans with mixture.
Spread on cookie sheet.
Bake at 250° for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.
Cool.
Serve as is or spread cream cheese between 2 halves.

Place pork loin into large baking dish. Add water and soy sauce. Garnish top of loin with salt, garlic powder, hot peppers and parsley leaves. Bake at 350° for approximately 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Serve immediately.
Scald milk and gradually stir in cornmeal.
Stir until thick and cook in a double boiler for 15 minutes.
Mix together sugar, molasses, salt, nutmeg and cinnamon.
Add to the cornmeal and stir until blended.
Add butter, egg and vanilla.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake in a moderate oven for 1 hour.
Serve with a dash of Cool Whip or whipped cream.
Dissolve jello in boiling water; stir in orange juice until thawed.
Stir in undrained pineapple.
Chill until partially set (consistency of unbeaten egg whites).
Fold in oranges.
Pour in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Chill until almost firm.
Beat whipping cream to soft peaks; set aside.
Beat pudding mix and milk until smooth (1 to 2 minutes).
Fold in whipping cream.
Spread over gelatin.
Chill 5 to 6 hours or overnight.
Cut into squares and serve on lettuce.
You can garnish with additional oranges.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Shake flour in large size (14 x 20-inch) cooking bag.
Place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Roll down top of bag.
Add barbecue sauce, onion and green pepper.
Squeeze bag gently to blend ingredients.
Cut ribs in serving size pieces; place in bag.
Turn bag gently to coat the ribs with sauce. Arrange ribs in an even layer.
Close bag with nylon tie; make six 1/2-inch slits on top.
Cook 1 1/2 hours or until tender.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add to Seven Minute Frosting. Spread over Cherry Pineapple Cake layers (see recipe for Cherry Pineapple Cake).
In a large skillet spray Pam and saute pounded chicken breasts for about 5 minutes on each side (until pink is gone).
Remove from pan.
Chop the celery, onion and green pepper and saute in pan until onion is transparent.
Add can of stewed tomatoes and can of tomato sauce.
Sprinkle in tarragon and basil.
Heat until bubbly, about 10 minutes.
Return chicken breasts to the sauce and heat another 10 minutes or so.
Serve with or over rice.
Crush 40 Ritz crackers.
Mix with 1 stick softened butter/margarine.
Press into 9x13 pan.
Bake potatoes for 1 hour in preheated 400° oven.
Cut potatoes in half and scoop out insides.
Place in a bowl.
Place shells on baking sheet and set aside.
Add margarine, tuna or meat, cheese soup, salt and pepper and mix well.
Spoon potato back in shells and place half a slice of cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until filling and cheese are hot.

Combine flour, yeast, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Combine egg yolks, sour cream, and vanilla. Add to flour mixture, stir or knead to form a smooth ball. Divide into 8 portions. Cover, chill. Sprinkle work surface with powdered sugar. Roll each dough portion into an 8 inch circle. Cut into 8 wedges. Place one slightly rounded teaspoon of Cranberry-Prune filling near wide end of each wedge. Roll up, starting with wide end. Place point side down on ungreased baking sheet. Curve slightly to form crescents. Bake in 350 degree oven 18 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. While warm, drizzle with Sour Cream Icing.
Boil shrimp.
Cool and drain.
Dice up (fine little tiny pieces) in large bowl.
Pour in dips and powder; blend well. Serve with rippled potato chips.
Bring jello, pudding and water to a boil.
Add marshmallows and stir until dissolved.
Add berries and juice.
Stir until melted. Put in a bowl or flat pan and chill until set.
This may also be used for pie by pudding it on a graham cracker crust and topping with Cool Whip.
First Layer:
Melt butter and stir in flour.
Spread over the bottom of a large Pyrex dish.
Add chopped pecans.
Press into dough.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Let cool completely.
Combine the first 4 ingredients in bowl; stir well.
Add crabmeat, crumbs and green onions; stir well.
Spoon 1 teaspoon crabmeat mixture onto each cucumber slice; sprinkle with paprika.
Beat the softened cream cheese.
Mix Jell-O according to directions and add to the cream cheese.
Add 1 can crushed pineapple and mix.
Pour into a mold or a fancy glass bowl.
This makes a pretty salad.
Chop peppers, onions and dried beef.
Mix all ingredients together, using enough Miracle Whip to make creamy.
Beat sugar, eggs, juice, vanilla and oil together; add dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Batter is very stiff.
In a greased 9 x 11-inch pan, spread half the batter.
Spread about 1 1/2 cans of cherries.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar mixture.
Spread remaining batter on top.
Do your best to cover all the cherries. Sprinkle with remaining cinnamon and sugar mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour and 325° last 1/2 hour.
My family's favorite!
Boil chicken with onion, celery, salt and pepper until well done.
Remove meat from bone.
Wash and cut up endive.
Add to chicken broth.
When it starts to boil, drop in tiny meatballs. Simmer 1 hour.
Dissolve soda in milk.
Add to crumbs.
Add egg and beat well. Stir in baking powder, sugar and salt.
Add flour to desired consistency.
Saute onion and hamburg and brown.
Then add remaining ingredients and bake at 325° for 1/2 hour.
(For best flavor, cook in crock-pot on low for 3 to 5 hours.) Mmmmmmmmmmm good!
Melt chocolate in saucepan.
Add sugar, milk, water, butter or butter substitute and salt.
Boil to soft ball stage (234° to 238°).
Remove from fire.
Add flavoring and popped corn.
Cool to room temperature.
Stir until creamy.
Pour into well buttered, shallow pan.
Cut in squares.
Brown broken up turkey until no pink remains.
Add green pepper, onion, kidney beans and seasoning mix to meat in skillet. Stir in water.
Cut bacon into small pieces; place in Dutch oven or large skillet and fry.
Remove bacon.
Fry slowly onions and potatoes until golden brown.
Add pepper, salt, milk and corn.
Heat very slowly.
When hot, remove from heat and allow to cool thoroughly. When ready to serve, add bacon pieces and reheat slowly for mealtime.
May add more milk according to degree of thickness preferred for chowder.
Even better if allowed to sit all day and reheat just before mealtime.
Great with green or fruit salad and cornbread.
Combine rhubarb, sugar and fresh lemon juice in a large pot or Dutch oven.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight.
Juices will form.
Over medium heat, stir mixture to dissolve sugar and incorporate juices.
Increase heat to high and boil rhubarb mixture until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Add raspberries; boil until thick, about 5 or 6 minutes longer.
May boil longer to further thicken, if desired.
Remove jam from heat; stir in cardamom.
Can be stored in the refrigerator, or you can ladle hot jam into clean, hot jars and process in a simmering water bath for 10 minutes.
Get a thick brisket (more than 1-inch thick) with a good rind of fat (the fat is essential).
Tenderize several hours before doing anything else.
Just before cooking, sprinkle with a little chili and garlic powders and salt and pepper and rub in.
Separate cauliflower into flowerets.
Set aside.
Cook in boiling water to tender, not mushy.
Drain.
Cut ham into small chunks.
Set aside.
Combine in top of double boiler tapioca, butter, salt, pepper, paprika and hot milk.
Cook over boiling water, stirring frequently, until tapioca is clear (about 8 minutes).
Brown chuck in large heavy saucepan; pour out drippings.
In another pan, heat butter and oil.
Add onion and garlic; cook until transparent.
Add eggplant and bell pepper; cook, stirring occasionally until tender.
Reduce heat.
Stir in mushrooms and tomatoes; stir-fry for several minutes.
Stir in chuck, basil, salt and pepper; cook down.
For each pie shell, sprinkle 1/2 cup cheese on bottom.
Spread half of beef-eggplant mixture over cheese.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Brown hamburger in large saucepan; drain fat.
Pour in all other ingredients, except cheese.
Divide evenly into 3 pie thins or 1 large casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for about 25 minutes. May be frozen and reheated for serving.
Cheese should be added before baking or before reheating.
Very good served with corn chips.
Peel eggplants.
Cut in 1/2-inch strips.
Mix egg, milk, black pepper, salt and 1 cup flour; beat well.
Dip eggplants in batter. Put 4 cups flour in a shallow pan and roll eggplants.
Fry in deep fat at 350° until brown.
Mix ground beef, eggs, oatmeal, onion, cheese, catsup and seasonings; form into tiny meat balls.
Melt 2 tablespoons of fat in a skillet.
Cook meat balls in the fat until brown.
Drain well. Pour barbecue sauce over meat balls if needed.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Preheat 20 minutes before serving.
Makes about 60 meat balls.

recipes.t: Clams In Black Bean Sauce(Recipe For One Pound Of Clams; May Use For Any Shellfish.)
d: Rinse clams thoroughly.
Place in 5 cups of water and bring to a boil.
As soon as clams start to open, remove from stove and set aside and drain.
Prepare black beans by soaking in warm water and mashing it.
Heat oil; add garlic and black bean.
Add broth, sugar, oyster sauce, shoyu, salt and ajinomoto.
Make cornstarch paste by adding water to the cornstarch.
Add to sauce to thicken.

recipes.t: Lite N' Lean Oven Fried Chicken
d: Heat oven to 400°.
Combine bread crumbs, flour, paprika, poultry seasoning, onion salt, garlic powder, thyme and pepper. Stir with fork until well blended. Add oil slowly.
Toss with fork to distribute.
Stir until well blended.
Moisten chicken with water.
Roll in coating mixture.
Place in single layer in a 15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch jelly roll pan or other large pan.
Sprinkle any remaining crumb mixture over chicken.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until no longer pink in center.
Serves 8.

recipes.t: Black Iron Kettle Old-Fashion Beef Stew
d: Put oil in bottom of kettle, enough so the beef cubes, onions and potatoes won't burn.
Brown beef, onions and potatoes.
Add carrots, peas, celery and a little water and cook slowly for 1 hour or until done.
Season with blend of herbs.
Then add soups.
Boil potatoes until tender. Peel and mash or chunk in large bowl. Mix margarine with potatoes while they are hot.
Mix onion, pickles, vinegar, pimientos, chilies and mayonnaise with potatoes. Add salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Cut boiled eggs in fourth and place on top of salad.
Dice onion and bacon fine.
Saute onion and bacon with 1/2 cup water until onion is transparent and water has evaporated.
Stir melted butter into the mixture.
Soak slice of bread in evaporated milk until completely saturated, stirring to break it up.
Set aside.

Blend together milk, sugar, lard, salt and egg. In 1/4 cup warm water, dissolve yeast, then add to milk mixture. Add enough flour to make a soft dough. Let rise until double in bulk, then make into rolls, coffee cake, cinnamon rolls, whatever you desire.
Cook black beans until tender; do not overcook.
Drain.
Pour olive oil in a frying pan and heat.
Place garlic, jalapeno pepper and onions in pan.
Saute until the onions are tender, translucent and start to take on some color.
Add corn, black beans, cilantro, tomatoes and lime juice.
Stir well and toss this mixture over high heat, until all ingredients are very hot.
Serve at once.
Yields 10 portions.
Soak the raccoon in a vinegar and water solution for about 1 hour.
Drain and cut into serving size pieces.
Salt and pepper the pieces and cover with water in a boiler.
Add garlic and bay leaves and boil until meat is partly tender.
Remove meat and brown in a roasting pan.
Add a little flour to the pan drippings and mix in enough water to make a thin gravy.
Place the vegetables in the pan and bake at 350° for about 45 minutes or until meat and vegetables are tender.
Cook jello, cornstarch and water until thick.
Add sugar to this mixture.
Drain strawberries and add water to make 1 cup. Let cooked mixture cool and get thick.
Add strawberries or cherry pie filling.
Whip Dream Whip with milk.
Whip together cream cheese and 1/2 cup milk.
Mix together cream cheese and Dream Whip.
Make a 9 x 13-inch graham cracker crust or butter and flour and spread in pan and bake.
I have to use a small amount of water and a little more flour to have enough to press up sides of dish. Let cool.
Put a layer of white filling (about 1/2) on crust. Add red mixture and top with white mixture.
I put cracker crumbs on top.
Keep in refrigerator.
Combine 2 1/2 cups flour with yeast and honey.
Beat in milk slowly, then water.
Continue
beating
to
3 minutes. Add butter.
Mix well.
Add
remaining
flour
to
make
dough stiff. Let rest 5 minutes.
Add raisins, apples and cinnamon. Knead for 6 to 7
minutes until fruits are evenly distributed. Place in large greased bowl
and cover with damp towel.
Place in warm place 1 to 1
hours.
Punch down dough.
Knead on floured surface 3 to 4 minutes.
Shape into large ball.
Place in greased and floured baking
pan.
Let
rise
uncovered
20 minutes in a warm place. Preheat
oven to 425°.
Place pan of hot water on lowest rack. Bake
bread for 30 minutes.
Remove water and reduce oven to 300°.
Bake
for
to 40 minutes. Cool on wire rack.
Breakfast bread.
Combine cornmeal, flour, salt, sugar and baking powder.
Add shortening and boiling water.
Stir until shortening is all dissolved.
Add beaten egg yolks and flavoring at once and beat well.
Fold in egg whites which have been beaten stiff.
Cook squash down.
Mash and add soup, sour cream, carrot, onion, salt, pepper and red pepper.
Butter a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish and sprinkle a layer of bread crumbs in the bottom. Add the squash mixture and cover the mixture with bread crumbs and generous bits of margarine or butter.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.

Combine cracker crumbs, coconut and nuts. Beat egg whites with salt and vanilla until foamy. Gradually add sugar and continue beating until egg whites form stiff peaks. Fold cracker mixture into egg white mixture. Spread in well-greased 9-inch pie plate or 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes. Cool. Cut in wedges and top with ice cream, if desired.
Combine the broth, potatoes, leeks and mushrooms.
Cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender.
Add lobster meat, wine (optional), and whipping cream.
Reduce heat to low.
In small bowl, combine flour with the milk and beat until smooth.
Add to the chowder along with the Old Bay seasoning.
Simmer until flavors have blended.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In blender container, place Green Goddess dressing and parsley.
Cover; blend until smooth.
Pour into small bowl.
Fold in whipped cream.
Cover.
Chill.
Cut avocado lengthwise in half. Remove pit.
Scoop avocado into 3/4-inch balls.
Place in bowl. Add lemon juice to keep from discoloring.
Drain off liquid from seafood.
Add seafood and celery to bowl; toss
very gently.
Line 4 salad plates with lettuce leaves.
Spoon avocado mixture into each.
Top with some dressing.
Serve rest separately.
Mix pudding, sugar and milk in large saucepan.
Cook on medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes.
Add nuts; boil 5 minutes more or until a soft ball stage when dropped in cold water.
Remove from heat, add margarine and vanilla.
Stir until mixture starts to thicken (like fudge).
Drop in small patties on waxed paper.
Cool, but remove pralines while still warm to prevent sticking.
Cut chicken into bite size pieces.
Heat oil in a large, nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add chicken, green pepper and seasonings.
Saute until chicken is lightly browned.
Stir in rice until coated with seasonings.
Stir in water and tomato sauce; bring to a boil, then cover skillet and reduce heat to low. Simmer until water is absorbed and rice is cooked.
Remove from heat and add parsley. Cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
This recipe is quite low in fat content.
Boil sweet potatoes until soft.
Peel and mash while still hot.
Add cream and mashed bananas.
Mix well and place in a buttered baking dish.
Cover mixture with marshmallows and place in hot oven.
Bake until marshmallows are golden brown.
Combine crushed cereal, brown sugar and butter; mix thoroughly.
Reserve 1/4 cup crumb mixture for garnish.
Press remaining mixture firmly into 9-inch pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 5 to 8 minutes.
Cool, then freeze.
Allow lemonade concentrate and ice cream to thaw just enough to mix easily.
Spread in pie shell and garnish with reserved crumbs and lemon slices.
Return to freezer; keep frozen until serving.
In large bowl, combine 2 cups flour and the remaining dry ingredients and mix together well.
In saucepan, heat water, molasses and butter to 120° to 130°.
Butter may not be melted. Add to dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Add remaining flour, until dough is soft, but not sticky.
Knead, let rise in greased bowl.
Punch down.
Shape into 2 loaves.
Let rise until double in bulk.
Bake at 350°.
Cook ground beef.
Crumble while draining.
Put some beef on tortilla; add a little tomato, lettuce and onion and top with cheese.
Roll up.
Pop in microwave for 30 seconds.
Take out and top with salsa.
Saute bell pepper, onion and bacon.
Add to beans.
(If you use the barbecue sauce, you may add diced green chiles or 1 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes.)
Simmer for 30 minutes or cook on slow in a crock-pot for 4 to 6 hours.
Good for pot luck dinners and picnics.
Arrange bacon slightly overlapping in a 13 x 9-inch ungreased pan.
Pour syrup over bacon.
Beat eggs in 1-quart bowl until foamy; beat in remaining ingredients, except applesauce, until smooth.
Pour over bacon and syrup.
Bake uncovered in a 400° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat applesauce to just warm. Cut pancakes into 8 pieces and top each with applesauce.
Beat together the eggs, milk and seasonings.
Gradually stir in the flour.
Set this aside and prepare the dredge by mixing together the flour, cornmeal, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne.
Add the oil to a deep fat fryer and heat. Prepare the frog legs by dipping them in the egg-milk preparation and then coating them with the dry ingredients.
Fry the legs, one pair at a time, until golden brown.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Combine cabbage, onion, green pepper.
Layer with salt, celery seed and white pepper.
Mix flour and butter or margarine.
Add salt, milk, sugar, baking powder and egg yolks.
Beat egg whites and add to mixture. Place 2 to 3 cups sliced fruit in bottom of deep dish (use peaches, apples, pears and nectarines).
Pour batter over fruit. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Serve with a dollop of ice cream.

Rinse chicken breasts; pat dry. Place in shallow baking dish; season with salt, pepper and garlic salt. Cover with Ragu sauce and marinate in refrigerator about 3 hours. Bake, uncovered, in 350° oven about 45 to 55 minutes (until tender). Cover with cheese and bake, uncovered, another 15 minutes (until melted and lightly browned). This is so good!
Soften butter to room temperature.
Cream butter and sugar with electric mixer until fluffy.
Sift cornstarch and flour 3 times. By hand, mix small amounts of triple sifted flour mixture to the creamed butter mixture.
Mixture will be stiff.
Pat into 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan.
Poke mixture randomly with a fork dipped in flour.
Bake in preheated 325° oven for 30 minutes, then reduce oven heat to 300° and bake additional 10 to 20 minutes until barely golden.
Cut into small squares but do not remove from pan until completely cooled.
Store in airtight container.
Keeps well up to 10 days.
Also freezes well.
In bottom of 3-quart baking dish put rice.
Layer with vegetables; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add one 8 ounce can tomato sauce mixed with 1/2 can water.
Add onion and green pepper.
Top with layer of ground beef.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour over 8 ounce can tomato sauce mixed with 1/4 can water.
Top with bacon strips.
Bake covered for 1 hour in 350° oven.
Uncover; bake 30 minutes longer.
Use large bowl.
Beat oil and sugar until well blended.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add pumpkin and beat well.
Sift flour and spices and add to pumpkin mixture.
Add dates and nuts.
Pour batter into 2 well-greased loaf pans.
Line the bottom of pans with wax paper.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cool in pan.
Serve plain or warm with whipped cream.
Freezes well. Makes 2 loaves.
Marinate meat ahead of time at room temperature in soy sauce, sugar, starch, salt, m.s.g. and sherry.
In saucepan, cook beans according to directions.
Drain.
Heat oil in wok.
Add the drained meat and stir-fry for a few minutes; add the beans and cook for a few minutes longer.
Serve over hot buttered rice. Serves 2 to 3.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease a 1-quart shallow baking dish. In small bowl, combine brown sugar, cinnamon and salt; set aside. Cut sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch slices.
Arrange half in baking dish.
Cover with apples.
Sprinkle half the brown sugar mixture over apples.
Top with remaining sweet potato slices.
Sprinkle with remaining brown sugar.
Spoon on 2 tablespoons of melted butter or margarine.
Cover and bake 35 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Shred chicken in strips about 2 inches long.
Arrange on spinach leaves on individual plates, alternating with apple, orange and onion rings.
Sprinkle apple slices with lemon juice to prevent darkening.
Mix crackers, dates, nuts, sugar, baking powder, salt and flavoring.
Fold dry mixture a teaspoon at a time into well-beaten egg whites.
Bake in well-greased 9 x 9-inch pan for 30 minutes at 350°.
Sprinkle goose inside and out with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Melt butter or margarine in a large saucepan.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Stir in apple, apricots, bread crumbs, salt and pepper.
Spoon stuffing lightly into cavity.
Truss bird. Cover breast with bacon slices and cheesecloth soaked in melted bacon drippings.
Melt butter in a 15 x 10 x 2-inch pan in a 250° oven.
Remove and stir in seasoned salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Add Chex cereals and nuts.
Mix until all pieces are coated.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Spread on paper towel to cool. May be stored or frozen in airtight container.
Recipe can be doubled. Makes about 9 cups.

Combine first 5 ingredients. Shake well. Add tomatoes and cheese. Toss gently. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Bring to room temperature to serve. Cut bread into 24 slices. Toast. Top with tomato mixture.
In skillet, brown beef and drain. Drain tomatoes, reserving liquid into skillet. Add onion, green pepper and cayenne.
Cook over high heat 5 to 8 minutes or until slightly thickened, stirring often. Stir in tomatoes and potatoes.
Heat thoroughly. Top with cheese; heat until melted.
Brown the onions, garlic and meat.
Drain off the fat.
Add the tomato sauce and water and simmer 20 minutes uncovered (add spices - basil, oregano etc. if desired).
Mix flour, salt and pepper; coat chops and brown on both sides. Place in baking dish.
Combine soup, water, ginger and rosemary; pour over chops; sprinkle with 1/2 of the onions.
Cover and bake until chops are tender.
Uncover; sprinkle with the balance of onions and bake 10 minutes.
Remove chops; add sour cream to the gravy.
Bake at 350° about 1 hour.
Separate eggs.
Beat yolks until very thick and lemon-colored. Beat whites until frothy; add water and salt and beat until stiff, but not dry.
Fold yolks into whites very gently.
Fold in cheese and any optional ingredients.
Bake in hot (preheated) buttered 10 to 12-inch skillet at 350° for 15 minutes or until golden.
(Done when knife inserted in center comes out clean.) Serves 2 to 4.
Melt chocolate bits with butter.
Break in eggs, add sugar, cookie wafers, nuts and marshmallows.
Mix.
Lay a piece of plastic wrap on counter.
Shape dough on it into a roll about 1 1/2 inch thick.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Chill.
Slice and eat.
Combine
pumpkin,
sugar and spices.
Add pecans.
In a chilled
bowl,
fold
pumpkin
mixture
into
ice cream.
Line bottom of 13
x 9 x 2-inch pan with half the gingersnaps.
Top with half
the ice cream mixture.
Repeat. Freeze until firm, about 5 hours.
Cut in squares, garnish with whipped cream and pecan halves, if desired.
Makes 18 servings.
Snap off any tough outer leaves from the cabbage and slice off stem.
Cut cabbage in half through its core, then slice each half into quarters, making 8 wedges.
Arrange wedges in two concentric circles in a 9-inch glass pie plate.
(Dish will be mostly full.) Sprinkle with onion, carrot and dill.
Pour on stock. Cover plate with vented plastic wrap. Microwave on High 6 minutes. Rotate dish a half turn and microwave another 6 minutes or until cabbage is tender.
Let stand, covered, about 5 minutes to finish cooking. Drain.
Makes 4 servings.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together biscuit mix, flour, Parmesan cheese, dried onion and parsley.
Beat egg white with milk and stir into dry ingredients until just moistened.
Fill muffin cups half full (should have been sprayed with nonstick cooking spray first).
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
You should be able to stick a toothpick in the center and have it come out clean. Makes 12 muffins.

recipes.t: Poppy Seed Coffee Cake(Very Easy!  Very Good!)
d: Combine poppy seed and buttermilk; soak overnight in refrigerator.
Cream butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Combine flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Add vanilla to buttermilk mixture.
Add dry ingredients and buttermilk mixture alternately to creamed mixture, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Spoon half the batter into a well-greased 10-inch tube pan or Bundt pan.
Combine 1/3 cup sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over batter.
Top with remaining batter.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour or until cake tests done.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Saute onions in small amount of margarine.
Add onion soup, bay leaf, bouillon, salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to a rolling boil and add cheese.
Simmer 1/2 hour, then thicken with cornstarch and cold water.
Pour into a long glass baking dish. Lay sliced Italian bread on top.
Add slices of Provolone cheese and toast under the broiler.
In medium mixing bowl, combine sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves.
Fold in raisins.
Spoon as much of the mixture into the cored apples.
Drizzle 1 1/2 tablespoons of orange juice concentrate into each apple.

recipes.t: Native American Cinnamon Wild Rice Pudding
d: Butter a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Set aside.
Combine eggs, dried cherries or raisins, maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla, rice and half and half.
Stir gently.
Pour into casserole.
Cream butter and brown sugar.
Add eggs.
Beat well.
Add cinnamon, vanilla and almond extract.
Fold in flour a little at a time.
Let stand for 30 minutes.
Keep in refrigerator.
Bake in pizzelle iron.
Makes 12 to 13 dozen.
Mix chopped dates and half of pecans with half box of dry cake mix.
Set aside.
Add eggs, brown sugar and water to other half of cake mix.
Beat well; stir in other half of cake mix.
Bake in a greased and floured jelly roll pan at 350° for 20 minutes.
When cool, spread with a can of butter pecan frosting mix.
Top with pecans.
In large heavy pan, brown roast in shortening; pour off fat. Add soup, water, onion and seasonings.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Add carrots and potatoes.
Cook 1 hour more or until meat and vegetables are done.
Remove bay leaf.
Thicken juice for gravy, if desired.
In large bowl, combine sour cream, pineapple, sweetened condensed milk and lemon juice. Mix well. Layer with nuts in parfait glasses. Garnish with cherries. Chill.

recipes.t: Beef And Bean Homemade Burritos(Quick And Easy)
d: In skillet brown ground beef. Salt and pepper to taste.
Add can of refried beans.
Stir until thoroughly mixed.
Simmer.
Heat tortillas individually.
Add meat mixture and toppings.
Heat the butter in the dish and fry cashews and raisins until the nuts are golden brown.
Add the milk, water and salt.
Bring it to a boil.
(Optional:
You might add food coloring.)
Stir in Cream of Wheat little by little to avoid lumps.
Add sugar and keep stirring for 2 minutes.
About 1 hour before serving, combine in a glass salad bowl the olive or salad oil, lemon juice, garlic and pepper.
Cover bowl and let stand 50 minutes.
Discard garlic.
Prepare cake mix according to directions on box.
Mix together Ricotta cheese, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and eggs.
Grease and flour 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Pour cake mix into pan.
Pour cheese mix on top.
Bake approximately 1 hour and 10 minutes at oven temperature according to cake mix directions (but watch).

Boil chicken, lemon pepper, salt and garlic powder until chicken is done. Leave the water and chicken in pot and cover with a lid. Let the chicken set in the water until completely cooled. When cooled, drain and tear chicken apart. Add celery and mayonnaise to taste.
Mix 2 cups of the flour, onions, 1 tablespoon oil, 1 teaspoon rosemary, salt, pepper and yeast in a large bowl.
Add warm water. Beat on low speed 1 minute, scraping bowl frequently. Stir in enough of the remaining flour, one cup at a time, to make dough easy to handle.
Place cream cheese in microwave until softened.
Dice as many green olives as you wish and add to cream cheese.
Crush two cloves of garlic and add to mix.
Start mixing very slowly and add milk (about 2 tablespoons at a time) until the dip reaches desired consistency.
Let sit overnight in refrigerator to allow ingredients a chance to combine.
It can be used with vegetables, chips or pretzels.
Brown meat in olive oil.
Add garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook slowly for 10 minutes.
Add tomatoes and tomato sauce mixed with spaghetti sauce mix.
Stir in thoroughly.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Boil lasagna noodles in salted water until tender. Drain and rinse.
Pour 1/3 of meat sauce into 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish.
Cover with layer of lasagna noodles, then layer of Mozzarella cheese and spoonfuls of cottage cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with meat sauce.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cook rice until tender, but not mushy.
Combine oil, vinegar, salt, pepper and tarragon.
While rice is hot, pour oil mixture over it and mix thoroughly.
Cool.
Fold in peppers, onion, peas and pimento.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Mix sugar, vanilla, salt and egg whites.
Add sugar until it forms a ball.
Chill in refrigerator several hours.
Place on cutting board sprinkled with powdered sugar.
Roll out with rolling pin to about 1/2-inch thickness.
Spread with peanut butter.
Roll into a rope shape.
Cut into slices 1/2-inch thick. Chill before serving.
Grate cheese and mix well with cracker crumbs.
Add liquid from asparagus to mushroom soup.
Put layer of cracker crumbs and cheese in bottom of casserole; add layer of asparagus tips. Sprinkle with nuts.
Cover with mushroom soup.
Repeat until all ingredients are used.
Put layer of cheese and cracker crumbs on top; decorate with whole blanched almonds or pecans.
Pour melted butter over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Toast coconut and almonds on cookie sheet at 350° for 4 to 6 minutes.
Watch carefully; stir occasionally.
Cream butter and white and brown sugars until light.
Add vanilla and coconut extracts.
Beat in egg.
Combine flour, baking soda, salt and cornstarch.
Stir into butter mixture using a spoon rather than a mixer.
Add coconut and almonds.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Place on lightly greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool slightly before removing to a rack to complete cooling.
Mix sugars and butter together.
Beat in eggs, vanilla, flour and pecans. Pour into 9-inch pie crust and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Put the eggs into a large bowl, add 1 cup of the sugar, and beat until stiff and creamy.
Put the butter and milk into a sauce pan and heat gently until the butter has melted.
Meanwhile, arrange the apple slices in a shallow ovenproof dish 12 inches diameter, buttered.
Brown beef and onions.
Drain grease.
Add remaining ingredients in skillet with beef and onions.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve on buns or bread.
Serves 6 to 8.

Pound chicken breast with mallet until evenly flat. Place cheese and ham on the flattened chicken and roll chicken. Melt butter in saute pan. Lightly dust chicken in flour. Saute chicken, seam-side down, four minutes on each side until brown. Drain butter. Remove chicken. Deglaze pan with wine. Reduce wine by half. Add the chicken breasts back to pan, heavy cream and soy sauce. Sprinkle with Romano. Garnish with parsley. Serve with mashed potatoes, fettuccine Alfredo or baked potatoes.

Sprinkle turnip with salt; set aside for 30 minutes. Melt 3 tablespoons butter. Saute butter and bread crumbs; set aside. Squeeze water from turnip. Combine with carrots. Melt 4 tablespoons butter and add turnip, carrots and sugar. Turn heat low, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Uncover and stir in dill, salt and pepper to taste. Put in covered casserole. Pour on cream. Top with crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Separate chicken wings into 3 pieces.
Discard tips.
Marinate wings in ingredients that have been heated until the sugars dissolve.
Cool.
Add wings and marinate 24 hours.
Remove wings from marinade.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan and bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Brush occasionally with marinade.
Clean celery, then cut into serving size pieces.
Spread softened cream cheese on each celery piece.
Cut cheese slices with 4 triangles per slice.
Place a cheese triangle upright in the cream cheese.
(This is the boat's sail.) Place raisins on cream cheese.
Chill.
Serve.
Put 1 cup sugar in heavy saucepan. Cook and stir over medium heat until sugar is melted and golden brown. Add hot water and stir until sugar is dissolved. Add remaining 2 cups sugar, milk and salt.
Cook over low heat to 242° or until candy forms almost a hard ball in cold water.
Remove from heat.
Candy will appear curdled.
Add butter, orange rind and nuts.
Beat at once until creamy.
Pour into greased dish. Cut into squares.
I leave out the orange rind.
Brown beef; drain.
Add sauce and water (swished in jar). Simmer 10 minutes.
Mix 3 cheeses, eggs, parsley and seasonings in bowl. Spread 1/2 cup of sauce on bottom of a 9 x 12-inch glass casserole dish.
Layer 1/3 of noodles next.
Follow in order with 1 1/2 cups sauce, 1/2 cheese mix, 1/3 noodles, 1 1/2 cups sauce, cheese, 1/3 noodles and rest of sauce.
Cover with aluminum foil. Place on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Uncover; bake 10 more minutes, if needed.
Mix cake mix and 1 dry vanilla pudding mix; bake as directed on cake mix in a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Mix sugar and crushed pineapple; boil 5 minutes. Pour over hot cake.
Refrigerate cake until it is cold.
Slice bananas and spread over top.
Mix one box of vanilla pudding and put on cake.
Ice cake with Cool Whip, coconut and pecans.
Prepare graham cracker crust, reserving 1/3 cup crumbs. Chill.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form.
Slowly add thawed concentrate, sweetened condensed milk and food color, mixing well. (Do not overbeat).
Pour into pie shell and sprinkle with crumbs. I thinly slice a clean lemon, half the slices and put facing the same direction denoting each piece.
It looks pretty and is easy to cut even pieces.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Peel shrimp and wrap with bacon strips.
Melt butter.
Add Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Mix together and pour over shrimp, then marinate for 15 to 30 minutes.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes, until done.
(Do not overcook, overcooking makes shrimp tough.)
Mix sugar, Bisquick, eggs and vanilla until smooth.
Add coconut and nuts.
Bake at 325° for about 35 minutes.
Cut when cool.
After cooking pasta, cut up vegetables (except tomato) and saute in olive oil.
Pour pasta in skillet with sauteed vegetables and stir.
Pour Italian dressing over pasta and vegetables.
Cut up tomato right before serving and put on top.
Melt chocolate and butter. Cream eggs and sugar. Add flour and chocolate mixture.
Mix well.
Bake in an 8 x 8-inch pan at 350° for 20 minutes. Turn oven off and bake 5 more minutes.
Place chicken in buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish.
Add next 3 ingredients in order.
Combine soup and water; mix well.
Add to casserole.
Toss stuffing mix and melted butter; sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes or until browned and bubbly.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Put garlic, onion and cheese through grinder.
Add seasonings and mix well.
Stir in enough beer or milk to make spreading consistency.
Add oats and salt to boiling water in saucepan.
Stir in sugar and butter.
Remove from heat.
Set aside until mixture cools between 105° to 115°.
In large mixing bowl, soften yeast in 1/4 cup warm water.
Add cooled oat mixture.
Gradually stir in flour to make a stiff dough.

Combine black beans, garbanzo beans, corn, onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, tomato, dressing, chiles and honey in medium glass or ceramic bowl; refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Pour water over gelatin and dissolve.
Add mustard, paprika, salt and food coloring.
Chill until partially set.
Fold in celery, onion and green pepper.
Combine cottage cheese, whipped cream and sour cream.
Fold into gelatin mixture.
Chill until firm.
Put nuts, chocolate and zwieback through food chopper.
Chop fine.
Add cinnamon, 1 1/2 tablespoons confectioners sugar and rose water.
Form into 36 small balls.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Store in airtight container.
Combine yellow split peas, ham hocks, onion (chopped fine), chopped thyme and water in large Dutch oven.
Bring to boil; reduce heat, cover and simmer until tender, 1 1/2 hours.
Add potatoes, rutabaga, celery root, 1 1/2 cups chopped leek and salt. Return to simmer and cook, covered, stirring occasionally, 30 or 40 minutes more, until vegetables are very tender.
Remove ham hocks; discard skin and bones.
Chop ham fine and return to soup. Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over top.
Dissolve jell-o in water; stir and let stand.
Blend drained peach halves and cream cheese together in blender for 2 minutes. Combine jell-o and peach mixture.
Pour into dish or mold and chill until firm.
Invert onto serving dish and top with a layer of Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with chopped walnuts and serve.
Rinse black beans; mash and mix with garlic.
Heat oil.
Add bean mixture and saute for 1 minute.
Add chicken and saute.
Add salt and onion.
Cover and cook until almost done.
Add green peppers, cornstarch and oyster sauce.
Cover and simmer until done.
Beat butter and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in egg and salt. Gradually stir in flour until soft dough is formed.
Cover tightly and refrigerate 30 minutes.

Cream sugar and butter, adding beaten egg yolks. Add vinegar, vanilla, nuts and raisins. Add beaten egg whites. (Do not beat egg whites until stiff.) Pour into uncooked pie crust. Bake in 300° oven until egg whites rise, then turn oven to 250°. Cook until brown or about an hour.
Cook corn and water for approximately 20 minutes.
Add sugar, salt and pepper.
Mix cornstarch, milk and flour.
Stir this until smooth.
Thicken the corn with it.
When thick remove from heat and add butter.
Ready to eat.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet; place a slice of cheese on each bread slice.
Place in oven to melt cheese.
In a large skillet, melt butter.
Add chicken pieces; cook until done.
Place 1 piece cooked chicken on top of each bread slice.
Return to oven to keep warm.
Pour wine into same skillet. Add mushrooms and onions; saute until cooked.
Stir in cornstarch, milk and salt.
Cook, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
Place chicken-topped bread on a platter.
Top with mushroom sauce.
Makes 6 servings.

Preheat oven to 350°. Grease 8-inch square baking pan; set aside. Melt unsweetened chocolate and butter in small saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly; set aside. Beat eggs in large bowl with electric mixer at medium speed 30 seconds. Gradually add sugar, beating at medium speed, about 4 minutes until very thick and lemon-colored. Beat in chocolate mixture and vanilla. Beat in flour and salt at low speed just until blended. Stir in baking bar pieces and walnuts, if desired. Spread batter evenly into prepared baking pan. Bake 30 minutes or until edges just begin to pull away from sides of pan and center is set. Remove pan to wire rack. Cool.
Boil potatoes in 1 1/2 cups water until tender; drain. Reserve 1 cup liquid.
Mash potatoes and set aside 1 cup to cool. Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm potato liquid.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Add potatoes, butter, honey, oil, eggs, salt and 1 1/2 cups flour.
Beat until smooth 6 to 8 minutes. Add enough flour to make dough.
Place in a greased bowl, turning once.
Cover and let rise in warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Shape into rolls. Bake at 375° for 20 minutes or until browned.
Slice top crust off rolls.
Hollow out leaving 1/2-inch shell. Brush with butter.
Heat beans, stir in 1/2 of cheese, fill rolls with
bean mix,
then
sour
cream.
Sprinkle with onion; cover with
sausage.
Top with remaining cheese. Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Serve with salsa.
Boil eggs, sugar and juice together until thick, stirring constantly.
While hot, mix in cream cheese.
Then cool and add the pineapple, marshmallows and Cool Whip.
Mix well and chill.

recipes.t: Fried Rice With Pork And Water Chestnuts
d: Heat peanut oil and sesame oil in wok over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger (do not brown).
Add rice and fry over high heat until rice begins to change color.
Sprinkle with soy sauce and continue frying.
Add ham and water chestnuts and stir well.
Move rice to sides and egg in middle.
Stir until almost dry.
Mix with rice and add green onions.
Serves 4 to 5.
Sprinkle chicken with salt, pepper and paprika.
Brown in butter.
Mix soup and curry together, pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Take chicken from pan.
Add large container of sour cream and mushrooms to the pan and mix well.
Return chicken to pan, sprinkle with almonds.
Return to oven for another 15 minutes.
Serve with rice or pasta.
Melt butter in large skillet over medium heat.
Add coconut and cook, stirring constantly, until golden, about 6 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Reserve 2 tablespoons coconut for garnish. Press remainder into bottom and sides of 9-inch pie plate.
Spread half of orange sherbet over crust.
Drizzle with liqueur.
Add remaining sherbet, mounding top.
Sprinkle with reserved coconut. Freeze until ready to serve or overnight.
Let stand 10 to 15 minutes before serving.
Garnish with mint, orange peel and mandarin orange segments.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix the oil, lemon juice and seasonings in a shallow casserole or 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Roll the chicken in mixture and place in pan skin side down.
Put pan in preheated oven and cook until chicken is done (basting with juices).
In skillet, saut onions and garlic in oil for 2 minutes.
Add chicken and cook 2 minutes more or until chicken is cooked through. One at a time, add broccoli, pepper and mushrooms, sauteing each for 1 minute before adding next ingredient.
Add soy sauce, ginger and parsley to chicken/veggies.
Reduce heat; cover and steam 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir and serve immediately.
Makes 2 servings.
Marinate the chicken in the brown barbecue sauce overnight. Remove the chicken from the marinade and grill.
As the chicken is being grilled, baste with the following Red Barbecue Sauce.
On a lightly floured surface, roll bread dough to a 13 x 9-inch rectangle.
Place dough in greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Cover; let rise in warm place about 1 1/2 hours or until nearly double.
In a saucepan, cook onion in butter until tender.
Stir in seasoning.
Cool mixture slightly; stir in cheese.
Spoon cheese mixture evenly atop dough.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cut into 3 x 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Serve warm.
Makes 24.
Mix together dry ingredients. Combine egg, orange juice, water and oil.
Add liquid to dry ingredients, stirring just until moist.
Let mixture rest for 30 seconds. Spoon or pour batter onto greased, hot griddle. Cook pancakes on the first side until bubbles appear on upper surface. Turn over and cook until bottom is golden.
Brown beef and onion. Drain excess fat.
Add taco seasoning. Remove from heat.
Place milk and margarine in bottom of deep baking dish. Alternate potatoes, meat, olives and grated cheese in layers.
Add salsa last. Cover and bake in preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour. Serves 4.
Melt cheese and Ro-Tel tomatoes with green chilies in crock-pot.
Cook in skillet the ground beef and then sausage. Drain well.
Mix meats in crock-pot with cheese.
Add Blue cheese mix.
Serve warm with tortilla chips or crackers.
Makes a lot.
Chop tomatoes, green peppers and onions.
Slice cucumber, carrots and radishes.
Break cauliflower up.
Pour Zesty Italian dressing over and let set 3 to 4 hours.
Keep in refrigerator. You can keep adding vegetables to dressing.
Cut rind of ham, if present.
Score top surface of ham; stud with cloves.
Place, fat side up, on a rack in a shallow baking pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven approximately 15 minutes per pound, or follow wrapper directions.
Combine sugar, syrup and mustard.
Use 3/4 cup of glaze to baste ham every 10 minutes during the last 30 to 45 minutes of baking.
Stir cornstarch into remaining glaze in saucepan.
Add pineapple with juice.
Simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Serve sauce with ham.
Combine ground beef and salad dressing mix; shape into meatballs.
Melt margarine in a skillet and brown meatballs on all sides.
Add broth, cover and simmer until cooked.
Serve warm with toothpicks.
Makes 2 dozen.
In an ungreased 8-inch square pan, stir together flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt.
In a separate bowl, mix together oil, vinegar and vanilla.
Make 3 indentations in the flour mixture and pour the oil mixture evenly into them.
Pour cold water over top of it all and stir until smooth.
(Be sure to mix well in the corners.)
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes until tester comes out clean.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot water.
Add cinnamon candies to 1/2 cup boiling water; stir to dissolve.
Add enough water to make 1 cup liquid.
Add to dissolved Jell-O.
Cool until partially set. Add remaining ingredients.
Pour into 1-quart mold or 6 individual molds; chill until firm.
Serve on lettuce.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan.
In a medium bowl, beat butter and brown sugar 5 to 8 minutes or until light and fluffy.
Add eggs; beat until blended.
Sift flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt into a medium bowl.
Stir flour mixture into egg mixture alternately with milk, stirring until combined.
Fold in chopped nuts.
Blend butter, flour and brown sugar and press into an 9 x 12 inch pan.
Bake 12 minutes at 350°.
Mix remaining ingredients together and pour over the hot crust. Bake about 20 minutes longer at 375°.
Serve in squares.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Arrange vegetables on the bottom of the dish.
Cut bread slices into 1/2-inch cubes. Sprinkle the vegetables with the bread cubes and chopped ham. Combine eggs, milk, mustard, garlic powder and onion powder; mix well.
Pour the egg mixture over the rest and sprinkle with cheese. Cover with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate 6 hours or overnight. Uncover and bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean.
Serves 8 to 10.
Sift first 4 dry ingredients together.
Mix in butter or shortening.
Put in raisins.
Beat egg in cup with fork; add milk. Add to mixed ingredients.
Bake in greased bread pan at 350° for 3/4 to 1 hour.
If buttermilk is used in place of sweet milk, add speck of baking soda.
Melt margarine for 30 to 45 seconds.
Mix in remaining ingredients.
Cook in low round dish with inverted saucer in the center or in a ring mold.
Cook 17 minutes on 80% power or until knife in center comes out clean like a cake.
For one half the recipe use 1 onion.
Fry beef with taco seasoning; cook until liquid is reduced. Place meat in a large pan or casserole dish.
Layer refried beans on top of meat.
Layer on onion, chilies, olives and tomato.
Pour salsa over top, then sour cream and guacamole dip.
Top with cheese.
Put in oven until cheese melts.
Cook in peanut oil in a wok the onions, garlic and green pepper for a few minutes until it begins to brown.
Then add the sliced zucchini and corn pieces and sprinkle with vegetable seasoning salt.
As this is cooking, slice the tomatoes and add them.
Then add about a cup or so of water and steam on low heat, covered, in the wok for about 30 minutes.
The corn and zucchini absorb the delicious taste of the onions, garlic and green peppers.
Must use all fresh vegetables for this dish.
Pound pork chops to 1/4-inch thickness.
Saute garlic in hot oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Remove garlic, reserving oil in skillet.
Combine flour and next four ingredients; dredge chops in flour mixture.
Brown in skillet, turning once.
Place chops in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Place one slice cheese on each chop.
Top with three asparagus spears.
Fold chops in half. Secure with wooden picks.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Serve with Tarragon Sauce.
Spread bean dip or refried beans in center of a large platter. Add in layers picante sauce, black olives, green onions, guacamole dip, sour cream and cheese.
Add more cheese and green onions on top to garnish.
Surround with chips.
Marinate chicken overnight in pineapple juice and Worcestershire.
Grill chicken until fully done.
Grill pineapple slices slightly heated and serve with chicken.
Chicken may be basted while grilling for added flavor with juice-sauce mix.
Tear off 4 pieces of heavy-duty aluminum foil.
On center, place 1 carrot, 1 potato and 1 chicken breast.
Stir together soups and spoon onto top of chicken.
Top with peas.
Wrap foil well.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 50 minutes or until tender with oven set at 350°.
Serves 4.
Mix frosting and sugar by hand. It will form a stiff dough. Roll out on waxed paper into a rectangle. Top with peanut butter, enough to cover and taste. Roll up jelly roll style. Chill.
Slice into pieces before serving.
Combine all dry ingredients and mix.
Beat egg and add to milk.
Add to dry ingredients, mix well and add melted oleo.
Mix in grated apples.
Bake on hot griddle.
Drain well all fruit; mix together. Butter a casserole and pour in fruit.
Combine brown sugar and crumbs; sprinkle generously on top. Sprinkle juice of lemon and orange and bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Serve warm or cold, with or without whipped cream.
Makes 12 to 16 servings.
Mix ingredients together, adding Velveeta cheese last.
Cook about 2 hours on low in crock-pot.
Mix eggs, cornmeal, milk and corn.
Pour 1/2 of this mixture into greased 9 x 5-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle 1/2 onion, bell pepper and jalapeno pepper over this.
Sprinkle 1/2 cheese over this, next add hamburger meat, then remaining cheese, onions and peppers.
Spread remaining cornbread mixture over top.
Bake at 350°
for 45 to 55 minutes, or until brown and firm in middle.
Brown meat well in shortening.
Add celery, onions, green pepper and tomatoes.
Cover and simmer about 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender, but firm.
Add salt, sugar and soy sauce. Add spinach and cook 5 minutes longer.
Serve over rice.
Arrange vegetables over bottom of roasting pan.
Rub lamb with salt and pepper.
Place on top of vegetables.
Pour grapefruit juice mixed with mint over lamb.
Bake at 325° for 2 hours, basting every 15 minutes with pan drippings.
Serve with strained pan drippings.
Brown 1/2 onion with ground meat in oil.
Season with dry fajita seasoning, salt and pepper.
Saute remainder of onion and pepper until crunchy (do not overcook).
Butter tortillas and microwave 10 seconds.
Fill with the ingredients and roll together.
Bake cake mix, cool.
Mix pudding, let cool.
Put pineapple on cake first, then pudding, sliced bananas and Cool Whip.
Top with coconut.
Store in refrigerator.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add egg, milk and oil.
Mix well.
Add hot water and beat well.
Pour into a 9 1/2 x 11-inch cake pan. Top batter with more brown sugar and cinnamon nuts if you want to.

recipes.t: Mozzarella Lasagna(This Is Good For People Who Don'T Like Ricotta Cheese.)
d: In large pan, brown ground meat and drain well.
Add onion and cook until transparent.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, garlic, pepper and water.
Cover and cook, over low heat, approximately 30 minutes.
Mix often to prevent sticking.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Line two 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch jelly roll pan with aluminum foil.
Prepare cake following package directions.
Divide batter into 1 medium pan.
Spread evenly.
Cut through batter with knife or spatula to remove large air bubbles. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until set.
Immediately invert cake onto towels covered with confectioners sugar.
Remove foil carefully.
Immediately roll up each cake with towel jelly roll fashion.
Cool completely.
Fold cherries, coconut and cherry juice into topping.
Unroll cakes and spread with filling.
Dust with confectioners sugar.
Mix Crisco, sugars, vanilla and milk.
Beat eggs, then add to the mixture.
In a separate bowl,
combine flour, soda and salt. Add this slowly to the creamed mixture.
Stir in chocolate chips, pecans and oatmeal.
Drop by spoonfuls and bake on a cookie sheet. Bake at 375 degrees for 8 to 10 minutes.
Sift the flour into a bowl and cut in shortening.
Add enough water gradually to hold pastry together.
Press into a ball. Divide into 5 parts and roll each part on a floured surface into a 5-inch circle. Drain the peaches and mash.
Add the cinnamon and butter.
Mix well. Place 2 tablespoons peach mixture on each circle and fold over. Seal edges with a wet fork.
Fry in deep fat at 375° until golden brown and drain on absorbent paper.
Cream butter until light.
Gradually beat in sugar.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add vanilla and sour cream.
Combine flour with baking powder, soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with beer.
Mix until silky smooth batter is achieved.
Put ingredients in saucepan over medium heat.
Stir until it starts to boil.
Set aside.
Make a biscuit dough.
Roll out and cut into small pieces.
Put sauce in a deep glass baking dish. Put biscuit dough in sauce.
Sprinkle sugar and nutmeg over top. Bake at 450° for 20 minutes.
Soak corn shucks in warm water 1 day before using.
Soak in warm water again before using.
Work shortening, chili powder and salt into masa.
Add water and knead with hands until smooth. Using back of spoon, spread mixture thinly and evenly on inside of shuck, covering about half of shuck.
Fill with following mixture.
Cook sausage and drain.
Cube bread; put bread in 9 x 13-inch pan and place sausage and cheese on top.
Mix eggs and half and half.
Pour over top.
Chill overnight.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Sift Jiffy mix and cornmeal together.
Combine dry ingredients and mix well with water. Pour mixture into greased pan.
Bake at 300° until golden brown.
Cook bacon until crisp; crumble.
Cook ground beef until pink is gone.
Mix meats, onions, beans, catsup, vinegar and mustard. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Melt candy coating in large heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat.
Stir in cereal and remaining ingredients.
Stir gently until morsels are partially melted.
Spoon mixture into a greased 9-inch square pan.
Let cool completely.
Cut into squares.
Yield:
3 dozen.
Boil potatoes, eggs and carrot for about 20 minutes.
Take out the carrot 10 minutes earlier.
After it's ready, remove it from the water and peel potatoes while it's hot.
Let everything cool off and start cutting the potatoes in small, half-a-bite pieces. The eggs, carrot, pickles and onion should be chopped in small pieces.
Cut the dill.
Add mayonnaise and peas and start mixing. Add 1/4 teaspoon of salt and a touch of pepper.
Drain peaches; to syrup from peaches, add sugar, vinegar and spices and boil 5 minutes. Add peaches and simmer 5 minutes. Allow fruit to stand in pickling syrup overnight. Serve chilled.
Mix egg yolks, cottage cheese, salt and raisins.
When mixed drop by tablespoonful unto pulled dough, rather close, drop cherries over cheese mixture.
Sprinkle with sugar and buttered bread crumbs.
Roll and bake as directed on Strudel dough page.
Put bacon in bottom of electric frying pan; heat until wilted.
Make small patties of ground round and put on top of bacon.
Sprinkle with Lawry's salt.
Slice vegetables on top of meat.
You can use as many vegetables as the family likes. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Put soup over this, then water. Let it simmer for several hours.
The longer the better.
Boil chicken in salted water.
When chicken is very tender, remove from stock, reserving the stock.
Cool, then take meat off the bones.
Cut chicken meat into bite size pieces.
In a skillet, melt the margarine.
Add the flour, salt and pepper; stir.
Slowly add the chicken stock, stirring to keep mixture smooth, then add milk.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat.
Add chicken and chopped eggs; mix well.
In a heavy skillet, brown pork chops on both sides; sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Peel sweet potatoes; slice thin. Add margarine and melt.
Add sweet potatoes, turning once.
Cook until nearly done.
Peel and slice apples in eighths.
Set pork chops aside.
Add apples, brown sugar and salt over apples and potatoes.
Cover skillet and cook on low until tender.
In a 10-inch skillet, cook sausage over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned.
Remove sausage from pan, leaving drippings.
Add potatoes and onion to drippings.
Cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally until potatoes begin to brown, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium.
Beat together eggs, milk, salt and parsley until blended.
Pour over potato mixture.
Add reserved sausage.
Scramble.
Top with Cheddar cheese, cover and heat until cheese melts.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In boiling water (enough to cover), simmer shrimp with cayenne, 5 minutes.
Drain and dice.
Arrange in 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Combine mustard, sugar, steak sauce, butter, Texas Pete and salt.
Pour over shrimp.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until crumbs are golden.
Put peaches in 9
x
13-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle with sugar and dry cake
mix. Mix together.
Drizzle melted butter over all and sprinkle top
with cinnamon.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350° until golden brown.
Can be served with ice cream.
Toast bread; lay tuna on slice. Top with vegetables, then cheese. Broil until cheese is melted.
Brown beef; drain off grease.
Add onions, garlic, jalapenos, chili powder, celery salt and pepper.
Cook this until onions are clear.
Add green chilies, tomatoes, tomato sauce and V-8 juice. Cook mixture for 2 hours on simmer.
Add the sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper to the beet juice.
Chop broccoli and scallions, including green tops.
Slice mushrooms.
Combine dressing and pour over vegetables.
Marinate all day in refrigerator.
Place biscuits on a cookie sheet.
Shape each biscuit with hand to form 4-inch tart shell.
Combine sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle on biscuits.
Place a spoonful of cherry pie filling on each tart.
Top with coconut or chopped nuts.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Heat oven to 300°.
Place oven rack in upper third of oven. Line a cookie sheet with foil.
In a large bowl, mix flours, oats, corn meal, liver powder, salt and garlic powder.
Add egg, oil and broth.
Mix with a wooden spoon to make a soft dough.
Dough should be soft but firm enough to roll out.
If too moist, add some flour; if too dry, add water.
On floured surface, roll out dough to 1/2-inch thickness and cut in 3 1/2-inch long dog bone biscuit shapes with floured cutter.
Place 1-inch apart on prepared cookie sheet.
Bake 2 hours.
Turn off oven and let biscuits stand in oven overnight to dry out and harden.
Can be stored in plastic bags at room temperature up to 3 months.
Makes about 24.
Per biscuit:
31 calories, 6 grams protein, 23 grams carbohydrates, 5 grams fat, 12 mg. cholesterol and 142 mg. sodium.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, spread pie filling evenly.
Sprinkle cinnamon over apples.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over all of this. Melt butter/margarine and drizzle over top.
Bake at 350° until lightly browned on top.
Brown meat and drain grease off.
Mix cheeses and meat together.
Stuff the cooked shells with mixture.
Cover cake pan with spaghetti sauce and put shells on top.
Cover with more sauce.
Cover pan.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Combine ingredients and bring to a rolling boil, making sure butter and sugar are completely dissolved.
Add all at one time to soda crackers; stir while it cooks for 3 minutes.
Add lemon juice and sprinkle of spice for flavor.
Pour into unbaked pie shell. Sprinkle top with sugar and a little spice.
Bake at 350° until crust turns a golden brown.
All ingredients must be cut.
Heat wok with oil.
Add 2 or 3 tablespoons ginger root and garlic cloves.
Brown.
Add cut-up meat; broil real good.
Add vegetables and 2 or 3 tablespoons soy sauce.
Stir constantly.
Vegetables should be crisp (not overcooked).
Add cheese (if using it) after veggies have cooked 2 or 3 minutes.
Serve over rice or just plain.
Place bacon in bottom of crock pot.
Add margarine, onions and celery.
Cook on high until margarine melts and cook celery and onion about 15 minutes.
Combine other ingredients and cook on high one hour - turn to low and continue to cook for about four hours.
The night before, cook noodles according to package instructions.
Rinse with cold water and drain.
Add bottle of McCormick Salad Supreme, Italian dressing and onion.
Toss and refrigerate overnight.
Add other ingredients a few hours before serving, then chill.
The longer it sets, the better it tastes. May also add chopped broccoli, cauliflower and black olives.
Combine margarine, evaporated milk, sugar and salt in a saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil.
Cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Start timing when mixture starts to bubble around edges of pan.
Remove from heat.
Add marshmallows, chocolate, vanilla, walnuts and raisins.
Stir vigorously 1 minute or until marshmallows melt and blend.
Working quickly, drop by teaspoons onto waxed paper.
Cool.
Makes about 2 pounds.
Melt butter and gradually add milk, flour, salt and pepper. Cook a little.
Set aside.
Combine beaten egg yolks and milk.
Cook pudding mix according to package directions using the egg-milk mixture as the liquid. Remove from heat.
Cut cream cheese in pieces and add to hot pudding; beat until cheese is melted.
Let mixture cool about 10 minutes.
Fry hamburg and onion, then add cabbage and tomatoes.
Add 1 cup water, if needed.
Simmer until cabbage is soft.
Put all of this in a casserole as first layer, then add layers of beans, peas and carrots.
Top with mashed potatoes or onion rings.
