Bake at 375° for 20 minutes to 1/2 hour until golden brown.
Any vegetables can be used.
Sprinkle cheese on vegetables before layer of mashed potatoes.
Saute seafood in butter for 3 to 6 minutes until scallops turn white.
Add sherry and simmer for about 1 minute.
Add cream and bring to a slow boil, stirring constantly.
Add egg, garlic, salt, pepper and a bit of fresh parsley.
Stir in cheese until smooth. Add cooked fettuccine and toss well.
Garnish with lemon wedges and fresh parsley.
Serves 4.
Scald the barley and put in pan with meat, peas and water. Bring to a boil and simmer 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Add diced vegetables except cabbage and parsley.
Season and cook slowly for 1/2 hour or until vegetables are tender.
Add cabbage and boil for 10 minutes. Add parsley and serve.
Mix buttermilk, baking soda, salt and baking powder thoroughly.
Stir in cornmeal and flour.
Add egg, cream style corn and green chilies.
Fry bacon.
Cool and crumble bacon and add to other mixture.
Pour excess drippings from skillet into mixture.
Stir well and pour into skillet.
Put grated cheese on top.
Bake in the oven at 450° until brown.
Melt lard in skillet.
Stir flour into lard.
Add chili powder; stir.
Stir in tomato puree, water, garlic and salt.
Cook until bubbly.
Mix peanut butter and butter.
Add to Raisin Nut Bran.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with milk chocolate chips and butter or Crisco.
Defrost and cook hamburger in large saucepan.
Drain grease. On medium heat, add tomato soup and 3/4 can water.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic salt.
Mix well.
Cook about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 3/4 can corn.
Cook 5 minutes more, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low.
Add cheese to hot mashed potatoes.
Stir until cheese is melted into potatoes. Serve tomato-hamburger mixture on top of potatoes.
Melt butter in small skillet.
Saute green pepper and onion until tender, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Beat eggs in medium size bowl.
Stir in milk.
Mix sugar, flour, salt and pepper in small cup.
Stir into egg-milk mixture.
Add cooked pepper and onion and corn.
Turn into buttered 4 to 6-cup shallow baking dish or 9-inch pie plate.
Bake in a slow oven (275°) for 40 minutes or until softly set.
Makes 4 servings.
Saute onion in butter in a large skillet.
Add next 6 ingredients and 1/2 cup of cheese.
Mix well.
Pour into lightly greased 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes. Sprinkle remaining 1 cup of cheese over top.
Bake an additional 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Yields 8 servings.
Beat egg and garlic salt with a fork.
Add milk.
Tear up bread in small pieces, add to the liquid and blend until it is thoroughly soaked.
(Add more milk if the bread will absorb more.) Add hamburger and knead until the meat and bread mixture is thoroughly combined.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In a large bowl, combine 2 cups flour, yeast, sugar and salt; mix well.
In a saucepan, heat water, beer and oil until warm (120° to 130°).
Add this heated liquid mixture to the flour mixture and blend at low speed until moistened, then beat 3 minutes at medium speed with mixer.
Stir in remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Knead on a floured surface or with an electric mixer using a dough hook until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; turn to grease top.
Cover.
Bring water to boil.
Add barley and bouillon cubes.
Cover and reduce heat.
Simmer 1 hour or until barley is tender.
Drain. Saute mushrooms, onions, garlic and butter until tender.
Stir in barley and spices.
Yields 6 servings.
Combine mix, oil and eggs.
Beat at medium speed for 3 minutes.
Add applesauce and beat 1 minute.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake 35 minutes at 350°.
Combine vegetables, bacon and cheese in large salad bowl. Combine salad dressings and pour over salad.
Toss to mix.
Chill. Yields 16 to 20 servings.
Brown meat and pepper; drain.
Add beans, tomatoes and seasoning mix.
Heat until bubbly.
Separate dough.
Place cheese cube in each and fold over; seal well.
Roll in butter; coat with crumbs.
Arrange biscuits on top of mixture.
Bake at 375° for 18 to 22 minutes until brown.
Cook in 2-quart casserole.
Cook macaroni and drain.
In saucepan, heat soup, milk and cheese.
Add Worcestershire sauce, flaked tuna and peas.
In the bottom of a greased bowl, place half of macaroni.
Pour on half of sauce.
Repeat layers.
Sprinkle top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Boil bones and trimming of fish to obtain stock.
Wash and dry fillets.
Season with salt.
Place in a saucepan which has been well buttered.
Add finely chopped shallots and coarse chopped parsley.
Moisten with wine, fish stock or water and lemon juice. Cover saucepan and cook 10 minutes.
Remove fillets.
Arrange them upon a long platter or oval dish and keep in a warm place.
Reduce juice of the fish until there is 4 teaspoons left.
Remove fillets. Add butter.
Shake pan to sauce will cover consistency.
Rectify seasoning.
Pour sauce over fillets and glaze in the oven.
Brown ground beef; drain and set aside.
Remove seeds from peppers and cut into big chunks.

Combine ground beef, peppers, rice, spaghetti sauce, 1 cup cheese and mushrooms in casserole dish. Top with remaining cheese and bake in covered dish until last 15 minutes at 350° for 30 minutes or until peppers are nice and tender.
Brown beef with onion and garlic.
Crumble beef. Stir in all remaining ingredients except raisins.
Stirring occasionally, bring mixture to a boil.
Remove from heat and stir in raisins. Serve warm with cheese sprinkled on top.
Use as a dip for tortilla chips and/or raw vegetable dippers.
Crumble ground beef and fry until done; drain fat.
Add taco season mix and set aside.
Heat mushroom soup, jalapeno pepper, onion and a soup can of water until hot.
Remove from heat and add sour cream.
Then layer first the chips, then meat, soup mixture and cheese in that order.
Repeat.
Heat in oven at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until hot.
Use 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chop onions and put in large kettle.
Add water and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add all ingredients, crumbling the hamburger. Cook until hamburger is done.
Makes about 24 sandwiches.
Prepare the pasta nuggets by following the cooking directions on the box.
Cut the broccoli into florets.
Place the broccoli florets in a saucepan with 1-inch of water.
Partially cook the broccoli florets.
Dice 1/3 cup of red pepper and 1 medium sized tomato.
Slice the imitation crab into bite sized pieces.
Combine all these ingredients in a large salad bowl.
Add desired amounts of mayonnaise and Italian dressing.
Refrigerate for at least an hour.
Beat together the milk, egg, oil, honey and 1 teaspoon orange peel.

Add to combined cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt, mixing just until dry ingredients are moistened.* Fill 12 greased or paper lined medium size muffin cups 2/3 full.** Sprinkle combined remaining peel and sugar evenly over batter.
Bake at 425° for about 15 minutes.
Makes 1 dozen.
Melt butter in 9 x 13 pan.
Layer 1/2 the bread and 1/2 the cheese.
Top with meat and mushrooms, followed by another layer of bread and cheese.
Beat eggs, dry mustard, pepper and milk.
Pour over bread mixture.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let set a while before cutting.
Spread muffin halves with mustard; top with beef, sauerkraut and cheese.
Place on a baking sheet and broil until cheese melts. Cut each muffin into quarters.
Makes 32.
Place chicken in shallow pan.
In skillet, saute onion in oil until tender.
Add apples; saute 1 minute longer.
Pour onion and apples over chicken, melt margarine.
Combine juice, honey and salt and pour over the chicken and vegetables.
Bake 45 minutes or until chicken is cooked.
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Crispy Chicken With Honey Dipping Sauce
d: Mix salad dressing, honey, mustard and peanut butter.
Remove 1/2 cup of the salad dressing mixture; set remaining aside.
Brush chicken with 1/2 cup of the salad dressing mixture; coat with crushed chips.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 425° for 9 minutes.
Turn.
Bake an additional 4 to 5 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned.
Serve with remaining salad dressing mixture as dipping sauce.
Cook spinach as directed; drain and squeeze out excess water. Make cream sauce; add sherry and cheese.
Combine cream cheese, shrimp, spinach and artichokes.
Place in casserole; top with crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Bake covered.
Serves 6 to 8.
Brown meat in oil.
Add celery, onion and cook until tender. Blend next 5 ingredients; pour over meat.
Cover.
Simmer 2 hours. Serve goulash over hot cooked noodles tossed with parsley.
Makes 6 servings.
Place breasts in a single layer in long, shallow casserole dish, and cover with layer of cheese.
Mix sherry and soup together; pour over breasts and cheese.
Top with croutons and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, depending on thickness of breasts.
This can be made in morning and refrigerated, all except melted butter.
Serves 6 to 8.
Simmer potatoes in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and add green pepper, onion and tomato juice.
Simmer 10 minutes longer or until potatoes are tender.
Add salt and pepper to taste while simmering.
Yields 6 servings.
Saute pecans in oleo one minute.
Add onion.
Remove from heat and cool.
Add cheese; stir.
Add mayonnaise; mix well.
Chill.
Brown beef in oil; add taco mix and water and stir.
Bring to boil; reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour warm over all other ingredients in large salad bowl; mix well and serve.
No other dressing needed. Serves 6 to 8.
Can serve with hot garlic bread or pizza.
In large skillet, melt butter and brown chicken.
Remove chicken.
Stir in tomatoes, garlic and soup.
Return chicken to pan and simmer, covered, stirring occasionally, 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Boil spaghetti until done and pour tomato sauce over spaghetti.
Serve with chicken.
Serve immediately.
Can be prepared ahead and frozen.
Cream together cheese and margarine.
Blend in dressing mix and 1/4 to 1/3 cup walnuts.
Roll into a ball in plastic wrap; chill well.
Brown onions and garlic in butter; remove from skillet.
Add chicken and brown.
Put chicken in covered dish.
Return onions and garlic to skillet.
Add paste and broth; bring to boil and pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Serve over rice.
Serves 4 to 6.
Empty spice cake mix in bowl.
Add apple, raisins and nuts. Coat well with mixture.
Add egg whites, milk and cooking oil. Mix well with wooden spoon and pour into Pam-sprayed Bundt pan; bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Turn on rack to cool.
Use your favorite icing, if desired.
Store in closed container.
Mix sugar and milk. Add fruit juice. Partially freeze, then fold in the whipped cream. Finish freezing. Makes a nice, smooth, and not too rich dessert.
In
a
large
bowl dissolve yeast in lukewarm milk (1/2 cup). Add
cup
of
sugar,
1/2 teaspoon salt and 2 cups flour. Let
stand in warm place 1/2 hour.
Beat egg yolks and whole
egg lightly.
Add
cup sugar and vanilla and beat lightly.
Add to yeast mixture.
Add melted margarine and rest of
the
flour. Do
not make dough too stiff.
A softer dough makes doughnuts light and fluffy.
Work the dough until smooth and
glossy.
Cover and let stand in a warm place until double in bulk.
Mix oil, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper together and pour over first 6 ingredients mixed together.
Beat Ricotta, eggs and sugar first, then add anise flavoring, lemon juice, milk and baking powder.
Mix well.
Melt butter and pour in bottom of baking pan.
Pour everything into pan.
Sprinkle candy over it.
Bake until golden brown at 350°.
Boil meat in salted water until done.
Grind meat and put it back in broth; let it come to a boil.
Add gelatin.
Season to taste.
When cold, slice and serve.
Tastes good with lefse or flatbread.
Cook the minced onion in the butter a few minutes.
Mix with parsley, mustard, lemon juice and a little salt and pepper.
Cut eggs in half, remove the yolks and mash.
Mix with the onion, seasonings and ham.
Add a little more lemon juice if needed for smoothness.
Fill the white halves and arrange them in a baking dish.
Pour the white sauce over them and sprinkle with the bread crumbs.
Heat in moderate oven (350°) until the top is browned. Serves 4 to 6.
Real good and filling, too.
Shred cabbage and add salt.
Let stand 1 hour.
Squeeze out juice and add carrot and green pepper.
While cabbage is standing or you may make this ahead:
Combine vinegar, water, sugar, celery seed and dry mustard.
Bring to a boil and boil for 1 minute.
Cool thoroughly and pour over cabbage mixture.
Mix well.
Place in containers and freeze.
This may be refrozen and slaw still remains crisp.
Whip sweet cream and beat egg whites.
Combine and add salt and water.
Mix together.
Then add sugar and vanilla.
Sift flour and baking powder into mixture.
Bake in layer cake pans at 350° for minutes.
Brown chicken in butter or margarine; drain.
Mix gravy mix with wine instead of water.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle mushrooms and artichoke hearts over all.
Simmer 1/2 hour, turning once or twice.
Serve with rice.
Melt butter; add soups.
Heat, then add rice and heat together.
Put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Lay chicken breasts over rice mixture.
Pour additional 1/4 cup melted butter over breasts. Sprinkle with paprika and bake at 275° for 2 1/2 hours.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Trim excess fat from pork chops, leaving about 1/4 inch fat on edge.
Form oven cooking bag by closing one end with one twist-tie provided.
Place in a 1 1/2 to 2 inch deep large open roasting pan, big enough to prevent bag from extending over sides.
Place macaroni in bottom of bag.
Top with onions and green pepper.
Arrange chops on top.
Cube steak or cut in strips.
Stir into marinade and refrigerate overnight or at room temperature for 2 hours.
Put onto skewers with water chestnuts.
Cook on grill for 12 minutes. Baste with sauce.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease a large cookie sheet.
Mix ham, half of the soup and 2 tablespoons of the onions.
Stir baking mix, margarine, water and mustard until soft dough forms. Turn onto surface dusted with baking mix.
Knead 5 times.
Roll into 13-inch circle; place on cookie sheet.
Spread ham mixture over crust to within 2-inches of edge.
Fold edge over mixture, leaving about 4-inch opening in center. Sprinkle with cheese. Bake 25 to 27 minutes or until crust is light golden brown and cheese is melted.
Sprinkle with remaining onions.
Heat remaining soup. Serve with pie.
Cut a loaf angel food cake into squares about 1 1/2-inches across.
Trim off corners so that cake will look slightly round. Cream butter; add confectioners sugar gradually.
Beat well. Flavor with vanilla or almond extract or any flavoring you prefer. Add double cream.
Completely cover the cake rounds with butter and sugar mixture; roll in ground toasted almonds.
Best to serve soon after making.
Place sliced cucumbers on rimmed baking sheet, sprinkle with salt.
Let stand at room temperature for 2 hours.
Drain.
Whisk vinegar and sugar until well dissolved.
Add cucumbers, parsley, and onions to mixture.
Season with freshly ground pepper.
Toss to blend.
Let stand at least 2 hours and up to 8.
Transfer to serving dish.
Makes 16 servings.
Prepare Jell-O with 1 cup boiling water to dissolve; add soda pop.
Blend 1/2 cup crushed pineapple with the ripe banana in blender.
Add this to the Jell-O along with the remaining pineapple.
Chill to the soft set stage.
Cream butter, margarine and sugar.
Add flavoring, flour and nuts.
Chill 1 or 2 hours.
Shape into fingers.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Cool and roll in confectioners sugar.
Makes 4 dozen.
Place ribs (single layer) in 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Drain off excess fat.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over ribs. Bake, uncovered, 45 minutes at 350°, basting frequently with sauce.
Put almonds in a blender until finely ground.
Stir together almonds, powdered sugar, water, orange peel and vanilla.
Mix to a stiff paste.
Chill about an hour.
Shape dough into 8 (1 1/4-inch diameter) wafers.
Chill and serve.
Stir biscuit mix and onion powder together in bowl.
Add milk, mix to form a soft ball.
Press in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 375° for about 15 minutes to partially cook.
Beat eggs until frothy.
Add cream, salt and pepper.
Combine with cheeses, shrimp and crab.
Pour over top of hot biscuit mixture and return to oven.
Bake 35 minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut in squares and serve warm.
Garnish with sprigs of dill or parsley and tomato wedges.
Makes 54 squares.
May be made ahead.
Cover and reheat.
Beat softened cream cheese until nearly smooth.
Gradually beat in wine.
Add onion and horseradish.
Chill mixture about 1 hour. Shape into 2 logs, each about 6 inches long.
Roll each in half of the beef.
Mix Dream Whip and milk; beat until stiff.
Add sugar, vanilla and cream cheese.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Spread cherries on top.
Chill overnight.
Combine pudding, milk, brown sugar and vanilla in a medium size saucepan.
Mix well and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until mixture comes to a boil and is thick.
Remove from heat and chill.
Add sugar, salt, margarine, vanilla, milk and the rest.
Mix well. Pour into greased casserole dish.
Mix jello and hot water; add cold water and freeze until thickens.
Set aside 1/2 cup jello.
Mix ice cream with 1/2 cup jello.
Then top with other mixture and chill!
Saute squash, green pepper and onion in oil until tender, but do not brown.
Add jalapeno peppers and place in buttered 3-quart dish.
Spread soup over top and sprinkle with cheddar cheese. Combine cracker crumbs and butter.
Spread over cheese.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Chop onion.
In separate bowls, grate cheeses.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add soup and olives.
Salt and pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Empty enchilada sauce into shallow dish.
Melt shortening and fry tortillas until soft.
Dip tortillas into enchilada sauce and place in baking dish.
Fill tortillas with meat mixture, onion and Jack cheese.
Fold, packing side by side.
Pour remainder of enchilada sauce over folded enchiladas and top with Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Can be frozen.
In
large
saucepan add all ingredients except vanilla. Stir over
a
low
heat until sugar dissolves.
Gradually increase heat to a rolling boil.
Boil for 1 minute, remove from heat and
add vanilla.
Set
pan in cold water and stir until thick pouring consistency.
Pour over cake and set aside until frosting resembles fudge.
Mix first eight ingredients and bake at 350° until done; makes 5 layers.
Cook sugar, syrup, water and salt until it will spin a good thread.
Pour half of mixture over stiffly beaten egg whites to which baking powder has been added.
Beat until mixture loses its gloss.
Add remaining syrup mixture and again.
Add chopped nuts, vanilla and cherries.
Mix and spread on cake layers.
Cream sugars, margarine, vanilla and eggs until fluffy.
Add milk with vinegar and beat.
Beat in flour.
Add cocoa and soda to boiling water and blend in slowly.
Pour into two 9-inch layer cake pans.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Cook vegetables according to package directions; drain.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Saute onion in a little butter.
Prepare gravy mix according to package.
Mix crawfish, potatoes, vegetables and onions together with gravy.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Cover top with second pie crust.
Cut a few slits in top of crust.
Flute edges.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Let sit for 5 minutes.
1. Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, butter and cheese into a dough with your hands.
Shred cabbage into glass bowl.
Stir in salt and ice cubes. Cover.
Let stand 1 hour.
After hour, squeeze out cabbage and put into glass or enameled container.
Add carrot, pepper and onion. In a saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar, water, celery and mustard seed.
Let come to boil, remove from heat.
Let cool.
Pour over vegetables.
Mix and put into freezer container.
Will keep as long as 1 year.
Yield depends on size of cabbage.
(This is a good way to use up garden cabbage.)
Let thaw in refrigerator.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente, tender but somewhat firm to the bite.
Drain and set aside. Meanwhile, cook chard or kale, using just the rinse water clinging to the leaves, in large skillet, covered, for 1 minute or just until wilted.
Drain and set aside.
Dry skillet.
Heat oil in same skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion; saute 1 minute. Add garlic; saute 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, wine, salt, black pepper and pepper flakes.
Simmer, stirring often, for 5 minutes, or until tomatoes are softened.
Stir greens and lemon juice into skillet.
Gently stir in shrimp.
Simmer 3 to 5 minutes, or until shrimp turn pink.
Serve over pasta.
Makes 6 servings.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Cut butter and cream cheese into 1-inch slices; place in bowl of food processor.
Add sugar and process until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Add eggs, vanilla and orange peel; process until blended. Add flour and baking powder; process until blended.
Stir in mini chocolate chips.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, or until cake pulls away from sides of pan.
Cool 10 minutes; remove from pan to wire racks.
Cool completely; sprinkle confectioners sugar over cake.

Preheat oven to 450°. Line roasting pan with aluminum foil. Core and cut apples into quarters. Cut sweet potatoes into 6 to 8 large pieces. Cut onions into small wedges. Combine apples, vegetables, olive oil and garlic. Roast in prepared pan 40 to 45 minutes or until sweet potatoes are tender. Sprinkle with balsamic vinegar before serving. Serve hot or cold. Makes 6 servings.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt.
Add vegetable shortening, grated orange peel, 2/3 cup liquid.
Mix in mixer on slow to medium speed for 2 minutes.
Scrape sides frequently.
Add remaining 1/3 cup liquid, eggs.
Continue beating 2 more minutes.
Pour batter into greased and floured pans.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Frost with 7 Minute Frosting.
Sprinkle each frosted layer with grated rind and chopped pecans.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add frozen strawberries. Just as it begins to thicken, fold in two-thirds of the container of whipped topping.
Add cake pieces and fold together until well coated.
Pour into angel food pan (tube pan) and put in refrigerator to set.
Unmold on cake plate and ice with remaining whipped topping tinted a pale pink.
Decorate with fresh strawberries and mint leaves, if desired.
Serves 12 to 14.
Heat oil in a large pot.
Add minced garlic, sliced ginger and chopped onion.
Cook until onion is wilted.
Add whole pork chops and cook until brown.
Pour in water and oyster sauce; simmer until pork chops are tender.
Chop cabbage and watercress into 2 to 3-inch pieces.
Add stems of cabbage and cook 5 minutes at slow boil.
Add remainder of cabbage and watercress.
Simmer until soft.
Season with pepper.
Add tofu cut into cubes and turn off fire.
Bake and cool cake as directed on package.
Pour boiling water on jello and dissolve.
Refrigerate jello until thick, but not set.
Add enough cold water to lemonade to make 2 cups.
Stir lemonade into jello.
Beat until foamy.
Fold Cool Whip into jello mixture.
Heat oil in heavy large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, bell pepper and garlic; saute until onion is tender, about 10 minutes.
Mix in tomatoes with their juices, chilies and thyme. Reduce heat to low and simmer until vegetables are very soft, about 10 minutes.
Add beans and 2 cups chicken broth.
Puree soup in batches in processor or blender until smooth. Return soup to pot.
(Can be prepared 4 days ahead.
Cover and refrigerate.) Bring soup to simmer. Thin with more broth if necessary. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Garnish with sour cream and sliced green onions.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cook noodles.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces and stir into noodles.
Add sugar to eggs and beat.
Add milk and mix well. Add melted margarine and vanilla.
Add to drained noodles and pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Can top with cinnamon, sugar and chopped nuts (optional).
Beat egg yolks and sugar.
Add bread crumbs, Cream of Wheat, baking powder and nuts.
Mix well.
Fold in egg whites.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool and break the cake into chunks.
Mound layers with whipped cream in between and on top, forming in the shape of a mountain.
Dribble toppings over top.
May garnish with cherries or strawberries.
Coat chicken breasts with 1/2 cup flour, salt and pepper. Place in preheated skillet with oil covering bottom of skillet. Brown both sides, drain oil.
Add 3 tablespoons butter or margarine.
Sprinkle both sides of breasts with basil and rosemary. Saute both sides for 1/2 minute.
Add wine and saute for 1 minute. Add brown gravy.
Place in preheated oven at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove chicken onto serving dish, mix remainder of ingredients left in pan, heat and pour over breasts on serving dish.

Cut up each apple to make 8 long slices for a total of 16 slices. Cook in a boiler the margarine and sugar until dissolved and add vanilla flavoring. Roll 1 slice of apple in each crescent roll. Place in an 11 x 13-inch pan all 16 rolls with apples. Cover them with butter and sugar mixture. Then add Mountain Dew over all the mixture. Cover with foil and bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes. Take foil off and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until rolls begin to brown. Serve with Cool Whip or ice cream.
Mix zucchini with salt and let stand 1 hour.
Squeeze out moisture.
Beat eggs; add zucchini, cheese, mint, flour and pepper to taste.
Shape and fry in butter over medium heat, 1 tablespoon at a time.
Brown both sides.
Makes 18, or 6 servings.
Cream together shortening and sugar.
Add vanilla and eggs; beat well.
Sift together flour and soda.
Add to mixture; mix well.
Add rolled oats and peanuts; mix well.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Put dates, sugar and shortening into a bowl; over this pour boiling water.
Let cool.
Sift flour with other dry ingredients; add nuts and mix well.
Pour the first mixture into the flour and mix until free of lumps.
Add beaten egg.
Pour into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 325° for about 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Petit Pois Frais A La Francaise(Julia Child'S Green Peas, French-Style)
d: Put all ingredients except lettuce into a 3-quart saucepan; top with lettuce.
Cover pan tightly and bring to a boil over moderately high heat.
Reduce heat and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until peas are tender, stirring once or twice.
Add extra water if pan is dry.
If too liquidy, transfer peas to dish and boil liquid until about 1/3 cup remains.
Pour over peas and serve.
Mix all together; save egg whites.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 300° until firm (about 1 hour).
Beat egg whites and add 2 tablespoons sugar for each egg white.
Add 1/4 teaspoon vanilla.
Bake until brown.
Take the
boned,
skinned and flattened chicken breasts and cut each in
half.
Mix
rice, celery, green pepper, parsley, pimento,
seasonings
and
sour cream together.
Sprinkle chicken breasts lightly
with
salt
and
pepper.
Place
1/2 tablespoon cold butter
and
tablespoons
rice
mixture
in center of each chicken
breast
half.
Fold
each breast over filling in envelope
fashion, folded narrow way first and then the
long way.
Fasten
with toothpicks.
Beat egg and cream. Roll
folded breasts in flour, then in egg-cream mixture, then in
crumbs. Allow
to
stand 10 minutes before frying in deep hot fat (360°) for 15 minutes.
Remove toothpicks.
Serve with Quick Sour Cream Sauce (see recipe below).
Makes 6 servings.
Skin chicken.
If wings are used, it is too hard to skin them. Wash and drain.
Prepare crumb mixture from the flour, Italian bread crumbs and corn flake crumbs in pot or bowl.
Pour evaporated milk into bowl.
Dip pieces of chicken in milk, then turn them over in crumbs.
Place in large baking pan.
Put into a 425° oven for 1/2 hour or until light tan.
In the last half, put on top shelf to brown.
Do not burn.
Take chicken out.
Mix above ingredients
except 1/2 cup beef broth (I use bouillon cubes).
Place mixture in loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
You
may use 1/2 cup broth as needed if meat becomes too dry.
Prick potatoes with fork.
Place in microwave-safe pan and microwave on High for 4 to 5 minutes or until fork-tender.
Cool enough to handle.
Hollow out each potato with spoon leaving a sturdy shell.
Puree cottage cheese in food processor until smooth.
Put in small bowl and stir in horseradish, chives, dill and black pepper.
Spoon into potato shells.
Serve warm or chilled.
Mix the
tuna, eggs,
cheese, onions,
pickle,
green pepper, mayonnaise, salt
and pepper together and put on split buns.
Place on a cookie sheet and broil until cheese melts.
In a skillet, add first 4 ingredients and cook on medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add to chicken the 2 cans of vegetables and cornstarch mixture.
Return to heat and heat until mixture thickens.
Drain crabmeat and squeeze lemon juice over.
Mix together crabmeat and cocktail sauce.
Pour over cream cheese.
Serve with Town House crackers.
Brown meat in heavy skillet.
Add onion, tomatoes, ketchup, sauce, green pepper and parsley.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Cook macaroni according to directions.
Combine macaroni and beef mixture in a casserole.
Season to taste.
Spoon (gently) mushroom soup into mixture, lifting from bottom.
Sprinkle grated cheese over top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
(This freezes well.)
Will make 2 medium size casseroles.
Mix cream cheese with salt, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Then add pineapple, sliced bananas, nuts and cherries.
Whip whipping cream and fold into mixture.
Pour into pan and freeze firmly. When frozen, slice and serve on lettuce leaves.
Serves 10.
Beat eggs until thick, about 3 minutes.
Continue beating and add sugar, salt, corn syrup, butter and vanilla.
Stir in coconut, oats and chocolate chips.
Pour into prepared pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes.
(Pie will be very dark.)
Cool completely before serving (leave the house if neccessary).
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
This comes from the California and Hawaii Sugar Company.
In an 8-inch square baking dish, combine the garlic and oil. Microwave on High for 1 minute.
Add the broth and paprika. Microwave on High for 1 minute.
Add shrimp and lemon juice. Toss to combine.
Cover with waxed paper and microwave on High for 1 minute.
Sift together all the dry ingredients.
Beat the eggs, sugar, oil and vanilla together.
Beat in the dry ingredients.
Stir in the grated squash.
Pour into a greased 8 x 8-inch pan.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for approximately 45 minutes.
Butter a large roasting pan.
Sprinkle raw rice in pan, then add nuts and chicken.
Heat all liquids and pour over chicken. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in a 275° oven for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, undisturbed and uncovered.
Saute onion and garlic in butter.
Add flour.
Blend in.
Add oyster liquid, chicken broth, artichokes and milk.
Season to taste.
I use Tony's.
Simmer (do not boil) for 10 minutes.
Add oysters, chopped green onions and parsley before serving.
Simmer 5 minutes.
If too thick, add a little hot water or thicken with a little cornstarch and water.
Mix first 6 ingredients until light.
Place vanilla wafer in cupcake papers.
Fill 3/4 full of cheese and bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Cool.
Top with pie filling.
Makes 24.
Roll beef cubes in flour; brown in shortening.
Add onion and brown.
Add mushrooms, water and spices.
Cover and simmer over low heat about 1 3/4 hours or until meat is tender.
Stir occasionally. While cooking stir in sour cream and heat through.
Serve over noodles.
Serves 6 to 8 people.
Mix the sugar, vinegar, hot water, salt and salad oil, then add the beans, celery and onions.
Chill.
Arrange cabbage in pot.
Place potatoes on top.
Add water and seasonings; cook until tender.
Cut sausage in pieces and cook 10 minutes longer.
Arrange on platter and serve.
Line the bottom of baked pie crust with the strawberries (fresh ones); mash the frozen strawberries.
Add enough water to make 2 cups.
Add sugar and cornstarch and cook until thick.
Dissolve gelatin in 1/4 cup cold water.
Add to hot mixture food coloring. Pour over the strawberries.
Be sure the glaze is cool before pouring on berries in crust.
Chill in refrigerator.
Top with sweetened whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Fry bacon in skillet, save drippings.
Mix egg and milk together.
Dip pork chops in flour, then egg mixture, then bread crumbs.
Brown pork chops in bacon drippings.
Pour half of the 1/2 pint of whipping cream over pork chops.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Remove pork chops and add remaining half and half to pan.
Heat to a boil; add bacon (crumbled) into sauce.
Pour sauce over noodles.
Pour 1/2 cup melted oleo into large baking pan.
Add popped corn and nuts.
Combine remaining oleo, sugar, syrup, vanilla and salt in a large pot and boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Continue boiling 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in baking soda.
Pour over corn mixture.
Mix lightly.
Bake at 250° for 1 hour and 30 minutes (STIRRING EVERY 15 MINUTES).
Makes about 7 quarts.
Cream butter and cheese.
Gradually add flour, mixing to make a soft dough.
Shape into smooth rounds and chill for an hour. Combine dates, sugar and water in saucepan (can add chopped nuts, if you want to).
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until soft (about 5 minutes).
Cool.
Roll chilled dough (take out of refrigerator a little at a time) on floured surface.
Cut into a small round.
Place a teaspoon of date mixture on half of rounds. Fold and seal edges with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes or until light golden brown.
May freeze.
In a large bowl, combine the undrained pineapple chunks, walnut halves, orange juice and ginger.
Stir to mix well.
Add the strawberry halves, blueberries and coconut.
Toss gently to coat the fruit with juice.
Makes 4 servings.
Heat oven to 400°.
In saucepan, heat water and butter to rolling boil.
Stir in flour.
Stir vigorously over low heat until mixture forms a ball, about 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Beat in eggs, all at once, until smooth and glossy.
Drop dough by slightly rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet.
Bake about 25 minutes or until puffed, golden brown and dry.
Remove puffs to wire rack; cool away from draft.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Cool until slightly thickened.
Beat to consistency of whipped cream.
Add flavoring to whipped cream and fold into jello.
Add macaroons, nuts and salt.
Chill until firm.
Cook potatoes in boiling salted water until tender.
Drain potatoes and leave over medium heat until excess moisture evaporates (approximately 1 minute); remove from heat.
Add 5 tablespoons butter and mash well.
Add milk until reaches desired consistency.
Season with salt and pepper.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in large skillet.
Add half of mushrooms; saut until beginning to soften (approximately 3 minutes).
Add remaining mushrooms and shallots.
Saut until juices evaporate and mushrooms brown (approximately 12 minutes); season with salt and pepper.
Mix 2/3 of mushrooms into potatoes.
Put in bowl and top with remaining mushrooms.
Sprinkle with chives.
Yield:
8 servings.
Warm cheese and butter slightly.
Add dill, onion, sugar, soda, salt and eggs.
Beat until blended.
Combine water and yeast; stir until blended.
Stir into cheese mixture.
Add flour. Knead.
Let rise.
Shape into 2 (8 x 4-inch) loaves.
Rise to top of pan.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Makes 2 loaves.
Mix butter, shallot, garlic, parsley, cheese and pepper until well blended. Twist off mushroom stems. Evenly spoon butter mixture into mushroom caps.
Place mushrooms on a rack in a broiler pan about 6-inches below heat.
Cook until butter is melted and mushrooms begin to shrivel slightly (about 5 minutes). Serve on bread slices to absorb buttery juices.
In medium skillet combine brown sugar, Crisco, half and half, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture boils.
Boil and stir for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add sliced bananas, stirring gently to coat.
Cook over low heat for 2 minutes or until soft, stirring occasionally.
Stir in brandy.
Serve over ice cream.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Spread dough onto pizza or cookie sheet.
Bake according to directions.
Mix cream
cheese
and
mayonnaise
with Hidden Valley dressing.
Spread
on dough.
Chop cauliflower, broccoli and peppers.
Spread vegetables over cream cheese generously.
Mix egg, vanilla and sugar.
Add flour and baking powder. Scald milk and margarine together and add to other mixture.
Pour in petit four pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
While hot, spread peanut butter.
Let cool good.
Melt chocolate in double boiler and spread on cold cake.
Enjoy.
Mix sugar, molasses, vinegar and butter in saucepan.
Cook, stirring, until sugar dissolves.
Continue to cook without stirring until syrup forms a brittle ball in cold water.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla, stirring only enough to mix it through the hot syrup.
Have corn and peanuts mixed well in a large bowl. Pour cooked syrup slowly over corn, mixing well.
Wet hands slightly and shape corn into balls.
Makes 12 balls.
Combine dry ingredients.
Combine wet ingredients.
Fold quickly wet and dry ingredients just until flour is moistened. Gently mix in blueberries.
Spoon into greased muffin tins.
Bake at 400° for about 20 minutes.
Makes 1 dozen large muffins.
Beat cream cheese, butter, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well.
Combine 2 cups flour, baking powder and salt.
Gradually add flour mixture to butter mixture. Mix remaining flour with cranberries and nuts.
Fold into batter; batter will be very thick.
Spoon into greased 10-inch pan and bake at 350° for 65 to 70 minutes or until inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Let stand 5 minutes before removing from pan. Cool on rack.
Dust powdered sugar on each slice before serving.
Mix together softened cheeses.
Add seasonings and about 1/2 cup of crushed stuffing mix.
Mix well.
Form into a ball or several smaller balls as per choice.
Roll in additional stuffing mix.
Wrap in wax paper and refrigerate until serving time.

recipes.t: Green Beans With Zucchini And Bacon
d: About 30 minutes before serving, prepare green beans as label directs but cook only half as long as directed; drain.
In 12-inch skillet over medium heat, fry bacon until crisp; drain and crumble. Set aside.
Pour fat from skillet; wipe skillet clean with paper towels.
To skillet, add butter or margarine and onion; cook until onion is tender, about 3 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add zucchini and cook, stirring quickly and frequently, until just tender-crisp, about 4 minutes.
Stir in crumbled bacon, green beans, salt and pepper and cook about 1 minute longer or until beans are hot.
Makes 6 servings.
Beat together eggs, half and half, salt and pepper.
Toss together meat, cheese and flour.
Add to egg mixture.
Pour into crust.
Bake pie on cookie sheet in 400° oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until knife inserted between center and edge comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before serving.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cream the butter, sugar, eggs, lemon juice and rind. Add vanilla. Add in raisins and pecans.
Add flour, one cup at a time, sifted with salt and baking powder.
Pour into greased and floured Bundt pan. Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 50 minutes.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Cool to touch, then crumble.
Saute zucchini in small amount of light olive oil, along with the sliced onion.
When zucchini is tender, add crumbled bacon to skillet and mix with zucchini and onion.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Cover skillet and cook over low heat until cheese melts.
Delicious!
Cook cake by directions.
While hot, pour condensed milk on top of cake; let cool.
Then layer with cherry pie filling, Cool Whip and coconut.
Keep in refrigerator.
Cut up lettuce, broccoli, cauliflower and onions into large bowl for first layer.
Sprinkle on top of first layer the bacon bits, frozen peas and grated Cheddar cheese for second layer. Cover all with Miracle Whip and sugar on top.
Chill 6 hours at least.
Toss before serving.
Yields 12 servings.
Stir chocolate, Krispies and coconut together.
Drop spoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Quickly stick "legs" into sides; add eyes. Refrigerate until set, about 15 minutes.
Saute onions and remove.
Cook sausage and crumble.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Bake pie shell 5 minutes at 450° and sprinkle bottom of pie shell after removing from oven with 2 1/2 tablespoons of Parmesan cheese.
Layer broccoli, onions, Swiss cheese and sausage in pie shell.
Mix remaining ingredients and pour over this.
Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake 10 minutes at 450° and then 30 minutes at 350°.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.t: Cabbage With Corn Flake Topping(Serves 8 People)
d: Mix and heat the first 5 ingredients.
Take corn flakes and melted margarine; toss.
Put half into large casserole, alternating cabbage and sauce.
Top with Cheddar cheese.
Add remaining corn flake mixture.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Generously butter a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mix first six ingredients well in a medium bowl.
In a small bowl, blend egg and milk with applesauce, honey and butter.
Pour over dry ingredients; mix with fork just until moistened.
Cook the hamburger and Italian sausage on high and drain.
Add the tomatoes, garlic, parsley and basil. Simmer 1/2 hour.
Cook potatoes in salted, boiling water until tender.
Remove from water, cool and grate coarsely.
Combine and add sour cream, grated cheese, onion, milk, salt and pepper and mix well.
Place in a well-greased baking pan.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter and add bread crumbs.
Mix well and scatter on top of potatoes.
Bake, uncovered, at 300° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Drain corn and beans.
Mix well.
Chill for 24 hours.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix melted margarine, flour and soup mix.
Dip chicken in mixture and then roll in crushed cornflakes. Put in pan and bake 55 to 60 minutes or until brown.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown hamburger and chopped onion in skillet.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Add rice, cream of celery soup, water and soy sauce to hamburger.
Mix well.
Cover skillet or transfer food to a baking dish and bake one hour.
Put in bowl to have ready the chocolate chips, German chocolate, Marshmallow Fluff, vanilla and nuts.
Mix together in large pot the sugar, butter and canned milk.
Bring to full boil. Stirring constantly, boil for 10 minutes; turn off heat.
Quickly put bowl mixture into pot and mix well.
Line pan in oil.
Pour and let cool, then refrigerate.
Dissolve strawberry Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Add pineapple with Jell-O.
Chill until firm.
Combine remaining ingredients except water and lime Jell-O.
Spread on firm jello and pineapple.
Refrigerate overnight.
Dissolve lime Jell-O in 2 cups boiling water.
Cool.
Pour over mixture.
Chill until firm.
Beat eggs, salt, paprika, mustard and milk together.
Add meat and pour over bread cubes in a greased pan.
Sprinkle cheese over the top.
Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes, covered.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes more.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
Serves 12 to 15, depending on the size of serving.
Mix the soup, sour cream and wine.
Pour over breasts placed in flat baking dish.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for over 1 hour.
Empty cheese soup into top of a double boiler; add cheese pieces.
Heat over hot water until well blended.
Brown ground beef and drain off fat.
Saute onions and pepper in a small amount of butter.
Add to cheese mixture.
Add all other ingredients. Keep warm over hot water until ready to serve.
Serve with taco chips.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle nuts evenly into pan. Place frozen rolls in pan (4 per row).
Sprinkle pudding mix on top of rolls.
Melt butter or margarine.
Add brown sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle over rolls.
Put a wet towel over pan and let rise overnight.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Dip chicken in batter of yogurt, egg, oil and thyme.
Fully cover all sides.
Dip chicken in bread crumbs (all sides).
Bake at 350° about 1 1/2 hours or until browned.
Tastes like fried chicken.
Serves 4.
Beat cream cheese.
Add sugar, salt and flour.
Mix well.
Add 1 egg at a time, beating after each addition.
Add sour cream, lemon juice and vanilla.
Blend well.
Pour into ungreased 10-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes on center shelf of oven.
Turn off oven.
Open and let stand for 1 hour.
Cool completely.
In glass baking dish arrange salmon.
Top with onion, bouillon, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, dill weed, 1/2 teaspoon salt and the water.
Cover with Handi-Wrap and microwave on High for 10 minutes.
Melt butter and blend in flour and salt.
Blend in cream and mix until smooth.
Add juice from fish; stir in 2 tablespoons lemon juice and pour over fish.
Microwave 3 minutes until mixture boils or until done (time varies with thickness of steaks).
Garnish with sprigs of parsley.
Serves 4.

recipes.t: Barley, Corn And Avocado Salad(Makes 4 Servings)
d: In a small bowl, whisk together vinegar and olive, salt and pepper.
Set aside.
In a medium saucepan, over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp, about 8 minutes.
With a slotted spoon, transfer the bacon to paper towels to drain.
Discard fat from the saucepan, add barley, salt and 2 cups of water to pan; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and maintain a simmer until barley is tender. Drain and press out excess moisture.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Add corn, red onions, bacon, and dressing.
Toss thoroughly.
Add tomatoes and avocados and toss gently.
(Let salad stand at room temperature before serving if it has been refrigerated.)

recipes.t: I Want To Live Again Twice Baked Potatoes
d: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Wash potatoes well.
Cut two small slits in each potato, then cook all at once in microwave on High for 7 minutes.
Bake potatoes in preheated oven for 30 minutes. Remove from oven and let stand for 15 minutes.
Cut potatoes in half and scoop out insides, leaving a thin shell.
In a mixing bowl, combine potato insides, cream cheese, butter, salt and pepper, milk and chives.
Mash until smooth.
Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Return potatoes to oven and bake, uncovered, until golden brown, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Top with cheddar cheese.
Cook shells according to package.
Rinse under cold water. Invert on towel to cool.
Put tuna in a bowl.
Add cheese, mayo, celery and onion.
Add pimento.
If too dry, add more mayo.
Stuff shells; cover and refrigerate until chilled.
Garnish if desired.
Mix flour, seasoning salt and pepper and pound into sides of meat.
(I prefer it cut into serving size pieces.)
Brown onion in 2 tablespoons shortening in heavy skillet or Dutch oven.
Remove; drain on paper toweling and set aside.
Add remaining shortening to skillet and brown meat slowly on both sides.
Add remaining ingredients; cover tightly and bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Uncover and add browned onion; cover again and cook until tender, about 1 hour more.
Skim sauce to remove excess fat.
If sauce seems too thick, thin to desired consistency. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine all vegetables in a 10-quart pot.
Add salt and pepper.
Cook until half done.
Add hamburger meat and tomato sauce.
Cover; cook on low heat.
Stir occasionally until done. Makes approximately 10 quarts.
Butter an 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan or a 7 x 11 x 2-inch pan; put sugar, milk and butter in frying pan.
Turn up to 280°.
Mix until starting to boil.
Continue stirring while boiling for 5 minutes. Mixture will turn brownish.
Turn off frying pan.
Add rest of ingredients quickly.
Mix together until well blended and mixture sugars.
Pour into pan, scraping frying pan well.
Allow to cool. Cut into 16 to 25 pieces.
Savor those crumbs, too!
Set cooked rice aside. Boil peppers in salt water for 5 minutes.
Drain.
Saute ground beef and onion.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in 1/4 cup water.
Add to meat mixture.
Mix rice and tomatoes and add to meat mixture. Mix rice and tomatoes and add to meat.
Stir thoroughly and stuff mixture into green peppers. Place peppers in greased baking dish.
Microwave cream cheese on medium for 30 seconds.
Mix cream cheese and salad dressing, Swiss cheese and onions until well blended.
Spoon into a 2 1/2 cups casserole dish.
Microwave on High for 4 minutes or until well heated, turning every 2 minutes and sprinkle with crumbled bacon.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Chicken Wings(Messy But Good!)
d: Break wings into thirds and discard tips.
Combine beaten egg and water; set aside.
Combine 1/2 teaspoon salt, flour and cornstarch in a large Ziploc bag.
Dip each piece of wing into egg/water mixture, then into Ziploc bag with flour mixture; coat evenly.
Brown in hot oil and let drain on paper towel.
Place browned chicken into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Combine sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, vinegar, broth, catsup and soy sauce in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Pour over chicken wings.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes, basting every 20 minutes.
Sauce will thicken during the final 15 minutes.
Marinate chicken in white wine and diced garlic clove.
Mix cream of mushroom soup and sour cream together.
Spray pan with nonstick spray.
Place chicken in pan.
Pour soup mixture over chicken.
Bake 45 minutes or until chicken is cooked through. Pour remaining sauce over baked potato or wild rice.
M-m-m good!
Brown beef and onion. Stir in salt and pepper, soup and corn; bring to boil. Pour into 8-inch dish. Put biscuits on top. Bake at 450° for 15 to 20 minutes or until biscuits are brown.

Divide cauliflower into separate flowerets. Parboil 8 minutes or until almost tender. Mix cauliflower with crumbs; add ham, cheese and green pepper. Place in casserole. Spread sour cream over top and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake 10 to 15 minutes or until heated through. Sprinkle with paprika.
Take water, vinegar, sugar, celery seed and turmeric and boil for 10 minutes.
Put in jars, seal and process 10 minutes.
Combine eggs, bread crumbs, parsley and garlic.
Stir in corned beef; mix well.
On foil or waxed paper, pat meat mixture to a 10 x 10-inch square.
Combine sauerkraut, caraway and shredded cheese; mound in center of meat mixture.
Wrap meat mixture around and over sauerkraut mixture, forming a loaf (be sure ends and seams are completely sealed).
Place loaf in greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Top with cheese triangles; bake for 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted.
In small bowl, stir together sugar and spices.
Stir into coffee.
Into each of 6 mugs, pour 1 cup coffee and a generous tablespoon warm milk; stir.
Sprinkle with an additional dash of ground cinnamon, if desired.
Pound chicken breasts to make thinner.
Brown in olive oil. Add onions, garlic, pepper and chutney.
Cover and cook until chicken is done, 3 to 5 minutes.
Uncover; add cream and cook a little more until sauce thickens.
Serves 2 or 3.
Melt butter; add vinegar, catsup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, lemon juice, onion, salt and pepper.
Mix well and pour over meat.
In bowl, crumble (thawed) potato patties with fork.
Add onion, soup and sour cream.
Pour ingredients into glass pie dish. Top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, uncovered. Makes 4 small servings, with a little leftover for the dog.
Can prepare and refrigerate the night before to be cooked the following day.
Put fish in baking dish.
Cover with butter, salt and pepper. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix soup and sour cream together. Cover fish with this mixture. Return to oven and bake 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine dry ingredients for bottom layer; cook for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Combine eggs, lemon juice and almond extract; pour over bottom layer.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes; while warm, sprinkle with 3 tablespoons of confectioners sugar.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Use a 9-inch square pan.
Place chicken in oblong pan (ungreased).
Mix all ingredients except lemon slices.
Pour over chicken.
Cook, uncovered, in a 375° oven.
Occasionally spoon the oil mixture over chicken.
Cook 30 minutes.
Turn; continue in the same manner another 30 minutes, or until thickest part of chicken is cooked.
Garnish with lemon slices.
Make jello according to package directions and let start to set.
Drain crushed pineapple.
Fold all ingredients into jello, whipped cream last.
Unmold on a bed of curly endive lettuce to look like a Christmas wreath.
Decorate with extra sliced stuffed olives.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In large saucepan or large skillet, brown ground beef.
Drain.
Add taco seasoning, garlic, cayenne pepper and water.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Set aside.
Spray 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam.
Place 6 tortillas in bottom of pan, overlapping and extending up sides slightly.
Layer 1 cup salsa, 1/2 meat mixture, 1/2 cup green onions, 1 cup sour cream mixture and 2 cups combined cheeses.
Repeat again, starting with tortillas.
Top with 6 tortillas and remaining salsa.
Bake 30 minutes.
Remove.
Add remaining cheese.
Bake 10 more minutes or until cheese melts.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Mix together Cool Whip, jello and cottage cheese.
Fold in oranges and pineapple.
Put in shallow dish.
Chill for at least 2 hours before serving.
Saute onion in oil in large frying pan on medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped mushrooms and garlic and saute 10 minutes longer.
Stir the cottage cheese into the mushroom mixture.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix until well blended.
Spoon into a well-greased (spray) 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Bake at 375° for 50 to 55 minutes or until set.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Slice eggplant; peel if very large.
Stir seasonings into sauce.
Layer eggplant, sauce and grated cheese.
Repeat.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until bubbly.

recipes.t: Susan'S Old Fashion Apple Stack Cake
d: Cream butter and sugar together.
Add eggs and sorghum and mix well.
Add soda to buttermilk.
Mix dry ingredients together. Add alternately with batter, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Bake in thin layers about 1/2-inch thick in either 9-inch pans or old fashion black griddle.
Bake at 350° for about 12 minutes.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
Brown hamburger or steak with mushrooms and onion; drain.
Lower heat and add ketchup, sour cream, soup and Worcestershire sauce.
Let simmer for 15 minutes and add noodles.
Fry sausage and drain.
Melt cheese in butter.
Combine sausage and cheese.
Add all other ingredients.
Spread on party rye bread.
Freeze on cookie sheets, then put in plastic bags and keep in freezer until ready to serve.
Cook at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Peel, core and slice apples.
Combine sugar and cinnamon. Toss apples in sugar mixture.
Put apples into 8 x 8-inch pan. Add any excess sugar mixture.
Pour dry cake mix over apples and pack tightly.
Cut 1 stick margarine into pieces and place over top of dry mix.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Mexican Chickena Delightful Variation Of King Ranch Chicken
d: Cook chicken and debone it.
Grate cheese.
In sauce pan, heat soups and chilies.
Tear tortillas in quarters.
Layer tortillas, chicken, sauce, and cheese.
If you like, put 1/2 cup of broth to soup.
Bake at 350° F. for 45 to 50 minutes.
Saute onions and olive oil in large skillet.
Add chicken and brown slightly on both sides.
Then pour spaghetti sauce, wine or beer, garlic, salt and pepper into skillet.
Mix well.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve over pasta of choice.
Blend sugar,
honey
and water in a pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring
frequently,
about
12 minutes or to soft ball (250° on candy thermometer).
Add sesame seed.
Spread on 8 x 8-inch buttered
pan, 3/4-inch thickness. When cool, cut into 2 x 1-inch pieces.
Saute onion in margarine until tender.
Stir in flour until smooth and remove from heat.
Combine salad dressing, turkey, cooked noodles, peas, pepper and oregano. Stir in onion mixture. Pour into shallow 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Mix bread crumbs and margarine.
Sprinkle over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes. Garnish top with tomato wedges, if desired.
Makes 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Mix and sift dry ingredients into a mixing bowl.
Cut in the shortening until crumbly.
Add the egg, mixing well.
Press half of the mixture into a greased 8-inch square pan.
Spread with the applesauce and lightly press the remaining dough mixture over the sauce.
Sprinkle with the brown sugar.
Bake 45 minutes, then turn off oven; open oven door a little and let cake sit another 30 minutes.
Cut into bars while warm.
Serve with whipped cream or ice cream, if desired. Favorite spices may be added to the applesauce as well.
Serves 8.
Cook rice; set aside and brown hamburger and onion and drain off fat.
Combine hamburger, onion, rice and rest of ingredients. Heat and blend.
Serve with cornbread.
Mix first three ingredients thoroughly; add remaining ingredients and mix.
Garnish with leftover mandarin oranges and cherry halves.
Chill about 6 hours before serving.
Grate carrot and zucchini.
Slice scallions.
Combine flour, baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Beat together egg, milk, carrot, zucchini and scallion.
Stir wet ingredients into dry, just until combined.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Pour batter by tablespoonfuls into pan, making a few pancakes at a time.
Cook until golden, about 2 minutes on each side.
Add remaining oil to pan as needed.
Saute shallots and mushrooms in a small amount of butter in skillet for 5 minutes.
Stir in next 6 ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Blend cornstarch with a small amount of water.
Stir into mixture.
Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Season to taste. Yields 4 servings.
Heat butter in saucepan.
Blend in flour, salt, pepper and thyme.
Cook over low heat until bubbly, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in chicken broth and milk, whisking vigorously to blend.
Return to heat and cook and stir until sauce is smooth and thickened.
Add cubed chicken, sauteed mushrooms and parsley. Taste and correct seasoning.
Add sherry just before serving and heat through.
Place about 1/3 cup chicken
mixture in center of each cooked crepe and roll up.
Garnish with small amount of filling and sprinkle of parsley.
Brown ground beef in skillet.
Stir in seasonings, soup and three soup cans of water.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in noodles. Cook until noodles are done.
Combine cranberries and sugar in a 1 1/2-quart casserole. Microwave at Medium 12 to 13 minutes, stirring once. Stir in brandy and walnuts. Cool. Cover and chill 2 to 3 hours. Makes 2 1/2 cups.
Put salt in boiling water.
Add cauliflower.
Cook until tender (15 to 20 minutes), turning to cook uniformly.
Remove to serving dish.
Melt butter.
Add other ingredients.
Mix.
Pour over cooked cauliflower.
Sift flour once before measuring.
Cream shortening; add sugar, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
Add some dry ingredients to shortening and sugar mixture.
Mix water and molasses and add alternately with the flour.
Roll into 1-inch balls.
Brush tops with water and bake.
Frost or roll in powdered sugar.
Flatten breast with cleaver, salt and pepper.
Place 1/2 slice cheese and 1/2 slice of ham on 1/2 chicken piece.
Fold other half over and seal with toothpick.
Dip each in flour, then egg and crumbs.
Saute in melted margarine over medium flame until golden brown.
Continue to cook on low flame until done.
6 servings.
Pour apricots and juice in baking dish, cut side down.
Top with brown sugar and cracker crumbs; dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Prepare tuna, onions and celery; mix together in a large bowl. Over low heat, warm tomato soup and cream cheese until cheese melts.
(Can use a mixer to help blend.)
Remove from heat.
Mix gelatin and water; add to soup mixture and stir well.
Add mayonnaise to soup mixture; stir well.
Pour into bowl with tuna, onions and celery, mixing well.
Pour into mold which has been sprayed with Pam.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours.
In a 3-quart saucepan, stir both soups and corn.
Gradually stir in milk and water.
Add turkey.
Over medium heat, heat to simmering, stirring occasionally.
Cook 10 minutes.
Garnish with tomatoes.
Makes 6 cups or 6 servings.
Microwave margarine, mushrooms and onion for 2 minutes.
Place 1/2 cheese in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Top with mushroom-onion mixture; add ham and remaining cheese.
Mix eggs, milk, flour and seasonings.
(May have to use mixer to mix in flour.)
Pour egg mixture over ingredients in dish.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°. Makes 10 servings.
Brown ground turkey in a large skillet.
Mix in salsa and beans.
Simmer.
Heat oven to 350°.
Roll out pizza crust in rectangle.
Put half the cheese in middle of crust.
Put meat mixture over cheese.
Put the rest of cheese on top.
Brush milk on outside edges of crust and fold over together.
Sprinkle corn meal on top.
Bake for 25 minutes.

recipes.t: Baton Rouge Cake(No Eggs, No Mixer)
d: Mix with spoon the sugar, oil and crushed pineapple.
Mix flour and spices separately.
Stir in applesauce.
Add to sugar mixture.
Add in diced bananas and nuts.
Gently stir and pour in a greased Bundt cake pan.
Bake 50 minutes in a 350° oven.
The aroma and taste is wonderful!
This cake never fails and keeps moist for days.
Take juice from cherries; add with water to make 2 cups.
Put in pan along with sugar, lard and raisins. Bring to boil; cool. Add eggs and rest of ingredients. Bake for 1 hour at 350°. Makes 2 or 3 loaves.
Bring sugar, cream and butter to a boil.
Boil 6 minutes.
Add vanilla.
Beat until creamy and of spreading consistency.
Spread on cooled cake.

recipes.t: No Boil Da' Noodles Vegie Lasagne
d: Spread layer of sauce in a baking dish.
Place a layer of noodles.
Mix cheeses together and place a layer of noodles, followed by a layer of lightly steamed vegetables (water squeezed out).
Repeat layers.
Add remaining sauce and press layers down. Bake at 400° for 55 minutes, covered with foil.
Wash and put livers in bowl. Break 1 egg with livers and sprinkle garlic salt over livers. Pour soy sauce over livers to cover. Mix really well. Cover and let set overnight in refrigerator.
Chop all vegetables.
Mix with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in skillet.
Add vegetables, brown, and turn until done. Very good with eggs.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large skillet over medium heat, cook meat until no longer pink.
Drain well.
Stir in water, chilies and seasoning mix.
Add cereal, stirring until well combined.
Set aside.
Roll bread dough into a 15 x 10-inch rectangle.
Spread 2 cups reserved meat mixture in a 4-inch wide strip lengthwise down center of bread.
Top with cheese.
Cover with remaining meat mixture.
Bring sides of dough up over filling.
Seal top and edges well.
Place seam side down on baking sheet.
Brush with margarine.
Sprinkle with chili powder.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until golden brown.
Slice and serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, black olives.
Great with Fajita Style Nachos.
Serves 6.
In a small saucepan, melt margarine.
Stir in onion soup and cornstarch, then reserved pineapple juice and lemon juice. Arrange chicken and pineapple chunks in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour onion mixture over chicken and bake 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Serve with hot vegetables or over rice.
Makes 6 servings.
Dredge meat with the flour, salt and pepper mixture.
In a large Dutch oven heat oil and brown steak on both sides.
Remove meat to crockpot.
Add onion, celery, Worcestershire sauce, sherry, soup and water.
Cover and cook on HIGH
for 6 hours or on LOW for 8 hours.
Makes 4 servings.
Heat oven to 375°.
Separate each biscuit into 2 or 3 thinner biscuits each. Lay each biscuit over top of mini muffin cup. Press each biscuit into cup.
Sprinkle several bacon pieces to each cup. Chop the tomato and add to each cup.
Finely chop the onion
and mix with mayonnaise, cheese and basil.
Mound a small amount of cheese mixture on top of tomato in cups.
Sprinkle a few more bacon pieces on top. Bake 10 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Makes 20 to 30 appetizers.

Put 1 can of chili in casserole dish. Put hot tamales on top. Then put the other can of chili on the hot tamales. Pour chopped onions on top of the chili, then sprinkle the grated cheese on top of the onions. Put the corn chips on top of the grated cheese and around the edges. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until the cheese melts.

recipes.t: Finska Kakor (Finnish Cakes)(Nut-Studded Butter Strips From Finland)
d: Mix butter, 1/4 cup sugar and flavoring thoroughly.
Measure flour by dip-level-pour method or by sifting.
Work in flour with hands.
Chill.
Heat oven to 350°.
Roll 1/4-inch thick.
Cut into strips 2 1/2 x 2/3 inch.
Brush tops with beaten egg white. Sprinkle with mixture of 1 tablespoon sugar and almonds.
Carefully transfer to ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 17 to 20 minutes.
Makes about 4 dozen cookies.

recipes.t: Broccoli With Cheese And Mustard Sauce
d: Steam broccoli until tender-crisp.
Place immediately in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch ovenproof dish.
Mix yogurt and mustard in a small bowl and spread it over the broccoli.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Place under a hot broiler until bubbly and browned. Serve hot.
Makes about 5 servings, 127 calories per serving if you use only low-fat yogurt.
Contains 142 calories per serving if you use yogurt and sour cream.
In a bowl, put flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut in Crisco with pastry cutter.
Slightly beat 2 eggs, milk and anise. Add to flour mixture.
With hands knead a few minutes to form smooth dough.
Break off pieces of dough to the size of a small cigar.
Saute onion, bell pepper and garlic salt in oil.
Remove from pan and saute ground beef, salt, pepper and chili powder.
Add remaining ingredients.
Brown ground chuck with onion. Drain fat.
Add taco seasoning and water (as if to make tacos). Then add green chilies and black olives.
Set aside.
Mix cornbread mix, milk, eggs and corn.
In 13 x 9 greased or sprayed pan, layer 1/2 cornbread mix and all meat; top with cheese.
Spoon on rest of cornbread mix. Spread evenly.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until brown.
Brown meat together with onion and pepper.
Drain fat.
Add other ingredients to pan.
Simmer until mixture thickens.
Serve on buns while hot with a slice of cheese placed over mixture.
Using a small cookie or canape cutter or a knife, cut desired shapes from bread slices.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a sauce pan and heat over low heat, stirring frequently, until melted and creamy.
Add salt and garlic.
Serve over pasta.

In small saucepan, bring 2 cups of water and the sugar to a boil over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and let simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in instant Espresso powder, hazelnut extract, cinnamon and vanilla. Stir in evaporated skimmed milk. Transfer mixture to 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan. Cover with foil and freeze until ice begins to form around the edge of the pan, about 2 hours. Spoon mixture into large bowl.

Using electric mixer on medium speed, beat until light and fluffy, 4 to 6 minutes. Divide mixture into 4 freezer-safe dessert dishes. Cover with foil and freeze until firm, at least one hour or overnight. To serve, remove foil and let stand in refrigerator for 10 to 20 minutes. Makes 4 servings.
With sharp knife, cut and discard fat and bones from chuck steak; cut meat into strips 1/4-inch wide.
In a large bowl, toss chuck with flour, salt and pepper.
In a large skillet over medium heat, in salad oil, brown steak.
In crock-pot or pan on stove, add onion soup mix, extra onions, 1 cup cold water, chili sauce and meat.
Heat on low for 2 hours. Serve garnished with parsley over bow tie noodles.
Serves 6 to 8.
Brown beef in a small amount of oil. Add onions and garlic. Cook until soft. Add next 7 ingredients. Simmer for about 2 hours. Add oatmeal. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often.
Preheat broiler to high.
Place meat, cut side down, on flat surface
covered with a clean cloth and pound with a flat mallet. Turn
meat over; cover with clean cloth and pound the second side. The
meat
at
this
point
should measure about 5-inches in diameter
and
1 1/2 to 2-inches thick.
Sprinkle meat on
both sides
with
salt and pepper to taste and brush with oil all over. Place meat on broiler rack and place under broiler so
that
the top
of
meat is only about 2-inches or slightly less from the source of the heat.
Broil 5 minutes on both sides.
Shift broiler
rack
to bottom of oven and broil another 5
minutes. Using
tongs,
transfer meat to a carving board and
wrap in heavy-duty foil to keep warm.
Let stand 15 minutes and serve with Bearnaise sauce.
Let cream cheese set to warm temperature; soften.
Spread flat crescent rolls in ungreased pan.
Bake.
Cool on wire rack.
Mix pumpkin sauce, brown sugar, salt and melted butter.
Add beaten eggs and coconut.
Bring milk to a boil and add last.
Put in greased baking dish.
Set dish in a skillet of boiling water and bake at 350° until done.
To test, take a knife and cut in custard; if knife comes out clean, custard is done.
Beat eggs until thick and foamy.
Add sugar, vanilla and soft butter beating until creamy.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt into eggs.
Mix until mixture is a smooth batter.
Bake cake mix according to directions in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Leave in pan; slice into 24 squares.
Mix sugar, cocoa, salt and milk in pan.
Boil for 15 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Add oleo and vanilla.
Pour over presliced cake, making sure syrup goes between slices.
Cook the vinegar, water and pickle salt for 3 to 5 minutes. Pour over fiddleheads that are already in canning jars.
Once this is done, place each amount of spice in each jar.
Seal jars; cook for 5 minutes in canner.
Blend bananas well in processor or blender.
Add pineapple and blend.
Add remaining ingredients (except 7-Up).
Blend and freeze in individual serving containers.
(2 lb. size butter bowls makes 4 servings).
Set out 15-30 minutes prior to serving.
Then pour some of the 7-Up over tops.
Will make a mush-ice consistency.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Rub tuna steaks with oil; season lightly with pepper.
In skillet, saute onion in remaining oil until it is limp.
Add chopped tomatoes and vermouth; cook briefly.
Place steaks in a shallow pan.
Pour on onion-tomato mixture.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness.
Sprinkle with basil.
Serves 4.
Put the flour into mixing bowl.
Make a well in the center of the flour and the egg.
While whisking, pour in the nondairy creamer and then the skim milk.
Continue to whisk until the batter is smooth and free of lumps, then whisk in the nutmeg and vanilla. Cover the batter and set it aside for 30 minutes.
Whisk sour cream, mayonnaise, juice concentrate, lemon juice and ginger in a large bowl.
Stir in apple, bacon, celery, dates and pecans.
Add sweet potatoes.
Serve over lettuce.
Cook rice in boiling water for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Cook ground beef and onions until the onions are tender and the meat is no longer pink; drain off the fat.
Combine cooked and drained rice and ground meat mixture with Worcestershire sauce and seasoned salt.
Butter a 3-quart casserole.
Place 1/2 of the chopped cabbage for the first layer.
Pour 1/3 of the tomatoes over cabbage.
Next, place meat mixture and the rest of the cabbage.
Press down some and add the rest of the tomatoes.
You may sprinkle salt, pepper, Italian seasoning or basil if you desire.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook 1/3 cup chopped onion in a little hot fat until golden. Add bread cubes and seasonings; toss in skillet until bread is lightly toasted.
Spread stuffing over steaks and roll as for jelly roll; fasten rolls with toothpicks and lace with string.
Roll in flour and brown on all sides in a little hot fat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add tomatoes, water, 1/4 cup onion and catsup.
Cover; simmer 1 3/4 to 2 hours or until tender.
Add green pepper, mushrooms and liquid last 15 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine crumbs, 1/4 cup sugar and butter; mix well.
Press firmly into bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Chill 15 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, remaining sugar and 2 tablespoons of milk in medium bowl.
With electric mixer at medium speed, beat until smooth. Fold in 1 3/4 cups of the Cool Whip.
Spread over crust.
Layer with pecans.
Pour remaining milk into bowl.
Add pudding mix. Mix with electric mixer on low speed until well blended or 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour over pecan layer in pan.
Spread remaining Cool Whip over pudding.
Chill several hours or may freeze.
Bake yellow cake mix as directed in a 9 x 13-inch pan or jelly roll pan for thinner cake.
Before baking top with a mixture of flour, brown sugar, white sugar, oleo and oats.
Blend with pie crust blender.
Sprinkle over cake.
Bake as directed.
Mix
together
the
first
9 ingredients.
Pour mixture into a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan. Mix the cake mix and melted oleo; this
will be crumbly-gooey.
Put on top of the pumpkin mixture. Top
with
the
chopped pecans.
Bake in a 350° oven for
60 minutes,
or
until toothpick comes out clean.
Serve with Cool Whip.
Marinate sliced tomatoes in oil, garlic and oregano.
Line cookie sheet with foil.
Spray with Pam.
Place 1/4 slices of bread on sheet.
Top with cheese, tomato and any topping desired. Sprinkle with remaining oil.
Bake at 425° for about 10 minutes. Serves 6.
In small mixing bowl, combine whipping cream and sugar.
Chill bowl and beaters thoroughly.
In medium bowl, soften cheese.
Mix in mayonnaise.
Add cranberry sauce and pineapple.
Beat cream mixture until stiff.
Fold into cranberry mixture.
Pour into 8-inch square pan.
Cover.
Freeze until ready to use.
Remove from freezer 15 minutes before serving.
Cut into squares.
Serves 9.
Cook the chopped onions in the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the peas and water chestnuts.
Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the hot chicken stock, m.s.g. and dissolved cornstarch (mix cornstarch and water).
Add a little soy sauce if desired.
Stir and as soon as the sauce is transparent, serve at once.
Serves 4.
Arrange chicken, skin side up in greased baking dish. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over chicken.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Baste occasionally.
Heat oven to 350°.
Heat margarine in a jelly roll pan (15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch) in oven until melted.
Sprinkle and pat cake mix (dry) over margarine.
Sprinkle with marshmallows, chocolate chips and cereal.
Drizzle Eagle Brand milk evenly over the top. Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until cereal is golden brown.
While bars are warm, run knife around sides of pan to loosen edges.
Cool 2 hours.
Cut into 2 1/4 x 1 1/4-inch bars.
Makes approximately 48 bars.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Chill until slightly thickened. Combine other ingredients and fold into jello.
Chill and set.
In a small heavy stainless steel or enameled saucepan combine the lemon juice, the grated lemon rind, the egg yolks and 1/2 cup of granulated sugar.
Beat the mixture until it is well combined and cook it over moderate heat, stirring constantly until it thickens.
Do not let the mixture boil.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and let it cool.
In a bowl beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar and a pinch of salt until they hold soft peaks.
Add the remaining 1/2 cup sugar, 1 to 2 tablespoons at a time, beating and beat the meringue until it holds stiff peaks. Fold the meringue into the lemon mixture.
Steam carrots to desired doneness.
To carrots, add butter, maple syrup and parsley.
Mix so carrots are completely covered. Serve.
Wash and crush fully ripe blueberries one layer at a time. Wash, peel and cut into pieces and grind the peaches.
Measure fruit into 6 or 8-quart saucepan, if necessary, add water to equal exact amount.
Measure sugar into large bowl; set aside.
Combine fruit pectin and cinnamon with fruit.
Cook over high heat until it boils, stirring constantly.
Add sugar all at once.
Cook and stir over high heat until mixture comes to a full rolling boil (that cannot be stirred down).
Boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat; skim and stir to remove foam.
Ladle into hot jars, leaving 1/4-inch at top.
Wipe rim of jars clean; place lids on jars and screw firmly.
Place in canner and bring to a boil.
Boil 5 minutes.
Trim ends of beans.
Scrape carrots and slice.
Break cauliflower into florets.
Cook vegetables separately until barely tender.
Butter a shallow, 2-quart casserole.
Arrange vegetables with carrots around outside of casserole, cauliflower in the center and green beans between them.
Sprinkle with Worcestershire sauce, grated cheese and salt and pepper to taste.
Dot with butter.
Pour broth into bottom of casserole.
Bake in a moderate oven at 350° for 40 minutes, until hot and browned.
Serves 8.
Begin cooking enough noodles to cover the bottom of the baking dish.
In
a
skillet,
brown
the beef, then add salt, pepper, tomato
sauce, garlic and sugar.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Mix
the cream cheese, sour cream and onions.
In a greased baking
dish,
layer
the noodles, meat sauce, sour cream mixture and top with grated cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Thoroughly combine brown sugar, mustard and horseradish. Moisten with just enough cola to make a smooth paste.
Reserve, remaining cola.
Rub entire ham with mixture.
Place ham in crock-pot and add remaining cola.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 10 hours (on high for 2 to 3 hours).
Combine cocoa and boiling water, stirring until smooth; set aside.
Cream butter; gradually add sugar, beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, soda, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl; add to creamed mixture alternately with cocoa mixture, beating at low speed of electric mixer, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Stir in vanilla.
Do not overbeat. Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes; remove from pans and cool completely on wire racks.
Spread Whipped Cream Filling between layers; spread top and sides of cake with Perfect Chocolate Frosting.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Makes one 3 layer cake.
Put chopped prunes, raisins, orange juice and lemon juice into large kettle.
Heat to boiling.
Add Sure-Jell.
Bring to rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Add sugar; boil 1 minute.
Add nuts just before removing from stove.
Put into sterilized jars and seal.
Turn upside down for 5 minutes.

Brown hamburger meat. Shred cabbage. Open all cans. Throw in a great big pan. Add 2 cups water. Drop in beef broth cubes. Cook to boil, then turn to medium. It's done when cabbage is tender (about 45 minutes). DELICIOUS! AND QUICK!
Blend liverwurst, cream cheese (softened) and sherry until very smooth.
Also, add onion and parsley.
Spoon mixture in small bowl. Makes about 1 1/2 cups.
Cover cucumbers with lime and 8 1/2 quarts water.
Set 24 hours.
Drain and wash.
Soak in cold water 3 1/2 to 4 hours. Drain.
Simmer cucumbers in next 3 ingredients with enough water to cover cucumbers for 2 hour.
Drain and throw away liquid.
Bring next 5 ingredients to boil.
Add cucumbers.
Set overnight.
Drain and reheat syrup 3 times (morning, evening and next morning).
On third day, pack and seal.
Process 5 to 10 minutes.
Blend lemon juice and club soda thoroughly.
Serve at once over ice in stemmed glasses.
Strawberries on top.
Makes 1 gallon.
Place chicken in a greased casserole.
Mix chicken broth and can of soup and pour over chicken.
Add chopped, boiled eggs.
Mix flour, milk and melted margarine.
Pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until brown.
