Let cheese get to room temperature, if you can stand the wait. Mix all ingredients together with your hands (hard job). Separate into 3, 4, 5 or 6 parts and roll each part into a long roll.
(Like a snake about 14 to 18 inches long; whatever the diameter of a half dollar gets you.) Roll these rolls in chili powder sprinkled on a sheet of wax paper.
(This spread is not hot!)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix softened butter and sugars until creamy.
Add eggs and cream together.
Sift flour, pudding and soda into butter mixture.
Add vanilla extract and chocolate pieces.
Drop by rounded teaspoon on nonstick cookie sheet.
Bake until almost done.
Remove and cool slightly.
Freezes well while still warm.
Boil the sugar, water and cocoa; set aside to cool.
Cream together the powdered sugar and butter.
Add 3 beaten egg yolks to cream mixture, then add cocoa mixture.
Add the marshmallows, broken nut meats and vanilla.
Fold in beaten egg whites (3) and 12 graham crackers (rolled).
Sprinkle half of it in pan.
Pour in all mixture; sprinkle with crackers on top.
Saute seasoning in butter.
Add flour; stir until well blended. Add Pet milk; stir well.
Add crabmeat and bring to slight boil. Lower fire and add green onions.
Serve immediately over angel hair pasta.
Combine all ingredients together and stir until sugar is dissolved.
Makes 1 cup of sauce.
Serve as a barbecue meat sauce dip.
Cook fettucine until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat cream and garlic to boiling in medium saucepan.
Add scallops and cook just until centers are opaque, 1 1/2 to 2 minutes.
Using slotted spoon, transfer scallops to bowl.
Continue to boil cream until thick enough to coat back of spoon, about 6 minutes.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and corn and cook until heated through.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain fettucine well and transfer to large bowl.
Add cream sauce, scallops and basil; toss well.
Serve at once.
Brown sausage, celery, rice, onions and green pepper in frypan. Cook and stir over medium heat until meat and rice are brown.
Drain off any grease or the rice will not brown. Drain mushrooms; reserve
liquid
to add to water used in soup mix. When
meat mixture is brown, add drained mushrooms (chopped), half of the almonds and the soup mix.
Turn into buttered dish and sprinkle
remaining
almonds
on top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour. Serves 6 to 8.
Put celery, carrot, vinegar and salt in saucepan with 2 to 3 quarts of water.
Bring to rapid boil.
Add the unpeeled shrimp. If small shrimp are used (not over 1/2-inch diameter) they will be cooked shortly after the water returns to a boil.
Medium shrimp cook in 2 to 3 minutes.
When cooked, drain shrimp.
Peel and devein.

Put them in a shallow bowl and add the oil, lemon juice, salt to taste and pepper (optional) while shrimp are still warm. Mix well and steep in the seasonings at room temperature for 1 to 1 1/2 hours before serving.
Serve with crusty French bread or Italian bread.
Yields 6 servings.
In a large bowl, combine beef with bread crumbs, onion, tomato sauce, egg, 3 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce and salt.
Shape into 6 individual meat loaves.
Place in a shallow baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Increase oven temperature to hot 425°.
Mix pineapple with remaining teaspoon Worcestershire sauce.
Spoon on top of each loaf.
Return to oven.
Bake 15 minutes more.
Place 1 tablespoon tuna mixture inside flour tortilla.
Wrap and broil for 1 minute.
Fast and good.
Lay parsley in baking dish; add lemon slices.
Place fish on top.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Bake at 400° until tender. Mix sour cream and onion soup mix; spread over fish.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Broil until cream is slightly brown and bubbly (usually less than 5 minutes).
Serve hot.
Combine sugars, syrup, water and salt.
Microwave on High in glass casserole for 5 minutes.
Stir.
Place back in microwave on High for 9 minutes.
Beat egg whites and cream of tartar in mixer bowl until stiff peaks form.
Pour hot syrup mixture over egg whites.
Add vanilla.
Beat until mixture holds its shape and loses its gloss.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper.
Top with pecan half, if desired.
Brown chicken.
Add diced pepper, cream cheese and Pace picante to skillet.
Heat until smooth.
Fill flour tortillas with mix. Roll up and place in baking pan.
Cover with enchilada sauce and shredded Monterey Jack cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 225°.
Warm the taco shells in the heated oven.
Brown the beef in a frying pan.
Stir in the ground chiles, oregano, cumin, garlic and salt.
Cook until the flavors blend about 5 minutes.
Take the taco shells from the oven and raise the heat to 400°.
Fill the taco shells with the meat mixture.
Add cheese.
Heat in the oven until cheese melts, about 5 minutes. Top with lettuce, onion and tomato.
Serve with salsa.
Combine all ingredients except sauce; stuff shells with chicken mixture.
Spread thin layer of sauce on bottom of baking dish.
Place desired number of shells open side down in single layer.
Cover with sauce (1/3 cup per 3 shells).
Sprinkle with additional Parmesan cheese.
Bake covered at 350° for 30 minutes. Freeze remaining unsauced shells.
Melt in top of double boiler, marshmallows and milk.
Pour hot mixture over gelatin.
Stir until dissolved, then stir in cream cheese with blender.
Remove from blender; add pineapple.
Cool. Fold in whipping cream whipped together with mayonnaise.
Chill until firm.
Makes 12 servings.
Prepare rice as directed on the package.
In large skillet, combine chicken, vegetables, bouillon and oil.
Give 4 good shakes of pepper and 4 good shakes of ginger to the skillet; stir until chicken is cooked.
Experiment!
Open bag of rice into skillet; stir and serve.
Brown hamburger
meat; drain fat.
Add flour and let it brown. Add the other ingredients, except beans and cook until well seasoned.
Add
pork
and
beans
and cook about 15 to 20 minutes on low heat.
Great with a salad and garlic bread.
Drain tuna; flake.
Combine tuna, onion salt, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish and sour cream.
Cover; chill.
Garnish with parsley and surround with potato chips.
Yields 1 1/2 cups.
In large saucepan, combine carrots and salt with water to cover.
Bring to a boil over high heat and cook 20 minutes or until fork-tender; drain.
Return carrots to pan and add butter or margarine and sugar.
Shake pan over low heat to melt butter and glaze carrots.
Sprinkle with mint.

recipes.t: Angel Hair Pasta With Garlic And Lemon
d: Have large pot of water boiling for pasta while you prepare sauce.
Saute garlic in olive oil in saute pan over medium heat just until garlic begins to brown.
Remove pan from heat.
Return pan after adding wine.
Cook (simmer) for 1 to 2 minutes, until wine is reduced to half.
Stir in the lemon juice and tomato. Remove from heat.
Cook pasta in boiling water for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Drain.
Toss pasta with basil, Parmesan cheese, pepper and tomato mixture.
Serve immediately.
Combine vegetables in large bowl.
Add cheese, broken in small pieces, and bread.
Mix lightly so potatoes are not mashed. Season and put into greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Pour melted butter and milk over mixture and sprinkle with cornflakes.
Bake in 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Melt the margarine and marshmallows together; remove from heat.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Mix together.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan (pan should be greased).
Ice with a thin layer of chocolate icing.
Cut into squares.
Simmer celery until tender.
Brown meat in skillet; drain. Cook the noodles; drain.
Add meat with all other ingredients and simmer until well mixed, about 30 to 45 minutes.
Delicious.
Prepare brownie mix according to the package directions, stirring in 1 cup of pecans. Bake as directed. Let cool and break into small pieces.
Drain apricots, reserving
1 cup juice.
Boil juice and dissolve jello in it.
Whip cream cheese and apricots in blender until smooth.
Blend jello, Dream Whip and apricot mix and refrigerate in desired pan.
Can be poured over graham cracker crust before chilling.
Cream the sugars, Crisco and eggs.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and baking soda. Add vanilla.
Lastly add the rolled oats, Rice Krispies and nuts.
Roll into balls. Bake at 325°.
Roll 1 package of crescent rolls to fit the bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer 1/4 pound of each:
ham, salami and cheese and 1 jar of peppers.
Combine 5 eggs with Parmesan cheese and pour half over layer.
Layer 1/4 pound of each: ham, salami and cheese and 1 jar of peppers.
Top with rest of egg mixture.
In a small saucepan, combine margarine or butter and cinnamon. Heat and stir until margarine is melted.
Drizzle over popcorn. Toss.
Sprinkle cocoa powder over popcorn; toss to mix.
Serves 4.
Cook bacon crisp.
Saute ground beef and onion together.
Place in crock-pot, beans, catsup and brown sugar.
Add beef and bacon to crock-pot.
Cook in crock-pot 5 hours on low setting.
Mix first 5 ingredients together.
Cut shortening into dry ingredients until coarse.
Beat eggs well and add to sweet milk. Add currants to coarse mixture together with milk mixture.
Mix well and put out on floured baking sheet.
Roll out to 1 1/2-inch thickness.
Cut into desired shape.
Place on greased cookie sheet; dot each biscuit with generous piece of butter.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes or until a golden brown.
Brown onions in oil.
Mix and add all other sauce ingredients. Simmer 1/2 hour.
Pour over 2 pounds of weenies.
Heat in 350° oven for 20 minutes or cut wienies into bite size pieces, heat in chafing dish and serve with picks on the side for hors d'oeuvres.
Boil pasta.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Melt butter in pan and add pepperoni.
When butter is melted and pepperoni makes a sauce, add broccoli.
Toss together to coat broccoli.
Add pepperoni/broccoli mixture to cooked pasta.
Toss in Parmesan cheese.
Add garlic powder to taste.
Wash and cut squash and zucchini into 1/2-inch slices.
Simmer in water for 10 minutes; drain well.
Combine in bowl the squash and zucchini, butter, 1/2 cup cheese, onion, salt, pepper, garlic powder and 1/2 milk; mix well.
Slowly add eggs and fold into the mixture.
Pour mixture into a well-greased medium casserole dish; sprinkle remaining cheese evenly on top.
Drizzle remaining milk evenly; let casserole rest in refrigerator for 20 minutes. Sprinkle bread crumbs and paprika just before baking.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Brown beef until all pink is gone.
Drain well; blot with paper towel.
Add onion and cook until clear.
Add Worcestershire sauce and stir.
Add soups and corn; blend well.
Add sour cream and blend.
Place 1/2 of mixture in casserole and 1 cup of chips. Add remaining meat mixture and top with 1 cup of chips.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes or until edges are bubbly.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease the bottom of a 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sift together flour, baking soda, cloves, cinnamon, ginger and salt.
Cream together thoroughly the butter and sugar.
Add the egg; beat until light and fluffy.
Beat in molasses.
Add flour mixture with hot water until mixture is just smooth.
The batter will be very thin.
Turn batter into pan.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes. Remove the pan and cool on a rack.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.

In a quiche dish or 9-inch pie pan, layer the relish (or salsa), 1 cup Cheddar cheese and 1 cup Mozzarella cheese, then 1 cup Cheddar again. Beat the eggs and milk. Pour over the layered items. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes. Serve hot with your favorite crackers.
Place chicken in electric skillet, salt and pepper.
Add garlic, onions and pepper.
Pour catsup over chicken, onions and pepper, then cover with Coke.
Bake at 325° in electric skillet approximately 1 hour or until liquid is almost gone.
Saute meat, onion and pepper.
Drain off fat.
Season to taste.
Spread evenly in large casserole.
Drain whole corn and spread over meat; likewise with cream-style corn, then the mashed potatoes.
Top with the onion rings and heat in oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with salad.
Coat roast
with
mixture
of
flour,
salt and pepper. Brown roast in
12-inch
Dutch
oven with oil.
Mix broth, bay leaves, garlic salt,
marjoram
and basil. Pour over meat and bake 2 1/2 hours.
You
can
remove meat when done and thicken juices with flour for gravy.
Dissolve yeast in small amount of lukewarm water.
Add the water, molasses, sugar, salt, shortening and rye flour to the yeast; beat until bubbly.
Add enough white flour to make dough stiff enough to knead.
Knead dough until it springs back.
Put in greased bowl and set in warm place.
When double in bulk, knead again and let rise again.
When light, shape into 4 loaves and rise again.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine butter and water.
Pour over stuffing mix and toss. Stir in 1/2 can fried onions.
Spoon into a 9-inch (1 1/2-quart) baking dish.
Press mixture across bottom and up sides of dish to form a shell.
Combine soup, milk, turkey and peas; pour into a shell.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining onions and bake, uncovered, for 5 minutes more.
Melt chocolate and butter on low heat.
Cool slightly, then add powdered sugar and the egg.
Cool more and add nuts and marshmallows.
Spread coconut out on waxed paper.
Spoon out chocolate mixture on top of coconut.
Form rolls and sprinkle more coconut on top.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, then slice and eat.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix
salt,
pepper
and paprika with crushed cereal.
Dip chicken
in
skim
milk
and roll in crushed cereal mixture.
Spray foil lined pan with Pam or corn oil and add chicken pieces in one layer.
Cover and bake for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake
about
minutes more until chicken browns.
Line
pie
pan
with pastry.
Place apples in pan.
Mix 1/2 cup sugar, flour and salt.
Sprinkle over apples. Dot with 1 tablespoon
butter.
Bake
at 350° for 20 minutes.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar,
tablespoon
butter,
egg, milk and coconut. Sprinkle over hot pie.
Bake 30 minutes more.
Place bacon in bottom of a baking dish.
Sprinkle salmon with salt and pepper; lay on top of bacon.
Saute garlic, onion and green peppers together for 3 minutes in hot oil.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour over salmon.
Bake in a 400° preheated oven for 30 minutes, basting often.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix lemon juice, garlic, salt and oil.
Pat onto snapper; grill until flakes.
(It does not take long.)
Brown beef; skim off excess fat.
Season meat with salt and pepper.
Stir in beans, pizza sauce and onion; heat until boiling.
Oil a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Sprinkle bottom with brown sugar and spread with cranberry sauce.
In large bowl, pour cold water over stuffing mix and toss with fork.
Add onion, green pepper, egg, salt and ground meat to stuffing and mix well.
Spoon gently over cranberry sauce in pan.
(Do not pack down, but spread out to all corners, sealing in cranberries.)
Mix cream cheese, milk and sugar in a large bowl. Beat with wire whisk, until smooth.
Stir in cool whip.
Spread mixture on top of crust.
Pour cold milk into large bowl; add sweet potatoes, pudding mix and spices.
Beat with wire whisk until well mixed. Mixture will be thick.
Spread over cream cheese layer. Refrigerate at least 4 hours or until set.
Garnish with cool whip.
Store in refrigerator.

Boil water and add 1 teaspoon of salt to water with the potatoes. Boil potatoes for 8 to 10 minutes. After cooked, cool potatoes completely. Chop celery and onions along with 3 cooked eggs. Combine onion dip, brown sugar and remaining salt and pepper. Add potatoes, onion, celery and eggs to mixture. Chill overnight, then slice remaining egg on top to serve.
Heat 1 cup beet juice.
Mix jello into juice.
Add sweetener and vinegar.
Pour over beets.
Refrigerate; occasionally stir until set.
Melt oleo in pan.
Add almonds.
Brown lightly.
Add flour, salt and pepper.
Blend well.
Add soup and broth.
Stir until thick and smooth.
Defrost asparagus.
Grease a 2-quart casserole. Arrange chicken and asparagus in alternate layers.
Put sauce over.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Serve in patty shells or over toast points.

recipes.t: Potato With Apples And Ham(Jagaimo No Ringoni)
d: Rinse potatoes and put into microwave safe dish.
Microwave on High for 2 to 3 minutes.
Peel.
Peel apples.
Soak in water for 5 minutes, then grate.
Put potatoes and bouillon cube into a pot and cover with water.
Bring to boil.
Lower heat and add ham and grated apple.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain.
Add parsley and salt and pepper to taste before serving.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cube meat and brown with onions.
Slice carrots, thin, cube potatoes and chop celery.
Place all, except cabbage, in kettle. Bring to a boil and simmer about 2 hours.
About 45 minutes before soup is done, add cabbage and seasoning.
Serves 4 to 6.
Put peach halves in baking dish.
Put marmalade in center of each half, top with nutmeg, heat through in oven.
In sauce pan, melt butter.
Add brown sugar, corn syrup & salt. Cook over medium heat; stirring occasionally until mixture comes to a full boil (10 to 12 minutes).

Stir in sweetened condensed milk. Continue cooking; stirring occasionally, until candy thermometer reaches 245 degrees or small amount of mixture dropped into ice water forms into a firm ball (20 to 25 minutes).
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla.
Dip apples in caramel mixture.
Dip end of apples into chopped peanuts.
Place on waxed paper.
Refrigerate until firm (10 minutes).
Line bottom of one greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish with layer of potatoes.
Cover with layer of onions and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Next, sprinkle with grated cheese and then ham (chopped or ground).
Repeat layers until ham is top layer.
Heat grill.
Put ribs on grill over dripping pan.
Cook ribs until tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Meanwhile, in blender or food processor, puree garlic, ginger, soy sauce, wine and hoisin until smooth.
During last 30 minutes of cooking, baste ribs several times during cooking.
Serves 4.
Combine flour, nuts, butter and salt.
Press into greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until lightly browned.
Place butter in a 2-quart casserole dish.
Heat in microwave oven on Full power for 30 to 45 seconds or until melted.
Coat liver in flour.
Arrange in melted butter.
Cook in microwave oven on Full power for 5 1/2 to 6 1/2 minutes or until livers are no longer pink.

recipes.t: Dixie'S Chicken And Wild Rice Casserole
d: Cook wild rice as directed on box.
Boil chicken with salt, celery (2 stalks) and onion or onion salt.
When cooked and deboned, cut into bite size chunks.
Saute celery and onions in 1/2 stick butter.
Mix first 4 ingredients together with 1/2 of the Cheddar cheese.
Boil water and cook spaghetti.
Fry crumbled sausage; drain. Saute onion, garlic and bell pepper.
Stir in jar of spaghetti sauce.
Mix all ingredients, except eggs, milk and Parmesan cheese.
Beat eggs.
Add milk and Parmesan cheese.
Stir egg mixture into warm spaghetti-noodle mixture.
Slice broccoli and cauliflower.
Mix all ingredients together and sprinkle dill weed on top.
Dissolve each package of gelatin separately in 1 cup hot water, cool.
Stir pineapple and lemon juice into lemon gelatin; pour into 7 1/2 x 12-inch dish of pan and set aside to chill.
Mix strawberry gelatin with applesauce, cool but do not chill.
When pineapple layer is firm, carefully spoon applesauce layer over it. Chill until firm, at least 4 hours.
Spread Cool Whip over top and sprinkle with nuts.
Mix sugar and butter and add egg and whip.
Add syrup and mix well.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and cloves.
Add to liquid ingredients.
Add 1 c. hot water and mix very well.
Pour into greased pan and bake at 350 degrees until done.
Blend beets and juice from beets to smooth liquid.
Stir in buttermilk and dill salt.
Mix well and chill.
Garnish with fresh dill.
Combine yogurt, mustard and horseradish; blend well.
Spread yogurt mixture on cut sides of rolls.
On bottom halves of rolls, layer lettuce, ham, tomato slices and cucumber slices.
Cover with top half.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Stir in flour, baking powder and nuts.
Spray cookie sheets with Pam.
Make 2 strips and sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.
Mixture will be very thick.
Stir-fry vegetables in oil.
Add meat and fry until hot. Spoon in cooked rice.
Stir gently until vegetables and meat are mixed in.
Season with soy sauce and a dash of Accent.
Cook over low heat stirring frequently until rice is warm.
Heat
oven to
Have
cookie
sheets
ready.
Mix flour, cocoa and baking
soda.
Beat
butter and peanut butter in a large bowl with electric mixer until creamy.
Add 1/3 cup granulated sugar and the brown sugar; beat until fluffy.
Beat in egg, milk and
vanilla
until
well blended. With mixer on low speed gradually beat
in flour mixture just until blended. Shape heaping teaspoonfuls
into balls.
Roll in remaining 1/4 cup granulated sugar to
coat.
Place
1/2-inches
apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake
to
12 minutes until firm. Immediately place a chocolate
kiss
on each cookie, pressing down so that cookie cracks
around the edge.
Remove to racks to cool completely. Makes 48 cookies.

Mix together first 5 ingredients. Arrange chicken breasts in large baking dish. Top with diced tomatoes and peppers. Pour barbecue sauce over chicken. Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until chicken is no longer pink. The sauce is great poured over French fries.
Beat egg whites stiff.
Add sugar.
Beat egg yolks.
Add to egg whites, then add all dry ingredients, adding flour last.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Bake in cast-iron pan, greased and floured.
Mix pretzels, margarine and 2 tablespoons sugar together and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. Cool.
Slice beef thinly.
Rinse spinach.
Heat oil in pan, when heated, stir-fry beef until redness is gone.
Mix in spinach until all leaves have shrunk.
Put in soy sauce and pepper for seasoning.
Then beef and spinach is ready to be served with rice or potatoes.
Combine crumbled cornbread with crumbled white bread or biscuits.
Soak dry mixture with chicken stock.
In a skillet, saute onion and celery.
Add to other mixture along with beaten eggs and sage.
Mix well and add enough of the liquid to make right consistency.
Bake in bread pan at 400° about 1 hour.
Halve nectarines, pit and cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Set aside. Combine Bisquick, milk, 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, cooking oil and egg.
Beat for 30 seconds.
Spread in greased 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Arrange nectarine slices in rows on top of batter. Pour melted butter over fruit.
Combine the 1/2 cup granulated sugar, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle over nectarines.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Steam carrots, broccoli and pea pods together until crisp-tender.
Cool.
Cook fettuccine in chicken broth, just until tender.
Drain and cool.
In a 4-quart pan, cover peeled, diced potatoes and chopped onions with water.
Cook until potatoes are done (approximately 20 minutes).
Drain water thoroughly.
Add butter or oleo, sour cream and shredded cheese.
Cover and, when softened, blend with potatoes.
Add milk, if necessary, to reduce stiffness.
Add green peas and salt and pepper to taste.
Place in buttered 8 x 8 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Garnish with paprika and 6 to 8 dollops of butter or oleo.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Winter Squash, Raisin And Pine Nut Lasagna
d: Place flour in a small saucepan. Gradually whisk in milk and garlic. Warm over low heat, stirring constantly, until sauce simmers and is thickened, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in cheese, salt and pepper. Spread 1/4 cup cheese sauce over bottom of baking dish and cover with 3 lasagna noodles. Top with 1/3 of squash, 1/2 cup cheese sauce, 1/2 cup Mozzarella cheese and 1/4 cup raisins. Cover with 3 more noodles and spread 1/3 of remaining squash, 1/2 cup cheese sauce and 1/4 cup raisins. Cover with 3 more lasagna noodles and top with remaining squash and raisins. Cover with last 3 noodles, pressing down firmly. Top with remaining cheese sauce and sprinkle with pine nuts and remaining Mozzarella cheese. Bake about 30 minutes in a 350° oven until it bubbles around the edges and is brown on top.
Melt the butter and stir in the lemon juice.
Add almonds and parsley and cook until the almonds are golden.
Do not allow the butter to brown.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Trim stems and leaves off broccoli and separate flowerets. Steam flowerets until just tender.
Set aside.
In medium saucepan, melt margarine.
Remove from heat and stir flour into margarine to make a smooth paste.
Return to low heat and blend in chicken broth until sauce is thick and smooth.
Stir salt and mushrooms into sauce.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease a shallow pan with margarine.
Place broccoli in pan.
Cover with turkey, then sauce.
Bake, uncovered, 15 to 25 minutes.
Cut steak into 1-inch cubes.
Brown in skillet and drain on towel.
Heat crock-pot and add all three cans of soup and one can of water.
Add steak.
Cook on high for 4 to 4 1/2 hours.
Cook noodles and drain.
Serve steak and soup over noodles.
Cook pasta until al dente; drain and toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil.
In skillet, melt butter; add olive oil and garlic. Stir until garlic colors slightly.
Add shrimp, oregano, salt and pepper and cook until shrimp turns pink; remove from heat.
In large serving bowl, combine pasta and cheese.
Fold in shrimp mixture.
Let stand at room temperature to blend flavors.
Mix flour, mayonnaise and buttermilk.
Beat in sweet milk until biscuits are of dropping consistency, too sticky to roll, but stiff enough to sit up.
Drop by big spoonfuls on greased griddle or baking sheets and bake in preheated 350° oven until brown.
Put cookies in Ziploc bag and crush until mixture looks like dirt.
Set aside.
Cream margarine, cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Mix pudding and milk according to package directions.
Add to cream cheese mixture.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Layer cookies and cream mixture in a deep flower pot lined with aluminum foil or you may use a plastic sand bucket.
Top layer should be cookie (dirt) layer.
Decorate flower pot with an artificial flower and decorate plastic sand bucket with plastic sand shovel.
Process mustard, mustard seed, honey, vinegar and salt.
Cover and let stand overnight for the flavor to develop.
In
large
skillet, brown steak in oil.
Stir in water, soup mix,
salt,
pepper
and potatoes.
Heat to a boil, then simmer 30 minutes, covered, stirring occasionally.
Add green beans, cover and cook 10 minutes.
Remove meat and vegetables to platter.
Blend
water and flour.
Stir into hot liquid in skillet and stir until thickened.
Serve over meat and vegetables.
Wash 6 peaches, dry and cut in half.
Remove stems. Scoop out a little of the peach flesh into middle and put into bowl.
Mash to a puree.
Add sugar, 2 tablespoons of butter, egg yolk and macaroons to puree.
Mix well and fill each peach half with some of the mixture, piling it up in the middle.
Arrange the peach halves in a ovenproof dish and dot with the remaining butter. Bake in a moderate 375° oven for about 1 hour.

recipes.t: Apple, Peach Or Pear Crisp(So Easy, So Good)
d: Mix fruit with enough sugar to sweeten slightly.
Place in 2-quart baking dish.
In a pan, melt margarine.
Remove from heat. Add flour, oatmeal, sugar and cinnamon.
Stir until crumbly. Sprinkle over fruit.
Top with nuts.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Serve with ice cream or cheese if desired.
Put each lettuce leaf on a plate.
Lay a pineapple slice on top of each lettuce leaf.
Stand 1/2 banana in the hold of each pineapple slice.
Top bananas with salad dressing.
Place a cherry on top of each banana to make your salad glow.
Cream shortening; gradually add sugar, beating well. Add eggs; mix well.
Stir in pumpkin and water.
Combine flour, baking powder, soda, salt, cinnamon and cloves; add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Fold in nuts and dates.
Spoon into 2 well-greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until bread tests done.
Yields 2 loaves.
In large skillet, saute celery, onion and garlic in margarine for about 5 minutes, or until celery is crisp-tender.
Add remaining ingredients and bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve bouillon.
Cover and steam over low heat without stirring for 50 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Let stand covered 10 minutes before serving.
Fluff rice lightly with fork. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Saute onion and garlic in butter until tender.
Add shrimp, lemon juice, wine, salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes; stir occasionally.
Stir in dill weed and parsley.
Spoon over toasted rolls.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain; immediately return to pan.
Add olive oil; toss to coat.
Add milk, Parmesan cheese, onion, basil, lemon, garlic powder and pepper.
Cook over medium heat until bubbly, stirring constantly. Season.
Top with additional Parmesan cheese, basil and lemon slices.
Chop onion and slice sausage.
Saute in large skillet until sausage is evenly browned and onion is glazed.
Place all eggs in large bowl (you don't need all the yolks if you prefer not to) and beat.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Put eggs in skillet and cook with the sausage and onion until scrambled to your preference. You may use dill to taste (fresh or dried).
Strain and cool the fresh goat milk to 50° or less.
Pour into clean glass canning jars up to within 1-inch of the tops.
Put the lids and bands on and screw them down tightly.
Place jars in a large kettle that is partly filled with water. Cover and bring the water to a boil.
Let it boil for 1 hour, being careful that it doesn't boil down too far. Cool and store in a dark place.
Fry bacon and hamburger.
Drain well.
Combine with the rest of the ingredients in a large casserole dish.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Fry hamburg with butter and diced onion until brown.
Add hot water to cover meat and add carrots and potatoes (both cubed) and boil slowly.
Salt and pepper to taste and cook until tender.
Add soy sauce.
Mix 2 to 3 tablespoons of flour in cold water and add to hamburg mixture.
Stir until thick.
Pour into casserole dish; cover with pie dough and bake until brown.
Mix cocoa and sugar together dry.
Dissolve cornstarch in small amount of water.
Separate eggs.
Beat yolks.
Add sugar and cornstarch.
Heat milk and water; pour over the egg mixture. Return to double boiler.
Cook until thick.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Mix margarine, flour and 1/2 cup of nuts; pat in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake 10 minutes at 375°.
Cool completely.
Melt white chocolate, peanut chips and peanut butter until smooth.
Add nuts and pretzels and stir.
Pour onto cookie sheet covered with foil.
Put in refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Take out and check to see if it's firm.
If so, break and serve.
Mix beef, mushrooms, onion, green pepper and oregano in a large skillet; cook slowly.
When meat appears to be done (approximately 1/2 hour), pour off liquid and add tomatoes, tomato sauce and chili powder.
Let cook about 20 to 30 minutes longer on a very low heat.
Add the cooked macaroni into meat mixture. Makes approximately 8 servings.
Combine egg, pizza sauce, bread crumbs and beef.
Mix well, then on foil, pat beef mixture into a rectangle.
In small bowl, combine the Mozzarella cheese and parsley.
Spoon mixture onto beef to within 1/2-inch of edge.
Bring up the lengthwise side of beef and seal on top and at the ends.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Coat rabbit pieces with seasoned flour.
Brown well in hot oil in skillet.
Pour off excess fat.
Add small amount of hot water. Arrange bacon slices over rabbit.
Cover skillet; cook over low heat until rabbit is tender, adding water, if necessary.
Melt chocolate in top of double boiler over simmering water. Off heat, stir in remaining ingredients, except dredging sugar, in order listed.
As mixture stiffens, use hands to blend well. Shape into 1-inch balls; roll in confectioners sugar.
Let ripen 1 to 2 days before serving.
Makes 2 dozen.
Each bonbon contains about 95 calories.
In 1-quart bowl combine turkey, rice, celery, onions and red pepper.
In a small bowl thoroughly combine mayonnaise, sour cream, parsley, lemon juice, mustard and seasoning.
Pour dressing over salad and toss well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled.
Toss again just before serving.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Makes 2 servings.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar and garlic powder.
Place chicken, green peppers, mushrooms and tomatoes in bowl.
Add marinade and let stand one hour.
Arrange on small skewers.
Place on roasting pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 20 minutes.
Brush with marinade.
Cook 10 minutes. Turn, brush again and cook 10 additional minutes.
Place meat on rack in Dutch oven.
Combine mushroom mix, apricots and salt and spread over meat.
Cover tightly and cook at 325° for 2 hours.
Add onion and lemon juice to cooking liquid and continue cooking, covered, for 1 hour or until tender.
Remove meat to warm platter.
If thicker gravy is desired, combine water and flour to thicken liquid.
Add snipped parsley and cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Heat butter, cocoa, oil and water together in saucepan until butter is melted.
Sift flour, soda and sugar together into large bowl.
Pour heated liquid over dry ingredients, a little at a time.
Add eggs; mix well.
Then add buttermilk; mix until blended.

recipes.t: Pork Chops With Green Peppers And Pineapple
d: Brown pork chops in oil.
Season with garlic salt.
Add green peppers, pineapple and soy sauce.
Cover; cook over low heat for 15 minutes, or until peppers are tender and pork chops are done. Serve with white rice.
Soak the gum arabic in one cupful of the water and the orange-flower water.
Heat and melt it in a double boiler, then strain through a fine sieve.
Dissolve the crushed sugar with the remaining water, add the cream of tartar and boil to 245°, or until it forms a firm ball when tried in cold water.
Beat up the whites of the eggs to a stiff froth; beat in the vanilla and granulated sugars.
Mix the hot syrup with the dissolved gum and the beaten whites of eggs and beat until white and sufficiently firm to run into starch impressions.
Dust over with cornstarch and set aside for twelve hours.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Over low heat, melt the butter and brown sugar.
Add all remaining ingredients except powdered sugar. Place in a greased and floured 13 x 9 pan and bake at 300° for 40 minutes.
Cut into squares and roll in powdered sugar.
Combine all ingredients, except tomato sauce, salt and cheese, in electric slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low setting for 8 to 10 hours.
Stir in tomato sauce and salt.
Cover and cook on high setting for 15 to 20 minutes.
Garnish servings with shredded cheese.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Cook sausage in skillet.
Add onions, garlic, bell pepper and celery.
Fry until tender.
Add okra and rice.
Cook 20 minutes.
Combine 1/4 cup of the flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Add to meat, tossing to coat.
In skillet, brown the meat in hot shortening. Transfer to 3-quart casserole.
Drain off 1/2 cup liquid from tomatoes, reserving liquid.
Cut up tomatoes.
Add tomatoes and remaining liquid, carrots, onion, celery, chili sauce and bouillon granules.
Mix well.
Cover tightly and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Combine remaining 1/4 cup flour with reserved tomato liquid.
Stir into stew along with Mexican-style vegetables and green beans. Cover and bake for 1 1/4 hours longer.
Mix eggs and milk.
Mix in 2 drops of vanilla, 2 drops of almond extract and several dashes of cinnamon.
Mix by hand with fork or whip.
Heat griddle.
Grease lightly with real butter. Heat until water drops sizzle on griddle.
Dip bread long enough to coat both sides (do not soak too long), then lay on griddle. Sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Flip when bottom is dry.
Serve with real maple syrup.
Makes 10 to 12 slices.
In a large bowl, mix together yogurt, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, coriander, mustard, pepper, ginger, cloves and hot pepper sauce.
Add chicken, turning to coat.
Marinate in refrigerator about 1 1/2 hours. Reserve marinade.
Place chicken, skin side up, on prepared grill about 8-inches from heat. Grill, turning and basting with marinade every 10 minutes. Cook about 1 hour or until chicken is fork-tender.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven at 400°.
Place chicken, skin side up, in ungreased rectangular pan (13 x 9 x 2-inch).
Mix soup mix (dry), mushroom soup and water; pour over chicken.
Cover and bake for approximately 50 minutes.
Spoon mushrooms over chicken and bake an additional 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix Jell-O and hot water together.
Let cool.
Mix Eagle Brand milk, salad dressing, cottage cheese, nuts and pineapple.
Add to Jell-O.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch dish and chill until set.
Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add pepper, garlic and bay leaf.
Saut 30 seconds.
Add shrimp and salt.
Saut 3 minutes.
Remove shrimp from skillet.
Set aside. Add wine, parsley and thyme to skillet.
Bring to a boil and cook until reduced to 1/4 cup (about 1 minute).
Return shrimp to skillet.
Toss to coat.
Discard bay leaf.
Heat deep frypan and
add oil.
Add meat and brown well. Sprinkle with garlic, if desired.
Add onion, cabbage and bell pepper. Stir.
Add tomatoes, salt, pepper, Accent and water.
Stir well. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes.
Serve over rice or potatoes.
You may add soy sauce if desired.
In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, basil, oil, salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate until serving.
Serve on lettuce if desired.
Beat eggs; roll croquette in cracker crumbs, then egg, then cracker crumbs again.
Cook macaroni in hot water until tender. Drain; rinse with cold water.
Combine butter, flour, salt and milk.
Cook until thick; add salmon and macaroni.
Chill and form cakes.
Fry until brown.
Brown sausage; drain.
Make rice according to instructions on package.
Combine ingredients in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, for 30 minutes at 350°.
Trim the ends off the asparagus.
In a saute pan, large enough to contain the asparagus lengthwise, bring to boil enough water to just cover the asparagus.
Add salt and cook asparagus until tender, but crisp.
Drain.
Beat cream cheese and 1/2 cup sugar in large mixing bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg yolks, lemon juice and peel until smooth.
To the cracker crumbs, add the walnuts.
Beat egg whites with salt; when stiff, gradually beat in sugar.
Add lemon extract and vanilla.
Fold in crumbs and nuts.
Bake in buttered 9-inch pie pan at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cool.
Serve in wedges topped with raspberries (frozen) and juice and whipped cream.
Place rhubarb, marshmallows and 1 cup sugar in bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan, greased.
Beat 1 cup sugar and shortening together.
Combine eggs, milk, flour and baking powder with shortening-sugar mixture.
Pour over rhubarb.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and sugar into a large bowl. Add walnuts and orange rind; stir to coat evenly.
In a separate bowl, beat orange juice, marmalade, eggs and melted butter until blended.
Add to dry ingredients; mix.
Bake in a well-greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour or until bread tests done. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.
Remove from pan.
Cool before cutting.
Makes 1 loaf.
Mix egg yolk, sugar, lemon rind and 2 tablespoons lemon juice. In electric mixer, beat remaining lemon juice, water, egg white and milk at high speed until stiff.
Gradually beat egg yolk mixture into egg white mixture.
Spoon into refrigerator tray and freeze without stirring.
Approximately 508 calories in entire recipe.
Drain pineapple and save juice.
Combine pineapple juice and dry pudding mix and stir until smooth.
Fold in pineapple chunks. Stir in bananas, oranges and Triple Sec.
Serve over vanilla ice cream or angel food cake or just as a breakfast jelly.
Heat oven to 375°.
Remove dough from can.
Do not unroll. Cut dough into 8 slices; place slices on ungreased cookie sheet. Top each slice with 1/8 of the onions, garlic powder and Cheddar cheese; press topping gently into dough.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 13 minutes or until light golden brown.
Sprinkle with cheeses. Serve warm.
Great for dipping!
Drain juices from all fruit.
Chop peaches, pears and bananas in small pieces.
Put fruits in large container and mix with the vanilla pudding and then mix Cool Whip into the fruit.
Lite fruit can be used instead of regular fruit for diabetics.
In large bowl combine bread crumbs, cornbread, biscuits, onion, celery, parsley, sage, salt and pepper.
Toss well.
Add broth, butter and eggs.
Mix well but toss lightly.
Mixture should be extra moist just this side of soupy.
Slice cake.
Make pudding as directed.
Put layers of cake first, then layer of pudding, layer of pineapple and layer of fruit cocktail.
Repeat process.
Top with Cool Whip.
Put Jell-O and pudding in hot water. Cook until thick. Cool. Add oranges and Cool Whip. Stir and refrigerate until you serve.

Melt butter and saute onions. In a large bowl, beat soup and cream cheese until smooth. Stir in salt, pepper, onions and potatoes. Pour into 9 x 13-inch casserole. Top with cheese and bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.

recipes.t: Aunt Marie'S Pineapple Icing For Angel Food Cake
d: Mix first 3 ingredients, then add 2 1/2 cups more of the powdered sugar.
Add crushed pineapple.
Mix Miracle Whip, cheese and milk and set aside.
Mix other ingredients and add dressing mixture.
Let set overnight and serve on lettuce leaves.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Make thin hamburger patties.
Layer bottom of pan.
Layer carrots (quartered), potatoes (quartered), 1/2 can green beans, 1/2 can corn, 1/2 bell pepper, 1/2 onion, salt and pepper.
Repeat again.
Pour can of tomato juice.
If you have any meat left over, make patties and cover top of vegetables. Cover pan.
Cook approximately 2 1/2 hours.
Dissolve lime jello in boiling water.
Add cold water and orange juice.
Arrange pears in lightly oiled ring mold or rectangular Pyrex dish; cover with lime gelatin.
Chill until almost set.
Melt chocolate over hot water.
Remove from heat.
Cream shortening.
Gradually add 2 cups sugar, beating until light and fluffy.
Add melted chocolate, eggs, corn syrup, water and flavorings.
Mix well.
Put first 4
ingredients in pan and heat until you can no longer stand to stir with finger.
Remove from heat and beat until stiff and fluffy.
Beat in salt, flavoring and color, if desired.
Arrange half of the chiles in bottom of well-greased 9-inch baking dish.
Top with half of the tortilla strips and half of the cheese.
Arrange tomato slices on top of cheese layer.
Repeat layers with remaining chiles, tortillas and cheese.
Beat together the eggs, milk, cumin, garlic, onion, salt and pepper.
Pour over tortilla mixture.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika or mild chili powder.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for about 40 minutes until puffy and center is set.
Allow to stand about 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Serves 6 to 8.
Serves 10 to 12 if using a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine cookie mix, egg and water in large bowl.
Stir until thoroughly blended.
Stir in cherries and coconut.
Shape dough into 36 balls.
Roll in nuts.
Place 2-inches apart on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake for 11 to 12 minutes or until cookies are set and lightly browned.
Cool 1 minute on baking sheet.
Remove to cooling rack.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place chopped apples in medium bowl. Drain cherries; save juice.
Add cherries to apples; set aside. In small saucepan combine cherry juice, cornstarch, 1/2 cup apple juice concentrate and 1/4 cup fructose.
Stir over medium heat until thickened.
Add almond and pour over fruit.
Pour fruit mixture into 2-quart casserole which has been sprayed with vegetable spray.
Cook broccoli or peas and shrimp (do not overcook).
Chill. Wash spinach and mushrooms.
Rub garlic or garlic powder on bowl. Slice tomato; cut cheese into small chunks.
Toss all vegetables and shrimp together; put cheese and olives on top.
Use dressing and seasonings of choice.
Cut meat into thin strips diagonally.
Brown meat in butter or shortening.
Add water, soup mix and undrained mushrooms.
Simmer this until meat is tender.
Add sour cream, blended with flour. Cook and stir until gravy thickens.
Serve over noodles.
Mix cake mix, butter and 1 egg well.
Press into greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch rectangular pan.
Sprinkle pecans and coconut on top. Set aside.
Mix remaining ingredients in bowl. Pour over cake. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool, then cut into squares.
Store at room temperature.
These are very rich.
Brown brisket in a small amount of oil in Dutch oven.
Drain; sprinkle with soup mix.
Cover with onion rings and celery.
Spoon chili sauce and 1/2 cup water around brisket.
Bake covered at 350° for 45 minutes or until tender, basting occasionally over brisket. Refrigerate overnight.
Skim.
Slice brisket cross grain.
Heat. Serve on kaiser rolls with sauce.
Quarter potatoes.
Place in baking dish with oil and desired seasoning.
Preheat oven to 350°.
No lid.
Brown 1/2 hour.
Turn and brown 1/2 hour more.
Last 10 minutes, add peas.
Dissolve Jell-O in water; cool.
Add pineapple and chill until slightly congealed; add remaining ingredients.
Chill until set. Makes 8 servings.
Blend well.
Bake at 350° until hot and heated through. Sprinkle Mozzarella and Cheddar cheese on top.
Continue baking until cheese melts.
Serve with corn chips.
Have cheeses at room temperature.
Into a large bowl, blend by hand the cheeses, garlic and pecans.
Form into long rolls.
On wax paper, sprinkle the crushed peppers and roll the cheese rolls in the peppers.
Enclose in the wrap, then fold and freeze.
(The chili peppers can be put into a blender and pulverized; they blend into the cheese better.)

recipes.t: Sauteed Zucchini With Onion And Garlic
d: In skillet melt butter; add zucchini and onion.
Saute until tender.
Add garlic powder to taste.
Bring syrup and brown sugar to a boil.
Add peanut butter. Pour mixture over cereal and peanuts in 8 x 8-inch pan.
Let cool.
Cook
bacon in a heavy iron skillet until crisp.
Drain on paper
towel.
Cook
onion and
garlic in remaining bacon drippings
until tender.
Combine all ingredients in a lightly greased crock-pot. Cook
on
low
for 6 to 8 hours or on high for 3 1/2 to 4 1/2 hours.
Combine carrot juice, chicken broth and squash.
Blend in blender until smooth.
In medium saucepan, combine blended mixture with ginger juice.
Combine cream and potato juice and add to soup mixture.
Heat just to boiling, then simmer until soup thickens, about 5 minutes.
Stir frequently.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Garnish with chives or dill.
Serves 4.
Place chicken in a shallow glass bowl.
Pour in mixture of soy sauce, honey, ginger, garlic and sherry.
Turn chicken to coat well with soy marinade.
Cover and place in refrigerator overnight.
Remove chicken from marinade.
Place on grill about 6-inches above glowing coals.
Cook until well browned on both sides, turning once, for approximately 30 to 40 minutes.
Garnish chicken with green onions and watercress or parsley.
Cube the pork; fry in a skillet with onion and garlic.
In a large Dutch oven, add all ingredients, salt and pepper to taste and 1/4 teaspoon cumin and seasoned salt.
Heat for 1 hour.
Serve with crusty bread.
In a large container, crumble half the angel food cake.
Mix pudding as directed on box.
Spread half over the cake.
Put half of the drained pineapple and half sliced strawberries over the pudding.
Top with Cool Whip, then crushed pecans.
Repeat, refrigerate and enjoy.
Heat 4 quarts water, salted if desired, to boiling in 6-quart Dutch oven.
Cook pasta in boiling water 11 minutes.
Add asparagus to boiling water; cook about 3 minutes or until asparagus is crisp-tender.
Drain pasta and asparagus.
Rinse with cold water; drain.
If using fresh basil, finely chop before preparing dressing.
Mix Italian salad dressing, basil and red pepper in a large bowl.
Add pasta, asparagus and remaining ingredients; toss.
Yield: 6 servings.
Heat a large pot over moderate-high heat until hot.
Add oil and heat until hot.
Add onions and cook over low to moderate heat, stirring frequently until they start to brown, about 5 minutes.
Add sweet potatoes, apples, broth, 1 cup apple juice, thyme, basil, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes or until potatoes are soft.
Remove from heat and let stand until cool enough to handle.
Puree in food processor or blender to a coarse texture.
Return soup to pot, add remaining 3/4 cup apple juice and heat thoroughly.
For a thinner soup, add more juice.
Peel onions and carrots. Cut onions in fourths and slice. Slice carrots. Saute in enough oil to almost cover. Remove onions and carrots. Save oil.
Broil liver and cut in 1-inch cubes when done.
May be seasoned.

Put everything through grinder or food processor. Add enough oil to moisten. Salt and pepper to taste. Refrigerate before serving. Can be served on crackers or as an appetizer on bed of lettuce with a cherry tomato.
Makes 8 servings.
Put olive oil in frying pan to cover chicken (which has been cut into small or medium pieces).
Also can add oleo to olive oil and add chopped garlic.
Cook on medium heat until chicken is done. Steam broccoli.
Cook Ziti shells.
Add all together with cheese. Ready to eat!
Remove stem end, seeds and membrane from peppers.
Cook in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain.
Combine seasoning mix, tomato and water.
Add beef and corn.
Combine thoroughly. Lightly pack into peppers.
Combine crackers and butter together. Sprinkle over top of stuffed peppers.
Place in buttered baking dish.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour, or microwave about 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix potatoes, flour, salt and pepper.
Add eggs.
Brown bread cubes and onions in margarine, and blend into potato mixture.
Brown all sides of roast in hot oil.
Add salt and pepper to taste and onions and carrots.
Stir in cola, chili sauce and Worcestershire sauce.
Add enough water to mixture to cover approximately 2/3's of the roast with liquid.
Cover pot and place in a 325° oven for 3 to 4 hours.
Thicken liquid with cornstarch and water mixture.
Serve with hot mashed potatoes or extra wide egg noodles.
Make a crust with coconut, oleo, sugar and flour.
Blend together and press into the bottom of 9-inch round pan or 8-inch square pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Chill.
Spread on half of the strawberry preserves.
Boil carrots with a little salt until tender, drain.
In a small saucepan over low heat, blend oleo and brown sugar, ginger and lemon juice until sugar melts.
Toss carrots gently until coated in this mixture and serve hot.
Makes six servings.
Melt butter in saucepan over low heat.
Add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add chicken broth; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Stir in the sour cream and chopped peppers.
Pour half of the sour cream sauce into a lightly greased 12 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; set aside dish and remaining sauce.
Fry the tortillas, one at a time, in 2 tablespoons of oil for 5 seconds on each side or until softened.
Place 1 tablespoon each of chicken, cheese and onions on each tortilla and roll up. Pour remaining sauce over top.
Bake at 425° for 20 minutes. Sprinkle remaining cheese on top and bake 5 minutes more.
Garnish with Spicy Sauce.
Saute the onion in hot oil.
Add the diced meat, saute briefly and then add the carrot, celery, salt and pepper.
Saute together for 10 minutes.
Pour over the soup stock and cook for about 30 minutes.
Remove crust from bread.
Cut white bread into 1-inch squares. Fry bacon crisp.
Crumble.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch dish:
bread, cheese, bacon, cheese, bread, etc.
Beat eggs, add cream (do not whip) and salt.
Pour over layers.
Refrigerate overnight.
Remove from refrigerator about 30 minutes before cooking.
Melt margarine and pour over mixture.
In a large bowl, combine and set aside the rhubarb, 1 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cherry pie filling and 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon.
Heat oven to 350°F.
In large bowl, beat together sugar and butter until well blended.
Add eggs and vanilla, blend thoroughly.
In a small bowl, stir together flour, cocoa, and baking soda; add to butter mixture, blending thoroughly.
Stir in oatmeal and chocolate chips.
Drop by Tbsp. onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 7-8 min. till cookies begin to set, do not overbake.
Grease long baking pan.
Dip pieces of chicken in buttermilk. Roll in flour seasoned with salt, pepper and seasoned salt.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes in 350° oven.
Mix cream of chicken soup, buttermilk and water together; pour over chicken.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour or until tender at 350°.
Drain fruit, save juice.
Mix pudding with juice from canned fruit. Mix fruit into pudding mixture, add bananas and fold in Cool Whip.
Drain peas and cook liquid down to 1/4 or less. Combine drained peas and soup in a casserole. Add liquid. Rub chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Arrange on top, skin side up.
Tuck 1/4 of the bay leaf under each piece. Cover casserole and bake in a moderate oven at 350° about 1 hour.
Uncover and continue to bake for 20 minutes or until brown and tender.
Add lemon juice to milk.
Fold Dream Whip into lemon mixture. Fold in blueberries.
Pour into crumb crust; chill thoroughly. Yield:
6 to 8 servings.
Cook vegetables briefly and separately.
Combine all three vegetables and Cheez Whiz while hot.
Pour mushroom soup over all and top with buttered crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate; stir in peanut butter, then other ingredients. Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper.
Make custard of the following:
egg yolks, sugar, lemon juice and rind.
Cook in double boiler until it thickens.
Brown chops in oil.
Layer lima beans, soup, pepper, pork chops and onion in baking dish.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until tender.
Yields 4 servings.
Blend together honey, vinegar and Kitchen Bouquet.
Place meat in large glass baking dish (9 x 13-inch).
Marinate in mixture in refrigerator 2 to 4 hours (covered).
Turn frequently.
Brown meat on both sides in large heavy frying pan in oil.
Add mushroom liquid (from only 1 can) to catsup.
Add to marinade.
Pour around meat.
Cook tightly covered over low heat until tender, 1 to 2 hours.
Add mushrooms.
Cook 5 minutes.
Remove meat and mushrooms; thicken liquid with flour (or cornstarch) and water for gravy.
Brown sausage in a skillet over moderately high heat; drain and discard fat.
Add mushrooms and onion and cook, stirring, until tender.
Remove from heat and stir in pizza sauce, Mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses.
Set aside to cool.
Thaw pastry 20 minutes; unfold.
On lightly floured surface, roll each sheet to a 12-inch square; cut each into sixteen 3-inch squares.
Top each square with some of the sausage mixture.
Brush edges of pastry with egg mixture; fold in half to form triangles.
Press edges together with the tines of a fork.
Brush with more egg; transfer to ungreased baking sheets and bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in pan.
Pour in eggs and stir-fry egg until in tiny pieces.
Remove from pan.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil. Stir-fry shrimp and meat; add green peas.
Fry 1 minute and remove.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil; fry onion and cooked rice.
Add salt.
Reduce heat.
Heat thoroughly.
Add egg and meat mixtures. Combine well and serve.
Prepare lemon cake mix as directed.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch oblong glass or cake pan.
Cream together other ingredients.
Beat well.
Pour over unbaked cake mix.
Bake at 325° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Cake will rise to top, cheese mix goes to the bottom.
Snap off and discard woody bases from asparagus.
If desired, scrape off scales.
Cook, covered, in a small amount of boiling water until very tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain; cool.
Place asparagus in blender container.
Cover; blend until smooth. Transfer to bowl.
Stir in sour cream, taco sauce, lime juice, salt, pepper and red pepper.
Chill, covered, up to 24 hours.
Marinate the chicken with cilantro, parsley, onion, Worcestershire sauce and soy sauce, preferably overnight.
Save this marinade to add later.
Fry the chicken breast.
When cool, tear the chicken into small pieces.
In a frying pan, add the chicken, the remaining marinade and mixed vegetables.
Let it simmer for approximately 15 minutes.
If necessary, add 1/2 can tomato paste to make the sauce thicken, then add the olives and capers.
Mix the chicken/sauce mixture with rice.
Serve it warm.
Peel and devein shrimp.
Wrap a half a bacon slice around shrimp and secure with toothpick.
Mix together mayhaw jelly, chili sauce, butter and garlic powder.
Pour sauce over shrimp and marinate in refrigerator overnight.
The next day, place shrimp on broiler rack and broil shrimp for five minutes on each side or until bacon is browned.
Serve warm.

Mix together sugar, salt, flour and eggs. Put in a pan and stir while adding water, then the vinegar. Cook over medium or low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Add diced eggs, onions and cooled dressing to potatoes. The potatoes will soak up dressing. Keep salad refrigerated.
Melt butter in medium frying pan.
Saute onion and tomato with 2 or 3 hot chili peppers.
Add cheeses with onion, tomato and peppers.
Stir over medium heat until cheese is melted.
Serve hot over tortilla chips. Serves 8 to 10 people.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Cut chicken breasts into 1/2-inch wide strips.
Combine chicken and green onions in a shallow, nonmetallic container.
Combine pineapple juice and remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Pour over chicken mixture and toss.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Thread chicken, green onions and reserved pineapple chunks onto wooden skewers. Broil with skewers 5 to 6 inches from heat source, brushing with marinade often.
Icing:
Before baking your cake, blend by hand the Cool Whip, vanilla pudding and crushed pineapple.
Set in refrigerator and let cool until cake is done.
Bake cake per box instructions in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
While cake is baking, mix the jello in boiling water.
Cool until cake is baked.
When cake comes from oven, poke full of holes (good size ones) with a fork.
Spoon jello into holes until used up. Refrigerate cake until cold and jello is set.
Beat pudding with 3 cups cold milk.
Spread over cake, then top with Cool Whip. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Scrub squash and cut off ends.
Slice or cut into small cubes. Place in pan depth of 1 inch.
Cover and cook 15 to 20 minutes or until just tender.
Drain well and mash.
Heat butter, add onion and saute until soft and golden, not brown.
Stir squash, onions, shrimp, salt, pepper and beaten eggs.
Blend thoroughly and turn into well-greased 1-quart casserole.
Dust with bread crumbs.
Dot with 1 tablespoon butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until puffed and nicely brown.
Serves 6.
Bake potato in oven or microwave until done.
Immediately after taking from oven, slice open potato and remove "meat" of potato.
Place in medium sized bowl.
Mash potato with fork. Gradually mix in powdered sugar.
Add butter while hot.
Add coconut and vanilla.
Shape dough into little potato shapes.
In a small bowl, mix instant cocoa and cinnamon.
Roll mini potatoes in mixture.
Combine corn meal, flour, milk powder and salt in large bowl. Cut in Crisco until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Store in covered airtight container in cool place up to 6 weeks.
Stir mix lightly into measuring cup and level off with a knife.
Brown hamburger and onion in the oil and drain.
Cook macaroni according to directions and drain.
Mix tomato soup and milk together.
Combine all ingredients together and pour into a 9 x 13-inch dish, sprayed with Pam.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

In a large bowl, combine the coleslaw mix, romaine and onion. In a jar with a tight- fitting lid, combine the oil, vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper and contents of seasoning packet from noodles; shake well. Break noodles into small pieces. Sprinkle noodles, almonds and sunflower seeds over salad; mix well. Drizzle with dressing and toss to coat. Serve immediately.
Combine buttermilk, cucumber, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper in small bowl; mix well.
Cover; chill 30 minutes.
Serve over lettuce, tomatoes, mushrooms, sweet green peppers, celery, cucumbers or carrots.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix orange Jell-O with boiling water.
Add ice cream, oranges, crushed pineapple and lemon juice.
Mix well.
Refrigerate and serve.
In a 4-quart pan, combine water, frozen meatballs, undrained beans, beef bouillon granules, onion, basil and bay leaf.
Bring to boiling.
Add spaghetti.
Simmer, covered, 20 minutes or until meatballs are heated through.
Stir in drained mixed vegetables and undrained chopped or crushed tomatoes.
Heat.
Serve with Parmesan cheese or grated sharp cheese, Monterey Jack, Swiss or cheese of your choice.
Very good.
Cook together first 5 ingredients until thick, stirring constantly.
Remove from fire.
Cool 10 minutes.
Add margarine and pecans.
Stir in vanilla and salt.
Pour into a mound of powdered sugar and knead until a roll can be formed.
Roll in waxed paper.
Slice when hardened.
Cream butter or margarine until light and fluffy.
Add confectioners sugar and hot milk alternately.
Beat well after each addition.
Blend in the salt and lemon juice.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Makes about 2 cups.
Saute zucchini in 1/4 cup of the butter.
Season with salt and pepper.
Set aside.
Cook ziti; drain and return to pot.
Add remaining butter.
Toss to melt and coat ziti.
Add zucchini, ham, cream and 3/4 cup of the cheese.
Toss to coat.
Top with remaining cheese.
Serve immediately.
Brown burger; drain off fat.
Cut tomatoes in fourths.
Put everything in large pot.
Let this boil.
Add water for seashells, then add the shells.
Keep adding small amounts of water so as not to dry out the chili.
Mix together Eagle Brand cream and lemon juice.
Add drained pineapple and Cool Whip.
Stir and pour into crusts.
Keep in refrigerator.
Bake onions with a little olive oil in 420° oven until onions are soft.
Add to flour, sugar, and beef broth.
Bring to a boil for 30 minutes.
Remove from heat and serve.
Dice apple and bananas.
Combine with cherries.
Toss with pineapple, orange sections and nuts.
Mix in mayonnaise and serve on cool, crisp lettuce leaves.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Drain pineapple, reserving 2 tablespoons juice.
Combine pasta, pineapple chunks, cantaloupe and grapes.
Set aside. Combine yogurt and reserve 2 tablespoons pineapple juice in a small bowl.
Stir well.
Spoon over pasta.
Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Stir in strawberry halves just before serving.
Boil rapidly all ingredients together.
Add noodles last. Cook until done.
Use canned tomatoes according to taste.
If you like more soup use 2 cans, if less, only 1.
Delicious.
Cook macaroni until done; drain and chill.
Slice carrots; cube ham and tomatoes.
Chop onion and broccoli.
Mix with chilled macaroni.
Mix olive oil and Catalina dressing and toss with macaroni mixture.
Chill thoroughly for at least 3 hours.
Cream margarine and sugar. Add eggs. Combine baking soda and water; add to mixture. Add salt and vanilla; mix well.
Add dates, cherries and pecans. Stir in flour. Spread onto cookie sheet. Bake at 300° for 25 to 30 minutes; cool. Cut into bars.
Brown meat, drain and put meat back in skillet and add seasonings and cheese.
Stir until melted.
Put on bread and top with halved olives.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
The pizzas can be frozen and baked later.
Combine rice, milk and honey.
Add eggs; mix well.
Stir in raisins.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with cinnamon. Bake at 350° about an hour.
Serve with whipped cream.
Mix pineapple juice with jello and water; heat to dissolve jello.
Remove and stir in lemon juice, nutmeg and cranberry sauce.
Cool until thickened slightly.
Add sour cream and mix. Fold in pineapple and nuts.
Let set for 6 to 8 hours.
Mix tomato sauce,
salami,
cheese and spices together. Spread on open-faced
muffins.
Sprinkle
with grated Parmesan cheese and bake 12 to
minutes at 400°.
After baking, put under broiler to brown the tops.
Serves 6.

Mix all ingredients except vanilla in saucepan. Cover and cook slowly until mixture boils. Remove cover and cook without stirring until a little dropped into cold water forms a soft ball. Remove from heat, let stand until cool. Add vanilla. Beat until thick enough to spread.
In largest skillet brown hamburger and chopped onion with salt, pepper, garlic salt and lemon pepper.
Drain excess grease. Add remainder of ingredients to meat mixture and simmer until hot.

In a skillet, heat oil and brown the Rice-A-Roni. Add frozen veggies and 3 cups of water. Bring to boil, then simmer while covered. Stir frequently. When rice is fully cooked, add cheese and let melt. This is good with only meat.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs and mashed bananas. Combine flour, salt and baking soda and blend into banana mixture. Pour into two (1 pound) loaf pans and bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Cream cheese; combine honey, eggs, lemon, salt and milk.
Add to cheese a little at a time; blend.
Pour into unbaked pastry shell and sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes; reduce heat to 325° and bake for 30 minutes.
Chill before serving. Makes 1 pie.
Mix tomatoes, garlic, cumin and water; simmer 25 minutes. Divide grated cheese and mixture of liquid in half.
Mix 1/2 of liquid and 1/2 of grated cheese in blender, then second half. Reheat the entire mixture until well heated.
Cream butter, margarine, shortening, flavorings and 1/4 cup milk until well blended.
Add sugar and cream well; beat in one egg at a time.
Add dry ingredients alternately with remaining milk. Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Melt butter and oil.
Add flour and stir until smooth.
Blend in broth; stir until thickened.
Reduce heat to low and add garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add artichokes, 2 tablespoons Parmesan and capers. Cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Toss with cooked pasta and garnish with an extra tablespoon of Parmesan.
Sauce freezes well! Serves 4.

Line a 13 x 9 x 2 in baking pan with foil, buttered. Set aside. Combine syrup, cream and butter in large saucepan. Bring to boil. Cook 9 minutes after it starts to boil. Remove from heat, add nuts and extract. Stir with wooden spoon for 4 minutes in pan.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Add cream of tartar to egg whites and beat until dry and stiff.
Add sugar and beat well.
Add vanilla, almond extract and chocolate chips.
Cover cookie sheet with brown paper bag, drop mixture by spoonful on paper and turn heat off on oven before inserting cookie sheet.
Let stay overnight or until oven is completely cool.
This mixture doesn't change shape, so it can be put close together on cookie sheet.

recipes.t: St. Patrick'S Day Buffet Style Corned Beef Hash
d: Combine beef hash and onion in an 11 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Pour cream over hash.
Bake 35 minutes at 400°. Remove and arrange 16 deviled egg halves on hash.
Serve with heated chili sauce or catsup in pepper pots.
Serves 8 to 10.
Cook beef in small amount of lard for 10 to 15 minutes; add onions and garlic continuing to cook.
Season to taste with salt, red pepper and chili powder; add tomato paste.
Cook until all ingredients are done.
Let meat set for a few minutes; remove fat from top.
Make a mush by pouring boiling water over cornmeal; season to taste.
Spread mush over shucks.
Place thick line of meat in center of mush and roll up.
Place in large cooker or Dutch oven.
Pour in 3 cups boiling water.
Cover and cook slowly for 3 hours.
Dice all ingredients and place in large casserole dish.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and bake at 350° for about 1 hour or until carrots are tender.

Make cornbread according to recipe. Make roux (oil, flour and onions). Add mushroom soup. Boil giblets and grind (save broth to mix with cornbread and seasonings) until soft. Salt and pepper to taste. Add egg, parsley and garlic. Bake in greased casserole dish at 375° for 35 minutes.
Mix first 3 ingredients in medium bowl.
Stir in chilies, onion and seasoning mix until smooth.
Spread half the mixture into 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Layer Monterey Jack cheese and Cheddar cheese over top.
Spread with remaining bean dip mixture. Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Simmer the livers in broth until done, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain.
Puree in an electric blender with the eggs, using a little of the liquid in which the livers were cooked.
Combine eggs, sugar and flour.
Beat until mixed thoroughly. Add milk, cream and nutmeg.
Bake in a 9-inch unbaked pie shell at 350° until done, about 1 hour.
Cut off the bottom part of stem of white cabbage.
Cut the cabbage into shreds or pieces.
Brown them in butter in a frying pan.
Boil rice, water and 1/2 teaspoon salt for approximately 20 minutes.
Let the rice cool.
Mix ground beef with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and white or black pepper.
Add the rice and milk.
Lay the cabbage and the meat in alternate layers in a buttered ovenproof dish.
The top and bottom layers should be cabbage.
Bake in a 350° oven for 3/4 to 1 hour.
Serve with boiled potatoes and lingonberries.
Makes 4 servings.
Roll
out crescent rolls and flatten onto a large baking sheet, pressing down to flatten.
Brown as per directions.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, 1 teaspoon dill weed and 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash until well blended.
Spread mixture on cool rolls.
Combine the first 5 ingredients and 1 cup chopped nuts in mixing bowl; mix until well blended.
Shape into a ball.
Roll cheese ball in remaining nuts until well coated.
Yields 1 cheese ball.
Reserve 1/4
cup
cookie crumbs.
Spread remainder in a 10 x 6 1/2-inch pan.
In a saucepan, combine dates, water and salt; bring to
a boil and simmer for 3 minutes. Remove from heat; add marshmallows
and
stir until melted.
Cool to lukewarm.
Stir in nuts and spread over crumbs in pan.
Whip cream and
vanilla. Swirl
over
dates.
Sprinkle
with
reserved crumbs.
Top
with walnut
halves.
Chill
overnight, cut in squares and serve.
Sift the flour, baking powder, salt, cocoa and sugar together into a mixing bowl.
Add oil and milk and beat at a medium speed until smooth.
Fold the egg whites and nuts into the batter and pour it into a greased 9-inch square Pyrex cake pan.
Bake the brownies in a preheated slow oven (325°) for 30 minutes or until firm to the touch.
Cut the brownies into 4-inch squares while warm but not hot.
Bake pie shell.
In double boiler, heat water, lemon rind and juice, sugar and salt.
Let sugar dissolve thoroughly.
When real hot, pour over egg yolks which have been beaten until thick. Return to double boiler; cook until thick custard.
Remove from heat and add gelatin.
Beat egg whites until stiff and dry, gradually adding another 1/2 cup of sugar.
Fold into custard and brown in oven.
Mix oil, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper over heat.
Bring to boil until sugar is melted clear.
Set aside.
Mix all vegetables together in big bowl.
Pour liquid over vegetables.
Put in refrigerator for 1 hour or longer.
Serve cold.
Stir together corn, sugar and salt.
Beat 5 eggs and mix in half and half.
Combine and mix.
Put butter and paprika on top. Cook at 350° for 1 hour.
Stir after first 15 minutes and sprinkle more paprika on top.
Grate first four ingredients and drain, reserving juice. Dissolve Knox gelatin in small amount of water to soften.
Heat drained juice in microwave, add 1/4 c. of this juice to gelatin and stir this into the mayonnaise, mix, then add to the drained vegetables.
Refrigerate until firm.
Spread over your favorite sandwich bread.
Mix gelatin by directions.
Place in refrigerator and let thicken, but not gel.
Mix strawberries, sugar, salt and pecans by hand.
Place in refrigerator and let chill.
Thaw frozen raspberries and strain through a sieve.
Mix with fruit juices, tea, crushed pineapple and sugar. Pour over block of ice.
Just before serving, add sparkling water.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold tomato juice; soften, then add hot tomato juice.
When dissolved add 3/4 cup cold tomato juice, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, sugar and salt.
Chill until slightly thickened and add chopped pickles, celery and onion.
Fills a ring mold.
Combine tomatoes, onion and bacon drippings in a pot.
Bring to a boil.
Add Worcestershire sauce, Texas Pete, garlic salt and salt and pepper.
Add okra and cook until tender.
Yields 4 servings.
Heat rolls according to package directions; cut into halves, lengthwise.
In skillet, cook sausage until lightly browned.
Pour off excess fat.
Add onion, tomato paste, water and seasonings. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Spoon mixture over bottom half of roll; top with slices of cheese.
Replace top of roll.
Place in a 350° oven until cheese melts, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with oregano. Makes 2 to 4 sandwiches.
Brown hamburger and onion together. Add cooked noodles.
Mix in tomato soup and mushroom soup.
Add mushrooms and peas. Sprinkle with the cheese and bake in casserole for 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
In medium-size bowl, combine lemon juice, onions, chiles, 4 tablespoons oil and black pepper.
Stir well to mix.
Put chicken in marinade; let soak.
Prepare rice according to package instructions to allow chicken time to marinate.
When rice is complete, set aside.
Put 1 tablespoon of oil in a skillet.
Heat on low setting.
Brown chicken on both sides; remove.
Pour water in boiler, add browned chicken and remaining marinade.
Cook for about 20 to 25 minutes.
Add water, if necessary.
Serve over rice.
Relatively low-fat dish, depending on oil used, 24 g fat per serving.
Serves 6.
Bake cake according to box directions in sheet cake pan. While cake bakes, boil pineapple with sugar until syrupy.
When cake is done, poke holes in cake with wooden spoon handle.
Make a lot of holes.
Pour hot pineapple mix over top and spread to cover cake.
Cool completely.
When cake is cold, mix pudding mix with 3 cups of milk.
Let set enough to spread over entire cake.
Mix whipped topping with coconut and cover cake.
Refrigerate.
Cake is better if made 24 hours before serving.
Combine milk, salt, pepper, butter, sugar, eggs, cheese and onion in blender.
Grease casserole dish and pour in sauce.
Drain macaroni and add.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Set casserole in pan of water while baking (keeps casserole moist).
Serves 6.
Cream butter
and
sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix small amount
of
flour with fruits and nuts.
Add flour, soda, spices and milk to creamed mixture.
Add fruits and nuts.
Drop by teaspoon
on
greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
This makes a big batch.
Grease and flour a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish or pan.
Spoon pie filling over cake.
Mix together sugar and melted margarine. Crumble mixture over pie filling.
You will see the magic when the cake is done.
Bake as directed on cake box.
Beat eggs until foamy; add oil, sugar, vanilla and zucchini. Add all dry ingredients.
Blend well; add nuts and blueberries. Spoon into muffin tins.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
I like to use 2 1/2-inch bake cups.
Fill 3/4 full.
Makes 2 dozen.

Saut mushrooms in butter. Slice in thin strips the chicken and brown with mushrooms and butter. Add yogurt and cream cheese. Turn heat to simmer and add spices. Simmer 20 minutes, then add Parmesan cheese. Serve over brown rice.

Saute onions in melted butter a few minutes. Add livers and saute 3 to 5 minutes, depending on the size of the livers. Bruise sage. Add along with the salt, lemon juice, Port and pepper. Cook slowly about 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Correct seasoning and serve on toast or with crackers.
Mix graham crackers and oleo.
Press into cookie sheet.
Put in 350° oven for 10 minutes, turning with spatula.
Mix cream cheese, milk, powdered sugar and Dream Whip.
Beat until stiff. Add vanilla to cream cheese mixture.
Pour this over graham cracker crumbs.
Top with strawberry or cherry pie filling.
Set in refrigerator until firm.
Best to let set overnight.
Place crumbled bacon in pastry shell. Cover with onion. Slightly beat eggs with milk and pepper. Stir in kraut and cheese, saving enough to sprinkle over top.
Pour over bacon and onion. Top with cheese. Bake 45 minutes at 375°.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a bowl; beat at medium speed of electric mixer until smooth.
Stir in 1/2 cup of Swiss cheese, Parmesan cheese and next 3 ingredients.
Spread cheese mixture evenly over toast slices; sprinkle evenly with remaining 1/2 cup Swiss cheese.
Broil for 1 1/2 minutes or until Swiss cheese melts.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Yield:
16 servings.
Separate egg yolks from whites; set whites aside.
Mix sugar, flour, egg yolks, milk, vanilla, butter and salt in a boiler (that will not stick) over medium heat.
Beat egg yolks before adding to flour mixture.
Bring to boil, stirring often.
Continue cooking until it is as thick as you like.
Lay vanilla wafers in bottom of medium casserole dish.
Slice bananas and arrange them on top of wafers.
Pour pudding on top of wafers and bananas.
Chill until thickened.
Whip egg whites and 1/2 cup sugar until stiff.
Spread on top of finished pudding.
Bake until brown.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Add eggs one at a time; beat well.
Sift together the self-rising and cake flours.
Add flour and milk alternately.
Add vanilla.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Makes 3 layers.
Core and quarter pears. Core and cut apple into wedges.
Peel and slice oranges.
Arrange fruit on platter lined with salad greens.
Grease and flour 3-qt. casserole.
Melt 2 sticks butter with with 1/3 c. cocoa, then cool.
In second bowl, beat sugar and eggs until creamy.
Add flour and pecans.
Add the cooled cocoa mixture to the sugar mixture and add vanilla.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 35 minutes.
Spread marshmallow cream on hot cake as soon as it is removed from the oven.
While the cake is baking, prepare icing by melting the remaining butter, cocoa and milk, the add powdered sugar.
Nuts are optional.
Pour icing over the marshmallow cream.

recipes.t: Baked Cauliflower And Broccoli Au Gratin
d: Cut broccoli and cauliflower into bite size pieces.
Steam until tender, drain.
Place vegetables in an 8 1/2 x 11-inch baking dish.
Scald 1 1/2 cups milk in saucepan.
Add pepper and 2 tablespoons butter.
Pour remaining 1/2 cup milk into a jar; add flour.
Cover and shake until smooth.
Pour flour mixture into hot milk, stirring constantly.
Cook over low heat until mixture thickens.
Add cheese; mix well.
Pour sauce over vegetables; top with bread crumbs and wheat germ.
Dot with remaining butter and paprika.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Serves 6 to 8.
Place vegetables (uncooked) on bottom of casserole dish. Pound chicken to 1/4-inch thickness and place on top of vegetables.
Mix mayonnaise, soup and cheese.
Spread on top of chicken.
Sprinkle with Italian bread crumbs.
Bake 1 hour at 375°.
In a large skillet, heat oil; add chops and pan braise, turning chops so that both sides are lightly browned.
Cook until done.
Pare and slice potatoes.
When chops are done, add potatoes over the top of the chops.
Sprinkle on the green peppers.
Pour in the tomatoes.
The lemon slices go on top of all other ingredients.
If necessary, add a little water to cover potatoes. Cover skillet and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cut rounds from bread (2 per slice) and brush with butter on one side.
Toast on buttered side.
Place a mushroom on untoasted side.
Mix remaining ingredients and put a teaspoon of mixture on each mushroom.
Place under broiler until it puffs.
Serve at once.
Yields 32 puffs.
In a large skillet, brown beef and onion; drain.
Add all ingredients except rice and cheese.
Cover and bring to a full boil.
Add rice; reduce heat, cover and simmer 5 minutes. Sprinkle cheese to cover and melt.
Cook asparagus to desired tenderness.
Drain on paper towel, cover and refrigerate.
