Mash cooked egg yolk with raw egg yolk and mustard in a small bowl until smooth.
Slowly whisk in oil until smooth.
Add vinegar, salt and pepper to oil mixture, blending well.
Spoon mustard sauce over asparagus and garnish with egg white.
Mash the garlic cloves and finely chop the peppers.
Melt butter in the pot where you wish to cook rice.
Briefly saute the garlic and green pepper in melted butter.
Add the rice and saute a bit longer on medium heat.
Add the boiling water to the rice little by little.
Stir and add salt to taste.
When the water evaporates lower the heat and cover.
When rice is cooked, add peas and fluff with a fork.
Serve hot.
Combine apples in medium bowl.
Transfer 1/3 of apples to heavy medium sauce pan.
Add 1/2 cup water, sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, ginger and lemon peel.
Stir mixture over medium heat until sugar dissolves.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add half of remaining apples and 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes, stirring mixture occasionally.
Add all remaining apples and remaining 1/2 cup water.

Cover and simmer until all apples are tender, stirring occasionally and adding more water by 1/4 cupfuls if applesauce seems too dry, about 10 minutes longer. Can be prepared up to one day ahead. Cover and refrigerate.
Makes about 2 1/2 cups.
Blend
margarine,
brown sugar, white sugar and flour to crumbs and
reserve
cup for the top.
To the remainder, add sour milk, soda, cinnamon, eggs and salt.
Grease and flour 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Sprinkle 1
cup
of
chopped
pecans in pan. Pour in cake batter,
sprinkle
reserved
crumb
mix
over top. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Drain tuna.
Dice apples.
Add apples and raisins to tuna. Add mayonnaise, salt and pepper to taste.
Heat oven to 450°.
Cut shortening into flour with pastry blender until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Stir in just enough milk so dough leaves side of bowl and rounds up into a ball (too much milk makes dough sticky, not enough makes biscuits dry).
Dilute 1/2 cup Ranch dressing with milk.
Dip chicken in diluted dressing, then roll in bread crumbs.
Place on foil-lined pan and bake for 20 to 30 minutes at 375°.
To serve, use Ranch dressing as a sauce for dipping the chicken.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream the eggs, sugar, Crisco and flavorings together.
Add flour and milk; mix well.
Lightly flour and grease cake pan.
Cook for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until toothpick comes out of center clean.
Combine all except milk.
Cook on low for 6 hours.
Take out ham bone and chop up ham.
Put ham back in and add milk.
Cook 1/2 hour more.
Add more water or milk if too thick.
Stir butter and sugar together.
Add beaten eggs and mix well.
Then stir in flour, soda and vanilla.
Add oats, peanuts and chocolate bits.
Mix well but don't beat.
Drop by teaspoon on lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 12 minutes.
Mix hamburger, egg, onion and bread together.
Form into medium size balls and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Drain pineapple chunks and reserve liquid.
Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup water, then fill rest of cup with water.
Sift flour, soda and baking powder together and set aside. Cream softened oleo by hand.
Add sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Beat well after each.
Add milk and flour alternately; blend.
Add sour cream, bananas and nuts.
Do not overbeat.
Pour into greased and floured loaf pans or tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 50 to 55 minutes until it tests done with toothpick.
Very good.
Cook the first 4 ingredients all together until raisins are done, 5 to 10 minutes. Add the sugar and cornstarch.
Cook until thickened.
Let cool while making crust.
In a saucepan, heat the soup and cheese.
Stir until the cheese is melted.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add the peas and serve. Serves 8.
Brown 4 cloves of garlic and chopped onion in oil.
Remove after browning.
Pour tomatoes, parsley flakes, pepper, salt and cheese into hot oil.
Chop the other clove of garlic and stir.
Alternate layers of apples and cranberries in 13 x 9-inch casserole. Sprinkle each layer with sugar.
Melt margarine and add oats, pecans and brown sugar.
Spread over top layer and bake uncovered for 45 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Place cheese in a bowl of electric mixer; add sugar and mix well for 2 minutes.
Add Tia Maria and mix for 1 minute.
Add whipped cream and chopped strawberries; mix well using a spatula! Spoon into parfait glasses and refrigerate for 3 hours.
Decorate with fresh strawberries.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter shallow baking dish.
Arrange mushrooms in dish stemmed side down.
Melt 1/2 cup butter in small saucepan over low heat.
Increase heat to medium-high, blend in flour and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in half and half and bring to a boil.
Mix in stock and pepper and return to boil.
Pour sauce evenly over mushrooms.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and continue baking until cheese melts, 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cream butter and sugar together; add jam to egg yolks and mix together.
Add butter and sugar mixture.
Then mix all dry ingredients together.
With sour milk, fold in beaten egg whites and vanilla.
Blend all together.
Place in 3 round lined, floured cake pans sprayed with Pam.
Bake in preheated oven for 40 to 50 minutes at 350°.
Dip biscuits in butter, then in sugar and cinnamon mixture. Arrange in round pan with cinnamon sugar side up.
Place 1 apple slice between each biscuit and between each biscuit and side of pan.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
In quart glass combine water, onion, tomato paste, vinegar, garlic, chili powder, mustard and pepper until well blended. Cover with plastic wrap; microwave on High 5 minutes.
Stir and microwave uncovered 5 minutes longer.
Pour half the mixture over bottom of 12 x 8-inch microwave-safe dish.
Place drumsticks in dish and pour remaining sauce over them.
Cover with waxed paper. Microwave at Medium-high 12 minutes per pound.
Turn drumsticks often.
Mix the V-8 juice and Italian dressing together; set aside. Cut tomatoes into 1-inch pieces, enough to make 3 cups.
Cut cucumber into 1-inch pieces to make 1 3/4 cups.
Cut bell pepper into 1-inch pieces to make 1 1/2 cups.
In a large bowl, combine cut up chicken and vegetables.
Add salad dressing.
Toss well to coat chicken and vegetables.
Arrange lettuce leaves on a large serving platter.
Place salad on top.
Serve.
Serves 4.
Mix cream cheese and sugar; add coconut, cherries and nuts. Mix with hands.
Place in small dry bowl lined with Saran Wrap. Chill until firm.
Reshape and pat until round.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Garnish with cherries on top.
In skillet cover bottom of pan with oil.
Put meat in and cover completely with water.
Sprinkle all over with seasoning.
Cut up onion and pepper over meat.
Cover meat with ketchup or barbecue sauce.
May need a little water until tender.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut in margarine.
Stir in 1 1/3 cups milk.
Roll out half of dough 1/4 inch thick.
Fit into bottom of 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan. Cover with a layer of sliced ham, then a layer of sliced cheese. Mix eggs, mustard, Parmesan cheese and 2 cups milk.
Pour over ham and cheese.
Roll out remaining dough and place on top.
Make a few slits in the top crust.
Brush top with milk.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve.
May be frozen and reheated.
Line 12 muffin cups with paper liners.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the milk, butter or margarine, egg, vanilla and almond extract.
Mix until just moistened.
Half fill the muffin cups with batter. Spoon 1 teaspoon raspberry preserves into the center. Top with remaining batter.
Place blanched whole almonds on top of batter.
Press in lightly.
Sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 400° for 12 to 20 minutes until golden. Cool 5 minutes and remove from pan.

recipes.t: Escalopes De Veau A La Moutarde
d: Place the scaloppine on a flat surface and pound with a flat metal meat pounder or the bottom of a clean skillet.
Blend the flour with salt and pepper and dredge the scaloppine on all sides. Heat the butter in a large heavy skillet until it is quite hot but not brown.
Add the scaloppine (note that they shrink as they cook).
Cook quickly until golden, for about 2 minutes, on one side and turn.
Cook until golden on the other side.
Remove the scaloppine to a warm dish and keep warm and covered with foil.
Add the shallots to the skillet and cook briefly, stirring.
Add the wine and cook, stirring, until it is almost evaporated.
Add the cream and let it boil up, stirring.
Cook about 30 seconds and turn off the heat.
Stir in the mustard.
Do not cook further.
Pour sauce over veal and serve.
Yield:
2 or 3 servings.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt; mix well.
In medium bowl, beat together milk, sour cream, egg substitute and vanilla.
Pour milk mixture over dry ingredients and mix until batter is smooth; stir in margarine.
Gently fold in blueberries and lemon zest.
Butter nonstick skillet and set over medium heat; when hot, ladle 1/2 cup batter into pan to make 6-inch pancake.
Repeat this process until all of batter has been used.

Dissolve 1 tsp. sugar in the water and sprinkle the yeast over it. Add 1 Tbsp. of sugar, stir and let stand for 10 minutes. Combine the yeast with the milk, lightly beaten eggs, salt 2 Tbsp. of sugar, oil, and 2 cups of sifted flour. Beat until smooth. Cover and let rise in a warm place until light and bubbly, about 1 hour. Mix in enough flour to make a light but slightly sticky dough, then knead in bowl until smooth and elastic. Now form dough into a bowl and very lightly oil dough enough to cover the whole dough ball. Cover bowl of dough with a warm damp dish towel, lightly damp only. Let rise in warm place until it doubles in size. Punch down and allow dough to rise again slightly.
Beat egg yolks slightly.
Stir in pancake mix and corn.
Fold in slightly beaten egg whites.
Drop by teaspoonfuls into hot oil. Fry until golden brown.
Drain.
Serve with syrup.
Makes about 40.
Cream together shortening, sugar and vanilla.
Add eggs, beating well.
Mix together dry ingredients and stir into creamed mixture.
Add dates or raisins and nuts.
Divide into 4 portions. On a greased cookie sheet, spread each portion in 12 x 2 1/2 x 1/2-inch strips (about 3-inches apart).
Bake in 375° oven about 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Brown hamburger and add onion, chili and Worcestershire sauce, soup and water.
Drain beans and spread over hamburger.
Put cheese on top of beans.
While this mixture is coming to a boil, add milk and egg as directed on the Jiffy muffin mix.
Mix just until moist and pour over top of meat mixture.
Turn on low or simmer and cook for 25 minutes, covered (don't peek!).
During the 25 minutes of cooking, toss together a green salad and your meal is complete.
Brown sausage in bacon drippings; add onion and green pepper. Saute.
Stir in tomato paste and water; add rice and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer on low for 45 minutes or until rice is done.
In small bowl, combine 2 teaspoons soy sauce with the cornstarch; add chicken and toss to coat.
Wipe
mushroom
caps with damp cloth.
In a large bowl, combine
crumbs,
garlic,
parsley, paprika and melted butter. Add coarsely
chopped
lobster meat.
Stuff caps and place in buttered baking dish.
Bake at 425° until heated through for 8 to 10
minutes.
Serve
with lemon wedges and a sprinkling of chopped parsley.
In medium mixing bowl mix granola, dried fruit, peanuts and chocolate pieces.
Store in container.
Makes about 4 cups.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, sugar and cream of tartar. Cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Make a well in center.
Add milk, onions and parsley.
Stir until dough clings together.
On a lightly floured surface, knead dough gently 10 to 12 times.
Roll dough 1/2-inch thick.
Cut dough with 1 1/2-inch cutter.
Cook on ungreased pan at 450° for 6 to 8 minutes. Half biscuits, then split halves.
Put filling in biscuits.
Makes 24 to 28 appetizers.
Combine pecans, 1/4 cup sugar and cinnamon; set aside. Combine oleo and 1 cup sugar; cream to light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, bananas and vanilla; stir in sour cream.
Combine remaining dry ingredients; add to creamed mixture and stir just enough to mix.
Sprinkle 1/2 of reserved cinnamon mixture into bottom of well greased Bundt pan; spoon in 1/2 of batter.
Sprinkle rest of cinnamon mix and add rest of batter.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until done.
Cool 5 minutes on wire rack before turning out.
Scald peaches and tomatoes in boiling water in saucepan. Remove skins and cut into pieces.
Combine with sugar in large, heavy saucepan.
Cook for 3 hours or to desired consistency, stirring frequently with wooden spoon.
Put potatoes in pan; cover with water.
Cook 5 minutes.
Remove from heat; drain.
Melt margarine.
Mix 2 tablespoons with crumbs. Add flour and seasonings to remaining margarine.
Gradually stir in milk, blending until smooth.
Cook until thick and bubbly.
Layer potatoes and sauce in a casserole dish.
Sprinkle crumbs on top; garnish with parsley.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, or until tender.
Cook and drain cauliflower.
Melt butter; stir in basil.
Pour over cauliflower; toss lightly.
Add cheese; toss lightly until cauliflower is coated.
Sprinkle bread crumbs over cauliflower.
Brown ground chuck.
Boil egg noodles.
Chop green pepper and onion.
When meat is brown and noodles are done, pour into large Dutch oven.
Set on medium high.
Add green pepper, onion, tomato juice and cream of mushroom soup.
When mixture is boiling, start slicing cheese and add to mixture.
When cheese has melted, it's ready to serve.
Great with salad and garlic bread.
Cook beans in salted water.
They must remain firm.
Cook potatoes with skin in salt water.
Dice bacon and cook until crisp.
Peel potatoes and slice.
Drain beans and add to potatoes. Add parsley, onions, bacon and fat (as much as you like).
Pour vinegar in pan to loosen scrapings, reduce, add to salad.
Combine water, 2 cups of white flour, yeast and sugar.
Beat with mixer at low speed for 3 minutes.
Cover and let rise until double (30 minutes).
Dough will be spongy.
Stir in wheat flour, dry milk, oats, butter, honey and salt.
Mix. Add nuts and mix in as much white flour as you can with a spoon.
Knead on a floured surface and add remaining flour to make a fairly stiff dough (6 to 8 minutes).
Shape in bowl.
Place in greased bowl; turn once. Cover and let rise until double (30 to 45 minutes).
Mix together all ingredients, except sugar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Then shape small amounts in little balls, shaped like strawberries.
Dip bottom of the shaped strawberry in the green sugar and top top in the red sugar.
Cover well.
These store well in refrigerator over a long period of time.
Brown meat and drain fat.
Add sauce.
Place half of noodles in a 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with half of the cottage cheese, half of the Mozzarella cheese and half of meat mixture. Repeat layers and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Mix raisins and rum in bowl.
Set aside.
Stir 1 teaspoon sugar in warm milk and sprinkle with yeast.
Let stand 5 minutes or until the surface is frothy.
Stir gently to moisten any dry particles remaining to top.
Sift flour and salt into large bowl. Melt butter, cool slightly.
In medium bowl, mix remaining sugar, butter, eggs, and lemon peel.
Stir in yeast mixture.
Pour into flour mixture, combining to make a soft dough.
On floured surface, knead dough 5 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size-about 30 minutes. Grease loaf pan. Knead raisin and rum mixture into a loaf shape and place in greased loaf pan.
Let stand in a warm place for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brush loaf with egg yolk.
Bake 40-45 minutes or until loaf sounds hollow when tapped.
Brown turkey and sausage; drain excess liquid.
Combine cooked meat with rest of ingredients and simmer until flavors blend.
This is a very spicy chili!
If you prefer less spicy taste, use 1/2 can Ro-Tel and less of chili seasoning.

Place orange slices in a bowl. Combine honey and cloves; pour over oranges. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Discard cloves. Arrange greens on salad plates. Top with orange and banana slices.
Drizzle with honey mixture. Sprinkle with coconut. Yield: 2 servings.
Saute onions, ground beef and celery.
Combine all ingredients in a baking dish.
Bake one hour at 350°.
Five minutes before end of baking time, place Chinese noodles on top.
Place pudding in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Gradually stir in milk.
Cook full power 6 to 8 minutes or until pudding boils and is thickened.
Stir 2 to 3 times while cooking.
Add marshmallows. Heat full power 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes or until marshmallows melt.
Stir halfway through heating time.
Cover with wax paper and chill.
Whip cream until stiff in small bowl.
Fold into cooled pudding.
Slice bananas into pie crust.
Pour filling over bananas.
Chill several hours before serving.
May top with whipped cream.
Saute potatoes in small amount of oil until tender.
Add onions, reserving some of green tops for garnish.
Cook until onions are tender.
Add eggs and scramble all together.
Season to taste.
Drain juice from pineapple and add water to make 2 1/2 cups. Bring to boil.
Add to jello and stir until dissolved.
Cool for 10 minutes.
Add mayonnaise.
Cool 5 more minutes.
Mix mayonnaise real well.
Put in refrigerator until it starts to thicken, then add pineapple, cottage cheese and nuts.
Put in oblong 13 x 9-inch pan or loaf pan.
Chop cabbage and onion.
Steam fry with margarine, 2 or 3 ounces of water, salt, pepper and garlic.
Cook noodles are directed on package.
Cut bacon into pieces and fry for bacon chips.
Mix together with cottage cheese and serve.
Combine beaten egg yolks, sugar and melted margarine.
Add pineapple.
Beat whipped cream.
Layer with vanilla wafers, like a banana pudding.
Top with whipped cream.
Sprinkle nuts on top. Refrigerate.
Beat oleo with brown sugar.
Add egg white and beat.
Mix in dry ingredients along with yogurt and vanilla.
Fold in dates and nuts.
Drop on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° to 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Frost if desired.
Makes 40.
Mix in heavy saucepan the sugar, flour and salt (cocoa for chocolate).
Measure milk.
Add enough milk to make smooth paste. Beat in 3 egg yolks.
Add remainder of milk and 1/2 stick of oleo. Cook over high heat, stirring constantly, until thick. Remove from heat and add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
(Then 1/2 cup coconut or 1 small sliced banana or 1/2 small can crushed pineapple, well drained.)
Beat until smooth and creamy.
Pour into baked shell and add meringue.
You can also caramelize 1/4 cup of the sugar at the first to make caramel pie.
Butter 9 x 12-inch pan.
Combine chilies and sour cream. Layer rice, cheese and sour cream mixture.
Start and end with rice.
Top with Cheddar cheese and cover with foil.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In small bowl combine sugars and 1/2 teaspoon orange peel; set aside.

Reserve 1 teaspoon margarine; separate biscuits and brush tops with remaining margarine. Sprinkle tops with the brown sugar mixture, about 1 teaspoon. Arrange biscuits into a loaf by holding 1 biscuit on its side and gently pressing the sugared side against the unsugared side of another biscuit; repeat procedure, using all the biscuits. Carefully transfer loaf to a nonstick loaf pan and brush top with reserved teaspoon margarine.
Bake until loaf is lightly browned, about 35 minutes.
Transfer loaf from pan to wire rack and let cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Pour a little tomato juice in blender with your peppers; chop fine.
Add the rest of the ingredients and blend lightly.
Cook linguini according to package directions; drain.
In separate bowl, combine hot water and peanut butter.
Stir in soy sauce, vinegar, scallions, garlic, sugar and red pepper; mix well. Combine drained pasta with sauce; toss well.
Serve hot or at room temperature.
Grease and flour Bundt pan or three small loaf pans. Sprinkle some of the pecans on bottom of pan. Mix all ingredients except frosting.
Beat two minutes. Fold in frosting. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Blend together graham cracker crumbs and butter; press into buttered 12 x 9 x 1 1/2 pan.

Into mixer, add powdered sugar, eggs, soft margarine, vanilla and rum extract; beat for 5 minutes. Spread over crust and chill, then slice bananas lengthwise over cream mixture. Drain pineapple and spread over bananas.
Whip Dream Whip; spread on top and garnish with nuts and cherries.
Brown chicken in oil, about 10 minutes.
Spread cans of cream of mushroom soup in
13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Layer cans of English peas over soup.
Top with chicken pieces, placing a bay leaf under each one.
Bake for 1 1/2 to 2 hours (covered) until chicken is done and sauce is thick.

In a skillet, cook beef and onion over medium heat until meat is no longer pink. Drain. Add water and seasonings. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Yield: 2 1/2 cups.
Put candy and cookies in separate bags.
Crush with rolling pin until both are fine crumbs.
Mix into whipped cream.
Place mixture into an ice cube tray.
Freeze.
Cut into small squares to serve. Serves 8.
Mix nuts, coconut and jello together.
Pour Eagle Brand milk over and mix.
Form into strawberry shape.
Roll in red sugar crystals.
Dip end in green for stem.
Refrigerate until serving.
Measure rice and place into boiling water for 6 minutes. Measure milk and heat with vanilla until boiling.
Measure sugar. Whip cream.
Place mold into fridge.
Put rice in milk and simmer 20 minutes.
Add sugar and simmer 5 minutes.
Soften gelatin in cold water and whip into hot rice.
Place in fridge.
When cool and thick, add whipped cream and put in mold.
Garnish with fruit. Serves 8 to 10.
Mix altogether and bring to a boil.
Boil until mixture is boiled
down by half.
Remove from heat, leave cinnamon and whole cloves
in, cool and leave in refrigerator.
Melt butter in a 3 quart saucepan.
Saute onions until tender. Add shrimp and cook until shrimp turns pink.
Add green chilies. Add soups, cream cheese and creole seasonings.
Heat over medium heat until cream cheese melts and blends in.
Put 1/3 cup mixture in center of each tortilla and roll up jelly roll fashion.
Place seam side down in a greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Pour any remaining filling mixture over enchiladas.
Spread evenly.
Top with shredded cheeses.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Makes 10 enchiladas.
Cut apple and orange into small bite size pieces.
Use a small can of mandarin oranges if you don't have an orange.
Chop lettuce as for a salad.
Use other fruit as available like grapes or raisins.
Toss fruits and lettuce together.
Throw in a handful of nuts and marshmallows, if you like.
Mix salad dressing, such as Miracle Whip, and milk together and pour over fruit.
Toss to coat.
Bake potatoes until done.
When cool, cut into chunks.
Melt butter in large frying pan.
Add potatoes, cheese and bacon bits. Season with salt, pepper and seasoning salt to taste.
Cook until cheese is melted.
(Great for left over baked potatoes.)
Combine chicken, lettuce, peppers and tomatoes in a large bowl. Heat tortillas by placing them one at a time in a dry skillet. Turn once until brown and puffy. To assemble:
Place a tortilla on a plate and top with some of the chicken mixture. Garnish with sour cream, salsa and cheese. Serves 6.
Heat and dissolve cheese and milk.
Add chicken, beef seasonings, butter and water.
Add broccoli and pimento.
Heat all and serve.
Chop onion and pepper; saute in oil until tender.
Add meat; stir and cook until browned.
In large bowl, place mushrooms, tomatoes, corn and 1/2 of cheese.
Cook noodles in salted water until tender; drain.
Add to mixture in bowl.
Add meat mixture; blend well.
Pour in greased 3-quart casserole dish.
Let stand 12 to 24 hours.
Cover and bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and bake uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes longer. Serves 6 to 8.
In a large skillet, saute onion in margarine until limp.
Add rice, sour cream, cottage cheese and bay leaf.
Mix together.
In a buttered casserole, put layer of rice, then a layer of chilies, and 1/2 of the grated Cheddar cheese; repeat.
Bake for 25 minutes at 375°.
Yields 8 servings.
Mix together cream cheese, margarine and flour.
Make small balls.
Put in muffin tin and work with thumb to form cup.
Fill 3/4 with filling and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine flour, salt and pepper.
Add liver; toss to coat.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet.
Add onion and peppers; cook until crisp-tender.
Remove from pan; set aside. Add remaining oil to the skillet.
Cook and stir liver for 5 to 7 minutes, or until no pink remains.
In a small bowl, combine beef broth, soy sauce and cornstarch; stir into liver.
Cook and stir constantly until sauce thickens.
Return vegetables to the skillet; cook until heated through.
Serve over rice or noodles. Serves 4 to 6.
Cream butter and sugar.
Beat in egg, molasses and dry milk. Blend in dry ingredients, mixing well.
Roll dough into balls, then in sugar.
Place on well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 minutes at 375°.
Cool.
Makes 5 dozen.
Blend together cooked beef, dry onion soup mix and cream of mushroom soup.
Add water, rice and chopped onion.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake covered for 1 hour.
Remove cover, sprinkle cheese on top.
Broil a few minutes until cheese melts.
Cream sugar and shortening and add eggs one at a time.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt together.
Add flour mixture alternately with milk.
Add flavorings.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Fry hamburger with chopped onion.
Put in cake pan. Add milk and soup. Mix all together and spread in the pan. Put Tater Tots on top and sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Boil zucchini for 5 minutes; drain.
Mix grated carrot, chopped onion, sour cream, celery soup and seasonings with zucchini in a 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Mix stuffing flavor package with dry stuffing; sprinkle on top of dish contents.
Spread evenly (do not stir in).
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
In large bowl, combine milk and boiling water; let cool to about 110°F.
Stir in yeast and let stand until dissolved.
Stir in whole wheat flour, 1 cup of the all-purpose flour and the sourdough starter; beat until smooth and elastic (about 5 minutes).
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let stand in a warm place until mixture is very bubbly and spongy looking (about 1 hour).
Sift dry ingredients until well blended.
Combine beaten eggs, egg nog and melted butter.
Add to dry ingredients.
Mix until moistened.
Pour into a 9 x 5 x 3-inch greased pan or 2 smaller pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours for one loaf; 45 minutes for 2 loaves; or until done.
Stir together dry ingredients; reserve. Cream together butter and sugar. Add eggs to creamed mixture, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flour mixture to creamed mixture alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour. Add vanilla. Stir in sauerkraut and nuts.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch pan and bake in preheated 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes. Cool. Frost with Whipped Caramel Frosting.
Gradually add sugar to milk.
When well blended, add vanilla. Mix to a smooth rich ball.
Shape into balls and roll in tinted coconut (red and green).
Use to stuff dates.
Crush garlic. Mix with olive oil in small bowl. Add salt and pepper; set aside.
Melt butter in heavy small saucepan over low heat.
Place mustard in bowl. Whisk in lemon juice.
Gradually whisk in butter. Add chopped chives.
Season with pepper.
Place apples, raisins and water in baking dish.
Mix flour, sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Cut in margarine until crumbly. Sprinkle over apples.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Sprinkle with marshmallows.
Broil until brown.
Combine first 5 ingredients in food processor.
Blend on high until chocolate pieces are smooth.
Pour into 6 pots de creme or demitasse cups.
Chill until firm.
Garnish with fruit, dollop of whipped cream and/or chocolate shavings.
Serve with petite, elegant cookies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a loaf pan.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add banana and egg, mixing well.
In a separate bowl, sift the flour, baking soda and salt.
Stir creamed mixture into the flour mixture (add nuts, cherries or fruit, if you like). Pour half of batter into the pan.
Lay the banana in the batter; cover with remaining batter.
Bake about 1 hour, until golden brown.
Combine ingredients, mixing well.
Refrigerate several hours. Serve with chips, crackers or raw vegetables.
Makes 4 cups.
Rinse and pat dry chicken.
Mix all ingredients, except scallions and cilantro.
Rub chicken with some of the sauce.
Chop scallions in 2-inch lengths.
Stuff scallions and cilantro in cavity.
Pour in the rest of the sauce.
Roast at 300° for 1 hour and 45 minutes or until juices run clear when poked.
Serve with rice.
Serves 4.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, 1 at a time; beat well after each addition.
Sift dry ingredients together; combine brandy and cream.
Add dry ingredients and brandy-cream mixture alternately to margarine mixture, beginning and ending with dries. In a small bowl, combine mincemeat and 2 tablespoons flour until blended.
Fold into batter.
Spoon batter into greased and floured 9-inch tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes, until cake is golden brown.
Cool in pan 10 minutes.
Turn cake out onto dish.
Scald chocolate drink; remove from heat and add hot coffee. Whip the cream with sugar.
Add 1/2 of whipped cream to chocolate and coffee and whisk until frothy.
Serve hot, topped with remainder of whipped cream.
Sift together flour and sugar.
Cut butter in; knead thoroughly.
Add one egg; knead again.
Let stand, covered, in icebox for 1 hour.
Roll out as thin as possible on floured board; cut with round cutter.
Put a little beaten egg on middle of each cookie.
Add a few thin slices of almond; sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon mixed.
Bake in medium oven until light brown.
Peel and devein shrimp.
Combine shrimp, Five Spices, ginger, egg and cornstarch in blender and puree.
Spoon mixture onto bread and smooth out until it is 1/4-inch thick.
Heat pan of oil about 1/2-inch to 350°.
Put bread in, shrimp side down, until done, about 2 minutes.
Cut bread corner to corner.
Serve with sweet and sour sauce.
Boil sugars, syrup and milk together to firm ball stage.
Take from stove, add butter and vanilla.
Let cool.
Add peanut butter and beat until smooth.
Pour into buttered plate or pan.
Melt butter; add brown sugar, egg and vanilla.
Beat until creamy; add soda and salt and mix until blended.
Add remaining ingredients.
Drop by spoon on cookie sheet and bake for 10 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Award Winning Peaches And Cream Pie(This Has An Unusual Crust.)
d: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease sides and bottom of a 10 inch deep-dish pie pan.
Mix together flour, salt, baking powder and pudding mix.
Mix in butter, egg, and milk.
Beat for 2 minutes now pour this mixture into pie pan.
Arrange sliced peach slices on top of pudding mixture.
In a small mixing bowl, beast cream cheese until fluffy, add 1/2 cup sugar and 3 tablespoon reserve peach syrup, beat for 2 minutes.
Spoon mixture over peaches to within 1 inch of pan edge.
Mix together 1 tablespoon sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and sprinkle over top.
Use Freestone Peaches in heavy syrup.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden brown.
Chill and serve.
Mix
together the ham, celery, pecans, olives and onion in a large
bowl.
Stir
in
the
mayonnaise and chili sauce. Placing the stem down on a board, cut each tomato about 2/3 of the way down into 8 wedges.
Gently push wedges open to allow space
for stuffing.
Place
each
tomato
on a lettuce lined plate
and stuff with ham salad.
Garnish plates with parsley. Makes 4 servings.
Mix Cool Whip and softened cream cheese with sugar.
Stir in pineapple.
Spread on cake and top with coconut.
Mix flour, margarine, pecans and sugar.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan or two 9-inch pie pans for 20 minutes at 350°. Cool.
Peel, seed and dice cucumbers.
Sprinkle cucumbers with salt. Let stand for 15 minutes.
Pour off liquid.
Mash garlic in bowl with lemon juice.
Add yogurt, dill and cucumbers; mix well and chill.
Sprinkle with olive oil and mint.
Serve as an appetizer or accompany with a meal.
Cook carrots slightly and drain.
Cook onion in melted margarine for 2 or 3 minutes.
Stir in flour, salt, mustard and milk.
Cook until smooth.
Add pepper and celery salt.
Layer carrots and Cheddar cheese in 2-quart casserole, beginning and ending with carrots.
Pour sauce over layers and top with bread crumbs.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for approximately 25 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Mix soup, cream cheese and jello.
Heat until blended.
Add celery, onion and green pepper.
Stir in mayonnaise and almonds. May be molded or pour into a dish as a spread.
Any combination of these vegetables may be used.
Slice vegetables or cut in 1-inch pieces.
For each pound of vegetables, use 1/2 cup corn meal, 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Mix dry ingredients and coat vegetables well.
Heat 1/4 cup oil in baking pan.
Add coated vegetables and bake at 400° until well browned (30 to 45 minutes), stirring occasionally.
Wash and dry the fish fillets.
Dip first in egg, then in almonds and last in flour, cornmeal and crumbs mixed well together. After breading, refrigerate for several hours.
When the breaded fillets have rested, fry in oil heated to 375°, turning only when browned on one side.
Remove after browning to paper towels to drain fat.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Combine berries, water and sugar in a skillet.
Bring to a boil and simmer while you make the batter mix.
Mix margarine, baking mix and buttermilk.
Drop batter, by the spoonful, over berries.
Cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Saute onion in oil or margarine.
Add ham and saute, then add rice.
Stir for a few minutes.
Add the liquids; bring to a boil. Stir.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add frozen peas.
Stir. Cover and let sit for 5 minutes, then serve.
Beat together the cottage cheese, cream cheese and milk. Blend in rest of ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate.
This is good with carrot, celery or cucumber sticks or broccoli florets and cauliflowerets.
Tear angel food cake into bite-size pieces.
Place in a 9 x 12-inch baking pan.
Beat cream cheese and butter, softened.
Add sugar and blend.
Pour over angel food cake.
Mash strawberries and pour glaze over them.
Mix well.
Pour mixture over cake. Serve.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix grated cheeses and spread evenly in buttered 10-inch pie plate.
Beat eggs; add flour slowly and then beat in half and half.
If mixture is lumpy, strain it.
Pour egg mixture over cheeses in pie plate.
Carefully spoon chiles over the surface, then spoon picante sauce over all.
Bake about 45 minutes or until center is set.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Combine cabbage and green pepper.
Mix other ingredients; pour over cabbage.
Toss to blend.
Chill.
Heat
oven
Lightly grease 12-cup fluted tube baking pan.
Place
brown
sugar, cherry halves, nuts and 1/4 cup melted
butter
in bottom of pan.
Separate dough into 20 biscuits.
In
small
bowl combine sugar, cinnamon and pumpkin pie spice.
Dip one side of each biscuit in remaining butter, then into cinnamon sugar mixture.
Place 10 biscuits, coating side down, in prepared pan, overlapping slightly.
Repeat with remaining 10 biscuits
for
second
layer.
Bake
for 40 to 50 minutes or until
golden.
Cool 2 minutes; invert onto serving plate.
Cook noodles in boiling water with 1 teaspoon salt for about 5 minutes.
Melt butter in large skillet.
Add cream, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cook over very low for only a few minutes.
Remove from heat and add drained noodles and cheese.
Mix together well and serve immediately.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.

recipes.t: Cartwright'S Coleslaw(As Served At The Trolley Bar)
d: Shred fine cabbage, carrot and onion.
Combine with mayonnaise (salad dressing won't work), sugar, salt and pimentos; mix well. Store in refrigerator at least 2 hours.
Combine carrots, onion and 1 tablespoon butter in glass dish. Microwave, covered, on High for 12 minutes or until carrots are tender.
Mix parsley flakes, lemon rind, salt, sugar and pepper in small bowl.
Add to carrots.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon butter; mix well.
Microwave, covered, on High for 2 minutes longer. Yield:
6 servings.
Dredge chicken in flour.
Cut peppers in slices.
Saute chicken in 2 tablespoons of oil until golden (5 minutes each side).
Remove from pan and keep warm.
Add 1 tablespoon oil; add peppers and saute until tender.
Add crushed garlic and saute 1 minute.
Stir in wine and vinegar, stirring to coat.
Spoon over chicken.
Serves 4.
In food processor fitted with steel blade, combine flour, sugar, sour cream, butter and orange juice.
Pulse until well mixed and a sticky dough is formed.
Remove from processor bowl to another large bowl.
Stir in dried cranberries and toasted pecans. Turn out onto well floured surface and knead lightly until no longer sticky.
Divide into two portions.
Pat each portion to a circle that is about 1/2 inch thick.
Cut each portion into 8 wedges.
Place these wedges on ungreased baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart.
Bake at 375 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brush the tops with melted butter.
Serve with jam or preserves of choice.
Combine first four ingredients in heavy saucepan; cook over medium-low heat until cheese is melted and onion is tender.
Add shrimp and heat until they turn pink.
Serve over cooked pasta.
Mix first 4 ingredients and let jell overnight.
Add layer of Cool Whip or Dream Whip.
Mix pudding according to package directions.
Spread on top of Cool Whip layer.
Sprinkle chopped nuts on top.
Put rice and consomme in a casserole dish and bake until the consomme is absorbed, about 1 hour.
Brown beef.
Put aside. Brown sausage; drain off fat.
Mix ground beef, sausage, mushrooms and pepper to taste.
Add meat mixture to the rice mixture, stirring thoroughly.
Bake at 350° until completely heated.
Combine graham cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup sugar and butter. Press into 13 x 9-inch dish.
Combine cream cheese, eggs and 3/4 cup sugar; beat until fluffy.
Spread over crust.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cool.
Sift flour and sugar together.
Stir in pecans.
Blend bananas, egg, pineapple and oil together.
Add this mixture to flour mixture.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar before serving.
Dissolve jello in 3 cups liquid using juice from your crushed pineapple and spiced grapes to make 3 cups.
Add water if not enough.
When it starts to set, add nuts, grapes and pineapple.
In a large bowl, combine tahini, yogurt, lemon juice, garlic and parsley.
In another bowl, mix stuffing with sesame seed. Coat chicken pieces with tahini mixture.
Lift out and lay meatiest side in stuffing mix.

Place pieces, crumbs up, in a single layer in a 10 x 15-inch pan. Bake in a 375° oven until meat at thigh bone is no longer pink (cut to test), about 45 minutes. Accompany with lemon wedges, salt and pepper to add to taste.
Serves 4.

Cream margarine and sugars; blend in egg and vanilla. Sift together flour, baking powder, soda and salt. Add alternately with milk. Mix well after each addition. Stir in chips, cherries and nuts. Place by teaspoon on a greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Prepare peppers and set aside.
Grind or chop soybeans coarsely and combine with onion and cooked rice. Dissolve nutritional yeast in 1/4 cup stock or water.
Add the grated Cheddar cheese to rice-soybean mixture.
Salt to taste. Fill pepper halves and place them in casserole.
Pour 1 cup of stock or water into casserole or pan around (not over) peppers. Cover and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes.
Uncover peppers and top them with Parmesan cheese and wheat germ.
Bake, uncovered, another 15 minutes or until peppers are tender.
Serves 4 to 6.
Drain fruit well.
Heat oven to 325°.
Melt butter.
Add sugar and cinnamon.
Place drained pears and peaches in casserole dish. Arrange pineapple slices on top.
Place cherries in rings of pineapple.
Pour butter-sugar mixture over top.
Bake 1 hour uncovered.
Serve warm.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook peas as directed.
Mix with rice, ham, tomatoes, chopped onion and chopped green pepper.
Mix well; season with salt and pepper.
Pour into buttered casserole and bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Cut top off each pineapple.
Scoop out the center.
Place each pineapple in an open container.
Freeze 3 hours or until cavity is slightly icy.
In a small mixer bowl, beat cream cheese until smooth.
Add 2 tablespoons of reserved syrup and the lemon peel and beat until fluffy.
Stir in fruit (cherries or strawberries) and almonds.
Fill each pineapple.
Return to freezer until filling is hardened (about 3 hours).
Just before serving, cut each pineapple into 8 slices.
Makes 16 servings.

Melt vanilla chips and chunky peanut butter in microwave. Add Rice Krispies, Spanish peanuts and mini marshmallows. Mix all together. Drop by teaspoonful on wax paper on cookie sheet. Chill in the refrigerator until hardened.
In medium saucepan, mix flour and sugar. Add beaten egg yokes and milk.
Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened. Remove from heat; add butter and vanilla.Layer pan with vanilla wafers, sliced bananas and pudding mixture.
Make meringue by beating egg whites until stiff, adding 1/4 c. sugar at the end. Top pudding with meringue.
Bake in preheated 425 degree oven for 5 minutes or until meringue is slightly browned.
Cook roast in a crock-pot; top with 2 teaspoons lemon juice and one can of stewed tomatoes while cooking.
When done, shred beef with fork.
Mix dry cake mix with margarine and 1 egg.
Pat into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Combine brown sugar, granulated sugar and milk.
Stirring constantly, cook over medium heat to 228° (soft ball stage). Remove from heat and add vanilla and nuts.
Beat until mixture begins to thicken and turn opaque, about 2 minutes.
Drop quickly in patty shape from tablespoon onto buttered cookie sheet.
Makes about 30.
Whip the milk and water until thick and smooth.
Mix in the potatoes, onions, egg, salt and cayenne pepper; beat until light and fluffy.
Place in a 2-quart baking dish (well buttered).
Mix the cornflakes, Parmesan cheese and butter.
Sprinkle over the potatoes.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes or until potatoes are hot through and through.
This recipe can be put in 5 baked potato shells.
Cook dates, oleo and sugar 6 to 8 minutes; take off heat.
Add the rest of the ingredients; stir.
Pour on foil and let cool. Roll in balls in confectioners sugar, then serve.
Combine sugar, molasses and water.
Cook until it forms a soft ball in water, then add vanilla, vinegar and butter.
Cook until it turns brittle in cold water.
Pour syrup over popped corn, tossing kernels apart with a spoon.
Cook all ingredients to a soft stage and pour over popcorn and peanuts, stirring good.
Place in preheated oven at 200°, stirring every 15 minutes for 1 hour.
Remove and let cool and store in an airtight container.
Good stuff!

Preheat oven to 300°. Combine fruit and nuts with 1/4 cup flour; set aside. Cream together butter and sugar. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Mix in vanilla. Combine remaining 1 3/4 cups flour, salt and baking soda. Add to creamed mixture alternately with 1/2 cup apple juice. Start and end with flour mixture. Stir in fruit and nuts. Spoon batter into 2 (9 x 5-inch) loaf pans. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean. Cool. Makes 2 fruit cakes.
Blend potatoes, margarine, eggs, salt and sugar.
Add flour and mix thoroughly.
Finally, add yeast water to this mixture.
Place in a large covered bowl and refrigerate for several hours.
Three hours before dinner, take as much dough as needed and roll it out 1/2-inch thick.
Cut with a glass dipped in flour and arrange side by side in a slightly greased baking dish.
Butter tops lightly. Allow to stand on open countertop for 3 hours to rise.
Bake at 400° about 10 minutes.
Blend stick margarine and chocolate.
Add sugar to eggs and combine chocolate mixture.
Add flour that has been sifted with baking powder.
Stir in nuts and vanilla.
Pour in greased pan that has been dusted with cocoa or flour.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
In a bowl beat eggs and add brown sugar.
Stir in maple syrup, butter, salt and vanilla, then add nuts and cranberries.
Pour filling into pie crust.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Reduce heat to 350°.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until filling is set.
Cool.
Mix in a pan the first 4 ingredients.
Slowly add 3/4 cup and 2 tablespoons of milk.
Cook slowly, stirring constantly, until thickened.
In a bowl, beat egg yolks and vanilla.
Stir in 3 tablespoons of the hot mixture.
Gradually add egg mixture to mixture in pan, stirring constantly.
Heat until almost boiling. Cool slightly.
Add fresh fruit.
Cover and refrigerate.
Serves 4.
Combine the potatoes, onion, flour, sour cream, eggs and salt. Heat the lard in a large frying pan.
Drop the potato mixture (2 heaping teaspoons per cake) into the hot lard.
With a spatula, flatten slightly to make 3-inch circles.
Fry 4 to 5 minutes, until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels.
Makes about 16 cakes.
In medium bowl, combine milk powder and sugar substitute and set aside.
In small saucepan, sprinkle gelatin over water and let stand to soften, about 1 minute; add peanut butter and cook, stirring constantly, until peanut butter is melted and gelatin is dissolved.
Pour into milk mixture and add whipped topping and sunflower seeds; using a wooden spoon, mix until thoroughly combined.
Spray 8 x 8-inch pan with Pam and pour peanut butter mixture into the pan, using a spatula to spread evenly.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.
Combine first 4 ingredients; boil 1 minute.
Cool.
In frying pan, melt margarine; add almonds, sesame seed and noodles.
Stir constantly until evenly browned; cool.
Chop cabbage and onions; mix well.
Add almond mixture; mix well.
Just before serving, toss with sugar vinegar mixture.
In skillet, saute mushrooms and onions in melted butter until tender.
Add bouillon; bring to a boil.
Add instant rice.
Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Gently fluff with fork.
Serve immediately.
Makes 6 servings.
Rub the roast with the tarragon and other herbs, pepper and salt.
Pour vinegar over the roast.
Roast in a 200° to 250° oven for 4 hours.
Mix bread crumbs, garlic powder and grated Parmesan cheese together. Roll chicken breast in dry mixture and place on a baking stone. Bake at 400° for 15-20 minutes. Serve with Ranch dressing.
Combine blueberries, apple juice and lemon juice in an 8-quart stainless steel or enamel saucepan.
Place over high heat; stir until mixture comes to a boil.
Add honey, cinnamon and cloves. Continue stirring.
When mixture comes to a full boil again, begin timing for approximately 20 to 30 minutes.
Jam is ready when it is thick, jam like and sticks slightly to the bottom of the pan. Pour into hot, scalded half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Seal.
Process in a simmering water bath for 10 minutes.
Makes 4 half pints.

recipes.t: Pork Chops With Mushroom Pan Gravy
d: In 10-inch skillet cook bacon and onions over med. high heat, stirring occasionally, until browned (8 to 10 min).
Add pork chops, arranging bacon and onions on top of pork chops.
Cover; continue cooking for 10 minutes or until browned.
Turn pork chops. Reduce heat to med.
Cover; cook until pork chops are tender (10 to 15 minutes).
Place pork chops on platter; keep warm while preparing gravy.
In same skillet with drippings, brown particles, bacon and onions add remaining ingredients except half and half., mushrooms and rice.
Cook over med heat, stirring occasionally, until smooth and bubbly (1 min.)
Stir in half and half and mushrooms.
Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until mixture is thickened (8 to 10 minutes).
Serve gravy over rice or noodles and pork chops.
Fry diced bacon until brown and crisp.
Remove bacon from pan and set aside.
Saute onion and potatoes in bacon drippings.
Add corn, broth (herbal brand okay) and seasonings.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Then stir in whipping cream and bacon. Heat through and serve.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and baking soda together; add the chopped nutmeats.
Set aside.
Cream together the shortening and sugar until light and fluffy; add the eggs and bran.
Combine bananas, water and vanilla and add to the creamed mixture alternately with the dry ingredients.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans and let stand for 30 minutes.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes.
When done, let cool in pans for 5 minutes, then turn onto board or cake rack to cool.
Stir together sugar, corn syrup and milk.
Put in skillet and cook on stove top.

Cook mixture, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, for approximately 30 minutes on medium heat or until you can drop some of mixture into a cup of water and it can be formed into a ball without being very sticky to fingers.
When ready, remove from heat and put in peanut butter, margarine or butter and vanilla.
Beat quickly until all ingredients are mixed.
Mixture will start to set up quickly.
Before it sets up, pour it into a buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Let cool.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease 9-inch pan.
In medium pan, combine the first 3 ingredients.
Stir in cranberries.
Heat to a boil; reduce heat.
Simmer 5 minutes or until cranberries pop open.
Stir in pears.
Pour into pan.
Combine flour and 1/2 cup of sugar.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in oats; mix well.
Add egg, mixing until moist.
Crumble over fruit.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until top is golden brown.
Pour 1 cup boiling water over chopped dates, baking soda and chopped apples.
Mix well and cool.
Cream together margarine, sugar and eggs; add vanilla.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with date mixture.
Bake in greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Roll bread dough out on greased pizza pan or cookie sheet. Brush with olive oil. Crush garlic and brush onto oiled dough (I use 2 cloves).
Sprinkle with Mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until puffed and brown. Serve with pizza sauce. Tastes just like Little Caesar's Crazy Bread!
Saute onion and mushrooms.
Brown ground beef.
Cook Ro-Tel or Old El Paso sauce until it thickens a little bit; then cut up cheese and add.
When cheese is melted, add onion and mushroom mixture.
Drain ground beef and add.
Mix well and serve.
Remove the skin from the swordfish and cut into 1 1/2 to 2-inch cubes.
Cut peppers into 2-inch squares.
Cut tomatoes into 1/2-inch sections, discarding seeds and letting any juice run off. Slice lemons into 1/4-inch thick disks and then into half moon shapes.
In large saucepan, cook onion in butter until tender.
Add juice and remaining ingredients, except fish.
Bring to a boil; stir to separate beans.
Cook 5 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Add fish and cook 10 minutes more or until fish is done.
Makes about 6 cups (4 servings).
Melt chocolate morsels in the Eagle Brand milk. Add nuts and flavoring. Drop by teaspoons onto greased cookie sheet.
Brown beef, onion, green pepper and add spices.
Add the gravy, beans and macaroni.
Pour mixture into baking dish and bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Stir, then top with cheese and bake 10 more minutes.
Cook macaroni according to directions and drain.
Mix dressing, milk, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Add all ingredients together.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Combine pears, raisins, 3 tablespoons brown sugar, cinnamon and vanilla in a medium bowl.
Mix gently. Transfer to a 9 x 12-inch baking pan.
Combine oats, remaining brown sugar, flour, margarine and honey in a bowl.
Mix with a fork until margarine is evenly distributed.
Mixture will be crumbly.
Spoon on top of pear mixture.
Bake for 45 minutes or until browned.
Allow to cool slightly before serving.
Serve warm or chilled.

Mix pudding and sugar substitute in a large mixing bowl. Add the canned milk and vanilla. Mix well. Continue adding skim milk. Stir well. Pour the mixture into freezer container and add milk until almost full. Freeze according to manufacturer's directions.
Cut rolls in half lengthwise and remove most of the soft center bread from both top and bottom halves.
(Dry these crumbs and use in other cooking.)
Mix all other ingredients in a large bowl.
Fill centers of rolls with cheese mixture, replacing tops on bottoms.
Place roll in a wax paper sandwich bag and twist top of bag closed or wrap roll in waxed paper, twisting ends tightly to seal.
Do not use plastic bags or wrap.
Place as many as desired in a brown paper bag and heat in a 350° oven for about 20 minutes.
Store unused rolls in refrigerator or freezer.
When wanted, just place in a brown bag for oven.
No defrosting required.
Do not heat in microwave; it makes them soft instead of crunchy.
Melt margarine in large pan.
Brown minced garlic in margarine. Remove from heat and stir in half and half, heat through.
Stir in Parmesan cheese and melt.
Stir in parsley.
Stir in tomato and heat through.
Stir in cooked and drained cavetelli.
Serve with a little parsley sprinkled on top for garnish.
In a glass bowl, combine water, onion, salt and rosemary. Bring just to boiling, just about 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in rice. Cover tightly and let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork.
Stir in cheese, evaporated milk and eggs.
Add vegetables.
Bake, uncovered, in a flat casserole dish for 9 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Stew chicken; debone.
Reserve 2 cups of broth.
Place chicken pieces in bottom of large casserole dish.
Mix together soups, melted margarine and sour cream.
Pour over chicken and cover with Stove Top stuffing mix, including seasoning packet.
Pour 2 cups chicken broth over the layered casserole.
Cover; cook 40 minutes at 350°.
Uncover and bake 20 minutes.
Boil enough water for 1 cup of grits.
To hot water, add onion flakes, parsley flakes, butter and soy sauce; cook for 1 minute. Add seasoned salt and grits.
Cook with top on boiler on very low heat, stirring occasionally.
Add more butter, if you desire, before serving.
Brown chops; sprinkle with salt, pepper and chili powder. Mix green onions, olives, mushrooms, water and tomato sauce.
Pour over chops and cover pan.
Cook over low heat until chops are tender, approximately 1 hour.

recipes.t: Potatoes And Cabbage In Tomato Sauce(Patate E Verze Al Salsa Di Pomodori)
d: Clean
and
slice
up cabbage.
Peel and cube potatoes. Place cabbage and potatoes in large saucepan and add the rest of the ingredients.
Bring to a boil; then cook on medium heat until potatoes
are
tender,
about 45 minutes.
Stir mixture occasionally
to make sure it does not stick.
Check to see if there is enough
juice.
If potatoes and cabbage look too dry, add a little more water.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
This makes a great first course dish.
Combine the cheeses and stir; add eggs, one at a time and mix well.
Cut each pastry sheet into 3-inch strips and brush with melted butter.
Place 1 teaspoon of the filling on each strip and fold over to make a triangle.
Continue folding from side to side in the form of a triangle.
Proceed this way for the length of strip for each triangle.
Brown meat and drain well.
Add Ragu spaghetti sauce and simmer over medium heat.
Mix Ricotta, Mozzarella, egg, parsley, salt and pepper.
Layer in the following order in two 11 x 13-inch pans (good size so it doesn't cook over in oven): meat sauce, noodles, cheese mixture, then repeat layers.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add eggs, salt, soda and buttermilk. Mix thoroughly.
Add 2 cups flour and nuts.
Mix remaining 1 cup flour with candy slices and dates.
Cut candy and dates into small pieces, add to cake mixture.
Add coconut, mix thoroughly.
Pour into greased angel food cake pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 40 minutes.
Brown meats in skillet; drain.
Stir in tomatoes and gravy mix in casserole.
Add beans and molasses and onions.
Pierce sausage links with cloves.
Arrange on top of casserole and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.

Wipe eye of round with damp cloth. Make 4 knife slits and insert 1/2 clove garlic in each slit. Salt and sprinkle generously with freshly ground pepper. Flour generously. Criss-cross bacon strips and secure with toothpicks. Place roast on rack in shallow pan. Put bay leaf on bottom of pan under rack. Bake at 250° for 4 hours. Serves 6-8.

recipes.t: Honey Bread Pudding(How To Use Stale Bread Or Biscuits)
d: Toast bread cubes in oven for added flavor.
Place bread cubes in a small baking dish.
Combine the honey, butter or margarine, salt, eggs and vanilla.
Slowly stir in the milk.
Pour the mixture over the bread.
Sprinkle with the nutmeg.
Set the baking dish in a pan of hot water and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until pudding is set.
Makes 4 servings.
Place rabbit in pot; cover with water.
Add onion and bacon slices.
Bring to a boil.
Cook for about 30 minutes.
Add salt, if needed.
Cook rabbit until tender.
Remove from pot; drain. Place in hot skillet with small amount of cooking oil.
Brown quickly; place in a covered dish.
Keep warm.
Add salt, pepper, cornstarch, 1 1/2 cups water and a small amount of evaporated milk.
Serve gravy with rabbit.
Spray casserole dish with Pam.
Put uncooked rice on bottom of baking dish.
Mix all other ingredients in bowl and stir well. Reserve enough to spread over chicken.
Pour remainder over rice. Place on chicken; cover with remaining soup mix.
Cook covered at 350° for 1 hour.
Remove lid the last 15 minutes of cooking time to brown meat.
Recipe and cooking time may easily be doubled.

recipes.t: Chicken With Caper-Lemon Sauce For Two
d: Sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper.
In a 9-inch non-stick skillet, heat oil; add chicken and quickly brown, turning once (about 3 minutes each side).
Remove and keep warm.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add coconut, raisins, vanilla and nutmeg.
Add slightly beaten eggs.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to coconut/raisins mixture alternately with milk. Pour into well-greased and floured loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 1/2 hours or until center tests dry.
Let cool for a few minutes before removing from pan.
Delicious served with any hot beverage.
In a bowl, combine cheeses and cream and beat smooth.
Drop clean, dry grapes into cheese mixture.
Stir by hand to coat them. Roll in toasted nuts and chill until ready to serve.
Serves 8 to 10.
In
electric
blender,
beat avocado, consomme and onion juice at
high speed 5 seconds.
In mixing bowl, beat in cream and sour cream, salt and pepper.
Chill.
Garnish with paprika, parsley and scallions.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Melt butter; add cumin, red pepper and paprika.
Set aside.
Cut tips from wings, then cut remainder in half.
Spray two large broiling pans with nonstick cooking spray. Place wings on rack.
Bake on one side about 40 minutes, then turn and brown on second side.
Remove from oven and brush both sides with butter mixture.
Bake until crisp.
Place margarine in custard cup.
Microwave uncovered on High (100%) until melted; 30 to 45 seconds.
Stir in dill weed.
Cut potato lengthwise into fourths.
Brush cut sides with margarine mixture.
Arrange, cut sides up, on 9-inch plate.
Wrap corn in microwavable paper towel; place on plate next to potato.
Microwave uncovered on High (100%) until hot, 3 to 3 1/2 minutes.
Mix ground beef, bread crumbs, egg and 1 teaspoon of the soup mix; shape into loaf.
Place meat loaf on plate with corn and potato; sprinkle with remaining soup mix.
Cover plate with microwavable paper towel and microwave until beef is no longer pink inside, 6 to 7 minutes.
Bring to a boil the sugar, cocoa, milk and butter.
Cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat and quickly add oats, peanut butter, vanilla and nuts.
Drop by teaspoonful on waxed paper.
Let stand 1/2 hour until cool (if you can).
Melt chocolate chips.
Add other ingredients except whipped heavy cream.
Mix well with electric mixer.
Add whipped cream to chocolate mixture and pour into graham cracker crust.
Chill for 1 hour.
Place meat, onion and garlic in a 2-quart glass casserole. Cover with glass lid or wax paper.
Microwave 8 to 10 minutes on High.
Stir in broth, mushrooms and chives.
Pat shrimp dry and set aside.
Place bell pepper in center of a 12-inch microwaveable plate.
Arrange zucchini in an even layer around pepper.
Sprinkle pepper with water and cover with vented plastic wrap.
Microwave on high 5 to 6 minutes or until slightly softened.
Cut vegetables into French fries or small pieces. Dip into pancake mix, then deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Cut onions in small cubes.
Saute onion in butter until brown. Cut pork in cubes and add to onions.
Place onions and pork in large pan.
Add paprika, sauerkraut, 2 cups water and brown sugar. Bring mixture to boil, then simmer for 3 hours (6 hours in crock-pot on low setting).
Before serving, add 1/2 cup sour cream.
Place water in a 2-quart shallow casserole; microwave at High for 12 to 15 seconds.
Add bouillon granules; stir until the granules are dissolved.
Stir in seasoned salt and lemon juice. Scrub potatoes; cut into 1/2-inch slices.
Place in seasoned liquid in casserole.
Cover with heavy-duty plastic wrap; microwave at High for 14 to 16 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, stirring after every 4 minutes.
Add butter.
Cover and microwave at High for 1 minute.
Gently stir in parsley.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.

For dressing, in a food processor bowl, combine cottage cheese and catsup. Cover and process until smooth; transfer to a small mixing bowl. Stir in egg (if using), green onion, pickle relish and salt. Set aside. In a medium mixing bowl, combine chicken, celery and sweet pepper. Add dressing and toss gently to mix. To serve, divide salad among 4 lettuce-lined plates. Sprinkle with the toasted almonds. Makes 4 servings.
Layer sliced vegetables in buttered casserole.
Sprinkle oil over top and season with salt and pepper.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Should be firm, not mushy.

recipes.t: Homemade Cream Of Tomato Soup(4 To 6 Servings)
d: Put canned tomatoes, chopped onion, celery seed, sugar, bay leaf and whole clove in saucepan.
Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes. Make white sauce of butter or margarine, flour, salt, pepper and milk.
Force tomato-seasoning mixture through strainer or food mill to make tomato puree.
Stir puree slowly into white sauce and heat for 1/2 minute.
Serve immediately in hot soup bowls and garnish with croutons, parsley flakes or chopped chives.
Drain oysters, reserving 1/4 cup liquid.
Chop oysters.
In a 3-quart microwavable casserole, cook celery, onion and margarine, covered, on High power for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring once.
Stir in bread crumbs, oysters, 1/4 cup oyster liquid and pepper.
Cook, covered, 4 to 5 minutes, stirring once.
Crush 6 to 8 leaves of mint with the sugar and sprinkle it over the grapefruit segments.
Macerate in the refrigerator for several hours.
Serve in a chilled sherbet glass or goblet with a mint sprig on top.
Combine butter, frosting and corn syrup in bowl; mix well. Stir in cereal, coat well.
Press into waxed paper-lined 10 x 15-inch pan.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Spread ice cream over rice mixture.
Roll as for jelly roll.
Freeze until firm.
Thin slice from one end to the other.
Makes a tasty summer dessert.
Place acorn squash cut side down in greased shallow baking pan.
Bake in preheated moderate oven (350°) for 40 to 45 minutes or until squash is easily pierced.
Turn right side up and scoop out seeds.
Scoop out squash into bowl.
Reserve shells.
Mash squash and mix with pineapple, butter, bread, rum extract and brown sugar.
Spoon mixture into squash shells.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) oven for another 20 minutes or until lightly browned. This is delicious and it freezes well.
Prepare fresh or dry pasta (e.g. linguine).
Cut chicken in bite-size pieces and saute.
Prepare snow peas, sugar snaps or asparagus tips (just blanch crisp-tender).
Cut onions, diagonally, into 1-inch pieces.
Mix the box of oats with the glitter.
Sprinkle on sidewalk and front door steps.
The smell of the oats as well as the reflection of the glitter in the moon will make sure the reindeer stop at your house.
Cream shortening and sugar until light.
Beat in peanut butter, egg and milk.
Sift together flour, salt and soda.
Stir into creamed mixture.
Place dough on lightly floured waxed paper. Roll in 15 x 8 x 1/4-inch rectangle.
Melt chocolate bits over hot water.
Cool slightly; spread over dough.
Roll like jelly roll, lifting waxed paper slightly with each turn.
Chill 1/2 hour.
Slice cookies 1/4-inch thick.
Bake at 375° on ungreased sheet for 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen cookies.
Whisk vegetable oil, vinegar, sugar and seasoning together. Do in large bowl.
Core and cut peppers into strips.
Slice and separate onion.
Mix all together in bowl.
Toss and cover. Refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Save 1 tablespoon bacon grease, saute onion and bell pepper until tender.
Stir in milk, corn, margarine, salt and pepper. Cook on medium heat until bubbly.
Remove from heat and stir in potato flakes and sour cream.
Blend well.
Spoon into greased pan, top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake on 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cook coconut and pecans in butter until lightly browned; cool. Mix Cool Whip, cream cheese and condensed milk.
Put layer in pie crust; put caramel topping.
Sprinkle with coconut and pecans.
Put another layer of Cool Whip.
Put caramel icing on top.
Freeze.
Heat butter or oil in skillet.
Add garlic and heat; do not brown.
Add vegetables and sugar.
Stir with wooden spoon over high heat for 3 minutes. Serves 4.
Brown cubes in butter.
Add garlic and pearl onions; brown again with meat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add peppers (red and black); paprika can be substituted if you don't want it spicy.
Add allspice, cinnamon, salt and 4 cups of water.
(All spices are by taste, vary amounts as needed.)
Cook for 3 hours over medium-low heat until meat is very tender.
Combine butter and sugars.
Add egg, milk and vanilla.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour, oats, raisins and nuts.
Drop on cookie sheet by teaspoonfuls.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
In large saucepan, melt butter.
Stir in sugar, honey and vanilla until smooth, stir in oats and coconut; mix well.
Spread in well-greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake in 400° oven for 15 minutes or just until golden.
Cool in pan.
Cut into bars. Makes 24 bars.

1. Cook the pasta according to package directions; drain and rinse under cold water. 2. Mix together the pasta, shrimp, green onions and ranch dressing, then carefully work the shrimp into the pasta with your hands.
Combine in saucepan juice from lemon and orange.
Add egg and sugar; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until boiling. Boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat and cool.
Brown beef in oil in heavy saucepan.
Stir in onion soup mix, tomato paste and water.
Simmer, covered, 1 1/2 hours, or until meat is tender.
Serve over hot noodles with dollop of sour cream. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Dilute tomato soup with enough water to make 1 pint and heat until warm.
Add sugar and yeast, let stand until bubbling, 10 to 15 minutes.
Add butter, stir and add salt and flour.
Mix and let rise in warm place until light.
Form into desired shape and put in greased muffin tins and allow to rise until double in bulk. Bake 10 to 12 minutes in hot oven.
String the beans.
Cut.
Cook with water to cover.
Saute onion in heated oil.
Add can of tomatoes and tomato
sauce and cook slowly, about half hour.
Add to green beans.
Season with salt, pepper and the parsley (minced).
Cook until done.
Brown ground beef, bacon and onion.
Add sugars, catsup, mustard and molasses to the beef mixture, then add beans.
Put in a casserole dish.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Place shrimp flat, cut side up, on cookie sheet.
Sprinkle bread crumbs, oregano and parsley.
Moisten with butter and oil. Broil until shrimp are firm (4 to 5 minutes).
Top with bacon and lemon juice.
Broil 1 minute.
Serve hot.
Yields 4 servings.
Saute chicken with all of the ingredients in pan with a little oil (until sauce it thick).
(Sauce to your taste.) Serve in the pita bread pocket with a choice of peas, sauteed onions, avocado and sour cream.
Heat pineapple in water until hot; add jello and stir until dissolved. Combine cream cheese and Cool Whip and fold into jello mixture. Add nuts. Let set.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in large skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms, celery and onion; stir until vegetables are tender. Stir in flour, chicken and sour cream.
Reduce heat and simmer until thoroughly heated.
Stir in garlic salt and remove from heat. Cut each biscuit into quarters; press each piece into miniature muffin tins coated with vegetable cooking spray.
Brush each piece with melted butter.
Bake at 400° for 5 to 6 minutes.
Remove from oven; reduce oven temperature to 350°.
Cook the pasta as per package instructions.
Cut the onion and fry it with 2-3 tsp. oil.
Add all-spice and the beef.
Braise until meat turns brown.
Then add water and tomato sauce and salt. Cook meat for 10 minutes.
Boil red new potatoes until tender.
Drain and cool.
Place potatoes in Pyrex dish.
Pour 1 cup melted butter over potatoes. Sprinkle with garlic salt and chives.
Put in oven; bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cook peas, unseasoned, then drain.
In frypan, cook onions and celery in butter until tender.
Add water chestnuts that have been drained and sliced very thin.
Add soup, flour and peas.
Mix all together and heat on the top of stove.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Pour into casserole dish and cover with dressing mix. Bake at 350° until brown, about 15 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Place butter, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla, and bourbon in a large mixing bowl along with 4 cups of flour.
Knead thoroughly, gradually adding flour until the dough is pliable and doesn't stick to your hands.
You may need to add more than the indicated flour.
The pastry dough should be similar to pie crust dough. Chill the dough for 1/2 hour.
Place ground walnuts and confectioners sugar in a bowl and stir together.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking soda and nutmeg. In another bowl, beat eggs; add sugar and oil.
Mix well.
Stir in apples, nuts and coconut.
Stir in dry ingredients, just until moistened.
Rub garlic cloves over chicken breasts.
Spray 9 x 11-inch cooking dish with Pam.
Place chicken in dish.
Add tomato paste mixed with 1 1/2 cups water.
Dash of salt, pepper and oregano. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown beef, onion and pepper.
Add other ingredients to meat in a large pot, heat and serve.
In medium bowl, beat together 1 cup sugar and oil.
Stir in juice and eggs.
In small bowl, combine flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Blend into sugar-egg mixture just until mixed.
Stir in orange slices and chocolate chips just until mixed.
Combine cooked macaroni with other ingredients, reserving 1/2 cup of the cheese. Top with the Cheddar cheese and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Good way to use leftover ham.

recipes.t: Melt In Your Mouth Peanut Butter Fudge
d: Mix sugar, milk and water.
Cook on a medium/medium-high fire until mixture "balls" in water (it should stick to your teeth) approximately 30 to 35 minutes, stirring continually.
In food processor, process nuts and garlic until finely chopped.
Add remaining ingredients in order listed; whirl until basil and parsley are very finely chopped, scraping down sides of bowl as needed.
Transfer to a small bowl or jar with tight fitting lid.
Place plastic wrap directly on surface of pesto. Refrigerate up to 2 days.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
Toss with 1 pound cooked, drained pasta or serve over baked potatoes or tender-crisp cooked vegetables.
In bowl, combine Cheddar cheese, onion, green pepper and parsley.
In a blender container or food processor bowl, blend thoroughly Ricotta cheese, yogurt, catsup, mustard, hot pepper sauce and garlic salt.
Add the cheese mixture and blend until well combined (if using blender, you may have to mix in 2 batches).
Place in serving bowl and sprinkle with pimento and minced parsley.
Good served with crunch vegetables as a dip, over hot vegetables as a sauce or spread on slices of French bread and grill.
Put first 7 ingredients in a large pan.
Add enough water to make soup consistency.
Cook for 1 hour.
Add corn oil and salt and or sugar to taste.
Mix together first 3 ingredients.
Pour over vegetables and toss.
To make salad for a large group, increase oil, sugar and vinegar always to equal amounts and add more vegetables.
Brown meat, pour off grease.
Add diced onion and cook on low. Add tomatoes.
Cook on low 10 to 15 minutes, then add 28 ounces water and bring to boil.
Add noodles and cook until thick.
Beat 4 egg yolks with 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Add hot water slowly and cook in double boiler until thick.
Add one envelope of gelatin dissolved in cold water and stir; cool.
Add 1/4 cup rum and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg.
Beat egg whites gradually adding 1/2 cup sugar.
When custard has thickened, fold in egg whites.
Line pie pan with graham crackers.
Pour in custard mixture.
Top with 1/2 pint whipped cream.
Place in refrigerator until cold.
Top with grated unsweetened chocolate.
Whip cream and fold in fruits and marshmallows.
Mix powdered sugar and mayonnaise and add to fruit mixture.
Freeze in flat 9 x 10 inch pan.
Cut in squares and serve on lettuce leaves.
Slice garlic thinly; place inside slits in pork chops.
Brown quickly in olive oil.
Spread mustard over pork chops, add apples and water; put on medium and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serves 4 (or 2 very hungry people).
Serve with wild rice.
Heat the first 3 ingredients until sugar dissolves; cool.
Add milk and whipped cream.
Pour in ice cream freezer and turn until creamed.
Prepare pasta according to package directions.
Add broccoli, cauliflower and carrots for last 5 minutes of cooking time. Drain.
Tear tortillas into 3 or 4 pieces (like chips); brown gently until crispy in a small amount of oil.
Scramble eggs in a bowl; pour over the top of the tortillas.
Stir until cooked.
Sprinkle on cheese.
Top with cooked meat and onions.
Happy munchin' ... like morning nachos!

Melt butter. Mix the flour, coconut, almonds and brown sugar. Press into 9 x 13 pan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes until golden brown. Set aside and cool in pan baked in.
Butter 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread 1/2 crumbs on buttered pan. Cream butter and sugar, then add eggs.
Beat well.
Spread on crumbs.
Next, spread berries on cream mixture.
Top with whipped cream.
Sprinkle nuts and the remaining crushed wafers on the whipped cream.
Chill several hours before serving.
Marinate brisket in mixture of next 5 ingredients in roaster overnight.
Preheat oven to 250°.
Bake, covered, for 5 hours. Cool in refrigerator.
Blend drippings, brown sugar, catsup and flour in saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Slice brisket thinly across grain.
Cover with sauce.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Crumble and cook sausage in medium skillet over medium heat until browned.
Drain off any drippings. Spread bread cubes in greased 11 x 7 baking dish; top with sausage, peppers and cheese.
Wash eggs, milk, salt and dry mustard until well blended.
Pour over cheese and bake 30 to 40 minutes or until set.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting into squares.
Serve hot.
Prick top of cheese thoroughly.
Spread marmalade over top and sprinkle with almonds.
Place on baking sheet and bake in oven at 350° for 15 minutes or until cheese oozes out.
Serve with any bland crackers.
Heat oil.
Saute onions.
Add water and vegies; salt and pepper.
Simmer over low fire until soft (30 to 50 minutes). Preparing in advance enhances flavor.
Serves 4.
Cream butter and sugar.
Blend in flour.
Add pecans.
Roll into small balls.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Dip into the cinnamon sugar mixture.
Cool on rack.
Makes 30 cookies.
Combine water and sugar in a large saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until sugar dissolves.
Add remaining ingredients, stirring until grape juice melts.
Pour mixture into freezer trays or sheet cake pan.
Freeze until firm.
Stir several times during freezing process.
Mix together graham crackers, nuts, and melted margarine; press into pie pan or 12 x 12-inch baking dish.
Combine brown sugar and 1/2 cup granulated sugar, salt and tapioca; pour over peaches and mix gently.
Sprinkle mixture with almond extract.
Line 9-inch pie pan with pastry.
Pour in peach mixture.
Dot with butter.
Roll out remaining pastry and place over pie.
Seal edges by fluting; prick top with fork.
Brush top crust with cold water and sprinkle with small amount of sugar before putting pie in oven, if desired.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes; reduce heat to 375° and bake for 40 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve with bowl of freshly whipped cream on the side.
Makes one 9-inch pie.
Mix powdered sugar, margarine, egg, vanilla and almond extract.
Stir in flour, baking soda and cream of tartar.
Cover and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Heat oven to 375°.
Divide dough into halves.
Roll 3/16-inch thick on floured board.
Cut into shapes.
Place on lightly greased (or foil covered) cookie sheet. Prepare egg yolk paint.
Paint on cookies.
Bake until edges are light brown (about 7 to 8 minutes).
Use 1 dough bread and cut up into 10 portions.
Fix franks in dough like a sleeping bag, but first spread mustard and catsup on. Moisten edges with water to seal.
Let rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 17 minutes until brown.
Decorate using cheese to make hair and horns for hat, green pepper for eyes and pimientos for mouth.
Great for slumber party.
Split the loaf of bread lengthwise, then slice the halves crosswise just to the crust, but not through it.
Mix the cheese, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Beat in enough melted butter and olive oil to make a creamy, spreadable mixture. Spread this paste on the cut surfaces of the bread and let stand for an hour or two.
Just before serving, place on a baking sheet and heat thoroughly in a 375° oven for 10 minutes, then brown lightly under the broiler.
Fill a quart jar with whole, medium size cucumbers.
Add pickling spice (being sure not to add more than two of the red peppers from spice), salt, horseradish, alum and vinegar.
Fill jar with cold water.
Seal and shake.
Set aside for at least 6 weeks.
When ready to use, wash cucumbers.
Discard all juice and spice.
Cut in chunks and add 1 cup sugar.
Stir occasionally until sugar is dissolved; then put in refrigerator.
Will keep indefinitely.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain grease.
Simmer gravy, green chiles (undrained) and 3/4 of sour cream over low heat.
Do not allow to boil.
Soften tortillas by placing in wet dish towel and microwaving for 1 minute.
Place spoonfuls of meat mixture, gravy, cheese and salsa on tortillas.
Place seam side down in gravy-lined baking pan.
Pour remaining gravy and cheese over burritos.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes until hot.
Serve with remaining sour cream and salsa.
Mix the first 5
ingredients
in a large pitcher.
Fill tall glasses with ice;
pour
orange
juice
mixture over ice. Garnish drinks with orange slices and serve.
Cream shortening, sugar and egg. Add apples, nuts and vanilla. Add sifted dry ingredients.
Bake in oven at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes in an 8-inch square pan.
Serve with whipped cream or lemon sauce.
Saut onions, pepper, garlic and celery gently in margarine until wilted and tender.
Add shrimp and cook about five minutes, or until shrimp turns pink.
Add mushrooms and cook five minutes longer.
Add sour cream, stirring until blended and heated, but do not boil.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over hot rice.
