Saute ham in margarine.
Cook noodles as directed and drain when done.
Heat peas.
Toss peas, ham and cheese into noodles and serve.
Mix the first five ingredients; form into a loaf in a baking pan.
Squeeze a layer of ketchup over the top; smooth out. Sprinkle a desired amount of brown sugar over ketchup layer.
Cut slices of bacon in half and lay the slices across the loaf.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (350° to 375°) for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Cover raisins with hot tap water and soak until plump; drain. In large bowl, combine broccoli, onion, bacon, sunflower seeds and raisins. Set aside.
Slice the baked potatoes lengthwise and lay on bottom of baking pan.
Baste with melted butter.
Bake at 350° until crisp and golden.
Cover with shredded cheese and top with bacon bits or chives.
Bake just until the cheese bubbles.
Serve.
Fix stuffing according to directions; cook broccoli until almost done.
Use a 12 x 7 1/2 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix soup and chicken with 1/2 can milk.
Layer in baking dish: stuffing, soup, broccoli and cheese.
I usually mix everything together and pour over stuffing.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.t: So You Forgot To Defrost Chicken
d: Place frozen chicken in slow cooker.
Mix together soup, mushrooms, salt and pepper and pour over chicken.
Cover.
Cook on low 10 to 12 hours.
Serve over rice.
Yield: 6 servings.
Saute hamburg with onion.
Cook noodles until tender; add to vegetables.
Cook carrots; drain.
Heat peas; drain.
Blend meat with soup and milk.
Cook onion in melted oleo about 10 minutes.
Add cabbage, coat with butter.
Add broth, salt and pepper.
Over medium heat, cook, stirring often, about 8 to 10 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove pan from heat and stir in vinegar, brown sugar and orange peel.
Brown hamburger meat, salt and pepper; drain.
In large saucepan, combine enchilada sauce, soups, chillies and milk. Bring to a boil.
Layer crushed chips, meat and sauce mix. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake or microwave until cheese melts.
This recipe will serve 5 people.
In saucepan, stir in cocoa, milk, eggs and sugar substitute with flour or cornstarch. After it thickens, add butter.
Brown chopped celery, green pepper and onion in margarine. Add mushrooms and their liquid.
Combine with cooked rice; season to taste.
Bake in greased baking dish at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Lay fish in a single layer in a shallow rectangle or oval 1 1/2 to 2 quart baking dish.
Pour lemon juice over.
With a fork, mix together carrot, tomato, green onion, mayonnaise, cream cheese, parsley and pepper.
Add salt to taste.
Mound vegetable mixture equally atop fish.
If made ahead, cover and chill up to overnight.
Saute onion in butter until transparent.
Mix onion with cheese.
Stir together egg, cream and dry ingredients.
Combine the 2 mixtures.
Fill pastry shells 2/3 full.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Makes 48 tarts.
Cook chicken, noodles and broth until noodles are tender.
Add corn, chicken soup and mushroom soup.
Simmer for 1/2 hour.
(Use Kluski noodles for best results.)
Cook first 3 ingredients and drain.
Add spaghetti sauce, tomato sauce, mushrooms and green olives.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Put in large baking dish.
Spread sour cream over this.
Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese over sour cream.
Spread crescent rolls over top.
Brush with melted margarine and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Place ribs in one layer in shallow pan.
In medium bowl combine soy sauce, oil, scallions, garlic, salt (if using), pepper, honey and sesame seed.
Mix well and pour over ribs. Cover with plastic wrap and let marinate in refrigerator overnight.
The next day refresh marinade with a little water; some will have been absorbed by the meat.
Broil at least 8 inches from coals for about 30 minutes or until well browned on all sides. Turn frequently to prevent burning.
May be cooked in oven broiler as far as possible from heat element.
Beat egg whites to form
soft peaks.
Gradually beat in brown sugar, vanilla and salt.
Fold
in
pecans
and coconut. Drop by teaspoon onto a greased
cookie
sheet one inch apart. Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Turn off oven heat and let stand in the oven for 20 minutes more.
Place string beans on bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cut chicken into small pieces and place on top of string beans.
Add olives and water chestnuts on top of chicken.
Mix soup and salad dressing together.
Pour this mixture over everything.
Add cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Bake eggplant about 1 hour until soft. Cook onions in 4 tablespoons oil until soft.
Stir in green pepper and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Put in bowl with eggplant pulp, which has been chopped finely, along with tomatoes, sugar, salt and pepper.
Heat remaining oil in skillet and cook mixture about 1 hour on low.
Add lemon juice. Serve with rye, pumpernickel bread or sesame seed crackers.
Serves about 20 (more or less).
Beat eggs with mixer.
Add flour, baking powder, salt and cottage cheese.
Stir in Jack or Swiss cheese, melted butter and chilies.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until golden on top and knife comes out clean.
Good with salsa and sour cream.
Serves 20.
Combine beef, eggs, bread crumbs, onions, 2/3 cup tomato sauce, salt, pepper and parsley.
Mix well and shape into flat rectangle on a piece of wax paper.
Sprinkle 3 1/2 cups of cheese over meat mixture.
Starting with short edge, roll up like a jelly roll and press ends of roll to seal.
Bake in shallow pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain excess fat.
Pour remaining sauce over roll. Garnish with 1/2 cup cheese and green pepper rings.
Bake an additional 5 minutes.
Crush cookies in Ziploc bag.
Combine cookie crumbs and butter and press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Refrigerate.
Spoon softened ice cream on crust.
Heat hot fudge so it is warm.
Spread on ice cream.
Spread whipped cream over chocolate layer and sprinkle with nuts.
Freeze 2 hours, then cover with foil.
Keeps for a month.
Fry bacon crispy, drain and crumble.
Set aside.
Mix mayo, sugar and vinegar until smooth for dressing.
Toss remaining ingredients together.
Pour dressing mix over salad, adding bacon pieces and blending well.
Chill and serve.
Instead of peanuts you can add hard Chinese noodles just before serving.
Dissolve jello in water.
Add oranges, crushed pineapple and all juices.
Pour in 13 x 9 x 2-inch Pyrex dish.
Put miniature marshmallows all over top.
Let jell.
Add 1/2 cup mayonnaise to 1/2 pint of whipping cream (whipped).
Pour on top and put grated cheese on top.
Let sit overnight.
Slice eggplant into 1/3 to 1/2-inch thick slices (cut crosswise).
Dip slices in margarine and then bread crumbs. Sprinkle slices with oregano if desired.
Spoon spaghetti sauce on top of each slice.
Top eggplant with a slice of cheese.
Place eggplant in a 400° oven for about 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese is slightly brown.
Put milk and eggs into blender; process for a minute.
Add chocolate syrup; fill milk can with vodka or rum and add to blender.
(A little more may be added for desired taste.) Process until well blended.
Store liquor in refrigerator for up to 1 month.
Makes 1 fifth.
Split hens down middle.
Brown rice only 15 minutes in large Pyrex dish at 375°.
In separate bowl, mix water, package of seasoning from Rice-A-Roni and chicken soup.
After rice browns, lower oven to 350°; put hens over top of rice (will sizzle).
Pour mixture over hens; cover and cook 1 hour.
Uncover 30 minutes to brown.
Excellent side dish with this:
cut up fresh apples with poppy seed dressing.
Combine cereal and milk.
Let stand 2 minutes.
Add margarine and egg.
Mix well.
Add combined dry ingredients, mixing just until moistened.
Spoon into greased medium size muffin pan.
Make a deep indentation in top of batter for each muffin.
Fill with preserves.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Makes 1 dozen.
Melt chocolate and 1/2 cup butter in top of double boiler; stir in sugar, milk and salt.
Bring mixture to a boil; reduce heat and cook 4 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; stir in vanilla.
Let cool.
For sauce, spray a cold medium skillet with nonstick cooking spray.
Cook and stir the onion and garlic over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until onion is tender.
Stir in tomato sauce, water, honey, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, celery seed and pepper.
Bring to boiling.
Reduce heat.
Simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

recipes.t: Cornbread Broccoli Pie(A Quick Meal In A Pie Form)
d: Heat oven to 400°.
Prepare cornbread mix according to package directions.
Stir in Spam.
Spread into greased 9-inch pie pan. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until cornbread is done.
Arrange broccoli spears on top of cornbread, sprinkle with cheese.
Return to oven, continue baking for 5 to 10 minutes or until cheese is melted and cornbread is completely baked.
Place sliced apples in greased 9-inch pie pan.
Mix together soft butter or oleo, brown sugar, flour, spices and egg.
Drop by teaspoon on top of apples.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Cream together shortening, sugar and brown sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Sift and add salt, baking powder, soda and flour. Add walnuts, Rice Krispies and quick oats.
Drop on cookie sheet with a teaspoon.
Bake 10 minutes in a 350° oven.
Makes about 7 dozen.
Place first 7 ingredients in a large Mixmaster bowl.
Beat with mixer until well mixed.
Grate Colby cheese and add to cream cheese mixture, mixing well.
Mold into a ball.
Decorate with paprika and chopped almonds or any other nuts.
Chill.
Serve with crackers.
Layer 1/2 of ham, potatoes, onion, flour, salt and pepper. Repeat with remaining ingredients.
Pour milk over layers.
Mix bread crumbs and margarine; sprinkle atop.
Top with parsley. Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours, covered, and 15 minutes uncovered.
Mix rice, sugar, salt, soy sauce and boiling water; let stand. Brown meat, onions and celery; add soup and combine all ingredients.
Bake in a greased casserole for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Prepare Dream Whip as directed on the package.
Combine 1 cup of the prepared whipped topping with the pie filling mix, pumpkin, milk and spices.
Mix slowly until just blended.
Pour into pie shell.
Chill until set, at least 2 hours.
Garnish with the remaining whipped topping.
Dissolve gelatin in 1 cup hot water; add 1 cup cold water. Add pineapple, cottage cheese, milk, mayonnaise and nuts.
Mix together well; pour into desired mold.
Chill until set.
Yield: About 20 servings.
Mix all ingredients together, except the butter.
Melt butter or margarine in a pan and pour the corn bread mixture over butter. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until brown.
Cook macaroni per package instructions and drain and rinse. Add tuna, drained mushrooms and soup to macaroni.
Cook over medium heat until warm through.
Add cheese.
Mix until melted. Serves 6.
Combine butter, sugar and vanilla.
Cream until light and fluffy. Sift together the flour and cinnamon.
Add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Stir in corn flakes and pecans.
Blend together all dry ingredients.
Make a well in the middle and add milk and sour cream.
Blend until it holds together.
Knead in the bowl about 4 minutes.
Shape dough into a ball and then flatten it until it is about 3 inches high and slightly rounded on top.
Place loaf on greased cookie sheet.
Score a cross about 1/2-inch deep on top.
Lightly rub top of loaf with milk.
Bake for 45 minutes in preheated 400° oven.
Flip loaf over onto its top and bake another 5 minutes.
Wrap in a damp dish towel and stand loaf on its side to cool.

recipes.t: Apple Celery Salad With Banana Dressing
d: Combine first 3 ingredients and set aside.
Grind walnuts and then add bananas, honey and lemon juice.
Combine and serve immediately.
Soften gelatine in cold water.
To beaten egg yolks, add sugar and salt.
Slowly stir in the scalded milk.
Cook over hot, not boiling water, stirring constantly until mixture coats the spoon. Remove from heat.
Add gelatine and stir until dissolved.
Chill until mixture is slightly thicker than consistency of unbeaten egg whites.
Add the 3/4 cup coconut and the vanilla.
Beat until stiff the egg whites.
Beat 1/4 cup sugar in gradually.
Fold into gelatine-coconut mixture.
Pour into baked pastry shell.
Chill until firm.
Garnish with whipped cream and toasted coconut. Yield:
1 (9-inch) pie.
Put molasses, sugar, boiling water and vinegar in saucepan. Bring to boil, then add cream of tartar.
Boil until mixture will become brittle when dropped into cold water.
Stir constantly during last part of cooking.
When nearly done, add butter and soda.
Turn into a buttered pan; as mixture cools around sides, fold toward center.
When cool enough to handle, pull until porous and light colored, allowing candy to come in contact with tips of fingers and thumbs, not to be squeezed in the hand.
While pulling, add 1 teaspoon of vanilla or 1/2 teaspoon lemon extract.
Mix together Cool Whip and milk. Stir in lemonade or limeade. Pour mixture into graham cracker crust shell. Put into refrigerator until set. Decorate with chocolate chips and chopped nuts.
Cream together butter or margarine, sugar, eggs and vanilla until fluffy.
Beat 5 minutes.
Blend in cooled chocolate.
Sift together flour and soda.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with ice water, beating well after each addition.
Bake in 2 well-greased and floured 8-inch round pans in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
(This can also be baked in a 9 x 12-inch pan for 35 to 40 minutes.)
Mash cooked beans.
Combine sugar, salt and flour.
Add beaten eggs and milk.
Add oleo, vanilla, coconut and peanuts. Pour
into unbaked
9-inch
pie
shell.
Bake
at 350° for 45 minutes or until done.
Combine sour cream with tarragon, thyme, garlic powder, paprika and salt.
Dip pieces of chicken into sour cream mixture, then into cornflake crumbs, coating well.
Melt butter in baking dish.
Place chicken, skin side down, in dish.
Bake for 45 minutes; turn and bake approximately 20 minutes longer.
Melt butter; blend in flour, salt and pepper.
Cook over low heat, stirring until mixture is smooth; remove from heat.
Slowly stir in milk.
Bring to a boil over direct heat, stirring constantly.
Boil 1 minute.
Just before serving, stir in the rest of the ingredients, except biscuits and cheese.
Bring mixture just to a boil.
Serve over biscuits.
Sprinkle cheese over top. Makes 2 generous servings.
Sift together first 5 ingredients; set aside.
In a mixing bowl, cream butter and sugars.
Add eggs, vanilla and lemon extract; beat well.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Stir in nuts.
Divide dough into 4 parts and shape into 1 1/2 x 11-inch rolls.
Wrap in foil and chill overnight.
Slice cookies 3/8-inch thick.
Bake on greased sheets at 350° for about 10 minutes. Yields about 17 dozen cookies.
Combine celery soup and stewed tomatoes in a 1 3/4 quart saucepan.
Add onion and tuna.
Heat to serving temperature over medium heat.
May be topped with grated Parmesan cheese.
Brown meat, onion and green pepper; stir in soup, pimento and wine.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Add sour cream.
Place in greased (with margarine) casserole dish.
Top with biscuits.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Mix together hot water, jello and cake mix and let cool. Then add oil, eggs and lemon flavoring.
Bake in cake pan or loaf pans at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Whip heavy cream to a stiff froth.
Boil milk and sugar.
Soak gelatin in water and place in a warm place.
Add this to the boiled milk.
When slightly cool, add the egg yolks, well beaten. Stir in the fruit and juice of the crushed pineapple and lastly stir in the whipped cream.
Place in sherbet glasses in refrigerator.
Prepare noodles as label directs.
Meanwhile in 10-inch skillet over medium heat, cook ground beef, onions and dill until meat is browned.
Stir in undiluted soup, sour cream, salt, pepper and 1/4 cup water.
Cook until heated through.
Serve over hot noodles.
Makes 4 servings.
Toast bread and spread with all the butter/margarine while hot.
Arrange toast in buttered baking dish. Sprinkle with raisins. Stir salt and all but 4 tablespoons of sugar into the eggs.
Add milk and stir to mix well.
Pour over toast and let stand 10 minutes.
Press toast lightly down into milk occasionally.
Mix cinnamon and remaining sugar; sprinkle over the top.
Place pan directly on oven rack in a 350° oven about 25 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean and top is golden brown.
Dissolve sugar, molasses and yeast in warm water.
Add salt and oil.
Beat in whole grain flours, using electric mixer.
Cover large area with 3 cups white flour.
Place beaten mixture in center and knead white flour until proper elasticity of dough is achieved.
Additional flour may be needed.
Divide the dough into 4ths.
Form into loaves.
Place in loaf pans.
Cover with damp towel.
Place in warm place and let rise.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Remove from pans and cool.
Pour boiling water over oats and margarine (which has been broken into small chunks).
Stir until margarine melts.
Sift together flour, cinnamon, soda and salt.
Add oats and margarine. Mix well.
Add white sugar and eggs.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour into utility dish.
Bake 12 minutes, turning dish often.

Open package of biscuits and cut the 10 biscuits in halves, making 20 pieces. Stretch the pieces upward and sideways but try not to tear. Place piece of pepperoni in center and sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top of pepperoni. Close by pinching dough together on top and sides. Place in aluminum foil on a cookie sheet. Bake at 450° for 8 to 10 minutes. Should be golden brown.
Combine pie filling mix and 1/4 cup 7-Up in saucepan.
Blend in 2 egg yolks; add rest of 7-Up, stirring constantly.
Cook over medium heat to a full boil.
Remove from heat.
Add lemon juice, lemon rind and cream cheese, beating until smooth.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.
Fold into lemon mixture.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Chill until set.
Garnish with lemon slices and mint leaves, if desired.
Heat oil in a skillet that can go into the oven.
Add onions, green peppers and rice.
Saute until rice is translucent.
Add sugar and tomatoes; blend.
Cut kielbasi lengthwise and into bite-size pieces.
Cook kielbasi in frying pan with a little water and some of the pineapple juice.
Add pork and beans to a 2-quart baking dish along with drained pineapple and kielbasi; drain off fat.
Bake in oven at 350° until bubbly.
Saute 1/4 cup onion in small amount of vegetable oil in frypan or wok.
Add chicken breast, cut in small pieces, and brown on all sides.
Add 1 package of frozen mixed vegetables (Italian or California Blend).
Add 1/2 cup chicken broth.
Add 1/2 cup Minute rice and 1/4 teaspoon of Italian seasoning. Simmer, covered, until vegetables and rice are done (15 to 20 minutes).
Add 1/2 teaspoon fresh or dried parsley just before serving.
Serve with garlic toast.
Combine sugar, eggs, vanilla and oil.
Sift together dry ingredients and stir into liquid mixture.
Add carrots, apples and nuts.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Bake at 325° for 60 to 70 minutes.
In medium bowl, mix unflavored gelatine with 1/4 cup sugar. Add hot juice; stir until gelatine is completely dissolved.
With wire whip or rotary beater, blend in cranberry sauce and liqueur. Chill, stirring occasionally, until mixture mounds slightly when dropped from spoon.
Cream the butter and brown sugar.
Add flour and nuts.
Mix. Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes. Cool.
Put flour, pepper, garlic salt, parsley flakes and tarragon on chicken breasts.
Saute breasts for a few minutes in oil to brown only.
Place in casserole dish with scallions, sherry and butter. Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 325°.
Baste twice during baking.
Mix flour, pecans, brown sugar and margarine.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch buttered pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 400° (glass pan 375°). Cool completely and then refrigerate to get cold.
Soften cream cheese.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla.
Mix.
Prepare Dream Whip according to directions on package.
Blend cream mixture with Dream Whip and pour over crust.
Chill.
Lightly spoon pie filling over pie.
Chill at least 12 hours.
Brown hamburger; drain.
Add soup, sauce, celery, green pepper and onion.
Simmer at least 1 hour.
Cook noodles; drain.
In casserole, put layer of noodles, layer of meat sauce and layer of cheese slices.
Repeat (end with cheese on top).
Bake in oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
This can be made ahead and frozen.
Soak chickpeas in cold water overnight.
Drain, cover with fresh water and boil for about 1 1/2 hours.
Crush garlic with 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Put the tahini, lemon juice and garlic into the liquidiser goblet; add chickpeas and blend to a creamy paste.
Turn out, add more lemon juice and salt to taste.
(It should be slightly sharp.)
If you wish, add olive oil to give a softer texture.
If you have no liquidiser, rub peas through a sieve, then beat in the garlic.
Add the tahini gradually, then lemon juice and seasoning.
Turn into bowl and garnish.
Serves 6 to 8.
Drain liquid from beans.
Combine ingredients and marinate overnight in the refrigerator.

recipes.t: Pork Chops And Rice In Gravy
d: Flour pork chops and brown in own fat.
Cover and simmer until well done.
Remove chops, add 2 tablespoons flour to fat.
Add salt and pepper.
Add enough water to make thick gravy.
Mix in soup, stir until smooth.
Serve over cooked rice with pork chops.
Saute onions and green peppers together. Combine all ingredients and simmer for 2 to 3 hours. Serve on Italian buns.
Melt margarine in large saucepan and saute the onion.
Add potatoes and carrots and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add broth, cover the pan and simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs on bottom of 8 inch square baking pan. Beat cheese, yogurt, sugar and vanilla in medium bowl with electric mixer until smooth and creamy.
Sprinkle gelatin into water in cup; let stand 2 minutes.
Microwave at High 40 seconds, stir and let stand 2 minutes or until gelatin is completely dissolved. Gradually beat gelatin mixture into cheese mixture with electric mixer until well blended.
Pour into prepared pan; refrigerate until firm.
Spoon cherry topping onto cheesecake.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Fry bacon crisp and hold for later.
Saute onion in bacon grease.
Add soup, vinegar, salt, pepper and beans.
Heat.
Add potatoes and wieners.
Bake at 350° for 30 or 40 minutes. Sprinkle crumbled bacon on top.
Combine tea, orange juice granules, sugar, cloves, cinnamon and allspice, mixing thoroughly.
Store in tightly covered container.
Combine 2 or 3 teaspoons of mixture with 1 cup of hot water, stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Yield: 5 1/2 cups.
Break pasta into 1-inch pieces.
Cook pasta according to package directions, then drain.
In a covered saucepan, cook broccoli, onion, green or sweet red peppers and garlic in a small amount of water about 10 minutes or until broccoli is crisp and tender; drain.
Bring to a boil the sugar, milk, margarine and cocoa and cook one minute.
Remove from heat and add oatmeal, peanut butter and vanilla.
Stir well, but fast, because it will set.
Drop on wax paper.
Let cool.
Brown ground beef in skillet and drain.
Set aside.
Prepare yellow rice.
In large bowl, combine beef, rice and remaining ingredients except soup.
Mix well and pour into casserole dish. Pour soup on top.
Do not dilute soup.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Cube ham and put 1 cube of ham and 1 pineapple tidbit on a toothpick.
Wrap with 1/4 piece of bacon.
Place all in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Reserve juice from pineapple and add to 1 cup brown sugar, mustard and spices.
Mix and pour over kabobs.
Bake, uncovered, 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 40.
Cook carrots until fork-tender (do not overcook).
Cook sugar, butter and orange juice until syrupy.
Pour over carrots and mix lightly.
Serve hot.
Peel eggplant and cut up into squares. Chop onion. Cut up pepper into bite-size. Mix all together in dish.

Mix together tomatoes, salt and pepper to taste and minced garlic depending on how much you like. Pour over vegetables and drizzle with olive oil. Cook at 350° for 3 to 4 hours, stirring occasionally. Can be served hot or cold.
Stir together lettuce, bananas, apples, maraschino cherries and walnuts.
Mix equal amounts of sour cream and salad dressing together.
Thin with milk or cream and sweeten to taste.
Mix or toss together.
Keeps well.
Pare quince and
apples
and grate them.
Measure pulp. Measure 3/4 as much
sugar
as
pulp.
Pour boiling water over sugar and stir until sugar is almost dissolved.
Add the fruit pulp and lemon juice
and
cook
until mixture is clear.
Pour into clean hot jars and
cover
with paraffin.
It will be the appearance and consistency of honey.
Cut up chicken and brush with butter. Place in crockpot. Sprinkle Italian dressing over chicken. Add onion. Cook on low 6-8 hours. Add rest of ingredients. Heat through. Serve over rice or noodles.
Grease 1 1/2-quart casserole; place spinach in casserole. Coarsely flake tuna over spinach.
Drain mushrooms in 1 cup measure.
Add lemon juice and water to make 1 cup.
In saucepan over low heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter.
Stir in flour, onion, salt and season.
Stir in mushroom liquid and cook until thick.
Boil cabbage just to soften; cut onions, peppers, mushrooms and potatoes.
Cut trout by slicing off of bone.
Combine all ingredients into tinfoil.
Add butter on top and any seasonings. Fold up tinfoil package and place on broiler or barbecue.
Cook for 1/2 hour or until vegetables are done.
Serves 3 to 4 people.
Line a 9-inch pie pan with pastry.
Form a decorative edge and freeze.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large saucepan, simmer boiled cider, butter, maple sugar or syrup and sugar, water and salt for several minutes.
Transfer to a large bowl and let cool slightly. Blend egg yolks with liquids, then fold in the whites gently, but thoroughly.
Pour into chilled pie shell and bake for 30 to 40 minutes
until set.
Give pie a generous dust of nutmeg.
Serve cooled with lightly sweetened whipped cream.
Makes 8 servings.

recipes.t: Ellie'S Wine Punch(Prepare A Double Recipe For A Large Punch Bowl)
d: Combine syrup, wine and apple juice in punch bowl.
Float a decorated or plain chunk of ice in bowl when serving.
Combine pudding mix, cake mix and gelatin.
Add oil and milk, beating well.
Beat in eggs.
Bake in 3 greased 9-inch cake pans at 350° for 25-30 minutes.
Cool completely.
In mixing bowl, combine sour cream, powdered sugar, pineapple and coconut, blending well.
Reserve 1 cup for topping.
Spread remaining mixture between layers.
Fold together reserved pineapple mixture and whipped topping.
Frost top and sides of cake.
Store cake in covered container in refrigerator.

recipes.t: Green Beans, Potatoes With Bacon And Mushrooms
d: In a large kettle with a lid or a Dutch oven, place bacon pieces and onion slices. Over medium heat, cook until bacon is lightly brown and onion is crisp-tender. Add green beans, potatoes, water, salt and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and simmer until potatoes will break when pierced with a fork. Drain liquid from potatoes, reserving 1 1/2 cups of the liquid and return to the potatoes in the kettle. Add canned soup and sliced mushrooms. Stir gently to blend. Return to
medium-low heat for 5 to 8 minutes, covered. Remove from heat and allow to stand about 20 minutes for flavors to marry. Serves 8.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup hot water.
Melt vanilla ice cream into 1 cup heated ginger ale.
Combine the 2 liquids and refrigerate until it begins to thicken.
Pour into crust and chill.
Place turkey in browning bag and place in shallow roasting pan.
Combine parsley, olive oil, salt, pepper and vinegar.
Pour over turkey.
Seal bag and bake at 300° for 4 to 5 hours.
Cut several slits in top of bag before placing in oven.
Serve hot with thickened pan drippings.
Drippings can be thickened with a small amount (1 to 2 tablespoons) cornstarch mixed with water.
Mix popped corn and peanuts in very large ovenproof bowl.
Keep warm in 250° oven.
Melt margarine in heavy 2-quart saucepan.
Stir in brown sugar, corn syrup and salt.
Bring to rolling boil.
Stir constantly.
Boil without stirring 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in soda and vanilla.
Quickly pour over popcorn mixture, tossing until kernels and nuts are well coated.
Spread out in shallow baking pan.
Bake at 250° for 45 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Remove from oven.
Turn out on aluminum foil to cool. Break into pieces.
Store in tightly covered container.
Makes 3 quarts.
Mix flour with brown sugar, baking powder, salt, soda and ginger.
Cut butter into flour mixture in small particles.
Add egg, buttermilk and maple syrup.
Stir just until mixed.
Stir in walnuts and raisins.
Drop batter by heaping tablespoons onto lightly greased baking sheet 2 inches apart, making 10 mounds. Bake at 425° for 12 to 13 minutes.
Serve warm.
In an 8 x 8-inch serving dish, layer ingredients in the following order:
Spread bean dip on bottom of dish, mash avocados and add lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Mix sour cream with taco seasoning and layer on top of avocado mixture.
Top with olives, onions, tomatoes and grated cheese.
Serve with tortilla chips for dipping.
Boil chicken until done; drain and chop.
Layer tortillas in bottom of large
baking pan.
Combine soup, peppers, salt and pepper in mixing bowl.
Saute garlic, onions and celery, then mix with soup mixture.
Add chicken and spread over tortillas.
Cover top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
With mixer, blend soup mix, butter, brandy and ginger.
Turn onto wax paper and shape into an 8 x 2-inch log.
Wrap in plastic wrap on wax paper; chill until firm.
For pie, gently saute ground meat in heavy skillet, breaking into small pieces.
Cook until lightly browned.
Drain.
Add onion and saute until soft, but not browned.
Add mushrooms and saute until heated through.
Add mixed vegetables, Italian seasoning, parsley and sugar.
Stir gently.
Add broth.
Simmer until vegetables are done.
In small bowl, blend flour and butter. Gradually add to ground meat mixture, stirring gently.
Cook until slightly thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to baking dish.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Combine dry ingredients.
Rub in margarine; mix in enough water to form a stiff dough.
Roll out mixture, one-third at a time, between sheets of waxed paper to 1/8-inch thickness.
Cut into sticks, 1 x 3-inches.
Bake on cookie sheet at 325° until browned, approximately
8 to 12 minutes.
Watch carefully as outside sticks brown faster than inside ones.
Change position.
When cool, store in airtight container.
Combine ham, onion, cheese and dried parsley in bowl. In separate bowl, beat together egg, milk and oil.
Add 2 cups buttermilk baking mix, blending well.
Add ham mixture, stirring until mixed.
Then add remaining 1 cup baking mix, stirring until blended.
Turn dough out onto floured surface.
Knead about 10 times or until dough holds together.
Roll out dough, about 3/4-inch thick.
Cut with 2-inch biscuit cutter.
Repeat until all dough is used.
Place biscuits on greased baking sheet and brush tops with melted butter.
Sprinkle with herbs.
Bake in 425° oven for 10 to 12 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve warm.
Drain the gooseberries. Add the water to the syrup. Mix the 3/4 cup sugar, flour and salt. Add to the liquid.

Add the egg yolks and melted butter or margarine. Cook until thick. Add the vanilla. Gently fold in gooseberries. Cover pan and cool. When cool, pour into a baked 9-inch pie shell or tart shells. Beat together the 2 egg whites, cream of tartar and 4 tablespoons of sugar until all sugar is dissolved.
(When meringue weeps, you haven't dissolved the sugar.)
Pile meringue lightly on pie (seal to crust to stop shrinking).
Bake at 400° until delicately browned (about 8 minutes).
Cool slowly out of draft.
Put sugar, flour, salt, vanilla and eggs in a bowl.
Beat well. Add milk and beat again.
Add melted butter and beat again. Bake in unbaked pie shells at 375° for 45 minutes.
This will make three medium-size pies.
Pour boiling water over oats in a large bowl; add butter and allow to melt, stirring occasionally.
When cooled to lukewarm, add sugars, eggs and vanilla; stir briskly to combine.
Sift flour and remaining ingredients in another bowl and add to oat mixture. Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Let cool for a few minutes.
Spread with frosting and broil.
Combine first 8 ingredients in order given.
Blend 3/4 of cheese with milk with tuna mixture.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Set the butter out to soften ahead of time.
Beat the softened butter and brown sugar together until well blended.
Beat in the vanilla, egg yolks and lemon rind.
Mix in crock-pot the soup and rice.
Place chicken on top. Add diced celery.
Put lid on; cook on low for 4 hours, until chicken is done.
In heavy skillet, melt shortening.
Add chops and brown well on both sides
(about 15 minutes).
In greased casserole, alternate
layers
of
potatoes,
carrots
and onion.
Arrange chops
over
vegetables.
Stir flour in skillet.
Add salt and pepper.
Slowly
add
milk.
Cook,
stirring constantly, until smooth and thickened.
Pour over vegetables and meat.
Bake in hot oven at 400° for 45 minutes, covered.
Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.
Serves 6.
Score meat on both sides by making diagonal cuts at 1-inch intervals on surface.
Place in a plastic bag set in a shallow dish.
Add marinade and orange slices.
Seal bag; turn to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 6 to 24 hours, turning bag occasionally.
Cut pork into pieces 1 X 1 X 1/2-inch.
Mix flour and seasonings.
Mix egg and milk; beat well.
Roll pork in flour mixture and shake off excess.
Dip in milk mixture and mix thoroughly.
Drain well, then dip in flour mixture again, mixing until well coatd.
Shake off excess flour and fry in deep fat at 350° until the crust is brown and crisp, then drain and place on plate.
Serve with sweet and sour sauce.
Combine cheeses, garlic, mustard and salt in a bowl.
Add chopped mushrooms, onion, pimento and parsley.
Turn mixture into lightly buttered 3-cup mold.
Refrigerate until firm.
Unmold onto serving platter.
Garnish with sliced mushrooms and parsley. Serve with crackers.
Makes 3 1/2 cups spread.
Put everything except coconut, nuts and chocolate chips in blender.
Mix.
Stir in coconut, nuts and chocolate chips.
Put into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 350° until pie is golden brown.
Cook onion in margarine until tender; cool.
Lay slices of cheese over pie dough.
Follow with spinach, then onions.
Beat eggs, adding enough milk to make 1 cup.
Add seasoning and pour over ingredients in the pie shell.
Bake in 400° oven about 35 minutes or until a knife comes out clean.
Serve piping hot.
(Can be frozen after baking.)
Serves 4.
Butter square pan (9 x 9 x 2-inch).
Mix milk, sugar and salt in 2-quart saucepan.
Heat to boiling over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in marshmallows, chocolate chips, vanilla and nuts until melted.
Pour into pan.
Refrigerate until firm (at least 1 hour).
Cut into 1 1/2-inch squares. Yields 3 dozen candies.
Say prayer.
Season chops.
Put 1 slice tomato on each chop followed by a layer of rice.
(Use all the rice on this layer.) Next layer, add onion, then green pepper.
Bake at 300° to 325° for approximately 2 hours.
Combine ingredients in a bowl and work with hand until well mixed.
Pinch off piece of dough the size of a small walnut and roll between the palms of the hands.
Place on cookie sheet; press one-half blanched almond on top with thumb.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes at 350°.
Remove from pan at once.
Makes about 25 to 32 cookies.
Heat butter in saucepan and saute onion about 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in flour.
Add broth and milk gradually, stirring with wire whisk to form smooth sauce.
In a small saucepan, melt butter.
Stir in crumbs.
Reserve 1 tablespoon for garnish and pat crumbs on bottom of buttered 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Set aside.
In medium bowl, combine pie filling, condensed milk and lemon juice.
Mix until smooth. Spread into prepared pan.
Top with whipping cream and reserved crumbs.
Freeze for 3 hours.
Serves 9.
Melt cheese in pan over hot water.
Heat soup with all remaining ingredients except egg.
Add soup mixture to cheese. Add egg and mix thoroughly over hot water for 5 minutes.
Serve on toast or crackers.
Keeps for several weeks in refrigerator.
Mix all ingredients except Equal.
Cook on High 2 minutes; stir.
Cook on High 2 minutes; stir.
Cook and stir every 1 minute until thick.
Add small amount of chocolate to egg yolks, then return to chocolate mix.
Cook on Medium (1/2 power) for 1 minute. Cook on Medium 1 minute; stir.
Add margarine; stir.
Pour into baked pie crust.
After pie cools some, put in Equal (heat takes some sweetness away).
Add meringue.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Coat chicken breasts with flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Brown in 5 tablespoons of butter and remove.
Arrange breasts close together in shallow pan.
Add onions to pan drippings; cook until tender.
Stir in chicken broth and wine; bring to boil and pour over chicken.
Cover and bake for 1 hour or more, until chicken is tender.
Cook mushrooms in remaining 3 tablespoons of butter.
Add to chicken, along with grapes.
Cover and continue to bake for 10 minutes.
In a separate bowl combine 2 tablespoons of sugar and 2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix the butter, applesauce, 1 1/2 cup sugar and the eggs in thoroughly.
Blend in the flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt.
Take about a heaping tablespoonful of dough and roll it in cinnamon and sugar in a separate bowl.
Batter will be sticky.
You may need more cinnamon and sugar.
Place on a silver cookie sheet.
Bake for 9 minutes. Cookies will spread big, thin and chewy.
Salt and pepper chicken and fry in butter until browned.
Add mushrooms, wine and sour cream to the chicken and mix well, add artichokes.
Cover and simmer until chicken is tender (about 25 minutes).
Stir occasionally.
Serve over egg noodles.
Recipe can be easily doubled.
Reserve 1/3 cup mushroom juice.
Saute onions and mushrooms in margarine.
Add juice, milk, flour and scallops to onion and mushrooms in baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs and paprika. Bake, covered, for 30 minutes at 375°.

Rinse tuna in cold water; drain, then flake into a 3-cup bowl. Blend in the bread, celery, onion, mayonnaise, salt and pepper. Pour tuna mixture into lightly greased 1 1/2-cup baking dish; top with cheese.
Bake in oven preheated to 325° for 20 minutes. Makes 1 serving.

recipes.t: Died And Gone To Heaven Dessert
d: Mix devil's food cake mix following directions on box.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip.
Spread this mixture on cool cake.
Heat water and beans to boiling in 3-quart saucepan.
Boil 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover and let stand 1 hour.
Cook broccoli until barely tender.
Put in buttered 8-inch baking dish.
Make White Sauce; add cheese.
Beat egg yolks, sugar, salt and pepper to taste.
Add to White Sauce.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into sauce.
Pour over broccoli.
Bake in a 350° oven for 20 minutes or until firm.
Serves 4 to 6.
Toss nuts in soy sauce.
Bake at 400° for 3 to 5 minutes or until brown and toasted.
Cover pan with foil to avoid burning. Mix lettuce, grapes, walnuts and chicken in bowl.
Cover with dressing and serve.
Combine sugars, baking soda, salt, sour cream and corn syrup in a heavy saucepan.
Cook over moderate heat to thread stage (230° on candy thermometer), stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Beat in butter, vanilla and pecans.
Cool to warm, then beat until mixture begins to lose its sheen.
Working rapidly to prevent candy from setting, drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper. If candy begins to set, return to heat or put pot in a bowl of boiling water until mixture is soft and smooth.
When set and cool, remove pralines to a tray.
Makes about 36.

recipes.t: Fresh Basil And Tomato Pesto Without Pine Nuts(From Your Garden)
d: Food process the basil, olive oil and Parmesan cheese about 45 seconds and remove.
Add tomatoes.
Mix together with basil mixture.
Pour over vermicelli cooked al dente.
Combine sugar, flour, lemon peel and cinnamon.
Toss with apples and lemon juice.
Turn into pastry lined pie plate.
Adjust top crust.
Seal and flute edges.
Cut vents into crust.
Microwave at High 10 to 12 minutes or until filling is bubbly.
Then bake in conventional oven at 425° for 10 to 15 minutes or until golden.
Cream together the shortening, peanut butter, sugars and egg. Add dry ingredients; stir well.
Shape into little balls.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Place on ungreased pan, 2 inches apart.
Bake for 7 minutes.
Pour boiling water over cherry jello.
Stir until jello is dissolved.
Add cold water and stir.
Add pineapple juice, orange juice and lemonade.
Stir well. When ready to serve, add ginger ale.
Makes 16 (8-ounce) cups.
Flour sides of steak.
Brown in hot oil in a skillet.
Add all ingredients.
Cover.
Cook over low heat or in a 250 to 300 degree oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Uncover the last 15 minutes to cook down to a thick sauce.
Serves 6. Has a delicious smoked flavor.
Scald
milk.
Cool
to
lukewarm.
Add
sugar,
melted butter, salt, yeast cake and
the eggs.
Stir in cardamon seed and flour to mix. Turn out
on floured
board and knead until smooth and elastic.
Place in
greased bowl and let rise until double in size.
Turn out and
tie
in
bowknots or braid into two loaves. Ice, if
desired.
Bake
at 375° approximately 30 minutes.
Cook potatoes (boil).
Strain, place in crock or heavy bowl that will hold heat.
Heat green beans in potato water.
Drain. Heat oil until hot.
Slice onion.
Cube potatoes with knife. Place green beans over potatoes.
Place onion (separated) over green beans.
Sprinkle vinegar over onions.
Salt and pepper. With hot oil, drizzle over onions.
(If onions don't sizzle, oil isn't hot enough.) Mix gently!
Serve hot.
Saute meat in oil in a 10-inch skillet for 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Add onion.
Saute 2 to 3 more minutes.
Drain apricots.
Add syrup and barbecue sauce to pork.
Add salt and black pepper.
Bring to boil.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until meat is tender.
Add green pepper.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend cornstarch and water.
Stir in mixture.
Cook, stirring, until thickened.
Add apricots and pineapple; heat gently.
Serve over rice or parsley noodles.
Combine 1st five ingredients.
Place chicken mixture in center of crescent roll, wrap and pinch edges together.
Place in baking dish and pour melted butter over rolls.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs over all.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Make lamb into patties and fry, drain.
Place patties in baking dish.
Pour spaghetti sauce over top, then sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese begins to turn and bubble.
Dissolve gelatin in 1 cup boiling water.
Cool to room temperature.
Slowly add ginger ale.
Arrange apple wedges and some pineapple in a 4 1/2-cup mold.
Pour in 3/4 cup of the lemon gelatin mixture.
Chill until almost firm.
Split birds in half and sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Place each half on square of heavy foil.
Pour olive oil over each and grease well.
Place birds skin side down and fill cavity with other ingredients mixed together.
Fold foil squares around birds to keep in all juices.
Bake in a 300° oven for 1 hour or until tender.
Open foil and turn birds skin side up. Raise heat and brown about 20 minutes.
Bring 3 cups water to a boil and add orange and raspberry gelatin.
Mix well, then add cranberry sauce and crushed pineapple.
Stir well until cranberry sauce has dissolved.
Add chopped pecans.
Pour into large glass casserole or mold and chill overnight or until firm.
In skillet, heat 1 cup sugar, stirring until it melts.
Stir constantly until golden.
Carefully stir in warm milk, 2 cups sugar and the butter.
Cook to soft ball stage, 234°.
Remove from heat. Stir in the orange peel and nuts.
Pour into large Pyrex greased pan and spread evenly.
Cool completely before cutting into pieces. WATCH and add those last 2 cups of sugar while the first mixture is very light in color as it burns easily.
My favorite.
Cover
9 x 13-inch glass pan with cracker crumbs.
Slice bananas on top,
then
slices of ice cream on top of bananas. Sprinkle walnuts on top and freeze until firm.
Melt chocolate chips and 1/2 cup butter. Add
powdered
sugar and evaporated milk.
Cook until thick and smooth; add vanilla.
Cool.
Pour over
ice
cream and return to freezer.
Top with whipped cream and a cup of cracker crumbs.
Mash cheese in bowl with mixing fork.
Beat in butter, cream and add egg yolk.
Knead in flour.
Form into ball.
Wrap in wax paper and chill until firm. Roll out to 1/4 inch.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch rounds.
Brush with egg and bake at 425° for 10 to 15 minutes.
These can be baked, frozen and reheated for 5 minutes.
Mix cake as directed on box.
Substitute unsweetened applesauce instead of oil.
Use egg whites (no yolks).
Bake about 25 minutes.
Let cool.
Punch holes in cake.
Mix one box of sugar-free strawberry jello with 3/4 cup hot water and pour over cake.
Frost with lite Cool Whip and decorate with fresh strawberries.
In a saucepan, melt butter.
Cook onion until tender, but not brown.
Remove from the heat.
Add tuna, zucchini, eggs, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Add 1/2 of the bread crumbs.
Stir until well combined.
Shape into six patties; coat with bread crumbs and fry in hot cooking oil, about 3 minutes on each side, until golden brown.
In a large saucepan, bring to a boil the sugar, cream of tartar and evaporated milk.
When it comes to a boil, cook for 6 minutes by the clock, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Remove from heat.
Pour over bits of margarine.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Stir.
Pour into a greased pan (I use margarine).
Allow to stand at room temperature for approximately 1 hour.
Cut in squares or refrigerate overnight and cut the following day.
Brown meat and drain.
Add cheese but reserve some to garnish. Combine meat, soup, cheese, milk, green peppers and garlic salt. In a 2-quart casserole dish, layer 1 cup of meat mixture and 4 tortillas.
Repeat layer 2 more times.
Top with remaining mixture.
Cover and bake for 50 to 55 minutes at 350°.
Just be served top with lettuce, tomatoes and cheese.
Delicious with pinto beans.
Brown onion and beef.
Add potatoes, turnip, carrots and celery.
When almost done, add shredded cabbage and Gravy Master.
Cook macaroni 9 minutes in boiling water.
Drain and pour cold water over.
Put macaroni in buttered casserole dish.
Add oleo, cheese and salt.
Beat eggs and slowly add the hot milk to them. Add the egg and milk mixture to the macaroni.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes, uncovered.
Sift
together first
3 ingredients; set aside.
Cream butter.
Add
honey
a little at a time.
Mix well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mixture will appear to separate.
Gradually add dry ingredients; mix until moistened. Fold
in
coconut, morsels
and
cereal.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes
or until
golden
brown.
Remove
cookies to cooling rack.
Mix all ingredients except flavoring in saucepan.
Cook, stir while cooking, until soft ball stage.
Remove from heat, add flavoring and butter.
This will fill a two-layer cake.
Use your favorite cake recipe for the layers.
Mix meat, onions, sauerkraut and paprika.
Place in large casserole or Dutch oven.
Add bouillon.
Cook at 375° for 1 hour. Add cubed potatoes and more broth, if necessary.
Cook 1 more hour.
Remove from oven and stir in sour cream or yogurt.
Makes 10 servings.
Combine 1 cup flour, yeast, onion, salt and dill weed.
Add cottage cheese, water, egg and honey to flour mixture.
Beat 3 minutes by hand or with electric mixer.
Beat in remaining flour. Cover and let rise in warm place until double in bulk (about 1 hour).
Stir down batter; pour into a well-greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Let rise in a warm place until light (30 to 40 minutes).
Bake at 375° for 50 to 55 minutes or until done.

recipes.t: Dave'S Sweet And Sour Pork Chops
d: Mix together the brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic and pineapple juice.
Put the pork chops in a large Ziploc bag and pour the juice over them.
Let them sit in the refrigerator overnight.
Remove crusts from bread; cut in half.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch glass casserole dish.
Layer bread, ham, Cheddar cheese and Swiss cheese.
Repeat layers.
Combine and pour over the casserole the following:
dry mustard, eggs, onion salt and milk.
Put few pats of butter on top before baking.
Can be made the day before and refrigerated.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes or longer, if necessary, depending on your oven heat.
Serves 10.
Melt butter and stir in crumbs.
Press into 9 x 9-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cook onion in
butter until tender.
Add rice, cream of mushroom soup and
half
can
water.
Cook and drain broccoli. Mix all together.
Pour
in
casserole and cook for 30 minutes at 350°.
Let set a little while before serving.
Spoon 1/4 cup ice cream into each of 8 (4 ounce) chilled parfait glasses.
Freeze 30 minutes.
Toast and chop almonds. Crush toffee bars.
Layer 1/2 tablespoon each of almonds, candy and chocolate syrup.
Repeat layers of ice cream, almonds, candy and chocolate.
Cover and freeze until firm.
Garnish each parfait with whipped cream and a cherry.
Yields 8 parfaits.
Stuff each pitted date with a pecan half.
Roll in brown sugar. Cut bacon slices into 4 pieces each.
Wrap 1 piece bacon around each stuffed date; secure with a toothpick.
Broil until bacon is crisp.
Makes about 8 servings.
In large saucepan, cook bacon until crisp.
Drain, reserving 1 tablespoon drippings.
Crumble bacon; set aside.
Cook and stir onion in reserved drippings until tender.
Add carrots, potato, parsley, marjoram (if using), pepper and water.
Bring to boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer 20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Add sausage, beans and reserved bacon.
Cook until well heated.
Makes 6 servings.
Slice potatoes about 1/4 inch thick.
Arrange potatoes and onion slices with smaller pieces toward center.
Stir water and barbecue sauce together and pour over.
Cook on high about 12 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl; set aside.
Beat eggs and peanut butter until smooth.
Blend in apple juice concentrate, milk and margarine.
Add to dry ingredients, mixing just until dry ingredients are moistened.
Add peanuts.
Spoon half of batter evenly into 12 greased muffin pans.
Drop 1 1/2 teaspoons strawberry fruit spread into center of each.
Cover with remaining batter.
Bake at 350° for 18 minutes.
Let cool 5 minutes.
Remove from pan.
Serve warm.
Cook broccoli slightly.
Do not overcook.
Saute onion in margarine.
Cook rice in 2 cups water.
Drain broccoli.
Combine all ingredients, saving small amount of cheese for top of casserole.
Put in greased casserole and sprinkle with remainder of cheese.
Bake uncovered at 325° for 30 minutes.
Can be made a day ahead.
Also freezes well.
Allow extra 15 minutes cooking time if casserole has been refrigerated.
In a large saucepan, combine tomato juice and all soups.
Stir until well blended.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and let simmer. In a medium bowl, combine flour, salt, baking powder, milk and eggs.
Drop by level teaspoonfuls into simmering soup.
Cover; cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, or until dumplings are firm. Serve immediately.
Peel and cut root end off each onion so that it will sit level.
Remove about 1/2-inch core from each onion.
Press 1 tablespoon butter into cored center and sprinkle paprika over the top.
Place in 9-inch baking dish; cover with plastic wrap (leave one corner open for vent).
Cook on High power for 12 to 14 minutes or until tender.
Let stand for 5 minutes; sprinkle with salt before serving.
Pinch angel food cake in small pieces.
Place in oblong Pyrex dish.
In large bowl, add Cool Whip, sour cream, sugar, vanilla and lemon juice.
Pour over angel food cake pieces.
Top with red pie cherries.
Place in refrigerator overnight or until used.
Combine rice, sour cream, milk, salt, green chilies and 1/2 cup cheese.
Mix well.
Spoon into a buttered, shallow 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with remaining 1/2 cup cheese.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Heat marshmallows, milk and margarine over low heat until melted.
Mix crumbs, fruit and nuts; pour mixture over them. Shape into small balls and roll in coconut.
Store.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine sweet potatoes and sugar in a mixing bowl.
Mix well and add salt, eggs, cinnamon, milk, vanilla and 1 stick melted oleo.
Blend all ingredients well.
Spray 9 x 13-inch oblong dish with Pam and pour above mixture into the dish. In a medium size bowl, add brown sugar and flour.
Add 2/3 cup melted oleo and pecans.
Mixture will be crumbly.
Spoon over potato mixture and bake for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
You can also top with mini marshmallows and bake a few extra minutes.
Melt butter in sauce pan.
Stir in marshmallows.
Cook and stir over low heat til melted.
Remove from heat; stir in cereal & pecans.
Let cool just enough to handle with greased hands.
Shape into trees or cones.
Roll in green sugar.
Looks really festive on a silver tray with powdered sugar dusted on them & the tray.
Mix apple mixture well.
Put in bottom crust.
Dot with butter.
Cover with top crust.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes at 425°. Nice spicy flavor.
Slice pork and serve on platter over pasta.
Cover with tomatoes.
Garnish and enjoy.
Break the donuts into pieces.
Place in a buttered pan.
Mix the eggs with enough milk to saturate the donuts.
Add raisins, cinnamon and sugar to suit your taste.
You can add chopped apples, if you prefer.
Pour the liquid mixture over the donuts; the liquid will saturate the donuts.
Set the pan inside another pan partially filled with water for a steam bath.
Bake at 350° until knife will come out clean.
This will probably take at least 1 hour or more for a large batch and 45 minutes for a family size serving.
Let the pudding cool before serving.
In a 3-quart saucepan, brown ground beef and drain.
Add the butter or margarine with the rice mixture and onion to the beef. Slowly add the hot water, green pepper, tomatoes and chili powder. Heat to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover saucepan and simmer until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, approximately 15 minutes. Sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Allow to melt.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown beef with salt, sugar, garlic and tomato sauce.
Simmer 15 minutes; add onions.
Simmer 5 more minutes.
Boil noodles (per package directions).
Mix the cream cheese and sour cream.
Stack in layers like lasagna; top with Cheddar and Mozzarella cheese, grated.
Put in oven at 350° to melt the cheese for 40 minutes.
Fry cubed pork steak until browned and almost cooked.
Stir in tomatoes, seasonings and chilies.
Add water (1, 2 or more cups) to make the green chili a saucelike consistency.
Cook until meat is done and tender.
Serve with cooked pinto beans, fried bread or tortillas.
Great.
Cream shortening with sugar.
Add egg, potato water and yeast. Mix well and add currants, citron, raisins and flour sifted with salt.
Let rise until light.
Drop from spoon in hot fat (365°). Drain on absorbent paper and roll in sugar.
Wash and drain lettuce.
Break into small pieces.
Chill.
Add artichoke hearts, red onion and pimento . Mix olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper and cheese.
Add to lettuce just before serving.
Toss until mixed completely.
Combine bread and cheese.
Dip breast halves in crumb mixture to coat lightly. Arrange in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Set remaining crumb mixture aside.
Mix vegetables with as much mayonnaise as desired.
Salt and pepper to taste and chill.
Season pork chops with salt and pepper.
Spread mustard to one side.
Fry chops in oil with mustard side fried first.
Use fried oil to make flour gravy.
Add rice soup, place pork chops in gravy and simmer until ready to serve.
Rinse the blueberries and remove any stems, leaves or green berries.
Put the berries in a kettle and add the water, cloves and cinnamon stick.
Set over moderate heat and bring to a boil.
Stir in honey; reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, until berries are very tender, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
Force the soup through a strainer or through the medium blade of a food mill.
Stir in lemon juice, creme de cassis and vinegar.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Serve in chilled bowls, garnished with a few whole blueberries, a dollop of plain yogurt and a sprinkle of grated orange rind.
Serves 6.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add 7-Up and cold water. Stuff apricots with cream cheese and pecans.
Place in jello mold and pour jello over stuffed apricots.
Place in refrigerator and let set.
In a medium saucepan, melt chocolate chips and margarine over low heat, stirring frequently.
Remove pan from heat.
Cool to lukewarm.
Beat in egg until smooth and glossy. Add sifted powdered sugar, vanilla and salt.
Mix well. Stir in the 1/2 cup coconut and the chopped peanuts. Chill about 1 hour.
Form into 1-inch balls.
Roll in additional flaked coconut.
Arrange on a baking sheet. Chill at least 3 hours or until firm.
Makes about 2 1/2 dozen balls.
Combine liqueur and gelatin in heat-resistant cup; mix until gelatin is softened.
Place cup in simmering water; heat until gelatin is completely liquefied, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Beat egg yolks in large bowl of electric mixer until light and lemon colored.
Combine water and sugar in medium saucepan; bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until sugar is completely dissolved.
Reduce heat; cook until syrup registers 230° on candy thermometer, about 5 minutes.
With mixer at low speed, slowly add hot syrup to egg yolks in steady stream, beating until well blended.
Add gelatin mixture; continue beating until thick, about 6 minutes.
Let cool.
Spread 1 cup croutons in lightly greased 8 x 11-inch baking dish.
Combine soups, salad dressing and packet of dry soup; spread over croutons.
Top with chicken, broccoli, water chestnuts and mushrooms.
Spread with remaining cup of croutons.
Cover loosely with foil and bake in 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 15 more minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Rub fish with salt, pepper and lemon.
Wrap in foil.
Bake slowly at 250 - 300° for three hours or until done.
Remove foil. Remove skin.
Place salmon on large platter.
Serve with melted butter and lemon.
Perfect side dishes to accompany the baked salmon are parsleyed new potatoes and green peas with pearl onions.
Lemon meringue pie would make an excellent dessert.

In blender, pour entire contents of 1 can of tomatoes and only juice from the second can. Dice tomatoes from second can and set aside. Add onion, bell pepper, cucumber, garlic, onion powder, hot sauce and black pepper. Blend until pureed.
Pour mixture into large bowl.
Add diced tomatoes and mix well. Chill well.
Butter bread slices.
Spread each slice with mayonnaise. Spread one slice with peanut butter.
Cover one slice with chopped celery.
Assemble sandwiches and cut into thirds.
Place the brisket in a large roasting pan.
Fill roasting pan with water to half-way level of brisket.
Add spices.
Cook 6 to 8 hours, covered, at 250°.
During last hour, add red chilies.
Fry the bacon until crisp.
Remove from pan and drain well. Discard all but 1 tablespoon fat.
Saute the onion 2 to 3 minutes over low heat.
Add the beans and stir several minutes.
Season with garlic salt, salt and pepper to taste.
Add sour cream; stir until smooth.
Transfer to a bowl; crumble the bacon on top and serve.
Delicious with baked potatoes or raw or poached vegetables.

Cream butter and sugar together. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Melt the chocolate bar in the top of a double boiler (or microwave to melt) with 1/4 cup of the butter. Add chocolate to the egg mixture. Add soda to the buttermilk; fold in buttermilk mixture and flour alternately by hand. Stir in salt, nuts, and vanilla. Pour into a 10-inch tube pan, greased and floured. Bake at 325° for 90 minutes. Remove from pan and cool.
Beat eggs; add sugar and pineapple.
Cook until it boils; remove and add jello.
Stir until dissolved.
Place in cold water until cool.
Beat milk and fold into mixture; pour into a vanilla wafer pie crust.
Refrigerate to set.
Melt butter in a frying pan and add Gioia Rosa Marina.
Saute and mix constantly on low-medium heat until brown.
This will take 5 to 10 minutes.
Be careful not to burn the Rosa Marina!
Grease 1 1/2-quart casserole and place ingredients in dish in order listed.
Dot each layer with a little butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
To speed up baking time, cook potatoes partially before using.
Brown the hamburger meat and drain. Cook shell macaroni as directed and drain well. Combine hamburger meat, macaroni, tomato soup and cheese (cut in chunks) in a large soup pan.
Cook on low heat until cheese has melted. Stir frequently.
Serve hot. Serves 8 to 10.
Drain the fruit cocktail, reserving syrup.
Dissolve the jello in the boiling water.
Add the reserved syrup and enough water to measure 1 3/4 cups.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Fold in fruit cocktail.
Pour into a 9-inch dish. Chill until firm. Unmold. Combine the heavy cream, Miracle Whip and marshmallows. Spoon over jello.
Chill thoroughly.
Makes 9 to 12 servings.
Add vinegar to beaten eggs and sugar.
Cook until thick, turn on low and add marshmallows.
Stir until dissolved.
Add gelatin softened in cold water.
Add crushed pineapple, fruit cocktail, nuts and whipped cream and chill.
Heat butter in large skillet.
Add scallops and salt and pepper to taste.
Cook until scallops are cooked.
Remove and put aside.
Add onions, celery and carrots.
Cook for 7 minutes.
Add sage and white wine.
Cook 3 minutes.
Add milk.
Lower heat to simmer and clam juice.
Heat until hot.
Add potatoes and scallops.
Let simmer for 20 minutes, then serve.
Cook macaroni by directions on box; rinse and drain.
Add vegetables, cheese and pickles to macaroni.
Combine mayonnaise, sour cream and salt.
Mix with the macaroni mixture.
Chill.
Combine thoroughly beef, bread crumbs, milk, onion, garlic salt and pepper.
Shape into 35 meatballs.
Chill 1 hour.
Melt butter in electric skillet.
Brown meatballs.
Spoon out extra grease.
Combine soup and water.
Add to meatballs and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Heat corn syrup to boiling in 3 quart saucepan.
Reduce heat. Add chocolate chips and vanilla.
Stir over low heat until chocolate is melted.
Remove from heat.
Fold in cereal until well coated.
Fold in marshmallows.
Drop by tablespoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Let clusters stand at room temperature until firm, about 2 hours.
Toss together the first 5 ingredients.
Meanwhile, heat the oil at medium high in a deep medium sized skillet until it begins to smoke slightly.
Stir the boiling water into the cornmeal mixture.
(Add more cornmeal as needed.
You should end up with a stiff paste you can push off the end of a spoon.)
Form rounded tablespoonfuls of the mush, flatten slightly and drop into the hot oil.
Fry until crisp and golden, about 4 minutes.
Remove the cakes with a slotted spoon to drain on paper towels.
Keep warm. Makes about 30 pieces.
In a large skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of margarine; add salt, pepper and shrimp.
Saute for 2 minutes until shrimp turn pink. Remove with slotted spoon.
Melt remaining margarine; add green onions and tarragon and saute for 3 minutes.
Add rum, stirring constantly to deglaze and cook for 30 seconds.
Return shrimp to pan with any extra liquid and cook for 1 minute or until hot. Serve over yellow rice.
Thaw frozen fillets and remove skin.
Cut fillets into 1-inch pieces.
Fry bacon until lightly browned in a large kettle over low heat.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Add tomatoes, potatoes, corn, peas, catsup and seasonings.
Bring to the boiling point.
Reduce heat and cook covered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add fish and continue cooking for 40 to 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Yields 10 servings.
Cream the sugar and butter together.
Add 1 cup of flour at a time.
Mix well.
Add rest of ingredients.
Measure by teaspoon and drop on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° approximately 20 minutes.
Saute bacon and onion.
Add catsup and heat through.
Cook noodles until tender and drain.
Combine noodles and bacon mixture.
Heat through and serve.
Makes 6 average servings.

recipes.t: Creamy Crunchy Potatoes(Great Barbecue Side Dish)
d: In a saucepan cook onion in 2 tablespoons butter until tender. In a bowl, combine thawed hash browns, sour cream, cream soup, onion mixture and jalapenos, if you like.
Transfer to a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle with cornflakes and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 45 minutes or until golden.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Soften yeast in warm water. Sift together flour and salt in a large mixing bowl. Cut in butter/margarine and shortening.
Blend in the beaten eggs, sour cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla and yeast.
Mix thoroughly and chill at least 2 hours. Combine 1 1/2 cups sugar and 2 teaspoons vanilla. Set aside.

Roll out 1/2 of chilled dough on surface sprinkled with 1/2 cup vanilla sugar. Roll out into an 8 x 16-inch rectangle. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon vanilla sugar. Fold one end over dough over center, then fold the other end to make 3 layers. Turn 1/4 of the way around and repeat rolling and folding twice, sprinkling surface with additional vanilla sugar each time as needed.
Roll again out to an 8 x 16-inch rectangle, 1/4-inch thick.
Cut into 4 x 1-inch strips.
Twist each strip 2 or 3 times.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Combine sugar, milk and egg.
Add salt, ginger, cinnamon, lemon
extract
and
biscuit
mix; beat until well mixed. Fold in cranberries
and
nuts.
Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Bake in moderate
oven
at 350° for 60 to 65 minutes.
Remove from pan; cool before slicing.
Place all ingredients through food chopper or grater and into a large bowl.
Add grated cheese and tomato sauce.
Mix well. Place a good portion on each wiener bun and wrap in wax paper and bake in slow oven at 200° at least 1 hour.
Serve and enjoy.
May be frozen and used later.
Makes 24 servings.
Mix the hamburger, chorizo, turkey, cheese and beans into a large mixing bowl.
Spread a large spoonful of the mix onto each of the tortillas.
Roll and bake at 375° for fifteen minutes or until the tortillas begin to brown.
Dissolve the two gelatins in boiling water.
Add vinegar, pepper and salt and dissolve.
Add cold water.
Chill.
When slightly thickened, fold in remaining ingredients.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill and let set until firm.
Cut into squares. Serves 8.
Combine dry ingredients.
Combine banana, milk, egg and shortening.
Add to flour mixture; stir to blend.
Pour into greased 9 x 9-inch baking pan.
Arrange cranberry slices on top and then pecan halves.
Sprinkle a little sugar over the top and bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cook and crumble sausage.
Drain.
In a large bowl, combine biscuit mix and cheese.
Add the sausage and stir until well blended.
Stir in water just until mixed.
Shape into 1 1/2-inch balls.
Place on greased baking sheets.
Bake at 375° for about 15 minutes or until golden.
These may be frozen.
Yield:
4 dozen.
Chop chocolate into small chunks; set aside.
Cream butter until soft.
Add sugars, eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Blend in flour, soda and salt.
Stir in chocolate pieces and nuts.
Drop from teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheets about 2-inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Makes 4 to 5 dozen.
Grease and flour 10-inch tube pan.
Heat oven to 325°.
Cream sugar, eggs, margarine and shortening until fluffy.
Blend in lemon extract.
Add flour and milk, alternately beating after each addition.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake for 60 to 65 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes before removing from pan.
Allow to cool before serving.
Serve plain, sprinkle with confectioners sugar or top with your favorite glaze.
Cook bacon, onion rings and green pepper until tender; drain. Combine all ingredients in a 2 qt. casserole.

recipes.t: Even Better The Next Day Casserole
d: Fry bacon until it starts to get crisp.
Then add onion and green pepper and continue frying for a few minutes.
Then add ground beef and cook until tender and browned.
When well done, add tomatoes, cooked spaghetti and mushrooms and simmer on a low heat for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Then pour into 2 medium-size greased casseroles.
Sprinkle with sharp cheese and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Good the first day, but "even better the next" as the flavors blend.
Prepare fettuccine as package directs.
In medium saucepan over medium heat, melt margarine; stir in flour, broth, basil, garlic powder and pepper.
Gradually stir in milk; cook and stir until slightly thickened and bubbly.
Stir in chicken; heat through.
In large serving bowl, combine hot cooked fettuccine and sauce; toss to coat.
Serve immediately with cheese.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Brown sausage, hamburger and onion.
Add pepperoni, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Drain.
Return to pan and add pizza sauce.
Cook all macaroni together until tender.
Drain.
Mix meat, sauce and noodles together.
Put into baking pan and top with Mozzarella cheese.
Bake in oven about 25 minutes, basically until cheese is melted.
Dissolve lemon jello in 2 cups boiling water and add 1 cup cold water; chill until syrupy.
Add celery, pineapple, cheese and then Dream Whip.
Chill.
When serving, you can put a small amount of mayonnaise on each serving and put a cherry on it.
Serve on a lettuce leaf.
Grease pan.
Put in hamburger, tomatoes, vegetables and salt and pepper.
Bake in oven at 375° about 2 1/2 hours .
Cover with lid to bake.
Prepare cake mix as directed on box.
Make 3 layers.
Let cool.
Beat together in top of double boiler egg whites, Karo syrup,
sugar and cream of tartar and water.
Beat until it stands in peaks.
Remove double boiler from heat.
Add vanilla; beat until vanilla is mixed.
Spread frosting and coconut between cake layers and on top.
Preheat oven to 425°.
In large bowl combine flour and next 4 ingredients; mix well.
Add butter, using two knives or pastry cutter to cut butter into dry mixture.
Cut mixture until it resembles coarse meal; set aside.
In small bowl, beat eggs and milk.
Pour all at once into dry ingredients.
Stir quickly with fork until just moistened.
Fold in frozen berries.
Gather dough into ball.
Place on lightly floured board.
Sprinkle with 2 teaspoons flour.
Knead 6 times.
Press into a rectangle, about 3/4 inch thick.
Cut into 6 squares, then in half to form 12 triangles. Place 1 inch apart on buttered baking sheet.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes or until lightly browned.
Serve immediately with Honey Butter. Makes 12 scones.
Crust:
Mix cake mix with the water, brown sugar, margarine and eggs.
Put foil on pizza pan and grease it.
Spread cake mixture over the foil.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool.
For ease in serving, peel off foil and replace cake on pizza pan.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix baking mix, 1/3 cup mayonnaise and the milk until soft dough forms.
Beat vigorously for 30 seconds.
Turn onto surface floured with baking mix.
Knead 10 times.
Pat into rectangle, 12 x 8-inches, on greased cookie sheet.
Bake until light brown, about 8 minutes.
Combine egg yolks, sugar, vinegar, pineapple syrup and salt in top of double boiler.
Cook over hot, not boiling, water until thick, stirring constantly.
Add butter and cool.
Fold in whipped cream, a little at a time.
Add to fruit.
Spoon into serving bowl.
Chill in refrigerator.
Saute onion and celery in butter.
Brown ground beef.
Cook rice.
Mix meat, rice and vegetables together.
Add tomato sauce, sugar, salt and pepper.
Put 1/2 of mixture in 9-inch pan.
Cover with Velveeta slices.
Repeat.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt over hot water the chocolate chips and shortening.
Stir until melted and smooth.
Pour half into an 8-inch foil lined square pan.
Refrigerate until firm (15 minutes). Return remaining to low heat.
Combine over hot water the caramels, butter and water. Stir until caramels are melted and mixture is smooth. Stir in nuts.
Pour over cooled chocolate.
Spread and refrigerate 15 minutes. Top with remaining chocolate.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Cut in squares.
Combine vegetable oil, vinegar, sugar, pepper and salt as a dressing.
Combine vegetables.
Just prior to serving, add sunflower seeds and crushed noodles.
Pour dressing over all.
Place mushrooms, onion, celery and butter in a 3-quart casserole.
Cook, covered, on High for 2 to 3 minutes or until tender.
Stir in stuffing mix and enough broth to moisten. Stuffing should be very moist.
Spread stuffing evenly in casserole and cook on High for 2 to 4 minutes.
Let stand, covered, 5 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
Brush jelly pan or cookie sheet with oil.
Line with wax paper; oil paper.
Beat yolks and regular sugar until pale yellow and thick.
Beat in ground walnuts and baking powder.
Beat egg whites until stiff; fold into egg and sugar.
Spread batter in pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cover with damp cloth and cool.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Spread Cool Whip on cake. Roll up.
Cover cake with Cool Whip and blueberries.
Combine cocoa and hot water, stirring.
Cool.
Cream oleo and sugar; beat in egg yolks, one at a time.
Blend in vanilla and cocoa mixture.
Sift flour, salt and soda together; add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk, beating well.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites; pour mixture into 2 greased and floured pans. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool and frost.
In a bowl, grate potatoes and onion.
Add flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg; blend.
Fry in hot greased skillet until golden brown. Perfect!

In a pan or skillet, melt butter and mix with salt and pepper. Lay pork chops in melted butter mixture. Pour ketchup on each chop and pour enough Coke to cover the chops in the pan. Let come to a boil. Simmer for 45 minutes or until tender and sauce begins to thicken.
Mix corn, cream, oil, peppers and cheese.
Add dry ingredients and eggs.
Mix.
Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Combine dry mustard and vinegar; let set 30 minutes.
Mix in all other ingredients and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick.
Slice bread diagonally, almost through.
Mix first 3 ingredients and spread between bread slices and on top.
Sprinkle bread with paprika and parsley flakes.
Wrap bread in foil, bake in preheated oven at 400° for 20 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Saute shrimp in a little oil until pink.
Drain and cool. Sift all dry ingredients.
Add pounded green chilli peppers, onion and chopped coriander.
Add shrimp and mix into a stiff batter. Deep fry in oil until brown.
Preheat oven to a broil.
In a large skillet, combine margarine, lemon juice, salt and spices.
Cook over low heat until margarine has melted.
Cut cherries, pineapple, oranges, marshmallows and peaches into very fine pieces.
Mix with coconut and refrigerate and chill for
1 hour.

Remove from refrigerator and fold in whipped cream. Put in trays or rectangular containers and freeze for 4 hours. Cut into squares and serve on lettuce leaves with mayonnaise as salad or alone as dessert.
Brown sausage almost done; put onion in and cook until tender. Add chicken, rice, raisins and wine.
Let simmer 15 minutes and serve.

recipes.t: Sweet Zucchini Or Yellow Squash Pickles
d: Place squash, onions and garlic in an enamel or crockery pan with salt added.
Cover with ice.
Let set 3 hours.
Drain off salt.
Pour vinegar, sugar, mustard seed and turmeric over squash. Bring to a boil.
Put in hot jars.
Heat lids and seal.
Bake cake as directed on box.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water; add 1/2 cup cold water.
Punch holes in cake with fork.
Pour gelatin in holes.
Combine chicken, drained pineapple (reserve juice), grapes, celery and nuts.
Taste for salt.
(Salted nuts may furnish enough.)
Stir in tarragon leaves.
Combine mayonnaise, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of pineapple juice into chicken mixture.
Serve on lettuce with parsley or small celery leaves for garnish.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine
pork, green
onion,
water
chestnuts, egg, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and salt; mix well.
Place 1/4 cup of filling
on each won bok leaf;
roll.
Place won bok rolls in skillet; add water and simmer 45 minutes, covered. Arrange rolls on serving platter.
Combine remaining ingredients; add to liquid in skillet.
Simmer until gravy thickens, stirring constantly. Pour over won bok rolls.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook beans and one very small onion in boiling water until tender.
Melt fat; add flour.
Gradually stir in milk.
Cook until thick.
Add 1/4 cup cheese; cook until melted.
Add mustard.
Arrange eggs and beans in alternate layers using 8-inch casserole and cover with sauce.
Top with crumbs mixed with rest of cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
In skillet, cook and stir ground meat over medium heat 8-10 minutes or until it is no longer pink, breaking it into small pieces.
Add taco mix and amount of water as directed on pkg. Continue cooking according to pkg. directions.
Remove skillet from heat.
Stir in one cup of salsa.
Place all ingredients in small containers on a table and allow guests to make their own taco.
Makes 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Butter a 10-inch Bundt cake pan and dust with flour.
Toss the chocolate chips with 2 tablespoons flour and set aside.
In a medium bowl, stir together the remaining flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl stir together the bananas, milk and vanilla.
In a large bowl beat together the butter and sugar.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
In three additions each mix in the flour and banana mixtures, mixing until just combined.
Using a wooden spoon, stir in the chocolate chip mixture.
Pour batter into the Bundt pan, bake for 65 to 75 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes in pan.
Remove from pan to rack to cool completely.
For garnish, sift confectioners sugar over top or drizzle with melted chocolate chips.
Dry lentils; pick out the bad ones.
Put them in a large pot; cover under 1/2 pot with water.
Cook until lentils are almost soft, slightly hard.
Add rice or barley.
When rice or barley is almost done, add carrots, peppercorns, garlic, onions and celery. Cook until they are done.
If it's dry, add more water.
In the end, add oil or some vinegar, however much you want to.
Shred cabbage.
Add finely chopped pepper, onion and carrot. Combine with salad dressing.
Add celery seed, vinegar, salt and sugar.
Garnish with paprika.
Peel and mash sweet potatoes.
Reheat.
Add butter, cider and maple syrup.
Beat with an electric mixer until very light.
Add more cider if needed.
Add nutmeg and citrus peel.
Serves 6.
Saute onion in butter until clear.
Add small amount of flour for light roux.
Add tomatoes (chopped) and cook down.
Add peas with liquid from one can only.
Cook down.
Add sliced, boiled eggs before serving.
Mix powdered sugar with condensed milk and oleo.
Add pecans, coconut and vanilla.
Refrigerate mixture for 2 hours.
Form into small balls.
Melt paraffin and chocolate chips.
Dip balls into chocolate mixture and place on waxed paper.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix thoroughly the flour, margarine and powdered sugar.
Press evenly with hands in bottom and about 5/8-inch
up sides of an 8 x 8 x 2-inch square pan.
(If dough is sticky, flour fingers.)

Bake 20 minutes. Beat remaining ingredients with mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy. Pour over hot crust. Bake just until no indentation remains when touched lightly in center, about 25 minutes.
Let stand until cool, then cut into about 1 1/2-inch squares.
If desired, stir in 1/2 cup flaked coconut when mixing batter, when light and fluffy.
Defrost 2 loaves frozen bread in wrapper.
Cut each loaf into 8 pieces.
Grease Bundt pan well.
