Dip each bread piece into melted butter, then into Parmesan cheese, mixed with 1 package of onion soup mix.
Layer first 8 pieces on bottom layer and second 8 pieces on top layer of same Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Bring corn syrup to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat.
Add peanut butter and butter.
Continue cooking over low heat, stirring constantly until peanut butter and butter are melted and well blended.
Remove from heat and stir in oats, brown sugar and flour.
Drop by teaspoonfuls about 3-inches apart onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake in preheated oven at 300° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cook 2 minutes on cookie sheet.
Remove and cool. Drizzle melted chocolate over cookies.
Dissolve lime jello in 1 1/2 cups boiling water and cool.
Add pineapple when it begins to set.
Pour into a mold and chill until set.
Dissolve lemon jello in 1 cup boiling water and cool.
Add whipping cream to cottage cheese and beat.
Add lemon jello when it begins to set.
Pour over congealed lime mixture and chill until firm.
Dissolve red jello in 2 cups of boiling water.
Cool and pour over salad.

recipes.t: Grilled Salmon With Sherry Vinegar Honey Glaze
d: In a small saucepan, reduce the vinegar to 1/4 cup.
In a mixing bowl, combine vinegar syrup with mustard, honey and chili powder.
Let rest 30 minutes.
Preheat grill.
Brush salmon with glaze and grill 3 minutes per side for medium.
Lightly butter a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Over very low heat or in a double boiler, melt chips and peanut butter.
When melted, cool just a little.
Stir in marshmallows and nuts.
Pour into prepared pan.
Cool.
Cut when cold.
Cover ham with water.
Bring to a boil, turn down, simmer for 1 hour.
Remove meat.
Add beans and potatoes.
Cut meat into bite-size pieces and return to broth.
When beans and potatoes are cooked, soup is done, about 1 hour.
Dissolve the Jell-O in 1 1/2 cups hot water.
Add in the dissolved Knox gelatine.
Add the raspberry sherbet and lemon juice.
Chop the cranberry sauce into pea size pieces and add to the mix.
Pour into a circle mold and refrigerate for 2 days.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Combine in saucepan the cottage cheese, sugar, onion and butter.
Place in mixer, dill seed, soda, eggs and softened yeast.
Add flour to form stiff dough.
First addition of flour, use mixer on low speed.
Add cottage cheese mixture to mixer; beat well until batter cleans sides of bowl. Cover and let rise in warm place until double in bulk, 50 to 60 minutes.
Stir down dough.
Form and turn in 2 well-greased loaf pans.
Poke holes with fork in dough.
This makes a very stiff dough when baked.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Turn out on towel. Butter and sprinkle top with kosher salt.
Combine carrots, jalapeno, green onion and ginger in food process. Whirl until finely chopped.
Add peanut butter, soy sauce and water.
Process until smooth, scraping down side of bowl as needed.
Add additional water if thinner consistency is desired. Serve immediately or refrigerate, covered for up to 1 day.
In a mixing bowl combine corn and celery.
For dressing, in a screw-top jar combine oil, sugar, vinegar, celery seed, dry mustard and onion powder.
Cover and shake well.
Pour dressing over corn mixture.
Mix until coated.
Brown chicken breasts in shortening or butter (doesn't take too long).
Sprinkle with a bit of garlic powder and paprika, if desired.
Place chicken breasts in long casserole dish.
Sprinkle mushrooms all over.
Mix together the soups and thyme.
Arrange asparagus spears in a long row over the top of mushrooms.
Pour soup mixture over all.
Cover with foil and bake in 350° oven for about 50 minutes.
Good served with warmed spiced peaches and chicken or herbed rice.
Sprinkle the cavity of the hens with salt and pepper.
Truss and rub the outside with salt and pepper.
Heat butter or oil in a heavy casserole with a cover.
Add game hens and brown all over for about 15 minutes.
Add giblets and cook 5 minutes longer.
Add mushrooms and garlic and cook briefly before adding onion.
Cook onion for 5 minutes and then add bay leaf and thyme.
Cover and cook 10 minutes.
Add vinegar and broth and cook for 10 minutes, covered.
Untruss the birds and drain the cavity juices back into pan.
Discard garlic and bay leaf.
Serve hens hot with mushrooms and hot pan juices.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease baking sheets.
Combine cake mix, eggs and oil in a large bowl.
Stir until thoroughly blended. Stir in chips and walnuts.
Shape dough into 36 (1 1/4-inch) balls.
Place 2 inches apart on pans.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until set.
Cool 1 minute.
Remove to cooling racks.
Makes 3 dozen cookies.
Mix sugar and water; boil for 12 minutes.
Cool; add apricots, bananas, pineapple, strawberries, salt and nuts.
Pour into molds; freeze.
Serve partially frozen.
Yield: 16 servings.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Line a small baking pan with aluminum foil and spray with vegetable cooking spray.
Trim off the root ends of the onions but leave the skin intact.
Place upright in the prepared pan and bake for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until very tender. Remove the skins and discard.
Top each with melted butter or margarine.
Season with salt and pepper and serve piping hot, garnished with parsley sprigs.
Serves 4.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease a 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie plate.
Brown ground turkey and onion; drain.
Stir in salt and pepper.
Spread in pie plate.
Beat milk, baking mix (Bisquick) and eggs until smooth (15 seconds in blender on high, 1 minute with beater on high).
Pour into plate.
Stir in Cheddar cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, then add tomatoes and Mozzarella.
Bake until knife comes out clean, 5 to 8 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes and serve.
Melt caramels; add cream and stir until smooth.
Add pecans to mixture and drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Let stand until firm (will set quicker in fridge).
Pour a teaspoon of the melted cooled chocolate over each cluster and let stand until chocolate is firm.
Brown meat in large heavy pot.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Add tomatoes, water, onion soup mix, sugar and lemon juice.
Next shred up cabbage and bring to a boil.
Cook about 2 hours.
You may want more sugar or lemon juice.
Beat shortening and sugars together.
Add eggs and peanut butter; beat well.
Stir together flour, soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Stir in oats.
Shape to form 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheets; with tines of fork, press to make crisscrosses on each.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes 6 dozen.
Place blueberries, cinnamon sticks and nutmeg in a 6-cup container.
Combine vinegar and sugar in a saucepan; heat to almost boiling, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Pour hot vinegar over berry mixture.
Cover jar tightly; let stand 48 hours.
Strain and pour into a clean bottle.
Mix
corn flake
crumbs
and
Parmesan cheese.
Remove crusts from toast slices; cut
each
into
narrow
strips. Combine margarine and onion
salt. Roll
strips in margarine, then in crumb mixture.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 400° about 5 minutes or until crisp.
Better served slightly warmed. Makes approximately 25.

Cook pasta to desired texture, (a little firm is best). Cool five minutes. While pasta is cooking, cut peppers in half, roast in oven with skin side up. When browned, skin and chop, put in large bowl. Chop olives, mince garlic, add anchovies (chopped to size). Add washed and cleaned spinach, pour olive oil over this to wilt. Mix all ingredients, feta cheese is added as last ingredient. Top with capers for garnish, optional.
Skin breasts,
dry
and
salt. Brown in skillet in the margarine. Remove to greased baking pan when browned.
To the skillet add almonds, chestnuts, mushrooms and onion flakes and saute.
Add
soup
and
water (or wine); blend.
Pour over the chicken breasts.
Cover
and
bake at 375° for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours.
Uncover last 20 minutes.
Serve with rice.
Mix shortening, sugar and eggs together.
Stir dry ingredients together and add to first mixture with sweet milk slowly.
Beat well; add nuts and fold in cherries, use juice also.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350°.
Makes 3 layers.
Cream the shortening. Continue creaming while adding honey in a fine stream.
Add egg and beat well. Add orange peel.
Sift flour once; measure. Add baking powder, soda and salt and sift together.
Add flour alternately with orange juice, a small amount at a time, to first mixture, beating after each addition until smooth.
Stir in pecans; blend.
Turn into a 9 x 5 x 3-inch greased loaf pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until done.
Let cool in pan 10 minutes. Turn out of pan and let stand until cool. Wrap in waxed paper or
aluminum foil. Store overnight to blend flavors and for easy slicing.
Makes 1 loaf.
Spread potato chips on a cookie sheet.
Sprinkle cheese and herbs.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts.
Serve hot.
Cook bow tie pasta with dash of salt and 1 tsp olive oil in water until almost done. Drain and rinse.
Make layers of pasta, cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses until
they are gone.
Bake at 350 until top is brown (approx. 20 minutes).

recipes.t: Scallop Soup Of The Tribes From N.E. Coast
d: Place scallops, water, scallions and watercress in a large saucepan and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Drain juice from pineapple and oranges into saucepan and add flour, sugar and egg yolks.
Cook over medium heat until thick. Add dry jello, stirring until dissolved.
Cool jello mixture and pour over oranges and marshmallow mixture.
Whip cream and fold into other mixture.
Refrigerate until solid.
This salad will be slightly less solid than regular jello salad.
Cut each tomato into 3 large slices.
Squeeze gently to remove some seeds.
Combine sour cream, salt, pepper, sugar, flour, green onion and green chili.
Stir well.
Spoon over tomato slices. Sprinkle with cheese.
Just before serving, place in preheated broiler 4-inches from heat.
Broil until bubbly, about 4 minutes.
Combine cranberry sauce, butter, brown sugar and pineapple in bowl; mix well.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Pour cranberry mixture over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Yields 4 servings.
Combine cake mix, 3 tablespoons of shortening (melted), cake flour, and egg in a large bowl.
Add the water a little bit at a time until the dough forms.
Cover and chill for 2 hours.
Boil cocoa, water and sugar 3 minutes.
Add milk, additional water, salt and cinnamon.
Heat, but do not let boil.
Add vanilla just before serving.
Serves approximately 4 to 6 servings.
Mix dough according to directions.
Let rise.
Roll out lengthwise.
Spread lightly with margarine and cover with meats and cheese.
Let beaten egg drizzle over 1-inch from edges.
Roll up lengthwise.
Let rise.
Bake at 375° until brown.
Slice and serve.
In saucepan, combine celery, potato, onion, 1 cup water, 1/2 teaspoon salt and dash of pepper.
Simmer, covered, until vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes; stir often.
Coarsely chop shrimp.
Combine water,
sugar,
and corn starch; cook until thick, approximately 5 minutes.
Stir in Jello; let it cool slightly. Slice berries into baked and cooled pie shells.
Cover with mixture.
Make sure there are plenty of berries.
Let chill several hours.
Top with Cool Whip.
Drain the kraut well.
Boil the sugar and vinegar for 5 minutes and cool slightly.
Pour over kraut.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Chill for several hours.
Season approximately 1/2 cup flour with salt and pepper. Place in paper bag.
Add veal cubes; shake, holding top of bag closed, until veal is well covered.
Add floured veal to melted butter and brown.
Stir in water, onions and paprika.
Turn down heat so that meat and gravy mixture in pan barely bubbles.
Cover and cook 2 hours or until meat is tender, stirring occasionally. Add more water if necessary to prevent sticking.
Add hot gravy slowly to sour cream, stirring to prevent curdling.
Return to skillet of meat.
Serve over mashed potatoes or noodles.
In a large, nonstick frying pan over medium heat, saute the onion in the oil until transparent, about 5 minutes.
Add stock; bring to a boil.
Add lettuce; cook until it starts to wilt, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and pepper.
Add the fish and cook until just firm to the touch, about 5 minutes.
Carefully drain the excess liquid from the pan into a 2-quart saucepan.
Over high heat, cook until reduced by half, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Process onions and peppers, a few at a time, mixed with vinegar in blender.
Mix all ingredients together and boil until slightly thickened (about 45 minutes), stirring occasionally. Pack boiling hot into hot sterilized jars.
Seal and process in water bath for 5 minutes.
Good with vegetables or on hot dogs and hamburgers.
Sift together the first 6 ingredients; set aside.
In a bowl, beat together the eggs, oil, milk and liqueur, then add the plums. Add dry ingredients; mix well.
Add nuts.
Line 2 loaf pans with foil.
Spray foil with Pam.
Pour batter into pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Remove from oven and pour glaze on top while still warm.
Place chicken in casserole dish.
Place ham and cheese on top of chicken.
Mix soup and wine.
Pour over chicken.
Top with buttered crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Break broccoli in pieces.
Add crumbled bacon and cheese.
Mix mayo with sugar and vinegar and frost the broccoli.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Stir well and serve.
Heat oil
in
Dutch
oven over medium heat. Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Remove chicken; add onion, celery and carrots and
saute
minutes.
Add
tomatoes, tomato paste, wine, salt,
pepper and cinnamon.
Bring sauce and vegetables to boil. Return
chicken to pan.
Bake in 350° oven, covered, about 1
1/2 hours
or
until fork can be inserted in chicken with ease. Serve with pasta.
Serves 4.
Mix tomato, onion, green pepper, beans and salad dressing and marinate overnight.
Spread soups over meat.
Top with chips, crushed.
Wrap in foil.
Cook for 1 hour.
Baste occasionally with sauce.
Heat the oven to 375°.
Combine flour, 1/3 cup of the sugar and the salt.
Cut the butter into small pieces and rub into the flour mixture until crumbly.
In a mixing bowl, combine the remaining 1/3 cup sugar, cornstarch, orange zest and cinnamon.
Peel the apples, core and cut into chunks.
Add to the sugar mixture and toss to coat.
Cook tortellini and drain.
Heat butter over medium heat.
Add cream, pepper and nutmeg.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer for 7 minutes.
Add Parmesan; cook 2 minutes until sauce starts top thicken.
Add tortellini, stirring 1 to 2 minutes, until heated through.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Put yeast and sugar
in
bowl.
Pour water over all and let stand.
Cut oleo into
flour and salt.
Put egg yolks into yeast. (Save
egg whites in another bowl.) Pour yeast and egg yolks
into flour, and mix and knead.
Let rise for 45 minutes or until double in size.
Cook and debone chicken.
Add poultry seasoning to broth. Bring to a boil.
Mix flour, margarine and milk in bowl.
From dough into balls.
Roll 1/4-inch thick on a floured board and cut into 1-inch squares.
Drop dumplings into broth.
Keep broth boiling.
Cook dumplings 20 minutes on medium heat.
Add chicken. Stir together.
Cut wings at joints; discard wing tips.
In large recloseable plastic food bag, combine 2/3 cup picante sauce, ketchup, honey, cumin, chili powder and garlic.
Mix well.
Add chicken wings to marinade; seal bag and turn several times to coat.
Place bag in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Refrigerate, turning bag occasionally, at least 2 hours.
Cream sugar and oleo.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each egg.
Alternate adding flour and buttermilk to which soda has been added.
Bake 1 hour and 12 minutes at 325°.
Combine meat, onions, sugar
and chili powder and saute until meat changes color.
Add
tomatoes and pintos and simmer for 15 minutes.
While
this cooks, mix cornbread:
corn meal, flour, sugar, salt, baking
powder, egg, milk and cooking oil. Mix well. Put meat mixture
in
a greased casserole, then put cornbread over and cook at 425° for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Sweet And Tangy Kielbasa With Shells
d: Simmer kielbasa in 1/2 cup water (covered) for 20 minutes. Cook shells and drain. Drain and slice kielbasa. Set aside.
Cook bacon and drain. Reserve 3 tablespoons drippings.
Crumble bacon and set aside.

Cook mushrooms in drippings for 2 minutes. Stir in sugar, flour and pepper. Add the 3/4 cup water and vinegar. Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Add kielbasa, shells, bacon and parsley. Toss together.
Place toast in a greased 8 x 8-inch dish or pan.
Top with the salmon (drain all juice).
Put the salmon on the toast with your hands (works better).
Mix soup with cream or milk; add parsley and onion.
Spoon over salmon; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes, until cheese melts and is bubbly.
Makes 4 big servings.
Peel and cut eggs in half.
Mix together the sour cream, mayonnaise, horseradish, salt and pepper.
Gently mix in the egg yolks.
Fill egg whites with yolk mixture; sprinkle with paprika. Chill at least 1 hour.

Prepare macaroni and cheese. Brown meat and onions. Cook until tender. Stir in corn, tomato paste, water, salt and pepper. Add macaroni and mix well. Pour into 2-quart casserole; bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix the macaroni, whole kernel corn and cream-style corn in a baking dish.
Microwave the butter or margarine and cheese in a microwave-safe dish until melted.
Add to the corn mixture.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix the dry ingredients together with the coconut.
Add the lemon pie filling.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch greased and floured cake pan.
If desired, you can add pecan meats.
Bake about 20 minutes in a 350° oven.
Frost with a thin powdered sugar frosting.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Chill.
Shape into small balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and press flat with tines of fork.
Leave plain or decorate with sugar or chocolate bits.
Bake at 350° for approximately 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Yields 9 dozen small cookies.
Bring barely to a boil vinegar, water and salt.
Pack cucumbers in jar.
Put 1 grape leaf, 2 cloves garlic and 1 sprig of fresh dill in the bottom of jar.
Pour liquid mixture over pickles.
Add 4 peppercorns to each jar.
Put through hot water bath 10 minutes. Use small cucumbers 2 1/2 to 3-inches long.
These are crispier. Add another sprig of dill and another grape leaf on top.
Use all fresh ingredients.
Microwave Directions:
On a 9-inch microwave-proof plate, combine cereal, pepper, dressing and Italian seasoning; toss to coat well.
Microwave at High (100%) for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes until hot; stir.
Sprinkle with cheese. Microwave at High for 30 to 40 seconds or until cheese melts. Serve at once.
For rhubarb sauce, combine the sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon. Add rhubarb and water.
Cook and stir until mixture is boiling; cook 1 minute more.
Pour into a baking dish; dot with margarine. Place in a hot 400° oven while preparing biscuits.
Melt sugar, brown sugar, milk and butter; boil 15 minutes. Just before 15 minutes are up, turn heat to warm.
Remove from heat; add marshmallow cream, chocolate bits, butterscotch bits, nuts and vanilla.
Mix well.
When all melted, pour into 13 x 9-inch buttered pan.
Cool.
Cut in squares.
Store in covered container at room temperature.
Cook Creamettes according to general package directions. Drain; do not chill.
While still hot, drizzle with oil and vinegar.
Add onion, seasonings and cheese.
Toss well.
Gently mix in remaining ingredients.
Chill thoroughly.
Serve on salad greens (lettuce).

recipes.t: Creole Tomato And Peanut Butter Soup
d: Heat oil in a 2-quart pot and saute onions and pepper about 5 minutes until soft.
Add cayenne and cook 1 minute longer.
Stir in flour and when smooth, add milk and peanut butter.
Continue to cook over moderate heat, stirring all the while until the soup is smooth, hot and thickened.
This will take 5 to 10 minutes.
Slowly stir in tomato pulp and tomato juice until warmed through.
Makes 1 quart.
Serves 4.
Melt butter; remove from heat.
Blend in flour.
Add salt and milk.
Return to heat; cook slowly, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens.
Add cheese, stirring until melted.
In casserole dish, layer asparagus and sliced egg, then sauce. Repeat.
Heat in 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
(Crushed Ritz crackers or Rice Krispies may be put on top of added appeal.)
Combine sour cream, lemon juice, pepper, salt and garlic.
Coat breasts well with sour cream mixture.
Place on a nonstick baking sheet that has been brushed with butter.
Refrigerate overnight for best results.
Before baking, roll chicken in bread crumbs. Drizzle with half of margarine.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Drizzle with remaining margarine and return to oven for 15 minutes.
Mix shortening and sugars.
Add egg yolks to water; add vanilla.
Mix flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda and add to first mixture.
Mix until well blended.
Pat out on cookie sheet. Cover dough with chocolate chips; Pat down.
Beat egg whites and sugar until stiff.
Cover chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Cut in squares.

recipes.t: Wester Apple Pie(Don'T Like Cinnamon?  This Is For You.)
d: Mix apple slices with sugar and flour.
Sprinkle lemon extract over fruit and mix lightly with a fork to distribute it evenly. Put apples in pie shell; dot with butter and put on top crust. Sprinkle crust with white sugar.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat and bake at 350° until apples are done.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Beat egg yolks until light; beat into creamed mixture.
Soak macaroons in bourbon.
Beat chocolate into creamed mixture; add vanilla and pecans.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry.
Fold into chocolate mixture. Line bottom and sides of 10 inch spring-form pan with split lady fingers.
Alternate layers of soaked macaroons with chocolate mixture in lined pan.
Decorate top with whipped cream. Refrigerate.
Makes 16-20 servings.
Cut flour, salt, pepper and shortening as one would for pie crust.
Then add beaten eggs and cut in.
Then add chicken broth a tablespoon at a time.
Form into ball.
Roll on floured pastry cloth, about 1/4-inch thick and cut into desired shapes.
Cook, debone and cut up chicken.
Drop dumplings into boiling broth from chicken; add 1/2 cup of milk and cook until tender.
Return chicken pieces to broth and dumplings.
Cook rice as directed.
After rice is completely cooked, let cool before you mix ingredients.
Boil eggs, then cool.
Mix all ingredients in rice and stir.
Add mayonnaise, mustard, salt and a dash of pepper.
Mix well, then refrigerate until ready to serve.
Scoop out cheese and save shell.
Break up cheese and mix to taste with Worcestershire sauce, mustard, chives and olives.
Put mixture back into shell.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Line 9-inch loaf pan with waxed paper.
Mix ham with 1/2 cup real mayonnaise.
Press into bottom of pan.
Mix next 6 ingredients with remaining real mayonnaise.
Add potatoes; toss.
Press lightly over ham layer.
Cover; chill 4 hours.
Unmold.
Serves 6.
Cook corn according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Melt butter in heavy saucepan over low heat.
Add cream cheese; stir until blended.
Stir in corn, onions, sugar and green chiles.
Spoon into a lightly greased 1-quart baking dish.
Cover; bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Brown ground beef, onion and bell pepper together in a pot. Add cabbage and let cook for a few minutes, until cabbage cooks down a little.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook until cabbage is tender.
(You may want to add more chili powder if spicier flavor is desired.)
Serve immediately.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Cool, peel and slice.
Sprinkle a deep well-greased (Pam) oven-proof dish with some of the bread crumbs.
Place a layer of sliced potatoes over this.
Chop bacon and fry until crisp.
Scatter half of the bacon over the potatoes in the dish.
Melt butter and cottage cheese in saucepan over low heat.
Pour 1/2 of this mixture over bacon and potatoes.
Add another layer of bacon and potatoes; pour remaining butter and cottage cheese mixture over dish.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle remaining bread crumbs on top and dot with butter.
Bake in moderate oven (275° to 300°) uncovered for 30 minutes.
Arrange fruit and cheese on salad greens.
The fruit can be cut to your choosing.
Cut cheese into squares.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Melt butter in baking dish in oven. Remove.
Stir in garlic, creamer, soup, 1/2 of Parmesan cheese and seasonings.
Stir to combine.
Gently stir in broccoli and pasta. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over top.
Bake 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Beat cheese until smooth.
Gradually beat sugar.
Blend in sour cream and vanilla.
Fold whipped topping, blending thoroughly.
Gently add fruit, folding carefully so as not to mash.
Spoon into crust.
Chill until set, about 4 hours.
Fry sausage until well done; drain well.
Pat with paper towels to remove excess grease.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Mound on slices of cocktail rye and broil or bake 3 to 5 minutes.
Melt cheese and half and half in double boiler (may add more half and half until desired consistency).
Boil peppers until soft.
Add to melted cheese.
Add garlic powder, green chilies and jalapenos.
Stir until mixed well.
Put in crock-pot to keep warm. Serve with tortilla chips.
Mix sour cream, lemon juice and seasonings together in bowl big enough to dip chicken in.
Coat chicken using all mixture. Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Soak dried mushrooms in warm water; squeeze dry and cut into pieces.
Cook tomatoes, garlic and mushrooms until reduced to a thick paste.
Cut up chicken; remove excess fat (or skin entirely) and pat dry.
In heavy saucepan, brown chicken pieces lightly and pour off oil.
Return chicken to pan.
Add tomatoes, chicken broth, parsley, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, cover and reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook approximately 1 hour.
Serve with rice or noodles.
Mix butter and crushed cookies.
Bake for 12 minutes at 350°, then cool about 10 minutes.
Mix together pudding, milk and ice cream and spread on crust.
Let stand in freezer overnight.
Cook onion, celery and garlic in 2 tablespoons oil until just tender.
Stir in chicken, tomato sauce, olives, 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1 teaspoon salt and chili powder.
Bring remaining broth to boil.
Add remaining salt and salad oil.
Pour into casserole dish.
Beat eggs, measure 3 bottle caps of Sucaryl.
Pour into eggs. Add shortening; beat until creamy.
Blend in salt, flour and lemon juice.
Stir in walnuts and coconut.
Turn into loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for about 40 minutes, or until cake tests done.
Yields 20 slices.
In a saucepan over low heat, combine vinegar and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer, stirring until sugar is thoroughly dissolved.
Stir in catsup, soy sauce, water and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Pour into glass jars, seal tightly and refrigerate for up to 2 months.
In a large kettle or Dutch oven, boil meat and chicken together the day before the dish is to be served.
Soak the beans overnight, then cook until soft enough to mash.
Reheat the meat and fowl.
Skim off fat from broth and add sliced turnip and potatoes.
Cook slowly.
When nearly done, add the mashed bean pulp and corn.
Stir often.
Serve immediately.
Cut sponge layers in half crosswise to make 4 layers.
Prepare pudding mix as directed on package, using the 2 cups milk.
Press one of the cake layers into a medium sized mixing bowl.
Add 1/3 of the cooked pudding, another cake layer and so on, ending with the 4th cake layer.
Chill several hours or overnight.
Unmold on serving plate and swirl whipped cream on top and sides.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook frozen corn according to directions and drain.
Put in skillet and add oleo, 3/4 can milk and sugar.
Mix 2 tablespoons flour with remainder of canned milk.
Can add a little water to thin.
Stir into corn mixture and cook until thick.
Finely chop seeded peppers in food processor; do not puree!
Cook chicken in boiling water to cover for 45 minutes or until tender.
Remove chicken, reserving 3 cups of broth in a Dutch oven.
Let chicken cool, then skin, bone and cut into bite-size pieces.
Set aside.
Bring reserved broth to a boil.
Cut tortillas into quarters and dip into broth for 5 seconds to soften.
Set aside.
Place half of tortillas in a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Layer with half each of chicken, onion and green pepper.
Repeat layers.
Sprinkle top with cheese, chili powder and garlic salt.
Combine soups and spread over cheese. Top with undrained tomatoes.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until cooked through.
For a slightly different flavor, you may marinate the chicken overnight in Italian dressing and pineapple chunks.
Remove crust from bread and cube.
Melt butter and dash of red coloring.
Coat the bread with butter mixture and add sugar; mix well until the bread is sugared.
Fold rhubarb into sugared bread mixture.
Pour into baking dish.
Put 1 tablespoon water in each corner of pan.
Do not mix.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Good as a vegetable or dessert.
Serves 6.
Heat oven to 350°.
Beat cake mix, 1 package pudding mix, eggs, water and oil in large bowl with electric mixer on low speed 1 minute.
Beat on medium speed 4 minutes. With wooden spoon, stir in1 1/2 cups of coconut.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9-inch round pans.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean when inserted in cake.
Cool 15 minutes.
Pour milk into large bowl.
Add remaining package pudding mix.
Beat with wire whisk 2 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes or until thickened.
Gently stir in whipped topping.
Mix 1 1/2 cups of the pudding mixture and pineapple.
Slice each cake layer in two, making 4 layers. Frost cake layers with pudding-pineapple mixture.
Frost top and sides of cake with remaining pudding mixture.
Press remaining coconut on top and sides of cake.
Refrigerate.
Cream the cheese, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Fold in whipped cream and put in graham cracker crust.
Cook sugar, flour, salt and cherry juice until clear.
Cool about 5 minutes.
Add cherries and butter.
Cool thoroughly.
Place thickened mixture on cream mixture.
Keep refrigerated.
Serves 6.
Place salmon in an 8-inch square baking dish.
Combine onions and next 6 ingredients; stir well.
Pour over salmon.
Cover and marinate in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Bake, uncovered, at 450° for 15 minutes or until salmon flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Serve with mango wedges.
Contains 236 calories per serving.
Flake fish and dice potatoes small.
Add cream to fish and potatoes.
Add 2 slightly beaten egg yolks, salt and pepper.
Whip the egg whites, then fold into mixture.
Blend well.
Put in buttered baking dish; sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes at 400° or until a knife comes out dry.
Pour melted butter and parsley over and serve from the baking dish.
Mix instant pudding and milk together.
Pour in condensed milk and stir.
Add about 1/3 of cool whip and stir.
Layer mixture with bananas and wafers.
Top with remaining cool whip.
Pie Filling: Mix sugar, flour, egg yolks, milk, vanilla and coconut. Cook on medium heat until thickened. Pour into pie crust.
Cut off the top of each pepper; remove all the inside of peppers.
In a 2 to 3-quart saucepan, bring approximately 2 inches of water to a boil; add peppers.
Cover and boil 5 minutes.
Drain and place cut side down to cool.
In small skillet, heat oil; add onions and garlic and saute until soft.
Add mushrooms.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender.
Put mushrooms in a medium bowl.
Add all ingredients except peppers; toss to combine.
Stuff each pepper 1/4 with mixed mushroom mixture. Place peppers in a casserole dish in upright position; cover and bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Each serving equals to 2 1/2 serving vegetable, 1 serving fat, 1/4 cup limit vegetables, 1/2 serving bread and substitutes for 3/4 egg.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Peel potatoes and cut in halves.
Boil until tender (20 minutes); drain.
Cook bacon in microwave until crisp; crumble into fine pieces.
Sift flour, salt, baking powder, soda and spices together.
Set aside; mix sugar and margarine until blended; add eggs and beat in pumpkin, then add flour.
Pour into greased pans and bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at about 325°.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.
Heat peanut butter and butter slightly to mix.
Transfer to large bowl.
Cream in sugar and dry milk.
Add raisins.
Spread and press into a sheet pan or cookie sheet.
Melt chocolate chips and butter in double boiler, then pour over peanut butter mixture. When cooled, cut into squares (makes 25).
Fry hamburger until well done; set aside.
Fry onions and green pepper until tender; add to hamburger.
Boil macaroni until tender. Add macaroni to hamburger and vegetables.
Stir in the can of stewed tomatoes; heat and serve.
Blend ham, bread crumbs, egg, milk and ketchup; sprinkle in cloves.
Put sugar and margarine in a loaf pan; heat until melted. Place halved pineapple slices on sugar and margarine in bottom of pan.
Cover with ham mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes. Invert on platter to serve.
Combine the ingredients in the order they are listed.
Chill thoroughly and serve in sherbet glasses.
Garnish with more whipped cream and with a cherry and mint leaf.
Bring to a boil chocolate and water.
Let cool.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add egg and sour milk.
Stir well.
Then add the cooled chocolate and vanilla.
Mix well.
Fold in flour, soda, salt and nuts.
Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes in 350° oven. Can frost with chocolate or vanilla frosting.
Prepare crust.
With electric mixer, beat eggs until foamy, about 1 minute.
Add honey, milk, pumpkin, spice, salt and orange juice concentrate.
Beat until well blended.
Pour pumpkin filling into graham cracker crust.
Bake at 375° for 60 to 65 minutes or until knife inserted off center comes out clean.
Garnish with orange zest, if desired.
Spray foil lasagna pan with Pam.
Lay bread on the bottom. Spread cheese and mushrooms on bread.
Beat eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper.
Pour in pan.
Let pan sit for a few hours or overnight in refrigerator.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Wash and slice tomatoes into 1/2-inch slices.
Dredge thickly with flour.
Fry in hot oil, browning well on both sides.
Drain; place on serving dish and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add butter to pan fryings; blend in flour and add milk.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Pour over tomatoes and serve.
Gently add the chicken broth to the mayonnaise.
Lightly toss together chicken, celery, olives, pecans and salt.
Add broth and mayonnaise dressing; chill.
Put strawberries in food processor or blender.
Blend until fruit is pureed.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Stir in lemonade until melted.
Add cranberry juice cocktail, cold water and strawberry puree.
Pour over ice in large punch bowl.
Slowly pour in ginger ale.
Makes about 30 (4 ounce) servings.
Mix together the first seven ingredients. Cut the chilled cranberry sauce with fluted cookie cutter, slice across the fluted cranberry sauce.
Spread each slice of bread with turkey salad and top each with cranberry star.
Makes about 25 canapes.
Cook cut up chicken in oil; set aside.
In skillet, add vegetables, water and soy sauce.
Cook until thawed.
Add chicken, ginger and cornstarch.
Heat through.
Serve over rice.
Fillet fish and cut into small pieces.
Place in jar.
Add 1/2 cup salt for each quart of fish.
Cover with white cider vinegar. Let stand 5 days in refrigerator, then remove and rinse with cold water.
Place fish back in jar and add sliced onions, 1 quart of white vinegar, sugar and pickling spices.
Let stand 1 week.
The longer they stand, the firmer they get.
Enjoy.
Keep refrigerated.
Combine bread crumbs, cheese and basil in small bowl.
Place tomato slices in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Pour dressing over tomatoes and sprinkle with bread crumb mixture.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes or until crumbs are golden brown.
Combine sauce and
mincemeat;
pour
into pastry shell. Combine pecans, sugar and butter; sprinkle over filling.
Bake at 425° for 30 minutes
or until crust is brown and filling is bubbly.
Cool on rack
at
least
1 hour before slicing.
Just before serving, heat brandy
over
low
heat.
Ignite
with
a match and pour over pie.
Combine beef
and
onion
in
large skillet; cook until meat is brown, then drain.
Saute tortillas in hot oil briefly to soften; spoon meat mixture evenly in center of each tortilla. Roll up
and
place,
seam
side
down,
in pan.
Combine remaining ingredients,
except Cheddar cheese, in small saucepan. Cook
over
medium
heat
until cheese slices are melted; pour over
enchiladas.
Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20
to
30 minutes, or bubbly.
Yields 18 enchiladas. Prepare ahead of time; refrigerate until needed.
Spread coconut on a cookie sheet and bake at 325° until light brown.
Put into bowl and toss with melted butter.
Spread lightly over bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate.
Do not press.
Cool for 1 hour or more in refrigerator.
Heat oil in wok.
Stir-fry mushrooms.
Add celery, sugar and soy sauce.
Stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes or until celery becomes bright green.
Serve hot.
Reconstitute orange juice according to directions.
Prepare cherry and orange Kool-Aid according to package directions. Combine orange juice, pineapple juice and cherry and orange Kool-Aid in punch bowl; stir in sugar.
Place bananas in blender container.
Process to puree.
Stir into punch just before serving.
Yield: 40 to 50 servings.
Drain pineapple, reserving 1/4 cup syrup.
Over high heat, bring to full boil the cranberries, sugar, raisins, ginger, salt, allspice and reserved pineapple syrup; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until cranberries pop.
Add pineapple chunks and cook for 5 minutes more or until mixture thickens. Will keep for 2 weeks in refrigerator.
Saute onion, celery and garlic in butter.
Add soups, milk, chicken and chiles; stir until warm.
In 3-quart casserole, put chicken mix and 1/2 chips.
Top with remaining chips and cheese. Sprinkle with paprika for color.
Bake at 325° (uncovered) for 30 minutes; let stand a few minutes before serving to set.
Serves 6.
Cream the cheese, vanilla, sugar and nuts.
Then pour into prepared crust (dust crust lightly with egg white; bake at 350° for 3 minutes.)
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until lightly brown. Let cool.
Add cherries; let cool in refrigerator.
Top with Cool Whip and serve!
Melt butter or margarine in large saucepan or kettle, then stir in flour.
Stir constantly over medium heat, 1 minute, until thick and bubbly.
Add milk, ham and onion, stirring constantly, over medium heat until thickened.
Reduce heat to lowest setting. Stir in cheese and continue stirring until cheese is melted and soup is smooth.
Serves 4.
Combine cottage cheese, butter and flour into a smooth dough. Refrigerate 8 hours.
Divide dough into 3 to 4 pieces.
Roll each piece out to about 1/4-inch thick.
Cut into sticks about 1/2-inch wide by 2 1/2-inches long.
Put onto ungreased baking sheets. Brush tops with beaten egg.
Sprinkle with generous coating of grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Chop medium onion and saute in stick of margarine.
Gradually add 1/2 cup flour.
Put in heavy saucepan.
Add 2 cans chicken broth and 4 cups milk.
Add both jars Cheez Whiz and 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper.
Boil carrots and green onions in 2 cups water for 5 minutes, then drain and add to rest of soup.
Cook over low heat until cheeses are melted and everything is good and hot.
Watch closely so it won't scorch.
Brown onion in oil.
Add beef and brown.
Drain off excess fat.
Place noodles in layer over meat.
Combine juice and seasonings.
Pour over noodles.
Bring to boil; cover and simmer over low for 20 minutes.
Add sour cream and mushrooms.
Heat through.
Soak bread crumbs in milk for 1/2 hour.
Cream the butter and sugar together, add molasses, flour sifted with the spices and soda, then the raisins.
Add this to the bread crumbs and milk.
Make lime Jell-O with 1 cup of hot water.
Use the pineapple juice for the cold water.
If not 1 full cup, fill with water to get 1 cup.
Mix pineapple into Jell-O and let set in refrigerator. When set, mix cream cheese together.
If too thick, add a little mayo or milk.
Beat together cream cheese, nuts and Cool Whip. Spread over set Jell-O.
Cool.
Next, make strawberry Jell-O using 1 cup of hot water and 1 cup of cold water.
Pour over other 2 layers and cool.
You can also add strawberries or pears to strawberry Jell-O.
Top with mini marshmallows.
Whip together butter, margarine and 8 tablespoons sugar.
Beat in 2 eggs.
Gradually add 4 additional tablespoons sugar until fluffy.
Scramble hamburger in skillet over medium heat until half done.
Add chopped onions and bell pepper.
Continue cooking until hamburger and onions are done.
Put hamburger, peppers and onions with other ingredients and simmer in boiler pan for 30 minutes.
Soak the navy beans overnight in water enough to cover them. Drain off water and add onion with 1 quart water.
Cover and cook slowly for 1 hour.
Add more water if necessary until tender, drain.
In deep casserole dish, add beans, salt, molasses, mustard and sour cream.
Mix well.
Add salt pork with rind exposed.
Pour enough boiling water to cover the beans.
Cover and bake at 300° about 3 hours, adding water if it evaporates.
Uncover the last hour to brown.
Sprinkle broccoli, then chicken, then cheese evenly in the pie shell.
Beat eggs, cream, lemon juice, garlic salt and pepper until mixed but not frothy.
Pour into shell.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 40 to 50 minutes or until center is set.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add onion and cook until soft. Remove pan from heat; stir in flour and then milk.
Return to heat.
Cook, stirring constantly, until smooth and thickened. Arrange fish and shrimp in buttered casserole.
Sprinkle with parsley and mushrooms.
Pour half of the sauce over fish.
Top with layer of sliced potatoes and pour remaining sauce over all. Bake in 350° oven for 40 minutes or until potatoes are done.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Stir in peanut butter and syrup. Mix well.
May have to use hands!
Roll into 1 1/2-inch balls. Shake or roll in powdered sugar.
*Blend 1 envelope onion soup with 1/2 pound butter or margarine.
Makes 1 1/4 cups.
Boil chicken and debone.
Use broth from chicken and cook with fettucini.
Saute onion, celery and butter.
Add mushrooms, Velveeta cheese, cream of chicken soup and cream of mushroom soup. Add this to cooked chicken and fettucini.
Brown hamburger meat with onion and seasonings; drain grease. Add mushrooms, tomato soup and Mexicorn.
Cook noodles and drain. Put cooked noodles in an oven-safe dish and cover with meat mixture.
Cut cheese into sticks or, if grated, pour over top. Bake at 350°, covered, for 30 minutes.
Serve with hot bread and salad or a green vegetable and the table is set!
Combine first 6 ingredients in a shallow dish.
Dip fish in milk and dredge in cornmeal mixture.
Place in
lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan and drizzle with butter.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
You can use any kind of fish fillets.
Melt butter in saucepan. Add onions and apples. Cook 10 minutes covered, stirring occasionally. When apples are soft and onions slightly browned, add salt and pepper.
Serves 4 as a side dish.
Combine the chicken, pineapple, grapes, peanuts and celery. Stir in the tarragon.
Salt to taste.
In another bowl, combine the mayonnaise, lemon juice and pineapple juice.
Fold this mixture into the chicken-fruit mixture.
Makes 8 servings.
Beat butter and shortening gradually.
Add sugar, creaming until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Sift dry ingredients.
Add alternately with cream and vanilla.
Stir in nuts.
Drain Veg-All thoroughly and combine with potatoes, green pepper, sweet pickles, onions and chopped eggs.
Chill thoroughly.
Cook barley for 1/2 hour and drain.
Brown ground beef with chopped onion.
Add the green pepper and peas with liquid.
Add the tomato soup and paste with one can of water and the mushrooms. Salt and pepper to taste.
Add the barley (cooked).
Mix all ingredients and bake in covered casserole for 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Melt butter in large, iron frypan.
Add brown sugar and stir until smooth and even.
Arrange maraschino cherries, spoon on crushed pineapple evenly.
Mix cake mix according to directions, using pineapple juice for liquid.
Pour into frypan on top of pineapple.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean.
Invert on plate.
Serve with whipped topping.
Empty one large can of fruit cocktail with juice in a serving bowl.
Empty one small can of mandarin oranges (drained) into same bowl.
Take small package of instant pudding (either vanilla, lemon, coconut or banana) and empty the dry powdered pudding into bowl and stir contents.
(Do not prepare the pudding; use it only as a powdered substance.)
Refrigerate few minutes.
In double boiler, blend 2 tablespoons cornstarch with orange juice and lemon until smooth.
Place over heat and stir constantly until thick.
Remove from heat and add 1/4 cup sugar and oleo, rinds, salt and pepper.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Blend well. Stir in beets and heat over low heat.
Serves 6 to 8.
Heat oven to 350°.
Line muffin pans with foil cupcake cups, 2-inches in diameter.
Place one vanilla wafer in bottom of each cup.
In large bowl, beat cream cheese and sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat well.
Stir in peanut butter chips.
Spoon heaping tablespoonfuls of cream cheese mixture into each cup.
Bake 15 minutes, or until set, but not browned.
Cool in pans.
In small microwave-safe bowl, place chocolate chips and butter.
Microwave on High 30 seconds to 1 minute or until melted and mixture is smooth when stirred.
Drop teaspoonfuls of chocolate mixture onto center of each cheesecake.
Place almond slices around dab of chocolate to resemble petals.
Cover and refrigerate.
Makes 2 dozen cupcakes.
Combine sugar, salt, milk and syrup in a saucepan; cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Stir occasionally and cook until soft ball stage (236°) or until syrup dropped into cold water forms a soft ball.
Remove from heat.
Add peanut butter and vanilla; stir until blended.
Stir in oats and peanuts. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Cool.
Makes 3 1/2 dozen cookies.
Remove crusts from bread.
Cut slices into 4 triangles.
Toast on both sides.
Mix onions, bacon, mayonnaise and pepper together. Spread on toasts (use about 1 teaspoon on each triangle).
Makes 5 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray medium-size casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Layer in casserole, rice, beans, onion, celery and cheese.
Season each layer with small amount of seasonings and hot sauce.
Pour chicken broth over casserole.
Bake uncovered in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until most of liquid is absorbed.
Makes 8 servings.
Pour liquids into bowl.
Slice orange, lemon and lime into 1/2 moons.
Add lime and orange sherbet just before serving.
Float sherbet balls in bowl.
Marinate chicken in lime juice, garlic and seasonings for 15 minutes.
Cook chicken in oil 2 to 3 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink.
Add onion and peppers.
Continue cooking 3 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Stir in salsa.
Spoon onto tortillas.
Top with cheese.
Yield: 4 servings.
Preparation time: 20 minutes (including marinating).
Cooking time:
6 minutes.
Carefully rinse seeds from chilies with cold water.
Spread chilies in single layer on paper toweling.
Gently pat with another piece of toweling until dry, then carefully slip a strip of Monterey Jack cheese into each chili.
Beat eggs; gradually add flour, beating until smooth.
Add milk, salt, black pepper and liquid red pepper and beat thoroughly.
Arrange half the stuffed chilies in well-greased 7 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with half the Cheddar cheese and paprika.
Repeat layers, ending with cheese.
Carefully pour egg mixture over all.
Bake, uncovered, in preheated 350° oven about 45 minutes or until knife inserted in custard comes out clean.
Mix cream cheese (room temperature), 1 cup margarine and flour all together as you would a pie crust.
Roll into a ball and chill dough at least 2 hours.
Then, roll into balls; shape into tassie pans.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
When baking tassies, remove from oven before done; press pastry down gently and place back in oven to finish baking time.
Cool completely.
Heat together in double boiler Kraft caramels and 1/2 cup evaporated milk until smooth. Keep heating on low while filling cups 3/4 full.
Let cool until firm.
Brown hamburger.
Add green pepper, ground oregano, salt and pepper to taste.
Add tomato sauce.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes. Cook and drain noodles.
Place noodles in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch buttered casserole dish, spreading evenly.
Pour the hamburger mixture over the noodles.
Place sliced onion over entire surface. Put grated Mozzarella over surface.
Place pepperoni slices over top of cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Let sit for 5 minutes, then cut into squares.
Serve with green salad.
Saute meat, onions and mushrooms.
Beat eggs, spices and milk. Line pan with bread.
Layer with meat mixture.
Pour egg mixture over all and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until set.
Serves 6 to 8.
Boil chickens in salted water.
Use broth for cooking rice. Heat cans of soup with can of milk.
Combine soup with eggs, mushrooms, pimento, almonds, onion juice, rice and seasonings to taste.
Cut up chicken into pieces and combine in a casserole dish with soup mixture.
Top with potato chips.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Serves 16.
In large bowl, combine the cake mix, oil, baking powder and eggs.
Prepare pudding mix according to directions on the package. Add the pudding to the cake mixture and stir together.
Pour into well oiled 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Sprinkle with chocolate chips and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes on lowest shelf in the oven.
Sometimes I mix the chocolate chips and nuts with the batter and frost the cake with buttercream frosting.
It is yummy either way, but has a tendency to fall.
If this is a problem, make cupcakes instead.
Cream together the cream cheese, egg yolk, powdered sugar, salt and vanilla.
In a large circle, place crescents with the points toward the center and slightly overlapping.
Crimp the outside edge to keep the filling in.
Place cream cheese mixture in a circle in the middle of crescents.
Put pie filling over cream cheese mixture.
Pull inside of crescents to the outside. Bake 22 minutes at 350° to 375°.
Drizzle with powdered sugar frosting.
(I warm about 1/2 cup ready to spread frosting in the microwave and drizzle over cake.)
Beat eggs.
Combine butter and buttermilk.
Combine dry ingredients, caraway seed and raisins.
Pour in egg mixture; mix very well.
Pour into well-greased bread pan.
Bake for 1 hour, or until done, at 350°.
In a 5 qt. pot, melt 1/4 c. butter on low heat.
Add the celery and saute briefly.
Add the salmon and its juice, flaking with a fork, and stir.
Drain potatoes and dice; add to soup.
Add remaining butter and flour to thicken.
Add condensed milk and stir.
Add enough room temperature milk to reach desired thickness and amount of soup you want, and stir.
Add dash of salt and any additional seasonings, such as celery salt or pepper, to taste. Stir slowly over medium heat until warm.
Never boil!
Cream shortening; add sugar and cream until light and fluffy. Add egg, beat well. Add banana, oats, nuts and dry ingredients. Drop by teaspoons onto greased baking sheet.
Bake at 400° for 9 minutes.
Cut apples in half crosswise and core.
Put apples cut side up in a 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Blend syrup, margarine and cinnamon.
Add cereal; toss to coat.
Spoon over apples.
Bake uncovered at 350° until apples are fork-tender, about 35 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Let cool and spread with strawberry jam.
Then beat egg whites; add sugar, water, cornstarch and baking powder.
Spread over jam. Sprinkle top with graham cracker crumbs or chopped nuts.
Bake for 30 minutes at 300°.
Cool thoroughly before cutting.
Bring to boil the vinegar, water and sugar.
Dissolve Jell-O. Cool with beet juice.
Add beets, diced onion, celery and mustard seed.
Mix well and refrigerate overnight.
Chop peanuts into small pieces.
Add cream cheese, milk and brown sugar.
Serve with apple slices.
Bring 1/2 inch of water to boil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add cauliflower and broccoflower florets.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer for 6 to 9 minutes, until firm-tender when
pierced. Drain, rinse with cold water, and drain again.
Repeat with broccoli florets, but cook only 3-5 minutes, until crisp-tender. Refrigerate tightly covered.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In a medium skillet, brown sausage. Drain well.
Stir in celery, onion, marjoram, walnuts, apples and cheese; pour into one pie crust.
Cut a large apple shape from remaining pie crust and place on top of filling.
Cover top of pie with aluminum foil and bake 30 minutes.
Remove foil and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes before serving.
Makes 6 servings.
Rinse kraut.
In saucepan, put bacon, apple, celery and carrot. Simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Add sauerkraut, vinegar, sugar, caraway seed, salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and cook slowly until carrots are tender.
Wipe roast with damp cloth.
Sprinkle garlic salt over entire surface.
Add sauces to top of roast.
Wrap in aluminum foil using double folds to seal.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Make graham cracker crust and put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix lemon jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Refrigerate until quivery stage.
Cream the 2 packages of cream cheese with the sugar, vanilla and dash of salt.
Gradually add jello, then fold in the drained, crushed pineapple.
Fold 2 cups Cool Whip into mixture. Put into pan and refrigerate.
Spray 14 x 9-inch dish with Pam.
Put in raw rice, consomme, drained mushrooms, parsley, garlic and onion juice.
Stir.
Brown pork chops in oil after seasoning with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Place undrained pork chops on rice mixture.
Place bell pepper rings on top of pork chops.
Cover with foil.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes in 325° oven.
Serves 4 to 8 according to number of chops per person.
Can be assembled and refrigerated for a day prior to baking.
Rinse off chicken.
Place in roasting pan.
Place pieces of cheese over chicken until all of chicken is covered.
Mix 1/2 cup of water with soup.
Pour over chicken.
Add sliced carrots and mushrooms.
Cover with foil.
Bake for one hour at 350°.
Serve over rice or egg noodles.
Brown sausage.
Add tomato sauce and about half of the water. Cover and simmer 1/2 hour.
Add green pepper and onion.
Cover; simmer 1 hour.
Add more water if too thick.
Serve on rolls.
Pat dough into tiara pan.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 12 minutes, or until done.
Mix cream cheese and powdered sugar together. When cake is cooled, turn onto plate and pour cheese and sugar mixture in middle of cake.
Arrange fruit on top.
Good with strawberries, fresh peaches or Mandarin oranges.
Brown ground chuck; drain.
Boil water, adding vermicelli. Cook until tender; don't overcook.
Drain.
Cut vermicelli into short pieces.
Wash bean sprouts and break into very small pieces.
Chop cabbage, onions, peppers and carrots very finely.
Thoroughly wash and dry chicken pieces.
Dip each piece in egg, then roll in bread crumbs.
Melt butter or margarine in skillet and brown chicken on both sides.
Transfer chicken to baking dish.
Add chicken stock and bay leaf.
Cover and bake for 50 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven.
Place a piece of cheese on each piece of chicken.
Cover and return to oven for 7 to 8 minutes.
Serve with boiled potatoes, rice or pasta alfredo.
Heat oven to 390°F/200°C.
Mince the cabbage head (except the coarse parts).
Parboil in salted water; pour off water.
Mince the onion and mash the potatoes.
Mix all ingredients for the filling, except bread crumbs and butter.
Flavor with salt and pepper.
Open and drain pineapple and mandarin oranges very good.
Add all ingredients together; mix in sour cream.
Refrigerate and serve.
Keep remaining in refrigerator.
Combine undrained pineapple, drained oranges, fruit cocktail, coconut and lemon juice. Sprinkle pudding over fruit and toss lightly. Add bananas and walnuts. Chill.
Wash and core a small apple.
Fill with peanut butter or peanut butter and raisins or peanut butter and pineapple chunks, topped with nuts.
Grease ultra loaf cover; coat with cornmeal.
In small mixing bowl, combine biscuit mix and milk.
Stir just until mixed.
Pat into cover.
To bake, bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Top with remaining ingredients and bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes more, until cheese melts.
Dissolve jello in the boiling water. Add ice cream by spoonfuls. Stir until melted and smooth. Blend in Cool Whip. Add fruit. Spoon into crust. Chill 3 hours.
In a large bowl, combine all the beans.
Mix to distribute evenly.
Divide bean mixture equally among 12 pint plastic bags or other containers; each should contain about 1 3/4 cups mixed dried beans.
Heat oven to 400°.
Spray both sides of tortillas with Pam cooking spray.
Place 2 tortillas into each of two loaf pans, gently shaping each tortilla to create a bowl.
Heat chili, stir in potatoes and cook until heated.
Divide chili mixture among tortillas.
With back of spoon, make an indentation in each chili mixture.
Break egg into each indentation.
Bake 10 minutes. Cover loosely with foil.
Bake 5 to 10 minutes longer or until eggs are done.
Lift out of pans.
Place on plates.
Spoon on tomato and onions.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Serve with salsa. Serves 4.
Brown meat; add seasonings.
Stir in soup and pickle relish. Simmer 10 minutes.
Spoon over toasted split muffins.
Serve immediately.
Gas Grilling:
Combine tomato sauce, olive oil, orange juice, vinegar, oregano, salt and garlic; pour over chicken in shallow dish.
Cover and refrigerate overnight; turn occasionally.
Drain; save marinade.
Preheat both sides of gas grill on high for 10 minutes.
Turn both sides to low.
Place chicken on grill; close hood and cook 45 to 50 minutes.
Turn and baste often.
Just before serving, brush with mixture of honey and mustard.
Makes 6 servings.
Mash garlic with salt in bottom of bowl.
Peel ripe avocados and chop into same bowl.
Squeeze lime over avocados and mash with fork.
Add chopped tomatoes and chopped onions and mix thoroughly. Put 1 avocado seed into mixture until ready to serve.
Serve with chips as dip or use as salad served on lettuce leaf.
Combine raisins and dates in a bowl.
Mix soda and boiling water, then pour over dates and raisins.
Let sit until other ingredients are mixed.
Add raisins and dates to mixture.
Put in greased and floured Bundt pan or large pan.
Bake at 250° for 3 hours.
Optional toppings:
Sauteed thinly sliced Italian frying peppers, red onion, bell peppers or mushrooms, olives, cooked and crumbled Italian sausage, thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Line a jelly roll pan with a sheet of foil.
Place the butter, vinegar, Tabasco, cayenne pepper, garlic salt and salt in a medium-sized saucepan over medium heat and stir until the butter and seasonings are well incorporated.
Add cashews and toss until they are well coated with mixture.
Mix together in bowl, sugar and corn syrup.
Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Stir in peanuts.
Cook on High for 3:40 minutes.
Stir in butter and vanilla.
Cook on High for 1:20 minutes.
Remove from microwave and add baking soda.
Stir until light and foamy. Pour onto buttered foil and quickly spread very thinly.
Cool and break up.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large pitcher.
Chill 2 hours.
Strain mixture through dampened cheesecloth.
Return juice to pitcher and chill.
Combine sugar, cream, syrup, salt and butter.
Stir while cooking over medium heat.
When mixture starts to boil, add soda and stop stirring.
Cook to soft ball stage.
Cool 5 minutes. Beat until it holds its shape.
Pour into buttered pan or drip on wax paper.
Also makes excellent cake icing.
Clean chicken.
Lay out on a table and coat with the following: salt, pepper, paprika and onion flakes.
Place into a deep dish pan.
Bake at 450° for 1 hour.
Take pan out of the oven and turn over into a new pan.
Place back into oven at 450° for another hour.

Preheat oven to 350°. Skin chicken and place in baking dish. Quarter potatoes and place around chicken, as well as the mushrooms. Top each piece of chicken with a generous tablespoon of butter. Sprinkle entire baking dish with 1 envelope of dry onion soup mix (may need more than one package if cooking for a large number of people). Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Turn oven down to 250° and cook another 2 hours.
Clean out pumpkin for carving; clean the seeds from the flesh and soak for 2 hours in salt water.
Mix the rest of the ingredients together and toss with the pumpkin seeds.
Place seeds on a cookie sheet and bake at 250° for 1 hour, turning every 15 minutes.
After pumpkin is carved and lights turned low, admire your work of art while munching on those delicious pumpkin seeds. Happy Halloween!!
Chop zucchini in large pieces.
Put in wok or skillet to toss and stir-fry.
Add tomatoes, onion and chili.
Add chili powder and toss and cook together over low heat.
When crisp-tender, add corn.
Heat and serve.
Thoroughly cream the margarine and sugar.
Add sweet potatoes and beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sift together the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and nutmeg; gradually add to creamed mixture, beating well.
Blend in vanilla and orange extracts. Pour into a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until done.
Cool about 5 minutes and remove from pan.
While still hot, drizzle with glaze.

Cook potatoes in water until done, soft. Drain, reserving one cup liquid from potatoes. Mash potatoes. Place 1/2 c. very warm, not hot, potato water in a bowl. Dissolve 1 tsp. sugar and the yeast in the water, let stand. Place sugar, salt, margarine and shortening in the hot mashed potatoes. Mix in well with mixer. Add the other 1/2 c. of potato water. Put this mixture in a very large bowl. Cool until very warm (not hot).

Mix in yeast then eggs. Add two cups of flour and beat with mixer. Add flour until you have a very nice soft dough, about 6 cups. Put the rest of the flour on dough board or counter. Place dough on the flour and knead until smooth and elastic. Grease a very large pan or bowl and put the dough into the bowl, turning over to grease the top. Cover with a light towel and let rise until double in bulk. Make into rolls or loaves of bread. Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes. Butter tops of rolls or bread when removed from oven.
Mix together meal, celery, onion, egg and buttermilk.
Mix like cornbread and bake.
Cool and crumble in large bowl.
Add chicken, chicken soup, salt, pepper, sage and chicken broth.
Bake at 350° until brown and firm.
Lightly brown sausage and remove from skillet.
Add cabbage, potatoes and onion.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle on the flour and mix well.
Add water to broth to make 1 1/2 cups broth.
Put sausage back in, add broth, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer until potatoes are tender.
In a large pot, parboil head of cabbage until leaves may be removed carefully, one at a time.
In small skillet, saute mushrooms.
Put rice in large bowl.
Add mushrooms, celery, onion, parsley, sage and garlic powder, then add soy sauce.
Fill lower end of each leaf with stuffing and sprinkle grated cheese over the top of rice stuffing.
Roll leaf at once, folding sides of leaf toward center; continue rolling to end.
Tie with a string or secure with a toothpick.
Lay stuffed leaves side by side in a sprayed baking dish.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Serves 6.
Simmer ham for 1 hour. Trim fat.

Place ham in baking pan, trimmed side up. Score. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Stud with cloves and spread brown sugar over ham. Add mustard and 1 1/2 cups boiling water to vinegar. Pour into baking pan. Cover. Bake at 325° for 3 hours.
Plunge shrimp into large saucepan of boiling lightly salted water and cook for about 45 seconds, or until they turn pink. Drain, refresh under cold water; pat dry.
In food processor or blender, blend cream cheese, garlic, chilies, coriander, salt and pepper to taste until smooth.
Transfer to bowl and chill for about 30 minutes, until firm.
Transfer the mixture to a pastry bag fitted with a small star tip and pipe it into the slit of each shrimp.
Chill shrimp on a plate for 1 hour.
Makes 25 hors d'oeuvres.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a large bowl.
Combine 1/2 cup mayonnaise, lemon juice and salt.
Stir well.
Pour over chicken mixture; toss gently.
Cover and chill chicken mixture at least 2 hours.
Spoon 3/4 cup mixture on croissant.
Top with alfalfa sprouts and serve.
Yields 8 servings.

Boil fettucini as directed on package; drain. In a pan, heat oleo and picante sauce; add cheese. Remove from heat when oleo melts. Add the sour cream and salt. Add the still warm fettucini and mix in.
Peel all crust off of the French bread.
Cut bread into 8 or 10 thick slices diagonally.
In a saucepan, melt 4 tablespoons margarine and add mustard, onions and poppy seed.
Spoon mixture between slices.
Place 1 slice of cheese between each bread piece. Drizzle 2 tablespoons melted margarine over loaf.
Arrange 1 to 2 slices bacon over each piece.
Bake on greased foil at 375° for 20 to 30 minutes or until bacon is crisp.
Brown bacon in frypan; drain.
Crumble and reserve bacon; pour off fat.
Add oil, butter, garlic and ham to pan; saute lightly. Add spaghetti, bacon, cheese, parsley, salt and pepper; stir well. Turn off heat.
Pour eggs over and quickly toss to coat spaghetti evenly.
Decorate with parsley.
Serve immediately.
Serves 4 to 5.
Grease a small casserole dish with fairly high sides.
In bottom, layer thawed and drained frozen spinach.
Mix 3/4 cup sour cream with the cooked rice and layer over spinach.
Flake tuna over rice.
Spread remaining sour cream over tuna and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Warm completely covered in a 350° oven for about 1 hour.
Cook potatoes in boiling water for 15 minutes.
Peel, cut lengthwise in half.
Place all ingredients except potatoes in heavy skillet.
Arrange potatoes on top, cut side down.
Cook over very low heat, basting occasionally, about 2 hours until tender and well glazed.
Heat sugar, salt and milk to just under boiling point (just warm).
While heating milk, mix egg yolks, cornstarch and enough water to make a very thin paste.
Add to heated milk.
Let cook until thickened, about 1 minute.
Add butter and vanilla. Pour into precooked shell and refrigerate.
Can also be used as a pudding without pie shell.
If using a shell, graham cracker is great.
Cream butter well with dark brown sugar.
Add eggs, pancake syrup, and cinnamon.
Stir well.
Add self-rising flour, oatmeal, and raisins.
Stir and drop by spoonful onto ungreased cookie sheet.
(No need to grease the cookie sheet, but a very light spraying of Pam is good.)
Bake at 350° for 7 - 10 minutes (ovens vary).
Put a layer or two of raw potatoes in casserole dish or 13 x 9 x 2-inch glass cake pan.
Sprinkle chopped onions over potatoes. Add a layer of ground beef.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Continue doing layers until desired quantity.
Keep layers 1/2 inch below top of dish.
Dilute 1 can soup with 3/4 can water. Pour over potatoes and meat.
Bake covered at least 1 1/2 hours at 350° or until potatoes are done.
Place casserole dish on an edged cookie sheet to catch drippings.
Let dish set in oven for 15 minutes before serving.
Fry rice in heated cooking oil in a large frying pan until slightly brown.
Add onion, garlic and tomato; stir over a medium flame for about 5 minutes.
Add 4 cups of water and 2 cups chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Add smoked oysters, clams and roasted peppers.
Bring to low flame.
Stir-cook for about 20 minutes or until water is dissolved.
Mix carrots, cabbage and onions together.
Put vinegar, sugar, mayonnaise, oil and salt in a pan and bring to a boil for 1 minute. Pour over cabbage mixture.
Let cool for a few minutes and ready to eat.
Boil and cool chicken; debone and cut into bite-size pieces. Drain asparagus and spread in bottom of buttered casserole. Top with the chicken.
Mix the mayonnaise, soup, lemon juice and cheese; pour over the chicken.
Mix the crackers and melted butter, then sprinkle on top. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Place onion in 5-quart cooker; top with the ribs.
Combine the barbecue sauce, syrup, mustard, salt and pepper.
Pour over the ribs.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours or until the meat is tender.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Grease pan with butter and line bottom of pan with marshmallows.
Drain pineapple (save juice).
Mix cake as directed.
Use pineapple juice in mix.
Pour the mixture over the marshmallows.
Spread the crushed pineapple over the mix.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until tester comes out clean.

Peel the vegetables and cut into 3-inch julienne strips. Cook in a saucepan with the apple juice and 2 cups of water until tender. Drain and discard the liquid. Add the butter, honey, lemon juice, milk, nutmeg and pepper. Cook, uncovered, for 3 minutes more over medium heat, stirring to glaze.
Sprinkle the first 6 ingredients in a casserole dish.
Mix the Bisquick, milk, eggs, salt and pepper and pour the batter over the ingredients in the casserole dish.
Bake at 375° or 400° for about 30 minutes or until done.
Mix eggs, potato and yogurt very gently.
Allow to stand for 1 to 2 minutes.
Coat nonstick skillet with vegetable cooking spray. Pour in egg mix and top with veggies.
Cook over low heat until nearly set and lightly browned on the bottom.
Turn and cook another minute or two.
Cook chopped broccoli until almost tender.
Drain.
Gently mix mayonnaise, cheese and onions with broccoli.
Top with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° until heated through and bread crumbs are lightly browned, about 20 minutes.
Slice pork lengthways into about three fillets, then slice into bite-sized pieces.
Place unsalted peanuts in food processor with knife blade; process until they are the consistency of flour.
Be careful not to make peanut butter.
Mix peanut flour with all-purpose flour (half and half).
Add salt and pepper to taste, set aside.
Beat one egg and add as much water.
Dip meat in egg wash, then into peanut flour.
Drop into hot grease and fry until golden brown and crispy.
Heat Eagle Brand milk just warm enough to melt Hershey bar. Add evaporated milk and vanilla.
Beat eggs and sugar until smooth.
Mix all together and pour into 1 gallon freezer.
Finish filling with milk and freeze.
Combine cornflake crumbs, Parmesan cheese, parsley flakes and seasonings.
Set aside.
Separate crescent dough into 8 triangles. Sprinkle with cheese.
Roll up, starting at shortest side of triangle and roll tightly to opposite end.
Roll to stretch each into a stick about 6 inches long.
Roll sticks in butter.
Coat with crumb mixture.
Place on ungreased pan.
Bake in 375° oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine the oil, onion, basil, red pepper flakes and salt.
Let stand 30 minutes.
Cut each zucchini lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Lay slices on baking sheet.
Brush the zucchini slices with half of the oil mixture. Preheat broiler.
Broil 2 inches from heat source 5 to 7 minutes or until browned.
Repeat with remaining oil mixture.
Combine flour and baking powder.
Add butter and shortening. Cut in.
Add milk, all at once.
Stir until moist and form into a ball, handling as little as possible; set aside.
Place berries, sugar, water and lemon juice in a deep saucepan and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Drop dough one teaspoon at a time onto the fruit mixture around the edge of the pan.
Cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook 25 to 30 minutes, until dumplings are cooked.
Place dumplings into individual dessert dishes and spoon blueberries over them.
Serve warm or cold with heavy cream.
Serves 8 to 10.
Melt butter, in saucepan, over low heat.
Stir in flour and celery salt.
Add milk gradually; stir until thickened and smooth. Stir in mayonnaise.
Cover raisins with 3 cups water.
Add spices and cracked cardamon seeds and shells.
Simmer covered for 2 hours.
Remove from heat; add wine.
Bring almost to a simmer (160°) for 2 hours. Leave overnight.
Drain.
Squeeze raisins to get all wine out. Put in bottles.

recipes.t: Seaside Shell Salad(Say This 3 Times Fast!)
d: Boil shells, drain and rinse.
In food processor, chop onion, green pepper, carrot, celery and tuna.
(If using water packed tuna, add a little olive oil to mixture, not much, a tablespoon or so.)
Unfold pie crusts; cut out with 2 1/2 inch cutters.
Place cut-outs on ungreased cookie sheet; prick each several times with fork.
Bake at 425° for 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown; cool.
Combine cream cheese, milk, onion salt and Worcestershire sauce, mixing until blended.
Spread on cut-outs.
Top with remaining ingredients, as desired.
Makes 2 dozen.

In 2-quart pitcher, combine cranberry juice, grapefruit juice, vodka, lime juice and sugar. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Add wine. Stir briefly. Garnish with lime slices. Makes 16 (1/2 cup) servings.
Cook broccoli al dente.
Layer on bottom of baking pan. Prepare chicken; pat dry and season with salt and pepper.
Layer chicken over broccoli, pushing broccoli completely under chicken. With a wire whip, mix soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder until creamy smooth.
Pour over chicken. Sprinkle generously with bread crumbs, grated cheese and paprika.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Serve with fettucine or rice pilaf.
Drain strawberries, reserving syrup.
Pour boiling water over gelatin in bowl, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
Add enough cold water to reserved syrup to measure 1 cup; stir until dissolved gelatin.
Chill until almost set.
In chilled bowl, beat cream until stiff.
(If using dessert topping mix, prepare as directed on package.)
Beat gelatin until foamy.
Fold gelatin and strawberries into whipped cream.
Pour into 1-quart mold or into individual molds.
Chill until firm.
Unmold; if desired, serve with sweetened whipped cream or Creamy Stirred Custard and garnish with strawberries or other fruits.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Drain tuna; flake.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Combine with remaining ingredients except puff shells.
Cut tops from shells. Fill each with 2 teaspoons mixture.
Yields 30 appetizers.
Stir together butter and salt; blend in herbs.
Keep butter soft.
Pull back corn husk; remove silks with a brush.
Place ear of corn on a piece of heavy-duty foil; brush with 1 tablespoon of the butter mixture.
Wrap up corn in foil.
Roast the corn directly on hot coals of grill until tender, turning frequently, 12 to 15 minutes.
Dump pineapple and
juice
in large
Pyrex
dish (9 x 13-inches).
Mix apples with lemon juice, cornstarch, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Spread
over
pineapple. Sprinkle
dry cake mix over top.
Sprinkle
with
nuts.
Slice margarine or butter in thin pats
and
cover entire pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°. Serve warm, with whipped cream, if desired.
(May be made day before and heated.) Makes 15 servings.
Cream shortening and sugar; add beaten eggs and vanilla.
Mix well.
Sift dry ingredients and add to creamed ingredients.
Stir in coconut, oatmeal, gumdrops, pecans and chocolate chips.
Form into balls; place on greased cookie sheet.
Press with fork.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Makes about 6 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine tomato sauce, basil, oregano, garlic and sugar.
Spray an 8 x 8-inch baking dish with Pam. Arrange vegetables in layers in baking dish as follows:
Zucchini, onion, tomato, tomato sauce, 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.
Repeat twice more.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, covered.
Let cool a few minutes before serving.
Butter an 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan or small rectangular pan. In a 2-quart saucepan, mix brown sugar, evaporated milk and salt. Stir over low heat.
Bring to a boil; boil for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in chocolate chips, peanut butter and vanilla until chips are melted and mixture is smooth.
Pour into baking pan.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, or until firm.
Cut into small squares.
Cook macaroni.
Brown hamburg, celery and onions; pour off grease.
Add tomato sauce and macaroni.
Spread cheese on top. Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a medium skillet, heat olive oil; add onions and green pepper and saute till onions are translucent, remove and clean skillet.
In skillet melt butter; add honey, mustard, curry and salt, mix well.
Dip chicken, both sides in mixture.
Place chicken in a 13x9-inch dish, top with onions and peppers, and add remaining sauce and bake 30 to 45 minutes, uncovered.
EAT.
Cook sausage in a skillet until brown, stirring to crumble. Drain; set aside.
Combine rice and 1 1/2 cups cheese.
Spread mixture into a greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with sausage.
Combine eggs and next 4 ingredients; mix well.
Pour mixture over sausage.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and bake an additional 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to
and grease an 8-inch square cake pan. Melt chocolate and butter in double boiler over hot, but not boiling
water
(lowest heat), stirring occasionally.
Set aside to cool.
Sift
flour,
salt
and
baking
powder into a large bowl and
set aside.
Break eggs into another large bowl and beat until frothy.
Beat in sugar a little at a time.
Add the chocolate
mixture,
vanilla,
nuts and marshmallows; stir well. Stir
in
the
flour mixture and spread evenly into the pan.
Bake 30 minutes.
Let cool in pan for 10 to 15 minutes. Cut into 2-inch squares and remove to a cake rack.
Use a whisk to mix.
Add milk to flour.
Mix well until smooth.
Add egg, pepperoni and grated cheese.
Do not put too much pepperoni in each muffin as it will be too greasy.
Spoon mixture in muffin tins and bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Makes approximately 36 muffins.

Blend together carrots, cucumber, onion, bell pepper and celery. Allow to drain well. Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise, lemon juice and salt, blending well. Add to vegetables, stirring until well mixed.
Refrigerate to blend flavors at least overnight.
Makes about 10 sandwiches or 30 finger sandwiches.
Squeeze fruit; remove seeds.
Put juice with pulp in blender. Add sugar, vanilla, protein powder and ice.
Blend on high.
Stop every now and then to stir.
Add 1/4 cup water, if needed.
Blend in slushy drink.
Pour into glasses and enjoy.
Place brownie on individual plate.
Top each brownie with scoop or square of ice cream.
Spoon on cherry pie filling.
Top with whipped cream.
Nuts are optional.
Place eggs, cheese, salt and pepper in a covered jar and shake well.
Heat butter in skillet until melted over medium heat.
Be sure skillet is coated with butter.
Pour egg mixture into hot skillet and cook over medium heat without stirring.
Turn gently with pancake turner when eggs on the bottom start to get firm. Cook 5 to 8 minutes or until eggs are slightly firm.
Melt cream cheese over low heat, stirring constantly.
Blend in mayonnaise, garlic, onion, mustard, sugar and salt.
Stir in crab and wine; heat through.
Makes about 2 cups.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Melt cheese in milk in saucepan. Add 1 slice of bread, crumbled, and thicken. Add tuna.
Place in small uncovered casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or microwave for 7 minutes.
Serves 1.
Grease a 9 x 13 inch casserole dish.
Press pie crust to conform to bottom of casserole dish.
Break chicken into small pieces and place on crust.
Mix soup with broth from chicken (as much broth as you need to get soupy consistency).
Add peas and potatoes to mixture; pour over chicken.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Take crescent rolls out of cans and slice roll into 1 inch strips.
Unroll strips and place in a criss-cross pattern over pie filling.
Bake at 350 to 400° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Cover lightly with foil if needed.
