In a medium saucepan, melt butter or margarine over medium heat. Stir in Prosciutto and saute 1 minute. Add cream and tarragon; season with salt and pepper. Simmer 2 minutes or until cream is slightly thickened.
Grease and flour 4 (8 x 8-inch) pans.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Cream together margarine, sugar and vanilla.
Beat in, one at a time the eggs.
Beat until fluffy.
Add milk alternately with the flour mixture.
Spread in pans.
Bake about 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Unroll dough into 4 long rectangles. Place crosswise in ungreased 15 x 10-inch baking pan.
Press over bottom and up 1-inch sides to form crust.
Firmly press perforations to seal.
Bake at 375° for 14 to 19 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool completely.
Spread beans over crust.
In bowl, mix sour cream and taco seasoning.
Spread over beans.
Spread onions, peppers, tomatoes and olives next.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Cut into squares and serve with salsa.
Makes 30 appetizers.
Combine the first 4 ingredients in a pan and heat.
Drain the broccoli and put it in a serving bowl.
Pour the sauce over the broccoli and sprinkle with cheese.
Crumble sausage and beef in a wide frying pan; cook until meat loses pink color.
Add onion and garlic, cook, stirring occasionally, or until soft but not brown. Blend in liquid ingredients and spices; simmer slowly, uncovered, until reduced to about 6 cups (about 30 minutes).
In a mixing bowl, combine the first 4 ingredients.
In a sauce pan, combine water, oil, butter and cocoa.
Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Pour over dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Add eggs, buttermilk, vanilla and baking soda.
Mix well.
Pour into greased and floured 15 x 10 x 1 inch baking pan.
Bake at 375° for 15-20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Combine Pineapple Juice, Soy Sauce, Lemon Juice in a large mixing bowl.
Add Scallops and Pineapple Rings; toss to coat. Marinate, covered, in a refrigerator for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Preheat broiler.
Remove Scallops and Pineapple Rings from the marinade, discard the marinade.
In pot, put cabbage, onion, bay leaves, catsup and kielbasa. Fill with water about 1-inch over ingredients.
Cook until cabbage is done (not soft).
Serve as is or over boiled cut up potatoes.
Boil and debone chicken.
Mix chicken, soups, onion, cheese and peppers.
Cook over low fire until mixture starts to bubble. Fry tortillas quickly on both sides until soft.
Layer tortillas and chicken mixture in casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Slice squash very thinly and cook in covered saucepan with 1/4 cup water until very soft.
Drain.
Saute onions in butter just until browning.
Remove both from heat and combine with cream of chicken soup and mushroom soup, eggs, 1 cup bread crumbs, corn and 1 cup of cheese.
Put in buttered 9 x 9 dish.
Combine remaining bread crumbs and cheese and cover top.
Sprinkle paprika over the contents and bake in a preheated 350°
oven for 30 minutes, or until the casserole is firm and the top is slightly brown.
In covered blender, blend 1 cup fruit at high speed 30 seconds.
In 2-quart pan, mix cornstarch and water until smooth. Add mashed fruit, syrup and lemon juice.
Stirring constantly, bring to boil over medium heat and boil 1 minute.
Turn into bowl; cover surface with waxed paper.
Cool 1 hour.
Fold in remaining fruit.
Spread cream onto bottom and sides of pie crust.
Fill with fruit mixture.
Chill 3 hours or until set.
Serves 6 to 8.
In a large saucepan, combine milk and flour and whisk over medium heat until no lumps remain (about 1 minute).
Stir in mustard, salt, black pepper and cayenne.
Cook, stirring frequently, until lightly thickened and no floury taste remains (about 4 minutes).
Stir in the Pepper Jack cheese and remove from heat.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to boil.
Add broccoli and cook until crisp-tender (about 3 minutes).
Drain well and transfer to a serving dish.
Pour in cheese sauce and toss to coat well.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook broccoli according to package directions until almost tender.
Put in a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Place chicken on top.
Mix cream of chicken soup, mayonnaise, milk, cheese, lemon juice and curry powder and pour over chicken.
Sprinkle a mixture of butter and bread crumbs over sauce.
Bake near center of 350° oven 20 to 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Decorate with pimento strips.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.

Slice the cookie dough into 24 slices and arrange on the bottom and the sides of a 9 inch deep dish pie plate that has been coated with non-stick baking spray. Press the dough together, making a uniform crust; set aside.
In a large bowl, with an electric mixer on medium speed, beat the cream cheese, eggs, sugar and vanilla for 1 minute until well mixed. Stir in the candy pieces and pour into the pie plate.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, until the center is firm.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
Cover loosely, then chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Combine cereal, flour and seasons in Ziploc bag. Melt butter. Dip chicken in butter and toss in cereal mixture. Place in greased 11 x 7 dish.
Sprinkle remaining cereal on top of chicken. Drizzle leftover butter on top of chicken. Bake at 400°, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes or until chicken is done.
Cut bread in half lengthwise, and tear out some of the inside, leaving a shallow indentation.
Spread with butter, sprinkle with oregano and garlic powder.
Slice cheese, layer on top.
Reserve peel and boil potatoes, about 20 minutes, add milk, butter and salad dressing to taste, mash.
Put bread in 325° oven for 10 minutes.
Heat creamed corn in saucepan over medium heat.
When bread is warm and cheese is melted, remove from oven.
Cover with mashed potatoes, spoon creamed corn liberally over all.
Serves 4.
Saute onion and bacon together.
Slowly add flour so as to avoid lumping.
Add sugar, lowering heat.
Add vinegar and water. Bring to low boil, stirring constantly (mixture looks glassy). Add potatoes (with or without skins), piece by piece, mixing well yet not mashing potatoes.
Season to suit with salt and pepper. Serve hot or lukewarm.
Serves six.
Separate egg.
Set white aside.
Mix flour, sugar, shortening and egg yolk.
Add milk and flavoring.
Beat until smooth. Pour into a 9 x 12-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Take out of oven.
Beat egg white and 1/4 cup sugar.
Add another teaspoon flavoring.
Spread on top of cake.
Return to oven for about 10 minutes.
Serve while hot.
Coat shallow roasting pan with olive oil.
Place meat in center.
Quarter potatoes (skins on) and place around meat. Coat potatoes with remainder of olive oil. Sprinkle Lipton soup over meat and potatoes. Add water around potatoes.
Place in a 325° oven and let simmer, turning meat and potatoes every 15 minutes until done (approximately 2 hours). Serves 4.
Brown beef
and
onion.
Let
cool
and drain.
Stir in cheese, egg, salt and chili powder; mix well.
Use rolling pin and roll
out each individual crescent roll as large as possible. Spoon
filling
into crescent roll and fold over, making into a turnover.
Place
on
greased baking sheet and bake at 425° until crust is golden brown.
Serve hot.
Sprinkle salt and pepper on chicken.
Place skin side up in baking dish. Combine all other ingredients.
Pour over chicken. Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Serve over potatoes, noodles or rice.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix salmon, milk, bread crumbs and eggs. Add onion, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Mix well, but do not overmix.
Place into greased 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes.
Prepare Dill Sauce (recipe follows).
Heat diced bacon, ground meat and chopped onion in skillet on high temperature.
Switch to medium heating until slightly brown. Add remaining ingredients in order given.
When steaming, turn to low heat.
Cook about 35 minutes covered tightly.
Mix bread, onions, celery and seasonings in a large bowl.
Add eggs and butter and mix well.
If mixture seems too dry, add more broth to moisten but do not make pastry.
Put in a greased baking pan or muffin pans.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Combine strawberries, 1/2 cup water, lemon juice and cinnamon in a small Dutch oven, stirring well; bring mixture to a boil.
Stir together butter, corn syrup, salt, vanilla and desired extract.
Gradually add powdered sugar and stir until the mixture is smooth.
Knead in the last of the powdered sugar with your hands.
Add desired food coloring.
Knead until the food coloring is evenly distributed.
Roll candy into balls; coat with granulated sugar and press into molds.
Remove from molds.
Cover candies with paper towels; let dry overnight.
Store in a tightly covered container.
Makes 96 candies.
Combine the first 5 ingredients; place in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Mix the oats, 1/2 cup brown sugar and margarine; sprinkle over berries.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Dip chicken breasts in flour to coat.
Then dip in egg (scrambled), then put chicken in breadcrumbs mixed with cheese. Pound with hand to coat.
In frying pan, put 1/4 cup oil.
When oil is hot (small piece of breadcrumbs sizzle), add chicken breasts.
Fry each side about 5 to 10 minutes.
Turn when lightly brown.
Serve immediately.
Tastes great with a little lemon juice sprinkled over or salsa!
Bring water and carrots to a boil in skillet.
Cook, covered, until almost tender.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Stir together reserved juice, brown sugar, vinegar, cornstarch and soy sauce.
Add with pepper to skillet and stir until thickened.
Add meat and cook, covered, until heated through.
Serves 4.
May be served with rice or chow mein noodles.
Boil together all ingredients except sesame oil.
Simmer desired number of chicken wing pieces for 20 minutes. Cool in the liquid.
Serve cold with a bit of sesame oil on top.
Refrigerate and use sauce over and over. Replenish favorite flavors.

Preheat oven to 325°. Mix cake mix and orange or lemon Jell-O powder. Add vegetable oil and water and beat on medium speed 2 minutes. Add eggs one at a time and beat well after each addition. Pour batter into greased and floured tube pan. Bake at 325° for approximately 1 hour or until cake tester comes out clean. Remove from oven. Let stand 5 minutes. Turn out onto cake rack and allow to cool. Serve plain or sprinkle with powdered sugar. Makes 12 servings.

Pound chicken to flatten evenly; set aside. In a skillet, melt 3 tablespoons of butter; add garlic and 1/2 teaspoon dill. Add chicken; cook until juices run clear. Remove and keep warm. Spread both sides of bread with remaining butter. In a skillet or griddle, grill bread on both sides until golden brown. In small bowl, combine cream cheese, lemon juice and remaining dill; spread on one side of grilled bread. Place lettuce, chicken and tomato on 4 slices of bread; top with remaining bread. Makes 4 servings.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch deep baking pan.
Cut the bread into 1-inch thick slices and arrange in a single layer in the pan.
In a large bowl, combine the eggs, salt, milk, sugar and vanilla, beating with an electric mixer.
Pour the mixture over the bread. Sprinkle with the cinnamon and allspice.
Cover with foil and refrigerate 6 to 24 hours.
Dot with butter and bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 45 to 50 minutes, until the bread is lightly browned.
Remove from the oven and let stand for 5 minutes.
Serve with warm maple syrup or confectioners sugar, yogurt or fresh fruit.
Serves 4.
Brown pork chops on both sides in oil in 10-inch skillet over medium heat, drain fat.
Stir in water, celery and soup mix. Cover; cook over low heat 30 minutes or until chops are tender. Take skillet off heat.
Move chops to one side.
Mix together mushrooms and flour.
Stir flour-mushroom mixture, parsley flakes and evaporated milk into skillet.
Stir over low heat until steaming.
Do not boil.
Serve over hot rice.
Serves 4.
Saute ground beef in a skillet until browned.
Add peppers, garlic and onions and cook for another 2 minutes.
While meat is cooking, make corn muffin mix batter according to directions. Place half of the batter in a greased bread pan.
Over the batter, place a layer of the meat mixture.
Add a layer of zucchini, then cheese.
Keep layering until mixture is gone.
Finally, add the rest of the corn muffin mix.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Peel onions and cut into thin slices.
Pour over boiling water and leave to cool.
Spread the bread thinly with butter and sprinkle over half of the dill.
Drain the sardines and arrange 2 on each piece of bread.
Cut the tomatoes into thick slices. Place the drained onion and tomato slices on the sardines and top with cucumber mixed with mayonnaise or sour cream, sugar and remaining dill.
Serves 4.
Cream together sugar, butter and cream.
Beat eggs and add to creamed ingredients.
Add Karo, salt and nuts.
Mix and pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 325° for 45 to 50 minutes, on "bottom rack of oven".
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease cookie sheet.
In small bowl, combine cheese and salt.
Brush potato wedges with margarine; place on greased cookie sheet.
Sprinkle wedges with cheese mixture to coat.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender and lightly browned.
Serve warm.
Makes 32 appetizers.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Prepare spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
Beat milk and eggs together.
Toss with spaghetti.
Spread spaghetti mixture into greased cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Top with Ragu sauce. Crumble beef evenly over sauce.
Add pepperoni and mushrooms. Sprinkle on Mozzarella.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting.
Using a stand mixer and paddle attachment, cream the butter. Add the cheese and
mix thoroughly. Add the flour, egg yolks, nutmeg and salt and pepper. Mix until dough just comes together and gently pat into a square. Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Mix by hand the sugars, oil and vanilla.
Add eggs, flour and baking powder.
Pour half of the batter into a 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.
Spread with pie filling. Pour remaining batter over the top.
Sprinkle again with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake in a 350° oven for 50 to 60 minutes.
Serves 15.
Fix potato flakes according to package directions adding onion flakes to water.
Set aside to cool.
Add egg, cottage cheese and grated Cheddar, mixing well.
Put in well buttered casserole, top with Parmesan and garnish with chopped parsley.
Bake in 350° oven 30 to 40 minutes until set and lightly browned.
Serves 8.
In medium bowl combine sour cream, mayonnaise and seasoning. Stir in onion, spinach, water chestnuts and red pepper.
Cover. Refrigerate to blend flavor.
Serve with crisp vegetable dippers, assorted crackers or bread.
Makes 3 1/2 cups.
Fry bacon over low heat until crisp.
Drain and crumble.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and salt.
Mix egg, water, vinegar and onion. Add to sugar mixture and add all to bacon drippings.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add crumbled bacon.
Saute zucchini and mushrooms in butter in a large skillet until softened.
Add tomatoes, spinach and salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Mix in pasta.
Spray large glass baking dish.
Place corned beef slices on pan.
Place chicken breasts on corned beef.
Roll chicken breasts. Wrap bacon around chicken breasts.
Cover with soup.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix baking mix, milk, ham and cheese until soft dough forms.
Beat vigorously for 30 seconds.
Turn onto surface well-floured with baking mix.
Gently roll in baking mix to coat.
Knead 10 times.
Pat or roll dough into ten 10-inch strips.
Place about 1-inch apart on ungreased cookie sheet. Brush strips with margarine.
Bake until light brown, 8 to 10 minutes.
Cook and mash squash or add frozen squash.
Mix brown sugar, margarine, cinnamon, salt and milk together.
Pour into greased pan.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons brown sugar.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat skillet; heat oil.
Add onion, carrots, broccoli, red pepper and garlic; stir-fry.
Add beans, black pepper, paprika and Mrs. Dash to vegetables.
Add water and bouillon.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Makes 4 servings.
Place the temperature of the oven at broil.
Place broil in an aluminum pan and slice about 10 slits into it.
First season it with the onion, garlic and seasoned salt on top and under.
Now poke holes into the broil with a fork.
Then take a 1/4 to 1/2 cup of soy sauce and a 1/2 cup of melted butter and marinate the London Broil.
Flip it once or twice so the seasoning gets through the whole steak.
Let the steak set for about 15 to 25 minutes.
Mix together mushrooms, bacon, cheese, parsley, rosemary and mayonnaise.
Heat oven to 400°.
Butter bread lightly.
Then cut each slice into 4 squares.
Place squares buttered side down on a cookie sheet.
Spoon small amount of mushroom mixture onto each square.
Bake 5 minutes and serve hot.
Makes 24 canapes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Peel, core and slice apples.
In a bowl, mix apples, cranberries, sugars, spices, flour and cornstarch; mix well.
Place apple-cranberry mixture into crusted pie plate.
Cut butter into small slices and place over apple-cranberry mixture. Place second crust over pie; create vents on top crust.
Bake at 375° for 50 to 70 minutes until juices flow over pie.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon-colored.
Gradually beat in 1/3 cup sugar;
add
vanilla.
Beat
egg
whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 1/2
cup
sugar
and
beat
until stiff peaks form.
Fold yolks into whites.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cocoa and salt; fold into
egg
mixture.
Spread
batter evenly in greased and lightly floured 15 1/2
x 10 1/2 x 1-inch jellyroll pan.
Bake in moderate 375° oven about 10
to
12 minutes or until done.
Immediately loosen sides and turn
out on towel sprinkled with confectioners sugar.
Starting at narrow end, roll cake and towel together; cool on rack.
Unroll; spread with 1 quart ice cream, softened to spreading consistency.
Frost with chocolate gloss.
Roll and freeze.
In large bowl stir together bran cereal, zucchini, milk, egg, sugar and oil.
Set aside; let stand until cereal softens in 2 to 4 minutes.
In small bowl mix flour, baking powder, cinnamon and ginger; add flour mixture to bran mixture.
Stir just until combined.
Evenly divide batter among 12 greased muffin cups. Bake in 375° oven until brown; about 30 minutes.
Cream butter, sugar and egg yolk until light in color.
Add cinnamon, salt, vanilla and flour to make a thick dough.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle nuts evenly over top; press in slightly.
Put unbeaten egg white on top.
Tilt pan to spread; pour off excess.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cut into squares while still warm.
Mix graham crackers with butter and line deep 9-inch pie plate, saving 1/4 cup of mixture for topping.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Add lemon juice and sugar and let stand while whipping Carnation milk to a stiff froth.
Add gelatin mixture to whipped milk and continue whipping until stiff peak forms.
Stir in lemon rind.
Pour in crust.
Top with remaining crumbs.
Chill 4 hours or until firm.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix together the flour, yeast, salt, sugar and Crisco; mix well.
Add water to make a dough; knead well.
Let rise 1 hour. Knead again; make 2 balls with dough.
Sprinkle with flour; let stand for 1/2 hour.
Roll out on floured board 1 inch thick; spread butter all over.
Add grated cheese all over and fold in dough, making sure the ends are tucked in.
Place on a greased baking sheet; bake at 375° until light brown.
Cook rice; set aside.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Add 1/2 cup reserved juice to 1 cup liquid measure.
Stir in vinegar, soy sauce, cornstarch and brown sugar.
Set aside.
Cook the pasta 10 to 20 minutes and drain.
Blend the oil, ketchup, cayenne pepper, white wine vinegar and the paprika.
Toss with the pasta.
Stir in the tuna, dill and scallions. Refrigerate and chill thoroughly.
Mix together first 4 ingredients.
Put in bean pot or other baking pan.
Place bacon strips across top.
Bake at 300° for 3 hours.
Add water as necessary to prevent becoming too dry.
Melt butter; add garlic.
Pour into 1-quart casserole.
Add tomatoes and mash lightly; stir in wine and mushrooms.
If scallops are large, cut into bite-size pieces; add to casserole and mix.
Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes, or until scallops break easily with a fork. Serve over a bed of rice or pasta.
Yields 4 servings.
Brown bacon until crisp.
Remove and let drain.
Add onions to drippings and saute for 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain fat off. Meanwhile, in saucepan, mix cold masted potatoes and soup until smooth.
Add milk gradually to desired consistency, stirring constantly.
Add bacon and onions; season with salt, pepper and parsley.
Heat through.
Mix salad dressing, vinegar and sugar.
Toss other ingredients and pour dressing over.
Whip first 2 ingredients at low speed.
Heat next 2 ingredients to approximately 210°.
Add heated mixture to the beaten egg whites and whip again on high speed until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla.
Store in covered container.
Use in any recipe calling for Marshmallow Cream.
Shred potatoes.
Soak
in salted water (1/2 cup salt to 2 quarts water).
Soak
for
to 1 1/2 hours;
wash.
Drain. Place in uncovered
pan. Pour syrup over (3 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups water
and 1
cup Karo)
potatoes.
Boil 5 minutes over medium heat.
Add orange juice, grated orange rind and butter. Bake in 350° oven 35 minutes or until potatoes are transparent and syrup is lightly thickened.

Cook meat in skillet with garlic and salt for 10 minutes. Add 7-Up and cook until liquid has evaporated. Add chili powder. Mix well. Pour into a large saucepan and add the other ingredients. Cook 15 minutes on low heat.
Cook Brussels sprouts 5 minutes in boiling water; drain them. Melt butter or margarine in skillet.
Stir-fry Brussels sprouts, onion, caraway seed and bouillon 5 minutes.
(Add 1/4 cup water if bouillon does not dissolve readily.)
Add tangerine segments and mushrooms and heat through.
Brown the ground beef and onions.
Add next four ingredients. Simmer 10 minutes.
Serve on the buns.
In small bowl, mix water, soy sauce, cornstarch, bouillon and ginger; set aside.
In large skillet, over medium-high heat, cook shrimp, peppers and water chestnuts in margarine for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in green onions and cornstarch mixture; heat to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; cover and cook 10 minutes or until shrimp is done.
Serve hot.
I usually serve with rice.
Beat cream cheese, mayonnaise and sugar.
Add pineapple, cranberries and nuts.
Stir thoroughly, then fold in Cool Whip. Put in a 9 x 9-inch or 12 x 9-inch Pyrex baking dish and freeze overnight.
Take out and cut in squares when needed.
Fry bacon in heavy skillet; break into pieces.
Add onions, rice and meat; stir until all are hot.
Add egg(s) and mix.
Heat water and dates on stove until dates are tender.
Simmer blackberries in saucepan.
Add dates and dash of cinnamon, then add glaze powder.
Pour into hot jar and seal.
Will keep in refrigerator 3 to 4 weeks.
Spread the cream cheese on tortilla.
Sprinkle garlic powder. If desired, add diced chili.
Roll up as for snack.
Or roll and cut, serving as pinwheels.
Add the sherry to the langostinos in a bowl.

Place the bread crumbs in another bowl and pour the evaporated milk over them. Add the cheese, dry mustard and nutmeg to the bread mixture. Combine the langostinos and bread mixture and place in a flat casserole dish.
Put the remaining bread crumbs (crust pieces) and melted butter on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Grease pie plate.
To egg whites, add sugar, vanilla, Ritz crackers and nuts.
Pour in pie plate and bake 25 minutes at 325°. Cool crust.
Whip the cream; add powdered sugar.
Cover baked pie and top with coconut.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Combine egg white, honey and anise seed in bowl.
Gradually add sugar, beating after each addition with electric mixer.
Place 12 to 14 peppermints in bowl, coat all sides and place on wire rack.
Wash and dry apples.
Insert craft sticks into stem end of each apple; set aside.
Combine caramels and water in a medium bowl; microwave at High for 3 1/2 to 4 1/2 minutes, or until smooth, stirring after each minute.
Dip 2/3 of each apple into hot caramel sauce, turning to coat.
Scrape excess sauce from bottom of apples; roll coated bottoms in peanuts.
Place on wax paper coated with cooking spray.
Store in refrigerator.
Let stand at room temperature 15 minutes before serving to allow caramel to soften.
Stir all ingredients together.
Do not use beaters.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Test for doneness by inserting toothpick into cake.
When toothpick is dry, cake is done.
Frost with chocolate fudge frosting.
1. Brown ground beef & onions in 1/4 c. Salad oil.
2. Combine remaining ingredients in baking dish or pan.
3. Bake at 400° for 30-40 minutes.

recipes.t: Chicken Breasts With Mushrooms And Sauce
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook mushrooms in oil until soft.
Add onion and garlic powder.
Add tomatoes, paste and seasonings.
Let simmer for 1 hour.
Add sugar, pepper and Parmesan cheese.
Oil baking dish.
Lay chicken in dish.
Pour the sauce with mushrooms over top of chicken.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until tender.
Add flour to skim milk.
Beat or stir until smooth.
Place broth or drippings and onion in saucepan; heat to boiling.
Add flour-milk mixture to broth very slowly, stirring constantly. Season and reduce heat.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Beat egg whites and salt until stiff.
Add vanilla, sugar and chocolate.
Drop on greased tins.
Stir flour with 1 cup sugar,
cocoa
and
baking
soda. Mix 1 cup water with vanilla, oil and
vinegar.
Add liquid to dry ingredients and mix well with
wooden spoon.
Place midget 2-inch baking cups on baking sheet.
Spoon
batter
into
cups and fill only half full.
In small mixing
bowl,
mix egg with cream cheese and remaining sugar until
well blended.
Stir in mini
chocolate chips.
Place
teaspoon
of
cream
cheese mixture in each cup. Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 20 to 23 minutes.
Yields 40 to 42 cupcakes.
Slowly bring to a boil the milk and cornstarch.
Set aside until cool.
Cream margarine and shortening until smooth; add powdered sugar and vanilla.
Add milk mixture and whip for about 3 minutes.
Beat butter and honey together.
Add eggs and rice.
Add milk and dry ingredients.
Stir until well blended.
Fill greased muffin pan 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Combine melted Candiquik with peanut butter and peanuts. Sprinkle marshmallows over bottom of waxed paper-lined 9 x 9-inch pan.
Pour chocolate over marshmallows.
When firm, cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Combine eggs and pumpkin.
Blend in sugar, spice, salt and flour; mix well.
Pour into an unbaked pastry shell.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes; then reduce heat to 325° and continue baking for 35 to 40 minutes or until done.
Makes 3 pies.
Cut cushaw in 4-inch cubes and steam slowly in the 1/2 cup water until tender.
Pour off water, but save if mixture is too dry.
Mash cushaw and add butter, 3/4 cup sugar, salt and vanilla. Pour into buttered 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Mix 1/2 cup sugar and spices together and sprinkle on top of cushaw.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
For further browning, put under broiler for 2 minutes.

Prepare lemon pudding according to package directions using 1/2 cup sugar and 3 cups water. Remove pan from heat. Add butter and stir until completely mixed. Put shortcake cups in individual serving bowls. Put a large scoop of vanilla ice cream in the center of each shortcake cup. Pour warm lemon sauce over the ice cream to form an ocean around the frozen island. Quick, easy and delicious dessert.
Cut bacon up small and fry crisp.
Drain off grease except for a tiny bit.
Add broccoli, cut up small, and add water and cook until broccoli is done.
Add potatoes.
Add barley and simmer all together, about 10 minutes or until all warmed and flavor is through.
Add salt and pepper to taste and lots of butter.
Mix all ingredients in ovenproof casserole dish. Sprinkle with additional cheese.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Peel shrimp leaving shell next to tail.
Cut inside shrimp halfway through (clean).
Make Stove Top stuffing per recipe. Dice Surimi and garlic.
Add Tabasco and Worcestershire and saute in butter.
Add stuffing and mix well.
Refrigerate.
Take cold stuffing and stuff cut shrimp.
Wrap stuffed shrimp with pastry sheet, leaving seam on bottom.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes or until pastry is golden brown.
Serve with sauteed mushrooms. Serves 4.
Slice pork chops into strips; brown in oil.
Add chopped celery and frozen corn; simmer for about 3 minutes.
Stir in can of tomatoes and seasonings.
Simmer for about 15 to 20 minutes. To make it really Cajun style, I add 1/2 to 3/4 pound sliced smoked sausage.
Serve over white rice.
Serves 4 to 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Line a cookie sheet with foil.
Mix olives, shredded Swiss and salad dressing.
Spread about a tablespoon of the mixture on each slice of bread.
Bake in preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove from cookie sheet and place on serving plate.
Serve warm.
Wash beans; add water. Bring to boil, then reduce heat.

Cook gently for 1 hour. Saute onions, garlic and fat until golden. Add with remaining ingredients; cover and continue to simmer for 1 hour or longer. Do not add salt to initial cooking water, since it will tend to make the beans tough.
Place olive oil in heavy skillet.
Add zucchini and garlic salt to heated oil, then add the dry vermouth.
Put lid on pan and shake about 2 minutes.
Pour off excess liquid; shake another 1 minute.
Serve immediately.
Mash or press carrots through coarse sieve.
Add salt, nutmeg, egg and butter and mix thoroughly.
Form into shapes, resembling carrots.
Roll in bread crumbs and chill for several hours.
Fry in hot, deep fat at 380° until browned.
Drain on absorbent paper. Tuck sprig of parsley on top and serve at once.
Serves 8.

recipes.t: Sweet Potato Cake With Fresh Coconut Filling
d: Sift together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and salt.
In a large bowl with electric mixer, beat sugar and oil for 2 minutes.
Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in dry ingredients, hot water, sweet potatoes and walnuts.
Beat egg whites until stiff, fold into batter.
Pour into 3 well-greased and floured 8-inch round pans.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 minutes or until cake springs back to touch.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes.
Turn out of cake pans and cool completely.
In heavy 2-quart saucepan, melt butter or margarine and chocolate.
Add sugar and milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugar is dissolved and thoroughly blended. Remove from heat and stir in nuts, coconut and vanilla.
Fold in oats.
Cool mixture to medium-warm.
Roll teaspoonfuls of mixture into balls.
Place on waxed paper-lined cookie sheets.
Chill until firm.
Makes about 6 dozen.
Contains about 30 calories each.
Crush wafers; mix with milk and syrup.
Let warm to room temperature.
In a separate bowl, mix fruits and nuts.
Mix well with wafers.
Pack tightly in a buttered pan that can be put in oven.
Put into refrigerator overnight.
Next day, preheat oven to 400° for 15 minutes.
Then turn oven off and place cake in oven about 15 minutes.
Run knife around edge of pan and turn cake out onto double layer of foil.
Wrap and keep in refrigerator.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to boil.
Remove the tough stalks of the cauliflower.
Separate the florets and cook for 10 minutes in the boiling water.
Drain and cool.
Heat the oil in a skillet or nonstick pan.

Add cauliflower, salt, pepper and anchovies and saute over medium-high heat for a few minutes. Beat the eggs in a small bowl; add the capers and salt and pepper. Pour this mixture over the cauliflower.
Cook until the frittata is golden on the bottom.
Invert onto a lid, then slide it back off the lid into the pan and cook the other side.
Transfer the frittata to a serving plate and serve immediately.
Place croutons in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Top with cheese and mushrooms.
Brown sausage and onion.
Drain and spread over cheese layer.
Beat eggs with 2 cups of milk and seasonings; pour over sausage.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
(May be frozen at this point.)
Mix soup with 1/2 cup milk and spread on top before baking.
Bake at 325° for 60 minutes.
Serves 8.
Thaw Rock Cornish hens and quarter.
Beat egg slightly and combine with milk.
Gradually add to flour, mixed with salt; stir to a smooth batter.
In a 2-quart micro-safe casserole, combine celery, onion and butter.
Micro-cook, covered, on High for 2 to 3 minutes or until onion is tender.
Add milk.
Micro-cook, covered, on High for 4 to 6 minutes or until steaming and foamy, but not boiling.
Stir in uncooked rice.
Let stand, covered, 2 minutes.
Stir in turkey, soup, stuffing mix, 1/2 cheese and if desired, chili peppers. Micro-cook, covered, on High for 5 to 7 minutes or until heated through, stirring once.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Let stand until cheese is melted.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In medium bowl, combine mashed potatoes, 1/2 cup cheese and 1/2 can fried onions, mix thoroughly. Spoon potato mixture into greased 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Using back of spoon, spread potatoes across bottom and up sides of dish to form shell.
In large bowl, combine chicken, green beans, soup, milk and seasoning; pour into shell.
Bake uncovered, at 375° for 30 minutes or until heated through.
Top with remaining cheese and onions; bake uncovered 3 minutes or until golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Saute garlic in oil until limp; add tomatoes and stir; simmer 5 minutes.
Add bouillon cube, mustard, salt, pepper, garlic powder and basil.
Simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve over pasta.
Cook chicken and save broth.
When chicken is cool, tear into chunks.
Cut tortillas into 1-inch squares.
Mix soups, milk, onion, salsa and 2 tablespoons broth.
In large casserole, layer 1/2 the tortillas.
Cover with 1/2 the chicken chunks and 1/3 of the sauce.
Repeat tortillas, chicken and 2/3 of the sauce.
Let set for 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Cover with grated cheese. Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Flatten rolls in bottom of 2-quart casserole.
Cook and drain sausage.
Pour crumbled sausage over rolls.
Mix together eggs, sauces and milk and pour over sausage.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 425° for 20 minutes.
(May be prepared the night before.
Just refrigerate and cook in the morning.)

Cook beef in large skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until cooked through and brown (about 5 minutes). Stir in 2 cups tomatoes, cumin and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in 1 1/2 cups water. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until most of liquid has evaporated (about 20 minutes). Wrap tortillas in a clean kitchen towel. Microwave until hot (about 2 minutes).
Defrost fish, if frozen.
Spray a nonstick pan until slick with cooking spray.
Sprinkle cornmeal on plate.
Fork whip egg, oil and lemon juice together in another dish.
Dip fish in the egg mixture, then the crumbs, coating both sides.
Arrange fish in a single layer on the nonstick pan.
Place the pan on the bottom shelf and bake at 475° for about 15 minutes or until fish flakes easily and is golden brown.
In a heavy 2-quart pot, saute onions in olive oil for 1 minute over high heat, stirring.
Add rice, lentils, pimento, kidney beans, corn, broth, salsa, garlic powder and chili powder.
Stir to blend.
Bring to a boil.
Cover; reduce heat and cook for 20 minutes.
Spread bean dip on pizza pan; spread avocado dip over bean dip. Mix sour cream, Miracle Whip and taco seasoning.
Spread cream mixture over avocado dip; spread Jack cheese.
Then spread Cheddar cheese, then chili peppers, if wanted.
Then spread green onions, then chopped olives, then chopped tomato.
Cream butter and sugar.
Beat yolks until thick; add cream. Beat into butter and sugar.
Cook in double boiler until thick. Pour slowly over egg whites.
Serve hot.
Cut apple and celery into small pieces.
Add carrot, raisins and corn.
When rice has cooled, add a little at a time so that rice is evenly distributed.
About an hour before you want to use it, mix with 3 to 4 tablespoons of mayonnaise.
Top with a pinch of paprika.
Serves 4.
Fry the hamburger.
Add the onion, green pepper and celery; fry until tender.
Cook the noodles.
After noodles and meat mixture are cooked, put in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Add corn, soup, olives and cheese.
Save a little cheese for the top.
Bake for 1/2 hour at 375°.
Heat corn syrup and sugar until boiling.
Add peanut butter. Add cornflakes, nuts and raisins.
Spread evenly in a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Let it cool.
Cut in squares.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Blend in vanilla.
Combine salt, flour and nuts; mix well.
Shape into 1-inch balls and chill 1 hour.
Mix together nutmeg and confectioners sugar.
Bake cookies at 300° for 15 to 20 minutes.
While warm, roll in nutmeg mixture. Makes about 86 cookies.
In small bowl, stir together mustard and mayonnaise.
In separate bowl add chicken, celery, onion, pineapple, and oranges. Stir in mustard/mayonnaise mixture.
Chill.
Right before serving, stir in Chinese noodles.
Cook celery and onion in butter or margarine until golden brown.
Cover.
Cook until vegetables are tender.
Melt chocolate with butter on temperature controlled burner set at 150°.
Remove and add corn syrup, milk, vanilla and salt. Blend well.
Gradually blend in sugar, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in raisins and nuts, mixing well.
Turn into a lightly buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch square pan, spreading evenly. Chill in gas refrigerator until firm, about 2 1/2 hours.
Cut into squares.
Makes 3 dozen squares.
Combine beans, water chestnuts and onion rings in large bowl. Dissolve sugar in vinegar in pint jar tightly covered.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover and shake.
Pour over beans.
Chill overnight.
Serves 8.
Spread bread with butter and garlic.
Toast in oven.
Top with pesto.
Add half the cheese, spinach and then the remaining cheese.
Scatter chopped tomatoes across the top and sprinkle with basil and oregano.
Bake in oven 5 minutes at 375 degrees.
Cut slices in half and garnish plate with lemon wedges.
Put grape and apple juice concentrate into a pan and bring to a boil.
Mix unbleached flour and water in a small bowl.
Add this to boiling mixture, stirring consistently for 2 minutes. Makes about 16 ounces.
With a rolling pin, crush soup mix in pouch.
On wax paper combine soup mix, bread crumbs and black pepper.
Mix sugar and 1/2 of milk or water.
Sprinkle yeast and let raise in warm place.
Cut up shortening in small pieces; add remainder of milk and put aside in warm place to melt butter.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix Bisquick, mayonnaise and egg.
Add tuna, Cheddar cheese, celery, onion and lemon juice.
Spread mixture on muffins or buns, split apart.
Sprinkle a little cheese on top.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet until golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Beat sugar and eggs together.
Add vanilla and dry ingredients.
Fold in apples and nuts.
Put in greased 9-inch pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes; cool.
Mix whipped topping and pineapple; spread on cooled pie.
Refrigerate until serving time.
Thaw and drain spinach.
I saut vegetables before mixing them with beaten eggs.
Add cheese and mix well.
Wash tomatoes and remove stem ends.
Cut into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Arrange half the slices in a shallow serving dish and sprinkle with half the sugar, salt and pepper.
Top with remaining slices and sprinkle with the rest of the sugar, salt and pepper. Pour vinegar over top.
Refrigerate, covered, at least 1 hour before serving.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Grind the tomatoes to make like applesauce.
Heat tomato pulp, margarine, sugar and raisins together.
Cool.
Add flour, spices, soda and salt sifted together. Add nutmeats.
Mix well. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
To cucumber pulp, add cream, flour, butter and eggs.
Mix well.
Add salt and pepper.
Batter will be very thick.
Drop by spoonfuls into hot 375° vegetable oil.
Fry until crisp and brown. Drain on brown paper.
Combine soup, sour cream, chilies, half the cheese and half the olives. Divide mixture into two bowls.
Add chicken to one bowl, setting other bowl aside.
Use chicken mixture to fill tortillas.
Fold and place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan, seam side down.
Pour remaining soup mixture over all.
Top with remaining cheese and olives.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 6.
Brown chicken on all sides.
Grease a large pan.
Place uncooked rice in the pan.
Mix and heat the soup and milk on the stove.
Pare parsnips and cut in halves.
Boil parsnips in water, about 30 minutes or until tender; drain.
Mash parsnips.
Mix parsnips, flour, salt, pepper, margarine, onion and egg.
Shape into 8 patties.
If mixture is too soft to shape, mix in some of the bread crumbs until stiff enough.
Coat patties with bread crumbs.
Heat shortening in skillet over medium heat until hot.
Cook patties about 5 minutes, turning until golden brown.
Brown chicken in skillet in salad oil.
Remove chicken to bowl. In drippings, cook onions, green peppers, cut into strips.
Add peach liquid from can to skillet, stir in vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, salt and pepper and 1/4 cup water.
Heat to boiling, reduce heat to low.
Add chicken.
Simmer 30 minutes.
In cup, mix cornstarch and 4 tablespoons water into simmering chicken liquid. Add peaches and tomatoes and heat.
Serve over rice.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Pound chicken breast between wax paper to flatten slightly.
Cut sheets of puff pastry if large and roll out to hold each piece of chicken.
Spread cheese spread on chicken and put on puff pastry.
Fold over and seal edges.
It will look like pocket pastry.
Paint with egg wash and put in oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
I have done it without the egg wash and it works.
Take beans and wash and run through hot water until beans are white again.
Add beans to 4 quarts of boiling water.
Add smoked ham hocks and simmer approximately 3 hours in covered pot.
Remove ham hocks; chop meat and return to soup.
Saute onion in a little butter and when light brown, put in soup.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add salt when ready to serve.
Serves 8.
Mix all ingredients, except noodles, bacon and Parmesan cheese, in large mixing bowl.
Add noodles and bacon; toss until well mixed.
Turn into buttered 2-quart casserole.
Cover; bake at 350° for 30 minutes, or until heated through.
Remove cover; sprinkle with 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.
Broil until golden brown. Top with additional Parmesan cheese and sour cream.
Yields 8 servings.
Combine corn syrup, brown sugar and salt in saucepan; bring to a full boil.
Stir in peanut butter; remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla, cereals and lastly, chocolate chips.
Quickly press into buttered 8 x 8-inch pan.
Chill 1 hour.
Cut into squares.
Store in refrigerator.
Cut shortening into
sifted
dry
ingredients and brown sugar as for pie crust.
Add
egg
and
milk;
mix thoroughly. Spread in bottom and a little up
the
sides of
a
x 9 x 2-inch pan; mixture will
be moist.
Top with rhubarb. Sprinkle gelatin powder over.
Mix
butter
with sugar and flour as for pie crust. Sprinkle over
rhubarb.
Bake in 350° oven for 50 minutes.

In medium bowl, stir in boiling water into jello. at least 2 minutes or until completely dissolved. Stir in cold water. Refrigerate about 1 1/4 hours or until slightly thickened. Reserve a few oranges for garnish if desired. Gently stir in remaining oranges in thickened jello. In a separate bowl, beat cream cheese and sugar with wire whisk until well blended. Gently stir in 2 cups whipped topping. Spoon into large serving bowl; cover with jello mixture. Refrigerate 2 hour or until firm. Garnish with remaining whipped topping and oranges. Yield 16 servings.
Heat sugar and vinegar in small pan.
Stir until sugar is dissolved.
Cool.
Pour over vegetables and apple.
Toss.
Let stand overnight.
To make the bread:
Combine 1 cup of starter, oil, eggs and vanilla in a bowl; mix well.
Combine dry ingredients; stir into starter mixture just until combined.
Fold in chocolate chips and nuts.
Spoon into two well greased 9 x 4 x 2-inch baking pans. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until breads test done.
Cool in pans for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack.
Dust with confectioners sugar.
Combine all ingredients (except milk).
Heat and then cool. Beat the milk with mixer until stiff.
Fold into Jell-O mixture. Pour into graham cracker pie shell.
Chill and serve with whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Meantime, heat oil in large skillet.
Add onion and garlic; cook until soft.
Add reserved clam juice and wine to skillet; boil until reduced by half, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add clams, thyme, parsley, salt (if needed; canned clams may be sufficiently salty) and red pepper flakes, if desired.
Drain pasta; toss with clam sauce and serve immediately.
Line pie or quiche dish with pastry.
Cook white sweet corn according to package directions; drain.
Place in bottom of pastry. Sprinkle cheese over corn.
Beat eggs, cream, onion and seasonings together and pour over corn-cheese mixture.
Sprinkle bacon over top.
Bake 25 minutes at 400°.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake an additional 20 minutes.
Serve immediately.
Saute butter and garlic, boil broccoli (see package) and drain. Boil tortellini (see package) and drain.
Mix gently, broccoli, tortellini, butter and garlic.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and Parmesan cheese.
Grate the first 3 items together.
Cut 1/2 jar sweet pickles; add to other ingredients, then add 1/3 to 1/2 of
the juice from pickles.
Add enough mayonnaise to hold together.
Brown meat in stew pot; drain good.
Add onions, peppers and garlic; cook until tender.
Add tomatoes and spices.
Simmer for 2 hours.
Add beans.
Simmer 30 minutes longer.
In a large skillet with cover, brown small pieces of chicken on high flame for about 10 minutes.
Add sliced onions, olives, stewed tomatoes, oregano, garlic and white wine.
Bring to a boil, about 2 minutes.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 45 minutes. Serve over your favorite rice.

recipes.t: Low-Fat Seafood With Angel Hair Pasta
d: Heat olive oil in a large nonstick pan.
Put water on to boil for pasta.
Add garlic and tomatoes to olive oil and saute, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes.
Add wine, seafood and basil or parsley and bring to a boil and then immediately turn heat to low.
Add pasta to boiling water.
Simmer seafood mixture for about 7 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add cooked pasta to seafood mixture.
Sprinkle with additional parsley or basil and Parmesan cheese.
Serves 4.
About 6 grams of fat per serving.
Heat oil and garlic in a medium saucepan until slightly browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and basil.
Simmer on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine corn syrup, sugar and water.
Cook to soft ball stage. Remove from heat.
Add chocolate.
Mix well.
Add vanilla; slowly add evaporated milk.
Mix thoroughly.
Makes 1 1/4 cups.

Saute first 4 ingredients until mushrooms are barely done. Section bread in 1-inch diagonals, keeping bread in a whole. Spoon little of mushroom mix between each slice. Also, insert pie shape of cheese in each slice.
Wrap loaf in foil and bake at 300° for about 20 to 30 minutes.
In a 2 quart saucepan, combine water, tomatoes and carrots. Cover, bring to a boil, approximately 5 - 10 minutes.
Add beef base and noodles; stir.
Lower heat simmer for 15 minutes or until noodles are cooked.
Mix all ingredients except bell peppers and cheese.
Clean and hollow out bell peppers and stuff with mixture.
Top with cheese. Place in covered baking dish and bake at 375° for 50 minutes. Remove cover and bake another 10 minutes.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add sugar and cocoa and blend well.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 2 small unbaked pie shells. Place on bottom rack of oven preheated to 350°.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Allow to cool.
Heat pressure cooker and brown bacon.
Place browned bacon on a plate.
Add cabbage, corn and pepper to bacon drippings.
Season with salt and brown sugar.
Add water.
Place cover on cooker. Allow steam to flow from vent pipe to release all air from cooker. Place indicator weight on vent pipe and cook 3 to 5 minutes with stem at cook position.
Cool cooker at once.
Garnish with bacon strips and paprika.
Place broccoli flowerets in microwave dish with 1/4 cup water and cover with Saran Wrap.
Microwave on High 6 minutes.
Grease four custard cups with margarine.
Arrange 2 sole fillets per cup so they are covering the inside edge.
Place microwave broccoli flowerets in center; flower heads up.
Cover flowerets with Swiss cheese.
Microwave on High for 7 minutes.
Remove from cups carefully and serve immediately.
Mix margarine and sugar together.
Blend in eggs or egg substitute (Egg Beaters, Scramblers, etc.).
Blend in dry ingredients, alternating with applesauce.
Fold in raisins and nuts.
Fry and drain meats.
Combine meats, oregano and salts.
Cook cheese until melted and add to meat mixture.
Blend well.
Spread on party rye.
Freeze on cookie sheet until set.
Place in baggies in freezer until ready to use.
Beat cream cheese and 1/2 c. of milk until smooth.
Add pudding mix and remaining milk; mix well.
Fold in marshmallows. Pour into crust.
Refrigerate until serving.
Boil Ramen noodles until done.
Add seasoning that comes with Ramen noodles.
Put 1 teaspoon mustard and hot sauce to taste. Add crumbled sausage.
Mix and enjoy!
Brown ground beef, onion and pepper in a large skillet, using a fork to break up meat.
Mix chili powder and hot water; pour over meat mixture.
Simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Add cheese, beans with juice, salt and pepper.
Simmer until cheese melts.
Be careful not to let burn.
Cream the sugar, shortening and molasses together.
Stir the hot water and soda until dissolved.
Mix flour and ginger, then add everything together to make a thick dough.
Drop by spoonful into a dish of sugar.
When coated with sugar, roll into a ball. Flatten on cookie sheet.
Bake 8 minutes at 375°.
Roll biscuits out and spread mustard on it.
Then you put a slice of cheese on it.
Take your hot dog and put holes in it with a fork.
Place hot dog on biscuit and roll.
Put on a lightly greased pan and bake for 10 to 15 minutes in 350° oven.
Cook macaroni. Scramble ground beef, pepper and onion in skillet.

When cooked, add tomatoes and simmer 5 to 10 minutes. Add squash and seasonings. Steam for approximately 5 minutes or until tender. Add macaroni. If making casserole, alternate mixture with layers of shredded cheese and top with bread crumbs. Bake until cheese is melted and bread crumbs toasted. Tomato juice may be used if mixture becomes too dry. May be cooked in skillet without layering. Add any of your favorite vegetables (snow peas, green beans, etc.).
Drain pineapple and reserve liquid.
Combine 1 cup boiling water and lemon gelatin in mixing bowl.
Stir to dissolve gelatin. Add drained pineapple and 1 cup ice cubes.
Stir until ice is melted. Pour into 9 x 13-inch baking pan and put in refrigerator to set.
Repeat with orange gelatin, using remaining water and ice.
Stir in marshmallows instead of pineapple.
Pour over lemon layer.
Return to refrigerator to set.
In a bowl, whisk the sour cream, pineapple and pudding mix until blended and thick. Serve with vanilla wafers.
Dice eggs and bacon and combine with macaroni.
Add other ingredients (mayonnaise last).
Toss and chill.
Serves 16 to 20. Keeps well in refrigerator.
Good tasting and healthy!
Bring broth to a boil.
Add remaining ingredients and cook until spinach barely wilts.
Serve immediately.
Serves 6.
Drain pineapple.
Add enough water to the juice to make 1 cup. Heat with marshmallows until they are melted.
Add 1 cup hot water to jello and dissolve.
Chill until partially jelled.
Mix Dream Whip and set aside.
When jello is partially jelled, mix all ingredients, and chill well.
Soften cream cheese.
Mix together cocktail sauce, celery and clams (drained).
Pour over blocks of cream cheese.

Lay out one flour tortilla. Lay one piece of ham on top of tortilla. Layer Ranch dip on ham and sprinkle some black olives on, then green onions, then cheese. Roll as tightly as you can, then slice it about 1-inch thick. Chill and serve.
Mix together thoroughly beef, onion, rice crumbs, milk and seasonings.
Shape with hands into 1-inch balls.
In blender, puree egg and prunes until finely chopped.
Add sugar.
Combine flour, baking soda and salt; add to prune mixture and mix well.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto greased baking sheets.
Top each cookie with a pecan half.
Bake at 350° for 13 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove to wire racks to cool. Makes 2 dozen.
Melt margarine in frying pan; add mushrooms, walnuts and onion and stir until almost cooked.
Stir in seasoning and bread crumbs. Stir in eggs and mix well.
Let mixture get cold.
Shape mixture into cutlet shape or rounds.
Dip in flour, then egg, then flour and pan-fry until golden brown.
Season doves to taste with salt, pepper and thyme.
Place in casserole dish and pour soup and water over top.
Bake, covered, at 250° for 3 to 3 1/2 hours.
Serve over rice.
Chop vegetables.
Sprinkle with salt and let stand overnight; drain.
Dissolve sugar in vinegar and mix in celery and mustard seed.
Mix well and seal in airtight containers.
Brown ground beef and drain.
If using onion, add and cook until tender.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole dish.
Add 1 cup of water.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Scrub potatoes.
Bake or microwave until done.
Halve potato and scoop out inside.
Combine cooking oil, chili powder and hot pepper sauce.
With a pastry brush, brush the inside potato halves with oil mixture.
Return to baking sheet.
Sprinkle potatoes with bacon, tomato and green onion.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 450° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Serve with sour cream.
In a saucepan, combine sugar, cornstarch and water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened and clear. Quickly stir in egg yolks.
Boil 1 minute more.
Remove from heat. Stir in 1/3 cup of lemon juice, salt and butter.
Cool.
Blend cream cheese and condensed milk until smooth.
Add pudding mix and remaining 1/3 cup lemon juice.
Fold into cooled pudding.
Divide in pie shells.
Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Garnish with whipped cream and lemon slices.
Enjoy!
Beat cream cheese with next 2 ingredients in mixer bowl until smooth.
Add fruit.
Whip the cream in mixer bowl until soft peaks form.
Fold into salad gently.
Spoon into mold.
Freeze until firm.
Unmold onto serving plate.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a medium bowl.
Add tenderloins.
They can marinate 5 minutes or overnight, depending on your schedule.
In a small pan, or in the microwave, toast sesame seeds until light brown.
Set aside.
Use a baking sheet with shallow sides to roast the pork.
Grease sheet lightly, then remove pork from soy sauce mixture and place on sheet.
Bake 20 minutes.
Pour remaining marinade over the tenderloin and continue baking another 5 minutes.
Remove pork from oven, slice thin slices on the diagonal and place on platter.
Pour the pan juices over the pork, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve. Suggestion:
Serve with steamed rice and fresh asparagus.
Cook fettucini according to package.
In large skillet, brown chicken and garlic in olive oil.
Add soup, wine and spices. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve over fettucini.
In large skillet, melt margarine and stir in salt.
Add Chex, stirring until well coated.
Cook over low heat about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle with cheese, stirring until Chex are well coated.
Spread on paper towel; makes about 6 cups.
Cut off stems, keeping flowers and leaves.
Wash thoroughly 3 times.
Drain.
Fry garlic in oil.
Add greens, salt and red pepper.
Simmer until tender.
Add a little water, if dry.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Melt 1/2 cup oleo.
Add sugar, salt, milk, 6 1/2 cups flour and yeast.
Stir until mixture forms ball.
Turn out on a well floured surface and knead, adding more flour if needed.
Place in greased bowl.
Let rise until double bulk.
Roll out.
Melt 2 tablespoons oleo and brush top.
Sprinkle with dill.
Roll up jelly roll, cut in 1 inch pieces.
Put in muffin tins.
Let raise 15 minutes.
Brush rolls with beaten egg. Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Sift all dry ingredients into mixing bowl.
Combine egg, milk and margarine in separate bowl.
Add egg mixture to dry ingredients.
Blend only until flour is moist.
Fold in apples.
Preheat oven to 450°.
In a 2-quart saucepan, bring the water to a boil.
Add the Bisquick and stir vigorously over medium heat until the mixture leaves the side of the pan, forming a ball. Cool 5 minutes.
Beat one egg at
a time into the mixture, beating thoroughly.
Add garlic salt and cheese.
Drop by a spoon onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes, then 350° for 15 minutes.
(Should be golden brown.)
Serve hot.
Makes four servings.
Place coffee and nutmeg in blender.
Add extracts while running machine.
Stop and scrape sides.
Process 10 seconds or longer.
Place mix in a bowl and stir in almonds.
Store in airtight container in refrigerator.
Yield:
Mix for 8 six-ounce servings.
Buy a small angel food cake and break into small pieces, then place in bottom of long glass pan.
Place Jell-O in boiling water. Place frozen strawberries into the hot Jell-O mixture and pour over the cake pieces while still hot.
Place in refrigerator until Jell-O sets.
Spread Cool Whip or whipped cream on top.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Slice up the gizzard into a skillet.
Add water to cover the gizzards.
Cover and let the water come to a boil.
Remove from the heat and drain in a colander.
Add enough olive oil to the skillet so that the gizzards do not stick to the bottom.
Heat the oil; add the gizzards, garlic and onion.
When the gizzards start to fry, add more olive oil.
Season to taste with salt, pepper, parsley and garlic powder.
Add the mushrooms and gravy mix.
Cook until the gizzards are chewable, approximately 30 minutes.
Serves five.
Mix cabbage, onions, almonds and sesame seeds. Whisk together vinegar, salt, pepper, sugar, oil and ramen seasoning. Just before serving, toss salad with broken noodles and dressing.
Cover seedless raisins with boiling water and simmer 10 minutes.
Drain.
Combine raisins, cooked rice, frozen orange juice, pepper, nutmeg and beaten egg.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Pare and slice potatoes; arrange half the slices in a greased casserole.
Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle 1/2 of the cheese and 1/2 of the onion over the potatoes. Spoon 1/2 of the soup over top, then pour 1/2 of the wine over the soup.
Repeat layers; cover casserole.
Bake for 1 hour.
Remove cover; bake 15 minutes longer.
Simmer together tomato soup, pepper and onion for 5 minutes in skillet.
Add rest of ingredients and simmer for 1 hour.
Serve on hot buns.
Combine chocolate chips and peanut butter.
Melt in microwave until blendable (1 to 2 minutes).
Stir ion mini marshmallows and raisins.
Fold into 9 x 9-inch square pan lined with foil.
Chill and cut into 1-inch squares.
Brown pork chops in skillet; set aside.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add onions and celery.
Cook over low heat until onion is soft.
Add sage, pepper and salt.
Blend well.
Add crumbs and water.
Toss lightly until bread is slightly moistened.
Place meat in shallow pan.
Combine Coca-Cola and brown sugar and pour over ham.
Spread mustard over ham also.
Stick cloves in fat part of ham.
Preheat oven to 350° and bake 45 minutes.
Wipe the chicken dry with a paper towel. Dilute soy sauce one to one with plain water.
Add onion and sugar.
Add the chicken. Using medium heat, cook the chicken with a cover.
The heat should be strong enough to bring all the mixture to a boil, bubbling around and over the chicken, but not too strong as to evaporate the mixture too quickly.
Turn the chicken every five minutes.
Put raw hamburger in the bottom of the crock-pot.
Put diced potatoes, cut carrots and onions on top of burger.
Pour soup over and crock during the day.
Beat cream cheese until fluffy and add milk, lemon juice and flavoring.
Chill 3 hours and add strawberries and glaze.
Brown
and
drain hamburger.
Place Velveeta, Mozzarella and Cheddar
cheese
(shredded)
in
4-quart crock-pot on low. Dice onion and green pepper.
Drain tomatoes and green chillies and dice finely.
Place
hamburger,
onion, green pepper, tomatoes and green chillies
in
crock-pot
with the cheese and add garlic salt to taste.
Let
cook
for
about 1/4 hour, stirring occasionally. Serve hot over tortilla chips.
Mix cracker crumbs with butter or margarine.
Spread over fillets.
Sprinkle on Parmesan cheese and paprika.
Sprinkle on small shrimp.
Spread on can of cream of mushroom soup.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Serves 4.
Cream the sugar, shortening and eggs in mixer bowl for 1 minute. Sift flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together. Add to creamed mixture, stirring with a wooden spoon.
Add water, vanilla, apples and pecans, stirring to mix. Spoon into greased 9 x 13-inch cake pan. Bake at 350° for 45
to 50 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cut into squares. Spoon warm Caramel Sauce over each serving.
Boil opossum until tender.
Bake sweet potatoes until tender. Place meat in a roasting pan, season with salt, pepper, garlic powder and thyme.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake further until browned.
In a bowl, combine brown sugar and egg yolks.
Add whipping cream, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine flour, orange peel, baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar and salt.
Stir in chopped cranberries and completely coat them.
Add brown sugar mixture and butter; mix well (batter will be very stiff).
Beat egg whites until foamy.
Add remaining cream of tartar; beat until soft peaks form.
Fold into batter.
Pour into a greased 9-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.

Mix vanilla, milk, water, eggs, sugar, and oil in large bowl. Sift in rest of ingredients. Mix well. If needed add a little more flour to make dough so you can handle it. It should be soft. Fry in shortening or lard at 350 degrees until cooked through. Approximately a minute on each side.
For Dip:
In large mixer bowl combine the drained spinach, cream cheese, milk, minced garlic, shredded lemon peel, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 teaspoon salt and hot pepper sauce.
Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until combined. Stir in sliced green onion; cover and chill mixture until serving time.
Dissolve jello in boiling water. Chill and let set slightly. Whip Dream Whip and set aside.
Cream the cream cheese and add to jello.
Add crushed pineapple. Fold in Dream Whip with electric mixer. Add celery and nuts. Mold and chill.
Pat rings dry.
Put in low buttered pan.
Drizzle with butter and honey.
Broil about 4-inches from heat for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbly.
Serve on warm plates with 2 tablespoons of yogurt.
Spread cream cheese in a 9-inch baking dish (1/4-inch thickness).
Sprinkle diced vegetables over cream cheese.
Top with 1/2 bag Monterey Jack cheese.
Pour whole bottle of chili sauce over vegetables and cheese.
Sprinkle remaining Monterey Jack over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, until cheese is melted.
Serve with nacho chips.
In 2-quart glass casserole, heat butter 30 seconds.
Add onion and cook for 2 minutes, stirring once.
Stir in eggs, milk, salt and lemon juice.
Cook, covered, 4 to 5 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes.
When almost set, lightly fold in cream cheese.
Cook one minute longer, rest 5 minutes, serve.
Brown hamburger, onion and celery.
Drain.
Then add catsup, chili sauce, mustard, sugar, salt, pepper and water.
Simmer about 10 minutes and serve on rolls.
Dissolve Jell-O in a quart of hot water.
Add other ingredients except ginger ale.
Makes 2 1/2 gallons.
Freeze until ready to use.
Add ginger ale and serve.

Mix romaine lettuce, spinach, and red onion together in a bowl; portion lettuce mixture onto serving plates. Top each serving with macaroni, chicken, roasted red peppers, and bacon. Serve with poppy seed dressing and French-fried onions on the side.

Cook and stir chocolate chips, peanut butter, and butter together in a pot over low heat until melted, about 5 minutes. Place cereal squares in a bowl and pour chocolate mixture over cereal and stir until evenly coated. Add confectioners' sugar to coated cereal and stir to coat. Allow puppy chow to cool.
Mix puppy chow, peanuts, marshmallows, sunflower seeds, chocolate pieces, and raisins together in a large bowl.

recipes.t: Not Your Grandma'S Chopped Chicken Liver
d: Melt butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Saute onions until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add sugar, stir, and saute until onions are softened and lightly browned, about 5 minutes more. Transfer onions to a food processor, leaving as much butter in the pan as you can.

Fry livers in the hot butter until lightly browned on 1 side, about 4 minutes. Turn and continue frying until slightly pink in the center, 3 to 4 minutes more. Add livers to the food processor with the onions.

Pour bourbon into the same skillet and bring to a boil while scraping the browned bits off the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Boil until thickened and reduced by half, about 6 minutes. Pour liquid into the food processor.
Combine eggs, thyme, salt, and pepper in the food processor with the liver mixture. Process until smooth.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan.

Blend cake mix, 3 eggs, milk, and softened butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer on low speed until moistened, about 30 seconds. Increase speed to medium and beat until batter is smooth, about 4 minutes. Pour into prepared pan.
Beat remaining 2 eggs, ricotta cheese, sugar, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl until smooth. Pour evenly over cake batter in the pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour.
Chill cake in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
Beat eggs and red pepper flakes together in a bowl. Stir tomatoes, feta, and basil leaves into egg mixture.
Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over high heat until oil starts to shimmer. Pour egg mixture into hot oil and cook, without stirring, for 5 seconds.
Cook and stir egg mixture until eggs are scrambled and softly set, about 30 seconds. Transfer eggs to a plate and sprinkle with sea salt.
Blend strawberries, Greek yogurt, mango, milk, and protein powder together until smooth. Add mint leaves and pulse until leaves are chopped, 4 to 5 pulses.

Pour the jar of pickles and the liquid into a large bowl. Stir in the sugar, hot pepper sauce, garlic and red pepper. Return to the pickle jar and refrigerate for at least 1 day before serving to soak up the flavors.

Combine goat cheese, cream cheese, 5 garlic scapes, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and garlic in a bowl; mix with a fork until blended. Scoop into a serving bowl. Garnish with remaining garlic scape and toasted pecans.
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, vinegar, mayonnaise, mustard and sesame oil. Pour atop salad and serve.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in the sirloin strips, and cook a few minutes until the strips begin to brown, but are still a little pink. Stir in the onion and garlic; cook for 2 minutes. Add the celery and ginger, continue cooking until the onion has softened, about 3 minutes. Season with soy sauce and chili oil. Divide among hoagie rolls and serve.
Mix water and sugar together in a 2-quart pitcher until dissolved.
Stir lime juice, lemon juice, and orange juice into pitcher. Add tequila and triple sec; stir.
In a large skillet over medium high heat, saute the sausage for 10 minutes, or until browned. Stir in the margarine until well blended, then stir in the flour until mixture is thick and pasty.
Reduce heat to medium low and slowly add the milk, stirring constantly, until mixture is thick and bubbly and to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Place potatoes into a large pot with enough salted water to just cover; bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer, turning occasionally, until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain potatoes and set aside to cool.

Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, remove from heat, and let eggs cook in hot water for 15 minutes. Remove eggs from hot water and rinse with cold water until cool. Peel and chop eggs; put into a large glass dish.
Peel cooled potatoes and chop; add to eggs in glass dish.

Stir coleslaw dressing and creamy salad dressing together in a bowl until smooth; add chives and stir. Pour dressing over the potatoes and eggs; stir to coat. Season salad with salt and pepper; dust with paprika.
Cover dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.
In a large skillet over medium heat, warm condensed soup. Do not dilute soup. Add cheese and stir until melted and thoroughly mixed. Stir in salt.
Add seashell pasta to cheese mixture and stir until evenly coated; serve immediately.
Pour enough oil into a frying pan to cover the bottom 1/3-inch deep; add garlic, cumin, salt, turmeric, and black pepper. Heat oil mixture over medium heat.

Cook and stir potatoes in the hot oil, turning occasionally, until cooked through, golden brown, and crisp on the outside, 10 to 15 minutes. Add fresh cilantro and curry paste and stir to coat. Fry until cilantro is dark green and crisp, about 1 more minute. Remove potatoes with a slotted spoon and transfer to serving dish.
Spread peanut butter onto the cut side of the banana halves, and seal the halves back together. Slice into coins, and set aside.
In a saucepan over low heat, whisk together the egg yolks and 1/2 cup of the sugar. Stir in the vinegar and butter. Cook, whisking constantly until clear. Whisk in remaining sugar if you like.
Place the bananas into a serving bowl, and pour the sauce over them. This dish may be served hot or cold.
Stir the salt, cocoa powder, white sugar, brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, chili powder, and black pepper in a small bowl until combined. Store in an airtight container.
To use, rub 2 to 3 teaspoons of the spice mixture onto a serving of meat, and let stand at least 10 minutes before cooking.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Stir blue cheese salad dressing and cream cheese together in a mixing bowl. Stir chicken, Buffalo wings sauce, and blue cheese crumbles into the salad dressing mixture; pour sauce into a baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven until bubbling, 15 to 20 minutes.

Combine the potatoes, salt, coconut cream, green chiles, curry leaves, cayenne pepper, saffron powder, garlic, and water in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the coconut cream thickens, about 15 to 20 minutes.

Test the potatoes for doneness by piercing them with the tip of a paring knife. When the potatoes are tender, remove the pan from the heat. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with plain rice.

Cream together the ricotta and cream cheese. Add sugar and continue beating until smooth. Add lemon juice, vanilla, flour, and cornstarch, beating well after each addition. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Gradually beat in melted butter. Blend in sour cream, continue beating all ingredients until well blended.
Pour into ungreased 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake at 320 degrees F (160 degrees C) for 1 hr. Turn off oven and leave inside for 2 hours.
Cut into squares. Top each with strawberry, blueberry, or cherry pie filling. Note: Bars can be frozen.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

In a large skillet, brown ground beef and sausage. After beef and sausage are browned, add cheese. Mix often. Once all ingredients are combined spoon 1 tablespoon of the mixture onto each piece of rye bread. Arrange bread with toppings on a baking sheet.
Bake 5 to 7 minutes.
Mix minced onion, beef bouillon, onion powder, sugar, and celery seed together in a bowl. Store in an airtight container.

In a large saucepan, combine tomatoes, olive oil, and red pepper flakes. Simmer 30 to 40 minutes, or until sauce is thickened. Stir in garlic, and simmer 10 minutes. Remove from heat, and stir in basil, salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a 9x13-inch baking dish with parchment paper or grease.
Mix graham cracker crumbs and butter together in a bowl; press into the prepared baking dish.
Stir cranberries, sweetened condensed milk, pecans, coconut, white chocolate chips, and bittersweet chocolate chips together in a bowl; gently spread over the graham cracker crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden brown, 25 to 28 minutes; cool on a wire rack.
In a nonporous glass dish or bowl, combine the mushrooms, vinegar, rosemary, and salt and pepper. Stir to coat. Cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill for high heat.

Brush grate with oil, and arrange marinated mushrooms on hot grill. Turn after 2 to 3 minutes, and continue grilling until mushrooms are heated through and look wilted and black. Serve hot off the grill.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Place garlic bulbs on large sheets of aluminum foil, up to 3 bulbs per sheet. Lightly drizzle olive oil over bulbs and season with salt and pepper. Wrap foil tightly around bulbs.

Place bulbs inside the preheated grill on the top rack away from the flames; cook until garlic cloves are butter-soft, about 30 minutes. Allow garlic bulbs to cool until easily handled. Squeeze garlic from bulb into a bowl and mash with a fork until spreadable.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add the spaghetti, and cook until al dente, or 8 to 10 minutes. Drain, and rinse under cold water. Toss with 1/4 cup olive oil, cover and keep warm.

Place another 1/4 cup olive oil in a skillet, and heat over medium heat. Stir in the garlic, and cook just until golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the sardines, and cook 1 minute more. Stir in the bread crumbs and 1/3 cup Parmesan cheese. If necessary to give the mixture a crumbly texture, stir in the remaining 1/4 cup of olive oil. Stir in the parsley and pepper, and remove from the heat. If desired, serve with additional Parmesan cheese.
Cover baking sheets with wax paper and set aside.
Combine sugar and cocoa in a large saucepan. Stir in milk, butter and peanut butter. Cook and stir over medium heat until butter melts and mixture is combined, about 5-20 minutes. Remove from heat.

Stir in the vanilla, oats and nuts, and mix thoroughly. Take a teaspoon and scoop out a spoonful of the mixture; drop the spoonful onto the waxed paper-covered baking sheet. Repeat with the rest of the mixture. Place in the refrigerator until the cookies are cooled and set. Store the cookies in an airtight container.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, combine olives, green onions, cheese, salt and curry powder. Spread this mixture on top of the sliced muffins. Arrange muffins on a cookie sheet.
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) until cheese is melted and slightly browned, about 10 minutes. Cut muffins into bite-sized wedges.
Turn on a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot(R)) and select Saute function. Add oil, celery, onion, and garlic. Saute until slightly softened, 3 to 5 minutes.

Mix bone broth, chicken broth, chicken thighs, chicken breasts, carrots, herbes de Provence, broth base, red pepper flakes, salt, pepper, and bay leaves into the pot. Close and lock the lid. Select low pressure. Set timer for 25 minutes. Allow 10 to 15 minutes for pressure to build.
Release pressure using the natural-release method according to manufacturer's instructions, 10 to 40 minutes. Remove bay leaves before serving.

Toss together the garbanzo beans, mango, romaine lettuce, cucumber, carrot, celery, lemon juice, and salt in a large bowl. Let the mixture set for 30 minutes. Top the salad with the pineapple to serve.

recipes.t: Pork Meatballs In White Wine Sauce
d: Mix the pork, egg, Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, onion powder, tarragon, and salt until everything is well incorporated; form into meatballs the size of a tablespoon. Spread bread crumbs into a shallow dish; roll meatballs in bread crumbs to coat.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook meatballs in hot oil until golden brown on all sides, 3 to 5 minutes. Add white wine half a glass at the time; cook at a simmer until the wine is reduced to a nice thick sauce, about 15 minutes.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain and rinse under cold water to cool.

Place pasta in a large bowl, and toss with the sesame oil, soy sauce, and cayenne pepper. Add the red bell pepper and cilantro and toss again until well mixed. Cover and refrigerate for one hour. Serve chilled.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place salmon on a lightly oiled sheet pan or in a shallow baking dish, folding under thin outer edges of fillets for even cooking. Top salmon with chopped tomatoes and green onions, and season with salt and pepper.
Cook salmon in the preheated oven, uncovered, for approximately 20 minutes. Fish is done when easily flaked with a fork.
Place bread in a large saucepan; cover with dark ale and water. Let soak, at least 3 hours.

Bring bread mixture to a simmer over low heat; cook until thickened, 15 to 20 minutes. Puree with an immersion blender until smooth. Stir in lemon zest, lemon juice, and sugar; bring to a boil. Ladle into bowls; top each bowl with 1 tablespoon whipping cream.
Heat oven to 350 degrees F. Grease and flour two 9-inch round baking pans.

Stir together sugar, flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt in large bowl. Add eggs, milk, oil and vanilla; beat on medium speed of mixer 2 minutes. Stir in boiling water (batter will be thin). Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes; remove from pans to wire racks. Cool completely. Frost with "PERFECTLY CHOCOLATE" CHOCOLATE FROSTING.
"PERFECTLY CHOCOLATE" CHOCOLATE FROSTING: Melt butter. Stir in cocoa. Alternately add powdered sugar and milk, beating to spreading consistency.
Add small amount additional milk, if needed. Stir in vanilla.

Combine the olive oil, whiskey, soy sauce, green onion, garlic, pepper, parsley, thyme, and rosemary in a large, sealable plastic bag; seal and shake to mix. Add the steaks to the marinade. Seal the bag, squeezing out as much air as possible. Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Remove steaks from marinade; discard the marinade. Allow the steaks to come to room temperature before cooking.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Cook the steaks until they are beginning to firm and are hot and slightly pink in the center, 6 to 7 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 140 degrees F (60 degrees C). Cover the meat with two layers of aluminum foil and allow to rest in a warm area for 10 minutes before serving.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a medium-sized mixing bowl, beat margarine and sugar until very soft. Add beaten egg, custard powder, flour, and salt. Knead well on a floured surface.
Roll out and cut with a plain biscuit cutter. Bake for 10 minutes or until pale brown.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, saute onion until translucent. Stir in flour, milk, mozzarella cheese, cottage cheese, sugar and salt; cook, stirring, until thickened.
